bsam gtan dang po'i dngos gzhi khyad par can na yod pa'i dpyod pa las gzhan pa'i yid la sogs pa de dag dang*/ 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang po'i{ dngos gzhi bsam gtan khyad par can gyi dbang shes gsum ni rtog med dpyad tsam mo/ / yang na gnyis ka yod kyang dang po'i dngos gzhi tsam so so'i sas bsdus so zhes 'dod do/ /} dngos gzhi tsam po na yod pa'i rtag pa ni rtog pa med cing dpyod pa dang bcas pa yin te/{ 'dod ngan rtog pa la rtog pa gnyis pa med cing grogs su dpyod pa nges par ldan la khyad par can na rtog pa spangs shing dpyod pa yod pa'i phyir ro/} rtog pa spangs shing dpyod pa dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i phyir dang{ phyi ma gnyis kyi} rtog pa la rtog pa gnyis pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad kyi yid la sogs pa dang*/ bsam gtan dang po'i dngos gzhi khyad par can na yod pa'i dpyod pa dang*/ sems las byung ba ma yin pa'i chos kyi khams thams cad ni rtog pa yang med dpyod pa yang med pa yin te/ bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad rtog dpyod spangs pa'i sa pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ dpyod pa la dpyod pa gnyis pa med pa'i phyir dang*/ mtshungs ldan ma yin pa dag rtog dpyod gnyis ka dang mi ldan pa'i phyir ro/{ de'i phyir rtog dpyod dang bcas pa'i sa na chos bzhi yod do/} 'o na ni dpyod pa med la rtog pa tsam yang yod par 'gyur te/ dpyod pa thams cad la'ang dpyod pa gnyis pa med pa'i phyir dang*/ bsam gtan dang po man chad kyi dpyod pa ni rtog pa dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ de ni de lta yin mod kyi 'on kyang mdo las rtog bcas dpyod bcas la sogs pa la gsum dang*/ ting nge 'dzin gsum gsungs pa dang rjes su mthun par mdzad nas tha ma gsum ni rnam gsum mo zhes gsungs pa yin no/ /

(2) The mental element that is other than analysis that exists in the special actual basis of the first absorption, {the three sense consciousnesses of} the desire realm, and the special actual basis of {the first absorption are merely analytical and not investigative. It is also asserted that if both exist, they must be associated with the specific level of the ordinary actual basis of the first absorption.} Investigation that exists in the ordinary actual basis of the first absorption is merely analytical and not investigative {because investigation in the desire realm has no second concomitant investigation though it definitely possesses analysis as a companion state, but on the special actual basis of the first absorption investigation is abandoned yet analysis remains.} That is because investigation is abandoned but concomitant analysis exists, and investigation {of the latter two} has no second concomitant investigation. (3) Those that are neither investigative nor analytical are the mental element and so on that exist on and above the second absorption, analysis that exists on the special actual basis of the first absorption, and all phenomena elements that are not mental factors, because those on and above the second absorption are levels devoid of investigation and analysis. That is because analysis does not possess analysis, and nonconcomitant states possess neither investigation nor analysis. {Therefore there are four possibilities with respect to investigative and analytical levels.} Objection: Those that are nonanalytical and merely investigative exist because no analysis possesses a second concomitant analysis, and analysis on or below the first absorption is concomitant with investigation. Reply: Indeed, it is true [that a fourth possibility — those that are nonanalytical and merely investigative — ]exists. [70] However, the sūtras declare just three possibilities, for they mention three with respect to the investigative and analytical, three regarding concentration, and three regarding compatible final states.
lhag ma mig la sogs pa gzugs can bcu po rnams ni rtog dpyod gnyis ka spangs pa yin pas gcig tu rtog pa yang med dpyod pa yang med pa nyid du nges pa yin te mtshungs ldan min pa'i phyir ro/ /

The remainder, the ten physical elements such as form, definitely possess neither investigation nor analysis; those [ten] are not concomitant with [investigation and analysis] since they lack both investigation and analysis.
nges par rtog dang rjes dran pa'i/ / rnam par rtog pas rnam mi rtog / de dag yid kyi shes rab g.yeng / / yid kyi dran pa thams cad nyid/ / 33

They are nonconceptual since they are neither decisive conception nor recalling conception. They are wisdom concomitant with distracted mental consciousness and all memory concomitant with mental consciousness. (1:33)

gal te mig la sogs pa'i rnam shes lnga po dag rtog dpyod dang bcas pa yin na/ mdo las dge slong dag mig gi rnam par shes pa dang ldan pas sngon po shes kyi sngon po'i snyam du ma yin no zhes rtog bral du bshad pa dang {rtog med kyis lus ngag gi las mi slong bar bshad pa dang } 'gal lo zhe na/

Objection: If the five consciousnesses such as eye consciousness are investigative and analytical, then it would contradict a sūtra that explains eye consciousness to be free of conception (avikalpa) {and explains that nonconceptual states do not motivate physical and verbal karma}: Monks, since you have eye consciousness you know blue, but eye consciousness does not think about blue.[378]

rtog pa ni rnam pa gsum ste/ ngo bo nyid kyi rtog pa dang nges par rtog pa'i rtog pa dang rjes su dran pa'i rtog pa'o/ / de la dbang po'i rnam shes rnams ni nges par rtog pa dang rjes su dran pa'i rnam par rtog pas rnam par mi rtog bar bshad pa yin gyi ngo bo nyid kyi rtog pa dang bral bar bshad pa ni ma yin no/ / 'o na rtog pa de dag gang zhe na/

Reply: Conception has three types: (1) natural conception (svabhāvavikalpa), (2) decisive conception (nirūpaṇavikalpa), and (3) recalling conception (anusmaraṇavikalpa). It is said that sense consciousnesses are nonconceptual since they are neither decisive conception nor recalling conception, though they are not free from natural conception. Question: What are these conceptions?

ngo bo nyid kyi rtog pa ni sems byung gi nang du 'chad par 'gyur la/ nges par rtog pa dang rjes su dran pa'i rtog pa de dag ni rim pa bzhin du yid kyi rnam shes dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i shes rab yul la rnam par g.yeng ba dang*/ yid kyis rnam shes dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i ming la ma ltos par don dran pa mnyam par bzhag ma bzhag thams cad nyid yin par shes par bya'o/ / de la yid kyi shes rab rnam par g.yeng ba ni de dang mtshungs par ldan{ pa mnyam gzhag min} pa'i thos pa dang bsams pa las byung ba dang skyes nas thob pa'o/ /

Reply: (1) Natural conception is said to be the mental factor [of investigation]. Respectively, (2) decisive conception is wisdom (prajñā) concomitant with mental consciousness that is distracted (vyagra) with regard to its object, and (3) recalling conception is all equipoise and nonequipoise memory (smṛti) concomitant with mental consciousness that recalls objects without reliance on names. Distracted mental wisdom is wisdom obtained from birth or derived from hearing or contemplation that is concomitant with distraction {and devoid of equipoise}.
gsum pa dmigs bcas la sogs pa lnga ni
Five possessing a focal object and so on
dmigs bcas sems kyi khams bdun no/ / chos kyi phyed kyang ma zin dgu/ / brgyad po de dag rnams dang sgra/ / dgu po gzhan ni rnam pa gnyis/ / 34
The seven mental elements possess focal objects as does part of the phenomena element. The nine not conjoined are those eight plus sound. The other nine have two types. (1:34)

yang khams bco brgyad las gcig tu dmigs pa dang bcas pa'i khams ni yul la dmigs nas 'dzin par byed pa'i phyir sems kyi khams bdun yin no/ / chos kyi khams kyi phyed sems las byung ba rnams kyang dmigs pa dang bcas pa yin no/ / khams lhag ma phyed dang bcu gcig ni mtshungs ldan ma yin pas dmigs pa med par grub bo/ /

From among the eighteen elements all seven mental elements (cittadhātu) possess focal objects (sālambana) because they apprehend such objects through focusing on them, as do the mental factors that constitute a part (ardha) of the phenomena element. The remaining ten and a half elements lack focal objects since they lack concomitance.[379]

khams de dag las gcig tu sems kyis ma zin pa ni dgu yin no/ / gang zhe na/ gang dag dmigs bcas su bshad pa phyed dang brgyad dang chos khams kyi phyed dang bcas pa brgyad po de dag rnams dang sgra'o/ /{ */de la brgyad po ni gzugs can min pas dbang po lnga'i tshogs pas ma bsdus pa'i phyir dang sgras ni rig bya 'dzin pa ma skyed pas so } khams lhag ma mig la sogs pa lnga dang gzugs dang dri dang ro dang reg bya zhes bya ba gzhan dgu po rnams ni zin pa dang ma zin pa rnam pa gnyis ka yin no/ / de la dbang po lnga 'das pa dang ma 'ongs pa ni ma zin pa dang*/ da ltar byung ba dag zin pa dag yin no/ gzugs la sogs pa bzhi ni da ltar byung ba dbang po'i tshogs pa na yod pa dag ni zin pa yin la/ de dag las gzhan pa rgyud kyis bsdus pa da ltar ba yin kyang rtsa ba ma gtogs pa'i skra dang ba spu dang sen mo dang so dang bshang gci dang mchil ma dang sna bas dang khrag la sogs pa dang*/ rgyud kyis ma bsdus pa'i gzugs sogs bzhi po rnams kyang ma zin pa'o/ /

From among the [eighteen] elements, nine are not conjoined (anupātta) with mind. Question: What are they? Reply: They are the eight elements said [to possess] focal objects: seven and a half elements plus half the phenomena element, plus sound. {That is because those eight are not included in the fivefold collection of sense faculties since they are not physical form, and sound does not generate apprehension of tactility.} The other nine elements remaining are the five sense organs along with the objects of form, smell, taste, and tactility. These have two types: conjoined (upātta) and not conjoined (anupātta) [with the mind]. The five sense organs of the past and future are not conjoined, but those of the present are conjoined. The four elements of form and so on that exist in the collection of sense faculties in the present [71] are conjoined. Other states associated with the mindstream exist in the present; however, hair, body hair, nails, and teeth except for their roots, and feces, urine, mucus, blood, and so on, as well as the four elements such as form, are not associated with the mindstream and not conjoined with mind.

'dir zin pa'i don ni dbang po la phan gnod byas pa'i dbang gis tshor ba bde sdug skye ba'i phyir sems dang sems byung rnams kyis rten gyi dngos por nye bar gzung ba ste 'jig rten na sems dang bcas pa zhes brjod pa gang yin pa'o/ / de nyid kyi phyir slob dpon gang spel gyis kyang zin pa ni lus su gtogs pa rnams te/ phan tshun mthun par byed pa'i phyir sems dang sems las byung ba dag gis rten gyis dngos por nye bar gzung ba'i phyir ro zhes bshad do/ / 'dir mig sogs dbang po lnga 'das pa dang ma 'ongs pa ma zin pa yin no zhes bya ba ni bye brag smra bas kun btags pa yin te/ 'das ma 'ongs ni 'gags pa dang ma skyes pa nyid kyis dngos por med pa'i phyir dang*/ dngos po med pa'ang dbang por mi 'thad pa'i phyir ro/ / des na kun las btus dang phung po lnga pa las kyang mig sogs lnga zin pa kho nar bshad cing*/ bye bshad las kyang*/ gzhan las 'di dag gnyis su ma bstan tam zhe na/ bstan mod kyi de la yang 'das pa dang ma 'ongs pa ni zin pa ma yin par ma brjod de/ de ni med pa nyid do/ / med pa ni zin pa'am zin pa ma yin par brjod du mi rung ngo*/ / da ltar ba ni rang yod par gnas pa dang*/ sems dang sems las byung ba rnams kyis zin pa nyid de/ mig la sogs pa ni ma zin pa ma yin no zhes bshad do/ /
de'i phyir dbang po dag ni gcig tu zin pa yin pas na ma zin pa dgu dang zin pa lnga dang gnyis ka yin pa ni bzhi yin no zhes bya ba nyid rigs par mngon no/ /

Here “conjoined” means that the mind and mental factors fully pervade the supportive basis because feelings of pleasure and pain arise through benefiting or harming the sense faculties. Thus they are known in the world as “associated with mind.” Master Pūrṇavardhana also notes: “Conjoined” refers to those states connected to the body. Because minds and mental factors fully pervade their supportive base, they mutually interact.[380] The Vaibhāṣikas here speculate that the five past and future sense faculties of the eyes and so on are not conjoined because they don’t exist as things, past and future sense faculties have ceased or have not yet arisen, and it is untenable that nonexistent things are sense faculties. Therefore the Compendium of Abhidharma and Five Aggregates explain that only the five sense organs are conjoined.[381] The Great Treatise on Differentiation mentions: Aren’t the others taught to be both? Indeed, that is so, but those of the past and future are not said to be “conjoined” because they do not exist and one cannot say that nonexistent entities are conjoined or not conjoined. Those of the present exist and are conjoined with minds and mental factors because it is not that the eyes and so on are not conjoined.[382]
Therefore, since all sense faculties are conjoined with the mind, it is logical to state that nine are not conjoined, five are conjoined, and four are both.
reg bya rnam pa gnyis yin te/ / lhag ma gzugs can dgu po ni/ / 'byung gyur chos khams phyogs gcig kyang / / gzugs can bcu ni bsags pa'o/ / 35
Tactile objects have two types. The nine remaining physical elements are derivative form along with one part of the phenomena element. The ten physical elements are composites. (1:35)

yang khams bco brgyad las reg bya'i khams ni 'byung ba dang 'byung ba las gyur pa rnam pa gnyis ka yin te sa la sogs pa bzhi 'byung ba dang*/ 'jam pa la sogs pa bdun 'byung ba las gyur pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / lhag ma mig la sogs pa gzugs can dgu po ni 'byung ba las gyur pa yin no/ / chos kyi khams kyi phyogs gcig rnam par rig byed ma yin pa'i gzugs kyang 'byung ba las gyur pa yin te/ 'byung ba che rnams rgyur byas pa/ / de ni rnam rig byed min brjod/ / ces rig byed ma yin pa 'bras bu'i gzugs su 'dod pa'i phyir ro/ / lhag ma sems kyi khams bdun rig byed ma yin pa ma gtogs pa'i chos kyi khams ni 'byung ba dang 'byung gyur gnyis ka ma yin no zhes bya bar grub{ ste gzugs can min} bo/ / 'dir btsun pa sangs rgyas lha skye mched gzugs can bcu 'byung ba tsam yin no zhes zer ba ni rigs pa ma yin te/ mdo las 'byung ba rnams ni bzhi nyid du gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ de dag kyang sra ba la sogs pa'i mtshan nyid can du gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ sra ba la sogs pa de dag kyang reg bya yin pa'i phyir dang*/ mig la sogs pas sra ba la sogs pa mi 'dzin zhing lus kyi dbang pos kyang kha dog la sogs pa mi 'dzin pa'i phyir dang*/ mdo las/ dge slong{ reg bya ni phyi'i skye mched yin te 'byung ba chen po bzhi dag dang 'byung ba chen po bzhi dag rgyur byas pa'o zhes pa dang} mig ni nang gi skye mched yin te/ 'byung ba chen po bzhi dag rgyur byas pa gzugs dang ba gzugs can bstan du med la thogs pa dang bcas pa'o zhes bya ba la sogs pa gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na mdo las/ gang mig gi sha'i gong bu la sra ba mkhrang bar gyur pa gang yin pa zhes{ mig dang sa khams gcig tu} gsungs pa'i don ji ltar yin zhe na/ de ni dbang po dang tshogs pa'i dbang rten gyi dbang du byas nas gsungs pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ dge slong mi 'di ni khams drug pa yin no zhes{ khams drug las med pa skad du bstan} pa'ang sems can gyi rdzas kyi gzhi bstan pa'i phyir gsungs pa yin gyi de tsam kho na ni ma yin te/ sems las byung ba rnams med par thal ba'i phyir dang*/ rnam shes nyid sems las byung ba'ang ma yin te/ mdo las/ 'du shes dang sems pa'i chos 'di ni sems las byung ba sems la brten pa'o zhes pa dang*/ sems 'dod chags dang bcas pa la sogs pa gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

From among the eighteen elements, the element of tactile objects (spraṣṭa) has two types, (1) the primary elements and (2) derivative form, because there are four primary elements — earth and so on — and seven derivative forms — smooth and so forth. The nine remaining physical (śeṣarūpin) elements such as the eyes are derivative form (bhautika). One part of the phenomena element, nonindicative form, is derivative form because nonindicative form is asserted to be resultant form, since the Abhidharmakośa states, “[that] related to the great elements that act as its cause is called nonindicative form” (1:11cd).[383] The remaining seven mental elements and the phenomena element except for nonindicative form are neither primary elements nor derivative form {for they are not established as physical entities.} In this context Bhadanta Buddhadeva says that the ten form bases are primary elements alone. Reply: That is unreasonable, for a sūtra declares, “The primary elements are four” and “They possess [72] the characteristics of solidity and so on,” because that solidity and so forth is a tactile object, the eyes and so on do not apprehend solidity, and the body sense faculty does not apprehend color and so on. A sūtra states: Monks, {tactile objects are said to be external bases because they are the four great elements and the four great elements act as their cause.[384] And:} The eye is an internal sense base because the four great elements act as the cause of subtle organs and form that is undemonstrable and impeded.[385] Question: What is the meaning of the sūtra that declares {that the eye and earth element are one}: The flesh of the eyeball is solid and hard.[386] Reply: That is stated from the perspective of the sense faculty and the composite basis of the sense faculty. A sūtra states: Monks, a human is the six elements.[387] Though {this teaches that humans don’t exist apart from the six elements,} it teaches the substantial basis of sentient beings. But it does not teach that a human is just that, because it would then follow that humans would have no mental factors. Consciousness is not a mental factor,[388] for a sūtra states: The phenomena of discernment and intention are mental factors and they rely on the mind.[389] And: The mind is associated with attachment and so on.[390]
yang khams bco brgyad las mig la sogs pa'i khams gzugs can bcu ni{ rdul phran 'dus pa'i phyir} gcig tu rdul phran bsags pa'o/ / lhag ma brgyad ni bsags pa ma yin pa'o/ /

From among the eighteen elements, all ten physical elements such as the eyes are composites (saṃcita) of atoms (paramāṇu) {because they are made up of atoms}. The remaining eight are not composites of atoms.
gcod byed gcad par bya ba nyid/ / phyi rol gyi ni khams bzhi yin/ / de bzhin bsreg bya 'jal byed pa'o/ / sreg dang gzhal la mi mthun smra/ / 36
The four external elements are those that dissect and are dissected. So too they are burned and weighed. There is disagreement over what burns and what is weighed. (1:36)

yang khams de dag las gcod par byed pa sta re lta bu dang*/ bcad par bya ba shing la sogs pa lta bu nyid ni gzugs dri ro reg bya zhes bya ba phyi rol gyi khams bzhi po de dag nyid yin gyi dbang po rnams ni bcad par bya ba ma yin te/ de ni 'dus pa'i rgyun 'brel par 'byung ba dum bur byed pa la brjod pa na dbang po rnams ni 'brel pa'i rgyun gnyis su byar med de/ lus la sogs pa bcad pa'i yan lag la dbang po{ pas dbang po gnyis su byar} med ba'i phyir ro/{ yod na des kyang de bskyed par 'gyur ro/ /}

From among those elements, the four external (bāhya) elements of form, smell, taste, and tactile objects are those that dissect (chinati), like an axe, and those that are dissected (chidya), like wood and so on. But the sense faculties cannot be dissected because when the primary elements related to the composite continuum [of a sense faculty] are split, the sense faculty is not split into two related continua. Therefore, since there is no sense faculty in a severed physical limb and so on, {sense faculties cannot be divided. But if it did exist there, that limb would regenerate.}

'o na sna la sogs pa'i rtse mo bcad pa 'byar ba na de dag gis reg bya 'dzin par ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/ bcad pa'i sna'i rtse mo la sogs pas ni reg bya mi 'dzin gyi de dag 'byar ba na 'dzin pa ni dbang po can gyi lus dang 'brel pas rgyas byung gi dbang po slar skyes pas yin no/ / rmig pu la sogs pa'i mjug ma bcad pa 'gul ba'ang rlung gis yin gyi dbang po dang sems pas ni ma yin te/ rgyud gnyis su thal ba'i phyir ro/ / dbang po rnams ni gcod par byed pa'ang ma yin te/ 'od ltar dang ba'i phyir ro/ / sgra ni rgyun med pa'i phyir dang*/ chos kyi khams dang sems kyi khams bdun ni lus med pas 'dus par mi gnas pa'i phyir gcod par byed pa dang bcad par bya ba gnyis ka ma yin no/ / ji ltar phyi rol gyi khams bzhi po dag gcod byed dang bcad bya yin pa de bzhin du mes bsreg par bya ba dang srang gis 'jal bar byed pa'ang bzhi po de dag nyid do/ / sreg par byed pa me dang gzhal bar bya ba mar la sogs pa la ni mi mthun par smra'o/ / ji ltar smra zhe na/ kha cig na re sreg par byed pa ni me kho na yin pas reg bya dang*/ gzhal bar bya ba ni lci ba kho na yin pas gnyis ka'ang reg bya kho na yin no zhes zer la/ kha cig na re reg bya kho na ma yin gyi 'on kyang phyi rol gyi khams bzhi po de dag nyid{ 'dus pa} yin no zhes zer ro/ /

Question: If a severed nose tip or the like is reattached, how does it apprehend tactile objects? Reply: The severed tip of the nose or the like does not apprehend tactile objects, but if reattached, it regenerates due to [reestablishing] its relationship with the body sense faculty and the power of enhancement (aupacayikabala). The movement of the severed tail of a lizard and so on is due to subtle wind energy and not due to the sense faculties or the mind; otherwise it would follow that there would be two mindstreams. The sense faculties do not dissect other objects; they are translucent (accha), like light. Because sound does not possess a continuum and the phenomena element and the seven elements of the mind do not abide as [physical] composites since they are nonphysical, these [elements] neither dissect nor are dissected. [73] Just as the four external elements dissect and are dissected, so too these four are burned (dāhya) by fire and weighed (tulaya) by scales. There is disagreement (vivāda) over what burns (dagdhṛ), such as fire, and what is weighed (tulya), such as butter. Question: What is meant by that? Some say: That which burns is a tactile object, since it is fire alone, and since that which is weighed is just something’s heaviness, both are solely tactile objects. Others say: They are not solely tactile objects, since the four external elements are {included in} those.
bzhi pa byung ba gsum gyi rnam pa'i rab tu dbye ba ni
Three types of derivation
rnam par smin las byung ba dang / / rgyas las byung ba nang gi lnga/ / sgra ni rnam smin las skyes min/ / rgyu mthun las byung rnam smin skyes/ / 37

The five internal elements arise from karmic maturation and enhancement. Sound does not arise from karmic maturation. The eight unimpeded elements arise from natural outflow and from karmic maturation. The others have three types. (1:37)

yang khams bco brgyad las rnam par smin pa las byung ba dang rgyas pa las byung ba ni mig la sogs pa nang gi khams lnga yin te/ mi dge ba dang dge ba zag bcas kyis bskyed pa'i phyir dang*/ rgyas pa'i rgyu dag gis rgyas par byas pa'i phyir ro/ / de la rnam par smin pa'i rgyu las byung bas na rnam par smin pa las byung ba zhes rgyu zhes pa'i bar gyi tshig mi mngon par byas pa ste dper na ba lang dang ldan pa'i shing rta la ba lang gi shing rta zhes bya ba bzhin no/ / de yang las nus pa mthu ldan du smin pa ni rnam par smin pa ste/ de las byung ba'i phyir rnam par smin pa las byung ba zhes 'bras bu la rgyu'i ming gis btags pa'am/ yang na rnam smin gyi rgyu la 'bras bu rnam smin gyi ming gis btags nas de las byung ba'i phyir rnam par smin pa las byung ba ste lo ma la tshod ma zhes brjod pa bzhin no/ / de la rgyas pa'i rgyu ni bzhi ste/ zas dang*/ bskum mnye dang dril phyis la sogs pa legs par bya ba dang*/ gnyid dang ting nge 'dzin nyid do/ /

Among the eighteen elements, the five internal elements of the eyes and so on arise from [the causes of] karmic maturation (vipākaja) and enhancement (aupacayika) because (1) they are generated by contaminated virtue and nonvirtue and (2) enhanced by the causes of enhancement. Internal elements “arise from karmic maturation” since they “arise from the cause of karmic maturation” (vipākahetuja), with the middle term “cause of” omitted, just as a cart yoked to an ox is called an “ox cart.” Further, karmic maturation refers to the powerful maturation of karmic potency. And because something arises [from karma], it “arises from karmic maturation,” for the name of the cause [“karma”] is applied to the result [“maturation”]. Again, something “arises from karmic maturation” because the name of the resultant maturation is applied to the cause of maturation, like calling certain leaves the name they are given once they are cooked. The causes of enhancement are four: (1) food, (2) pressing, rubbing, and massaging the skin, (3) sleep, and (4) concentration.

kha cig ni tshangs par spyod pa dang lnga yin no zhes zer mod kyi de ni mi gnod pa tsam du zad kyi rgyas par byed pa ni ma yin no/ / zhes {bye brag tu smra ba/ } slob dpon 'chad do/ / de dag las byung ba'i phyir rgyas pa las byung ba'o/ / rgyas pa'i rgyud ni rnam smin gyi rgyud{ de dbang po} la phyir bzhin du bskor te gnas pas kun du srung ngo*/{ ste zas sogs kyis rgyas pas rnam smin gyi dbang po la yang phan 'dogs pas so/} gal te nang gi lnga la rgyu mthun las byung ba yod na byung ba gnyis kho nar mi 'thad la/ med na tha ma gsum/ skad cig ma ste zhes pa'i 'grel par sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa'i tshogs kyi skad cig dang po ma gtogs pa'i 'dus byas gzhan ni rgyu mthun pa las ma byung ba 'ga' yang med do zhes bshad pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/ de gnyis la rang rang gi rigs 'dra snga ma las phyi ma 'byung ba'i rgyu mthun yod pas skyon phyi ma med la gnyis las ma gtogs pa'i rgyu mthun las byung ba gsum pa med pas skyon dang po las grol lo/{ tha dad pa yod na shi ba'i ro la yang dbang po gzugs can gyi rgyun dmigs par thal te gzugs sogs kyi rgyu mthun dmigs pa bzhin no/ / spyir rnam smin chad kyang rgyas byung gis gnas pa yod de rol bzhin/ rgyas byung med kyang cig shos kyi gnas pa yod pa de dmyal ba'i lus bzhin no/}

sgra'i khams ni rnam smin las skyes pa yin te/ rnam smin gzugs can ni{ chad nas mtshams mi sbyor zhing} 'dod pa tsam gyis 'byung ba ma yin la/ sgra ni{ chad nas mtshams sbyor zhing brjod par} 'dod pa'i dbang gis 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / 'o na gdags pa'i bstan bcos las/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i gsung sgra gdangs kyi mtshan/ / gang gis 'thob par 'gyur ba mnyan par gyis/ / tshig rtsub dang ni kyal pa rnam spangs pas/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i mtshan ni thob par 'gyur zhes{ ston pa'i gsung} rnam smin las skyes par bshad pa dang*/ lung phran tshegs las/ {tshe dang ldan pa/} snyan pa bzang ldan gyi nga ro snyan pa'ang sngon sangs rgyas 'khor ba 'jig gi mchod rten la dril bu phul ba dang khu byug tu skyes pa na sangs rgyas 'od srung la sems dad pas skad snyan pa byung ste bskor ba byas pa'i rnam smin las byung bar bshad pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/ 'di la nyi 'og bye brag tu smra ba rnams ni las de dag las rnam smin gyi bdag nyid kyi 'byung ba dag 'grub la/ de las ni gsung tshangs pa'i sgra dbyangs ltar snyan pa 'byung bas brgyud pa gsum pa yin no zhes bya bar 'dod la/ kha che ba ni las las rnam smin las skyes pa'i 'byung ba dang*/ de las rgyas byung dang*/ de las rgyu mthun las byung ba dang*/ de las gsung dbyangs 'byung ba'i phyir brgyud pa lnga pa yin no zhes zer te/

The element of sound does not arise from karmic maturation (vipāka) because physical karmic maturation {does not link [with a subsequent similar state] when disrupted,} nor does it arise through desire alone, but sound {does link [with a subsequent similar state] when disrupted and} arises due to the desire {to express something}. Objection: This contradicts the Treatise on Designation, which explains {that a buddha’s speech} arises from karmic maturation: By listening to how you obtain the mark of the clear intonation of a tathāgata’s speech through abandoning harsh words and nonsense, you come to obtain the mark of a tathāgata.[394] And it is said in the Kṣudraka Collection: The melodious voice of the {honorable} Priyabhadraka was the karmic maturation of offering a bell to the stūpa of Buddha Krakucchanda, and when born a cuckoo with a melodious voice, he circumambulated Buddha Kāśyapa with a mind of faith.[395] Aparāntaka Vaibhāṣikas assert that the series is threefold, since from (1) those karmas (2) the state of karmic maturation is established, and from that arises (3) melodious speech like the euphony of Brāhma’s speech. Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas state that the series is fivefold, since from (1) karma arises (2) that which is generated through karmic maturation, from that arises (3) enhancement, from that arises (4) natural outflow, and from that arises (5) a euphonic voice.

gnyis ka ltar na'ang de dag las brgyud nas byung bas de ltar bshad kyi dngos su ni ma yin te/ de ni 'dod pa tsam gyis mi 'byung ba dang*/ chad nas mtshams mi sbyor bar thal ba'i phyir ro/{ de tsam gyis rnam smin du mi 'gyur na tshor ba la'ang mtshungs te las las 'byung ba de las tshor ba skyes pas so zhe na mi mtshungs te sgra 'dod dgur 'byung bas dang lus tshor 'ga' zhig mi 'dod kyang 'byung bas rnam smin yin la da ltar gyi yul gyi rkyen las byung ba kha cig ni rnam smin yin no/ /} de'i phyir sgra{ lus rgyas na skad che bas} rgyas byung dang{ rigs 'dra phye ma yod pas} rgyu mthun las byung ba ni yod do zhes bya bar shes so/ /

Reply: Thus both [schools] explain how [speech] arises indirectly in a series, and they do not assert it arises directly, because in that case it would [absurdly] follow that [speech] would not arise from the mere desire [to speak] nor link [with prior speech] when disrupted. {Objection: If [speech] does not arise merely through karmic maturation, then feeling also would be similar, since [karmic maturation] arises from karma, and feeling arises from [karmic maturation]. Reply: They are not similar; sound arises through a particular desire [to speak], and physical feelings that arise without any desire for them are karmic maturation. Some say: They are karmic maturation since they arise due to present objects acting as their conditions.} In that case sound should be understood as arising from enhancement {since if the body is enhanced, the voice is louder}, and it arises from natural outflow {since sound of a subsequent, similar type exists}.

rgyu mthun las byung ba dang rnam smin las skyes pa ni sems kyi khams bdun dang chos kyi khams te thogs pa med pa brgyad po de dag yin te/ skal mnyam dang kun 'gro'i rgyus bskyed pa dang*/ rnam smin gyi rgyus bskyed pa dag yod pa'i phyir dang*/ rgyas byung ni med de/ brgyad po de dag bsags par ma gnas pas gzugs can rgyas pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / khams lhag ma gzhan gzugs dri ro reg bya rnam pa bzhi ni rnam smin las byung ba la sogs pa rnam gsum ga yod de/ dbang po'i tshogs pa na yod pa dag la rnam pa gsum ga dang*/ phyi rol ni rgyu mthun las byung bar gnas so/ /

The eight unimpeded (apratighā) elements — the seven mental elements and the phenomena element — arise from natural outflow and from karmic maturation because they are generated by a homogeneous cause, omnipresent cause, as well as the cause of karmic maturation. Those eight do not arise from enhancement; they do not possess physical enhancement since they are not [physical] composites. The other remaining elements — the four elements of sound, smell, taste, and tactility — have three types, such as arising from karmic maturation, because the collection of sense faculties has three types and the external elements arise from natural outflow.
lnga pa rdzas yod la sogs pa lnga bshad pa ni
Five such as substantial existence
thogs pa med brgyad gzhan rnam gsum/ / rdzas dang ldan gcig tha ma gsum// skad cig ma ste mig dang ni/ / rnam shes khams dag so so dang / / 38 lhan cig tu yang 'thob pa yod/ /
One possesses substantial existence. The last three are momentary. The elements of eye and eye consciousness are obtained separately. They are also obtained simultaneously. (1:38)

yang khams bco brgyad las gcig tu rtag cing brtan pa'i rdzas su ngo bor yod pa dang ldan pa ni chos kyi khams zhes bya ba gcig pu'i phyogs 'dus ma byas so/ / de la rdzas su yod pa ni rtag cing brtan par gnas pa dang*/ don byed nus pa dang*/ rang rgyud du grub pa dang*/ de las gzhan pa bzhi las 'dir ni dang po'i dbang du byas pa'o/ / de las gzhan pa'i khams lhag ma rnams ni{ 'dus byas yin pas} rtag cing brtan pa'i rdzas su med par grub bo/ /

From among the eighteen elements, one part [75] of the phenomena element — the unconditioned — possesses stable and permanent substantial existence (dravyavāt). Substantial existence has four possible attributes: (1) stability and permanence, (2) the capacity to function, (3) establishment within a continuum, and (4) that other than those. As such [unconditioned phenomena] are defined in light of the first attribute, and the remaining elements {since they are conditioned phenomena} are not substantially existent stable and permanent states.

khams de dag las tha ma yid dang chos dang yid kyi rnam shes kyi khams gsum gyi phyogs gcig ni rgyu mthun las ma byung ba'i skad cig ma{ yang yod} ste/ de dag kyang gang zhe na/ sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa'i skad cig ma dang po'i tshogs pa na yod pa'i yid dang chos dang yid kyi rnam shes kyi khams zag med gsum ni 'jig rten chos mchog man chad zag bcas yin pas zag med snga ma sngon du ma song bas{ de yang 'di dus mtha' ma'i skad cig yin la/ sdug bsngal la chos bzod bya rdzogs kyi skad cig yin pas de yang dus mtha'i skad cig gnyis pa phan chad rgyu mthun las byung ba yin no} 'di dag gis ni rgyu mthun las byung rnam smin skyes/ thogs pa med brgyad ces bya ba'i spyir btang ba la dmigs kyis bsal ba ston par byed de/ {zag med skad cig dang po'i/ } yid la sogs pa gsum rgyu mthun dang rnam smin las ma byung ba dang*/ chos kyi khams kyi phyogs gcig 'dus ma byas rtag pa ni byung ba gsum ga ma yin par bstan pa'i phyir ro/{ zag med dang po skad cig dang po ma yin pa'i 'dus byas thams cad ni rgyu mthun las byung ba yin no/ /} 'o na gang mig gi khams dang mi ldan pa las gsar du thob pa de mig gi rnam shes kyi khams kyang gsar du thob bam zhe na/ mu bzhi ste/

{Also} within the last three elements — the mental element, phenomena element, and mental consciousness element — one part is momentary (kṣaṇika) but not derived from natural outflow. Question: What [part] is that? Reply: That is the three uncontaminated parts of the mental element, phenomena element, and mental consciousness element that exist in the first moment of perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering. Uncontaminated phenomena do not precede them since elements on or below the supreme mundane state are contaminated. {Since these three constitute a smallest moment[396] while perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering constitutes a moment required to complete an action, they arise from natural outflow from the second [i.e., the subsequent] smallest moment on.} Due to that, [the words] “the eight unimpeded elements arise from natural outflow and from karmic maturation” (1:37cd) in general teach a special case because they teach that the three elements: the mental element and so on {of the first moment of the uncontaminated state} do not arise from natural outflow or from karmic maturation. Yet permanent, unconditioned states of the phenomena element do not arise from any of the three causes. {All conditioned phenomena other than the first moment of the uncontaminated state arise from natural outflow.} Question: Does one who initially does not possess the eye element but who newly obtains it also newly obtain the eye consciousness element?

'di ltar mig gi khams dang mig gi rnam shes kyi khams dag so so dang zhes pas mu dang po gnyis bstan te/ de la mu dang po mig gi dbang po dang mi ldan pa las ldan pa thob la mig shes dang mi ldan pa ni 'dod par skyes pa rim gyis mig gi dbang po 'thob pa{ la lung ma bstan gyi thob pa phyir mi 'byung gi dus mnyam pas} dang*/ gzugs med nas shi 'phos nas bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad du skyes pa ste/ dang po ni mig shes dge ba dang nyon mongs can{ gyi thob pa dus gsum du 'byung bas des na} sngar du thob zin pa'i phyir dang*/ gnyis pa gzugs med ni bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad rang sa na mig shes med pa'i phyir dang*/ dbang po ni gsar du thob pa'i phyir ro/ { de yang mig mkhan dang ldan pa ni bsam gtan phyi ma gsum du skyes pa mig shes mngon du mi byed pa na'o/ / mig shes kho na dang ldan pa ni 'dod pa na mig ma thob pa dang nyams pa dang ste/ mig lung ma bstan gyi thob pa sngar phyir mi 'byung ba mig shes dang nying mtshams sbyar ba dang ldan no/ / gnyis ka dang ldan pa ni 'dod pa na mig thob la ma nyams pa dang*/ dang po dang gnyis pa la sogs par skyes pa gzugs la blta ba'i tshe ste/ bsam gtan dang po gsum la ni gzhan gyi sa pa'i mig kyang srid do/ / bzhi pa ni gzugs med du skyes pa na'o/ / de bzhin du mig dang gzugs dag dang*/ mig shes dang gzugs dag thob pa dang ldan pa'i mu bzhi sogs kyang rig par bya ste/ mig dang yin la gzugs dang ma yin pa ni rim gyis mig dbang thob pa na'o/ / gzugs gsar du thob la mig ma thob pa ni med de/ gzugs med nas 'og mar skye ba'ang bar srid dbang po tshang bar 'byung nges so/ / mu gsum pa dang bzhi pa ni sngar bshad pa thams cad shes par bya'o/ /

Reply: There are four possibilities since “the elements of eye and eye consciousness are obtained separately (pṛthag),” and this [statement] reveals the first two possibilities. (1) The first possibility is that the eye sense faculty is obtained after not possessing it but eye consciousness is not possessed. This refers to (a) those who take birth in the desire realm who obtain the eye sense faculty in stages, {since obtainment of neutral states occurs simultaneously not later,} or to (b) those who die in the formless realm who are reborn in the second absorption or higher. That is because, in the first case, {obtainment of} virtuous or afflicted eye consciousness {occurs in the three times} after the eyes are obtained, whereas in the second case — {that of formless beings} reborn in the second absorption or higher — beings do not have eye consciousness but newly obtain the eye sense faculty. {(a) Those who possess eyes alone are those born in the latter three absorptions, where eye consciousness does not manifest. (b) Those who possess eye consciousness alone are those in the desire realm who either do not obtain eyes or they degenerate, for the obtainment of neutral states such as the eyes does not occur earlier or later and it is linked to eye consciousness. (c) Those who possess both are those who obtain eyes in the desire realm that do not degenerate, or those born in the first or second absorption and so on. It is also possible that those in the first three absorptions use eyes of other levels. (d) [Those who possess neither] are those born in the formless realm. So too, you should recognize [76] that there are four possibilities regarding the obtainment of eyes and form, or eye consciousness and form: (a) Obtaining eyes but not form occurs when the eye sense faculty is obtained in stages. (b) Newly obtaining form but not obtaining eyes does not exist because those to be born in lower levels [after dying in] the formless realm definitely arise as intermediate beings complete in sense faculties. (c) The third and (d) fourth possibilities should be understood in accordance with all prior explanations.

yang gang mig gi khams dang ldan pa de gzugs dang yang yin nam zhe na tshig snga ma dang sbyor te mig dang ldan pa de gzugs dang yang ldan no/ / gzugs dang yin la mig dang ma yin pa yod de/ dmus long dang mig ma thob pa nur nur po la sogs pa dang rkyen gyis nyams pa'o/ / mig shes gsar du thob pa de gzugs kyang thob bam zhe na/ so so dang*/ lhan cig tu yang thob pa yod ces pa mu bzhi ste/ dang po ni bsam gtan gnyis pa la sogs par skyes pa mig shes mngon du byed pa na'o/ / gnyis pa ni gzugs med nas bsam gtan gong ma gsum du skyes pa na'o/ / gsum pa ni gzugs med nas 'dod pa dang tshangs pa'i 'jig rten du skyes pa na'o/ / bzhi pa ni gzugs med nas de nyid du skye ba dang*/ 'dod pa dang*/ dang po nas shi nas de nyid du skye bas te 'di la sngar nas ldan pas so/ / mig shes dang ldan pa de gzugs dang yang ldan nam zhe na ldan no zhes brjod de/ gzugs dang ldan pas mig shes dang mi ldan pa ni bsam gtan gong ma gsum du skyes pa mig shes mngon du ma byas pa na'o/ / rna ba la sogs pa la'ang de bzhin du sbyar ro/ /}

Question: Is the possession of the eye element also the possession of form? Reply: One should apply the above words because the possession of eyes is also the possession of form. Those who possess form but do not possess eyes are those born blind, or embryonic states such as kalala[397] that have not yet obtained eyes, or those whose eyes degenerate due to adverse conditions. Question: Do those who newly obtain eye consciousness also obtain form? Reply: There are four possibilities, for there is separate as well as simultaneous obtainment: (a) those born in the [form realm’s] second absorption and higher, who manifest eye consciousness, [newly obtain eye consciousness but not form], (b) those newly born in these same three higher absorptions after the formless realm [newly obtain form but not eye consciousness], (c) those born in the desire realm and the heaven of Brahma [i.e., the first absorption] after the formless realm [newly obtain both], and (d) those born [in the formless realm] after the formless realm and those reborn [in the formless realm] after death in the desire realm and the first absorption, who possessed this state before, [obtain neither]. Question: Do those who possess eye consciousness also possess form? Reply: It is said they do possess form since those who possess form but do not possess eye consciousness are those born in the three higher absorptions, where eye consciousness does not manifest. This also applies to the ears and so on.}

mig shes mi ldan pa ldan pa thob la mig dang mi ldan pa'i mu gnyis pa ni bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad pa dag bsam gtan dang po'i mig shes mngon du byas nas gzugs la lta ba dang*/{ rang sa na mig shes med pas sngar nas mi ldan no/} bsam gtan gnyis pa la sogs pa nas shi 'phos nas 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang por bar srid du nying mtshams sbyor ba'i tshe na ste/ dang po ni gzugs khams pa dag dbang po tshang ba can yin pas mig sngar nas yod pa'i phyir dang*/ phyi ma ni bar srid du nying mtshams sbyor ba na rnam shes dge ba dang nyon mongs can{ gsar du} thob kyang TI ka las mig gi khams dang ni sngar med ldan pa ma yin te/ dbang po ni bar ma chad pas thob zin pa bzhin du ldan pa'i phyir ro zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

(2) In the second possibility, eye consciousness is obtained after not possessing it, but the eyes are not possessed. This refers to those in the second absorption and above who, due to having had eyes from before, view form through manifesting eye consciousness of the first absorption, since those of the form realm have complete faculties. Or it refers to those who, {not previously possessing eye consciousness of their own level,} die in the second absorption and so on and become intermediate beings of either the desire realm or the first absorption. For when they become intermediate beings, they {newly} obtain virtuous or afflicted eye consciousness. The Subcommentary clarifies: It is not that the eye element is possessed without having been previously possessed; it is possessed having already been obtained, since the sense faculties are unobstructed.[398]

mu gsum pa mig gi khams dang mig gi rnam shes kyi khams dag lhan cig tu yang 'thob pa yod de/ gzugs med nas shi 'phos nas 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang por skye ba lta bu ste/ de ni sngar de gnyis dang mi ldan pas bar srid du nying mtshams sbyor ba na bar srid pa ni dbang po tshang ba can yin pa'i phyir dang*/ mig shes dge ba dang nyon mongs can 'das ma 'ongs kyi thob pa'ang gnas skabs der 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / mu bzhi pa gnyis ka ma yin pa ni yang zhes pas bstan te rnam pa de dag ma gtogs pa{ ste gzugs med nas shi ba de nyid du skye ba dang*/ bsam gtan phyi ma gsum du skyes pa mig shes mngon du mi byed pa dang*/ 'dod pa'i mig ldan cig car shi ba khams gong ma gnyis su skyes pa dang rgyud kyis ma bsdus pa rnams so }'o/ gzhan yang yang gi sgras 'grel pa las ldan pa'i mu bzhi dang mig dang gzugs dang*/ mig shes dang gzugs kyis 'thob pa dang ldan pa gzung bar 'chad do/ /

(3) The third possibility is that [both] the eye element and the eye consciousness element are also obtained simultaneously (sahā). This refers to those who die in the formless realm and are reborn in the desire realm or the first absorption, becoming intermediate beings with complete sense faculties. Since they did not possess those two before they became intermediate beings, the obtainment of past and future virtuous and afflicted eye consciousnesses occurs at that time. (4) The fourth possibility, that which is neither, is taught by the term “also” (1:38d), which excludes those [mentioned in the first three possibilities such as] {those who die in the formless realm and are reborn in either the formless realm or any of the three higher absorptions who do not manifest eye consciousness; and those who possess eyes in the desire realm who die and are simultaneously reborn in either of the two higher realms, and who possess neither in their mindstreams.} Again, the Autocommentary explains that the term “also” (1:38d) refers to the four possibilities for obtainment of the eyes and form or of eye consciousness and form.[399] [77]
nang gi bcu gnyis gzugs la sogs/ / ma gtogs chos zhes bya ba ni/ / rten pa dang bcas lhag ma ni/ / 39 de dang mtshungs pa dag kyang yin/ / gang zhig rang gi las mi byed/ /
Twelve are internal except for form and so on. That which is called phenomena is homogeneous. The remainder are also partially homogeneous [when their] own discrete function is not activated. (1:39)

yang khams de dag las gcig tu nang gi yin pa ni mig la sogs pa{ drug dang rnam shes drug dang} bcu gnyis te/ gang zhe na/ gzugs dang sogs pas bsdus pa sgra dang dri dang ro dang reg bya dang chos kyi khams te drug ma gtogs pa'o/ / des na gzugs la sogs pa drug ni phyi'i yin par grub bo/ / chos kyi khams la tshor ba la sogs pa mtshungs par ldan pa dag nang yin la/ mtshungs par mi ldan pa'i 'du byed phal che ba dang 'dus ma byas dag phyi yin pas gnyis ka yin par bshad par rigs mod kyi 'on kyang phyi'i skye mched drug ces grags pa dang mthun pa'i dbang mdzad nas bshad par mngon no/ / 'dir nang dang phyi ni sems can gyi rgyud kyis bsdus pa dang ma bsdus pa la brjod par 'dod kyi bdag la nang dang bdag med pa la phyi yin no zhes phyi rol pas kun btags pa ltar ni ma yin no/ / 'o na lung sil bu las/ bdag nyid bdag gi mgon yin gyi/ / gzhan lta su zhig mgon du 'gyur/ / mkhas pas bdag nyid shin tu ni/ / dul bas mtho ris thob par 'gyur/ / zhes gsungs pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/ de ni sems la bdag gi sgra mdzad pa yin te/ de'i mjug thogs su gzung bar dka' zhing myur bar 'jug gang du 'dod pa der 'jug byed/ / sems dul ba ni legs pa ste/ / sems dul bas ni bde ba 'dren/ / zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

From among those elements, twelve are internal (ādhyātmika): {the six} eyes and so on {and the six consciousnesses}. Question: What are they? Reply: They are those except for the six such as form and so on, including sound, smell, taste, tactile objects, and the phenomena element. Therefore the six including form and so on are established as external. Still, it is appropriate to call the phenomena element both internal and external since states concomitant with feeling and so on within the phenomena element are internal and unconditioned phenomena and most nonassociated formative factors are external. However, together they are called “the six external elements” to conform with common usage, where elements are called “internal” or “external” due to whether or not they are conjoined to the mindstreams of sentient beings but not to conform with the non-Buddhist assertion that “the self is internal and the selfless is external.” Objection: This contradicts what is said in the Miscellaneous Discourses: I am my own protector; who else could be my protector? The wise who completely tame the self come to obtain high rebirth.[400] Reply: The term “self” is applied to the mind because that text states, in conclusion: The self engages whatever object it desires; it is difficult to hold and extremely swift. But taming the mind is excellent for the tamed mind brings happiness.[401]

yang khams bco brgyad po de dag las chos kyi khams zhes bya ba ni gcig tu rten pa dang bcas pa zhes bya ba yin te/ {yul gang zhig shes pa gang gi yul du nges la de la shes pa de skyes pa'am skye bar 'gyur ba'i yul de ni rten bcas yin na yid shes ma skyes pa'am skye bar mi 'gyur ba'i yul lam chos de ni gang med pas 'di ltar/ } 'phags pa'am so so'i skye bo yang rung ste de dag gis yid kyi rnam shes skye ba'i bya ba byed pas khyab pa'i phyir te/ 'di'i lugs kyi rang rig mi 'dod pas chos thams cad bdag med do zhes bya ba'i yid kyi yul du ni rang gi shes pa dang de dang lhan cig 'byung ba'i mtshungs ldan ma yin pa dag ma gtogs pa thams cad kyang 'gyur ba'i phyir ro zhes bya bar 'dod de/ rang rig 'dod na ni de yang 'gyur ba'i phyir 'di ni bye brag tu smra ba'i yin no/ / 'di'i lugs kyis kyang skad cig ma gnyis pa'i yid shes kyi dmigs par ni chos thams cad gyur pas chos kyi khams ni rtag tu rten bcas yin no/{ 'o na khams bco brgyad po thams cad rten bcas kho nar 'gyur te bdag med rtogs pa'i shes pa'i yul yin pa'i phyir ro zhe na de kho nas rten bcas su mi 'jog gi ste/ lhag ma rnams la ni rang rang byed pa gzhan re yod pas de mi byed pa ni de mtshungs so/ /}

khams lhag ma bcu bdun po dag ni de dang mtshungs pa dag kyang yin no/ / kyang gi sgras rten pa dang bcas pa'ang yod do zhes bsdu ba'i phyir ro/ / 'o na rten bcas de mtshungs kyi don gang zhe na/ mig gang gis gzugs bltas pa dang lta ba dang lta bar 'gyur ba ni rten bcas yin pa nas lus kyi bar du'ang de bzhin du shes par bya ste/{ khams gang zhig rang gi las byed pas so/ /} de dang mtshungs pa ni mig gang gis gzugs ma mthong bar 'gags pa dang*/ 'gag pa dang*/ 'gag par 'gyur ba dang mi skye ba'i chos can dang bzhi yin no zhes kha che ba dag zer la/ nub phyogs ba ni mi skye ba'i chos can la{ 'dod pa dang dang po'i lta bu} rnam shes dang ldan pa dang{ gnyis pa sogs kyi} mi ldan pa gnyis yod pas sngar 'gyur ro zhes zer ro/ / de bzhin du gzugs la sogs pa'i khams lnga la'ang{ mthong ba dang ma mthong bar 'gyur ba dang zhes sogs} sbyar bar bya'o/{ de la mig sogs bzhi'i rdul ni res 'ga' can rten bcas sam de mtshungs dang res 'ga' phyogs re'o/ / lus ni thams cad kyis mi bskyed de zhig par thal bas so zhes zer kyang thams cad kyis skyed kyang zhig par mi 'gyur te las kyis gzung bas so zhes lan 'debs so/ /} sems kyi khams bdun ni skye ba thams cad rten bcas{ yin te dmigs pa 'dzin pas} dang*/ mi skye ba{ de mi 'dzin pa} ni de dang mtshungs pa yin no zhes rig par bya ste/ rnam shes skye ba dag rang gi yul la bya ba byed par nges pa'i phyir ro/ /

The remainder — the seventeen elements — are also partially homogeneous (tatsabhāga). The term “also” indicates that “there are those that are also homogeneous.” Question: What is the meaning of “partially homogeneous”? Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas say that form that was seen, is seen, or [78] will be seen by the eyes is homogeneous, and that applies up to [objects] of the body, {since [eyes] are an element whose own function is activated.} That “partially homogeneous” refers to the four: form not seen that (1) has ceased, (2) is ceasing, (3) will cease, or (4) is an instance of nonarising. Aparāntaka Vaibhāṣikas say nonarising is twofold, making five instances in all. Eye consciousness, they say, is possessed {in the desire realm and first absorption, for example,} but not possessed {in the second absorption and so on}. So too, this should be applied to the five elements — form {that is said to be seen or not seen and so forth.} {Regarding that, some say that [the subtle] particles of the four such as eyes and so on are sometimes entirely homogeneous and sometimes partially homogeneous. But if the body were not generated by all [four elements], it would disintegrate. In response it can be said that though it is not generated by all, it does not disintegrate because it is held together by karma.} It should be recognized that the seven mental elements are homogeneous for all instances of arising {since their focal objects are apprehended} and partially homogeneous for instances of nonarising {since their focal objects are not apprehended}. For consciousness definitely ascertains instances of arising that it takes as its object.
'o na rten bcas dang de mtshungs kyi khyad par gang zhe na/
Question: What is the difference between homogeneous and partially homogeneous?

khams gang zhig rang gi bya ba'i las mi byed pa de dang mtshungs pa dang*/ byed pa de ni rten bcas te/ de yang mig nas yid kyi bar khams drug ni skyes bu gnyis la sogs pa mig la sogs pa gcig gis lta ba la sogs pa byed pa mi srid pas gcig gis rten bcas yin pa de thams cad kyi rten bcas dang*/ gcig gi de mtshungs yin pa de thams cad kyi de mtshungs yin la/{ de yang gcig gi rten bcas yin pa de kun gyi rten bcas yin te gzhan la ltos nas kyang rang gi bya ba byas pas so/ / gzhan gyi lta ba la sogs pa'i bya ba ma byas pa'i phyir de la rten bcas min no zhe na gzhan gyi lta ba la sogs pa kho na'i bya ba ma yin te gang zag gcig gi dbang po dang shes pas gang zag du ma'i yul lta ba la sogs pa'i bya ba mi byed pas so des na 'di gang zag thams cad kyi thun mong ba yin pas de'i bya ba yang rgyud gcig gi bzhag go} gzugs nas reg bya'i bar khams lnga ni zla ba dang bro gar dang gyad dang rnga sgra la sogs pa la gcig lta ba la sogs pa byed pa de la gzhan mang po'ang lta ba la sogs pa byed pa srid pas de dag thun mong ba yin pas gang zhig lta ba la sogs pa de la ltos nas rten bcas dang*/ gang zhig lta sogs mi byed pa de la ltos nas ni de mtshungs yin no/{ de yang yul ni thun mong ma yin pas gang zag du ma'i shes pa skyed pa'i nus pa yod pa'i phyir rgyud du ma'i dbang gis 'jog go}

Objection: It is understood that both form and sound are apprehended without contact, whereas smells and so on are apprehended through contact. But since anything apprehended by Devadatta’s sense faculties is not apprehended by Pūjādatta’s sense faculties, [form and so on] would be similar to the eyes because sense faculties are not shared. Reply: They are not similar because if those [smells and so on] contact Devadatta’s nose sense faculty and so on, then his nose consciousness and so forth is generated, and if they contact Pūjādatta’s nose sense faculty [79] and so on, then his nose consciousness and so forth is generated. But it is uncertain that the nose consciousness of just one person is produced, because it is uncertain that contact with a specific nose sense faculty and so on generates nose consciousness for just that being, since it is possible that nose consciousness is produced in a parasite living in that being’s nose. Therefore the eyes and so on are posited in terms of one mindstream since they are not shared, but the five elements of form and so on are posited in terms of many mindstreams since they are shared. {Objection: Phenomena are homogeneous through being apprehended and partially homogeneous through not being apprehended. Reply: But since this refers to the five [sense] objects alone, it negates those who do not take them as their objects, and since all phenomena of the three times and those not subsumed by time are objects of the second moment of mental consciousness, [this assertion] is inappropriate.}

'dir sems kyi khams bdun la rten bcas dang de mtshungs gnyis ka yod par bshad pa ni bye brag tu smra bas ma 'ongs pa mi skye ba'i chos can zhes bya ba 'dod pa'i dbang du byas pa ste/ gong ma ba dag ni de mi 'dod pas kun las btus dang*/ phung po lnga pa la sogs pa las dngos su mig la sogs pa nang gi khams gzugs can lnga po nyid rten bcas dang de mtshungs su bshad la/ khams gzhan dag la ni de gnyis ma bshad med kyi shugs kyis sems kyi khams bdun dang chos kyi khams dang brgyad ni rten bcas kho na yin la/ gzugs sogs phyi rol gyi khams lnga ni rten bcas dang de mtshungs gnyis kar 'gyur te/ bye bshad las/ mig la sogs pa 'di dag ni thun mong ma yin pa'i phyir gcig gi rten pa mtshungs pa dang de dag dang mtshungs pa gang yin pa de dag ni sems can thams cad kyi'ang yin pas 'di dag gi rten pa mtshungs pa dang de dag dang mtshungs pa ni nges pa'o/ / gzugs la sogs pa ni so so'i rgyud la rten pa mtshungs pa dang de dag dang mtshungs pa nyid du gnas so/ / rnam par shes pa las byed pa gzhan med pa'i phyir gzhan dag la ni rten pa mtshungs pa dang de dag dang mtshungs pa zhes mi brjod do zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

Vaibhāṣikas here explain that the seven mental elements are both homogeneous and partially homogeneous from the perspective of asserting the instance of future nonarising. Higher schools do not assert this, since the Compendium of Abhidharma, Five Aggregates, and so on explicitly state that the five internal physical elements are both homogeneous and partially homogeneous.[403] Though they do not state that other elements are both, indirectly they explain that eight — the seven elements of mind and the phenomena element — are homogeneous alone, and that the five external elements such as form are both homogeneous and partially homogeneous. The Great Treatise on Differentiation states: Because elements such as the eyes are not shared, they are homogeneous for one [being]; those that pertain to all sentient beings are partially homogeneous. Therefore they are ascertained as homogeneous and partially homogeneous. Form and so on exist as homogeneous and partially homogeneous in each mindstream. Because there is no active agent other than consciousness, the remainder are not called either “homogeneous” or “partially homogeneous.”[404]
drug pa mthong spang la sogs pa'i rnam pa'i dbye ba ni
Objects to be eliminated by the path of seeing
bcu ni bsgom pas spang bya yin/ / lnga yang tha ma gsum rnam gsum/ / 40 nyon mongs can min mthong spang min/ / gzugs min drug pa min skyes min/ /

Ten are abandoned by meditation. Also five. The last three have three types. They are not abandoned by seeing because they are not afflictive. Form is not. Those not arising from the sixth are not. (1:40)

yang khams bco brgyad las/ mig gi khams la sogs pa gzugs can bcu ni sgom pas spang bar bya ba yin te/ zag bcas yin pas spang bya yin pa'i phyir dang*/ bden pa la log par mi rtog pa'i phyir dang*/{des kun nas ma bslangs pas/}de dang 'brel ba'ang ma yin pas mthong spang yang ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / ji ltar gzugs can bcu sgom spang yin pa de bzhin du mig la sogs pa'i rnam shes lnga yang sgom spang yin te/{ kha phyir ltos shing*/} rgyu mtshan ni snga ma dang mtshungs pa'i phyir ro/ / khams tha ma yid dang chos dang yid kyi rnam shes kyi khams gsum ni sgom spang dang*/ mthong spang dang*/ spang bya ma yin pa rnam pa gsum du 'gyur ro/ / lta ba{ dang the tshom} la sogs pa 'og nas 'chad pa'i phra rgyas brgyad cu rtsa brgyad dang*/ de dag dang mtshungs par ldan pa dang*/ de dag gi mtshan nyid dang*/ rjes su mthun pa'i mtshan nyid dang*/ thob pa dang bcas pa ni mthong spang dang*/ zag bcas lhag ma rnams ni sgom spang dang*/ {nyes pa med pas/ } zag med rnams ni spang bya ma yin pa'o/ / 'dir gnas ma'i bu'i sde pa dag so so skye bo dang ngan song ba'i lus ngag gi las mthong spang yin te/ {'phags lam dang 'gal bas/ } mthong lam skyes pa na so so'i skye bo 'gag pa'i phyir dang*/ mdo las rgyun du zhugs pa'i ngan song gi 'gro ba 'gags so zhes gsungs pa'i phyir zhes bya bar 'dod do/ /

From among the eighteen elements, the ten physical elements such as the eye element are objects to be abandoned (heya) by the path of meditation (bhāvana). They should be abandoned because they are contaminated, because they do not wrongly conceive the four truths, and because they are not objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing, {being neither motivated by wrong conception} nor related to it. Just as the ten physical elements are objects abandoned by the path of meditation, for similar reasons the five sense consciousnesses are also objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation {and because they rely on external objects}. The last three elements — the mental element, the phenomena element, and the mental consciousness element [80] — have three types: (1) that which is to be abandoned by the path of seeing, (2) that which is to be abandoned by the path of meditation, and (3) that which is not to be abandoned. The eighty-eight negative tendencies — view, {doubt,} and so on — those concomitant with them, their characteristics, their secondary characteristics, and their obtainment, which is explained below, are objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing. The remaining contaminated entities are objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation. Uncontaminated phenomena are not to be abandoned {since they are faultless}. The Vātsīputrīya school asserts that ordinary beings and the physical and verbal karma of those reincarnating in lower realms are objects abandoned by the path of seeing. {Since ordinary beings are incompatible with the ārya path} an ordinary being ceases when the path of seeing arises. A sūtra declares: A stream enterer stops reincarnating in lower realms.[405]
de dgag pa ni so so'i skye bo nyid ni nyon mongs pa can min pa'i phyir mthong bas spang bar bya ba min te/
Reply: That is refuted, for ordinary beings are not abandoned by the path of seeing (na dṛṣṭiheya) because they are not afflictive (akliṣṭaṃ).

{Question: How is it established that they are not afflictive?} Reply: If ordinary beings were afflictive, then it would follow that ordinary beings of the desire realm freed from attachment by the mundane path would no longer be ordinary beings, and {if ordinary beings were virtuous,} those who have severed their root of virtue would not be ordinary beings; therefore ordinary beings are also not virtuous by nature. As such, ordinary beings are unobscured-neutral states. Also the physical and verbal karma of those reincarnating in lower realms is form (rūpa). But it is not abandoned by the path of seeing because such form does not wrongly conceive the four noble truths, and neither do its complements nor its obtainment. {Therefore, though such form and sense consciousnesses are afflicted, they are not objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing.}

de la ngan song ba'i lus ngag ni der skye ba'i rgyu las mi dge ba'o/ / so so'i skye bo dang ngan song ba'i lus ngag gnyis ka'ang drug pa yid kyi rnam shes min pa las skyes pa'i phyir mthong spang min te/ mthong spang la yid las skyes pa dang de dang 'brel pas khyab pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yang so so'i skye bo mthong spang yin{ 'gag 'gyur gyis spong bas} na sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa'i tshe so so'i skye bor yang 'gyur te/ de'i tshe na mthong spang yod pa'i phyir ro zhes bya ba'ang brjod do/{ 'dod na so skyes gang zhe na 'phags pa'i chos rnams kyis ma thob pa'o zhes 'byung bas 'di ni 'phags pa yin pas gsal la/ bye brag tu smra ba so skyes ni sa dgu pa ste/ sgom lam gyis so so'i nyon mongs sa dgu pa'i rnam pa spong ba na de yang spong ste/ nyon mongs pa can min pa'i zag bcas thams cad kyi spong tshul ni der 'dod do/ / 'o na 'phags pa chags bcas kyang so skyer 'gyur ro zhe na mi 'gyur te/ duHkha la chos shes pa'i bzod pa skyes pa na de thob pa gcod pas rnam par nyams pa'i phyir te/ de thob dang*/ sa 'phos nas ni rnam nyams 'gyur/ / zhes pas so/ / de tsam gyis spangs par mi 'gyur te gnyen po skyes na yin no/ /}

The cause generating the body and speech of those reincarnating in lower realms is nonvirtuous karma. Objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing arise from mental consciousness and are necessarily related to it, but because both the body and speech of those reincarnating in lower realms do not arise from the sixth element of mental consciousness, they are not abandoned by the path of seeing. Again, if ordinary beings were objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing {through abandoning what is to be negated,} then ordinary beings would exist when engaged in perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering because objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing exist at that time. {Question: If that is so, what are ordinary beings? Reply: Since it is said “Those who do not obtain ārya states,” it is clear those who do are āryas. Vaibhāṣikas assert that “ordinary beings” are those of the nine levels, and when the path of meditation abandons the nine levels of individual affliction, the state [of an ordinary being] is also abandoned. And this is the method of abandoning all unafflicted contaminated phenomena. Objection: But āryas with attachment would become ordinary beings. Reply: They would not, because when perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering arises, the state of an ordinary being degenerates, its obtainment having been severed. [The Abhidharmakośa] states, “It degenerates through obtaining the path or relocating” (2:40cd). But the state of an ordinary being does not cease merely through that; it also ceases through the arising of its antidote.}
'o na mthong lam skyes pa na de dag 'gag pa ci zhe na/ de ni so sor brtags min gyis 'gog pa yin no/ /
Question: When the path of seeing is generated, what cessation is the cessation of the state of an ordinary being? Reply: It is nonanalytical cessation.
bdun pa lta ba dang lta ba ma yin pa'i rnam pa'i dbye ba ni
View and nonview
mig dang chos kyi khams phyogs ni/ / lta ba yin te rnam pa brgyad/ / 41 rnam shes lnga dang mtshungs skyes blo/ / nges rtog med phyir lta ma yin/ /
The eye and part of the phenomena element are view. This has eight types. Intelligence arising concomitantly with the five consciousnesses is not view because it is not decisive conception. (1:41)

yang khams bco brgyad las mig gi khams dang chos kyi khams kyi phyogs gcig ni lta ba yin te/ mig ni gzugs la lta ba'i phyir dang*/ chos kyi khams kyi phyogs gcig ni yul la nges par rtog pa'i phyir ro/ / chos kyi khams kyi phyogs gcig gang zhe na/ 'jig tshogs la lta ba la sogs pa lnga dang*/ 'jig rten pa'i yang dag pa'i lta ba dang*/ slob pa'i lta ba dang*/ mi slob pa'i lta ba ste rnam pa brgyad do/ / de la dang po lnga ni nyon mongs can dang*/ drug pa ni dge ba zag bcas dang*/ phyi ma gnyis ni sgom spang gi sa bon dang bcas pa dang de med pa'i zag med yin pas de dag gis shes bya'i chos la lta ba na rim pa ltar{ zag med ye shes kyi snang ba med cing ma rig pa'i sprin gyis g.yogs pas dang*/ bden bzhi spyi'i tshul tsam du rtogs pas log lta sprin med pas dang*/ mthong spang gi sprin med la sgom spang gi sprin yod pas dang nyon sgrib kyi sprin med pas so} sprin dang bcas pa dang sprin med pa'i mtshan mo dang nyin mo gzugs la lta ba bzhin du mi gsal ba dang cung zad gsal ba dang shin tu gsal ba dang shin tu ches gsal ba yin no/ /

From the eighteen elements, [81] the eye (cakṣu) element and one part of the phenomena element (dharmadhātu) are view (dṛṣṭi) because the eye views form, and one part of the phenomena element is decisive conception (nirūpaṇavikalpa). Question: What is the one part of the phenomena element? Reply: It has eight types: (1–5) the five views[406] such as the afflicted view of the self, (6) mundane correct view, (7) learner view, and (8) nonlearner view. The first five are afflicted and the sixth is contaminated virtue. The last two are, respectively, that which possesses the seed to be abandoned by the path of meditation, and that which is the uncontaminated state free of [such seeds]. They view phenomena that are objects of knowledge in this order: (1–5) {those that lack the illumination of uncontaminated transcendent wisdom and are covered by the cloud of ignorance [of the five views], (6) those that lack the cloud of wrong view since [mundane correct view] comprehends the general mode of the four noble truths, (7) those that lack the cloud of objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing [due to learner view] but possess the cloud of objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, and (8) those that lack the cloud of the afflictive obscurations [due to obtaining nonlearner view].} They are similar to form viewed [respectively] on a cloudy night, a cloudless night, a cloudy day, and a cloudless day — that is, unclear, a little clearer, very clear, and extremely clear.

'jig rten pa'i yang dag pa'i lta ba ni yid kyi rnam shes dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i shes rab dge ba zag bcas kho na yin gyi mig la sogs pa'i rnam shes lnga dang mtshungs ldan du skyes pa'i blo ste shes rab dge ba ni ji ltar 'jig rten pa'i yang dag pa'i lta ba {ma yin zhe na de ni } ma yin te/ {lta ba } de ni nges par rtog pa yin na de dag ni nges par rtog pa med pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

{Question:} Mundane correct view is contaminated virtuous wisdom concomitant with mental consciousness alone, but why is virtuous wisdom, which is intelligence (dhī) arising concomitantly (sahajā) with the five sense consciousnesses (vijñāna), {not} mundane correct view? {Reply: It} is not view because if that {view which is concomitant with mental consciousness} is decisive conception, then that which is concomitant with sense consciousness is not decisive conception (atīraṇa).
mig gis gzugs rnams mthong sten bcas/ / de la brten pa'i rnam shes min/ / 42 gang phyir bar du chod pa yi/ / gzugs ni mthong ba min phyir lo/ /
The eyes see form. The homogeneous [sees]. It is not that consciousness dependent on those always sees. Why? Because it is said it does not see form that is obscured. (1:42)
'o na ni mig kyang lta ba ma yin par 'gyur te/ nges par rtog pa med pa'i phyir ro zhe na/
Objection: Even the eyes do not view objects because they have no decisive conception.
mig gis ni gzugs rnams mthong ba'i phyir lta ba zhes bya'i nges par rtog pa'i phyir ni ma yin no/{ shes rab ni de lta ma yin pa'o/} mig thams cad kyis lta'am zhe na/
Reply: The eyes are called “view” because they see (paśyati) form, not because they are decisive conception. {Wisdom is not like that.} Question: Do all eyes view objects?
rnam shes rten pa dang bcas pa'i mig gis mthong gi de dang mtshungs pas ni ma yin no/ / de lta na mig la brten pa'i rnam shes kho nas mthong bar 'gyur ro zhe na/
Reply: Consciousness sees {obstructed objects} with eyes that are homogeneous but not with those that are partially homogeneous. Question: Thus does consciousness dependent on the eyes always see?

Reply: It is not that consciousness dependent on those (tatāśrita) eyes always sees. Why? Because it does not see form that is obscured (antarita) by obstructing walls and the like, for when consciousness sees, it is due to being unimpeded, and it even sees form obstructed by walls and so on. “It is said” (kila) indicates that the Sautrāntikas disagree with this position. Though consciousness sees, it does not penetrate all obstructive states; consciousness does not arise when conditions are incomplete and it is hindered by obscuring states {such as darkness and so on}. But consciousness does arise even when {crystal}, water, glass, medicinal stones, and so on intervene. {Likewise, consciousness may be unimpeded but obscured objects remain unseen, because consciousness relies on such conditions as light, conviction, and so on.} Objection: This contradicts a sūtra that states: The eyes see forms.[407] Reply: This explains that consciousness supported by the eyes sees. It is like saying “I summon the chairs.”[408] [82] Question: If eyes {see form, does} each eye see {by means of each generating a separate eye consciousness}, or do both eyes see {by means of generating a single eye consciousness}?
mig ni gnyis ka dag gis kyang / / mthong ste gsal bar mthong phyir ro/ / 43 mig dang yid dang rna ba ni/ / yul dang ma phrad gsum gzhan du/ /
Both eyes also see because they see clearly. The eye element, mental element, and ear element apprehend objects without contact. Three are different. (1:43)

mig ni gnyis ka dag gis rnam shes{ rdzas} gcig skyed pa'i tshul gyis gzugs mthong ste mig gcig gis bltas na mi gsal ba la mig gnyis ka phye nas bltas na shin tu gsal bar mthong ba'i phyir{ dang gcig kho nas mthong na snga phyi khyad med du thal ba'i phyir} ro/ / rten rnam par chad pas rnam shes chad par thal{ de 'dod na rnam shes rdzas re re bar mtshungs pa'i rdzas mtshungs nyams par thal} ba'ang med de/ rnam shes ni gzugs can ma yin pas yul na mi gnas pa'i phyir{ dang brgya byin lta bu'i mig stong gis kyang mig shes gcig bskyed pa'i phyir} ro/ / kyang zhes pa ni gang rung re res kyang mthong bar ston pa'o/ / gal te mig la sogs pas yul phrad nas 'dzin na/{ nye ring mi 'thad la/} 'on te{ phrad pa} ma yin {na thogs pa mi 'thad do/ } zhe na/

Reply: The three — (1) the eye element, (2) mental element, and (3) ear element — apprehend their objects (viśaya) without contact (aprāpta) because {objects are seen when glass and so on intervenes}; distant form and sound is seen and heard; the mental faculty apprehends past, future, and distant objects; and the mental faculty is not physical. {The mental faculty apprehends its object without contact because it is not physical. The eyes also apprehend their object without contact because if they were to apprehend through contact, they would see eye balm and so on that is applied to the eyes, and they would see distant form through contact from a distance. For as it is said: The eyes possess mobility and see across great distances covering long periods. Some say: Sound is apprehended through both contact and noncontact, since it hears the internal sound of the ear. Reply: Indeed, that is so. But sound is apprehended without contact, for otherwise it would follow that if a familiar sound in the east and so on were to carry here, it would possess a continuum, or if consciousness were to proceed there, it would not contact that sound since it would lack a supportive body. Objection: If they must contact their object, then the higher perceptions (abhijñā) such as the divine eye and divine ear would not arise in those who have obtained the absorptions in the desire realm, just as higher perception is not possible for the nose and so on since they must apprehend their objects through contact. But if they don’t contact their objects, they would not apprehend any form that is distant, or obscured, and so on. Reply: They [apprehend their objects in a way] similar to those that contact [their objects]. Question: But why don’t they apprehend eye balm or innate smell and so on? Reply: They do not apprehend other potential objects due to a difference of potency, like a magnet that attracts iron.}

sna dang lce dang lus kyi khams gsum ni ma phrad pa las gzhan du yul dang phrad nas 'dzin te/ {rten rgyang ring na gnas pa'i dri yang } dbugs ma rdubs par mi 'dzin pa'i phyir dang*/ gzhan yang gzhan gyis bar du chod pa'i dri la sogs pa mi 'dzin pa'i phyir ro/ / phrad pa zhes bya ba'ang{ dbang po dang yul gyi rdul phran} 'dab chags par gnas pa ste/ de yang bar{ na rdul phran gzhan} med par gnas pa la brjod kyi reg pa ni ma yin te/{ de yang bar na rdul phran gzhan med cing gnyis 'dab chags par gnas pa ni phrad pa'i don no/} phyogs thams cad kyis reg na rdul phran rnams 'dres {pas rags pa rtsom mi nus par 'gyur } pa dang*/ phyogs res reg na cha bcas su 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / des na rdul phran ni mi reg la bsags par gnas pa reg kyang de ni cha bcas su 'dod pa'i phyir skyon med do/ /

The three — (1) the nose element, (2) the tongue element, and (3) the body element — apprehend their objects through contact and are different (anyathā) [from those that apprehend] without contact because {the smell of a distant object} is not apprehended without breathing, and a smell is not apprehended when obstructed by another. Also, “contact” refers to {the atoms of the object and sense faculty} approaching, since they are said to abide without {other atoms} between them though they do not touch, because if all sides touched, their atoms would merge {and gross objects could not form,} and if one side touched [another atom] [83] it would have parts. No error applies because atoms do not touch, but since accumulations of atoms do touch, [coarse matter] is asserted to possess parts.
sna la sogs pa gsum gyis ni/ / yul ni mnyam pa 'dzin par 'dod/ / 44 tha ma'i rten 'das lnga rnams kyi/ / de dag lhan cig skyes pa'ang yin/ /

The three elements of the nose and so on are said to apprehend through matching their object. The support of the last is the prior mental faculty. The support of the five also arises simultaneously with them. (1:44)

yang sna la sogs pa yul dang phrad par bshad pa gsum gyis ni dbang po'i rdul phra rab dang yul gyi rdul phra rab rnams ni mnyam par 'dzin par 'dod de/ gang phrad pa de 'dzin cing ma phrad pa mi 'dzin pa'i phyir ro/ / yid ni lus can ma yin pas tshad mi dpyad la/ mig dang rna ba gnyis kyis ni ma nges te/ res 'ga' dbang po bas che ba dang*/ res 'ga' chung ba dang*/ res 'ga' mnyam par 'dzin pa'i phyir ro/{ bsags pa la dmigs pas rdul phran gcig gis bskyed pa med do/ /}

The three elements — the nose and so on — that contact their object are said to apprehend (grahaṇa) their object (viṣaya) through the molecular structures (paramāṇu) of the sense faculties matching (tulya) the molecular structures of their object. For whatever is contacted is apprehended and whatever is not contacted is not apprehended. The mental faculty cannot be measured since it is not physical, and there is no certainty with the eyes or ears, because sometimes the faculties are larger, sometimes they are smaller, and sometimes they are matching. {And since they focus on accumulations of atoms, contact therefore is not generated by a single atom.}

yang khams de dag las tha ma yid kyi rnam par shes pa'i khams kyi rten ni 'das pa 'gags ma thag pa'i yid kho na yin la/ mig gi rnam shes la sogs pa lnga po rnams kyi rten ni mig la sogs pa rnam shes de dag dang lhan cig skyes pa'i dbang po gzugs can da ltar ba'ang yin no/ 'ang gi sgras ni yid 'das pa'ang yin no zhes bsdu ba'i phyir ro/ / 'dir 'grel pa las de nyid kyi phyir gang mig gi rnam par shes pa'i rten gyi dngos po yin pa de de'i mtshungs pa de ma thag pa'i rkyen gyi dngos po yang yin nam zhe na/ mu bzhi ste zhes 'byung bas rnam shas tshogs lnga la ltos nas dbang po gzugs can lnga ni rnam shes lnga'i rten gyi dngos po yin gyi sems dang sems byung ma yin pas mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen gyi dngos po ni ma yin pas mu dang po dang*/ chos kyi khams kyi sems byung 'das ma thag pa ni/ sems dang sems byung skyes pa rnams/ / tha ma min mtshungs de ma thag ces 'byung bas mu gnyis pa{ yin te rnam shes drug rten dbang po drug tu nges pas} dang*/ 'das ma thag pa'i yid ni gnyis ka yin pas mu gsum pa dang*/ phyi'i khams gzugs can lnga dang chos kyi khams mtshungs ldan ma yin pa rnams ni gnyis ka ma yin pas mu bzhi pa'o/ / yid kyi rnam shes la ltos nas yid snga ma rten dang de'i mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen gyis dngos po gnyis ka yin pas mu gsum pa dang*/ mu gnyis pa dang bzhi pa ni sngar bshad pa dang 'dra la/ mu dang po ni med de/ yid shes kyi rten gang yin pa de de'i mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen kyang yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te mig gi rnam shes la sogs pa yid dang mig la sogs pa gnyis ka la rten pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ gzugs la sogs pa las kyang skye ba yin na ci'i phyir mig gi rnam shes la sogs par brjod kyi gzugs kyi rnam shes la sogs par mi brjod ce na

From among those elements, the support (āśraya) of the last (carama) element — mental consciousness — is the prior (atīta) mental faculty alone that has just ceased. The support of the five sense consciousnesses — the present physical sense faculties — also arises simultaneously (sahajā) with eye consciousnesses and so forth. The term “also” includes the prior mental faculty. Here the Autocommentary states: Is anything that is the support of eye consciousness also something that is its equivalent immediately preceding condition? There are four possibilities.[409] The first possibility is the five physical sense faculties that support the fivefold collection of consciousness.
