They are things that support the five consciousnesses but not things that are equivalent immediately preceding conditions since they are neither minds nor mental factors. The second possibility is the immediately preceding mental factors of the phenomena element, since the Abhidharmakośa mentions, “Final minds and mental factors are not equivalent immediately preceding conditions” (2:62ab) {and the six consciousnesses determine the six supportive sense faculties.} The third possibility is the immediately preceding mental faculty, since it is both. The fourth possibility is the five external physical elements and those not concomitant with the phenomena element, since they are neither. Things that are both the support of the prior mental faculty supporting mental consciousness and its equivalent immediately preceding condition are the third possibility, and the second and fourth possibilities are the same as those just explained. There is no first possibility because whatever is a basis of mental consciousness is also its equivalent immediately preceding condition. Question: If eye consciousness depends both on the mental faculty and on the eyes and so on, and it also arises from form and so forth, why is it called “eye consciousness” and not “form consciousness”?
de dag gyur pas 'gyur nyid phyir/ / rten ni mig la sogs pa yin/ / 45 de phyir thun mong ma yin phyir/ / de dag gis ni rnam shes bstan/ /

They transform due to the eyes transforming. The eyes and so on are the support of consciousness. Because of that, and because they are specific causes, they are designated “eye consciousness” and so on. (1:45)

mig la sogs pa de dag gyur pas mig gi rnam shes la sogs pa rnams 'gyur ba nyid kyi phyir te/ phan gnod kyis bde sdug dang mtshungs ldan du skye ba'i phyir dang*/ rnam 'grel las/ gal te ring mthong tshad yin na/ / tshur shog bya rgod brten par gyis/ / zhes 'byung ba ltar bya rgod kyi mig ni rang bzhin gyis gsal bas gzugs mi gsal ba yang dpag tshad du mas bar du chod pa la'ang mig shes skye zhing*/ rna ba la sogs pa'ang de dang 'dra bas dbang po gsal ba dang mi gsal bas rnam shes gsal pa dang mi gsal bar skye ba'i phyir dang*/ gzugs sogs 'gyur bas ni rnam shes de dag 'gyur bar ma nges pa'i phyir ro/{ yul sdug mi sdug gi tshor ba bde sdug tu 'gyur ba ni yul la chags bral lam 'dod pa la chags bral la med pa'i phyir dang*/ dbang po gsal na yul mi gsal yang bya rgod ltar shes pa gsal bar skye ba'i phyir dang*/ dbang po mi gsal na yul gsal yang de lta ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /} de lta bas na mig gi rnam shes la sogs pa'i rten ni mig la sogs pa yin no/

Reply: Eye consciousness and so on transform (vikāra) due to the eyes and so forth transforming (vikāritvāt); they arise with concomitant pleasure and pain due to being benefited or harmed. The Exposition of Valid Cognition states: If you are at the limit of seeing distant objects, go closer. Otherwise, rely on a vulture.[410] [84] Therefore, due to the natural clarity of a vulture’s eyes, eye consciousness arises even though the form [that is its object] is unclear and many yojanas distant. So too, clear or unclear consciousness arises due to clear or unclear sense faculties such as the ears, but there is no certainty that consciousness transforms when form and so forth transform. {Feelings of pleasure and pain do not arise from attractive or repulsive objects if you are free of attachment to objects or free of attachment to desire[-realm objects]. However, if the sense base is clear even though the object is unclear, clear consciousness arises as it does for a vulture, but that is not so when the sense faculties are unclear even though the object is clear.} Therefore the eyes and so on are the support of eye consciousness and so forth.

gang gi phyir mig gi rnam shes la sogs pa'i rten dbang po de dag kho na yin pa de'i phyir dang dbang po de dag rgyud gcig dang tha dad la ltos nas rnam shes skyed pa'i thun mong ma yin pa'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir mig gi rnam shes zhes bya ba la sogs pa bdag rkyen dbang po de dag gi sgo nas ni rnam par shes pa bstan te rnga'i sgra dang nas kyi myu gu zhes bya ba lta bu'o/ gzugs la sogs pa'i yul dang yid dang yid ni mig la sogs pa'i rnam shes dang yid kyi rnam shes gnyis ka'i thun mong gi rgyu yin pa'i phyir de dag gis ni ma bstan te/{ gzugs ni shes pa thun mong ba'i rgyu yin te mig shes dang yid shes gnyis kyi rgyu yin la mig ni mig shes 'khor bcas kho na'i yin pas thun mong ma yin no/ / gzugs ni gang zag thun mong ba'i shes pa'i rgyu yin te gang zag du ma'i mig shes dang yid shes skyed pas so mig gis rgyud gcig kho na'i mig shes skyed pas thun mong ma yin pas/ /}

Because the sense faculties alone are the support of eye consciousness and so on, because those sense faculties are the specific (asādhāraṇa) cause generating consciousness supported in the same or different mindstreams, and because the sense faculties are their dominant conditions, they are designated “eye consciousness” and so on, like the term “drumbeat” or “barley shoot.” The [five sense consciousnesses] are not designated due to their objects — such as physical form — nor due to the mental faculty because they are causes shared by both eye consciousness and mental consciousness. {Material form is a shared cause of consciousness because it is the cause of both eye consciousness and mental consciousness. Eyes are not a shared cause since they solely complement eye consciousness. Material form is a shared cause of the consciousness of beings since it generates eye consciousness and mental consciousness in many beings. The eyes generate eye consciousness in the mindstream of a single person alone, therefore they are not shared.}

de nyid kyi phyir tshad ma kun las btus las kyang*/ thun mong ma yin rgyu yi phyir/ / de'i tha snyad dbang pos byas/ / zhes bshad do/ / yang gal te lus gang la gnas te mig{ yid dang ba} gi gzugs la lta ba dang rna ba la sogs pas sgra la sogs pa nyan pa la sogs pa byed pa na lus dang mig la sogs pa dang gzugs la sogs pa dang rnam shes rnams sa gcig gam tha dad ce na/ tha dad pa dang gcig pa'ang yod do zhes bstan pa'i phyir lus la zhes bya ba la sogs pa smos te/

The Compendium of Valid Cognition affirms: Because it is its specific cause, the sense faculty gives it its name.[411] Question: If the eyes {and the clear mental faculty} view form, or the ears hear sound and so forth, then do the body, eyes, form, consciousnesses and so on belong to the same or to a different level? Reply: “Lower eyes do not depend on a higher body” (1:46a) and so on is stated because it teaches that they belong to the same and different levels.

{ de la 'dod par skyes pa rang gi sa pa'i mig gis gzugs la lta ba na thams cad rang gi sa pa'o/ / 'dod pa bas bsam gtan bzhi pa'i mig gi bsam gtan gnyis pa dang gsum pa'i gzugs la lta na bzhi gas tha dad pa ste/ gzhan la ni ci rigs su sbyar ro/ / bzhi ga sa gcig pa ni 'dod pa dang dang po'i sa pa kho na ste de yan chad na rang gi sa pa'i dbang zhes med pas so/ / rten bcas kyi dbang po dang*/ yang na shes pa kho nas yul mthong ba la sogs yin na bsam gtan gong ma gsum dbang shes mngon du ma byas pa'i tshe yul mi mthong ba sogs su thal lo/} lus ni 'dir rten khog pa la 'dod do/ / de la mig la sogs pa dbang po gzugs can lnga dang yul gzugs sgra reg bya gsum ni{ sa lnga pa ste} 'dod pa dang bsam gtan bzhi na yod do/ / mig sna lus kyi rnam shes gsum ni 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang po'i sa kho na na yod do/ / dri ro dang sna lce'i rnam shes ni 'dod pa'i sa pa kho na yin no/ /

{If those born in the desire realm view form with eyes of their level, all belong to their level. If desire-realm beings view form of the second and third absorptions with eyes of the fourth absorption, all four belong to different levels. This should be applied to the other instances as appropriate. If the four belong to the same level, they belong to the desire-realm level or the level of the first absorption alone, since there is no sense consciousness belonging to the levels above that. If objects are seen by a supportive sense faculty or consciousness alone and so on, it would follow that such objects would not be seen when abiding in the three higher absorptions, where sense consciousness does not manifest.} Here the body is asserted to be the support cavity. The five physical sense faculties and the three objects — form, sound, and tactile objects — exist on {five levels}: the desire realm and the four absorptions. Smell and taste, and nose and tongue consciousness, exist only on [85] the desire-realm level.
lus la 'og ma'i mig ma yin/ / mig gi gong ma'i gzugs ma yin/ / 46 rnam par shes pa'ang de yi gzugs/ / lus kyi'ang gnyis ka thams cad du/ /

Lower eyes do not depend on a higher body. Higher form is not an object of lower eyes. Also higher consciousness. That form is seen. Also in terms of the body, both are supported on all levels. (1:46)

de la gong ma'i lus la 'og ma'i mig rten pa ma yin te/ rang sa na mig mchog yod pas 'og ma'i mig gis dgos pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / des na de'i sa pa'i mig gam gong ma'i sa pa'i mig gi rten yin no/ / 'og ma'i mig gi yul ni sa gong ma'i gzugs ma yin te/ gong ma'i gzugs ni phra bas des de mthong bar mi nus pa'i phyir ro/ / des na rang gi sa pa dang 'og ma'i sa pa'i gzugs ni mig gi yul yin no/{ des na 'dod pa'i mig sa gcig nas bzhi pa'i sa lnga pa yin no/ /}

Eyes of lower level (adhara) do not depend on a body of higher (ūrdhva) level because the eyes of one’s own level are best, and one does not need the eyes of a lower level. Therefore one depends on the eyes of one’s level or those of a higher level. The form of higher realms is not an object of the eyes of lower realms, since higher form is subtle and [lower eyes] cannot see it. Therefore the object of one’s eyes is the form of one’s own level and lower level. {Thus there are five [engaging desire-realm form]: eyes of the desire realm plus those from the first to fourth absorption levels.}

sa gong ma'i mig gi rnam par shes pa'ang sa 'og ma'i mig la rten pa ma yin te/ gong ma'i rnam shes mchog ni 'og ma'i mig dman pa la mi rten pa'i phyir ro/{ gal te rten na dbang shes des rang gis pa'i yul mi mthong bar thal te de'i rten mig res yul gong ma mi mthong ba'i phyir ro khyab pa yod de dbang shes ni de'i rten dbang po de dang yul la lhan cig tu 'jug pa'i phyir ro/ / dmigs bsal/ } 'og ma'i{ bsam gtan dang po} rnam shes dang rang gi sa pa ni rten pa yin no/ /
'on kyang 'og ma'i rnam shes rten pa zhes bya ba'ang 'dod pa'i rnam shes ni bsam gtan dang po'i mig la rten pa ma yin te/ dang po na rnam shes gya nom pa yod pas{ de mngon du byas pa la} dgos pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / des na bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad rang sa na sgo lnga'i rnam shes med pa'i dbang du byas nas de skad du bstan te/ bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad gzugs la lta ba na dang po'i mig shes mngon du byed pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na rnam shes kyis sa gang pa'i gzugs mthong la lus gang la brten nas sa gang gi rnam shes kyi rten byed cing gzugs mthong zhe na/

Also, eye consciousness of a higher level does not depend on the eyes of a lower level because higher consciousness that is superior does not depend on lower eyes that are inferior. {If lower eyes supported higher consciousness, then in consequence “higher sense consciousness would not see objects of its own level because each eye supporting it would not see the higher object,” since sense consciousness simultaneously engages its own supportive sense faculty and object.} {The exception is} lower consciousness {of the first absorption,} which depends on its own level.
Though it is said that “consciousness of a lower level depends on it,” desire-realm consciousness does not depend on eyes of the first absorption because there is no need {to manifest lower consciousness} since consciousness of the first absorption is superior. This is taught from the perspective of consciousness of the five sense doors not existing on or above the second absorption because if one were to view form on or above the second level, one would have to manifest consciousness of the first absorption. Question: Form of what level, supported by which body, supporting what consciousness, is seen by consciousness?

rnam shes kyis sa thams cad pa'i gzugs mthong bar ma zad rten lus kyi'ang {yul }gzugs dang rnam shes gnyis ka sa thams cad du mthong zhing rten byed {nus }de/ 'di ltar gzugs ni 'dod pa'i lus la brten nas rang gi sa pa dang{ gong ma'i mig skyed nas dang po'i mig shes kyis lta na/} gong ma'i sa pa{'i gzugs }mthong ngo*/ / bsam gtan dang po nas gsum pa'i bar gyis rang sa dang 'og sa dang gong sa'i gzugs mthong ngo*/ / bsam gtan bzhi pa'i lus las na rang sa dang 'og ma'i gzugs thams cad mthong{ thams cad mthong ba'i rten du rung ba ni 'dod pa'i lus la bsam mo} ngo*/{gong na gzugs med pas so/}/ rnam par shes pa'i ni 'dod pa'i lus la brten nas rang sa'i rnam shes dang bsam gtan dang po'i rnam shes skyed par byed do/ / bsam gtan dang po'i lus la ni rang sa'i rnam shes kho na skyed par byed do/ / bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad kyi lus la ni 'og ma bsam gtan dang po'i rnam shes kho na skyed par byed do/ / des na lus kyi'ang gnyis ka thams cad du zhes bya ba'ang ci rigs kyi dbang du byas nas gsungs so zhes rig par bya'o/ /

Not only is the form of all levels seen by consciousness, but also in terms of the supporting body, both {the object} form and consciousness {can} be seen and supported on all levels. In this way form that is {form} of its level and higher levels is seen in dependence on the desire-realm body {if viewed by eye consciousness of the first absorption through generating eyes of higher levels.} Form of lower levels, its level, and higher levels is seen by the first to third absorptions. All form of its level and lower levels [86] is seen in reliance on the body of the fourth absorption {since there is no form above it. The desire-realm basis is considered to be a suitable basis for seeing all.} In terms of consciousness, consciousness of the desire-realm level and consciousness of the first absorption are generated in dependence on the desire-realm body. Only consciousness of its own level is generated in dependence on the body of the first absorption. Only consciousness of the lower first absorption is generated in dependence on the body of the second absorption and above. Therefore, the statement “Also in terms of the body, both are supported on all levels” (1:46d) should be understood as correct.
rna ba'ang de bzhin gsum dag ni/ / thams cad rang gi sa pa nyid/ / 47 lus kyi rnam shes 'og dang ni/ / rang gi sa yid ma nges te/ /

Ears should also be understood in that way. All those of the three elements belong to their own level. Body consciousness belongs to a lower level or its own level. The mental faculty is not definite. (1:47)

dbang po gzhan la sbyar ba'i dbang du byas nas ji ltar mig la rgyas par bshad pa ltar rna ba'ang de bzhin du shes par bya'o zhes bya ste/ lus la 'og ma'i rna ba min/ / rna ba'i gong ma'i sgra ma yin/ / rnam par shes pa'ang de yi sgra/ / lus kyi'ang gnyis ka thams cad du/ / zhes rgya cher sbyar bar bya'o/ /

Ears should also be understood in that way (tathā), for what applied [to the eyes] should be applied to the other sense faculties in just the way it is explained at length for the eyes. Therefore: Lower ears do not depend on a higher body. Higher sound is not the object of lower ears. Also higher consciousness. That sound is heard. Also in terms of the body, both are supported on all levels.

sna dang lce dang lus kyi khams gsum po dag gi ni yul dang rnam shes dang rten gyi lus thams cad rang gi sa pa nyid yin te/ de dag dbang po dang phrad pa 'dzin pas chod pa dang ring ba'i don la mi 'jug pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar spyir btang nas dmigs kyis bsal ba ni lus dang lus kyi dbang po dang reg bya ni rang gi sa pa yin la lus kyi rnam shes ni bsam gtan gnyis pa nas bzhi pa'i bar du skyes pa dag reg bya 'dzin na 'og ma bsam gtan dang po'i sa pa dang*/ 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang por skyes pa dag reg bya 'dzin na rang ngar gi sa pa kho na yin no/ / yid dang chos dang yid kyi rnam shes dang de'i rten lus ni sa ma nges te/ res 'ga' thams cad sa mtshungs pa dang res 'ga' mi mtshungs pa'i yang phyir ro/

All objects, consciousnesses, and supportive bodies of the three elements of the nose, tongue, and body belong to their own level (svabhūmika) because they do not engage obscure or distant objects, and they apprehend their objects through contact with their sense faculty. This applies in general, but the exceptions are the body, body sense faculty, and tactile objects. If those born from the second to fourth absorptions apprehend tactile objects, their body consciousness (kāyavijñāna) belongs to the lower level of the first absorption, and if those born in the desire realm or the first absorption apprehend tactile objects, it belongs to its own level (svabhūmi) alone. The level of the mental faculty, phenomena, mental consciousness, and their supportive body is not definite (aniyata) because sometimes all belong to the same level and sometimes not.

{ de yang sa lnga char gyi lus la ci rigs su sbyar te de la bzhi ka sa mtshungs pa 'dod pa'i lus la 'dod pa'i yid dbang gis 'dod pa'i chos la dmigs pa'i 'dod pa'i yid kyi rnam shes skyed pa lta bu'o/ / mi mtshungs pa 'dod pa'i yid kyi bsam gtan la 'jug pa'am/ 'dod pa'i sprul ba las ldang ba na yid ni 'dod pa yin la yid shes ni bsam gtan gar rung ngo gong nas 'og tu skye ba na yid ni sa gong ma dang rnam shes dang rten ni 'og sa pa ste 'og nas gong du skyen bzlog pa'o/ / chos ni rang sa dang sa thams cad pa dang sas ma bsdus pa'ang yul du byed do/ / bsam gtan dge yul yod dgu yin/ / zhes pa dang*/ gzugs med dngos gzhi dge rnams kyi/ / spyod yul zag bcas 'og ma min/ / zhes dmigs bsal dang bcas te 'chad pas so/ /} 'di ni gnas gsum pa dang brgyad par{ yang} 'chad par 'gyur ro/ /

{One should properly link [consciousness, faculty, and object] to the bodies of the five levels.[412] Four that are the same are, for example, a desire-realm mental consciousness generated in a desire-realm body, through a desire-realm mental faculty, observing desire-realm phenomena. That which is not the same is, for example, the desire-realm mental faculty that enters absorption or rises from [the mind of] desire-realm emanation, where the mental faculty belongs to the desire realm but the mental consciousness is any of the absorptions, or if one is born in a lower level from a higher level, then the mental faculty belongs to the higher level but consciousness and its support belong to the lower level. If one is born in a higher level from a lower level, that is reversed. Phenomena are taken as an object on their own level, on all levels, or not subsumed on any level. The Abhidharmakośa notes an exception, “The object of virtuous absorption is all objects” (8:20d) and “The object fields of those virtuous, formless, actual bases are not contaminated lower levels” (8:21ab).} This is explained in part 3 and {also} part 8.
brgyad pa gnyis kyis shes par bya ba la sogs pa gsum bshad pa ni
Three, such as those known by two and so on
gnyis kyis rnam shes phyi yi lnga/ / 'dus ma byas chos rtag pa'o/ / 48 chos kyi phyed dang gang dag ni/ / bcu gnyis nang gir bshad dbang po/ /
The five external bases are known by two consciousnesses. Unconditioned phenomena are permanent. Part of the phenomena element and the twelve explained as internal are faculties. (1:48)

{Question:} From among the eighteen elements, {what consciousness knows what? Reply: Phenomena and the eyes and so on have been clarified.} The five external (bāhya) bases {alone,} from form to tactile objects, [87] are known by two consciousnesses because form is known by eye consciousness and by mental consciousness and so on. Therefore a sūtra also states: Monks, consciousness aware of form has two aspects because it depends on sense faculties and it depends on the mental faculty.[413] The remaining thirteen elements are established as the objects of knowledge of mental consciousness alone, since they are not the objects of consciousness of the five sense doors. {In [the Buddha’s conversation with] the brahman Jātiśrona, he lists twenty-two faculties:[414] the six sense faculties, the male and female faculties, life force, the five such as pleasure, the five such as faith, and the three such as knowing the unknown. Ābhidharmikas indeed list the mental faculty after the faculty of life force, since it possesses a focal object. Sautrāntikas say that if this is done, they would lose respect for the principles of the six bases, therefore they recite them in accordance with how they occur in the sūtras.}

yang khams bco brgyad las chos kyi khams kyi phyogs gcig 'dus ma byas kyi chos ni skad cig ma ma yin{ zhing brtan} pas rtag pa zhes bya'o/ gzhan dag ni 'dus byas yin pas mi rtag pa nyid du shes par bya'o/ / yang mdo las/ / dbang po rnams shes 'byung na khams de dag las dbang po yin pa ni du/ ma yin pa ni du zhe na/

From among the eighteen elements, unconditioned phenomena (asaṃskṛta), which form one part of the phenomena element, are called “permanent” (nityā) since they are {stable and} not momentary. The remainder are known to be impermanent since they are conditioned states. Again, a sūtra states: If you understand the faculties, how many elements are faculties, how many are not?[415]

khams de dag{ bram ze rang bzhin nyan gyi dbang du mdzad nas mdo las/ mig sogs drug dang*/ mo dang pho dang srog dang bde ba la sogs pa lnga dang dad sogs lnga dang mi shes pa kun shes par byed pa la sogs pa zag med gsum ste dbang po nyi shu rtsa gcig gsungs pa} las chos kyi khams kyi phyed srog dang tshor ba bde ba la sogs pa lnga dang dad pa la sogs pa lnga dang zag med kyi dbang po gsum gyi cha ste bcu bzhi dang*/ mig la sogs pa'i khams gang dag nang gir bshad pa bcu{ mig sogs lnga dang*/ sems kyi khams bdun te} gnyis po de dag ni dbang po yin te/ mig la sogs pa lnga ni so sor dbang po lnga dang*/ pho mo'i dbang po ni lus kyi nang du bsdus pa'i phyir dang*/ yid kyi dbang po ni sems kyi khams bdun dang zag med kyi dbang po gsum gyi cha yin pa'i phyir ro/ /
de ltar na lhag ma chos kyi phyed dang gzugs la sogs pa lnga ni dbang po ma yin pa zhes bya bar grub bo/
dge slong gnas gsum dag la mkhas 'dod pa/ / gang de chos mngon gzhung gi cha shas las/ / yin phyir gang la 'dun pa rab 'jug pa/ / de yis dang por gzhung 'dir 'jug par gyis/ /

From among those elements, part of the phenomena element constitutes fourteen faculties: life force, the five feelings such as pleasure, the five such as faith, and the three uncontaminated faculties. And the twelve explained to be internal elements (ādhyātmika) {the five sense organs and seven mental elements} are faculties because the five sense organs are five separate faculties, the male and female faculties are included in the body, and the mental faculty is the seven mental elements and the three uncontaminated faculties.
The remainder of the phenomena element and the five sense objects are not faculties.
Monks, whoever desires to master the three realms should enter whatever topic they aspire to know from any part of the Abhidharma literature by first entering this text.
chos mngon pa'i mdzod kyi tshig le'ur byas pa las/ /khams bstan pa zhes bya ba ste gnas dang po'o// //
chos mngon pa'i mdzod kyi 'grel pa mngon pa'i rgyan las khams bstan pa zhes bya ste gnas dang po'i bshad pa'o// ! //
This has been part I, the “Exposition of the Elements,” from Ornament of Abhidharma: A Commentary on the Verses of the Abhidharmakośa. [88]
gnas gnyis pa dbang po bstan pa/
6. The Nature of the Faculties
da ni gnas gnyis pa 'chad pa na
THE EXPOSITION OF THE FACULTIES

'das ma thag par chos kyi phyed dang gang dag ni/ / bcu gnyis nang gir bshad dbang po zhes bshad pa'i dbang po'i grangs dag ni du/ don gang zhe na/ dbang po'i grangs ni mdo las/ bram ze rang bzhin nyan gyi dbang du mdzad nas/ bram ze dbang po ni nyi shu rtsa gnyis po 'di dag yin te/ nyi shu rtsa gnyis gang zhe na/ thams cad kyi mthar drug pa'i sgra dang dbang po zhes sbyar te mig dang rna ba dang sna dang lce dang lus dang yid dang mo dang pho dang srog dang bde ba dang sdug bsngal dang yid bde ba dang mi bde dang btang snyoms dang dad pa dang brtson 'grus dang dran pa dang ting nge 'dzin dang shes rab dang mi shes pa kun shes par byed pa dang kun shes pa dang kun shes ldan pa'i dbang po'o/ / bram ze 'di dag ni dbang po nyi shu rtsa gnyis te/ 'di tsam gyis dbang po rnams bsdus pa yin no zhes nyi shu rtsa gnyis gsungs so/ /

Question: How many faculties (indriya) are there, and what is their meaning as stated in the immediately preceding verse: “Part of the phenomena element and the twelve explained as internal are faculties” (1:48cd)? Reply: Regarding the number of faculties, a sūtra declares that there are twenty-two: The Buddha said to the brahman Jātiśrona: “Brahman, the faculties are these twenty-two. What are these twenty-two? They are the faculties of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, mental faculty, female, male, life force, pleasure, pain, mental satisfaction, mental dissatisfaction, equanimity, faith, effort, mindfulness, concentration, wisdom, producing complete knowledge of the unknown, complete knowledge, and possessing complete knowledge.[416] Brahman, these are the twenty-two faculties. Just these constitute the faculties.”[417]
de'i don ni lhag par dbang byed pa yin pas de bshad pa la dbang po'i rang bzhin nges par bya ba dang*/ zhar la 'dus byas kyi skye tshul rgyas par bshad pa gnyis las/

The meaning of faculty is said to be “that which specifically controls.” This is explained in two headings: determining the essential nature of the faculties and elaboration of how conditioned states arise.
dang po
DETERMINING THE ESSENTIAL NATURE OF THE FACULTIES
['di] la drug las
This has six headings: definition of faculty, set number of the faculties, nature of the faculties, taxonomies, how the faculties are obtained and relinquished, and how one possesses the faculties.
dbang po'i mtshan nyid
Definition of faculty
dbang po'i mtshan nyid ni gang zhig gang la thun mong ma yin par dbang byed pa yin no/ / gang zhig gang la dbang byed ce na/
The definition of faculty is “whatever controls [or facilitates] something.” Question: What controls what?
lnga po rnams ni don bzhi la/ / dbang byed bzhi rnams gnyis la lo/ / lnga dang brgyad po de rnams ni/ / kun nas nyon mongs rnam byang la/ / 1
It is said five control four things, four control two. Five and eight, respectively, control unenlightened and enlightened states. (2:1)

mig la sogs pa'i dbang po lnga po rnams ni lus mdzes par byed pa dang*/ lus yongs su bsrung ba dang mig gi rnam shes mtshungs ldan dang bcas pa la sogs pa skyed pa dang*/ gzugs bltas so/ / sgra snyan no zhes bya ba la sogs pa tha snyad thun mong ma yin pa zhes bya ba'i don bzhi bzhi la dbang byed do/ / de la lus yongs su bsrung ba la dbang byed pa ni mig dang rna bas yul yid du mi 'ong ba dag mthong ba dang thos nas yang ba las lus srung ba'i phyir dang*/ sna lce lus gsum gyis kham zas la longs spyad pas lus rgyas par byed pa'i phyir/ pho mo dang srog dang yid kyi dbang po bzhi po rnams ni re re zhing don gnyis gnyis la dbang byed do/ / de la pho mo'i dbang po de dag ni pho'o mo'o zhes pho dang mo ma yin pa'i sems can las bye brag tu 'byed pa dang*/ khyad par du pho'i dbang pos ni mo las kyang khyad par la dbang byed pa dang*/ de dag las bzlog pa mo'i dbang pos ni pho las khyad par la dbang byed do/ / gzhan dag ni kun nas nyon mongs dang rnam byang la'ang dbang byed do/ / de dag ni sdom min dang mtshams med dang*/ dge rtsa gcod pa dang*/ sdom pa dang*/ 'bras bu 'thob pa dang*/ 'dod chags dang bral ba'i gzhir rung gi za ma dang ma ning dang mtshan gnyis pa ni ma yin pa'i phyir ro zhes 'chad do/ / srog gi dbang pos ni ris mthun par nying mtshams sbyor ba dang*/ de'i rgyun gnas pa gnyis la dbang byed do/ /yid kyis ni yang srid du nying mtshams sbyor ba dang*/ yid dge bar gnas na de'i dbang gis byung ba'i lus la sogs pa'ang dge bar byed pa la sogs pa dbang po'i ngo bo dang mthun par dbang byed de/ rnam par 'byed pa bsdus pa'i sdom gyi tshigs su bcad pa gnyis pa'i dang po'i mdo las/ 'jig rten sems kyis khrid pa ste/ / sems kyis yongs su drangs pa yin/ / sems kyi chos ni gcig pu yi/ / dbang gi rjes su chos kun 'gro/ / zhes gsungs pa lta bu'o/ /

Reply: The five sense faculties such as the eyes control (ādhipatya) four things: (1) beautifying the body, (2) protecting the body, (3) generating that which is concomitant with eye consciousness and so on, and (4) naming that which sees form, hears sound, and so forth. The eye and ear control the protection of the body, since they protect the body from serious danger through seeing and hearing threatening objects, and the nose, tongue, and body control enhancement of the body through utilizing oral food and so on. Each of the four faculties — male, female, life force, and the mental faculty — controls (ādhipatya) two things. Male and female faculties distinguish sentient beings who are not males from males and those not females from females; in particular, the male faculty controls [or governs] distinction from females, and conversely, the female faculty controls distinction from males. Alternately, they also control unenlightened states and enlightened states, for it is said that [male and female faculties] are the basis for obtaining negative commitments (asaṃvara), [89] for committing heinous acts, and for severing the root of virtue. Or they are for obtaining vows and their result and for attaining freedom from attachment, but eunuchs (saṇḍha), neuters (paṇḍaka), and hermaphrodites (dvidhākṛtin) do not [possess such a basis]. The faculty of life force controls both (1) connecting with states of similar type and (2) maintaining their continuity. The mental faculty controls (1) connecting with rebirth and (2) maintaining the [ethical] nature of the sense faculties for if the mental faculty is virtuous then the body and so on will act virtuously and so forth.[418] The first of two verses of condensed analysis in the Sūtra of Primary Analysis remarks: Worldly beings are led by the mind. Mind fully guides them. All phenomena follow the nature of the mind alone.[419]

lo zhes bya ba ni bye brag tu smra ba'i 'dod pa la ma rangs pa ste/ lus mdzes par ni dbang rten gyi byed pa'i phyir dang*/ lus srung ba dang tha snyad thun mong ma yin pa'ang dbang po la rten pa'i rnam shes kyis byed pa'i phyir dang*/ mdo las pho tshangs pa byed pa'i gnas yod kyi bud med tshangs pa byed pa'i gnas med do zhes gsungs pas pho mo'i dbang po med pa'i gzugs khams pa'i lha dang bskal pa dang po'i mi'ang pho yin pa'i phyir dang*/ srog kyang nyon mongs can ma yin pas nying mtshams sbyor byed ma yin pa'i phyir rnam par bzhag pa de dag ni mi 'thad do zhes bya ba ni mdo sde pa la sogs pas brjod pa yin no/

“It is said” (kila) indicates that Sautrāntikas and so on hold the assertions of the Vaibhāṣikas to be implausible because [Sautrāntikas and so on assert] that it is the basis of the sense faculties that beautifies the body; it is consciousness supported by the sense faculties that protects the body and also [determines their] designation; and form-realm gods lack male or female faculties whereas humans of the first eon are male, since a sūtra states: It is the abode of male celibacy but not the abode of female celibacy.[420] And life force does not connect to rebirth since it is not afflicted.

tshor ba lnga dang dad sogs lnga dang kun shes byed sogs gsum ste brgyad po de rnams ni rim pa ltar kun nas nyon mongs pa dang rnam par byang ba la dbang byed de/ tshor ba bde ba yid bde ba dang*/ sdug bsngal yid mi bde ba dang*/ btang snyoms kyis rim pa ltar chags sdang rmongs gsum bskyed pa'i phyir dang*/ / tshogs sbyor gyi dad sogs lnga rnam byang gi rgyu dang*/ mthong sgom mi slob pa'i lam gyi brgyad po rnam byang gi ngo bo yin pa'i phyir ro/ / kha cig na re bde ba la sog pas kyang rnam byang la dbang byed de/ 'di ltar skye mched drug gi mdo dang*/ ched du brjod pa bsdus pa'i sdom gyi tshigs su bcad pa gnyis pa'i mdo las/ bde bar gyur pa'i sems mnyam par 'jog par 'gyur ro zhes bya ba la sogs pa dang*/ sdug bsngal gyi rgyu can gyi dad pa zhes bya ba dang*/ mig gis rnam par shes par bya ba'i gzugs rnams la rten te yid bde ba nges par 'byung ba la rten pa skye'o zhes bya ba la sogs pa yid bde ba nges par 'byung ba la rten pa drug dang*/ yid mi bde ba nges par 'byung ba la rten pa drug dang btang snyoms nges par 'byung ba la brten pa drug gsung pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ / de la skyes bu la la ni thob par bya'o snyam du yid bde ba yin no/ / la la ni spang bar bya'o snyam du yid mi bde ba yin no/ / la la ni gzugs la sogs pa la so sor brtags nas btang snyoms su byed pa yin no/ /

The five feelings and the eight — the five such as faith and the three such as producing complete knowledge — respectively, control [or produce] unenlightened (saṃkleśa) and enlightened states (vyavadāna). That is because the feelings of pleasure, mental satisfaction, pain, mental dissatisfaction, and equanimity generate aversion and confusion; the five such as faith pertaining to the paths of accumulation and preparation are the cause of enlightened states; and the eight pertaining to the paths of seeing, meditation, and no more learning are by nature enlightened states. Some say: Pleasure and so on also control enlightened states because the Six Bases Sūtra[421] and the Sūtra in Verse of the Compendium of Aphorisms explain: The mind that has attained blissful states will attain equipoise . . .[422] And: Faith that is caused by suffering . . .[423] And: Mental satisfaction arises in dependence on form that is known by the eye, and in dependence [on that] renunciation . . .[424] This passage mentions there are six types of renunciation dependent on mental satisfaction, six types of renunciation dependent on mental dissatisfaction, and six types of renunciation dependent on equanimity.[425] For some beings, mental satisfaction is the thought “I will obtain this”; for some, mental dissatisfaction is the thought “I will lose this”; and for some, equanimity arises through [90] the analysis of material form and so on.
rang gi don dang thams cad la/ / dmigs par dbang byed phyir dbang drug / mo nyid pho nyid la dbang phyir/ / lus las mo dang pho dbang dag / 2

Because they control the observation of specific objects and all objects, there are six faculties. Because they control femininity and masculinity, female and male faculties are separate from the body. (2:2)

mdo sde pa'i lugs ni mig la sogs pa lnga po rnams ni rang rang gi don gzugs la sogs pa la dmigs par byed pa'i rnam shes mtshungs ldan dang bcas pa skyed pa la dbang byed pa'i phyir dang*/ yid ni don gzugs la sogs pa yul thams cad la dmigs par byed pa'i rnam shes mtshungs ldan dang bcas pa skyed pa la dbang byed pa'i phyir na mig la sogs pa dbang po drug go gzugs la sogs pas kyang rnam shes skyed par ni byed mod kyi lhag par dbang byed pa ni ma yin pas de dag dbang por thal ba ma yin no/ /

In the Sautrāntika system there are six sense faculties because the five sense organs control the generation of consciousness and its concomitant states that observe (upalabdhi) specific objects such as form, and because the mental faculty controls the generation of consciousness and its concomitant states that observe form and all such objects. Though form and so on indeed generate consciousness, it does not follow that they are faculties since they do not specifically control consciousness.

mo'i dbang po ni nu ma che ba la sogs pa dang nga ro chung ba dang bsam pa zhan pa dang pho la sems pa la sogs pa nyid la dbang byed pa dang*/ pho'i dbang po ni nu ma chung ba dang dbyibs 'jar ba la sogs pa dang nga ro gsang mtho ba dang bsam pa drag pa dang mo la sems pa zhes bya ba'i pho'i chos nyid la dbang byed pa'i phyir dbang por gzhag cing*/ de dag kyang lus kyi dbang po'i cha shas las mo'i dbang po dang pho'i dbang po dag tu gzhag gi rdzas logs su grub pa ni med {reg bya la dmigs pa'i shes bskyed pa'i bdag rkyen gzugs dang ba yin pa'i phyir ro } do/ /

Because the female faculty controls femininity (strītva), such as the attributes of larger breasts, softer voice, timid thoughts, and interest in males, and the male faculty controls masculinity (pūṃstva), such as the attributes of a flat chest and protruding organs, resonant voice, robust thoughts, and interest in females, they are posited as faculties. Also the female (strī) and male (purūṣa) faculties are posited as separate from the body sense faculty, but they are not a separate substance {because the dominant condition generating consciousness focusing on tactile objects is the subtle organ.}
rigs gnas kun nas nyon mongs dang / / rnam par byang la dbang byed phyir/ / srog dang tshor ba rnams dang ni/ / sogs dbang po lngar 'dod do/ / 3

Because life force controls maintenance of type, feeling controls unenlightened states, and the five faculties of faith and so on control enlightened states, they are considered to be faculties. (2:3)

srog gi dbang po ni ris mthun par gnas pa la dbang byed pa dang*/ tshor ba'i dbang po lnga po rnams ni kun nas nyon mongs pa la dbang byed pa dang*/ dad pa la sogs pa'i dbang po lnga ni rnam par byang ba la dbang byed pa'i phyir te/ chos sbyin gyi mdo las/ tshe dang ldan pa sa ga /bde ba'i tshor ba la 'dod chags rgyas par 'gyur ro/ / sdug bsngal gyi tshor ba la zhe sdang rgyas par 'gyur ro/ / bde ba yang ma yin sdug bsngal yang ma yin pa'i tshor ba la gti mug rgyas par 'gyur ro zhes bde ba la sogs pa la 'dod chags la sogs pa rgyas par gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ 'jig rten pa'i lam gyi tshogs pa na yod pa'i dad sogs kyis nyon mongs pa rnams kyang rnam par gnon cing nyams smod pa'i phyir dang*/ mdo las/ 'phags pa nyan thos dad pa'i sgo gtan phun sum tshogs pa/ brtson 'grus kyi dpung phun sum tshogs pa/ dran pa'i sgo bsrungs phun sum tshogs pa/ sems mnyam par bzhag pa ni shes rab kyi mtshon gyis rnam par grol bar 'gyur ro zhes 'byung bas nges 'byed cha mthun la sogs pa'i lam yang 'dren pa'i phyir so sor dbang por 'dod do/ /

They are considered to be separate faculties because the faculty of life force (jīvita) controls maintenance of type continuity (nikāyasthiti), the five faculties such as feeling control unenlightened states, and the five faculties of faith (śraddhā) and so on control enlightened states. That is because pleasure increases attachment and so forth, since the Dharmadinnā Sūtra states: Honorable Sage, attachment increases through feelings of pleasure, aversion increases through feelings of pain, delusion increases through feelings that are neither pleasure nor pain.[426] And [this is also true] because faith and so on existing in the collection of mundane paths suppresses and degrades affliction; and they take up the path conducive to penetrative insight and so on since a sūtra observes: Śrāvaka āryas who possess excellent stable faith, excellent effort, and excellent protective mindfulness abide in equipoise and are liberated by the sword of wisdom.[427]
mya ngan 'das sogs gong nas gong / / 'thob pa la ni dbang byed phyir/ // kun shes byed dang kun shes dang / / de bzhin kun shes ldan dbang po/ / 4

Because they control the obtainment of progressively higher states, nirvāṇa, and so on, they are the faculty producing complete knowledge, the faculty of complete knowledge, and so too the faculty possessing complete knowledge. (2:4)

mya ngan 'das sogs zhes bya ba la/ gong nas gong dang myang 'das 'thob/ / sogs pa la ni dbang byed phyir/ / zhes bya bar sbyar te/ rang gi gong ma kun shes pa'i dbang po 'thob pa la dbang byed pa'i phyir kun shes par byed pa'i dbang po dang*/ gong ma kun shes ldan pa'i dbang po 'thob pa la dbang byed pa'i phyir kun shes pa'i dbang po dang*/ lhag med kyi myang 'das 'thob pa la dbang byed pa'i phyir kun shes ldan pa'i dbang por gzhag go /de bzhin zhes pa ni ji ltar mig la sogs pa nas dad sogs kyi bar rnams so sor dbang po yin pa de bzhin du kun shes byed pa la sogs pa gsum yang so sor dbang po yin no zhes bstan pa'i phyir ro zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/ / sogs pa'i sgras ni mi shes pa kun shes par byed pa'i dbang po ni mthong spang spong ba dang*/ kun shes pa'i dbang po ni sgom spang spong ba dang*/ kun shes ldan pa'i dbang po ni mthong ba'i chos la bde bar gnas pa la dbang byed de/ nyon mongs las rnam par grol bas yid bde ba dang shin tu sbyangs pa'i bde ba dag so sor myong ba'i phyir ro zhes pa sdud pa'o/ /

Because they control the obtainment (prāpti) and so forth of progressively higher states (uttarottara) and nirvāṇa, they link to nirvāṇa and so on. Therefore [the first] is posited as the faculty producing complete knowledge (ājñāsyāmi) because it controls the obtainment of the faculty of complete knowledge, which is higher than it. [The second] is the faculty of complete knowledge (ājñā) because it controls the obtainment of the faculty possessing complete knowledge, which is higher again. So too, [the third] is posited as the faculty possessing complete knowledge (ājñātāvi) because [91] it controls the obtainment of remainderless nirvāṇa and so on. Master Pūrṇavardhana explains that “so too” indicates that just as the faculties from the eyes to faith [and so on] are individual faculties, so too the three faculties of producing complete knowledge and so on are also individual faculties.[428] The term “and so on” indicates that the faculty producing knowledge of the unknown controls abandoning that which is to be abandoned by the path of seeing, the faculty of complete knowledge controls abandoning that which is to be abandoned by the path of meditation, and the faculty possessing complete knowledge controls abidance in comfort in one’s current life. In brief, you experience mental satisfaction and the bliss of pliancy due to liberation from affliction.
gnyis pa dbang po'i grangs nges bshad pa ni
Set number of faculties
sems kyi rten dang de'i bye brag / gnas dang kun nas nyon mongs nyid/ / tshogs dang rnam byang ji snyed pa/ / dbang po dag kyang de snyed du/ / 5
The support of mind, categories, maintaining, and unenlightened states. Collection and enlightened states. However many are enumerated, that many are faculties. (2:5)

gal te dbang byed pa'i phyir dbang po yin na ma rig pa la sogs pa'ang 'du byed la sogs pa la dbang byed pa'i phyir dang*/ kha dang lag pa dang rkang pa dang rkub dang 'doms rnams kyang tshig smra ba dang zas la sogs pa len pa dang 'gro ba dang bshang gci 'byin pa dang kun du dga' ba la rim pa bzhin dbang byed pa'i phyir dbang por 'gyur ro zhe na/ rgyu byed pa tsam gyis ni dbang por mi 'jog gi 'on kyang dgos pa la bltos nas mdo las dbang po nyi shu rtsa gnyis su bshad de/ kun nas nyon mongs dang rnam byang gi gzhi dang ngo bo'am/ 'bras bu'i dbang du byas pa'i phyir ro/ /

Objection: Because ignorance controls formation and so on, and because the mouth, hands, legs, anus, and penis respectively control conversation, handling food and so on, movement, passing feces, and great joy, they are also faculties, since something becomes a faculty if it controls [or facilitates] something. Reply: Something is not posited as a faculty through merely acting as a cause. Instead, the sūtras explain that there are twenty-two faculties from the perspective of being (1) the basis, (2) the nature, or (3) the result, of unenlightened or enlightened states.

de la sems can gyi rdzas kyi gzhi'i dbang du byas nas sems rnam shes kyi rten du gyur pa mig la sogs pa'i dbang po drug dang*/ sems can de'i bye brag tu 'byed pa'i dbang du byas nas pho mo'i dbang po dang*/ sems can de dag ris mthun par gnas pa'i dbang du byas nas srog gi dbang po gsungs te/ de ltar na dbang po dgu po de dag ni kun nas nyon mongs pa'i gzhi yin no/ / tshor ba rnams ni kun nas nyon mongs par byed pa'i ngo bo nyid yin pa'am/ de'i 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir bstan to/ / dad sogs lngas tshogs gsog par byed pa'i phyir rnam byang gi gzhi yin no/ / dbang po tha ma gsum gyis ni rnam par byang bar byed pa'am/ rnam byang gi ngo bo yin pa'i phyir bstan te/ de ltar na kun nas nyon mongs dang rnam byang gi gzhi dang rang gi ngo bo'i grangs ji snyed pa dang rjes su mthun par dbang po dag kyang de snyed du bstan to zhes bya ba yin no/ /

The basis of unenlightened states is the nine faculties: (1–6) the six faculties such as the eyes are the support of consciousness or the mind (citta) and are called faculties from the perspective of acting as the substantial basis of sentient beings; (7–8) the faculties of male and female are called faculties from the perspective of distinguishing categories (vikalpa) of sentient beings; and (9) the faculty of life force is called a faculty from the perspective of maintaining (sthiti) the continuity of sentient beings. (10–14) The feelings are taught to be either the nature or result of unenlightened states. The basis of enlightened states is (15–19) the five such as faith, because they accumulate [to form] the collection (saṃbhāra) [of merit and wisdom]. (20–22) The last three faculties are taught to either activate enlightened states or to be the nature of enlightened states. Thus however many (yāvat) are enumerated as the basis or specific nature of unenlightened and enlightened states, that many (tāvat) are taught to be faculties concordant with them.
yang na 'jug pa'i rten dang ni/ / skye dang gnas dang nyer spyod las/ / bcu bzhi de bzhin ldog pa la/ / dbang po rnams ni gzhan yin no/ / 6
Again, fourteen are the support of entry, birth, abidance, and enjoyment. So too there are different faculties when exiting saṃsāra. (2:6)

yang na sde pa gzhan dag ni 'khor bar 'jug ldog gi dbang du mdzad nas gsungs par 'dod de/ de la 'khor bar 'jug pa'i rten ni dbang po drug yin te/ sems can gyi rdzas kyi gzhi yin pa'i phyir dang*/ bar do'i skye mched drug la brten nas skye srid du nying mtshams sbyor ba'i phyir ro/ / 'khor bar skye ba ni pho mo'i dbang po yin te/ de dag las skye ba'i phyir ro/ / rdzus te skye ba la sogs pa la med kyang gtso che bas de skad brjod do/ / sems can de dag gnas par byed pa ni srog gi dbang po dang*/ sems can rnams kyi nye bar longs spyod pa las ni bde ba la sogs pa lnga ste/ de ltar 'khor bar 'jug pa'i dbang du mdzad nas bcu bzhi yin no/ / ji ltar 'khor bar 'jug pa la rten dang skye ba dang gnas pa dang longs spyod pa bzhi yod pa de bzhin du 'khor ba las ldog pa la'ang rten dang skye ba dang gnas pa dang*/ gnas pa nyer spyod ni snga ma rnams las gzhan dbang po brgyad po rnams yin no/ / de la ldog pa'i rten ni dad sogs lnga yin te/ de dag la brten nas 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam mngon du byed pa'i phyir ro/ / rnam byang nyid du skye ba ni mi shes pa kun shes par byed pa'i dbang po yin te/ de ni zag med du dang por skye ba'i phyir ro/ / rnam par byang bar gnas pa ni kun shes pa'i dbang po yin te/ sgom lam rnam pa dgu rgyun chags su gnas pa'i phyir ro/ / rnam par byang ba nye bar longs spyod pa ni kun shes ldan pa'i dbang po yin te/ rnam par grol bas dga' ba dang bde ba so sor myong ba'i phyir ro/ / dbus mtha' las ni/ 'dzin dang gnas dang rgyun mi chad/ / spyod dang dag pa gnyis kyi phyir/ / zhes mig sogs drug dang*/ srog dang*/ pho mo gnyis dang*/ tshor ba lnga dang*/ dad sogs lnga dang*/ kun shes byed sogs gsum po rnams rim pa ltar yul drug 'dzin pa dang mi 'chi bar gnas pa dang rigs 'tsho ba pas rgyun mi chad pa dang*/ dge mi dge'i las kyi 'bras bu la nye bar spyod pa dang*/ 'jig rten pa'i rnam dag dang*/ 'jig rten las 'das pa'i rnam dag la dbang byed pa'i phyir dbang po nyi shu rtsa gnyis su grangs nges par bshad do/ /

Again, other schools assert that the faculties are declared from the perspective of entering or exiting saṃsāra. There are fourteen from the perspective of entering saṃsāra, which include (1–6) six faculties that are the support of entry (pravṛtti) to saṃsāra because they are the substantial basis of sentient beings, and beings connect to birth existence in reliance on the six bases of an intermediate being. (7–8) Male and female faculties produce birth (utpatti) in saṃsāra because beings are born[429] from them. Though they are not required in supernatural birth and so on, they are mentioned [92] since they are the main [generators of physical birth]. (9) The faculty of life force controls the continued abidance (sthiti) of sentient beings, and (10–14) the five such as pleasure constitute the enjoyment (upabhogata) of sentient beings. Just as entry to saṃsāra has four types — support, birth, abidance, and enjoyment — so too, when exiting (nivṛtti) saṃsāra, there are four: support, birth, abidance, and enjoyment [established by] eight faculties that are different from the former. They include (1–5) the five of faith and so on that support exiting saṃsāra because the transcendent path manifests in dependence on them. (6) The faculty producing complete knowledge of the unknown gives rise to birth in enlightened states because it initially gives rise to the uncontaminated [path of seeing]. (7) The faculty of complete knowledge maintains abidance in enlightened states because it maintains continuous abidance in the nine types of the path of meditation. (8) The faculty possessing complete knowledge is the enjoyment of enlightened states because joy and pleasure are experienced through liberation. Differentiating the Middle and Extremes states: Apprehension, abidance, uninterrupted continuity, enjoyment, and the two purities.[430] Therefore the faculties are explained to be definitely twenty-two in number because the six sense faculties control apprehension of the six objects, life force controls abidance until death, the faculties of both male and female control uninterrupted continuity of family lineage, the five feelings facilitate enjoyment of the results of virtuous and nonvirtuous action, the five of faith and so on control mundane purity, and the three such as producing complete knowledge control transcendent purity.
gsum pa dbang po'i ngo bo bshad pa ni
The nature of the faculties
lus tshor sim pa ma yin gang / / sdug bsngal dbang po'o sim pa ni// bde ba'o bsam gtan gsum pa na/ / sems kyi de ni bde dbang po/ / 7
Any unpleasant feeling of the body is the faculty of pain. Pleasant feeling is the faculty of pleasure. Pleasant feeling of the mind in the third absorption is the faculty of pleasure. (2:7)

dbang po nyi shu rtsa gnyis las mig sogs drug dang pho mo'i dbang po ste brgyad ni bshad zin la/ dad sogs lnga dang srog gi dbang po ste drug ni 'og nas 'chad par 'gyur bas 'dir ni tshor ba'i dbang po lnga dang zag med kyi dbang po gsum ste brgyad 'chad de/

From among the twenty-two faculties, eight — the six such as the eyes and the male and female faculty — have been explained, and six — the five such as faith and the faculty of life force — will be explained below. Now the five faculties such as feeling and the three uncontaminated faculties will be explained.

de la lus ni 'dir dbang po gzugs can thams cad la brjod par 'dod de/ de la brten nas skyes pa'i tshor ba sim pa ma yin pa gang yin pa de ni sdug bsngal gyi dbang po yin te/ mig la sogs pa'i rnam shes lnga'i 'khor du skyes pa'i tshor ba gdung ba la de skad du brjod do/ / de dag gi 'khor du skyes pa'i tshor ba sim pa ni bde ba'i dbang po ste/ phan 'dogs par byed pa'i tshor ba ni sim pa yin no/ / rnam shes lnga'i 'khor du skyes pa'i sim pa kho na bde ba yin par ma zad bsam gtan gsum pa na sems te yid kyi rnam shes kyi 'khor du skyes pa'i tshor ba sim pa gang yin pa de ni bde ba'i dbang po yin te/ de na sgo lnga'i rnam shes med pas lus tshor med pa'i phyir dang*/ dga' ba las 'dod chags dang bral bas sim pa de yid bde'ang ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Here “body” refers to all the physical sense faculties, and any unpleasant (aśāta) feeling arising in dependence on them is the faculty of pain, which is designated as painful feeling generated in the retinue of the five sense consciousnesses. Pleasant (śāta) feeling generated in their retinue is the faculty of pleasure (sukha) since beneficial feeling is pleasant. Not only is pleasure a pleasant feeling arising in the retinue of the five consciousnesses, but any pleasant feeling arising in the retinue of mental consciousness or the mind in the third absorption is the faculty of pleasure (sukhendriya). Feeling of the body does not exist there because the consciousnesses of the five sense doors do not exist there. Also that pleasant feeling is not “mental satisfaction” since beings in the third absorption are free from attachment to joy. [93]
gzhan na de yid bde ba yin/ / sems kyi sim pa ma yin pa/ / yid mi bde ba'o btang snyoms ni/ / bar ma'o gnyis ka'i mi rtog phyir/ / 8
Excepting that, it is mental satisfaction. Unpleasant feeling of mind is mental dissatisfaction. Equanimity is intermediate because it arises nonconceptually. (2:8)

'o na yid bde gang zhe na/ bsam gtan gsum pa las gzhan 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang po dang gnyis pa dag na yid kyi rnam shes kyi 'khor du skyes pa'i tshor ba sim pa gang yin pa de ni yid bde ba yin te/ dga' ba las 'dod chags dang ma bral bas sa de dag gi yid kyi 'khor du skyes pa'i sim pa ni dga' ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Question: What is mental satisfaction? Reply: Any pleasant feeling arising in the retinue of mental consciousness in the desire realm, first absorption, or second absorption, but excepting that (anyatra) of the third absorption, is mental satisfaction (saumanasya) because pleasant feeling arising in the retinue of those lower minds is joyful (prīti) since it is not free from attachment to joy.

'o na sems bde dang yid bde'i khyad par gang yin zhe na/ 'dod pa nas bsam gtan gnyis pa'i bar gyi yid dga' ba rnam par rtog pa tsam gyis skye zhing mi brtan pa ni yid bde yin la/ bsam gtan gsum pa na brtan par gnas pa'i yid kyi sim pa ni sems bde'i dbang po yin no/ / bsam gtan gsum pa na dga' ba med pa dang bde ba yod par yang mdo las shes te/ de dga' ba las 'dod chags dang bral bas dran pa dang ldan zhing shes bzhin du btang snyoms su gnas te/ bde ba lus kyis myong la 'phags pa rnams kyis de la dran pa dang ldan pa bde ba la rnam par spyod pa btang snyoms pa'o/ / zhes brjod pa ste dga' ba med pa'i bsam gtan gsum pa rdzogs par byas te gnas so zhes bya ba la sogs pa gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / sems te yid kyi rnam shes kyi 'khor du skyes pa'i tshor ba sim pa ma yin pa gang yin pa de ni yid mi bde ba'i dbang po'o/ / btang snyoms kyi dbang po ni sngar smos pa'i tshor ba de dag gi bar ma'i tshor ba'o/ /

Question: What is the difference between “mental bliss (sukhacitta)” and “mental satisfaction (saumanasya)”? Reply: Mental satisfaction is mental joy from the desire realm to the second absorption; it is unstable and arises due to conception alone. Mental well-being that endures stably in the third absorption is the faculty of mental bliss. Also we know from the sūtras that pleasure exists in the third absorption but not joy: Āryas are free from attachment to joy, possess mindfulness, and consciously abide in equanimity, for they are mindful that the body experiences pleasure, and in enjoying that pleasure [they experience] equanimity.[431] Therefore it is stated that one should accomplish the third absorption, which is free of joy and so on. Any unpleasant feeling arising in the retinue of mental consciousness or the mind is the faculty of mental dissatisfaction (daurmanasya). The faculty of equanimity (upekṣā) is a feeling intermediate (madhyā) to those feelings mentioned before.
ci de lus kyi'am sems kyi yin zhe na/
Question: Does it pertain to the body or mind?

lus dang sems gnyis ka'i bar ma ni bsdoms nas btang snyoms su gzhag go /ci ste zhe na/ rnam par mi rtog par ngang gis skye ba'i phyir te/ sems kyi bde sdug ni rnam rtog tsam gyis skye la lus kyi ni ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ lus kyi bde sdug ni lus la phan pa dang gnod par byed pa'i phyir de dag ni tha dad du byas la/ btang snyoms ni rnam par mi rtog par skye ba'i phyir dang*/ phan gnod med par skye ba'i phyir gnyis ka gcig tu bsdoms so/ /

Reply: Intermediate feeling of both the body and mind is posited as equanimity through combining both. Question: Why? Reply: That is because [equanimity] arises nonconceptually (avikalpa). Other [feelings] are distinguished because mental pleasure and pain only arise due to conceptuality and not due to the body, and physical pleasure and pain either benefit or harm the body. But both [physical and mental] equanimity are combined as one because they arise nonconceptually and they arise without such benefit or harm.
mthong bsgom mi slob lam la dgu/ / gsum yin...
Nine faculties on the paths of seeing, meditation, and no more learning are three faculties. (2:9ab)

mthong ba dang sgom pa dang mi slob pa'i lam gsum la rim pa bzhin yid dang bde ba dang yid bde dang btang snyoms dang dad sogs lnga ste dgu po de dag ni mi shes pa kun shes par byed pa dang*/ kun shes pa dang*/ kun shes ldan pa'i dbang po gsum yin gyi de dag rdzas gzhan dag ni med do/ / de la bde ba ni bsam gtan gsum pa la brten pa yin na sems bde yin pas de skad brjod kyi lus bde ni ma yin te/ sgo lnga'i rnam shes 'khor bcas ni zag bcas nyid du nges pa'i phyir ro/ { dbus mtha'i TIka dang*/ kun las btus kyi 'grel par rnal 'byor spyod pa ltar na dang po nyid kyi gdags gzhi yid mi bde'ang yin pas bcur bshad do/ / tshor ba gsum po de dag kyang mi lcogs med dang*/ khyad par can dang*/ bsam gtan bzhi pa dang*/ gzugs med dang po gsum gyi sa pa yin na/ btang snyoms dang*/ bsam gtan dang po dang gnyis pa'i sa pa yin na yid bde dang*/ bsam gtan gsum pa'i sa pa yin na bde ba 'byung bas tshor ba gsum gdags gzhir bshad kyi tshogs pa gcig la gsum char 'byung ba ni ma yin no/ /}

Nine faculties, which are respectively (1) the mental faculty, (2) pleasure, (3) mental satisfaction, (4) equanimity, and (5–9) the five such as faith on the three paths (patha) of seeing (dṛg), meditation (bhāvanā), and no more learning (aśaikṣa), are the three faculties — producing complete knowledge, complete knowledge, and possessing complete knowledge — for they are not distinct in substance. If pleasure is supported by the third absorption, it is called “mental bliss” and not “physical pleasure” because the five sense consciousnesses and their retinue are definitely contaminated. {In the Commentary on Differentiating the Middle and Extremes[432] and Elucidation of the Compendium of Abhidharma,[433] Yogācāras explain that there are ten faculties since mental dissatisfaction is described as a basis designated [as a path] from the outset. Also they explain that the three feelings are each a basis designated [as a path], since equanimity occurs on the level of unrestricted access concentration, special [first absorption], the fourth absorption, and the first three levels of the formless realms; mental satisfaction occurs on the level of the first and second absorptions; and pleasure occurs on the level of the third absorption. [94] They do not, however, occur together as three components of a single collection.}

Three are without stain. The physical faculties, life force, and [both] pains are contaminated. Nine have both aspects. (2:9cd)
