Question: How many faculties are solely contaminated? How many are uncontaminated?

'das ma thag par bshad pa'i mi shes pa kun shes par byed pa la sogs pa gsum ni gcig tu dri ma ste zag pa med pa kho na yin no/ / mig la sogs pa dbang po gzugs can bdun dang*/ srog gi dbang po dang*/ yid mi bde dang*/ sdug bsngal dag ste bcu ni sgom spang yin pas gcig tu zag pa dang bcas pa yin no/ / yid dang bde ba dang yid bde dang btang snyoms dang dad sogs lnga ste dgu ni zag bcas zag med rnam pa gnyis ka yin te/ lam gsum gyi tshogs pa na yod pa zag med dang*/ gzhan dag ni zag bcas yin pa'i phyir ro/ / kha cig dad sogs lnga yang gcig tu zag med kho na yin no/ / zhes zer ba ni ma yin te/ lung gzhi las/ sems can 'jig rten du skyes shing 'jig rten du rgas pa rnams la dbang po rnon po dag kyang mchis/ dbang po 'bring po dag kyang mchis/ dbang po rtul po dag kyang mchis so zhes chos kyi 'khor lo mi bskor ba'i dus su gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ gzhan yang mdo las/ ngas ji srid du dbang po lnga po 'di dag gi kun 'byung ba dang*/ mi snang ba dang*/ ro myang ba dang*/ nyes dmigs dang*/ nges par 'byung ba yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin ma shes pa de srid du nga 'jig rten lha dang bcas pa/ bdud dang bcas pa/ tshangs pa dang bcas pa/ dge sbyong dang bram ze'i skye dgu dang bcas pa lha dang mir bcas pa 'di las 'grol ba dang*/ nges par 'byung ba dang*/ mi ldan pa dang*/ bral ba dang*/ phyin ci log dang bral ba'i sems kyis mang du gnas par mi 'gyur ro zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs pa'i phyir te/ gal te zag med yin na nyes dmigs la sogs pa'i brtag pa mi rigs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na mdo las/ gang la dbang po lnga po 'di dag thams cad du thams cad med pa de ni phyi rol so so'i skye bo'i phyogs la gnas par nga smra'o zhes 'byung ba ji lta bu zhe na/ de ni 'phags pa'i gang zag rnam par bzhag pa lam gsum gyi dad pa la sogs pa'i dbang du byas nas gsungs pa'am/ yang na dge rtsa kun du chad pa la phyi rol so so'i skye bo zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: All three faculties such as producing complete knowledge of the unknown, which were just explained, are entirely without stain (amala) or contamination. Ten faculties — the seven physical (rūpiṇi) sense faculties, and the faculties of life force, mental dissatisfaction, and pain — are entirely contaminated since they are objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation. Nine faculties — the mental faculty, pleasure, mental satisfaction, equanimity, and the five such as faith — have both contaminated and uncontaminated aspects because those associated with the three paths are uncontaminated and those that are not are contaminated. Some say: All five faculties such as faith are entirely uncontaminated. Reply: That is not so because Chapters on Vinaya declares: From among sentient beings who are born and age in the world, those of sharp intellectual faculty practice them, those of medium faculty practice them, and those of dull faculty practice them.[434] This was stated with respect to a time when the wheel of Dharma had not yet been set in motion. Again, a sūtra states: For as long as I had not correctly understood the five faculties as they are, their origin, nonappearance, taste, disadvantages, and renunciation, for that long I accompanied mundane divine beings, demons, Brahma, various śramaṇas and brahmans, the divine and human. I did not find release from them, nor renounce them, nor not acquire them, nor be freed from them, and I did not abide with a mind free from distortion.[435] If these five faculties were uncontaminated, it would be illogical to investigate their disadvantages. Question: Why, then, does a sūtra say: Where do none of these five faculties exist in the least? I say they do not exist in tīrthikas who reside at the stage of ordinary beings.[436] Reply: This is stated either from the perspective of the faculties such as faith existing in the three paths posited for ārya beings or from the perspective of tīrthikas who are ordinary beings who have totally severed their root of virtue.

{slob dpon 'phags pas ni kun las btus las mi shes pa kun shes par byed pa'i dbang po gang zhe na/ sbyor ba'i lam dang mthong ba'i lam gyi sems kyi skad cig bco lnga la gang dbang byed pa'o zhes pa dang*/ phal che ba'i dbang du mdzad nas rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las kyang byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyis mi shes pa kun shes par byed pa'i dbang po la sogs pa gsum ji ltar rnam par bzhag ce na/ smras pa/ mos pas spyod pa'i sa la ni dang po rnam par bzhag go /de las gzhan pa lhag pa'i bsam pa rnam par dag pa'i sa dag la ni gnyis pa kun shes pa'o/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i sa la ni dbang po gsum pa kun shes ldan pa rnam par bzhag par lta bar bya'o zhes pa dang*/ mi shes pa kun shes par byed pa'i dbang po ni dge sbyong gi tshul gyi 'bras bu dang thag ring zhing 'jig rten pa'i rnam par rtog pa gang yin pa de ni zag pa dang bcas pa yin la/ dge sbyong gi tshul gyi 'bras bu dang thag nye zhing 'jig rten las 'das pa'i rnam par rtog pa gang yin pa de ni zag pa med pa yin par lta bar bya'o zhes sa mtshams dang ngo bo 'di las gzhan du bshad do/ /}

{Master Asaṅga states in the Compendium of Abhidharma: What is the faculty producing complete knowledge of the unknown? It is whatever controls [or empowers] the path of preparation and the fifteen moments of mind of the path of seeing.[437] Also, from a general perspective, the Compendium of Ascertainment discloses: How should bodhisattvas posit the three faculties such as producing complete knowledge of the unknown and so on? They should posit the level of Resolute Conduct as the first (producing complete knowledge); the next level of Universal Responsibility as the second (complete [95] knowledge); and the level of the Tathāgata as the third (possessing complete knowledge).[438] And: The faculty producing complete knowledge of the unknown is contaminated when a mundane state distant from the result of training in virtue but uncontaminated when it is close to the result of training in virtue and any transcendent thought.[439] This explains the range and nature of the three faculties differently from [the former].}
srog ni rnam smin bcu gnyis gnyis/ / tha ma brgyad dang yid mi bde/ / ma gtogs pa ste de gcig ni/ / rnam par smin bcas bcu rnam gnyis/ / 10
Life force is karmic maturation. Twelve have two types. They are those, except the last eight and mental dissatisfaction. It alone possesses karmic maturation. Ten have two aspects. (2:10)

yang dbang po de dag las srog ni gcig tu rnam par smin pa kho na yin te/ mtho ris na dge ba zag bcas dang*/ ngan song na mi dge bas 'phangs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na bstan bcos las/ tshe'i 'du byed dag ji ltar 'jog par byed ce na/ dge slong dgra bcom pa rdzu 'phrul dang ldan pa sems la dbang thob pas dge 'dun nam gang zag la lhung bzed dam/ chos gos sam/ dge sbyong gi 'tsho ba'i yo byad gang yang rung ba phul nas/ de bsams te rab kyi mtha' pa'i bsam gtan bzhi pa la snyoms par 'jug cing*/ de de las langs nas bdag gi longs spyod kyi rnam par smin pa gang yin pa de tshe'i rnam par smin par gyur cig snyam du sems skyed par byed cing tshig tu yang smra bar byed de/ de'i longs spyod kyi rnam par smin pa gang yin pa de tshe'i rnam par smin par 'gyur ro zhes 'byung ba'i dgra bcom pa tshe bsrings pa{ 'i tshe} de gang gi rnam smin du 'gyur te/ mtshungs ldan las gzhan pa'i rnam par smin pa ni 'dod dgur sngon du mi 'gyur ba zhig na de 'jog par 'dod na gnas pa dang gtong bar 'dod na 'dor ba'i phyir ro/ / zhe na/ kha cig na re de ni{ sgo gsum gyi las dge ba zag bcas de'i} mthong chos kyi las kyi rnam smin kho na yin no zhes zer ro/ / kha cig ni dgra bcom pa thams cad la tshe bsring du yod pa ma yin gyi sngon tshe ma zad par bar ma dor {dus min du } shi 'phos te tshe'i lhag ma lus pa dag dge 'dun la yo byad phul nas{ rab mtha'i bsam gtan gyi stobs kyis} 'dren par 'dod de/ de'i ltar na longs spyod kyi rnam par smin pa tsher 'gyur ro zhes bya ba ni{ sngar gyi} rnam par smin pa{ smon lam gyi} 'dren par byed pa la de'i rnam par smin pa zhes btags pa nyid du shes so/ / btsun pa dbyangs sgrogs ni bsam gtan gyi stobs kyis gzugs na spyod pa'i 'byung ba tshe dang mthun pa{ 'am 'gal ba} dag mngon du byed do/ / de'i stobs kyis tshe ring{ ba dang thung} bar byed pas de ni rnam smin ma yin no/ / longs spyod kyi rnam par smin pa tsher 'gyur ro zhes bya ba ni btags pa ba dang*/ srog gi dbang po rnam smin du bshad pa ni gtso che bas bshad do zhes 'chad do/

From among those faculties, all life force is karmic maturation alone, because higher rebirth is projected by contaminated virtue and lower rebirth is projected by nonvirtue. Question: The treatise (Attainment of Knowledge)[440] expounds: How is the composite of lifespan established? Fully ordained arhats with supernatural power, who have obtained control over their minds, offer their bowls, robes, and any other property of the virtuous life to the Saṅgha and other beings. Then, while contemplating this, they enter meditative attainment on the limit of the fourth absorption, and when rising from that, they generate the thought and state the words: “May all my karma maturing as enjoyment transform into karma maturing as lifespan,” and all their karma maturing as enjoyment transforms into karma maturing as lifespan.[441] But {when} arhats extend their lifespan, what is it that matures? Karmic maturation not associated with mind, which was not previously transformed according to the arhat’s wish, perishes. But if they wanted it to remain, it would abide, and if they desired to relinquish it, it would be discarded. Some say: It is just the karmic maturation of {contaminated virtuous} karma {of the three doors} in this life. Some assert: Not all arhats can extend their lifespan, but karmic maturation that is not exhausted or destroyed in a previous life due to {untimely} death can be dedicated to the Saṅgha and offered as Saṅgha requisites {due to the power of the limit of the fourth absorption}. Thus you should understand that the statement “Karma maturing as enjoyment transforms into lifespan” refers to dedicating the karmic maturation {of prior virtue through prayer}, and that this is designated “its karmic maturation.” Bhadanta Ghoṣaka explains that primary elements utilized in the form realm actually promote {or impede} lifespan due to the power of absorption. Therefore lifespan is extended {or shortened} by its power and not by karmic maturation. Thus the explanation that the faculty of life force is karmic maturation is the main explanation, while the statement “karma maturing as enjoyment transforms into lifespan” is provisional.

{ longs spyod kyi rnam smin tsher bsgyur ba dang tshe lhag 'dren par 'dod pa gnyis ka ltar yang tshe ni sngon gyi las kyi rnam smin yin la longs spyod dang smon lam sogs ni de bsgyur ba'i rkyen tsam yin no/ / slob dpon ni ting nge 'dzin gyi mthu kho nas sngon gyi las kyis 'phangs pa'i tshe'i dus nges pa zlog nas/ ting nge 'dzin las gsar du skyes pa'i tshe gtong 'jog byed par 'dod do/ / de dang dbyangs sgrogs ltar na srog rnam smin du bshad pa ni tha mal pa'i dbang du byas nas gtso che ba la dgongs pas ci dgar byar yod pa'i tshe'ang yod do zhes so/} de bzhin du tshe gtong ba'ang{ sman la sogs pas gnas pa'i thabs ma mthong na} bsam gtan bzhi pa la snyoms par zhugs pa las langs nas yo byad gang yang rung ba dge 'dun {nam 'gog pa las langs ma thag pa la sogs pa'i gang zag }la phul nas{ rab mtha'i bsam gtan bzhi pa la zhugs nas de las langs te} bdag gi tshe'i rnam smin gang yin pa de longs spyod kyi rnam smin du gyur cig snyam du sems bskyed cing tshig tu'ang smras pas gtong bar byed do/{ rab mtha'i bsam gtan de'i longs spyod kyi rnam smin tshe'i rnam smin du 'gyur ro zhes bstan bcos las byung ste de dag ni lus dang yid dang ngag gi las so/ / gtong na de nyid zlog go /} de yang gson pas gzhan na phan pa dang dgos pa ma mthong zhing*/ rang gi lus nad la sogs pa lta bur mthong nas tshe gtong ba yin te/ lung rnam 'byed las{ nye sde la shA ri'i bus smras pa} tshangs spyod 'di la legs spyad cing*/ / lam la'ang shin tu bsgoms na ni/ / tshe zad pa la dga' 'gyur te/ / dper na nad dang bral ba bzhin/ / zhes gsungs pa lta bu'o/ / 'jog pa ni gzhan gyi don dang bstan pa gnas pa la sogs par mthong nas {ting nge 'dzin dang sems la dbang ba dang nyon mongs spangs pa'i phyir/ } dus dang mi sbyor ba'i dgra bcom pa pho mo gnyis ka'i cha las rnam par grol ba dag gis gling gsum gyi mi'i nang kho nar{ dbang po rno bas} tshe bsring bar byed do/{ de yang gnas brtan bcu drug lta bu'o/}

{Though it is asserted that either (1) karma maturing as enjoyment transforms into lifespan or (2) the remaining lifespan is dedicated, the main point is that it is the maturation of past karma, whereas enjoyment, prayer, and so on are merely conditions for that transformation. Vasubandhu asserts that lifespan projected by past karma may be reversed due to the force of concentration alone, [96] and when one newly arises from concentration, it may be reassigned. Ghoṣaka says that explaining life force to be karmic maturation is from the conventional perspective through taking into consideration the main explanation, but whatever exists [as life force potentially] also exists as lifespan.} Similarly, arhats can relinquish lifespan {when they do not see any means of surviving through medicine and so on}. Thus when they rise from meditative attainment of the fourth absorption, they offer any appropriate possessions to the Saṅgha {or persons who have just arisen from cessation and so on, and then they enter the limit of the fourth absorption, and when they rise from that} they generate the thought and state the words, “May my karma maturing as lifespan transform into karma maturing as enjoyment,” and they relinquish it. {The treatise (Attainment of Knowledge)[442] mentions that there are [those who rise from] the limit of the fourth absorption and proclaim that their karma maturing as enjoyment will transform into karma maturing as lifespan.[443] This refers to physical, mental, and verbal karma. But if relinquished, then it is stopped.} Further, if [arhats] see no purpose or benefit for others [if they continue to] live but see just their own physical illness and so on, they will relinquish their lifespan because in Vinaya Divisions {Śāriputra said to close disciples:} If you thoroughly meditate on the path, having well practiced pure conduct, you will take joy in the exhaustion of lifespan, like separating yourself from a disease.[444] Arhats remain due to seeing a purpose for others and for the survival of the teachings and so on {in order to empower concentration, and the mind, and to abandon afflictions}. Male or female arhats {with sharp intellectual faculty} whose time has not come, and who are liberated from both aspects, extend their lifespan as humans of the three continents alone {such as the sixteen arhats (sthavira)}.

'o na lung phran tshegs las bcom ldan 'das kyis srog gi 'du byed dag byin gyis brlabs nas tshe'i 'du byed dag gtong ngo zhes gsungs pa'i tshe srog la khyad par ci zhig yod ce na/ kha cig na re khyad par cung zad kyang med de/ ye shes la 'jug pa las/ srog gi dbang po gang zhe na/ khams gsum pa'i tshe yin no zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro zhes{ bye brag smra ba} zer ro/ / kha cig na re sngon gyi las kyi 'bras bu ni tshe yin la/ da ltar gyi las kyi 'bras bu ni srog yin te/ rim pa ltar las kyi mthus ris mthun par gnas pa dang*/ dus gzhan gyi bar du 'tsho ba'o zhes zer ro/ / dag ces mang po'i tshig gis bstan pa ni tshe srog gi 'du byed kyi skad cig ma mang po'i rgyun la gtong 'jog byed kyi skad cig ma gcig la ni dus thung bas gtong ba dang byin gyis rlob pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / kha cig na re de dag ni 'du byed kyi rgyun mang po rnams la tshe srog ces bya ba'i phyi rol pas brtags pa lta bu'i rdzas gcig pu ni med do zhes bstan pa'i phyir dag ces mang po'i sgra smos so zhes zer ro/ / gal te bcom ldan 'das kyis ci'i phyir sku tshe gtong ba dang byin gyis brlabs pa dag mdzad ce na/ sku tshe la mnga' brnyes pa nyid du bstan pa'i phyir dang*/ de phyin chad gdul bya'i don med pa'i phyir grong khyer rtswa can du ni sku'i 'du byed btang la/ tshe la mnga' brnyes pa dang*/ gang yang ngas rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa bzhi po de ltar bsgoms pa dag gis 'dod na bskal pa'am bskal pa las lhag par bzhugs par bya'o zhes dam bcas pa de yang bsgrub pa'i phyir yangs pa can du zla ba gsum byin gyis brlabs te bzhugs {de tsam gyis rab bzang smin pas so } so/ /

Question: It is mentioned in the Kṣudraka Collection: The Bhagavan, having blessed the composite (saṃskāra) of his life force, relinquished the composite of his lifespan.[445] What is the difference between lifespan and life force? {A Vaibhāṣika} says: There’s not the least difference, because Attainment of Knowledge states: What is the faculty of life force? It is lifespan in the three realms.[446] Some say: The result of prior karma is lifespan and the result of present karma is life force because, respectively, through the power of karma one maintains one’s current life or survives for the time being. A pluralizing particle is added [“composites,” quoted in the Kṣudraka Collection] to indicate that arhats relinquish or maintain a continuum of many moments of a composite lifespan and life force. A single moment [of lifespan or life force] cannot be relinquished or blessed since one moment is an extremely short time. Some say: A pluralizing particle is added to indicate that a single substance called “lifespan” or “life force” that is asserted by non-Buddhists, something imputed to the many moments of a composite continuum, does not exist. Question: Why did the Bhagavan bless and relinquish his lifespan? [97] Reply: He did this to teach that he had attained control over his lifespan. Then he relinquished the composite of his body in Kuśinagara because no further purpose was served by remaining for his disciples. He then stayed in Vaiśālī for three months by the power of his blessing to establish his pledge that “I could live for an eon or more in the desire realm” through having attained control over his lifespan and by meditating on the four supernatural limbs. {Through just those actions, he matured absolute purity.}

bye brag tu smra ba na re bdud bzhi las rgyal bar bya ba'i phyir te/ byang chub kyi shing drung du ni nyon mongs pa dang lha'i bu'i bdud las rgyal lo/ / yangs pa can du sku tshe byin gyis brlabs pas 'chi bdag gi bdud las rgyal lo/{ des na byin gyis brlabs so/ /} rtswa can du sku tshe btang bas ni phung po'i bdud las rgyal ba'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ /

A Vaibhāṣika says: He conquered the four māras because he conquered (1) affliction and (2) the devaputra māra in the vicinity of the bodhi tree. He conquered (3) the māra Lord of Death in Vaiśālī by blessing his lifespan. {Therefore, it was blessed}. He conquered (4) the māra of the aggregates in Kuśinagara by relinquishing his lifespan.

dbang po bcu gnyis ni rnam smin dang rnam smin ma yin pa gnyis ka yin no/ / bcu gnyis gang zhe na/ dad pa la sogs pa dge ba'i dbang po tha ma brgyad dang yid mi bde ba ma gtogs pa srog gi dbang po las gzhan pa rnams te/ dad sogs brgyad ni dge ba 'ba' zhig pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ yid mi bde ni yid mi bde ba rnam gnyis zhes 'byung bas yang na dge ba dang yang na mi dge ba nyid du nges pa'i phyir ro zhes bya ba'o/ / de la mig la sogs pa bdun gyi rgyas byung rnams ni rnam smin ma yin la/ rnam smin las byung ba rnams ni de yin no/ / yid dang tshor ba gzhan bzhi ni dge ba dang*/ nyon mongs can dang*/{ 'bad de sgrub dgos pa'i phyir/} spyod lam pa dang*/ bzo'i gnas pa dang*/ sprul pa{'i sems }rnams ni rnam smin ma yin la/ { de la spyod lam pa dang bzo'i gnas pa gnyis ni yid bde dang btang snyoms dang*/ spyod lam pa ni gzugs na bde ba dang*/ ldan pa yang yod la/ sprul pa sems ni thams cad du yang btang snyoms dang ngo*/ / btsun pa go cha mtha' yas ni de gsum ga btang snyoms dang ngo zhes pa ni mi rigs te/ sbyor ba'i khyad par gyis sgrub pa la bde ba dang yid bde bkag go /lhag ma rnams ni rnam smin te srog dang gzugs can bdun ni bde 'gro na dge ba dang*/ ngan 'gro na mi dge ba'i rnam smin no bde ba yid bde btang snyoms gsum ni dge ba dang sdug bsngal ni mi dge ba'i rnam smin no/ / }

Twelve faculties have two types: karmic maturation or not karmic maturation. Question: What are those twelve? Reply: They are those faculties except for the faculty of life force, the last eight virtuous faculties of faith and so on, and mental dissatisfaction (daurmanasya), because the eight faculties beginning with faith are solely virtuous, and mental dissatisfaction definitely has two aspects: virtuous and nonvirtuous, since it is said to have “two types.” The seven such as the eyes that are derived from enhancement are not karmic maturation, but those arising from karmic maturation are karmic maturation. The mental faculty and the other four feelings that are virtuous or afflicted, and also {the minds governing} demeanor (īryāpatha), creativity (śilpasthāna), and emanation,[447] are not karmic maturation {because they are necessarily established through exertion}. {Both the mind governing demeanor and [that governing] creativity possess mental satisfaction and equanimity, and the mind governing demeanor also possesses pleasure in the form realm. The mind governing emanations possesses equanimity at all times. Bhadanta Anantavarman asserts that those three possess equanimity [alone]. Reply: That is illogical, for such [minds] established by specific preparatory application [can possess] pleasure and mental satisfaction, and thus this is refuted. The remainder are karmic maturation because life force and the seven physical faculties are the karmic maturation of virtue in fortunate reincarnations and of nonvirtue in unfortunate reincarnations; the three faculties of pleasure, mental satisfaction, and equanimity are the karmic maturation of virtue; and pain is the karmic maturation of nonvirtue.}
rnam smin las skyes pa rnams ni de yin no/ / tha ma brgyad dang yid mi bde ni gcig tu rnam smin ma yin pa nyid du grub bo/ /
Those arising from [the cause of] karmic maturation are [karmic maturation]. The last eight and mental dissatisfaction, together, are not established as karmic maturation.

{Objection: If mental dissatisfaction cannot be karmic maturation, it contradicts the explanation that mental dissatisfaction is karma to be experienced. Reply: That is stated intending karma experienced as a concomitant state, not karma experienced as maturation. Objection: But mental satisfaction and equanimity are similar in being states to be experienced. Reply: They are not similar. It is not contradictory that both are states to be experienced, since at times mental satisfaction and neutral equanimity arise nonconceptually. But mental dissatisfaction is never karmic maturation since it arises due to conception alone, such as [the conception] that does not desire [something that has occurred].}

yang dbang po de dag las gang sngar ma gtogs par bshad pa'i yid mi bde ba de gcig pu ni 'bras bu rnam par smin pa dang bcas pa kho na yin te/ de la lung du ma bstan pa med cing*/ mnyam par bzhag pa ma yin pa'i phyir zag med kyang med pas mi dge ba'am dge ba zag bcas kho nar nges pa'i phyir ro/ / dbang po bcu po dag ni rnam smin dang bcas pa dang rnam smin med pa rnam pa gnyis ka yin no/ / bcu gang zhe na/

From among those faculties, the one not yet explained is mental dissatisfaction and it alone [98] possesses the result of karmic maturation (savipāka) because it is not undeclared [or neutral] (avyākṛta) and not equipoise, and it is definitely either nonvirtuous, or a contaminated virtuous state alone since it is not uncontaminated. Ten faculties have two aspects: with karmic maturation or without karmic maturation. Question: What are these ten?
yid dang tshor gzhan dad la sogs/ / dge ba brgyad yid mi bde ba/ / rnam gnyis yid dang tshor gzhan ni/ / rnam gsum gzhan ni rnam pa gcig / 11

The mental faculty, the other feelings, faith and so on. Eight are virtuous. Mental dissatisfaction has two aspects. The mental faculty and the other feelings have three aspects. The others have one aspect. (2:11)

yid kyi dbang po dang yid mi bde ma gtogs pa'i tshor ba gzhan bzhi dang dad pa la sogs pa lnga'o/ / de la yid dang tshor ba bzhi ste lnga po de dag mi dge ba dang*/ bcu char gyi dge ba zag bcas rnams ni rnam smin dang bcas pa dang*/ lung ma bstan dang zag med rnams ni rnam smin med pa'ang yin no/ / lhag ma dbang po gzugs can bdun dang srog dang{ brgyad ni lung ma bstan kho na yin pas sa bon rul ba dang 'dra la} zag med kyi dbang po gsum ni{ sred pas ma brlan pas} rnam smin med pa kho na yin no/ /

Reply: They are (1) the mental faculty, (2–5) the four feelings (vitti) other than mental dissatisfaction, and (6–10) the five of faith and so on. Five faculties — the four feelings and the mental faculty that are nonvirtuous — and the ten that are contaminated virtuous states possess karmic maturation. Neutral and uncontaminated states are without karmic maturation. {Since eight} — (1–7) the remaining seven physical faculties and (8) life force — {are neutral alone, they are like decayed seeds. Since} the three uncontaminated faculties {are not moist with craving,} they solely lack karmic maturation.

yang dbang po de dag las gcig tu dge ba ni tha ma brgyad yin la/ dad sogs lnga dang zag med kyi dbang po gsum mo/ / yid mi bde ba ni dge {ba zag bcas dang }mi dge rnam pa gnyis ka yin no/ / yid kyi dbang po dang yid mi bde ma gtogs pa'i tshor ba gzhan bzhi ni dge ba dang mi dge ba dang lung ma bstan rnam pa gsum ga yin te/ gsum ga dang mtshungs par ldan pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / dbang po lhag ma gzhan mig la sogs pa bdun dang srog ni lung ma bstan gyi rnam pa gcig tu nges pa yin no/ /

Again, from among those faculties the final eight — (1–5) the five such as faith and (6–8) the three uncontaminated faculties — are all virtuous (kuśala). Mental dissatisfaction has two aspects: virtuous and nonvirtuous. The mental faculty and the other four feelings, except for mental dissatisfaction, have three aspects — virtuous, nonvirtuous, and neutral — because they are concomitant with those three states. The other remaining faculties, including the seven such as the eyes and life force, definitely have one aspect that is neutral.
dri med ma gtogs 'dod par gtogs/ / pho mo'i dbang dang sdug bsngal dag / ma gtogs gzugs gtogs gzugs can dang/ / bde ba'ang ma gtogs gzugs med gtogs/ / 12

Those except for stainless faculties belong to the desire realm. Those except for male and female faculties and pain belong to the form realm. Those except for the physical faculties and pleasure belong to the formless realm. (2:12)

yang dbang po de dag las dri ma med pa'i dbang po gsum ma gtogs pa dbang po bcu dgu ni 'dod par gtogs pa ste 'dod pa'i sa pa yang yod do/ / bcu dgu po de dag las pho mo'i dbang po dang*/ sdug bsngal dag ste yid mi bde dang sdug bsngal gyi dbang po dag ma gtogs pa dbang po bco lnga ni gzugs su gtogs pa yin te/ de na 'khrig pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i phyir dang*/ mi mdzes par byed pa'i phyir pho mo'i dbang po dag med la/ mnyam gzhag gi sa pa yin pa'i phyir sdug bsngal gyi dbang po dag kyang med de/ lus shin tu dang ba'i phyir bsnun pa la sogs pa 'phral gyi rkyen gyis bskyed pa'i sdug bsngal med cing mi dge ba med pa'i phyir rnam par smin pa'i sdug bsngal yang med la/ rgyud zhi gnas kyis brlan pa'i phyir dang*/ kun nas mnar sems kyi gzhi dgu med pa'i phyir yid mi bde'ang med do/{ bsam gtan dang po na bco lnga yod do/} gal te gzugs khams na pho'i dbang po med na khams mang po pa'i mdo las/ mo tshangs pa nyid byed par 'gyur ba gang yin pa de ni gnas ma yin zhing go skabs med de/ pho gang yin pa de ni gnas yod do zhes gsung par ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/ pho'i mtshan nyid nga ro gsang mtho ba la sogs pa 'dod pa na yod pa de dag gzugs na'ang yod pa'i phyir de skad du brjod do/ /

From among the faculties, nineteen faculties, except for (hitvā) the three stainless faculties, belong to the desire realm (kāmāpta) and also exist on the desire-realm level. From those nineteen, fifteen faculties except for the male and female (strīpumi) faculties and pain — the faculties of mental dissatisfaction and [physical] pain — belong to the form realm (rūpāpta). Male and female faculties do not exist there because form-realm beings are free from attachment to sexual intercourse, and they do not beautify [the body]. The [two] faculties of pain do not exist there because this is the level of equipoise. There is no pain generated by the incidental condition of striking and so on because their bodies are completely translucent, and there is no pain as karmic maturation because there is no nonvirtue there. There is no mental dissatisfaction because the mindstream is moistened with calm abiding, and the nine bases of the tormented mind do not exist there. {Therefore fifteen faculties exist in the first absorption.} Question: If there is no male faculty in the form realm, then why does the Multiple Elements Sūtra proclaim: No female has the possibility or opportunity to become Brahma. Any male has that possibility.[448] Reply: This is stated because such characteristics as a resonant voice possessed by a male in the desire realm also exist in the form realm.

bco lnga po de dag las gzugs can gyi dbang po mig la sogs pa rnams dang bde ba dang yid bde ba'i dbang po'ang ma gtogs pa lhag ma {srog yid btang snyoms dang dad sogs lnga ste/ } brgyad ni gzugs med par gtogs pa{ yin} ste/ gang zhe na yid dang srog dang btang snyoms dang dad sogs lnga ste brgyad yin no zhes bya ste/ zag med kyi dbang po gsum ni thams cad du'ang khams su ma gtogs par shes par bya'o/ /

From among those fifteen, the eight remaining faculties, except for the physical faculties such as the eyes and the faculties of pleasure (sukha) and mental [99] satisfaction, belong to the formless realm (arūpyāpta). Question: What are they? Reply: The eight are the (1) mental faculty, (2) life force, (3) equanimity, and (4–8) the five such as faith. You should understand that the three uncontaminated faculties do not belong to any realm.
yid dang tshor ba gsum rnam gsum/ / gnyis kyis spang bya yid mi bde/ / dgu ni bsgom pas lnga po ni/ / spang bar bya min yang gsum min/ / 13
The mental faculty and the three feelings have three types. Mental dissatisfaction is abandoned by both. Nine by meditation. Five are also not objects to be abandoned. Three are not. (2:13)

yang dbang po de dag las yid dang bde ba dang yid bde dang btang snyoms kyi tshor ba gsum ste bzhi ni mthong spang dang mtshungs par ldan pa mthong spang dang*/ sgom spang dang mtshungs par ldan pa sgom spang dang*/ spang bya ma yin pa dang mtshungs par ldan pa spang bya ma yin pa zhes bya ba rnam pa gsum du 'gyur ro/{ bde ba der 'gyur ba ni bsam gtan gsum pa'i bde ba yid shes 'khor du skyes pa'i sems bde yin gyi dbang shes 'khor du skyes pa ni sgom spang kho na'o/ /}

From among those faculties, four — (1) the mental faculty (manas), and (2–4) the three feelings of pleasure, mental satisfaction, and equanimity — have three types: (1) that which is to be abandoned by the path of seeing and states concomitant with it, (2) that which is to be abandoned by the path of meditation and states concomitant with it, and (3) that which is not to be abandoned and states concomitant with it. {Such pleasure is pleasure of the third absorption, which is the mental bliss arising in the retinue of mental consciousness, whereas pleasure arising in the retinue of sense consciousness is an object to be abandoned by the path of meditation alone.}

mthong sgom gnyis kyis spang bar bya ba ni yid mi bde ba ste/ de ni zag bcas su nges shing spang bya gnyis ka dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / mig la sogs pa gzugs can bdun dang srog dang sdug bsngal gyi dbang po dang dgu ni bsgom pas spang bar bya ba yin te/ zag bcas su nges shing drug pa las ma skyes la mthong spang ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / dad pa la sogs pa lnga po ni zag bcas bsgom pas spang bar bya ba'ang yin la/ zag med spang bar bya ba min pa yang yin te/ zag bcas zag med kyi bye brag gis so/ / mi shes pa kun shes par byed pa la sogs pa{ tha ma} gsum ni spang bar bya ba min te/ zag med nyes med ni spang bar 'os pa ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ gnyen po yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Mental dissatisfaction (durmanas) is abandoned by both (dviheyā) the path of seeing and the path of meditation because it is definitely contaminated and concomitant with those to be abandoned by both. Nine faculties — (1–7) the seven physical faculties such as the eyes, and the faculties of (8) life force and (9) pain — are abandoned by the path of meditation because they are definitely contaminated. They are not objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing since they do not arise from the sixth. The five faculties of faith and so on are objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation if contaminated. But also they are not objects to be abandoned (aheyā) if uncontaminated since they are subsets of contaminated and uncontaminated states. The {final} three faculties such as producing complete knowledge are not objects to be abandoned because faultless uncontaminated states are not suitable to be abandoned, and they are antidotes.
lnga pa dbang po'i 'thob pa dang gtong ba bshad pa
How the faculties are obtained and relinquished
'dod par dang por rnam smin gnyis/ / rnyed de rdzus te skye bas min/ / de yis drug gam bdun nam brgyad/ / gzugs na drug go gong mar gcig / 14
The first gain two from karmic maturation in the desire realm. Those born supernaturally do not. They gain six, seven, or eight. Six in the form realm. Life force alone above. (2:14)

['di] la dang po 'thob pa ni 'dir dbang po thams cad kyi 'thob tshul ston pa ni ma yin gyi 'on kyang rnam par smin{ pas bsdus} pa'i dbang po dag 'thob pa'i tshul 'chad de/ de yang 'dod par nying mtshams sbyor ba na skye gnas dang po gsum gyis ni dang por rnam smin{ gyi ngo bo lus srog} gyi dbang po gnyis gsar du rnyed de/ lus kyi dbang po dang srog gi dbang po dag go /yid la sogs pa ni rnam par smin par ma nges pa'i phyir{ te yid dang btang snyoms nyon mongs can yin la mig sogs lnga med pa'i phyir} dang*/{kha cig /}sngar yod pa'i phyir ro/ /

The means of obtaining all the faculties is not taught here, just the method of obtaining faculties {subsumed by} karmic maturation. Those born by means of the first three birth processes[449] newly gain two faculties from karmic maturation when linking to the desire realm: the faculties of body and life force. That is because it is not certain that the mental faculty and so on are karmic maturation {because the mental faculty and equanimity can be afflictive, and the five sense organs do not yet exist.} {Some say:} They exist from before.

thams cad du'am zhe na/ rdzus te skye bas ni gnyis kho na rnyed pa min gyi 'o na du zhe na{ bskal pa dang po'i mi lta bu pho mo'i mtshan gnyis ka med pa zhig yin na mig sogs lnga srog dang} rdzus te skye ba de yis ni drug gam zhes bya ba ni de gal te mtshan med pa zhig yin na ni dbang po drug rnyed de/ mig sogs lnga dang srog gi dbang po'o/ / de gal te {'phags pa lha dang 'dod lha lta bu/ } pho mo'i dbang po gang rung zhig dang ldan pa yin na de bsnan pa'i bdun rnyed do/ / de gal te mtshan gnyis pa zhig yin na brgyad rnyed de/ de la rdzus skyes mtshan med pa ni bskal pa dang po'i mi rnams lta bu'o/ / mtshan gcig pa ni 'phags pa lha dang 'dod pa'i lha rnams lta bu'o/ / mtshan gnyis pa ni ngan song rnams na srid do/ / gzugs khams su nying mtshams sbyor ba na ni mig sogs lnga dang srog dang drug rnyed de/ pho mo'i dbang po dag ni de na med par bshad zin pa'i phyir ro/ / gzugs khams kyi gong ma gzugs med pa'i khams su ni srog dbang gcig pu gsar du rnyed de/ rnam smin gyi dbang po gzhan dag ni sa de na med pa'i phyir ro/{ rdzus skyes dbang po tshang bar skyes pas mig sogs lnga dus gcig tu 'thob la/ rnam smin lung ma bstan gyi thob pa snga phyir mi 'byung ba dus mnyam du 'byung ba'i dbang du byas nas so/}

Question: Is this the same for all? Reply: Beings who are born supernaturally (upapāduka) do not gain just two faculties. Question: How many do they gain? Reply: It is said that those born supernaturally gain six, for if they lack a sexual organ they gain: (1–5) the five sense organs and (6) life force. Or, if they possess either the male or female faculty, they gain seven by adding that organ. If they have two organs, they gain eight. Those who are born supernaturally yet lack a sexual organ are, for example, humans of the first eon. Those with a single organ are, for example, ārya divine beings or desire-realm divine beings. Those who possess both organs are possible in the lower realms. [100] Six faculties are gained when linking to the form realm — (1–5) the five sense organs and (6) life force — because it has already been explained that male and female faculties do not exist there. Life force alone (eka) is newly gained in the formless realm, which is above (uttara) the form realm, because other faculties derived from karmic maturation do not exist on that level. {Those who are born supernaturally simultaneously obtain the five sense organs since they are born with faculties complete. But that is from the perspective of obtaining neutral karmic maturation, which arises simultaneously and not earlier or later.}
gal te skye ba na de ltar 'thob na 'chi ba na du lhan cig gtong zhe na/
Question: If those are obtained at birth, how many are simultaneously relinquished at death?
gzugs med dag tu 'chi ba ni/ / srog dang yid dang btang snyoms nyid/ / 'gag par 'gyur ro gzugs na brgyad/ / 'dod par bcu'am dgu'am brgyad/ / 15
When beings die in the formless realm, life force, the mental faculty, and equanimity cease. In the form realm, eight. In the desire realm, ten, or nine, or eight. (2:15)

{ ma bsgribs lung ma bstan dang nyon mongs can gyi sems la gnas te/} gzugs med pa'i khams dag tu 'chi ba'i tshe ni srog dang yid kyi dbang po dang tshor ba btang snyoms kyi dbang po nyid dang gsum dus gcig tu 'gag par 'gyur ro/ / zhes gsungs te/ sems dge ba la gnas te 'chi 'pho ba ma yin pa'i dbang du byas nas zhes sbyar ro/ / gzugs khams su 'chi ba na rdzus skyes thams cad ni dbang po rnams tshang bar skye zhing 'chi bas mig sogs lnga dang sngar bshad pa gsum ste brgyad dus gcig la 'gag par 'gyur ro/ / 'dod par rdzus skyes mtshan gnyis pa{ dbang po tshang ba} zhig 'chi ba na gzugs can bdun dang srog la sogs pa gsum ste bcu 'gag pa'am/ gal te mtshan gcig pa zhig yin na{ pho mo gang rung gcig dang} dgu'am/ mtshan med pa zhig yin na{ srog sogs gsum mig sogs lnga ste} brgyad 'gag par 'gyur ro/{ 'dod pa'i rdzus skyes dbang po ma tshang bar 'chi ba'ang yod do/ /}

Reply: It is said that, when {those abiding with unobscured-neutral or afflicted minds} die (uparama) in the formless realm, the three faculties of life force, the mental faculty, and the feeling of equanimity simultaneously cease (nirodha).[450] But this is not from the perspective of dying with a virtuous mind. When beings die in the form realm, eight faculties simultaneously cease — the five sense organs and the three previously explained — since all who are born supernaturally are born or die with all faculties complete. When those who were born supernaturally in the desire realm with two organs {and all faculties complete} die, ten cease: the seven physical faculties and the three: life force [the mental faculty, and equanimity]. Or, when those possessing {either a male or a female} organ die, nine cease. Or, when those possessing no organ die, eight cease, {namely, the three faculties such as life force and the five sense organs}. {Also there is supernatural birth in the desire realm where the faculties are incomplete.}
rim gyis 'chi ba dag la bzhi/ / dge la thams cad dag tu lnga/ / 'bras bu tha ma gnyis dgus 'thob/ / gnyis ni bdun dang brgyad dang dgus/ / 16
For those with gradual death, four. For the virtuous, five in all realms. Both the first and last results will be obtained by nine. Two are obtained by seven, eight, or nine. (2:16)

de ltar na cig car 'chi ba{'i rdzus skyes }la ni tshul de lta bu yin la/{ cig car 'chi ba ni rdzus skyes yin la/} mngal skyes la sogs pa skye gnas dang po gsum las skyes pa zhig 'chi 'pho ba ni rim gyis 'chi 'pho ba yin pas de dag la ni{ mig sogs sngar 'gags pas mthar} lus dang srog dang btang snyoms dang yid dang bzhi{ cig car} 'gag par 'gyur ro/ /

Thus the {supernatural birth of} those who die instantaneously exists in this way {because those who die instantaneously are born supernaturally}. But for those born by means of the first three birth processes, such as womb birth, death is gradual death (kramamṛtyu), since for them the four faculties — the body, life force, equanimity, and the mental faculty — {simultaneously} cease {after the five faculties such as the eyes cease}.

de dag thams cad ni{ 'chi sems gsum las} ma bsgribs lung ma bstan{ gyi sems} dang sems nyon mongs can gyi dbang du byas te bshad pa yin gyi sems dge ba skyes thob la gnas te 'chi ba dag la ni khams gsum{ gyi gnas skabs drug} po thams cad dag tu sngar gyi{ gsum la sogs pa }rnams kyi steng du dad sogs lnga bsnan pa'i dbang po rnams dus gcig la 'gag par 'gyur te/ gzugs med pa'i khams su brgyad 'gag pa la sogs pa'o/ / 'dir dbang po zag med rnams ni 'chi ba na 'gag par ma bshad de/ de dag ni rnam smin kyang ma yin zhing*/ 'chi sems kyang ma yin la/ 'chi ba ni de dag gi gtong rgyu'ang ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

{From among the three minds of death,} all previous instances have been explained from the perspective of unobscured-neutral {minds} and afflicted minds. But for those who die maintaining a virtuous (śubha) mind obtained at birth, the former {three faculties and so on} as well as the five faculties such as faith simultaneously cease in all {six states of} the three realms, because eight cease in the formless realm and so on. The uncontaminated faculties are not said to cease at death because they are neither karmic maturation nor the mind of death, and death is also not the cause of relinquishing them.
'bras bu de dag dbang po dus 'thob/
rgyun zhugs la sogs pa'i 'bras bu de dag dbang po dus 'thob ce na/
Question: How many faculties obtain the results of stream entry and so on?

'bras bu tha ma ste snga phyi rgyun zhugs dang dgra bcom gnyis ni dbang po dgu dgus 'thob ste/ de la rgyun zhugs kyi 'bras bu ni dad sogs lnga dang{ de dang mtshungs ldan gyi} yid dang{ 'phags pa chags bcas yin pas mi lcogs med kyi tshor ba} btang snyoms dang kun shes byed pa dang kun shes pa'i dbang po dang dgus 'thob ste/ skad cig bco lnga pa man chad ni kun shes byed pa dang*/ bcu drug pa ni kun shes pa yin te/ rim pa ltar bar chad med pa dang rnam grol gyi lam yin pas dang pos ni bral ba'i thob pa 'dren pa dang*/ gnyis pas ni bral thob 'dzin pa'i phyir ro/ / dgra bcom pa ni dad sogs lnga dang yid dang tshor ba ni bsam gtan dang po dang gnyis pa'i dngos gzhi la brten na yid bde dang*/ gsum pa'i dngos gzhi la brten na{ sems yid kyi} bde ba dang sa gzhan{ gong ma dang mi lcogs med} la brten na btang snyoms te gang yang rung ba zhig dang*/{ da ltar ba/} bar chad med pa'i lam la{ rdor ting ni} kun shes pa{ da ltar ba} dang rnam grol gyi lam la kun shes ldan pa'i dbang po ste dgus 'thob bo/ /

Reply: Both the first and last (antya) results (phala), namely stream entry and arhat, will be obtained by nine each, because the result of stream entry is obtained by nine faculties: [101] (1–5) the five such as faith, (6) the {concomitant} mental faculty, (7) {the feeling of} equanimity {of unrestricted access concentration, since that ārya possesses attachment}, (8) producing complete knowledge, and (9) complete knowledge. Up until the fifteenth moment of the path of seeing is [the faculty] producing complete knowledge, and the sixteenth moment is complete knowledge; the former initiates the obtainment of separation and the latter maintains the obtainment of separation, since they are respectively the uninterrupted and the liberated paths. The state of an arhat is obtained by nine: (1–5) the five such as faith, (6) the mental faculty, (7) feeling that is either mental satisfaction dependent on the actual basis of the first or second absorptions, {mental} bliss dependent on the actual basis of the third absorption, or equanimity dependent on other {higher} levels and {unrestricted access concentration}, (8) {vajra concentration} on the {present} uninterrupted path, which is {present} complete knowledge, and (9) possessing complete knowledge on the liberated path.

'bras bu bar pa lan cig phyir 'ong dang phyir mi 'ong gnyis ni dbang po bdun dang brgyad dang dgus 'thob pa'ang yod de/ de la lan cig phyir 'ong bdun gyis 'thob pa ni{ rgyun zhugs thob rjes su} 'phags pa mthar gyis pa zhig 'jig rten pa'i lam{ zhi rags can} gyis {'dod pa'i sgom spang drug pa'i bar du spangs nas }'bras bu thob par byed pa{ na zag med yin pas kun shes pa'i dbang po'i ming thob la/ bar chad med lam dang rnam grol lam gnyis ka yang tshor ba'i dbang po mi lcogs med kyi btang snyoms su gcig pas so} ste/ de la dad sogs lnga dang yid{ de kun 'gro drug} dang{ mi lcogs med kyi} btang snyoms dang bdun no/ gal te{ phyir 'ang} mthar gyis pa de 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam gyis 'thob par byed na brgyad kyis 'thob ste/ sngar gyi bdun dang kun shes pa'i dbang po{ dang brgyad kyis te dad sogs }'o/ gal te sngar 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis phal cher las 'dod chags dang bral ba{ 'i chags bral sngon 'gro} zhig mthong ba'i lam mngon du byas pas lan cig phyir 'ong 'thob par byed na ni dgus 'thob ste/{ rgyun zhugs bzhin du/} sngar gyi brgyad kyi steng du kun shes byed pa'o/ /

The two intermediate results — once return and nonreturn — are obtained by seven, eight, or nine faculties. Once return is obtained by seven faculties. Ārya serial abandoners[451] {who have obtained stream entry} obtain it {through abandoning up to six objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation in the desire realm} by the mundane path {comparing coarse and refined aspects}. {They obtain the name “those with the faculty of complete knowledge” since it is uncontaminated, and they have the faculty of the feeling of equanimity of unrestricted access concentration to both the uninterrupted and the liberated paths.} Therefore the seven are: (1–5) the five such as faith and (6) the mental faculty, {which [together] constitute six omnipresent states}, and (7) equanimity. If {once-returner} serial abandoners obtain [the result of once return] through the transcendent path, it is obtained by eight faculties: (1–7) the previous seven and (8) the faculty of complete knowledge. If {āryas previously freed from attachment,} who are free from most degrees of attachment through the mundane path, obtain once return by manifesting the path of seeing, they obtain that by nine [faculties,] because the faculty of producing complete knowledge is added to the former eight, {as in stream entry}.

Nonreturn is obtained by seven faculties. If serial abandoners of dull intellectual faculty seek to obtain it through the mundane path, it is obtained by (1–5) the five such as faith, (6) the mental faculty, and (7) the feeling of equanimity {of unrestricted access concentration}, because those of dull faculty cannot manifest mental satisfaction of the {first} actual basis at the time of the ninth liberated stage, {nor can they manifest the first}. If serial abandoners of dull faculty obtain nonreturn by the transcendent path, it is obtained by eight: (1–7) the previous seven plus (8) the faculty of complete knowledge. If those of sharp faculty seek to obtain it through the mundane path, it is obtained by eight — {(1–7) the former seven, and (8) mental satisfaction} — because they manifest equanimity {of unrestricted access concentration} to the uninterrupted path and manifest mental satisfaction of the actual basis of the first absorption [102] at the time the ninth liberated path manifests. If serial abandoners of sharp faculty seek to obtain it by the transcendent path, it is obtained by nine: (1–5) the five such as faith, (6) the mental faculty, (7) complete knowledge at the time of the uninterrupted path, (8) equanimity {of unrestricted access concentration}, and (9) mental satisfaction {of the actual basis of the first absorption} manifesting at the time of the ninth liberated path. {All their uninterrupted paths possess the equanimity of unrestricted access concentration alone. And if their intellectual faculty is dull, it is equanimity at the time of the ninth liberated path. It is also said that they do not obtain the actual basis and their path of liberation does not rely on other access concentrations.} Again, when those freed from attachment to the desire realm obtain nonreturn, it is obtained by nine: (1–5) the five such as faith, (6) the mental faculty, (7) any one of the three feelings, (8) complete knowledge, and (9) producing complete knowledge.

{Objection: Those of sharp faculty obtain nonreturn by ten faculties, since they see the four truths in dependence on unrestricted access concentration and they are capable of also entering realization of the truths in dependence on the actual basis. Reply: Jinaputra declares that they do not enter the actual basis of absorption since: That would devalue what is already obtained.[452] Objection: This answer is illogical since if that were devalued, your textual system would be undermined. Reply: The first response is correct, for it is obtained by nine faculties alone, whether of dull or sharp faculty, since the result of āryas previously freed from attachment is obtained by the sixteenth moment of the path of seeing, and the remaining moments depend on whatever level the first moment of the path of seeing depends. Since there is no relocation to another level, how could the feeling of another level arise? Therefore any person of dull faculty obtains it through nine faculties alone.}
gal te dgra bcom pa dbang po dgus 'thob na ye shes la 'jug pa las/ dbang po du zhig gis dgra bcom pa nyid 'thob ce na/ smras pa/ bcu gcig gis 'thob bo zhes bshad pa de ji ltar drang zhe na/

bcu gcig dag gis dgra bcom nyid/ / 'ga' zhig srid phyir bshad pa yin/ /
It explains that the state of an arhat is obtained by eleven because that is possible for some arhats. (2:17ab)

Reply: That is not so because it is impossible that a nonreturner of sharp faculty degenerates, and though {it is possible for} a {serial abandoner} of dull faculty to degenerate, it is impossible to heal [the degenerated state] through the faculty of pleasure. {Therefore, if the result of nonreturn degenerates, then the faculty of pleasure of the third absorption is not available to him, for if it were available he would not degenerate because a learner Hīnayāna ārya who possesses pleasure of the third absorption is necessarily a nonreturner.} If the result of nonreturn degenerates in that way and desire-realm affliction manifests, then that affliction is abandoned in reliance on the mind of access concentration {to the first absorption} alone, and that {access concentration} exists on the level of equanimity. Further, it is possible that those degenerated {serial abandoners} of dull intellectual faculty — who manifest equanimity through access concentration and mental satisfaction {to the actual basis of the first absorption} when on the ninth liberated stage — can upgrade {from dull to sharp intellectual} faculty. But though it is possible that they obtain restoration through mental satisfaction, they obtain nonreturn through nine alone: (1–5) the five such as faith, (6) the mental faculty, (7) complete knowledge, and the feelings of (8) equanimity and (9) mental satisfaction because it is impossible that it is obtained by more faculties.

{ gal te phyir mi 'ong nyams pa ni dbang rtul rim gyis pa yin dgos la/ des bar chad med lam gyi btang snyoms kyi dbang po rnam grol dgu pa'i cha dngos gzhi'i yid bde ba'i dbang por spo mi nus pas/ yid bde'i 'bras bu sor chud pa med do zhe na/ srid de dbang rtul rim gyis pa nyams pa des phyis mi lcogs med la brten nas dbang po rnon por 'phos te phyir mi 'ong gi 'bras bu thob par byed pa la rnam grol dgu pa'i tshe yid bde sogs srid pas dgus thob bo zhes bshad do/ /}

{Objection: If nonreturners degenerate, then they must be serial abandoners of dull intellectual faculty. But they cannot restore the result through mental satisfaction since they cannot transform the faculty of equanimity of the uninterrupted path into the faculty of mental satisfaction of the actual basis at the time of the ninth liberated stage. Reply: That is possible because degenerated serial abandoners of dull faculty can obtain the result of nonreturn by upgrading to sharp faculty in dependence on unrestricted access concentration, and since mental satisfaction is possible at the time of the ninth liberated stage, they obtain it by nine faculties.}

Objection: Those who are freed from attachment to the desire realm by the mundane path and who definitely enter [the transcendent path] through the mind of the fourth absorption and above obtain [their result] by nine: (1) the feeling of equanimity, (2) producing complete knowledge, (3) complete knowledge, (4–8) the five such as faith, and (9) the mental faculty. That is also obtained by eleven because mental satisfaction and pleasure are also possible {at the time of the ninth liberated stage} when restoring degeneration {through upgrading their intellectual faculty by means of unrestricted access concentration}. Reply: That is not so because it is impossible for a nonreturner who was previously freed from attachment to degenerate, because by obtaining both the mundane and transcendent paths, {that result} is stabilized by those two paths. Therefore the Autocommentary maintains: After complete degeneration, restoration is never obtained by the faculty of pleasure. For āryas previously freed from attachment, there is no complete degeneration because those freed from attachment obtain {that result} by both {the earlier mundane and transcendent} paths.[455]

If any one of the three faculties of equanimity, life force, or the mental faculty are possessed (yukta), definitely all three are possessed (anvita), {since they pervade all, and they pervade every supportive basis of sentient beings}. [104]

Objection: Because the mental faculty and the feeling of equanimity do not exist in the meditative attainment of the two mindless states, life force also is not possessed. Reply: Though they do not manifest, their possession is tenable because they are obtained. Faculties other than the first three are not definitely possessed, because in the desire realm the faculties of eyes, ears, nose, and tongue are not obtained {by the [embryonic states of] kalala and so on}, they degenerate {in the blind and so on}, and they are not possessed {in the stages of death}. Again, in the desire realm male and female faculties may not be obtained, or they may degenerate or not be possessed, and those born in both higher realms do not possess {male and female faculties. Those born in the formless realm do not possess the body faculty.} Those born in the two higher realms do not possess the faculties of pain. Those free of attachment to desire-realm objects do not possess mental dissatisfaction because a sūtra declares: Those not free from attachment are said to have two painful feelings because they experience physical pain and mental dissatisfaction. And: Those free of attachment have one painful feeling since they experience only physical pain.[456]

Also a treatise[457] discloses: Mental dissatisfaction is not possessed by those free of attachment.[458] The seven physical faculties such as the eyes are not possessed in the formless realm, and ordinary beings do not possess uncontaminated faculties. Also, those abiding on the paths of meditation and no more learning do not possess the uncontaminated faculty of producing complete knowledge since they relinquish that which was previously obtained. Those abiding on the paths of seeing and no more learning do not possess the faculty of complete knowledge. Learners (śaikṣa) do not possess the faculty of possessing complete knowledge. Those who have severed the root of virtue do not possess the five such as faith. Those ordinary beings of the third {and fourth} absorptions and above do not possess {respectively} mental satisfaction or pleasure. Similarly, males do not possess the female faculty, and females do not possess the male faculty. Those possessing the faculty producing complete knowledge do not possess the latter two, and those possessing complete knowledge do not possess the former or latter. Those possessing complete knowledge do not possess the former two because those are to be understood in accordance with what is stated below.

Those possessing the body faculty function in the desire and form realms because they possess four: the three previously explained and the body faculty. Those possessing the body faculty but not eyes and so on are those in the desire realm who do not obtain eyes or for whom the eyes degenerate and so on.
