Intention (cetanā) is like a magnet that attracts iron, for it is mental karma, which conditions the mind that focuses on the six objects and directs the mind to its focal objects. It is said: How does the mental faculty, which neither is an agent nor abides for another moment, come to have eyes as well as to act? It is through intention, which is mental karma.[502]

If classified, there is the sixfold collection of intention. Its function is to motivate physical and verbal karma. The definition and classification of discernment (saṃjñā) have already been explained. {Yogācāra Levels says: What function does discernment have? It functions to designate objects through apprehending the mark of its focal object.[503]} Therefore its function is to impute designation.

'dun pa ni yul drug la dmigs nas byed 'dod pa ste dmigs pa'i yul don du gnyer ba'o/ / dbye ba ni 'das pa la phrad pa dang*/ da ltar ba la mi 'bral ba dang*/ ma 'ongs pa la don du gnyer bar 'dun pa ste/ brtson 'grus rtsom pa'i las can no/ / reg pa ni yul dang dbang po dang rnam shes gsum 'dus nas yul gyi 'gyur ba yongs su dpyod pa ste/ dbye na reg pa'i tshogs drug go /las ni tshor ba'i rten byed pa'o/ / blo gros ni shes rab ste/ zag bcas zag med la sogs pa'i chos rnam rab tu rnam par 'byed pa ste/ dbye na skyes thob dang thos pa dang bsams pa dang bsgoms pa las byung ba'i shes rab bzhi'am/{ yang na sa'i dngos gzhi las 'byung ba'i phyin ci log bzhi dang bral ba'i dge ba'i zag bcas zag med dang*/ de las bzlog pa dang*/ lung ma bstan gyi shes rab kyis chos la nye bar sems pa rnams ni rim pa ltar} rigs pas bskyed pa dang*/ rigs pa ma yin pas bskyed pa dang*/ de gnyis las gzhan pa gsum mo/ / byed las ni som nyi zlog pa'i las can no/ /

Aspiration (chanda) is the desire to act that focuses on the six objects and seeks its focal object. If it is classified, there are three: (1) the aspiration to maintain contact with past states, (2) the aspiration not to be separated from present states, and (3) the aspiration seeking future states. It functions to instigate effort. Contact (sparśa) is the thorough analysis of the emerging object due to the convergence of three things: the object, sense faculty, and consciousness. If classified, there is the sixfold collection of contact. It functions as the support of feeling. Intelligence (mati) is wisdom that fully differentiates [or discerns] phenomena as contaminated or uncontaminated and so on. If classified, there are four: (1) wisdom obtained at birth and that derived from (2) hearing, (3) contemplation, and (4) meditation. [120] {Again, those that occur in the Yogācāra Levels are (1) wisdom closely contemplating phenomena that are contaminated virtuous states or uncontaminated states, (2) the opposite of those, and (3) neutral states that are free of the four wrong engagements.[504] These are, respectively, the wisdom of} states that are appropriately produced, states that are inappropriately produced, and states that are neither. Its function is to stop indecision.

'o na som nyi dang ldan pa'i sems la shes rab yod na som nyi med par 'gyur la/ med na de sems kyi sa mang po par mi 'gyur ro zhe na/ som nyi dang ldan pa'i sems la'ang shes rab cung zad yod mod kyi de shas chung la/ som nyi shas che ba'i phyir de med par yang mi 'gyur te ba tshwa can gyi rgya mtsho dang 'dres pa'i yan lag brgyad dang ldan pa'i chu bzhin no/ / de bzhin du khro ba dang ldan pa'i sems la 'dun pa dang*/ rnam g.yeng dang ldan pa la ting nge 'dzin dang*/ brjed ngas dang ldan pa la dran pa dang*/ ma dad pa la mos pa yod dam med ces bya ba la sogs pa'i dpyad pa'ang shes par bya'o/ / sde pa gzhan gyis ni de lta bu'i nyes pa yod pa'i phyir 'dun pa la sogs pa lnga ni yul so sor nges pa yin gyi kun du 'gro ba ni ma yin no zhes bzhed do/ / dran pa ni dmigs pa mi brjed pa ste/ dbye na nyon mongs pa can dang de ma yin pa gnyis so/ / las na dmigs pa la sems mi g.yeng bar byed pa'o/ /

Question: If wisdom exists in minds possessing indecision, there would be no indecision. If wisdom doesn’t exist in all minds, it would not be a universal mental state. Reply: Minds possessing indecision have some wisdom that is subordinate and weak when indecision is dominant. But wisdom is not nonexistent, for it is like [pure] water possessing the eight qualities that is mixed with brine. So too, minds possessing wrath have aspiration, those possessing distraction have concentration, those possessing forgetfulness have mindfulness, and those possessing faithlessness have resolute belief and so on. This will be understood through analysis. Other schools assert that the five such as aspiration and so on are object-determining mental factors but are not omnipresent mental factors because they possess faults such as these. Mindfulness (smṛti) is not forgetting the focal object. If classified, there is afflicted and unafflicted mindfulness. Its function is to prevent the mind being distracted from its object.

yid la byed pa ni sems yul la gtod pa'i sems kyi 'jug pa ste/ dbye na tshul bzhin du yid la byed pa dang*/ tshul bzhin ma yin par yid la byed pa gnyis so/ / las ni mdo las/ yid la byed pa thob pa ni ting nge 'dzin thob pa'o/ / zhes 'byung bas dmigs pa la sems 'dzin par byed do/ / mos pa ni 'dod pa'am dmigs pa la yon tan can du 'dzin pa ste/ dbye na yang dag par mos pa dang*/ log par mos pa gnyis so/ / las ni slob dpon blo gros brtan pas mos pa gces su byed pa ni phas kyi rgol ba rnams kyis rang gi grub pa'i mtha' las 'phrog par mi nus so zhes bshad pas dmigs pa las mi 'phrogs par byed pa'o/ / ting nge 'dzin ni dmigs pa gcig la rnam pa gcig tu 'jug pa'i rtse gcig pa ste/ 'dir rtse ni dmigs pa'o/ / dbye na sa dgu na ting nge 'dzin dgu dang*/ 'jig rten las 'das te sa bcu'o/ / las ni sems mnyam par bzhag na yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du shes pa 'byung bas ji lta bar shes pa'i rten byed pa'o/ / bcu po de dag ni sems thams cad la 'byung ba'i phyir sems kyi sa mang po pa zhes bya'o/ / gal te sems thams cad la de dag 'byung na 'dun pa dang mos pa dang dran pa dang*/ ting nge 'dzin dang shes rab bskyed pa'i phyir brtul zhugs can rnams brtson pa don med par 'gyur ro zhe na/ ma yin te/ de dag khyad par can bskyed pa'i phyir ro zhes bye brag tu smra ba 'dod do/ /

Attention (manaskāra) engages the mind and directs it to its object. If it is classified, there are two: appropriate attention and inappropriate attention. A sūtra explains: The obtainment of attention is the obtainment of concentration.[505] Therefore its function is to hold the mind to its focal object. Resolution (adhimokśa) holds its desired object or focal object to possess good qualities. If it is classified, there are two: (1) correct resolution and (2) incorrect resolution. Master Sthiramati writes: Through cherishing your resolute beliefs, your opponents cannot deprive you of your philosophical tenet.[506] Therefore its function is to prevent the loss of one’s focal object. Concentration (samādhi) is the single-pointed state that engages a single aspect of a single focal object, and that “point” is what is observed. If classified, there are ten: (1–9) the nine concentrations of the nine levels and (10) transcendent [concentration]. Its function is to support the knowledge of phenomena just as they are, since the perfect knowledge of phenomena just as they are arises when the mind is in equipoise. These ten are called “universal mental states” because they occur in all minds. Objection: If they arise in all minds, it would be meaningless for those engaged in ascetic practices to make effort to generate them because aspiration, resolution, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom would already be produced. Vaibhāṣikas assert that is not so because they generate superior instances of these mental factors.

gal te sems gcig la de lta bu'i tha dad pa bcu ni ma dmigs so zhe na/ 'di dag gi khyad par ni yid ches pa'i lung las shes par bya ba yin gyi phra bas rtogs par dka' ba'i phyir dbang po'i yul ni ma yin te/ gang dag dbang po'i yul du gyur pa sbyar ba'i sman la sogs pa gzugs can rnams la'ang tha dad pa'i khyad par gzung bar mi nus na sems dang sems las byung ba rnams la lta ci smos/ de nyid kyi phyir 'grel pa las/ sems dang sems las byung ba rnams kyi bye brag ni phra bas de ni re zhig rgyun rnams la yang yongs su bcad par dka' na skad cig ma dag la lta smos kyang ci dgos/ re zhig sman la sogs pa gzugs can rnams la yang ro mang po kha cig gi ro'i khyad par dbang pos gzung bar bya ba rnams nges par gzung bar dka' na chos gang dag gzugs can ma yin zhing blos gzung bar bya ba rnams lta smos kyang ci dgos zhes bshad do/ / gal te khyad par ma mthong ba tsam gyis tha dad med par rtog na kun du 'gro ba lngar smra ba rnams la'ang mtshungs pa'i phyir ro/ / lung las ji skad du bshad ce na/ dran pa nyer gzhag gi mdo las/ 'di ltar sa chen po'i chos bcu ni tshor ba dang 'du shes dang sems pa dang reg pa dang yid la byed pa dang 'dun pa dang mos pa dang dran pa dang ting nge 'dzin dang shes rab ste de ltar dmigs pa gcig la mtshan nyid gzhan du 'dod do/ / rnam par shes pa la sogs pa chos bcu gcig po de dag kyang ji ltar nyi ma'i 'od zer gcig tu 'du yang 'on kyang ngo bo nyid gzhan yin pa de bzhin du rnam par shes pa'i ngo bo nyid gzhan pa nas sems pa'i bar du gzhan no zhes sa mang po pa bcu yin pa dang*/ sems sems byung de dag rdzas tha dad yin par yang bshad pa'i phyir ro/ /

Objection: But ten such distinct mental factors are not observed in a single mind. Reply: Their difference is difficult to comprehend because they are subtle [121] and therefore they should be understood from scripture that inspires conviction. Also they are not objects of the sense faculties, and if one cannot apprehend distinct physical states that are sensory objects such as ointment applied [to the eyes], what need is there to mention the inability to comprehend minds and mental factors? Therefore the Autocommentary states: If it is difficult to ascertain the streams of specific minds and mental factors since they are subtle, what need is there to mention momentary instances? Also, if it is difficult for the tongue sense power to definitely apprehend specific tastes in the mouth from among the many tastes of a physical substance such as medicine, what need is there to mention nonphysical phenomena apprehended by consciousness?[507] Question: If distinct entities were considered nondistinct due to seeing no difference between them, then this would also apply to those who advocate five omnipresent mental factors. What does scripture state? Reply: The Foundations of Mindfulness Sūtra declares: The ten universal phenomena — (1) feeling, (2) discernment, (3) intention, (4) contact, (5) attention, (6) aspiration, (7) resolution, (8) mindfulness, (9) concentration, and (10) wisdom — possess the same focal object but separate characteristics. Just as the eleven phenomena of consciousness and so on are subsumed as one but have different natures, like the rays of the sun, so too the nature of consciousness is distinct from them and they are distinct, up to intention.[508] This explains that universal mental states are ten in number, and that minds and mental factors are distinct in substance.
dge ba'i sa mang po pa bshad pa/
VIRTUOUS MENTAL STATES
dad dang bag yod shin tu sbyangs/ / btang snyoms ngo tsha shes khrel yod/ / rtsa ba gnyis rnam mi 'tshe dang / / brtson 'grus rtag tu dge la 'byung / / 25
Faith, diligence, pliancy, equanimity, shame, embarrassment, the two roots, nonviolence, and effort always occur in virtuous minds. (2:25)

gnyis pa dge ba'i sa mang po pa bshad pa'i dad pa ni sems nyon mongs pa dang nye ba'i nyon mongs pa'i rnyog pa dang bral bar byed pa'i dang ba ste/ dbye na las 'bras la yid ches pa dang*/ dkon mchog gsum gyi yon tan la dang ba dang*/ bden bzhi la spang zhing bsgrub par 'dod pa'o/ / las ni 'dun pa bskyed par byed pa'o/ / bag yod pa ni dad pa la sogs pa'i dge ba'i chos rnams la gces spras su byed cing sgom pa{ 'am zag pa dang zag pa'i gnas las sems bsrung} ste/ dbye na bsod nams dang thar pa dang nges 'byed cha mthun dang zag med kyi dge ba sgom pa'i bag yod pa bzhi'o/ / las ni 'jig rten dang de las 'das pa'i phun sum tshogs pa thams cad rdzogs par byed pa'o/ / shin tu sbyangs pa ni sems dmigs pa la gtad bzod pa'i las su rung ba ste/ dbye na lus shin tu sbyangs pa sgo lnga'i rnam shes kyi 'khor du byung ba dang*/ sems shin tu sbyangs pa yid shes kyi 'khor du byung ba gnyis so/ / yang na lus shin tu sbyangs pa lus shing bal ltar yangs ba dang rked pa gser gyi dong tshe brtsegs pa ltar mnyam pa la sogs pa lus nyid las su rung ba yin pa'i phyir sems las byung ba ni ma yin no/ / 'grel pa las kyang*/ lus shin tu sbyangs pa des sems las su rung ba byang chub kyi yan lag 'dren par byed pas de dang mthun pa'i phyir de la'ang byang chub kyi yan lag tu btags nas brjod de/ dper na mdo las/ dga' ba dang dga' ba'i gnas lta bu'i chos rnams dga' ba yang dag byang chub kyi yan lag tu gsungs pa dang*/ khong khro ba dang khong khro ba'i rgyu mtshan gnod sems kyi sgrib par gsungs pa dang*/ yang dag pa'i rtog pa dang rtsol ba shes rab kyi rang bzhin ma yin yang de dag mthun pas shes rab kyi phung por brjod pa bzhin no zhes bshad do/ / las ni nyon mongs pa la sogs pa'i sgrib pa thams cad sel bar byed pa'o/ / {'du byed } btang snyoms ni sems bying rgod dang bral ba'i rnal du 'dug pa ste/ / dbye na thog mar res 'ga' bying rgod 'byung ba'i mnyam pa nyid dang*/ bar du dogs pa yod kyang mi 'byung ba'i rnal du gnas pa dang*/ tha mar dogs pa'ang med pa'i lhun gyis grub pa gsum mo/ / las ni zag pa rnams kyi skabs mi 'byed pa'o/ / ngo tsha shes pa dang khrel yod pa ni 'chad par 'gyur la/ de dag gi las ni nyes spyod sdom pa'o/ /

Faith (śraddhā) is the clarity of mind freed from the agitation of the afflictions and branch afflictions. If classified, there are three: (1) conviction in karmic causation, (2) clear confidence in the qualities of the Three Jewels, and (3) the desire to abandon the first two and establish the last two of the four truths. Its function is to generate aspiration. Diligence (apramāda) esteems and meditates on virtuous phenomena such as faith and so on {or guards the mind from contaminants and contaminated abodes}. If classified, there are four: diligence meditating on factors conducive to (1) merit, (2) liberation, (3) penetrative insight, and (4) uncontaminated virtue. Its function is to accomplish all mundane and transcendent qualities. Pliancy (praśrabdhi) is the flexibility of the mind patiently directed to its focal object. If classified, there are two: (1) the physical pliancy occurring in the retinue of the five doors of sense consciousness, and (2) the mental pliancy occurring in the retinue of mental consciousness. Again, physical pliancy is light like wool, balanced like the core of a stack of gold coins, and so on. It is the flexibility of body and not a mental factor. [122] Also the Autocommentary states that physical pliancy leads to the mental flexibility that is a requisite of enlightenment. Therefore it is imputed to be a requisite of enlightenment because it assists enlightenment. For example, a sūtra declares: Phenomena such as joy and states of joy are called joy, which is a requisite of enlightenment.[509] And: Anger and the cause of anger are called the obscuration of harmful intent. Right investigation and right exertion are not in essence wisdom, but they are called the aggregate of wisdom since they assist it.[510] Its function is to eliminate all obscuration such as confusion and so on. {Applied} equanimity (upekṣā) is abiding in rest, free from mental laxity (saṃsīdan) or excitation (auddhatya). If classified, there are three: (1) the evenness occurring with intermittent laxity and excitation, (2) abiding at rest, which does not occur when hesitancy exists, and (3) spontaneous equanimity, which is free of doubt. Its function is to not grant opportunity to contaminated states. Shame (hrī) and embarrassment (apatrāpya) have been explained. Their function is to restrain one from negative action.

rtsa ba gnyis ni 'dod chags med pa dang zhe sdang med pa ste/ gti mug med pa ni shes rab kyi cha la btags pa'i phyir 'dir ma brjod do/ / 'dir ma chags pa dang 'dod chags med pa zhes pa'i ma dang med ces pa ni med pa dang*/ gzhan pa dang*/ gnyen po gsum la 'jug pa las 'dir ni chags pa'i gnyen po la 'jug gi med pa dang gzhan pa la ni mi 'jug go /de bzhin du zhe sdang med pa dang gti mug med pa la'ang brjod par bya'o zhes bye bshad las bshad do/ / de dag gi las ni srog gcod pa la sogs pa nyes spyod la mi 'jug par byed pa'o/ / rnam par mi 'tshe ba ni snying brtse ba ste/ dbye na sems can la dmigs pa dang*/ chos la dmigs pa dang*/ dmigs pa med pa'o/ / sems can la dbyug pa la sogs pas tho mi 'tsham pa'i las can no/ / brtson 'grus ni dge ba'i bya ba la sems mngon par spro ba ste/ mi dge ba'i bya ba la sems mngon par spro ba ni brtson 'grus ma yin gyi bya ba ngan zhen gyi le lo yin te/ mdo las/ 'di las phyi rol pa rnams kyi brtson 'grus gang yin pa de ni le lo kho na yin no/ / zhes gsungs pas brtson 'grus dman pa la dgag pa'i sgrar brjod do/ / dbye ba {theg pa chen po'i mdo sde'i rgyan las/ thog mar go cha'i brtson 'grus de nas ni/ / tshul bzhin rab zhugs sbyor ba'i brtson 'grus te/ / ma zhum mi 'gong chog mi shes brtson 'grus/ / zhes pa lnga'am/ kun las btus las ni go cha dang*/ sbyor ba dang*/ mi 'gong ba dang*/ mi ldog pa dang*/ chog par mi 'dzin pa la sems mngon par spro ba ste zhes pa lnga dang*/ yang na } ni go cha dang sbyor ba dang*/ phyir mi ldog pa'i brtson 'grus gsum mo/ / las ni dge ba thams cad rdzogs par byed pa'o/ / bcu po 'di dag ni rtag tu dge ba'i sems thams cad la 'byung ba'i phyir dge ba'i sa mang po pa dag ces bya'o/ /

The two roots (mūladvaya) are nonattachment and nonaversion. Nondelusion is imputed to be a component of wisdom, but it is not expressed here. The Vibhāṣā states: The “non-” of nonaversion and nonattachment refers to three things: “nonexistence,” “other,” and “antidote.” Here it means the antidote of attachment and does not mean “nonexistence” or “other.” Nonaversion and nondelusion are also explained in this way.[511] Their function is to prevent engagement in negative actions such as taking life. Nonviolence (avihiṃsā) is compassion. If classified, there are three: nonviolence regarding (1) sentient beings, (2) phenomena, and (3) the unobserved. It functions to prevent contempt for sentient beings, which can manifest as beating them with sticks and so on. Effort (vīrya) is the mind that takes delight in virtuous action. The mind taking delight in nonvirtuous action is not effort but laziness attracted to evil action. A sūtra declares: Any effort of the tīrthikas that is other than that is laziness alone.[512] This sūtra states that one should avoid inferior types of effort. If classified, {the Ornament of the Mahāyāna Sūtras explains there are five: First, armored effort, then there is proper, well-engaged, prepared effort, undefeated effort, undaunted effort, and discontented effort.[513] or the Compendium of Abhidharma explains there are five: Armored, applied, undaunted, irreversible, and insatiable effort, which delight the mind.[514] Again} [123] there are three: (1) armored effort, (2) applied effort, and (3) irreversible effort. Its function is to bring all virtuous action to completion. These ten are called “virtuous mental states” because they always occur in all virtuous minds.

gal te dad pa ni dga' ba'i rnam pa can yin pa'i phyir dang*/ snying brtse ba ni yid gdung ba yin pa'i phyir sems gcig gi 'khor du de dag ji ltar 'byung bar 'gyur/ de bzhin du yid la byed pa rtsol bcas dang btang snyoms rtsol med dang*/ 'dod khams pa rnams ni rnam par g.yeng ba dang bcas pa'i phyir shin tu sbyangs pa 'byung bar ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/ de dag shas che chung ma gtogs pa cha shas kyis thams cad la 'byung bar 'dod do zhes sngar bshad zin to/ / sde pa gzhan gyis ni 'di dag ngo bo nyid kyis dge ba yin gyi dge ba'i sems thams cad la ni 'di dag gis khyab pa ma yin no zhes bya bar bzhed pa nyid rigs pa yin no/ /

Question: Because faith possesses the aspect of joy, and altruism is mental yearning, how do they occur in the retinue of one mind? Similarly, how do attention that possesses exertion and equanimity that lacks exertion occur in the retinue of a single mind? And how does pliancy occur in desire-realm beings who possess distraction? Reply: It was explained earlier that though some are dominant and some subordinate, they occur in all minds to some extent. Other schools assert that virtuous mental states are virtuous by nature, but it is not that they necessarily pervade every virtuous mind. This assertion is logical.
nyon mongs pa'i sa mang po pa bshad pa/
AFFLICTED MENTAL STATES
rmongs dang bag med le lo dang / / ma dad pa dang rmugs dang rgod/ / nyon mongs can la rtag tu 'byung / / mi dge la ni khrel med dang / / 26
Confusion, negligence, laziness, faithlessness, lethargy, and excitation always occur in all afflicted minds. Nonembarrassment and shamelessness pervade all nonvirtuous minds. (2:26)

gsum pa nyon mongs pa'i sa mang po pa'i rmongs pa ni las 'bras dang bden pa dang dkon mchog la sogs pa mi shes shing mi gsal ba ste rmongs pa dang ma rig pa dang gti mug ces bya ba ni rnam grangs te/ las ni rtsa ba dang nye ba'i nyon mongs pa thams cad kyi rten byed pa'o/ / bag med pa ni bag yod pa'i mi mthun phyogs dge ba mi sgom zhing zag bcas las sems mi bsrung ba ste/ las ni nyes spyod kyi rten byed pa'am/ mi dge ba 'phel ba dang dge ba 'grib par byed pa'o/ / le lo ni brtson 'grus kyi mi mthun phyogs dge ba la sems mngon par mi spro ba ste/ las ni dge ba la sbyor ba'i bar du gcod pa nyid do/ / ma dad pa ni dad pa'i mi mthun phyogs sems ma dang ba ste/{ dbye na bya bar ngan zhen dang*/ sgyed lug pa dang*/ snyom las 'dzin pa'i le lo ste gsum mo/} las ni le lo'i rten byed pa'o/ / rmugs pa ni lus sems lci zhing dmigs pa mi gsal ba'i blong blong po ste lus sems las su mi rung ba'o/ / dbye na{ sgo lnga'i rnam shes dang yid shes kyi 'khor du 'byung ba} lus sems kyi rmugs pa gnyis so/ / de la lus kyi rmugs pa ni sgo lnga'i rnam shes kyi 'khor du 'byung ba'o/ / las ni nyon mongs pa dang nye ba'i nyon mongs thams cad kyi grogs byed pa'o/ / rgod pa ni sems ma zhi bar dmigs pa las gzhan du 'phro ba ste/ las ni zhi gnas kyi bar du gcod pa nyid do/ / drug po de dag ni nyon mongs pa can gyi sems thams cad la rtag tu 'byung ba'i phyir nyon mongs pa'i sa mang po pa yin no/ / gal te rgod pa ni dmigs pa la gsal bar 'jug la/ rmongs pa dang rmugs pa dag ni mi gsal bar 'jug pa'i phyir sems gcig la de dag ji ltar 'byung zhe na/ 'di yang snga ma bzhin du shes par bya'o/ / 'o na mngon pa'i bstan bcos las rmugs pa mi 'byung la/ brjed ngas dang*/ rnam par g.yeng ba dang*/ shes bzhin ma yin pa dang*/ tshul bzhin ma yin pa yid la byed pa dang*/ log par mos pa dang*/ rmongs pa la sogs pa lnga ste bcu 'byung ba'i snga ma lnga 'dir mi 'chad pa ci ste zhe na/ bye brag tu smra ba rmugs pa ni ting nge 'dzin dang rjes su mthun pa'i phyir mngon pa las ma smros la/ brjed ngas la sogs pa ni dran pa la sogs pa la btags pa yin pa'i phyir 'dir ma smos so zhes so zhes bya bar 'dod la/ slob dpon ni rmugs pa'ang rgod pa dang 'dra bar ting nge 'dzin dang mi mthun pas 'dir smos so zhes bzhed do/

Confusion (moha) neither knows nor clarifies karmic causation, the four truths, the Three Jewels, and so on; and confusion, ignorance (avidyā), and delusion (mūḍha) are synonymous. Its function is to support all root and branch afflictions. Negligence (pramāda) is the opposite of diligence (apramāda). It does not meditate on virtue and does not guard the mind from contaminants. Its function is to support negative action, increase nonvirtue, and decrease virtue. Laziness (kauśidhya) is the opposite of effort, and does not take delight in [nor inspire] the mind to virtue. Its function is to interrupt preparation for virtue. {If classified, there are three: the laziness of (1) longing for evil states, (2) slothfulness, and (3) idleness}. Faithlessness (āśraddhya) is the opposite of faith and is unclarity of mind. Its function is to support laziness. Lethargy (styāna) is the heaviness of body and mind and the mental and physical inflexibility that is a dull obscured state lacking clarity to its focal object. If classified, there are two: lethargy of body and lethargy of mind {occurring as the retinue of consciousness of the five sense doors and mental consciousness}. Lethargy of body occurs in the retinue of the five sense consciousnesses. Its function is to assist all root and branch afflictions. Excitation (uddhāti) does not pacify the mind and moves the mind from one focal object to another. Its function is to interrupt calm abiding. These six are afflicted mental states because they always occur in all afflicted (kliṣṭa) minds. Question: If excitation clearly engages its focal object, but confusion and lethargy do not clearly engage their focal objects, then how do they occur in the retinue of a single mind? Reply: They should be understood in the same way as the former [instances]. Question: Lethargy does not occur in the Abhidharma treatise,[515] but ten mental factors do: (1) forgetfulness, [124] (2) distraction, (3) nonintrospection, (4) inappropriate attention, (5) wrong resolution, and (6–10) the five such as confusion. Why are the former five not explained here? Vaibhāṣikas assert that because lethargy conforms with concentration, it is not mentioned in the Abhidharma treatise, and because forgetfulness and so on are designated relative to mindfulness and so forth, they are not mentioned here.[516] Vasubandhu asserts that since lethargy is like excitation and does not conform with concentration, it is mentioned in this [text].[517]

{ grangs mang po pa yin pa de dag nyon mongs pa'i sa mang po pa yang yin nam zhe na mu bzhi ste/ dang po ni kun 'gro lnga'o/ / gnyis pa ni ma dad pa la sogs pa lnga'o/ / gsum pa ni dran pa nyon mongs can la sogs pa yul nges lnga'i zlog phyogs so/ / bzhi pa ni de dag las gzhan no/ /}

It is stated that it should be known that both nonembarrassment (anatrapā) and shamelessness (ahrīkya) pervade all nonvirtuous minds. These have been explained already. Their function is to assist all afflictions and branch afflictions.

spang bya sgom spang kho na dang*/ sgom spang gi yid kyi rnam shes kho na dang mtshungs par ldan{ pa'i yid kyi sa pa yin} pa'i phyir ro/ /

Wrath (krodha) is the deep disturbance of the mind manifesting with respect to sentient beings who harm oneself and so on. It functions to provoke contempt. Resentment (upanāha) continuously maintains [a negative attitude] to that [object] after wrath has arisen. Its function is to support impatience. Guile (śāṭhya) is a crooked mind {that casts aside advice} and does not accept as faults {the faults one has committed}. It functions to interrupt the attainment of proper instruction. Envy (īrṣyā) cannot endure the excellent qualities of others. It acts to support the dissatisfied mind. Spite (pradāsa) craves immorality [or misdeeds]. Treatise on the Five Aggregates notes: What is spite? It is disturbing the mind with abrasive words.[519] Therefore it is logical to explain it to be disturbing another’s mind with abrasive words through a wrathful mind and that it is associated with aversion. Its function is to generate negative action, prevent attainment of happiness, and to increase demerit. Therefore Master Sthiramati explains: It is difficult to associate with a person who possesses it.[520] Concealment (mrakṣa) is hiding and keeping your faults secret. It functions to support regret when faults are concealed, regret through the arising of mental dissatisfaction, and not attaining happiness. Avarice (matsara) is withholding Dharma, worldly things, and the attributes of knowledge {through avarice for such qualities} and, out of attachment, not giving them to others. Its function is to prevent any decrease in one’s possessions. Deceit (māyā) is acting as if you possessed qualities you don’t possess [125] through attachment to property, respect, and so on. Its function is to support wrong livelihood. Arrogance (mada) is haughtiness. Its function is to support all afflictions and branch afflictions. Violence (vihiṃsa) is the desire that sentient beings suffer. Its function is to injure [others]. These ten are specific-afflicted mental states (parīttakleśabhūmika) because they are concomitant with ignorance alone {as their companion, since they are autonomous and not concomitant with other} root afflictions. They are objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation alone {since they do not wrongly comprehend the four truths}. And because {they exist on the level of the mental faculty}, they are concomitant with mental consciousness alone, which is an object to be abandoned by the path of meditation.

Indeterminate mental factors

'o na slob dpon gang spel dang dbyig bshes kyi TI ka las/ rtog dang dpyod dang 'gyod pa dang*/ / gnyid dang khong khro chags rnams dang*/ / nga rgyal the tshom zhes bya ba/ / brgyad ni nges pa min par bshad/ / ces gsungs pa dag kyang sems las byung ba'i dbye bar ci'i phyir ma bshad ce na/ nges pa rnams dngos su bshad pa nyid kyis de dag ma nges par shugs la go ba'i phyir ma bshad do/ /

Question: The commentaries of both Masters Pūrṇavardhana and Vasumitra declare: Investigation, analysis, regret, sleep, anger, attachment, pride, and doubt. Those eight are explained to be indeterminate.[521] Why are they not explained in the classification of mental factors? Reply: They are not explained there because indeterminate mental factors are implicitly understood through explicitly explaining determinate mental factors.

ji ltar ma nges she na/ re zhig{ sde tshan dang po bzhi ni ma nges te/ rim pa ltar ro/ /}sa mang po pa ni ma yin te/ sems thams cad kyi 'khor du mi 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / dge ba'i sa pa'ang ma yin te/ dge ba thams cad kyi 'khor du mi 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / nyon mongs pa'i sa pa'ang ma yin te/ nyon mongs can gyi sems thams cad kyi 'khor du 'byung bar ma nges pa'i phyir ro/ / mi dge ba'i sa pa'ang ma yin te/ mi dge ba thams cad kyi 'khor du 'byung bar ma nges pa'i phyir ro/ / nyon mongs pa chung ngu'i sa pa'ang ma yin te/{ nyon mongs chung ngu'i sa par mi 'jog pa'i rgyu mtshan/} rtog dpyod la gsum char dang*/ 'gyod pa la dang po dang*/ gnyid la dang po gnyis{ med de spang bya gnyis ka yin pas} dang*/ chags sdang la tha ma gnyis{ su ma nges pas} dang*/ nga rgyal{ spang bya gnyis ka} dang the tshom{ mthong spang yin pas de} la bar ma med pas ma rig pa tsam dang sgom spang tsam dang yid tsam dang mtshungs par ldan pa kho na ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de lta bu'i rgyu mtshan yang gang las she na/

Question: In what way are they indeterminate? Reply: {They are indeterminate with respect to the first four divisions since, respectively,} they are not universal mental states because they don’t occur in the retinue of all minds; they are not virtuous mental states because they don’t occur in the retinue of all virtuous minds; they are not afflicted mental states because they definitely do not occur in the retinue of all afflicted minds; and they are also not nonvirtuous mental states because they do not exist in the retinue of all nonvirtuous minds. Further, they are not specific-afflicted mental states {and the reason why they are not posited as specific-afflicted mental states is} because they are not solely (a) concomitant with ignorance alone, (b) objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation alone, or (c) concomitant with the mental faculty alone. That is because (1) investigation and (2) analysis are not those three; (3) regret is not the first; (4) sleep is not the first two {since it is abandoned by both}; (5) attachment and (6) aversion {are not certain to be} the final two; (7) pride is not the second {since it is abandoned by both}; and (8) doubt is not the second {since it is abandoned by seeing}. Question: What is the source of that reasoning?

Twenty-two mental factors occur in all virtuous minds in the desire realm, including investigation and analysis. Regret is added to some. (2:28)
gsum pa sems gang gi 'khor du sems byung du 'byung ba bstan pa ni
WHICH MENTAL FACTORS OCCUR IN THE RETINUE OF WHICH MINDS

'dod pa'i khams na{ dge ba dang mi dge 'dres ma 'dres gnyis dang*/ lung ma bstan bsgribs ma bsgribs gnyis te sems lnga yod pa las} dge ba'i sems thams cad la ni sems las byung ba nyi shu rtsa gnyis 'byung ngo zhes sbyar ro/ / ci ste na/ sde tshan dang po gnyis dang*/ rtog pa dang dpyod pa gnyis dang bcas pa'i phyir dang*/ dge ba'i sems yin par sde tshan phyi ma gsum dang*/ ma nges pa'i khong khro dang chags pa dang nga rgyal dang the tshom rnams mi 'byung la/ gnyid dang 'gyod pa res 'ga' 'byung yang ma nges pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du 'og ma rnams su'ang ci rigs par gtan tshigs shes par bya'o/ / 'dod pa'i dge ba'i sems thams cad la 'gyod pa mi 'byung bas gang la 'gyod pa dge ba yod pa'i sems la la dag tu ni 'gyod pa bsnan pas de dang nyi shu rtsa gsum du rig par bya ste/ dge ba ma byas pa dang mi dge ba byas pa la 'gyod pa ni dge ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'gyod pa ni ngan par byas pa la dmigs pa'i yid la gcags pa yin la/ dge ba la 'gyod pa la'ang ngan par blo la snang ba dang*/ ma byas pa la 'gyod pa'ang bya bar 'os pa ma byas pa la ngan par byas pa'i ming gis brjod pa'i phyir ma khyab pa ma yin na zhes 'chad mod kyi dmigs pa la gnod pa'i yid la gcags pa yin par rigs so/ / las ni sems gnas pa'i bar du gcod par byed pa'o/ /

{From among the five types of mind — (1) virtuous, (2) mixed nonvirtuous, (3) unmixed nonvirtuous, (4) neutral-obscured, and (5) neutral-unobscured} — there are twenty-two mental factors that occur in all virtuous minds in the desire realm. Question: What are they? Reply: They are (1–20) the first two divisions, including both (21) investigation (vitarka) and (22) analysis (vicāra). Neither those of the latter three divisions nor the indeterminate mental states of anger, attachment, pride, and doubt occur in [the retinue of] virtuous minds. Sleep (middha) and regret (kaukṛtya) sometimes [126] occur, but their occurrence is not definite. Similarly, those explained below should be understood through appropriate proofs. Regret does not occur in the retinue of all virtuous desire-realm minds. But since regret is added to some minds, specifically, those that have virtuous regret, there are twenty-three mental factors in the retinue of virtuous minds because regret for virtue not committed or nonvirtue committed is virtuous. Regret is remorse focused on negative actions one has committed, but because even regret for virtue manifests negatively in one’s mind and regret for [a nonvirtuous act] not committed is [equivalent to] not committing a worthy action, [such deeds] are described as “committing negative actions.” Indeed this is said to apply in all cases, and it is appropriate to have remorse for [generating the mind intent on] harming [other beings as] its focal object. Its function is to interrupt the placement of mind.
la la dag tu 'gyod pa bsnan/ / mi dge ba ni ma 'dres dang / / lta dang ldan la'ang nyi shu 'byung / / nyon mongs bzhi dang khro sogs dang / / 29

Nonvirtuous unmixed minds occur with twenty mental factors since they are also concomitant with view. Minds concomitant with the four afflictions, or wrath and so on, or regret occur with twenty-one mental factors. (2:29)

de la 'dir 'dod pa na spyir sems dge mi dge lung ma bstan gsum yod cing*/ mi dge ba'i sems la'ang ma 'dres pa ma rig pa tsam dang mtshungs par ldan pa dang*/ 'dres pa nyon mongs pa gzhan dang yang mtshungs par ldan pa gnyis dang*/ lung ma bstan la'ang bsgribs pa dang*/ ma bsgribs pa gnyis yod pas lngar 'gyur ba las de la re zhig / mi dge ba'i sems la ni{ rtsa nyon gzhan dag nyon mong can yin pas} ma 'dres pa ma rig pa tsam dang mtshungs par ldan pa{ la'ang nyi shu 'byung la} dang{ gi sgras 'dres pa la'ang nyi shu 'byung ba yod de de yang} 'jig tshogs dang mthar 'dzin las gzhan pa log lta la sogs pa lta{ phyi ma} ba/ gsum dang mtshungs par ldan pa{ 'dres pa} la'ang sems las byung ba nyi shu 'byung ste/ {sems sems byung yin pas/ } sa mang po pa bcu dang*/ {nyon mongs can yin pas } nyon mongs pa'i sa pa drug dang*/ {mi dge ba yin pas } mi dge ba gnyis dang*/ {'dod sems yin pas/ } rtog dpyod gnyis dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i phyir dang*/ ma rig pa rang nyid ni{ dngos su mi smos pa} nyon mongs pa'i sar bgrangs shing*/ lta ba{ mi smos pa} ni shes rab kyis bsdus pas rdzas gzhan du med la/ dge ba'i sa pa rnams mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dir 'dres pa ni rtsa nyon gzhan dang yang mtshungs par ldan pa yin la/ ma 'dres pa ni rtsa nyon ma rig pa kho na dang mtshungs par ldan pa yin te/ 'grel pa las/ ma 'dres pa zhes bya ba ni sems gang la ma rig pa 'ba' zhig yod kyi 'dod chags la sogs pa nyon mongs pa gzhan med pa'o zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/{ lta ba dang po gnyis dang mtshungs ldan ni 'dir mi gzung ste/ mi dge ba ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /} sems mi dge ba lta ba dang ldan pa ni 'jig tshogs dang mthar 'dzin las gzhan pa'i lta ba gsum dang mtshungs par ldan pa yin te/ de gnyis ni bsgribs la lung ma bstan yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

In general there are three minds in the desire realm: (1) virtuous, (2) nonvirtuous, and (3) neutral. Nonvirtuous minds are of two types: unmixed minds concomitant with ignorance alone, and mixed minds concomitant with other afflictions. Neutral minds also are of two types: obscured and unobscured. From among those five minds, nonvirtuous minds unmixed (āveṇika) {with other root afflictions that are afflicted} but concomitant with ignorance alone occur with twenty mental factors, since they are also concomitant {and mixed} with the three {latter} views (dṛṣṭi) such as wrong view but not with the afflicted view of the self and extreme view. {Since they are minds associated with mental factors,} they are concomitant with (1–10) the ten universal mental states, and {since they are afflicted,} they are (11–16) the six afflicted mental states. {Since they are nonvirtuous,} they are concomitant with (17–18) the two nonvirtuous mental factors. {Since they are desire-realm minds,} they are concomitant with (19) investigation and (20) analysis. Ignorance itself, {though it is not explicitly stated,} is counted as an afflicted mental state. View {is not stated} since it is subsumed by wisdom, it is not a separate substance, and it is impossible it is a virtuous mental state. Here “mixed” means “concomitant with other root and branch afflictions,” and “unmixed” means “concomitant with the root affliction of ignorance alone,” because the Autocommentary affirms: “Unmixed” refers to any mind that possesses ignorance alone and does not possess other afflictions such as attachment.[522] {Minds that are concomitant with the first two views are not meant here because they are not nonvirtuous.} Nonvirtuous minds that possess view are concomitant with the three views other than the afflicted view of the self and extreme view because these two views are obscured-neutral states.

'dod chags dang khong khro dang nga rgyal dang the tshom ste rtsa ba'i nyon mongs pa bzhi{ po gang yang rung ba}dang khro ba la sogs pa nyon mongs pa chung ngu'i sa pa rnams{ gang yang rung ba} dang*/ 'gyod pa mi dge ba dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i sems la ni nyi shu rtsa gcig 'byung{ ba ni sngar gyi nyi shu'i steng du rang rang bsnan pa} ste/ sngar smos pa'i nyi shu dang*/ 'dod chags la sogs pa re re{ po rang nyid} bsnan pa'i phyir dang*/ 'dod chags dang mtshungs par ldan pa ni ma rig pa ma gtogs pa rtsa ba'i nyon mongs pa khong khro la sogs pa gzhan dang mtshungs par mi ldan pa'i phyir dang*/ khong khro dang mtshungs par ldan pa'ang ma rig pa ma gtogs pa rtsa ba'i nyon mongs pa 'dod chags la sogs pa gzhan dang mtshungs par mi ldan la/ khro ba la sogs pa'ang ma rig pa tsam dang mtshungs par ldan gyi rtsa nyon gzhan dang de dag nang yang phan tshun mtshungs par mi ldan pa'i phyir dang*/{ 'di dag ni chig skya thub pa'i nyon mongs yin pa'i phyir dang*/} ma rig pa ni nyon mongs pa'i sa par bgrangs zin pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las ni 'di dang mthun par 'dod chags dang khong khro dang nga rgyal dang the tshom rnams ni phan tshun mi mthun pa'i phyir phan tshun mtshungs par mi ldan te zhes ma rig pa ma gtogs pa phan tshun mtshungs par mi ldan par bshad la/ kun las btus las ni 'dod chags dang nga rgyal dang lta ba rnams kyang mtshungs par ldan zhing*/ khong khro dang the tshom yang phan tshun mtshungs par ldan par bshad mod kyi 'dir ni ma rig pa ma gtogs pa rtsa nyon rnams phan tshun mtshungs ldan du mi 'dod de/{ gal te de dag mtshungs par ldan na 'dod chags la sogs pa bzhi dang mtshungs ldan gyi sems la sems byung nyi shu rtsa gnyis 'byung bar thal ba las nyi shu rtsa gcig las 'byung bar bshad pas gnad do/}
'gyod pa dang ni nyi shu gcig / bsgribs la bco brgyad lung ma bstan/ / gzhan la bcu gnyis dag tu 'dod/ / gnyid ni kun la mi 'gal phyir/ / 30

Obscured minds occur with eighteen mental factors. Some assert that other neutral minds occur with twelve. Sleep is added to any mind possessing it because it is not contradictory that it occurs in all. (2:30)

'jig tshogs la lta ba dang mthar 'dzin par lta ba dang*/ mtshungs par ldan pa{ 'i sems gang yin de ni bsgribs la lung ma bstan yin pas/} bsgribs la lung ma bstan gyi sems la ni sems las byung ba bco brgyad 'byung ste/ sems kyi sa mang po pa bcu dang*/ nyon mongs pa'i sa pa drug dang*/ {ma nges pa'i sa pa'i/ } rtog dpyod gnyis dang bcas pa'i phyir ro/ / bsgribs la lung ma bstan las gzhan ma bsgribs lung ma bstan dang ldan pa'i sprul sems sogs bzhi la ni sems las byung ba bcu gnyis 'byung ba dag tu{ kha che ba} 'dod de/ sems kyi sa mang po pa rnams dang rtog dpyod gnyis dang bcas pa'i phyir ro/ / gnyid ni rgyu nyam chung ba dang ngal ba dang lus lci ba dang mun pa'i mtshan ma yid la byed pa dang kha zas la sogs pa la brten nas lus 'dzin mi nus par 'jug pa rang dbang med par dbang po la sems sdud pa ste/ bya ba shor ba'i rten byed pa'i las can no/ / de lta bu de ni kun slong dang mtshungs ldan gyi dbang gis dge mi dge lung ma bstan gsum ga srid pas dge mi dge'i sems dang bsgribs pa dang ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gyi sems kun la mi 'gal bar 'byung srid pa'i phyir sems gang la gnyid yod pa de dag la gnyid des bsnan te bgrang bar bya'o/ / de ltar na nyi shu dang ldan pa la ni nyi shu rtsa gcig la sogs pa 'byung ngo*/ /

{Since any mind} concomitant with the afflicted view of the self and extreme view {is an obscured-neutral state}, obscured (nivṛta)-neutral minds occur with eighteen mental factors: they have (1–10) the ten universal mental states, (11–16) six afflicted mental states, and (17–18) both investigation and analysis {of indeterminate level}. Some {Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas} assert that unobscured-neutral (avyakṛta) minds, which are other than obscured-neutral minds and possess the four minds of emanation and so on, occur with twelve mental factors: the ten universal mental states and both investigation and analysis. Sleep (middha) is the uncontrolled dissolution of the mind into the sense faculties and the inability to hold the body erect due to weakness, tiredness, heaviness of body, placing one’s attention on the mental image of darkness, eating food, and so on. It functions to support disengagement from action [or inaction]. Sleep is added to any mind possessing sleep because it is not contradictory that sleep can occur in all virtuous, nonvirtuous, and obscured and unobscured neutral minds, [128] since sleep can be virtuous, nonvirtuous, or neutral by the power of its concomitant motivation. Thus twenty-one mental factors and so on occur in minds that already possess twenty.

nyi 'og bye brag tu smra ba dang sde pa gzhan dag ni 'gyod pa'ang dge mi dge lung ma bstan gsum char du 'gyur ba srid pa'i phyir gnyid dang 'dra bar 'dod de/ de la 'gyod pa lung ma bstan ni byas pa'am ma byas pa la yid la gcags pa ste ngas ma zhu bar ci'i phyir zas zos zhes pa'am/ rtseg pa de la ci ste ri mo ma bris snyam pa yin la/ de dang mtshungs ldan gyi yid mi bde ba'ang yid bde dang 'dra bar lung ma bstan du 'dod do/ / de dag gi ltar na ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gyi sems 'gyod pa dang mtshungs par ldan pa la ni bcu gsum du 'gyur ro/ / kha che ba rnams ni yid mi bde ba dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i phyir dang*/ 'dod chags dang bral ba la yid mi bde med pa'i phyir 'gyod pa lung ma bstan ni med de/ yid mi bde ba ni dge ba dang mi dge bar nges{ par sngar bshad zin} pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir rnam smin ma yin no zhes kyang bshad zin to zhes zer te de'i rgyu mtshan yang dri bar bya'o/ / de lta bu ni 'dod khams kyi sems kyi dbang du byas pa yin no/ /

Aparāntaka Vaibhāṣikas and other schools assert that regret is like sleep because regret can have three aspects: virtuous, nonvirtuous, and neutral. Therefore neutral regret is keeping in mind actions committed or not committed, such as the thought “Why did I eat what I did not beg for?” or “Why did I not mark the wall?”[525] They assert that mental satisfaction and pain concomitant with such regret are similar in being neutral. According to them, an unobscured-neutral mind concomitant with regret has thirteen mental factors. Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas assert that there is no neutral regret because it is concomitant with mental dissatisfaction; that is, there is no mental dissatisfaction free of attachment, and mental dissatisfaction is determined to be either virtuous or nonvirtuous. It has already been explained that it is not karmic maturation. Reply: Such reasoning should be examined, for it assumes the mind of the desire realm.
khams gong ma dag gi bshad pa ni
THE EXPLANATION OF THOSE OF HIGHER REALMS
gang la yod pa de bsnan no/ / de las 'gyod gnyid mi dge rnams/ / bsam gtan dang po dag na med/ / rtog pa'ang bsam gtan khyad par can/ / 31 de yi gong na dpyod pa yang / /

From among those, regret, sleep, and nonvirtuous mental factors do not exist in the first absorption. Also investigation does not exist in special absorption. Also analysis does not exist above that. (2:31)

'dod khams kyi sems gang la sems las byung ba du zhig 'byung ba bshad pa des las 'gyod pa dang gnyid dang mi dge ba'i sems las byung ba ma nges pa'i khong khro dang mi dge ba'i ngo tsha med pa dang khrel med gnyis dang*/ g.yo sgyu dang rgyags pa gsum ma gtogs pa nyon mongs pa chung ngu'i sa pa bdun po rnams ni bsam gtan dang po dag na med de/ 'gyod pa ni yid mi bde dang mtshungs par ldan pa yin pa la de ni rgyud zhi gnas kyis brlan pas de na grogs yid mi bde med pa'i phyir dang*/ gnyid ni de las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i phyir dang sems mngon par sdud pa'i mtshan nyid can yin la/ gzugs khams pa dag ni sems bsdus pa na ting nge 'dzin kho nar 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/

From among those mental factors previously mentioned in the explanation of how many mental factors occur in any desire-realm mind, (1) regret, (2) sleep, and the nonvirtuous mental factors of (3) indeterminate anger, the two nonvirtuous mental factors of (4) shamelessness and (5) nonembarrassment, and (6–12) the seven specific-afflicted mental states except for guile, deceit, and arrogance do not exist in the first absorption (dhyāna). Master Pūrṇavardhana explains that regret is concomitant with mental dissatisfaction, and when the mindstream is moistened with calm abiding (śamatha), it does not possess mental dissatisfaction or associated regret. Because sleep is free of attachment and it possesses the characteristics of actually contracting the mind, it transforms into concentration alone when subsumed in the minds of form-realm beings.[526]

{ nyon mongs skyes kyang rnam smin sdug bsngal mi 'byin cing lus ngag gi nyes spyod mi slong bas khro sogs med do/ / des na de na dge ba la mang na sa mang bcu rtog dpyod gnyis te nyi shu rtsa gnyis dang*/ nyon mongs can ma 'dres pa la sa mang bcu nyon mongs kyi sa pa drug rtog dpyod gnyis te bco brgyad do/ / 'dres pa la lta ba dang ldan pa la'ang bco brgyad po de nyid de lta ba btags yod yin pas so/ / gzhan chags sogs dang ldan pa la de nyid dang bcu dgu'o/ / ma bsgribs pa'i sems gsum la sa mang bcu/ rtog dpyod gnyis dang bcu gnyis so/ / de na bzo'i sems med do/ / spyir khams gong na mi dge ba med pas sems bzhi yod de dge ba dang*/ nyon mongs can la 'dres ma 'dres gnyis dang*/ ma bsgribs lung ma bstan no/ / de la nyon mongs can thams cad ni bsgribs pa kho na yin te de mi dge bar mi 'gyur zhing zhi gnas kyis brlan pas so/}

{Though affliction arises, there is no wrath and so on in the first absorption because pain that is karmic maturation does not manifest and negative physical or verbal action does not arise. Therefore twenty-two mental factors occur in virtuous minds: (1–10) universal mental states, (11–20) virtuous mental states, (21) investigation, and (22) analysis. Eighteen mental factors occur in afflicted-unmixed minds: (1–10) universal mental states, (11–16) the six afflicted mental states, (17) investigation, and (18) analysis. Eighteen mental factors occur in mixed minds that also possess [the mental factor of] view since view is nominally existent. Nineteen mental factors occur in other minds possessing attachment since they possess that attachment. Twelve mental factors occur in the three unobscured minds: the ten universal mental states, investigation, and analysis. There is no mind governing creativity there. In general, four types of mind exist in the higher realms — virtuous minds, afflicted-mixed minds, afflicted-unmixed minds, and unobscured-neutral [129] minds — since nonvirtuous minds do not exist there. All afflicted minds in [the higher realms] are solely obscured, and they do not become nonvirtuous since they are moistened by calm abiding.}

gang dag bsam gtan dang po na med pa de dag dang de dag tu ma zad rtog pa'ang bsam gtan dang po'i dngos gzhi khyad par can na med cing*/{ thams cad la rtog pa phri bas dge ba sngar bshad pa nyer gcig /ma 'dres pa la bcu bdun 'dres pa la lta ba dang ldan na'ang bcu bdun/ gzhan chags sogs ldan pa bco brgyad/ ma bsgribs pa'i sems la bcu gcig go /}bsam gtan dang po'i dngos gzhi khyad par can de yi gong ma bsam gtan gnyis pa nas srid rtse'i bar na ni bsam gtan dang po dang de'i dngos gzhi khyad par can na med par bshad pa rnams dang de dag tu ma zad dpyod pa yang med do zhes sbyar ro/ / yang zhes pas de dag na g.yo sgyu gnyis kyang med do zhes ston pa ste/ gang na rgyal rigs dang*/ bram ze dang*/ khyim bdag dang*/ dge sbyong dang*/ rgyal chen bzhi dang*/ sum cu rtsa gsum dang*/ bdud dang*/ tshangs pa'i 'khor te 'khor brgyad po de dag dang 'brel ba de na g.yo sgyu yod kyi bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad na 'khor dang 'brel ba med pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan dag ni 'dod pa'i khams ji lta ba bzhin du shes par bya ste/ bsam gtan dang po'i dngos gzhi man chad kyi dge ba'i sems dang bsgribs pa dang ma bsgribs pa ni 'dod par bshad pa ltar nyi shu rtsa gnyis dang*/ bco brgyad dang*/ bcu gnyis dang ldan zhing*/ dngos gzhi khyad par can na rtog pa ma gtogs pa nyi shu gcig dang*/ bcu bdun dang*/ bcu gcig dang*/ bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad ni{ rtog dpyod gnyis por ba'i sa mang bcu dge bcu ste/ nyon mongs can ma 'dres pa la sa mang bcu/ nyon mongs pa sa mang drug ste} nyi shu dang bcu drug dang{ 'dres ma'i lta ba dang ldan la'ang bcu drug dang chags sogs gzhan dang ldan pa la sa bcu nyon mongs kyi sa ming drug chags sogs rang nyid dang bcu bdun dang ma bsgribs pa las mang} bcu dang ldan par 'byung bar nges so zhes bya'o/ /

Added to those mental factors that do not exist on the first absorption, also investigation does not exist on the special actual basis of the first absorption. {Since investigation is subtracted from all minds that were previously explained, twenty-one mental factors occur in virtuous minds, seventeen in unmixed minds, seventeen in minds mixed with view, eighteen in those minds possessing attachment and so on, and eleven in unobscured minds.} Those mental factors that were explained not to exist in the first absorption and the special actual basis of the first absorption, plus analysis also, do not exist above the special actual basis of the first absorption — from the second absorption to the summit of existence. “Also” indicates that both guile and deceit do not exist there. Guile and deceit are related to the eight retinues — kṣatriyas, brahmans, householders, śramaṇas, gods of Cāturmahārājakāyika (Heaven of the Four Great Kings), gods of Trāyastriṃśa (Heaven of the Thirty-Three), māras, and the retinue of Brahma — but they are not related to the retinues of the second absorption and above. The others should be understood as in the desire realm. Virtuous minds, obscured minds, and unobscured minds on or below the actual basis of the first absorption possess respectively twenty-two, eighteen, or twelve mental factors, in accordance with the explanation for the desire realm. The special actual basis that lacks investigation possesses twenty-one, seventeen, or eleven mental factors. Minds above the second absorption possess twenty: {ten universal mental states and ten virtuous mental states, omitting investigation and analysis. Minds of afflicted-unmixed level possess sixteen: the ten universal mental states and the six afflicted mental states. Mixed minds possessing view} possess sixteen, {and other minds possessing attachment and so on possess seventeen: the ten universal mental states, the six afflicted mental states, and attachment itself. Unobscured minds} definitely possess the ten {universal mental states}.

Question: Aren’t shamelessness and nonembarrassment {the same as immodesty}? Why are they differentiated?
ma gus ngo tsha med khrel med/ / kha na ma tho 'jigs mi lta/ / dga' dang gus nyid ngo tsha shes/ / 32 de gnyis 'dod dang gzugs dag na/ /
Shamelessness is not respecting. Nonembarrassment is not viewing offensive acts as something to be feared. Joy is faith, respect is shame. Both exist in the desire and form realms. (2:32)

yon tan dang yon tan can la ma gus pa ni ngo tsha med pa dang*/ khrel med pa ni srog gcod pa la sogs pa'i kha na ma tho ba la 'jigs par mi lta ba ste de dag gi khyad par ni de yin no zhes bya'o/ / de la'ang mi 'jigs par lta ba ni shes rab yin la/ 'jigs par mi lta na ni ma rig pa yin pa'i phyir de gnyis kyi rgyu nye ba'i nyon mongs pa yin no zhes bye brag tu smra ba 'dod do/ / sde pa gzhan gyis ni rim pa ltar bdag gzhan la ltos nas sdig pa la mi 'dzem par 'jug pa ni ngo tsha med pa dang*/ khrel med pa yin no zhes zer ro/ / ngo tsha med pa dang khrel med las bzlog pa ni ngo tsha shes pa dang khrel yod yin no/ / yang dga' ba dang gus pa la tha dad du bya ba ci yod ce na/

The difference is that shamelessness (ahrī) is not respecting (agurutā) qualities, or those who possess qualities. Nonembarrassment (anatrapā) is not viewing offensive acts (avadya) such as taking life as something to be feared (bhayā). Also in this regard Vaibhāṣikas assert that the cause of both is the branch afflictions because wisdom views them without fear but ignorance does not view them with fear. Other schools assert that shamelessness and nonembarrassment are, respectively, the lack of consideration for oneself or for others when committing negative actions. Shame and embarrassment stop shamelessness and nonembarrassment. [130] Question: Why are joy and respect differentiated?

dga' ba la gnyis las nyon mongs can ma yin pa yon tan dang yon tan can la dga' ba ni dad pa yin la/ nyon mongs can bu dang chung ma la sogs pa la dga' ba ni 'dod chags yin no/ / dad pa la'ang dga' bas khyab pa med de/ sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung la dmigs pa lta bu'o/ / dga' ba la'ang dad pas ma khyab ste/ dga' ba nyon mongs can bu dang chung ma la sogs pa la dga' ba lta bu'o/ / de nyid kyi phyir 'grel pa las dga' ba dang dad pa la mu bzhi bshad do/{ de yang dad pa dang dga' ba la chos dang gang zag la ltos nas mu bzhi ste/ dang po chos la dmigs pa'i mu bzhi la/ bden pa dang ngo gnyis la yid ches pa ni dad pa yin la dga' ba min te de gnyis dga' bya min pas so/ / dga' ba nyon mongs can ni gnyis pa ste sred pa yin pas so/ / gsum pa ni 'gog lam la dmigs pa'i dad pa ste yid ches shing dga' bya yin pas so/ / bzhi pa ni de dag min pa'i sems 'byung dang ldan min sogs so/ / gang zag la dmigs pa'i dga' gus kyi mu bzhi ni bu dang chung ma la sogs la dga' ba ni dga' ba yin/ gus pa min pa'i mu dang po'o/ / gnyis pa ni gzhan gyi bla ma la sogs la gus pa dang*/ gsum pa ni rang gi bla ma sogs la gus pa dang*/ bzhi pa ni sdang ba'i yul gyi sems can la dmigs pa lta bu'o/ / 'di gnyis khyad che ste gus pa ni dge ba kho na yin la dga' ba la dge ba dang 'dod chags gnyis yod pas so/} gus pa nyid ni yon tan dang yon tan can la bkur ba'i ngo tsha shes pa yin no/ /

Reply: There are two types of joy (prema): (1) faith (śraddhā) that takes joy in unafflicted qualities and those who possess such qualities and (2) attachment that takes joy in an afflictive son or wife. Faith is not necessarily pervaded by joy, such as faith that focuses on the truths of suffering and origin. Joy is not necessarily pervaded by faith, because there is afflicted joy such as taking joy in a son and wife. Therefore the Autocommentary explains that joy and faith have four possibilities.[527] {There are four possibilities for joy and faith regarding either Dharma or persons. When focused on Dharma, the four possibilities are as follows: (1) Conviction in the first two truths is faith but not joy since those two truths are not the object of joy. (2) Afflicted joy is the second [joy but not faith] since it is craving. (3) The third is faith focused on cessation because it is conviction and the object of joy. (4) The fourth is a mental factor that is neither [joy nor faith] or those lacking concomitance and so on. The four possibilities for joy and respect focused on persons are the following: (1) Taking joy in a son or wife and so on is joy but not respect. (2) [Respect but not joy] is respect for the guru of another and so on. (3) [Respect and joy together] is respect for one’s own guru. (4) [Neither respect nor joy] is focusing on sentient beings who are an object of aversion. These two are very different, since respect is virtuous alone, but joy can be either virtuous or attached.} Respect (gurutva) is shame (hrī) that venerates qualities and those who possess qualities.

sde pa gzhan dag ni dga' ba dang gus pa nyid ni dad pa dang ngo tsha shes pa ma yin gyi dad pa dang gus pa ni rim pa ltar yon tan la yid ches pa dang yon tan dang yon tan can la bkur ba dang bcas pa yin la/ de gnyis las skyes pa'i dga' ba dang 'jigs pa dang bcas pas 'dzem pa ni rim pa ltar dga' ba dang ngo tsha shes pa yin no zhes 'dod do/ /

Other schools assert that joy is not faith and respect is not shame. They assert that faith is conviction in good qualities and respect is venerating good qualities and those who possess good qualities, joy is the joy arising from those two, and shame is conscientiousness arising due to fear.

It is said that both joy and respect exist in the desire and form realms when they are focused on persons {since both activate verbal and physical karma}. When both are focused on Dharma, they also exist in the formless realm. Question: What distinguishes investigation and analysis?
rtog dang dpyod pa rtsing zhib nyid/ / nga rgyal khengs pa rgyags pa ni/ / rang gi chos la chags pa yi/ / 33 sems ni yongs su gtugs pa'o/ /
Investigation and analysis are coarse and fine. Pride inflates the mind. Arrogance depletes the mind attached to one’s own qualities. (2:33)

bsam gyis mi khyab pa bstan pa'i mdo las/ zhi ba'i blo gros gang gi nub mo de bzhin gshegs pa bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas pa dang*/ gang gi nub mo len pa mi mnga' bar yongs su mya ngan las 'da' bar 'gyur ba de'i bar du de bzhin gshegs pas tha na yi ge 'bru gcig kyang ma gsungs so/ / gsung bar mi 'gyur ro/ / de ci'i phyir zhe na/ zhi ba'i blo gros de bzhin gshegs pa ni rtag tu mnyam par bzhag pa ste/ de bzhin gshegs pa la dbugs 'byung ba'am rngub pa mi mnga' 'o/ / rnam par mi rtog go /rnam par mi dpyod do/ / rnam par rtog pa dang rnam par dpyod pa med na ngag mi 'byung ba ste zhes gsungs pa lta bu'o/ / bsam gtan dang po yan lag lngar bshad pa'ang sa las yin gyi skad cig las ni ma yin no zhes bya bar 'chad do/ / yang nga rgyal dang rgyags pa la tha dad du bya ba ci yod ce na/

Reply: Investigation (vitarka) and analysis (vicāra) are, respectively, the coarse (audārya) examination of the nature of an object of mind and the fine (sūkṣmata) examination of the attributes of the object. They both function to support the attainment or nonattainment of happiness. Question: How do these two simultaneously occur in one mind? Some say: Through investigation, the mind does not become [131] too fine, and through analysis, it does not become too coarse, like sunlight striking butter in water.[528] If that were not so, then the first absorption would not have five branches, for when either investigation or analysis exists, the other would not exist. Other schools say: Investigation and analysis exist up to the summit of existence because coarse investigation and fine analysis, which observe objects, exist on the level of that being observed. But they do not exist in the same mind because coarse and fine examination exclude each other when observing the same object. Moreover, investigation is the mental factor occurring in the retinue of mental consciousness that examines the nature of an object, and analysis examines its attributes. Further, {investigation and analysis} [respectively] motivate speech {that expresses the mere nature of an object and speech that expresses its attributes,} because a sūtra declares: Verbal expression is due to investigation and analysis and not due to noninvestigation and nonanalysis.[529] The Inconceivable Secrets of the Tathāgata Sūtra states: Śāntimati, from the night the Tathāgata actually attained highest, perfect, complete enlightenment up until the night he attained parinirvāṇa free of craving, the Tathāgata did not utter even one syllable, nor would he have uttered one syllable. Why? Śāntimati, the Tathāgata is always in equipoise. A tathāgata has no inhalation or exhalation, no investigation, no analysis. If there is no investigation or analysis, no speech occurs.[530] Also the explanation that there are five branches in the first absorption is from the perspective of levels not moments. Question: Why are pride and arrogance differentiated?

nga rgyal ni pha rol po las gang yang rung ba'i khyad par brtags nas rigs la sogs pa la dmigs nas sems{ kho las nga mtho snyam du} khengs pa yin la/ dbye na bdun yod de 'og nas 'chad par 'gyur ro/ / las ni bla ma la sogs pa rnams la mi gus pa dang yang srid kyi sdug bsngal 'byung ba'i rten byed pa'o/ / rgyags pa ni rang gi rigs dang gzugs la sogs pa'i chos la chags pa'i sems yongs su gtugs shing zad par byed pa'o/{ de gnyis rang gi chos la dmigs pa dang gzhan gyi chos la dmigs pa'i khyad yod/ /} slob dpon 'dun bzang ni rigs la sogs pa la chags nas sems dge ba las phyir log pa ni gtugs pa'i don du 'chad do/ / slob dpon kha cig ni rang gi rigs la sogs pa la chags pa las skyes pa'i yid dga' ba yin no zhes 'dod do/ / 'di bye brag tu smra bas ni mi 'dod de/ yid dga' ba bsam gtan gsum pa nas med la rgyags pa khams gsum par bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / dbye ba ni bshes spring las/ rigs dang gzugs dang thos pa lang tsho dang*/ / dbang thang che bas rgyags pa dgra bzhin gzigs/ / zhes rnam pa lnga bshad pa yin no/{ byed las dge ba la sems mi 'jug par byed pa'o/} ma nges pa'i sa pa'i 'dod chags dang khong khro dang the tshom rnams ni 'og tu ston pa'i phyir 'dir ma bshad do/ /

Reply: Pride (māna) is that which inflates (unnati) the mind {with the thought “I am superior to another”} through focusing on another’s social class and so on and investigating how one is different from another. If classified, there are seven types of pride, which are explained below. Its function is to support disrespect for gurus and so on and the suffering of rebirth. Arrogance (mada) depletes (paryādāna) and exhausts the mind attached (raktasya) to one’s own qualities (svadharma), such as one’s own class, body, and so on. {These two are distinguished [from each other], since arrogance focuses on one’s own qualities and pride focuses on others’ qualities.} Master Saṅghabhadra explains that “depletes” refers to attachment to one’s class and so on stopping virtuous minds. Another master asserts that it refers to the mental joy that arises from attachment to one’s own class and so on. Vaibhāṣikas do not assert this because they explain that mental joy does not exist on and above the third absorption but arrogance exists in the three realms. [132] If classified, Letter to a Friend explains five aspects: Arrogance arises through class, physical form, education, youth, and influence. View it as an enemy.[531] {Its function is to prevent the mind engaging in virtue.} The indefinite levels of attachment, anger, and doubt are not explained here but taught below.
lnga pa sems dang sems byung rnams kyi rnam grangs bshad pa ni
SYNONYMS OF MINDS AND MENTAL FACTORS
sems dang yid dang rnam shes ni/ / don gcig sems dang sems byung dang / / rten dang dmigs dang rnam bcas dang / / 34 mtshungs par ldan pa'ang rnam pa lnga/ /
Mind, mental faculty, and consciousness are equivalent. Minds and mental factors are concomitant in five ways through possessing support, focal object, and aspect. (2:34)

mdo las sems dang yid dang rnam par shes pa zhes gsungs pa ni don gcig la ming gi rnam grangs kyi brjod pa yin te/ dge mi dge la sogs par 'byed pas na sems dang*/ gzugs la sogs pa shes pas na yid dang*/ dmigs pa rnam par shes pas na rnam shes zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro zhes bye brag tu smra bas 'dod do/ / mdo sde pa ni dge mi dge'i bag chags bsags pas na sems dang*/ rten du gyur pas na yid dang*/ brten par gyur pas na rnam par shes pa dang*/ de bzhin du{ don gsang las nyon thos kyi theg pa'i dbang du mdzad nas byed pa dang dus dang gdul bya la bstan pa'i bye brag gis nges tshig gsum du bshad do/ / dang po ni ring du 'gro zhing gcig pu rgyu zhes 'byung bas ring du 'gro bar byed pas na sems dang chos thams cad yid sngon du 'gro ba can no zhes 'byung bas na sngon du 'gro bar byed pas na yid dang*/ 'du byed kyi rkyen gyis rnam par shes pa'o zhes 'byung bas nying mtshams sbyor bar byed pas na rnam par shes pa dang*/ gnyis pa ni} ma 'ongs pa ni sems dang 'das pa ni yid dang*/ da ltar byung ba ni rnam par shes pa dang*/ {gsum pa ni } khams{ bstan par sems kyi khams bdun} dang skye mched bstan par yid kyi skye mched dang*/ phung po bstan par rnam par shes pa'i phung po zhes gsungs so/ / de'i phyir mkhas pa dag byed pa gsum dang*/ dus gsum dang*/ bstan pa gsum gyi dbang gis so zhes 'chad do/ / rnal 'byor spyod pa pa ni sems ni kun gzhi rnam shes dang*/ yid ni nyon yid dang*/ rnam shes ni 'jug pa'i rnam shes la 'dod do/ / 'thug po bkod pa'i mdo las/ sems ni kun gzhi rnam shes te/ / de la ngar 'dzin yid yin no/ / yul la rnam par rig pa gang*/ / de ni 'jug pa'i rnam shes 'dod/ / ces gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Mind (citta), mental faculty (manas), and consciousness (vijñāna), which are described in the sūtras,[532] are called “equivalent” (ekārtha) and “synonymous.” For as the Vaibhāṣikas assert, something is the mind because it differentiates virtue and nonvirtue and so on, it is the mental faculty because it is aware of form and so on, and it is consciousness because it is conscious of its focal object. Sautrāntikas state that something is the mind because it accumulates imprints of virtue and nonvirtue, it is the mental faculty because it supports, and it is consciousness because it is supported. Similarly {Exposing the Hidden Meaning[533] specifically explains three etymologies from the perspective of the Śrāvaka Vehicle: action, time, and teaching disciples. (1) [Regarding action,] something is the mind since it proceeds far, for it is said, “wanders far and moves alone”;[534] it is the mental faculty since it precedes other states, for it is said, “The mental faculty precedes all conditioned states”; it is consciousness since it links with other states, for it is said, “Consciousness is conditioned by formation (saṃskāra).” (2) Regarding time,} the future is mind, the past is the mental faculty, and that which occurs in the present is consciousness. {(3) Regarding disciples,} when teaching elements {it is the seven mental elements}; when teaching bases it is the mental base (mana-āyatana); and when teaching aggregates it is the consciousness aggregate. Therefore scholars differentiate those three from the perspective of three actions, three times, and the three teachings. Yogācāras assert that the mind is foundation consciousness, the mental faculty is afflicted intellect (kliṣṭamanas), and consciousness is consciousness that engages objects.[535] The Dense Array of Ornaments Sūtra declares: The mind is foundation consciousness. Grasping that as “I” is the afflicted intellect. That which cognizes objects is engaged consciousness.[536]

Formative factors not associated (viprayuktāsaṃskāra) with the mind have fourteen types: (1) obtainment (prāpti); (2) nonobtainment (aprāpti); (3) homogeneity (sabhāga); (4) the state of nondiscernment (āsaṃjñika); the two types of meditative attainment (samāpatti) — (5) meditative attainment of nondiscernment and (6) meditative attainment of cessation; (7) the faculty of life force (jīvita); (8–11) the four characteristics (lakṣaṇa) of conditioned states such as arising and so on; and (12) the collection of nouns (nāmakāya). The term “and so on” refers to (13) the collection of predicated phrases and (14) the collection of letters. The term “also” includes Saṅgha schisms and so on. {If what is obtained is not conjoined with the mindstream but a shared external object, then it would be possible for an arhat to obtain the afflictions of ordinary beings, since [that obtained] does not [depend] on being near or far, and it would not be contradictory for all [beings] to have [liberation]. But if so, it would be pointless for an arhat to strive to abandon afflictions, and ordinary beings would obtain nonlearner paths. If that were so, ordinary beings would be liberated without exertion. But exertion is not meaningless, and neither is there liberation without exertion. Therefore there is no obtainment of conditioned phenomena not conjoined to the mindstream, and their nonobtainment is similar because ordinary beings don’t obtain ārya Dharmas even though they obtain nonthings [or permanent entities]. Therefore [objects that are obtained] must be conjoined with the mindstream.}

Some say: It is not that “nonperishing substance is also conjoined,” for that is the textual system of the Sāṃmitīya Vaibhāṣikas and not the system of the Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas because they assert that nonperishing substance is impermanent as a continuum and not impermanent as a momentary state. This is sourced in the texts of the Mādhyamikas. Yogācāras explain twenty-three nonassociated formative factors in their texts: those fourteen, plus nine:
1. Continuity (pravṛtti) signifies the unbroken continuity of causation, since there can be no causation devoid of momentariness and continuity. 2. Distinction (pratiniyama) signifies causal virtue and nonvirtue producing distinct pleasant and unpleasant results and so on. 3. Union (yoga) signifies the possession of compatible and appropriate resources as the result of generosity. Some say that this is also called connection. 4. Rapidity (java) signifies the swift occurrence of cause and effect. 5. Sequence (anukrama) signifies cause and effect arising serially and not simultaneously. 6. Time (kāla) signifies cause and effect in terms of having ceased after arising, having not arisen, or having not ceased after arising. 7. Location (deśa) signifies physical causation existing in the ten directions. 8. Enumeration (saṃkhyā) signifies [134] individual, distinct conditioned states. 9. Assembly (sāmagrī) signifies the assembly of causes and conditions that produce results. Moreover, it is well known that the Sūtra Teaching the Ten Abodes explains seven hundred nonassociated formative factors.[537]

Question: Why are they called nonassociated formative factors? Reply: Because they are formative factors that are not form and not associated [or concomitant] with minds or mental factors. Vaibhāṣikas assert that they are phenomena substantially distinct from form, mind, or mental factors. Sautrāntikas assert that they are imputed in the context of those three. Yogācāras assert that they are imputed in the context of minds and mental factors.

A sūtra explains: If one possesses the ten nonlearner Dharmas — the eightfold noble path, liberation, and perfectly liberated transcendent wisdom — one is an ārya who has abandoned the five branches: both attachments, excitation, pride, and confusion.[538] This explains that those ten nonlearner Dharmas and ārya Dharmas are substances possessed in the mindstream of that person. For Vasubandhu, this should not be taken as obtainment. However, merely obtaining control over an obtainable object is designated as “possessing it.” For example, the seven precious articles [of a cakravartin king,] — the jewel, wheel, and so on — cannot be obtained since they are external objects, and you accept that conditioned states not conjoined with the mindstream cannot be obtained. However, one who merely takes control of the seven precious articles of a cakravartin is designated as “one who possesses the seven precious articles,”[539] for the term possession is applied in this way.

[Some say:] If possession is not substantially existent, then it would follow that āryas would not be different from ordinary beings in what they abandon and realize when they [i.e., āryas] manifest the mundane path, because they would have no manifest transcendent path and they would have no substantially established obtainment of the transcendent path, just like ordinary beings. [Some say:] Again, it would follow that there would be no difference in abandonment and realization between āryas such as stream enterers, once returners, and nonreturners, because there would be no substantially existent obtainment of superior or inferior objects of abandonment and realization. Therefore, since those are obtained, they are substantially existent. Vasubandhu asserts that though obtainment is not substantially existent, there is a difference between the abandonment and realization of āryas and of ordinary beings because there is a difference in the abandonment or nonabandonment of the seeds to be abandoned by the path of seeing. Also, there is a difference among [different ranks of] āryas with respect to how many objects of abandonment are abandoned and how many uncontaminated faculties are obtained.[540]

Beginningless possession is [for instance] ordinary beings {who obtain afflictions through never having generated the antidote to} afflictions of the summit of existence.[541] In brief, the Vaibhāṣikas explain that there are five types.

Question: Do obtainment and nonobtainment exist for all phenomena?

Reply: Obtainment (prāpti) and nonobtainment (aprāpti) occur for all objects that belong to one’s own mindstream (svasaṃtāna) but not for those belonging to another’s mindstream nor for those belonging to the mindstreams of sentient beings, because if one’s own qualities were obtained by others, then {it would be possible that ordinary beings would be āryas}. But that is contradictory because there is no obtainment of objects not belonging to one’s mindstream, {such as clothes and ornaments, for these are shared objects,} and obtainment is the obtainment by a person {of unique or unshared objects, and this is definite for conditioned states}.

It is a special instruction that, in general, the obtainment of both analytical and nonanalytical cessations (nirodha) occurs in the mindstreams of beings even though they don’t belong to their mindstreams. The Abhidharma (Attainment of Knowledge)[542] states: Who possesses uncontaminated phenomena? All sentient beings.[543] Nonanalytical cessation is possessed by all ordinary beings and āryas. Analytical cessation is possessed by some ordinary beings and all āryas except those abiding on the first moment of the uncontaminated path who still possess all the ties (bandhana), because the first moment of the uncontaminated path possessing all the ties is the uninterrupted path and not the liberated path. {Moreover, those [ties] are yet to be abandoned,} and some ordinary beings obtain the mark of separation from attachment from level to level, through the strength of access concentrations to the absorptions and formless states. Space is not described as something obtained because there is no obtainment whatsoever {of objects not related to the mindstream, as there would then be too many objects of obtainment. The two cessations are not similar because [here] that which has ceased is related to the mindstream}.

It is a tenet of the Vaibhāṣikas that if something has no obtainment it also has no nonobtainment, but if it has obtainment it also has nonobtainment. Also that obtainment is a quality to be obtained.

Obtainment in the three times has three types. Obtainment of virtuous states and so on is virtuous and so forth. Obtainment belonging to a realm belongs to that specific realm. Obtainment that does not belong has four types. (2:37)

Obtainment in the three times (adhvan) that occurs in the past, future, and present also has three types: the past, future, and present, [making nine combinations].

{Some say: Obtainment of powerful objects of obtainment is possible in the three times. For example, [regarding past objects:] (1) past obtainment of past objects of obtainment is all obtainment of objects occurring at the same time and before that object; (2) present obtainment of those is obtainment of those just before they cease; and (3) future obtainment of those is obtainment of those from the second moment of cessation on. [Regarding present objects:] (1) past obtainment of present objects of obtainment is obtainment of those before they occur; (2) present obtainment of those is obtainment of those when they occur; and (3) future obtainment of those is obtainment of those after they cease. [Regarding future objects:] (1) future obtainment of objects that will be produced in the future is obtainment of those when they occur; (2) present obtainment of those is obtainment of those in the moment they transform into present objects; and (3) past obtainment [136] of those is obtainment of those from the second moment on, having transformed into present objects. Obtainment exists in the three times, for it is asserted that objects obtained in the future transform into present and past objects since the Abhidharmakośa declares, “In just the way perseverance and knowledge arise on the path of seeing, future states will be obtained” (7:20abc).}

It is possible that the obtainment of past objects exists in the past and that obtainment of past objects exists in the present and also in the future. Similarly, it is possible that the obtainment of present objects occurs in the past, present, and future, and that the obtainment of future objects occurs in the past, present, and future. {Though the obtainment of both cessations is subsumed within time, the objects obtained are not differentiated by time.}

Question: What is the obtainment of virtuous, nonvirtuous, and neutral states?
