Reply: The obtainment of virtuous (śubha) states and so on — referring to nonvirtuous, and neutral states — is also respectively virtuous and so forth. {If that were not so, it would follow that those free of attachment could possess nonvirtuous phenomena and those who sever their root of virtue could possess virtuous phenomena, since it would be possible to possess obtainment and objects obtained of dissimilar type.} Similarly, the obtainment of phenomena belonging to the desire, form, and formless realms belongs to that specific realm (dhātu) for, respectively, the obtainment of desire-realm phenomena belongs to the desire realm and so on.

Obtainment of either the uncontaminated cessation or the [uncontaminated] path that does not belong to the phenomena element has four types: those of the desire, form, and formless realms and those not belonging to any realm. {Obtainment of any phenomenon that is an object of obtainment, such as} nonanalytical cessation, obtained in the desire realm belongs to the desire realm; that obtained in the form realm belongs to the form realm; and that obtained in the formless realm belongs to the formless realm, because the specific mindstream has greater power. {Further, in whatever realm or level nonanalytical phenomena are obtained, their obtainment is also posited as subsumed by that realm and level, for the mindstream of the person has greater efficacy and the nonarising of those phenomena is not established as distinct from it. If it is posited according to the phenomena obtained, then the path’s obtainment of nonanalytical cessation would not be subsumed by the realms.}

The obtainment of analytical cessation by mundane absorption belongs to the form realm, and its obtainment by mundane formless states belongs to the formless realm. {Analytical cessation belonging to the desire realm does not exist since it is not obtained there; it is an antidote to the desire realm and thus incompatible.} That obtained by the uncontaminated path belongs to the uncontaminated path because it has greater power as a cause or antidote. {The obtainment of analytical cessation by an ārya with the mundane path possesses two types of obtainment: uncontaminated and contaminated. So too, it is said that an ārya’s obtainment of separation from affliction has two types.

de la zag med khams su ma gtogs la/ zag bcas ni thob byed kyi dbang gis gzugs gzugs med gang rung du gtogs kyi 'dod par mi gtogs pa sngar bzhin no/ / slob pas brtags 'gog 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis thob pa'i thob pa zag med ni slob pa dang zag bcas ni gnyis min no/ / dgra bcom la'ang de bzhin sbyar ro/ /} lam gyi bden pa'i thob pa ni zag med du gtogs te/ de ni chos stobs che ba'i phyir ro/ /

Uncontaminated states do not belong to a realm, but contaminated states belong to either the form or formless realm by the power of obtainment but not to the desire realm, as previously explained. The uncontaminated obtainment of analytical cessation by a learner [137] due to the mundane path is learner [obtainment], while contaminated [obtainment] is neither [learner nor nonlearner obtainment]. This should also be applied to arhats.} The obtainment of the truth of path belongs to uncontaminated phenomena because it has greater power in terms of Dharma.
slob dang mi slob min gyi gsum/ / spang bya min pa'i rnam gnyis 'dod/ / lung bstan min thob lhan cig skye/ / 38 mngon shes sprul pa ma gtogs pa/ /

Obtainment of neither learner nor nonlearner attributes has three types. Obtainment of those not to be abandoned is asserted to have two types. Obtainment of those not declared arises simultaneously except for emanation and higher perception. (2:38)

yang slob{ pa dang mi slob} pa'i chos{ lam bden} rnams kyi thob pa ni{ rim pa ltar} slob pa dang*/ mi slob pa'i chos{ lam bden} rnams kyi thob pa ni mi slob pa yin la/ slob pa dang mi slob pa gnyis ka min pa'i chos{ de yang nam mkha' dang rgyud kyis ma bsdus pa la thob pa med pas 'gog pa gnyis dang*/ rgyud kyis bsdus pa'i zag bcas} rnams kyi thob pa ni slob par gtogs pa dang*/ mi slob par gtogs pa dang*/ gnyis ka ma yin par gtogs pa gsum yin no/ / de la slob pa dang mi slob pa'i chos ni lam gyi bden pa dang*/ gnyis ka ma yin pa ni zag bcas dang 'dus ma byas rnams yin te/ de yang zag bcas kyi thob pa dang*/ so sor brtags min gyi 'gog pa'i thob pa dang*/ so sor brtags 'gog gi thob pa 'phags pa ma yin pas thob pa rnams ni slob pa'ang ma yin mi slob pa yang ma yin no/ / so sor brtags 'gog gi thob pa slob pas thob pa{ 'das lam} ni slob pa dang*/ mi slob pas {'das lam srid rtse spong ba'i rnam grol dgu pas }thob pa ni mi slob pa yin no/ { gal te mi slob pas brtags 'gog thob pa'i thob pa mi slob par 'dod pa ni mi rigs te mi slob pa ni rnam grol gyi lam yin pas spang bya dang 'bral ba'i lam ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ mi slob pas brtags 'gog thob pa ni rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin gyis srid rtse'i sgom spang chung ngu'i chung ngu spangs pas thob pa'i phyir slob pa'i thob pa yin gyi mi slob pa'i ma yin pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ bden mod kyi bar chad med pas drangs pa'i bral thob kyi rten byed pas na mi slob pa'i thob par brjod do/ /}

Moreover, the fact that obtainment of objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing belongs to objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing and that the obtainment of objects abandoned by the path of meditation belongs to objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation are not explained because these are easily understood. The obtainment of those not to be abandoned (aheya) is asserted to have two types: (1) objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation and (2) {uncontaminated states} not to be abandoned, because both are uncontaminated objects not to be abandoned. Therefore (1) {all neutral} obtainment of nonanalytical cessation and obtainment of analytical cessation by non-āryas are objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation {since they are contaminated virtue}; (2) obtainment of analytical cessation by the ārya {transcendent} path and the obtainment of the truth of path are definitely not to be abandoned. {The contaminated obtainment of analytical cessation obtained by āryas through the mundane path is an object to be abandoned by the path of meditation, whereas uncontaminated states are not to be abandoned.}
gal te chos thams cad thob pa dus gsum par nges sam zhe na/
Question: Does the obtainment of all objects definitely exist in the three times?

de'i dmigs kyis bsal ba ni dge ba dang nyon mongs can du lung bstan pa{ dbang po lta bu} min pa'i chos ma bsgribs lung ma bstan rnams kyi thob pa ni thob bya'i chos dang lhan cig skye'i snga phyir skye ba med de/ {rnam smin med pas sam 'dus ma byas par skye bas } chos de rnams stobs chung ba'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: The exception is the obtainment of unobscured-neutral objects not declared (avyākṛtā) to be virtuous or afflicted, {such as the sense faculties,} which arises simultaneously (sahajā) with the object obtained and not before nor after. That is because those objects have little power, {they lack karmic maturation, or they arise as unconditioned states}. [138]
'o na ma bsgribs lung ma bstan de yang thams cad du nges sam zhe na/
Question: Is that definite for all unobscured-neutral objects?

lha'i mig dang rna ba'i mngon shes lung ma bstan gnyis dang*/ sprul pa'i sems lung ma bstan ma gtogs pa rnams ni da ltar nges la/ de gsum ni mi 'dra ste/ de dag gi thob pa ni dus gsum du'ang skye ba yod de/ sbyor ba{ drag po'i} khyad par gyis bsgrub{ dgos} pas stobs che ba'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du{ 'du byed kyi khyad par gyis bsgribs pas las thams cad pa'i lta bu} bzo shin tu goms pa dang*/ spyod lam la shin tu goms pa{ bcom ldan 'das dang rta thul gyi spyod lam lta bu} kha cig gi thob pa'ang dus gsum par skye ba srid{ par bye brag smra ba 'dod} do/

Reply: That is definite except for the neutral mind of emanation (nairmāṇika) and both neutral higher perceptions (abhijñā) of the divine eye and ear. Those three are not similar because their obtainment arises in the three times. They have greater power since they {must be} established by special {intense} preparation. {Vaibhāṣikas assert} that it is possible that obtainment arises in the three times through the intense cultivation of the mind governing creativity (śilpasthāna), {such as all actions that establish specific artistic works,} and the intense cultivation of the mind governing demeanor (īryāpatha), {such as the demeanor of a Bhagavan or that required for taming horses}.
{ ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gyi thob pa de ltar nges na 'o na/ /}chos dang thob pa lhan cig skye ba gzhan yang{ yod dam zhe na}
{Question: If the obtainment of unobscured-neutral states is definitely simultaneous, then} do other objects and their obtainment also arise simultaneously {or not}?
bsgribs pa'i gzugs kyi'ang 'dod pa na/ / gzugs kyi sngar ni skye ba med/ / ma thob ma bsgribs lung ma bstan/ / 39 'das ma skyes kyi de rnam gsum/ /

That is applied also to obscured form. Obtainment of form in the desire realm does not arise prior to [form]. Nonobtainment is an unobscured-neutral state. Past and unarisen objects have three types. (2:39)
yod par bstan pa ni bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa'i gzugs kyi rig byed kyi'ang thob pa lhan cig tu skye'o zhes sbyar ro/ /
Reply: The explanation that they are simultaneous is applied also to indicate obscured (nivṛta)-neutral form whose obtainment arises simultaneously.

de yang bsgribs la lung ma bstan gyi gzugs ni 'dod pa na med de/ kun slong med pa'i phyir ro/ / des na de ni bsam gtan dang po na rang gi sa pa'i nyon mongs pas kun nas bslang ba'i lus ngag gi las thams cad yin pas{ de kho na na yod kyi kun slong med pas khams dang sa gzhan na med do} gnyis pa yan chad rang sa na bsgribs pa'i gzugs med par 'dod do/

Moreover, obscured-neutral form does not exist in the desire realm because there is no motivation for it to arise there. As such, it is all physical and verbal karma motivated by affliction of its own level, the first absorption {alone, and not on other levels and realms, since they lack such motivation.} Therefore no obscured form of its own level on or above the second absorption is asserted.

{ dge mi dge la dmigs bsal ni/} gzhan yang 'dod pa na spyod pa'i dge mi dge'i rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa'i gzugs kyi thob pa'ang lhan cig dang phyis skye ba yod kyi chos las sngar ni skye ba med{ ces bkag pas de dag gi skad cig ma dang po lhan cig kho na dang gnyis pa sogs la phyis skye ba'ang yod} de/ so so thar gnas ji srid du/ / ma btang bar dag da ltar gyi/ / rnam rig min ldan skad cig ma/ / dang po phyin chad 'das pa dang*/ / sdom min gnas pa'ang de dang 'dra/ / zhes pa dang*/ rnam rig byed ni thams cad la/ / byed pa dag la da ltar ldan/ / ma btang bar du skad cig ma/ / phyin chad 'das ldan ma 'ongs med/ / ces 'chad par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/

{The exception regarding virtuous or nonvirtuous form refers to} the obtainment of form that is virtuous or nonvirtuous, indicative or nonindicative action in the desire realm that does not arise prior (nāgrajā) to the object but simultaneously or later. {Since prior arising has been refuted, obtainment only arises simultaneously in the first moment or subsequently in the second moment and so on.} The Abhidharmakośa explains: “For as long as they maintain pratimokṣa vows and do not relinquish them, they possess present nonindicative form. They possess past indicative form after the first moment. Negative commitments also are attained like that”[544] (4:19–20a) and: “All those who produce indicative form always possess indicative form in the present. They possess past indicative form after the first moment until relinquished. They do not possess future indicative form”[545] (4:23).

{ 'di ni don rdzogs pa min gyi snyoms 'jug gnyis dang skye ba'i chos can gyi mthong lam dang mngon shes dang chad med lta bu ma 'dres pa rnams dang ye shes bstan pa'i shes pa dang lta ba la sogs pa sbyor bas thob pa phal che ba rnams la'ang sngar skyes med do/ /}

{But this presentation is incomplete since in general there is no prior arising of obtainment for those requiring preparation such as both meditative attainments, the path of seeing that is an instance of arising, unmixed states such as nonannihilation, knowledge revealing transcendent wisdom, view, and so on.}

des na 'di skad bstan pa yin te/ sems sems byung nyon mongs can rnams dang*/ dge ba rnams dang*/ gzugs na yod pa'i dge ba gzugs can rnams dang*/ mi ldan pa'i 'du byed dge mi dge thams cad kyi thob pa ni dus gsum pa yin no zhes bya'o/ / 'dir smras pa/ chos kun thob pa dus gsum bar/ / gsungs la lung ma bstan pa dang*/ / bsgribs gzugs 'dod pa'i gzugs dag gi / thob pa dmigs kyis bsal ba'i phyir/ / mtshungs ldan nyon mongs can dang dge gong ma'i dge ba gzugs can dang*/ / mtshungs ldan min pa dge mi dge /thams cad dus gsum par 'dod do/ /

Therefore this is taught because the obtainment of all afflicted minds and mental factors, virtues, physical virtues existing in the form realm, and virtuous or nonvirtuous nonassociated formative factors exist in the three times. It is said: The obtainment of all phenomena is said to exist in the three times except the obtainment of neutral-obscured form and desire-realm form. It is said that all concomitant afflicted states, virtue, physical virtue of the higher realms and virtue or nonvirtue that is nonconcomitant exist in [139] the three times.
gal te thob pa thob bya'i chos dang rgyud las tha dad par yod do zhes bya ba la tshad ma ci yod ce na/
Question: What is valid in the statement “Obtainment and the object obtained are distinct from the mindstream”?

bye brag tu smra ba lung tshad ma nyid du ston te/ 'di ltar mdo las/ de mi slob pa'i chos bcu po 'di dag bskyed cing so sor thob la kun tu ldan pas na yan lag lnga rnam par spangs pa'i 'phags par 'gyur ro zhes gsungs te/ de la yan lag lnga ni khams gong ma gnyis kyi 'dod chags gnyis dang rgod pa dang nga rgyal dang ma rig pa ste gong ma'i cha mthun lnga yin la/ 'phags pa ni dgra bcom pa yin no/{ de rdzas su yod de de'i 'bras bu dmigs pa'i phyir zhes zer ro/ /}

de slob dpon gyis sun 'byin pa na lung de ni 'phags pa dag dbang 'byor bas ldan par bshad pa yin gyi thob pa rdzas su yod par bzhed pa ni ma yin te/ de lta na rin po che bdun la sogs pa rgyud du ma gtogs pa rnams la'ang thob pa yod par 'gyur te/ mdo las dge slong dag 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal po ni rin po che sna bdun dang ldan pa yin no zhes bya ba la sogs pa rgyas par gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / de la gnod par byed pa'ang yod de/ 'di ltar rgyud dang chos las tha dad pa'i thob pa ni dngos por yod pa ma yin te/ de dag rtogs pa'i tshad ma la bltar rung ba las ma dmigs pa'i phyir sa phyogs la sogs par bum pa la sogs pa bzhin no/ / gzhan yang de la nges par yod pa'i tha snyad du'ang mi 'gyur te/ tshad mas ma grub pa'i phyir dang*/ lung gi don yang gzhan du bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du ma thob pa la sogs pa gzhan la'ang sbyar bar bya'o/ /

Vasubandhu criticizes this assertion because scripture explains that āryas possess objects through attaining mastery over them, but it does not explain that obtainment is substantially existent. Otherwise there would be obtainment of objects that do not belong to the mindstream, such as the seven precious articles that are frequently mentioned in the sūtras: Monks, a cakravartin king possesses seven precious articles . . . and so on.[548] That explanation is further harmed [or weakened], for there are no phenomena where obtainment is distinct from the mindstream and the object obtained; valid cognition capable of comprehending that does not observe it, just as a vase that is not observed in a particular place and so on does not exist there. Moreover, it does not exist even conventionally because it is not established by valid cognition, and the meaning of that scriptural passage has been explained differently elsewhere. Such reasoning also should be applied to nonobtainment and so on.

gzhan yang thob pa chos rnams kyi{ sngar skyes nas} bskyed pa'i rgyu yin nam/ 'on te rnam par 'jog pa'i rgyu yin/ dang po ltar na 'dus ma byas gnyis la thob pa med par 'gyur te/ skye ba med pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du zag med kyi skad cig dang po ma thob pa dang*/ sa 'og mar skye ba dang*/ 'og ma las 'dod chags dang bral ba la sogs pa rnams la rim pa bzhin du zag med kyi lam dang*/ 'og ma'i sas bsdus pa'i nyon mongs pa can ma yin pa dang nyon mongs pa can rnams dang*/ gong ma'i sas bsdus pa'i de dag mi skye bar 'gyur te/{ thob pa phyi ma skyes snga ma btang bas/} de dag gi gong du thob pa med pa'i phyir ro/ /

Question: Is obtainment (1) a productive cause of phenomena {that arose in the past} or is it (2) a categorizing cause? Reply: (1) If the first were true, then there would be no obtainment of the two unconditioned states because they do not arise. So too, the uncontaminated path, unafflicted and afflicted states subsumed by lower levels, and unafflicted and afflicted states subsumed by higher levels would not arise, respectively, in those who have not obtained the first moment of the uncontaminated state, those born in lower levels, or those who are free from attachment to lower levels and so on, because they are not obtained prior to their [arising] {since arising precedes and obtainment follows}.

But what if it is the cause of simultaneously arisen [phenomena]? That also is untenable. {Since you do not assert these [phenomena] are produced by obtainment but generated through arising,} then the arising [of phenomena] {not previously arisen but newly acquired} that you assert to be the defining characteristic [of arising] would be pointless. {Moreover, it would follow that distinguishing the ties (bandhana) in nine degrees of affliction — small, medium, great and so on — would be untenable because there would be no difference between obtaining their cause and simultaneously arising. It is pointless to posit obtainment as their cause, since if they were larger or smaller due to familiarity [or strength of habit] and so on, then they would arise from other causes alone [not obtainment].}

gal te thob pa rnam par 'jog pa'i rgyu yin te/ so so'i skye bo'i chos kyi thob pa dang ldan pas so so'i skye ba dang*/ 'phags pa'i chos kyi thob pa dang ldan pas 'phags pa'o/ /zhes bya ba la sogs par ro zhe na/ de ni ma yin te/ mthong spang gi nyon mongs pa la sogs pa'i sa bon spangs pa dang ma spangs pa nyid kyis 'gyur ba'i phyir thob pa don med do/ / gal te sa bon nyid thob pa yin no zhe na/ ming du 'dod na mi dgag go /don ni ma yin te/ de lta na thob pa chos rnams kyi rgyur 'gyur na de ni bkag zin to/ / gzhan yang da ltar ba'i thob pa ma 'ongs pa na 'byung bar mi 'gyur te/ de'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du rnam par byang ba'i sa bon la sogs pa la'ang sbyar bar bya'o/ / gzhan yang thob pa la'ang thob pa dang ma thob pa yod la/ ma thob pa la'ang thob pa dang ma thob pa yod do/ /zhes pa'ang rigs pa ma yin te/ thob pa la thob pa yod na thug med du 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ thob pa dngos por ma grub pas de ma thob pa'ang mi 'thad pa'i phyir dang*/ ma thob pa la thob pa 'gal ba'i phyir dang*/ ma thob pa la ma thob pa yod na'ang thug med du 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ /

Objection: (2) Obtainment is a categorizing cause, since it is said that one is an ordinary being due to obtaining ordinary qualities, one is an ārya due to obtaining ārya qualities, and so on. [140] Reply: That is not so, because one becomes an ārya, for instance, by abandoning or not abandoning the seeds of affliction to be abandoned by the path of seeing. It is meaningless to assert that this is due to obtainment. Objection: The seed itself is obtained. Reply: If that is asserted then, nominally, that is not refuted. But that is not the meaning [here] because obtainment being the cause of phenomena has already been refuted. Also, present obtainment does not occur in the future because it is the cause of future states. This should be applied as well to the seeds of purity and so on. Moreover, the statement “Obtainment has obtainment and nonobtainment. Nonobtainment has obtainment and nonobtainment” is illogical, because if obtainment has obtainment, there would be an infinite regress. And since obtainment would then not be established as a phenomenon, nonobtainment would not be tenable and the obtainment of nonobtainment would be contradictory. If nonobtainment has nonobtainment, there would also be an infinite regress.

de'i phyir chos rnams kyi sa bon dang dbang dang mngon du rgyu gsum skye bo dang 'phags pa rnams kyi rgyud la ldan pa la thob pa dang*/ mi ldan pa la ma thob pa zhes gdags kyi rdzas gzhan gyur pa ni ci yang med do/ / de la sa bon ni bag la nyal ba dang*/ dbang ni sa bon mngon du rgyu skye ba la phyogs pa dang*/ mngon du rgyu ni chos rnams kyi rang gi ngo bo yin no/ / zhes shes par bya'o/{/de yang dge ba skyes thob ni rten la log ltas sa bon nyams par mkhas pa'i phyir ldan la/ nyams na mi ldan no zhes gdags so/ / sbyor byung ni skyes pa dang rgyud la de skye ba'i dbang thogs med yod pa'i phyir ldan no/ / thogs bcas ni mi ldan no/}

Therefore obtainment is designated as the possession of (1) seeds, (2) faculties, and (3) manifest causal phenomena in the mindstreams of ordinary beings and āryas; nonobtainment is designated as the nonpossession of those. But there is no transformation of substance. One should understand that (1) seeds refers to latent states, (2) faculties awaken seeds of manifest causal phenomena, and (3) manifest causal phenomena are the individual natures of phenomena. {Further, virtue obtained from birth is possessed because it is skilled in counteracting seeds placed on that basis by wrong view. If it degenerates, it is designated as “not possessed.” [Virtue] derived from preparation is possessed because it has arisen and the capacity for it to arise in one’s mindstream is not impeded. When impeded it is not possessed.}
gnyis pa ma thob pa bshad pa ni
Nonobtainment

ma thob pa ni sems can gyi rgyud kyis bsdus pa'i chos rnams dang 'gog pa gnyis dang mi ldan pa'o/ / de yang ma rnyed pa dang*/ mi ldan pa dang*/ ye nas mi ldan pa ste/ de la ma rnyed pa ni chos de dag sngar thob pa las gsar du mi ldan pa'o/ / mi ldan pa ni de'i rgyun mi ldan pa'o/ / ye nas mi ldan pa ni so so'i skye bo la zag med kyi lam mi ldan pa lta bu'o/

Nonobtainment (aprāpti) is not obtaining phenomena conjoined with the mindstreams of sentient beings and [not obtaining] the two cessations. Further, it is (1) not acquiring, (2) not possessing, and (3) never possessing, because (1) “not acquiring” refers to not newly possessing those phenomena that were previously obtained, (2) “not possessing” refers to not possessing them continuously, and (3) “never possessing” is, for example, ordinary beings never possessing the uncontaminated path.

{ thob pa bzhin du ma thob pa la'ang dge mi dge sogs yod dam zhe na med de/ /} de lta bu'i ma thob pa'i ngo bo ni ma bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa kho na yin te/ gal te ma thob pa nyon mongs pa can{ gyi chos dang 'dra ba} yin na nyon mongs spangs pa rnams la med par 'gyur la/{ zag med kyi ma thob pa'ang zag med du 'gyur zhing*/} dge ba yin na dge rtsa chad pa rnams la med par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / zhes bye brag tu smra ba zer te/ la lar ni dge ba yin zhing*/ la lar ni nyon mongs can yin la/ la lar ni ma bsgribs lung ma bstan yin no zhes smra ba la su zhig dgag pa byed par 'gyur/ 'o na chos rnams kyi ma thob pa'ang dus gsum pa yin nam zhe na/

{Question: Is nonobtainment, like obtainment, also virtuous or nonvirtuous and so on? Reply: That is not so.} The nature of nonobtainment is {solely} an unobscured-neutral (akliṣṭāvyākṛta) state, because if it {were similar to the objects of} afflicted obtainment, those who have abandoned affliction would not have it {and those who have not obtained uncontaminated states would have uncontaminated states,} and if it were virtuous, those who have severed their root of virtue would not have it. This is asserted by the Vaibhāṣikas, for some advocate nonobtainment is virtuous, some advocate it is afflicted, some advocate it is an unobscured-neutral state. But who would bother to refute them? Question: Does the nonobtainment of phenomena occur in the three times?

khyad par yod de/ chos 'das pa dang ma skyes pa ma 'ongs pa rnams kyi ma thob pa de ni rnam pa gsum yin te/ { ma thob pa dus gsum pa de yang sdom pa lta bu la dpe brjod na so thar gyi sdom pa 'das pa de 'das pa'i gang zag des 'das par ma thob pa ni rang skyes pa'i gang zag de'i rgyud la de ma skyes gong du de'i ma thob pa skyes pa lta bu'o/ / 'das pa'i de da ltar ma thob pa ni de gtong rgyus btang ba'i skad cig gnyis par de'i ma thob pa skyes pa lta bu'o/ / 'das pa'i de ma 'ongs par ma thob pa ni de btang ba'i skad cig gnyis pa phyin chad de'i ma thob pa skyes pa rnams lta bu'o/ / so thar gyi sdom pa da ltar ba'i ma thob pa da ltar ba ni med de da ltar ba yin na de ma thob par 'gal bas so/ / de'i ma thob pa 'das pa ni de thob pa'i gang zag de'i rgyud la de ma thob pa gong du de'i ma thob pa skyes pa lta bu'o/ / de'i ma thob pa ma 'ongs pa ni de gtong rgyus btang ba'i skad cig gnyis pa la de'i thob pa btang zhing ma thob pa skyes pa lta bu'o/ / so thar gyi sdom pa ma 'ongs pa skye ba'i chos can gyi ma thob pa ma 'ongs pa ni/ ma 'ongs pa rang dang dus mnyam du sdom pa de'i ma thob pa 'byung ba lta bu'o/ / de'i ma thob pa da ltar ba ni de'i ma thob pa rang nyid da ltar bar 'phos pa lta bu'o/ / so thar gyi sdom pa ma 'ongs par ma thob pa de'i ma thob pa ma 'ongs pa ni ma thob pa ma 'ongs pa da ltar bar 'phos pa de'i skad cig gnyis pa phan chad du de'i ma thob pa byung ba rnams lta bu'o/ / de ltar du nges te/} chos 'das pa de 'das par ma thob pa dang*/ da ltar ma thob pa dang*/ ma 'ongs par ma thob pa yod pa'i phyir dang*/ ma 'ongs pa'ang de dang 'dra ba'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: There is a difference because nonobtainment of past (atīta) phenomena and unarisen (ajāta) future phenomena has three types, for {it is definite that} past phenomena are (1) not obtained in the past, (2) not obtained in the present, and (3) not obtained in the future, and future phenomena are also like that. {Nonobtainment in the three times can be illustrated by the pratimokṣa vows. (1) Nonobtainment of past pratimokṣa vows in the past by a past person is, for example, the arising of the nonobtainment of vows [141] prior to vows arising in the mindstream of that person in whom those vows will arise. (2) Nonobtainment of past vows in the present is the arising of the nonobtainment of vows in the second moment of relinquishment after having relinquished those vows. (3) Nonobtainment of past vows in the future is the arising of the nonobtainment of vows after the second moment, having relinquished those vows. (1) The present nonobtainment of present pratimokṣa vows does not exist because if [the vows are] present, it would be contradictory that they are not obtained. (2) The past nonobtainment of present vows is, for example, the arising of the nonobtainment of vows before vows are obtained in the mindstream of that person who has obtained them. (3) The future nonobtainment of present vows is, for example, the arising of the nonobtainment and the relinquishment of the obtainment of vows in the second moment of relinquishment [after] having relinquished those vows. (1) The future nonobtainment of unarisen future pratimokṣa vows is, for example, not obtaining vows at the same time in future. (2) The present nonobtainment of future vows is, for example, the nonobtainment of those vows transforming into present nonobtainment. (3) The future nonobtainment of that nonobtainment of pratimokṣa vows in the future is, for example, the nonobtainment of those after the second moment of that future nonobtainment transforming into present nonobtainment.}

gal te 'das pa'i chos 'das par ma thob pa dang*/ ma 'ongs pa'i chos ma 'ongs par ma thob pa ni mi srid de/ de dag tu chos de dag yod na ma thob par 'gal ba'i phyir ro zhe na/ dus de dag ni ring bas 'od srung gi dus na yod pa'i chos ni 'khor ba 'jig dang gser thub kyi dus su ma thob pa yod cing*/ byams pa'i dus kyi chos kyang seng gi dang rab gsal la sogs pa'i dus na ma thob pa srid pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes bya ste/ 'on kyang 'di dag ni bye brag tu smra bas rnam par brtags pa ste ri bong gi rwa la ring thung dpyod pa dang 'dra'o/ / da ltar ba'i chos kyi ma thob pa ni 'das pa dang ma 'ongs pa kho na na yod kyi da ltar ba ni ma yin te/ chos de yod na ma thob pa 'gal ba'i{ phyir dang nges par thob pa yod pa'i} phyir ro/ /

Objection: It is impossible that past phenomena are not obtained in the past or that future phenomena are not obtained in the future because if those phenomena exist at those times, it is contradictory that they are not obtained. Reply: Since their times are distant from each other, phenomena existing at the time of Kāśyapa existed as nonobtained phenomena at the time of Krakucchanda or Kanakamuni, and it is possible that phenomena of the time of Maitreya will be nonobtained phenomena at the time of Hari and Suviśada, and so on. Though these issues are investigated by Vaibhāṣikas, it is similar to analyzing the length of the horns of a rabbit! Nonobtainment of present phenomena exists only in the past and future and not in the present because if a phenomenon exists, it is contradictory that its nonobtainment exists {because its obtainment definitely exists}.
'o na ma thob pa khams gang du gtogs she na/
Question: Nonobtainment belongs to what realm?
'dod sogs gtogs dang dri med kyi'ang / / lam ma thob pa so so yi/ / skye bor 'dod do de thob dang / / 40 sa 'phos nas ni rnam nyams 'gyur/ /
It belongs to the desire realm and so on. Also the stainless path. Nonobtainment of the path is said to exist for ordinary beings. It degenerates through obtaining the path or relocating. (2:40)

'dod pa'i chos 'dod par ma thob pa ni 'dod pa dang*/ sogs pa'i sgras gzung ba{ khams gong ma gnyis su ma thob pa yang khams de dag nyid du} gzugs su ma thob pa gzugs dang*/ gzugs med par ma thob pa gzugs med par gtogs la/ de bzhin du gzugs dang gzugs med pa'i chos 'dod pa la sogs pa gsum du ma thob pa'ang de dag tu gtogs pa dang { de yang 'dod pa'i rten la 'dod pa'i chos 'dod pa'i yon tan sbyor byung dang skyes thob dang gong ma gnyis kyi yon tan sbyor byung dang zag med kyi ma thob pa'ang 'dod pas bsdus pa yin pa nas gong ma gnyis kyi yang de bzhin te/ 'di ni rten gyis gzhag gi chos kyis min te zag med kyi ma thob pa zag bcas yin pa la sogs pa chos dang 'gal bas so/ / kha cig gzugs med kyi rten la 'og ma gnyis kyis thob pa mi sbyar te de gnyis kyis thob pa mi 'jug pas so/ / zhes pa rigs so} khams sum gtogs pa dri ma med pa lam dang 'gog pa gnyis kyi ma thob pa'ang 'dod pa la sogs par gtogs so zhes sbyar ro/ /

Reply: The nonobtainment of past phenomena in the desire realm belongs to the desire realm. The term “and so on” refers to {nonobtainment in the two higher realms,} where the nonobtainment in the form realm belongs to the form {realm} and the nonobtainment in the formless realm belongs to the formless realm. Similarly, the nonobtainment of form and formless phenomena in the three realms of desire and so on belongs to those realms. {Moreover, for desire-realm beings, the nonobtainment of desire-realm phenomena and desire-realm qualities derived from preparation and obtained from birth, the qualities of higher realms derived from preparation and obtained from birth, and uncontaminated states are subsumed by the desire realm, while nonobtainment in the two higher realms is similar. These are posited in accordance with the basis, [that is, the realm,] and not the phenomena. And since the nonobtainment of uncontaminated states is contaminated, this also contradicts [that nonobtainment is posited in terms of] the phenomena. Some say: Formless beings do not engage in obtainment in the lower two realms since they do not enter obtainment in either. Reply: That is logical.} Also nonobtainment of the stainless path (amala) and the two cessations that do not belong to the three realms belongs to the desire realm and so on.
gal te zag med kyi ma thob pa ji ltar khams gsum du gtogs she na/
Question: How does the nonobtainment [142] of the uncontaminated belong to the three realms?

zag med kyi lam gyi ma thob pa ni so so'i skye bor 'dod pas zag bcas kho nar nges pa'i phyir te/ bstan bcos rab tu byed pa las so so'i skye bo nyid gang yin zhe na/ 'phags pa'i chos rnams kyis ma rnyed pa'o zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'phags pa'i chos rnams zhes bya ba'ang nyan rang dang sangs rgyas kyi rigs can rnams kyi chos gang yang ma rnyed pa yin gyi gang rung gi ni ma yin te/ gal te yin na de dag kyang so so'i skye bor 'gyur te/ nyan thos kyis rang rgyal gyi ma rnyed pa la sogs pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du 'gog pa gnyis kyi ma thob pa'ang zag bcas kho na yin te/ de gnyis ni zag med yin la/ zag med ma thob pa ni zag bcas yin pa'i phyir ro zhes bya'o/ / 'on kyang so sor brtags min gyi 'gog pa'i ma thob pa ni 'phags pa rnams la'ang yod de/ ye shes la sogs pa'i so sor brtags min gyis 'gog pa'i ma thob pa med na ye shes la sogs pa so sor brtags min gyis 'gog pa yod par 'gyur la/ de lta na'ang ye shes dang yon tan la sogs pa med par thal ba'i phyir ro/ / 'gog pa de'i ma thob pa zag bcas yin no zhes bya ba'ang ma yin te/ ye shes la sogs pa las gzhan du med pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yang zag med kyi ma thob pa zag bcas yin pa ltar zag bcas kyi ma thob pa ci'i phyir zag med du mi 'gyur te/ khyad par med pa'i phyir ro/ / zag bcas kyi ma thob pa so so'i skye bo la yod pa rnams ni khams gsum pa dang*/ 'phags pa la yod pa rnams ni 'gog pa las gzhan du med pa'i phyir ro zhes bya bar yang mi rung ste/ de ni zag med kyi ma thob pa la'ang mtshungs pa'i phyir dang zag bcas kyi ma thob pa 'gog pa gnyis yin na ma thob pa thams cad zag bcas su 'dod pa nyams pa'i phyir dang*/ gzhan yang lam gyi ma thob pa so so'i skye bo yin na de'i ma thob pa lam du ci'i phyir mi 'gyur te/ khyad par med pa'i phyir ro/ / de lta na'ang ma thob pa zag med yod do zhes nges par bya'o/ /

Reply: Nonobtainment of the uncontaminated path is definitely a contaminated state alone because it is said to exist for ordinary beings. Treatise on Designation states: What is an ordinary being? One who has not acquired ārya qualities.[549] Ordinary beings do not acquire any “ārya qualities” of the lineages of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and buddhas. It is not that some are not acquired, for otherwise āryas would become ordinary beings because sŕāvakas do not acquire qualities of pratyekabuddhas and so on. Similarly, the nonobtainment of the two cessations is solely contaminated, because although both [cessations] are uncontaminated, the nonobtainment of uncontaminated states is contaminated. However, āryas also have the nonobtainment of nonanalytical cessation, because not having the nonobtainment of the nonanalytical cessation of transcendent wisdom and so on is to have the nonanalytical cessation of transcendent wisdom and so on. But then in consequence [āryas] would not have [that] transcendent wisdom, qualities, and so on. Still it is not that “the nonobtainment of that cessation is contaminated,” because it does not exist separately from [that] transcendent wisdom and so on. Question: Just as the nonobtainment of uncontaminated states is contaminated, why isn’t the nonobtainment of contaminated states uncontaminated, for [the logic] is not dissimilar? Reply: Although you assert that it is similar to the nonobtainment of uncontaminated states, it is untenable to assert that the nonobtainment of contaminated states that belongs to ordinary beings exists in the three realms and that belonging to āryas does not exist except for cessation. Moreover, if the nonobtainment of contaminated states consists of the two cessations, then the assertion that all nonobtainment is contaminated would fail. Question: If an ordinary being is one who does not obtain the path, why doesn’t its nonobtainment become the path since [the logic] is not dissimilar? Reply: In that case one should evaluate whether they have uncontaminated nonobtainment.

so so'i skye bo de ji ltar gtong bar 'gyur zhe na/ { de yang 'og sa las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i rnam grol dgu pa las de'i so skye 'dun pa'i 'dod chags dang bral bas spong yang rnam par nyams pa ma yin la/ gong du skyes pa'i sa 'phos pas rnam par nyams pa yin yang spong ba ma yin te/ sngar spangs zin pa'i phyir ro/ / so skyes spangs na 'phags par 'gyur ro zhe na mi 'gyur te/ sa gcig gi so skye spangs kyang sa gzhan gyi so skye skye bas so/ / zhes 'chad kyang*/ byis pa'i dbang du byas kyis 'phags pa la ni lam gyi mthu kho nas so skye'i thob pa mi skye ba yin no/ / ci ma thob pa'i thob pa dang*/ thob pa'i ma thob pa'ang yod dam zhe na/ gnyis ka'ang gnyis ka yod de/ ma thob pa'i thob pa 'chad la/ thob pa 'chad pas ma thob pa skye ba'i phyir ro/ / 'o na thob pa thug med du 'gyur ro zhe na/

Question: How is the state of an ordinary being relinquished? {Reply: Due to being freed from attachment [to lower levels] through the ninth liberated [path] that frees from attachment to lower levels, the state of that ordinary being is abandoned but it doesn’t degenerate. When relocating to a higher level, [the state of that ordinary being] degenerates but it is not abandoned because it was already abandoned. Objection: If the state of an ordinary being has been abandoned, that being becomes an ārya. Reply: They do not, because though they abandon the state of an ordinary being of one level, it is said that the state of an ordinary being of another level arises. However this is from the perspective of childlike [ordinary] beings. For āryas, due to the power of the path alone, obtainment of the state of an ordinary being does not arise. Question: Does obtainment without any obtainment and nonobtainment of obtainment exist or not? Reply: Both exist for each, because when the obtainment of nonobtainment is explained, nonobtainment arises through explaining obtainment. Objection: Obtainment would become an infinite regress.

phan tshun ldan pa'i phyir mi 'gyur te/ 'di ltar so thar gyi sdom pa lta bu la thob pa'i dga' ston dper brjod na/ thob bya'i chos so thar gyi sdom pa skad cig dang po dang de'i thob pa dang thob pa'i thob pa gsum dus gcig tu skye la/ thob pas ni chos dang thob pa'i thob pa gang zag de'i rgyud la ldan par byed la/ thob pa'i thob pas rtsa ba'i thob pa kho na ldan par byed do/ / skad cig ma gnyis pa la chos gsum po de ldan par byed pa'i thob pa gsum/ thob pa gsum po ldan byed rjes kyi thob pa gsum ste drug dus gcig tu skye la chos dang bcas na dgu'o/ / skad cig gsum pa la chos dgu po ldan byed thob pa dgu de dgu ldan byed rjes thob dgu ste bco brgyad dus gcig la skye la chos dang bcas na nyer bdun no/ / skad cig bzhi pa la chos nyer bdun po ldan byed thob pa nyer bdun/ de ldan byed rjes thob nyer bdun te lnga bcu nga bzhi dus gcig tu skye la chos dang bcas na gya gcig dang*/ skad cig lnga pa la chos gya gcig po ldan byed thob pa gya gcig /de ldan byed rjes thob gya gcig ste brgya re gnyis dus gcig tu skye la/ chos dang bcas na nyis brgya zhe gsum/ sogs su 'gyur ro/ / de ltar gong nas gong du bsgres na dpag tu med do/ / de yang skad cig ma dang po'i thob pa'i tshul cung zad yin gyi/ gnyis pa sogs la rtsi na thug pa med pas sems can gcig gi thob pa 'jig rten du mi shong ba gzhan yang 'dod do/}

Reply: That does not occur because there is mutual possession. For example, in the case of the ceremony conferring pratimokṣa vows, three states arise simultaneously: (1) the first moment of pratimokṣa vows, [143] which is the object obtained, (2) the obtainment of that, and (3) the obtainment of that obtainment. By obtaining that, beings come to possess that object, and the obtainment of that obtainment, in their mindstreams. By obtaining obtainment, the root obtainment alone is possessed. In the second moment, there are nine: six including (1–3) the three obtainments that possess the three objects, (4–6) three obtainments after those three obtainments, and (7–9) the three objects that arise simultaneously. In the third moment, there are twenty-seven: eighteen including (1–9) the nine obtainments that possess those nine objects, (10–18) nine obtainments after those nine obtainments, along with (19–27) objects that arise at the same time. In the fourth moment, there are eighty-one: fifty-four including (1–27) twenty-seven obtainments that possess twenty-seven objects, (28–54) twenty-seven obtainments after those twenty-seven obtainments, along with (55–81) objects that arise at the same time. In the fifth moment, there are two hundred and forty-three: one hundred and sixty-two including (1–81) eighty-one obtainments that possess eighty-one objects, (82–162) eighty-one obtainments after those eighty-one obtainments, along with (163–243) objects that arise at the same time. If that method is applied progressively, possession is thus immeasurable. Further, the method of obtainment of the first moment is limited, but since there are limitless obtainments if the second moment and so on are calculated, it is asserted that the obtainment of one sentient being would not fit within the world.}

'phags pa'i lam de thob pa dang*/ 'dod pa nas bsam gtan dang por skye ba la sogs pa gong mar 'pho ba dang*/ srid rtse nas ci yang med par skye ba la sogs pa 'og mar skye ba'i sa 'phos nas ni so so'i skye bo rnam par nyams par 'gyur ro zhes sbyar te/ de yang 'phags pa'i lam thob pas ni khams gsum char gyi sas bsdus pa'i so so'i skye bo gtong bar 'gyur la/ sa 'phos pas ni gang nas 'phos pa de'i so so'i skye bo gtong bar 'gyur ro zhes shes par bya'o/ / 'dir yang bye brag tu smra bas sems can gyi rgyud las tha dad pa'i so so'i skye bo 'dod pa ni rigs pa ma yin te/ 'phags pa dang so so'i skye bo gnyis ka ma yin pa'i sems can srid par thal ba'i phyir dang*/ de lta bu ma dmigs pa'i yang phyir ro/ / de'i phyir 'phags pa'i lam dang mi ldan pa'i sems can gyi rgyud nyid so so'i skye bo yin te/ de nyid las dang nyon mongs pa'i dbang gis khams gsum dang*/ sa dgu dang*/ ris lngar so so so sor skye ba dang 'chi 'pho ba'i phyir te/ zla ba sgron ma'i mdo las/ so so tha dad 'gro bas na/ / so so'i skye bor brjod pa yin/ / zhes bshad pa yin no/ / des na 'phags pa'i lam dang ldan pa'i rgyud ni 'phags pa yin no/ / 'grel pa las/ gzhan dag gi yang de bzhin du sbyar bar bya'o zhes gsungs pa'i don ni 'di yin te/ khams gsum gyi dge ba sbyor byung dang skyes thob kyi ma thob pa ni dge ba de dag thob pas gtong bar 'gyur la/ khams gsum pa'i 'gro bas bsdus pa'i phung po rnams ni sa 'phos pas gtong ba yin no zhes kha cig ni rnam par phye ste 'chad do/ /

Reply: The state of an ordinary being degenerates (vihīyate) either through obtaining the ārya path or through relocating (saṃcāra) from the desire realm to a higher level by taking rebirth in the first absorption or from the summit of existence to nothingness and so on by taking rebirth in a lower level. For in obtaining the ārya path, the state of an ordinary being subsumed by the three realms is relinquished, and in changing levels, the state of an ordinary being of the level from which one transfers is relinquished. Vaibhāṣikas assert that the state of an ordinary being is distinct from the mindstream of a sentient being. Reply: This is untenable, because it would follow that the existence of sentient beings who are neither āryas nor ordinary beings would be possible, yet such beings are not observed to exist. Therefore the mindstreams of sentient beings who do not possess the ārya path are ordinary beings because they each proceed in the three realms, or the nine levels, or the five stages at birth and death due to the power of karma and affliction. The Moonlight Sūtra declares: Since each proceeds separately they are called ordinary beings.[550] Therefore the mindstream possessing the ārya path is an ārya. The Autocommentary states: That should be applied in the same way to others.[551] Some say: This means that nonobtainment of virtue derived from preparation or obtained from birth in the three realms is relinquished by obtainment of those virtues, and the aggregates subsumed by the reincarnating beings of the three realms are relinquished by changing levels.

kha cig na re de dag gis ma thob pa ni thob pa dang sa 'phos pa gnyis kas gtong ste/ bsam gtan dang po'i dge ba dang 'gro ba'i phung po ni 'dod pa na spyod pa bas ma thob la/ de ni de dag thob pa dang*/ bsam gtan dang por sa 'phos pa gnyis kas gtong ba lta bu'o zhes zer ro/ / 'on kyang sbyor ba las byung ba ma thob pa ni thob pas gtong la/ gzhan dag ni thob pa dang sa 'phos pa gnyis kas gtong ngo zhes shes par bya'o/ /

Some say: Their nonobtainment is relinquished by both obtainment and changing levels. The virtue and aggregates of reincarnating beings of the first absorption are not obtained [144] by those active in the desire realm, but [such nonobtainment] is relinquished by both obtaining those and relocating to the first absorption level. However, it should be understood that nonobtainment derived from preparation is relinquished by obtainment. Again, both obtainment and changing levels relinquish that.
gsum pa skal mnyam 'chad pa ni
Homogeneity
skal mnyam sems can 'dra ba'o/ / 'du shes med pa pa 'du shes/ / med par sems dang sems byung rnams/ / 41 'gog pa'o rnam smin de 'bras che/ /
Homogeneity causes similarity in sentient beings. The state of nondiscernment stops minds and mental factors in nondiscernment. Its karmic maturation is Bṛhatphala. (2:41)

skal ba mnyam pa ni slob dpon gang spel gyis/ g.yo ba rang bzhin mtshungs 'gyur cing*/ / bsam pa gus mtshungs sems can rnams/ / gang gis mnyam par 'gyur ba ni/ / de la skal ba mnyam zhes brjod/ / ces bshad pas sems can dang sems can gyis bsdus pa'i chos rnams kyi 'dra ba'i spyi'o/ / sems can smos pas sems can gyis ma bsdus pas lus la sogs pa la skal mnyam med par bstan pa'i phyir ro/ / skal mnyam yang gnyis te/ spyi'i skal mnyam sems can thams cad kyi spyi dang*/ bye brag gi skal mnyam mi dang lha la sogs pa'i spyi lta bu'o/ / yang na sems can gyi skal mnyam sngar smos pa de lta bu dang*/ chos kyi skal mnyam phung po dang khams dang skye mched la sogs pa'i spyi lta bu'o/ / 'di la ye shes la 'jug pa la sogs pa las ni ris mthun pa zhes bshad do/ / bye brag tu smra ba rnams na re gal te de lta bu'i skal mnyam gyi spyi med na sems can dang chos rnams la sgra dang blo mthun pa 'jug par mi 'gyur te/ rgyu mtshan med pa'i phyir ro/ / bcom ldan 'das kyis kyang*/ srog gcod pa kun du bstan pa dang goms par byas pa dang lan mang du byas pas dmyal ba dag tu skye bar 'gyur ro/ / brgya la mi rnams dang skal ba mnyam pa 'di lta bu nyid du 'ong na yang srog bcad pas tshe thung bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba la sogs pa rgya cher skal mnyam gsungs pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/

Master Pūrṇavardhana writes: That which causes uniformity in sentient beings, creating similar natures and movements, similar thoughts and [degrees of] respect, is called homogeneity.[552] Therefore homogeneity (sabhāgatā) causes the general similarity in sentient beings (sattvasāmya) and phenomena subsumed by sentient beings. “Sentient beings” indicates that homogeneity does not exist for wild rice (salu) and so on, which are not included in the class of sentient beings. There are two types of homogeneity: (1) external homogeneity, such as the general class of all sentient beings, and (2) specific homogeneity, such as the general classes of humans, gods, and so on. Again, it is, for example, (1) the homogeneity of sentient beings, as previously noted, and (2) the general homogeneity of phenomena such as aggregates, realms, and bases. The Attainment of Knowledge and so on explain that homogeneity refers to the same type. Vaibhāṣikas say: If there were no general homogeneity in sentient beings and phenomena, then language and minds would not engage them as similar states because there would be no reason for it. Also the Bhagavan extensively described homogeneity: Those who always promote killing, habitually kill, and frequently kill will be born in hell. In time, even if they are reborn among humans due to homogeneity, their lifespan will be short due to killing and so on.[553]

{ 'chi 'pho zhing skye la skal mnyam mi 'dor ba yod dam zhe na mu bzhi ste/ dang po 'chi 'pho zhing skye la skal mnyam mi 'dor ba ni sa gang nas 'chi 'phos nas sa de nyid du skyes na'o/ / gnyis pa skal mnyam 'dor la 'chi 'pho min pa ni nges pa la 'jug pa ste sems can gyi skal mnyam 'dor la 'phags pa'i skal mnyam thob pas so/ / gsum pa gnyis yin ni 'gro ba 'pho ba na'o/ / bzhi pa gnyis min ni skye 'phags gson bzhin sa gong ma'i yon tan cung zad kyang ma thob pa'i rgyun no/ / 'di ni bye brag gi 'dra ba la rtsi yi gzhan du ni mu gsum pa mi 'grub bo/ / chos las tha dad pa'i spyi rdzas grub 'dod pa/ / } de ni legs pa ma yin te/ mdo'i don ni 'gro ba ris mthun pa'i dbang du mdzad nas gsungs kyi spyi tha dad pa ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ skal mnyam{ gyi spyi} med pas sgra blo mthun pa mi 'jug nas lu la sogs pa la'ang mi 'jug par thal ba'i phyir dang*/ tha dad par snang ba'i bdag nyid ma dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ so so'i skye bo don med par thal pa'i phyir dang*/ bye brag pa'i spyi dgag pa dang mtshungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

{Question: Isn’t homogeneity destroyed through death and rebirth? Reply: There are four possibilities: (1) Homogeneity that is not destroyed through death and rebirth is, for example, those who are reborn in just that level where they died. (2) Destruction of homogeneity without death [and rebirth] is, for example, destroying homogeneity with ordinary beings[554] through attaining definite entry to the path of seeing and obtaining homogeneity with āryas. (3) Both is when reincarnating beings relocate [to another] level. (4) Neither is the continuous nonobtainment of the least quality of higher levels while living as an ordinary being or ārya. These are calculated in terms of specific similarity. For [general similarity] the third possibility is not established. Any assertion that a general class distinct from phenomena is substantially established} is not correct because this sūtra refers to reincarnating beings of the same type and not to a separate general class. That is because if language and minds do not engage compatible objects due to there being no {general class of} homogeneity, in consequence they would not even engage wild rice and so forth. Because they would not observe states that appear differently, in consequence the term “ordinary being” would be meaningless and equivalent to negating the general class of specific beings.
de'i phyir sems can dang chos ris mthun tsam la skal mnyam zhes btags kyi sems can dang chos la tha dad par ni med do/ /
Therefore homogeneity is imputed to sentient beings and phenomena that are merely of the same type, but it is not distinct from sentient beings and phenomena. [145]
bzhi pa 'du shes med pa pa bshad pa
The state of nondiscernment

['di] la 'du shes med pa pa ni 'du shes med par skyes pa'i sems can gyi rgyud la ma 'ongs pa'i sems dang sems las byung ba rnams 'gog pa'i rdzas gang yin pa'o/ / de yang re zhig skyer mi ster bar chu lon gyis chu bskyil pa ltar 'gog gi gtan du ni ma yin te/ 'gog pa gnyis dang khyad par med par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / de yang {ngo bo ni/ } 'du shes med pa'i snyoms 'jug gi{ rdzogs pa'i} rnam smin gyi 'bras bu yin gyi/ rgyas byung ni ma yin te/ gzugs can ma yin pa'i phyir ro/{ 'di'i srog dang ris mthun la sogs pa'i 'phen byed ni bzhi pa'i nyer bsdogs yin no/} de lta bu dang ldan pa'i sems can de yang 'bras bu che'i phyogs gcig na yod de/ de'i phyir bsam gtan bzhi pa'i lha yin{ pas gnas gzhan med pa yin} no/ / de la sems dang sems las byung ba thams cad du mi 'byung ngam zhe na/ skye ba dang 'chi ba na 'byung bar 'gyur te mdo las/ sems can de dag dus ring mo zhig tu 'dug 'dug ste 'du shes skyes nas gnas de nas 'chi 'pho bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba dang*/ 'di nyid las kyang*/ 'chi 'pho skye ba btang snyoms la zhes bya ba dang*/ 'chad dang mtshams sbyor 'dod chags bral/ / mnyam dang 'chi 'pho skye ba rnams/ / yid kyi rnam shes kho nar 'dod/ / ces bya ba 'di nges pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di yang lha tshe ring po'i rgyud las tha dad pa'i rdzas ni med de/ mtshungs ldan bkag pa ni dngos por 'gal ba'i phyir dang*/ ji srid du mtshungs ldan bkag pa de srid du ni gtan du bkag pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ ma 'ongs pa na skye ba rnams ni de'i dgag bya ma yin pa'i phyir{ gtan du 'gog gi} re zhig 'gog pa'ang mi 'thad do/ /

The state of nondiscernment (āsaṃjñika) is that substance that stops (nirodha) the emergence of future minds and mental factors in the mindstreams of sentient beings born in the state of nondiscernment (asaṃjñiṣu). Further, it blocks like a levy that intermittently retains and dams water, but it does not do so continuously; otherwise it would not be different from the two cessations. Moreover, {by nature} it is the result of the {complete} karmic maturation (vipāka) of the meditative attainment of nondiscernment, but it does not arise from enhancement because it is not physical. {Further, access concentration to the fourth absorption projects the life force and similarity of type of such beings,} and sentient beings who possess such karmic maturation exist in one part of Bṛhatphala (Great Result Heaven) because they are gods of the fourth absorption {who do not exist in other abodes}. Question: Don’t minds and mental factors exist there at all [times]? Reply: [Discernment] occurs at birth and death because a sūtra declares: Discernment arises, reflecting “I will die from this realm” in sentient beings who have lived there for a long time.[555] That sūtra also states: Death and rebirth possess equanimity.[556] And it should be ascertained that: Severance, linkage, freedom from attachment, degeneration, death, and rebirth exist only for mental consciousness.[557] Further, it does not exist as a substance distinct from the mindstreams of long-lived gods (1) because stopping concomitant states excludes phenomena, (2) because for as long as concomitant states are stopped for that long, they are continuously stopped, and (3) because those generated in the future are not objects to be stopped. Therefore {it continuously stops,} and it is unacceptable that it stops intermittently.

des na mdo sde pas las kyi 'phen pas lha de'i lus la bskal pa chen po lnga brgyar mtshungs ldan thams cad 'gog par 'dod la/ rnal 'byor spyod pa pa ni kun las btus las/ 'du shes med pa pa gang zhe na/ sems can 'du shes med pa'i lha rnams kyi nang du skyes pa'i sems dang sems las byung ba'i chos brtan pa ma yin pa rnams 'gog pa la 'du shes med pa pa zhes gdags so zhes 'byung bas kun gzhi dang nyon yid la tshogs drug 'khor bcas 'gog par 'dod do/ / gnyis ka ltar na'ang lus sems la mtshungs ldan bkag pa'i phyir btags pa ba yin gyi rdzas ni med do zhes bya ba yin no/ / de lta bu'i sems can de yang{ yun ring gnyid log pa las sangs pa ltar} sngon gyi las{ dang snyoms 'jug} kyi 'phen pa zad pa dang*/{ sems med pas/} las gsar pa ma bsags pa'i phyir shi 'phos nas 'dod pa kho nar skye bar 'gyur gyi gzhan du ni ma yin la/ 'dod par skye ba ni {sgra mi snyan pa la 'dod lhar skye ba'i las yod pa ltar 'dod par/ } lan grangs gzhan la myong bar 'gyur bas yin no zhes bzhed pa yin no/ /

Sautrāntikas assert that all concomitant states cease for five hundred great eons in the body of that god projected by karma. Yogācāras assert that the foundation consciousness, afflicted intellect, the sixfold collection of consciousness, and their retinue cease since the Compendium of Abhidharma says: What is the state of nondiscernment? The cessation of unstable minds and mental factors that arises in sentient beings who are gods devoid of discernment is designated as the state of nondiscernment.[558] Both assert that it is a nominal state and not substantially existent because it stops states that are concomitant with body and mind. Such sentient beings die and are reborn in the desire realm alone and not elsewhere because they exhaust the projection of prior karma {and meditative attainment, like rising from a long sleep,} and they do not accumulate new karma {since they do not possess mind}. Their birth in the desire realm is due to karma to be experienced in a third life {projecting birth in the desire realm, just as a being of the Uttarakuru continent has karma to be born as a desire-realm god}. [146]
lnga pa 'du shes med pa'i snyoms 'jug bshad pa ni
The meditative attainment of nondiscernment
de bzhin 'du shes med snyoms 'jug / bsam gtan tha mar 'byung 'dod pas/ / dge ba'o skyes nas myong 'gyur nyid/ / 42 'phags pa'i ma yin dus gcig 'thob/ /

So too the meditative attainment of nondiscernment. It belongs to the final absorption, through desire to transcend; it is virtuous, experienced after rebirth, not by āryas, obtained in one instant. (2:42)

ji ltar 'du shes med pa pa sems dang sems byung 'gog pa de bzhin du 'du shes med pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa'ang sems dang sems byung 'gog pa yin no/ / 'du shes med pa pa'i rgyun yin pa'i phyir ram/ 'di la 'bras bu 'du shes med pa yod pa'i phyir 'du shes med pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa'o/ / de yang bye brag tu smra bas snyoms 'jug de las ma langs kyi bar du mtshungs ldan rnams 'gog pa'i rdzas su yod do/ / de rdzas su med na sems dang sems byung rnams skye bar 'gyur te/ 'gog byed med pa'i phyir chu lan med pa'i rgyun ngogs su chu klung 'bab pa bzhin no/ / de bzhin du 'du shes med pa pa dang 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug la'ang shes par bya'o/ / zhes 'dod do/ / snyoms 'jug de yang sa ni bsam gtan tha ma bzhi bar gtogs pa yin la/ bsam pa ni{ 'khor ba'i} sdug bsngal las nges par 'byung ba ste thar par 'dod pas{ te snyoms 'jug la lam dang 'du shes med pa pa la thar par 'du shes pas} snyoms par 'jug go /de'i phyir kun slong gis dge ba'o/{ de yang bsam gtan gyis bsdus pa'i dge ba'o/ /}

Just as the state of nondiscernment stops minds and mental factors, so too the meditative attainment of nondiscernment (asaṃjñisamāpatti) stops minds and mental factors. It is called the “meditative attainment of nondiscernment” either because it is the cause of the state of nondiscernment or because it possesses the result of nondiscernment. Vaibhāṣikas assert that until one rises from it, it substantially exists to stop concomitant states. If it were not substantially existent, minds and mental factors would arise because there would be no agent to stop them, like a river that breaches its banks when there is no levy. The state of nondiscernment and the meditative attainment of cessation should also be understood in this way. Also this meditative attainment belongs to the level of the fourth and final absorption (dhyāna). Its motivating thought is to enter meditative attainment through the desire (iṣya) for liberation that definitely transcends (niḥsṛta) the suffering {of saṃsāra by discriminating meditative attainment to be the path and the state of nondiscernment to be liberation itself}. Therefore it is virtuous by motivation, {and that virtue is subsumed by the absorptions}.

de yang skyes nas myong bar 'gyur ba'i dge ba nyid yin te/{ skye 'chi'i sems yod pas/} 'di'i rnam par smin pa ni 'du shes med pa'i sems can gyi phung po lnga 'grub bo/ /
gang dag gis 'di thob nas nyams pa de dag kyang {de la gus pas de } gdon mi za bar sor chud par byas nas skyes pa'i phyir lan grangs gzhan la myong ba dang myong bar ma nges pa'ang ma yin la/ snyoms 'jug de dang ldan pa tshe 'di la 'du shes med par skye ba med pa'i phyir mthong chos la myong 'gyur yang ma yin no/{ de'i phyir de thob pa nges pa la mi 'jug ste 'gog pa mngon sum du mthong bar rlom pas sangs rgyas kyi'ang gdul bya min pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ /}

Moreover, it is virtue experienced after rebirth (upapadya) because its karmic maturation establishes the five aggregates of a being devoid of discernment {since it exists for the minds of birth and death}.
It is experienced in a third life, and its experience is definite because those who once obtained it, and for whom it has degenerated, without doubt regenerate it through restoring it {out of regard for it}. It is not experienced in the current life because when meditative attainment is possessed, the state of nondiscernment [or the absence of discernment] does not arise. {Therefore one should definitely not seek to obtain it because one could not even become a disciple of the Buddha due to possessing the conceit that one has directly seen cessation.}

slob dpon gang spel ni 'grel pa las/ gang zhig gis 'di bskyed nas yongs su nyams pa de yang gdon mi za bar yang bskyed nas 'du shes med pa'i sems can rnams kyi nang du skye bar 'gyur ro/ / zhes grag go zhes 'byung ba'i grag go zhes bya ba'i sgra ni lugs gzhan bstan pa'i phyir te/ gzhan dag na re skyes nas myong 'gyur dang myong bar ma nges pa'ang yin no zhes zer ro/ / des na nyams sam ma nyams kyang rung ste/ gal te dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang phrad pa las skyon du lta bar gyur na ni de nas nges pa la 'jug cing yang mi skyed cing mngon du'ang mi byed do zhes 'chad do/ / de yang gang zag ni so so skye bo kho na'i yin gyi{ thar ba de dang de'i lam mngon du gyur pa'o} 'phags pa'i ni ma yin te/ 'di las lha tshe ring por skye ba yin la/ de yang mi khom pa'i gnas yin pa'i phyir rnam par ltung ba'i gnas su gzigs pa'i phyir{ dang srid pa la thar bar 'du shes med pa'i phyir} ro/ / de'i phyir 'di la thar par 'du shes pa'i byis pa rnams kho na 'jug pa yin no/ / des na gang dag yid la byed pa thams cad bkag nas sgom pa de dag ni 'du shes med pa'i snyoms 'jug kho na yin te/ mtshan nyid thams cad tshang ba'i phyir ro//de yang 'das ma 'ongs ni mi 'thob kyi{ skad cig ma dang po la ni }dus gcig pa da ltar ba kho na 'thob ste{ 'di 'dres pa yin yang 'bad pa chen pos sgrub dgos shing} sems med pa'i phyir ro/{ 'di 'dres pa yin yang 'bad pa chen pos sgrub dgos shing*/ /}'on kyang ma btang gi bar du ni{ thob pa} 'das pa dang yang ldan te so so thar ba'i sdom pa bzhin no/{ sems med pas ma 'ongs pa ni mi 'thob bo/}

'dir yang yid la byed pa'i khyad par gyi lus sam sems la rnam shes tshogs drug bkag pa la de lta bu'i snyoms 'jug tu btags kyi lus sems las rdzas gzhan du gyur pa ni med do/ / de rdzas su med kyang yid la byed pa'i khyad par gyis mtshungs ldan rnams skye bar yang mi 'gyur te/ rtog pa thams cad nang du bsdus pa'i ting nge 'dzin bzhin no/ / de bzhin du gong 'og dag la'ang shes par bya'o/ /

Here, the mind or body that possesses special mental attention that stops the sixfold collection of consciousness is designated as such meditative attainment, but it has no substance other than the mind or body. Though it is not substantially existent, concomitant states do not arise due to this special mental attention, for it is like concentration that subsumes [or contracts] all conception. This too may be understood by consulting either the Upper or Lower Abhidharma.[560]
drug pa 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug bshad pa ni
The meditative attainment of cessation
'gog pa zhes pa'ang de bzhin nyid/ / 'di gnas don du srid rtse skyes/ / dge ba'o gnyis su myong 'gyur dang / / 43 ma nges 'phags pa'i sbyor bas 'thob/ /

That which is called “cessation” is also the same. They enter it to abide in peace. Born in the summit of existence. It is virtuous, experienced as both, indefinite, and āryas obtain it through application. (2:43)

That which is called “meditative attainment of cessation” (nirodha) is also the same as the earlier meditative attainment of nondiscernment in which minds and mental factors cease. Those with special mental attention and so on enter this meditative attainment when mental attention first engages meditative attainment to abide (vihāra) {in peace, through reflecting that peace is} the pacification of discernment and feeling. They do not enter it due to renunciation. They are born on the level of the summit of existence (bhavāgra), supported by the base of neither discernment nor nondiscernment, because it is easier to stop concomitant states at the conclusion of subtle minds; as the Abhidharmakośa states, “After the subtle of the subtle” (8:33b). {It exists on the level of the summit of existence because its karmic maturation is the establishment of the four aggregates of the summit of existence, and it exists on no other level because it is liberation, which shuns existence and engages the final mind.}

slob dpon gang spel gyis kyang*/ ci'i phyir srid rtse kho nar 'gag pa la snyoms par 'jug gi sa gzhan 'og ma dag tu ma yin zhe na/ rnam par thar pa de ni dmigs pa la rgyab kyis phyogs pa dang*/ sems mthar thug par gcod pa ste rgyu gnyis kyis bzhag na sa 'og ma rnams na de gnyis med pa'i phyir ro zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di sde pa gzhan gyis bsam gtan bzhi pa'i sa par 'dod pa ni ma yin te/ bcom ldan 'das kyis bsam gtan bzhi dang gzugs med bzhi dang 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug rnams mthar gyis gnas pa'i snyoms 'jug tu gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Master Pūrṇavardhana explains: Why is the meditative attainment of cessation only found at the summit of existence and not at other, lower levels? It is liberation that is established by two causes — shunning focal objects and severing the final mind — and those two do not exist on lower levels.[561] Other schools assert: [the meditative attainment of cessation exists] on the fourth absorption. Reply: This is not correct because the Bhagavan stated that the four absorptions, the four formless states, and the meditative attainment of cessation are meditative attainments that arise in sequence.

{'phags pa rnams nyon mongs can nam lung ma bstan la zhi bar mi 'dzin pas } ngo bo ni kun slong gis dge ba'o/{ 'di dge ba zag bcas yin par 'dod pas/ /}myong 'gyur ni skyes nas myong 'gyur dang*/ lan grangs gzhan la myong 'gyur zhes bya ba gnyis su myong bar 'gyur ba dang*/ myong bar ma nges pa gsum du 'gyur gyi mthong ba'i chos la myong 'gyur ni ma yin te/ 'di'i rnam smin srid rtse'i ming bzhi'i phung po yin la/ 'dod gzugs su skyes pa dag skye ba de la der skye ba mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / de la skyes nas myong 'gyur ni 'dod pa'i 'phags pa dag de thob nas ma nyams par srid rtser 'gro ba'o/ / lan grangs gzhan la myong 'gyur ni 'dod par thob pa nyams pa dag gzugs khams su mngon du byas te srid rtser 'gro ba'o/ / myong bar ma nges pa ni de gnyis ka 'dod gzugs su dgra bcom pa thob par byed pa'o/ / gang zag ni 'phags pa'i yin gyi byis pa'i skye bo'i ni ma yin te/ mdo las/ yang srid med pas gnod 'gyur te/ / g.yang sa dag gis byis pa bzhin zhes 'byung bas{ srid rtse thob pa'i byis pa ni sems kyi rgyud la bdag tu zhen pa bkag na} bdag chad du dogs pas 'jigs pa'i phyir dang*/ 'phags pa'i lam gyi stobs kyis bskyed par bya ba yin pa'i phyir dang*/ mthong ba'i chos la mya ngan las 'da' bar nus pa'i phyir mi 'ong dang dgra bcom dag ni 'gog pa 'di la mos pa'i phyir dang*/ so so'i skye bo ni de lta bu yang ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

{Since āryas do not hold afflicted or neutral states to be peace,} it is virtuous (śubha) by nature. {Since it is asserted to be contaminated virtue,} it is experienced as both (dvivedhā) karma to be experienced after rebirth and karma to be experienced in a third life, along with the third type whose experience is not definite. It is not experienced in this life because its karmic maturation consists of the four aggregates of the summit of existence, and it is impossible for those born in the desire or form realms [148] to be born there in this life. “Karma to be experienced after rebirth” occurs when desire-realm āryas have obtained [the meditative attainment of cessation], that obtainment does not degenerate, and they proceed to the summit of existence. “Karma to be experienced in a third life” occurs when beings obtain the meditative attainment of cessation in the desire realm, it then degenerates, but then it manifests again in the form realm and they proceed to the summit of existence. Karma whose experience is indefinite (niyatā) occurs when arhats in the desire or form realms obtain both. That person is an ārya and not a childlike being because {when childlike beings who obtain the summit of existence stop the conception of a self in their mindstreams,} they are afraid since they think that they have annihilated the self, as indicated in a sūtra: Like childlike beings experiencing vacant space, they are harmed [or frightened] thinking there is no rebirth.[562] Such beings are āryas because that [cessation] is produced by the power of the ārya path. Nonreturners and arhats capable of transcending sorrow in this life resolve to attain such cessation but ordinary beings cannot do this.

de'i phyir slob dpon 'dun bzang gis kyang srid rtse'i mthong spang ma spangs par der 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug bskyed mi nus la/ so so'i skye bos ni de spangs pa ma yin pa'i phyir ro zhes bshad do/ / des na 'phags pa'ang thams cad kyis 'di la snyoms par 'jug mi nus te/ 'di ni srid rtse'i sems la brten nas 'jug na 'phags pa chags bcas dang*/ phyir mi 'ong kha cig dang*/ shes rab kyis rnam par grol ba'i dgra bcom pa rnams kyis ni srid rtse'i sems ma thob pa'i phyir ro/ / de nyid kyi phyir sa'i dngos gzhi las kyang 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug la chos gnyis gces spras byed pa yin te/ zhi gnas dang lhag mthong ngo*/ / de la zhi gnas ni 'dir mthar gyis gnas pa'i snyoms 'jug brgyad yin la/ lhag mthong ni 'phags pa'i shes rab yin te/ de gnyis las gcig med na snyoms par 'jug tu mi rung ba'i phyir gnyis ka tshogs na gces spras byed par 'gyur ro zhes bshad do/ / des na phyir mi 'ong srid rtse'i sems thob pa dang*/ gnyis ka'i cha las rnam par grol ba'i dgra bcom pa ni mthong ba'i chos la zhi ba'i 'gog pa lus kyis mngon sum du byed nus pa yin pas de dag dang*/ rang rgyal dang byang chub sems dpa' sa drug pa yan chad dang sangs rgyas rnams kyis 'di la snyoms par 'jug nus so/ / 'phags pa'i yang sems kyi stobs bskyed pa'i sbyor bas 'thob kyi 'dod chags dang bral ba tsam gyis ni ma yin te/ de'i phyir {yongs su nyams nas skyed na yang sngon med pa kho na dus gcig 'thob ste } so so thar pa'i sdom pa bzhin du da ltar ba kho na 'thob kyi 'das ma 'ongs ni mi 'thob bo/ / 'o na 'phags pa thams cad kyi sbyor bas 'thob bam zhe na/

Therefore Master Saṅghabhadra explains: If that to be abandoned by the path of seeing belonging to the summit of existence is not abandoned, the meditative attainment of cessation cannot be generated there. Ordinary beings have not abandoned it.[563] Moreover, not all āryas can enter the meditative attainment of cessation because it is entered dependent on the mind of the summit of existence, and āryas with attachment, some nonreturners, and arhats liberated by wisdom do not obtain the mind of the summit of existence. Therefore Yogācāra Levels explains: In the meditative attainment of cessation, two things are valued: calm abiding and insight. Calm abiding consists of the eight meditative attainments (samāpatti), which abide in a series. Insight is ārya wisdom. Since the meditative attainments are not possible if either does not exist, the union of both is highly valued.[564] Therefore nonreturners who obtain the mind of the summit of existence, arhats liberated from both aspects who are able to physically manifest pacifying cessation in this life, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas on the sixth level and above, and buddhas are able to enter the meditative attainment of cessation. Further, āryas obtain it through application (prayoga), which awakens mental force, and not through merely being free from attachment. {Even though it is regenerated after it has degenerated, it will be obtained in one instant alone without having previously existed} and obtained in the present alone, like pratimokṣa vows, and not obtained in the past or future. Question: Do all āryas obtain it by preparation?
thub pa'i byang chub kyis thob bya/ / dang por ma yin skad cig ma/ / sum cu rtsa bzhis thob phyir ro/ / 44 gnyis ka 'dod dang gzugs rten can/ / 'gog pa dang por mi'i nang du/ /

He did not manifest it first because he obtained enlightenment through the thirty-four moments. Both [meditative attainments] possess support in desire- and form-realm beings. Cessation is first manifested among humans. (2:44)

{de ni nyan rang gi tshul lo dmigs bsal ni } thub pa'i ni zad pa mkhyen pa thob pa na de dang dus mnyam du brnyes pas na {srid rtse la 'dod chags dang bral bas thob par bya ba yin pas/ dus ni 'jug sems kyi 'phen pa ltar te/ 'gog snyoms la zhugs dus su 'chi ba med kyang langs ma thag 'chi bas/ 'dod par kham zas kyi nus pa gtugs par 'gyur bas zhag bdun las lhag par mi 'jug la/ gong mar ji ltar 'dod pa ltar ro } byang chub kyis 'thob par bya ba yin gyis sbyor bas ni ma yin te/ yon tan thams cad la rtsol ba med pa'i phyir te/ thams cad mkhyen pa grub par/ bstod pa las/ dge ba mthar phyin khyod la ni/ / sbyor ba las byung cung zad med/ / khyod ni gang du bzhed nges pa/ / bzhed pa tsam la rag las lags/ / zhes bshad pa lta bu'o/ / gal te thub pas zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa mngon du byas pa'i tshe 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug thob pa yin gyi mngon du byas pa ma yin na de gnyis ka'i cha las rnam grol ma yin par 'gyur te/ 'gog pa mngon du ma byas par snyoms 'jug gi sgrib pa las mi grol ba'i phyir ro zhe na/

Reply: {That is the method of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. The exception is that} the Sage acquired the meditative attainment of cessation when he obtained the wisdom of elimination. {The summit of existence is obtained [149] through freedom from attachment, and the duration of the meditative attainment depends on the projection of the engaging mind. Though one cannot die while engaged in the meditative attainment of cessation, one can die immediately upon rising from it. Therefore one should not engage it for more than seven days since that is the limit of the potency of oral food in the desire realm, and this accords with the former assertion.} The Sage did not obtain it through [engaging in] preparation since he obtained it through enlightenment (bodhi) because he obtained all qualities without exertion through establishing omniscience. Praise of the Buddha Beyond All Praise explains: You have perfected virtue that is not derived from the least preparation. Whatever you desire is definitely accomplished reliant on your mere wish.[565] Objection: If the meditative attainment of cessation were obtained but not manifested when the Sage manifested knowledge of elimination and nonarising, it would not be liberation from both parts, because without manifesting cessation he would not be liberated from obscuration to meditative attainment.

'di la kha che'i nub phyogs na 'khod pa'i bye brag tu smra ba dag na re thub pas byang chub kyi shing drung du bsam gtan bzhi pa'i sems la brten nas mthong lam bskyed cing*/ de'i rjes la srid rtse'i sems la brten nas 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug bskyed la/ de las langs nas bsam gtan bzhi pa'i sems la brten te srid rtse'i sgom spang rnams spangs te zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa mngon du byas pa'i phyir gnyis ka'i cha las rnam grol yin te/ gnas brtan nye bsrungs kyi lugs kyi tshig gi bstan bcos la/ de bzhin gshegs pa ni 'gog pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa bskyed nas zad pa mkhyen pa bskyed par mdzad do zhes brjod par bya'o zhes bshad pa'i phyir zhes zer ro/ /

Vaibhāṣikas living to the west of Kāśmīr [i.e., Western Vaibhāṣikas] say: At the foot of the bodhi tree, the Sage generated the path of seeing dependent on the mind of the fourth absorption. After that he generated the meditative attainment of cessation dependent on the mind of the summit of existence. Having arisen from that, he abandoned objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation of the summit of existence dependent on the mind of the fourth absorption and manifested knowledge of elimination and nonarising. He was liberated from both aspects, because the Treatise on Words of the system of the elder Uparakṣita notes: The Tathāgata, having generated the meditative attainment of cessation, generated the realization of elimination.[566]

kha che ba na re zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa'i dang por te sngon du ni 'gog pa mngon du byas pa ma yin te/ ci'i phyir zhe na/ byang chub sems dpa' ni stan gcig kho na la bar chad med pa dang rnam grol gyi lam gyi ye shes skad cig ma sum cu rtsa bzhi rgyun chags su bskyed nas byang chub 'thob pa'i phyir ro/ / sum cu rtsa bzhi ni mthong lam la bar chad med pa dang rnam grol gyi ye shes skad cig ma bcu drug dang*/ srid rtse'i sgom spang dgu spang ba'i phyir sgom lam bar chad med pa dang rnam grol gyi ye shes skad cig ma bco brgyad de/ 'og sa brgyad kyi mthong spang dang sgom spang rnams ni de bzhin gshegs pa chags bral sngon 'gro yin pas ring 'phur lhag phad kyi drung du sngar nyid du 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis spangs zin pa'i phyir de dag gi gnyen po ni 'dir mi bskyed do/ / 'dod pa'i mthong spang sngar spangs zin pas da spang du med pa'i phyir chos bzod bskyed mi dgos par thal lo zhe na de spangs kyang chos bzod chos shes brgyad bskyed pa ni chos shes phyogs kyi mthong lam med par rjes shes phyogs kyi mthong lam skye mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin gshegs pa gnyis ka'i cha las rnam grol ni{ yin te 'gog snyoms bskyed pa'i gegs dang bral bas} 'gog pa mngon du byas pa dang 'dra bar mnga' brnyes pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/{ mthong sgom gyi bar du 'gog pa bskyed na byang chub ma thob kyi bar du zag pa med pa'i lam las mi ldang bar bya'o zhes dam bcas pa'i dam bca' dang 'gal zhing bsam pa ldang ba can du 'gyur ro zhes so/ /}

Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas say: He did not manifest cessation first before the knowledge of elimination and nonarising. Why? Because the bodhisattva obtained enlightenment through progressively generating the thirty-four moments (kṣaṇa) of transcendent wisdom of the uninterrupted and liberated paths in just one sitting. The thirty-four moments are (1–16) the sixteen moments of uninterrupted and liberated transcendent wisdom of the path of seeing, and (17–34) the eighteen moments of uninterrupted and liberated transcendent wisdom of the path of meditation, which abandons the nine objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation of the summit of existence. The Tathāgata was previously freed from attachment because he had previously abandoned objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing and objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation of the eight lower levels through the mundane path in the presence of Alārā Kālāma and Udraka Rāmaputra.[567] Therefore he did not generate their antidote at this time. Objection: Since he previously abandoned desire-realm objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing, it follows he would not need to generate Dharma perseverance (dharmakṣānti) because he did not abandon them at this time. Reply: Though he had abandoned them, he generated the eight types of Dharma perseverance and Dharma knowledge (dharmajñāna) because it is impossible that subsequent knowledge (anvayajñāna) on the path of seeing arises without Dharma knowledge on the path of seeing. It is said that a tathāgata is liberated from both aspects because he acquires control [150] over a state similar to manifest cessation {since he is free of the impediments to developing the meditative attainment of cessation}. {If he were to generate cessation while meditating on the paths of seeing and meditation, that would contradict his pledge that “I will not arise from the uncontaminated path until I obtain enlightenment,” and he would become one who has discarded his intended action.}
