nub phyogs pa rnams na re skad cig ma sum cu rtsa bzhi rgyun ma chad par bskyed pa'i phyir zhes bya ba ni ma grub ste/ mthong sgom gyi lam gyi bar du 'gog pa zhugs pa'i phyir ro/ / de dag rim par goms pas byang chub thob pa'i phyir zhes bya ba ni ma nges pa yin no zhes zer ro/ / kha che ba rnams na re 'gog pas bar chod na byang chub sems dpa' bsam pa ldang ba can du 'gyur ro zhes zer ro/ / nub phyogs pa ni mi 'gyur te/ lung gzhi las ji srid zag pa zad pa ma thob kyi bar du skyil mo krung gzhig par mi bya'o zhes dam bcas par gsungs kyi zag med kyi lam las mi ldang bar ni ma yin pa'i phyir skyon med do zhes lan 'debs par byed do/{ mdo las kyang*/ stan 'dir bdag gi lus 'di bskams kyang rung*/ / pags pa rus pa'i tshogs rnams zhig kyang rung*/ / bskal mang rnyed dka'i byang chub ma rnyed bar/ / stan 'di las ni lus skyod mi bya'o/ / zhes gsungs pas so/ / slob dpon gyi bzhed pa ni/ /} 'grel pa las ni/ snga ma kho na yin no zhes brjod de zhes 'byung bas bar du 'gog pa ma bskyed kyi zad pa mkhyen pa dang dus mnyam du brnyes pa nyid rigs so zhes bya ba'o/ { snyoms 'jug 'di gnyis khyad par ni mang ste/ sa ni bsam gtan bzhi pa dang srid rtse/ yid byed nges 'byung dang gnas pa/ rten so skye dang 'phags pa/ 'bras bu 'du shes med pa dang srid rtse las myong bar nges pa dang gnyis ka /dang por skye ba la'ang khams gnyis dang mir skyed pa'i khyad par yod do/ /

Western Vaibhāṣikas say: The thirty-four moments are not generated in an unbroken stream because the bodhisattva enters cessation during the paths of seeing and meditation. Therefore the statement that “enlightenment is obtained through progressively cultivating those” is not definitive. Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas say: If cessation interrupts that meditation, a bodhisattva would arise from contemplation. Western Vaibhāṣikas say: That would not occur, because the Chapters on Vinaya mentions the pledge: “Until I obtain the elimination of contaminants, I will not rise from the vajra crossed-legged position.”[568] Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas respond that there is no error because they don’t arise from the uncontaminated path.[569] {Also, a sūtra states: Though my body may wither on this seat and the aggregate of my skin and bones disintegrate, until I acquire enlightenment difficult to acquire for many eons, my body will not move from this seat.[570] Vasubandhu} declares in the Autocommentary: It is just the former.[571] Therefore it is logical that cessation is not developed in that intermediate period, and it is acquired at the same time as the realization of elimination. {There are many differences between the two meditative attainments [of nondiscernment and cessation] because their levels are, respectively, (1) the fourth absorption and (2) the summit of existence; their attention is focused on, respectively, (1) renunciation and (2) abidance [in peace]; their supports are, respectively, (1) an ordinary being and (2) an ārya; and their results are, respectively, (1) the definite experience of nondiscernment and (2) the summit of existence. Also, when they first arise they are different, respectively, in being generated (1) in the two realms and (2) in the human [realm].

nyan thos gzugs med 'gog pa la mi 'jug ste der skyes pa'i 'phags pa la mtshungs ldan ma zhi ba med pas/ ma zhi ba'i tshor 'dus mi skye zhing*/ so skye la sems sems byung 'gags na mi ldan pa'i 'du byed 'ba' zhig gnas pa'i mthu med pas/ de la zhugs na lhag med du 'da' bar thal ba las myong nges kyi las 'bras bu ma rdzogs par mya ngan las 'da' mi srid de las de gegs kyi ngo bor gnas pas so/ / yang na rten med pas mi 'jug ste/ srog ni yang na gzugs dang yang na sems la brten nas 'jug na der 'gog pa la zhugs na de rgyun chad par 'gyur bas so zhes 'dod do/ /}

Śrāvakas do not enter formless cessation because śrāvaka āryas who are born there are not distressed by unpacified feeling and discernment since they do not have unpacified concomitant states. Śrāvaka ordinary beings do not enter cessation since they lack the capacity to remain with nonassociated formative factors alone when minds and mental factors have stopped, and if they were to enter cessation it would follow they would enter remainderless transcendence, but nirvāṇa is impossible without experiencing the results of karma that must be experienced and they remain impeded by the nature of such karma. Again, they do not enter [cessation] since [such beings] have no supportive basis for [cessation], for if they entered [cessation] on the basis of their lifeforce, form, or mind, their mindstreams would be severed when they enter cessation.}
'o na snyoms 'jug lus gang la brten pa yin zhe na/
Question: Meditative attainment is supported on what body?

snyoms 'jug gnyis ka 'dod pa dang gzugs kyi khams pa'i rten can yin gyi gzugs med pa'i ni ma yin te/ dgag gzhi med pa'i phyir dang*/ 'du shes med pa'i snyoms 'jug bsam gtan bzhi pas bsdus pa'i phyir dang*/ 'gog pa ni 'du shes dang tshor ba rags pas skyo bas yin na gzugs med pa ni zhi bar gnas pas de dag gis skyo ba med pa'i phyir ro/ / rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las/ skye ba las ni kun gzhi rnam shes rnam par ma bzhag na ni dang por 'dir skyed cing de'i 'og tu gzugs kyi khams su mngon du byed de/ mngon du byed pa de ni gzugs kyi lus la rags las pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / kun gzhi rnam shes rnam par bzhag na ni mngon du byed pa khams gsum thams cad du 'gro ba yin par lta bar bya'o zhes 'byung bas rnal 'byor spyod pa pa gang dag kun gzhi rnam shes nyid dgag gzhir 'dod pa de dag gi ltar na ni 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug gzugs med kyi khams su'ang mngon du byed do/ /

Reply: Both meditative attainments possess support (āśraya) in desire- and form-realm beings. They do not possess support in formless-realm beings, who possess no basis to be negated, [for two reasons:] (1) the meditative attainment of nondiscernment is subsumed by the fourth absorption, and (2) cessation is due to disgust with coarse discernment and feeling, whereas those abiding in the peace of the formless realm have no such disgust. According to Yogācāras who assert [the meditative attainment of cessation] to be a basis of negation of foundation consciousness, meditative attainment of cessation also manifests in the formless realm since the Compendium of Ascertainment mentions: If foundation consciousness is not posited distinct from birth, it would first be generated here and then it would manifest in the form realm, because its manifestation would rely on a form-realm body. If foundation consciousness is posited [distinct from birth] [151] you should view its manifest state as functioning in all three realms.[572]

khyad par ni 'di yod de 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug ni sngar ma thob pa dag gis dang por mngon du byed pa ni mi'i nang du yin te/ sngar ma 'dris pas bskyed dka' la mi blo gsal ba'i phyir ro/ / de thob nas nyams pa dag gis ni phyis gzugs kyi khams su'ang mngon du byed do/{ kha cig 'gog snyoms ni myang 'das dang 'dra bas nyams pa mi srid par 'dod kyang mi bshad de/ /} slob dpon gang spel gyis kyang 'gog pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa ni dang po mi kho na'i nang du bskyed de/ ston pa po dang 'chad pa po dang sbyor ba'i stobs yod pa'i phyir ro/ / phyis nyams pa ni gzugs su yang bskyed la/ gzugs med du ni ma yin te/ rten med pa'i phyir ro/ / 'du shes med pa'i snyoms 'jug ni dang po gzugs kyi khams su yang bskyed de/ 'khor ba thog ma med pa nas 'dris pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes bshad cing*/ 'char byed kyi mdo las kyang tshe dang ldan pa shA ri'i bus/ dge slong rnams la smras pa/ tshe dang ldan pa dag 'di na dge slong tshul khrims phun sum tshogs pa yang yin/ ting nge 'dzin phun sum tshogs pa yang yin/ shes rab phun sum tshogs pa yang yin pa de ni yang dang yang du 'du shes dang tshor ba 'gog pa la snyoms par 'jug pa dang ldang ba'i gnas de yod do zhes bya bar yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du rab tu shes so/ / de ni mthong ba'i chos kho na la dang po nyid du kun shes pa'i chos thob par yang mi byed cing*/ 'chi ba'i dus kyi tshe yang ma yin la/ lus zhig nas kyang kham gyi zas za ba'i lha las 'das te yid las byung ba'i lha'i lus gang yang rung ba zhig tu skye bar 'gyur ro/ / de der skyes nas yang dang yang du 'du shes dang tshor ba 'gog pa la snyoms par 'jug pa dang ldang ba'i gnas de yod do/ / zhes bya bar yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du rab tu shes so zhes gsungs pa'i phyir te/ 'di la kun shes pa'i chos ni dgra bcom pa'o/ / kham gyi zas za ba'i lha ni 'dod pa'i lha rnams so/ / yid las byung ba'i lha'i lus ni gzugs kyi khams pa'i lha rnams so/ /

In particular, it exists, in that those who have not previously obtained the meditative attainment of cessation (nirodha) first manifest it among humans (nṛṣu), because those without prior familiarity have difficulty manifesting it, and humans have clarity of mind. For those who previously obtained it but for whom it has degenerated, it later manifests in the form realm. {Some assert: Since the meditative attainment of cessation is like nirvāṇa, its degeneration is impossible. Reply: That is not so, because} Master Pūrṇavardhana also explains: The meditative attainment of cessation is first generated only among humans because they have instructors, expositors, and the capacity for application. Though it later degenerates, it is generated in the form realm but not the formless realm, because there is no support for it there. The meditative attainment of nondiscernment is first generated in the form realm, where beings are familiar with it from beginningless saṃsāra.[573] The Udayana Sūtra says: Venerable Śāriputra said to the monks: “Venerables, you should correctly understand how frequently abiding in and rising from this meditative attainment that stops discernment and feeling is excellent discipline for monks as well as excellent concentration and excellent wisdom.[574] It manifests in this life alone, it is not taken as the primary object to be obtained — namely, the state of complete knowledge — and it does not exist at the time of death. After disintegration of the body, due to cultivating it one surpasses the gods who eat oral food and one takes birth among gods whose bodies are derived from the mind. Having been born there, one frequently enters and rises from the meditative attainment that stops discernment and feeling. You should understand this correctly.[575] “The state of complete knowledge” refers to the state of an arhat, “gods who eat oral food” refers to desire-realm gods, and “gods whose bodies are derived from the mind” refers to form-realm gods.

gal te 'dod par 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug thob pa ma nyams na srid rtser skye ba'i phyir gzugs kyi khams su skyes nas 'gog pa mngon du byed par ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/ nyams pa sor chud par byed par 'gyur ro/ / 'o na 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug las nyams pa yod na 'phags pa la nyams pa yod par 'gyur te/ 'di ni 'phags pa kho nas mngon du byed pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ bye brag tu smra ba ni 'phags pa la'ang nyams pa yod par 'dod de/ mdo sde pa ni 'phags pa'i lam la nyams pa med kyi mdo'i don ni srid rtse'i sems dang 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug las nyams pa yod par bshad pa yin no zhes bya bar 'dod do/ / 'du shes med pa'i snyoms 'jug ni dang po mngon du byed pa'ang 'dod gzugs gnyis kar mngon du byed la/ nyams pa sor chud pa'ang so sor yin 'dod par nyams pa gzugs su sor chud pa dang*/ bsam gtan dang por nyams pa gnyis pa la sogs par mngon du byed pa ni med de/ myong bar ma nges pa dang*/ lan grangs gzhan la myong 'gyur du thal ba'i phyir ro/ / rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las ni 'du shes med pa'i snyoms 'jug ni dang por 'dir bskyed cing*/ de'i 'og tu gzugs khams su bsam gtan bzhi par 'bras bu myong bar 'gyur ro zhes dang po 'dod pa kho nar bskyed par yang bshad do/ / kha cig gis 'du shes med pa'i snyoms 'jug gzugs khams su mi 'dod pa ni mi rigs te/ ye shes la 'jug pa las/ gzugs kyi srid pa yin pa de rnam par 'drid pa can lnga ma yin pa yod de/ gzugs na spyod pa'i sems can lha 'du shes can sems mi 'dra ba la gnas pa rnams 'du shes med pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa dang*/ 'gog pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa la snyoms par zhugs pa rnams dang*/ lha 'du shes med pa 'du shes med pa pa thob pa rnams kyi srid pa gang yin pa lta bu'o zhes gsungs te/ 'di la rnam par 'drid pa can lnga zhes bya ba ni nye bar len pa'i phung po lnga ste/ 'dun pa dang 'dod chags dang ldan pa'i phung po lnga ni dbu brdos pa la sogs pas pa dang 'dra bas byis pa rnams 'drid cing slu ba'i phyir sangs rgyas 'od srung gi dus na phung po lnga la ming de skad du grags so/ / sems mi 'dra ba ni sems med mngon du byas pa yin la/ 'dra ba ni zag bcas kyi sems yod pa'i tshe yin no/ /

Question: If the obtainment of the meditative attainment of cessation in the desire realm does not degenerate, then because one will take birth in the summit of existence how does one manifest cessation through taking birth in the form realm? Reply: One must restore the degenerated state. Objection: If the meditative attainment of cessation degenerates, then the ārya state would also degenerate, because only āryas manifest it. Vaibhāṣikas assert that degeneration also exists for āryas. Sautrāntikas assert that āryas do not degenerate. And they explain that the [Udayana] Sūtra speaks [only] of degeneration from the summit of existence [152] and the meditative attainment of cessation. When the meditative attainment of nondiscernment first manifests, it manifests in both the desire and form realms. But restoration of the degenerated state is specific, for degeneration in the desire realm is restored in the form realm, and degeneration in the first absorption does not manifest in the second absorption and so on. Otherwise, in consequence, its result would not definitely be experienced [in one’s next life] or it would be experienced in a third life. The Compendium of Ascertainment remarks: The meditative attainment of nondiscernment is first generated here. After that the result is experienced in the fourth absorption of the form realm.[576] This explains that it is first generated in the desire realm alone. Some say: It is illogical not to assert that the meditative attainment of nondiscernment exists in the form realm, because the Attainment of Knowledge notes: [The first possibility:] The possibility of being a form-realm god and one who does not possess the five beguilers exists. For example, there are gods active in the form realm who possess discernment and abide with atypical minds who then (1) enter the meditative attainment of nondiscernment or (2) enter the meditative attainment of cessation. (3) And there are gods who are devoid of discernment who obtain the state of nondiscernment.[577] The five appropriated aggregates are called “the five beguilers” because the five aggregates that are objects of aspiration and attachment beguile (vañcana) and deceive childlike beings like bubbles in water and so on. The five aggregates were known by this name at the time of Kāśyapa Buddha. “Atypical minds” refers to manifest mindless states, and “typical minds” refers to minds when they are contaminated.

kha cig sems mi 'dra ba la gnas pa rnams dang zhes 'don cing sems 'dra ba dang mi 'dra ba ni zag bcas dang zag med la 'dod do/ / des na gzugs na spyod pa'i sems can lha 'du shes can sems mi 'dra ba snyoms 'jug gnyis la gnas pa'i srid pa ni sems med yin pa'i phyir dang*/ 'du shes med pa'i lha 'du shes med pa pa thob pa la'ang sems med pa'i phyir rnam par 'drid pa can lnga ma yin te/ de dag gsum ga la'ang zag bcas mtshungs ldan gyi phung po bzhi med pa'i phyir ro/ / gzugs kyi srid pa ni yin pa'i phyir mu dang po yin te des na de lta bu'i bstan bcos dang 'gal lo/ / mu gzhan ni de nyid las rnam par 'drid pa can lnga'i srid pa yin la gzugs kyi srid pa ma yin pa ni 'dod pa na spyod pa'i sems can sems 'dra ba la gnas pa rnams kyi srid pa gang yin pa lta bu'o/ / gzugs kyi srid pa'ang yin la srid pa de rnam par 'drid pa can lnga'ang yin{ pa'i mu gsum} pa ni gzugs na spyod pa'i lha 'du shes can sems 'dra ba la gnas pa rnams dang*/ 'du shes med pa'i lha rnams kyi 'du shes med pa pa ma thob pa rnams kyi srid pa gang yin pa lta bu'o/ / gzugs kyi srid pa'ang ma yin la srid pa de rnam par 'drid pa can lnga'ang ma yin{ pa'i mu bzhi} pa'ang yod de/ 'dod pa na spyod pa'i sems mi 'dra ba la gnas pa rnams 'du shes med pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa dang 'gog pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa la snyoms par zhugs pa rnams kyi srid pa gang yin pa dang*/ gzugs med pa rnams kyi srid pa gang yin pa lta bu'o zhes gsungs te/ 'du shes med pa'i lha 'du shes med pa pa ma thob pa ni der skye ba dang 'chi ba'i tshe sems 'byung bas de la zag bcas kyi phung po lnga yod pa'i phyir ro snyam du dgongs pa'o/ /

Some assert: The statement “abide with atypical minds . . .” indicates that typical and atypical minds refer to contaminated and uncontaminated minds. Therefore, the [first] possibility is a form-realm god with discernment and atypical minds who then enters either meditative attainment but does not possess the five beguilers because he has no mind; and a god devoid of discernment who obtains the state of nondiscernment but does not possess the five beguilers because he has no mind. And that is because these three[578] do not possess the four contaminated, concomitant aggregates. Because they are the possibility of being form-realm gods, this constitutes the first possibility. However [your initial assertion[579]] contradicts this treatise. Regarding the four possibilities, this treatise continues: [The second possibility:] The possibility of being one who possesses the five beguilers but not the possibility of being a form-realm god is, for example, any sentient being existing in the desire realm who is a being abiding with typical minds. {The third possibility} is a form-realm god who also possesses the five beguilers, for example, a divine sentient being existing in the form realm with typical minds possessing discernment, but who is a [153] being who does not obtain the state of nondiscernment among the gods who possess nondiscernment. {The fourth possibility} is one who is not a form-realm god and who does not possess the five beguilers, for example, those abiding with atypical minds active in the desire realm who are beings entering the meditative attainment of nondiscernment or cessation, or any formless-realm being.[580] It is considered that gods devoid of discernment who do not obtain the state of nondiscernment have five contaminated aggregates, since the mind occurs when they are born or die there.

gal te 'gog pa 'di dag sems med yin na rjes kyi sems rgyu med par 'gyur ro zhe na/ bye brag tu smra ba 'das pa'ang rdzas su grub pa'i phyir 'das pa'i sems{ snyoms 'jug gi de ma thag rkyen} las skye bar 'dod la/ mdo sde pa lus sems phan tshun sa bon can yin pas dbang po dang bcas pa'i lus la sems kyi sa bon yod pa'i phyir de las skye bar 'dod med kyi bye brag tu smra ba la 'das pa'i sems de'i rgyud la yod na sems med de dag la mtshungs ldan thams cad bkag pa ma yin par thal ba'i phyir dang*/ de'i rgyud la med na 'das pa rdzas su ma grub par 'gyur ro zhes brjod par bya'o/ / sde pa gzhan la'ang sems kyi sa bon sems su 'dod na mtshungs ldan thams cad bkag pa ma yin par 'gyur zhing*/ sa bon don du 'dod na bems po sems kyi nyer len gyi rgyur 'gyur la/ don dang mtshungs ldan las gzhan pa'i dngos po'ang mi srid pa'i phyir rgyu med par thal bar 'gyur ro zhes brjod par bya'o/ / de'i phyir rnal 'byor spyod pa pa dag gis kun gzhi rnam shes ma bkag pa'i phyir de las skye'o zhes smra ba nyid legs pa yin no/ / gal te de lta na snyoms 'jug gnyis la khyad par med par 'gyur te/ sems dang sems byung thams cad lus la bkag pa nyid de dag gi ngo bo yin pa'i phyir ro zhe na/

Objection: If these cessations are mindless states, then there would be no movement of minds later. Vaibhāṣikas assert that such cessations arise from past minds that are {the immediately preceding condition of meditative attainment} because they are past as well as substantially established. Sautrāntikas assert that the body that possesses faculties has the seeds of mind, since the body and mind mutually possess seeds. They say to Vaibhāṣikas, who do not assert that they arise from seeds, that if past minds exist in their mindstreams, it would follow that all concomitant states would not be stopped in mindless states. But if they did not exist in their mindstreams, they would not be established as past substance. Other schools say that if the seeds of mind are asserted to be mind, then all concomitant states would not be stopped. And if seeds are asserted to be objects, then matter would become a substantial cause (upādānahetu) of mind. It would therefore follow that they would be causeless, because phenomena other than objects or concomitant states are impossible. Yogācāras are correct to advocate that such cessations arise from foundation consciousness, because foundation consciousness is not stopped. Objection: If that is so, then the two meditative attainments would not be different, because their common nature is to stop all minds and mental factors in the body.

mdo sde pa dang bye brag tu smra ba ni de tsam du khyad par med kyang kun slong dang*/ dang po skyed tshul dang*/ khams dang*/ sa dang*/ gang zag dang*/ rnam smin dang*/ myong 'gyur la khyad par yod pa'i phyir te/ 'du shes med pa'i snyoms 'jug ni de la thar par shes pa'i log pa'i kun slong dang*/ dang po'ang khams 'dod pa dang*/ { des na snyoms 'jug 'di gnyis kyi rten la mu bzhi ste/ dang po 'du shes med snyoms kyi rten ma yin pa ni tshangs chen dang 'dod lha rigs drug go /'gog pa'i yin la cig shos kyi min pa ni gnas gtsang lnga'o/ / gnyis ka'i yin pa ni gzugs kyi lha ris gnas gtsang ma ma gtogs pa bcu gcig dang gling gsum gyi mi pho mo'o/ / gnyis min ngan song gsum dang sgra mi snyan dang gzugs med bzhi'o zhes so/} khams ni 'dod gzugs kyi khams dang*/ sa ni bsam gtan bzhi pa dang*/ gang zag ni byis pa dang*/ rnam smin ni 'du shes med pa'i sems can dang*/ myong 'gyur ni skyes nas myong 'gyur nyid du nges la/ 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug ni zhi bar gnas pa'i kun slong dang*/ dang po mi'i nang kho nar dang*/ gzugs med pa'i khams pa dang*/ srid rtse'i sa pa dang*/ 'phags pa'i gang zag dang*/ srid rtse'i rnam smin dang*/ skyes nas myong 'gyur la sogs pa gsum du nges pa'i phyir ro zhes lan 'debs par byed do/ /

Sautrāntikas and Vaibhāṣikas both assert that though there is no difference regarding that feature alone, they are different in motivation, initial means of generation, realm, level, person, maturation, and experience. The meditative attainment of nondiscernment is motivated by distorted consciousness holding [that state] to be liberation, and it is first generated in the desire realm. {There are four possibilities regarding beings who are a supportive basis for these two meditative attainments: (1) The first, those who are not the support [or basis] of the meditative attainment of nondiscernment, are the gods of Mahābrahma Heaven and the six types of desire-realm gods. (2) Those who are the support of cessation but not [nondiscernment] are the gods of the five pristine abodes.[581] (3) Those who are both are the eleven remaining types of form-realm gods, excluding [Mahābrahma and] the pristine abodes, and male and female humans of the three continents. (4) Those who are neither are reincarnating beings of the three lower realms, Uttarakuru, and the four formless realms.} [The meditative attainment of nondiscernment] exists in the desire or form realms, its level is the fourth absorption, [its basis] is a child-like being [i.e., a nonārya] whose karmic maturation is birth as a being devoid of discernment and it is experienced as something definitely experienced from birth. The meditative attainment of cessation [154] is motivated by the desire to abide in peace. It is first generated among humans alone, it exists in the formless realm, its level is the summit of existence, the person is an ārya, its karmic maturation is birth in the summit of existence, and it is experienced as the three: definite experience from birth and so on.

rnal 'byor spyod pa pa rnams ni dgag bya la'ang khyad par yod de/ kun las btus las/ 'du shes med pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa gang zhe na/ dge rgyas kyi 'dod chags dang bral la steng ma'i 'dod chags dang ma bral ba 'byung ba'i 'du shes sngon du btang ba'i yid la byed pas sems dang sems las byung ba'i chos brtan pa ma yin pa rnams 'gog pa la 'du shes med pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa zhes gdags so/ / 'gog pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa gang zhe na/ ci yang med pa'i skye mched kyi 'dod chags dang bral ba srid pa'i rtse mo las gyen du bskyod pa zhi bar gnas pa'i 'du shes sngon du btang ba'i yid la byed pas sems dang sems las byung ba'i chos brtan pa ma yin pa rnams dang brtan pa de dag las kyang kha cig 'gog pa la 'gog pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa zhes gdags so zhes dang pos tshogs drug 'khor bcas dang*/ gnyis pas tshogs bdun 'khor bcas 'gog par bshad do/ / srid pa'i rtse mo las gyen du bskyod pa ni dgra bcom dang phyir mi 'ong gi rim pa ltar srid rtse las 'dod chags dang bral ba dang de'i mthong spang spangs pa'o/ / de la gang yang gnas brtan dbyig bshes kyis yongs su dri ba zhes bya ba'i bstan bcos las/ 'di ni gang gi ltar na 'gog pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa sems med pa yin pa de la skyon du 'gyur gyi kho bo ni 'gog pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa sems dang bcas pa yin no zhes zer ro/ / zhes 'byung ba de yang sems kun gzhi rnam shes la 'dod na ni de lta mod kyi 'on kyang de ni mi 'dod de/ bye brag tu smra ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ / rnam shes tshogs drug la 'dod na de 'du shes dang tshor ba 'gog pa ma yin par 'gyur te/ de dag ni sems kyi kun 'gro yin pa'i phyir ro/ / mtshungs ldan rags pa 'gog gi phra ba mi 'gog go zhes bya bar yang mi rung ste/ phra ba'i don ni kun gzhi rnam shes 'khor bcas yin na de ni mi 'dod la rnam shes tshogs drug la ni phra rags kyi khyad par dbye bar mi nus pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir btsun pa dbyangs sgrogs kyis mdo las/ rnam par shes pa yod na gsum 'dus pa las reg pa dang reg pa'i rkyen gyis tshor ba dang 'du shes dang sems pa'i tshogs rnams 'byung bar gsungs pa dang 'gal lo zhes brjod pa'ang rigs pa yin no/ /

Yogācāras assert that there is also a difference in their object of negation because the Compendium of Abhidharma maintains: What is the meditative attainment of nondiscernment? The cessation of unstable minds and mental factors due to attention preceded by discernment that is free from attachment to the heaven of Śubhakṛtsna (Complete Bliss) but not free from attachment to the highest stage, is designated as the meditative attainment of nondiscernment.[582] What is the meditative attainment of cessation? The cessation of unstable — and even stable — minds and mental factors due to attention preceded by the discernment of the state of peace that is free from attachment to the base of nothingness and progresses beyond the summit of existence is designated as the meditative attainment of cessation.[583] This explains that the first [meditative attainment] stops the sixfold collection of consciousness and their retinue, while the second stops the sevenfold collection of consciousness and their retinue.[584] “Emerges from the summit of existence” refers to freedom from attachment to the summit of existence, and abandoning objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing belongs to the summit of existence, in accordance with the stages of a nonreturner and arhat. At any rate, Elder Vasumitra notes in his Thorough Inquiry: However we view this, there is error in asserting the meditative attainment of cessation to be a mindless state. I say the meditative attainment of cessation is associated with mind.[585] For those who assert the mind of foundation consciousness, then indeed that is so. However, this is not asserted, because this is the presentation of the Vaibhāṣikas. Since they assert the sixfold collection, discernment and feeling would not stop, because they are omnipresent states of mind. It would also be untenable to say coarse but not subtle concomitant states are stopped, because “subtle” cannot refer to the foundation consciousness and its retinue for Vaibhāṣikas, who do not accept that it exists, and the sixfold collection of consciousness cannot be divided into coarse and subtle aspects. Therefore, Bhadanta Ghoṣaka notes, with reason, that it contradicts a sūtra passage: If consciousness exists, feeling, discernment, and intention occur due to contact, and the condition of contact occurs through the assembly of the three.[586]

gal te de dag la sems med na snyoms par 'jug par ji ltar 'gyur te/ de ni bsam gtan pa dag dmigs pa la sems mnyam par 'jog pa la 'dod pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ ma yin te/ yid la byed pa'i khyad par gyis 'byung ba chen po dag sems skye ba dang mi mthun par cha mnyam par sgrub pa'i phyir ram/ yang na snyoms 'jug gi sbyor ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi stobs kyis rim pa ltar 'du shes dang tshor ba 'gog pa'i phyir de dag gi snyoms par 'jug pa zhes bya'o zhes sde pa dag gis lan 'debs so/ / rnal 'byor spyod pa pa ni yid la byed pa'i stobs kyis kun gzhi la rnam shes tshogs drug dang bdun skye ba med par 'jog pa'i phyir de dag la snyoms par 'jug pa {de dag rdzas su yod de sems skye ba'i gegs byed nus pas so zhes so } zhes zer ro/ { slob dpon ni de dag gis gegs byas pas sems ma skyes pa min gyi snyoms par 'jug sems kyis gegs byas pas sems ma skyes pa yin na de yang sems skye ba dang mi mthun pa'i lus sam kun gzhi skyed pa yin no/ / de yang ma 'ongs pa'i sems sems 'byung mi skye ba de tsam la snyoms 'jug ces btags so/ / de ma skyes pa'i gnas skabs kyi lus sam kun gzhi la snyoms 'jug tu btags pas 'dus byas su 'dod do/ /}
bdun pa srog gi dbang po bshad pa ni
The faculty of life force
srog ni tshe yin drod dang ni/ / rnam shes rten gang yin pa'o/ / 45 mtshan nyid dag ni skye ba dang / / rga dang gnas dang mi rtag nyid/ /
Life force is life that is the support of heat and consciousness. The characteristics [of conditioned states] are arising, aging, enduring, and impermanence itself. (2:45)

srog gi dbang po ni khams gsum pa'i tshe yin te/ {chos mngon pa las } srog gi dbang po gang zhe na/ khams gsum pa'i tshe yin no zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / tshe de yang{ mi ldan pa'i 'du byed rdzas grub} lus kyi drod dang{ gsum ga na} rnam par shes pa'i rten gang yin pa ste de ni mi ldan pa'i 'du byed rdzas su grub pa'o/ / de yang khams 'og ma gnyis su ni lus dang rnam shes gnyis ka'i rten yin la/ gzugs med du ni rnam shes gcig pu'i rten yin gyi rnam shes ris mthun pa tsam ni srog gi dbang po ma yin te/ 'du shes med pa pa dang sems med pa'i snyoms 'jug{ la gnas pa} dag la/ srog gi dbang po med par thal ba'i phyir dang*/ gzugs med pa'i sems can dag gi skyes nas ma shi'i bar gyi rnam shes thams cad rnam smin kho nar 'gyur te/ de na ni yid kyi rnam shes gcig pu las med pa'i phyir dang*/ de yang srog gi dbang po yin pa'i phyir dang*/ srog gi dbang po'ang rnam smin kho nar nges pa'i phyir ro/ / de lta na'ang gzugs med pa la dge ba mi srid par 'gyur te/ rnam smin ni lung ma bstan kho na yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir srog gi dbang po ni lus dang rnam shes kyi rten du gyur pa'i mi ldan pa'i 'du byed rdzas su grub pa kho na yin te/ dge slong ma chos sbyin gyi mdo las/ tshe dang drod dang rnam shes 'dis/ / gang tshe lus ni 'dor byed cing*/ / bor nas de tshe 'dug pa ni/ / sems med ji ltar shing bzhin no/ / zhes gsungs so zhes bye brag tu smra ba zer ro/ /

The faculty of life force (jīvita) is life (āyus) in the three realms because {the Attainment of Knowledge explains:} What is the faculty of life force? It is life in the three realms.[587] Further, life is the support (ādhāra) of heat (ūṣma) of the body and consciousness (vijñāna) {in all three realms}, which is a substantially established, nonassociated formative factor. As such, [life force] is the support of both heat and consciousness in the desire and form realms and the support of consciousness alone in the formless realm. But consciousness merely [maintaining subsequent moments] of the same type is not the faculty of life force, because it would then follow that beings possessing nondiscernment and those {abiding in} mindless meditative attainments would have no life force. It would also follow that all consciousness between the birth and death of formless-realm beings would be karmic maturation alone because they have no consciousness other than mental consciousness, that [mental consciousness] would comprise the faculty of life force,[588] and the faculty of life force is definitely just karmic maturation alone. But if that were the case, then virtue would be impossible in the formless realm because karmic maturation is solely neutral. Vaibhāṣikas therefore assert that the faculty of life force is just a substantially established nonassociated formative factor that supports the body and consciousness, because the Bhikṣuṇī Dharmadinnā Sūtra declares: When life, heat, and consciousness cast aside and discard this body, then what remains lacks mind, just like a tree.[589]

de la mdo sde pa dag ni lus dang rnam shes srog la brten par 'dod na srog gang la brten pa yin/ de yang rten med par gnas par mi 'gyur te lus dang rnam shes bzhin no/ / srog kyang lus dang rnam shes la brten pa yin no zhe na/ de lta na phan tshun ltos nas 'grub pa'i phyir gnyis ka ma grub pa'am/ gal te grub na'ang{ srog} ldog par mi 'gyur te/ rgyu{ rnam shes} ma tshang ba mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te de dag las kyis 'phangs pa'i phyir 'jug pa dang ldog par 'gyur ro zhe na/ 'o na ni lus dang rnam shes las tha dad pa'i srog gi dbang po don med de/ las kyi stobs kyis lus dang rnam shes dus nges par 'phangs pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir yid kyi rnam shes sa bon dang bcas pa ris mthun par gnas pa la srog gi dbang por gdags so zhes 'dod do/ / rnal 'byor spyod pa pa dag phyogs gnyis ka la sngar smros pa'i klan ka yod pa'i phyir las kyi stobs kyis kun gzhi rnam shes ris mthun par gnas pa la srog gi dbang por gdags so zhes 'dod pa ni ches legs pa yin no/ /

Sautrāntikas inquire: If the body and consciousness are supported by life force, what supports life force? Moreover, it would not abide without support, like the body and consciousness. Objection: Life force also is supported by the body and consciousness. Reply: If that is so, neither would be established because they are established through mutual reliance. Or if established, {life force} would not be stopped because it would be impossible for {consciousness, as} a cause, ever to be incomplete. [156] Objection: It engages or disengages because it is projected by karma. Reply: But a faculty of life force distinct from the body and consciousness is meaningless because the duration of the body and consciousness is definitely projected by the power of karma. Therefore Sautrāntikas assert that that which maintains the lineage [or stream] of mental consciousness, along with its seeds, is designated as “the faculty of life force.” Yogācāras assert that because the former two positions may be censured, that which maintains the lineage [or stream] of foundation consciousness due to the power of karma is designated as “the faculty of life force.” This {assertion} is best.

gal te tshe zad pa kho nas 'chi 'pho bar 'gyur ram zhe na/ gdags pa las/ tshe zad nas 'chi ba dang*/ bsod nams zad nas 'chi ba dang*/ gnyis ka zad nas 'chi ba dang*/ bar ma dor 'chi ba bzhi yod par gsungs te/{ de la tshe zad pas 'chi la bsod nams zad pas min pa'i mu dang po ni tshe'i rnam smin can gyi las zad pa'o mu gnyis pa/} bsod nams zad pa ni longs spyod kyi rnam smin{ can gyi las} zad pa'o/{ mu gsum pa de ni gnyis ka zad nas 'chi ba'o/ / bzhi pa ni de gnyis ka ma zad par bar ma dor shi ba'o/ /} bar ma dor 'chi ba ni dug la sogs pa'i zas dang*/ g.yang sa la sogs pa'i sbyor ba dang*/ gdon la sogs pas mdangs 'phrogs pas gnod pas 'chi {ba dang tshe la dbang ba rnams tshe gtong } ba'o/ /

Question: Does death occur solely through the exhaustion of life? Reply: Presentation on Karma states: One dies through the exhaustion of life. One dies through the exhaustion of merit. One dies through the exhaustion of both. Untimely death constitutes four.[590] {(1) The first possibility, death through the exhaustion of life but not through the exhaustion of merit, is the exhaustion of karma maturing as life. (2) The second possibility,} death through the exhaustion of merit, is the exhaustion of {karma} maturing as enjoyment. {(3) The third possibility is death through the exhaustion of both. (4) The fourth possibility is untimely death where neither is exhausted.} Untimely death is the exhaustion of life through poison and so on, or death due to events such as falling over a precipice and so forth, or through harm by evil spirits who steal one’s health and so on, {and those with power over life relinquishing life}.

de la tshe zad pa dang*/ tshe dang bsod can nams gnyis ka zad nas 'chi ba ni 'phags pa chil dbang 'byor ba rnams ma gtogs pa tshe bsreng ba'i thabs med do/ / bsod nams zad nas 'chi ba la ni dge sbyor dang sbyin pa la sogs pas tshe bsring du yod do/ / dug dang g.yang sa la sogs pa'i bar ma dor 'chi ba la ni sman dang spyod lam gyis tshe bsring du yod do/ / gdon la sogs pa 'byung po'i gnod pa la ni rig sngags 'chang grub pa rnams kyi cho gas tshe bsring du yod do/ / tshe la dbang ba rnams tshe gtong ba'ang bar ma dor 'chi ba yin par snang ngo*/ / yang mdo las/ lus thob pa ni bzhi ste/ lus thob pa gang la bdag nyid{ kyis} 'chi bar 'gyur gyi gzhan gyis gsod pas 'chi ba ma yin pa yang yod ces pa la sogs pa mu bzhi gsungs pa las/ bdag nyid kyis 'chi la gzhan gyis mi 'chi ba{ mu dang po} ni sangs rgyas rnams dang 'dod pa'i lha rtsed mos myos pa dang yid rab tu 'khrugs pa rnams so/ /

Except for āryas who exercise power over life, there is no means of prolonging life when facing death due to the exhaustion of life and the exhaustion of both life and merit. Life may be extended when facing death due to the exhaustion of merit by practicing virtuous actions such as giving. Life may be extended when facing untimely death, such as preventing death by poison through taking medicine, avoiding falling over a precipice through one’s physical dexterity, and so on. Life may be extended when harmed by elementals (bhūta) such as evil spirits through the rites of vidyādharas. And it appears that those with power over life relinquish their lives or even experience untimely death. Also, a sūtra states: Those obtaining bodies are of four types: those who obtain a body and who die by their own hand but do not die through being killed by others, and so on.[591]
This sūtra declares four possibilities: {The first possibility,} those who die by their own hand and who do not die through others’ intervention, are buddhas or desire-realm gods intoxicated by play with confused minds.

gzhan gyis 'chi la bdag gis ni mi 'chi ba{ mu gnyis pa} ni mngal na gnas pa dang sgo nga na gnas pa rnams so/ gnyis kas 'chi ba ni{ ma gsum pa} 'dod pa na spyod pa phal che ba rnams so/ / gnyis kas mi 'chi ba{ mu bzhi pa} ni 'dod pa na dmyal ba pa rnams dang*/ byang gi sgra mi snyan pa rnams dang*/ mthong lam dang*/ byams pa dang*/ sems med pa'i snyoms 'jug gnyis la snyoms par zhugs pa rnams dang*/ rgyal po'i drang srong dang*/ rgyal po'i pho nya dang*/ rgyal bas lung bstan pa dang*/ chos len dang*/ mchog can dang*/ gang gi len dang*/ tshong dpon gyi bu grags pa gzhon nu dang*/ 'tsho byed la sogs pa rnams dang*/ lung phran tshegs las/ srid pa tha ma pa'i sems can zag pa zad pa ma thob kyi bar du bar ma dor rgyun chad cing dus byed par 'gyur ba gang yin pa de ni gnas ma yin zhing go skabs med do zhes 'byung bas srid pa tha ma pa rnams dang*/ srid pa tha ma pa'i byang chub sems dpa'i yum de lhums na gnas pa dang*/ 'khor los bsgyur ba dang*/ 'khor los bsgyur ba'i ma de mngal na gnas pa dang*/ srid pa bar ma pa thams cad dang*/ khams gong ma gnyis kyi lha rnams lta bu ste/ de la rgyal po'i drang srong ni sngon 'khor los bsgyur ba las rab tu byung ba'o/ / de yang bdag gis 'chi ba ni lceb pa yin la/ gzhan gyis 'chi ba ni gsod pa'o/ /

{The second possibility,} those who die through others’ intervention but not by their own hand, are those abiding in the womb and those abiding in an egg. {The third possibility,} those who die through both, are most of those living in the desire realm. {The fourth possibility,} those who do not die through either, are hell beings in the desire realm, beings of Uttarakuru, beings on the path of seeing, Maitreya, those entering meditative attainment in the two mindless meditative attainments, rishis (seers or sages) of the king and messengers of the king, those predicted by conquerors, [157] those accepting Dharma, those possessing the supreme state, those accepting any, the youthful Kīrti the son of the chief trader, physicians, and so on. It is said in the Kṣudraka Collection: Until sentient beings in their last existence obtain the end of the contaminants, there is no opportunity or occasion for their mindstreams to be severed or to die (kālakriyā).[592] Such beings are, for example, those in their last existence, bodhisattvas in their last existence abiding in the womb of their mothers, wheel-turning kings, wheel-turning princes abiding in the womb of their mothers, and all intermediate existences. “Rishis of the king” refers to those who were formerly wheel-turning kings who take ordination. Further, “those who die by their own hand” are suicides, and “those who die through others’ intervention” are those who are murdered.
brgyad pa mtshan nyid 'chad pa ni
The four characteristics

'dus byas kyi mtshan nyid dag ni {'dus byas kyi } chos rnams {ma 'ongs pa nas da ltar bar }skyed par byed pa'i skye ba dang*/ rnyings par byed pa'i rga ba dang*/ gnas par byed pa'i gnas pa dang*/ 'jig par byed pa'i mi rtag pa nyid ces bya ba bzhi'o/ { de la 'dus byas gcig skye ba na 'dus byas su mtshon pa'i mtshan gzhi bum pa lta bu gcig dang de skye bar byed/ gnas par byed/ rga bar byed/ 'jig par byed pa'i rtsa ba'i mtshan nyid bzhi dang*/ rtsa ba'i skye ba skyed par byed pa'i skye ba'i skye ba dang*/ rtsa ba'i gnas pa skyed pa'i gnas pa'i gnas pa dang*/ rtsa ba'i rga ba skyed pa'i rga ba'i rga ba dang*/ rtsa 'jig 'jig pa skyed byed 'jig pa'i 'jig pa ste mthun pa'i mtshan nyid bzhi ste chos brgyad ma 'ongs pa nas da ltar bar skyed par byed cing rang yang de dus skye bas chos dgu dus gcig tu skye'o/ / sgra med phra rabs rdul rdzas brgyad la sogs pa nges par lhan cig tu skye ba gzhan dag ni rtsa ba'i skye bas skyed do/ / rga 'jig gis ni da ltar nas ma 'ongs par 'pho bar bskyed la/ gnas pa ni 'dus ma byas la'ang yod pas de ni byed las chung ngo*/ / de bzhin du rtsa ba'i gnas rga 'jig gsum gyis kyang rang rang ma gtogs pa chos brgyad brgyad bskyed pas rtsa ba'i mtshan nyid bzhi po re re la'ang 'dus byas kyi mtshan nyid gsum gsum tshang mod/ skye ba la skye ba ma tshang ba nas 'jig pa la 'jig pa ma tshang ba'i bar du'o zhe na/ skye ba'i skye bas rtsa skye kho na skyed pa nas 'jig pa'i 'jig pas rtsa 'jig kho na skyed pa'i bar du yin pas skyon med do/ / des na 'dus byas kyi mtshan nyid bzhi'ang 'dus byas su mtshon pa la rang ma gtogs pa'i mtshan nyid grogs po gsum gsum mthun pa'i mtshan nyid skye sogs re re bsnan pas mtshan nyid bzhi bzhi'ang tshang ngo zhes so/} { nyid ni dngos po'i rkyen no/ /

The characteristics (lakṣaṇa) of conditioned states are four: (1) arising (jāti), which generates {conditioned} phenomena {that pass from the future to the present}, (2) aging (jarā), which causes decay, (3) enduring (sthiti), which maintains, and (4) impermanence (anitya), which destroys. {If one conditioned phenomenon arises, such as a conditioned vase, then nine qualities arise at the same time: eight generated from the future to the present, including the four primary characteristics — (1) arising, (2) enduring, (3) aging, and (4) disintegrating — and the four secondary characteristics: (5) the arising of arising, which generates primary arising, (6) the enduring of enduring, which generates primary endurance, (7) the aging of aging, which generates primary aging, and (8) the disintegration of disintegration, which generates primary disintegration, and (9) the object itself, which arises at that time. The eight substantial particles excluding sound and so on arise simultaneously, and the others are generated by primary arising. Aging and disintegration generate change from future to present states. Enduring also exists for unconditioned states, but that is its minor function. Objection: Thus primary enduring, aging, and disintegrating produce eight qualities each, excluding themselves. Therefore each of the four primary characteristics are complete in each of the three characteristics of conditioned states, but they would be incomplete respectively in the arising of arising, up to the disintegration of disintegration. Reply: There is no error, since the arising of arising generates primary arising alone, up to the disintegration of the disintegration, which generates primary disintegration alone. Therefore, with respect to the four characteristics of conditioned states that represent conditioned states, the four characteristics are complete, since their three associated characteristics, except for themselves, are added to each secondary characteristic such as arising and so on.} The term “itself” (2:45d) refers to the [natural] condition of things.

'o na mdo las/ dge slong dag gsum po 'di dag ni 'dus byas kyi mtshan nyid yin no/ / gsum gang zhe na/ dge slong dag 'dus byas skye bar yang mngon no/ / 'jig par yang mngon no/ / gnas pa gzhan du 'gyur ba nyid du yang mngon no zhes gsum du ji ltar gsung bar 'gyur zhe na/ mtshan nyid bzhi yin mod kyi mdo las/ gnas pa gzhan du 'gyur ba'i rgas pa dang 'brel par bstan pas rtag 'dzin dgag cing 'dus byas la yid skyo bar bya ba'i phyir te bkra shis ma dang 'brel pa'i rna nag ma bzhin no/ / gal te bum pa la sogs pa 'dus byas su byed pa la skye ba la sogs pa tha dad dgos par 'dod na de dag 'dus byas su byed pa la'ang skye ba la sogs pa tha dad dgos par 'gyur la/ mi dgos na ni bum pa la sogs pa'ang mi dgos so zhe na/

Question: A sūtra states: Monks, these three are the characteristics of conditioned states. What three? Monks, conditioned states manifest in arising, manifest in disintegrating, and manifest in enduring through transforming.[593] Why are these three stated? Reply: Indeed there are four characteristics, for this sūtra teaches that enduring is related to aging[594] through the transformation of one state into another — and this stops grasping at permanence and induces disappointment with conditioned states, like the black-eared goddess being related to the goddess of fortune.[595] Objection: If it is asserted that arising and so on are necessarily distinct from specific conditioned states such as vases and so on, [158] then arising and so on would necessarily be distinct from conditioned states. But if that were not necessary [in general], it also would not be necessary for [specific instances such as] vases and so on.
de dag skye ba'i skyes la sogs/ / de chos brgyad dang gcig la 'jug / 46 rgyu dang rkyen dag med par ni/ / skye bas bskyed bya skyed byed min/ /
They have arising of arising and so on. Some engage eight qualities, some one. Without causes and conditions, those to be generated through arising are not generated. (2:46)

skye ba la sogs pa de dag la'ang skye ba'i skye ba dang*/ sogs pa'i sgras bzung ba rga ba'i rga ba dang*/ gnas pa'i gnas pa dang*/ mi rtag pa'i mi rtag pa nyid ces bya ba rjes su mthun pa'i mtshan nyid bzhi yod do/ / 'o na ni de dag la'ang gzhan dgos pa'i phyir thug pa med par 'gyur zhe na/

Reply: Those characteristics of arising and so forth have four secondary characteristics, such as the arising of arising (jātijāti) and so on — the aging of aging, the enduring of enduring, and the impermanence of impermanence. Objection: There would be an infinite regress because [each of] those requires the others.

ma yin te/ skye ba de ni rga ba la sogs pa gsum dang*/ skye ba'i skye ba la sogs pa bzhi dang*/ bum pa la sogs pa'i mtshan gzhi dang*/ chos brgyad la 'jug cing skyed par byed la/ skye ba'i skye ba de ni skye ba'i chos gcig pu de kho na la 'jug cing skyed par byed pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du rga ba la'ang shes par bya ste/ de'i phyir thug pa med par yang mi 'gyur zhes 'dod do/ / mdo sde pa la sogs pa ni bum pa la sogs pa las tha dad pa'i skye ba la sogs pa ni yod pa ma yin te/ tshad ma la ltar rung ba'i bdag nyid ma dmigs pa'i phyir sa phyogs la bum pa ma dmigs pa bzhin no/ / gzhan yang 'dus byas dang skye ba tha dad par 'dod na ni 'dus byas rang nyid skye ba med par 'gyur la/ rang nyid skye ba yin pa na'ang tha dad par mi 'gyur ro/ / skye ba'ang ma yin skye ba med pa'ang ma yin na ni de dag rnam par spyod pa'i 'gal ba ma yin par 'gyur ro/ / 'o na mdo las/ btsun pa gnyis kas mi dgum pa de gang lags/ shA ri'i bu 'du shes med min skye mched nye bar 'gro ba rnams yin no/ / zhes gsungs she na/

Reply: That is not so, because arising has three qualities such as aging; and arising of arising has four; whereas instances such as a vase and so on engage (vṛtta) and generate eight qualities (dharma), and the arising of arising engages and generates just one quality, that of arising. Aging should also be understood in that way. Therefore it is held that no infinite regress occurs. Sautrāntikas and so on assert that there is no arising and so on that is distinct from a vase and so forth because such states are not observed. But [if they existed] they would appear to valid cognition, just like a vase that is not observed in a particular location. Again, if it is asserted that conditioned states and their arising are distinct, then conditioned states themselves would not arise, and even if they did arise they would not be distinct. And if they did arise but also lacked arising, then they would possess contradictory modes of being, but that cannot be so. Question: A sūtra reads: “Venerables, what happens to those who do not perish by either means?” Śāriputra: “They proceed to the base of neither discernment nor nondiscernment.”[596]

'dir bdag nyid 'chi ba ni rang sa'i zag med dang*/ gzhan gyis gsod pa ni gong sa'i nyer bsdogs kyis spong ba la dgongs te/ 'du shes med min pa na de gnyis ka med pa la dgongs so/ / 'o na med min pa der yang sa gzhan gyi 'phags lam gyis spong ngo*/ /zhe na mnyam gzhag gi sa pas spong ba la rang sa zag med dang gong ma'i nyer bsdogs kyis spong bar mos pas mnyam gzhag gi sa gnyis ka der go'o/ / gzhan yang 'dus byas las skye ba tha dad par 'dod na skye ba 'dus ma byas su 'gyur ro/ / 'dus byas kyang ma yin 'dus ma byas kyang ma yin na ni de dag rnam par gcod pa'i 'gal bar mi 'gyur ro/ / de'i phyir mdo las/ gang cung zad skye ba'i chos can de thams cad 'gog pa'i chos can yin no zhes gsungs pa dang yang 'gal ba yin te/ chos can gyi sgra ni rang bzhin la bzhed pa yin no/ / de bzhin du rga ba don gzhan la sogs pa la'ang brjod par bya'o/ / gsum po 'di dag ni 'dus byas kyi mtshan nyid yin no zhes bya ba la sogs pa'i mdo'i don ni 'dus byas kyi rgyun dang po ni skye ba dang*/ rgyun rjes su 'jug pa gnas pa dang*/ rgyun gyi snga phyi'i bye brag ni gnas pa gzhan du 'gyur ba dang*/ rgyun 'gog pa la mi rtag pa'i dbang du mdzad nas gsungs la/ de dag kyang 'dus byas kyi bdag nyid yin gyi gzhan ni ma yin te/ slob dpon gyi 'grel pa las/ rgyun gyi dang po skye ba yin/ / chad pa 'jig pa gnas pa de/ / de nyid snga phyi'i bye brag ni/ / gnas pa gzhan du 'gyur ba nyid/ / ces bya ba dang*/ sngon med las byung skye ba ste/ / rgyun gnas de chad 'jig pa yin/ / rgyun gyi snga phyi'i bye brag ni/ / gnas pa gzhan du 'gyur bar 'dod/ / ces gsungs pa yin no/ /

Reply: Here, the intention is that death by one’s own hand is abandoned by the uncontaminated states of one’s level, and being killed by others is abandoned by access concentration to a higher level. Neither exists on the [formless-realm] level of neither discernment nor nondiscernment. Objection: Even the level of neither discernment nor nondiscernment is abandoned by the ārya paths of other levels. Reply: Since abandonment by its level of equipoise is indeed abandonment by its uncontaminated level and by access concentration to a higher level, both levels of equipoise should be understood here. Again, if arising is asserted to be distinct from conditioned states, then arising would be unconditioned. But if it were neither conditioned nor unconditioned, then those states would not be absolutely contradictory. Therefore it would contradict the sūtra that declares: Instances of arising, however brief, are all instances of cessation.[597] This is because the term “instance” refers to essence. Similarly, aging is also expressed for other instances. The sūtra statement above that “these three are the characteristics of conditioned states” means that arising is the first part of the continuum of a conditioned state, enduring is the subsequent engagement of the continuum, transformation of endurance refers to specific earlier and later moments of the continuum, and impermanence is the cessation of the continuum. These pertain to conditioned states and not other entities because Vasubandhu declares in his Autocommentary: The first [part of] the continuum is arising, its severance is disintegration, [it itself is] enduring. Specific earlier and later [moments] of that [continuum] are just the transformation of endurance.[598] And: The occurrence of that which is not previously existent is arising, enduring is the continuum, disintegration is severance. Specific earlier and later [moments] of the continuum are asserted to be the transformation of endurance.[599]

mdo las/ skad cig ma'i dbang du mdzad nas gsungs pa ni ma yin te/ skad cig ma ni skad cig re re la 'jig pa yin na de la gnas pa mi srid cing gnas na'ang skad cig ma ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / skad cig ma gcig tu gnas so zhes bya ba'ang ma yin te/ de ni mi gnas pa'i mthar thug pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar yang 'grel pa las/ skad cig ma'i chos la ni/ / gnas pa med na 'jig par 'gyur/ / de yang 'jig 'gyur de'i phyir/ / de yi de rtog don med do/ / zhes gsungs te/ de la gnas pa med na 'jig par 'gyur zhes bya ba ni gnas pa med pa'i phyir 'jig pa yin no zhes bya ba'o/ / de yang zhes bya ba ni skad cig ma'o/ / der rtog ces bya ba ni gnas pa der ro/ / des na skad cig ma ni 'jig pa yin pa'i phyir gnas pa ma yin no zhes bya ba'o/ / 'dis kyang skad cig ma la skye ba dang mi rtag pa ni don gcig par ston pa ma bkag pa'i phyir don gcig tu bstan to/ / skad cig ma la rga ba'ang yod pa ma yin te/ 'grel pa las/ de bzhin na ni rga mi 'gyur/ / gzhan du 'gyur na de gzhan nyid/ / de lta bas na dngos gcig la/ / rga zhes bya ba mi 'thad do/ / zhes 'byung bas rga ba ni gzhan du 'gyur ba yin na skad cig ma gcig po de nyid gzhan du 'gyur bar mi rigs pa'i phyir dang*/ 'gyur na'ang skad cig ma gcig tu mi 'thad pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar yang de'i phyir mdo'i don ni rgyun gyis dbang du mdzad nas gsungs pa yin gyi skad cig la ni ma yin la/ de mtshan nyid du 'dod na'ang skad cig la ma khyab par 'gyur bas 'dus byas kyi mtshan nyid ni yang dag par na sngar med pa skye ba dang*/ skyes nas kyang 'gag pa nyid yin te/ mdo las 'dus byas zhes bya ba ni gang ma byung ba las 'byung ba dang*/ byung nas kyang yang mi 'byung ba 'di ni 'dus byas kyi mtshan nyid yin no zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro zhes 'dod do/

This sūtra does not state this from the perspective of momentariness, because if momentariness is disintegration in each moment, then enduring is not possible, and if something endures, it is not momentary. Further, it does not “endure for one moment” because that is the final limit of nonendurance. Therefore the Autocommentary states: If a momentary [159] phenomenon does not endure, it disintegrates. Also that disintegrates. Therefore it is meaningless to conceive it as that.[600] “If a momentary phenomenon does not endure, it disintegrates” means that it disintegrates because it does not endure. “Also that” refers to momentariness. “Conceive it as that” means conceiving it as enduring. Therefore, it does not endure because momentariness is disintegration. Through this logic, arising and impermanence are taught to be equivalent to momentariness, because teaching them to be equivalent cannot be refuted. Momentariness has no aging, for the Autocommentary states: If it is like that, it does not age. If it transforms, it becomes something other. Thus it is unacceptable to say that a single thing “ages.”[601] If aging means transforming, it is illogical for just a single moment to transform, for transformation is untenable for a single moment. Thus this sūtra is stated from the perspective of a continuum and not a single moment. Though “aging” is asserted to be a characteristic, it cannot be confined to a single moment. Therefore the characteristics of conditioned states are correctly posited as the arising of that which did not previously exist and the cessation of that which has previously arisen. A sūtra expounds: Those called “conditioned states” come to exist from a nonexistent state and become nonexistent from an existent state. This is the defining characteristic of conditioned states.[602]

{ gal te dus gcig tu chos gcig mtshan nyid bzhi tshang na skye 'jig gnas rga dus gcig tu byed par thal la ma tshang na 'dus byas su mi 'gyur ro zhe na skye ba ma 'ongs pa chos ma 'ongs pa la bya ba byed la/ da ltar ba'i chos la gnas pa sogs bya ba byed pas dus tha dad pas skyon med do } yang*/ gal te ma 'ongs pa'i skye bas 'dus byas skyed par byed pa yin na 'dus byas thams cad cig car skye bar 'gyur ro zhe na/

Vaibhāṣikas say: Such a consequence does not arise, because without {the assembly} of its causes (hetu) and conditions (prataya), those to be generated (janikā) in the future through arising (janya) alone are not generated (jāti) {in the present}. {Objection:} Yet they are generated by the assembly of causes and conditions. {Reply: They are causes because they generate a result through the assembly of causes and conditions. Though arising possesses other meanings, it would be meaningless to assert that nongeneration through the nonassembly of causes and conditions — such as the faculties — is a cause.} Other meanings of arising have been refuted.
dgu pa ming gi tshogs la sogs pa bshad pa ni
Collection of nouns, predicated phrases, and letters
ming gi tshogs la sogs pa ni/ / ming dang ngag dang yi ge'i tshogs/ / 47
The collection of nouns and so on refers to the collection of nouns, predicated phrases, and letters. (2:47ab)

mdor bstan par ming gi tshogs la sogs pa yang zhes bya ba'i sogs pa'i sgras ni ngag dang yi ge gzung bas de dag ni ming dang ngag dang yi ge'i tshogs gsum mo/ / de la ming ni don gyi ngo bo rjod par byed pa ste gzugs zhes pa lta bu'o/ / ngag ni tshig ste don gyi khyad par ston pa kye ma 'dus byas rnams mi rtag ces bya ba la sogs pa'am/ bstan du med la thogs pa dang bcas pa'i gzugs zhes bya ba lta bu ji tsam gyis don yongs su rdzogs pa{ ra ston pa bstan bcos la sogs pa} ste/ tshig gang gis lhas byin{ dkar sham} 'gro zhes pa la sogs pa'i bya ba dang*/ kha dog dkar sham la sogs pa'i yon tan dang*/ bcos so 'tshed do 'tshed par 'gyur ro zhes pa la sogs pa{ ngo bo dang yon tan dang bya ba dang} dus kyi 'brel pa'i khyad par rtogs par 'gyur ba'o/ /

Briefly, the collection of nouns (nāmakāya) and so on refers to the three — the collection of nouns, predicated phrases (vākya), and letters (akṣara) — since the term “and so on” includes predicated phrases and letters. Nouns (nāman) express the essential nature of an object, such as “form.” Speech consists of words that indicate a specific meaning, such as “Alas, conditioned states are impermanent,” or {treatises and so on that} seek to fully resolve a specific meaning, such as “undemonstrable and impeded form.” Furthermore, through such phrases we come to comprehend specific actions such as “Devadatta made progress {in purity},” or specific qualities such as “the color of purity,” or specific {natures, qualities, actions, or} times through the words “he has cooked, he is cooking, he will cook,” and so on.

yi ge ni ming dang tshig gi gzhir gyur pa'am cha shas te ka la sogs pa'o/ / nges tshig ni ak+Shar zhes bya ba mi 'gyur ba ste/ /brda'i dbang gis rnam grangs gzhan du mi 'gyur ba'i phyir te ka zhes bya ba'i yi ge ni brda mi mthun pa'i skye bo du ma la 'gyur ba med pa bzhin no/ / bya ny+dza na zhes{ byed las} pa gsal bar byed pa ste/ ming dang tshig gi gsal byed yin pa'i phyir ro/ / yang na{ dgos pa} rgyud nas don rjod par byed pa'i phyir yi ge'o/ / de'i phyir sgra pa dag gis/ rnam grangs du ma med pa dang*/ / ming tshig gsal bar byed pa dang*/ / don rnams brjod par byed pa'i phyir/ / yi ge zhes ni brjod pa yin zhes bshad do/ / ming dang tshig ni brda'i dbang gis gzhan dang gzhan du 'gyur te lto ldir la sogs pa la bum pa dang g+ha Ta la sogs pa bzhin no/ / tshogs ni 'dus pa ste phreng ba la sogs pa bzhin no/ / don ston pa'ang bye brag tu smra ba ni ngag ming la 'jug la ming gis don brjod par byed do zhes 'dod do/ / mdo sde pa na re{ bum pa zhes sogs} brdas mtshams bcad na ni gnyis kas don{ lto ldir ba} go bar rung ba'i phyir ngag dang ming gi rim pa la mi ltos te/ 'grel pa las/ ngag phyogs sa dang 'od zer dang*/ / phyugs dang mig dang rdo rje dang*/ / mtho ris chu dang don dgu las/ / mkhas pas gau'i sgra nges gzung bya zhes gaus don dgu brjod par bshad pa lta bu'o/ /

Letters such as ka form the basis or the components [160] of nouns and predicated phrases. The etymology of “letter” is akṣara,[603] which means “nontransforming” because letters do not transform in different contexts due to their power as conventional symbols, just as the letter ka does not transform in the many beings who apply it as a distinct conventional symbol. {Their function is} vyañjana,[604] which means “to make manifest,” because they are consonants forming nouns and predicated phrases. Again, they are letters because {their purpose is} to express meaning indirectly. Therefore grammarians call them “letters” because they have few synonyms, they create nouns and predicated phrases, and they express meaning. Nouns and predicated phrases indicate a distinct [entity] due to the power of conventional symbols, just as vase or ghaṭa and so on designates that which is pot-bellied and so on, or rosary and so on designates a collection that is an aggregation. In terms of communicating meaning, Vaibhāṣikas assert: Speech engages nouns, and nouns express meaning. Sautrāntikas assert: When delineated by conventional symbols {such as vase and so on,} the meaning {of “pot-bellied”} can be understood through both, but the meaning does not rely on the order of nouns and linguistic elements. For example, the [Sanskṛit] term go has nine meanings as the Autocommentary clarifies: Scholars recognize the term go as having nine meanings: speech, direction, ground, light, cattle, eyes, vajra, high lineage, and water.[605]

brdas mtshams ma bcad na ni gnyis ka'ang don gyi rjod byed du mi 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ ngag ming la 'jug pa'ang gsal bar byed pa dang skyed par byed pa gnyis ka mi 'thad pa'i phyir te/ ngag ni sgra'i rang bzhin yin pa'i phyir sgra tsam thams cad kyis ming gsal ba dang skyed par 'gyur ro zhes bya ba dang*/ ming la sogs pa'ang sgra'i rang bzhin la 'dod na ni gzugs kyi phung po la btags pa yin la/ rnam rtog gi yul gyi sgra'i spyi la 'dod na ni ngo bo nyid med pa'i phyir rdzas su med do zhes zer ro/ / bye brag tu smra ba ni sgra'i rang bzhin ni ma yin gyi 'on kyang rnam rtog gi yul nyid yin no/ / de yang rdzas su med na don rjod byed ma yin par thal bar 'gyur ro zhes 'dod do/

They say that if the meaning is not demarcated by conventional symbols, then neither [names nor linguistic elements] would express meaning, and if speech engages names, then it would be untenable that [nouns] would both generate and clarify [meaning,] for speech is by nature sound and anything that is mere sound would not make clear, or generate, names. If names and so on are asserted to be by nature sound, they would be designated as the aggregate of form, but if they are asserted to be sound universals that constitute objects of conception, then they would not be substantially existent because they would have no [substantial] nature. Vaibhāṣikas assert: They are not by nature sound but objects of conception. [Sautrāntikas reply:] But if they are not substantially existent, it would follow that they would not express meaning.

{gal te yi ge'ang yig 'bru'i yan lag gi min nam zhe na/ min te yi ge ni yid kho na la gsal ba'i ka sogs yin la de dag go bar bya ba'i phyir yig 'bru'i gzugs su gyur pa'i ka sogs byas pa yin no/ / sgra tsam gyis don mi go ba'i phyir ming tshig yi ge gsum ni sgra min des na ngag ni ming gsal ba'am skyed pa'i ming la 'jug la/ ming gi don brjod cing rtogs par byed do zhes bye brag smra ba zer ro/ / mdo sde pa sgra tsam ngag min gyi/ / sgra gang zhig smra ba pos don la bum pa zhes sogs brdas mtshams bcad pa ni don go bar byed pas ngag yin pas rtogs yul gyi ming sogs btags pas ci zhig bya zhes zer ro/ }
gsum pa chos kyi khyad par bshad pa'i sgo nas don bsdu ba ni
DISTINGUISHING ATTRIBUTES

'dod dang gzugs gtogs sems can ston/ / rgyu mthun lung bstan min de bzhin/ / skal mnyam rnam par smin pa'ang yin/ / khams gsum pa ste thob rnam gnyis/ / 48 mtshan nyid rnams kyang snyoms 'jug dang / / mi ldan pa dag rgyu mthun pa/ /

They belong to the desire and form realms, they are communicated to sentient beings, arise from natural outflow, undeclared; (2:47cd)
so too [they are] homogeneous, also karmic maturation, which exists in the three realms. Obtainment has two types, also characteristics. Meditative attainments and nonpossession arise from natural outflow. (2:48)

ming la sogs pa de dag{ khams gsum las} 'dod pa'i khams dang gzugs kyi khams su gtogs kyi gzugs med par ni ma yin te/ de dag ni sgra rang gi mtshan nyid 'dzin pa'i shes pa'i rjes su 'brang ba'i rnam rtog la snang ba yin na gzugs med na sgra dang snang ba'i rnam shes med pa'i phyir dang*/ ming la sogs pa ni don rjod byed yin la/ gzugs med na ni gang zag phan tshun yul ma yin pas rjod byed ma yin pa'i yang phyir ro/ / kha cig na re gzugs med na ni ming med na rnam rtog med par thal bar 'gyur pa'i phyir ming yod kyang tshig med pa'i phyir brjod bya dang rjod byed ni ma yin no zhes 'dod do/

In brief, nouns and so on belong to the desire realm and the form realm but not to the formless realm {from among the three realms} [161] because they appear to conception after sense consciousness apprehends the characteristics of sound but consciousness to which sound appears does not exist in the formless realm. Nouns and so on express meaning, but they are not the shared objects of beings in the formless realm. One asserts: If there are no nouns in the formless realm, it would follow that conceptuality would not exist there. Even if names existed, there would be no [meaning] expressed, nor the means to express it, because there are no words there.

{ ston pa gnyis las/ /} sems can du ston pa'ang yin te/{ brjod pa po'i/} rtsol ba las byung ba dang*/ rgyud du gtogs pa'i phung po'i tshogs pa na yod pa'i phyir ro/{ skal mnyam gyi rgyus bskyed bas byung ba gsum las/} rgyu mthun las byung ba yin gyi rgyas byung dang rnam smin las byung ba ni ma yin te/ rdul phran bsags pa ma yin pas rgyas pa'i rgyu dag gis rgyas par mi 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ 'dod pa tsam gyis skye ba dang 'gag pa'i phyir dang*/{ mtshungs ldan ma yin pa la/} rnam smin las byung ba ni 'dod pa'i rjes su mi byed pa'i phyir ro/ / dge ba dang nyon mongs can du lung bstan pa ni min te/ 'dod chags dang bral ba dang dge rtsa chad pa rnams la'ang ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir ma bsgribs lung ma bstan kho na yin no/ /

Also {from the two modes of communication} [nouns] are communicated (khyā) to sentient beings (sattva) because they arise from the exertion {of the speaker} and they always exist in the collection of aggregates. {From the three that are generated by homogeneous cause,} they arise from natural outflow (niṣyandā) but not from enhancement. The cause of enhancement does not enhance them because they are not a collection of atoms and because they are generated or stopped by mere desire. They do not arise from karmic maturation because that which is derived from {nonconcomitant} karmic maturation does not follow [a person’s] desire. They are not declared (āvyākṛta) to be virtuous or afflicted because they are possessed by those free from attachment as well as by those who have severed their root of virtue. Therefore they are unobscured-neutral states.

Just as nouns and so on that are communicated to sentient beings are unobscured-neutral states that arise from natural outflow, so too they are homogeneous (sabhāga). And such homogeneity also arises from karmic maturation (vipāka) because homogeneous states of karmic maturation such as the sense faculties arise from past karma. {Those arising from natural outflow are homogeneous states such as virtue.} Unlike the former [i.e., nouns and so on, homogeneity] exists in the three realms (dhātu) such as the desire realm since it is said that homogeneity exists in the formless realm.

thob pa ni rgyu mthun dang rnam smin las byung ba rnam pa gnyis yin la/ khyad par gzhan dag ni bshad zin to/ / de bzhin du skye ba la sogs pa'i mtshan nyid rnams kyang rgyu mthun dang rnam smin las byung ba dang*/ khams gsum pa dag yin no/ / sems can du ston mi ston gnyis ka dang*/ dge mi dge lung ma bstan gsum ga yod do/ /

Obtainment (āpta) has two types — that arising from natural outflow and karmic maturation — and its other attributes have already been explained. Also characteristics (lakṣaṇa) such as arising occur from natural outflow and karmic maturation and exist in the three realms. They are either demonstrable (Tib. ston) or not to sentient beings, and they have three types: virtuous, nonvirtuous, and neutral.

snyoms 'jug gnyis dang*/ mi ldan pa dag ni rgyu mthun las byung ba yin gyi rgyas pa dang rnam smin las byung ba ni med de/ de gsum ga gzugs can ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/{ rnam smin gyi ma thob pa yang rnam smin min na gzhan lta ci smos shing*/} snyoms 'jug gnyis ka dge ba kho nar nges pa dang*/ mi ldan pa dag ni dge mi dge'i las kyis 'phangs pa ma yin par zhar la 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / de dag gi khyad par lhag ma dang*/ 'du shes med pa pa dang*/ srog gi dbang po'i khyad par dag ni bshad zin to// //

Both meditative attainments (samāpatti) and nonpossession (asamanvaya) arise from natural outflow (niṣyanda), but they do not arise from enhancement and karmic maturation because those three are not physical. {Also the nonobtainment of karmic maturation is not karmic maturation. What need then to mention the others?} In addition, both meditative attainments are definitely virtuous alone, and nonpossession is not projected by virtuous or nonvirtuous karma. Any remaining differences, and differences in the state of nondiscernment and the faculty of life force, have already been explained. [162]
10. Causes, Results, and Conditions
gnyis pa zhar la rgyu rkyen 'bras bu dang bcas pa bshad pa
IN ADDITION, EXPLAINING CAUSES, RESULTS, AND CONDITIONS
['di] la rgyu dang 'bras bu dang rkyen bshad pa gsum gyi
This has three headings: the six causes, the five results, and the four conditions.
dang po
The six causes
['di] la'ang gsum las
This also has three headings: overview, their individual natures, and the abbreviated meaning of those causes.
mdor bstan pa ni
OVERVIEW
byed rgyu lhan cig 'byung ba dang / / skal mnyam mtshungs par ldan pa dang / / 49 kun tu 'gro dang rnam smin dang / rgyu ni rnam pa drug tu 'dod/ /
They assert causes to be of six types: active, coemergent, homogeneous, concomitant, omnipresent, and karmic maturation. (2:49)

chos mngon pa pa rnams kyis rgyu ni rnam pa drug tu 'dod do zhes 'byung gis/ rgyu ni rnam pa drug tu gsungs zhes mi 'byung ba ni/ bstan bcos mngon pa'i mdzod rtsom pa'i dus su rab tu bsdu ba'i gzhi po nyams pas rgyu drug phyogs gcig tu ston pa'i mdo ma gzigs la rgyu drug so sor ston pa'i mdo ni gzigs te/ mig dang gzugs la brten nas mig gi rnam par shes pa skye'o zhes pa gsungs pa ni byed rgyu ston pa'o/ / lam gyis yan lag gsum po 'di dag ni yang dag pa'i lta ba'i rjes su 'brangs pa yin te/ lhan cig skyes pa'i tshor ba dang 'du shes dang sems pa'o/ / zhes gsungs pa ni lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu ston pa'i mdo'o/ / skyes bu gang zag 'di ni dge ba'i chos dang ldan la/ mi rig pa'i chos rnams dang yang ldan zhes bya ba nas 'di la dge ba'i rtsa ba kun du ma chad pa gang las 'di'i dge ba'i rtsa ba las dge rtsa gzhan skye bar 'gyur ba chung ngu dang lhan cig pa mngon/ de ltar na skyes bu gang zag 'di phyis rnam par dag pa'i chos can 'gyur ro zhes pa ni skal mnyam gyi rgyu ston pa'i mdo'o/ / rtogs nas shes pa dang ldan par mtshungs pa 'di ni mthong ba'i gzhi can gyi dad pa'o zhes pa ni mtshungs par ldan pa'i rgyu ston pa'i mdo'o/ / skyes bu gang zag log par lta ba can gyi lus kyi las gang yin pa dang*/ ngag gi las gang yin pa dang*/ sems pa gang yin pa dang*/ smon pa gang yin pa dang*/ de dag dang rjes su mthun pa'i 'du byed gang yin pa de thams cad mi 'dod par 'gyur bar mi sdug par 'gyur ba dang*/ mi dga' ba nyid du 'gyur ba dang*/ yid du mi 'ong ba nyid du 'gyur bar byed pa'o zhes pa kun 'gro'i rgyu ston pa'i mdo'o/ / ched du bsams pa'i las byas shing bsags pa'i rnam par smin pa zhes pa ni rnam par smin pa'i rgyu ston pa'i mdo'o/ / zhes sbyar ro/ /

Ābhidharmikas assert causes (hetu) to be of six types, but [a single sūtra that] “states causes to be of six types” does not exist. When the Abhidharmakośa was composed, the Condensed Principles was no longer extant, and so [Vasubandhu] did not see the sūtra teaching the six causes to be a single cause. He did see, however, sūtras individually teaching the six causes. For instance, the sūtra passage “In dependence on the eye and form, eye consciousness is generated”[606] teaches active cause; the passage “The three branches of the path are associated with right view because they simultaneously generate feeling, discernment, and intention”[607] teaches coemergent cause; the passage “This being who possesses virtuous states also possesses states of ignorance. For as long as he does not sever his root of virtue, and he develops his root of virtue from what it was previously, he simultaneously manifests a small increase [of virtue] and in this way that being gradually becomes purified”[608] teaches homogeneous cause; the passage “That which accords with knowledge through realization is faith based on seeing” teaches concomitant cause; the passage “Any physical action, verbal action, intention, prayer, or concordant formative factor of a being who possesses wrong view produces that which is not desired, ugly, disliked, unpleasant”[609] teaches omnipresent cause; and the passage “Having committed purposeful intentional karma, there is the maturation of [that] accumulated [karma]”[610] teaches the cause of karmic maturation.

Question: What are they? Reply: They are active cause (kāraṇa), coemergent cause (sahabhū), homogeneous cause (sabhāga), concomitant cause (saṃprayukta), omnipresent cause (sarvatraga), and the cause of karmic maturation (vipāka). {Causes are set as six in number because (1) active cause is the common cause of all results. In terms of specific causes, (2) coemergent cause is the cause of general coexistence, and (3) concomitant cause is the cause of specific coexistence. (4) Homogeneous cause generates similar states at different times. (5) Omnipresent cause generates similar afflicted states alone. (6) The cause of karmic maturation generates dissimilar states.} [163]
so so'i rang bzhin bshad pa
EXPLAINING THEIR INDIVIDUAL NATURES
['di] la drug las/
This has six headings: active cause, coemergent cause, homogeneous cause, concomitant cause, omnipresent cause, and cause of karmic maturation.
dang po byed rgyu ni
ACTIVE CAUSE
rang las gzhan pa byed rgyu'i rgyu/ /
Any state other than itself is an active cause. (2:50a)

{ rang la rang gi byed pa 'gal bas} 'bras bu rang nyid las gzhan pa{ 'dus byas ma byas} thams cad ni byed rgyu'i rgyu zhes bya bar 'dod do/ / ci ste na/ 'bras bu skye ba la gegs mi byed pa'i ngo bor gnas pa'i phyir ro/ /

Any {conditioned or unconditioned state} other than the result itself is a cause called active cause (kāraṇahetu), {since it would be contradictory for something to act on itself}. Question: Why? Reply: That is because by nature they do not stop the arising of an effect.

gal te gegs mi byed pa tsam gyis rgyur ji ltar 'gyur te/ myu gu la sogs pa'i rgyur 'dus ma byas dang*/ gzugs med pa'i phung po'i rgyu dmyal ba'ang yin par 'gyur ro zhe na/ 'dir byed rgyu ni nus bcas dang nus med gnyis las dang po ni myu gu la sogs pa la sa bon la sogs pa lta bu ste byed rgyu mtshan nyid pa yin no/ / gnyis pa ni/ 'dus ma byas la sogs pa dang gzugs med pa'i phung po la dmyal ba la sogs pa lta bu ste/ 'di ni gegs mi byed pa la rgyur btags pa yin te grong pa rnams rgyal pos khral dmag la sogs pas sdug bsngal bar ma byas pa la bdag cag bde bar byas so zer ba lta bu'o/ / kha cig na re thams cad kyang thams cad la brgyud nas ci rigs par 'dus ma byas dang dmyal ba la sogs pas kyang yid kyi rnam shes dmigs pa'i tshul gyis bskyed par nus la/ de las dge mi dge dang*/ de las kyang rim gyis snod kyi 'jig rten dang gzugs med kyi phung po la sogs pa skye ba'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ /

Question: How does something become a cause through merely not stopping something? In that case unconditioned states would become the cause of sprouts and so on, and hell beings would be the cause of formless-realm aggregates. Reply: Here, active cause is either (1) potent or (2) nonpotent. (1) The first refers to seeds and so on, which are actual active causes of sprouts and so forth. (2) The second refers to such things as unconditioned states or hell beings and so on [that act as causes of] formless-realm aggregates and so forth since they don’t prevent them from existing. It is like a king who imposes taxes, wars, and so forth on his subjects to ensure their happiness and not to cause them pain. Some say: Everything indirectly arises from everything, for any unconditioned states or hell beings and so on are capable of generating mental consciousness when mental consciousness focuses on them, and from that virtue or nonvirtue arises, and from that, respectively, physical world systems or formless-realm aggregates and so on may arise.

gal te skye ba la gegs mi byed pa rgyu yin na snang ba dang tsha reg la sogs pa mun pa dang grang reg la sogs pa'i byed rgyur mi 'gyur te/ de dag ni chos de dag la gegs byed pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar na'ang rang las gzhan pa thams cad byed rgyur mi 'gyur ro zhe na/ snang ba la sogs pa de dag mun pa la sogs pa mi skye ba'i chos can la gegs byed kyi skye ba la ni gegs bya bar mi nus{ te ma tshang med rgyud la ni/ 'bras bu gang gis bzlog par byed ces 'byung} pa'i phyir dang*/ byed rgyu ni skye ba la gegs mi byed pa yin pa'i phyir de dag kyang de dag gi byed rgyu{ yin te gegs byed nus kyang gegs ma byas pas rgyu yin te rje bos bde bar byas so zhes pa dang 'dra bas} yin no zhes bya ba ni bye brag tu smra ba'i grub pa'i mtha' yin no/ /

Objection: If that which did not stop arising were a cause, then light and hot sensation and so on would not be the active cause of darkness and cold sensation and so forth because they stop those phenomena. Thus they would not be active causes of all entities other than themselves. Reply: Light and so on stop unarisen instances such as darkness, but they are incapable of stopping arisen instances {because it is said, “What can block the results of causes that are not incomplete?”} and active causes do not stop arising. They are their active cause {since they don’t stop, though they are capable of stopping them. Therefore they are causes, because they are similar to a ruler who ensures the happiness of his subjects.} These are tenets of the Vaibhāṣikas.
