yang na snang ba la sogs pas mun pa la sogs pa nus chung ngu bskyed pa la gegs su 'dod na de ni byed rgyu nyid yin pa'i phyir dang*/ mun pa la sogs pa med pa dang 'jig pa ni snang bas byas pa ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ de dag las gzhan pa'i gegs kyang mi 'thad pa'i phyir yang dag par na gegs byed pa ni rgyu ma tshang bas 'bras bu mi skye ba'am/ nus chung ngu skyes pa'i rgyu la brjod pa'i phyir 'gal ba med do zhes bya'o/ /

Again, if it is asserted that light and so on stops darkness and so forth since it weakens its potency, then this is because it is the active cause itself, for light does not act to obliterate or destroy darkness and so on, and it is unacceptable that it stops other different states. In fact, there is no contradiction in stating that stopping refers to results not being generated through incomplete causes, or to causes that arise being weak in potency. [164]
lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu/
COEMERGENT CAUSE
lhan cig 'byung gang phan tshun 'bras/ / 50 'byung bzhin sems kyi rjes 'jug dang / / sems dang mtshan nyid mtshan gzhi bzhin/ /
Coemergent causes are reciprocal results like the great elements, like the mind and associates of the mind, and like characteristics and the basis characterized. (2:50bcd)

gnyis pa lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu ni gang zhig phan tshun gyi 'bras bu can yin no/ / de yang dper brjod pa{ tshogs pa gcig pa'i} ni sa la sogs pa'i 'byung ba chen po bzhi phan tshun lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu yin pa bzhin dang sems kyi rjes 'jug rnams dang sems kyang phan tshun lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu yin pa bzhin dang*/ 'dus byas kyi mtshan nyid rnams kyang mtshan gzhi'i rgyu yin la/ mtshan gzhi'ang mtshan nyid kyi rgyu yin pa bzhin no/ / bzhin zhes pa ni 'dir dngos su ma brjod pa sems kyi rjes 'jug phan tshun dang*/ mtshan nyid rnams kyang phan tshun 'bras bu yin no zhes mtshon pa'o/ / zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/ / gal te phan tshun du rgyur gyur pa yin na bum pa la sogs pa'i chos rnams skye ba'i skye ba la sogs pa mthun pa'i mtshan nyid rnams kyis lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyur mi 'gyur te/ mthun pa'i mtshan nyid rnams chos la phan mi dogs pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ de lta mod kyi 'on kyang 'di ni phal che ba'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi khyab pa ni ma yin no zhes kha bskang ba dang bcas pa'o/

Coemergent causes (sahabhūhetu) are reciprocal results (mithaḥphala), for example, like the four great elements (bhutā) such as earth being reciprocal coemergent causes {within a single collection}, or like the mind (citta) and associates of the mind (cittānuvarti) being reciprocal coemergent causes, or like the characteristics (lakṣaṇa) of conditioned states being the cause of the basis characterized and the basis characterized (lakṣyavat) being the cause of its characteristics. Master Purṇavardhana explains that though it is not directly expressed here, “like” indicates that associates of the mind [and the mind itself] are reciprocal results, and also that characteristics [and the basis characterized] are reciprocal results.[611] Objection: If [you think] they are reciprocal causes [of each other,] then secondary characteristics such as the endurance of endurance of objects such as vases would not be coemergent causes [of the object] because secondary characteristics do not benefit the object. Reply: Indeed, that is so from a general perspective, but “there is no logical pervasion” is stated to rectify a deficiency.

{ de la spyir 'dus byas su mtshon pa'i mtshan gzhi bum pa lta bu gcig gi rang gi mtshan nyid bzhi de dag gi rjes mthun gyi mtshan nyid bzhi dang brgyad kyi lhan kyi lhan cig 'byung rgyu byed cing skyed kyang mthun pa'i mtshan nyid bzhi ni mtshan gzhi dang rang rang gi grogs gsum gsum dang lhan cig tu 'byung yang de dag skyed pa'i lhan cig 'byung rgyu min te rgyal po'i nying g.yog gis rgyal po la dngos su bya ba byed mi nus pa bzhin dang*/ grogs gsum la'ang skyed pa'i bya ba mi 'jug pas so/ / sems dang sems kyi rjes 'jug rnams gcig gcig gi 'byung rgyu yin kyang mthun pa'i mtshan nyid thams cad rang rang gi mtshan gzhi thams cad kyi lhan cig gi 'byung rgyu min te nying g.yog bzhin no/ / gzugs sgra dri ro reg rnams dang so thar gyi spong bdun dang 'byung bzhi lhan cig 'byung zhing 'byung ba de dag gi yin yang de dag 'byung ba'i min no zhes so/ / de yang 'dus byas bum pa dang de'i mtshan nyid skye sogs rang rang ma gtogs pa chos brgyad brgyad kyi lhan cig 'byung rgyu byed cing skye ba'i skye bas rtsa skye kho na skyed cing lhan cig 'byung rgyu byed pa nas 'jig pa'i 'jig pas rtsa 'jig kho na skyed pa'i bar du'o/ / sems byung dang sdom pa gnyis dang sems dang sems kyi rjes 'jug de dag gi mtshan nyid rnams ni sems kyi rjes 'jug yin te rnam pa bcus sems kyi rjes su 'jug pa'i phyir ro/ / rnam pa bcu ni spyir dus tsam gcig ste/ sems grub pa'i dus su de dag kyang grub pa'i phyir ro/ / khyad par du skye dus gcig pa dang*/ gnas dus gcig pa dang*/'gag pa dus gcig pa ste/ dus gcig pa bzhi dang*/ bdag 'bras ni chos thams cad kyi thun mong ba yin pas de bor la/ skyes bu byed 'bras dang bral 'bras gcig pa 'bras bu tsam gcig pa dang*/ sems kyi rnam smin 'bras yin na de dag gi'ang yin pas rnam smin 'bras gcig pa dang*/ de'i rgyu mthun 'bras yin na de dag gi'ang yin pa rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu gcig pa ste 'bras bu gcig pa gsum dang*/ sems de dag ni rjes 'jug dge ba la sogs pa gsum ste bcus sems kyi rjes su 'jug go /}

'di'i mtshan nyid la kha cig dus mnyam pa'i rgyu 'bras mtshungs ldan gyi rgyu las gzhan pa zhes zer ba ni ma yin te/ mtshungs ldan gyi lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu ma yin par 'gyur ba dang*/ bum pa dang de 'dzin mig shes dang mar me dang 'od dang myu gu dang grib ma dang sa gzhi la chu brten pa la sogs pa'ang lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyur thal ba'i phyir ro/ / des na 'di'i mtshan nyid ni snga ma nyid yin no/ / ma khyab pa brjod pa ni grub mtha'i nyes pa yin no/ / 'o na sems kyi rjes su 'jug pa'i chos de dag gang zhe na/

Regarding their characteristics, some say: Cause and effect that occur at the same time are different from concomitant causes. Reply: That is not so, because then a concomitant cause would not be a coemergent cause, and it would follow that a vase and the eye consciousness apprehending it, the flame of a butter lamp and its light, a sprout and its shadow, and water and the earth supporting it and so on would become coemergent causes. Therefore, these characteristics are as explained before. The statement “there is no logical pervasion” indicates a fault of this tenet system.[612] Question: What are those phenomena that are associates of the mind?
sems las byung dang sdom gnyis dang / / sems dang de dag gi mtshan nyid/ / 51 sems kyi rjes 'jug dus dang ni/ / 'bras sogs dge la sogs pas so/ /
Associates of the mind are mental factors, both vows, and the characteristics of minds and mental factors. They have the same time, result, and so on and the same virtuous nature and so on. (2:51)

sems las byung ba rnams dang bsam gtan zag med kyi sdom pa gnyis dang sems dang{ sems kyi rjes 'jug} sems byung rnams dang sdom pa gnyis po de dag gi skye ba la sogs pa'i mtshan nyid rnams ni sems kyi rjes su 'jug pa yin no/ / ci'i phyir zhe na sems dang{ spyir} dus gcig pa'i phyir dang*/{ bdag 'bras dang skyes bu byed pa dang bral ba'o/ /} 'bras bu gcig pa dang sogs {pa rnam smin dang rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu gcig } pa'i phyir dang*/ dge ba la sogs pa gcig pas so/ / zhes pa'i gtan tshigs kyi phyir ro/ / de la dus gcig pa ni spyir dus {tsam } gcig pa dang*/ khyad par du skye ba gcig pa dang*/ gnas pa gcig pa dang 'gag pa gcig pa rnams bsdus so/ / 'bras bu gcig pa ni bdag po'i 'bras bu dang skyes bu byed pa dang bral ba'i 'bras bu rnams gcig pa'o/ / sogs pa'i sgras rgyu mthun dang rnam smin gyi 'bras bu gnyis gzung ste/ de 'bras bu gcig pa ni ngo bo gcig pa ste gang sems kyi rnam smin gyi 'bras bu yin pa de sems kyi rjes 'jug gi'ang yin no zhes bya ba la sogs pa'o/ / dus dang dge {ba la sogs/ } bar gcig pa ni sems {skye ba la sogs pa dang*/ } dge ba{ la sogs pa} yin na rjes 'jug rnams kyang{ skye ba la sogs pa dang} dge ba{ la sogs pa} yin pas/

Reply: Associates of the mind (cittānuvarti) are mental factors (caitta), both absorption and uncontaminated vows (saṃvara), and the characteristics (lakṣaṇa) of minds and mental factors {that are associates of the mind} and [the characteristics] of both vows, such as arising and so forth. Question: Why? Reply: That is because they exist at the same {general} time (kāla) as the mind; because they have the same result (phala) {dominant result, result of conscious effort, and result of separation} and so on, {including the same result of karmic maturation and result of natural outflow}; and because they have the same nature that is virtuous (śubha) and so on. Existing at the same time means they have the same general time {itself,} and that includes the same specific arising, the same endurance, and the same cessation. Having the same result means having the same dominant result, the same result of conscious effort, and the same result of separation. The [first] “and so on” refers to having the same result of natural outflow and karmic maturation, for having the same result is having the same nature, and the associates of the mind possess the same result of karmic maturation as the mind and so on. Having the same time and virtue {and so on} means that if the mind {and its arising and so forth} are virtuous {and so on,} then also its associates {such as arising and so forth} are virtuous {and so on}.

'di{ dag} ni 'dra ba la gcig par brjod pa yin no/ / sogs pa'i sgras ni mi dge ba dang lung ma bstan bzung ngo*/ / des na 'grel pa las/ rgyu bcus sems kyi rjes su 'jug pa zhes bya'o zhes gsungs pa'ang ci rigs {pa la sogs} kyi dbang du byas kyi yang dag par na brgyad yin te/ dge ba la sogs pa gsum sems gcig la 'du ba mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / brgyad kyang mang ba'i mtha' gzung ba yin gyi ma bsgribs lung ma bstan dang zag med la rnam smin gyi 'bras bu mi srid cing*/ mi skye ba'i chos can la ni dus gcig pa tsam ma gtogs pa skye ba dang*/ gnas pa dang*/ 'gag pa gcig pa'ang mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ { de yang lung ma bstan mi skye ba'i chos can la dge mi dge gnyis skye gnas 'jig gsum rnam smin gyi 'bras bu dor ba'i lhag ma bzhi/ rnam smin gyi rgyu mi skye ba'i chos can la sngar gyi bzhi'i steng du rnam smin 'bras bu bsnan pas lnga/ zag med skye 'gyur la mi dge ba lung ma bstan rnam smin gyi 'bras bu dang gsum dor bas bdun lung ma bstan skye 'gyur la'ang dge mi dge gnyis rnam smin 'bras dang gsum dor ba bdun/ rnam smin skye 'gyur la dge mi dge gnyis dor ba'i lhag ma brgyad 'byung ba sogs shes par bya'o/ /}

Therefore those that are similar are called “the same,” and the term “and so on” refers to nonvirtuous and neutral states. From any perspective {and so on} there are just eight, because even though the Autocommentary mentions: They are called associates of the mind due to ten causes,[613] it is impossible for the three states of virtue and so on to be included in one mind. Although eight is held as the upper limit, the result of karmic maturation is impossible for unobscured-neutral or uncontaminated states, unarisen instances do not belong to the same time, and it is impossible they have the same arising, endurance, and cessation. {Moreover, you should understand that neutral unarisen instances occur with the four remaining causes through omitting the result of karmic maturation of the three states of arising, endurance, and disintegration of both virtue and nonvirtue. Instances of the nonarising of karmic maturation occur with five: the previous four plus the result of karmic maturation. Uncontaminated states that are yet to arise occur with seven through eliminating three: nonvirtuous and neutral states and the result of karmic maturation. Also, neutral states yet to arise occur with seven through eliminating three: virtuous and nonvirtuous states and the result of karmic maturation. [166] Karmic maturation yet to arise occurs with the remaining eight through eliminating both virtue and nonvirtue.}

de la sems 'khor nyung ba bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad kyi ma bsgribs lung ma bstan ni{ 'khor kun 'gro bcu las mi 'byung bas khos phar la} lnga bcu rtsa brgyad kyi lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu byed de/ sems kyis mang po pa bcu dang*/ de dag gi mtshan nyid bzhi bcu dang*/ {sems/ } rang nyid kyi mtshan nyid bzhi dang*/ {rang gi } mthun pa'i mtshan nyid bzhi'o/ / sems {rang nyid/ } la{ tshur la rang gi bzhi 'khor bzhi bcu dang} ni lnga bcu rtsa bzhis byed de/ {rang gi } mthun pa'i mtshan nyid bzhi po{ dang 'khor gyi mthun pa'i mtshan nyid bzhi po} rnams ma gtogs pa ste/ de dag ni rang gi mtshan nyid skye ba{ chos kho na} la sogs pa la phan 'dogs pa lhur byed kyi gzhan la ni ma yin te rgyal po'i nying g.yog{ gis rgyal po la dngos su bya ba byed mi nus pa} bzhin no zhes kha che bye brag tu smra ba rnams 'dod do/ / nyi 'og pa rnams ni sems la bcu bzhis byed de sems las byung ba'i mtshan nyid rnams kyang rang gi mtshan gzhi la byed kyi stobs chung bas sems la ni ma yin te/{ ring ba'i phyir ro/} rgyal po'i nying g.yog bzhin no zhes 'dod do/ /

Unobscured-neutral minds with small retinues of the second absorption and above act as the coemergent cause of fifty-eight {when elaborated, since only the retinue of the ten omnipresent mental factors occurs} because there are (1–10) the ten universal mental states, (11–50) their forty characteristics, (51–54) the four characteristics of {mind}, and (55–58) {their} four secondary characteristics. Fifty-four act as [coemergent causes] for the mind {itself}: {the inner [ten universals], four of the mind itself, and forty as retinue,} omitting the four secondary characteristics {and the secondary characteristics of the retinue} because they genuinely benefit its characteristics such as {the property} of arising and so on. The others [i.e., the secondary characteristics] do not, for they are like the outer retinue of a king {who cannot serve the king directly}. This is asserted by Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas. Aparāntaka [Vaibhāṣikas] assert that fourteen act [as coemergent causes of] mind. The characteristics of mental factors act as [coemergent causes of] their characterized basis [i.e., the mental factors] but not of the mind since they are weak in strength {and distant from the mind,} like the outer servants of a king.

kha che ba rnams na re de lta na bstan bcos rab tu byed pa las sdug bsngal gyi bden pa la 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i rgyu can yin la 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i rgyu ma yin pa yang yod de/ 'jig tshogs la lta ba dang*/ de dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i chos rnams kyi skye ba dang rga ba dang*/ gnas pa dang*/ mi rtag pa dag ma gtogs pa de dag las gzhan pa'i sdug bsngal gyi bden pa nyon mongs pa can gang yin pa'o/ / 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i rgyu can yang yin la 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i rgyu yang yin pa ni ma gtogs pa gang yin pa'o zhes gsungs pa dang 'gal bar 'gyur te/ sems las byung ba'i mtshan nyid rnams {kyang mu dang por 'gyur gyi mu gsum par mi 'gyur te/} sems kyi lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu ma yin na 'jig tshogs la lta ba dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i sems dang sems las byung ba rnams kyi mtshan nyid rnams 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i rgyu can yin pa rgyu ma yin pa'i mur 'gyur te/ mtshan nyid rnams de'i skal mnyam dang kun 'gro dang mtshungs ldan gyi rgyu ni ma yin la lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu yang ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / des na rab tu byed pa las de dag gnyis ka yin pa'i mur bshad pa'i phyir dang*/ ji ltar 'jig tshogs la lta ba dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i sems dang sems las byung ba'i mtshan nyid rnams 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i lhan cig 'byung ba yin pa ltar rgyu mtshan mtshungs pa'i phyir sems dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i mtshan nyid rnams kyang sems kyi lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu yin no zhes zer ro/ / nyi 'og pa rnams ni de skad du ni rab tu byed pa las mi 'don gyi 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i skye ba dang zhes bya ba la sogs par 'don pa'i phyir 'gal ba med do zhes zer ro/ /

Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas say: If that is so, then that would contradict the treatise (Topic Divisions), which explains: The truth of suffering, which is caused by the afflicted view of the self but is not the cause of the afflicted view of the self, is [the first possibility:] any afflicted truth of suffering that includes the arising, aging, enduring, and impermanence of states concomitant with the afflicted view of the self. That which is caused by the afflicted view of the self and is also the cause of the afflicted view of the self is [the third possibility:] any not included [in that].[614] If the characteristics of the mental factors, {which are the first possibility but not the third possibility,} are not coemergent causes of mind, then the characteristics of minds and mental factors that are concomitant with the afflicted view of the self would be the [first] possibility — that caused by the afflicted view of the self but not the cause [of the afflicted view of self] — because those characteristics would not be the homogeneous cause, omnipresent cause, concomitant cause, or even the coemergent cause of [the afflicted view of self]. Then Topic Divisions explains the [third] possibility: those that are both. It declares: In whatever way the characteristics of minds and mental factors concomitant with the afflicted view of the self are coemergent with the afflicted view of the self, the characteristics concomitant with the mind are also coemergent causes of the mind, because the reason is similar.[615] Aparāntakas say that Topic Divisions does not proclaim that, but there is no contradiction because it does mention the arising of the afflicted [167] view of the self and so on.

kha che ba rnams ni{ dngos su} mi 'don kyang don gyis thob pas gdon par bya'o zhes zer ro/ / 'dir de tsam gyis chog mod kyi 'on kyang bshad pa mdzad pa rnams kyis rab tu byed pa'i gzhung gi {'jig tshogs la lta ba'i rgyu dang rgyu can gyi/ } mu'i bshad pa shin tu spros pa dang bcas par 'chad pa'i phyir kho bos {kyang } bri ste/ de la 'dir rgyu drug las byed rgyu nus med ni mi brtse ste/ btags pa ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ / nus bcas kyang {shes bya thams cad byed rgyu yin pas/ } rgyu lnga'ang kho'i khongs su gtogs pa'i phyir logs su mi bgrang ngo*/ / rnam smin gyi rgyu 'bras dang bral 'bras kyang mi gzung ste/ 'jig tshogs la lta ba{ bsgribs la lung ma bstan yin pas} rnam smin gyi rgyu 'bras gnyis kar mi 'thad pa'i phyir dang*/ 'jig tshogs la lta ba bral ba ma yin zhing{ lam min pas} bral ba'i rgyur yang mi rung ba'i phyir ro/ / bdag 'bras kyang mi brtsi ste/ 'dus byas thams cad bdag 'bras yin pa'i phyir ram/ yang na 'bras bu bzhi'i khongs su 'du ba'i phyir ro/ / des na rgyu ni lhan cig 'byung ba dang skal mnyam dang mtshungs ldan dang kun 'gro bzhi dang*/ 'bras bu ni rgyu mthun dang skyes bu byed 'bras gnyis la rgyu dang rgyu can gyi mu brtsi bar bya'o/{ de yang rab tu byed pa las bden bzhi la brtsams nas gsungs kyang 'dir bden bzhi dang nam mkha' brtags min dang bcas pa la brtsi ste/}

Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas say that though it does not {directly} declare this, since that meaning obtains, it is [tacitly] declared. Here, at least this much is agreed upon. Because commentators have extensively elaborated the explanations of the possibilities {of being the cause and being caused by the afflicted view of the self} stated in the text of the Topic Divisions, I {also} have written them down here. Still, in this context, from among the six causes, nonpotent [active cause] is not counted [as a possibility] because it is merely a nominal [cause,] and also potent [active cause] is not separately counted [as a possibility] from among the five causes {since all objects of knowledge are active causes}. Also the cause and effect of karmic maturation, and the result of separation, are not included because the afflicted view of the self is not accepted as either the cause or result of karmic maturation {since it is an obscured-neutral state,} and the afflicted view of the self is not separation and it is unsuitable to be the cause of separation {since it is not the path}. Nor is it counted as a dominant result, because either all conditioned states are dominant results or they are included within the four results. Therefore, cause is fourfold — (1) coemergent, (2) homogeneous, (3) concomitant, and (4) omnipresent; result is twofold — (1) the result of natural outflow and (2) the result of conscious effort; and the possibilities for being their cause and being caused by them should be calculated [with reference to them]. {Though Topic Divisions begins with the four truths, here the [four possibilities] are calculated [with reference] to the four truths along with space and nonanalytical cessation}.

de yang mu bzhi pa sngon la bshad na go bde bas bden pa bzhi las 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i rgyu 'bras gnyis ka ma yin pa ni 'gog lam gyi bden pa dang*/ nam mkha' dang brtags min gyi 'gog pa dang*/ sdug bsngal gyi bden pa'i sgom spang nyon mongs can ma yin{ dge ba zag bcas dang ma bsgribs lung ma bstan} pa rnams te/ de dag dang 'jig tshogs la lta ba la phan tshun du rgyu bzhi dang 'bras bu gnyis mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / rgyu mtshan de nyid kyis nam mkha' dang so sor brtags min gyi 'gog pa'ang gnyis ka ma yin par lta'o/ / 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i rgyu yin la 'bras bu ma yin pa'i mu gnyis pa ni mi srid de/ 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i rgyu rnam pa bzhi yin pa de ni nyon mongs can kho nar nges la/ nyon mongs can thams cad kyang 'jig tshogs la lta ba kun 'gro'i rgyu las skye ba'i phyir ro/ /

Further, the four possibilities that were previously explained can be made easier to understand: [The fourth possibility] is that which is neither the cause nor the result of the afflicted view of the self from among the four truths. This consists of the truth of path and the truth of cessation, space, nonanalytical cessation, and those {contaminated virtuous states and unobscured-neutral states} that are not afflicted objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation associated with the truth of suffering, since it is impossible for those to be [either] the four causes of the afflicted view of the self or the two results. And by that reasoning, even space and nonanalytical cessation would be neither. The second possibility is that which is the cause of the afflicted view of the self but not a result [of the afflicted view of self], which is impossible because the four aspects of the cause of the afflicted view of the self are definitely afflicted alone, and all afflicted entities are generated from the omnipresent cause of the afflicted view of the self.

'jig tshogs la lta ba'i 'bras bu yin la rgyu ma yin pa{ spang bya ris lnga las} ni sdug bsngal mthong spang gi phra rgyas{ bcu las} 'jig tshogs la lta ba rang nyid dang gzhan rnam pa dgu las ma rig pa ma gtogs pa brgyad po ma 'ongs pa mtshungs ldan dang bcas pa rnams yin te/ de dag ni nyon mongs can yin pas 'jig tshogs la lta ba 'das da ltar gyi kun 'gro'i rgyu las skyes pa'i phyir dang*/ 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i rgyu ni ma yin te ma 'ongs pa{ kun 'gro skal mnyam dus gnyis pa zhes pas} ni skal mnyam dang kun 'gro'i rgyu ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ ma rig pa ma gtogs pa rtsa ba'i nyon mongs pa phan tshun mtshungs par mi ldan pa'i phyir dang*/ lhan cig 'byung ba'ang ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'jig tshogs la lta ba rang nyid ma 'ongs pa'ang rang nyid 'das da ltar gyi skal mnyam kun 'gro las skye la/ ma 'ongs pa rgyu de gnyis ma yin zhing rang nyid rang dang lhan cig 'byung ba dang mtshungs par mi ldan pa'i phyir/ lta ba de'i 'bras bu yin la rgyu ma yin pa'o/ / de bzhin du kun 'byung mthong spang kun 'gro ma 'ongs pa mtshungs ldan {mtshan nyid/ } dang bcas pa rnams kyang {spang bya ris tha dad lhan cig tu mi 'byung ba sogs } rgyu mtshan de dag mtshungs pa'i phyir 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i 'bras bu yin la rgyu ma yin pa'o

[The first possibility] is that which is a result of the afflicted view of the self but not a cause [of the afflicted view of self]. This is just the afflicted view of the self {from the ten} negative tendencies that are objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering {from the five types of abandonment}, and the eight negative tendencies from the remaining nine, excluding ignorance and their future concomitant states because, being afflicted, they arise from the omnipresent cause of the past and present afflicted view of the self. But they are not the cause of the afflicted view of the self because the future is not a homogeneous cause. {As the Abhidharmakośa mentions, “Omnipresent and homogeneous causes exist at two times” (2:55a)}, for root afflictions [168] are not mutually concomitant except for ignorance, and they do not coexist. Also, the future afflicted view of the self is generated from past and present omnipresent and homogeneous causes because that future state is neither a cause nor is it concomitant or coemergent with them since that view is the result of them [i.e., past and present causes] and not a cause. Similarly, those possessing {characteristics} concomitant with future omnipresent objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of origin are the results of the afflicted view of the self but not causes of it, for a similar reason, {namely, that distinct types of abandonment do not simultaneously occur and so on}.

{ de rnams kun 'gro yin pas kun 'gro'i rgyur mi rung la/ ris tha dad pas skal ba mi mnyam la mtshungs par mi ldan pas lhan cig kyang mi 'byung bas} kun 'byung mthong spang kun 'gro ma yin pa mtshungs ldan dang bcas pa dus gsum pa rnams dang*/ 'gog lam mthong spang dang sgom spang nyon mongs can rnams kyang 'jig tshogs la lta ba kun 'gro'i rgyu las skyes la/{ sdug kun las gzhan la kun 'gro'i nyon mongs mi 'dod pas/} de dag ni kun 'gro'i rgyu ma yin zhing{ rang ris sa pa'o sngar skyes rnams zhes pas ris tha dad} skal ba mi mnyam la ris tha dad la mtshungs par mi ldan pa dang lhan cig 'byung ba'ang ma yin{ pas rgyu bzhi mi srid} pa'i phyir 'jig tshogs la lta ba ni de dag gi 'bras bu ma yin no/ / de bzhin du 'jig tshogs la lta ba la sogs pa nyon mongs can thams cad kyi thob pa{ dus gsum pa} rnams {kyang nyon mongs can yin pas 'jig lta'i 'bras bu yin la rgyu min pa'i mu ste 'di'i byed pa thob pa phyi ma 'jug gi chos la mi 'jug cing lhan cig 'byung yang nus pa mi 'jug pas rgyu ma yin pa'i phyir } dang{ dus gsum pa} 'jig tshogs la lta ba dang de dang mtshungs ldan rnams kyi mtshan nyid rnams ma gtogs pa nyon mongs can {pas rgyud ni mi srid} gzhan gyi mtshan nyid thams cad kyang 'jig tshogs la lta ba 'das da ltar gyi skal mnyam kun 'gro ci rigs pa'i 'bras bu yin la rgyu ma yin pa'o/ /

rgyu 'bras gnyis ka yin pa ni {tshan pa bzhi las } sdug bsngal mthong spang phra rgyas bcu po 'das da ltar ba mtshungs ldan dang bcas pa {rnams ni 'jig tshogs la lta ba snga ma'i skal mnyam kun 'gro'i rgyu las byung ba'i phyir dang*/ 'jig tshogs la lta ba'ang de dag snga ma'i skal mnyam kun 'gro'i rgyu ci rigs pa las byung ba yin te/ thams cad kyi skal mnyam dang*/ lta ba bzhi dang ma rig pa dang the tshom gyi kun 'gro'i rgyu las kyang byung ba'i phyir ro } yin te/ 'jig tshogs la lta ba ni bcu po de dag gi skal mnyam kun 'gro'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir dang*/ bcu po'ang 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i skal mnyam gyi rgyu yin zhing*/ de dag gi lta ba rnams dang the tshom dang ma rig pa ni lta ba dang po de'i kun 'gro'i rgyu'ang yin pa'i phyir ro/ / rtsa nyon las ma rig pa dang de las gzhan pa'i sems sems byung 'jig tshogs la lta ba dang mtshungs ldan dus gsum pa rnams kyang 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i rgyu 'bras gnyis ka yin te/ mtshungs ldan de dag 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i rgyu bzhi ka las 'byung ba'i phyir dang*/ 'jig tshogs la lta ba'ang mtshungs ldan 'das da ltar gyi rgyu bzhi dang*/ ma 'ongs pa'i lhan cig 'byung ba dang mtshungs ldan las 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du kun 'byung mthong spang kun 'gro'i phyogs 'das da ltar ba'ang 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i kun 'gro'i rgyu las 'byung ba'i phyir dang*/ 'jig tshogs la lta ba'ang de dag gi kun 'gro'i rgyu las 'byung ba'i phyir gnyis ka yin pa'i mu yin no/

[The third possibility] is both cause and effect {from the four divisions}. This is the ten negative tendencies that are objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering, and that are past, present, and concomitant. {The afflicted view of the self is derived from past homogeneous and omnipresent causes, and also the afflicted view of the self is derived from any type of homogeneity and omnipresent cause because it is derived from the homogeneity of all and from the omnipresent cause of the four views, ignorance, and doubt.} That is because the afflicted view of the self is the homogeneous and omnipresent cause of those ten, and also those ten are the homogeneous cause of the afflicted view of the self. And their views, doubt, and ignorance are also the omnipresent cause of the first view. Ignorance from the root afflictions, and those [afflicted states] of the three times concomitant with the afflicted view of the self, which are minds and mental factors other than that, [169] are both the cause and effect of the afflicted view of the self. This is because those that are concomitant are derived from the four causes of the afflicted view of the self, and also because the afflicted view of the self is derived from the four concomitant past and present causes and future coemergent and concomitant causes. Similarly, past and present omnipresent objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of origin are also derived from the omnipresent cause of the afflicted view of the self, and also the afflicted view of the self is derived from their omnipresent cause. Therefore, this is the [third] possibility: that which is both.

{ 'jig lta'i rgyu 'bras gnyis ka yin pa ni sdug bsngal mthong spang bcu po 'das da ltar la 'chad kyang de'i ma rig pa ni dus gsum pa la'ang de brtsir rung ngo*/ / ma rig pa ma gtogs pa dgu po ni snga phyi la bltas nas skal mnyam kun 'gro'i rgyu dang 'bras bu ni rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bur nges shing*/ ma rig pa dang 'jig lta gnyis dang mtshungs ldan gyi nyon mongs gzhan ni 'jig lta dang ci rigs su rgyu bzhi dang 'bras bu gnyis kar 'gyur ro/ / kho nyid ma 'ongs pa'i mtshungs ldan yang de bzhin te/ rgyu bzhi char du 'gyur la dus mnyam pa gnyis kyi 'bras bu'o/ / kho nyid dus gsum pa'i mtshan nyid dang*/ de'i mtshungs ldan gyi mtshan nyid rnams ni mtshungs ldan las gzhan pa'i rgyu gsum gyis rgyu dang rgyu can yin gyi mtshan nyid de dag mi ldan pa yin pas mtshungs ldan gyi rgyu 'bras min no/ / mu bzhi pa ni dge ba zag bcas dang*/ ma bsgribs lung ma bstan dang 'dus ma byas dang lam bden no/ /}

{Those which are both the cause and effect of the afflicted view of the self are said to be the ten past and present sufferings that are to be abandoned by the path of seeing, while ignorance of it that exists in the three times may also be counted. The nine except for ignorance that are causes and results of homogeneity and omnipresence dependent on whether they go before or after are determined to be results of natural outflow. The other afflictions concomitant with both ignorance and the afflicted view of the self are the four causes and two results of any type of afflicted view of the self. Also, future [affliction] concomitant with that itself is similar, because in being the four parts of cause, it is the result of both at the same time. Its characteristics of the three times, and the characteristics of those concomitant with it, are causes and possess causes through the three causes other than concomitant cause. Since it does not possess those characteristics, these are not concomitant cause and effect. The fourth possibility consists of contaminated virtue, unobscured-neutral states, unconditioned states, and the truth of path.}

'jig tshogs la lta ba'i mtshan nyid bzhi dang*/ de dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i sems sems byung rnams kyi mtshan nyid rnams kyang 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i skal mnyam dang kun 'gro dang lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu las skye la 'jig tshogs la lta ba'ang mtshan nyid de dag gi lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu las skye ba'i phyir gnyis ka yin no zhes kha che ba dag 'dod la/ nyi 'og pa ni 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i mtshan nyid rnams de'i rgyu 'bras gnyis ka yin gyi de dang mtshungs ldan rnams kyi mtshan nyid rnams ni 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i rgyu ma yin pas de ni 'bras bu yin la rgyu ma yin pa'i mu yin no zhes 'dod do/ / 'di dag kyang bye brag tu smra ba'i grub mthas brtags pa yin pas yang dag pa ma yin no/ / 'dir bye brag tu smra bas lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu yin pa de ni lhan cig pa kho nar nges la/ lhan cig 'byung ba la ni lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyus ma khyab ste/ mthun pa'i mtshan nyid rnams chos kyi lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu ma yin pa dang*/ mthun pa'i mtshan nyid nang rnams kyang lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu ma yin pa lta bu'o/ /

The four characteristics of the afflicted view of the self and the characteristics of minds and mental factors concomitant with it are generated from the homogeneous, omnipresent, and coemergent causes of the afflicted view of the self. Because the afflicted view of the self is also generated from their coemergent cause, it is both. This is asserted by Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas. Aparāntakas assert that the characteristics of the afflicted view of the self are the cause and effect of it. Since its concomitant characteristics are not the cause of the afflicted view of the self, being a result is possible but not a cause. Having investigated these issues through [the prism of] Vaibhāṣika tenets, they are seen to be incorrect. Vaibhāṣikas here ascertain that coemergent causes are simultaneous alone, but it is not necessary that coemergent entities are coemergent causes because, for instance, they admit that secondary characteristics are not coemergent causes of objects and internal secondary characteristics are not coemergent causes.

{de yang bum pa 'dus byas su mtshon pa'i mtshan nyid bzhi dang bum pa gcig gcig gi lhan cig 'byung rgyu yin gyi mtshan gzhi kun dang mtshan nyid kun gyi min no/ / spyir 'dus byas dang khyad par du/ sems kyi mthun pa'i mtshan nyid lhan cig 'byung yang 'dus byas dang sems ni rang rang gi mthun pa'i mtshan nyid kyi lhan cig gi 'byung rgyu yin te/ dper na rgyal po de rang gi 'khor kun skyong ba bzhin no/ / mthun pa'i mtshan nyid de dag ni 'dus byas dang sems kyi lhan cig skyes na 'byung rgyu min te de dag rgyal po dang 'dra ba nying g.yog gis dngos su bya ba byed mi nus pa bzhin no/ / yang 'byung gyur gyi gzugs sgra dri ro reg sogs rdzas brgyad 'dus pa lta bu'i gzugs sogs lnga lhan cig 'byung yang mtshan nyid kyis ring bas de dag lhan cig 'byung rgyu min no/ / bsam gtan zag med kyi spong bya ni nang phan tshun gcig gcig gi 'byung rgyu yin te gcig skye na gzhan rnams kyang nges par skye la gcig mi skye na gzhan rnams kyang mi skye ba'i phyir ro/ / so thar la ni nges pa med de sna gcig spyod sogs yod pas so/ / dus mnyam pa'i thob bya'i chos dang de'i thob pa dus gcig 'byung yang 'byung rgyu min te thob pa de ni shing shun dang 'dra bas chos dang rgyun tha dad pas 'bras bu mi gcig pas so/ }

{Furthermore, the four characteristics of a vase that characterize conditioned states and the vase itself are coemergent causes of each other but not of all characterized bases and all characteristics. Though in general conditioned states, and specifically the secondary characteristics of the mind, coexist, conditioned states and the mind are coemergent causes of their secondary characteristics, like the king who protects all his retinue. If those secondary characteristics are simultaneously generated with conditioned states and mind, they are not coemergent causes, like the outer [lower-ranking] servants who are unable to directly serve [170] someone like the king. Again, the five material forms [namely, form, sound, smell, taste, tactility, and so forth] — that are derivative form containing the eight substances — arise simultaneously, but they are not coemergent causes since their characteristics are far removed [from each other]. The objects abandoned by absorption and uncontaminated vows are internal reciprocal coemergent causes of each other, because if one is generated the other is definitely generated, and if one is not generated the other is not generated. But this is uncertain for pratimokṣa vows, since there are lay practitioners who possess one vow and so on. Though objects obtained and their obtainment occur at the same time, they are not coemergent causes because such obtainment does not have the same result, since the object and its continuum are distinct, like a tree and its bark.}

thob pa dang thob bya'i chos rnams dang*/ 'dod pa na gzugs dang dri la sogs pa rdzas brgyad nges par lhan cig skye{ yang ma yin} pa dang*/ bsam gtan zag med kyi sdom pa dag gi spong bdun{ de yin pas de} ma gtogs pa rgyur byas pa'i gzugs thams cad rang gi 'byung ba dag dang lhan cig 'byung yang lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu ma yin pa lta bu'o/ / gnyis ka ma yin pa ni shin tu mang ba yin no zhes 'dod do/ / mdo sde pa ni lhan cig 'byung ba dag ni rgyu ma yin te/ gnyis ka dus mnyam par grub pa dag la ni bskyed bya skyed byed med pa'i phyir dang*/ bskyed bya skyed byed dag kyang lhan cig 'byung ba ma yin te/ bsgrub bya dang sgrub byed yin pa'i phyir ro/ / mtshan nyid dang mthun pa'i mtshan nyid la sogs pa ni bye brag tu smra bas brtags pa yin la/ 'dod pa na gzugs la sogs pa lhan cig 'byung ba dang*/ 'byung ba la sogs pa ni tshogs pa snga mas gos gcig tu 'phangs pa'i phyir mtshe ma'i spun dang 'dra'o zhes bya bar 'dod do/ /

The obtainment and the objects obtained, and the eight substances such as form, smell, and so on, are {also not} definitely simultaneously generated in the desire realm. {Since} the seven objects of abandonment of the absorption and uncontaminated vows {are that}, all derivative form that is separate from it is not a coemergent cause, though it coexists with its primary elements. [Therefore the possibility] of neither is asserted to have many instances. Sautrāntikas assert that coemergent states are not causes because if both are established at the same time, they cannot be the object generated and its generator. The object generated and its generator do not coexist because they are the object established and its establisher. Vaibhāṣikas therefore analyze characteristics and secondary characteristics and so on and assert that, in the desire realm, coemergent states such as form, and their primary elements and so on, are produced in the same spatial location due to the prior assembly [of their causes], therefore they are like the offspring of twins.
gsum pa skal mnyam kyi rgyu bshad pa ni
HOMOGENEOUS CAUSE
skal mnyam rgyu ni 'dra ba'o/ / rang rigs sa pa'o sngar skyes rnams/ / 52 sa dgu'i lam ni phan tshun du/ / mnyam dang khyad par can gyi yin/ /
Homogeneous cause generates similar states of its own type and level, and those previously arisen. The path of the nine levels is a common cause of those equal or superior. (2:52)
skal ba mnyam pa'i rgyu ni dge ba dang*/ nyon mongs can dang*/ ma bsgribs lung ma bstan du 'dra ba skyed pa'i rgyu'o/
Homogeneous cause (sabhāgahetu) is a cause generating similar (sadṛśa) virtuous, afflicted, and unobscured-neutral states.

{ skal mnyam rgyu'i 'dra ba'i don ni 'bras bu dang dge ba'am nyon mongs can nam ma bsgribs lung ma bstan du rgyu 'bras 'dra'o zhe na/ 'o na 'dod pa'i 'dod chags dang 'jig lta gcig gi gcig gi skal mnyam gyi rgyu min par thal chags pa mi dge ba dang 'jig lta lung ma bstan ris mi 'dra bas so/ / des na dge ba zag bcas zag bcas su dang*/ zag med zag med du dang*/ nyon mongs can nyon mongs can du dang*/ ma bsgribs lung ma bstan ma bsgribs lung ma bstan du ris gcig pa gcig dgos so/ / de yang spang bya ris lnga las sdug bsngal mthong spang sdug bsngal mthong spang du ris 'dra ba nas/ sgom spang sgom spang du ris 'dra ba sogs so/ /

{Objection: The meaning of similarity regarding a homogeneous cause is that the result is similar to the cause, whether virtuous, afflicted, or unobscured-neutral. Reply: Then it would follow that desire-realm attachment and afflicted view of the self would not be homogeneous causes of each other because they are not of similar type, since attachment is nonvirtuous and afflicted view of the self is neutral. Therefore they must be of the same type: contaminated virtue being the same type as contaminated virtue, uncontaminated states being the same type as uncontaminated states, afflicted states being the same type as afflicted states, unobscured-neutral states being the same type as unobscured-neutral states. And they must be the same type of abandonment from among the five types: objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering being the same type as objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering, up to objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation being the same type as objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation.

de tsam 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal mthong spang dang khams gong gi la'ang yod pas de dag gcig gcig gi skal mnyam du thal bas/ des na 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal mthong spang gis 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal mthong spang gi skal mnyam byed pa la sogs pa 'dra ba gcig dgos so/ / de tsam 'dod pa'i lhas byin mchod sbyin la'ang yod pas gang zag rgyud gcig gis bsdus pa'i chos gcig dgos so/ / de tsam rgyud gcig gis sems sems byung dus mnyam pa la'ang yod pas de dag der thal bas dus sngar byung ba rnams rang gi rigs 'dra phyi ma rnams kyi yin no/ / des na 'dod pa'i lhas byin gyi sdug bsngal mthong spang ris 'dra snga ma rang gi ris 'dra phyi ma'i yin pa nas/sgom spang ris 'dra snga ma phyi ma'i skal mnyam yin pa'i bar du yin la/ ris gzhan dang sa gzhan ni skal ba mi mnyam pas min no/ / de yang sngar skyes rnams phyis kyi 'das da ltar gyi yin gyi ma 'ongs pa rnams ni snga phyi 'chol zhing phyi ma skye ba'i go skabs 'byed par ma nges pas skal mnyam gyi rgyur mi gzhag go /sems kyi skal mnyam ni de'i 'khor gyi'ang yin no/ /}

But if similarity were merely that, then objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering in the desire realm would also exist in higher realms, since it would follow that they would be homogeneous with each other. Therefore the similarity required for homogeneity would be, for instance, objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering in the desire realm being similar to objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering in the desire realm, and so on. But if similarity were merely that, then what exists for Devadatta would also exist for Pujadatta in the desire realm, yet they must be qualities subsumed within the mindstream of one person. But if similarity were merely that, it would follow that minds and mental factors included within one [171] mindstream that exist at the same time would be homogeneous, and that those that occurred before would be homogeneous with later instances of similar type. Therefore, for someone such as Devadatta in the desire realm, objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering of prior similar type are homogeneous with those of later similar type, and objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation of prior similar type are homogeneous with those of later similar type, but those of different type and different realm are not of similar type since they are not homogeneous. Furthermore, previously generated states are homogeneous with later past and present states, but future states are not posited as homogeneous causes since that would confuse the order of earlier and later states and it is not definite that they would grant opportunity for later generation.}

dge ba'ang zag bcas zag med so sor 'dra ba yin gyi dge ba tsam du 'dra bas ni ma yin te/ zag med kyi skad cig dang po'ang skal mnyam gyi rgyu las skye bar thal bar 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ { des na zag med skad cig dang po min pa kun la 'di yod do/ /}

Contaminated and uncontaminated virtue are distinct but similar, but they are not similar merely through being virtuous, because it would then follow that the first moment of the uncontaminated state would be generated from a homogeneous cause. {Therefore the homogeneous cause of uncontaminated states does not exist in the first moment, but it exists in all other moments.}

de yang sdug bsngal mthong spang dang kun 'byung mthong spang dang 'gog pa mthong spang dang lam mthong spang dang sgom spang ste spang bya ris lnga dang*/ khams gsum gyi sa dgu po rnams rang rang gi ris dang*/ rang rang gi sa pa skyed par byed pa skal mnyam yin gyi ris gzhan dang sa gzhan ni ma yin te/ ris gzhan dang sa gzhan ni skal ba mi mnyam pa'i phyir ro/

Moreover, the five abandonments — (1) objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering, (2) objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of origin, (3) objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of cessation, (4) objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of path, and (5) objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation — and (6–14) the nine levels of the three realms are homogeneous since they generate states of their own type (nikāya) and their own level (bhuva). Those of different type or level do not, because different types and different levels are not homogeneous.

{ dge ba'i phung po lnga ni de nyid kyi skal mnyam yin pa nas/ nyon mongs can dang ma bsgribs lung ma bstan yang rang rang gi yin pa'i bar du'o/ / lung ma bstan la kha cig gzugs ni dman pas phung po lnga'i yin la/ gzhan bzhi ni de las mchog yin pas gzugs kyi min zhes so/ / ris mthun pa gcig la mer mer po ni gnas skabs bcu'i yin pa na rgas pa ni rang ris phye ma kho na yi'o/ / mi nas mir skye ba lta bu la rgas pa yang bcu char gyi'o/ / phyi la nas ni nas kyi sogs so/ / nang la mig kyang mig gi sogs so/ / de yang g.yas ni g.yas kyi sogs so/ / 'dis ni 'das pa'i 'byung ba rnams kyang ma 'ongs pa'i 'byung ba'i skal mnyam du bstan te des de'i skal mnyam gyi rgyu las rgyu gzhan mi srid pas so/ /}

de yang sngar skyes pa 'das pa dang da ltar ba rnams phyi ma skyes pa dang ma skyes pa rnams kyi yin gyi ma 'ongs pa ni ma yin te/ skal mnyam dang kun 'gro dag ni go 'byed pa'i rgyu yin na 'das pas ni 'das pa dang da lta ba'i go 'byed la/ da ltar bas ni da ltar ba dang ma 'ongs pa'i go 'byed na ma 'ongs pa la go dbye bar bya ba'i 'bras bu nyid med pa'i phyir ro/ {gal te } ma 'ongs pas ma 'ongs pa 'byed na ma 'ongs pa la rgyu dang 'bras bu'i snga phyi'i dbye ba yod par 'gyur na ma 'ongs pa ni snga phyi'i dbye ba med do zhes 'dod do/ / de'i phyir bstan bcos las/ skal ba mnyam pa'i rgyu gang zhe na/ dge ba'i rtsa ba sngar byung ba rnams ni rang gi khams na dge ba'i rtsa ba phyis 'byung ba rnams dang*/ de dag dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i chos rnams kyi skal ba mnyam pa'i rgyus rgyu yin no/ / de ltar na 'das pa rnams ni 'das pa dang da ltar byung ba rnams kyi yin no/ / 'das pa dang da ltar byung ba rnams ni ma 'ongs pa rnams kyi yin no zhes brjod par bya'o zhes 'byung ngo*/ /

Further, those previously arisen (agrajā) in the past and present are homogeneous with those subsequently arisen or not arisen. But they are not homogeneous with future states because when those that are homogeneous and omnipresent act as accommodating causes, then past states accommodate the past and present, present states accommodate the present and future, but the future does not accommodate any effect. {If} the future were to accommodate the future, then the future would have earlier and later causal and resultant parts, but no earlier and later parts exist in the future. Therefore the treatise (Attainment of Knowledge)[617] states: What is the homogeneous cause? The root of virtue that occurred previously is the homogeneous cause of the root of virtue and those qualities concomitant with it that occur later in one’s realm. Thus past states are homogeneous causes of those occurring in the past and present. Those occurring in the past and present are homogeneous causes of future states.[618]

gal te ma 'ongs pa la snga phyi med pas skal mnyam dang kun 'gro'i rgyu 'bras mi rung na rgyu gzhan gsum yang mi rung bar 'gyur ro zhe na/ bye brag tu smra ba ni rgyu gzhan gsum po ni rgyu 'bras mtshan nyid tha dad pas rnam par dbye ba yod pa'i phyir dang*/ skal mnyam dang kun 'gro'i rgyu 'bras ni snga phyi'i bye brag gis bzhag gi mtshan nyid mi 'dra ba med pa'i phyir ma 'ongs pa la med do zhes 'dod do/ / ma 'ongs pa la snga phyi med la 'das pa la yod do zhes bya ba ni khyad par med pa la dbye ba byed pa bye brag tu smra ba'i grub mtha' yin gyi yang dag pa ma yin te/ 'das pa la snga phyi yod na ma 'ongs pa la'ang mtshungs la/ snga phyi med na 'das pa 'das pa'i skal mnyam dang kun 'gro ma yin par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / da ltar ba da ltar ba'i skal mnyam dang kun 'gro'i rgyu yin no zhes bya ba'ang mi rigs te/ da ltar ba la'ang snga phyi med pa'i phyir ro/ / snga phyi yod na da ltar ba ma yin par thal ba 'di spang dgos so/ / grub pa'i mtha' las ni sa lu ni sa lu'i skal mnyam dang*/ nas ni nas la sogs pa dang*/ mi ni mi'i skal mnyam dang*/ mig ni mig gi skal mnyam la sogs pa rang gi ris pa dang*/ 'dod pa ni 'dod pa'i skal mnyam la sogs pa rang gi sa pa kho nar bshad do/ / 'o na skal mnyam gyi rgyu rang gi sa pa dang rang gi ris pa kho nar nges sam zhe na/

Objection: If it is untenable that homogeneous or omnipresent causes exist in the future, since the future does not have earlier or later parts, [172] then it would be untenable that the other three causes exist in future. Vaibhāṣikas assert that the other three causes have such parts, since cause and effect have distinct characteristics, but that homogeneous and omnipresent causes and results do not exist in the future because they lack different characteristics that would be established by specific earlier and later parts. It is a Vaibhāṣika tenet to distinguish those that lack distinction when they state that “the future does not have earlier and later parts but the past does.” But this is incorrect because if earlier and later parts exist in the past, they would also exist in the future, since it is similar. And if earlier and later parts don’t exist in the past, then the past would not be a homogeneous or omnipresent cause of the past. It would also be untenable for Vaibhāṣikas to state that “present states are homogeneous and omnipresent causes of present states” because present states do not have earlier and later parts, for if they had earlier and later moments, it would follow that it would not be present, and this consequence must be refuted. In their tenet system it is explained that in terms of type, wild rice is the homogeneous cause of wild rice, barley is the homogeneous cause of barley and so on, a human is the homogeneous cause of a human, an eye is the homogeneous cause of an eye, and so on. In terms of level alone, the desire realm is the homogeneous cause of the desire realm and so on.[619] Question: Does the homogeneous cause definitely generate results on its level and its type alone?

zag bcas la de ltar nges kyi zag med la ni bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs dang*/ khyad par can dang*/ bsam gtan bzhi dang*/ {bsam gtan sa drug dang } gzugs med pa dang po gsum ste sa dgu'i lam gyi bden pa ni sa mi mtshungs pa dag kyang phan tshun du skal ba mnyam pa'i rgyu yin te/ lam de dag ni sa de dag tu glo bur du 'ongs pa yin pas sa de dag gi sred pas bdag gir ma byas pa'i phyir khams su ma gtogs pa'o/ / de yang sa 'og ma'i lam ni gong ma'i sa pa'i yang yin la/ gong ma'ang 'og ma'i sa pa'i yin pa'i phyir phan tshun du zhes smros pa yin no/ / thams cad du'am zhe na de{ yang rang dang} mnyam pa dang{ rang las} khyad par can gyi yin gyi dman pa'i ni ma yin no/ / de yang sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa ni mnyam pa rang nyid kyi rigs phyi ma dang*/ khyad par can sdug bsngal chos shes pa la sogs pa dang*/ sgom lam dang mi slob pa'i lam gyi bden pa khyad par can gyi rgyu yin pa dang*/ de bzhin du dad pas rjes 'brang ni rang nyid dang*/ chos kyi rjes 'brang dang*/ dad mos dang*/ mthong thob dang*/ dus kyis rnam par gral ba dang*/ dus dang mi sbyor bar rnam par grol ba drug gi yin pa la sogs pa'o/ / de yang bsam gtan bzhi pa'i sa pa'i dad pas rjes 'brang dang*/ gsum pa man chad kyi sa pa'i dad pas rjes 'brang yang mnyam pa yin te/ gnyis ka'ang dbang po rtul pa'i phyir ro/ / de dag pas ni bsam gtan dang po'i sa pa'i chos kyi rjes 'brang khyad par can yin te/ de'i phyir sa gong ma'i{ zag med kyi} lam gyis sa 'og ma'i{ zag med} lam gyi skal mnyam gyi rgyu byed pa ni bsam gtan bzhi pa'i sa pa dbang po rtul po dag dbang po sbyangs te gsum pa man chad kyi dbang po rnon po chos kyi rjes 'brang gi lam skyed pa lta bu'o/ / de bzhin du dad mos la sogs pa la'ang sbyar ro/ /

Reply: Contaminated states definitely generate results in that way. But uncontaminated states such as the truth of the path (mārga) of the nine levels {including the six levels of absorption} — (1) access concentration, (2) the special stage of the first absorption, (3–6) the four absorptions, and (7–9) the first three formless-realm states — are common (anyonya) homogeneous causes even though they are of dissimilar levels because the craving of those levels does not grasp them as mine, since those paths are adventitiously produced on those levels. Therefore they do not belong to the three realms. They are called “common causes” because the paths of lower levels are also paths of higher levels, and the higher are also paths of lower levels. Question: Is that true in all cases? Reply: That is so for those equal (sama) {with it} or superior (viśiṣṭa) {to it} but not for those that are inferior. Furthermore, persevering for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering is a cause of that equal to it — its later continuum; and that superior to it — Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering and so on; and the truth of the paths of meditation and no more learning. So too, followers of faith[620] are causes of six: (1) that equal to itself [and that superior:] (2) followers of reality,[621] (3) those resolute in faith, (4) those obtaining results by insight, (5) those liberated in time, and (6) those liberated without preparation in time. Further, followers of faith of the level of the fourth absorption and followers of faith of the third level and below are homogeneous because both are of dull faculty. They become causes of superior followers of reality of the first absorption level, and because of that [173] the {uncontaminated} path of higher level acts as the homogeneous cause of the {uncontaminated} path of lower level. This is through, for instance, those of dull faculty of the fourth absorption level upgrading their intellectual faculty and generating the path of a follower of reality with sharp faculty of the third absorption and below. Similarly, those resolute in faith and so on should be counted here.

slob dpon rgyal po'i sras ni dad mos sgom lam pa yin pas de la dbang po 'thob yod kyi dad pas rjes 'brang ni mthong lam pa yin pas de la ni med do zhes 'dod la/ slob dpon dbyig bshes ni yod par bzhed do/ /

Master Jinaputra asserts that since those resolute in faith are those on the path of meditation, they have obtained sharp intellectual faculty. Since followers of faith are those of the path of seeing, they have not.[622] Master Vasumitra asserts that they have.[623]
sbyor byung de gnyis kho na'i yin/ / thos dang bsams byung la sogs pa/ / 53
Virtue arising from preparation is of both alone: that derived from hearing, contemplation, and so on. (2:53ab)
