bzhi pa mtshungs ldan gyi rgyu ni
CONCOMITANT CAUSE
mtshungs ldan rgyu ni sems dag dang / / sems byung rten mtshungs can rnams so/ /
Concomitant cause is the mind and mental factors that possess the same support. (2:53cd)

mtshungs par ldan pa'i rgyu ni sems dag dang sems las byung ba mig la sogs pa'i rten mtshungs pa can rnams so zhes smros pas/ dmigs pa dang rnam pa dang dus dang rdzas mtshungs pa'ang gzung ngo*/ / des na sems dang sems byung ni phan tshun rgyu 'bras yin pa'i phyir dang*/ mtshungs par ldan pa lngas mtshungs par gnas pa'i phyir mtshungs ldan gyi rgyu zhes bya'o/ / de yang lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu ni spyi yin la/ mtshungs ldan gyi rgyu ni bye brag yin no/ /

Concomitant cause (saṃprayuktahetu) is said to be the mind (citta) and mental factors (caitta) and so on that possess the same support (samaśraya), focal object, aspect, time, and [similar] substance. Thus they are called “concomitant causes” because minds and mental factors are reciprocal causes and results of each other and because they are similar in being concomitant in five ways. Further, coemergent cause is the general set of concomitant cause, and concomitant cause is also a subset of coemergent cause.
lnga pa kun 'gro'i rgyu ni
OMNIPRESENT CAUSE
kun 'gro zhes bya nyon mongs can/ / rnams kyi rang sa kun 'gro snga/ / 54
Omnipresent causes are afflicted states belonging to their own level. Omnipresent cause is a prior state. (2:54ab)

kun 'gro zhes bya ba'i rgyu ni sdug bsngal mthong spang gi lta ba lnga dang the tshom dang ma rig pa ste bdun dang*/ kun 'byung mthong spang gi lta ba mchog 'dzin dang*/ log lta dang*/ the tshom dang*/ ma rig pa dang bzhi ste bcu gcig {dang khams gong ma gnyis na'ang de ltar bcu gcig bcu gcig ste phra rgyas sum cu rtsa gsum thob pa las gzhan mtshungs ldan dang mtshan nyid dang bcas pa gnas lnga par 'chad 'gyur rnams ni kun 'gro'i rgyu/ gnas lnga par 'chad par 'gyur ba'i khams gsum gyi bden pa dang po gnyis kyi phra rgyas kun 'gro sum cu rtsa gsum thob pa las gzhan pa mtshungs ldan dang mtshan nyid dang bcas pa rnams }yin te nyon mongs pa can rnams kyi sngon du 'gro ba'i rgyu thun mong ma yin pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Omnipresent causes (sarvatragahetu) comprise eleven states: seven objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering, including (1–5) the five views,[624] (6) doubt, and (7) ignorance; and four objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of origin — (8) the view clinging to [the first three] views as supreme, (9) wrong view, (10) doubt, and (11) ignorance. {Omnipresent causes should be explained as the five abodes: the obtainment of (1) those eleven in the desire realm, plus (2–3) eleven each in the two higher realms, making thirty-three, plus (4) other states concomitant with them and (5) their characteristics. The five abodes should be explained as the obtainment of the thirty-three omnipresent negative tendencies of the first two truths of the three realms, plus other states concomitant with them and their characteristics}. There are eleven because they are specific causes preceding the generation of afflicted (kliṣṭa) [174] states {in a single mindstream.}

thams cad du'am zhe na rang gi sa par gtogs pa'i yin gyi sa gzhan gyi lta ba la sogs pa ni sa gzhan gyi ma yin no/ / ris gzhan ni ris gzhan gyi kun 'gro'i rgyu yin te/ sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung {rgyun gcig gi }mthong spang ni nyon mongs pa'i ris lnga char gyi kun 'gro'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang ma 'ongs pa la kun 'gro'i rgyu mi 'thad pa'i phyir kun 'gro'i rgyu ni sngar skyes pa kho na yin no/ / 'o na 'phags pa'i gang zag gi kun nas nyon mongs pa rnams rgyu de las ma skyes par 'gyur te/ kun 'gro de dag spangs nas med pa'i phyir zhe na/ bye brag tu smra ba ltar na de dag ni 'das pa las skye bar 'dod de/ de ltar yang rab tu byed pa las/ mthong bas spang bar bya ba'i rgyu las byung ba'i chos rnams gang zhe na/ nyon mongs pa can gyi chos rnams dang*/ mthong bas spang bar bya ba'i chos rnams kyi rnam par smin pa gang yin pa'o zhes gsungs so/ / gang dag kun 'gro'i rgyu skal mnyam gyi bye brag yin no zhes bya ba ni nges pa med de/ sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung mthong spang kun 'gro rnams 'gog lam mthong spang dang sgom spang nyon mongs can gyi kun 'gro'i rgyu yin yang skal mnyam gyi rgyu ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Question: Is that true for all levels or not? Reply: It is true for those belonging to their own level (svabhūmi), but view that engages different levels and so on does not belong to different levels. Different type refers to omnipresent causes of different type because objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of suffering and origin are omnipresent causes of the five types of affliction. Moreover, the omnipresent (sarvagā) cause is only generated as a prior (pūrva) state because it is unacceptable that omnipresent causes exist in the future. Objection: The afflictions of ārya beings are not generated from omnipresent causes because they don’t have omnipresent causes, having abandoned them. Vaibhāṣikas assert that they are generated from past states. Thus Topic Divisions states: What are those phenomena derived from causes that are to be abandoned by the path of seeing? They are afflicted phenomena and any karmic maturation that is to be abandoned by the path of seeing.[625] The statement “Any omnipresent cause is a subset of homogeneous cause” cannot be verified because omnipresent objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of suffering and origin are omnipresent causes of afflicted objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of cessation and path and objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, but they are not homogeneous causes.
drug pa rnam par smin pa'i rgyu/
CAUSE OF KARMIC MATURATION
rnam smin rgyu ni mi dge dang / / dge ba zag bcas rnams kho na/ /
The cause of karmic maturation is nonvirtue and contaminated virtue alone. (2:54cd)

rnam par smin pa'i rgyu ni mi dge ba thams cad dang dge ba zag pa dang bcas pa rnams kho na yin te/{ rang gi ngo bo stobs dang ldan zhing rkyen sred pa'i rlan dang bcas pa'i phyir ro/ / lung ma bstan dang zag med ni rim pa ltar rang gi ngo bo stobs chung ba dang stobs dang ldan yang rkyen sred pa'i rlan med pa'i phyir rnam smin gyi rgyu ma yin te/ dper na sa bon rul ba dang*/ rlan dang bral ba'i sa bon grung po bzhin no/ / de gnyis las gzhan pa'i 'dus byas lhag ma ni rnam smin gyi rgyu yin no/ / mi dge ba ni las dang nyon mongs pa gnyis ka gzung ste sa gang gi sred pas rkyen byas pa der rnam smin 'grub po 'di'i 'bras bu las byas ma thag tu 'dren pa na med kyi rgyun la ltos nas mi 'dra ba smin te bskal pa brgyar yang chud mi za bas so/ /} 'bras bu rnam smin 'byin pa'i phyir ro/ / lung ma bstan rnams ni stobs chung ba'i phyir rnam smin 'byin pa med de sa bon rul ba bzhin no/ / zag med rnams ni sred pa'i rlan dang bral ba'i phyir rnam smin mi 'byin te rlan dang bral ba'i sa bon grung po bzhin no/ / des na 'bras bu rnam smin 'byin pa'i las de ni rnam smin gyi rgyu yin no zhes shes par bya'o/ /

The cause of karmic maturation (vipākahetu) is all nonvirtue (aśubha) and contaminated (sāsrava) virtue (kuśala) alone because they produce the results of karmic maturation {and because they are powerful by nature and are moist with craving as a condition. Neutral and uncontaminated states are not causes of karmic maturation since they are either weak by nature or, though powerful, they lack the moisture of craving as a condition, like a rotten seed or a seed lacking moisture. Except for those two, all remaining conditioned states are the causes of karmic maturation. Nonvirtuous states comprise both karma and affliction, and their maturation is established on that level where they are conditioned by craving. Their result does not manifest immediately after the karma is committed, but it matures separately within its own continuum without losing potency even after a hundred eons.} Neutral states do not produce karmic maturation because they have little power, like a rotten seed. Uncontaminated states do not produce karmic maturation because they lack the moisture of craving, like a seed that lacks moisture. Therefore you should understand a cause of karmic maturation from its production of the result of karmic maturation.
gsum pa rgyu de dag gi don bsdu ba ni
SUMMATION OF THOSE CAUSES
kun 'gro skal mnyam dus gnyis pa/ / gsum po dag ni dus gsum pa/ / 55
Omnipresent and homogeneous causes exist at two times. Three causes exist at three times. (2:55ab)

kun 'gro dang skal mnyam gyi rgyu ni {rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu skyed pas/ } 'das da lta ba'i dus gnyis pa kho na yin gyi ma 'ongs pa ni med de/ rgyu mtshan ni bshad zin pa nyid do/ / lhan cig 'byung ba dang mtshungs ldan dang rnam smin gyi rgyu gsum po dag ni dus gsum pa yin no/ / byed rgyu'i 'dus byas rnams ni dus gsum pa dang*/ 'dus ma byas dus kyis ma bsdus pa'ang yod pa'i phyir nges pa ma bshad do/ /

Since omnipresent and homogeneous causes {produce results of natural outflow,} they exist at two times (dvyadhvaga), the past and present alone. They don’t exist in the future, and the reason for that has already been explained. Three — coemergent cause, concomitant cause, and the cause of karmic maturation — exist in the three times (tryadhvaga). [175] Conditioned active causes exist in the three times. Unconditioned active causes are not explained as definitely [existing in the three times] because they exist but they are not subsumed by time.
gnyis pa 'bras bu bshad pa ni
The five results
'dus byas bral bcas 'bras bu yin/ / 'dus ma byas la de dag med/ /
Conditioned states and separation are results. Unconditioned states have neither. (2:55cd)

'dus byas la rnam smin dang rgyu mthun dang bdag po dang skyed pa'i skyes bu byed 'bras te phyed dang bzhi dang*/ 'dus ma byas la/ thob pa'i skyes bu byed 'bras dang zag bcas gnyen pos bral 'bras so sor brtags 'gog dang bcas pa{ phyed dang gnyis su phye ba} ni 'bras bu yin te/ bstan bcos las/ 'bras bu'i chos rnams gang zhe na/ 'dus byas kyi chos thams cad dang*/ so sor brtags pas 'gog pa'o zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / des na 'dus ma byas la ni 'bras bu phyed dang gnyis su 'gyur ro/{ nam mkha' ni bya byed dang bral zhing thob bya min la/ brtags min ni rkyen ma tshang ba tsam gyis thob pas 'bras bu min no/} gal te de ltar na brtags 'gog ni 'dus ma byas yin la de yang 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir de'i rgyu yang brjod dgos la/ 'dus ma byas byed rgyur 'dod pa'i phyir de'i 'bras bu'ang brjod dgos so { gal te lam de dag yod na 'dus byas su 'gyur ro} zhe na/

'dus ma byas la ni{ 'bras bur bzhag pa'i tshe} de skyed pa'i rgyu rnam pa drug dang{ rgyur bzhag pa'i tshe} des bskyed par bya ba'i 'bras bu lnga po de dag med pa'i phyir brjod par bya ba ma yin no/ / gal te lam bral ba'i byed rgyu ma yin nam zhe na/ ma yin te/ de ni skye ba la gegs mi byed pa yin na 'dus ma byas la skye ba med pa'i phyir ro/ / des na 'dus ma byas ni rgyu 'bras btags pa ba yin no/ / 'o na mdo las/ dbang po lnga po 'di dag kun tu bsten/ goms par byas/ lan mang du byas na 'das pa dang ma 'ongs pa dang da ltar byung ba'i sdug bsngal spangs par 'gyur ro zhes gsungs pa dang 'gal te/ sdug bsngal spangs pa ni 'gog pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ de lam gyis byed par bshad pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ der yang lam goms pas nyon mongs pa phyis skye ba la gegs byed pa'i phyir dang*/ nyon mongs dang bral ba'i rnam grol gyi ye shes bskyed pa'i phyir dang*/ lam gyi stobs kyis 'gog pa de yang mngon du byed pa'i phyir de ltar gsungs kyi 'gog pa gsar skyes bus las byed pa ltar rgyu rkyen tshogs pa'ang de dang 'dra bas du skyed pa ni ma yin te/ 'dus byas su thal ba'i phyir ro/ / 'o na 'bras bu de dag rgyu gang gi yin zhe na/

Reply: Unconditioned states (nāsaṃskṛta) have neither because {when posited as results} they do not have six generating causes, and {when posited as causes} they do not have five generated results. Question: Isn’t the path the active cause of separation? Reply: That is not so, because if unconditioned states do not impede arising, they cannot arise. Therefore unconditioned states are nominal causes and results. Objection: Now, this contradicts a sūtra that states: If you always rely on these five faculties, cultivate them, and practice them frequently, then suffering occurring in the past, future, and present will be abandoned,[628] because this explains that the abandonment of suffering is a cessation that is achieved by the path. Reply: That is stated here because cultivating the path stops the subsequent arising of affliction, because the transcendent wisdom of liberation free from affliction is generated, and because that cessation also manifests due to the power of the path. But cessation is not newly generated because it would then absurdly follow that it is conditioned. Question: What are the causes of those results?
rnam smin 'bras bu tha ma'i yin/ / bdag po'i 'bras bu dang po'i yin/ / 56 rgyu mthun skal mnyam kun 'gro ba'i/ / skyes bu pa ni gnyis kyi yin/ /
The result of karmic maturation is from the last. The dominant result is from the first. Natural outflow is from homogeneous and omnipresent. The result of conscious effort is from both. (2:56)

rnam smin gyi 'bras bu ni rgyu tha ma rnam smin gyi rgyu'i yin no/ / bdag po tha ma dbang byed pa'i 'bras bu ni rgyu dang po byed rgyu'i yin no/ / rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu ni skal mnyam dang kun du 'gro ba'i rgyu gnyis kyi yin no/ / skyes bu'i byed pa can gyi 'bras bu ni lhan cig 'byung ba dang mtshungs ldan gyi rgyu gnyis kyi yin no/ / de yang rgyu gnyis po de la 'bras bu gzhan nges pa med pa'i phyir dang*/ de ni nges pa'i phyir de ltar bstan gyi de gnyis kho na'i 'bras bu ni ma yin te/{ di dag gtso che ba'i dbang du byas kyi dus gcig tu nges pa med de 'dus byas thams cad la bdag byed gnyis ka yod la skyes na'ang dus mi mnyam yod pas so/} byed rgyu dang skal mnyam kun 'gro rnams kyis kyang skyes bu byed pa'i 'bras bu skyed pa'i phyir/ 'bras bu de dag gang zhe na/

Reply: The result of karmic maturation (vipākaphala) is from the last cause, the cause of karmic maturation. The dominant {or empowered} result (adhipatiphala) is from the first, active cause. The result of natural outflow (niṣyandaphala) arises from both homogeneous and omnipresent causes. {Since it is compatible with the collection of causes and conditions conforming with actions committed by beings,} [176] the result of conscious effort is from both: coemergent and concomitant causes. That is said because it is uncertain whether those two causes have other results, and because that result is certain. However, it is not a result of those two alone, because active cause, homogeneous cause, and omnipresent cause generate results of conscious effort. {That is stated from the central perspective, but it is uncertain that they exist at the same time, since all conditioned states have both dominant results and results of conscious effort, and even when generated they may not exist at the same time.} Question: What are {the characteristics of} those results?
rnam smin lung du ma bstan chos/ / sems can brjod lung bstan phyis 'byung / / 57 rgyu mthun rgyu dang 'dra ba'o/ / bral ba blo yis zad pa'o/ /

Karmic maturation is a neutral phenomenon said to be conjoined with sentient beings, declared, and arises later. Natural outflow is similar to its cause. Separation is elimination through the intellect. (2:57)

rnam smin gyi 'bras bu ni ma bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa'i chos yin no/ / de tsam ni phyi'i 'byung ba dang 'byung 'gyur la'ang yod pas sems can {gyi rgyud gi mtshan nyid }kyis bsdus pa'i chos su brjod do zhes gsungs so/ / {de yang las byed pa pos myong bas so } da lta na dbang po la sogs pa'i rgyas pa dang rgyu mthun las byung ba'ang der thal bar 'gyur bas rgyu lung bstan pa dge mi dge las byung ba{ dang} zhes gsungs so/ / de tsam ni ting nge 'dzin gyis rgyas pa{ 'i dbang po'i 'byung ba} dang sprul sems la'ang yod{ sprul sems kyis ni de thag tu sprul ba 'dren cing sa tha dad pa yod pa'i phyir ro} pas de gsal ba'i phyir dge ba dang mi dge ba las dus phyis{ las kyi nus pa smin nas} 'byung ba smros pa yin no/ / de ni las kyi rnam smin yang yin la 'bras bu'ang yin pa'i phyir rnam smin gyi 'bras bu'o/ / rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu ni rgyu dang 'dra ba{ ra phyis skyes pa} ste/ de yang zag bcas la ni ngo bo dang ris dang sa 'dra ba yin la/{ de yang kun 'gro skyed pa ni sa dang nyon mongs can du 'dra la skal mnyam gyi skyed pa ni ris dang rnam pa'ang 'dra'o/ /} zag med la ni ngo bo 'dra ba yin te skal ba mnyam par bshad pa bzhin no/ / bral ba'i 'bras bu ni blo yis te shes rab kyi stobs kyis spangs bya zag bcas zad pa ste so sor brtags pas 'gog pa'o/ /

Reply: The result of karmic maturation (vipāka) is an unobscured-neutral (avyākṛta) phenomenon (dharma). But if it were merely that, then external elements and derivative form would be results of karmic maturation. Therefore it is said to be phenomena conjoined with the mindstreams of sentient beings (sattva).[629] {Further, it is experienced by the agent of karma.} But if it were merely that, it would follow that the five sense faculties and so on that are derived from enhancement and natural outflow would also be [the results of karmic maturation]; therefore it is said to arise from causes declared (vyākṛta) to be virtuous or nonvirtuous.[630] But if it were merely that, then {elements of the sense faculties} would be enhanced by concentration, and in terms of the mind of emanation, {objects instantly projected by the emanating mind would exist on other levels.} In order to refute that, it is said that it arises later (udbhava) from virtue or nonvirtue {due to the maturation of potent karma}. Therefore something is a result of karmic maturation because it is both the maturation of karma and a result. The result of natural outflow (niṣyanda) is similar (sadṛśa) to its cause (hetu) {and arises later} because contaminated states have similar nature, type, and level. {Further, omnipresent generation has similarity of level and afflicted state. Homogeneous generation has similarity of type and aspect.} Uncontaminated states have similarity of nature, as explained for homogeneity. The result of separation (visaṃyoga) is the elimination (kṣaya) of contaminated objects of abandonment through the power of wisdom or the intellect (dhī), which constitutes cessation through analysis.
gang gi stobs kyis gang skyes pa'i/ / 'bras de skyes bu byed las skyes/ / 58 sngon byung ma yin 'dus byas ni/ / 'dus byas kho na'i bdag po'i 'bras/ /

Any result arising due to the power of its cause is a result arisen from conscious effort. Conditioned states that did not occur previously are the dominant results of conditioned states alone. (2:58)

rgyu gang gis stobs kyis 'bras bu gang skye ba'i 'bras bu de ni skyes bu'i byed pa las skyes pa'i 'bras bu zhes bya ste/ lam gyis so sor brtags 'gog thob pa la ni gang gi stobs kyis gang 'thob pa de ni zhes brjod par bya'o/ / rgyu de ni 'bras bu la skyes bu'i byed pa dang 'dra ba'i phyir skyes bu byed pa ste sman ser po khra rkang dang nag po bya rog rkang la sogs pa lta bu'o/ / 'di yang kha cig gis ni rgyu'i de ma thag gam cig car du 'byung ba la 'dod de/ {de yang skyed pa'i skyes bu byed 'bras ni } sa 'og ma'i sbyor ba'i sems kyis sa gong ma'i ting nge 'dzin dang*/ 'jig rten chos mchog gi rjes su mthong lam 'byung ba la sogs pa dang*/ lhan cig 'byung ba'i rgyu las 'bras bu 'byung ba lta bu'o/{ bsam gtan gyi sems kyis sprul sems lta bu'o/ / thob pa'i skyes bu byed 'bras ni/ / gang gi stobs kyis gang thob pa'i/ / 'bras de skyes bu'i byed las thob/ / ces brjod de/ nga'i nor skyes so zhes nor thob pa la'ang skyes pa'i sgra brjod pa bzhin no/ / de la gang mthong spang spangs ba ni 'phags pa mthar gyis pa'i skyes bu byed pa dang bral 'bras gnyis ka dang*/ chags bral sngon 'gro ni skyes bu byed 'bras kho na'o/ /}

kha cig ni chod pa'i rgyu las kyang skyes bu byed pa'i 'bras bu 'byung ste zhing pa rnams kyis lo tog lta bu'o/ / zhes zer te/ 'di ltar na 'bras bu thams cad la skyes bu byed pas khyab par 'dod do/{ de la 'bras bu snga na rgyu don med du thal bas rgyu la ltos nas/ /} sngon byung ba ma yin pa'i 'dus byas gsar du skyes pa{ rgyu dang dus mnyam pa dang phyis byung ba} thams cad ni 'dus byas thams cad kyi bdag po {'am dbang byed pa} 'i 'bras bu yin no/{ 'dus ma byas la 'bras bu 'dzin pa dang smin pa'i mthu med pas/ /} 'dus ma byas kyi ma yin pa'i phyir kho na zhes smros pa yin no/ / 'o na skyes bu byed 'bras dang khyad par ci yod ce na/ bye brag tu smra ba ni {skyes bu byed 'bras ni byed pa po kho na'i 'bras bu yin la bdag 'bras ni byed pa po las gzhan gyi'ang yin la gzhan yang} skyes bu byed 'bras ni bzo rnams ni bzo'i skyes bu byed pa dang bdag 'bras gnyis ka dang*/ sprul pa rnams ni bsam gtan gyi skyes bu byed 'bras dang bdag 'bras gnyis ka yin gyi gzhan gyi ni skyes bu byed 'bras ma yin no/ / zhes so sor nges pa yin la/ bdag po ni de dag kyang 'dus byas thams cad kyi bdag 'bras yin te/ de dag skye ba la 'dus byas thams cad mi sgrib par gnas pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes 'dod de/ de lta na 'dus ma byas kyi bdag 'bras su'ang thal bar 'gyur bas kun brtags so/ / 'on kyang bdag 'bras ni spyi dang gzhan ni bye brag yin no/ /

Some say: The result of conscious effort also is derived from a decisive cause because it is like farmers [producing] harvests. Reply: Thus it is asserted that all results are pervaded by conscious effort. All {that arise at the same time or after their cause} that are newly generated conditioned states (saṃskṛta) that did not occur previously (apūrva) are the dominant results (adhipatiphala) of all conditioned states (saṃskṛta). {They rely on causes since a result that precedes its cause is not possible}. “Alone” (eva) is stated because they are not unconditioned states {since unconditioned states do not possess the capacity to bear or to mature a result}. Question: How does this differ from the result of conscious effort? Vaibhāṣikas assert that {the results of conscious effort are results of agents alone but that dominant results are also results of nonagents. Again, they assert that} the results of conscious effort are both (1) manufactured by a manufacturing being as well as (2) dominant results. Emanations are both (1) the result of the conscious effort of beings possessing absorption and (2) dominant results. The rest are not the effects of conscious effort. Vaibhāṣikas assert that “dominant” refers to the dominant results of all conditioned states because conditioned states do not obstruct their arising. Reply: Such reasoning is erroneous since it would then follow that even the dominant result of unconditioned states would exist. Still, dominant results form the general set, and the others constitute its subsets.
rgyus 'bras bu skyed pa'i tshul ni
HOW CAUSES PRODUCE RESULTS
lnga po da ltar 'bras bu 'dzin/ / gnyis ni rab tu 'byin par byed/ / 59 da ltar gyi dang 'das pa dag / gcig ni 'das pas 'byin par 'gyur/ /
Five causes bear their result in the present. Two fully produce their result in the present. Two produce results as present and past causes. One produces its result in the past alone. (2:59)

byed rgyu las gzhan pa'i rgyu lnga po da ltar ba ni 'bras bu{ sa bon nam} nus pa'i tshul du 'dzin pa yin no/{ 'bras bu 'dzin pa ni 'bras bu skyed pa'i nus pa mthu can yin pas 'bras bu 'byin pa ni 'bras bu dngos su skyed pa'o/} 'das pa ni{ gsung zin pas} bya ba 'gags pa'i phyir dang*/ ma 'ongs pa bya ba ma skyes pa'i phyir dang*/ byed rgyu ni{ da ltar ba de dang 'dra med kyang} 'bras bu dang bcas pa la nges pa'i phyir nus pa can du ma brjod do/ / 'bras bu ji ltar 'byin zhe na/ lhan cig 'byung ba dang mtshungs ldan gyi gnyis ni 'bras bu 'dzin 'byin dus mnyam pas 'bras bu da ltar{ gyi/ las kho nas} du rab tu 'byin par byed pa'ang yin no/ / de la 'byin pa ni skyed pa ste rgyu dang dus mnyam du 'bras bu skyed pa zhes bya ba'i don to/ / da ltar gyi rgyu dang 'das pa'i rgyus 'bras bu 'byin pa ni skal mnyam dang kun 'gro'i rgyu dag gis te/ da ltar 'byin pa ni{ mjug thogs} de ma thag tu 'byin pa yin la/ 'das pas 'byin pa ni bar chod pa dag yin gyi dus mnyam pa ni med de/ 'di dag ni rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu skyed pa yin na de ni rigs 'dra ba phyi ma skyed pa la 'dod pa'i phyir ro/ / des na 'dir dag ces pa ni gnyis kyi sgra yin pas gnyis ni da ltar 'das pa dag gis zhes gdon par bya'o/

Five causes other than active cause bear (gṛhṇanti) their result (phala) {or seed} in the present (vartamāna) due to their potency. {“Bear their result” means that it produces an effect when the capacity to generate an effect gains sufficient strength to directly generate that effect.} Active cause definitely possesses a result {and indeed it corresponds to the present,} but because its action has stopped in the past {since it has already borne its result} and its action is not generated in future, these are not called “potent.” Question: How do they produce their results? Reply: Two causes — coemergent and concomitant — fully produce (prayacchata) their results in the present {by means of present action alone,} since bearing their result and producing their result occur at the same time. Producing results is generating results, which means that generating results occurs at the same time as the cause. Homogeneous and omnipresent causes produce their results as present (vartamāna) causes and past (abhyatīta) causes because present production is immediately preceding production {at the conclusion of its cause} and past production [pertains to causes] that have ceased. They do not occur at the same time because if they generate results of natural outflow, they produce subsequent states of similar type. Therefore here the pluralizing term is a term for “both,” and “both” means the past and present.

{gal te dge ba'i skal mnyam gyi rgyu 'bras bu 'dzin la ma 'byin pa yod dam zhe na mu bzhi ste/ mu dang po 'dzin la mi 'byin pa ni dge rtsa gcod pa na dge ba'i thob pa tha ma'o/ / gnyis pa 'byin la mi 'dzin pa ni nying mtshams sbyor ba'i tshe'i dge ba'i thob pa dang po'o/ / gsum pa gnyis ka yin pa ni dge rtsa ma chad pa'i gnas skabs lhag ma'o/ / bzhi pa gnyis min na de dag ma gtogs pa ste/ gang sa las nyams pa'am/ dge rtsa chad pa'i gnas skabs so/ } rnam par smin pa'i rgyu gcig pu ni 'das pa kho nas 'bras bu 'byin par 'gyur gyi dus mnyam pa dang de ma thag tu 'byin pa ni med do/ / chos mngon pa ba kha cig rten gyi 'bras bu rlung gi dkyil 'khor la chu brten pa la sogs pa dang*/ sbyor ba'i 'bras bu lam snga mas phye ma skyed pa dang*/ tshogs pa'i 'bras bu mig la sogs pa'i mig gi rnam shes la sogs pa dang*/ bsgoms pa'i 'bras bu gzugs na spyod pa'i lam gyi sprul pa'i sems lta bu'o zhes zer ba ni skyes bu byed 'bras dang bdag 'bras kyi bye brag yin no/ / yang rgyu du zhig gis 'bras bu gang zhig skyed ce na/

{Question: If a virtuous homogeneous cause bears its result, does it produce its result or not? Reply: There are four possibilities: The first possibility is that which bears its result but does not produce it, such as the final obtainment of virtue before the root of virtue is severed. The second is that which produces its result but does not bear it, such as the initial obtainment of virtue when linking. The third is that which is both, [178] such as the remaining instances when the root of virtue is not severed. The fourth is that which is neither, such as states other than those, when degenerating from a higher level, or severing the root of virtue.} One — the cause of karmic maturation — produces (prayacchati) its result in the past (atīta) alone. It does not produce its result at the same time, nor immediately after it. An Ābhidharmika says: The result of support is, for example, the wind maṇḍala supporting the water maṇḍala and so on. The result of preparation is, for example, the earlier path producing the later path. The result of collection is, for example, the eye and so on and eye consciousness and so forth. The result of meditation is, for example, the mind of emanation of the path operating in the form realm. Reply: These are subsets of the results of conscious effort and dominant results. Question: How many causes produce how many results?
nyon mongs can dang rnam smin skyes/ / lhag dang dang po 'phags rim bzhin/ / 60 rnam smin kun 'gro de gnyis dang / / skal mnyam ma gtogs lhag las skyes/ /

They are afflicted, arisen from karmic maturation, the remainder, and the first ārya moment that arises sequentially from the remaining causes except for both karmic maturation and omnipresent causes as well as homogeneous cause. (2:60)

'bras bu rnams ni mtshungs ldan sems dang sems byung dang*/ de ma yin pa gnyis su nges so/ / de dag kyang rnam pa bzhi bzhir nges te/ nyon mongs can dang*/ rnam smin skyes dang*/ zag med dang po dang*/ de dag gi lhag ma'o/ / de la mtshungs ldan sems sems byung nyon mongs can{ mi dge ba dang bsgribs pa} ni rim pa bzhin du rnam smin gyi rgyu ma gtogs pa lhag ma lnga las skye ste rnam smin gyi rgyu las mi skye ba ni nyon mongs can rnam smin gyi 'bras bur mi rigs pa'i gtan tshigs kyi phyir ro/ / rnam par smin pa las skyes pa rnams ni rim pa bzhin du kun 'gro'i rgyu ma gtogs pa lhag ma lnga las skye ste/ kun 'gro las mi skye ba ni nyon mongs can ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / lhag ma ni rnam smin skyes ma gtogs pa'i ma bsgribs lung ma bstan spyod lam pa dang*/ bza'i gnas pa dang*/ sprul sems la sogs pa rnams dang*/ zag med kyi skad cig ma dang po las gzhan pa'i dge ba rnams te/ de dag ni rim pa bzhin du rnam smin dang kun 'gro'i rgyu de gnyis ma gtogs pa lhag ma bzhi las skye ste/ de gnyis las mi skye ba {rig pa gang zhig } ni rnam smin skyes dang nyon mongs can ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / dang po 'phags pa ni sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa'i skad cig ma dang po ste de'i sems dang sems las byung ba ni rim pa bzhin du rnam smin dang kun 'gro'i rgyu de gnyis dang skal mnyam gyi rgyu ma gtogs pa lhag ma gsum las skye ste/ skal mnyam las mi skye ba ni 'jig rten chos mchog man chad zag bcas yin pas{ rigs 'dra sngon du ma song bas} de dag gi rgyu mthun las ma byung bas ris mi 'dra ba'i phyir ro/ / rnam smin dang kun 'gro las mi skye ba ni de dge ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: Results have two types: (1) concomitant minds and mental factors, and (2) states other than those. (1) Concomitant minds and mental factors have four types: [a] afflicted, [b] arisen from the cause of karmic maturation, [c] the first moment of the uncontaminated state, and [d] the remainder. [a] Concomitant minds and mental factors that are afflicted (kliṣṭa) {nonvirtuous or obscured states} arise sequentially from five causes except for the cause of karmic maturation because the proof that “they are not generated from the cause of karmic maturation” [establishes the thesis that] “afflictive states cannot be the results of karmic maturation.” [b] Those arisen from the cause of karmic maturation (vipākajā) arise sequentially from five causes except for omnipresent cause because those not arisen from omnipresent cause are not afflicted. [d] Except for those arising from the cause of karmic maturation, the remainder (śeṣa) are unobscured-neutral states such as the minds governing demeanor, creativity, and emanation, and virtuous states other than the first moment of the uncontaminated state. They arise sequentially from four causes except for the cause of karmic maturation and omnipresent cause. They do not arise from those two because they are {cognition} not arisen from the cause of karmic maturation and they are not afflicted. [c] The first ārya moment (prathamārya) is the first moment of perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering. Its mind and mental factors arise sequentially (yathākrama) from the remaining three, except for both the cause of karmic maturation (vipāka) and omnipresent (sarvatraga) cause, as well as homogeneous (sabhāga) cause. They do not arise from homogeneity since the supreme mundane state and below are contaminated {and thus they are not preceded by states of similar type}. They do not arise from the cause of karmic maturation and omnipresent cause since they are virtuous.
sems dang sems las byung ba yin/ / mtshungs ldan ma gtogs gzhan de bzhin/ / 61

de dag ni sems dang sems las byung ba'i dbang du byas pa yin no/ / ji ltar sems dang sems byung la bshad pa ltar sems dang sems byung las gzhan la'ang de bzhin du shes par bya'o zhes sbyar te/ de la gzhan ni mi ldan pa'i 'du byed dang gzugs so/ / thams cad du 'dra'am zhe na/ mtshungs ldan gyi rgyu ni ma gtogs te/ de dag ni{ bems po yin pas} sems dang sems byung ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ mtshungs ldan gyi rgyu yang de dag la brjod pa'i phyir ro/ / zag med skad cig ma dang po'i gzugs dang mi ldan pa'i 'du byed ni zag med kyi sdom pa dang por thob pa dang sems sems byung dang sdom pa de dag gi thob pa dang mtshan nyid la sogs pa la 'dod do/ / gzhan dag ni shes par sla'o/

That is stated from the perspective of minds (citta) and mental factors (caitta). (2) States other than minds and mental factors should be understood in just the way that minds and mental factors have been explained. States other than those are nonassociated formative factors and form. Question: Are they similar in all aspects? Reply: They are, except for concomitant (saṃprayukta) cause, because [form] is neither a mind nor a mental factor, {since it is matter,} [179] and coemergent cause is also described as [a nonassociated formative factor]. Nonassociated formative factors and form of the first moment of the uncontaminated state are the initial obtainment of uncontaminated vows and the obtainment of the characteristics and so on of mind, mental factors, and vows. The others are easily understood.
gsum pa rkyen bshad pa
The four conditions
rkyen ni bzhi po dag tu gsungs/ / rgyu zhes bya ba rgyu lnga yin/ /
Conditions are said to be four. That called “causal condition” consists of five causes. (2:61cd)
['di] la lnga las
This has five headings:
mdor bstan pa ni
OVERVIEW

rkyen ni bzhi po dag tu gsungs so zhes bya ste/ gang las gsungs she na/ mdo las rkyen ni bzhi ste/ rgyu'i rkyen nyid dang*/ de ma thag pa'i rkyen nyid dang*/ dmigs pa'i rkyen nyid dang*/ bdag po'i rkyen nyid do zhes gsungs so/ / 'o na de la 'dir rgyu dang rkyen gyi khyad par gang zhe na/ kha cig na re 'bras bu skyes pa na rang gi rgyun ldog pa dang mi ldog pa dang*/ 'bras bu la thun mong ma yin pa dang thun mong gi sgo nas phan 'dogs pa ni rim pa ltar de gnyis yin no zhes zer ba dang*/ TIka byed dag gis kyang nye ba'i rkyen ni rgyu yin no/ / ring ba ni rkyen kho na yin no/ / gzhan dag na re skyed par byed pa ni rgyu'o/ / rkyen ni dmigs pa tsam du zad do zhes zer ro zhes bya ba la sogs pa bshad mod kyi 'dir bye brag tu smra ba ni 'di gnyis ming gi rnam grangs tsam las khyad par med par 'dod de/ TIka don gsal las/ rgyu rnams dang rkyen rnams la khyad par ci zhig yod ce na/ smras pa/ cung zad kyang med de/ 'di ltar bcom ldan 'das kyis rgyu gnyis dang rkyen gnyis ni yang dag pa'i lta ba skyed par byed pa yin no/ / gnyis gang zhe na/ gzhan gyi sgra dang*/ nang gi tshul bzhin yid la byed pa'o zhes pa dang*/ dge slong dag ming ni rgyu dang bcas/ rkyen dang bcas/ gzhi dang bcas pa yin no/ / dge slong dag mig gi rgyu ni gang yin/ rkyen ni gang yin/ gzhi ni gang yin zhe na/ dge slong dag mig gi rgyu ni las yin no/ / rkyen ni las yin no/ / gzhi ni las yin no zhes dang*/ de bzhi du ma rig pa'i rgyu rkyen tshul bzhin ma yin pa yid la byed pa la'ang rgyas par{ sbyar nas} gsungs so/ / des na rgyu dang rkyen dang gzhi dang byed rgyu dang rgyu mtshan dang rtags rgyu dang 'bras gnas zhes bya ba ni rnam grangs dag yin no zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / des na 'bras bu skyed pa dang 'grub par byed pas na rim pa ltar rgyu dang rkyen du brjod kyi don la tha dad med par shes par bya'o/ / 'on kyang bcom ldan 'das kyis la lar rgyu drug dang*/ la lar rkyen bzhir gsungs pa ni phung po khams dang skye mched bstan pa ltar gdul bya'i mos pa dang bstun pa'i phyir ro/ /

Conditions (pratyaya) are said to be four. Question: Where is that revealed? Reply: A sūtra declares: There are four conditions: causal condition, immediately preceding condition, objective condition, dominant condition.[632] Question: What is the difference between cause and condition? Some say: When those two respectively generate a result, their continuum either subsides or does not subside, or they benefit their result in a specific way or a general way. Indeed Pūrṇavardhana’s commentary states: Proximate conditions are causes. Distant [conditions] are conditions alone. Others say that which generates [something] is the cause. Conditions are merely observed.[633] In this context Vaibhāṣikas assert these two are synonyms and they are not different, because the Subcommentary writes: What is the difference between cause and condition? There is none in the least, since the Bhagavan has declared that two causes and two conditions generate correct view. What are these two? They are alternative terms [for that which generates] internal appropriate mental attention.[634] So too [Pūrṇavardhana] observes at length that the cause and condition of ignorance is inappropriate mental attention {in reference to the statement}: Monks, eyes possess causes, possess conditions, possess a basis. Monks, what is the cause, what is the condition, what is the basis of the eye? Monks, the cause of the eye is karma. The condition is karma. The basis is karma.[635] Therefore cause, condition, basis, active cause, argument, reason, and resultant abidance are explained to be synonyms. Moreover, you should understand that those generating a result and those establishing a result are respectively described as causes and conditions, but they are not distinct states. Still, the Bhagavan has at times stated six causes or four conditions in accordance with the inclination of disciples, in the same way that he taught aggregates, bases, and elements.
rgyas par bshad pa ni
ELABORATION
rkyen bzhi po de dag kyang gang zhe na/
Question: What are the four conditions?
de la rgyu'i rkyen zhes bya ba ni byed rgyu ma gtogs pa rgyu lnga yin no/ / sems dang sems las byung ba rnams ni mtshungs pa de ma thag pa'i rkyen yin no zhes sbyar ro/ / thams cad dam zhe na/

Reply: That which is called “causal condition” (hetupratyaya) consists of [180] the five causes except for active cause. Minds and mental factors are equivalent immediately preceding conditions. Question: Are all minds and mental factors immediately preceding conditions?
sems dang sems byung skyes pa rnams/ / tha ma min mtshungs de ma thag / 62 dmigs pa chos rnams thams cad do/ / byed rgyu zhes bya bdag por bshad/ /
Final minds and mental factors are not equivalent immediately preceding conditions. Objective conditions are all objects. Active cause is said to be the dominant condition. (2:62)

dgra bcom pa mya ngan las 'da' ka ma'i sems dang sems las byung ba'i tha ma ni mtshungs pa de ma thag pa'i rkyen min te/ sems sems byung rgyun chad par 'dod pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dir rdzas mtshungs pa'i phyir mtshungs pa zhes bya ste/ rnam par shes pa gcig gi de ma thag tu rnam par shes pa gcig dang*/ tshor ba gcig gi de ma thag tu tshor ba gcig{ 'byung ba} la sogs pa'o/ / de'i phyir gzugs la ni de ma thag pa'i rkyen ma bshad de/{mi mnyam par 'byung bas/}rdzas mi mtshungs pa'i phyir ro/ / des na rkyen 'di ni mtshungs pa'ang yin la de ma thag pa'ang yin pas mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen zhes bya'o/ /

Reply: The final minds and mental factors of arhats about to pass into nirvāṇa are not equivalent (sama) immediately preceding (anantara) conditions (pratyaya) because for them the continuum of minds and mental factors are severed. Here, they are called “equivalent” because they are substantially equivalent, [and “immediately preceding”] because consciousness immediately precedes consciousness, feeling immediately precedes feeling, and so on. Form is not an immediately preceding condition because it is not equivalent in substance, {since it arises devoid of awareness}. Therefore something is called an “equivalent immediately preceding condition” when it is equivalent to and immediately precedes another.

de yang btsun pa dbyig bshes ni{ mi mnyam pa'i don} rgyas byung gi gzugs kyi rgyud gcig ma 'gags par rgyas byung gnyis pa 'byung ba'i phyir ro {des na 'chol lo } zhes 'dod de/ de'i don ni zas kyis rgyas pa ma 'gags par gnyid dang legs par bya ba dang ting nge 'dzin gyis rgyas pa 'byung ba'i phyir ro zhes bya'o/ / mdo sde pa'i gnas brtan btsun pa na re mang po las nyung ngu dang*/ nyung ngu las kyang mang po 'byung ba'i phyir te/ sog ma las thal ba nyung ngu dang*/ n+ya gro d+ha'i sa bon las yal ga la sogs pa mang po 'byung ba bzhin no/ / zhes zer ro/ / 'grel pa las mi mnyam par 'byung ba'i phyir gzugs ni mtshungs pa de ma thag pa'i rkyen ma yin te/ 'di ltar 'dod pa na spyod pa'i gzugs kyi mjug thogs su res 'ga' ni 'dod pa na spyod pa dang*/ gzugs na spyod pa'i rnam par rig byed ma yin pa'i gzugs 'byung ngo*/ / res 'ga' ni 'dod pa na spyod pa dang*/ zag pa med pa 'byung bas gzugs mngon du 'gyur ba 'chol pa yin no/ / mtshungs pa de ma thag pa'i rkyen ni 'chol pa ma yin no zhes 'byung ste/

Further, the venerable Vasumitra asserts that {the meaning of “devoid of awareness” is that} if a single continuum of form derived from enhancement does not cease, then a second moment derived from enhancement will occur. {Therefore they mix}. The meaning of that is that if enhancement due to food does not cease, then enhancement due to sleep, proper action, and concentration can occur. A venerable Sautrāntika elder says: Few arise from many and many arise from few because, respectively, little ash arises from burned straw, and many branches and so on arise from the seed of a nyagrodha [or bodhi tree]. The Autocommentary states: Because it arises devoid of awareness, form is not an equivalent immediately preceding condition. Occasionally, after utilizing form in the desire realm, nonindicative form may arise that is utilized in the desire realm and in the form realm. Occasionally form utilized in the desire realm may arise as an uncontaminated state. Therefore manifest form is mixed. But the equivalent immediately preceding condition is not mixed.[636]

This means that if one takes pratimokṣa vows but lacks equipoise, only pratimokṣa vows arise. If one enters equipoise in the contaminated absorptions, absorption vows arise. If one enters meditative attainment in the uncontaminated absorptions, the form of uncontaminated vows arises. Therefore form is indeed mixed. Minds and mental factors are equivalent because at times active minds {and} mental factors are utilized in the desire realm, at times they are utilized in the form realm, and at times {twenty-two} uncontaminated minds and mental factors arise. But the former presentation is better. Therefore “equivalent” refers to equivalent substance {such as two types of feeling [with different substance] not arising}. “Immediate” refers to a result that is generated immediately. {Also, nonassociated formative factors are mixed since they manifest at the same time in the three realms and in uncontaminated states.} [181]
Further, they are already generated {past and present} states alone and not future states because the future has no earlier and later parts, {just as the present is not the immediately preceding condition of the present.} However, immediately preceding conditions are posited with earlier and later parts.

gal te ma 'ongs pa la snga phyi med na rim par mi 'byung ba dang*/ de sangs rgyas kyis{ 'di'i rjes su 'di 'byung zhes} rim can du mi mkhyen par 'gyur ro zhe na ma yin te/ spyir rgyu dang 'bras bu 'brel ba'i phyir 'byung ba na rim par skye la/ de sangs rgyas kyis mkhyen pa ni 'das pa dang da lta ba'i rim pa dngos su mkhyen pa'i shugs la mkhyen pa'am 'das da ltar las rjes su dpags pas mkhyen to zhes kha cig 'dod la/ kha cig ni {sems can gyi rgyud la } ma 'ongs pa rim par 'byung ba'i 'bras bu'i rtags su gyur pa mi ldan pa'i 'du byed kyi khyad par zhig yod de/ de mngon sum du mkhyen nas ma 'ongs pa'i rim pa mkhyen pa yin gyi/ da ltar ba'i ye shes kyis ma 'ongs pa'i rim pa dngos su mkhyen pa ni ma yin te/ ma 'ongs pa'i tshe ni rim pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / ma 'ongs pa la rim pa gsungs pa ni de dag skyes pa na rim par 'byung bar 'gyur ba yin na skyes pa ni 'das da ltar bar 'gyur ba'i phyir zhes 'dod de/ ma 'ongs pa'i rim pa 'das da ltar ba'i shugs la mkhyen par 'dod pa la ni sngon gyi mtha' ma mkhyen par phyi ma'i mtha' mi mkhyen par thal ba'i skyon yod do/ / bcom ldan 'das kyis ma 'ongs pa che ge mo zhig gi mjug thogs su ma 'ongs pa 'di 'byung ngo zhes ma 'ongs pa rim par 'byung ba'i 'bras bu'i rtags mkhyen pa las mkhyen par 'dod pa la ni sangs rgyas la rjes su dpag pa yod par thal ba dang*/ rgyu bas snga ba'i 'bras bu srid par thal ba'i skyon yod do/ /

Objection: If the future has no earlier or later parts, it would not serially arise and the Buddha would not comprehend stages {when something occurs after something else}. Some assert: That is not so, because in general cause and effect are related, and if something arises, it is generated in stages. The Buddha comprehends the future either through implicitly comprehending it, having explicitly comprehended the stages of the past and present, or through comprehending it by inferring it from the past and present. Some say: The future exists {in the mindstream of a sentient being} as a specific nonassociated formative factor that marks the effect arising in stages because the stages of the future are comprehended through directly comprehending that. Present transcendent wisdom does not explicitly comprehend the stages of the future because there are no stages at the time of the future. [Reply:] It would therefore erroneously follow that the assertion that “stages arising in future” means that if they are generated they will arise in stages, because they transform into the past and present, and those who assert that the stages of the future are indirectly understood from the past and the present do not comprehend a final end since they do not comprehend an initial beginning. For those who assert that the Bhagavan comprehends the future through comprehending signs of the result occurring in stages since the Buddha stated “at the conclusion of a particular future state, that future state will occur,”[637] it would then follow that the Buddha had inference (anumāna), and it would be possible that a result could precede its cause.

gal te 'das pa'i sems dang sems byung rang gi dus na mtshungs pa de ma thag pa nyid du byung ngo zhes 'dod na ma 'ongs pa'i sems dang sems byung rnams kyang rang gi dus na 'byung bar 'gyur ba'i phyir ma 'ongs pa'ang de ma thag pa'i rkyen du 'gyur ro/ / ma 'ongs pa ma skyes pas da ltar ba'i tshe na rkyen ma yin par 'dod na ni 'das pa'ang ma yin par 'gyur te 'gags pa'i phyir ro/ / bya ba 'gags kyi dngos po ma 'gags so zhes bya ba'ang lan ma yin te/ ma 'ongs pa la'ang mtshungs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dis ni skal mnyam dang kun 'gro ma 'ongs pa la mi 'dod pa'ang bkag par lta'o/ / 'dir 'grel pa las/ sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can dang sems kyi de ma thag pa can gyi mu bzhi dang*/ sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can dang snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi de ma thag pa can gyi mu bzhi gnyis bshad do/ / de la dang po ni chos gang dag sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can yin pa de dag sems kyi de ma thag pa can yang yin nam zhe na/

If it is asserted that “past minds and mental factors arise as equivalent immediately preceding conditions in their time,” then even future [minds and mental factors] would be immediately preceding conditions because future minds and mental factors occur in their time. If it is asserted that “the future is not a condition since it does not arise in the present,” then the past also would not be [a condition] because it has ceased. Stating “The action has ceased but not the thing” is not an answer because the future is similar. Such logic refutes those who do not assert future homogeneity and omnipresence. Here, the Autocommentary explains: Those possessing equivalent immediately preceding minds and those possessing immediately preceding minds have four possibilities. Those possessing equivalent immediately preceding minds and those possessing the immediately preceding two meditative attainments have four possibilities.[638] Question: In the first case, do phenomena that possess equivalent immediately preceding minds also possess immediately preceding minds?
mu bzhi ste/
THE FIRST FOUR POSSIBILITIES

de la mu dang po ni sems med kyi snyoms 'jug gnyis las lta ba'i sems dang*/ snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma gnyis pa la sogs pa ste/{ 'jug sems kyis bskyed kyang bar du chod pa'i phyir ro/ /} de la ldang sems ni snyoms 'jug gi skad cig ma rnams kyis bar du chod kyang sems gzhan gyis bar du ma chod pa'i phyir dang*/ snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma gnyis pa la sogs pa ni gsum gyis snyoms par 'jug pa gnyis zhes 'byung bas sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can yin la/ ldang sems ni snyoms 'jug gi skad cig ma rnams kyis bar du chod pa'i phyir dang*/ snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma gnyis pa la sogs pa ni ci rigs par snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma dang po la sogs pas bar du chod pa'i phyir sems kyi de ma thag pa can ni ma yin no/ /

(1) The first possibility is the mind of view arising from both mindless meditative attainments [182] and from the second [and subsequent] moments of both meditative attainments {because they are generated by the mind entering meditative attainment but they are obstructed}. They possess equivalent immediately preceding minds because minds arising [from meditative attainment] are not obstructed [from arising] by other minds, though they are obstructed [from arising] by moments of meditative attainment. And the second moments of both meditative attainments and so on [possess equivalent immediately preceding minds] since the Abhidharmakośa mentions, “Three generate both meditative attainments” (2:64b). They do not possess immediately preceding minds because the mind arising [from meditative attainment] is obstructed by moments of meditative attainment, and the second moments of both meditative attainments and so on are obstructed by the first moments of both meditative attainments.

mu gnyis pa ni sems med kyi snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma dang po'i skye ba la sogs pa'i mtshan nyid dang rjes su mthun pa'i mtshan nyid dang thob pa la sogs pa dang*/ sems dang bcas pa'i gnas skabs kyi sems dang sems byung thams cad kyi skye ba la sogs pa'i mtshan nyid dang rjes su mthun pa'i mtshan nyid dang thob pa la sogs pa rnams te/ de dag ni sems snga ma dang gnyis kyi bar du skad cig ma gzhan gyis bar du mchod pa'i phyir sems kyi de ma thag pa can yin la/ sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can gyi ngo bo ma yin pas sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can ni ma yin te/ sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can ni sems dang sems byung rnams dang sems med kyi snyoms 'jug gnyis kho na yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'du shes med pa pa ni sems kyis mngon par 'dus ma byas par las kyi mthus skye ba'i phyir bstan bcos las sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can yin par mi 'byung ngo zhes rgyal po'i sras 'chad do/ /

(2) The second possibility is characteristics such as the arising of the first moments of both meditative attainments, their secondary characteristics, and their obtainment and so on; and the characteristics such as the arising of all minds and mental factors when minds are manifest, their secondary characteristics, and their obtainment and so on. They possess immediately preceding minds because they are not obstructed by other moments intervening between past minds and those two meditative attainments. Since by nature they are not states that possess equivalent immediately preceding minds, they do not possess equivalent immediately preceding minds, because those possessing equivalent immediately preceding minds are only minds, mental factors, and the two mindless meditative attainments. Jinaputra explains that the treatise[639] declares that beings possessing nondiscernment do not possess equivalent immediately preceding minds because they are born by the force of karma not actually subsumed by mind.

mu gsum pa ni sems med kyi snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma dang po dang*/ sems dang bcas pa'i gnas skabs kyi skad cig ma gzhan gyis bar ma chod par sems snga ma'i mjug thogs su sems dang sems byung phyi ma 'byung ba rnams te/ de dag ni rim pa ltar sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen gyis bskyed pa'i 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir dang*/ sems snga ma'i rjes su skad cig ma gzhan gyis bar du ma chod par de ma thag tu 'byung ba'i mtshungs ldan yin pa'i phyir sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can yang yin la sems kyi de ma thag ba can yang yin no/ /

(3) The third possibility is the first moments of both mindless meditative attainments and later minds and mental factors that arise at the conclusion of past minds not obstructed by other moments when associated with mind. They possess equivalent immediately preceding minds as well as immediately preceding minds because they are, respectively, (a) results generated by equivalent immediately preceding minds and (b) equivalent states occurring immediately after past minds that were not obstructed by other moments of mind.

mu bzhi pa ni sems med kyi snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma gnyis pa la sogs pa'i skye ba la sogs pa'i mtshan nyid dang thob pa la sogs pa dang*/ snyoms 'jug gnyis las ldang sems kyi skye ba la sogs pa'i mtshan nyid dang thob pa la sogs pa ste/ de dag ni sems dang sems byung dang snyoms 'jug gnyis ma yin pas sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can yang ma yin la/ snyoms 'jug gi skad cig ma dang po la sogs pas bar du chod pa'i phyir sems kyi de ma thag pa can yang ma yin no/ /

(4) The fourth possibility is characteristics such as the arising of the second moments of both mindless meditative attainments and their obtainment and so forth, and characteristics such as the arising of the minds that arise from both meditative attainments and their obtainment and so forth. They do not possess equivalent immediately preceding minds, [183] since they are not minds or mental factors and are neither [of the two mindless] meditative attainments. They do not possess immediately preceding minds since they are obstructed by the first moment and so on of meditative attainment.
mu bzhi gnyis pa ni
THE SECOND FOUR POSSIBILITIES

chos gang dag sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can yin pa de dag snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi de ma thag pa can yang yin nam zhe na/ 'di la'ang mu bzhi las mu dang po ni snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma dang po dang*/ sems dang bcas pa'i gnas skabs kyi sems snga ma'i mjug thogs su skad cig ma gzhan gyis bar du ma chod par sems dang sems byung phyi ma byung ba rnams te/ de dag ni rim pa ltar gsum gyis snyoms par 'jug pa gnyis zhes pa dang*/ bzhi yis sems dang sems byung rnams zhes 'byung bas snyoms 'jug gnyis yin pas sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen gyis bskyed pa'i 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir dang*/ sems snga ma'i rjes su skad cig ma gzhan gyis bar du ma chod par de ma thag tu byung ba'i mtshungs ldan yin pas sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen gyis bskyed pa'i phyir sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can ni yin la/ snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi de ma thag pa can ni ma yin te/ snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma dang po la snyoms 'jug gi skad cig ma snga ma sngon du song ba med pa'i phyir dang*/ sems dang bcas pa'i gnas skabs de dag la'ang snyoms 'jug gnyis skad cig ma gzhan gyis bar du ma chod par sngon du song ba med pa'i phyir ro/ /

Question: Are there any phenomena that possess equivalent immediately preceding minds that also possess the immediately preceding two meditative attainments? Reply: Even for this there are four possibilities: (1) The first possibility is the first moments of both meditative attainments and later minds and mental factors that are not obstructed at the conclusion of other earlier moments of the mind when minds are manifest. They possess equivalent immediately preceding minds because they are results produced by equivalent immediately preceding conditions, both being meditative attainments, for the Abhidharmakośa declares, respectively, “Three generate both meditative attainments” (2:64b) and “Four conditions generate minds and mental factors” (2:64a); and they are generated by the equivalent immediately preceding condition of the mind since they are equivalent states arising immediately [after it] without being obstructed by other subsequent moments of earlier minds. They do not possess the immediately preceding two meditative attainments because the first moment of both meditative attainments has no earlier preceding moment of meditative attainment, and when associated with the mind there is no preceding state obstructed by other moments of either meditative attainment.

mu gnyis pa ni snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma gnyis pa la sogs pa'i skye ba la sogs pa'i mtshan nyid dang thob pa la sogs pa dang*/ snyoms 'jug gnyis las ldang sems kyi skye ba la sogs pa'i mtshan nyid dang thob pa la sogs pa rnams te/ de dag ni skad cig ma gzhan gyis bar du ma chod par snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi de ma thag tu 'byung ba'i phyir snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi de ma thag pa can ni yin la/ snyoms 'jug gnyis dang sems dang sems byung ma yin pas sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can ni ma yin no/ /

(2) The second possibility is characteristics such as the arising of the second moments of both meditative attainments and their obtainment and so forth, and characteristics such as the arising of minds that arise from both meditative attainments and their obtainment and so on. They possess the immediately preceding two meditative attainments because they arise immediately after both meditative attainments without being obstructed by other moments. They do not possess equivalent immediately preceding minds since they are neither meditative attainments nor minds or mental factors.

mu gsum pa ni sems med pa'i snyoms 'jug gnyis las ldang sems dang*/ snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma gnyis la sogs pa ste/ de dag ni snyoms 'jug gi skad cig ma rnams kyis bar du chod kyang sems gzhan gyis bar du ma chod pa'i phyir dang*/ skad cig ma gzhan gyis bar du ma chod par snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi de ma thag tu 'byung ba'i phyir rim pa ltar sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can yang yin la/ snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi de ma thag pa can yang yin no/ /

(3) The third possibility is the mind arising from both mindless meditative attainments and the second moments of both meditative attainments and so forth. They respectively possess equivalent immediately preceding minds and possess immediately preceding meditative attainments because they are obstructed by moments of meditative attainment but are not obstructed by other minds, and because they arise immediately after both meditative attainments without obstruction by other moments.

mu bzhi pa ni snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma dang po'i mtshan nyid skye sogs dang thob pa la sogs pa dang*/ sems dang bcas pa'i gnas skabs kyi sems dang sems byung rnams kyi mtshan nyid skye sogs dang thob pa la sogs pa rnams te/ de dag ni snyoms 'jug gnyis dang sems dang sems byung ma yin pas sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can yang ma yin la/ de dag gi sngon du skad cig ma gzhan gyis bar du ma chod par snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma song ba med pa'i phyir snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi de ma thag pa can yang ma yin no/ / de ltar na mu bzhi tshan gnyis yod kyang mu bzhi dang po'i mu gsum pa dang bzhi pa ni mu bzhi gnyis pa'i mu dang po dang gnyis pa yin la/ mu bzhi dang po'i mu dang po dang gnyis pa ni mu bzhi gnyis pa'i mu gsum pa dang bzhi pa yin no/ / zhes 'grel pa las 'byung ngo*/ /

(4) The fourth possibility is characteristics such as the arising of the first moment of both meditative attainments and so on and their obtainment, and characteristics such as the arising of minds and mental factors [184] and their obtainment when minds are manifest. They do not possess equivalent immediately preceding minds since they are neither meditative attainments nor minds or mental factors. They do not possess immediately preceding meditative attainments because there are no moments of either meditative attainment that are not obstructed by other moments earlier than those. Though two divisions of four possibilities exist, the Autocommentary states: The third and fourth possibilities of the first set of four possibilities are the first and second possibilities of the second set of four possibilities, and the first and second possibilities of the first set of four possibilities are the third and fourth possibilities of the second set of four possibilities.[640]

des na grub pa'i mtha' smra ba 'di'i ltar na sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen dang sems kyi de ma thag rkyen dang snyoms 'jug gi de ma thag rkyen gsum yod pa las sems med kyi snyoms 'jug gnyis dang sems dang sems byung la ni spyir gsum ga yod de/ snyoms 'jug gnyis las ldang sems kyang snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi de ma thag pa can du bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / sems med kyi snyoms 'jug gnyis dang sems dang sems byung ma yin yang snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma dang po'i mtshan nyid skye sogs dang thob pa la sogs pa dang*/ sems dang sems byung gi mtshan nyid skye sogs dang thob pa la sogs pa la'ang sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen mi 'byung yang sems kyi de ma thag rkyen dang snyoms 'jug gi de ma thag rkyen gnyis kyis bskyed par 'dod la/ sems med kyi snyoms 'jug gnyis mtshungs ldan ma yin yang snyoms 'jug rang rang gi skad cig ma phyi ma rnams dang*/ snyoms 'jug gnyis kyi skad cig ma gnyis pa la sogs pa'i mtshan nyid skye sogs dang thob pa la sogs pa rnams kyang snyoms par 'jug pa'i de ma thag rkyen gyis bskyed par 'dod do/ /

Thus, according to the proponents of these tenets, there are three conditions: (1) equivalent immediately preceding conditions, (2) immediately preceding conditions, and (3) immediately preceding conditions of meditative attainment. The two mindless meditative attainments, and minds and mental factors in general, have three conditions, because the mind arisen from both meditative attainments is also said to possess immediately preceding meditative attainments. [The proponents of these tenets] assert that though both mindless meditative attainments are neither minds nor mental factors, characteristics such as the arising of the first moment of both meditative attainments and their obtainment and so forth, [and also] characteristics such as the arising of minds and mental factors and their obtainment and so on do not arise from the equivalent immediately preceding condition of the mind but are generated by the immediately preceding condition of the mind and the immediately preceding conditions of meditative attainment. They also assert that though the two mindless meditative attainments are not equivalent states, the later moments of each meditative attainment — characteristics such as the arising of the second moments of both meditative attainments and their obtainment and so forth — are generated by the immediately preceding conditions of meditative attainment.

gal te sems med gnyis kyi ldang sems ni de gnyis la 'jug sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa'i 'bras bur mi rung ste/ skad cig ma du mas bar du chod pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ skad cig ma du mas bar du chod pa tsam gyis ni de ma yin par mi 'gyur gyi sems gzhan gyis bar du chod na de ma yin par 'gyur ba las 'di ni sems gzhan gyis bar du ma chod pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir 'grel pa las kyang da ni ji ltar ldang ba'i sems yun ring mo zhig tu chad pa snyoms par 'jug pa'i sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa zhes bya zhe na/ sems gzhan gyis bar du ma chod pa'i phyir ro zhes bshad do/ / mdo sde pa ni dbang po dang bcas pa'i lus la sems kyi sa bon yod pa dang*/ sems tsam pa ni rnam shes brtan pa dag yin par 'dod do zhes bshad zin to/ /

Objection: The mind arising from both mindless states cannot be the result of the equivalent immediately preceding mind entering meditative attainment because many moments obstruct it. Reply: It is not that it would not be a result due merely to being obstructed by many moments but that it would not be a result due to being obstructed by other minds. But it is not obstructed by other minds, as the Autocommentary explains: Why is it called the equivalent immediately preceding mind that enters meditative attainment and obstructs the mind arising from meditative attainment for a long time? That is because it is not obstructed by other minds.[641] Sautrāntikas assert that the seed of the mind exists in bodies possessing sense faculties. Cittamātrins assert that it is those stable consciousnesses. This was previously explained.
dmigs pa'i rkyen/
OBJECTIVE CONDITION

dmigs pa'i rkyen ni mig gi rnam shes la sogs pa rang rang gi rnam shes mtshungs ldan dang bcas pa'i dmigs rkyen ni rang rang gi yul zag bcas gzugs la sogs pa'i chos da ltar ba rnams yin la/ yid kyi rnam shes kyi dmigs rkyen ni zag bcas zag med kyi chos dus gsum dang dus kyis ma bsdus pa{ yul du rung ba} thams cad do/ /

The objective conditions (ālambana) of eye consciousness and so on, and those concomitant [185] with eye consciousness, are present objects, such as contaminated material form, that comprise their objects. The objective condition of mental consciousness consists of all (sarva) contaminated and uncontaminated objects (dharma) subsumed or not subsumed by the three times {that are suitable to be objects}.

gal te gzugs la sogs pa dag la rnam shes kyis mi dmigs pa de'i tshe dmigs pa'i rkyen du ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/ dmigs pa'i gzugs la sogs pa dang ris 'dra ba'i phyir de dag kyang dmigs par gzhag ste dper na shing la sogs pa mi sreg pa dag kyang de lta ba'i ris dang mtshan nyid 'dra ba'i phyir bud shing zhes brjod pa bzhin no/ / yang na 'ga' zhig gis ma dmigs kyang 'ga' zhig gis dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ / ci ste chos thams cad yid kyi rnam shes kyi dmigs rkyen yin na 'dus ma byas kyang yin par 'gyur la/ de lta na'ang 'dus ma byas dngos por 'gyur te/ 'bras bu skyed pa'i don byed nus pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ bye brag tu smra ba ni 'dus ma byas de dag dngos por thal ba 'dod par byed mod kyi 'on kyang de dag gis 'bras bu skyed na rtag tu skyed pa'am/ yang na nam yang mi skyed par 'gyur te/ rtag pa'i dngos por khas blangs pa'i phyir ro/ / res 'ga' skyed pa dang mi skyed pa ni res 'ga' ba yin pa'i phyir mi rtag par 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'i skyon yod do/ / des na 'dus ma byas ni ngo bo med pa'i phyir dmigs pa'i yul tsam yin gyi 'bras bu skyed pa'i rkyen ni ma yin no zhes bya bar 'dod pa nyid legs pa yin no/ /

Question: If at a particular time consciousness does not focus on form and so on, how could they [i.e., form and so on] be objective conditions? Reply: They are posited as focal objects because they are form of the same type as that focused on. For instance, wood and so on that is not burning is called firewood because it is of the same type, and possesses the same characteristics, as firewood. Again, [they are posited as focal objects] because some consciousnesses focus on them and some do not. Objection: If all objects are the objective conditions of mental consciousness, then unconditioned states would also be its focal objects. Thus unconditioned states would become things [or functional entities] (bhāva) and capable of generating results. Vaibhāṣikas assert: Indeed, it follows that unconditioned states are things [or functional entities]. Reply: But then the error would arise that if [unconditioned states] generate results, such results would always be generated or never generated, since you accept the existence of permanent phenomena. And [unconditioned states] would become impermanent because they would intermittently generate results and intermittently not generate results.

DOMINANT CONDITION

What was formerly called active cause (kāraṇa) is said to be the dominant condition (adhipati) {since it benefits [or assists] in a nonspecific way}. Question: If all phenomena are objective conditions and dominant conditions, how do they differ? Reply: {Dominant conditions are all phenomena including those coemergent with it but excluding itself. Those objects coemergent with it, however, are not its objective conditions.} Regarding objective conditions, the objects of specific minds and mental factors are their objective conditions, and the objects of different minds and mental factors are different objective conditions. All phenomena are called “focal objects” (ālambana) since they are the focal objects of any type of mind and mental factor, but all minds and mental factors do not focus on all objects. Moreover, objective conditions are conditions for those phenomena that possess focal objects but not for those that do not. Dominant conditions differ since they consist of all objects other than themselves, and though concomitant and coemergent causes are dominant conditions, they are not objective conditions. Therefore the Autocommentary explains: Since this condition has greater pervasion, it is called “dominant condition.”[642] And: What greater pervasion does it have? Dominant conditions have greater pervasion since coemergent causes are never objective conditions but are dominant conditions. [186] Again, it is a condition of greater pervasion because it pervades all objects and all conditioned states except for itself.[643]
