HOW CONDITIONS PRODUCE RESULTS
rgyu gnyis po dag 'gag pa la/ / bya ba byed do gsum po ni/ / 63 skye la'o de las gzhan pa yi/ / rkyen dag de las bzlog pa yin/ /
Two causes act to manifest cessation. Three act to manifest generation. Two conditions are different and reverse that order. (2:63)

de la re zhig rgyu'i rkyen la rgyu rnam pa lnga yod pa las lhan cig 'byung ba dang mtshungs ldan gyi rgyu gnyis po dag ni 'bras bu 'gag pa la mngon du phyogs pa da ltar ba la bya ba byed de/{ phan tshun 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir ro/} skal mnyam dang kun 'gro dang rnam smin gyi rgyu gsum po ni 'bras bu skye ba la mngon du phyogs pa la ma 'ongs pa la bya ba byed pa'o/ / rgyu'i rkyen de las gzhan pa mtshungs pa de ma thag pa dang dmigs pa'i rkyen gnyis pa dag ni rgyu'i rkyen la da ltar ba la bya ba byed pa dang ma 'ongs pa la bya ba byed pa gnyis su bstan pa'i go rim de las bzlog pa mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen ni skabs 'byed pa'i phyir skye ba la mngon du phyogs pa ma 'ongs pa dang*/ dmigs rkyen ni sems dang sems byung rnams kyis 'dzin pa'i phyir 'gag pa la mngon du phyogs pa da ltar ba la bya ba byed do zhes bya ba yin no/ / gal te de ltar sems dang sems byung dag 'das ma 'ongs pa{ dang 'dus ma byas} la mi dmigs par 'gyur te/ dmigs rkyen da ltar bas sems dang sems byung da ltar ba skyed pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ { de ni gtso che ba'i dbang du byas pa'am/ yang na/} bye brag tu smra bas 'das ma 'ongs kyang da ltar dngos por yod pa'i phyir de dag la dmigs pa'ang dus mnyam pa kho na'o zhes bya bar mngon no/ / mdo sde pa ni rgyu 'bras thams cad dus mi mnyam pa kho na yin pa'i phyir rgyu rkyen thams cad 'bras bu skye bar 'gyur ba la bya ba byed pa yin gyi da ltar ba ni bya ba byed pa med do zhes 'dod de/ rnam 'grel las/ rgyu rnams thams cad sngar yod yin zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

Causal conditions have five types of cause. From among those, two causes (hetu) — coemergent and concomitant — act (kāritra) in the present to manifest the cessation (nirudh) of results. Three causes — homogeneous, omnipresent, and the cause of karmic maturation — act in the future to manifest the generation (kuruta) of results. Two conditions (pratyaya) — the equivalent immediately preceding condition and the objective condition — are different from the causal condition and reverse (viparyaya) that order where causal condition is said to act in both the present and future. Thus the equivalent immediately preceding condition acts in the future to manifest generation because it distinguishes earlier and later periods. And the objective condition acts in the present to manifest cessation because it is held by minds and mental factors. Objection: If minds and mental factors do not focus on past, future, {and unconditioned states,} then the present objective conditions would generate present minds and mental factors. {Reply: That is from the perspective of the main assertion.} Vaibhāṣikas actually state that because past, future, as well as present [objects] exist as things [or functional entities], then [objective conditions] only exist at the same time as those [minds and mental factors] that focus upon them. Sautrāntikas assert that because causes and effects never exist at the same time, all causes and conditions function to give rise to effects, but that present [minds and their focal objects] do not act in that way, for the Exposition of Valid Cognition declares: All causes exist at a prior [time].[644]

'o na lhan cig 'byung ba dang mtshungs ldan dag phan tshun rgyu 'bras su mi 'gyur la/ de lta na'ang rgyu de dag mi srid par 'gyur ro zhe na/ tshogs pa snga ma'i stobs kyis phyi ma dag lhan cig 'byung ba dang mtshungs ldan rnam pa lnga can du'ang 'byung ba'i phyir lhan cig 'byung ba dang mtshungs ldan gyi rgyu yin no/ / phan tshun rgyu 'bras su gsungs pa ni rgyun la ltos nas yin gyi skad cig ma'i rdzas la ni ma yin no zhes bya bar 'dod do/ / 'o na ni sems med las langs ma thag pa'i sems kyi skad cig ma dang po de la tshor ba la sogs pa med na de dag kun 'gro ma yin par 'gyur la/ yod na sems las byung bar mi 'gyur te/ dus mnyam pa'i sems las ni ma byung bar 'dod pa'i phyir dang*/ snga ma na sems med pa'i phyir ro/ / dang po dus mnyam pa'i sems las byung na phyi ma rnams kyang 'byung bar 'gyur te/ khyad par med pa'i phyir ro/ / tshor ba la sogs pa sems las ma byung na ni sems las byung bar 'dod pa nyams pa yin no/ / mdo las kyang*/ 'du shes dang sems pa'i tshogs 'di dag ni sems las byung ba/ sems la brten pa/ sems las skyes pa dag yin no zhes gsungs pa dang 'gal lo/ /

Objection: Coemergent and concomitant causes do not act as reciprocal causes and results; thus such causes are impossible. Reply: Coemergent and concomitant causes exist because states that are coemergent or concomitant in five ways arise due to the power of a prior collection of conditions. They are said to be reciprocal causes and results from the perspective of their continua and not their momentary substance. However, if feeling and so on do not exist in the first moment of the mind that has just arisen from mindless meditative attainment, they would not be omnipresent. If they do exist, then they would not be mental factors because they could not arise from the mind (sems ’byung) that exists at the same time as them and no mind exists prior to them. First, if they were derived from a mind that exists at the same time as them, then later states would also arise because there would be no difference between them. But if feeling and so on were not derived from mind, then the assertion that they arise from the mind would fail. A sūtra proclaims: These collections of discernment and intention are derived from mind, supported by mind, generated from mind.[645] [187]

gang yang kha cig gis sems med la snyoms par zhugs pa na kun gzhi rnam shes la sogs pa'i rnam shes ma 'gags pa yod pa de las byung ngo zhes bya ba de yang rigs pa ma yin te/ kun gzhi'i sems las byung ba ni sems gzhan dang lhan cig 'byung ba'i 'khor du 'gal ba'i phyir dang*/ kun gzhi'i sa bon las byung ba de lta na'ang de rgyu'i rkyen yin pa'i phyir ro/ / sems kyi skad cig ma dang po la ni tshor ba la sogs pa dus mnyam du med do zhes bya ba'ang rigs pa ma yin te/ phyi ma rnams la'ang med par 'gyur te/ khyad par med pa'i phyir ro/ / skad cig ma dang po la sems skye na ni sems las byung ba'ang skye bar 'gyur te/ rgyu ma tshang ba med par mtshungs pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir/ ma tshang med rgyu de las ni/ / 'bras bu gang gis zlog par 'gyur/ / zhes rnam 'grel las gsungs so/ / de'i phyir dus mnyam pa'i rgyu 'bras ni yod par shes so/ / 'on kyang 'das ma 'ongs la dmigs pa ni med pa la dmigs pa'i phyir de dag dmigs rkyen ma yin la/ gang dmigs rkyen yin pa de dmigs byed dang dus mnyam pa'o zhes bya ba'i lan legs so/ / bdag rkyen ni{ bya ba dang bcas par ma nges shing} gnas skabs thams cad du mi sgrib pa'i ngo bor gnas pas de dag las gzhan du med pa'i phyir logs shig tu ma bshad do/ / 'o na 'dus byas dag rkyen bzhi ga las skye'am/ 'on te re re las skye zhe na/

Some say: When entering mindless meditative attainment, there are types of consciousness, such as foundation consciousness, that do not cease, and mental factors are derived from them. Reply: That is illogical, because it would be contradictory for those derived from foundation consciousness to exist in the retinue of other coemergent minds, and even those derived from the seeds of foundation consciousness are its causal condition. It is also illogical to state that feeling and so on do not exist at the same time as the first moment of the mind, because they would then also not exist for later minds, since [the logic] is the same. If the mind were generated in the first moment, then mental factors would also be generated since they are similar in their causes not being incomplete. Therefore the Exposition of Valid Cognition asks: What will prevent a result arising from causes that are not incomplete?[646] Therefore one should understand that simultaneous cause and effect exists. However, with respect to focusing on past and future states, the best response is that they are not objective conditions because [focusing on them] would be focusing on nonexistent states, and whatever is an objective condition exists at the same time as the mind focusing on it. The dominant condition is not explained separately because {there is no certainty that it is associated with action, and} in all circumstances it abides with a nonobscured nature and it is not other than that. Question: Do conditioned states arise from four conditions together or do they arise from each separately?
bzhi yis sems dang sems byung rnams/ / gsum gyis snyoms par 'jug pa gnyis/ / 64 gzhan ni gnyis po dag las skye/ / dbang phyug sogs min rim sogs phyir/ /

Four conditions generate minds and mental factors. Three generate both meditative attainments. Other states arise from both. They do not arise from Īśvara and so on because they arise in sequence. (2:64)

rkyen bzhi po yis ni sems dang sems las byung ba rnams skyed par byed do/{ rgyu'i rkyen ni rgyu lnga ci rigs la sogs/ /} ri bong gi rwa'o/ / nam mkha'i me tog go zhes bya ba'i yid kyang kha cig gis ri bong dang rwa la sogs pa kha yar bar yod pa'i phyir de las skye bar 'dod cing*/ bye brag tu smra ba ri bong gi rwa la sogs pa'i ming dang mtshan ma rdzas su yod pa'i phyir de dag las skye'o zhes 'dod la/ kha cig sems dang sems byung phyin ci ma log pa dag dmigs rkyen las skye'i phyin ci log ni dmigs rkyen las mi skye'o zhes 'dod de de nyid legs so/ / dmigs rkyen ma gtogs pa gsum gyis ni 'du shes med pa dang 'gog pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa gnyis po dag skyed pa yin te/{ rgyu'i rkyen lhan cig 'byung ba dang sa mtshungs pa'i dge ba'i phung po lnga'am bzhi'o/ /} 'di la mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen ni snyoms par 'jug pa'i sems yin no/ / de'i phyir snyoms 'jug 'di gnyis sems kyis mngon par 'du byed pa las skye bas sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can yin gyi sems skye ba la gegs byed pas na mtshungs pa de ma thag pa'i rkyen ni ma yin no/ / dmigs pa'i rkyen las ni mi skye ste/ dmigs par byed pa ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: Four conditions generate minds (citta) and mental factors (caitta). {Causal condition is any of the five causes and so on,} and some assert that because statements such as “a rabbit with horns” and “a flower in the sky” exist, minds arising from them exist because rabbits, horns, and so on exist separately. Vaibhāṣikas assert that minds arise from them because the name and sign of “a rabbit with horns” substantially exist. Some assert: Undistorted minds and mental factors arise from objective conditions. Distorted minds and mental factors do not arise from objective conditions. Reply: This assertion is correct. Three conditions, except for the objective condition, generate both the meditative attainments (samāpatti) of nondiscernment and cessation, since {the causal condition consists of the five or four virtuous coemergent aggregates of equivalent level} and the equivalent immediately preceding condition is the mind of meditative attainment. Therefore these two meditative attainments possess an equivalent immediately preceding mind since they are generated by the mind through current mental application, but they are not equivalent immediately preceding conditions since they stop the generation of minds. They do not arise from an objective condition because they do not focus on objects.

des na bye brag tu smra bas gzugs mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen mi 'dod kyi mtshungs ldan ma yin pa 'ga' zhig la ni mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen 'dod de/ snyoms 'jug gnyis kyang mi ldan pa'i 'du byed mtshungs ldan ma yin pa bems po yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'du shes med pa pa ni sngon ma las kyis 'phangs pas rang gi ngang gis 'jug pa yin gyi sems kyis mngon par 'du byas pas bskyed pa ma yin pa'i phyir de ma thag pa'i rkyen las skye par ma brjod do/ / de'i phyir slob dpon rgyal po'i sras kyis 'du shes med pa ni sems kyis mngon par 'dus ma byas par las kyi mthus skye ba'i phyir bstan bcos las sems kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa can min par mi 'byung ngo zhes pa dang slob dpon gang spel gyis kyang*/ gal te 'du shes med pa pa'ang sems kyi de ma thag can yin na ci'i phyir gsum gyis snyoms par 'jug pa gnyis zhes bshad ce na/ bden mod kyi de ni rnam smin las skyes pa yin pas rang gi ngang gis 'jug pa'i sems kyi mngon par 'du byas pa las ma skyes pas ma brjod do/ / des na 'di ni mdo phyi mar bsdu'o zhes bshad do/ /

Vaibhāṣikas do not assert material form to be an equivalent immediately preceding condition, [188] yet they do assert that some nonconcomitant states are equivalent immediately preceding conditions, because for them both meditative attainments are material form, which is neither a nonassociated formative factor nor concomitant. The being possessing nondiscernment automatically enters that state, since he is established there by past karma. They do not say that it arises from an immediately preceding condition because it is not generated by the mind through current mental application. Therefore Master Jinaputra explains that because the state of nondiscernment arises due to the mind through the force of karma and not due to current mental application, a treatise[647] mentions that it does not occur without an equivalent immediately preceding mind.[648] Also Master Pūrṇavardhana explains: If the state of nondiscernment also possesses an immediately preceding mind, why is it said that “Three generate both meditative attainments” (2:64b)? Indeed it is true that it is not said to arise from the current application of the mind since it is entered automatically, arising from karmic maturation. This is included in the later sūtra.[649]

sems dang sems byung dang snyoms par 'jug pa dag las gzhan ldan pa ma yin pa lhag ma rnams dang gzugs can rnams ni rgyu'i rkyen dang bdag rkyen gnyis po dag las skye ba yin no/ / mtshungs pa de ma thag pa dang dmigs rkyen las ni mi skye ste/ mtshungs ldan ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de lta na snyoms 'jug gnyis kyang {mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen las } mi skye bar 'gyur ro zhe na/ snyoms 'jug sems med du 'dod pa dag la ni skyon 'di yod pa nyid de/ gal te sems kyi mjug thogs su byung ba tsam gyis mtshungs pa de ma thag pa'i rkyen las skye bar 'dod na rig byed ma yin pa dag kyang mtshungs pa de ma thag pa'i rkyen las skye bar 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir rnal 'byor spyod pa pa dag gis snyoms 'jug sems dang bcas par 'dod pa la mtshungs pa de ma thag pa'i rkyen las skye bar rung ngo*/ / de lta na dmigs rkyen las kyang skye bar 'gyur ro zhe na/ dgag gzhi ni de ltar yin mod kyi 'dir ni bkag pa'i ngo bo la brjod la/ de ni dmigs pa med pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na mtshungs pa de ma thag pa'i rkyen las kyang skyes par 'gyur ro zhe na/ de lta mod kyi 'jug pa dang ldan pa mtshungs pa de ma thag pa las skye ba'i phyir de skad du brjod do/ / 'on kyang bye brag tu smra ba ltar na 'byung bzhi la mi ltos par snyoms 'jug gi sbyor sems kyis mngon par 'dus byas pa las 'byung ba'i phyir snyoms 'jug gnyis mtshungs pa de ma thag rkyen las skye bar 'dod de/ mtshungs pa'i don yang rkyen dang rkyen can gnyis sems kyis mngon par 'dus byas par mtshungs pa nyid la 'dod pa'i phyir ro/ /

The remaining nonassociated formative factors other (anya) than minds, mental factors, and meditative attainments, as well as physical states, arise from both causal conditions and dominant conditions. They do not arise from either the equivalent immediately preceding condition or the objective condition because they are not concomitant states. Objection: Thus the two meditative attainments also do not arise {from equivalent immediately preceding conditions}. Reply: This error applies to those who assert mindless meditative attainment because if it is asserted that it arises from an equivalent immediately preceding condition since it merely arises at the conclusion of mind, then even nonindicative form would be generated from an equivalent immediately preceding condition. Yogācāras assert therefore that meditative attainment possesses mind and it can arise from an equivalent immediately preceding condition. Objection: Thus it would also arise from an objective condition. Reply: This indeed constitutes something to be negated and identifies what is to be refuted due to having no focal object. Objection: But it also arises from an equivalent immediately preceding condition. Reply: Indeed, that is so. It arises from an equivalent immediately preceding condition, but possessing [an objective condition] is refuted. Vaibhāṣikas assert that the two meditative attainments arise from equivalent immediately preceding conditions because they are derived from current mental application through the preparatory mind of meditative attainment without relying on the four elements. They assert that “equivalent” means that both the condition and that which is conditioned are equivalent in the current application of mind.

bye brag pa la sogs pa dbang phyug rtag pa gcig pu las 'gro ba 'di dag skye bar 'dod la sogs pas bsdus pa spyod pa la sogs pa bdag rtag pa gcig pu dang*/ grangs can pa gtso bo rtag pa gcig pu dang*/ kha cig gis rdul phran rtag pa dang*/ skyes bu dang dus la sogs pa rtag pa las skye bar 'dod mod kyi 'on kyang de dag las ni 'gro ba 'di dag skyes pa min te/ dus rim gyis 'byung ba'i phyir dang*/ sogs zhes bya ba yul res 'ga' ba dang*/ rdzas res 'ga' ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di ltar dbang phyug rtag pa de 'gro ba 'di skyed byed nyid du rtag tu gnas na ni rdzas thams cad yul thams cad du dus rtag tu 'byung bar 'gyur ba 'di nges pa yin no/ / skyed byed ma yin pa nyid du rtag na ni 'ga' yang gang du yang nam yang mi skye bar 'gyur ro/ / dus dang yul dang rdzas res 'ga' ba yin na ni mi rtag pa dang du ma yin te/ de dag gi mtshan nyid ni de lta bu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te dbang phyug rtag pa gcig pu yin yang de'i 'dod pas 'di ni sngon la skye bar gyur cig /'di ni phyis skye bar gyur cig /'di ni yul 'dir skye'i gzhan du ma yin la/ rdzas 'di skye'i gzhan ni ma yin no zhes 'dun pa'i phyir res 'ga' ba yin no zhe na/ 'o na ni 'di dag dbang phyug las ma skyes par 'gyur te/ 'dod pa mi rtag pa du ma las skye ba'i phyir dang*/ dbang phyug rtag pa gcig pu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dod pa nyid dbang phyug yin na'ang mi rtag pa dang du mar thal ba 'di se na yod do/ / de bzhin du skyes bu dang gtso bo la sogs pa la'ang sbyar bar bya'o/ / rgyu'i rkyen bye brag tu bshad pa

Vaiśeṣikas and so on assert that reincarnating beings arise from a single, permanent Īśvara. “And so on” refers to Mīmāṃsakas, who assert that the self is permanent and single; to Sāṃkhyas, who assert that the supreme principle is permanent and single; [189] and to some who say that particles are permanent and that beings and time and so on are generated from permanent phenomena. Reply: Reincarnating beings do not arise from [Īśvara] because they arise in temporal sequence (krama), and “and so on” refers to intermittent objects and intermittent substance. Thus, if a permanent Īśvara existed eternally as the creator of reincarnating beings, then all objects and all substance would definitely always arise at all times. If he existed eternally as a noncreator, then nothing anywhere would ever be generated. But if time, objects, and substance are intermittent, he would be impermanent and multiple because their characteristics are just that. Objection: Though Īśvara is permanent and single, objects arise earlier or arise later, or some arise in this region not in another, or one particular substance and not another arises through his desire. Therefore they are intermittent. Reply: They are not generated from Īśvara because they are generated from many impermanent desires, and Īśvara is permanent and single. If desire itself were Īśvara, it would follow that he would be impermanent and multiple. This logic should similarly be applied to beings, the self (ātma), and so on.
rgyu'i rkyen{ nam gnyis pa dag las skye ba} bye brag tu bshad pa ni
CAUSAL CONDITION {OR ARISING FROM BOTH}
de'i rgyu 'byung ba rnam pa gnyis/ / 'byung las gyur pa'i rnam pa lnga/ / 65 'byung gyur rnam gsum phan tshun du/ / 'byung ba rnams kyi de rnam gcig /
The primary elements are a cause in two ways. That derived from the elements in five ways. That derived from the elements mutually in three ways. That from the elements in one way. (2:65)

gal te 'byung ba de'i rgyu 'byung ba yin na ni skal mnyam dang lhan cig 'byung ba rnam pa gnyis yin te ris mthun snga mas phyi ma skyed na skal mnyam dang{ gzhan gsum dang tshogs pa gcig pa'i} dus mnyam pa dag ni phan tshun lhan cig 'byung ba yin no/ / 'byung ba dag gis 'byung ba las gyur pa'i gzugs {bdag rkyen byas nas } skyed na byed rgyu'i rgyu kho na rnam pa lnga byed do/ / rnam pa lnga ni 'grel ba las/ skyed phyir rten phyir gnas phyir dang*/ / rton pa'i phyir dang 'phel byed phyir/ / zhes pa dang*/ gang spel gyis de'i tshig rkang pa snga ma gnyis kha bskangs te/ skye dang rjes mthun rten dang ni/ / rgyun mi chad dang 'phel ba las/ / gsungs te/ 'bras bu'i gzugs sngar ma grub pa gsar du skyed pa'i phyir dang*/ slob dpon las slob ma ltar skyes pa'i rgyun rnams rjes su mthun par byed pa'i phyir dang*/ ri mo'i rtsig pa bzhin rgyun gnas pa'i gzhi byed pa'i phyir dang*/ lus kyi kha zas ltar rgyun mi chad pa'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir dang*/ gong nas gong du 'phel bar byed pa'i phyir rim pa bzhin du shes par bya'o/ / de rnams kyang bsdu na ma skyes pa bskyed pa dang*/ skyes zin gnas pa dang*/ gnas pa 'phel bar byed pa'i rgyu gsum du 'gyur ro/ / de ltar na rnam pa lnga pa de dag ni byed rgyu'i bye brag yin pa'i phyir 'byung ba rnams kyis ni 'byung ba las gyur pa'i byed pa'i rgyu byed kyi gzhan ni ma yin te/ skal ba mi mnyam pa dang*/ lhan cig 'byung yang phan tshun rgyu 'bras ma yin pa dang*/ kun 'gro ma yin pa dang*/ mtshungs par mi ldan pa dang*/ 'byung ba dag ni dge mi dger 'gyur ba mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ /

The primary elements (bhūta) are a cause (hetu) of the primary elements in two ways (dvidhā): as homogeneous and coemergent causes. They are homogeneous since earlier states produce later states of the same type, and they are mutually coemergent since {the single collection of the other three primary elements} exists at the same time. The primary elements generate form derived from the elements (bhautika) {through being its dominant condition} in five ways as an active cause alone. The five ways are enunciated in the Autocommentary: Because they generate, because they support, because they abide, because they rely on, and because they increase.[650] Pūrṇavardhana supplements those two lines of that verse by declaring: From arising, compatibility, support, not severing the continuum, and increase.[651] There are five types that should be understood in a series: (1) because [the primary elements] newly generate resultant form that was not previously established; (2) because they activate subsequent continua that arise in the student in the same way as in the teacher; (3) because they act as a basis for the endurance of the continuum, like a wall [on which there is] a drawing; (4) because they are the cause of sustaining the mindstream, like food for the body; and (5) because they act to progressively increase [those states]. In brief, they act as causes in three ways: generating that which has not yet arisen, maintaining that which is already arisen, and increasing that which abides. Thus the primary elements act as active causes of form derived from the elements [190] because these five ways are subsets of active cause. Other states do not do this because they are not homogeneous; though coemergent, they are not reciprocal causes and results [of each other]; they are not omnipresent; they are not concomitant; and it is impossible for those elements to be virtuous or nonvirtuous.

'byung ba las gyur pa'i gzugs{ kyis 'byung gyur} phan tshun du skyed na lhan cig 'byung ba dang skal mnyam dang rnam smin gyi rgyu rnam pa gsum byed do zhes sbyar ro/ / de la lhan cig 'byung ba ni {'byung bzhi tshogs pa gcig las skye bas } bsam gtan dang zag med kyi sdom pa'i spong ba bdun po dag phan tshun yin gyi gzhan {tshogs pa tha dad pas bskyed nas mig sogs dang de'i yul lnga dang so thar sogs } ni ma yin no/ / skal mnyam ni dge ba'am nyon mongs can la sogs pa ris mthun snga mas phyi ma skyed pa'i tshe'o/ / rnam smin gyi rgyu ni rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa dge ba zag bcas dang mi dge ba{ 'i lus ngag gi las} dag gis mtho ris dang ngan song gi dbang po dang bcas pa'i{ mig sogs dang} lus skyed pa lta bu'o/ /

Form derived from the elements mutually (anyonya) generates {[form] derived from the elements} in three ways (tridhā): coemergent cause, homogeneous cause, and the cause of karmic maturation. Coemergent refers to the mutually [coexistent] seven objects of abandonment of the absorption vows and uncontaminated vows, {since they are generated from one collection of four elements}. But other states, {such as the eyes, their five objects, pratimokṣa vows, and so on, which are generated by distinct collections of primary elements,} are not coemergent. Homogeneity refers to the time when earlier virtuous or afflicted states produce later states of the same type. The cause of karmic maturation refers, for instance, to {the physical and verbal karma of} indicative and nonindicative contaminated virtuous and nonvirtuous states that generate a body and sense faculties {such as the eyes} of beings of high rebirth or lower rebirth.
de ma thag rkyen rgyas par ston pa ni
IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING CONDITION
'dod yid dge dang mi dge dang / / bsgribs pa dang ni ma bsgribs pa/ / 66 gzugs dang gzugs med pa dag na/ / mi dge las gzhan zag med gnyis/ /
The desire-realm mental faculty is virtuous, nonvirtuous, obscured, and unobscured. The form and formless realms exclude nonvirtuous minds. Uncontaminated states have two. (2:66)

'dod pa'i khams kyi yid de sems sems byung dang bcas pa ni dge ba dang mi dge ba dang bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa dang ma bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa ste bzhi yin no/ / gzugs kyi khams dang gzugs med pa'i khams dag na ni mi dge ba'i sems las gzhan gsum gsum yod do/ / zag med la ni slob pa dang mi slob pa gnyis yod do/ / de ltar na 'khor 'das kyi sems thams cad rnam pa bcu gnyis su 'dus so/ / de dag gang gi de ma thag tu gang 'byung zhe na/ 'di la ni tshe drug gam brgyad kyi rnam par dbye ba shes par bya ste/ rgyun gyi tshe dang*/ sa mtshungs pa dang*/ snyoms par 'jug pa dang*/ {snyoms 'jug /} las ldang ba dang*/ nying mtshams sbyor ba dang*/ snyoms 'jug nyon mongs can gyis gzir ba'i tshe{ drug las dang po} 'o/ de la rgyun gyi tshe zhes bya ba ni ris 'dra ba rgyun chags su 'byung ba'i dus te/ de ni dge ba las dge ba dang mi dge ba las mi dge ba la sogs pa ris 'dra ba 'byung ba yin no/ /

The desire-realm mental faculty (manas) has four types: minds and mental factors that are virtuous (kuśala), nonvirtuous (akuśala), obscured-neutral (nivṛta), and unobscured-neutral (ānivṛta). The form and formless realms have three types, excluding nonvirtuous (akuśala) minds. Uncontaminated (anāsrava) states have two: learner and nonlearner minds. Thus all saṃsāric and transcendent minds are included in twelve types. Question: Which minds immediately precede which minds? Reply: This should be understood through the classification of six or eight occasions, since there is the occasion of (1) when maintaining that state, (2) when on the same level, (3) when entering meditative attainment, (4) when rising from {meditative attainment}, (5) when linking, and (6) when oppressed by afflicted meditative attainment. When maintaining that state {is the first of those six and} refers to the continuation of a similar-type mind, since it is the continuous occurrence of a similar-type virtuous mind from a virtuous mind, a nonvirtuous mind from a nonvirtuous mind, and so on.

sa mtshungs pa zhes bya ba {gnyis pa } ni{ ris mi mthun kyang} 'dod pa la sogs pa'i 'dra ba ste/ der ni rang gi sa pa'i de ma thag par rang gi sa pa'i sprul sems ma gtogs pa dge ba la sogs pa thams cad 'byung ngo*/ / snyoms par 'jug pa'i tshe{ gsum pa} ni 'og ma'i dge ba sbyor byung las gong ma'i dge ba sbyor byung dang zag med gnyis 'byung ba yin no/ / snyoms 'jug las ldang ba'i tshe{ bzhi pa} ni gong ma'i dge ba sbyor byung dang zag med gnyis kyi mjug thogs su 'og ma'i dge ba 'byung ba ni 'dod pa'i dge ba gnyis ka dang*/ khams gong ma gnyis kyi dge ba sbyor byung kho na 'byung ba nyid du nges so/ /

{The second,} when on the same level, refers to being of similar level, such as the desire-realm level, {even when not of similar type,} because it refers to all virtuous minds and so on that arise immediately preceding it on its level except for the mind of emanation of its level. {The third,} when entering meditative attainment, refers both to virtuous minds of higher levels derived from preparation and to uncontaminated minds [191] arising from virtuous minds of lower levels derived from preparation. {The fourth,} when rising from meditative attainment, refers to virtuous minds of lower levels arising at the conclusion of virtuous minds of higher levels derived from both preparation and uncontaminated minds. It is certain that only the two desire-realm virtuous minds, and virtuous minds of both higher realms derived from preparation, arise.[653]

sprul pa la 'jug pa'i tshe ni dag dang rang las de las gnyis zhes 'byung bas gzugs kyi dge ba sbyor byung gi rjes su 'dod pa'i sprul sems dang gzugs kyi sprul sems lung ma bstan gnyis kho na 'byung ngo*/ / sprul pa las ldang ba'i tshe ni sems gnyis po de'i mjug thogs su gzugs kyi dge ba sbyor byung 'gyur te/ sprul pa las langs nas bsam gtan gyi sems mngon du byed pa'i phyir ro/ / sprul pa las 'jug pa ni snyoms 'jug las ldang ba dang*/ sprul pa las ldang ba ni snyoms par 'jug pa yin pa'i phyir tshe logs su ma bshad do zhes 'dod mod kyi logs su byas te tshe brgyad du byas na 'jug pa bde bar snang ngo*/

(7) When entering emanation refers both to desire-realm neutral minds of emanation and to form-realm minds of emanation that arise after form-realm virtuous minds derived from preparation alone, as the Abhidharmakośa mentions, “That arises from pure absorption, and itself. Two arise from that.” (7:50cd) (8) When rising from emanation refers to form-realm virtuous minds derived from preparation arising at the conclusion of those two minds because having arisen from emanation, the mind of absorption manifests. Because entering emanation is rising from meditative attainment and rising from emanation is entering meditative attainment, indeed they are not explained as separate occasions. But if explained separately, eight occasions may be posited.

{Moreover, affliction of higher and lower levels that arise from the virtuous mind follows the virtuous minds obtained from birth. The form-realm virtuous mind that arises from the desire-realm neutral mind follows the desire-realm mind of emanation alone. Entry to uncontaminated states is through three mental attentions: (1) mental attention engaging the specific and generic characteristics of phenomena, (2) mental attention engaging the sixteen general aspects such as impermanence, and (3) mental attention engaging liberation, totality, subjugation, immeasurable repulsiveness, and so on. Since they are not minds engaging perfect reality, they are mental attentions that are resolute attention, and any of these three enter and rise from uncontaminated states. The mind that rises having obtained the state of an arhat dependent on unrestricted access concentration belongs either to just that level due to familiarity or to the desire-realm level. That which obtains [the state of an arhat] in dependence on [the base of] nothingness belongs to just that level. Or if [the state of an arhat] has arisen in the summit of existence, it rises on the level of the summit of existence. Minds that arise on the other remaining levels solely belong to their own level. Those of other levels must be established by preparation alone, and those of their own level rise due to themselves. Mental attention has three aspects in the desire realm: derived from hearing, derived from contemplation, and obtained from birth. It has three aspects in the form realm: derived from hearing, derived from meditation, and obtained from birth. It has two aspects in the formless realm: derived from meditation and obtained from birth. From among those, the ārya path, because it relies on preparation, manifests after five of these minds, leaving off the three obtained from birth. Since it is clear [and unobstructed], the desire-realm virtuous mind obtained from birth also manifests at the conclusion of the path. It acts as a mind arising from the first and second absorptions, and the mind oppressed by affliction also exists in dependence on it. Those obtained from birth in the two higher realms are not similar since they are not clear.}

{The fifth,} when linking, refers to the intermediate existence that links death existence {to the next} birth existence. Further, the mind of death is any virtuous mind of its own level obtained from birth, or nonvirtuous mind, or obscured-neutral mind, or mind arisen from karmic maturation, or the mind governing demeanor, except for both uncontaminated minds, virtuous minds derived from preparation, and the minds governing creativity and emanation. The mind of birth is either an obscured-neutral mind or a nonvirtuous mind because the level where one is born is the afflicted mind of that level. As it is said, “Birth existence is afflicted” (3:38a) and “At death any afflicted state can arise after pure [meditative attainment]” (8:16c). [192] Further, the mind of death of one taking birth from a lower to a higher level is either a virtuous mind obtained from birth, an unobscured-neutral mind arisen from [karmic] maturation, or the mind governing demeanor. The mind of birth is an obscured-neutral mind alone because it is impossible for a higher mind to arise from a lower afflicted mind and there are no nonvirtuous minds in higher realms. As it is said, “Higher states do not arise from afflicted states” (8:16d). The mind of death of one who takes birth in a lower level from a higher level is either a virtuous mind obtained from birth, an obscured or unobscured mind arisen from [karmic] maturation, or the mind governing demeanor. If one is born in the desire realm, the mind of birth is either a nonvirtuous mind or an obscured mind. If born in the higher realms, it is an obscured mind alone. If one is born in one’s own level from one’s own level, the mind of death is any mind existing on one’s own level except for a virtuous mind derived from preparation, the mind governing emanation, or the mind governing creativity. Indeed, the mind of birth is an afflicted nonvirtuous mind or obscured-neutral mind in the desire realm and an obscured mind alone in the higher realms. But in this context it has no specific requirements. Both uncontaminated minds are minds neither of birth nor of death because they are the antidotes to existence.

Keep the significance of this in mind, as which mind occurs at the conclusion of which mind is now presented.
Desire-realm minds and form-realm minds
DESIRE-REALM MINDS

Nine minds arise from desire-realm virtuous mind. It is derived from eight alone. Nonvirtuous minds arise from ten. Four arise from it. So too, an obscured mind. (2:67)

'dod pa'i sems dge ba las ni rjes thogs su sems dgu 'byung ste/ rgyun gyi tshe{ 'dod pa'i dge ba} dang sa mtshungs pa'i tshe ni{ zla bo gzhan gsum ste} rang gi sa pa bzhi 'byung la/ snyoms par 'jug pa'i tshe 'dod pa'i dge ba sbyor byung las gzugs kyi dge ba sbyor byung dang*/ zag med gnyis dang*/{ gzugs dge sbyor byung ni dang po'i nyer bsdogs dang dngos gzhi'o zhes rgyal sras zer/ kha cig thod rgal tshe gnyis pa la sogs kyang 'byung zhes so/ / zag med gnyis ni sngar thob zin 'byung gi gsar ba ma 'byung ngo*/} nying mtshams sbyor ba'i tshe 'dod pa'i dge ba skyes thob las khams gong ma gnyis kyi bsgribs pa gnyis so/ /

Nine minds (citta) subsequently arise from the desire-realm virtuous mind (śubhacitta) since four minds arise on its level: when maintaining that state, {(1) the desire-realm virtuous mind arises,} and when on the same level, {(2–4) its other three companions arise}. When entering meditative attainment, (5) a form-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation arises, and (6–7) both uncontaminated minds arise from a desire-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation. {Jinaputra observes that the form-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation is access concentration and the actual basis of the first absorption. Some say: Alternating meditation[656] arises in the second life and so on. The two uncontaminated states arise through previous obtainment; they do not newly arise.} When linking, (8–9) both obscured states of both higher realms arise from a desire-realm virtuous mind obtained from birth.

gal te snyoms par 'jug pa'i tshe 'dod pa'i dge ba'i rjes su gzugs med kyi dge ba'ang 'byung ba ma yin nam de lta na bcu 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhe na/ 'dod pa'i dge ba las ni gzugs med la snyoms par mi 'jug ste/ {rten la sogs pa/ } ring ba nyid bzhis ring ba'i phyir ro/ / de la rten ring ba ni gzugs med pa'i rten gyis 'dod pa'i sprul sems la sogs pa gang yang mngon du mi byed pas snyoms 'jug gi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa'i rkyen gyi rten du mi srid pa'i phyir ro/{ yang na 'dod pa'i sems ni gzugs med kyi mtshungs pa de ma thag pa'i rkyen du mi srid pas rten ring ba'o/ /} rnam pa ring ba ni 'dod pa la rags pa dang de la zhi ba'i rnam par mi lta ba'i phyir ro/ / dmigs pa ring ba ni{ des 'og sa la dmigs mi nus pas} des 'dod pa la mi dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ / gnyen pos ring ba nyid ni 'dod pa'i gnyen po des mi byed pa'i phyir{ te de'i 'dod pa yul min pas su nang byung mi nus pa'i phyir} ro/ / de'i phyir gzugs kyi sems kyis 'dod pa'i sprul sems mngon du byed pas gzugs kyi sems la brten pa dang*/ de la rags pa dang gzugs med la zhi ba'i rnam par lta ba dang*/ gzugs la dmigs pa dang*/ des gzugs kyi nyon mongs pa'i gnyen po byed pa'i phyir 'dod pa'i dge bas kun nas bslang nas gzugs med la snyoms par 'jug na'ang par du bsam gtan gyi sems mngon du byed pa la ltos pa'i phyir ro/ / des na gzugs med kyi dge ba dang*/ ma bsgribs lung ma bstan dang*/ gzugs kyi ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gsum dang 'dod pa'i dge ba la ni rgyu 'bras su gyur pa'i tshe drug po de dag mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ /

Question: When entering meditative attainment, doesn’t a formless-realm virtuous mind [193] arise after desire-realm virtuous mind? If so, ten occur. Reply: One does not enter meditative attainment in the formless realm from a desire-realm virtuous mind because those minds are distant through the four types of distance {such as support}. (1) Distant in terms of support means that formless-realm beings will never manifest a desire-realm emanating mind and so on, because it is impossible for their minds to act as the equivalent immediately preceding condition of such meditative attainment.[657] {Again, they are distant since it is impossible for a desire-realm mind to be the equivalent immediately preceding condition of a formless-realm mind.} (2) Distant in terms of aspect means that [a formless-realm mind] does not view the desire realm as coarse and the formless realm as refined. (3) Distant in terms of focus means that [a formless-realm mind] does not focus on the desire-realm level {since it cannot focus on lower levels}. (4) Distant in terms of antidote means that [a formless-realm mind] does not act as an antidote to the desire realm {because it cannot find fault with the desire realm, since [the desire realm] is not its object.} Therefore it is dependent on a form-realm mind, since a form-realm mind manifests the desire-realm emanation mind. It views the desire realm as coarse and the formless realm as refined. It focuses on the form realm. And because it acts as the antidote to form-realm affliction, even though it enters meditative attainment on the formless realm motivated by desire-realm virtue, in between it relies on manifesting absorption minds. Therefore six occasions are impossible for three minds: (1) formless-realm virtuous mind, (2) formless-realm unobscured-neutral mind, and (3) form-realm unobscured-neutral mind, in terms of acting as the cause or result of desire-realm virtuous mind.

'dod pa'i dge ba'i sems de ni sems brgyad po kho na las 'byung ste/ rgyun dang sa mtshungs pa'i tshe rang gi sa pa bzhi dang*/ snyoms 'jug las ldang ba na dge ba skyes thob la snyoms par 'jug pa mi srid pas gzugs kyi dge ba sbyor byung dang*/ zag med gnyis dang*/ snyoms 'jug nyon mongs can gyis gzir ba'i tshe gzugs kyis bsgribs pa'i sems las so/{ de yang gong ma'i nyon mongs can las 'og ma'i dge ba bzang bas so/ /} de yang 'dod pa'i dge ba skyes thob kyang gsal ba'i phyir gzugs kyi sbyor byung dang zag med gnyis dang snyoms 'jug nyon mongs can gyi ldang sems su 'gyur ba srid pas bzhi po de dag las 'dod pa'i dge ba skyes thob dang sbyor byung gnyis ka 'byung ngo*/ / 'dir sa mtshungs pa'i tshe 'dod pa'i dge ba las ma bsgribs pa 'byung bar bshad pa ni sprul sems las gzhan rnams 'byung ba yin gyi sprul sems ni dag dang rang las de las gnyis zhes 'byung bas rang nyid dang gzugs kyi dge ba sbyor byung kho na las 'byung gi 'dod pa'i dge ba la sogs pa'i sems rnams las ni mi 'byung ngo*/ / de bzhin du 'og ma rnams su rgyun dang sa mtshungs pa'i tshe'i skabs su'ang shes par bya'o/ / gzhan dag mi 'byung ba ni tshe drug gi rnam par bzhag pa mi 'thad pa'i phyir ro/ /

A desire-realm virtuous mind is derived from eight minds alone. When maintaining that state and when on the same level, it arises from (1–4) the four minds of its level. When rising from meditative attainment, it arises from (5) a form-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation, since it is impossible to enter meditative attainment with a virtuous mind obtained from birth, and from (6–7) the two uncontaminated minds. When oppressed by afflicted meditative attainment, it arises from (8) form-realm obscured mind. {Further, a lower virtuous mind derived from a higher afflicted mind is pure}. Moreover, because a desire-realm virtuous mind obtained from birth is clear, it is possible that it is a mind that rises from (1) a form-realm mind obtained by preparation, (2–3) the two uncontaminated minds, and (4) the mind of afflicted meditative attainment. Therefore both desire-realm virtuous minds that are obtained from birth and derived from preparation occur from these four. Here, when on the same level, the explanation that an unobscured mind arises from a desire-realm virtuous mind refers to the occurrence of minds other than emanation mind. A mind of emanation is only derived from itself and a form-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation, since it is said, “That arises from pure absorption and itself. Two arise from that” (7:50cd), and it is not derived from a desire-realm virtuous mind and so on. So too, that applies to lower levels when maintaining that state and when on the same level. Others do not occur because it is untenable to posit six occasions for them.

'dod pa'i mi dge ba'i sems ni zag med gnyis ma gtogs pa bcu po dag las 'byung ste/{ gong ma gnyis kyi sems drug po gang las shi yang 'dod par mtshams sbyor ba mi 'gal bas so de yang*/} rgyun dang sa mtshungs pa'i tshe sprul sems ma gtogs pa rang gi sa pa bzhi dang*/ nying mtshams sbyor ba'i tshe khams gong ma gnyis nas shi 'phos nas 'dir skye ba na gzugs kyi dge ba sbyor byung dang sprul sems dang gzugs med kyi dge ba sbyor byung ma gtogs pa la 'chi sems srid pas de dag gi sems gsum gsum gyi rjes su 'jug pa'i phyir ro/ / zag med gnyis dang ni tshe drug mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dod pa'i mi dge ba'i sems de las ni{ rang gi sa pa} bzhi{ kho na} 'byung ste rgyun dang sa mtshungs pa na sprul sems ma gtogs pa rang gi sa pa dag go{ mi dge ba ni sa gong ma'i dge ba'i sbyor bar mi srid la/de ma spangs par sa gong ma'i skye ba'i sems kyang mi 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ gzhan yang*/} gong ma'i sems drug dang zag med gnyis ni mi 'byung ste/ mi dge ba snyoms par 'jug sems ma yin pa dang*/ mi dge ba las gong mar nying mtshams sbyor ba mi srid pa dang*/ rgyun mi gcig pa dang*/ sa mi mtshungs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dod pa'i bsgribs la lung ma bstan gyi sems kyang ji ltar 'dod pa'i mi dge ba'i sems sems bcu'i rjes su 'byung zhing*/ de las bzhi 'byung bar bshad pa de bzhin du sems bcu'i rjes su 'byung zhing*/ de las bzhi 'byung bar shes par bya'o/ /

Desire-realm nonvirtuous (akuśala) [194] minds arise from ten minds, excluding the two uncontaminated minds, {since it is not contradictory that any of the six minds that occur at death in the two higher realms link with a desire-realm mind. Further,} when maintaining that state and when on the same level, it arises from (1–4) the four minds of its own level except for the emanating mind. When linking, through having died from the two higher realms and taking birth in this realm, a desire-realm nonvirtuous mind follows (5–10) three minds each of the two higher realms, since all minds of death are possible except for a form-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation, a mind of emanation, and a formless-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation. It is impossible for a desire-realm nonvirtuous mind to arise from the two uncontaminated minds on any of the six occasions. Four {of its level alone} arise from a desire-realm nonvirtuous mind because when maintaining that state and when on the same level, (1–4) the four of its level arise from it except for emanation mind. {It is impossible for nonvirtuous minds to prepare for higher virtuous minds, and even the mind of birth in higher realms does not occur due to not abandoning nonvirtuous minds. Further,} the six higher-realm minds and both uncontaminated minds do not arise from it, because nonvirtuous minds are not minds that enter meditative attainment, it is impossible for nonvirtuous minds to link with higher-realm minds, they are not of the same continuum, and they are not of the same level. Just as a desire-realm nonvirtuous mind is explained to arise after ten minds and four arise from it, so too, a desire-realm obscured-neutral mind arises after ten minds and four arise from it.
ma bsgribs pa ni lnga dag las/ / de las mjug thogs sems bdun no/ / 68 gzugs na dge las bcu gcig go/ / de ni dgu yi mjug thogs su/ /
An unobscured mind is derived from five. Seven minds arise from it at its conclusion. Eleven arise from a virtuous mind in the form realm. It arises at the conclusion of nine. (2:68)

'dod pa'i ma bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa'i sems ni sems lnga dag las 'byung ste/ rgyun dang sa mtshungs pa na rang gi sa pa bzhi dang*/ sprul pa la 'jug pa'i tshe 'dod pa'i sprul sems gzugs kyi dge ba sbyor byung las 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / 'dod pa'i ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gyi sems de las ni mjug thogs su sems{ lnga po de nyid dang gong ma gnyis kyi bsgribs pa gnyis te} bdun 'byung ba yin no/ / 'di ltar rgyun dang sa mtshungs pa na rang gi sa pa bzhi dang sprul pa las ldang ba na bsam gtan la ma zhugs par sprul sems las ldang ba med pas gzugs kyi dge ba sbyor byung ra dang*/ 'dod pa nas khams gong ma gnyis su nying mtshams sbyor ba na 'di dag la gnas pa la 'chi ba dang shi nas gong du skye ba srid pas 'dod pa'i rnam smin skyes dang spyod lam pa gnyis las khams gong ma de dag gi bsgribs pa gnyis 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

A desire-realm unobscured-neutral mind is derived from five minds because when maintaining that state or when on the same level, (1–4) the four of its own level arise from it, and when entering emanation, the mind of desire-realm emanation is derived from (5) a form-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation. Seven minds, {including the former five and obscured minds of both higher levels,} arise from a desire-realm unobscured-neutral mind at its conclusion (anantara). Thus, when maintaining that state or when on the same level, (1–4) the four minds of its level arise from it, and when arising from emanation, (5) a form-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation arises from it, since one cannot rise from a mind of emanation without entering absorption. When linking at death to both the higher realms from the desire realm, (6–7) both the obscured minds of those higher realms arise from both the desire-realm mind arisen from karmic maturation and from the mind governing demeanor, since it is possible to die there and, having died, take rebirth in higher realms.
FORM-REALM MINDS

gzugs na spyod pa'i sems dge ba las ni{ gzugs med kyi ma bsgribs lung ma bstan ma gtogs pa} sems bcu gcig 'byung ste/ rgyun dang sa mtshungs pa na dge ba sbyor byung las ma bsgribs pa gsum ga dang*/ skyes thob las sprul sems las gzhan gnyis dang*/ bsgribs pa ni dge ba gnyis ka las 'byung bas rang gi sa pa gsum dang*/ snyoms 'jug las ldang ba na gzugs kyi sbyor byung las 'dod pa'i dge ba gnyis ka dang*/ sprul pa la 'jug pa na gzugs kyi sbyor byung las 'dod pa'i ma bsgribs lung ma bstan sprul sems kho na dang*/ nyid mtshams sbyor ba na gzugs kyi skyes thob las 'dod pa'i mi dge ba dang bsgribs pa gnyis dang*/ gzugs kyi skyes thob las gzugs med kyi bsgribs pa dang*/ snyoms par 'jug pa na gzugs kyi sbyor byung kho na las gzugs med kyi dge ba sbyor byung dang zag med dag 'byung ba'i phyir ro*/ / gzugs med kyi ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gcig pu ni 'byung ba med de/ de dang tshe drug gi rnam par bzhag pa med pa'i phyir ro/ /

Eleven minds {except for formless unobscured-neutral mind} arise from the virtuous (śubha) mind active in the form realm. When maintaining that state and when on the same level, (1–3) the three [minds] of its [own] level arise from it, since three unobscured minds arise from a virtuous mind derived from preparation, the remaining two form-realm minds arise from the mind governing emanation obtained from birth, and an obscured mind arises from both virtuous minds. When rising from meditative attainment, (4) two desire-realm virtuous minds arise from form-realm minds derived from preparation. When entering emanation, (5) one desire-realm unobscured-neutral mind alone arises from a form-realm mind [195] derived from preparation. When linking at death, (6–7) both desire-realm nonvirtuous and obscured minds arise from the form-realm mind derived from preparation, and (8) a formless-realm obscured mind arises from a form-realm mind obtained from birth. When entering meditative attainment, (9) a formless-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation and (10–11) uncontaminated minds arise from a form-realm mind derived from preparation alone. A formless-realm unobscured-neutral mind alone does not occur because it does not arise on the six occasions.

gzugs kyi sems dge ba de ni{ gzugs med kyi ma bsgribs pa de dang 'dod pa'i nyon mongs can gnyis ma gtogs pa} sems dgu'i mjug thogs su 'byung ste/ rgyun dang sa mtshungs pa na{ dge ba} sbyor byung ni sprul sems kho na las 'byung la/ skyes thob ni gzhan{ rnam smin dang spyod lam pa} gnyis las 'byung bas rang gi gsum dang*/ snyoms par 'jug pa na 'dod pa'i dge ba sbyor byung las gzugs kyi'ang sbyor byung kho na dang*/ sprul pa las ldang ba na 'dod pa'i ma bsgribs lung ma bstan sprul sems las gzugs kyi sbyor byung dang snyoms 'jug las ldang ba na gzugs med kyi dge ba sbyor byung{ las} dang*/ zag med gnyis las {gzugs dge } sbyor byung kho na dang*/{ gzugs med kyi/} snyoms 'jug nyon mongs can gyis gzir ba na gzugs med kyis bsgribs pa'i rjes su gzugs kyi sbyor byung kho na 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / 'dod pa'i mi dge ba dang*/ bsgribs pa dang gzugs med kyi ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gsum las ni mi 'byung ste/ de dag dang tshe drug tu rnam par bzhag pa mi 'thad pa'i phyir ro/ /

A form-realm virtuous mind arises at the conclusion (anantara) of nine minds, {excluding the formless-realm unobscured minds and both desire-realm afflicted minds.} When maintaining that state and when on the same level, it arises from (1–3) the three of its level, since {a virtuous} mind derived from preparation arises from a mind of emanation alone, and the mind obtained from birth arises from both {karmic maturation and the mind governing demeanor}. When entering meditative attainment, also a form-realm mind derived from preparation arises from (4) a desire-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation alone. When rising from emanation, a form-realm mind derived from preparation arises from (5) a desire-realm unobscured-neutral mind. Also, when rising from meditative attainment, {a form-realm virtuous} mind derived from preparation arises only {from} (6) a formless-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation and from (7–8) both uncontaminated minds. When oppressed by afflicted {formless-realm} meditative attainment, a form-realm mind derived from preparation arises only after (9) a formless-realm obscured mind. It does not arise from three minds — namely, desire-realm nonvirtuous and [desire-realm] obscured minds, or from a formless-realm unobscured-neutral mind — because these six occasions do not occur for them.

bsgribs pa brgyad las de las drug / ma bsgribs pa ni gsum las so/ / 69 de las drug ste gzugs med pa'ang / / de yi tshul lo dge ba las/ / sems dgu dag go de drug go / bsgribs pa las bdun de de bzhin/ / 70 slob pa bzhi las de las lnga/ / mi slob pa ni lnga las so/ /

An obscured mind from eight, from it six. An unobscured mind from three. Six from it. Also formless-realm mind in that way. Nine minds arise (2:69) from virtuous mind. It after six. Seven from an obscured mind. So too. A learner from four. Five from it. A nonlearner mind from five. (2:70)

gzugs na spyod pa'i bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa'i sems ni sems {'dod pa'i nyon mongs can gnyis zag med gnyis ma gtogs pa/ } brgyad las 'byung ste/ {de yang 'dod pa'i nyon mngos can shi ba gong du mi skye la/ nyon mongs can gyi zag med las ldang ba mi srid pas so de la/ } rgyun dang sa mtshungs pa na sprul sems ma gtogs pa rang gi sa pa gsum dang*/ nying mtshams sbyor ba na 'dod pa'i dge ba skyes thob dang*/ ma bsgribs lung ma bstan spyod lam pa dang rnam smin skyes gnyis dang*/ gzugs med kyi sa pa dge ba sbyor byung ma gtogs pa{ 'i 'chi sems} gsum gyi rjes su 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / gzhan 'dod pa'i nyon mongs can gnyis dang zag med gnyis las mi 'byung ba ni snga ma bzhin no/ / gzugs kyi bsgribs la lung ma bstan gyi sems de las ni sems{ rang gi gsum 'dod pa'i dang po gsum dang} drug 'byung ste/ rgyun dang sa mtshungs pa na sprul sems ma gtogs pa rnams 'byung bas rang gi sa pa gsum dang*/ nying mtshams sbyor ba na 'dod pa'i mi dge ba dang bsgribs pa dang*/ snyoms 'jug nyon mongs can gyis gzir ba na 'dod pa'i dge ba gnyis ka 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / gzhan dag mi 'byung ba ni snga ma bzhin no/ /

An obscured (nivṛta) neutral mind active in the form realm is derived from eight, {except for both desire-realm afflicted minds and both uncontaminated minds. Further, a desire-realm afflicted mind is not generated after death since it is impossible for afflicted minds to arise from an uncontaminated mind. Regarding that,} when maintaining that state and when on the same level, (1–3) the three of one’s own level arise, apart from the emanation mind. When linking at death, it arises after (4) a desire-realm virtuous mind obtained from birth, (5) both unobscured-neutral minds — the mind governing demeanor and the mind arising from karmic maturation, and (6–8) the three {minds of death} of the formless-realm level, leaving off a virtuous mind derived from preparation. It is similar to the previous instance since it does not arise from desire-realm afflicted minds and both uncontaminated minds. Six minds arise — {namely, three of one’s own level and the first three of the desire-realm level} — from an obscured-neutral mind of the form realm. When maintaining that state and when on the same level, (1–3) the three of its own level arise from it, since all except for a mind of emanation arise. When linking at death, (4) a desire-realm nonvirtuous mind and (5) an obscured mind arise from it. When oppressed by afflicted meditative attainment, (6) both desire-realm virtuous minds arise from it. That the other minds do not arise is similar to the prior instance.

gzugs na spyod pa'i ma bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa ni rgyun gyi tshe sprul sems ni rang nyid las 'byung la/ spyod lam pa dang rnam smin skyes ni sprul sems ma gtogs pa phan tshun dang*/ sa mtshungs pa na dge ba sbyor byung la ma bsgribs pa gsum ga dang*/ skyes thob dang bsgribs pa las ni sprul sems las gzhan gnyis po 'byung bas na rang gi sa pa gsum las 'byung gi gzhan dag las ni mi 'byung ste/ tshe drug gam brgyad du rnam par bzhag pa mi 'thad pa'i phyir ro/ / gzugs kyi ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gyi sems de las ni{ rang gi sa pa gsum 'dod pa dang gzugs med kyi nyon mongs can gsum dang} sems rnam pa drug 'byung ste/ rgyun gyi tshe sprul sems rang nyid las dang*/ spyod lam pa dang rnam smin skyes phan tshun du 'byung ba dang*/ sa mtshungs pa na rang gi sa pa gsum dang*/ nying mtshams sbyor ba na gzugs kyi spyod lam pa dang rnam smin skyes gnyis las 'dod pa'i mi dge ba dang bsgribs pa dang*/ gzugs med pa'i bsgribs pa'o/ / gzhan dag mi 'byung ba ni snga ma bzhin no/ /

An unobscured (anivṛta)-neutral mind active in the form realm arises from (1–3) the three minds of its level. When maintaining that state, it arises from the emanating mind itself, [196] and the mind governing demeanor and the mind derived from karmic maturation arise together without the emanating mind. When on the same level, it arises from three unobscured minds derived from virtuous preparation, and it arises from the two minds different from the emanating mind, which are obtained from birth and the obscured mind. It does not arise from other minds because it is untenable that it arises from them on the six or eight occasions. Six types of mind — {three minds of one’s own level and three afflicted desire-realm and formless-realm minds} — arise from a form-realm unobscured-neutral mind. When maintaining that state, (1) the emanating mind arises from its own continuum, and the mind governing demeanor and the mind derived from karmic maturation arise together. When on the same level, (2–3) the three of its own level arise from it. When linking at death, (4) desire-realm nonvirtuous mind, (5) obscured mind, and (6) a formless-realm obscured mind arise from both the form-realm mind of demeanor and the mind arising from karmic maturation. That other minds do not occur is similar to the previous.
Formless-realm minds and uncontaminated minds
FORMLESS MINDS

ji ltar gzugs kyi ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gsum las 'byung zhing*/ de las drug 'byung bar bshad pa ltar gzugs med pa'i ma bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa'ang de'i tshul du shes par bya ste/ rang nyid ni rgyun dang sa mtshungs pa'i tshe rang gi sa pa gsum kho na las 'byung la/ de las ni nying mtshams sbyor ba na rnam smin skyes las 'dod pa'i nyon mongs can gnyis dang*/ gzugs kyi bsgribs pa dang*/ rgyun gyi tshe rnam smin skyes rang nyid dang*/ sa mtshungs pa na dge ba skyes thob kho na dang bsgribs pa 'byung bas rang gi sa pa gsum ste drug kho na 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

Just as [form-realm minds] are explained to arise from the three form-realm unobscured-neutral minds and six arise from it, so also formless-realm unobscured-neutral minds should be understood in that way. Therefore, when maintaining that state or when on the same level, it arises from (1–3) the three of its own level. When linking at death, (1–2) two afflicted desire-realm minds derived from maturation, and (3) a form-realm obscured mind arise from it. When maintaining that state, (4) the mind derived from [karmic] maturation arises from it. When on the same level, only (5) a virtuous mind obtained from birth and (6) an obscured mind arise from it.

gzugs med pa'i dge ba'i sems las ni{ 'dod pa'i dge ba dang 'dod gzugs kyi ma bsgribs pa gnyis por bas} sems dgu dag 'byung ste/ rgyun gyi tshe dge ba gnyis ka phan tshun dang*/ sa mtshungs pa na dge ba gnyis ka las bsgribs ma bsgribs gnyis ka 'byung bas rang gi sa pa gsum dang*/ snyoms par 'jug pa na sbyor byung kho na las zag med gnyis dang*/{ zag med slob pa ni sgom lam mo/} snyoms 'jug las ldang ba na gzugs med kyi sbyor byung kho na las gzugs kyi dge ba sbyor byung kho na dang*/ nying mtshams sbyor ba na gzugs med kyi dge ba skyes thob kho na las 'dod pa'i nyon mongs can gnyis dang*/ gzugs kyi bsgribs pa 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / gzugs med pa'i dag pa'i sems de ni{ rang sa gsum gzugs dge zag med gnyis te} sems drug gi rjes su 'byung ste/ rgyun gyi tshe dge ba gnyis phan tshun dang*/ sa mtshungs pa na bsgribs pa las dge ba gnyis ka dang*/ ma bsgribs pa rnam smin skyes las dge ba skyes thob kho na 'byung bas rang gi sa pa gsum dang*/ snyoms par 'jug pa na gzugs kyi dge ba sbyor byung kho na las gzugs med kyi'ang sbyor byung kho na dang*/ snyoms 'jug las ldang ba na zag med gnyis kyi rjes su gzugs med kyi sbyor byung kho na 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

Nine minds — {namely, desire-realm virtuous [minds], both desire-realm and form-realm unobscured minds} — arise from formless-realm virtuous (śubha) mind. Three arise from it on its own level, since when maintaining that state, (1) both virtuous minds arise together. When on the same level, (2–3) both obscured and unobscured minds arise from both virtuous minds. When entering meditative attainment, (4–5) two uncontaminated minds derived from preparation alone arise from it, {and an uncontaminated learner mind is the path of meditation}. When rising from meditative attainment, (6) a form-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation alone arises from a formless-realm mind derived from preparation. When linking at death, (7–8) two afflicted desire-realm minds and (9) a form-realm obscured mind arise from formless-realm virtuous minds obtained from birth alone. A formless-realm virtuous mind arises after six minds: {the three of one’s own level, a form-realm virtuous mind, and the two uncontaminated minds}. The three of its level arise from it since when maintaining that state (1) both virtuous minds arise together, and when on the same level, (2) both virtuous minds arise from obscured mind, and (3) a virtuous mind derived from preparation alone arises from unobscured minds derived from karmic maturation. When entering meditative attainment, a formless-realm mind derived from preparation alone arises from (4) a form-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation alone. When arising from meditative attainment, a formless-realm mind derived from preparation alone arises after (5–6) both uncontaminated minds. [197]

gzugs med pa'i bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa'i sems las ni{ rang sa gsum 'og gi nyon mongs can gsum dge ba sbyor byung ste} sems bdun 'byung ste/ rgyun dang sa mtshungs pa na rang gi sa pa gsum dang*/ nying mtshams sbyor ba na gzugs kyi bsgribs pa dang*/ 'dod pa'i nyon mongs can gnyis dang*/ snyoms 'jug nyon mongs can gyis gzir ba na gzugs kyi dge ba sbyor byung kho na 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / ji ltar gzugs med pa'i bsgribs pa las bdun 'byung ba ltar bsgribs pa de yang de bzhin du{ 'og ma gnyis kyi nyon mongs can gsum dang zag med gnyis por ba} bdun las 'byung ste/ rgyun dang sa mtshungs pa na rang gi sa pa gsum dang*/ nying mtshams sbyor ba na gzugs kyi dge ba skyes thob dang*/ 'dod pa'i dge ba skyes thob dang*/ 'dod gzugs kyi ma bsgribs lung ma bstan rnam smin skyes dang spyod lam pa kho na'i rjes su 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

Seven minds arise — {three of one’s level, three afflicted minds of lower level, and virtuous mind derived from preparation} — from a formless-realm obscured neutral mind, because when maintaining that state and when on the same level, (1–3) the three of one’s level arise. When linking at death, (4) a form-realm obscured mind and (5–6) both desire-realm afflicted minds arise. When oppressed by afflicted meditative attainment, (7) a form-realm virtuous mind derived from preparation alone arises. Just as seven arise from a formless-realm obscured mind, so too an obscured mind arises from seven: {three afflicted minds of both lower levels and both noncontaminated minds}. When maintaining that state and when on the same level, it arises from (1–3) the three of its level. When linking at death, it arises from (4) a form-realm virtuous mind obtained from birth, (5) a desire-realm virtuous mind obtained from birth, [and both] (6) a desire-realm [unobscured-neutral mind] and (7) a form-realm unobscured-neutral mind derived from [karmic] maturation and the mind governing demeanor.
UNCONTAMINATED MINDS

slob pa'i sems ni bzhi las 'byung ste/ snyoms par 'jug pa'i tshe khams gsum gyi dge ba sbyor byung gsum po kho na dang*/ rgyun gyi tshe slob pa rang gi mjug thogs su slob pa rang nyid 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / slob pa'i sems de las ni lnga 'byung ste/ snyoms 'jug las ldang ba na 'dod pa'i skyes thob kyang gsal bas skyes thob dang sbyor byung gnyis ka 'byung la/ khams gong ma gnyis kyi skyes thob ni mi gsal ba'i phyir ldang sems ma yin pas sbyor byung gnyis po kho na 'byung bas na khams gsum gyi dge ba gsum dang*/ rgyun gyi tshe slob pa dang nyid dang*/ snyoms par 'jug pa'i tshe slob pa rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin gyi mjug thogs su mi slob pa zad shes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

A learner (śaikṣa) mind arises from four because when entering meditative attainment, it arises from (1–3) the three virtuous minds derived from preparation of the three realms alone. When maintaining that state, (4) a learner mind itself arises at the conclusion of its own continuum. Five arise from a learner mind because when arising from meditative attainment, (1–3) three virtuous minds of the three realms arise for both a desire-realm mind obtained from birth and one derived from preparation arise from it since a desire-realm mind obtained from birth is clear. Only two minds derived from preparation in the two higher realms arise from it, since minds obtained from birth in the two higher realms are not clear and are not minds that rise from it. When maintaining that state, (4) a learner mind itself arises from it. When entering meditative attainment, (5) a nonlearner knowledge of elimination arises at the conclusion of learner vajra-like concentration.

A nonlearner (aśaikṣa) mind arises from five because when entering meditative attainment, it arises after (1–3) the three virtuous minds derived from preparation of the three realms alone and (4) after a learner vajra-like concentration. When maintaining that state, (5) a nonlearner mind itself arises.

Four minds arise from it. Those twelve are also explained as twenty through classifying virtuous minds in the three realms, in two types: obtained from birth and derived from preparation. (2:71)

Four minds arise from a nonlearner mind because when entering meditative attainment, (1–3) three minds arise: two of the desire realm and both minds derived from preparation of the two higher realms, making three, like the past virtue of the three realms. When maintaining that state, (4) a nonlearner mind itself arises, {such as knowledge of nonarising through knowledge of elimination}. Objection: If that is so, then five minds would arise from a nonlearner mind, because when complete degeneration occurs, a learner mind occurs at the conclusion of nonlearner mind. Reply: The nonmanifestation of an afflicted mind is nondegeneration from a nonlearner mind. If affliction manifested, affliction would interrupt it {because it is not its immediately preceding condition}. Therefore the Subcommentary also explains: A learner mind does not arise at the conclusion of a nonlearner mind because even when complete degeneration occurs, it is obstructed by the occurrence of affliction.[658] Thus one must abandon the faults arising due to the three or seven obscured minds [198] of the three realms. {Objection: At the conclusion of a nonlearner mind, it follows that eight occur. The eight are (1–3) the three virtuous minds, (4) a nonlearner mind itself, (5–7) the three afflicted minds of the three realms when degeneration from that occurs, and (8) learner mind. Reply: Afflicted and learner minds do not arise immediately after nonlearner minds because their nonemergence from nonlearner minds indicates the nondegeneration [of nonlearner minds.] But if they did emerge, they would have to arise from a virtuous mind, but virtuous minds obstruct those afflicted minds and learner minds.} Those are the twelve minds explained as immediately preceding conditions.

Again, those twelve minds are also explained as twenty. Question: How? Reply: Through classifying virtuous minds in the three realms, in two types {each,} they are explained as {fifteen}. Question: What are the two types? Reply: Obtained from birth (upapattyāpta) and derived from preparation (prāyogika). {(1) Obtained from birth is obtainment when the intermediate existence links to the two lower realms without reliance on preparation, and obtainment when birth existence links to the formless realm. (2) Derived from preparation is any of the three wisdoms derived from hearing, contemplation, or meditation obtained through cultivating preparatory states.} Question: But aren’t there more than fifteen?

Reply: {There are eighteen through} differentiating the four types of unobscured-neutral mind that are not declared to be virtuous or afflicted in the desire realm. Question: What are these four? Reply: They are minds arising from karmic maturation (vipākaja) {such as hell rebirth and so on}, demeanor (airyāpathika), creativity (śailpasthānika), and emanation (nairmita) {in order to create emanations}. Question: Thus are there eighteen? Reply: In the form realm, there are three types, leaving off creativity. Creativity does not exist there because the form realm lacks creative activity. {Celestial mansions, clothing, and ornaments and so on arise from karma and emanation; they are not manufactured by an agent in the least.} In the formless realm, the mind arising from karmic maturation alone exists because the minds governing demeanor and emanation do not exist there. Therefore there are twenty minds. The Autocommentary explains which minds occur at the conclusion of which minds. Therefore I have not written this down here for fear of being verbose. Thus virtuous minds in the three realms have two types, and unobscured-neutral minds in the lower two realms are differentiated as four and three types. In the context of the twelve minds, the two virtuous minds are enumerated as one, and the four unobscured-neutral minds are enumerated as one. {From among the four neutral minds, that arisen from maturation focuses on all objects and exists within the sixfold collection of consciousness. The latter three focus on any of the five objects, since the mind governing demeanor focuses on the four objects of form, taste, smell, and tactility, and the mind governing creativity focuses on [these plus] sound as well. Conception arises as mental consciousness alone since it requires current mental application. The five sense consciousnesses are antecedents of the minds governing demeanor and creativity because they are generated from seeing and hearing and so on. Minds arising from [karmic] maturation have no antecedent since they arise automatically due to the force of karma. The antecedent of the mind governing emanation is the mind of the actual basis of absorption. Therefore there are twenty minds: (1–8) eight minds in the desire realm, (9–14) six minds in the form realm, and (15–18) four in the formless realm as well as [199] (19–20) two uncontaminated minds. Moreover there are eight virtuous minds, four afflicted minds, and eight obscured minds, making twenty.}

THE NEED TO CLASSIFY MINDS IN TWENTY

The mind of death exists for virtuous minds obtained from birth in the three realms, unobscured-neutral minds arising from [karmic] maturation, and the mind governing demeanor, but it does not exist for virtuous minds derived from preparation and the other two unobscured-neutral minds. The mind of meditative attainment exists for virtuous minds derived from preparation of the three realms alone, and it does not exist for other minds. Both minds governing emanation in the desire and form realms arise from form-realm virtuous minds derived from preparation and itself, and they are not derived from other minds. Minds rising from meditative attainment, also when oppressed by afflicted meditative attainment, are desire-realm virtuous minds obtained from birth, since they are clear. Since minds obtained from birth in the two higher realms are not clear, they exist for virtuous minds derived from preparation alone that are not minds rising from meditative attainment. These special cases should be understood.

{The twelve or twenty are analyzed as to which has the greater pervasion.} Question: Now what is the difference between the twelve and twenty minds? Reply: The twelve has the greater pervasion. The Autocommentary states: Others say: One possessing the mind governing creativity focuses on the twelve bases with mental consciousness that actually creates.[659] {Thus there are neutral minds that focus on all supportive entities [or things].} Also, Master Jinaputra teaches it indicates this but others also exist. If that were not so then, he writes: In the second [absorption] and so on, consciousness of body, eye, ear, and cognition arise. All of them belong to the first [absorption]. They are undeclared [i.e., neutral], not[660] affliction.[661] And: Also those of lower [level] engage in speech. Therefore those four explained previously are not included in these. Also, Bhadanta Anantavarma explains in his commentary: There are other neutral consciousnesses not belonging to those four categories.[662] Therefore this should be understood to be a supplementary explanation. Yaśomitra’s commentary on part III explains: Also, the mind governing demeanor of an arhat entering nirvāṇa without remainder is similar to [an ordinary] mind governing demeanor, for we don’t assert that neutral minds are exhausted by just those four.[663]

Afflicted minds of the three realms (traidhātu) such as the desire realm acquire six minds when the two afflicted minds of the desire realm manifest: (1–2) two comprising the nonvirtuous and obscured minds in the desire realm, and (3–6) four comprising the two obscured minds of each higher realm. Or they acquire six when a form-realm obscured mind manifests. Or they acquire two when a formless-realm obscured mind manifests. Moreover the Autocommentary states in this context: When born, entering meditative attainment, free of attachment, completely degenerated, [200] and linking with virtue, one acquires minds that were not previously possessed.[664] “Born” is when one again returns to the lower realm from the higher realms. “Entering meditative attainment” is when one enters meditative attainment that respectively obtains a virtuous mind of the two higher realms, having obtained access concentration to the first absorption or the base of infinite space. “Free of attachment” is when one is free of attachment to levels and from levels. “Completely degenerated” is when the state of an arhat degenerates through manifesting afflictions of the three realms. “Linking with virtue” is when, after severing the root of merit, one again links with virtue through doubt or correct view. These are five occasions that were previously explained. Thus, when again returning to the desire realm, if any desire-realm afflicted nonvirtuous or an obscured mind manifests, then (1) obtainment of both afflicted minds and (2) obtainment of a {desire-realm} virtuous mind obtained from birth occurs. When those who sever their root of virtue in the desire realm link again with virtue through doubt {and are born in this realm from the two higher realms}, then there arises (3) obtainment of the virtuous minds obtained from birth that were enumerated before. When an arhat degenerates through a desire-realm nonvirtuous mind, (4–5) both the obscured minds of the two higher realms and (6) obtainment of a learner mind occurs. Thus, in general, if a desire-realm afflicted mind manifests, six minds that were not formerly obtained are newly acquired, but they do not manifest.[665] {Moreover, the six are not simultaneously acquired. If an afflicted mind is first manifested, then acquisition of the six from any type of mind may occur. You should analyze the series.

FIVE OCCASIONS ARE CALCULATED

(1) In linking with manifest afflicted doubt of the desire realm, having severed the root of virtue, the obtainment of a virtuous desire-realm mind obtained from birth is newly acquired. Even if one is born in the desire realm from the two higher realms, just that mind is newly acquired, because the obtainment of earlier desire-realm virtuous minds is relinquished by the later birth. (2) For birth in the desire realm from the form realm, the obtainment of both desire-realm afflicted minds are newly acquired,[666] though either of the two desire-realm afflicted minds can manifest. Further, they are acquired in the intermediate existence. (3) When born in the desire realm from the formless realm, the intermediate existence newly acquires obtainment of the three minds: a form-realm afflicted mind and both desire-realm afflicted minds. (4) When one degenerates from the state of an arhat through manifesting a desire-realm nonvirtuous mind, one newly acquires the obtainment of the three afflicted minds of the three realms and the obtainment of a learner mind. (5) An ārya mind degenerates due to the obscured minds, such as afflicted view of the self and wrong view, excluding desire-realm nonvirtuous and afflicted minds, since these are abandoned by the path of seeing.

Therefore, when a desire-realm afflicted mind first manifests, it can newly acquire the obtainment of six minds: three desire-realm minds, which are (1) the desire-realm virtuous mind obtained from birth and (2–3) both afflicted minds, (4–5) the two afflicted minds of the two higher realms, and (6) a learner uncontaminated mind.} Also, from manifest form-realm afflicted mind, six not formerly possessed are acquired. Therefore, when taking birth from the formless realm to the form realm, if a form-realm obscured mind manifests, then four minds are obtained: (1) itself, (2) a form-realm virtuous mind [201] obtained from birth, and {both} (3) a form-realm emanation mind and (4) a desire-realm emanation mind, {since the prior generation of obtainment exists}. If degeneration from the state of an arhat due to a form-realm obscured mind occurs, then {obtainment of} (5) a formless-realm obscured mind and (6) a learner mind occurs. If degeneration from the state of an arhat by a formless-realm obscured mind occurs, then both the formless-realm obscured mind itself and a learner mind are acquired. {There is no acquisition from this [being] returning to his realm since there is no other abode above it and he possesses his own level from before.}

Those free of attachment to the desire realm who are born in the form realm and manifest a virtuous mind of the actual basis of {the first} absorption obtain three minds: {(1) the virtuous mind of one’s level and (2–3) the two emanation minds of the desire realm and form realm}. They obtain a form-realm virtuous mind and both desire-realm and form-realm emanating minds because when the mind of absorption is obtained, those also are definitely obtained.
