Those who manifest a learner (śaikṣa) mind obtain four. When they enter {the first moment of the uncontaminated state} definitely, (1) the learner mind itself occurs. {When on the ninth liberated path} free from attachment to the desire realm due to the ārya path {of uncontaminated access concentration}, (2–3) both desire- and form-realm emanation minds occur. When free of attachment to the form realm through the ārya path {dependent on any of the six levels}, the obtainment of (4) a formless-realm virtuous mind occurs. Thus there are four types. Since the continuum of a form-realm virtuous mind is merely maintained {through} having previously {obtained the heat stage of the path of preparation}, it is not newly obtained by the power of the learner mind and therefore not enumerated.

The remainder are six because there are (1–2) desire-realm and formless-realm virtue, (3) nonlearner mind, and (4–6) the three unobscured-neutral minds of the three realms. [Yaśomitra] states: Scholars say that masters who engage in enhancement acquire nine afflicted minds — {[those twelve] except three: both the virtuous mind and unobscured mind of the formless realm and the nonlearner mind.} Six virtuous minds are acquired: {(1–2) both minds of emanation, (3–4) both higher virtuous minds, (5) the first [uncontaminated mind], and (6) the final uncontaminated mind}. A neutral mind acquires itself.[667] This explanation — that any of the nine are acquired: (1–4) four minds of the desire realm, (5–7) three minds of the form realm, (8) a formless-realm obscured mind from the manifest afflicted minds of the three realms, and (9) an uncontaminated mind — does not contradict that which was previously taught. {With obtainment of individual concentration,} six are acquired: (1–3) three virtuous minds of the three realms {or the two higher minds} from manifest virtuous mind, (4–5) two desire-realm and form-realm emanation minds {from obtainment of freedom from attachment}, and (6) uncontaminated mind. Indeed, one uncontaminated mind is contemplated. However, it is appropriate to express [202] seven virtuous minds here. {Some say: Since a desire-realm virtuous mind occurs by correct view linking with the severed root virtue, seven are asserted. Others say:} Because there are both uncontaminated learner and nonlearner minds, {seven are asserted}.

Therefore Vasubandhu remarks: Definite entry at the time of an arhat is learner and nonlearner.[668] When the path of seeing that is definite entry is obtained, it is said to be uncontaminated learner mind, and when that state of arhat is obtained, it is uncontaminated nonlearner mind. For the three unobscured-neutral minds, the acquisition of just that occurs, {since the Abhidharmakośa declares, “Obtainment of those not declared arises simultaneously” (2:38c),} and this was stated before, {for it was also said that “the obtainment by self or other, before or after, does not exist”}.

There are nine minds acquired by themselves alone: (1–6) The six minds other than the two emanation minds of the eight unobscured-neutral minds are acquired when they themselves manifest, since there is no prior generation of obtainment. (7–8) Both desire-realm and form-realm virtuous minds derived by preparation are obtained by their own preparation. (9) A nonlearner mind is obtained by the knowledge of elimination. There are four acquired by others alone: (1–2) Both emanation minds are acquired by form-realm virtuous mind, obscured mind, and learner mind. Also (3–4) minds obtained from birth in the two higher realms are acquired by an obscured mind when linking at death. There are seven acquired by both: (1) When a desire-realm mind obtained from birth links through correct view, it is acquired by itself. When it links through doubt and when taking birth, it is acquired by others. (2–3) When both afflicted minds arise, whichever manifests is acquired by itself, and the other is acquired by the other. (4–5) If both afflicted minds of higher realms degenerate by themselves, then they are acquired by themselves. If they degenerate due to lower minds, they are acquired by others. (6) When a formless-realm mind derived from preparation enters access concentration to [infinite] space, it is acquired by itself. If acquired by learner mind, it is acquired by other. (7) Also a learner mind at the time of the first moment of the uncontaminated is acquired by itself. When degenerating from the state of an arhat, it is acquired by others.} The reality of the faculties, the method of generating conditioned states, physical states, concomitant and nonconcomitant states, as well as causes, conditions, and results, are correctly fathomed via this section. Thus to study such an explanation is appropriate.

11. Classification and Attributes of Sentient Beings
gnas gsum pa 'jig rten bstan pa
THE EXPOSITION OF THE COSMOS

da ni 'jig rten bstan pa'i mdzod 'chad pa na khams bstan par 'dod khams gtogs pa thams cad do zhes bya ba la sogs pa dang*/ dbang po bstan par dri med ma gtogs 'dod par gtogs zhes bya ba la sogs pas khams gsum gyi ming tsam zhig bshad pas de'i don bstan pa'i phyir 'jig rten bstan pa'i mdzod 'chad par byed do/ { yang na gnas dang po gnyis kyis ji lta ba dang ji snyed pa'i dmigs pa thun mong du bshad nas/ 'di man chad kyis gtso cher ji lta ba'i dmigs pa ston no/ / de yang bden pa bzhi yin pa las thog mar sdug bden 'chad pa'i mtshan gzhi ni gang skye ba sems can dang gang du skye ba snod kyi 'jig rten dang gnyis te/ thun mong min pa dang thun mong gi las grub pa'o/ / mtshan nyid ni sdug bsngal gsum gyis ci rigs su sdug bsngal ba'o/ / 'jig rten thams cad sdug bsngal yin nam zhe na/ sde pa gnyis ni de ltar 'dod de/ de gsum zag bcad zag pa med/ / lhag ma rnams ni zag bcas so/ / zhes bshad pas so/ / 'on kyang sdug bsngal gyi sdug bsngal dang mi ldan pa de dag yongs su dag pa'i 'jig rten yin no/ / dag pa'i 'jig rten slob dpon 'phags pa lam bden du 'dod cing bsdu ba las de dag dus gsum pa thob pa'i byang sems rnams smin lam gyi dbang gis skye bar bshad do/ /}

Now the Abhidharmakośa’s presentation of the cosmos is explained. The mere names of the three realms were mentioned in the presentation of elements, in such statements as “All exist in the desire realm” (1:30a), and in the presentation of faculties, in such statements as “Those except for stainless faculties belong to the desire realm” (2:12a). Therefore the Abhidharmakośa’s presentation of the cosmos is now explained in order to reveal the meaning of those terms. The first two parts specifically explain reality and diversity[669] as focal objects. The [parts] after that primarily teach the focal object of reality or the four truths. From among those, the truth of suffering is first taught, and that is exemplified by both sentient beings and the physical world systems where they are born. Both are established from the individual and shared karma of beings and defined as “that associated with suffering through any of the three sufferings.” Question: Is the cosmos in its entirety suffering or not? Both schools assert that it is, because [the Abhidharmakośa] mentions, “These three are contaminated or uncontaminated. The remainder are contaminated,”[670] (1:31cd) and those [realms] free of the suffering of pain constitute the thoroughly pure cosmos. Master Ārya Asaṅga asserts that the pure cosmos is the truth of path, and the Compendium of Bases explains: Bodhisattvas who obtain control over the three times are born [in contaminated realms] by the power of prayer.[671]

EXPLANATION OF THE DESIRE REALM
dmyal ba yi dgas dud 'gro dang / / mi rnams dang ni lha drug dag / 'dod pa'i khams yin dmyal ba dang / / gling dbye ba las de nyi shu/ / 1
Hell beings, ghosts, animals, humans, and the six gods constitute the desire realm. Through classifying hells and continents, there are twenty. (3:1)

bsod nams ma yin pa'i las kyis khrid pa'am/ dga' bar mi byed pa'i phyir dmyal ba ste/ na ra ka zhes bya ba la na dgag pa dang ra ka dga' ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ / slob dpon 'dun bzang na re skyabs med pas na dmyal ba zhes bya'o zhes zer ro/ / zas skom yid la btags pa'am der song ba rnams phyir mi ldog pas sam/ skom pa dang ldan pas yi dwags te pre ta zhes bya ba'i don to/ / dud cing 'gro bas na dud 'gro ste tir+Ya ka zhes bya ba'i don to/ / 'jig rten pa rnams yid kyi bu zhes zer zhing yid shas che bas mi ste ma nu Sha'i don to/ / des na bskal pa dang po'i mi rnams kyang yid las skyes zhes bya bar sgrogs so/ / rnams zhes pa ni bzhi ga la sbyar ro/ / lha ni tshangs pa'i lus las skyes pa dang*/{ bdud rtsi za bas sam lus la 'od yod pas sam/} bde ba la rol pa dang*/ mchod par 'os pa dang*/ gzhal yas khang nam mkha' la yod pa'i phyir te de ba'i don to/ / de yang rgyal chen{ ris bzhi} pa dang*/ sum cu rtsa gsum pa dang*/ 'thab bral ba dang*/ /dga' ldan pa dang*/ 'phrul dga' ba dang*/ gzhan 'phrul dbang byed pa ste drug go /de ltar na dmyal ba nas lha drug gi bar snod dang bcas pa dag ni 'dod pa'i khams ni/ 'dir sems can rnams ni{ yul} kham zas dang 'khrig pa la 'dod chags dang bcas shing 'don yon lngas 'tsho ba'i phyir dang{ mnyam par ma gzhag pa dang 'dod pa'i 'dod chags rgyas par 'gyur ba'i phyir dang} snod kyang 'dod pa dang ldan pa'i sems can gyi gnas yin pa'i phyir dang*/ rang gi mtshan nyid 'dzin pa'i phyir te/ lung sil bu las/ 'jig rten sna tshogs gang de 'dod pa min/ / skyes bu'i kun rtog 'dod chags 'dod pa yin/ / 'jig rten dag na sna tshogs de bzhin gnas/ / 'on kyang brtan rnams 'di la bdun pa 'dul zhes gsungs pa bzhin no/

They are hell beings (naraka) because they are led by nonmeritorious karma or because they are joyless, since the Sanskrit term naraka is composed of na, a term of negation, and raka, which means “joy.” Master Saṅghabhadra says that they are called hell beings since they lack refuge.[672] They are ghosts (preta) since they yearn for food and drink, or since those who have departed cannot return, or since they possess thirst, and this is the meaning of preta. They are animals (tiryañc) since they move while bowed over, and this is the meaning of tiryañc. They are human (manuṣya) since they are mundane beings who are “the progeny of mind” and “those for whom the mind is dominant,” and this is the meaning of manuṣya. Also humans of the first eon [204] are said to be “born from mind” (manojanmā). A pluralizing particle is applied to these four. The gods (deva) are born from the body of Brahma, {consume nectar, have radiant bodies}, play blissfully, are worthy of offerings, and live in the sky in crystal palaces. This is the meaning of deva. Further there are six abodes: (1) Cāturmahārājakāyika (Heaven of the {Four} Great {Lineages of} Kings), (2) Trāyastriṃśa (Heaven of the Thirty-Three), (3) Yāma (Heaven Free of Conflict), (4) Tuṣita (Heaven of Joy), (5) Nirmāṇarati (Heaven Enjoying Emanations), and (6) Paranirmitavaśavartin (Heaven Controlling Others’ Emanations). The environment and [its inhabitants,] from the hells to the six divine realms, constitute the desire realm (kāmadhātu) (1) because sentient beings there possess desire for {objects such as} food and sex, and they survive through the five sense objects, {(2) because their attachment to desire-realm objects increases in the absence of equipoise,} (3) because their environment is the abode of sentient beings who possess desire, and (4) because they seize its [desirable] characteristics. It is said in the Miscellaneous Discourses: The various mundane [worlds] are not desire; conceptuality that is the attachment of beings is desire. Various [beings] abide in that way in those mundane [worlds]; however, those who are steadfast tame the aspiration[673] [to live] there.[674]

{Objection: It follows that attachment to desire-realm objects would also increase for the mind of desire-realm emanation. Reply: Smells and tastes that are solely objects of attachment or desire for the emanating mind are projected by the power of emanation. But the emanating mind of one level does not produce emanations on other levels, and attachment does not arise through hearing of other emanations. However, when one’s own emanation degenerates, attachment may arise for [other emanations], but it does not increase for them.}

de rnams kyang rgyas par dbye na dmyal ba la tsha dmyal brgyad dang*/ mi la gling bzhir dbye ba las ni 'dod pa'i khams de nyi shur shes par bya'o/ / grang dmyal dang nye 'khor ba rnams ni tsha dmyal gyi 'khor gnas pa'i phyir dang nyi tshe ba la gnas nges pa med pa'i phyir ma bgrangs so/ / gling phran rnams kyang gling gi 'khor yin pa'i phyir ro/ / lha ma yin la sogs pa rnams kyang 'dod khams yin mod kyi de ni 'dod pa'i 'gro ba lngar 'dus par 'chad par 'gyur ro/ / de ltar na ngan song gnas bcu dang mtho ris gnas bcu ste nyi shu'o/ / sa'i dngos gzhi las ni tsha dmyal brgyad/ grang dmyal brgyad/ yi dwags dang*/ lha ma yin dang*/ mi'i gling bzhi gling phran brgyad de bcu gnyis/ rgyal chen ris bzhi la sogs pa lha ris drug ste gnas gzhan sum cu rtsa drug po 'di dag ni 'dod pa'i khams zhes bya'o/ / dud 'gro ni lha dang mi dang lhan cig rgyu ba nyid yin pas de'i phyir de dag gis gnas gzhan logs shig tu rnam par mi gzhag go zhes bshad cing*/ slob dpon klu sgrub kyis kyang sA lu ljang pa'i 'grel pa las/ khams 'gro skye 'gro bye brag gis/ / 'dod srid rnam pa sum cu drug /ces pa dang mthun par sum cu rtsa drug nyid du bshad de/ gzhan dag ni dmyal ba la bco brgyad dang*/ yi dwags dang dud 'gro la gnas na gnas pa dang*/ kha 'thor ba gnyis gnyis su phye bas bzhi dang*/ mi la bcu gnyis dang*/ lha ma yin {la sgra gcan mgul 'phreng rab gnon/ thag bzang ris te } bzhi dang*/ lha drug ste{ mtho ris nyer gnyis/ ngan song nyer gnyis te 'dod pa'i gnas gzhan} bzhi bcu rtsa bzhi'o zhes zer ro/ /

If they are extensively categorized through classifying the eight hot hells (naraka) for hell beings and the four continents (dvīpa) for humans, the desire realm has twenty types.[675] The cold hells and surrounding hells are not counted because they are abodes near the hot hells, while the occasional hells are not counted because their abode is not fixed. The minor continents are not counted since they exist as retinue to the four continents. The abodes of demigods and so on exist in the desire realm, and their [inhabitants] are included among the five types of desire-realm reincarnating beings. Thus there are ten abodes of lower rebirth and ten abodes of higher rebirth, making twenty. Yogacarā Levels declares: The eight hot hells, eight cold hells, ghosts, demigods, the twelve human abodes such as the four continents and eight minor continents, and the six god abodes such as Cāturmahārājika comprise the thirty-six individual abodes called the “desire realm.” Because animals move among gods and humans, their individual abodes are not posited separately.[676] Also Master Nāgārjuna explains that there are thirty-six abodes. This conforms with his Commentary on the Śālistamba Sūtra, which notes: In terms of specific realms and births there are thirty-six types of desire-realm existence.[677] Others say: There are forty-four: (1–18) hell beings have eighteen abodes; (19–22) ghosts [205] and animals abide where they abide, but if separately divided into two each, they have four abodes; (23–34) humans have twelve abodes; (35–38) demigods have four, {namely, Rāhu, Kaṇṭhābharaṇa, Kharaskandha, and Vemacitra}; and (39–44) gods have six. {Thus there are twenty-two higher rebirths and twenty-two lower rebirths as individual desire-realm abodes}.
gzugs kyi khams bshad pa ni
EXPLANATION OF THE FORM REALM
gong ma'i gnas dag bcu bdun ni/ / gzugs khams yin der so so yi/ / bsam gtan sa ni gsum pa yin/ / bzhi pa sa ni brgyad pa yin/ / 2
The seventeen higher abodes are the form realm. Each absorption level has three stages. The fourth level has eight. (3:2)

'dod pa las yon tan dang gnas gzhan gyis gong ma'i gnas bcu bdun po dag ni gzugs kyi khams kyi gnas yin te/ 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral zhing gzugs la 'dod chags dang bcas pa'i phyir dang*/ {snyoms 'jug dang de'i rten la lus la gzugs kyi 'dod chags dang bcas pa'i phyir dang byed pa med la } rang gi mtshan nyid 'dzin pa'i phyir ro/ gal te gzugs kyi khams ni bsam gtan bzhis bsdus pa'i phyir ji ltar bcu bdun du dbye zhe na/

The seventeen higher abodes that are superior in terms of qualities and domain to the desire realm are the abodes of the form realm (rūpadhātu). Beings there are free from attachment to the desire-realm objects, though they possess attachment to the form realm, {because they possess attachment to form-realm meditative attainment and the body that is its basis} and because they maintain those characteristics {even when they are not utilized}. Question: If the form realm is subsumed by the four absorptions, how are they classified in seventeen?

gzugs kyi khams der bsam gtan dang po gsum po so so'i sa ste rgyu snyoms 'jug gi sems ni chung ngu dang 'bring dang chen po gsum gsum du goms pas 'bras bu skye ba'i gnas gzhan yang tshangs pa'i sder gtogs pas tshangs ris pa dang*/ tshangs pa'i mdun na rig byed 'don pa ltar gnas pas tshangs pa'i mdun na 'don dang*/ tshe dang kha dog la sogs pa khyad par 'phags shing tshangs pa'i gtso bo yin pa'i phyir tshangs chen te bsam gtan dang po la gsum dang*/ gong ma bas 'od chung bas 'od chung dang*/ 'od tshad med pas tshad med 'od dang*/ 'od shin tu gsal ba'i phyir 'od gsal te bsam gtan gnyis pa la gsum dang*/ gong ma bas sems kyi bde ba chung bas bde chung dang*/ bde ba tshad med pa dang ldan pa'i phyir tshad med bde dang*/ bde ba shin tu rgyas pa'i phyir bde rgyas te bsam gtan gsum pa la gsum ste/ 'di la dge chung la sogs par bshad pa ni ku sha la zhes bya ba bde ba dang dge ba gnyis ka la 'jug pas lo tsA ba rnams kyis dge bar bsgyur te/ don ni yid kyi sa pa'i bde ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: In the form realm, the first three absorption (dhyāna) levels have three stages each, and by cultivating each of these three stages — the small, medium, and great minds of causal meditative attainment — their resultant states arise. As such there are three for the first absorption: (1) Brahmakāyika (Brahma Assembly), since beings there belong to the assembly of Brahma, (2) Brahmapurohita (Brahma Priests), since they abide reciting the vedas in front of Brahma, and (3) Mahābrahma (Great Brahma), because they excel others in lifespan, complexion, and so on, and they are the main retinue of Brahma. There are three in the second absorption: (1) Parīttābha (Small Radiance), since beings there are less radiant than those higher, (2) Apramāṇābha (Immeasurable Radiance), since their radiance cannot be measured, and (3) Ābhāsvara (Clear Radiance), because their radiance is extremely bright. There are three in the third absorption: (1) Parīttaśubha (Small Bliss), since beings there are less blissful than those who are higher, (2) Apramāṇaśubha (Immeasurable Bliss), since their bliss is immeasurable, and (3) Śubhakṛtsna (Complete Bliss), because their bliss is extremely great. These three are also called Small Virtue and so on because translators construed this term to mean “virtue” since the term kuśala[678] can mean either bliss or virtue, but it means “bliss of the level of the mental faculty.”

des na bsam gtan dang po gsum re re la'ang gsum gsum pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ bsam gtan bzhi pa ni rgyu zag bcas kyis bsam gtan bzhi pa chung ngu 'bring chen po gsum dang*/ de nyid zag med dang spel ma chung ngu dang 'bring dang chen po dang shin tu chen po dang ches shin tu chen po lnga ste brgyad du bsgoms pa'i bye brag gis 'bras bu gnas gzhan yang 'og gzhi sprin ltar 'dab chags par gnas pa med pas sprin med dang*/ mi g.yo ba'i bsod nams las skyes pas bsod nams skyes dang*/ gzugs kyi khams pa'i so so'i skye bo rnams kyi dge ba'i 'bras bu shin tu che shos yin pa'i phyir 'bras bu che zhes bya ba so so'i skye bo'i gnas gzhan gsum dang*/ gnas gtsang ma gong ma dag pas dman pa'i phyir mi che ba dang*/ nyon mongs pas gdung ba med pa'i phyir mi gdung ba dang*/ chos mthong ba bzang ba'i phyir gya nom snang ba dang*/ lta ba bzang ba'i phyir shin tu mthong ba dang*/ de'i gong na gnas gzhan med pa'i phyir 'og min zhes bya ba 'phags pa'i gnas gzhan lnga ste brgyad pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'phags pa'i gnas lnga po dag la so so'i skye bo dang ma 'dres pas gtsang ma'i ris zhes kyang bya'o/ /

Therefore each of the first three absorptions has three stages each. The fourth absorption level (bhūmi) has eight stages: three, which are the (1) small, (2) medium, and (3) great stages of the causal contaminated fourth absorption; and five, which are the (4) small, (5) medium, (6) great, (7) extremely great, and (8) supremely great stages of enhancement of the uncontaminated fourth absorption. By specifically meditating on these eight, you will first attain the three individual abodes of ordinary beings: (1) Anabhraka (Cloudless), since there is no abiding together with lower beings who are likened to clouds, (2) Puṇyaprasava (Born of Merit), since beings there are born from invariable merit, and (3) Bṛhatphala (Great Result), because it is the greatest virtuous result of ordinary beings of the form realm. Moreover, there are five separate ārya abodes: (4) Avṛha (Lesser Measure), because it is inferior to the higher pure states of the pristine abodes, (5) Atapa (Unperturbed), because there one is not tormented by afflictions, (6) Sudṛśa (Sublime Appearance), because the perception of Dharma is [206] pure there, (7) Sudarśana (Pure Vision), because view is pure there, and (8) Akaniṣṭha (Supreme)[679] because there is no other abode higher than it. The five ārya abodes are also called “pristine regions” since they are not populated by ordinary beings.

Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas assert that there are sixteen individual abodes since there is no separate abode of Mahābrahma distinct from Brahmapurohita. The Autocommentary explains: It is well known that Brahmapurohita is the same as the main supreme great abode of Mahābrahma. It does not exist as another actual level that one could travel to.[680] Aparāntaka Vaibhāṣikas and the Sautrāntikas assert that there are seventeen abodes since these are separate individual abodes. Mahāyānists assert that above Akaniṣṭha there is Great Akaniṣṭha, which is the field of the enjoyment body (saṃbhogakāya), since Yogācāra Levels declares: If one transcends the pristine abodes, there is the great abode of Īśvara, because those bodhisattvas abiding on the tenth level are born on higher levels through thoroughly meditating on the ten levels.[681] And the Drop of the Secret Moon states: In the delightful abode Akaniṣṭha, having abandoned the pristine abodes, the perfect buddha attains enlightenment, and an emanation here attains enlightenment.[682] Great Akaniṣṭha is also called “the abode of Great Īśvara” because the Commentary on the Praise explains that Great Īśvara obtains the state of “Dharma Īśvara” in Dharmamegha, and the light of the buddhas confers empowerment on the tenth-level bodhisattva.[683] Also each of the absorptions is explained to have four types, since a sūtra states: In the first absorption there are [four:] Brahmakāyika (Brahma Assembly), the Attendants of Brahmadeva, the Retinue of All Brahmas, and Mahābrahma (Great Brahma). In the second there are [four:] Radiance, Parīttābha (Small Radiance), Apramāṇābha (Immeasurable Radiance), and All-Radiant Clarity. In the third there are [four:] Śubha (Bliss),[684] Parīttaśubha (Small Bliss), Apramāṇaśubha (Immeasurable Bliss), and Śubhakṛtsna (Complete Bliss). In the fourth there are [four:] the Great, Small of the Great, the Immeasurably Great, and Bṛhatphala (Great Result).[685] The first term appears to be an abbreviated teaching, and the others, name equivalents of the actual three. The meaning of the term form realm is that which possesses supreme form and maintains those characteristics.

The formless realm is not a separate abode. It has four types through specific generation. Here the mindstream depends on type and life force also. (3:3)

The formless realm (ārūpyadhātu), {as previously explained,} is not a distinct, separate abode (sthāna). Why? Because there is no form there, and distinct and separate abodes are differentiated by form. As such, a being is born in {any previously obtained} formless concentration in just that place where {the body of} that being dies. [207] Question: How does it have four types, {lower to higher}? Reply: The formless realm is posited as four types, such as infinite space, through the specific generation (upapattya) of different resultant meditative attainments in that realm due to cultivating their prior causes: the meditative attainment of the base of infinite space (ākāśānantyāyatana), the base of infinite consciousness (vijñānānantyāyatana), the base of nothingness (akiñcanyāyatana), and the base of neither discernment nor nondiscernment (naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana). The definition of formless realm is “that which is free from attachment to the desire and form realms but not free from attachment to the formless realm.” The meaning of realm is as before. The meaning of the term is explained in part 8. Other schools, such as the Tāmraśaṭīya and so on, assert that subtle form also exists in the formless (arūpya) realm, since [in this case] the term of negation [“a” in arūpya] applies merely to inferior form, and subtle form exists above Akaniṣṭha and the other abodes. Question: If there is no form whatsoever in the formless realm, on what does the mind depend?

gzugs med pa'i khams der ni ris mthun pa dang srog gi dbang po la sems kyi rgyud ni brten par 'dod pa yin la/ yang gi sgras ni las la brten pa gsung ngo*/ / slob dpon rgyal po'i sras ni yang gi sgras so so'i skye bo dang*/ mi ldan pa dang*/ thob pa dang*/ skye ba la sogs pa bsdu'o zhes 'chad do/ / gal te 'dod gzugs na'ang de dag la ji ltar mi brten zhe na/ de dag tu gzugs kyi 'du shes dang ma bral bas srog la sogs pa stobs chung ba'i phyir ro/ / gzugs med pa'i khams su ni gzugs kyi 'du shes dang bral ba'i snyoms par 'jug pa'i khyad par las skyes pas sngon gyi las kyis 'phangs pa'i srog la sogs pa stobs che ba'i phyir de la sems rten la sems la'ang de dag brten pa yin no zhes bya ba ni grub pa'i mtha'o/ / mdo sde pa ni sngon gyi las kyi stobs kyis der ming bzhi'i phung po 'grub kyi srog la sogs pa'i rdzas gzhan ni mi 'dod do/ / de la'ang gzugs med pa'i ming bzhi'i phung po ril po rnam par smin par thal ba'i skyon yod pa'i phyir rnal 'byor spyod pa pas ming bzhi'i phung po gzhan ni kun gzhi rnam shes la rten la/ kun gzhi ni sngon gyi las la brten pa nyid rigs pa yin no zhes 'dod pa yin no/ / {'dod pa dang gzugs dang ming bzhi'i phung po la sred pas so sor bcad pas khams gsum yin la/ 'dod pa na gnas rigs du ma yod kyang sa so so'i sred pa mi 'dra ba med pas sa'ang gcig go gong ma gnyis ni sred pa mi 'dra ba bzhi bzhis ris su bcad pas sa'ang mi 'dra ba bzhi bzhi byung ngo */}de ltar na khams gsum du rnam par bzhag pa yin no/ /

Reply: It is asserted that in the formless realm the mindstream (cittasaṃtati) depends on minds of the same type (nikāya) and the faculty of life force (jīvita). The term “also” includes dependence on karma. Master Jinaputra explains: The term “also” subsumes ordinary beings, nonpossession, obtainment, birth, and so on.[686] Question: Why don’t the mindstreams of desire- and form-realm beings depend on those as well? Reply: Life force and so on are weak [in the material realms] since beings there are not free from the discernment of form. Life force and so forth that are projected by the prior karma of beings in the formless realm are very strong since they are generated from the special meditative attainment free from the discernment of form. This implies the philosophical tenet that “the bases on which the mind depends themselves depend on the mind.” Sautrāntikas assert that the four mental aggregates are established there by the power of prior karma but that the substances of life force and so on are separate substances. Yogācāras assert that because that entails the erroneous consequence that all four formless mental aggregates would be [results of] karmic maturation, it is logical to assert that the four mental aggregates depend on the foundation consciousness and that the foundation consciousness depends on prior karma. {The three realms are differentiated since (1) the craving for desire-realm objects, (2) the craving for form-realm objects, and (3) the craving for four mental aggregates are differentiated. Though many types of abodes exist in the desire realm, just one level is differentiated since the craving for each desire-realm level is the same. In each of the two higher realms, four different levels arise for each, since there are four different cravings for each.} Thus the realms are posited in three.

The five reincarnating beings, as well as their individual natures, are neither afflicted-obscured (akliṣṭa) nor nonvirtuous, nor are they declared (avyākṛtā) to be virtuous, because if they were afflicted or virtuous they would not include āryas or reincarnating beings who have severed their root of virtue. Some say: They are virtuous. Some say: They are afflicted. Some say: They are obscured-neutral.[688] Reply: Such assertions are illogical because it would follow that reincarnating beings would transmigrate without changing lives. Though these reincarnating beings are called “sentient beings” (sattva), they are not intermediate beings (antarābhava). The Sūtra Teaching Seven Existences explains that the intermediate existence is separate from the hell existence and so on: There are seven existences: hell existence, animal existence, ghost existence, god existence, human existence, karmic existence, and intermediate existence.[689] Also Presentation on the World declares: The four birth processes include the five types of reincarnating beings, but the five types of reincarnating beings do not include all those born of the four birth processes. What do they not include? The intermediate existence.[690] Also Aggregate of Phenomena states that the eye of an intermediate being is distinct from that of a hell being and so on: What is the eye element? Translucent form derived from the four great elements, that is the subtle organ of the eye, eye faculty, eye base, or eye element of those born among hell beings or animals, in the regions of ghosts, among gods or humans, among beings born from meditation, or as intermediate beings.[691]

gal te 'gro ba lnga yin na mdo gzhan dag las lha ma yin dang dri za la sogs pa gang dag bshad pa de dag gang gis bsdus she na/ lha ma yin ni dran pa nyer gzhag las yi dwags kyi 'gro bar gtogs pa dang*/ dud 'gro'i 'gro bar gtogs pa rnams so/ / de la dang po'i bdud kyi ris kyi yi dwags rnams dang*/ yi dwags rdzu 'phrul chen po rnams so/ / gnyis pa ni rgya mtsho'i gting gi sa gzhi la gnas pa ste ri rab kyi rten dpag tshad brgyad khri bzhi stong yod pa'i sa 'og na gnas so zhes yi dwags dang dud 'gror 'dus par gsungs la/ slob dpon thogs med ni lha dang longs spyod 'gran bzod pa dang gnyen yang sdeb pa'i phyir lha'i nang du 'dus par bzhed de/ sa las/ lha ma yin rnams kyang lha'i 'gro bas bsdus pa kho nar lta bar bya'o/ / 'on kyang de dag g.yo sgyu shas che bas lha rnams bzhin du dkar po'i chos kyi snod du ma gyur pas de'i phyir ched 'ga' mdo gzhan dag las 'gro ba tha dad par bstan to/ / de dag lha nyid yin yang lha'i chos yang dag par blangs te gnas pa ma yin pas de'i phyir lha ma yin rnams zhes bya'o/ / zhes dman pa la dgag pa'i sgrar bshad do/

Question: If there are just five types of reincarnating beings, then which one includes demigods and gandharvas and so on, which are mentioned in other sūtras? The Foundation of Mindfulness Sūtra declares that they are included within ghosts and animals: Demigods belong to ghost and animal reincarnating beings. The first are wild animals of demon type and ghosts [209] with great supernatural power. The second abide in the depths of the ocean 84,000 yojanas below the ground of the base of Meru.[693] Master Asaṅga asserts that they are subsumed among the gods because they vie for the resources of the gods and even make friends with them. Yogācāra Levels explains that demigod (asura) contains a term of negation [“a” in asura] that indicates an inferior being: Also demigods should be solely included among the gods. However, due to a predominance of guile and deceit, they are not vessels of white Dharma like the gods. Because of that, some sūtras teach that they are distinct reincarnating beings. Though they are gods, they are called demigods since they are not vessels for receiving perfect instruction.[694]

{Detailed Explanation of Yogācāra Levels criticizes [the view they are ghosts] when it states: Master Saṅghabhadra says that demigods belong to ghost reincarnations since they are definitely nonhuman and since they do not comprehend the four truths. But this reason is indeterminate and therefore inappropriate.[695]} Master Guṇaprabha asserts that they are included among gods and ghosts because the Exposition of the Five Aggregates explains: Because demigod reincarnating beings are included among god and ghost reincarnating beings, they are not mentioned separately.[696] Some say: There are six types because the Meeting of Father and Son Sūtra states: What are the six beings taught within the collection of sentient beings?[697] {They are sentient beings who are hell beings, animals, ghosts, and those by type demigods, humans, and gods. The lion among men has designated them as conventional truths. The cause of becoming one who observes Brahma is to pray and then immediately take rebirth there.}

Gandharvas may be either intermediate beings or divine musicians. The former are not included among reincarnating beings, but the latter are gods. Kumbhāṇḍas and pūtanās are ghosts predominantly belonging to the category of gods. Nāgas (mythical snakes), garuḍas (mythical birds), kinnaras (mythical creatures part horse part human), and mahoragas (mythical serpents) belong among the animals. Piśācas (flesh-eating spirits), unmadas (beguiling ghosts), apasmāras (demons who cause sickness), female demons, piśācas who live in refuse grounds, and so on are ghosts. Rākṣasas (demonic beings) are a subset of humans. Yakṣas (supernatural beings), direction protectors, mundane protectors, and demons mainly belong to the category of gods, but they also belong to nāgas and ghosts.

The five types of reincarnating beings [who occupy] the three realms are said to have seven abodes of consciousness. A sūtra states: Sentient beings with different material bodies and different discernments are humans and some of the gods. This is the first abode of consciousness.[698] Sentient beings with different bodies (kāya) and discernments (saṃjñā) are {those of the three lower rebirths,} humans, desire-realm gods, and those subsequently born in the first absorption whose bodies have different colors, [210] marks, and shapes, and also whose discernments differ in terms of pleasure, pain, and equanimity. The same sūtra states: Sentient beings with different material bodies and the same discernment are any gods of Brahmakāyika who first arise. This is the second abode of consciousness.[699]

de la lus tha dad cing 'du shes gcig pa ni bsam gtan dang por sngar skyes pa rnams te/ {smra ba dang gos dang tshangs chen } lus che ba dang{ 'khor} chung ba'i phyir dang*/ 'du shes ni tshangs pa chen po ni 'di dag bdag gi 'dod pa las byung ngo snyam {du rgyu 'dis byed par mtshungs } la/ de'i 'khor du dang por skyes pa de dag kyang bdag cag ni tshangs pa chen po'i 'dod pa las byung ngo snyam du sems pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te tshangs pa'i 'khor du byung ba de dag gis bdag cag tshangs pa chen po'i smon pa las byung ngo zhes ji ltar shes te/{ de dag gis bsam gtan gnyis pa'i sems thob na tshangs pa la dmigs pa'i tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog 'dzin spangs pas 'byung bar mi rigs la/ ma thob na dman pa'i yul mchog ma yin pas gnyis pa'i sngon gyi gnas dran par mi rigs pa'i phyir ro/ /} de dag ni bsam gtan gnyis pa nas shi 'phos pa yin na sa de na gnas pa'i tshe tshangs pa chen po smon lam 'debs pa mthong yang 'og mar skyes pa na dran pa med pa'i phyir te/ dran na ni sa 'og ma pa dag gong ma la dmigs par thal ba'i phyir ro/ / gong man gnas pa de'i tshe tshangs pa chen po'i smon lam las bdag cag skye'o zhes 'dzin pa'ang ma yin te/ de ni sa gong ma'i sems can yin pa'i phyir tshangs pa chen po la dmigs pa'i rgyu ma yin du 'dzin pa mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / srid kyang gong ma'i 'du shes yin pa'i phyir ro/ / kha cig na re bar do'i tshe sngon gyi gnas dran pa yin no zhes zer ba'ang rigs pa ma yin te/ bar do ni dus thung ba yin pas tshangs pa chen po'i yun ring por gcig pur gnas pa mi mthong ba'i phyir dang*/ mdo las/ bdag cag gis sems can 'di tshe ring zhing dus ring por gnas par mthong la zhes yun ring por gnas pa mthong bar bshad pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ bsam gtan dang por skyes pa nas de pa'i sngon gnas rjes dran skyes thob kyis sngon tshangs pa chen po smon lam 'debs pa dran pa'i phyir skyon med de/ gnyis ka'ang bsam gtan dang po'i sa par mtshungs pa'i phyir ro/ / yang na de las thos pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes rgyal po'i sras 'chad do/ / yang mdo las/ sems can gzugs can lus gcig cing 'du shes tha dad pa dag kyang yod de/ 'di lta ste 'od gsal gyi lha rnams so/ / 'di ni rnam par shes pa gnas pa gsum pa'o zhes gsungs te/

Beings with different bodies and the same discernment are those first born in the first absorption, because the {voice, clothing, and} body {of Mahābrahma} are greater and those {of his retinue} are smaller. And in terms of discernment, Mahābrahma thinks, “They arise from my desire,” {which is similar to acting as their cause,} and his retinue who are first born think, “We have arisen from the desire of Mahābrahma.” Question: How do those in the retinue of Brahma understand that they arise from the prayer of Mahābrahma? Reply: {If they obtain the mind of the second absorption, it is illogical for them to assert that they arise from Brahma, since they abandon clinging to rules and rituals that focus on Brahma as supreme. If they do not obtain it, it is illogical that they remember their former abode of the second absorption, since it is not a supreme [or accessible] object of the inferior state.} If when dying from the second absorption, they saw Mahābrahma praying for their birth when they were abiding on the second level, they would not remember that when born on the lower level. If they did remember, it would follow that those of lower level could focus on higher levels. Also, when abiding on higher levels they do not hold that “We are born from the prayers of Mahābrahma” because they are sentient beings of higher level and they are not causal focal objects for Mahābrahma, and it is impossible for him to apprehend them. If that were possible, it would be discernment of higher levels. Some say: When one is an intermediate being, one remembers one’s former abode. Reply: That is illogical, for a bardo being would not see its long and solitary life as Mahābrahma since the intermediate existence is of short duration. Objection: But a sūtra declares: We see that this sentient being had a long lifespan and endured for a long time. Reply: This explains that [the bardo being] sees that it [previously] lived for a long time. Jinaputra explains: When one is born in the first absorption, the wisdom obtained at birth, recalling former abodes, recalls the prayer of Mahābrahma. Because both are similar, both being the level of the first absorption, there is no error. Otherwise it is knowledge gained from hearsay.[700] Again, that sūtra states: Sentient beings with the same material bodies and different discernments are gods of Ābhāsvara. This is the third abode of consciousness.[701]

de la lus tha dad cing 'du shes gcig pa las bzlog pa lus gcig cing 'du shes tha dad pa ni bsam gtan gnyis pa'i lha rnams te/ lus ni 'od kyi rang bzhin du gcig pa dang kha dog dang dbyibs dang rtags kyang 'dra ba'i phyir dang*/ 'du shes ni dngos gzhi'i yid bdes skyo na nyer bsdogs kyi btang snyoms mngon du byed la/ nyer bsdogs kyi btang snyoms kyis skyo na dngos gzhi'i yid bde mngon du byed pas tha dad pa'i phyir ro/ / de lta na bsam gtan gsum pa rnams kyang der thal bar 'gyur ro zhe na/ mi 'gyur te/ yid bde ni sems g.yo bar byed pas ma zhi bas des skyo la/ bde ba ni zhi ba yin pas des mi skyo ba'i phyir ro/ / mdo sde pa ni mdo las bsam gtan gnyis par skyes nas ring du lon pa 'jig chags la mkhas pa rnams ni bskal pa 'jig pa na dang po man chad mer 'bar bas 'jigs pa med pa'i phyir dang*/ der skyes nas ring po ma lon pa 'jig chags la mi mkhas pa rnams ni 'jigs pa dang bcas par gsungs pa'i phyir 'du shes tha dad par 'dod do/ / 'di la mdo las 'od gsal gyi lha 'ba' zhig smros pa ni ya mtha' gzung bas 'od chung dang tshad med 'od kyang mtshon pa'i phyir te/ de lta ma yin na de dag rnam shes gnas pa bdun gyis ma bsdus par 'gyur ro/ / mdo las/ sems can gzugs lus gcig cing 'du shes gcig pa dag kyang yod de/ 'di lta ste dge rgyas kyi lha rnams so/ / 'di ni rnam par shes pa gnas pa bzhi pa'o/ / zhes gsungs te/

This is the reverse of having different bodies and the same discernment. “The same bodies and different discernments” refers to gods of the second absorption because their bodies in essence have the same radiance and similar [211] color, shape, and marks. Their discernments are different because when the mental satisfaction of the actual basis weakens, the equanimity of access concentration manifests, and when the equanimity of access concentration weakens, the mental satisfaction of the actual basis manifests. Objection: It would follow that also those of the third absorption would experience that. Reply: That is not so. For while mental satisfaction weakens the mind by agitating it and not pacifying it, pleasure [or bliss] does not weaken it since it is peace. Sautrāntikas assert that their discernments are different because that sūtra states: Those born in the second absorption, who have lived there long and are familiar with destruction and formation, are not terrified by the inferno [that annihilates] the first absorption and below in the eon of destruction. Those born there but who have not lived long and are not familiar with destruction and formation are scared.[702] Sūtras speaking only of the gods of Ābhāsvara also include Parīttābha and Apramāṇābha, since they refer to that stage and above. If that were not so, they would not be included in the seven abodes of consciousness. That sūtra declares: Sentient beings with the same material bodies and the same discernments are gods of Śubhakṛtsna. This is the fourth abode of consciousness.[703]

de la lus dang 'du shes gnyis ka gcig pa ni bsam gtan gsum pa'i lha rnams te/ lus ni kha dog dang dbyibs dang rtags 'dra ba'i phyir dang*/ 'du shes ni sems bde bar 'dra ba'i phyir ro/ / 'di la'ang mdo las dge rgyas 'ba' zhig smros pa ni 'og ma gnyis kyang mtshon pa'i phyir {de la 'du shes dang po ni nyon mongs can dang*/ gnyis pa ni snyoms 'jug gi dbang gis dge ba dang gsum pa ni rnam smin skyes kyi 'du shes su gcig pa ste/ gzhan du na btang snyoms kyang yod do de dag ni gzugs can gyi rnam shes gnas pa bzhin yin no/ } ro/ {de bzhin du/ } gzugs can ma yin { pa nam mkha' mtha' yas dang*/ rnam shes mtha' yas dang*/ ci yang med pa'i skye mched/} gsum po dag kyang rnam shes gnas pa yin te/ mdo las/ sems can gzugs can ma yin pa gang dag rnam pa thams cad du gzugs kyi 'du shes las yang dag par 'das te nam mkha' mtha' yas so snyam nas nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched rdzogs par byas te gnas pa'ang yod de/ 'di lta ste nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched du nye bar 'gro ba'i lha dag go / 'di ni rnam par shes pa gnas pa lnga pa'o/ /

Those having both the same bodies and [the same] discernments are gods of the third absorption because their bodies are similar in color, shape, and marks and their discernments are similar since they possess mental bliss. Also the sūtra that speaks of Śubhakṛtsna alone also represents the lower two [stages of the third absorption]. {Those [gods] have the same discernments, the first discernment is afflicted, the second is virtuous by the power of meditative attainment, the third is arisen from karmic maturation, and otherwise there is also equanimity. These are abodes of consciousness of material beings. So too,} the three nonmaterial (arūpiṇa) states — {the bases of infinite space, infinite consciousness, and nothingness} — are abodes of consciousness, for as that sūtra states: Nonmaterial [or formless] beings who correctly transcend the discernment of form in all aspects accomplish the base of infinite space through reflecting that “space is limitless” and abide there because they are gods who proceed to the base of infinite space. This is the fifth abode of consciousness.

sems can gzugs can ma yin pa gang dag rnam pa thams cad du nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched las yang dag par 'das te rnam par shes pa mtha' yas so snyam nas rnam shes mtha' yas skye mched rdzogs par byas te gnas pa'ang yod de/ 'di lta ste rnam shes mtha' yas skye mched du nye bar 'gro ba'i lha dag go / 'di ni rnam par shes pa gnas pa drug pa'o/ / sems can gzugs can ma yin pa gang dag rnam pa thams cad du rnam shes mtha' yas skye mched las yang dag par 'das te ci yang med do snyam nas ci yang med pa'i skye mched rdzogs par byas te gnas pa dag kyang yod de/ 'di lta ste ci yang med pa'i skye mched du nye bar 'gro ba'i lha dag go / 'di ni rnam par shes pa gnas pa bdun pa'o zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

Nonmaterial beings who correctly transcend the base of limitless space accomplish the base of infinite consciousness through reflecting that “consciousness is limitless” and abide there because they are gods who proceed to the base of infinite consciousness. This is the sixth abode of consciousness. Nonmaterial beings who correctly transcend the base of limitless consciousness [212] accomplish the base of nothingness through reflecting that “there is nothing at all” and abide there because they are gods who proceed to the base of nothingness. This is the seventh abode of consciousness.[704]
rnam shes gnas pa bdun lhag ma/ / de 'joms byed ldan srid rtse dang/ / 'du shes med pa'i sems can rnams/ / sems can gyi ni gnas dgur bshad/ / 6

These are the seven abodes of consciousness. The remainder function to impair consciousness. [These, along with] the summit of existence and the nondiscernment of beings, are said to be the nine abodes of sentient beings. (3:6)

de ltar na de dag ni rnam shes gnas pa zhes bya ste/ de dag tu rnam shes{ srid pa'i tshul gyis rten cing} rgyas pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te sems kyi gnas gzhan dag kyang yod pa ma yin nam ci'i phyir de dag kho na rnam shes gnas par bstan zhe na/

They are called “the seven abodes of consciousness” (vijñānasthitaya). They are called “abodes of consciousness” because consciousness {is supported and} develops in these abodes {due to beings existing there}. Question: Don’t other abodes of mind exist? Why are just those taught to be abodes of mind?

sngar smros pa de dag gi lhag ma ngan song gsum dang bsam gtan bzhi pa dang srid rtse ba rnams ni rnam par shes pa gnas pa ma yin te/ {ngan song gsum na sdug bsngal dang*/ bsam gtan bzhi pa na 'du shes med pa pa rgyu 'bras dang srid rtse na 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug gis } rnam par shes pa de 'joms par byed pa dang ldan pa'i phyir dang*/ ngan song rnams su sdug bsngal gyis 'joms pa'i phyir dang*/ bsam gtan bzhi pa na 'du shes med pa pa dang 'du shes med pa pa'i snyoms 'jug dang*/ srid rtse na 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug gis rnam shes 'joms pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yang ngan song ba ni der gnas par mi 'dod par gong du bskyod par 'dod pa'i phyir dang*/ bsam gtan bzhi pa'i so so'i skye bo rnams ni 'du shes med pa dang*/ 'phags pa rnams ni gnas gtsang mar bskyod par 'dod pa'i phyir{ dang gnas gtsang ba rnams myang 'das su bskyod par 'dod pa'i phyir} de dag rnam shes gnas pa ma yin te/ rnam par shes pa gnas pa ni gzhan na gnas pa der 'gro bar 'dod pa dang der gnas pa gzhan du bskyod par mi 'dod pa yin na de dag ni de lta ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/{ rnam shes gnas pa ni sems gsal la/} srid rtse ba sems kyi rgyu ba mi gsal ba'i phyir ro zhes 'chad do/ /

Reply: The remainder, which are distinct from those previously mentioned, are consciousnesses of the three lower rebirths, the fourth absorption, and the summit of existence (bhavāgra). They are not abodes of consciousness; they function to suppress (paribheda) consciousness because painful sensation impairs consciousness in beings of lower rebirth, the state of nondiscernment and the meditative attainment of nondiscernment impair consciousness in the fourth absorption, and the meditative attainment of cessation impairs consciousness at the summit of existence. Furthermore, it is said that such abodes are not abodes of consciousness, because beings of lower rebirths do not desire to abide there but desire to proceed to higher realms, ordinary beings of the fourth absorption desire nondiscernment, āryas desire to proceed to pristine abodes, {and those in the pristine abodes desire to proceed to nirvāṇa}. If abodes of consciousness referred to different abodes, to the desire to go there, to abiding there, and to not desiring to proceed elsewhere, then this is not so. Moreover {the abodes of consciousness are [abodes of] mental clarity, but} for the mind of the summit of existence, unclarity arises due to [subtle] mental fluctuation.
sems can gyi gnas dgu bshad pa/
yang sems can gyi gnas dgu bshad pa gang zhe na/
Question: What is the explanation of the nine abodes of sentient beings?

sngar smros pa'i rnam shes gnas pa bdun dang*/ srid pa'i rtse mo dang 'du shes med pa'i sems can rnams ni sems can gyi gnas dgu yin par mdo las bshad{ 'di dag tu sems can rnams rang dgar gnas pas so} do/ / 'di la 'du shes med pa'i sems can smros pas bsam gtan bzhi pa thams cad gzung ste/ 'du shes med pa'ang sems can gyi gnas yin na gzhan lta ci smros pa'i phyir ro/ / slob dpon 'dun bzang ni 'du shes med pa'i sems can ma gtogs pa'i bsam gtan bzhi pa gzhan rnams ni sems can gyi gnas ma yin te/ sngar rnam shes gnas pa ma yin par bshad pa ltar bsam gtan bzhi pa'i so so'i skye bo rnams ni 'du shes med par 'jug par 'dod la/ 'phags pa ni sprin med pa dang bsod nams skyes pa rnams gnas gtsang ma dang gzugs med du 'jug par 'dod cing*/ gnas gtsang ma pa rnams myang 'das su 'jug par 'dod pas de na gnas 'dod kyi blo med cing*/ de nas bskyod par 'dod pa'i blo dang ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na slob dpon gyis 'grel pa las/ gzhan gang zhe na/ ngan song rnams te zhes bshad pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/ de ni sgo tsam zhig bshad par zad do zhes 'dod do/ /

Reply: (1–7) The seven abodes of consciousness previously mentioned, (8) the summit of existence (bhavāgra), and (9) the beings devoid of discernment (āsaṃjñisattva) are said in the sūtras to be the nine abodes of sentient beings (sattvāvāsa),[705] {since sentient beings abide there according to their wishes}. “Beings devoid of discernment” mentioned here refers to all beings of the fourth absorption, because if nondiscernment is also an abode of sentient beings, then of course the others are abodes. Master Saṅghabhadra asserts that other states of the fourth absorption, except for states of beings devoid of discernment, are not abodes of sentient beings because according to the previous explanation of what are not abodes of consciousness, ordinary beings of the fourth absorption enter nondiscernment[706] and āryas enter the heaven of Anabhraka and the heaven of Puṇyaprasava, pristine abodes, and formless states. Since those [beings] of the pristine abodes desire to enter nirvāṇa, they have no desire to abide there, and [213] they possess a mind that desires to depart from there. Objection: But this contradicts the explanation of Vasubandhu, who observes in his Autocommentary: What are the others? They are the lower rebirths.[707] Reply: We assert this to be merely the start of his explanation.
gal te ngan song rnams sems can gyi gnas su ji ltar mi 'gyur zhe na/
Question: How are lower rebirths not the abode of sentient beings?
mi 'dod bzhin gnas phyir gzhan min/ / gnas pa dag ni yang bzhi ste/ / zag dang bcas pa'i phung po bzhi/ / rang gi sa pa nyid rnam shes/ / 7
Others are not, because beings do not desire to abide there. There are four extra abodes that are the four contaminated aggregates of their own level. (3:7)

de dag tu ni sems can sngon gyi las kyis mi 'dod bzhin gnas kyi rang dgar gnas pa med pa'i phyir sngar gyi dgu las gzhan ngan song ba rnams ni sems can gyi gnas min par rig par bya ste/ btson ra dang gshed ma la sogs pa sems can gyi rang dgar dga' mgur gnas pa'i gnas ma yin pa bzhin no/ / yang mdo gzhan las/ rnam par shes pa{ 'dod par} gnas pa gzugs su nye bar 'gro ba dang*/ {gzugs su } tshor ba dang{ gzugs med dang po gsum du} 'du shes dang{ srid rtser} 'du byed du nye bar 'gro ba'o zhes rnam par shes pa'i gnas pa dag ni yang bzhir gsungs te/{ rnam shes gnas pa} de dag kyang rim pa bzhin du zag pa dang bcas pa'i gzugs la sogs pa'i phung po bzhi yin la/ de yang rang gi sa pa nyid yin gyi zag med dang*/ sa gzhan ni ma yin te/ zag med ni rnam shes kyi gnyen po yin pa'i phyir dang*/ sa gzhan ni sa gzhan gyi rnam shes kyi brten du mi 'thad pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te gzugs la sogs pa kho na yin gyi rnam shes ma yin pa ci zhe na/

Reply: You should recognize that lower rebirths other than the nine preceding abodes are not abodes of sentient beings, because sentient beings do not desire to abide there. They abide there only unwillingly due to past karma. They are like a prison or a slaughterhouse and are not abodes where sentient beings abide willingly. Another sūtra says: Consciousness that abides {in the desire realm} proceeds to the form [aggregate], [it proceeds to] feeling {in the form realm}, [it proceeds to] discernment {in the first three formless states}, and it proceeds to formation {at the summit of existence}.[708] This sūtra states that there are four extra abodes of consciousness, and that these {abodes of consciousness} are respectively the four contaminated aggregates (skandha) of form and so on, which belong to their own level (svabhūmi). They are not uncontaminated because uncontaminated states are antidotes to consciousness. They do not belong to other levels because it is untenable that other levels support those consciousnesses. Question: Why are such abodes only form and so on and not consciousness itself?
'ba' zhig gnas par ma bshad do/ / bsdu na mu ni bzhi yin no/ /
Consciousness is not explained as a separate abode. If what they subsume is analyzed, there are four possibilities. (3:8ab)

rnam shes ni rnam par shes pa'i gnas par ma bshad do/ / ci ste na/ rnam shes ni gnas pa po{ yin pas rnam shes kyi ngo bo} 'ba' zhig{ ni gnas pa ma} yin pa'i phyir dang*/ gnas pa po dang gnas ni sa bon dang zhing ltar brten pa dang rten yin pa'i phyir dang*/ gcig la rten dang brten pa 'gal ba'i phyir ro/ / gal te rnam shes gnas pa bdun dang gnas pa bzhi po dag gang gis gang bsdus she na/

Reply: Consciousness (vijñāna) is not explained to be an abode of consciousness. Why? That is because {the nature of consciousness is not} a separate (kevala) {abode, since} consciousness is that which abides, and the abider and abode are like a seed and a tree that are the object supported and its support, and it is contradictory for one entity to be both the object supported and its support. Question: What do the seven abodes of consciousness subsume, what do the four abodes of consciousness subsume, and what are they subsumed by?

de dag gi bsdu ba dpyad na mu ni bzhi yin no/ / 'di ltar bdun gyis bsdus la bzhis ma bsdus pa ni rnam par shes pa gnas pa bdun du gtogs pa'i rnam shes so/{ de yang bdun ni phung po lnga'i ngo bo yin pas so/ /} bzhis bsdus la bdun gyis ma bsdus pa ni ngan song gsum dang bsam gtan bzhi pa {zag bcas/ } dang srid pa'i rtse mo pa rnams kyi rnam shes las gzhan pa'i phung po'o/ / gnyis ka yin pa ni rnam par shes pa gnas pa bdun du{ gtogs la rnam shes su ma} gtogs pa'i phung po bzhi'o/ / gnyis ka ma yin pa ni ngan song gsum dang bsam gtan bzhi pa dang srid rtse'i rnam shes dang zag pa med pa'o/ /

Reply: If what they subsume is analyzed, there are four possibilities (koṭi): (1) That subsumed by seven and not subsumed by four is consciousness belonging to the seven abodes of consciousness. {Further, these seven possess the essential nature of the five aggregates.} (2) That subsumed by four and not subsumed by seven is the four aggregates excluding consciousness of the three lower rebirths, the {contaminated} fourth absorption, and the summit of existence. (3) That which is both is the four aggregates belonging to the seven abodes of consciousness {but not belonging to consciousness}. (4) That which is neither is the consciousness of the three lower rebirths, the fourth absorption, the summit of existence, and uncontaminated states. [214]
12. Birth of Sentient Beings
sems can gyi skye ba bshad pa/
Birth processes
{sems can } da ni de rnam gzhag gis rgyas par bshad pa
ELABORATION {OF SENTIENT BEINGS} ACCORDING TO THOSE PRINCIPLES
['di] la sems can gyi skye ba dang*/ gnas pa dang*/ 'chi ba bshad pa gsum las
This has three headings: birth of sentient beings, abidance of sentient beings, and death of sentient beings.
dang po
BIRTH OF SENTIENT BEINGS
['di] la'ang
[This has two: birth processes through which beings enter birth, and their attributes]
gang du 'jug pa'i skye ba'i gnas ni
BIRTH PROCESSES THROUGH WHICH BEINGS ENTER BIRTH
der ni sgo nga las skyes sogs/ / sems can skye gnas bzhi dag tu/ / 8
Here they are the four birth processes of sentient beings, such as birth from an egg and so on. (3:8cd)

'gro ba la sogs pa'i bye brag gis tha dad pa'i khams gsum po bshad pa gang yin pa der ni sems can skye ba'i gnas bzhi dag tu rig par bya'o/ / gang zhe na sgo nga las skye ba dang*/ sogs pas gzung ba{ nang ma'i} mngal nas skye ba dang*/ {phyis 'byung ba'i dang } drod gsher{ rgyun chags} las skye ba dang*/ {mdzes par skye ba } rdzus te skye ba'i skye gnas {cig car yan lag dang nying lag skye bas rgyu gzhan gsum la mi ltos } so/ / de dag ni sems can rnams skye ba'i gzhi yin pa'i phyir gnas so/ / slob dpon gang spel ni skye gnas zhes bya ba ni sems can rnams kyi rigs yin gyi skye ba ni ma yin no/ / des na sgo nga las skyes pa'i skye gnas ni sgo nga las skyes pa'i rigs zhes bya ba'i don to/ / de bzhin du skye gnas gsum la'ang sbyar ro/ / 'di dag gi rang bzhin yang rdzus skyes ni phung po bzhi dang lnga'i rang bzhin yin la/ gzhan gsum ni phung po lnga'i rang bzhin yin no/ / thams cad kyang rnam smin dang rgyas pa'i rgyud kyi rang bzhin yin no zhes pa dang*/ skye gnas thams cad du skyes pa rnams la 'phags pa'i chos thob pa'i go skabs yod mod kyi 'phags pa'i chos thob zin pa rnams ni sgo nga dang drod gsher skyes kyi skye gnas dag tu mi skye'o zhes 'chad do/ /

Specific reincarnating beings and so on who were explained to exist in three distinct realms should here be recognized in terms of the four birth processes (yoni) of sentient beings. Question: What are they? Reply: They are birth from an egg (aṇḍaja) and so on. “And so on” refers to birth from the {mother’s} womb, {that which occurs subsequently,[709]} birth from {continuous} warmth and moisture, and {pleasant} supernatural birth, {which doesn’t rely on the other three causes for the major and minor limbs are simultaneously generated}. They are processes because they are bases for the birth of sentient beings. Master Pūrṇavardhana explains: “Birth process” refers to the type of sentient being, not the birth. Therefore the birth process of egg birth refers to the type of being born from an egg. Similarly that should also be applied to the three other birth processes. Regarding their nature, supernatural birth utilizes by nature four or five aggregates, and the other three by nature utilize five aggregates. Also, all by nature involve the stream of karmic maturation and enhancement.[710] And: Indeed, those born via any birth process have the opportunity to obtain ārya qualities, but those who have already obtained ārya qualities do not take birth through the birth process of heat and moisture.[711]

{skye gnas de dag gang bzang zhe na/} sgo nga las skye ba ni mngal nas kyang skye ba'i phyir skye gnas gnyis pa ste 'di kho na dman pa yin no/ / de bas mngal nas skye ba dang*/ de bas drod gsher las skye ba dang*/ de bas kyang rdzus te skye ba'i skye gnas bzang ngo*/ / 'gro ba gang na skye gnas du zhig yod ce na/

{Question: Which of those birth processes is best? Reply:} Because birth from an egg is also birth from a womb, egg birth alone, which involves two birth processes, is inferior. Therefore birth from the womb, birth from heat and moisture, and supernatural birth are the best birth processes. Question: What birth processes exist for what reincarnating beings?
mi dang dud 'gro rnam pa bzhi/ / dmyal ba rnams dang lha rnams dang / / srid pa bar ma rdzus te skye/ / yi dgas mngal nas skye ba'ang yin/ / 9
Humans and animals are of four types. Hell beings, gods, and intermediate beings are born supernaturally. Ghosts are born from the womb as well. (3:9)

mi dang dud 'gro rnams ni skye gnas rnam pa bzhi ga las skye ba yin te/ de la re zhig mi sgo nga las skye ba ni gnas brtan brag dang nye ba'i brag dang*/ ri dwags 'dzin gyi ma{ sa ga} 'i bu sum cu rtsa gnyis dang*/ rgyal po lnga len {gyi btsun mo lha chen la sgo nga lnga brgya skyes pa/ sgrom du bcug nas chu la bskur ba las/ } bu lnga brgya{ byung ba} rnams lta bu'o/ / mngal nas skye ba ni da ltar gyi mi rnams lta bu'o/ / drod gsher las skye ba {rgyal po bsnyen gnas pa'i spyi bo las skyes pa } ni rgyal po nga las nu dang*/ {de'i phrag pa g.yas la skyes pa } mdzes pa dang*/ {de'i g.yon las } nye mdzes dang*/ {de'i brla g.yas las/ } mdzes ldan dang*/ {de'i brla g.yon las } mdzes can dang*/ {de'i brang las skyes pa } bu mo thi ba'i phreng ba can dang*/ {a mra'i sdong po las skyes pa } a mra skyong ma la sogs pa lta bu'o/ / rdzus te skye ba ni bskal pa dang {rgyal po'i bsnyen gnas pa'i spyi bo las sokyes pa} po'i mi rnams dang*/ 'phags pa lha dang*/ mtsho skyes la sogs pa bzhin no/ / dud 'gro la skye gnas gzhan dag ni mngon du gyur la/ rdzus te skye ba ni klu dang nam mkha' lding rnams la yod par {'dod de stong spyi phud kyi 'jig rten gyi khams na klu rigs stong rgya mtsho chen po na gnas so/ / nam mkha' ldeng gi rigs stong shing shal ma li la gnas so/ / de la sgo nga las skyes pa stong dang mngal nas skyes pa stong dang*/ drod gsher las skyes pa stong dang*/ rdzus te skyes pa stong rnams so zhes } gdags pa las bshad do/ /

Reply: Humans (nara) and animals (tiryañc) are born from the four types of birth process because at times humans are (1) born from eggs, such as the elders Śaila and Upaśaila, the thirty-two sons of {Viśākha} the mother of Mṛgāra, and the five hundred sons {born} of the king of Pañcāla, {whose queen Mahādevi laid five hundred eggs in a box that was discarded in water}. (2) Birth from the womb is, for example, current human beings. (3) Birth from heat and moisture is, for example, the king Māndhātar {who was born from the crown of King Upoṣadha}, Cāru {who was born from his right shoulder}, Upacāru {who was born from his left shoulder}, Abhirūpa {who was born from his right thigh}, Cārumat {who born from his left thigh}, the girl Kapotamalinī {who was born from his chest}, or Āmrapālī {who was born from a mango tree}, and so on. [215] (4) Supernatural birth is, for example, humans of the first eon, Āryadeva, those born from a lotus, and so forth. Animals manifest other birth processes since (1) supernatural birth {is said} to exist for nāgas and garuḍas {because in the world systems of the trichiliocosm, one thousand types of nāgas abide in the great ocean and one thousand types of garuḍas abide in the śālmalī[712] forest. In that place, there are one thousand born from eggs, one thousand born from wombs, one thousand born from heat and moisture, and one thousand born supernaturally.} This is explained in Presentation on the World.[713]

dmyal ba rnams dang lha rnams dang srid pa bar ma rnams ni rdzus te skye ba 'ba' zhig yin la/ yi dwags rnams ni mngal nas skye ba'ang yin no/ / 'ang gi sgra ni phal cher rdzus te skye ba yin no zhes bsdu ba'o/ / mngal nas skye ba yod par ni yi dwags mo'i rtogs pa brjod pa las{ yi dwags mos} bdag gis mtshan mo bu lnga dang*/ / de bzhin nyin mo gzhan lnga dag /bskyed nas de dag za mod kyi/ / 'on kyang bdag ni tshim pa med/ / ces gnas brtan mo'u 'gal gyi bu la smras pas shes so/ /
gal te skye gnas dag las rdzus skyes bzang{ de lta} na srid pa tha ma pa'i byang chub sems dpa' skye ba la dbang thob pa mngal nas skye bar ston zhe na/

Hell beings (nāraka), gods (deva), and intermediate beings (antarābhava) are only born supernaturally (upapāduka). Ghosts (pretā) are born from a womb (jarāyuja) as well. The term “as well” implies that they are mainly born supernaturally. However, ghosts have birth from the womb, since in the Story of Female Ghosts {a female ghost} declares: I give birth to five sons at night and similarly five during the day. I eat them once they are born, but I get no satisfaction.[714] This was said to the elder Maudgalyāyana.
Question: If supernatural birth is best from among those birth processes, why did the bodhisattva in his final existence, in which he obtained power over birth, demonstrate birth from the womb?

Reply: He did that for the purpose of bringing the clan {of the Śakya who possess the conceit of being of good lineage} to the Dharma, for the purpose of making others enter spiritual practice through understanding that they are of the lineage of a cakravartin, to conform with the common birth process of humans, and for the purpose of generating delight in disciples that “we who are born as humans may obtain this feat.”[715] Others also say: It is to stop tīrthikas, naked ascetics, sons or daughters of the clan, and so on from conceiving the Buddha to be a vilifiable illusion, {since he would possess no lineage or relics}. Therefore he leaves physical relics, {but this would be impossible for those born supernaturally, since they leave no corpse}. Therefore, from among all birth processes, supernatural birth is the most common because it exists for both {god and hell} reincarnating beings, the {other} three states, and all intermediate existences.
da ni gang gis 'jug pa'i bar srid
INTERMEDIATE BEINGS WHO ENTER DUE TO THAT
'dir gang 'chi dang skye ba yi/ / srid pa'i bar du 'byung ba'o/ / bgrod pa'i yul du ma phyin phyir/ / srid pa bar ma byung ba min/ / 10
Here the intermediate existence occurs between death existence and birth existence. It is not called “fully developed” because it has not attained its destination. (3:10)
['di] la'ang gsum las
This has three headings: {first} nature, then proof, and then establishing that through scripture.
{dang po } ngo bo ni
NATURE

'dir phung po { lnga'i rgyun} gang zhig {yul gzhan du skye bar bya ba'i phyir sngar gyi} 'chi srid dang gang du skye ba'i srid pa gnyis kyi bar du 'byung ba de ni srid pa bar ma'o/ / de ni bgrod par bya ba'i yul rnam par smin pa'i phung po yongs su rdzogs par ma phyin pa'i phyir srid pa bar ma la byung ba'i srid pa zhes bya ba ni min te/ byung ba ni sngon dus kyi srid pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ { dbye na khams kyi gnyis dang*/ sas lnga dang*/ gnas gzhan gyi so bdun dang rab 'bring gis sangs rgyas rang rgyal 'khor los sgyur ba gsum de las gzhan dang bzhi yin no gsung ngo*/}

Here the intermediate existence (antarābhava) is {the continuum of the five} aggregates that occurs between both the death (mṛtyu) existence and the birth existence (upapattibhava). The intermediate existence is not called a “fully developed” existence because it has not completely attained the maturational aggregates that are its destination (gamyadeśa), since the fully developed existence is the prior existence. {If they are classified, there are four: (1) two of the realms, (2) five by level, (3) thirty-seven of other abodes, and (4) those supreme and intermediate beings other than the three: buddhas, pratyekabuddhas, and cakravartins}.
gnyis pa sgrub byed ni
PROOF

phal chen pa'i sde pa dag ni 'chi srid nas skye srid du 'jug pa'i bar na ni srid pa med de/ des na bar chad pa kho na las skye ba'i srid par 'jug ste/ bcom ldan 'das kyis bram ze rgan po'i dbang du mdzad nas/ bram ze na tshod khyer zin rga ba dang*/ / na ba yin te gshin rje'i drung du phyin/ / bar na khyod kyi gnas kyang yod min zhing*/ / khyod kyi lam rgyags kyang ni yod ma yin/ / zhes srid pa gnyis kyi bar na gnas med par bshad pa'i phyir dang*/ bdud sun 'byin byed ces bya bas sangs rgyas 'od srung gi nyan thos mkhas mgu zhes bya ba'i klad du khu tshur bsnun pa las des ma rangs pa'i skad phyung ba dang skad cig de nyid la rang gi lus kho nas sems can dmyal ba chen po mnar med par lhung bar bshad pa'i phyir dang*/ gzhan yang mdo las/ mtshams med pa lnga'i las gang dag byas shing bsams nas de ma thag tu dmyal ba dag tu skye'o zhes gsungs pa'i phyir zhes 'dod do/ / de ni 'thad pa ma yin pas

The Mahāsāṃghika school asserts: there is no intermediate existence to be inserted between the death existence and birth existence because one enters the birth existence without interruption. For as the Bhagavan said to a brahman elder: [216] Brahman, completing the stages of life is to age and be diseased, for one approaches the Lord of Death. Between [birth and death] there is no abode, and as for provisions they do not exist.[716] This explains that there is no abode between these two existences. Also the māra called Dūṣin struck the head of a śrāvaka student of Buddha Kaśyapa called Vidura with a clenched fist, causing him to utter a painful cry, and at that moment [Dūṣin] fell into the great hell of Avīci.[717] Again, a sūtra reveals: Through committing and accumulating one of the five heinous actions, one is immediately born in the hells.[718] Reply: That is untenable.

'bru yi rgyun dang chos mthun phyir/ / srid pa chad las byung ba min/ / gzugs brnyan ma grub phyir pa dang / / mi 'dra'i phyir na dpe ma yin/ / 11
gcig na lhan cig gnyis med phyir/ / rgyun min phyir gnyis las byung phyir/ /

Existence does not arise if it is interrupted because it is similar to the continuum of rice. A reflection is not an example because it is not established, because it does not conform, (3:11)
because both do not exist in the same place simultaneously, because it is not a continuum, and because it is derived from both. (3:12ab)

skye ba'i srid pa de ni 'chi srid dang gnyis kyi bar chad pa las 'byung ba min te zhes bya bas bar srid las byung ba yin no zhes bsgrub par bya'o/ / gang gi phyir zhe na/ sa bon las myu gu dang de las sdong bu la sogs pa bar ma chad par 'byung ba'i 'bru'i rgyun dang rgyun gyi 'bras bu nyid du chos mthun pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di ni rtags dang dpe cig car du ston pa'i ngag ste 'bru'i rgyun bzhin zhes bya ba ni dpe'o/ / de dang chos mthun pa ni snga ma'i phung po'i rgyun gyi 'bras bu yin pa'o des na gang zhig rgyun gyi 'bras bu yin pa de ni snga ma'i rgyun ma chad pa las skyes pa'i 'bras bu yin te 'bru'i rgyun bzhin no/ / skye ba'i srid pa'ang rgyun gyi 'bras bu yin no zhes rgyu sngon du song ba nyid du sgrub pa'i 'bras bu'i rtags yin no/ / gal te bar ma chad pa yin mod kyi bar srid ni mi 'grub ste/ 'chi srid kyi rjes nyid du skad cig ma gzhan gyis bar ma chad par skye srid 'byung ba'i phyir ro zhe na/ de ni 'thad pa ma yin te/ 'di nas shi 'phos nas mnar med dang lha'i gnas la sogs pa yul thag ring por skye ba rnams la skad cig ma tsam la 'gre ba mi rigs pa'i phyir ro/ / gang du shi ba'i yul de nyid du yul gzhan dang ris gzhan gyi srid pa 'grub pa'ang ma yin te/ 'gro ba rnams yul la sogs pa 'chol bar thal ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir 'di nas shi 'phos nas skye srid du sbyong ba'i phung po'i rgyun ni bar srid yin no/ / gal te yul dus kyis bar du chod pa las kyang 'bras bu 'byung ba mthong ste/ skyes bu'i byad bzhin las me long la sogs par gzugs brnyan 'byung ba bzhin no/ /de'i phyir rtags 'di ma nges pa yin no zhe na/

Therefore it is said that birth existence does not arise if [the mindstream] is interrupted (vicchinna) after the death existence, and this proves that [birth existence] arises after the intermediate existence. Question: Why? Reply: Because it is similar to the continuum of rice (vrīhisaṃtāna) and its resultant continuum, where the sprout uninterruptedly arises from its seed, the plant uninterruptedly arises from the sprout, and so on. This syllogism[719] demonstrates a reason and an example simultaneously, where “like the continuum of rice” is the example. An instance compatible with that is the result of the continuum of earlier [moments of the] aggregates. Therefore that compatible with the continuum is the result generated without interruption of its earlier continuum, like the continuum of rice. Also “birth existence is a resultant continuum” is a reason of result that establishes the prior existence of its cause. Objection: If indeed it were uninterrupted, the intermediate existence would not be established, because with the passing of another moment, the birth existence would uninterruptedly occur immediately after the death existence. Reply: That is unacceptable because it would be illogical to proceed from death here to birth in a distant place, such as the hell of Avīci or the god abodes and so on, in just one moment. A birth existence of a different abode and different type is not established at the place of death, for it would follow that reincarnating beings and places would mix chaotically. Therefore the intermediate existence is the continuum of the aggregates that connects death existence to birth existence. Objection: It is seen that a result occurs even though it is separated from its cause by place and time, just as a reflection in a mirror arises from the shape of a being. Therefore your reason is indeterminate.

me long gi nang du ni gzugs brnyan gyi gzugs ma grub pa'i phyir 'khrul pa'i dpe ma yin {zhing rtags grub } te/ yul gcig na dus lhan cig tu me long dang gzugs brnyan gyi gzugs gnyis med pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di ltar me long las tha dad pa'i gzugs brnyan ni ma grub ste/ me long gi yul las tha dad par ma dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ me long gi yul na yod na'ang rdul phran rnams thogs bcas ma yin par thal ba'i phyir ro/ / me long nyid byad bzhin gyi rnam pa can du skyes so zhes bya ba'ang mi rigs te/ zur na gnas pas kyang de de ltar du mthong bar thal ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir gzugs brnyan ni 'ga' zhig gi 'bras bu nyid du ma grub ste/ rkyen gyi stobs kyis med bzhin du snang ba'i phyir sgra brnyan la sogs pa bzhin no/ / rnam pa gcig tu na gzugs brnyan grub tu zin kyang rgyun gyi 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir zhes bya ba'i rtags dang mi 'dra ba'i phyir na 'khrul pa'i dpe ma yin te/ gzugs brnyan ni byad bzhin gyi rgyun gyi 'bras bu min pa'i phyir dang*/ byad bzhin dang me long gnyis las 'byung ba'i phyir dang*/ skye srid ni bar srid kyi phung po'i rgyun gcig pu'i 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / des na 'di skad du gzugs brnyan ma grub pa'i phyir ram/ grub kyang byad bzhin gyi rgyun gyi 'bras bu ma yin pa'i phyir rtags khyad par ba ma zhugs pas ma nges pa'i yul ma yin no zhes bstan pa yin no/ / skye srid bar srid gcig pu las skyes pa zhes bya ba ni gtso bo'i rgyu'i dbang du mdzad pa yin te/ mngal nas skye ba dag bar do dang phyi'i khu khrag la sogs pa las kyang skye ba'i phyir dang*/ khu khrag la sogs pa gtso bo'i rgyu yin no zhes bya ba'ang rigs pa ma yin te/ rdzus te skye ba rnams la de med kyang skye ba'i phyir ro/ / des na rigs pas srid pa bar ma yod pa nyid du shes so/ /

Reply: This is erroneous. A reflection (pratibimba) is not an example because it is not established (asiddha) in the mirror, but {that reason is established} because both the mirror and the form that is reflected do not exist in the same place simultaneously. A reflection distinct from the mirror is not established because it is not observed to be distinct from the object in the mirror, and if it existed as the object in the mirror, in consequence its atoms would not be impeded [by the mirror]. Also it would be illogical to state [217] that the mirror possesses the aspect of shape because in consequence [the shape] would be seen to abide in one part [of the mirror]. Therefore the reflection is not established as the result of some [substantial continuum,] because it appears through the power of conditions like an echo and so on, as if nonexistent. From another perspective, though the reflection has been established because it does not conform with the reason “because it is a result of the continuum,” it is not an erroneous example. That is because the reflection is not a result of the continuum (saṃtāna) of its shape because it is derived from both the shape and the mirror, and because the birth existence is the result of the same continuum of aggregates as the intermediate existence. Thus it is said that because a reflection is not established in the mirror, or because, though established, it is not the result of the continuum of the shape, it does not apply to this specific reason, and this reason is therefore not indeterminate. Stating that the birth existence is derived from the intermediate existence alone is from the perspective of the main cause, because birth from the womb is birth from the intermediate state as well as from the external conditions of semen and blood and so on. But it is illogical to state that semen, blood, and so on are the main cause because those who are born supernaturally are born without those. Thus one should understand through logic that the intermediate existence exists.
lung gis bsgrub pa ni
ESTABLISHING THAT THROUGH SCRIPTURE
mgur nas gsungs phyir yod dri za/ / lngar gsungs 'gro mdo las kyang grub/ / 12
They exist because they are mentioned in songs, as gandharvas, in the sūtra stating five, and the Sūtra on Progress. (3:12cd)

srid pa bdun pa'i mdo las/ srid pa ni bdun te/ dmyal ba'i srid pa dang*/ dud 'gro'i srid pa dang*/ yi dwags kyi srid pa dang*/ lha'i srid pa dang*/ mi'i srid pa dang*/ las kyi srid pa dang*/ srid pa bar ma'o zhes ston pa'i mgur nyid nas dngos su gsungs pa'i phyir bar srid yod par grub bo/ / gal te mdo de mi 'don no zhe na/ 'o na mngal du 'jug pa'i mdo la sogs pa las/ gnas gsum mngon du gyur pa las ma'i mngal du bu 'chags par 'gyur te/ gsum gang zhe na/ ma rung zhing zla mtshan dang ldan pa dang*/ pha ma chags par gyur cing phrad pa dang*/ dri za yang nye bar gnas par gyur na'o zhes dri za gsungs shing dri za ni srid pa bar ma yin pa'i phyir te/ ci ste de yang dri za zhes ni mi 'don gyi/ phung po zhig pa{'i med dgag gcig gsar du } nye bar gnas par gyur na'o zhes 'don to zhe na/

The Sūtra Teaching Seven Existences declares: There are seven existences: hell existence, animal existence, ghost existence, god existence, human existence, karmic existence, and intermediate existence.[720] Therefore intermediate beings exist because they are explicitly mentioned in the songs (kaṇṭhoktas) [or chants]. Objection: That sūtra does not mean that. Reply: The Sūtra Taught to Ānanda on Entry to the Womb records: A son is formed in the mother’s womb through actualizing three states. What are the three states? (1) A female suitable to be a mother exists and she is fertile, (2) the parents have desire for each other and join in sexual union, and (3) the gandharva abides nearby.[721] When this sūtra mentions “gandharva,” gandharva is the intermediate existence. Objection: The term “gandharva” here does not mean “intermediate existence” but that {a nonimplicative negation of} the disintegrated aggregates[722] {newly} abides nearby.
