de lta na rta len gyi bu'i mdo las/ bcom ldan 'das kyis bram ze rta len gyi bu la/ rta len gyi bu khyod kyis mchos brang la dri za nye bar gnas pa gang yin pa de rgyal rigs sam/ bram ze'am/ rje'u rigs sam/ dmangs rigs sam/ 'on te shar phyogs nas 'ongs pa zhig gam/ 'on te lho dang nub dang byang nas 'ongs pa zhig shes sam zhes gsungs pa'i phyir te/ phung po zhig pa la rigs dang phyogs kyi brtag pa dang*/ de ni 'ong bar yang mi 'thad pa'i phyir ro/ / lung phran tshegs las/ dga' bo pha ma chags par gyur cing phrad pa dang*/ ma yang rung bar gyur cing zla mtshan dang ldan pa dang*/ dri za yang nye bar gnas par gyur cing 'jug par 'dod na ste/ dga' bo dri za zhes bya ba de ni srid pa bar ma pa'i sems can gyi tshig bla dgas yin no zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'on te de yang kho bo cag mi 'don no zhe na/

Reply: The Āśvalāyana Sūtra states: The Bhagavan said to the brahman Āśvalāyana: “Āśvalāyana, do you know whether the gandharva who abides near the altar is a brahman, kśatriya, vaiśya, śūdra, or one coming from the east, or the south, west or north?”[723] That is stated because it is unsuitable to investigate the caste or position of the disintegrated aggregates or to state that they have come [here]. It is said in the Kṣudraka Collection: Nanda, when the parents desire each other and join in sexual union and the mother is capable and fertile and the gandharva abides nearby, [218] it enters that union. Nanda, “gandharva” is a term of convenience to indicate the sentient being who is an intermediate existence.[724] Objection: But we don’t say this.

'o na phyir mi 'ong ba lngar gsungs pa'i mdo las shes te/ bcom ldan 'das kyis phyir mi 'ong ba ni lnga ste/ bar ma do dang*/ skyes nas dang*/ mngon par 'du byed pa med pa dang*/ mngon par 'du byed pa dang bcas par yongs su mya ngan las 'da' ba dang*/ gong du 'pho ba'o zhes gsungs pa'i bar ma dor mya ngan las 'da' ba ni srid pa bar ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te de yang khams bar ma'am bar ma do zhes bya ba'i lha dag cig yin no zhe na/ de lta na skyes nas la sogs pa'ang lha dag cig yin par thal bar 'gyur ro/ / gzhan yang skyes bu dam pa'i 'gro ba bdun bstan pa'i mdo las gzhags ma'i me chung ngu mngon par grub bzhin du 'chi ba dang*/ lcags kyi tshwa tshwa gnam du yar bzhin du 'chi ba dang*/ lcags kyi tshwa tshwa gnam du yar nas sa la ma lhung ba nyid du 'chi bar 'gyur ba lta bu'i dpe gsum gyis mtshon nas bar ma dor mya ngan las 'da' ba la myur ba dang*/ myur ba ma yin pa dang*/ yun ring mo zhig na yongs su mya ngan las 'da' ba gsum du phye nas skyes mya ngan las 'da' ba la sogs pa bzhi ste skyes bu dam pa'i 'gro ba bdun gsungs pa'i phyir yang grub ste/ khams bar ma dor myur ba la sogs pa ni skyes nas mya ngan las 'da' ba la sogs pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: Still, that is understood from the sūtra stating that there are five nonreturners, because the Bhagavan said: Nonreturners are five: those attaining nirvāṇa (1) in the intermediate state, (2) from birth, (3) without application, (4) with application, and (5) through relocating to higher level.[725] It is the intermediate being that attains nirvāṇa in the intermediate state. Objection: These are the same as the gods called “those of the intermediate realms” or “those of the intermediate states.” Reply: If that were so, in consequence they would be gods from birth and so on. Again, that is also established because the Sūtra Teaching the Seven Ways of Progress of a Holy Being[726] differentiates three modes of attaining nirvāṇa in the intermediate state — (1) swiftly, (2) less swiftly, and (3) slowly — represented by the three examples such as (1) dying like a brief spark on a wick, (2) dying like an iron spark that rises in space, and (3) dying like an iron spark that rises in space and falls to the ground. Also it teaches (4–7) nonreturners attaining nirvāṇa from birth and so on.[727] Those gods of the intermediate realm who attain nirvāṇa swiftly and so forth are nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa from birth and so on.

gzhan yang kyang zhes pas de lta ma yin na gzugs med du'ang bar ma dor myang 'das gsung bar 'gyur ba zhig na nyan thos kyi rnam par bshad pa'i sdom gyi tshigs su bcad pa nyi shu pa las spel ma mdzad pas/ bsam gtan dag gis bcu tshan bzhi/ / gzugs med dag gis bdun tshan gsum/ / 'du shes kyis ni drug tshan du/ / mdzad nas tshoms su yang dag bsdebs/ / zhes bsam gtan re re la gnas gzhan gsum gsum dang*/ lngar bshad pa'i bar ma dor mya ngan las 'da' ba nas gong du 'pho ba'i bar rnam pa lnga dang*/ 'chi ba med pa'i dbyings la sems gtod pa dang*/ sems rnam par grol ba zhes bya ba bcu bcu dang*/ gzugs med dang po gsum la bar ma dor mya ngan las 'da' ba ma gtogs pa bzhi bzhi dang*/ gnas gzhan tha dad med pa'i ris gcig dang*/ 'chi ba med pa'i dbyings la sems gtod pa dang*/ sems rnam par grol ba bdun bdun dang*/ 'du shes med 'du shes med min la gong du 'pho ba ma gtogs pa drug gsungs pas kyang grub ste/ de la 'chi ba med pa ni mya ngan las 'das pa dang*/ sems rnam par grol ba ni zag pa las grol ba'i ye shes te lhag bcas lhag med kyi myang 'das yin par mngon no/ / des na gzugs khams su bar ma dor mya ngan las 'da' ba gsungs la/ gzugs med du ma gsungs pa'i phyir yang bar srid yod par shes {rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las kyang*/ shi 'phos nas sems dang sems byung rten med pa rnams ni yul gzhan du phyin mi srid pa'i phyir dang*/ rnam par 'khrul pa tsam yin pas brag cha lta bur mi rung*/ ma 'gags pa'i phyir gzugs brnyan lta bur yang mi rung ngo*/ / med pa'i phyir dmigs pa 'dzin pa lta bur yang mi rung ste/ gang gi phyir dpe de dag mi rung ba de'i phyir bar ma do'i srid pa yod par rig par bya'o zhes gsungs so } so/

Again, if the term “also” were to refer not to that but to attaining nirvāṇa in the intermediate state in the formless realm, then the twentieth verse of the Śrāvaka Exposition composed in verse and prose explains: The absorptions are four times ten. The formless states are three times seven. Discernment is sixfold. These are properly collated in a single category.[728] In each [of the four] absorptions there are ten each: (1–3) three individual abodes, (4–8) five types, from attaining nirvāṇa in the intermediate state previously explained up to relocating to a higher level, (9) entrusting one’s mind to the sphere of the deathless, and (10) the liberated mind. In each of the first three formless states, there are seven each: (1–4) the four types of attaining nirvāṇa except for attaining nirvāṇa in the intermediate state, (5) one type of nondistinct individual abode, (6) entrusting one’s mind to the sphere of the deathless, and (7) the liberated mind. There are six [in the summit of existence]: (1–4) the four ways of attaining nirvāṇa except for relocating to a higher level from neither discernment nor nondiscernment, (5) the deathless state, which is nirvāṇa, and (6) the liberated mind that is transcendent wisdom liberated from the contaminants. These manifest as nirvāṇa with remainder and without remainder. Therefore, because attaining nirvāṇa in the intermediate state is stated for the form realm and not for the formless realm, [219] one should understand that the intermediate state exists. {The Compendium of Ascertainment also states: It is not possible for those who lack a basis of minds and mental factors to proceed to another place after death. But since they are merely illusory, [bardo beings] are unreal like an echo. Because they are not obstructed, they are unreal like a reflection. Because they lack [concrete] existence, they are unreal like an apparition. For the [same] reason that these examples [exist but] are unreal, bardo beings are recognized to exist.[729]}

bram ze la bar na gnas med par bshad pa ni skye ba 'di dang ngan song gi bar na mtho ris kyi gnas med par bshad pa yin la/ bdud sun 'byin byed me 'bar bzhin pa'i lus kyis dmyal bar song ba ni mthong ba'i chos la lus 'di la me 'bar te shi nas bar srid nas dmyal bar skye bar gsungs pa la dgongs pa yin no/ / {de yang skyes nas myong 'gyur skye ba de nyid du smin pa med pa'i phyir ro } mtshams med pa lnga'i las gang dag byas shing bsags nas de ma thag tu dmyal ba dag tu skye'o zhes gsungs pa ni skye ba gzhan gyis bar ma chod pa'i dbang du mdzad nas gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

The statement “brahmans do not have intermediate abidance” means that between this life and the lower rebirths they do not abide in higher rebirth. The statement “the māra called Dūṣin fell into hell with a body like blazing fire” refers to his body blazing with fire in the present life and then, after death and the intermediate state, being born in hell. {Further, karma to be experienced after rebirth does not mature in that birth.} The statement “After committing and accumulating any of the five heinous actions, you are instantly born in hell”[730] is stated from the perspective of taking birth in hell uninterrupted by any other birth.
gnyis pa khyad par gyi chos
Attributes of birth
['di] la khyad par gyi chos rgyas par bshad pa dang*/ skye gnas su 'jug pa'i tshul gnyis las
This has two headings: elaboration of attributes, and how birth states are entered.
dang po ni
ELABORATION OF ATTRIBUTES
de ni 'phen pa gcig pa'i phyir/ / sngon dus srid 'byung sha tshugs can/ / de ni 'chi ba'i sngon rol te/ / skye ba'i skad cig phan chad do/ / 13
It has the appearance of the prior existence because it shares the same projecting karma. [The prior existence] takes place prior to death existence after the moment of birth existence. (3:13)

yang gal te bar srid gang du skye bar 'gyur ba'i sha tshugs can yin na/ 'o na 'dzam bu'i gling nas 'og min du skye ba'i bar srid 'dzam bu'i gling du 'grub pa'i skabs med par 'gyur te/ bar srid ni gang du shi ba der 'grub pa yin pa la 'og min pa'i lus dpag tshad khri drug stong ba yin pa'i phyir dang*/ gzugs khams pa'i bar srid lus rdzogs par 'grub pa'i phyir dang*/ 'dzam bu'i gling la ni dpag tshad drug stong dang phyed dang bzhi las med pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ nam mkha' yangs shing rten 'od ltar dang bas 'gar yang thogs pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/ / de'i phyir kun las btus las kyang gang du skye bar 'gyur ba de'i byad gzugs so zhes bshad do/ / de'i kha dog ni lung phran tshegs las/ de yang kha dog bzang po dang ngan pa rnam pa gnyis te/ sems can dmyal ba rnams kyi srid pa bar ma ni kha dog ngan pa dper na sdong po 'tshig pa lta bu'o/ / dud 'gro'i skye gnas su song ba rnams kyi srid pa bar ma ni kha dog du ba lta bu'o/ / yi dwags rnams kyi ni kha dog chu lta bu'o/ / mi rnams dang lha rnams kyi ni srid pa bar ma ni kha dog gser lta bu'o/ / gzugs na spyod pa'i lha rnams kyi ni dkar po'o zhes pa dang*/ kun las btus las kyang*/ mi dge ba byed pa'i bar mdo'i srid pa mngon par grub pa ni dper na phyar ba nag po'am mtshan mo mun pa mun nag tu snang ba lta bu'o/ / dge ba byed pa ni dper na snam bu dkar po'am zla ba'i 'od dang bcas pa'i mtshan mor snang ba lta bu'o zhes bshad do/ / 'o na byang chub sems dpa' don thams cad grub pa glang po che thal kar mche ba drug dang ldan par yum gyi rmang lam du snang ba dang*/ slob dpon chos ldan rab 'byor gyis kyang*/ glang chen dkar po mche ba drug ldan pa/ / rkang bzhi mdzes dang ldan par zhal bzhes nas/ / drang srong gnas shes pa ni ji bzhin du/ / yum gyi lhums kyi gnas su zhugs par gyur/ / zhes gsungs pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/

Objection: If the intermediate existence has the appearance of the being it shall take birth as, then the intermediate existence of one to be born in Akaniṣṭha from Jambudvīpa would have no opportunity to be established in Jambudvīpa, because the intermediate existence is established where a being dies and a body of Akaniṣṭha measures 60,000,000 yojanas, the intermediate existence of the form realm is completely established, and the earth measures no more than 6,350 yojanas. Reply: Master Pūrṇavardhana notes: Since space is broad, supportive, and clear like light, it has no impediment whatsoever.[731] Therefore the Compendium of Abhidharma also explains: It has the physical shape of the beings where it is to be born.[732] [220] Regarding its color, the Kṣudraka Collection declares: Further, the color [of an intermediate existence] has two types: good and bad. The intermediate existence of a hell being has a bad color like burned wood. The intermediate existence of one proceeding to the birth state of an animal has a color like smoke. That of a ghost has a color like water. That of a human or god has a color like gold. That of a god of the form realm is white.[733] Also the Compendium of Abhidharma states: The intermediate existence actualized through committing nonvirtue is like a black cloth cover or that which appears darkly in the blackness of night. That actualized through committing virtue it is like white cloth or that which appears in a moonlit night.[734] Objection: Now, that contradicts the statement that the all-accomplishing bodhisattva [Siddhārtha] appeared in a dream of his mother [Mahāmāya] as a six-tusked elephant, and also it contradicts Master Dharmasubhūti, who said: It is said that the handsome white elephant who possessed six tusks and four legs entered the womb of his mother consciously, as a rishi enters the forest.[735]

yum gyi rmang lam ni rmi lam gyi rnam pa nyid yin pa'i phyir dang*/ slob dpon rta dbyangs kyis kyang rmang lam dang rjes su mthun par mdzad pa'i phyir te/ dper na ma ga d+ha bzang mo'i rtogs pa brjod pa las/ rgyal po kri kris glang po che lus thon nas mjug ma skar khung la thogs pa dang*/ khron pas skom pa ma rnyed pa'i mi'i rjes bsnyegs nas nga la 'thung zhes zer ba dang*/ phye dang mu tig mnyam por brje ba dang*/ tsan+dan gor shir sha dang shing phal pa mnyam por brje ba dang*/ dge 'dun gyi kun dga' rwa ba dang skyed mos tshal chom rkun pas longs spyod pa dang*/ glang po che'i phrug gus spos kyi glang po che skod pa dang*/ spre'u zhig rang gi rgyab mi gtsang pas gos par gyur pa de spre'u gzhan la bkod par byed pa dang*/ spre'u gcig gis gcig la dbang bskur ba dang*/ mi bco brgyad ras yug gcig la brtsad pas thams cad kyis ras yug re re thob nas gcig shul du lus pa dang*/ skye bo phal po che 'thab pa zhes bya ba'i rmi lam bcu shAkya'i rgyal po'i nyan thos kyi rnam par thar pa'i mtshan ma nye bar shar bar gsungs pa bzhin no/ / de'i phyir byang chub sems dpa'i bar srid kyang gzhon nu thor bu mtshan dang dpe byad kyis brgyan pa yin la/ mi gzhan rnams {glang po khron pa phye dang tsan dan tshal glang phrug sprel gnyis ras yug 'thab mo 'os zhes pa }kyis ni lo lnga'am drug gi tshad du yod cing*/ gzugs khams pa'i lha rnams kyi ni lus rdzogs pa dang*/ ngo tsha shes pa shas che bas gos dang bcas pa yin la/ byang chub sems dpa' dang*/ dge slong ma dkar mo ni 'dod khams pa yin yang gos dang bcas pa yin no/ / 'dod khams na srid pa bar ma gzhan dag ni ngo tsha med pa shas che ba gcer bu yin no/ / dran pa nyer gzhag las rab tu tsha ba dang mnar med kyi bar srid ni tshe lo brgyad khri bzhi stong thub pa'i byis pa lo brgyad lon pa'i tshad du gsungs so/ / gal te srid pa bar ma sngon dus kyi srid pa 'byung bar 'gyur ba'i rnam pa can yin na sngon dus kyi srid pa nyid gang zhe na/

Reply: The dream of the mother has just the aspect of a dream, and Master Aśvaghoṣa also asserted that this conformed to a dream. For example, the Story of Sumāgadha relates: King Kṛkin dreamed that (1) a body of an elephant passed through a window but its tail was caught, (2) a well in a drought chased a man, saying, “Drink me,” (3) pearls and sand were exchanged as if equal, (4) gośīrṣa[736] sandalwood and ordinary wood were exchanged as if equal, (5) thieves appropriated and utilized a Saṅgha grove, (6) an elephant calf drove away an incense elephant, (7) a monkey covered with filth wiped it on other monkeys, (8) a monkey crowned another monkey, (9) eighteen men tore up a single cloth, each obtained a piece of cloth, and yet one piece remained, and (10) many beings fought among themselves.[737] These ten dreams {of an elephant, well, sand, sandalwood, grove, elephant calf, two monkeys, cloth, and fighting[738]} were stated as the dawning of the signs of liberation of śrāvaka disciples of the king of the Śākyas.[739] The intermediate existence of the bodhisattva is adorned with the signs and features of youth. For other humans the intermediate existence appears to be that of a five- or six-year-old child, and those of the gods of the form realm have a fully developed body that is clothed, since they possess a strong sense of shame. The intermediate existences of bodhisattvas and the white bhikṣuṇī[740] have clothes even though they are desire-realm beings. [221] The intermediate existences of others in the desire realm are naked since they predominantly engage in shameless acts. The Foundations of Mindfulness Sūtra mentions that intermediate-state beings of the hells of Pratāpana and Avīci appear as a children of eight years whose life endures for 84,000 years.[741] Question: If an intermediate existence comes to possess the appearance of a prior existence, what is a prior existence?

sngon dus kyi srid pa de ni 'chi ba'i srid pa'i sngon rol gyi srid pa yin te/ skye ba'i srid pa'i skad cig ma phan chad kyi nyer len gyi phung po lnga'i rgyun nyid do/ / des na srid pa bzhi las bar srid dang sngon dus kyi srid pa ni bshad zin la/ skye ba'i srid pa ni 'gro ba rnams su nying mtshams sbyor ba'i skad cig ma'o/ / sngon dus kyi srid pa ni de phan chad skyes nas ma shi'i bar gyi phung po lnga'i rgyun no/ / 'chi ba'i skad cig ma tha ma ni 'chi ba'i srid pa yin te/ gal te sems can gzugs can dag gi nang du skye na gang gi 'og tu bar srid 'byung ba'o/ / des na skye srid dang 'chi srid gnyis ni skad cig ma dang*/ srid pa gzhan gnyis ni rgyun yin no/ / de yang 'das pa ni byung ba yin la/ srid pa bar ma ni 'byung bar 'gyur ba'i sngon dus kyi srid pa'i cha byad can yin no zhes shes par bya'o/ /

Reply: The prior existence takes place prior to the death (maraṇa) existence. It is the continuum of the appropriated aggregates after the moment (kṣaṇa) of birth existence (upapattibhava).[742] Thus, from among the four existences, intermediate existence and prior existence have been explained. Birth existence is the moment of linkage as a reincarnating being. Prior existence is the continuum of aggregates from conception until death. The last moment of death is death existence. If one is to be conceived among material beings, the intermediate existence will occur after that. Therefore both birth existence and death existence last one moment and the other two existences constitute continua. Moreover, one should understand that when the past [death existence] has occurred and the intermediate existence is arising, it possesses the appearance of the prior existence that will arise.
rigs mthun lha mig dag pas mthong / / las kyi rdzu 'phrul shugs dang ldan/ / dbang po kun tshang thogs med ldan/ / mi zlo de ni dri za'o/ / 14

They are seen by similar type and pure divine eye. They possess the energy of supernatural power due to karma. They are complete in all faculties and unimpeded. They cannot change. They are called “smell eaters.” (3:14)

srid pa bar ma de yang lha la sogs pa'i srid pa bar mar ris mthun pa dang*/ lha'i mig rnam par dag pa bsgoms pa las byung ba rnams kyis mthong gi {bar srid 'di } shin tu dang bas skyes nas thob pa la sogs pa gzhan gyis ni ma yin no/ / de'i phyir kun las btus las kyang skal ba mnyam pa'i sems can rnams kyang mthong ngo zhes bshad do/ / de la lha'i mig rnam par dag pa ni don rgyas pa'i chos kyi rnam grangs las 'byung ba'i the tshom dang*/ yid la mi byed pa dang*/ lus kyi gnas ngan len dang*/ rmugs pa dang gnyid dang rgod pa dang*/ brtson 'grus brtsam drags pa dang*/ sems ya ya bo dang*/ bag tsha ba dang*/ 'du shes sna tshogs dang*/ smra ba mang ba dang*/ ha cang sgom drags pa zhes bya ba'i skyon bcu gcig dang bral ba'o/ / kha cig na re ris mthun pa dang*/ de yang lha'i bar srid kyis 'gro ba lnga ga'i bar srid mthong ba nas mi dang yi dwags dang dud 'gro'i bar srid kyis bzhi dang gsum dang gnyis dang dmyal ba'i bar srid kyis dmyal ba'i bar srid kho na mthong bas gong ma gong ma'i srid pa bar ma dang{ dman pa'i yul mchog min par bsam pa'o} lha'i mig rnam par dag pa gsum gyis mthong ngo zhes zer ro/ /

Again, intermediate beings, such as the intermediate beings of gods and so on, are seen by those of similar type (sajāti) and by the pure divine eye (divyākṣi) derived from meditation. {Intermediate beings,} who are completely diaphanous, obtain this capacity through birth and so on and not by other methods. Therefore the Compendium of Abhidharma also explains: One sees sentient beings of similar status.[743] The pure divine eye is free of the eleven errors extensively explained in the Enumeration of Phenomena: (1) doubt, (2) inattention, (3) physical dysfunction, (4) mental dysfunction, (5) lethargy-sleep-excitation, (6) strong initiating effort, (7) mental wavering, (8) trepidation, (9) various discernments, (10) excessive speech, and (11) overly intense meditation. Some say: Also the intermediate being of a god sees the intermediate being of the same type and the five reincarnating beings. The intermediate beings of humans, ghosts, and animals respectively see four, three, and two types of intermediate being, and hell intermediate beings see hell intermediate beings alone. Therefore {it seems} higher [intermediate beings] see higher intermediate beings through the divine eye possessing three purities, {but inferior [intermediate beings] do not [see] superior objects.}

srid pa bar ma de yang sngon gyi las kyis bskyed pa'i rdzu 'phrul gyi shugs chen po dang ldan pas shin tu mgyogs pa yin no/ / de'i phyir 'grel pa las kyang*/ des na 'di ni sangs rgyas rnams kyis kyang dgag par mi spyod de las stobs dang ldan pa'i phyir ro zhes bshad do/ / de yang rnam par smin pa'i snying po dang po yin pa'i phyir ro/ / srid pa 'tshol ba yin pa'i phyir mig la sogs pa'i dbang po gzugs can lnga po kun tshang zhing*/ ri dang brag la sogs pa la'ang thogs pa med pa dang ldan pa yin te/ rdo ba dang brag sra ba la sogs pa'i dkyil na'ang srin bu la sogs pa dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'on kyang ma'i lto dang rdo rje'i gdan la thogs so zhes grag go /de nyid kyi phyir 'grel pa las/ srid pa bar ma pa ni lto brdol te 'jug pa ma yin gyi skye gnas kyi sgo nas 'jug ste/ de nyid kyi phyir mtshe ma las gang phyis byung ba de ni pho bo zhes bya'o/ / gang sngar byung ba de ni nu bo zhes bya'o zhes bshad do/ / kha cig ri rab la'ang thogs par 'chad pa ni mi rigs te dran pa nyer gzhag las 'byung ba phra mo de ltar med cing thogs pa med pas gang ri rab phug nas 'gro ba'ang bdag nyid dang ri rab la'ang gnod pa med na ri gzhan dag la lta smros kyang ci dgos zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / kun las btus las kyang*/ 'gre ba la thags thogs med do zhes 'byung ngo*/ /

Moreover, intermediate beings are extremely swift since they possess the energy of supernatural power (ṛddhivega) generated due to past karma. Thus the Autocommentary explains: Therefore, even buddhas cannot stop an intermediate existence because it possesses the power of karma.[744] Further, it is the first essential result of karmic maturation. Because they seek existence [222] they are complete in all five physical sense faculties such as the eyes. They are unimpeded (apratigha) even by mountains and rocks and so on because minute lifeforms are observed amid stones and solid rocks and so forth. However, it is well known that they are obstructed by their mother’s womb and at Vajrāsana. Therefore the Autocommentary states: Intermediate beings do not enter [the womb] through piercing the womb; they enter via the birth site. Therefore, from among twins, whoever is born later is elder. This explains that the first born is the younger sibling.[745] Some say: Also it is illogical to state that Meru impedes because the Foundations of Mindfulness Sūtra declares: Since there are no primary elements as subtle as an intermediate being, it is not impeded, and if it traverses the depths of Meru, neither it nor Meru is harmed. What need, then, is there to mention other mountains?[746] The Compendium of Abhidharma mentions: There is no impediment to movement.[747]

dmyal ba la sogs pa 'gro ba gang du skye bar 'gyur ba'i srid pa bar ma grub na ni lha la sogs pa'i bar srid gzhan du mi bzlog te/ las kyis 'phangs pa'i rnam par smin pa grub zin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na shi 'phos pa'i rjes su dge ba byed pa rnams don med par 'gyur ro zhe na/

If the intermediate being who will take birth as any type of being, such as a hell being, has already been established, it cannot change (anivartya) into another intermediate being, such as that of a god and so on, because the [result of] karmic maturation that is projected by karma has already been established. Objection: Then it would be meaningless to practice virtue after death.

mi 'gyur te/ dmyal ba la sogs par skyes kyang sdug bsngal chung ba dang myur du thar ba dang*/ de nas mtho ris su skye ba la sogs pa'i don byed pa'i phyir ro/ / kun las btus las ni/ ci ste na ldog go /de na gnas pa yang las gsog go zhes dmyal ba la sogs pa'i srid pa bar ma grub nas mi'i srid pa bar mar 'gyur te mir skye ba la sogs pa'ang yod par bshad de/ de dag gi lugs la ni shi 'phos pa'i don gyi dge ba ni shin tu'ang 'bras bu dang bcas pa yin no/ /

Reply: That is not so, because though one is born as a hell being and so on, practicing virtue has the function of making the suffering shorter, liberation quicker, and from there one is born in higher rebirths and so on. But the Compendium of Abhidharma states: Even so it may be stopped, for even while abiding in that state one can accumulate karma.[748] This explains that even though one has established the intermediate being of a hell being and so on, one can still transform it into the intermediate being of a human from where one is born as a human being.

'dod pa'i bar srid de ni skal ba bzang ngan gyis dri zhim pa dang mi zhim pa za ba'i phyir de la dri za zhes kyang bya'o/ / gzugs kyi lha'i bar srid ni dri za ba ma yin te/ kham gyi zas la 'dod chags dang bral ba'i phyir ro/ / 'o na srid pa bar ma pa de dus ji srid kyi bar du gnas she na/ btsun pa dbyig bshes na re zhag bdun du gnas la/ gal te de'i tshe skye gnas kyi tshogs pa ma rnyed na de shi 'phos nas yang srid pa bar mar skyes nas skye ba'i gnas 'tshol bar byed do zhes zer ro/ / kun las btus las kyang*/ re ltar thogs na zhag bdun gnas te de tshun chad kyis 'chi 'pho'o zhes bshad de/ gzhan dag ni zhag bdun phrag bdun du gnas so zhes 'dod do/ / mdo sde pa btsun pa na re de lta bu'i nges pa ni med de ji srid skye gnas kyi tshogs pa ma rnyed kyi bar du gnas la/ de'i tshe 'phen pa logs shig na med de/ ris mthun pa gcig pa'i phyir ro/ / de lta ma yin na de'i tshe zad pas 'chi srid du'ang thal bar 'gyur ro zhes zer ro/ / bye brag tu smra ba rnams ni 'di srid pa 'tshol ba yin pas dus thung bar gnas te skye ba'i gnas su 'jug go / 'o na skye ba'i gnas ma rnyed na ji ltar zhe na/

Because desire-realm intermediate beings imbibe pleasant or unpleasant smells according to their fortune, they are also called “smell eaters” (gandharvas). The intermediate being of a form god is not a smell eater because it is free of attachment to oral food. Question: Now, how long does that intermediate being live? The venerable Vasumitra says that it lives for seven days. If at that time it does not find the assembly of conditions necessary for the birth process, it dies and is again born as an intermediate being that searches for a birth site. Also the Compendium of Abhidharma explains: It abides for up to seven days at most, and then dies.[749] Others assert: The intermediate being abides for seven weeks. A venerable Sautrāntika says that is not definite, because the intermediate being abides until it finds the assembly of conditions for the birth process. At that time there can be no reversal of karmic projection because [223] [the intermediate existence and the prior existence] share compatible type. If that were not so, then at that time [the intermediate existence] would transform into a death existence, since [the intermediate existence] would end. Vaibhāṣikas say that since it searches for an existence it abides for just a short time before it enters a birth existence. Question: What if it doesn’t find a birth site?

gal te der nges par skye bar 'gyur ba zhig yin na ni de'i las kyis skye gnas kyi tshogs pa{ pha ma la sogs} 'dren la/ 'on te der skye bar ma nges na ni de las gzhan pa'i yul du skye bar 'gyur ro zhes zer ro/ / gzhan dag na re de dang 'dra ba'i skye gnas su 'jug par 'gyur te dbyar lta bu dus nges pa can ba lang gi srid pa bar ma rang gi skye gnas ma rnyed pa rnams ni dus ma nges pa ba men dang*/ khyi rnams ni lce spyang dang*/ rta rnams ni bong bu dang*/ dom rnams ni dred rnams su skye'o zhes zer te/ de la ni 'phen pa gcig pa'i phyir gang du skye bar 'gyur ba'i byad gzugs can yin no zhes pas gnod pas snga ma nyid 'thad pa yin no/ /

Reply: If it is certain that a being will take rebirth, then the requisite conditions for its birth process {such as its parents and so on} will manifest due to its karma. However, if it is not certain that it will be reborn in a specific place, it will be born elsewhere. Others say: It will enter another birth site that is similar because the intermediate existence of an ox, which has a fixed time of birth such as summer and does not find a birth site, will take birth as a gayal (wild ox), and dogs will take birth as jackals, horses as donkeys, bears as snow bears. Reply: Since this would harm the statement “It has the appearance of the prior existence because it shares the same projecting karma” (3:13ab), just the earlier statements are acceptable.
gnyis pa skye gnas su 'jug pa ni
HOW BIRTH STATES ARE ENTERED
blo ni phyin ci log gyur pas/ / rtse dgas 'gro ba'i yul du 'gro/ / dri dang gnas la mngon 'dod gzhan/ / dmyal ba yi ni spyi'u tshugs yin/ / 15
Beings develop a distorted mind and proceed to their destination through desire for pleasure. Desire for smells and abodes is different. Hell intermediate beings are led upside down. (3:15)

sems can de {las las byung ba'i mig gis thag ring na gnas pa'i rang skye ba'i gnas mthong ste } phor skye bar 'gyur ba yin na ni pha la sdang ba dang ma la{ 'khrigs pa bya bar} chags pa'i blo ni phyin ci log tu gyur pas ma de dang brtse ba dang dga' bar bya bar 'dod pas 'gro bar bya ba'i yul du mngon par 'dod pa'i mngal du 'gro ste/ der song nas ma'i lto g.yas phyogs su kha rgyab tu bstan te tsog tsog por skye'o/ / 'on te mor skye ba zhig yin na ma la sdang ba dang*/ 'on te pha la chags pa'i blo phyin ci log tu gyur pas pha dang brtse ba dang dga' bar bya bar 'dod pas 'gro ba'i yul ma'i mngal du song ste ma'i lto g.yon du kha mdun phyogs su bstan te 'dug go gal te ma ning du skye ba yin na'ang bar srid ni pho mo gang rung zhig tu yod de/ dbang po kun tshang bar 'dod pa'i phyir ro/ /de'i phyir mngal du zhugs pa na phyis ma ning gi lus 'dzin cing pho mo'i 'dod chags gang dang ldan pa bzhin du gnas par 'gyur ro/ / de'i phyir gdags pa las/ de'i tshe dri za la sems gnyis las rjes su chags pa dang ldan pa'am khong khro ba dang ldan pa'i sems gang yang rung ba zhig mngon du gyur pa yin no/ / zhes pa dang*/ slob dpon gang spel gyis kyang*/ 'di ni rang gi rigs su mngal skyes sam/ / gal te sgo nga las skyes 'byung 'gyur na/ / de'i dus su ma de dang ni pha/ / sbyor ba mthang nas dregs pas rab dgar 'gyur/ / brtse dgas de dag drung rgyug pha yi ni/ / khu chu de mthong kun tu rmongs pa yis/ / bdag nyid ji bzhin de la chags 'gyur te/ / mo na mo bzhin pho na pho bzhin no zhes bshad do/ / de ltar mngal du zhugs pa na bar srid thogs med 'gags nas rnam smin thogs bcas 'grub par 'gyur ro/ /

If sentient beings who enter the birth process {who see the place of their rebirth at a great distance with the divine eye derived through karma} are to be born male, they develop a distorted mind (viparyasta) of aversion for the father and desire for {sexual union with} the mother, and through desire for sexual pleasure (riraṃsa) with the mother proceed to their destination (gatideśa), the womb they manifestly desire. Once there, they reside on the right side of the womb, facing backward. However, if they are to be born female, a distorted mind of aversion for the mother and attachment to the father arises. Through desire for sexual pleasure with the father, they proceed to the mother’s womb, their destination, and reside on the left side, facing forward. Though such a being may later be born as a neuter, the intermediate existence is either male or female because it has complete faculties. Therefore, when it enters the womb, it abides with attachment to either the male or female, though later it will take the body of a neuter. The Treatise on Designation declares: At that time the gandharva manifests either of two minds, the mind possessing attachment or the mind possessing anger.[750] Also Master Pūrṇavardhana writes: If the type of intermediate being is to be born from the womb or from an egg, then at that time it sees its future mother and father become infatuated and join their lower bodies in sexual union. It sees the father ejaculate through the quickening of the sexual act, and in complete confusion it develops desire for such sexual union. If it is to become female, it emulates the female; if it is to become male, it emulates [224] the male.[751] Through entering the womb in this way, the intermediate being ceases to be unimpeded, and its impeded nature ripens.

gal te pha ma'i mi gtsang ba las dbang po rnams skye na de dag nyid las sam/ 'on te de dag las byung ba'i 'byung ba gzhan zhig las yin zhe na/ kha cig na re de dag las skye ste/ khu khrag dbang po med pa 'gags nas nur nur po dbang po dang bcas pa skye ba'i phyir te/ mdo las/ dge slong dag khyed kyis ni yun ring por sdug bsngal drag pa tsha ba rtsub pa nyams su myong zhing dur khrod bskyed do/ / khrag gi thigs pa blangs so zhes pa dang*/ yang mdo gzhan las kyang*/ pha ma'i nur nur po mi gtsang ba las skyes pa zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ / kha cig na re pha ma'i mi gtsang ba las 'byung ba gzhan zhig skye la/ de las ni dbang po dang bcas pa'i lus skye ste lo ma las byung ba'i srin bu la sogs pa bzhin no/ / mdo'i don ni mi gtsang ba la brten nas skyes pa la de skad brjod par zad do zhes zer ro/ / de dag ni skye gnas dang po gnyis su 'jug tshul lo/ / 'grel par gzhan la ni ci rigs par brjod par bya'o zhes zer te/ de la rigs pa ni 'di yin par snang ngo zhes 'byung ba ni chos mngon pa ba'i slob dpon dag skye gnas phyi ma gnyis la ni ci rigs par brjod par bya'o zhes zer ba'i rigs pa'i don slob dpon gyis 'chad pa ni las ji lta ba bzhin du dri dang gnas la mngon par 'dod cing sred pas {skye gnas su } 'jug pa{ re 'dod pa} ni{ rim pa ltar} skye gnas{ dang po gnyis las} gzhan drod gsher skyes dang rdzus skyes gnyis su 'jug tshul lo/ /

Question: If these faculties arise from the unclean elements of its parents, do they arise from just those elements or from other elements derived from them? Some say: They arise from those elements because the first embryonic stage of kalala, which possesses faculties, arises from blood and sperm that do not possess faculties. A sūtra states: Monks, for a long time you experience the intense suffering of the searing heat generated in the cremation ground. Then you are born in a drop of blood.[752] Again, another sūtra notes: The first embryonic stage of kalala arises from the unclean elements of the parents.[753] Others say: Other elements arise from the unclean elements of the mother and father, and from those a body with faculties arises, like an insect larva arising from a leaf and so on. The meaning of that sūtra is that they arise in dependence on unclean elements, and that is the full meaning of that statement.[754] These are the methods of entering the first two birth processes. The Autocommentary states: Since it is said that “Others have various types,” it appears that these methods are appropriate.[755] Abhidharma masters say that “various types” refers to the latter two birth processes. Vasubandhu explains the actual point is that entry {to birth processes} through desire and craving for smells (gandha) and abodes (sthāna) in accordance with their karma {are, respectively,} methods of entering birth through heat and moisture and supernaturally, which are different from the {first two} birth processes.

gal te dmyal bar me 'bar ba dang grang ba'i reg pa la mngon par 'dod pa ji ltar 'byung zhe na/ { 'dir yang*/} blo phyin ci log tu gyur pa'i phyir te rlung dang char pa la sogs pas sdug bsngal ba dag me 'bar bar 'dod pa dang*/ nyi ma dang me la sogs pas gdungs pa dag bsil bar 'dod nas rgyug pa'i phyir tsha ba dang grang ba'i dmyal bar skye ba len no/ / sngon gyi slob dpon thogs med la sogs pa kha cig ni sngar srog gcod la sogs pa byas pa'i sems can dag rmi lam ltar mthong ste/ de dag la zhugs pa na dmyal bar skye ste/ mdo las/ ji ltar 'gyur bas de myong las/ / sngar byas pa ni rmi lam ltar/ / sems can de 'dra mthong gyur nas/ / dmyal bar rab tu rgyug par 'gyur/ / zhes gsungs so zhes zer ro/ { 'o na sha'i phung po ri rab tsam yod na 'bu ri tsam 'grub 'gyur gyi bar srid de dag sha de ma byung bar du gang du gnas she na/ de ma byung gi bar du sdod pa ni min te/ 'di ltar srin bur gyur pa'i bar srid grangs med pa yod de/ de dag rang skye ba dang mthun pa'i drod gsher gyi tshogs pa gang dang phrad pa der skye'i drod gsher gyi tshogs pa 'di kho na las skye ba'i nges pa med par mngon no/ /}

Question: How does the desire to enter the blazing fires or the cold of the hells arise? Reply: The minds of intermediate beings {here also} are distorted because those suffering from [the cold of] wind and rain desire a blazing fire, and those tormented by the sun and fires and so on desire what is cool. Therefore they rush to those destinations and take rebirth in the hot or cold hells. Early masters such as Asaṅga say that sentient beings see others whom they have previously killed and so on as if in a dream, and when they follow them they are born in hell. A sūtra declares: Our experience arises due to our past deeds. And, as if in a dream, we see sentient beings [affected by our past actions], and immediately we descend into hell.[756] {Question: If there were a mass of flesh like Meru, a mountain of maggots would arise. But until those intermediate beings arise as maggots in that flesh, where do they abide? Reply: Until they arise as maggots, they do not abide there. Those intermediate beings who will become maggots are countless, and they are born there when the conducive conditions of heat and moisture that are compatible with their generation assemble. In reality, birth arising solely from the assembly of heat and moisture is not ascertained anywhere.}

srid pa bar ma de dag las dmyal ba'i srid pa bar ma'i dbyibs ni gshin rje'i zhags pas btags te spyi'u tshugs kho nar 'khrid pa yin te/ yongs su gdung ba dang bcas pa dang yongs su gdung ba med pa bstan pa'i mdo las/ yang dag sdom dang dka' thub can/ / drang srong rnams la skur 'debs pa/ / de dag spyi'u tshugs dag tu ni/ / dmyal ba kho nar ltung bar 'gyur/ / zhes pa dang*/ rin po che'i phreng ba las kyang*/ gzhan yang 'di ni log gzung na/ / blun po mkhas pa'i nga rgyal can/ / spong bas ma rungs bdag nyid can/ / mnar med par ni spyi'u tshugs 'gro/ / zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / yi dwags dang dud 'gro'i ni skas la 'bab pa lta bu'o/ / mi'i ni thang la 'gro ba lta bu'o/{ yi dwags kyi ni rgyab kyis 'gro ba yang bshad do/ /} lha yi ni stan las ldang ba lta bur gyen du 'gro'o/ / gal te blo ni phyin ci log gyur pas/ / brtse dgas 'gro ba'i yul du 'gro/ / zhes gang bshad pa de mngal du 'jug pa thams cad la de ltar nges sam zhe na/ ma nges te/ 'di la rnam par dbye ba yod pas mdo dang lung phran tshegs las/ dga' bo mngal du 'jug pa ni bzhi ste zhes gsungs te/ 'dir gnas pa dang 'byung ba 'jug pa ma yin yang 'jug pa gtso bo yin pas de'i ming gis bstan to zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/ / bzhi gang zhe na/

From among those intermediate beings, the physical bearing of intermediate beings of hell (nāraka) resembles someone bound by Yama’s rope and led upside down. [225] The Sūtra Teaching the Tormented and Untormented expounds: You who deprecate those who hold their vows correctly, or those who practice austerities, or ṛṣis, descend into hell alone, upside down.[757] And Precious Garland states: Again, fools who wrongly apprehend this come to possess the pride of scholars. Such unruly beings who abandon Dharma plummet head first into the hell of Avīci.[758] The intermediate beings of ghosts and animals move as if descending stairs, {those of ghosts are said to move backward,} those of humans move as if on flat ground, and those of gods move upward, as if rising from a seat. Question: Is it certain that the statement “Beings develop a distorted mind and proceed to their destination through desire for pleasure”[759] (3:15ab) applies to all who enter the womb? Reply: That is not certain, because this is classified further. As [both] the sūtras and the Kṣudraka Collection mention: Ānanda, those who enter the womb are four in number.[760] Master Pūrṇavardhana explains that though abiding and exiting the womb are not entering it, they are known by this name since entering is the main function.[761] Question: What are the four?
gcig ni shes bzhin du 'jug go/ / gzhan ni gnas pa yang gzhan ni/ / 'byung ba 'ang gzhan ni thams cad rmongs/ / sgo nga las skyes rtag tu'o/ / 16
The first consciously enters. Another also consciously abides. Another also consciously exits. Another is confused in all three. Birth from an egg is always confused. (3:16)

de la gcig ni ma'i mngal du shes bzhin du 'jug go gnas pa dang 'byung ba ni mi shes pa dag go /gzhan dag ni 'jug par ma zad gnas pa yang shes bzhin du gnas la 'byung ba ni mi shes pa dag go /yang gzhan dag ni 'jug pa dang gnas pa shes bzhin du byed par ma zad 'byung ba'ang shes bzhin du 'byung ngo*/ / yang mngal du 'jug pa snga ma gsum las gzhan dag ni 'jug gnas 'byung ba thams cad la rmongs pa dag go / 'di la sgo nga las skyes pa ni rtag tu 'jug gnas 'byung ba la rmongs pa kho na'o/ / 'dir skyes pa zhes brjod pa ni 'byung 'gyur gyi ming gis bstan pa ste phye 'thag ces zer ba bzhin no/ / de'i phyir gnas brtan brag dang nye ba'i brag dang yul lnga len gyi rgyal po'i bu sgong skyes kyi rang rgyal rnams kyang 'jug pa la sogs pa la rmongs pa yin no/ / des na blo phyin ci log gis mngal du 'jug pa ni shes bzhin ma yin par 'jug pa rnams kyi dbang du byas pa yin gyi thams cad la ni ma yin no/ /

Reply: The first consciously (samprajāna) enters (viśati) the mother’s womb, though it abides and exits unconsciously. Another not only enters but also abides (tiṣṭha) consciously, yet exits unconsciously. Again, another not only enters and abides consciously but also exits consciously. Another, distinct from the three former types of entry to the womb, is confused (mūḍha) in all [three] phases of entering, abiding, and exiting. One who will experience birth from an egg (aṇḍaja) is always confused as to entry, abidance, and exiting. Here the term “birth” indicates the name of something that will occur, like the term “that which is to be ground into flour.” Even the elders Śaila and Upaśaila, and the son of the king of Pañcāla, who were pratyekabuddhas born from eggs, were confused when entering the womb and so on. Therefore entry to the womb through distorted awareness is from the perspective of those who enter unconsciously and not for all.

gzhan yang shes bzhin ma yin par mngal du 'jug pa ni gnyis las sems can dbang chung bar grags pa rnams ni ma'i mngal du 'jug pa na rlung langs pa'am char pa 'bab pa'am grang ba'am yul ngan nam skye bo phal po che'i ca co 'don pa snyam byed nas rtswa thibs po'am nags thibs po'am rtswa dang lo ma'i spyil po dang shing drung ngam rtsig pa'i drung du 'gro'i snyam nas 'jug la/ gnas pa dang 'byung ba na'ang de dag tu gnas pa dang de dag nas 'byung ba'i 'du shes dang mos pa phyin ci log 'byung ngo*/ / sems can dbang che bar grags pa rnams ni 'jug pa na kun dga' rwa ba'am skyed mos tshal lam khang bzang du 'jug pa'am/ khang pa brtsegs pa'am/ khri la 'dzeg go snyam pa dang*/ gnas pa dang 'byung ba na yang de dag tu gnas so/ / de dag nas 'byung ngo snyam du 'du shes dang mos pa phyin ci log 'byung ba'o/ / shes bzhin du 'jug pa ni ma'i mngal nyid du shes nas de nyid du 'jug pa dang gnas pa dang de nyid nas 'byung bar shes pas phyin ci log gi 'du shes dang mos pa mi 'byung ba'o/ /

Again, unconscious entry to the womb has two types: (1) Sentient beings with lesser merit before entering their mothers’ wombs reflect: “The wind is blowing, or it is raining, or it is cold, or it is a bad place, or a host of beings are chattering” and seeking shelter, they enter the womb thinking, “I am entering dense grass, or dense forest, or a hut of grass and leaves, or woods, or approaching a wall.” Also, such beings have distorted discernment and resolve that they are abiding in those places and exiting those places. (2) Sentient beings with greater merit enter the womb thinking, “I am entering a pleasure grove, or a garden or a fine house, [226] or I am climbing the stairs into a house or ascending a throne.” When abiding and exiting, the discernment and resolve that one abides there or one exits from there is distorted. Conscious entry is knowing it is one’s mother’s womb, knowing one is entering it, knowing one is abiding in it, and knowing one is exiting it. Distorted discernment and resolve do not occur.

gal te sngar pha ma la chags sdang gis mngal du 'jug par bshad bzhin du yang 'dir nags thibs po dang kun dga' rwa ba la sogs par 'jug pa'i tshul gzhan bshad ce na/ de ni chags sdang gnyis kho nas 'jug pa'i nges pa med kyi 'on kyang rtswa'i thibs po dang kun dga' rwa ba la sogs par 'du shes pas kyang 'jug par bstan pa'i phyir te/ de ltar bshad na skye ba'i srid pa nyon mongs can/ rang gi sa pa'i nyon mongs kun zhes pa 'di'ang 'thad par 'gyur ro zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/ / kha cig na re snga ma ni rang dang ring pa'i gnas skabs su yin la/ 'di ni rang dang nye ba'i gnas skabs su yin no zhes zer ro/ /

Objection: It was previously explained that one enters the womb through attachment or aversion to one’s father or mother. But now a different method of entry to the womb is explained — namely, that it is like entering a dense forest or a pleasure garden. Reply: It is uncertain whether one enters the womb through either attachment or aversion alone, but it is taught that one enters the womb through discriminating it to be dense grass or a pleasure garden and so on because Master Pūrṇavardhana also affirms this explanation, since he writes: The birth existence is afflicted with all the afflictions of its level.[762] Some say: The former method of entry applies when distant from the womb, but this method applies when close to it.
mngal du 'jug pa gsum dag ste/ / 'khor los sgyur dang rang byung gnyis/ / las sam ye shes sam gnyis ka / rgya che'i phyir na go rims bzhin/ / 17
Entry to the womb has three types — cakravartins and the two self-arisen beings — because respectively they have karma, transcendent wisdom, or both extensive collections. (3:17)

de dag 'jug pa na sangs rgyas la sogs pa ma yin kyang 'byung bar 'gyur ba'i ming gis bstan pa'o/ / sgo nga las skye ba dang gang zag gsum po de la dmigs kyis bsal bas skye gnas gzhan dag la ni shes bzhin du 'jug pa la sogs pa bzhi po de ci rigs par yod do zhes bya ba 'di shugs la 'phangs pa yin no/ / gal te rang sangs rgyas kyis 'jug gnas gnyis shes pa dang sgong skyes rtag tu rmongs pa gnyis 'gal te/ lnga len gyi rgyal po'i bu la sogs pa sgong skyes yin yang rang sangs rgyas yin pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ 'jug gnas shes pa ni rang sangs rgyas bse ru lta bu'i dbang du byas nas gsungs pa yin la/ sgong skyes de dag ni tshogs na spyod pa yin pas nyes pa med do/ / zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/ / yang na 'jug gnas shes pa ni mngal skyes kyi dbang du byas pa'o/{ 'jug pa mi shes pa la gzhan gnyis shes pa med do/ /}

When they enter the womb they are not yet a buddha and so on, but they are so designated since they will transform into those beings. Since these three beings and those born from eggs are exceptions, we may infer that other birth processes possess any of the four types such as conscious entry to the womb and so on. Objection: It is contradictory that pratyekabuddhas are conscious of both entry and abidance in the womb and those born from eggs are confused in all phases, because beings such as King Pañcāla and so on were born from eggs but were also pratyekabuddhas. Master Pūrṇavardhana explains that being conscious of entry and abidance is stated from the perspective of pratyekabuddhas of rhinoceros type, and since those born from eggs here were acting in a group, there is no fault.[763] Again, being conscious of entry and abidance is from the perspective of womb birth. {Those not conscious of entry do not know the other two phases}.
13. Twelve Links of Dependent Origination
da ni bar du gnas pa'i tshul 'chad pa
Existence of sentient beings
['di] na ji ltar gnas pa'i rten 'brel dang*/ gang gis gnas pa'i zas bshad pa gnyis las
This has two [227] headings: dependent origination that facilitates abidance, and the food by which one abides.
dang po [ji ltar gnas pa'i rten 'brel]
DEPENDENT ORIGINATION THAT FACILITATES ABIDANCE
['di] la gsum gyi
This has three headings: {first} overview, [then elaboration, and the four existences.]
{dang po} mdor bstan pa ni
OVERVIEW

chos 'di las phyi rol pa rnams ni 'chi srid nas skye srid du nying mtshams sbyor ba ni bar srid ma yin te/ de ni mi rtag par khas blangs pa'i phyir ro/ / skye ba gzhan du 'pho ba'i gang zag mi rtag pa yin na bdag chad pa dang las byas pa chud zos pa dang ma byas pa dang phrad par thal ba'i skyon yod do/ / de'i phyir bdag rtag pa nyid skye ba gzhan du 'pho ba yin no zhes zer ro/ / de lta bu'i srid pa gzhan du 'pho ba'i bdag rtag pa ni med de/ skye srid la sogs pa las gzhan du ma dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ de dag gi bdag nyid yin na mi rtag par thal ba'i phyir te/ de ni mi rtag par tshad mas grub pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di dgag pa rgyas par ni gang zag dgag pa nyid du shes par bya'o/ / 'o na 'chi srid nas nying mtshams sbyor ba de gang zhe na/

Non-Buddhists assert: That which links death existence to birth existence is not the intermediate-state existence, because you accept the intermediate existence to be impermanent. If the being who progresses to another life were impermanent, it would erroneously follow that the self would be annihilated, karma committed would lose its potency, and that being would experience karma it hadn’t committed. Therefore a permanent self progresses to other lives. Reply: There is no permanent self or other such existence that progresses to another life because no existence different from the birth existence and so on is observed, and it follows that such a self is impermanent because it is established as impermanent by valid cognition. The extensive refutation of this position should be understood from the refutation of the self of person. Question: What links death existence to birth existence?
bdag med phung po tsam nyid do/ / nyon mongs las kyis mngon 'dus byas/ / srid pa bar ma'i rgyun gyis na/ / mar me bzhin du mngal du 'gro/ / 18
There is no self, just the aggregates. The continuum of the intermediate being created by karma and affliction proceeds to the womb, like the flame of a lamp. (3:18)
gzugs la sogs pa'i phung po lnga'i rgyun tsam nyid do/ / de la tsam ni lhag pa 'gog pa ste/ phung po chos tsam las ma gtogs pa'i bdag med pa'i phyir ro/ / ji ltar zhe na/
Reply: Just the continuum of the five aggregates (skandhamātra) such as form. The term “just” negates any other entity because there is no self (ātma), just the aggregates. Question: How?

skye ba snga ma'i nyon mongs pa dang las kyi mngon par 'dus byas pa'i srid pa bar ma'i phung po'i rgyun gyis na skye ba 'di'i skye ba'i gnas su gyur pa'i mngal du 'gro ste skye ba'i srid par mtshams sbyor ro/ / mngal du 'gro bas ni drod gsher la sogs pa'i skye gnas gzhan du 'gro ba'ang mtshon par byed do/ / bar srid nyid skye srid du 'pho ba ni ma yin te/ bar do'i phung po la brten nas skye srid kyi phung po lnga skye ba dang*/ de las dus snga ma dang*/ de las 'chi ba dang*/ de las bar do dang*/ de las skye srid du nying mtshams sbyor ba'i phyir te/ dper na mar me skad cig ma yin yang rgyun gyis yul gzhan du 'gro ba bzhin du 'dir yang yin no/ / des na bdag rtag pa med kyang phung po'i rgyun ma'i mngal du 'jug pa mi 'gal lo/ / dpe 'dis ni kha thon las pha rol po la rtogs pa skye ba dang*/ me long las gzugs brnyan dang*/ rgya las 'bur dang*/ me shel las me dang*/ skyur ba'i ro las 'gram chu dang*/ sa bon las myu gu 'byung ba la sogs pa rten cing 'pho ba med pa'i dpe gzhan yang shes par bya ste/ 'phags pa klu sgrub kyis/ kha thon mar me me long rgya/ / me shel sa bon skyur dang sgras/ / phung po nying mtshams sbyor ba yang*/ / mi 'pho bar yang mkhas rtogs bya/ / zhes gsungs so/ /

Reply: The continuum (saṃtatya) of the aggregates of the intermediate being (antarābhava) created by the karma and afflictions of a past birth proceeds to the womb (kukṣi) that is the place of birth in this life and links with the birth existence. Proceeding to the womb represents proceeding to a birth site other than that of heat and moisture and so on. The intermediate existence does not transform into the birth existence. Instead the five aggregates of the birth existence arise in dependence on the aggregates of the intermediate existence, from those there is linkage to [the aggregates of] prior existence, from those to death existence, from those to intermediate existence, and from those there is linkage to birth existence. For example, it is like the flame of a lamp (pradīpa) that is momentary but proceeds elsewhere since it possesses a continuum. Therefore, though the self is not permanent, it is not contradictory that the continuum of the aggregates enters the womb of the mother. Through this example one comes to understand dependence without transference, such as the generation of comprehension in others through speech, the occurrence of reflections in mirrors, an imprint from a seal, fire from a magnifying glass, saliva from a sour taste, a sprout from a seed, and so on. Ārya Nāgārjuna states: Through speech, the flame of a lamp, a mirror, seal, a magnifying glass, a seed, sourness, and sound, scholars should comprehend that aggregates link and humans progress to other abodes.[764]

don de nyid stong pa nyid chen po'i mdo las kyang*/ las ni yod do/ / rnam par smin pa ni yod do/ / chos su brdar btags pa ma gtogs pa gang phung po 'di dag 'dor zhing phung po gzhan dag tu nying mtshams sbyor bar byed pa po ni mi dmigs so/ / de la chos su brdar btags pa ni 'di yin te/ 'di lta ste/ 'di yod pas 'di 'byung zhes bya ba la sogs pa dang*/ lung phran tshegs las bram ze rgya shug gi bu'i dbang du mdzad nas/ 'di na bdag gam sems can med/ / chos 'di dag ni rgyu dang bcas/ / zhes bya ba dang*/ khyad par du 'phags pa'i bstod pa las kyang*/ lus las lus gzhan dag tu ni/ / phra ba'i srog ni 'pho zhes grag /khyod kyi lus las gzhan gyur pa'i/ / srog yod pa ni min zhes gsungs zhes pa dang*/ bram ze 'gro ba rnams kyi rgyu/ / skyes bu rtag pa yin zhes bsgrags/ / khyod kyis rtag pa zhes bya ba'i/ / rgyu ni ci yang med ces bstan/ / zhes pa dang*/ ser skya de nyid rig pas ni/ / gtso las 'gro ba skye bar bshad/ / khyod kyis 'gro ba'i skye ba ni/ / nyon mongs las las 'byung bar bsgrags/ / zhes gsungs so/ /

Also, just this point is expressed in the Great Emptiness Sūtra: Other than the process of designating entities such as “karma exists, maturation exists,” the aggregates are destroyed and an agent linking to other aggregates is not observed. The process of designating entities is just this: “Through this existing, that arises”. . . and so on.[765] It is said in the Kṣudraka Collection, in the context of the brahman Daridra:[766] Here there is no self or sentient being; [228] these phenomena possess causes.[767] Praise of Excellence declares: It is often said that the subtle life force transfers from one body to another. But there is no life force that passes from your body to another.[768] And: Brahmans proclaim that the cause of reincarnating beings is a permanent self. But you teach that a permanent cause does not exist anywhere.[769] Some say reincarnating beings are born from the supreme principle, since just this is recognized by Viṣṇu. But you proclaim that the birth of reincarnating beings arises from karma and affliction.[770]
gal te bar srid las skye srid 'byung na de las ci 'byung zhe na/
Question: If a birth existence arises from an intermediate existence, how does it arise?
ji ltar 'phangs bzhin rim gyis rgyun/ / skyes nas las dang nyon mongs kyis/ / 'jig rten pha rol dag tu 'gro/ / srid pa'i 'khor lo thog ma med/ / 19

The continuum develops gradually as it was projected. From birth, through karma and affliction, a being proceeds to another mundane existence, and the wheel of existence turns without beginning. (3:19)

sngon gyi las dang nyon mongs pas ji ltar 'phangs pa bzhin nur nur po dang*/ mer mer po dang*/ nar nar po dang*/ 'khrang gyur dang*/ rkang lag 'gyus pa ste/ mngal gyi gnas skabs lnga dang*/ de las skye mched drug dod pa dang*/{ de nas mngal nas byung ste} byis pa dang gzhon nu dang dar la bab pa dang dar yol ba dang rgas pa zhes bya ba btsas pa'i gnas skabs lnga'i rim gyis phung po lnga'i rgyun skye ste/ gnod sbyin dbang pos zhus pa'i mdo las/ ji ltar rim gyis gong bur 'gyur/ / ji ltar lus 'di mngon 'phel 'gyur zhes gnod sbyin dbang pos zhus pa'i lan du dang por nur nur po yin no/ / nur nur po las mer mer skye/ / mer mer po las nar nar{ po} skye/ / nar nar po las 'khrang gyur skye/ / 'khrang{ gyur} las rkang lag 'gyus pa dang*/ / skra spu sen mo la sogs dang*/ / dbang po gzugs can rnams dang ni/ / mtshan rnams rim gyis skye bar 'gyur/ / zhes gsungs pa lta bu'o/ / 'di dag la sa'i dngos gzhi las ni/ nur nur po la sogs pa mngal na gnas pa'i dus dang*/ btsas nas 'khogs pa'i bar spyi la btsas pa'i dus dang*/ btsas nas 'gro ba dang rtse mi nus pa man chad byis pa'i dus da nga*/ de dag nus la 'dod pa spyod mi nus pa'i bar la gzhon nu'i dus dang*/ 'dod pa spyod nus nas lo sum cu man chad lang tsho'i dus dang*/ de nas lo lnga bcu man dar la bab pa'i dus dang*/ de nas lo bdun cu man chad rgas pa'i dus dang*/ de man chad 'khogs pa'i dus so zhes{ dus brgyad du} bshad do/ /

Reply: The continuum (saṃtāna) of the five aggregates develops gradually as it was projected (kṣepa) by past karma and affliction. There are five stages in the womb: kalala, arbuda, peśin, ghana, praśākhā, and from those there is the formation of the six sense bases. Then, {having exited the womb,} there are five stages post-birth: child, youth, adult, middle age, and elder. The Sūtra Requested by the Yakṣa Lord declares: How does the fetus arise in stages? How does this body actually develop? In answer to these questions of the yakṣa lord, the Buddha replied: “The first embryonic stage is kalala, then the second embryonic stage of arbuda arises from kalala, the third embryonic stage of peśin arises from arbuda, the fourth embryonic stage of ghana arises from peśin, and the fifth embryonic stage of praśākhā arises from ghana. Then the signs such as hair, body hair, nails, as well as the physical sense bases and so on serially arise.”[771] Yogācāra Levels explains {eight periods}: (1) The period of abidance in the womb is kalala and so on. (2) The period post-birth is in general from post-birth up to infirmity. (3) The period of a child is from post-birth up to but not including mobility and play. (4) The period of youth is from play up to but not including engaging in sex. (5) The period of adult is from engaging in sex up to but not including the age of thirty years. (6) The period of middle age is from then up to but not including fifty years. (7) The period of elder is from then up to but not including the age of seventy. (8) The period of infirmity is from then on.[772]

de ltar skyes nas nyon mongs pas las gsog cing yang 'chi srid dang tshe 'dir bsags pa'i las dang nyon mongs pa rnams kyis 'jig rten pha rol kyi bar srid dang*/ de nas yang de'i skye ba'i srid par rim gyis skye ba dag tu 'gro la/ bdag med rtogs pa'i ye shes kyis srid ba'i rtsa ba ma bcad pa rnams de nas kyang 'chi 'pho dang skye bar gzhol ba thug pa med pa'i phyir srid pa bzhi'i 'khor lo 'khor ba la ni thog ma dang tha ma'ang med pa yin no/ { 'chi ba 'byung bar yang mi rtag pa'i tshoms las/ kha cig mngal du 'chi 'gyur te/ / de bzhin kha cig bcas pa dang*/ / de bzhin kha cig gog tsam dang*/ / de bzhin kha cig yongs rgyug dang*/ / la la gzhon dang la la rgan/ / dar la bab par gyur pa'i mi/ / rim gyis rab tu 'chir 'gyur te/ / 'bras bu smin pa ltung ba bzhin/ / zhes gsungs so/ /}

Thus from birth, where karma is accumulated due to affliction, a being gradually proceeds to the death existence, and through karma and affliction accumulated in this life they proceed to another mundane (paraloka) intermediate existence, and then again to birth existence. Those who do not sever the root of existence through the transcendent wisdom comprehending selflessness enter birth and death without limit, and thus the wheel of the four existences (bhavacakra) turns without beginning or end. {The chapter on death and impermanence [in the Collection of Aphorisms] states: Some die in the womb. Some die when newly born. Similarly, some die when just able to crawl, and some die having only learned to walk. Some die young and others when old. [229] And those who are fully grown all gradually pass away, like the falling of ripe fruit.[773]}

'dir skye ba snga ma dang phyi ma sgrub pa'i rigs pa'ang shes par bya ste/ rnam 'grel dang*/ ka ma la shI la'i tshad ma'i de kho na nyid bsdus pa'i 'grel pa la sogs par rgyas par blta'o/ / des na kha cig gis 'khor ba thams cad stongs par 'gyur ro zhes zer ba ni rigs pa ma yin te/ / sems can la mtha' yod par thal ba las bzang po spyod pa las/ nam mkha'i mthar thug gyur pa ji tsam pa/ / sems can ma lus mtha' yang de bzhin te/ / zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'khor ba la mtha' yod par 'gyur te/ snon pa med la 'brid pa yod pa'i phyir dbul po'i nor bzhin no zhes bya ba'ang rigs pa ma yin te/ chad med pa rnams ni phri yang zad par mi 'gyur ba'i phyir te nam mkha' la sogs pa bzhin no/ / de'i phyir 'khor ba la thog ma ni spyi dang bye brag thams cad la med de/ gang thog ma dang bcas pa'i sems can de rgyu med par thal ba'i phyir dang*/ rgyu med na res 'ga' ba ma yin par thal ba'i phyir ro/ / mtha' ma ni spyi la med la bye brag 'ga' zhig la yod do/ / zhes bya bar 'dod de/ lus zhig tshor ba bsil bar gyur/ / 'du shes 'gags shing 'du byed zhi/ / rnam par shes pa nub gyur pa/ / 'di 'dra 'di ni sdug bsngal mtha'/ / zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Here one should understand the logic of earlier and later lives through examining Dharmakīrti’s Exposition of Valid Cognition and Kamalaśīla’s Commentary on the Compendium on Reality. Some therefore say: All saṃsāra will become empty. Reply: This is illogical because it follows that there would be a limit to sentient beings. Prayer of Noble Conduct states: Whatever is the final limit of space, that is the limit of all sentient beings.[774] Also, it would be illogical to state that “There is a limit to saṃsāra because it does not increase but decreases, like the wealth of the poor,” because that which is immeasurable, like space and so on, does not decrease nor disappear. Therefore neither a general nor a specific beginning to saṃsāra exists, because it follows that any sentient beings who possessed a beginning would have no cause, and if they are without a cause it follows they would not be intermittent. In general, an end to saṃsāra does not exist, but it does for some specific beings. As the Collection of Aphorisms notes: The body and feelings become cool, discernment is stopped, formation is pacified, and consciousness subsides. This is the end of suffering.[775]

'o na dgra bcom pa mya ngan las 'da' ka ma'i sems des sems phyi ma skyed na bye brag la'ang mtha' med par 'gyur la/ mi bskyed na dngos po med par 'gyur te/ don byed pas stong pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ sde pa dag gis ni sems kyi rgyun phyi ma mi bskyed pa'i phyir dang*/ thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes kyi dmigs rkyen la sogs pa 'ga' zhig byed pa'i phyir skyon gnyis ka med do zhes 'dod do/ / theg pa gong ma pa dag ni 'khor ba las grol ba'i ye shes kyi rgyun phyi ma bskyed pa'i phyir dang*/ 'khor ba'i nang du chud pa'i sems ni mi bskyed pa'i phyir skyon du glengs ba med do zhes lan 'debs so/ /

Objection: If the mind of an arhat who has just attained nirvāṇa generates later minds, it would generate limitless specific minds. But if it does not generate [a result], it would not be a thing because it would be empty of function. Some schools assert: Neither error exists (1) because a later continuum of the mind is not generated, and (2) some such minds act as the objective condition and so on of omniscient transcendent wisdom. Mahāyānists answer: There is no error (1) because a later continuum of transcendent wisdom liberated from saṃsāra is generated, but (2) the mind entering saṃsāra is not generated.
gsum pa rgyas par bshad pa
ELABORATION
['di] la gnas skabs pa'i rten 'brel dang*/ kun nas nyon mongs pa gsum du bsdu ba dang*/ rgyu dang 'bras bu'i dbye ba dang*/ mdo'i don bshad pa dang*/ rgyun chags pa dang*/ mtshon pa'i dpe drug las

This has six headings: dependent origination in three phases, how the twelve links are subsumed in the three afflicted states, classification of cause and effect, explaining the meaning of the sūtras, continuous dependent origination, and metaphors for the links.
dang po ni
Dependent origination in three phases
de ni rten cing 'brel 'byung ba'i/ / yan lag bcu gnyis cha gsum mo/ / sngon dang phyi mthar gnyis gnyis dang / / bar du brgyad yongs rdzogs ldan la/ / 20
The wheel of the twelve links of dependent origination has three parts. The initial phase has two, the last phase has two, and the middle phase has eight when fully complete. (3:20)

de ltar phung po'i rgyun skye ba snga ma dang da ltar ba dang phyi ma'i bdag nyid kyis 'khor ba'i 'khor lo gang yin pa de ni{ ma rig pa nas rga shi'i bar} rten cing 'brel par 'byung ba'i yan lag bcu gnyis su 'gyur ro/ / de yang sngon gyi mtha' dang*/ phyi ma'i mtha' dang*/ da ltar gyi cha'am sde tshan gsum mo/ / de yang ji ltar zhe na/ sngon gyi mtha' ma rig pa dang 'du byed gnyis dang*/ phyi ma'i mthar skye ba dang rga shi gnyis dang*/ bar du rnam shes dang ming gzugs dang skye mched drug dang reg pa dang tshor ba dang sred pa dang len pa dang srid pa'i bar ste brgyad do/ / de yang 'dod pa'i skye gnas dang po gsum gyis bsdus pa'i tshe yongs su rdzogs pa dang ldan pa la dgongs pa yin gyi rdzus skyes dang bar ma dor 'chi ba dang khams gong ma pa gnyis la ni de ltar ma nges pa'i phyir ro/ / de lta bu de dag kyang gang zhe na/

That wheel of the continuum of the aggregates, which cycles through earlier, present, and later rebirths, is the twelve links (aṅga) of dependent origination (pratītyasamutpāda) {from ignorance to aging and death}. [230] Further, that wheel has three segments or parts: the initial phase, the last phase, and the present phase. Question: How? Reply: The initial phase has two links: (1) ignorance and (2) formation. The last phase has two: (11) birth and (12) aging and death. And the middle phase has eight: (3) consciousness, (4) name and form, (5) the six bases, (6) contact, (7) feeling, (8) craving, (9) grasping, and (10) existence. The twelve links are considered fully complete for the first three birth processes of the desire realm, but there is no certainty that they are complete for supernatural birth or for death in the intermediate state and the two higher realms. Question: What is the nature of such links?

ma rig nyon mongs mngon gnas skabs/ / 'du byed dag ni sngon las kyi/ / rnam shes mtshams sbyor phung po yin/ / ming dang gzugs ni de phan chad/ / 21 skye mched drug dod tshun chad do/ / de ni gsum 'dus tshun chad do/ / reg pa bde sdug la sogs kyi/ / rgyu shes nus pa tshun chad do/ / 22

Ignorance is when affliction was activated previously. Formation is when karma was activated previously. Consciousness is the aggregates that link with this life. Name and form exist from that moment (3:21) until the development of the six bases. Those bases exist until the assembly of the three. Contact exists until the capacity to recognize the cause of pleasure, pain, and so on. (3:22)

Reply: Ignorance (avidya) is the five aggregates {or affliction} at the time when affliction was activated in a previous birth {or former life}. {It is said that, though one may accept that “ignorance, that is the projecting agent, is abandoned by the path of seeing,” it is not contradictory that the ignorance that is abandoned by the path of meditation projects rebirth for those who have not yet seen the four truths, or that the ignorance that is abandoned by the path of seeing motivates completing karma. Once the path of seeing is attained, projecting karma that craves saṃsāra ceases. Master Asaṅga asserts that there is ignorance that is abandoned by the path of seeing and ignorance that is abandoned by the path of meditation.}

Formation (saṃskāra) is the five aggregates {or karma} when {any of the three types of} karma, such as virtuous {meritorious} karma, was activated in a previous birth {or former life}. Consciousness (vijñāna) is the five aggregates at the moment they link with the womb of one’s mother in this life. {Both the link of consciousness and the link of birth exist for a moment, and the others are continua}. Name and form (nāmarūpa) exist from that moment of linkage until the development of the six bases (śaḍāyatana). {The first four stages of the womb} occur before the development of the six bases. “Name” is feeling, discernment, formation, and mental consciousness because they are not impeded, like names. “Form” is the first embryonic stage of kalala and so on. Those six bases {that are posited as the six bases from their development} exist until objects are engaged through the assembly of the three conditions: the object, sense faculty, and consciousness. From the development of the six bases until the assembly of the three states — the object, sense faculty, and consciousness — is the period of the development of the eyes and so on {up until actual birth}. Contact (sparśa) exists from the point of determining the object due to the assembly of those three states until the capacity to recognize (jñānaśakti) that the engagement or rejection of pleasant, unpleasant, and neutral objects is the cause (kāraṇa) of pleasure (sukha), pain (duḥkha), and equanimity {and so on} arising. Moreover, it refers to the five aggregates until the capacity to recognize the cause of the three feelings through the assembly of those three {such as touching fire and so on when not recognizing it to be a cause of pain} arises.
tshor 'khrig tshun chad sred pa ni/ / longs spyod 'khrig pa chags can gyi/ / nye bar len pa longs spyod rnams/ / thob par bya phyir yongs rgyug pa'i/ / 23
Feeling exists until sexual union. Craving is associated with attachment to pleasure and sexual union. Grasping is intensely pursuing enjoyable objects to obtain them. (3:23)

{yul longs spyod nus nas tshor bar 'jog ste } tshor ba ni tshor ba gsum gyi rgyu spyod nus pa de nas bzung nas 'khrig pa la spyod mi nus pa tshun chad de dngos su mi spyod pa'i bar gyi phung po lnga'o/{ 'khrig spyod nus nas sred par 'jog ste/} sred pa ni 'dod yon gyi longs spyod dang 'khrig pa la spyod cing yul 'tshol ba la ma zhugs kyi bar gyi chags pa can gyi phung po lnga'o/ / nye bar len pa ni sred pa'i yul du gyur pa'i longs spyod rnams thob par bya ba'i phyir yongs su rgyug{ pa ste 'tshol ba la zhugs nas thams cad du rgyu pa}'i gnas skabs kyi phung po lnga'o/{ de ni zhing las dang gnyen thabs la sogs pa'i dus kyi srid pa phyi ma'i las slong byed tshor ba'i rgyu la dmigs pa'i 'dod chags kyi char gtogs pa'i phung po lnga yin no/ /}

Feeling (vitti), {which is posited as feeling through its capacity to engage objects of enjoyment,} exists from the capacity to engage the causes of the three feelings until the capacity to engage in sexual union (maithuna) arises. These constitute the five aggregates incapable of directly engaging in sexual union. Craving (tṛṣṇā), {which is posited as craving through its capacity to engage in sexual union,} is the aggregates associated with attachment (rāga), which exist until one enters the path seeking the pleasure of sense objects and sexual union. Grasping (upādāna) is the five aggregates when [231] intensely pursuing enjoyable objects (bhoga), which are objects of craving, in order to obtain them. {These [three links] constitute the five aggregates associated with attachment; they focus on the causes of feeling and propel the karma of future existence after one becomes a farmer, engages in family matters, and so on}.
de srid 'bras bu 'byung 'gyur ba'i/ / las byed de ni srid pa yin/ / nying mtshams sbyor ba skye ba yin/ / tshor ba'i bar ni rga shi yin/ / 24
Just those aggregates that activate karma, producing results in a future rebirth, are existence. That connecting death to rebirth is birth. The four up to feeling are aging and death. (3:24)

de nas de ltar rgyug pa de yang srid skye ba phyi ma'i bde ba dang sdug bsngal la sogs pa'i 'bras bu 'byung bar 'gyur ba'i rgyu las dge mi dge byed pa'i phung po lnga po de nyid ni srid pa yin no/{ 'grel pa las 'di la rnam par shes pa'i yan lag gang yin pa de ni tshe gzhan du skye ba yin no zhes pa dang*/ 'di la yan lag bzhin po ming dang gzugs dang skye mched drug dang reg pa dang tshor ba gang dag yin pa de dag nyid gzhan du rga shi yin no zhes 'byung bas/ /} 'di nas shi 'phos nas skye ba phyi {ba ste 'tshol ba la zhugs las tnams cad du rgyu} mar nying mtshams sbyor ba de ni skye ba yin la/ 'di la rnam shes kyi yan lag gang yin pa de ni tshe gzhan du skye ba yin no/ / zhes 'grel pa las 'byung ngo*/ / phyi ma'i gnas skabs kyi ming gzugs nas tshor ba'i bar bzhi ni{ tshe 'di gzhal ba'i} rga shi yin no/ /

Then, through such pursuit, just those five aggregates that activate virtuous or nonvirtuous karma — which are the cause producing the result of pleasure, pain, and so on in a future rebirth — are existence (bhava). Then that connecting (pratisaṃdhi) death to future rebirth {through proceeding everywhere in search of it} is birth (jāti). {The Autocommentary maintains: Any link of consciousness will arise in another life. And: Any of the four links of name and form, the six bases, contact, and feeling are otherwise known as aging and death.} And: That which is consciousness in this life is birth in another life.[776] The four links from name and form to feeling (vedanā) of a subsequent phase are aging and death (jarāmaraṇa), {which are the measure of this life}.
'di ni gnas skabs par 'dod lo/ / gtso bo'i phyir na yan lag bsgrags/ / sngon dang phyi mtha' bar dag la/ / rmongs pa rnam par bzlog phyir ro/ / 25
According to some, this is dependent origination in phases. The links are designated according to what is dominant in order to stop confusion about the initial, last, and middle phases. (3:25)

de lta bu'i rten 'brel de yang skad cig ma dang*/ rgyun chags pa dang*/ 'brel ba can dang*/ gnas skabs pa dang bzhir gsungs pa las de ltar bstan pa 'di ni gnas skabs pa'i rten cing 'brel par 'byung bar 'dod pa yin no/ / lo zhes bya ba ni bye brag tu smra ba'i 'dod pa ste 'di'i dpyad pa ni 'og tu bya'o/ / gal te phung po lnga pa nyid du thams cad nges pa yin na ci'i phyir ma rig pa la sogs par bstan zhe na/

Such dependent origination is stated to have four types: (1) momentary, (2) continuous, (3) related, and (4) situational, and this is situational (āvasthika) dependent origination. “According to some” (kila) indicates that this is an assertion of the Vaibhāṣikas, and an analysis of this occurs below. Question: If all [twelve] links are ascertained as the five aggregates, why are they designated as ignorance and so on?

gnas skabs de na ma rig pa gtso bo yin pa'i phyir na gtso bo'i ming gis yan lag bsgrags pa yin te dpung gi tshogs yan lag bzhi dang ldan pa la'ang rgyal po byung ngo zhes brjod pa bzhin no/ / de bzhin du 'du byed la sogs pa la'ang shes par bya'o/ / de nyid ni 'brel ba can da nga*/ rgyun chags pa'i rten 'brel yang yin te/ rgyu dang 'bras bur 'brel ba'i phyir dang*/ tshe gsum bar chad med par rgyun chags su 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / skad cig ma'i rten 'brel ni srog gcod pa la sogs pa'i tshe kun nas slong ba rmongs pa ni ma rig pa dang*/ sems pa las 'dus byed dang*/ yul rig pa rnam shes dang*/ de dang lhan cig 'byung ba'i phung po bzhi ming dang gzugs dang*/ mig gi dbang po la sogs pa skye mched drug dang*/ gsum 'dus pa reg pa dang*/ reg pa nyams su myong ba tshor ba dang*/ sha la sogs pa la chags pa sred pa dang*/ de dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i ngo tsha med pa la sogs pa'i kun nas dkris pa rnams len pa dang*/ des kun nas bslang ba'i lus ngag gi las ni srid pa dang*/ sngar med pa 'byung ba skye ba dang*/ yongs su smin pa rga ba dang*/ de zhig pa shi ba zhes bya ba rnams skad cig ma gcig la tshang bar yod pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te sems can ma yin par ston pa sa bon las myu gu la sogs pa 'byung ba'ang rten cing 'brel par 'byung ba ma yin nam/ sems can du ston pa ma rig pa la sogs pa kho na ci'i phyir rten cing 'brel par 'byung bar gsungs she na/

Reply: The links (aṅga) are designated according to what is dominant (prādhānya), for ignorance is dominant in its own phase just as a king who possesses four army divisions. Formation and so on should also be understood in the same way. They are also called “related” and “continuous” dependent origination because they are related as causes and effects or because they arise continuously without interruption over three lives. In momentary dependent origination, the confusion motivating a being to take life and so on is ignorance. Intentional action is [karmic] formation. Cognition of the object is consciousness. The four aggregates arising simultaneously with it are name and form. The eye sense base and so on are the six bases. The assembly of the three conditions is contact. Experience through contact is feeling. Attachment to meat and so on is craving. Engaging in sexual union without concomitant shame and so on is grasping. Physical and verbal karma motivated by that is existence. The occurrence of that which was not previously existent is birth. Its complete maturation is aging, and its destruction is death. These are completed in one moment. Question: If such dependent origination is not taught to be a sentient being, then is it something such as a sprout arising from a seed? [232] Or if it is taught to be a sentient being, why are ignorance and so on said to be dependent origination?

sngon gyi mtha' dang phyi ma'i mtha' dang bar gsum po dag la bdag 'das pa'i dus na byung bar gyur to/ / ma 'ongs pa na 'byung bar 'gyur ro/ / da ltar bdag zas ni 'di lta bu zhig za'o/ / gos ni 'di lta bu zhig gyon no zhes pa dang*/ ci bdag 'das pa na byung ngam/ ma byung ngam/ ma 'ongs pa 'byung ngam/ mi 'byung ngam/ da ltar gyi 'di ji lta bu zhig snyam du the tshom skye bas de lta bu'i the tshom dang de'i rgyu bdag tu rmongs pa rnam par bzlog pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: [Such dependent origination is taught to be a sentient being] in order to stop confusion (saṃmoha) regarding the self and doubt caused by it, since doubt arises about the initial (pūrvā) phase, last (aparānta) phase, and the middle (madhya) phase concerning what happened to the self in the past, what will happen to the self in future, and what happens in the present about food the self eats or clothes the self wears, or what self existed in the past, what self will exist in future, and what self exists at present.
gnyis pa kun nas nyon mongs pa gsum du bsdu ba ni
How the twelve links are subsumed in the three afflicted states
