Demigods abide in empty caverns below the water line on Meru. Further, the Foundations of Mindfulness Sūtra states: There are four tiers below the water line on Meru extending to a depth of 84,000 yojanas. Within the first tier [extending] 21,000 yojanas below the water line, there is an empty cavern measuring 11,000 yojanas. Within it is a city called Radiant measuring 8,000 yojanas [across], where Rāhu, the son of the lioness, lives. Within the second tier separate [from the first], there is an empty cavern measuring 11,000 yojanas. Within it, in a place called Garland of the Moon, [demigods] sleep and play. Then in the city of Kaṇṭhamālī abide the demigods Kaṇṭhābharaṇa and Balin,[884] and in the center of Kaṇṭhamālī is a lake called All-Seeing five yojanas across. It shows the gods and demigods engaged in battle. It also reveals who will be defeated and who will be victorious, who will die in battle, which humans possess virtue, and who will die and be reborn as gods. Within the third tier, there is an empty cavern measuring 11,000 {yojanas}. There in a place called Pure Abode there is a city [264] called Profound where Mālya lives. Within the fourth tier there is an empty cavern measuring 11,000 {yojanas} within which is the beautiful city called Immutable, where deities such as Prakarśa, Vemacitra, and Īśvara live. Also it is said that [the measure of] the latter three tiers is 21,000 yojanas, and the latter cities are 8,000 yojanas across.[885] Presentation on the World declares: Just as the divine cities have guardians, byways, pure Dharma, radial paths, canals, groves, waterfowl, foundations, wish-fulfilling stones, elephants, also the demigods have places similar to that.[886] Just as beings from guardians to horses exist in the heaven of Trāyastriṃśa, as explained below, so too, in the four demigod [abodes] there are guardians, the golden city that is the abode of Vemacitra, byways, canals, bridges, teeming palaces, the wish-fulfilling tree Citapali, the assembly of Maṇibhadra, pure flat stones, and the four groves called “always joyful,” “extremely joyful,” “joyful,” and “always extremely joyful,” and the four foundations called “always joyful,” “extremely joyful,” “joyful,” and “always extremely joyful,” and elephants fearless in battle and difficult to overcome, and elephants who sport in the groves and scale Kailāśa, and the king of horses called Uccaiḥśravas, who competes with all, including Indra.
lha'i gnas bshad pa
The domains of gods
nyi zla lhun po'i phyed na'o/ / dpag tshad lnga bcu gcig dang bcas/ / 60 nam phyed nyi ma nub pa dang / / nyi ma phyed dang 'char dus gcig/ /
The sun and moon transit at half the height of Meru. They measure fifty yojanas and fifty-one yojanas. Midnight, sunset, midday, and sunrise occur at the same time. (3:60)
['di] la gzhal yas khang la gnas pa bshad pa ni
First the abodes of the palaces are explained.

nyi ma dang zla ba dang skar ma rnams ni lhun po'i phyed gnya' shing 'dzin gyi rtse mo dang mnyam pa dpag tshad bzhi khri'i steng na 'khor ba'i rlung gi steng nas rgyu'o/ / {zla ba'i 'og gzhi ni chu'i khams shas che ba'i shel yin te yon tan bsil ba dang mig la phan pa dang lo thog smin par byed pa dang snang bar byed pa'i las can no } de dag gi tshad ni zla ba'i dbus kyi thad kar dpag tshad lnga bcu dang nyi ma'i {gzhi ma me shel las grub pa las gnyis zlog gnyis zla ba dang mthun pa tshad } thad kar lnga bcu gcig dang bcas pa ste mtha' skor du zla ba la dpag tshad brgya lnga bcu dang nyi ma la brgya lnga bcu rtsa gsum gyis 'khor ba'o/ / gnyis ka'i 'phang du ni dpag tshad phyed dang drug dang {dpag tshad gcig gi } bco brgyad kyi cha gcig yod pa'o/ / de dag gi 'og gi phyi rol nyi ma'i rin po che me shel las grub cing zla ba'i nor bu chu shel las grub pa gnyis ka'i steng na gser gyi rwa bas bskor ba dngul dang bai DUr+Ya dang shel dang gser gyi rtsig skyabs bzhi dang*/ mda' yab dang*/ zam pa brgyud bzhi dang ldan pa/ gzhal yas khang dang*/ skyed mos tshal dang*/ {yang thog dang bsil khang dang bdud rtsi rnam pa bzhi dang sbrang rtsi dang sbrang chang rol mo rnams kyang bsams pa tsam gyis lag tu 'ong ba dang } dpag bsam gyi shing la sogs pa'i 'byor ba du ma dang bcas pa ste lha'i bu nyi ma dang zla ba 'khor dang bcas pa'i gnas yin no/ / skar ma rnams ni 'grel pa las/ chung ba la rgyang grags gcig yod par bshad cing*/ slob dpon gang spel gyis ni/ skar ma'i gzhal med khang gang zhig thams cad kyi nang na che ba de'i tshad ni dpag tshad bcu drug go zhes bshad la/ gdags pa las ni che ba la rgyang grags bco brgyad dang chung ba la rgyang grags gsum dang phal che ba ni rgyang grags bcu pa dang bcu gnyis par bshad cing*/ sa las che ba la rgyang grags bco brgyad dang 'bring la rgyang grags bcu dang chung ngu la rgyang grags bzhir bshad do/ /

The sun (arka), moon (candra), and stars transit forty thousand yojanas above the rotating wind maṇḍala at the same height as the peak of Yugandhara, which is half the height of Meru. {The lower base of the moon is crystal, with a predominance of the water element that functions to cool, aid the eyes, mature the harvest, and illuminate.} The measure of the diameter of the moon is fifty yojanas, and the diameter of the sun {is established from a substratum of fire crystal, and whichever way it is measured it is similar to the moon, at} fifty-one yojanas. The moon revolves in an orbit of 150 yojanas, and the sun, 153 yojanas, at a height for both of five and a half yojanas and one-eighteenth part {of one yojana}. The external foundation beneath them is made from the jewel fire crystal of the sun and the jewel water crystal of the moon. Upon both is the fourfold protective barrier of silver, vaiḍūrya, and crystal, surrounded by a golden wall. Its many features include parapets, four arched bridges, celestial mansions, groves, {and roofs, cool houses, the four nectars, honey, honey beer, music,} wish-fulfilling trees {that produce anything that one wishes for,} and so on. [265] The devaputras of the sun and moon and their retinue abide there. Regarding the stars, the Autocommentary explains: The smaller stars are one krośa.[887] Master Pūrṇavardhana writes: Within the inestimable palace of the stars, the measure of the greater stars is sixteen yojanas.[888] Presentation on the World explains: The greater stars are eighteen krośas and the smaller three krośas, and the majority are ten to twelve krośas.[889] Also Yogācāra Levels declares: The greater stars are eighteen krośas, the intermediate are ten krośas, and the smaller are four krośas.[890]

de dag ni dkyil gyi tshad de mtha' skor du sum 'gyur dang bcas pa yod do/ / gling bzhi gcig gi skar ma'i grangs ni {drang srong gar ga'i ltas kyi rnam pa bstan pa las } dung phyur gnyis dang bye ba brgyad dang sa ya lnga yod par bshad do/ / skar ma de dag ni rgyu shel las grub pa steng na thams cad la'ang gser gyi rwa bas bskor ba rin po che'i rtsig skyabs dang*/ mda' yab dang zam pa brgyud ma bzhi dang ldan pa ste rgyu skar la gnas pa'i lha rnams kyi gnas yin no/ / nyi mas gling bzhi nyin zhag gcig la 'khor bar byed de/ de yang byang gi sgra mi snyan du nam phyed pa dang*/ shar gyi lus 'phags su nyi ma nub pa dang*/ 'dzam bu'i gling du nyi ma phyed pa dang*/ ba lang spyod du nyi ma 'char ba rnams dus gcig go /de bzhin du gzhan la'ang sbyar te/ de yang sa'i stod 'grel las/ gang gi tshe nyin zhag mnyam pa de'i tshe na de ltar bgrang gi gzhan na ni cha yod par blta'o zhes 'byung bas nyin mtshan mnyam pa'i dbang du byas kyi mi mnyam pa'i dus su ni de ltar nges pa med pa'i phyir ro/ /

These are the measure of the diameter, while the circumference is three times that. It is stated {in the Instruction on the Omens of Garga} that the number of stars of one of the four continents is 285 million.[891] These stars are made from causal crystal, and all are surrounded on high by a golden barrier with a protective jewel wall, parapets, and four arched bridges, and they are inhabited by gods who abide in the constellations. The sun circles the four continents in one day. When it is midnight in Uttarakuru, it is sunset in Videha, midday in Jambudvīpa, and dawn in Godānīya, and these occur at the same time. This relationship also applies at other times. Again, Detailed Explanation of Yogācāra Levels states: When the day and night are equal, they are calculated in this way. Otherwise they vary.[892] This is from the perspective of the day and night being equal, but there is no such certainty when they are not equal.
The seasons
nyi ma ldog pa'i dus ni
THE SOLSTICES

'jig rten pa rnams kyi dbyar dang ston dang dgun dang dpyid la zla ba gsum gsum du rtsi la/ 'dul ba las dgun dang dpyid dang dbyar dang dbyar thung ngu dang dbyar ring po zhes bya ba lnga dgun zla ra ba nas bzung rim pa ltar zla ba bzhi dang bzhi dang gcig dang zhag gcig dang zhag gcig gis chad pa'i zla ba gsum dang*/ yang ston zla tha chung gi tshes bcu drug nas bzung ste zla ba bzhi bzhir byas nas dgun dang dpyid dang dbyar gsum dang*/ yang re re la zla ba gnyis gnyis su byas te dgun stod dang dgun smad dang dpyid dang so ga dang dbyar dang ston zhes drug tu byed pa'ang bshad mod kyi de dag las 'dir ni{ dbyug gu/ smin drug /smal po/ rgyal dang bzhi} dgun dang{ rta pa/ bya khra/ nag pa/ sa ga dang bzhi} dpyid dang{ gdu bu/ bra nye/ bya sbo/ sgrog khrums dang bzhi} dbyar te zla ba bzhi bzhi par bshad pa de skabs su bab pas de la dgun gyi zla ba dang po ni ston zla tha chung gi tshes bcu drug nas 'dzin pa las kha cig mdo sde nyi ma'i snying po las/ bdag gis rgyu skar smin drug brjod/ / zla ba nya tshe zla rangs 'gyur/ / ston zla tha chung zhes bya ba/ / 'di ni rab tu brjod pa yin/ / zhes pa dang*/ bra nye dang ni smin drug kyang*/ / lan gnyis yongs su 'khor bar byed/ / ces smin drug gi zla ba la ston zla tha chung du bshad pa'i phyir de nyid kyi tshes bcu drug nas dgun zla dang po yin par 'dod la/ kha cig ni dge tshul gyi dang po'i lo dri ba las/ rgyal dang dbo dang sa ga can/ / chu stod khrums smad smin drug can/ / 'di rnams kyi ni nag po'i phyogs/ / zla phyed gso sbyong bcu bzhi pa'o/ / zhes pa dang*/ / 'dul ba tshig le'ur byas pa las kyang*/ sa ga dang ni cha stod dang*/ / de bzhin khrums smad smin drug dang*/ / rgyal dang dbo zhes bya ba nyid/ / drug po'i mar ngo bcu bzhir brjod/ / ces smin drug gi mar ngo'i tshes bcu bzhi la gso sbyong mi thub pa byed par bshad la/ gso sbyong mi thub pa'ang {'dul ba'i mdo las/ nyin zhag gcig gis ma chog par bya'o/ / dus tshigs rnams kyi zla ba phyed lus pa nyid la'o zhes pa dang }

In the world some calculate [four] seasons: summer, autumn, winter, and spring, each lasting three months. The Vinaya explains five: winter, spring, summer, short summer, and long summer.[893] They begin from the first winter month and last, respectively, four months, four months, one month, one day, and three months less one day. Again, some assert [three] seasons: winter, summer, and spring, starting from the sixteenth day of the last autumn month, each lasting four months. Some assert six seasons lasting two months each: early winter, late winter, spring, hot season, summer, and autumn. From among those here, [three] seasons are explained with four months each: winter {the months of Āśvina, Kārttika, Mārgaśīrṣa, Pauṣa}; spring {the months of Māgha, Phālguna, Caitra, Vaiśākha}; and summer {the months of Jyeṣṭha, Āṣāḍha, Śrāvaṇa, Bhādrapada}. In this presentation the first month of winter (Āśvina) would begin from the sixteenth day of the last autumn month. Some say, quoting the Sūryagarbha Sūtra: The lord calls it the constellation Kārttika (Pleiades). When the moon is full, the month finishes; it is properly described as the last autumn month. [266] And: [The moon] cycles twice, through Bharaṇī (Arietus) and Kārttika.[894] Because this explains that the month of Kārttika is the last autumn month, the first month of winter [begins] from the sixteenth day of Kārttika. Some say: The confession ceremony on the fourteenth of the waning phase of the last autumn month is held on the omitted day, because Questions Concerning the First Year of a Novice states: Bimonthly confession is held on the fourteenth in the dark phase of the months of Pauṣa, Phālguna, Vaiśākha, Āṣāḍha, Bhādrapada, and Kārttika.[895] Also, the Vinaya Verses states: The month of Vaiśākha, Āṣāḍha, so too Bhādrapada, Kārttika, Pauṣa, and Phālguna are called “the six [months where confession is held] on the fourteenth of the waning phase.”[896] This explains that confession falls on the fourteenth of the waning phase of the month of Kārttika due to omitting a day. {The Vinaya Sūtra says: One solar day is to be omitted in the remaining half months of those periods.[897]}

'grel pa las/ dgun dang dpyid dang dbyar rnams kyi/ / zla ba phyed dang gnyis 'das shing*/ / zla ba phyed ni lus pa na/ / mkhas pas zhag mi thub pa dor/ / zhes zla ba phyed dang gnyis 'das shing phyed lus pa na byed par bshad pa'i phyir dbyug gu'i zla ba nyid ston zla tha chung yin pas de nyid kyi tshes bcu drug nas dgun zla dang po yin no zhes 'dod mod kyi/ 'on kyang 'dir ni sgrog khrums kyis nya ba'i zla ba ni ston zla tha chung yin la/ de'i tshes bcu drug nas tha skar gyi zla ba yin pas de'i mar ngo dang tha skar gyi zla ba'i yar ngo bsdoms pa ni dgun zla dang po dang tha skar gyi zla ba'ang yin par shes te/ dgun rnams kyi zla ba bzhi pa'i yar ngo la{ dbyar} nyi ma ldog par bshad cing*/ de nyid dpyid zla ra ba yin par 'grel pa las bshad pa'i phyir dang*/ zla ba nya tshe zla rangs 'gyur zhes skar ma gang gis nya ba de yan chod{ kyis} de'i zla {ba rangs zhing rdzogs } bar bshad pas sgrog khrums kyis nya ba'i tshes bcu drug nas dbyug gu'i zla ba yin pa'i phyir dang*/ smin drug gi nag po'i phyogs la gso sbyong mi thub pa 'byung bar bshad cing*/ ji ni rang gi zla stod yin kyang zla ba 'grib pa la ltos na nag po'i phyogs yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir 'dir dbyar gyi zla ba gnyis pa zhes bya ba dang*/ 'grel pa las/ ston zla ra ba'i yar gyi ngo tshes dgu nas mtshan mo ring ngo zhes bshad pa'ang shes par bya'o/ / de lta ma yin na mchu dang dbo'i zla ba la dgun dang*/ byi zhun dang sgrog khrums kyi zla ba la dbyar gyi nyi ma ldog par 'gyur na dgun rgyal dang dbyar chu stod la ldog par mngon sum gyis grub pa dang 'gal ba'i phyir ro/ /

And the Autocommentary notes: When one and a half months of winter, spring, and summer have passed scholars discard the omitted day in the half months that remain.[898] Because this mentions “in the half months that remain of the one and a half months that have passed,” then the month of Āśvina would be the last autumn month, and the first month of winter [would begin] from the sixteenth day of Āśvina. But here, due to Bhādrapada, the full moon would be the last autumn month. At that time, it would be the month of Āśvina from the sixteenth day. Therefore, know that if the waning phase of [Bhādrapada] is added to the waxing phase of Āśvina, it is the first month of winter and the month of Āśvina. The {summer} solstice is said to occur [after] the waxing phase of the fourth month of winter. This is explained in the Autocommentary to occur in the first spring month. The statement “When the moon is full, the month finishes” explains that the month {finishes and is completed} by those stars [through which the moon courses] after that full moon. Therefore from the sixteenth day after the full moon of Bhādrapada is the month of Āśvina. It is said that confession occurs on the omitted day in the dark phase of Kārttika and that whatever occurs in the latter part of that month is the dark phase reliant on the waning of the moon. Here one should understand what is explained by “the second month of summer”[899] and by the Autocommentary, which explains: From the ninth day of the waxing phase of the first autumn month, the nights lengthen.[900] For if that were not so, if the winter solstice occurred [later] in the months of Maghā or Phālguna, and the summer solstice occurred [later] in the months of Śrāvaṇa or Bhādrapada, this would contradict that the solstices are actually seen in the months of Pauṣa and Āṣāḍha.
dbyar gyi zla ba gnyis pa yi/ / tha ma'i tshes dgu nas mtshan ring / / 61 dgun rnams kyi ni bzhi pa la/ / thung ngur 'gyur ro nyin mo bzlog /
The nights lengthen after the ninth day of the second half of the second month of summer. The nights shorten in the fourth month of winter. Days stop [decreasing from that time]. (3:61)

des na 'dir dbyar gyi zla ba gnyis pa ni ston zla ra ba ste/ de ni dbyar zla tha chung{ bra nye dang} snron gyi zla ba'i mar ngo dang*/ ston zla ra ba chu stod kyi zla ba'i yar ngo bsdoms pa ste de'i tha ma ni{ chu stod zla ba'i} yar ngo ste/{ snon zla ba'i/} mar ngo ni dang po yin pas sngar song ba'i phyir dang*/ yar ngo ni tha ma yin pas phyi nas 'byung ba'i phyir dang*/ TIka byed dag gis kyang*/ zla ba thams cad mar gyi ngo snga ste zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i tshes brgyad kyi nyin mo ring du song ste yud tsam bco brgyad kyi yun du thub pa'i phyir ro/ / mtshan mo shin tu thung ste/ yud tsam bcu gnyis las mi thub pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i rjes la {tshes brgyad tshes ma thag dbyar gyi } nyi ma log ste tshes dgu nas mtshan mo ni {chu srang gnyis dang dbugs gsum gyis } ring bar 'gyur la/ nyin mo ni ring ba las bzlog nas {chu srang gnyis dang dbugs gsum gyis } thung du 'gyur ro/ /

Here the second month of summer[901] also refers to the first autumn month for it combines the last summer month, {Āṣāḍha, and} the waning moon of the month of Jyeṣṭha, with the first autumn month, the waxing moon of the month of Āṣāḍha. The latter — the waxing moon {of the month of Āṣāḍha} — occurs in the second half. Since the waning phase {of the month of Jyeṣṭha} is first, it is established first, and since the waxing phase is last, it occurs later. [267] Pūrṇavardhana’s commentary also states: For all months the waning phase is earlier.[902] At that time the eighth day lengthens because it is increased by eighteen instants. The night is extremely short because it is decreased by twelve instants. After that the {summer} solstice occurs {immediately after the eighth day}, and the night of the ninth day lengthens {by two minutes and three breaths}; the day stops lengthening and shortens {by two minutes and three breaths}.

dgun rnams kyi ni{ zla ba} bzhi pa{ ni dgun zla tha chung mgo'i zla ba'i mar ngo dang dpyid zla ra ba rgyal gyi zla ba'i yar ngo bsdoms pa yin la/ de'i tha ma rgyal gyi yar ngo'i tshes brgyad la mtshan mo shin tu ring ste yud tsam bco brgyad dang*/ nyin mo shin tu thung ste yud tsam bcu gnyis las mi thub pa las de'i rjes la nyi ma log ste tshes dgu} la{ ni mtshan mo} thung ngur 'gyur ro/ / zhes bya ba la dgun gyi zla ba bzhi pa ni dgun zla tha chung mgo'i zla ba'i mar ngo dang*/ dpyid zla ra ba rgyal gyi zla ba'i yar ngo bsdoms pa yin la de'i tha ma rgyal gyi yar ngo'i tshes brgyad kyi tshe mtshan mo shin tu ring ste yud tsam bco brgyad thub pa'i phyir ro/ / nyin mo shin tu thung ste yud tsam bcu gnyis las mi thub pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i rjes la nyi ma log ste{ rgyal gyi yar ngo'i tshes brgyad kyi khongs su dgun} tshes dgu'i tshe nas ni mtshan mo{ chu srang gnyis dang dbugs gsum gyis} thung du 'gyur ro/ / nyin mo ni de las bzlog ste ring du 'gyur ro/ / rang gi rnam bshad kyi 'gyur 'ga' zhig dang slob dpon 'dun bzang dang phyogs glang gi 'grel pa las ni dbyar gyi zla ba gnyis pa dang dgun rnams kyi zla ba bzhi pa ni rim pa ltar dbyar zla tha chung dang dgun zla tha chung gnyis la bshad de/ de dag gi ltar na ni ston zla tha chung gro zhun gyi zla ba yin pas de'i tshes bcu drug nas dgun gyi zla ba dang po brtsi bar bya'o/ /

It is said that in the fourth {month} of winter {the night} shortens. The fourth month of winter combines the last winter month, the waning phase of Mārgaśīrṣa, with the first spring month, the waxing phase of Pauṣa. The night of the eighth day in the waxing phase of Pauṣa during the last period of that month is extremely long because it lengthens by eighteen instants. The day is extremely short because it shortens by twelve instants. After that the sun reverses since the night shortens {two minutes and three breaths} from the ninth day {of winter within the eighth day of the waxing phase of Pauṣa}. Days stop [decreasing] and lengthen from that time. In some translations of explanatory works and in the commentaries of Saṅghabhadra and Dignāga, the second month of summer and the fourth month of winter are explained, respectively, as the last summer month and the last winter month.[903] In accordance with these traditions, the last autumn month is the month of Āśvina,[904] and the first month of winter is calculated from the sixteenth day of that month.

de nyid kyi phyir kha cig dbyar ldog gi yar ngo {dang mar ngo la ldog na rim pa ltar ston zla ra ba dang*/ dbyar zla tha chung yin la/ dgun ldog pa'ang yar ngo dang mar ngo la ldog na rim pa ltar/ dpyid zla ra ba dang*/ dgun zla tha chung yin par 'chad la/ 'jig rten pa dag kyang mgo dang rgyal la nyi ma ldog na rim pa ltar zla smad dang zla stod la ldog go zhes zer ro } la ldog pa thams cad ni ston zla ra ba yin la/ mar ngo la ldog pa thams cad ni dbyar zla tha chung yin no/ / de bzhin du dgun ldog la'ang yar ngo la ldog na dpyid zla ra ba dang mar ngo la ldog na dgun zla tha chung yin no zhes 'chad la/ 'jig rten pa dag kyang mgo'i zla ba la nyi ma ldog na rgyal smad dang rgyal la ldog na zla stod la ldog go zhes zer ro/ / {'di ni dpe brjod pa tsam ste dbyar tshes brgyad la ldog na dgun bcu drug la ldog la/ de bzhin du nur bas lo gsum gsum na dbyar ldog gi shul du lan re 'khor bas/ nyi ma brgyad gsum dag la ldog /lnga 'gyur dag gis shes par bya zhes 'jig rten pa la grags pa ltar yin no } tshad ji tsam zhig gis ring thung du 'gyur zhe na/

Therefore some say: {If} the summer solstice occurs in the waxing phase {or waning phase, then respectively it would occur in the first autumn month or the last summer month. If the winter solstice occurs in the waxing or waning phase, then respectively it would occur in the first spring month or the last winter month. It is commonly said that if the solstice occurs in Mārgaśīrṣa or Pauṣa, then respectively the solstice would occur in the later part of the month or the earlier part of the month.} All [summer] solstices occuring in the waxing phase occur in the first autumn month. All such solstices occuring in the waning phase occur in the last summer month. So too, it is said that the winter solstice occurs in the [first] spring month if the sun reverses [its course] in the waxing phase,[905] and it occurs in the last winter month if the sun reverses in the waning phase. Also, it is commonly said that if the solstice occurs in the month of Māragśīrṣa, the sun reverses in the later part of Pauṣa, but if it occurs in Pauṣa, the sun reverses in the earlier part of that month. {But this is merely an illustration, for if the sun reverses on the eighth day of summer, it reverses on the sixteenth day of winter. Similarly, by shifting in each third year, it cycles each time after the summer solstice. Thus there is a saying, “On the eighth, three reversals and five advances.”} Question: By how much does it lengthen?
nyin mtshan ring ba thang cig go/ / nyi ma lho byang 'gro tshe'o/ / 62 nyi ma dang ni nye ba las/ / rang gi grib mas 'grib par snang / /
The days and nights lengthen incrementally when the sun travels to the south or north. Sunlight strikes the side facing the sun, and since the other is covered in shadow, it is obscured. (3:62)

nyin mo dang mtshan mo ring ba{ dang thung ba} ni nyin zhag re la thang gcig{ re res} ring thung du 'gyur la de ni nyin zhag gcig gi dgu brgya'i cha ste dus 'khor ba ltar na dbugs 'byung 'jug gnas gsum gcig tu byas pa'i dbugs nyi shu rtsa bzhi yin te/ chu srang bzhi bzhis ring thung byed par bshad cing chu srang re la dbugs drug drug yod pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dir nyi ma ldog pa thams cad spyir tshes dgu 'ba' zhig la{ nyi ma} ldog par 'dod pa ni ma yin te/ dgu la ldog pa gsal ba'i dpe byas nas gzhan yang mtshon pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang dbyar dgu la log na dgun bco lnga la ldog pa la sogs pa zhag drug drug phyir nur pa'i phyir lo gsum na ni dgu la ldog par sor chud par 'gyur ro zhes kha cig zer ro/ / 'o na nyi ma ldog pa nyid gang zhe na/

Reply: The days and nights lengthen {and shorten} incrementally each day, [268] where {each} lengthens or shortens by one nine-hundredth part of a day. In accordance with Kālacakra, they lengthen or shorten by twenty-four breaths, where one breath consists of the three parts — (1) inhalation, (2) exhalation, and (3) the pause [between breaths] — because the size of lengthening or shortening is explained as four minutes and each minute is six breaths.[906] Here, in general it is not asserted that all solstices are reversals {of the sun} on the ninth day alone, merely that reversal on the ninth acts as a clear example representing the other [dates]. Further, some say: Reversal on the ninth recurs over three years, for six days are ceded, and reversal on the ninth in summer is reversal on the fifteenth in winter and so on. Question: What is a solstice [or the reversal of the sun]?

de'i phyir nyi ma lho byang 'gro tshe'o/ / zhes bya ste/ de la nyi ma lhor {zla ba drug tu }'gro ba ni dbyar gyi ldog pa ste 'dzam bu'i gling gi dkyil nas rgyu ba'i tshe nyin mo shin tu ring la mtshan mo thung bar yod pa de lhor nye bar gyur pa ni byang nas lhor ldog pa'i phyir dbyar gyi ldog pa'o/ / gang tshe rim gyis lhor bgrod de 'dzam bu'i gling las dpag tshad drug dang bco brgyad kyi chas phyi rol tu gyur pa'i rgya mtsho'i steng nas 'char ba de'i tshe mtshan mo ring la nyin mo shin tu thung ngo*/ / de'i tshe byang du{ zla ba drug} nye bar 'gro ba ni dgun gyi ldog pa ste 'dir dgun ldog pa ni byang sgra mi snyan du'ang dgun ldog pa dang*/ 'dir dbyar ldog pa ni sgra mi snyan du'ang dbyar ldog pa yin la gling gzhan gnyis sa ni de las bzlog par 'dod de/ nyi ma ring ba dang thung ba'i dus su shar nub dang lho byang du shin tu ring ba dang thung ngur rgyu bar 'dod pa'i phyir dang*/ {nyi ma log nas zla gsum dang zhag gsum na } mtshan mo dang nyin mo yud {tsam bco lnga bco lnga }mnyam pa na nye ring med par mnyam por {'gyur ba gdags pa las dpyid zla tha chung gi yar ngo'i tshes brgyad la mnyam par bshad kyang brtag dgos par snang ngo*/ / mnyam dus der } zlum por bskor ba'i phyir te/ rma bya chen mo las/ nyi ma dang ni zla ba dang*/ / sum cu rtsa bdun tshang ba dag /'char ba dang ni nub pa na/ / 'khor lo'i mtshon cha bzhin du rgyu zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir so ga ni nyi ma'i 'od zer tsha ste/ 'od zer gling gi steng nas thad kar 'bab pa'i phyir ro/ / nyi ma ring ba'ang yin te/ shar nub tu rgyu ba'i thag ring ba'i phyir ro/ / dgun ni nyi ma'i 'od zer de tsam du che ba ma yin te/ gling gi steng gi thad ka nas mi 'phog par lho nas 'dir zur gyis 'phog pa'i phyir ro/ / nyi ma thung ba'ang yin te/ shar nub tu bgrod pa'i thag thung ba'i phyir ro zhes{ mkhas pa dag} 'chad do/ /

Reply: It is when the sun travels to the south or north. The summer solstice is when the sun [begins to] travel to the south {for six months}. When it moves from the center of Jambudvīpa, the day lengthens greatly and the night shortens. Summer solstice occurs when [the sun] begins to move south when it stops its progress north. As the sun gradually progresses to the south, it shines above the ocean six yojanas and one-eighteenth part outside Jambudvīpa. At that time the nights are long and the days extremely short. The winter solstice is when the sun begins to move north {for six months}. The winter solstice here is also the winter solstice in Uttarakuru. The summer solstice here is also the summer solstice in Uttarakuru. It is asserted that such reversal occurs on the other two continents because when the day lengthens or shortens, the sun moves to a greater or lesser degree to the east and west or to the north and south. {Three months and three days after the solstice,} the equinox occurs when the days and nights are equal {to fifteen periods each}; there is no difference in their lengths. {Presentation on the World explains that they are equal on the eighth day of the waxing phase of the last month of spring, but this must be analyzed.[907] When they are equal} it is because the sun and moon revolve [about Mount Meru] in circular orbits. The Great Peacock Queen of Knowledge states: The sun and moon complete in thirty-seven[908] rise and set in a motion like a weapon wheel.[909] Therefore, in the hot season the light of the sun is hot because the light shines straight down on the continent from above. The days are long because the sun moves in a long arc from east to west. In winter the sun’s light is not strong because it does not shine straight down from above the continent but at an angle from the south. The duration of sunlight is reduced because the sun travels a shorter distance from east to west. {This is explained by scholars.}

{lhor bgrod la nyi ma ldog dus su gling las dpag tshad drug dang gcig gi bco brgyad cha gcig gis gling las nyi ma phyir rgya mtsho'i steng du yol nas 'od zer phal cher rgya mtshor phog pas rgya mtsho dang rgya mtsho las 'bab pa'i chu rnams dro zhing chu la skyes pa'i shing sogs skye'o/ / dbyar byang bgrod dus su de las zlog par gling dro la/ rgya mtsho grang ngo*/ / de yang gdags pa las de'i tshe 'dzam bu'i gling gi mtha' myur du spong ba'i phyir mtshan mo ring la/ dbus yun ring pos spong bas dpyid dang dbyar nyin mo ring ngo zhes so/ / gling gang gi mtha' nas nyi ma rgyu ba thung la/ dbus nas rgyu ba'i tshe ring ba yin no } dpal dus kyi 'khor lo pa rnams ni zlum por bskor ba nyid nye ring byed par 'dod do/ / 'o na zla ba yar gyi ngo la dang po cung zad kyang mi snang ba dang*/ de nas rim gyis snang ba dang rangs pa snang ba dang mar gyi ngo la 'grib par ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/

{When the sun reverses in its southernmost travels, the sun passes above the ocean six and one-eighteenth yojanas off the shore of the continent. Since sunlight strikes the ocean, the ocean water where the sun shines heats up and aquatic plants grow. In summer, as the sun travels to its northernmost point where it reverses, the continent heats up and the ocean cools. Further, Presentation on the World proclaims: At that time, [269] because the border of Jambudvīpa is crossed, the nights are long. Since the central land is crossed, the days of spring and summer are long.[910] Therefore the days shorten when the sun travels toward the periphery of any continent, and they lengthen when it travels toward the center.} Followers of Kālacakra assert that the distance is determined through circular rotation.[911] Question: Initially the moon does not appear at all in the waxing phase, then it appears and gradually becomes whole, and in the waning phase it diminishes. Why is this?

'di ltar nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor dang shin tu nye ba las de'i 'od zer zla ba la phog ste phar phyogs su rang gi grib ma 'bab pas zla ba ma lus pa 'grib par snang ba'i phyir dang*/ {de yang gnam stong la nyi zla sbyar bas cung zad kyang mi mthong ba'i phyir ro } nyi ma dang ring bar gyur pa dang rang gi grib mas bsgribs pa chung bar gyur pa'i phyir zla ba snang ba che bar 'gyur la/ gang gi tshe zla ba nyi ma dang shin tu ring bar gyur pas rang gi grib mas cung zad kyang bsgribs pa med pa de'i tshe zla ba ma lus pa snang ba yin no/ / 'dir kha cig na re 'phags pa thogs med la sogs pa ni zla ba'i phyed ni chu shel las grub la phyed ni baiDUr+Ya las grub pa'i phyir de bla 'og 'gyur pa'i khyad par las 'phel ba dang 'grib par snang ste/ chu shel ma lus pa snang ba'i che rangs pa snang la/ baiDUr+Ya ma lus pa snang ba'i che mi snang zhing*/ de dag phyed mar snang ba'i che snang ba phyed yin no zhes 'dod do zhes zer ba ni de lta ma yin te/ 'phags pa thogs med kyis grib ma bla 'og 'dzur ba'i bye brag las 'phel ba dang 'grib par bshad la/ de'i bla 'og ni pha rol dang tshur rol gyi ngos la bzhed pa'i phyir snga ma dang 'dra la baiDUr+Ya las grub par bshad pa ni med do/ / nyi zla dang rgyu skar la gnas pa'i lha de dag ni rgyal chen ris bzhi pa'i nang du bgrang ba dag yin no/ / {zla ba'i ra ri na lha'i dbang pos byang sems ri bong gi gzugs lha la bstan pa'i phyir bris pa'o/ / gdags pa las bang rim 'og ma chu las dpag tshad khris gyen du 'phags par bshad pas/ bang rim bzhi pa las ri rab kyi rtse mo dpag tshad sum khris gyen du 'phags so/ / bang rim dang po ni ri rab las dpag tshad stong phrag bcu drug phyir 'phags la/ gzhan gsum phyed phyed 'phags so }

Reply: Sunlight strikes the moon on the side facing the sun, and the other side, since it is covered in shadow, is obscured. {During the new moon, the sun and moon are arranged in such a way that the moon is not seen in the least.} After that the moon appears to grow because its sunlit part increases and its shadow decreases. When the sun and moon are spread farthest apart, the moon is not obscured by its shadow in the least, and the entire moon appears. Some say in this context: Ārya Asaṅga and so on assert that because the moon is half water crystal and half vaiḍūrya, these distinct upper and lower sides are seen to increase and decrease. When the water crystal fully appears, the moon appears full; when the vaiḍūrya fully appears, the moon does not appear. When half of each appears, a half moon appears. Reply: That is not so, because Ārya Asaṅga explains that the moon’s increase and decrease arise from the specific retreat of upper and lower shadow. Because he asserts that upper and lower shadow occur on this side and the other side, he does not state that it is made from vaiḍūrya, as previously inferred. Those gods abiding in the sun, moon, and stars are counted among the gods of Cāturmahārājika. {Because the lord of the gods demonstrated the form of the bodhisattva rabbit to the gods, it was inscribed on the surface of the moon. Presentation on the World explains that the terraces [of Meru] rise 10,000 yojanas above the water below, the peak of Meru rises 30,000 yojana above the fourth terrace, the first terrace extends 16,000 yojanas from [the center of] Mount Meru, and the other three terraces extend by half that each.}[912]
The domains on Mount Meru and in space
ri la gnas pa bshad pa ni
DOMAINS ON MOUNT MERU

Meru has four terraces, and the distance between them is 10,000 yojanas. They extend 16,000, 8,000, 4,000, and 2,000 yojanas. (3:63)

Meru has four terraces above the water level, and the distance between them is 10,000 yojanas each. The first terrace extends (nirgata) [in breadth] 16,000, the second, 8,000, the third, 4,000, and the fourth, 2,000 yojanas. Also some assert that [Meru] extends 30,000 yojanas above the surface of the water, then 10,000 yojanas above that [Meru] reduces by 16,000 yojanas, and so forth. [Learned] lamas assert that the bulk of Meru is established in layers above the surface of the water. It reduces in breadth [each] 10,000 yojanas [270] by 16,000 yojanas and so on. Also in accordance with both, they extend from the foundations of Meru. Master Saṅghabhadra explains that Meru is like a stūpa that progressively narrows as it rises above the water level because Meru [progressively] decreases in breadth by 16,000 yojanas and so on. He also asserts that the statement “Each side of it is 80,000 yojanas” (3:65b) is a reference to the perimeter.[913]

On the first live Karoṭapāṇis, then Mālādhāras, Sadāmattas, and the Cāturmahārājakas and their retinue gods. Also they live on the seven mountains. (3:64)

bang rim bzhi yod pa de la dang po la gnod sbyin lag na rin po che'i gzhong thogs zhes bya ba dang*/ gnyis pa la me tog gi phreng ba thogs pa dang*/ gsum pa la dgun chang gis rtag tu myong pa dang*/ bzhi pa la ni rgyal po chen po bzhi bdag nyid dang de dag gi 'khor ba'i lha rnams gnas so/ / ji ltar bang rim rnams la rgyal chen bzhi'i ris kyi lha gnas pa de bzhin du gser gyi ri bdun po dag la yang rgyal chen ris bzhi pa'i lha dag gnas so/ / yang gi sgras ni khor yug dang gling rnams kyi ri dang zhing dang chu la sogs pa la'ang yod do zhes bsdu ba'i phyir ro/ / de nyid kyi phyir lha'i ris de ni lha thams cad pas che ba yin no zhes 'grel pa las 'byung ba la TIka byed dag che ba'i don yang rab tu mang bas yin gyi phun sum tshogs pas che ba ni ma yin no zhes 'chad do/ / gdags pa dang sa las ni gnya' shing 'dzin gyi shar dang lho dang nub dang byang na {steng gi phyogs bzhi na ngos re la dpag tshad nyis brgya lnga bcu ste mtha' skor du } dpag tshad stong gis 'khor ba'i yul 'khor srung dang*/ 'phags skyes po dang*/ sna tshogs gzugs dang*/ lcang lo can zhes bya ba'i pho brang yod de/ de dag ni rim pa ltar rgyal po chen po yul 'khor srung dang*/ 'phags skyes po dang*/ mig mi bzang dang*/ rnam thos sras 'khor dang bcas pa lha'i 'byor pa chen pos brgyan te gnas la/ ri rab kyi bang rim gnyis pa lag na khrag thogs pa dang*/ bzhi pa la phreng ba thogs pa yod par bshad do/ /

There are four terraces. On the first lives yakṣas called Karoṭapāṇis (Those Bearing Pitchers); on the second, Mālādhāras (Those Wearing Garlands); on the third, Sadāmattas (Those Always Intoxicated); and on the fourth terrace live the Cāturmahārājakas (Four Great Kings) and their retinue of gods. Just as the Cāturmahārājika gods live on the terraces, so also the Cāturmahārājika gods live on the seven golden mountains (parvata). The term “also” includes “those who live in the mountains, forests, water, and so on of the perimeter and the continents.” Because of that it is stated in the Autocommentary: That type of god exceeds all the gods.[914] Pūrṇavardhana’s commentary explains that “exceeds” means many times greater in number, not greater in excellence.[915] Presentation on the World[916] and Yogācāra Levels state that to the east, south, west, and north of Yugandhara are the palaces of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, Viśvarūpa, and Kubera one thousand yojanas in circumference {and 250 yojanas on each side, as above}. In each of those live the great kings Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, and Vaiśravaṇa, and they are adorned with the great treasures of the gods and their retinue. It is said that Rudhirapāṇis live on the second terrace of Meru and Mālādhāras on the fourth.
lhun po'i rtse na sum cu gsum/ / de yi ngos la brgyad khri'o/ / 65 phyogs mtshams brtsegs pa bzhi la ni/ / lag na rdo rje gnas dbus na/ /
The gods of Trāyastriṃśa live on the summit of Meru. Each side of it is 80,000 yojanas. At the corners of Meru there are four peaks and on them live vajrapāṇis. (3:65)

de na nor lha brgyad dang*/ drag po bcu gcig dang*/ nyi ma bcu gnyis dang*/ tha skar gyi bu gzhon nu gnyis te dbang po dang nye dbang sum cu rtsa gnyis te sum cu rtsa gsum yod pa'i phyir ram/ rnam par mnyam 'phrul dang*/ rab 'bab dang*/ ljang bu dang*/ yid seng seng po dang*/ me tog gi 'phral thabs dang*/ dga' ba'i tshal la sogs pa gnas 'dzam bu'i gling pa la bsgrag tu rung ba sum cu rtsa gsum yod pa'i phyir ro/ /

From among the eight wealth gods, the eleven fierce gods, the twelve suns, and the two youthful sons of Aśvinī, there are thirty-two powerful gods and one near-powerful god, making thirty-three. Or there are the thirty-three well-known abodes in Jambudvīpa, such as the land of identical emanations, the land teeming with rain, the land of green shoots, the land of gaping fissures, the land of transient flowers, the joyful grove, and so forth.

ri rab de'i ngos re re la dpag tshad brgyad khri brgyad khri ste mtha' skor du dpag tshad sum 'bum nyis khri yod do zhes slob dpon 'chad la/ lung gzhi las kyang*/ ri rab kyi ngos re re la'ang dpag tshad brgyad khri yod de/ de'i kho ra khor yug tu dpag tshad sum 'bum nyis khri yod do zhes gsungs so/ / slob dpon 'dun bzang ni ngos re la dpag tshad nyis khri yod pas ngos kun bskor na brgyad khri yin la lung las bshad pa ni chu mtshams kyi dbang du byas pa yin no zhes 'chad do/ /

Vasubandhu explains that each side of Meru is 80,000 yojanas, and it is 320,000 yojanas in circumference.[917] Chapters on Vinaya also declares: Each face of Meru is 80,000 yojanas, and it is 320,000 yojanas in perimeter.[918] Master Saṅghabhadra explains: Since it is 20,000 yojanas on each side, it is 80,000 yojanas if one circles all sides. That explained in scripture is from the perspective of the water level.[919]

ri rab de'i phyogs mtshams grwa bzhi na gdags pa ltar na ngos re la dpag tshad brgya nyi shu rtsa lnga yod pa mtha' skor na lnga brgya lnga brgyas 'khor ba/ 'phang du ni 'di dang sa las dpag tshad lnga brgya 'phags par bshad la/ gdags pa ltar na dpag tshad phyed dang lnga gyen du 'phags pa'i brtsigs pa bzhi yod de/ de dag la la ni gnod sbyin lag na rdo rje gos sngon po can zhes bya ba gnas te/ de dag ni bag med pa'i lha rnams bsrung ba'i phyir ro zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/ / gsang ba pa'i bdag po ni de dag gi cha lugs su sprul nas sems can gyi don byed pa yin gyi de'i sder gtogs pa ni ma yin no/ / de dag ni gdags pa las nub lho shar byang rim pa bzhin dngul dang baiDUr+Ya dang shel dang gser gyi rang bzhin las grub par bshad do/ /

There are four peaks at the corners of Meru. According to Presentation on the World, they are 125 yojanas on each side and 500 yojanas in circumference, and both Presentation on the World and Yogācāra Levels explain that they rise 500 yojanas in height.[920] The four peaks rise steeply to 4.5 yojanas according to Presentation on the World, and on them live yakṣas called blue-clothed vajrapāṇis.[921] Master Pūrṇavardhana explains that they are guarded by immodest gods. The Secret Lord (guhyapati) works for the purpose of sentient beings through emanating in their guise, but he does not belong to that division.[922] Presentation on the World explains that the western, southern, eastern, and northern peaks are made, respectively, of the essence of silver, vaiḍūrya, crystal, and gold.[923]
grong khyer blta na sdug ces pa/ / ngos la nyis stong lnga brgya pa/ / 66 dpag tshad phyed dang gnyis gser gyi/ / rang bzhin gzhi bkra mnyen pa yod/ /
In the center is the city of Sudarśana, 2,500 yojanas on each side, 1.5 yojanas in height, gold in essence. Its foundation is variegated and pliable. (3:66)

ri rab kyi rtse mo de'i dbus na grong khyer blta na sdug ces bya ba ngos re re la dpag tshad nyis stong lnga brgya lnga brgya pa mtha' skor na dpag tshad khris 'khor ba yod do/ / de'i 'phang du dpag tshad phyed dang gnyis{ sam phyed dang gsum} gyen du 'phags pa gser gyi rang bzhin dbyibs legs shing blta na sdug la mdzes pa rin po che'i ka ba drug khri yod pa gser gyi rwa ba 'phang du dpag tshad phyed dang gsum pas bskor ba dang*/ rwa ba de la gser dngul baiDUr+Ya shel bzhi las byas pa'i rtsig skyabs dang*/ gyen du 'phang ba dang thur du 'phang ba'i mda' yab dang*/ rin po che sna bzhi'i zam pa brgyud ma bzhi dang*/ nang gi sa gzhi tshon sna brgya rtsa gcig gis bkra bar byas pa mnan na noms zhes byed pa bteg na spar zhes byed pa'i mnyen pa dang ldan pa me tog man da ra bas pus nub tsam du khebs shing de dag rlung gis rnying pa 'dor zhing gsar pa 'grems par byed pa yod de/ gdags pa las/ lha rnams bsod nams dbang gis mthu stobs kyis/ / lha'i grong khyer dag na rlung chen ldang*/ / me tog rnying pa rnams ni 'dor bar byed/ / me tog gsar pa rnams ni legs par 'grem zhes 'byung ngo*/ /

In the center of Meru’s summit is the city called Sudarśana, which is 2,500 yojanas on each side, 10,000 yojanas in circumference, and rising steeply to a height of 1.5 {or 2.5} yojanas. In essence it is gold (haima), possessing an excellent shape beautiful to behold. It has 60,000 jeweled pillars, and it is surrounded by a golden barrier 2.5 yojanas in height that is a protective wall of the four layers: gold, silver, vaiḍūrya, and crystal. It has parapets [272] that project steeply upward and downward, and four arched bridges of the four types of precious substance. The foundation inside is variegated with 101 colors, and it sinks a little when stepped on and is pliable and light when [one’s foot] is raised. It is covered with māndārava flowers,[924] and the wind scatters new flowers and removes the old. Presentation on the World states: The powerful might of the merit of the gods raises great winds in the divine cities to remove withered flowers and distribute new flowers.[925]

gzhan yang lha'i grong khyer la rin po che sna bzhi'i skar ma'i gzugs dang zla ba phyed pa dang me long la sogs pas brgyan cing 'phang du dpag tshad phyed dang gsum zheng du dpag tshad phyed dang gnyis yod pa'i sgo stong du gcig gis ma tshang ba yod la/ sgo re re la'ang sum cu rtsa gsum pa'i lha rnams bsrung ba'i phyir srung ma go cha bgos shing mtshon cha thogs pa'i gnod sbyin gos sngon po can lnga brgya lnga brgya bkod de gnas so/ / de'i lam srang srid du dpag tshad nyis stong lnga brgya zheng du dpag tshad bcu gnyis pa gser gyi bye ma bdal zhing tsan dan gyi chus chag chag btab pa yod la/ de'i g.yas g.yon na chu bsil zhing sbrang rtsi lta bus gang zhing me tog dang skad snyan pa 'byin pa'i bya sna tshogs dang ldan pa'i rdzing bu rin po che sna bzhi'i pha gu brtsigs shing them skas dang ldan pa dang*/ rdzing bu'i nye 'khor na sems bskyed ma thag tu gang 'dod pa'i me tog dang 'bras bu dang gos dang rgyan dang rol mo dang bdud rtsi kha dog bzhi pa sbrang rtsi dang sbrang chang la sogs pa 'byung ba'i shing sna tshogs skyes shing thang las skyes pa'i bya sna tshogs skad snyan pa 'byin pa yod do/ /

Again, the divine cities are ornamented with the forms of the stars of the four varieties of precious substance, half moons, mirrors, and so on. The wall is 2.5 yojanas in height and 1.5 yojana in breadth, less one yojana above the gates because 500 guardians wearing armor and 500 yakśas in blue dress bearing weapons are stationed at each gate to protect the gods of Trāyastriṃśa.
Its byways are 2,500 yojanas in length and twelve yojanas wide, spread with golden sand and sprinkled with sandalwood water. To their right and left are terraced ponds constructed with walls of the four varieties of precious substance, filled with cool water like honey and accommodating various birds that make melodious sounds. When in the vicinity of these pools, as soon as one generates the wish for something, various trees grow, producing such things as flowers, fruit, clothing, ornaments, music, honey or honey beer of the four colored nectars, and so on, and various plain birds produce melodious sounds.

gzhan yang grong khyer de la rin po che sna bzhi'i pha gus brtsigs shing chu bsil zhing sbrang rtsi lta bus gang ba me tog dang chu bya skad snyan pa 'byin pa sna tshogs dang*/ gang du lha rnams zhugs nas chu la rtse ba'i gru sna tshogs dang bcas pa'i 'obs zabs dang kha tshon du dpag tshad re re yod pa rim pa bdun gyis bskor ba dang*/ 'obs de'i nye 'khor na'ang dpag bsam gyi shing dang thang las skyes pa'i bya sna tshogs skad snyan pa 'byin pa yod do/ / gzhan yang yang thog dang khang pa brtsegs pa dang khang bzang dang bsil khang dang ltad mo lta ba'i sa dang zam pa rnams lha'i bu mo'i tshogs kyis mdzes shing yid du 'ong ba'i 'dod yon dang ldan pa dag na lha rnams rtse zhing dga' bas rang rang gi las kyi 'bras bu nyams su myong bar byed do zhes gdags pa las 'byung ngo*/ /

Again, that city is constructed of walls with four varieties of precious substance, with pools filled with cool water like honey, possessing flowers and waterfowl producing pleasant sounds. Where the gods abide there are deep canals, well supplied with various leisure boats. Each yojana of the canal surface is surrounded by seven canals. Surrounding those canals are wish-fulfilling trees and various plain birds producing pleasant sounds. Again, the domes and upper stories of the mansions, the cool turrets on the house roofs and lookouts, are beautified with various goddesses. And the gods take joy in playing with various desirable objects, experiencing the results of their karma. This is stated in Presentation on the World.[926]
de na rnam par rgyal byed de/ / ngos la nyis brgya lnga bcu'o/ / 67 phyi rol shing rta sna tshogs dang / / rtsub 'gyur 'dres tshal dga' bas brgyan/ /
In the center of that city is Vaijayanta, 250 yojanas on each side, adorned by Caitraratha, Pāruṣyaka, Miśrakā, and Nandana. (3:67)

grong khyer de'i dbus na lha'i dbang po brgya byin gyi khang bzang rnam par rgyal byed ces bya ba yod de/ de'i ngos re re la dpag tshad nyis brgya lnga bcu yod cing mtha' stong gis 'khor ba gyen du lha'i grong khyer las dpag tshad phyed dang lnga 'phags pa ka ba bzhi bcu dang ldan pa yod de/ de la ba gam brgyad dang ba gam re re la'ang khang pa brtsegs pa bdun bdun/ de re re la'ang gnas khang bdun bdun/ de re re la'ang lha'i bu mo bdun bdun/ de re re la'ang g.yog mo bdun bdun/ de re re la'ang sil snyan bdun bdun yod pas brgya byin bsu skyel dang mi skyo bar byed par gdags pa las bshad la/ sa'i dngos gzhi las ni ba gam brgya rtsa gcig dang*/ ba gam re re la'ang khang pa brtsegs pa bdun bdun/ de re re la'ang khang mig bdun bdun/ de re re la'ang lha'i bu mo bdun bdun/ de re re la'ang g.yog mo bdun bdun yod par bshad kyi gnyis ka las rdzing dang pad+ma ni ma bshad do/ / khang bzang rnam par rgyal ba'i nang na sngar bshad pa'i khyad par dang ldan pa'i rdzing bu chu zheng du dpag tshad lnga bcu lnga bcu mtha' nyis brgyas 'khor ba yod do/ /

In the center of that city there is the palace of Śakra, the lord of the gods, called Vaijayanta, 250 yojanas on each side and 1,000 yojanas [273] in circumference. It rises steeply 4.5 yojanas above the divine city with forty pillars, eight balconies, and seven stories for each balcony. In each there are seven cymbals that welcome Śakra and remove sorrow. This is explained in Presentation on the World.[927] Yogācāra Levels declares that there are eighty-one balconies, and seven stories for each balcony. On each of those there are seven goddesses, and for each of those there are seven female servants. In both of these explanations, ponds and lotuses are not explained.[928] In the palace of Vaijayanta there are ponds 50 yojanas wide and 200 yojanas in circumference, as explained before.

grong khyer blta na sdug de'i phyi rol dpag tshad nyi shu nyi shu'i shar na shing rta sna tshogs can dang*/ lho na rtsub 'gyur dang*/ nub na 'dres pa'i tshal dang*/ byang na dga' ba'i tshal zhes bya bas brgyan te/ re re'ang chu zheng du dpag tshad nyis brgya lnga bcu lnga bcu pa mtha' stong gis 'khor ba'i gru bzhi pa gser gyi rwa ba 'phang du dpag tshad res bskor ba/ de'i rtsig skyabs dang mda' yab dang nang gi sa gzhi la sogs pa sngar bshad pa 'dra bar yod de/ de dag gi dang po na rin po che'i shing rta sna tshogs yod do/ / gnyis par ni lha'i bu dag der zhugs pa na shes pa rtsub par 'gyur ro/ / gsum par ni lha'i bu dang bu mo dag 'dres nas spyod lam sna tshogs la 'jug go /bzhi par ni lha'i bu dang bu mo dag 'dod pa'i yon tan la dga' zhing rtse bar byed do/ / gzhan yang tshal bzhi po de dag na rim pa ltar sngar bshad pa'i khyad par dang ldan pa'i rdzing bu sna tshogs dang*/ rtsub 'gyur dang 'dres pa dang*/ dga' ba zhes bya ba chu zheng du dpag tshad lnga bcu lnga bcu mtha' nyis brgyas 'khor ba yod do/ /

The area 20 yojanas outside the city of Sudarśana is adorned by the groves called Caitraratha to the east, Pāruṣyaka to the south, Miśrakā to the west, and Nandana to the north. The city is surrounded by a square golden fence one yojana high, 250 yojanas on each side, and 1,000 yojanas in length. Its protecting walls, parapets, and foundations are as explained before. In the first of those, there are various chariots of precious substances. In the second, when sons of gods are seated there, their minds become coarse. In the third, sons and daughters of the gods mix and enter into various activities. In the fourth, sons and daughters of the gods take joy in and play with desirable objects. Again, in those four groves there are, in order, various ponds possessing the features explained before: various substances, coarse [minds], mixed activities, and joyful play. In breadth they are 50 yojanas and surrounded by a 200-yojana perimeter.
de dag gi ni phyogs bzhi na/ / nyi shus bcad na sa gzhi bzang / / 68 byang shar mtshams na yongs 'du ste/ / lho nub mtshams na chos bzang ngo/ /
Twenty yojanas beyond these in the four directions are the pure fields. In the northeastern subdirection is Pārijātaka. In the southwestern subdirection is Sudharmā. (3:68)

tshal de dag gi phyi rol gyi phyogs bzhi na dpag tshad nyi shu nyi shus bcad pa na shar phyogs na sa gzhi bzang po sna tshogs can dang*/ lho na rtsub 'gyur dang*/ nub na 'dres pa can dang*/ byang na dga' ba zhes bya ba tshal gyi tshad dang mnyam pa phan tshun 'gran pa lta bu bzhi'ang yod de/ de dag na lha'i drang srong rnams kyang rang dgar tshangs par spyad pa spyod pa yod do/ / lha'i grong khyer dang skyed mos tshal dang*/ skyed mos tshal nas sa gzhi'i bar dag na grong khyer nas tshal dang*/ tshal nas sa gzhir 'gro ba'i lam sngar bshad pa'i khyad par dang ldan pa tshur dpag tshad nyi shu nyi shu zheng du dpag tshad phyed dang gnyis gnyis yod pa dag na glang po che dang rta dang shing rta dang khyogs kyi bzhon pa bkod pa dag yod pa la lha rnams zhon te tshal dang sa gzhir 'gro zhing 'dod yon gyi dga' ba myong bar byed do/ /

Twenty yojanas beyond each of these groves in the four directions are various pure fields, in the east a variegated field, in the south a field of coarse [minds], in the west a field of mixed activities, and in the north a field of joyful play. The four fields are equal in measure and vie with each other for popularity, and divine rishis also practice celibacy there. From the divine city to the pleasure groves, and from the pleasure groves to the fields, there are paths possessing the features previously explained. On these paths, twenty yojanas long and a yojana and a half wide, gods ride elephants, horses, chariots, and palanquins and proceed to the groves and fields and experience the joys of sense objects. [274]

grong khyer blta na sdug de'i phyi rol gyi byang shar gyi mtshams na dpag bsam gyi shing yongs 'du sa brtul zhes bya ba yod de/ 'di dang sa las dpag tshad lnga thur du zug par bshad la/ gdags pa ltar na rtsa ba dpag tshad lnga bcu thur du zug pa steng du dpag tshad brgya 'phags pa steng du yal ga dang lo 'dab kyis dpag tshad lnga bcu lnga bcur khyab pas chu zheng du dpag tshad brgya lnga bcu lnga bcu ste mtha' skor du dpag tshad zhi brgya lnga bcu yod pa de'i me tog dang 'dab ma rgyas pa'i dri yis rdzi phyogs ma yin par dpag tshad lnga bcur ldang ba rdzi phyogs su dpag tshad brgyar ldang ba {'og dpag tshad brgya bcur gsal pa } zhig yod do/ / 'o na lung bar ma'i yongs 'du'i mdo las/ me tog dri ni rdzi phyogs min mi 'gro/ / rtsa ba'am rgya spos tsan dan yang ma yin/ / mkhas rnams dri ni rdzi phyogs min 'gro ste/ / skyes bu dam pa phyogs rnams kun du 'gro zhes bshad pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/ kha cig na re rdzi phyogs ma yin par 'gro ba ni shing de'i yal ga dang lo 'dab kyis dpag tshad lnga bcur khyab pas de las ma 'das pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ba ni ma yin te/ de ni shing gzhan la'ang yod na de kho na'i ngo mtshar ba'i chos su mi 'grub pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir mdo'i dgongs pa ni mi'i me tog gi dbang du byas pa yin no zhes gsungs pa 'dod par bya'o/ /

In the northeastern subdirection outside the city of Sudarśana there is a wish-fulfilling tree called Pārijātaka. It is said that its roots thrust downward five yojanas into the ground.[929] In accordance with Presentation on the World, its roots thrust downward fifty yojanas, and above that its branches, leaves, and flowers rise eight yojanas and extend fifty yojanas. Therefore it covers an area of 150 yojanas, with a circumference of 450 yojanas. The extensive scent of its flowers and leaves travels fifty yojanas against the wind and a hundred yojanas with the wind {and permeates eighty yojanas below}.[930] Objection: However, doesn’t this contradict the explanation of a sūtra from the Medium-Length Discourses, which states: The scent of the flowers does not spread against the wind, nor does their essence, Chinese incense, or sandalwood. But the fragrance of scholars travels against the wind, and the purity of beings proceeds in all directions.[931] Some say: Spreading against the wind means that since the branches and leaves of this particular tree pervade fifty yojanas, its scent does not go beyond this. Reply: That is not so, because that also happens for some trees. Therefore that alone is not established as an extraordinary quality, for the intention of this sūtra is considered to be from the perspective of human flowers.

{sa'i stod 'grel las kyang gal te rdzi phyogs ma yin par dri 'gro ba ni mi rigs te/ 'di na ma mthong ba'i phyir ro zhe na de lta na gzugs med pa rnams kyang med par 'gyur ro/ / gzhan yang de dang 'di'i 'byor pa'i khyad par mi 'dra bas rdzi phyogs su yang dra ldang pa mi 'gal te/ las kyis khyad par gyis mngon par grub pa'i phyir dper na 'di na ma brdungs par rnga las sgra mi 'byung yang de na ma brdungs par yang sgra 'byung ba bzhin no zhes bshad do }

{Also, Detailed Explanation of Yogācāra Levels declares: If it is said that it is illogical that such scent travels against the wind “because it is not observed,” then even formless states would not exist. Again, it is not contradictory that scent also spreads with the wind, since what is obtained differs in different places because what arises is established by diverse types of karma. For example, sound may not arise from a drum not beaten here, but sound may arise when not beaten there.}[932]

sa ston sde pa ni rdzi phyogs su dpag tshad brgyar dri'i ngad ldang ngo*/ / rlung med na ni dpag tshad lnga bcur ldang ngo zhes 'don to/ / de lta bu'i shing de ni sum cu rtsa gsum pa'i 'dod pa'i yon tan dag ster ba'i dpag bsam gyi shing yin no/ / shing de'i drung na la ba dkar po lta bu'i rdo leb ces bya ba chu zheng du dpag tshad lnga bcu lnga bcu mtha' dpag tshad nyis brgyas 'khor ba'i gru bzhi pa 'phang du dpag tshad phyed dang drug dang dpag tshad bco brgyad cha gcig yod pa tshon sna brgya rtsa gcig gis bkra shis reg na 'jam pa me tog man da ra bas pus nub tsam du khebs pa yod de/ de'i dbus su brgya byin gyi seng ge'i khri dang de'i drung na nye dbang la sogs pa rnams kyi seng ge'i khri bshams pa la lha'i dbang po brgya byin 'khor dang bcas pa dbyar zla ba bzhir lha'i 'dod yon la rtse zhing rang rang gi las kyi 'bras bu myong bar byed do zhes gdags pa las bshad do/ /

The Mahīśāsaka school asserts that pleasant fragrances spread for a hundred yojanas with the wind. If there is no wind, they spread for fifty yojanas. This tree is a wish-granting tree that bestows qualities desired by the gods of Trāyastriṃśa. At its foot there is a white, flat square stone fifty yojanas wide, two hundred yojanas in circumference, and five and a half plus one-eighteenth yojana in height. In its center is the lion throne of Śakra, and at its foot are arranged the lion thrones of Viṣṇu and so on. Śakra, the lord of the gods, and his retinue sport for the four months of summer with the sense objects of the gods, experiencing the results of their individual karma. This is explained in Presentation on the World.[933]

grong khyer gyi phyi rol gyi lho nub kyi mtshams {dpag tshad bcu gnyis } na gang du lha rnams 'khod nas bya ba dang bya ba ma yin pa 'gro bar byed pa chos bzang lha'i mdun sa zhes bya ba chu zheng du dpag tshad sum brgya sum brgya mtha' skor du dgu brgya yod pa lha'i grong khyer las dpag tshad phyed dang bzhis gyen du 'phags pa mdzes shing blta na sdug pa sa gzhi dang ya thog dang bgab pa dang spyi bsdus kyi gdung dang yang thog gi rtse bzhi dang phyam rten dang phyam dgu po thams cad shel las byas pas/ sprin dkar po'i phung po ltar dkar ba/ rin po che sna bzhi'i lan kan gyis bskor ba phyam dgu po re re'ang ka ba bcu drug bcu drug gis brten pa/ dbus na bai DUr+Ya 'i ka ba zur brgyad pa gsal zhing 'phan med pa spyi bsdus kyi gdung la skra rtse tsam gyis ma reg pa de'i drung na brgya byin chos ston pa'i gser gyi khri bshams pa yod do/ / de'i mthar nye dbang gzhan rnams kyi gser gyi khri bshams te der sum cu rtsa gsum pa'i lha rnams 'dus nas lha dang mi rnams kyi don dang chos sems shing dpyod pa dang chos dang chos ma yin pa'i mdun ma 'gro bar byed do/ / der sum cu rtsa gsum pa'i lha rnams gnas pa na sum cu rtsa gsum pa'i srung ma rgyal po chen po bzhi'i g.yog zho shas 'tsho pa rnams dang*/ rgyal chen bzhi'i bu rnams dang*/ rgyal po chen po bzhi po rnams kyis go rim bzhin du zla ba phyed kyi tshes brgyad dang bcu bzhi dang bco lnga la 'jig rten 'di thams cad myul zhing 'jigs rten pa rnams chos dang mthun pa dang mi mthun pa sgrogs par byed do/ / de'i tshe chos dang mi mthun pa thos na lha rnams mi dga' zhing smod la/ chos dang mthun pa thos na dga' zhing bsngags par brjod do/ /

In the southwestern subdirection {twelve yojanas} outside the city [275] there is the meeting place called Sudharmā, where the gods gather and discuss what is proper and improper action. It is three hundred yojanas wide and nine hundred yojanas in circumference.
Three and a half yojanas from the divine city, rising above the plain, are elegant divine dwellings that are beautiful to behold. Their foundations and covering roofs, central beams, four roof pinnacles, roof spars, and curved frame are all made of crystal. They are white like a mass of white clouds, surrounded by upper stories of the four varieties of precious substance, and each curved frame is supported by sixteen pillars. In the center of each are eight-sided vaiḍūrya pillars that are luminous and support the central beam that they do not touch by a hair’s breadth. In front of that is placed Śakra’s golden throne for teaching Dharma, and beyond it the golden throne of Viṣṇu. When the gods of Trāyastriṃśa gather there, they contemplate and analyze the purpose of gods and humans and discuss what is Dharma and non-Dharma. When the gods of Trāyastriṃśa abide there, the guardians of Trāyastriṃśa, assistants who serve the four great kings, sons of the four great kings, and the four great kings [themselves] serially scrutinize the entire world on the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth of the half-month and proclaim which worldly beings act in accordance with Dharma or not. At that time, if they hear of actions incompatible with Dharma, the gods express their dislike and disapproval. If they hear of actions compatible with Dharma, they like and praise them.

lha'i grong khyer nas mdun sa chos bzang du rgyu ba'i lam srid du dpag tshad bcu gnyis zheng du dpag tshad gnyis yod pa gser gyi bye ma bdal zhing tsan dan gyi chus chag chag btab pa g.yas g.yon na me tog dang 'bras bu'i shing sna tshogs skyes shing thang las skyes pa'i bya sna tshogs skad snyan pa yod de/ 'di'i ltar na mdun sa ni grong khyer nas dpag tshad bcu gnyis na yod par mngon no/ / de lta bu'i mdun sa de yang gdags pa las/ shar lho'i mtshams na yod par bshad la/ sa'i dngos gzhi las ni grong khyer gyi byang shar gyi mtshams na mdun sa dang*/ shing yongs 'du sa brtol ni grong gi nang na yod par bshad de phyogs gang na yod pa ni ma bshad do/ / drang srong rgyas pas zhus pa'i mdo las ni mdun sa dbyibs gru bzhi lham pa mtha' skor du dpag tshad brgya yod par gsungs so/ / gzhan yang brgya byin la g.yul ngor spyod pa'i glang po che rab brtan dang*/ skyed mos tshal du spyod pa'i glang po che sa srung gi bu gnyis ka'ang mtha' dpag tshad bdun bdun gyis 'khor ba 'phang du dpag tshad phyed dang gnyis kyi tshad du yod par re re'ang glang g.yog brgyad stong dang bcas pa dang*/ phal cher nub phyogs kyi gling phran kham bu can zhes bya ba na gnas pa rta'i rgyal po sprin gyi shugs can zhes bya ba rta g.yog brgyad stong dang bcas pa yod do/ / lha'i rnga po che chos kyis mtho ba zhes bya ba las 'dus byas thams cad ni mi rtag pa/ zag pa dang bcas pa thams cad sdug bsngal ba/ chos thams cad bdag med pa/ mya ngan las 'das pa ni zhi ba yin na lha'i bu dag ci'i phyir bag med par gnas zhes lha'i bu dag 'dod pa'i yon tan gyis myos pa las skul bar byed pa dang*/ kye lha rnams rgyal bar 'gyur/ lha ma yin rnams pham par 'gyur ro/ / zhes lha ma yin gyi dmag gi 'tshe ba nye bar zhi bar byed pa'i sgra 'byung ba yod do/ /

From the city of the gods, there is a path proceeding to the meeting place of Sudharmā that is twelve yojanas long and two yojanas wide. It is spread with golden sand and sprinkled with sandalwood water. To the left and right various flowers and fruit trees grow, and there are various plain birds with pleasant voices. In accordance with this, the meeting place exists twelve yojanas from the city. Also, Presentation on the World explains that the meeting place exists in the southeast subdirection.[934] Yogācāra Levels explains that the meeting place exists in the northeast subdirection and that the wish-fulfilling tree exists within the city limits, but it does not explain where it exists. The Sūtra Requested by Rishi Vyāsa says that the shape of the meeting place is square and eight yojanas in circumference.[935] Further, Śakra has two elephants: Airāvata, who is fearless in battle, and the son of the earth-guardian elephant, who sports in the pleasure groves. They are seven yojanas around and a yojana and a half wide, and each has eight thousand elephant attendants. Also he has the horse king called Bālāhaka (Mighty Cloud) with eight thousand horse attendants who lives in the western minor continent called “the place of apricots.” If the hammer [276] of Dharma of the great divine drum proclaims the sound “All conditioned states are impermanent, all contaminated entities are associated with suffering, all phenomena are selfless, nirvāṇa is peace,” why would the sons of the gods not abide with diligence? Therefore the sons of gods are exhorted not to be intoxicated by sense objects. Also, it proclaims: “Ah! The gods are victorious and the demigods are defeated,”[936] and the violence of the war of the demigods is pacified.

Above those are the mansions of the gods. Those who utilize sense objects are the six gods. In two they engage in sexual union through uniting both organs, or by embracing, holding hands, laughter, and observing. (3:69)

sum cu rtsa gsum de'i steng na ni 'thab bral nas 'og min gyi bar gyi lha rnams kyi gzhal med khang rnams sprin gyi phung po ltar gong nas gong du brtsegs nas gnas pa las 'dod pa spyod pa ni rgyal chen ris bzhi nas gzhan 'phrul dbang byed kyi bar drug yin no/ / dang po gnyis na ni lha ma yin rnams dang 'thab pa yod de/{ shes spring las/ lha min na yang rang bzhin gyis lha yi/ / dpal la sdang zhing yid kyi sdug bsngal che/ / de dag blo dang ldan yang 'gro ba yi/ / sgrib pas bsgribs pas bden pa mthong ba med/ / ces 'byung bas/} 'di ltar lha ma yin dang lha rnams lha ma yin gyi bu mo dang lha'i bdud rtsi la ser sna dang phrag dog gis brtsod pa'i phyir 'thab pa na res 'ga' ni thags bzang ris la sogs pa'i lha ma yin gyi rgyal po bzhi ga 'ong la res 'ga' gong ma dag 'ong ste/ gser dngul bai DUr+Ya shel bzhi'i go cha sra ba rnams gyon zhing ral gri dang mdung dang 'phang mdung dang mda' gzhu thogs pa'i dpung gi tshogs yan lag bzhi dang bcas pa chu mtshams nas 'thon te/ brgya byin gyis srung ma lnga las dang po dkar po la dga' ba'i klu'i rgyal po rol mtsho na gnas pa dang g.yul sprod cing de dag gis thub na ldog la gal te ma thub na srung ma gnyis pa gzhong thogs pa dang*/ gsum pa phreng thogs pa dang*/ bzhi pa rtag myos pa dang*/ lnga pa rgyal po chen po bzhi po dag tu rim gyis song zhing 'og ma 'og ma dang bsdoms shing 'thab par byed pa na phal cher ni de dag gis bzlog par 'gyur ro/ / gal te de dag gis ma bzlog na rgyal chen bzhi po dag sum cu rtsa gsum gyi gnas su song ste/ kye lha'i dbang po mkhyen par mdzod cig /bdag cag srung ma lnga po dag gis lha ma yin gyi dmag bzlog par mi nus so {zhing ri rab gyi bang rim la rjes la mkhyen par mdzod cig } zhes zhu bar byed do/ / de nas lha'i dbang po brgya byin gyis sum cu rtsa gsum pa rnams la bsgos te g.yul sprad par byed do/

Above those gods of the heaven of Trāyastriṃśa are the celestial mansions of the gods of the Yāma heaven to Akaniṣṭha, arrayed progressively higher and higher, like a mass of clouds. Those who utilize sense objects are the six gods from the heaven of Cāturmahārājika to Paranirmitavaśavartin. The first two are demigods and those who engage in conflict. {Letter to a Friend reads: Demigods are by nature gods who hate the exalted gods and have great mental suffering. Though they possess intelligence, they are obscured by the defilements of reincarnating beings and do not see the four truths.[937]} Gods and demigods argue and fight, due to avarice and jealousy, over female āsuras and the nectar (amṛta) of the gods. At times the four kings of the demigods, such as Vemacitra and so on, come; at times, those higher come. They wear solid armor of four substances — gold, silver, vaiḍūrya, and crystal — and rise from beneath the level of the water with four army batallions bearing swords, spears, throwing spears, and bows and arrows. Śakra sends the first of the five guardians, Nando Nāgarājā, who likes white and abides in the pleasure ocean, to enter battle, and if he prevails, the demigods are stopped. But if he does not prevail, Śakra in turn sends the second guardian, Karoṭapāṇi, then the third, Mālādhāra, then the fourth, Sādamatta, and then the fifth, the four great kings, each reinforcing the former. And if they fight, they will probably defeat the demigods, but if they cannot defeat them, the four great kings go to the land of Trāyastriṃśa and proclaim, “Ah! Powerful gods, hear this! Our five guardians cannot defeat the demigods in battle: {make this known on the terraces of Meru.”} Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, commands the gods of Trāyastriṃśa to enter the war.
