'phags pa'i lam yan lag brgyad par bshad pa ni mnyam par bzhag pa'i stobs kyis de las langs pa na rdzun la sogs pa mi byed pa thob pa'i phyir yan lag brgyad par bshad pa yin no/ / sdom pa rnams ni dran shes bzhin gyis zin pa'i sems pa'i rgyun la 'dod pa'i phyir dang*/ chu lon du gsungs pa ni spang bya nye ba na ngo tsha shes pas dam bcas pa dran nas gnyen po 'chal tshul spong ba yin gyi/ gal te rig byed ma yin pa kho nas 'chal tshul gyi gegs byed na brjed pa la sogs pa la tshul khrims 'dral ba mi srid par 'gyur ro zhes brjod par byed do/ / 'on kyang bye brag tu smra ba ni/ gzugs su yod do zhes 'dod do/ / gal te rnam par rig byed ma yin pa'i gzugs rdzas su yod la de yang 'byung bzhi rgyur byas par 'dod na/ de ci rnam par rig byed skyed byed kyi 'byung ba kho na las skye'am/ 'on te rig byed skyed byed las gzhan pa'i 'byung ba las skye zhe na/ rig byed ma yin pa bstan med thog med yin pas phra ba dang*/ rig byed de las bzlog pas rags pa yin la/ 'byung bzhi'i tshogs pa gcig gis 'bras bu phra rags gnyis bskyed pa 'gal bas rig byed skyed byed las gzhan pa'i 'byung ba las skye'o/ / 'o na rig byed ma yin pa rang rang dang dus mnyam pa'am dus tha dad pa'i 'byung ba las skye zhe na/

The branches of the ārya path are said to be eight because the actions of not telling lies and so on are obtained by the power of equipoise after arising from equipoise. The vows are asserted to exist in the continuum of the mind conjoined with mindfulness and introspection. They are said to be a “dam” because they abandon unethical conduct due to the application of their antidote through shame in considering nonvirtue and through mindfulness of one’s commitments. If, as claimed, nonindicative form alone stopped unethical conduct, it would be impossible to damage one’s ethics through forgetfulness and so on. Nonetheless, Vaibhāṣikas assert that it exists as form. Question: If nonindicative form is substantially existent and it is asserted that the four primary elements act as its cause, does it arise solely from the primary elements that generate indicative form, or does it arise from primary elements other than those that generate indicative form? Reply: Since nonindicative form is undemonstrable and unimpeded, it is subtle, but since it opposes indicative form, it is coarse. But nonindicative form arises from primary elements other than those generating indicative form, since it is contradictory that both a subtle and coarse result arise through a single collection of the four primary elements. Question: Yet does nonindicative form arise from primary elements occurring at the same time or at a different time from nonindicative form?

'dod pa na spyod pa'i rnam par rig byed ma yin pa ma gtogs pa rnam par rig byed dang*/ bsam gtan zag med kyi sdom pa dang*/ phyi nang gi gzugs thams cad ni rang rang dang dus mnyam pa'i 'byung ba kho na las skye la/ 'dod par gtogs pa'i rnam par rig byed min pa sdom pa sdom min bar mas bsdus pa rnams ni skad cig ma dang po ni rang dang dus mnyam pa lhan cig pa da ltar ba'i 'byung ba las skye ste/ slob dpon rgyal po'i sras kyis/ 'dod pa na spyod pa'i rnam par rig byed ma yin pa ni sdom pa la sogs pa nod pa'i tshe lhan cig skye ba'i 'byung ba chen po dag rgyur byas nas 'byung la/ de bzhin du rnam par rig byed ma yin pa gzhan yang de dag kho na rgyur byas nas 'byung ngo*/ / 'di ltar de dag ni gzhi'i don du 'gyur te zhes pa dang*/ slob dpon gang spel gyis kyang*/ skad cig ma dang po ni 'phen par byed pa'i 'byung ba dang*/ lhan cig skye ba'i phyir ro zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: Leaving aside nonindicative form existing in the desire realm, all indicative form, uncontaminated absorption vows, and external and internal form arise from primary elements occurring at the same time as them alone. Nonindicative form of the desire realm, which includes vows, negative commitments, and interim precepts, arises in the first moment from the present primary elements that are concurrent and coemergent with it. Master Jinaputra writes: When nonindicative forms active in the desire realm — vows and so forth — are obtained, they arise from the great elements that arise simultaneously and act as their cause. So too, other types of nonindicative form arise from them alone, and [the great elements] act as their cause. Thus they function as foundational states.[1030] Also Master Pūrṇavardhana explains: The first moment arises simultaneously with the projecting elements.[1031]
des na de dag ni 'di'i ngo bo skyed byed dang 'jug pa dang 'phen pa'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir gzhi'i don gyi 'byung ba zhes bya ste/ dper na 'khor lo sa la 'dril pa lag pas 'phul ba bzhin no/ /

Therefore they are called “basic entities” (padārtha) because they generate the essential nature of nonindicative form and act as the cause of its continuance and projection, just like a wheel rolling on the ground pushed by a hand.

skad cig ma dang po phyin chad ni 'das pa'i 'byung ba chen po dag las skye ste/ lus kyi tshogs pa na yod pa'i 'byung ba da ltar ba rnams ni skyes zin gnas pa dang rjes su 'jug pa dang rten par byed pa'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir/ rten gyi don gyi 'byung ba zhes bya ste/ dper na 'khor lo 'dril ba la sa phyogs bzhin no/ / des na 'dod pa'i rnam par rig byed ma yin pa'i gzugs ni srog gcod pa spong ba lta bu gcig kyang skad cig ma dang po'i tshe lhan cig pa da ltar ba'i 'byung ba bzhi tshan kho na dang*/ skad cig ma gnyis pa phan chad ngo bo skyed byed gzhi'i 'byung ba 'das pa dang*/ skyes zin gnas pa'i rten gyi 'byung ba da ltar ba lus kyi tshogs pa na yod pa las kyang skye bas 'byung ba bzhi tshan gnyis gnyis las skye zhing*/ bsam gtan zag med kyi sdom pa ni spong ba bdun char yang dus mnyam pa dang da ltar ba'i 'byung ba bzhi tshan gcig kho na las skye la/ de dag las gzhan brgyur byas pa'i gzugs thams cad ni rang rang dang dus mnyam pa lhan cig pa'i 'byung ba bzhi tshan tha dad kho na las skye ste/ slob dpon gang spel gyis bsam gtan dang zag pa med pa'i sdom pa gnyis kyi rten 'byung ba chen po rnams ni sems dang 'dra bar dus mnyam pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes pa dang*/ spyir btang gi dbang du byas nas slob dpon chen po'i sras kyis kyang*/ rgyur byas pa'i gzugs rnam par rig pa dang*/ rnam par rig byed ma yin pa dang*/ bsam gtan dang zag pa med pas bsdus pa dang*/ mig dang rna ba dang gzugs dang sgra la sogs pa thams cad ni da ltar dus mnyam pa'i 'byung ba chen po dag kho na rgyur byas nas 'byung ngo zhes pa dang*/ ji ltar rgyur byas pa'i gzugs gzhan dag gi gzhi da ltar ba'i 'byung ba chen po rnams yin pa de bzhin du de'i rten ni 'das pa rnams yin no zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/ /

After the first moment nonindicative form arises from past great elements because the present elements that compose the body maintain that which has arisen, sustain it, [308] and act as its supportive cause. They are called “supportive elements” since they are like the ground upon which the wheel turns. Therefore nonindicative form of the desire realm arises in two phases: (1) that arising in the phase of the four present and coemergent primary elements in the first moment of an action, such as abandoning taking life, and (2) that arising in the phase of the four primary elements that compose the body, which is derived from the four past basic elements that generate the essential nature of nonindicative form and the present supportive primary elements that maintain that which is already arisen. Uncontaminated absorption vows that abandon seven aspects arise from a single cluster of four present and concurrent primary elements alone. All derivative form other than them arises from separate clusters of the four concurrent and coemergent primary elements alone. Master Pūrṇavardhana notes: The primary elements that are the basis of both uncontaminated vows and absorption vows are concurrent like the mind [concurrent with them].[1032] And from a general perspective Master Jinaputra also explains: All derivative indicative and nonindicative form, form subsumed by absorption and uncontaminated states, and the eyes, ears, form, sound, and so on arise from the present, concurrent, great elements alone.[1033] And: Just as the present great elements are the foundation of other derivative forms, similarly their foundation is the past [primary] elements.[1034]
zag bcas lus dang ngag gi las/ / rang gi 'byung ba dag rgyur byas/ / zag med gang du skyes pa'i yin/ / rnam rig byed min ma zin dang / / 5
Its primary elements act as the cause of contaminated physical and verbal karma. The uncontaminated arises where the vows arise. Nonindicative form is not conjoined. (4:5)
'byung ba de yang sa gang gis bsdus pa yin zhe na/
Question: On what level do these elements exist?

zag bcas kyi lus dang ngag gi las rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa thams cad ni rang gi sa pa'i 'byung ba dag rgyur byas pa yin te/ 'dod par gtogs pa'i lus ngag gi las 'dod pa'i 'byung ba rgyur byas pa yin pa nas bsam gtan bzhi pa'i sa pa'i lus ngag gi las ni bsam gtan bzhi pa'i sa pa kho na'i 'byung ba rgyur byas pa'i bar du'o/ / zag med kyi lus ngag gi las ni rten dbang btsan pas sdom pa de gang du skyes pa'i sa pa de'i 'byung ba dag yin te/ zag med khams su ma gtogs shing 'byung ba la nges par ltos la zag med la 'byung ba gzhan med pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir 'dod khams pa'i rgyud la zag med kyi sdom pa skyes na de 'dod pa'i 'byung ba las skyes so zhes bya ba la sogs pa'o/ / de yang rnam par rig byed min pa de'i rang gi ngo bo ni rdul phran bsags pa'i gzugs ma yin pas yul na mi gnas shing phan gnod kyis tshor ba bde sdug la sogs pa sems sems byung gi rten ma yin pas ma zin pa dang*/

Reply: The primary elements of a specific level act as the cause of all indicative and nonindicative contaminated (sāsrava) physical and verbal karma of that level because the primary elements of the desire realm act as the cause of physical and verbal karma belonging to the desire realm, and the primary elements of the fourth absorption alone act as the cause of the physical and verbal karma belonging to the fourth absorption level. Uncontaminated (anāsrava) physical and verbal karma arises from the primary elements of the level where the vows arise due to the powerful support [of the elements] because uncontaminated states do not belong to any [specific] realm but definitely rely on the primary elements, and no separate primary elements exist in uncontaminated states. Therefore if uncontaminated vows arise in the mindstream of a desire-realm being, they arise from the primary elements of the desire realm and so on. Further, nonindicative form does not reside in a particular place since in essence it is not form composed of atoms. It is not conjoined (anupāttika) with awareness since it does not act as the basis of minds and mental factors, such as the feelings of pleasure and pain that arise through being benefited or harmed.
rgyu mthun las byung sems can ston/ / rgyu mthun zin pa'i 'byung las skye/ / ting 'dzin skyes 'byung ma zin dang / / rgyas byung tha dad min las skyes/ / 6

It arises from natural outflow, made known in sentient beings. It arises from conjoined elements, from natural outflow. It arises from concentration, those unconjoined, those derived from enhancement, those undifferentiated. (4:6)

skal mnyam gyi rgyu las skyes pa'i phyir rgyu mthun las byung ba yin gyi rnam smin dang rgyas byung ni ma yin te/ rim pa ltar dge mi dger nges pas lung ma bstan ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ rdul phran bsags pa ma yin pas rgyas pa'i rgyu dag gis rgyas par mi byed pa'i phyir ro/ / sems can du ston pa yin te/ rgyud du gtogs pa'i chos yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Because nonindicative form is generated from homogeneous causes, it arises from natural outflow (naiṣyanda). It does not arise from the causes of either karmic maturation or enhancement because, respectively, it is not neutral (since it is definitely either [309] virtuous or nonvirtuous) and it is not enhanced by causes of enhancement (since it is not composed of atoms). It is made known in sentient beings (sattvākhyā) because it is a phenomenon belonging to their mindstreams.

'dod pa'i rig byed ma yin pa de ni kun slong gi sems la ltos pa dang*/ mnyam gzhag ma yin pa dang*/ gzugs can chad nas mtshams sbyor pa'i phyir rim pa ltar gnyis dang*/ ting nge 'dzin gyis rgyas pa dang*/ rnam smin skyes kyi 'byung ba las skye ba ma yin gyi/ skal mnyam gyis bskyed pas rgyu mthun las byung ba'i 'byung ba dang*/ da ltar gyi lus kyi tshogs pa na yod pas rgyud kyis zin pa'i 'byung ba chen po'i rgyu las skye ba dang*/ sems kyi rjes 'brang ma yin pas 'byung ba bzhi tshan tha dad las skye ba yin no/ / ting nge 'dzin las skyes pa'i rig byed ma yin pa bsam gtan dang zag med kyi sdom pa ni TIk+kar mnyam par bzhag pa'i sems kyi ngang gis lus de la sems kyi rjes su 'byung ba'i 'byung ba 'byung ba'i phyir te/ zin pa'i 'byung ba chen po rnams ni 'gog pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa la sogs pa'i gnas skabs dag na sems med par 'byung ngo*/ / zhes 'byung bas ma zin pa'i 'byung ba dang*/ rgyas pa las byung ba'i 'byung ba las skye ste/ ting nge 'dzin gyis rgyas pa'i phyir ro/ / sems kyi rjes su 'jug pas 'byung ba tha dad min pa las skye ba yin te/ spong ba bdun ka'ang 'byung ba bzhi tshan gcig la brten pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir 'grel pa las/ sems bzhin du 'byung ba tha mi dad pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes pa dang*/ TIka byed dag gis kyang*/ ji ltar de skyed par byed pa'i sems tha dad pa ma yin pa de bzhin du de skyed par byed pa'i 'byung ba rnams kyang tha mi dad pa kho na yin no/ / 'byung ba chen po dag ni rten gyi don gyis rnam par rig byed ma yin pa'i gzhir gyur pa ma yin no/ / 'o na ci zhe na/ de 'jug par byed pa'i don gyis te/ de lta bas na 'byung ba tha mi dad pa las skye'o zhes bshad do/ / 'dis ni ting nge 'dzin las skyes pa ma yin pa ni spong ba re re'ang 'byung ba bzhi tshan so so las skye ba'i phyir tha dad pa'i 'byung ba las skye'o zhes bstan pa yin no/ /

Nonindicative form of the desire realm (1) relies on the motivating mind, (2) is not associated with equipoise, and (3) continues when [other] physical states cease. Therefore, respectively, (1) it does not arise in sleep, (2) it is not enhanced by concentration, and (3) it does not arise from the primary elements of maturational birth. It arises from the great elements derived from natural outflow (niṣyanda), since it is generated by homogeneous causes, and it arises from the primary elements conjoined (upātta) with the mindstream, since it exists in the present composite body. Further, it arises from a separate cluster of the four great elements, since it does not complement the mind. Nonindicative form that arises from concentration (samādhi) refers to the absorption vows and uncontaminated vows. Purṇavardhana writes in his Commentary: The primary elements arising in the body due to the mind of equipoise arise subsequent to the mind. Therefore the primary elements conjoined [with the mind] arise during the meditative attainment of cessation and so on when the mind does not exist.[1035] Therefore [nonindicative form] arises from unconjoined primary elements and primary elements derived from enhancement because it is enhanced by concentration. It arises from undifferentiated primary elements that are subsequent to the mind because the seven actions to be abandoned are each reliant on a single cluster of the four primary elements. Therefore the Autocommentary declares: Like the mind, the elements are not differentiated.[1036] And also the Subcommentary elaborates: Just as the mind generating it is not differentiated, so too the elements that generate it are solely undifferentiated. The great elements do not act as the foundation of nonindicative form or its support. Why is that? It is because the [elements] enter [nonindicative form]. Thus it arises from undifferentiated elements.[1037] This text indicates that [nonindicative form,] which does not arise from concentration, arises from differentiated elements because it arises from separate groups of four elements for each action to be abandoned.
gsum pa de dag gi khyad par
Distinguishing indicative and nonindicative form

['di] la'ang ngo bo dang sa'i khyad par dang*/ dge ba dang mi dge ba dang lung ma bstan gyi dbye ba dang*/ rig byed ma yin pa rgyas par dbye ba dang*/ ldan pa'i tshul dang*/ 'thob pa'i tshul dang*/ gtong ba'i tshul dang*/ rten gyi khyad par bdun las

This has seven headings: differences of nature and level; classification of virtue, nonvirtue, and neutral states; detailed classification of nonindicative form; how vows are possessed; how vows are obtained; how vows are relinquished; and difference of karmic agent.
dang po ni/
DIFFERENCES OF NATURE AND LEVEL
rnam rig min lung bstan min med/ / gzhan ni rnam gsum mi dge ni/ / 'dod na'o gzugs na'ang rnam rig min/ / rnam rig dpyod dang bcas dag na/ / 7

Nonindicative form is never neutral. Others have three types. Nonvirtuous states exist in the desire realm. Nonindicative form also exists in the form realm. Indicative form exists in those possessing analysis. (4:7)

rnam par rig byed min pa ni lung bstan pa dge mi dge min pa lung ma bstan ni cung zad kyang med de/ 'di ni kun slong gis dge ba la sogs par 'gyur ba yin na lung ma bstan gyi sems la stobs chung bas kun slong 'gags kyang rgyun rjes su 'jug pa'i las 'phen pa'i nus pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / de las gzhan rig byed dang sems pa dag ni dge mi dge lung ma bstan rnam pa gsum yin no/ / de dag las mi dge ba'i rig byed ma yin pa dang rig byed dang sems pa dag ni 'dod pa kho na na yod par rig par bya'o/ / gzugs na'ang bsam gtan zag med kyi sdom pa rnam par rig byed min pa yod la/ 'ang gi sgras ni 'dod pa na yod par ston pa ste/ gzugs med na ni gzugs can thams cad med pa'i phyir ro/ / lus ngag gi rnam par rig byed ni gnyis pa yan chad na kun slong med pas rtog dpyod dang bcas pa'i sa 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang po dag kho na na yod kyi

Nonindicative form is never neutral (vyākṛta) or not declared [by the Buddha] to be virtuous or nonvirtuous. It is virtuous and so on [310] due to that which motivates it, but that motivation can be countered by weak neutral minds, rendering it incaple of maintaining its own continuum. Other indicative forms and intentions have three types: (1) virtuous, (2) nonvirtuous, and (3) neutral. From among those, it should be understood that nonvirtuous nonindicative form, indicative form, and intention exist in the desire realm alone. Uncontaminated absorption vows that are nonindicative form also exist in the form realm. The term “also” indicates that it exists in the desire realm, but no physical objects exist in the formless realm. Physical and verbal indicative form only exist in those desire-realm and first-absorption levels possessing investigation and analysis, since motivation does not exist in the second absorption and above.
'dod pa na yang bsgribs pa med/ / gang phyir kun slong med thar pa/ /
Also there is no obscured form in the desire realm. Why? There is no obscured mind that motivates it. (4:8ab)

'dod pa'i khams na yang bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa'i rig byed med de/ gang gi phyir zhe na de na kun nas slong ba'i bsgribs pa'i sems med pa'i phyir te/ 'di ltar 'dod pa na lta ba dang po gnyis mtshungs ldan dang bcas pa bsgribs la lung ma bstan yod mod kyi de dag ni mthong spang yin pas/ kha nang du bltas pa'i phyir rig byed kun nas slong ba ma yin no/ / de'i phyir bsgribs pa'i lus ngag gi rig byed ni tshangs pa chen po g.yo rgyus kun nas bslangs nas ngag smra ba la sogs pa byed pas bsam gtan dang po kho na na yod do/ /

Also there is no obscured-neutral indicative form in the desire realm. Question: Why? Reply: That is because there is no obscured mind there that motivates it. Indeed, obscured-neutral minds concomitant with the first two views[1038] do exist in the desire realm, but they are objects abandoned by the path of seeing, and they do not motivate indicative form because they view internal states. Therefore obscured physical and verbal indicative form exists only in the first absorption in gods of Mahābrahma who engage in speech and so on that is motivated by guile and deceit.
gnyis pa
CLASSIFICATION OF VIRTUE, NONVIRTUE, AND NEUTRAL STATES
['di] la don dngos ni/ 'dir dge ba ni don dam pa dang*/ ngo bo nyid dang*/ mtshungs ldan dang*/ kun slong gis dge ba bzhi las
The actual meaning. Here virtue has four types: (1) ultimate virtue, (2) virtue by nature, (3) virtue by concomitance, and (4) virtue by motivation.
dam pa'i don du dge rtsa ba/ / ngo tsha khrel yod bdag nyid kyis/ / 8
Liberation is ultimate virtue. The roots of virtue, shame, and embarrassment are virtuous by their very nature. (4:8cd)

thar pa mya ngan las 'das pa ni dam pa'i don du dge ba yin te/ mi dge ba dang sdug bsngal thams cad nye bar zhi bas mchog tu bde ba'i phyir nad med pa la bde ba zhes zer ba bzhin no/ / 'dod chags med pa la sogs pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba gsum dang ngo tsha shes pa dang khrel yod pa dag ni/ mtshungs ldan dang kun slong la mi ltos pas 'phrod pa'i sman ltar bdag ste ngo bo nyid kyis dge ba'o/ / bcu gcig po thams cad kyang ngo bo nyid kyis dge ba yin mod kyi 'dir lnga smros pa ni bzlog pa ngo bo nyid kyis mi dge bar bstan pa'i phyir ro/ /

(1) Liberation (mokṣa) that is nirvāṇa is ultimate (paramārtha) virtue because it brings supreme bliss by pacifying all nonvirtue and suffering, as in the statement, “Freedom from disease is blissful.” (2) The three roots of virtue — nonattachment, nonaversion, and nonignorance — and shame (hrī) and embarrassment (apatrapa) are virtuous by their very nature since they are like effective medicine that doesn’t rely on concomitance or motivation. Indeed, all eleven virtuous mental factors are by nature virtue, but here only five are mentioned because their opposites are taught to be nonvirtuous by nature.
de dag dang ldan mtshungs ldan gyis/ / bya ba la sogs kun slong bas/ / bzlog pa mi dge don dam par/ / lung ma bstan pa bstan pa dag/ / 9

Those concomitant with them are virtuous through concomitance. Action and so on are virtuous by motivation. Its opposite is nonvirtue. [Saṃsāra] is ultimate nonvirtue. Neutral states are stable states. (4:9)

ngo bo nyid kyis dge ba de dag dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i sems dang sems byung rnams ni de dag dang mtshungs par ldan na dge bar 'gyur gyi mi ldan na mi 'gyur bas sman dang sbyar ba'i btung ba ltar mtshungs ldan gyis dge ba yin no/ / ngo bo nyid dang mtshungs ldan de dag gis kun nas bslangs ba'i lus ngag gi bya ba'i las rnams dang*/ sogs pa'i sgras gzung ba thob pa dang mtshan nyid dang sems med pa'i snyoms 'jug gnyis po rnams ni/ sman dang sbyar ba'i btung ba las byung ba'i 'o ma ltar kun nas slong bas dge ba yin no/

(3) Minds and mental factors concomitant with those mental factors that are virtuous by nature become virtuous when concomitant and do not become virtuous when not concomitant. Therefore they become virtuous through concomitance, like a drink to which medicine is added. (4) The karma of physical and verbal action that is motivated by minds concomitant with mental factors virtuous by nature, the obtainment [of such karma], their characteristics, and the two mindless meditative attainments and so on are virtuous by motivation, like [311] milk derived from [cows that] drink a medicinal tonic.

{gal te de lta na dge rtsa chad pa the tshom gyis mtshams sbyar ba dang nying mtshams sbyor ba'i tshe'i dge ba'i thob pa rnams ji ltar dge ba yin te/ skal ba mi mnyam pa'i sesam kyis kun nas bslang bas dge ba bzhi gang yang min pas so zhe na/ 'di la de dag ni thob pa'i gegs sel ba'am/ skye ba'i rkyen tsam du zad de/ dge bar ni thob bya nyid kyis byed do zhes lan 'debs so }

{Objection: In that case, if the root of virtue is severed, how could that which obtains virtue when linking or closely linking with doubt be virtuous, since it is motivated by a mind of dissimilar type [to virtue] and it is none of the four types of virtue? Reply: In response, it can be said that [doubt] overcomes impediments to obtaining [virtuous minds], or it merely constitutes the condition for their arising, but it does take virtue as something to be obtained.}

dge ba nyid du bshad pa de dag las bzlog pa ni mi dge ba rnam pa bzhi yin te/ 'khor ba ni mi dge ba dang sdug bsngal thams cad 'jug pas mchog tu mi bde ba'i phyir nad ltar don dam par mi dge ba yin no/ / mi dge ba'i rtsa ba gsum dang ngo tsha med pa dang khrel med pa rnams ni mi 'phrod pa'i sman ltar ngo bo nyid kyis mi dge ba'o/ / khro ba dang khon du 'dzin pa la sogs pa'ang ngo bo nyid kyis mi dge ba yin mod kyi gong ma pa rtsa ba gsum gyi cha la btags pa'i phyir logs shig tu ma bstan pa'am/ 'di pa ltar na dge rtsa gsum las bzlog pa ma yin pas ma bstan to/ / ngo bo nyid kyis mi dge ba de dag dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i sems dang sems byung rnams ni mi 'phrod pa'i sman dang sbyar ba'i btung ba ltar mtshungs ldan gyis mi dge ba yin no/ / de dag gis kun nas bslang ba'i lus ngag gi las dang mtshan nyid dang thob pa rnams ni mi 'phrod pa'i sman dang sbyar ba'i btung ba las byung ba'i 'o ma ltar kun slong gis mi dge ba yin no/ /

The opposite of those virtuous states is the four types of nonvirtue: (1) Saṃsāra is ultimate nonvirtue that induces supreme dissatisfaction (mi bde), since it encompasses all nonvirtuous states and all suffering like an illness. (2) The three roots of nonvirtue [i.e., attachment, aversion, and ignorance], shamelessness, and nonembarrassment are nonvirtuous by nature, like wrongly prescribed medicine. Wrath, spite, and so on are also nonvirtuous by nature, but either they are not taught separately from the three roots because they are included within the three former roots, or they are not taught since they are not the opposites of the three roots of virtue. (3) Minds and mental factors concomitant with mental factors that are nonvirtuous by nature are nonvirtuous by concomitance, like a drink to which wrongly prescribed medicine is added. (4) The karma, characteristics, and obtainment of physical and verbal action motivated by [minds] that are concomitant with [mental factors] that are nonvirtuous by nature are nonvirtuous by motivation, like milk derived from [cows that] drink a poisonous tonic.

lung ma bstan rnam pa bzhi las don dam par lung du ma bstan pa ni brtan pa so sor brtags min gyi 'gog pa dang nam mkha' dag yin no/ / ci'i phyir zhe na/ rtag cing dge ba bzhi dang mi dge ba bzhir 'gyur mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan dag ni ci rigs par dge ba bzhi dang mi dge ba bzhi'i nang du 'dus te/ zag bcas thams cad don dam par mi dge ba dang*/ lam bden ni ngo bo nyid dang mtshungs ldan dang kun nas slong ba dang don dam par par dge bar yang 'dus pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dus pa dag la'ang bzo dang spyod lam pa dang sprul sems dang rnam smin skyes kyi sems bzhi dang {phyi nang gi } bem po rnam ni ngo bo nyid kyis lung ma bstan yin no/ / {'dod pa na 'jig lta mthar lta mtshungs ldan dang bcas pa dang gong ma gnyis kyi sems sems byung nyon mongs can thams cad dang } bzo'i sems la sogs pa dang mtshungs par ldan pa ni mtshungs par ldan pas lung ma bstan yin no/{ rnam smin skyes ma gtogs pa/ /} bzo dang spyod lam pa dang sprul sems kyis {bslang ba'i } lus ngag gi rig byed {mtshan nyid thob pa dang bcas pa } dag ni kun slong gis lung ma bstan {yin la bsgribs pas bslang ba ni dang po kho na na yod pa } yin no/ / dge mi dge lung ma bstan gyi dbye ba 'di dag la gcig gcig gi nang du 'du ba ni yod mod kyi/ ldog pa la ltos nas 'byed pa'i phyir khyad par yod do zhes bya'o/

From among the four neutral states, (1) ultimate neutral states are the stable states of nonanalytical cessation and space. Question: Why? Reply: Because it is impossible for something permanent to be the four virtues or the four nonvirtues. Other entities are contained within any of the four types of virtue or the four types of nonvirtue because all contaminated entities are ultimate nonvirtue and the truth of path is included in virtue by nature, concomitant virtue, virtue by motivation, as well as ultimate virtue. (2) Also, regarding those included within neutral states, the four including creativity, demeanor, emanation mind, and maturational birth, plus {internal and external} matter are neutral by nature. (3) {All contaminated minds and mental factors concomitant with afflicted view of the self and extreme view in the desire realm and the two upper realms, and} those concomitant with the mind of creativity and so on, are neutral by concomitance. (4) Those physical and verbal indicative forms {along with the obtainment of their characteristics} that arise through creativity, demeanor, and the emanating mind {except for maturational birth} are neutral by motivation. {Those motivated by obscuration exist on the first absorption alone.} Indeed, these classifications of virtuous, nonvirtuous, and neutral states include each within the other, but because they are differentiated in reliance on their opposites, there is a difference. [312]

{gal te sems pa dge mi dges kun nas bslang bas dge mi dger 'jog na/ lus ngag gi rten 'byung ba'ang dge mi dger 'gyur te/ sems kyis lus ngag gi las dang lhan cig tu 'byung ba'ang slong bar byed pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ lan la byed pa pa ni las bya'o snyam du sems kyi 'byung ba la mi sems pas de ltar mi 'gyur ro zhe na/ bsam pa'i dbang gis yin gyi kun slong tsam las min na mnyam gzhag gi rig byed min pa dge bar mi 'gyur ro/ / mnyam par 'jog pa'i sngon du bsams so zhe na/ de ni skal pa mi mnyam pas de kun nas slong byed ma yin no/ / yin na lha'i mig dang rna ba yang dge bar 'gyur te/ sbyor ba'i tshe de la sems pa'i phyir ro/ / mi mtshungs te/ lus ngag gi las ni sems med par ma mthong la/ 'byung ba rnams ni sems med kyang 'byung bas dge ba la sogs par mi dbye ste mig la sogs pa bzhin no/ / 'on kyang mtshan nyid dang thob pa la sogs pa la mi mtshungs te/ 'di dag chos kyi dbang gis dge ba la sogs par 'jog la/ 'byung ba rnams ni ngo bo nyid kyis lung ma bstan yin no/ / lha'i mig dang rna ba'i sbyor ba yang snang ba dang sgra yid la byed pa yin pas sbyor ba'i dbang gis dge ba ma yin no zhes bshad do }

{Objection: If virtuous or nonvirtuous states are posited due to being motivated by virtuous or nonvirtuous intention, then even dependently arisen physical and verbal entities would become virtuous or nonvirtuous because those states arise simultaneously with physical and verbal karma motivated by mind. Some say in response: The agent must think “I commit this karma,” but the primary elements do not think this. Objection: If [form becoming virtuous] were due to the power of mind and not due to motivation alone, then the nonindicative form of equipoise would not be virtuous. Response: It is due to the thought prior to equipoise. Some say: That does not motivate it since it is not homogeneous with it. If it did, then the divine eye and ear would become virtuous because of the [virtuous] intention to generate them when preparing [to generate them]. Reply: That is not the same because physical and verbal karma are not seen to exist when there is no mind, whereas the primary elements exist when there is no mind and [the primary elements] are not differentiated as virtuous and so on, like the eyes and so forth, [which are composed of primary elements]. Morever, their characteristics and obtainment are not similar, for [physical and verbal karma] are posited as virtuous and so on due to the power of Dharma, but the primary elements are neutral by nature. Also, the preparation to generate the divine eye and ear mentally engages physical appearance and sound, so [the divine eye and ear] are not virtuous through their preparatory states.}
zhar la kun slong bshad pa ni
SUPPLEMENTARY EXPLANATION OF MOTIVATORS
kun slong rnam gnyis rgyu dang ni/ / de yi dus kyi slong zhes bya/ / gnyis las dang po rab 'jug byed/ / gnyis pa rjes su 'jug byed yin/ / 10
Motivators are of two types: the causal motivator and the concurrent motivator. From those two, the first initially engages karma and the second subsequently engages karma. (4:10)

gal te mthong spang gis rig byed mi slong na 'o na mdo las log par lta ba de las ni log par rtog pa dang log pa'i ngag dang log pa'i las kyi mtha' 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhes gsungs pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/

Objection: If objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing do not activate indicative form,[1039] then it would contradict a sūtra that states: Wrong conception, wrong speech, and wrong action arise from wrong view.[1040]

'di ltar kun nas slong ba ni rnam pa gnyis te/ rgyu'i kun slong dang{ bya ba} de'i dus kyi kun slong zhes bya'o/ / kun slong gnyis po de dag las dang po rgyu'i kun slong ni las la dang por rab tu 'jug par byed pa'i rgyu{ sbyor ba lta bu} yin la/ gnyis pa dus kyi kun slong ni las bya ba'i dus su mthun par byed pa'i phyir rjes su 'jug par byed pa {dngos gzhi lta bu } yin no/ /

Reply: Thus motivators are of two types called (1) the causal motivator and (2) the concurrent motivator of an {action}.”[1041] From those two motivators, the first, the causal motivator, is the cause that initially engages karma. The second, the concurrent motivator, is {like the actual basis} that subsequently engages karma and harmonizes the [karmic] process at the time of the action.
mthong bas spang bya'i rnam shes ni/ / rab tu 'jug byed yin yid ni/ / bsgom pas spang bya gnyis ka yin/ / lnga ni rjes su 'jug byed yin/ / 11
Consciousness to be abandoned by seeing initially engages indicative form. Mental consciousness to be abandoned by meditation is both. The five subsequently engage it. (4:11)

de dag las mthong bas spang bar bya ba'i yid kyi rnam shes ni {log lta las de bstan 'dod kyi shes pa kha phyir bltas 'byung bas des lus ngag slong bas sam/ log ltas gsod sogs kun nas slong bas so zhes pa'am } kha nang du bltas pas rig byed kyi rab tu 'jug par byed pa rgyu'i kun slong yin gyi dus kyi kun slong ni ma yin no/ yid kyi rnam shes bsgom pas spang bar bya ba ni rig byed kyi rgyu'i kun slong dang dus kyi kun slong gnyis ka yin no/ { rtog bcas kha phyir bltas kyang yod pas so/ /} mig la sogs pa'i rnam shes lnga ni rtog med yin pa'i phyir rjes su 'jug par byed pa dus kyi kun slong kho na yin no/ / de'i phyir de dag dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i sems las byung ba rnams kyang de bzhin du shes par bya'o/ / de'i phyir mdo las/ log par lta ba mthong spang gis rig byed kun nas slong bar bshad pa ni rgyu'i kun slong gi dbang du mdzad pa yin la/ 'dod khams na bsgribs pa'i rig byed kyi kun slong med par bshad pa ni dus kyi kun slong gi dbang du mdzad pa yin te/ des na 'dod pa'i 'jig tshogs la lta ba dang mthar 'dzin par lta ba {dang po gnyis } bsgribs la lung ma bstan mthong spang gis rig byed kyi rgyu'i kun slong byed kyang dus kyi kun slong ni sgom spang gi rnam shes kho na la ltos/ sgom spang gi rnam shes bsgribs pa'ang 'dod pa na med pa'i phyir 'dod pa na bsgribs pa'i rig byed med do zhes bya ba yin no/ / 'o na ni dus kyi kun slong gtso bo yin pa'i phyir rgyu'i kun slong dge bas byas nas dus kyi kun slong mi dge ba'am lung ma bstan gyis byas pa'i sdom pa dge bar mi 'gyur ro zhe na/ kun slong gi bsam pa de dag mthong spang dang sgom spang rigs tha dad na dus kyi kun slong gtso bor 'gyur gyi ris gcig pa la ni rgyu'i kun slong nyid gtso bo yin pa'i phyir de ltar thal ba med do zhes lan 'debs par byed do/ / gal te rgyu'i kun slong dang dus kyi kun slong dag 'dra ba'am mi 'dra ba yin zhe na/

Mental consciousness that is to be abandoned by the path of seeing is the causal motivator that initially engages (pravartaka) indicative form by viewing internal objects, but it is not a concurrent motivator. {Or wrong view that controls consciousness viewing external objects definitely activates body and speech, or wrong view activates killing, and so on.} Mental consciousness to be abandoned by the path of meditation is both a causal and concurrent motivator of indicative form. {So too is investigative [mental consciousness] that views external states.} The five sense consciousnesses are concurrent motivators alone that subsequently engage (anuvartaka) [indicative form] because they are nonconceptual. Mental factors concomitant with them should also be understood in that way. Therefore the explanation in the sūtra that wrong view to be abandoned by the path of seeing is the motivator of indicative form is from the perspective of the concurrent motivator,[1042] and the explanation that the motivator of obscured indicative form does not exist in the desire realm is from the perspective of the concurrent motivator. Therefore {the first two views} — the afflicted view of the self and the extreme view belonging to the desire realm, which are obscured-neutral states to be abandoned by the path of seeing — act as causal motivators of indicative form. However, the concurrent motivator views consciousness that is an object to be abandoned by the path of meditation alone. Because obscured consciousness that is to be abandoned by the path of meditation does not exist in the desire realm, [313] it is said that there is no indicative form that is obscured in the desire realm. Objection: Vows initiated by a virtuous causal motivator but completed by a nonvirtuous or neutral concurrent motivator do not become virtuous because a concurrent motivator is the main motivator. Reply: If those motivators of thought are of distinct types, where one is to be abandoned by the path of seeing and the other is to be abandoned by the path of meditation, then the concurrent motivator is the main motivator. If they are of the same type, then the causal motivator is the main motivator. Thus such a consequence does not arise. Question: Are the causal motivator and concurrent motivator similar or not?
rab tu 'jug byed dge sogs las/ / rjes 'jug byed kyang rnam gsum 'gyur/ / thub pa'i 'dra ba'am de dge ba/ / rnam smin las skyes gnyis ka min/ / 12
From virtuous initial engagement, subsequent engagement arises, which has three types and so on. For the Sage, similar or virtuous states arise. That arisen from maturation is neither. (4:12)

de ni ci rigs par yod de/ rab tu 'jug par byed pa rgyu'i kun slong dge ba las rjes su 'jug dus kyi kun slong yang dge mi dge lung ma bstan rnam pa gsum du 'gyur la/ de bzhin du sogs pa'i sgras bzung ba rab tu 'jug byed mi dge ba dang lung ma bstan las kyang rjes su 'jug byed rnam pa gsum du shes par bya'o/ / {des na rab tu 'jug byed dang rjes su 'jug byed la mu bzhi ste/ mthong spang gi sems ni rab tu 'jig byed kho na dang*/ sgo lnga'i rnam shes ni rjes su 'jug byed kho na dang*/ yid shes sgom spang ni gnyis ka dang*/ zag med ni gnyis ka min pa'i mu'o }

Reply: Various responses are possible. From the virtuous causal motivator of initial engagement (pravartaka), the concurrent motivator of subsequent engagement (anuvartaka) arises, which has three types: virtuous, nonvirtuous, or neutral. The “and so on” indicates that from a nonvirtuous and neutral motivator of initial engagement, three types of subsequent engagement also arise. {Initial engagement and subsequent engagement have four possibilities: (1) Minds to be abandoned by the path of seeing are initial engagement alone. (2) Consciousness of the five sense doors is subsequent engagement alone. (3) Mental consciousness to be abandoned by the path of meditation is both, and (4) uncontaminated states are neither.}

de la dmigs kyis bsal ba ni 'di yin te/ thub pa'i rab tu 'jug byed dge ba dang lung ma bstan las rjes su 'jug byed kyang dge ba dang lung ma bstan du 'dra ba 'byung ba'am/ yang na sangs rgyas rnams kyi ston pa ni dman par mi 'gyur bas dge ba las lung ma bstan du mi 'gyur gyi dge ba las dge ba dang lung ma bstan las kyang dge ba kho na 'byung bas rjes su 'jug byed de ni dge ba kho na yin no zhes bye brag tu smra ba 'dod do/ / sde pa gzhan dag na re sangs rgyas rnams kyi rgyud ni rtag tu mnyam par bzhag pa'i phyir spyod lam bzhi char yang dge ba kho nar rgyud gcig pa yin gyi lung ma bstan gyi sems med de/ mdo las kyang*/ glang chen gshegs na'ang mnyam par bzhag glang chen bzhengs na'ang mnyam par bzhag glang chen mnal na'ang mnyam par bzhag /bzhugs na'ang mnyam par bzhag pa yin zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / de la 'dir glang chen zhes bya ba ni sangs rgyas te nyes pa mi mnga' bas na glang chen te/ mdo las/ 'char byed de bzhin gshegs pa ni sku dang gsung dang thugs kyis ngan par mi mdzad pas na glang po che chen po zhes bya'o zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ / bye brag tu smra ba ni sangs rgyas kyi thugs ni spyod lam bzhi char du bzhud na'ang bzhud do snyam pa la sogs pa nas bzhugs na'ang bzhugs so snyam du dgongs pa nye bar gnas pas thugs mi bzhed bzhin du yul la mi 'jug pa'i phyir mdo las de skad du gsungs kyi sangs rgyas la lung ma bstan rnam smin skyes dang spyod lam pa dang sprul sems mi mnga' ba ni ma yin no zhes 'dod do zhes zer ro/ { yid dang sgo lnga'i shes pa kun slong du bshad pa yang rnam min skyes las gzhan la dgongs kyi/}

The exception is that from the virtuous or neutral initial engagement of the Sage, similar virtuous or neutral subsequent engagement arises. Or, again, the teachings of buddhas do not transform from virtuous to neutral states since they do not transform into inferior states, but since the virtuous transforms into virtuous states, and neutral states also transform into virtuous states alone, subsequent engagement is virtuous alone. This is asserted by Vaibhāṣikas. Other schools say that a buddha’s four types of physical demeanor constitute a single virtuous continuum alone without any neutral minds because the mindstream of a buddha is always in equipoise. Also, a sūtra states: Though the elephant walks, it is in equipoise. Though the elephant stands, it is in equipoise. Though the elephant lies down, it is in equipoise. Though the elephant sits, it is in equipoise.[1043] Here the buddha is called an elephant. He is an elephant since he doesn’t possess any faults. As a sūtra states: Udayin, since the body, speech, or mind of a tathāgata does not engage in evil, he is called an elephant.[1044] Vaibhāṣikas assert that a sūtra mentions that the mind of a buddha does not engage objects without recognizing them, since he closely moniters his four types of physical demeanor, reflecting, “I walk” when walking, and so on, up to “I sit” when sitting. A buddha has no neutral [314] states arisen from karmic maturation, or physical demeanor, or minds of emanation.[1045] {Though mental consciousness and consciousness of the five sense doors are said to be motivators, what is meant is states other than those that arise from karmic maturation.}

rnam par smin pa las skyes pa'i sems ni mngon par 'du byed pa med par ngang gis 'jug pa'i phyir dang*/ kun slong yang 'du byed pa yin pa'i phyir rab tu 'jug byed dang rjes su 'jug byed gnyis ka min la/ de bzhin du zag med kyi sems kyang mi rtog cing nang du mnyam par bzhag pa'i phyir gnyis ka ma yin no/ / don 'di la rig byed ma yin pa kun slong gis dge mi dger 'gyur ro zhes bya ba ni rigs pa dang ldan pa ma yin te/ kun slong gi bsam pa ni rig byed ma yin pa la sems pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te bsam pa'i stobs tsam las byung bas yin na rig byed ma yin pa dang lhan cig pa'i 'byung bzhi dang mig dang rna ba'i mngon shes dag kyang dge bar thal ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir sdom pa la sogs pa ni rig byed ma yin pa'i gzugs nyid ma yin gyi phan pa dang gnod pa'i sems pa'i rgyun yin pa'i phyir 'dir rnam par bzhag pa thams cad ni bye brag tu smra bas kun brtags pa kho nar snang ngo*/ /

Minds arisen from karmic maturation (vipākaja) neither initially engage karma nor subsequently engage karma because they engage objects free from the actual [process of] karmic formation, because motivation is karmic formation. So too, the uncontaminated mind [engages karma] neither [initially nor subsequently] because it is nonconceptual and internal equipoise. This means that it is illogical to state that nonindicative form becomes virtuous or nonvirtuous through motivation, because the motivating thought has no intention to be nonindicative. If it arises merely through the power of thought, then it would follow that nonindicative form, the four coemergent elements, and the higher perceptions of eye and ear would become virtuous states. Therefore the vows and so on are not nonindicative form itself but a continuum of the mind that benefits or harms. Everything that is posited here is the fabrication of the Vaibhāṣikas alone.
rig byed ma yin pa rgyas par dbye ba/
19. Detailed Classification of Nonindicative Form
da ni rig byed ma yin pa'i dbye ba
THIS HAS TWO HEADINGS: overview and elaboration.
mdor bstan pa ni
Overview
rnam rig min rnam gsum shes bya/ / sdom dang sdom pa min dang gzhan/ / sdom pa so sor thar zhes bya/ / de bzhin zag med bsam gtan skyes/ / 13
Nonindicative form should be known as three types: vows, negative commitments, and others. Vows are called pratimokṣa as well as that arising from uncontaminated states and the absorptions. (4:13)

sngar bshad pa'i rnam par rig byed min pa de ni rnam pa gsum du shes par bya ste/ gang zhe na/ gzhan la gnod pa gzhi dang bcas pa spong zhing 'chal ba'i tshul khrims kyi rgyun sdom zhing 'gog pas na sdom pa dang*/ gnod pa gzhi dang bcas pa la rgyun du zhugs pa ni sdom pa min pa dang*/ gnod pa'am gnod pa'i gzhi dag phyogs re spong ba'am phyogs re la 'jug na sdom pa dang sdom min gnyis las gzhan pa'i bar ma yin no/ / 'di la'ang rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa gnyis ka yod de/ gnod pa dang phan pa'i stobs re la rgyun dang ldan par gnas pa ni rig byed ma yin pa ste sngar smros pa'i rdzas las byung ba'i bsod nams kyi gzhi bdun la sogs pa dang*/ lo re re zhing lug la sogs pa 'di bsad do zhes dam bcas nas gsod pa lta bu'o/ / de la gnod pa ni lus ngag gi mi dge ba bdun dang gzhi ni yid kyi gsum mam/ yang na gnod pa rang bzhin dang gzhi bcas pa'i kha na ma thob ba'o/ /

The nonindicative form explained previously should be known as three types. Question: What are they? Reply: They are (1) vows (saṃvara) that abandon harming others and the basis of harm, and that restrain and stop unethical conduct; (2) negative commitments (asaṃvara) that continuously promote harm and the basis of harm; and (3) interim precepts, other than vows or negative commitments, that abandon a specific type of harm or basis of harm or engage in a specific type of harm or basis of harm. This last one has both indicative and nonindicative aspects, for continuously maintaining either strong benefit or harm to others is nonindicative form, such as the seven bases generating merit from material generosity previously mentioned, or each year killing a sheep and so on due to the pledge to kill it. “Harm” refers to the seven nonvirtues of body and speech, and “basis of harm” refers to the three mental actions, or again they refer to offensive acts that are the essence of harm and their basis.
rgyas par bshad pa
ELABORATION
['di] la sdom pa'i dbye ba dang*/ so so thar pa'i sdom pa'i khyad par dang*/ bsam gtan zag med kyi sdom pa'i khyad par gsum las
This has three headings: classification of vows, the attributes of pratimokṣa vows, and the attributes of absorption and uncontaminated vows.
dang po
CLASSIFICATION OF VOWS
sdom pa la dbye na
If vows are classified,

so so thar pa'i sdom pa zhes bya ba dang*/ de bzhin du zag med dang bsam gtan las skyes pa'i sdom pa gnyis te gsum yin no/ / {dge slong gi spong bdun dang*/ zag bcas kyi mnyam gzhag las skyes pa'i spong bdun dang*/ zag med kyi mnyam gzhag las skyes pa'i spong bdun rnams mtshan gzhi/ so thar dang*/ bsam gtan dang*/ zag med kyi sdom pa'i tha snyad du byar rung*/ mtshan nyid rim pa ltar/ 'dod pa'i dge ba gzugs can gang gi nges pa lnga dang bral ba dang*/ sems kyi rjes 'brang gi gzugs zag bcas dang*/ sems kyi rjes 'brang gi gzugs zag med do/ / gsum du grangs nges pa ni mnyam par 'jog pa'i rten dang*/ de'i 'bras bu zag bcas zag med kyi ting nge 'dzin gnyis kyi dbang gis so/ / go rim nges pa ni snga ma snga ma las phyi ma phyi ma skye bas so/ / 'o na phyi rol pa la so thar med pa'i phyir bsam gtan gyi sdom pa med par thal lo zhe na/ skyon med de de dag gi bsam gtan gyi sdom pa ni lus ngag gi nyes spyod sdom pa las skye bas so/ / yang na 'bras bu la spyi ming gis btags pa ste ka ba dang mig shes rgyu 'bras su brjod pa bzhin no }

there are three types: (1) those called “pratimokṣa vows” as well as (2) vows that arise from uncontaminated states and (3) the absorptions. {Their instances are the seven abandoning [negative action] of a fully ordained monk (bhikṣu), the seven abandoning [negative action] arising from contaminated absorption, [315] and the seven abandoning [negative action] arising from uncontaminated absorption. They are properly called (1) pratimokṣa vows, (2) absorption vows, and (3) uncontaminated vows. Their definitions are, respectively, (1) “desire-realm physical virtue that lacks the five certainties,” (2) “contaminated form that complements the mind,” and (3) “uncontaminated form that complements the mind.” They are fixed in number as three from the perspective of being (1) the basis for establishing equipoise, (2) the result of contaminated concentration, and (3) the result of uncontaminated concentration. Since the later [vows] arise from those earlier, their order is certain. Objection: Because non-Buddhists do not have pratimokṣa vows, it follows that they would not have absorption vows. Reply: There is no error, since their absorption vows are generated through restraining negative physical and verbal action [and not by pratimokṣa vows]. Again, the result is designated by a general name, just as a pillar and eye consciousness are said to be cause and effect.}[1046]
gnyis pa so so thar pa zhes bya ba'i sdom pa ni
Pratimokṣa vows
so sor thar zhes bya rnam brgyad/ / rdzas su rnam pa bzhi yin no/ / mtshan las ming ni 'pho ba'i phyir/ / tha dad de dag 'gal ba med/ / 14
Pratimokṣa vows have eight types. In substance there are four types because they are redesignated when their sex changes. Though distinct, it is not contradictory. (4:14)

gang zag gis phye na rnam pa brgyad de/ dge slong pha ma dang*/ dge slob ma dang*/ dge tshul pha ma dang*/ dge bsnyen pha ma dang*/ bsnyen gnas pa'i sdom pa'o/{ bshes spring 'grel par dge slob ma dor nas bsnyen gnas la gnyis su phye nas brgyad du mdzad do/} gang zag tha dad pa ma gtogs pa sdom pa'i rdzas su ni rnam pa bzhi yin te/ {spang bya lnga brgyad bcu la sogs pa mtshan nyid so sor nges pas so } dge slong pha ma'i sdom pa dag ni rdzas 'dra ba dang*/ dge slob ma dang dge tshul pha ma gsum yang sdom pa'i rdzas 'dra ba dang*/ dge bsnyen pha ma dag kyang sdom pa'i rdzas 'dra ba'i phyir ro/ / 'dir rdzas ni mtshan nyid la 'dod do/ / {de la nyes spyod dang mi tshangs spyod ji srid 'tsho'i bar du spong ba'i dbang du byas nas sdom pa dang po lnga bzhag la/ nyes spyod dang log g.yem ji srid 'tsho'i bar du spong nus tsam gyi dbang du byas nas dge bsnyen gyi sdom pa bzhag la/ nyes spyod dang 'dod log zhag re tsam spong nus pa'i dbang du byas nas bsnyen gnas pa'i sdom pa rnam par bzhag go /}bsnyen gnas la gnyis su ma phye ba ni yun thung ba'i phyir ro/{ bsdu ba las za ma la sogs pa la'ang skye bar bshad pa'i phyir ro/} gal te dge slong pha ma la sogs pa'i sdom pa'i rdzas 'dra bar ji ltar 'gyur te/ dge slong ma'i lci ba'i chos brgyad dge slong la ma bcas shing*/ dge slob mas dge tshul{ pha ma'i bcu po spong ba'i steng du yang lo gnyis su} skyes pa la reg pa dang skyes pa dang {dben pa skyabs yod du } lhan cig tu 'dug pa dang*/ gcig pur lam du 'gro ba dang*/ rkyal byed pa dang*/ smyon byed pa dang*/ zla mo'i nyes pa 'chab pa ste chos drug dang*/ gser la reg pa dang*/ mdoms kyi spu 'dreg pa dang*/ byin len ma byas pa za ba dang*/ gsog 'jog byas pa za ba dang*/ rtsa gcod pa dang*/ sa rko ba ste/ nye ba'i chos drug ste bcu gnyis spangs nas/ dge slong ma byed par bshad pas spang bya la mang nyung yod pa'i phyir ro zhe na/

spang bya la 'phel 'grib yod kyang de dag sdom pa'i rdzas la khyad par med de/{ de'i spong ba bcu ni dge tshul pha ma'i sdom pa'ang yin pa'i phyir dang*/} mtshan{ lan gnyis su} gyur pa las ni ming 'pho ba tsam yin pa'i phyir te/ dge bsnyen mtshan gyur na dge bsnyen ma dang*/ dge bsnyen ma mtshan gyur na dge bsnyen dang*/ dge tshul mtshan gyur na dge tshul ma dang*/ dge tshul ma dang dge slob ma mtshan gyur na dge tshul dang*/ dge slong mtshan gyur na dge slong ma dang*/ dge slong ma mtshan gyur na dge slong du 'gyur ba tsam las sdom pa sngar yod {gtong rgyu lnga po gang gis kyang } gtong ba dang{ gzhan gyi rig byed la sogs pa'i rgyu gang gis kyang} sngar med 'thob pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / rdzas la khyad par yod na mtshan gyur pa tsam gyis de dag tu 'gyur bar mi rigs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: Though there is a difference in the number of actions to be abandoned, there is no difference in the substance of their vows, {because the ten vows abandoning those actions are also novice monk and novice nun vows, and} because they are merely redesignated when their sex changes {twice}. If a male layperson (upāsaka) changes sex he becomes a female layperson (upāsikā), when a female layperson changes sex she becomes a male layperson, when a novice monk (śrāmaṇera) changes sex he becomes a novice nun (śrāmaṇerikā), when a novice nun [316] or probationary nun (śikṣamāṇā) changes sex she becomes a novice monk, when a fully ordained monk (bhikṣu) changes sex he becomes a fully ordained nun (bhikṣuṇī), and when a fully ordained nun changes sex she becomes a fully ordained monk. They do not relinquish vows they previously had {due to any of the five causes of relinquishment} or obtain vows they did not previously have {due to any cause such as another’s indicative form}. If there were a difference in the substance of their vows, it is illogical that it would arise due to changing sex alone.

yang dge bsnyen la sogs pa'i sdom pa de dag tha dad pa yin gyi snga ma snga ma gnas gyur pa phyi ma phyi ma'am gcig tu yod pa ni ma yin te/ dge slong gi sdom pa phul bas dge tshul la sogs pa'ang gtong bar thal ba'i phyir dang*/ phyi ma rnams snga ma'i gtong rgyur thal ba'i phyir ro/ / {de lta ma yin na gzhan gnyis kyang der 'dus pas dge slong gi sdom pa btang bas gsum char gtong bar 'gyur na de ni mi 'dod de na smad tsam du 'gyur bar bshad pas so/ / gal te dge slong gi rtsa ltung byung bas snga ma gnyis la mi gnod par thal/ de dag rdzas tha dad pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ skyon med de zag med kyi lam gcig gis spang bya'i rdzas du ma dus gcig la nyams par byed pa bzhin no/ / 'on kyang rig byed mngon gyur ni rdzas gcig ste dge slong du 'dzin pa'i bsam pas slong zhing der brjod pas so/ / spong sems la 'dod pa ltar na'ang rdzas mtshungs nyams par mi 'gyur te/ sa bon tha dad pas so/ / zhes gsung ngo*/ / tha dad kyang sdom pa phyi ma blangs pas snga ma gtong ba ma yin te/ de dag phan tshun 'gal ba med pa'i phyir ro } 'o na dge slong gi rgyud gcig la sdom pa gsum ga yod na tha dad pa gsum 'gal lo zhe na

The vows of laypeople and so on are distinct, and it is not that any change to earlier vows would apply equally to later vows because it would then follow that by offering back full-ordination vows, novice vows and so on would be relinquished, and in consequence relinquishing the earlier [vows] would act as the cause of relinquishing the later [ones]. {If that is not so, all three vows would be relinquished by relinquishing full-ordination vows, since the other two vows would be included in full-ordination vows. But that is untenable since they are explained to be inferior. Objection: It follows that the former two vows are not harmed by incurring a root downfall of full-ordination vows because they are substantially distinct from them. Reply: There is no error, because it is like one uncontaminated path causing the simultaneous subsidence of multiple substances that are objects to be abandoned. However, it is said that manifest indicative form is just one substance, since it arises due to the thought of being fully ordained and being described as that. It is said that even if vows are asserted to be minds that abandon [negative actions], a shared substance [of the three vows] would not degenerate since their seeds are distinct. Though distinct in substance, earlier vows are not relinquished by taking later vows because they are not mutually exclusive.} Objection: Now, if the three vows exist in the single mindstream of a fully ordained monk, it would be contradictory that those three are distinct.

de dag tha dad du'ang rgyud gcig la 'gal ba med de/ 'di ltar dge slong la srog gcod spong ba nas chang 'thung ba spong ba'i bar lnga ni gsum gsum dang*/ glu gar la sogs pa spong ba gnyis gnyis dang*/ spong ba gzhan dag ni re re ba yin no/ / 'on kyang {bslab pa'i gzhi mang po len par 'dod pa'i sems pa las skyes pas rgyags pa dang bag med pa'i gnas ches mang po las zlog la gzhan ni de lta ma yin pas } gzhi dang bsam pa'i khyad par gyis dge slong gi srog gcod spong ba che la/ dge tshul gyi 'bring*/ dge bsnyen gyi chung ngo zhes bya bar 'dod do/ / 'o na dge slong de nyid dge tshul dang dge bsnyen du'ang 'gyur ro zhe na/ de ltar ni yin mod kyi dge slong zhes brjod pa ni gtso che ba'i phyir te/ dgra bcom pa dge slong yin yang dgra bcom zhes brjod pa bzhin no/ / de dag ni sde pa'i lugs so/ / don la gnas pa ni 'di yin te spong ba'i sems pa gcig yin gyi tha dad pa ni ma yin te/ sems pa gnyis dang gsum la sogs pa dus cig car mi 'byung ba'i phyir dang*/ tshigs snga ma med pa la bsnyen par rdzogs pa skye ba dang*/ na smad pa dag ni sems pa'i khyad par khas blangs pa'i stobs kyis 'thob pa dang gtong ba'i phyir ro/ / 'on kyang dge tshul gyi sdom pa'i khongs su dge bsnyen 'du ba dang*/ dge slong gi khongs su 'og ma gnyis ka'ang 'du ba'i phyir sdom pa gsum ldan zhes bya bar brjod do/ /

Reply: Though distinct, it is not contradictory that they exist in a single mindstream since the five vows, from abandoning taking life to abandoning drinking intoxicants, exist in three beings, vows abandoning singing and dancing and so on exist in two beings, and vows abandoning other actions exist in each individual being. However, {since they arise [in the fully ordained] from a mind desiring to take multiple bases of training, they counter manifold states of arrogance and negligence, but other vows do not do this. Therefore} it is asserted that due to differences in the basis and motivating thought, killing is an extremely serious act to be abandoned for the fully ordained, not as serious for a novice, and even less serious for a layperson. Question: But isn’t that fully ordained being also a novice and layperson? Reply: Indeed, that is so, but the fully ordained constitutes the foremost category, like an arhat who is fully ordained being called an arhat. These assertions reflect the system of this school. But the simple fact is that there is just one intention to abandon [negative actions] and not distinct intentions. This is (1) because two or three intentions and so on do not occur concurrently, (2) because full ordination arises without the earlier pratimokṣa stages, and (3) because those possessing a downfall incomplete in one branch obtain or relinquish [that training] by the power of acceptance according to their specific intention. However, because lay vows are included within the vows of the novice, and both lower vows are included within the vows of the fully ordained, the fully ordained are called “possessors of the three vows.” [317]
spang bya lnga brgyad bcu dang ni/ / thams cad spong ba mnos pa las/ / dge bsnyen dang ni bsnyen gnas dang / / dge tshul ched dang dge slong nyid/ / 15
Through receiving vows abandoning five, eight, ten, or all actions to be abandoned, one becomes a layperson, one-day vow-holder, novice, or fully ordained. (4:15)

gnyis pa ni dge bsnyen nyid la gnas pa'i ched du {skyabs 'gro dang thar pa 'dod pa sngon du song bas } srog gcod dang*/ ma byin len dang*/ 'dod log dang*/ rdzun dang*/ chang 'thung ba zhes bya ba'i spang bya lnga spong ba mnos pa las dge bsnyen dang*/ de bzhin du nyid dang ched du zhes bya ba bsnyen gnas la sogs pa la'ang sbyar te/ srog gcod dang*/ ma byin len dang*/ mi tshangs spyod dang*/ rdzun dang*/ chang 'thung ba dang*/ spos dang me tog phreng dang byug pa dang gar dang glu dang rol mo{ ste 'di dag sdom pas gcig} dang khri stan mthon po dang*/ khri stan chen po ste/{ 'di gnyis gcig tu bsdus pa/} dus ma yin pa'i kha zas te spang bya brgyad spong ba mnos pa las bsnyen gnas dang*/ de dag las gar dang glu dang rol mo la reg pa gcig dang*/ spos dang me tog phreng dang byug pa gcig ste gnyis su phye la/ gser dngul len pa bsnan pa'i spang bya bcu spong ba mnos pa las ni dge tshul dang {snga ma la gar sogs phreng sogs gcig tu bzhag pa ni bslab bya mang ngo snyam pas khyim pa rnams sgyid lug pa spang bar bya ba'i phyir sla bar bstan pa'i phyir gcig du byas so/ bsdu ba las rab byung gar sogs byed pa dang gsog 'jog gis 'tshe na nyes pa che bas nyes pa gnyis dang gser dngul spong ba bstan to zhes so } pham pa bzhi dang*/ lhag ma bcu gsum dang*/ spang ltung sum cu dang*/ ltung byed{ 'ba' zhig pa} dgu bcu dang*/ so sor bshags par bya ba bzhi dang*/ bslab bya'i nyes byas brgya dang bcu gnyis te nyis brgya lnga bcu rtsa gsum po thams cad {dam lus ngag gi las bdun po thams cad } spong ba mnos pa las dge slong du 'gyur ro/ /
tshul khrims dang ni legs spyad dang / / las dang sdom pa zhes bya'o/ / dang po'i rnam rig rnam rig min/ / so sor thar dang bya ba'i lam/ / 16
It is called ethics, positive action, karma, and restraint. Indicative and nonindicative form of the first moment is pratimokṣa and the path of action. (4:16)
ming gi rnam grangs ni
NAME EQUIVALENTS

mi dge ba'i las ni sems can la mi mnyam par 'jug pas tshul khrims blangs pa na las mi mnyam pa can rnams yang dag par 'jog cing 'dor bas sam/ yang na mdo las/ lus la yongs su gdung med pas/ / tshul khrims yang dag blang ba bde/ / gnyid log pa yang bde ba ste/ / sad pa na yang bde bar 'gyur/ / zhes 'byung bas 'gyod pa la sogs pa lus sems la gdung ba med pas bsil ba thob pa'i phyir tshul khrims dang mkhas pa rnams kyis bsngags pa'i phyir legs spyad dang*/ bya ba'i rang bzhin yin pas las {yin te rig byed dang sems pa dag gis byed pa'i phyir } dang lus ngag gi nyes spyod sdom pa'i phyir sdom pa zhes bya'o/ / de bzhin du rtsa ba dang rgyan dang byug pa dang spos zhes kyang bya'o/ /

It is called ethics (śīla) since nonvirtuous actions treat sentient beings in a biased [or unbalanced] way, but when ethics are practiced one can correctly determine biased action and discard it. Or it is called ethics because one obtains a cool state, since regret and so on do not torment the body or mind. A sūtra declares: Since the body is not tormented the correct practice of ethics is blissful, falling asleep is blissful, even waking from sleep is blissful.[1047] It is positive action (sucarita) because it is praised by scholars. It is karma since it is the essence of action {because it functions through indicative form and intention}. It is restraint (saṃvara) because it restrains negative action of body and speech. Similarly, it is also called “the root,” “an ornament,” “perfume,” and “fragrance.”

Again, indicative and nonindicative form of the first moment of the obtainment of pratimokṣa vows is called (1) pratimokṣa, and (2) vows {compatible with the basis}, and (3) the {actual} karmic path of action because, respectively, it is {the first} liberation from immorality, it restrains body and speech, and it is a door to producing karma. The second and subsequent moments are pratimokṣa vows alone and not pratimokṣa because if the meaning of pratimokṣa is taken to be “first liberation,” then one would already be emancipated [in the first moment]. It is the end of the path of action [318] but not the actual path. {[Pratimokṣa vows] are ethics that are derived through a rite while absorption and uncontaminated vows are obtained spontaneously.}
so sor thar dang ldan pa brgyad/
Eight persons possess pratimokṣa vows. (4:17a)
gsum pa {bsam gtan zag med kyi sdom pa'i khyad par} ni
Absorption and uncontaminated vows
bsam gtan skyes dang de ldan pa/ / zag med 'phags pa'i sems can dang / / tha ma gnyis ni sems rjes 'brang / / 17
Those who possess them possess vows arisen from the absorptions. Ārya sentient beings possess uncontaminated vows. The last two are complements of the mind. (4:17bcd)

bsam gtan las skyes pa'i sdom pa dang ni bsam gtan nyer bsdogs{ yar bcad dang dngos gzhi} dang bcas pa de dang ldan pa rnams dang ldan la/{ nyer bsdogs la'ang rten du brjod do/} zag med kyi sdom pa dang ni 'phags pa'i sems can{ slob mi slob} rnams dang ldan no/ / sdom pa gsum po de dag las tha ma bsam gtan dang zag med kyi sdom pa gnyis ni sems kyi rjes su 'brang ba ste mnyam par bzhag pa na yod la ma bzhag pa na med pa'i phyir ro/ / {so thar ni g.yengs pa dang sems med pa'i rjes su byed pas min no } yang spong ba'i sdom pa zhes bshad pa gang zhe na/

Those who possess access concentrations to the absorptions — {that is, superior access concentration — and the actual basis} possess vows arisen from the absorptions. {Access concentrations are also called the support of absorption vows}. {Learner and nonlearner} ārya sentient beings possess uncontaminated vows. From among those three vows, the last two — absorption and uncontaminated vows — are complements of the mind (cittānuvartina) because they exist in equipoise and not in nonequipoise. Question: Again, how are vows of abandonment explained?
bar chad med lam skyes de gnyis/ / mi lcogs med la spong zhes bya/ / shes bzhin dang ni dran dag gnyis/ / yid dang dbang po'i sdom pa yin/ / 18
Both vows that arise on the uninterrupted paths and unrestricted access concentration are called abandoning vows. Both introspection and mindfulness are mental vows and sensory vows. (4:18)

bar chad med pa'i lam dgu dag tu skyes pa'i bsam gtan dang zag med kyi sdom pa de gnyis ni spong ba'i sdom pa zhes bya'o/ / bar chad med pa'i lam thams cad dam zhe na/ bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs mi lcogs pa med pa la yin te/ 'chal pa'i tshul khrims dang de kun nas slong ba'i nyon mongs rnams spong ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir bsam gtan gyi sdom pa yin la/ spong ba'i sdom pa ma yin pa ni mi lcogs pa med pa'i bar chad med pa'i lam ma gtogs pa'i zag bcas kyi bsam gtan gyi sdom pa'o/ / spong ba'i sdom pa yin la bsam gtan gyi sdom pa ma yin pa ni nyer bsdogs kyi bar chad med pa'i lam gyi zag med kyi sdom pa'o/ / gnyis ka yin pa ni nyer bsdogs mi lcogs med pa'i bar chad med pa'i lam gyi bsam gtan gyi sdom pa'o/ / gnyis ka ma yin pa ni de las ma gtogs pa mi lcogs pa med pa'i lam ma gtogs pa'i zag med kyi sdom pa'o zhes bya ba'i mu bzhi dang*/ de bzhin du zag med kyi sdom pa yin la spong ba'i sdom pa ma yin pa la sogs pa'i mu bzhi'ang shes par bya'o/ / yang so so thar pa las/ lus kyi sdom pa legs pa ste/ / ngag gi sdom pa legs pa yin/ / yid kyi sdom pa legs pa ste/ / thams cad du ni sdom pa legs zhes pa dang*/ tshul khrims kyi phung po'i mdo las/ gang yang mig gi dbang po sdom pas bsdams te gnas so zhes gsungs pa'i lus ngag gi sdom pa ma yin pa yid dang dbang po'i sdom pa de dag kyang rig byed ma yin pa yin nam zhe na/

Reply: Both uncontaminated vows and absorption vows that arise on the nine uninterrupted paths (ānantaryamārga) are called abandoning vows. Question: Does this apply to all uninterrupted paths? Reply: This applies to unrestricted (anāgamya) access concentration to the first absorption because it abandons unethical conduct and the afflictions motivating it. Therefore there are four possibilities: (1) That which is an absorption vow but not an abandoning vow is a contaminated absorption vow not belonging to the uninterrupted path of unrestricted access concentration. (2) That which is an abandoning vow but not an absorption vow is an uncontaminated vow of the uninterrupted path of access concentration. (3) That which is both is an absorption vow of the uninterrupted path of unrestricted access concentration. (4) That which is neither is an uncontaminated vow not belonging to those, or not belonging to the unrestricted path. Similarly, it should be understood that there are four possibilities for that which is an uncontaminated vow but not an abandoning vow and so on. Question: Again, the Pratimokṣa Sūtra declares: The vows of body are excellent. The vows of speech are excellent. The vows of mind are excellent. These vows are excellent in every way.[1048] And the Aggregate of Ethics Sūtra advises: Abide with restraint through restraining the eye sense faculty.[1049] Therefore, are mental vows and sensory vows that are not vows of body and speech nonindicative form or not?
ma yin te/
Reply: They are not,

ltung ba dang de'i gnyen po shes pa'i shes bzhin dang*/ spong ba'i sems pa ma brjed pa'i dran pa dag gnyis ka ni yid kyi sdom pa dang de gnyis ka dbang po'i sdom pa'ang yin te/ de gnyis kyis yid kyi nyes spyod kyang spong la dbang po yul la log par spyod pa dag kyang spong ba'i phyir ro/ /

because both introspection (samprajñāna) aware of downfalls and their antidotes and mindfulness (smṛti) that does not forget the intention to abandon them are mental vows (manasaṃvara), and also both are sensory vows (indriyasaṃvara) because both of those abandon [319] negative mental action as well as perverse acts directed to objects of the sense faculties.
de dag gis ldan pa'i tshul ston pa ni
How vows are possessed
so sor thar gnas ji srid du/ / ma btang bar dag da ltar gyi/ / rnam rig min ldan skad cig ma/ / dang po phyin chad 'das pa dang / / 19
For as long as they maintain pratimokṣa vows and do not relinquish them, they possess present nonindicative form. They possess past indicative form after the first moment. (4:19)

so so thar pa la gnas pa'i gang zag ni ji srid du 'og nas 'chad pa'i gtong rgyu dag gis ma btang gi bar de srid du rtag tu da ltar gyi rnam par rig byed min pa dang ldan la/ sdom pa thob pa'i skad cig ma dang po phyin chad {ni der ma zad } 'das pa dang yang ldan te/{ de lta min na sdom pa snga ma rnams btang bar thal te thob nas mi ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di sems kyi rjes 'brang ma yin pas gtong rgyus mtshams bcad pa dang ma 'ongs pa'i thob pa ma byung ba'i phyir skad cig ma dang po da ltar ba kho na dang ldan par bshad do/} de yang ji srid du ma btang gi bar du zhes bya ba dang sbyar ro/ /

For as long as beings maintain pratimokṣa vows and do not relinquish them through the causes of relinquishment explained below, for that long they continuously possess present nonindicative form. {Not only that,} they also possess past indicative form after the first moment (kṣanā) of obtainment of those vows. {If that were not so, it would follow that former vows would be relinquished because having been obtained they would no longer be possessed. And the first moment would possess present vows alone because former vows would stop, having been relinquished and no longer complementing the mind, and the obtainment of future vows will not yet have occurred.} Further, the phrase “for as long as they are not relinquished”[1050] should also be applied.
sdom min gnas pa'ang de dang 'dra/ / bsam gtan sdom dang ldan pa ni/ / rtag tu 'das dang ma 'ongs dang / / 'phags ni dang po 'das dang min/ / 20
So too, negative commitments abide in that way. Those who possess absorption vows continuously possess past and future vows. Āryas do not possess past vows in the first. (4:20)
so so thar pa'i sdom pa'i ldan pa ji lta ba da ltar sdom min la gnas pa'ang de dang 'dra{ bas 'don pa bsgyur} bar shes par bya'o/ /
It should be understood that in just the way pratimokṣa discipline comes to be possessed, so too, present negative commitments (asaṃvara) abide {and manifest} in that way.
gzhan dag ni bsam gtan gyi sdom pa dang ldan pa'i tshul bzhin du shes par bya'o/ /
Other vows should be understood according to the way that absorption vows are possessed. This presentation is from the perspective of past and future vows.
mnyam gzhag 'phags lam gnas de gnyis/ / da ltar dang ldan bar gnas la/ / yod na dang po bar gyi dang / / phyin chad dus ni gnyis dang ngo/ / 21
Those in equipoise or abiding on the ārya path possess the present form of either. Those with interim precepts have nonindicative form in the interim and of both times after the first moment. (4:21)

de dag ni 'das ma 'ongs kyi dbang du byas pa yin la/ da ltar ba'i dbang du byas na zag bcas kyi bsam gtan la mnyam par bzhag pa dang 'phags pa'i lam la gnas pa ste snyoms par zhugs pa'i tshe bsam gtan dang zag med kyi sdom pa de gnyis kyi rig byed ma yin pa da ltar ba dang ldan gyi mnyam gzhag las langs pa na ni ma yin te/ de dag da ltar ba ni{ mnyam gzhag gi} sems kyi rjes su 'brang ba'i phyir ro/ / 'das ma 'ongs kyi thob pa ni mnyam par ma bzhag pa'i tshe'ang gtong rgyu ma byung gi bar du ldan no zhes bya ba ni grub pa'i mtha'o/ /

From the perspective of present vows, those in equipoise (samāhita) in contaminated absorption, or those abiding on the ārya path who enter meditative attainment (samāpatti), possess the present nonindicative form of either absorption vows or uncontaminated vows. But they do not possess such vows after rising from equipoise because present nonindicative form complements the mind {of equipoise}. The statement “past and future obtainment is possession until relinquished, even when not in equipoise” is [the assertion of a particular] philosophical tenet.

sdom pa'ang ma yin sdom min yang ma yin pa'i bar ma la gnas pa la gal te rig byed ma yin pa yod na skad cig ma dang po la gnas pa'i bar da ltar gyi dad ldan la skad cig ma dang po phyin chad 'das pa dang da ltar ba'i dus gnyis kyi dang ldan no/ / de yang ma btang gi bar du'o/ /

If those with interim precepts (madhyastha) — who have neither vows nor negative commitments — have nonindicative form, then they possess present nonindicative form in the interim between [past and future] while abiding in the first moment, and they possess past and present nonindicative form of both times after the first moment. Further, they have those until they are relinquished.
sdom min gnas pa dge ba dang / / sdom la gnas pa mi dge ba'i/ / rnam rig min ldan ji srid du/ / rab dang nyon mongs shugs ldan par/ / 22
Those abiding with negative commitments possess virtue, and those abiding with vows possess nonindicative nonvirtue for as long as they possess strong afflictions. (4:22)
'o na sdom min dang ldan pa{ bar ma'i} dge ba'i rig byed ma yin pa dang*/ sdom pa dang ldan pa'ang{ bar ma'i} mi dge ba'i rig byed ma yin pa dang ldan pa yod dam zhe na/ yod de/
Question: Can those possessing negative commitments [320] have nonindicative {interim} virtue? Also, can those possessing vows have nonindicative {interim} nonvirtue? Reply: They can.

{ dus ji srid du yod ce na/} sdom min la gnas pa shan pa la sogs pa'ang dge ba'i rnam par rig byed min pa dang ldan te/ ji srid du rab tu dang ba'i shugs dang ldan pas mchod rten la phyag 'tshal ba la sogs pa byed pa'i bar de srid du bar ma dge ba'i rig byed ma yin pa 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du so so thar pa'i sdom pa la gnas pa'ang mi dge ba'i rnam par rig byed min pa dang ldan te/ ji srid du nyon mongs pa'i shugs dang ldan pas srog chags gsod pa dang 'ching ba dang rdeg pa dang 'tshe ba la sogs pa byed pa'i bar de srid du bar ma mi dge ba'i rig byed ma yin pa dang ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / de dag ni rig byed ma yin pa'i dbang du byas pa'o/ /

{Question: For how long do they have it?} Reply: Those abiding with negative commitments, such as butchers and so on, can possess nonindicative virtue because for as long as that butcher pays homage to stūpas with strong, clear faith and so on, for that long nonindicative virtue occurs. So too, those abiding with pratimokṣa vows also can possess nonindicative nonvirtue, because for as long as they possess strong afflictions due to which they kill, bind, strike, and act cruelly to living beings and so on, for that long they possess nonindicative nonvirtue. These are from the perspective of nonindicative form.
da ni rig byed kyi dbang du byas nas ston te/
NOW TEACHING FROM THE PERSPECTIVE OF INDICATIVE FORM
rnam rig byed ni thams cad la/ / byed pa dag la da ltar ldan/ / ma btang bar du skad cig ma/ / phyin chad 'das ldan ma 'ongs med/ / 23

All those who produce indicative form always possess indicative form in the present. They possess past indicative form after the first moment until relinquished. They do not possess future indicative form. (4:23)

lus ngag gi rnam par rig byed ni sdom pa dang sdom pa ma yin pa dang bar ma la gnas pa thams cad la'ang rig byed dngos su byed pa dag la da ltar ba dang ldan la gtong ba'i rgyu dag gis ma btang gi bar du skad cig ma dang po phyin chad ni 'das pa dang yang ldan no/ / ma 'ongs pa{ 'i rig byed} dang ni ldan pa med de/ rig byed ni sems kyi rjes 'brang ma yin pa'i{ phyir dang} bem po yin pa'i phyir de lta bu'i nus pa med do/ /

Also, all those with vows, those with negative commitments, and those with interim precepts who directly produce indicative form always possess physical and verbal indicative form in the present. They also possess past indicative form after the first moment until it is relinquished by the causes of relinquishment. They do not possess future {indicative form because} it is not a complement of mind; it is matter, and it lacks that potency.
bsgribs pa dang ni ma bsgribs pa/ / 'das pa dag dang ldan pa'ang med/ /
The obscured and unobscured also do not possess past indicative form. (4:24ab)

dmigs kyis bsal ba bsgribs pa'i rig byed dang ma bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa'i rig byed dang ni ma 'ongs pa mi ldan par ma zad 'das pa dag dang ldan pa'ang med de/ lung du ma bstan pa'i chos rnams ni stobs chung bas {de dang lhan cig skyes pa'i } thob pa'ang stobs chung ba'i phyir {chos de 'gags nas de'i } thob pa snga phyir 'dren mi nus pa'i phyir ro/ /

The exception is that not only do obscured indicative form and unobscured-neutral indicative form not possess future indicative form, they also do not possess past indicative form, because neutral phenomena are weak in strength and the obtainment {of those arising simultaneously with it} is also weak in strength, and it cannot induce obtainment {of it since that phenomenon has ceased}.
zhar la sdom pa ma yin pa'i rnam grangs ni
IN ADDITION, THE EQUIVALENTS OF NEGATIVE COMMITMENTS
sdom pa min dang nyes spyad dang / / 'chal pa'i tshul khrims las de'i lam/ / 24
They are called negative commitments, negative action, unethical conduct, karma, and its path. (4:24cd)

lus ngag mi sdom pa'i phyir sdom pa min pa dang*/ dam pa rnams kyis smad cing 'bras bu yid du mi 'ongs pa skyed pa'i phyir nyes spyad dang*/ tshul khrims kyi mi mthun phyogs yin pas 'chal pa'i tshul khrims dang*/ lus ngag gi las yin pa'i phyir las dang*/ dngos kyis bsdus pa'i phyir las de'i lam zhes bya'o/ / des na 'dir rig byed dang ldan la rig byed ma yin pa dang mi ldan pa'ang yod ces pa mu bzhi ste/

They are called negative commitments (asaṃvara) because they do not restrain body and speech. They are called negative action (duścarita) because they are condemned by holy beings and generate an unpleasant result. They are called unethical conduct (dauḥśīlya) since they counter ethics. They are called karma because they are physical and verbal karma. And they are called the karmic path because they are subsumed by that phenomenon. Therefore, there are four possibilities regarding (1) possessing indicative form and (2) not possessing nonindicative form.
bar ma dor gnas sems zhan pas/ / byed na rnam rig nyid dang ldan/ / rnam rig btang dang ma skyes pa'i/ / 'phags pa'i gang zag rnam rig min/ / 25
One with interim precepts with a weak mind, possesses indicative form. Ārya beings who have relinquished indicative form and for whom it does not arise possess nonindicative form. (4:25)
