sdom pa sdom min gnyis ka ma yin pa'i bar ma der{ bar ma dge mi dge gang rung la} gnas pa zhig kun slong dge mi dge'i sems zhan pa ste drag po ma yin pa'i sems kyis dge mi dge'i lus ngag gi rig byed dag byed na ni{ sems zhan pas rig byed min pa slong mi nus pas} rnam par rig byed nyid dang ldan la rig byed ma yin pa dang ni mi ldan no 'dir dge mi dge'i sems zhan pa zhes smros pa ni sems drag pos byed na ni rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa dang ldan no zhes pa dang*/ dge mi dge'i sems zhan pas kyang rig byed ma yin pa skyed mi nus na lung ma bstan gyis byed na lta smros kyang ci dgos zhes bstan pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dir yang spyir btang ba ste dmigs kyis bsal na ni rdzas las byung ba'i bsod nams bya ba'i dngos po bdun dang*/ srog gcod pa la sogs pa las kyi lam rnams ni sems zhan pa dang lung ma bstan gyis byed kyang rig byed min pa dang ldan no/ /

[First possibility:] This is one who abides with {either virtuous or nonvirtuous} interim precepts that are neither vows nor negative commitments. They are motivated by a weak mind of virtue or nonvirtue that lacks intensity, which activates virtuous or nonvirtuous indicative [actions of] body and speech, and while one possesses indicative form, one does not possess nonindicative form {since a weak mind cannot invoke nonindicative form}. Here the statement “a weak mind of virtue or nonvirtue” [321] means “when a forceful mind is produced, indicative and nonindicative form is possessed.” Also, if weak minds of virtue or nonvirtue cannot generate nonindicative form, then what need is there to state that this also applies when neutral minds are activated. However, though this is true in general, there are exceptions, such as the seven things generating merit from material generosity, the karmic paths such as taking life, and so on. Although such actions are produced by weak and neutral minds, a person may come to possess nonindicative form through them.

tshe 'di'i rnam par rig byed btang ba dang phyi ma'i rnam par rig byed ma skyes pa'i 'phags pa'i gang zag {nur nur po la sogs pa dang gzugs med du skyes pa lta bu rig byed nyams pa } dag ni{ zag med kyi} rnam par rig byed min pa kho na dang ldan te/ rig byed ni 'gags shing ma skyes la zag med kyi sdom pa'i thob pa dang nges par ldan pa'i phyir ro/ {'dir so so'i skye bo dper ma brjod pa ni de bsam gtan thob pa tshe brjes nas rig byed ma skyes pa la de yod kyang spyir byis pa la ma nges 'phags pa la nges pas so/ / yang na 'dod pa la bsam nas smras la/ yang na 'phags pa ni dper brjod pa yin la so so'i skye bo yang de dang 'dra ba yod ces rgyal sras gsung ngo*/ / gal te byis pa bsam gtan gyi nyer bsdogs dang po thob pa dag shi na 'dod par yang yod do zhe na/ ma hA'i zhal nas byas pas dngos gzhi ma thob pa'i nyer bsdogs na shi bas gtong bar mtshan nyid 'dra ste/ bstan bcos las lus dang ldan la lus kyi las dang mi ldan pa ni sgo nga'i nang na 'dug pa'i mer mer po la sogs pa'o/ / zhes bshad pas so zhes gsung la/ 'on kyang 'dod pa'i rten la yang rdzas la ltos pa dang mi ltos pa'i bsod nams skye ba 'ga' zhig la 'di srid par rtogs so } 'di yang sa 'phos pa dag gi dbang du mdzad pa yin gyi sa ma 'phos pa ni so so'i skye bo bsam gtan gyi sdom pa thob pa shi 'phos pa la'ang de yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de la ni mnyam gzhag las langs pa na da ltar gyi rig byed ma yin pa med do zhes na/ de ni 'phags pa la'ang mtshungs so/ / de la 'das pa dang ma 'ongs pa'i thob pa yod do zhe na/ de ni bsam gtan la'ang mtshungs so/ /

[Second possibility:] Ārya beings who have relinquished the indicative form of this life and for whom indicative form does not arise in later lives, {such as in the embryonic stage of kalala, or those born in the formless realm where indicative form degenerates}, possess {uncontaminated} nonindicative form alone because indicative form is stopped and does not arise, and they definitely possess the obtainment of uncontaminated vows. {In this context Jinaputra mentions that ordinary beings are not said to be examples, for when they obtain the absorptions, indicative form does not arise through such transformation. But in general this is not certain for childlike [ordinary] beings, whereas it is certain for āryas. Further, this is stated with respect to the desire realm, and the example is declared for āryas, but similar states also exist for ordinary beings. Objection: If childlike [ordinary] beings who have obtained access concentration to the first absorption die, they exist in the desire realm. Reply: Since this is proclaimed by the Mahāsattva, if one dies in an access concentration without obtaining the actual basis, this situation is similar in its characteristics to relinquishing. Therefore a treatise reports: It is explained that one who possesses a body but does not possess physical karma is a being such as the embryonic stage of arbuda that exists in an egg and so on.[1053] However, it is understood that this is also possible for some desire-realm beings who do or do not generate merit from material generosity.} Further, this is from the perspective of those who relocate [to other] levels. Among those who do not change level, this is also the case for ordinary beings who have obtained absorption vows, when they die. Objection: If they arise from equipoise, they have no present nonindicative form. Reply: This is also the same for āryas. Objection: They have the obtainment of past and future nonindicative form. Reply: This is also the same for the absorptions.

gnyis ka dang ldan pa ni sdom pa dang sdom min dang{ bar ma dang} ldan pa {sems drag pos dge mi dge'i } rig byed{ byed bzhin pa} dang bcas pa'o/ / gnyis ka dang mi ldan pa ni gzugs med kyi so so'i skye {dang 'dod chags dang ma bral bar shi nas rig byed ma byung ba } bo'o/ / de bzhin du sdom pa dang ldan la bar ma dang mi ldan pa la sogs pa'ang shes par bya'o/ /
'thob pa'i tshul bshad pa ni
How vows are obtained
bsam gtan las skyes bsam gtan gyi/ / sa nyid kyis 'thob zag med ni/ / 'phags des so sor thar zhes pa/ / gzhan gyi rnam rig byed stsogs kyis/ / 26

Vows arising from the absorptions are obtained through the level of the absorptions. Uncontaminated vows are obtained by that ārya. Those called pratimokṣa vows are obtained by the indicative form of others and so on. (4:26)

bsam gtan las skyes pa'i sdom pa ni zag bcas kyi bsam gtan dngos gzhi dang*/ nyer bsdogs kyi sa ste sems gang yang rung ba thob pa nyid kyis 'thob ste/ de dag dang dus mnyam du 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / zag med kyi sdom pa ni 'phags pa zag med kyi bsam gtan sa drug gi sems thob pa des 'thob pa yin no/ {bsam gtan gyi sdom pa 'thob pa'ang*/ nyer bsdogs kyis bsdus pa ni 'og sar sbyor ba dang*/ gong nas 'og tu skye bas 'thob bo/ / dngos gzhis bsdus pa ni 'dod chags dang bral bas sam/ skye bas te bshad ma thag ltar ro/ / zag med 'thob pa yang*/ mi lcogs med la brten pa ni sbyor bas dang*/ rnam grol dgu pa la dngos gzhis bsdus pa ni 'dod chags dang bral bas te/ 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis yin na ma 'ongs pa kho na dang*/ 'das pas da ltar ba'ang 'thob bo/ / phyir mi 'ongs chags bral sngon 'gros sbyor ba kho nas 'thob bo }

Vows arising from the absorptions (dhyānaja) are obtained through obtaining any mind of the level of the actual basis and access concentration to the contaminated absorptions because [322] they arise at the same time as that absorption. Uncontaminated vows are obtained by that ārya who obtains the mind of the six uncontaminated absorption levels. {The obtainment of absorption vows that are subsumed by the access concentrations to the absorptions is obtained through preparation in lower levels or through birth from higher to lower levels. Obtainment subsumed by the actual basis of the absorptions is due to nonattachment or through birth, as just explained. Regarding the obtainment of uncontaminated vows, those dependent on unrestricted access concentration are obtained through preparation. Those subsumed by the actual basis of the absorptions on the nine liberated paths are obtained through freedom from attachment. If they are obtained by the mundane path, it is future obtainment alone, but if they are obtained by the transcendent path, it is present obtainment. A nonreturner previously freed from attachment obtains them through preparation alone.}

so so thar pa zhes bya ba'i sdom pa ni gzhan gyi{ mkhan slob} gsol ba dang brjod pa la sogs pa'i rnam par rig byed sogs kyis bsdus pa rang gi rig byed kyis kyang 'thob bo/ / de la sogs pa'i sgras ni rang gi sems pa dang lus ngag gi rig byed gzung ngo*/ / de yang dge slong pha ma dang dge slob ma'i sdom pa rnams ni dge 'dun las 'thob la/ dge bsnyen pha ma dang*/ dge tshul pha ma dang*/ bsnyen gnas pa rnams ni gang zag las so/ /

Those called pratimokṣa vows are obtained by one’s own indicative form and that subsumed by the indicative form of others, such as requests, the words {of abbots and masters}, and so on. Here “and so on” refers to one’s intention and the indicative form of body and speech. Further, the vows of male and female fully ordained beings and probationary nuns are obtained from the Saṅgha. Male and female lay vows, novice monk or novice nun vows, and one-day vows are obtained from other persons.

bye brag tu smra ba'i 'dul ba 'dzin pa rnams na re bsnyen par rdzogs pa'i tshul bcu bzung ba'i phyir sogs pa'i sgra mdzad de/ sangs rgyas dang rang sangs rgyas ni rang byung gis bsnyen par rdzogs pa'o/ /
Vaibhāṣika Vinaya masters say: The “and so on” refers to the ten methods of taking full ordination: 1. Ordination by oneself, such as buddhas and pratyekabuddhas
kun shes ko'u Dir+Ya dang*/ rta thul dang*/ bzang po dang*/ rlangs pa dang*/ ming chen te lnga sde rnams ni nges pa la 'jug pa ste bden pa mthong bas so/ /
2. Ordination through seeing the four truths such as the group of five: Ājñātakauṇḍinya, Aśvajit, Bhadrika, Vāṣpa, and Mahānāma
grags pa dang lag bzang dang ba lang bdag dang dri med dang gang po ste nye ba'i lnga sde la sogs pa rnams ni dge slong tshur shog ces brjod pas so/ /
3. Ordination through stating “Come forth, bhikṣu,” such as the five close disciples: Kīrti, Subāhu, Gavāṃpati, Vimala, and Pūrṇa
'od srungs chen po ni ston par khas blangs pa tsam gyis so/ /
4. Ordination by merely accepting [Śākyamuni] as one’s master, such as Mahākāśyapa
dri bas mnyes pas ni legs sbyin {legs byin gcig tu gces pa'i chos gang yin/ thar pa lags so/ /de la dgos pa gang yin/ dad pa lags so/ /zhes lan btab ces paN chen gsung ngo } no/ /

5. Ordination by answering a question such as Sodāyin. {A mahāpaṇḍita said that he obtained ordination by his answers. The Buddha asked: “Sodāyin, what is cherished by all?” He answered: “Liberation.” The Buddha asked: “What does one need to obtain that?” He answered: “Faith.”}
skye dgu'i bdag mo la sogs pa ni lci ba'i chos brgyad khas blangs pas te/
6. Ordination by accepting the eight heavy rules such as Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī

brgyad gang zhe na/ dge slong las bsnyen par rdzogs par bya ba dang zla ba phyed phyed cing dge slong las gdams ngag mnod par bya ba dang*/ dbyar dge slong med pa'i gnas su mi 'gro ba dang*/ dgag dbye'i tshe gnyis ka'i dge 'dun la gnas gsum gyis dgag dbye bya ba dang*/ dge slong gi ltung ba gleng bar mi bya ba dang*/ dge slong la ltung ba byung ba la khro bar mi bya ba dang*/ bla ma'i chos{ te lci chos brgyad} kyi ltung ba byung ba zla ba phyed du mnyes par bya ba spyad par bya ba dang*/ bsnyen par rdzogs nas lo brgya lon pa'i dge slong mas kyang dge slong gsar bu la'ang phyag bya ba rnams so/ /

Question: What are these eight? Reply: [a] Taking full ordination from fully ordained monks, [b] accepting instruction from fully ordained monks each fortnight, [c] not going to abodes where there are no fully ordained monks in the summer rains retreat, [d] conducting retreat cessation with both saṅghas in the three abodes at retreat cessation, [e] not proclaiming the downfall of a fully ordained monk, [f] not being enraged at the downfall of a fully ordained monk, [g] being pleased at the bimonthly confession of the downfalls of {the eight heavy} higher rules, [h] and — even for a nun who has been fully ordained as many as one hundred years — prostrating to a new fully ordained monk.

rgyal rigs chos sbyin zhes bya ba btsun mo'i 'khor gyi nang na 'dug pa las ne tso bzhin sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das kyi drung du rab tu byung bar gsol ba'i 'phrin gyis so/ / yang na sa ga'i chung ma chos sbyin ma ut+pa la'i mdog las 'phrin gyis bsnyen par rdzogs pa lta bu'o/ /

7. Ordination by messenger, such as the kṣatriyī Dharmadinnā, who requested ordination in front of the Bhagavan [by repeating the rite] parrot fashion while living in the retinue of the queen. Again, it is like Dharmadinnā, the wife of Saga, being fully ordained by messenger from Utpalavarṇā. [323]
dge slong bzhi dang 'dul ba 'dzin pa dang lngas ni mtha' 'khob kyi mi rnams te/ 'dul ba 'dzin pa ni TIka byed dag gsol ba brjod pa po la 'dod de gsol ba dang las brjod mkhan no/ /

8. Ordination by five for those of remote areas: four fully ordained monks and a Vinaya master. Pūrṇavardhana’s commentary asserts that the Vinayadhara is the one who responds to the one who makes the request with affirmations and he is the one who conducts the rite.
yul dbus su ni gsol ba brjod pa gtogs pa bcu'i tshogs kyis so/ /
9. For those of central regions, ordination by an assembly of ten, including the one who makes the request

dbus dang mtha' 'khob kyi khyad par ni dpag tshad drug cu'i nang dang phyi rol te lung ko lpags kyi gzhi las/ rdo rje'i gdan nas shar na li kha ra shing 'phel gyi nags dang*/ lho na chu klung 'dam bu dang 'dam bu'i chu rgyun can dang*/ nub na bram ze spun gnyis kyis byas pa'i grong ka ba dang nye ba'i ka ba dang*/ byang na u shi ra'i ri ste de dag phan chad ni mtha' 'khob dang tshun chad ni dbus su bshad do/ /

The difference between “remote” and “central” is the difference between being more than or less than sixty yojanas from the center. The Chapter on Hides explains: The central region stretches from Vajrāsana to Puṇḍravardhana in the east, to the city of Sarāvatī and the Sarāvatī River in the south, to the two brahman villages Sthūṇa and Upasthūṇaka in the west, to the mountain of Uśīragiri in the north. Beyond these lie the remote regions.[1054]
skyabs su 'gro ba lan gsum brjod pas ni sde bzang drug cu po rnams bsnyen par rdzogs so/ /
10. Ordination by taking refuge three times is the method of taking ordination by the pure group of sixty.

de dag gi bsnyen par rdzogs pa'i sdom pa ni gdon mi za bar gzhan gyi rnam par rig byed la{ ltos par ma nges pas de la nges par} mi ltos pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/{ sde lnga po dang grags pa la sogs pa ni sngon gyi smon lam gyi dbang ste bsam pa phun sum tshogs pa'am/ sangs rgyas kyi mthus rnam par rig byed med par yang so so thar pa'i sdom pa 'thob bo zhes 'chad do/ /}

It is said that the vows of the fully ordained are without doubt {definitely} taken without relying on the indicative form of others {since such reliance is uncertain. It is explained that the group of five as well as Kīrti and so on obtained pratimokṣa vows without indicative form through the power of past prayer, due to their excellent thought, or by the might of the Buddha.}
dus ji srid du blang bar bya zhe na/
Question: For how long are they taken?
ji srid 'tsho dang nyin zhag tu/ / sdom pa yang dag blang bar bya/ / nyin zhag pa yi sdom min med/ / de de ltar nod med ces grag / 27
They take vows correctly for as long as they live or for a day and night. One-day negative commitments do not exist because it is well known that they cannot be taken in that way. (4:27)

dus kyi mtha' ni srog gi mtha' dang nyin zhag gi mtha' gnyis las dge bsnyen la sogs pa bdun ni srog gi mtha' ji srid 'tsho ba ma shi'i bar du dang*/ bsnyen gnas pas ni nyin zhag gi mtha' nyin zhag gcig tu sdom pa yang dag par blang bar bya ba yin no/ / gal te ji srid 'tsho'i 'og tu ni yang dag par blangs pa yod kyang lus skal ba mi 'dra ba'i phyir dang*/ des kyang tshe phyi ma der sbyor ba ma byas pa'i phyir dang*/ mi dran pa'i phyir sdom pa mi skye bar rigs na/ nyin zhag gi 'og tu bsnyen gnas kyi sdom pa mi skye ba la rgyu mtshan ci zhig yod ce na/ mdo las nyin zhag gcig pa kho nar bstan pas nyin zhag gi 'og tu skye ba la gegs byed yod par shes so/ / de lta na re zhig ston pas nyin zhag gi 'og tu bsnyen gnas kyi sdom pa mi skye bar gzigs nas nyin zhag pa'i bsnyen gnas bstan nam/ 'on te dbang po gdul dka' ba zhag mang po srung mi nus pa rnams kyi ched du yin zhe na/

Reply: The period of time is either (1) the period of one’s life or (2) the period of a day and night. The seven beings such as laypeople and so on take vows correctly for the period of their entire lives, for as long as they live before dying; one-day vow-holders take vows for the period of one day and night. Question: When vows are correctly taken, they arise for as long as one lives; however, it is logical that vows may sometimes not arise: because of the specific condition of the body, because one does not use this life to prepare for future lives, or because one is not mindful. But what are the causes for one-day vows not arising for longer than one day and night? Reply: Since a sūtra proclaims that they last just one night and day, one should understand that their arising for longer than one day and night is refuted.[1055] Question: Therefore did the Master proclaim one-day vows lasting one day and night, having seen that one-day vows do not arise for longer than one day and night, or were they proclaimed for those who are difficult to tame and incapable of protecting vows for many days?

slob dpon 'dun bzang na re de lta bu'i rgyu mtshan ni brtag par mi nus te/ 'dul ba'i don dag ni thams cad mkhyen pa ma yin pa rtog ges khong du chud par mi nus te/ gang sdom pa de dag las kha cig ni tshogs kyi nang du gsol ba dang bzhi'i las kyis 'thob la/ kha cig ni gang zag gcig las gsol ba tsam gyis 'thob pa 'di la'ang rgyu ci zhig yod/ des na 'di la rgyu mtshan btsal bar mi bya'o/ / dbang po gdul dka' ba la ltos pa'ang ma yin te/ ches gdul dka' ba la yud tsam dang nyin mo tsam dang mtshan mo tsam pa'ang ston par thal bar 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ gzhan yang khyim pa thams cad dbang po gdul dka' bar yang ma nges pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ / slob dpon ni mdo las de ltar gsungs par zad kyi 'on kyang ji srid 'tsho ba ltar nyin zhag gi 'og tu bsnyen gnas kyi sdom pa skye ba la'ang rigs pa dang 'gal ba ni med do zhes bzhed do/ /

Master Saṅghabhadra observes that the reason for this cannot be discerned since the meaning of Vinaya cannot be understood by those such as dialecticians who are not omniscient. Some say: Any of those vows are obtained by the rite of the four requests within the assembly. Some say: They are obtained by merely requesting them from another person. What reason exists for this? Do not seek a reason for this. Also, it is said that they were not given according to the difficulty in taming the sense faculties, because it would then follow they would have been proclaimed for one session, one night, or one day for those who are extremely difficult to tame, and it is not certain that all householders have faculties that are [324] difficult to tame.[1056] Vasubandhu explains that this is stated in a sūtra but it does not contradict the logic that one-day vows arise for longer than one day and night, like vows taken for as long as one lives.[1057]

nyin zhag pa'i sdom pa min pa ni med de/ ci'i phyir zhe na/ bdag ni nyin zhag gcig tu sdom min dang ldan par gyur cig ces de de ltar nod pa med pa'i phyir ro zhes grag go /de'i phyir sdom min ni ji srid 'tsho ba yin no zhes bye brag tu smra ba 'dod mod kyi de ltar len pa med pas med par 'gyur na ni ji srid 'tsho ba'i sdom min yang med par 'gyur te/ las smad pa yin pas len pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te ji srid 'tsho'i bar du srog gcod pas 'tsho bar bya'o snyam du sems pa nyid len par 'dod na nyin zhag pa'ang yod pa'i phyir ro/ / gro bzhin skyes kyi rtogs pa brjod pa las nyin zhag pa'i sdom pa dang sdom min yang gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / {mdo sde pa mi dge ba'i sems pa la sdom pa min par 'dod do }

Further, one-day negative commitments do not exist. Question: Why? Reply: That is because it is well known that they cannot be taken in that way: by stating, “May I come to possess negative commitments for one day.” Indeed, Vaibhāṣikas assert that negative commitments last for as long as one lives. But if they are not taken since they are not taken in that way, then negative commitments lasting for as long as one lives would not exist, because they could not be taken since they are inferior karma. But if one desired to take [such negative commitments] with the intention to live through, say, killing for as long as one lived, then negative commitments lasting for one day and night would also exist. Moreover, the Story of Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa mentions that there are vows and negative commitments lasting a day and night.[1058] {Sautrāntikas assert that negative commitments exist when there is nonvirtuous intention.}
bsnyen gnas kyi sdom pa/
'o na bsnyen gnas kyi sdom pa len pa'i tshul ji ltar zhe na
Question: What is the method of taking one-day vows?
mnod par bya'o zhes khyad gzhir byas la/ gang gis/ ji srid du/ gang*/ gang gi tshe/ gang las mnod par bya zhe na/
Reply: One takes the statement “May I take these vows” as the basis. Question: (1) By whom, (2) for how long, (3) what, (4) when, and (5) from whom should they be taken?
dma' bar 'dug smras bzlas pa yis/ / mi brgyan nam ni nang par du/ / bsnyen gnas yan lag tshang bar ni/ / nang par gzhan las nod par bya/ / 28
Vows are taken by assuming a low position, without adornment, by repeating the words, from dawn until sunrise, complete in branches, in the morning from another. (4:28)

rim pa ltar {ji ltar nus pa bzhin du } lus kyi spyod lam ma gus pa la sdom pa mi skye bas nad pa ma gtogs pa stan dma' bar tsog tsog po'am pus mo btsugs te 'dug nas lag pa thal mo bsnol ba'am sbyar te/ nar mas gsar du rgyags par mi byed pas nar ma ma gtogs pa rgyan gsar pas mi brgyan pa dang*/ ngag gi spyod lam slob dpon gyis smras pa'i rjes su bzlas pa yis gnod par bya'i/ spar dang kha bsnyams te smras pas ni 'bogs nod kyi don med pas gzhan las gnod par mi 'gyur ro/ / dus ni nang par nam nangs nas nyi ma shar gyi bar du'o/ / ngo bo ni yan lag ma tshang na bar mar 'gyur bas bsnyen gnas kyi sdom pa srog gcod spong ba la sogs pa'i yan lag brgyad po tshang bar ni mnod par bya ste/ spong ba rnams phan tshun rag lus pa'i phyir ro zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/ /

Reply: Since vows do not arise in those with a disrespectful physical attitude, vows should be taken {in accordance with one’s capacity}, respectively, (1) by assuming a low position — squatting or kneeling unless sick — with hands interlaced or with palms together, without adornment by special jewelry but merely that normally worn since they do not generate fresh vanity. And in terms of verbal action, the vows should be taken by repeating the words after they are stated by the preceptor. If the words are stated before or at the same time as the preceptor, the vows are not received from the other person since there is no giving and receiving. (2) Their duration is from dawn until the following sunrise. (3) Since by nature they become interim precepts when incomplete in requisites, one should take one-day vows complete in the eight branches such as abandoning taking life because the actions to be abandoned mutually rely on each other. This is stated by Master Pūrṇavardhana.[1059]

de yang nangs par nyi ma ma shar zhing zan ma zos kyi gong du dang*/ { rkyen yod kyang mi 'da' bar bya ba'i phyir/} yul gzhan las mnod par bya'o/ / gzhan de yang 'dul ba las dge slong las len par bshad mod kyi/ gnas 'jog gi mdo las/ rigs kyi bu'am rigs kyi bu mo dad pa dang ldan pa yan lag brgyad dang ldan pa'i bsnyen gnas blang bar 'dod pas nangs par langs la dge sbyong ngam bram ze gzhan gang yang rung ba shes pa zhig gi drung du song ste zhes gsungs pa'i phyir cho ga shes pa tsam gyis kyang chog par bshad la/ rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las ni yul med na rang gis len pa'ang bshad{ cing tshe gang gi bsnyen gnas gnas gcig tu len pa'ang bshad} do/ /

Further, (4) they should be taken in the morning before the sun rises and before preparing food, and (5) from another being. {All these conditions should be present and none overlooked.} Indeed, the Vinaya explains that “other” refers to taking vows from a fully ordained being. The Geography Sūtra advises: Faithful sons and daughters of good lineage who desire to take one-day vows possessing the eight sections should rise in the morning and proceed to the presence of a monk or a brahman who is knowledgable.[1060] This explains that it is permissible to take the vows from one merely knowledgable in the rite. The Compendium of Ascertainment explains that if another being does not exist, one may take them by oneself, and {it explains that when taken, they are taken in the same place}.
ci'i phyir yan lag brgyad ces bshad ce na/
Question: Why are eight branches[1061] explained?
tshul khrims yan lag bag yod pa'i/ / yan lag brtul zhugs yan lag ste/ / bzhi gcig de bzhin gsum rim bzhin/ / de yis dran nyams dregs par 'gyur/ / 29
The branches of ethics, the branch of vigilance, and the branches of asceticism are, respectively, four, one, and so too three. Through it, mindfulness degenerates, one becomes vain. (4:29)

rang bzhin gyi kha na ma tho ba spong ba'i phyir tshul khrims kyi yan lag dang po bzhi dang*/ chang 'thungs na tshul khrims dang ldan yang bag med par gyur pas na bag yod pa'i yan lag chang spong ba gcig pu dang de bzhin du skyo ba dang rjes su mthun pa'i phyir brtul zhugs kyi yan lag phyi ma gsum ste rim pa bzhin du sbyar ro/ / gal te srog gcod spong pa la sogs pa bzhi blangs pas tshul khrims rdzogs na chang la sogs pa spangs te ci bya zhe na/

Reply: Respectively, the first four are the branches (aṅga) of ethics (śīla) [325] because they abandon natural offenses, one is the branch of vigilance (apramāda) that abandons alcohol, since those with ethics become negligent through drinking alcohol, and so too the last three are the branches of asceticism (vrata) because they conform with disgust. Question: If ethics are complete through abandoning the four such as taking life, what need is there to abandon alcohol and so on?

chang 'thungs pa de yis ni spong ba'i gnyen po bya ba dang bya ba ma yin pa'i dran pa dang shes bzhin nyams par 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ glu dang gar la sogs pa bstan pas ni dregs pa dang rgyags par 'gyur zhing dregs par gyur pa la 'chal ba'i tshul khrims thag mi ring ba'i phyir dang*/ dus ma yin pa'i kha zas ma spangs na bsnyen gnas kyi dran pa dang skyo ba'i dran pa mi 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir de dag ni tshul khrims de srung ba'i yan lag tu gsungs pa yin no/ / bsnyen gnas pa la gar sogs dang phreng sogs spong ba yan lag gcig tu mdzad la dge tshul la de dag spong ba yan lag gnyis su mdzad pa ni khyim pa rnams la ni de dag ha cang tshul dang mi mthun pa ma yin pas de dag dang 'gal na nyes pa gcig bshags pas chog pas yang bar mdzad nas gcig tu bsdus te bcas la/ rab tu byung ba la ni de dag tshul dang mi mthun pas de dag dang 'gal na nyes pa gnyis bshags dgos pas lci bar mdzad de gnyis su bcas so/ / de bzhin du gser dngul len pa spong ba'ang rab tu byung ba'i phyogs la ni tshul dang mi mthun pas bcas kyi khyim pa la ni de lta ma yin pas ma bcas so zhes rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las bshad do/ / slob dpon gang spel ni shin tu mang ngo snyam du sgyid lug pa'i khyim pa rnams la sla bar bstan pa'i phyir gcig tu rnam par bzhag ste bri rdzi'i bu la bslab pa'i gzhi bstan pa bzhin no zhes 'chad do/ / ci'i phyir bsnyen gnas zhes bya zhe na/ 'dis dgra bcom pa la nye bar gnas pa'i phyir ram ji srid 'tsho ba'i sdom pa dang nye ba'i phyir ro/ / yang na bsnyen gnas ni dge bsnyen rnams kyi gso sbyong yin pas dge ba gso ba dang ltung ba sbyang ba'i phyir 'di ni gso sbyong yan lag brgyad pa zhes bya ste/ lung las/ gang phyir yid kyi dge ba gsos 'debs de yi phyir/ / 'di ni bcom ldan 'das kyis gso sbyong bshad ces grag ces gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na dge bsnyen ma yin pa la bsnyen gnas med dam zhe na/

Reply: Because through drinking alcohol, the antidotes that abandon nonvirtue, such as mindfulness (smṛti) and introspection of proper and improper action, degenerate; through singing and dancing and so on, one becomes vain (mada) and arrogant; through becoming vain, one draws close to unethical conduct; and if one does not abandon untimely eating, then mindfulness of one-day vows and disgust do not arise. Therefore these are said to be the branches that protect ethics. For one-day vow-holders, abandoning dancing and so on as well as garlands and so forth are taken as one branch. For novices, abandoning these is taken as two branches. For householders, they are subsumed in a single branch since they are not taken as highly inappropriate acts but as milder faults that, when transgressed, may be confessed as a single fault. But for the ordained, they are heavier inappropriate acts that form two branches and, if transgressed, must be confessed as two faults. Similarly, though touching silver and gold is abandoned, it is taken as an inappropriate act for the ordained but not so for householders.[1062] This is explained in the Compendium of Ascertainment. Master Pūrṇavardhana explains that these are posited as one branch because such rules are taught less rigorously to householders who may otherwise be discouraged, thinking there are too many vows, in just the way the basis of the training was taught to Vṛjiputra.[1063] Question: Why are they called “one-day vows”?[1064] Reply: Because one abides near to [or in the service of] arhats, or they are near to lifelong vows. Again, since one-day vows restore [the virtue of] laypeople, they are called the “eight branches of restoration” because they restore virtue and purify downfalls. A scripture mentions: Why is that? It is because mental virtue is restored. It is well known that the Bhagavan explained this to be restoration.[1065] Question: Are there any one-day vows in the absence of laypeople?
gzhan la'ang bsnyen gnas yod mod kyi/ / skyabs su ma song ba la med/ / dge bsnyen nyid du khas blangs pas/ / sdom pa bstan pa dge slong bzhin/ / 30
Indeed, other one-day vow-holders exist, but none who do not take refuge. Vows arise by accepting to become a layperson through enunciating, like the fully ordained. (4:30)

{skyabs su song nas len na } dge bsnyen las gzhan la'ang bsnyen gnas yod mod kyi dkon mchog gsum la skyabs su ma song ba la med do/ / de yang 'grel pa las/ dge bsnyen ma yin pa yang gang zhig nyin zhag de la sangs rgyas dang chos dang dge 'dun la skyabs su song ste bsnyen gnas nad pa de la bsnyen gnas kyi sdom pa skye bar 'gyur te gzhan du ni ma yin no/ / mi shes pa ni ma gtogs so zhes 'byung ba'i ma gtogs pa'i don ni slob dpon rgyal po'i sras skyabs 'gro brjed pa dang {mi shes pa } ma byang ba la 'chad mod kyi/ slob dpon gang spel gang zhig /dkon mchog gsum la the tshom za ba dang log par zhugs pa'i bsam pas skyabs su mi 'gro ba can la ni sdom pa mi skye la/ gang zhig 'bogs pa po dang len pa pos skyabs su 'gro dgos par ma shes pas skyabs su mi 'gro ba yin gyi log par zhugs pa'am the tshom za bas skyabs su mi 'gro ba ma yin pa de la ni skyabs su ma song yang bsnyen gnas kyi sdom pa skye'o zhes 'chad pa ltar yin no/ /

Reply: Indeed, one-day vow-holders other than laypeople do exist {who have taken refuge} but none who do not take refuge in the Three Jewels. Further, the Autocommentary explains: When one who is not a layperson takes refuge day and night [326] in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, then one-day vows are generated in that person who takes one-day vows, but not in others. Those who do not know refuge are not included.[1066] Indeed, Master Jinaputra explains that “not included” refers to those who forget refuge and do not purify {not knowing}.[1067] Master Pūrṇavardhana writes: Vows do not arise in those who do not go for refuge either through having doubts about the Three Jewels or through wrongly conceiving them. Those who merely don’t know that one needs to go for refuge by means of a bestower and receiver do not go for refuge, but since their not going for refuge is not due to misconception or doubt, then even though they do not go for refuge, one-day vows arise.[1068]
dge bsnyen gyi sdom pa/

'o na ming chen gyi mdo las/ ming chen 'di ltar khyim pa gos dkar po bgos pa skyes pa pho'i dbang po dang ldan pa zhig sangs rgyas la skyabs su 'gro/ chos dang dge 'dun la skyabs su 'gro zhing bdag la dge bsnyen du gzung du gsol zhes tshig tu'ang smra na 'di tsam gyis dge bsnyen du 'gyur ro zhes gsungs pa de ci skyabs su 'gro ba kho nas dge bsnyen du 'gyur ram zhe na/ nyi 'og pa rnams na re 'gyur ro zhes zer{ 'di ni thob pa la bsams so} ro/ /

Now, the Mahānāma Sūtra declares: Mahānāma, if a householder wearing white clothes, male, and possessing a male organ takes refuge in the Buddha, takes refuge in the Dharma and Saṅgha, and utters the words “Consider me to be a layperson,” then by just this rite he becomes a layperson.[1069] Question: Does this mean that one becomes a layperson through taking refuge alone? Aparāntaka [Vaibhāṣikas] say they do, {but here they mean obtainment.}

kha che ba rnams ni de tsam gyis mi 'gyur{ te sdom pa ma skyes pa'i phyir des na} gyi dge bsnyen nyid du khas blangs pas 'di'i sdom pa skye bar 'gyur ro/ / de'i phyir mdo de las kyang bdag dge bsnyen du gzung du gsol zhes khas blangs pa nyid yin no/ / 'o na slob dpon dgongs su gsol/ ji ltar 'phags pa dgra bcom pa de dag gis ji srid 'tsho'i bar du srog gcod pa spangs te srog gcod pa las slar log pa de bzhin du bdag ming 'di zhes bgyi bas kyang dus 'di nas gzung ste ji srid 'tsho'i bar du srog gcod pa spangs te srog gcod pa las slar ldog par bgyi'o zhes bya ba la sogs pa'i bslab pa'i gnas bstan pa don med par 'gyur ro zhe na/ sdom pa dge bsnyen du gzung du gsol zhes bya bas thob kyang srog gcod spong ba la sogs pa'i bslab pa'i gnas bstan pa na dper na dge slong gi sdom pa gsol ba dang bzhi'i las kyis thob kyang bslab pa'i gnas rnams brjod dgos pa bzhin no/ /

Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas say they don’t become laypeople merely through taking refuge {because vows are not generated. Thus} the vows of such beings arise by accepting to become a layperson. Therefore this sūtra mentions that vows are taken through stating “Consider me to be a layperson.” Question: Now, it would become meaningless to declare modes of training in such statements as “Master, please consider this, just as ārya arhats abandon taking life for as long as they live, and desist from again taking life, similarly, I, by the name of [so-and-so,] also from this time on, for as long as I live, will abandon taking life and refrain from taking life . . .”[1070] and so on. Reply: Vows are obtained by stating “Consider me to be a layperson” as well as through enunciating the modes of training — abandoning taking life and so on — like, for example, the vows of the fully ordained (bhikṣu) that are obtained though the rite of the four requests, but there is still need to explain the modes of training.
gal te thams cad bsdams yin na/ / sna gcig spyod sogs ji lta bu/ / de srung ba la gsungs zhes grag / chung ngu la sogs yid ji bzhin/ / 31
If lay vows restrain all, how can there be practitioners of one vow and so on? They assert they guard it by nominating it. They are weak and so on according to the mind. (4:31)

gal te sdom pa ni yan lag{ lnga po} thams cad {kyis } bsdams pa yin na ming chen gyis zhus pa las srog gcod spong ba'i sna gcig spyod pa dang*/ sogs pas bsdus pa srog gcod dang ma byin len gnyis spong ba'i phyogs gcig spyod pa dang*/ 'dod log dang gsum spong ba'i phal cher spyod pa dang*/ rtsa ba bzhi chang dang lnga char srung ba'i yongs su rdzogs pa'i dge bsnyen zhes bya ba'i dbye ba gsungs pa ji lta bu yin zhe na/ bye brag tu smra ba ni{ dang po na lnga kar blangs par mtshungs kyang de las re re gnyis gnyis nyams pas lhag ma de srung ba la dgongs nas} gang zhig sna gcig pa dang phal cher dang yongs su rdzogs pa la sogs pa de dang de srung ba la de dang de lta bur gsungs par zad kyi thams cad kyang{ dang por} sdom pa lnga char thob par ni 'dra'o/ / zhes grag ste/ {rtsa ba'i ltung ba gcig byung bas sdom pa gzhan mi gtong ba 'dod pas so de ni mi rigs te } de lta bu la zhu ba dang dri ba'ang mi rigs pa'i phyir 'dir mdo'i dgongs pa ni dang po nyid nas sna gcig la sogs pa blangs nas srung ba nyid yin par shes so/ / gzhan yang lung rnam 'byed las/ bzhin bzang ji srid 'tsho'i bar du bcom ldan 'das kyi spyan sngar lnga pa tshangs par spyod pa'i bslab pa'i gzhi dag long zhig ces mi tshangs spyod spong ba'i dge bsnyen yang gsungs la/ ji srid 'tsho'i bar du bsnyen gnas yan lag brgyad srung ba go mi'i dge bsnyen zhes bya ba dang*/ skyabs gsum tsam 'dzin pa dang nyin mo tsam dang mtshan mo tsam pa'i dge bsnyen yang slob dpon a b+h+ya la sogs pa'i gzhung las bshad do/ /

If [lay] vows restrain all {five} branches, then how can the Sūtra Requested by Mahānāma state classifications such as: (1) a practitioner of one vow (ekadeśakārin) and so on? The “and so on” includes (2) a practitioner of two vows (pradeśakārin) who abandons both taking life and taking what is not given, and (3) a practitioner of most vows (yadbhūyaskārin) who abandons three, including sexual misconduct, and (4) a complete practitioner (paripūrṇakārin) who guards four or five parts of the root discipline. Vaibhāṣikas, {who think that laypeople are initially similar in taking five vows, then, when one or two vows degenerate, they guard [327] the remainder,} assert that practitioners of (1) one vow, (3) most vows, and (4) complete practitioners guard this or that vow by nominating a specific vow; however, {initially} all are similar in obtaining the five sections of the vows. {But it is illogical to assert that through the occurrence of one root downfall the other vows are not relinquished,} because then also [the rite of] requesting and questioning would be illogical. Here the intention of the sūtra [above] is that, having taken the practice of one vow and so on, one should know what is to be guarded from the beginning. Again, Vinaya Divisions declares: Bhadramukha, in the presence of the Bhagavan take as your basis of training the fifth branch, celibacy, for as long as you live. This refers to the layperson who abandons impure conduct, [that is, noncelibacy]. One guarding eight sections of the one-day vows for as long as one lives is called a “gomin layperson.” And also there are those lay practitioners holding three refuges alone or for a day, or for a night. This is also explained in the texts of Master Abhaya[1071] and so on.

dge slong la sogs pa'i sdom pa chung ngu dang*/ sogs pas gzung ba 'bring dang chen po ni yang dag par len pa'i kun slong gi yid chung ba dang 'bring dang chen po ji lta ba bzhin yin no/ / de'i phyir dgra bcom pa bas so so'i skye bo'i sdom pa che ba'ang srid do/ /

The vows of the fully ordained and so on are weak, medium, or strong and so on, according to the strength of the mind (manas) that motivates the proper taking of vows, whether small, medium, or great. Therefore it is possible that the vows of an ordinary being are stronger than those of an arhat.
skyabs 'gro bshad pa/
gal te sdom pa thams cad skyabs su 'gro ba sngon du 'gro ba can yin na gang zhig dkon mchog gsum la skyabs su 'gro ba de ci la skyabs su 'gro zhe na/
Question: If refuge precedes the taking of all vows, then taking refuge in the Three Jewels is taking refuge in what?
gang zhig gsum la skyabs 'gro de/ / sangs rgyas dge 'dun byed pa'i chos/ / mi slob pa dang gnyis ka dang / / mya ngan 'das la skyabs su 'gro/ / 32
Taking refuge in those three is taking refuge in the Buddha, in both learners and nonlearners that represent the Saṅgha, and in nirvāṇa. (4:32)

gang zhig sangs rgyas dang dge 'dun dang chos gsum la skyabs su 'gro ba de ni go rim bzhin du sangs rgyas su byed pa'i chos mi slob pa'i lam dang*/ dge 'dun du byed pa'i chos slob mi slob gnyis ka'i lam dang*/ chos su byed pa'i chos mya ngan las 'das pa so sor btags 'gog la skyabs su 'gro ba yin te/ mi slob pa'i lam ni sangs rgyas kyi chos kyi sku yin pa'i phyir dang*/ slob mi slob kyi dge 'dun gang zag ya brgyad du 'byed par byed pa'i phyir dang*/ mya ngan las 'das pa ni 'gog pa'i chos yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na sangs rgyas kyi sku la ngan sems kyis khrag phyung ba mtshams med du mi 'gyur te/ chos kyi sku la khrag dbyung du med pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ de'i rten la gnod pa'i phyir ram/ gtso che bas chos kyi sku zhes smros kyi gzhan du na gzugs kyi sku sangs rgyas su byed pa'i phyir ro/ / skyabs su 'gro ba'i don gang zhe na/ kun nas slong ba dang bcas pa'i ngag gi rig byed de/ kun slong ni de la brten par 'dod pa'o/ / 'grel pa las kyang*/ skyabs su 'gro ba rnams kyi rang bzhin ci zhe na/ ngag gi rnam par rig byed kyi ngo bo nyid dag yin no/ / zhes 'byung ste/ TI ka las/ de ni nod pa'i dus kyi dbang du byas pa yin no zhes 'byung ngo*/ / gang las skyob ce na/ sdug bsngal thams cad las skyabs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'grel pa las kyang*/ skyabs kyi don ci zhe na/ de la brten nas sdug bsngal thams cad las gtan du nges par thar pa'i phyir ro zhes 'byung ngo*/ /

Reply: Taking refuge in those three — the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha — is taking refuge, respectively, in the nonlearner path that represents the Buddha, in the paths of both learners and nonlearners that represent the Saṅgha, and in the analytical cessation of nirvāṇa that represents the Dharma. The nonlearner path is the Dharma body of the Buddha, learner and nonlearner Saṅgha are classified in eight, and nirvāṇa is the state of cessation. Objection: Now, spilling the blood of the body of the Buddha [motivated] by an evil mind would not be a heinous act because one cannot spill the blood of the Dharma body. Reply: [It is a heinous act] because it harms the physical basis, or because while it is predominantly the Dharma body that is taken to be the Buddha, it is also sometimes the form body. Question: What is the meaning of taking refuge? Reply: It is verbal indicative form associated with motivation. Motivation is the desire on which that depends. Also, the Autocommentary explains: What is the essence of taking refuge? It is, by nature, verbal indicative form.[1072] The Subcommentary notes: It is from the perspective of the time when refuge is taken.[1073] Question: What does it protect from? Reply: It protects from all suffering. The Autocommentary affirms: One is definitely completely freed from all suffering in dependence on that.[1074] [328]

de'i phyir 'jig rten pa'i skyabs su 'gro ba las yul dang kun slong dang byed pas khyad par du 'phags te/ lung phran tshegs las/ 'jigs pas skrag pa'i mi rnams ni/ / phal cher ri dang nags tshal dang*/ / kun dga' dang ni mchod gnas kyi/ / ljon shing rnams la skyabs 'gro ste/ / skyabs de gtso bo ma yin zhing*/ / skyabs de mchog gyur ma yin la/ / skyabs de la ni brten nas kyang*/ / sdug bsngal kun las mi bgrol gyi/ / gang tshe gang zhig sangs rgyas dang*/ / chos dang dge 'dun skyabs song la/ / sdug bsngal sdug bsngal kun 'byung dang*/ / sdug bsngal yang dag 'das pa dang*/ / 'phags lam yan lag brgyad bde ba/ / mya ngan 'das par 'gro 'gyur dang*/ / 'phags pa'i bden pa bzhi po dag / shes rab kyis ni lta byed pa/ / skyabs de gtso bo yin pa ste/ / skyabs de mchog tu gyur pa yin/ / skyabs de la ni brten nas kyang*/ / sdug bsngal kun las grol bar 'gyur zhes gsungs so/ / yang ci'i phyir sdom pa gzhan dag la mi tshangs spyad spong ba yan lag tu bzhag la dge bsnyen la 'dod log spong ba yan lag tu 'jog pa'i rgyu gang zhe na/

Therefore it is superior in object, motivation, and function to mundane refuge because the Kṣudraka Collection declares: Humans, out of fear and terror, mainly seek refuge in mountains, forests, groves, and shrine trees, but such refuge is not supreme. For one is not liberated from all suffering, even though one depends on its shelter. Taking refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha has profound meaning. One proceeds to liberation from suffering and the origin of suffering, to the transcendance of suffering and the bliss of the eight branches of the ārya path. The four ārya truths are seen by wisdom. But the main practice is refuge, and that refuge is supreme. Through depending on that refuge, one is liberated from suffering.[1075] Question: Why is abandoning impure conduct posited for other vows, but abandoning sexual misconduct posited for laypeople?
log g.yem shin tu smad phyir dang / / sla phyir mi byed thob phyir ro/ / sdom pa ji ltar khas blangs bzhin/ / 'thob kyi rgyud las ma yin no/ / 33

Because sexual misbehavior is widely censured, easily abandoned, āryas obtain vows for not practicing it. Vows are obtained in just the way they are taken; they are not taken for another being. (4:33)

'dod pas log par g.yem pa ni gzhan gyi chung ma sun 'byin pa'i phyir dang*/ {gcig tu } ngan song gi rgyu yin pas 'jig rten na shin tu smad pa'i phyir dang*/ khyim pa rnams kyis spang sla ba'i phyir dang*/ 'phags pa rnams kyis tshe brjes nas kyang 'dod log mi byed pa'i sdom pa thob pa'i phyir de dge bsnyen gyi sdom pa la spong bar bshad la/ {khyim pas spang dka' zhing 'byung nye bas } mi tshangs spyod ni de lta ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / dge tshul la sogs pa ni spang dka' ba de spong bar bshad pa ni rim gyis bslab pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te dge bsnyen rang gi chung ma ma yin pa la 'dod log spong na dge bsnyen sngar chung ma med pa dag phyis len pa'am chung ma snga ma shi nas gsar pa len pa na sdom pa nyams par 'gyur te/ sdom pa len pa'i dus na de dag la'ang 'dod log mi spyod par dam bcas pa'i phyir ro zhe na/

Reply: Sexual misbehavior (mithyācāra) with another’s wife out of desire is condemned and explained to be an action to be abandoned in the vows of laypeople because, as a cause of {exclusively} lower rebirth, it is widely censured in the world; householders easily abandon it; and because āryas obtain vows that endure even after rebirth for not practicing sexual misconduct. Noncelibacy is not like that, {since householders have difficulty in abandoning [noncelibacy], and it happens commonly}. For novices and so on, the advice that one should abandon that which is difficult to abandon is part of the gradual training. Objection: If a layperson engages in sexual misconduct with a woman who is not his wife, then when that layperson, if he was previously unmarried, later takes a wife, or when he takes a new wife after his former wife has died, the [lay] vow would degenerate, because when taking lay vows he pledged not to practice sexual misconduct.

dge bsnyen gyi sdom pa ni len pa'i dus su 'dod log mi spyod do zhes ji ltar khas blangs pa bzhin du 'thob kyi rgyud 'di la 'dod pa mi spyod do zhes rgyud las ni khas len pa dang 'thob pa ma yin no/ / de'i phyir bud med de dag dge bsnyen gyi chung mar ma byas pa'i tshe de dag la 'dod log tu 'gyur gyi chung mar byas pa na ni ma yin te/ rang gi chung ma la spyad pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / yang ci'i phyir rdzun dang phra ma dang tshig rtsub dang kyal pa dag ngag gi las mi dge bar khyad par med pa la rdzun spong ba kho na sdom pa'i yan lag tu 'gyur zhe na/

Reply: Lay vows are obtained in just the way they are taken, by stating, “I will not practice sexual misconduct” when taking them. They are not taken and obtained for another being, by stating, “I will not entertain desire for this being.” Therefore, when a female is not regarded as the wife of a layperson, it is sexual misconduct, but not if she is regarded as his wife because she is treated as his wife. Question: Since lies, slander, harsh words, and gossip are all alike in being nonvirtuous verbal karma, why is only abandoning lying a branch of lay vows?
bslab pa thams cad 'das gyur na/ / rdzun du thal bar 'gyur ba'i phyir/ / bcas pa'i kha na ma tho ba/ / myos 'gyur las gzhan bsrung phyir ro/ / 34
Because if one transgresses any training rule, one may lie as a consequence. Because intoxicants are proscribed offenses, one guards other training rules. (4:34)

srog gcod pa spong ba la sogs pa bslab pa thams cad las 'das par gyur na khyod la ltung ba 'di dag byung ngo zhes brjod pa na rdzun spong ba ma bshad na ma byung zhes rdzun du smra bar thal bar 'gyur ba'i phyir rdzun du smra ba spong ba bshad do/ / phra ma la sogs pa spang bar bya ba yin yang de lta bu'i dgos pa med pa'i phyir ma bshad do/ / de bzhin du rdzun smra shin tu smad phyir dang*/ / slar phyir mi byed thob phyir ro zhes bya ba yang shes par bya'o/ { mdo las kyang*/ chos gcig las ni 'das gyur cing*/ / 'jig rten pha rol dor ba yis/ / lus can rdzun du smra ba yis/ / 'di na sdig pa mi bya med ces so/ /}

Reply: Abandoning lies is emphasized because if one transgresses any training rule (śikṣā), such as abandoning taking life and so on, and someone says, “You have incurred this downfall,” if abandoning lying has not been explained, one may lie by saying “I did not do it” as a consequence. Though slander and so on are also actions to be abandoned, they are not stated [329] because there is no similar need. Moreover, this should be understood to apply to lying because speaking lies is greatly condemned, it is easy to do, and a lie may transpire through inaction. {A sūtra also states: Embodied beings who engage in lying, who set aside the one true Dharma and destroy the life beyond — there is no sin they would not commit.[1076]}
'di ni dge tshul la sogs pa la'ang shes par bya'o/ / yang ci'i phyir bcas pa'i kha na ma tho ba dag las chang spong ba kho na de'i yan lag tu brjod ce na/
This should be understood for novices and so on. Question: Why is abandoning alcohol alone declared to be a section of lay vows from among the proscribed offenses?

sangs rgyas kyis bkag cing bcas pa'i kha na ma tho ba myos par 'gyur ba spong ba ni de spangs pas de las gzhan srog gcod spong ba la sogs pa'i bslab pa srung ba'i phyir ro/ / myos par 'gyur ba ma spangs na ni{ des dran shes bzhin nyams nas} bslab pa gzhan de dag nyams par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / 'dir bye brag tu smra pa'i 'dul ba 'dzin pa rnams ni chang 'thung ba ni rang bzhin gyi kha na ma tho ba yin te/ ston pas shAkya nad pa rnams la bcas pa'i kha na ma tho ba {gzhan mtha' dag } gnang chang rtswa'i rtse mos kyang 'thung ba ma gnang ba'i phyir dang*/ gzhan yang chang 'thung ba ni rang bzhin gyi kha na ma tho ba yin te/ 'phags pa rnams tshe 'phos kyang mi spyod pa'i phyir/ srog gcod pa la sogs pa bzhin no/ / de bzhin du chang 'thung ba ni rang bzhin gyi kha na ma tho ba yin te/ 'dul ba mu tig gi lus ngag gi nyes par spyod pa'i tshom dang*/ dga' byed kyi mdo las/ lus kyi nyes spyod du gsungs pa'i phyir srog gcod la sogs pa bzhin no/ / de la dang po ni lung phran tshegs las nye bar 'khor gyis bcom ldan 'das la btsun pa bdag gis nad pa rnams kyi ji ltar bro g.yog bgyi zhes zhus pa na/ nye bar 'khor rang bzhin gyi kha na ma tho ba ma gtogs pa rnams kyis nad pa rnams gso bar bya'o zhes bka' stsal nas/ gzhan du shAkya nad pa rnams la'ang chang 'thung ba bkag pa'i phyir dang*/ 'dul ba tshig le'ur byas pa las kyang*/ kha yi nad la 'khur phug tu/ / srel pa tsam la nyes pa med/ / sman pa'i ngag gis 'thungs par ni/ / srog la bab kyang 'dod mi bya zhes bshad pa'i phyir dang*/ gzhan yang lung rnam 'byed las/ dge slong dag nga ston pa yin par smra ba rnams kyis myos par 'gyur ba rtswa'i rtse mos kyang btung bar mi bya'o zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ /

Reply: It is because one abandons intoxicants [whose consumption] is a proscribed offense (pratikṣepaṇāvadya) prohibited by the Buddha, and through abandoning that one guards other training rules such as abandoning taking life and so on. If one does not abandon intoxicants, other types of training will degenerate {through mindfulness and introspection degenerating.} Here, Vaibhāṣika holders of Vinaya say: (1) Drinking alcohol is a natural offense because the Master gave permission for sick Śākyas to commit {all other} proscribed offenses but did not give them permission to drink a drop of alcohol. (2) Again, drinking alcohol is a natural offense because āryas do not utilize alcohol even when reborn [in a new life], just as they do not kill and so on. (3) So too, drinking alcohol is a natural offense because it intensifies the faults of body and speech, and the section on negative physical and verbal action of the Pearl of Vinaya and the Pramodayāti Sūtra state that because it is said to be a negative physical action, it is like taking life and so on.[1077] The first is established because the Kṣudraka Collection states: Upāli said to the Bhagavan: “How should the venerables nurse the sick?” The Bhagavan said: “Upāli, heal the sick by any means except by what is naturally offensive.”[1078] In other sources Śākyas who are ill are prevented from drinking alcohol. The Vinaya Verses advises: There is no fault in simply treating oral disease with care. But even at the risk of one’s life, do not accept the advice of a doctor to drink alcohol.[1079] Again, Vinaya Divisions states: Monks, those who call me Master do not drink even a drop of any intoxicant.[1080]

mngon pa ba rnams na re{ chang 'thung pa ni rang bzhin gyi kha na ma tho ba ma yin te/ de'i mtshan nyid dang ma ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / bcas pa'i kha na ma tho ba yin te/ de'i mtshan nyid dang ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / de la de dag gi mtshan nyid ni rim pa ltar sems nyon mongs can kho nas spyod cing*/ gang zag bslab pa bcas ma bcas thams cad la sdig tu 'gyur ba srog gcod pa lta bu dang*/ res 'ga' gnyen po'i blos kyang spyad du rung zhing bslab pa bcas pa kho na la sdig tu 'gyur ba sa rko ba lta bu yin pa ni/ chang 'thung ba na bslab pa ma bcas pa'i nad pa lta bu 'ga' zhig gis myos par mi 'gyur bar gnyen po'i blos kyang btung bar nus pa'i phyir ro} rang bzhin gyi kha na ma tho ba ni bcom ldan 'das kyis ma bkag kyang sdig par 'gyur ba yin na chang ni res 'ga' gnyen po'i blos kyang btung bar nus pa'i phyir de bcas pa'i kha na ma tho ba yin te bcas pa zhes bya ba ni bcom ldan 'das kyis bkag pa'o/ / des na khrims su byas pas bkag pa spyad na sdig tu 'gyur ba de ni bcas pa'i kha na ma tho ba ste bcom ldan 'das dang bstan pa la ma gus pa'i sgo nas sdig par 'gyur ba'o/ /

Ābhidharmikas say: {Drinking alcohol is not a natural offense because it does not possess those characteristics, but it is a proscribed offense because it possesses those characteristics. Their characteristics are, respectively, “that which is performed by those possessing afflicted minds alone, by which anyone becomes an immoral being whether engaged in [ethical] training or not” such as taking life, and “that which can be performed even by those possessing a conscientious mind, which makes just those engaged in [ethical] training immoral” such as digging the earth. When drinking alcohol, some beings, such as those who are ill and not engaged in [ethical] training, can consume alcohol without becoming intoxicated and maintain a conscientious mind.} The Bhagavan did not prohibit it [330] as a natural offense, but it is a proscribed offense because alcohol tends to make a person immoral, though at times it may be drunk with a conscientious mind. “Proscribed” means it is prohibited by the Bhagavan. Thus, that which is prohibited by ethical rule, and thus immoral when practiced, is a proscribed offense. It is immoral due to disrespecting the Bhagavan and his instruction.

rang bzhin gyi kha na ma tho ba ni bcom ldan 'das kyi khrims kyis ma bkag kyang sdig tu 'gyur ba ste srog gcod pa la sogs pa lta bu'o/ / lung las nad pa la bcas pa'i kha na ma tho ba gnang ba na spyir btang ba yin la/ shAkya nad pa la ma gnang ba ni dmigs kyis bsal ba'o/ / rtsa'i rtse mo'i tshad kyis kyang 'thung ba bkag pa ni de'i nus pa ma nges pa'i phyir te/ la la ni nyung ngus kyang myos par 'gyur la/ la la ni mang pos kyang mi myos pa'i phyir dang*/ chags pa 'phel bas tshod mi zin pa'i phyir te/ mdo las kyang*/ gnas gsum po chang dang*/ mi tshangs par spyod pa dang*/ rmugs pa dang gnyid la brten pa ni ngoms pa'am chog pa'am tshim pa med do/ / zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du 'phags pa rnams tshe brjes nas kyang mi gsol ba ni mdo las dad pa dang brtson 'grus dang ngo tsha shes pa dang*/ khrel yod pa dang*/ shes rab kyi stobs zhes bya ba bslab pa'i stobs lnga gsungs pas ngo tsha khrel yod dang ldan pa'i phyir dang*/ dga' byed la sogs pa'i mdo las/ lus kyi nyes spyod du gsungs pa ni bag med pa'i gnas yin pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ /

Natural offenses are immoral, such as taking life and so on, but not through being prohibited by the ethical rules of the Bhagavan. In the scripture, permission to engage in proscribed offenses is the general case, while not giving permission to sick Śākyas is an exception. Drinking even a drop of alcohol is prohibited because the potency of alcohol cannot [easily] be determined. Some are intoxicated through taking a little, some are not intoxicated though they drink a lot. And since alcohol increases the desire for more, no fixed measure can be prescribed. A sūtra declares: There is no satisfaction, contentment, or joy when one relies on three things: alcohol, impure conduct [noncelibacy], and lethargy-sleep.[1081] Similarly, āryas who take rebirth possess shame and embarrassment without [a rite of] request, since the sūtras state that they possess the five powers: the powers of faith, effort, shame, embarrassment, and wisdom. The Pramodayāti Sūtra states: That called negative physical action is the domain of negligence.[1082]
da ni de dag thob pa'i gzhi la sogs pa ston pa ni
THE BEINGS THAT OBTAIN THOSE VOWS AND SO ON
'dod gtogs thams cad gnyis ka dang / / da ltar dag las 'thob par 'gyur/ / bsam gtan zag med sdom pa ni/ / dngos dang dus ni thams cad las/ / 35

Those belonging to the desire realm are obtained relative to all paths, both bases, and present states. Absorption and uncontaminated vows are obtained relative to the actual basis and all three times. (4:35)

'dod par gtogs pa'i sdom pa so so thar pa ni{ dge ba'i} las kyi lam gyi sbyor ba dang dngos dang mjug thams cad las dang*/ gzhi sems can du ston pa dang mi ston pa gnyis ka dang rang bzhin dang bcas pa'i kha na ma tho ba gnyis ka las dang*/ {'di sems can gyi rten la 'jug pas } dus da ltar ba'i phung po dang khams dang skye mched dag las 'thob par 'gyur gyi 'das ma 'ongs las ni ma yin te/ de dag sems can du mi bgrang ba'i phyir ro/{ des ni sems can du ston pa ma yin pa yang da ltar kho na las thob par ston no/ /}

Pratimokṣa vows belonging to the desire realm are obtained relative to all preparatory, actual, and concluding paths of {virtuous} karma; relative to both bases — those taught to be sentient beings and those not; relative to both natural and proscribed offenses; and relative to present aggregates, elements, and bases {since they act as the basis of sentient beings}. [Pratimokṣa vows] are not obtained relative to past and future [aggregates and so on] because these are not counted as sentient beings. {Though [aggregates] are not taught to be sentient beings, vows are obtained relative to them in the present.}

bsam gtan dang zag med kyi sdom pa ni las kyi lam dngos gzhi kho na las dang*/ {'di dag la mnyam par bzhag pa na las kyi lam dngos gzhi 'og sa spangs pa'i ngo bor skye bas sbyor mjug ni phal cher 'og sa'i ngo bor gtogs pa'i phyir ro/ / des na las kyi sbyor mjug las kyang ma yin na bcas pa'i kha na ma tho ba las lta ci smros te khas blangs pa med pa'i phyir zhes pa'am/ yang na 'di gnyis ni nyon mongs dang des bslab pa'i las spong ba yin pa las bcas pa'i kha na ma tho ba ni nyon mongs kyis blang bar ma nges pas so zhes 'chad do } dus ni gsum{ ste sems rjes 'brang} po thams cad{ kyi phung khams} las 'thob pas so/ / de'i phyir sbyor mjug dang bcas pa'i kha na ma tho ba dang sems can ma yin pa las mi 'thob bo zhes shes par bya'o/ /

Absorption and uncontaminated vows are obtained relative to the actual basis of the karmic path alone. {When in equipoise, the actual basis of the karmic path arises with a nature that abandons lower levels, while in general its preparation and conclusion by nature belong to lower levels. Therefore it is said that if absorption vows are not obtained relative to preparatory and concluding karma, they must be obtained relative to abandoning proscribed offenses because there is no formal acceptance of vows. Again, they are obtained relative to abandoning afflictions and the karma of committing them, but it is not certain that proscribed offenses arise due to the afflictions.} They are obtained relative to {the form aggregate of} all three times {that complements the mind}. Therefore it should be understood that such vows are not obtained relative to preparatory or concluding karma, [331] proscribed offenses, or that which is not a sentient being.
yang {sdom pa dang sdom min ni sems can thams cad dang yan lag thams cad rgyu thams cad las 'thob pa'am/ 'on te bye brag 'ga' zhig las 'thob ce na }
{Question: Are vows and negative commitments obtained relative to all sentient beings, all branches, and all causes, or are they obtained relative to some specific states?}
sdom pa sems can thams cad las/ / yan lag rgyu la dbye ba yod/ / sdom pa min pa thams cad dang / / yan lag kun las rgyus min no/ / 36

Vows are obtained relative to all sentient beings. They are differentiated in terms of branches and causes. Negative commitments are obtained relative to all beings and all branches but not by all causes. (4:36)

sdom pa{ gsum po} ni sems can thams cad las 'thob la/ yan lag dang rgyu la ni dbye ba yod de/{ las kyi lam dang*/} yan lag thams cad las 'thob pa ni dge slong gi sdom{ de las lam thams cad spong ba} pa'o/ yan lag lnga las 'thob pa ni dge bsnyen no/ / brgyad las 'thob pa ni bsnyen gnas so/ / bcu las 'thob pa ni dge tshul lo/ / yang na las kyi lam bcu po thams cad las 'thob pa ni dge slong ngo*/ / srog gcod pa la sogs pa gsum dang rdzun du smra ba dang bzhi las 'thob pa ni dge tshul la sogs pa yin par 'grel pa las bshad do/ / rgyu ni ma chags pa la sogs pa dge rtsa gsum yin na thams cad las dang*/ sems chung ngu dang 'bring dang chen pos yin na dus gcig la gsum car mi 'byung bas re re las 'thob pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: The {three} vows are obtained relative to all sentient beings (sarvasattva). They are differentiated in terms of branches (aṅga) and causes (kāraṇa) because full-ordination vows {that abandon all karmic paths} are obtained relative to {the karmic path and} all branches. Lay vows are obtained relative to five branches. Again, full-ordination vows are obtained relative to all ten karmic paths. Novice vows and so on are obtained relative to the three physical actions, such as taking life and so forth, and the four verbal actions, such as lying and so on. This is explained in the Autocommentary. If the cause is the three roots of virtue — nonattachment and so on — novice vows are obtained relative to all [minds]. If obtained by a small, medium, or great mind, they [novice vows] are obtained relative to each, since three minds do not arise simultaneously.

sdom pa min pa ni sems can thams cad las 'thob pa dang*/ yan lag kyang srog gcod la sogs pa las kyi lam kun las 'thob {ste ma tshang ba'i sdom pani med ces 'dod do } la/ rgyu ni chags sdang gnyis mtshungs par mi ldan pas 'dod chags kyis rgyu byas na zhe sdang gis ma yin pa la sogs pa'i phyir dang*/ chung ngus byas na chen pos ma yin pa'i phyir {chung ngu la sogs pa cig car mi 'byung bas } thams cad kyis 'thob pa min no zhes bye brag tu smra ba 'dod do/ / de la sdom min can ni 'grel pa las/ shan pa dang*/ bya gag gsod pa dang*/ phag gsod pa dang*/ bya ba dang*/ nya ba dang*/ ri dwags 'chor ba dang*/ choms rkun pa dang*/ gshed ma dang*/ btson rdzi dang*/ glang po che 'chor ba dang*/ khyi 'chor ba dang*/ pa gu ri 'chor ba rnams so zhes dngos su bcu gnyis bshad do/ / 'grel pa las/ rgyal po dang blon po dang shags zin po rnams kyang don gyis na sdom pa ma yin pa can yin no zhes 'byung ba la/ TIka byed dag rgyal po dang blon po rnams kyang chad pas gcod par byed pa'i phyir mdo la sogs pa las dngos su mi 'byung yang sdom min can kho nar lta'o zhes 'chad do/ / kun las btus las ni 'dir bshad pa'i dang po bcu dang*/ bong rgyas 'chor ba dang*/ sbrul bzung nas rtse bas 'tsho ba dang*/ sbrul kyis 'tsho ba dang*/ gzhan la phra ma byas nas 'tsho ba'i nyan rna byed pa dang*/ gnod pa byed pa dang bzhi ste sdom min can bcu bzhi bshad la/ slob dpon a b+h+yas ni de dag dang rgyal po'i chad pa pa dang yul chos pa rnams kyang sdom min can du bshad do/ /

Negative commitments are obtained relative to all sentient beings, and they are obtained relative to all karmic paths, such as the branches on not taking life and so on, {since Vaibhāṣikas assert that vows that are incomplete do not exist.} They are not obtained by all causes because if attachment acts as a cause, then aversion does not and so on, since attachment and aversion are not concomitant. Or, if they are produced by a weak mind, they are not produced by a strong mind, {since weak or strong minds and so on do not occur simultaneously}. This is asserted by the Vaibhāṣikas. The Autocommentary explicitly mentions that there are twelve who possess negative commitments: Butchers of sheep, chicken, and pigs, bird hunters, fishermen, hunters of wild game, thieves, executioners, jailors, and hunters of elephants, dogs, and deer.[1083] Also the Autocommentary explains: Kings, ministers, and judges naturally possess negative commitments.[1084] The Subcommentary expands: Because kings and ministers inflict punishment, they are viewed as possessing negative commitments, even though this is not explicitly mentioned in the sūtras and so on.[1085] The Compendium of Abhidharma observes that the first ten explained here plus the four: (11) hunters of donkeys, (12) snake charmers, (13) those who live by deception, and (14) spies who slander and harm others, constitute the fourteen who possess negative commitments.[1086] Master Abhaya also explains that such beings, as well as those who impose the king’s punishment and those who oversee local laws, possess negative commitments.[1087]

drin lan bsab pa las ni dar gyi srin bu gso ba'ang sdom min can du gsungs so/ / mdo sde pa la sogs pa ni de lta ma yin te/ sems can thams cad gsod par 'dod pa dang sgo thams cad dang las kyi lam thams cad spyod pa ni mi srid pa'i phyir te/ shan pa la sogs pa'ang rang gi pha ma la sogs pa gsod par mi 'dod pa'i phyir dang*/ srog gcod kyang ma byin par mi len{ pa'ang yod} pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te pha la sogs pa'ang lug la sogs par gyur pa na gsod par 'dod pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ 'o na ni lug kyang pha mar gyur pa gsod par mi 'dod pa'i phyir lug la'ang gsod par 'dod pa med par 'gyur ro/ / pha mar gyur pa na lug ma yin no zhes bya ba'ang mtshungs te/ lug tu gyur pa na pha ma ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yang lug tu gyur pa thams cad bdag gis bsad do snyam du sems shing gsod pa'ang mi srid pa'i phyir sdom min ni sems can thams cad las kyang ma yin la yan lag thams cad las kyang ma yin no/ / 'on kyang bdag gis srog gcod pa tsam dang ma byin par blangs pa tsam gyis 'tsho bar bya'o/ / gzhan gyi bud med la rgyun du spyad do snyam du bsams te de dag gis las rdzogs par spyad pa tsam gyis sdom min du 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du rdzun la sogs pa la'ang shes par bya'o zhes bya bar 'dod de de nyid rigs pa yin no/ /

The Repaying the Buddha’s Kindness Sūtra says also that breeders of silkworms have negative commitments.[1088] Sautrāntikas and so on assert that they are not [obtained relative to all] because it is impossible to desire to kill all sentient beings, and to practice this by means of all doors [332] and all karmic paths, because butchers and so forth do not desire to kill their parents and so on, and though they take life they do not steal. Question: What if they desire to kill sheep and so on who were their parents and so forth? Reply: Because they don’t desire to kill sheep who have been their parents, they have no desire to kill such sheep. Also, it is similar to stating, “If they become my parents, they are not sheep” because if they become sheep, they are not one’s parents. Again, because killing would be impossible if one had the thought, “I will kill all who have become sheep,” negative commitments are not obtained relative to all sentient beings, nor relative to all branches. However, through thinking, “I will make a living just through killing and stealing” or “I will repeatedly exploit this woman who belongs to another,” negative commitments arise merely through the act that completes that karma. So too, it is logical that they arise through the wish, “May my lies and so on be accepted [as true].”

sdom pa la ni sems can thams cad dang*/ rang rang gi yan lag thams cad dang*/ yul thams cad dang*/ dus thams cad dang*/ tshe'am gnas skabs thams cad du spong ba ma yin {par lhas byin lta bu'i sems can nges pa dang*/ srog gcod pa lta bu'i yan lag nges pa dang*/ bod lta bu'i yul nges pa dang*/ zla ba gcig gi bar du zhes pa lta bu'i dus nges pa dang*/ 'thab mo'i tshe ma gtogs so zhes pa lta bu'i tshe nges pa lnga dang bral ba ma yin } na legs spyad tsam du 'gyur gyi sdom par mi 'gyur bas na nges pa lnga dang bral ba nyid nges par dgos so/ / rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las ni/ rgyu drug gis dge slong gi sdom pa len par mi 'dod cing 'dod kyang mi 'thob ste/ rgyal po dang chom rkun dang bu lon pa dang 'tsho ba med pas 'jigs te 'tsho ba tsam la sogs pa'i bsam pas/ rab tu 'byung bar 'dod pa'i bsam pa nyams pa dang*/ lus la 'bras dang phol mig la sogs pa nad sna tshogs dang ldan pas bla ma la sogs pa la bsnyen bkur dang sbyin bdag gi yon sbyar bar mi nus pa'i lus nyams pa dang*/ za ma dang ma ning dang mtshan gnyis par gyur pa skyes pa nyid nyams pa dang*/ mtshams med byed pa dang dge slong ma sun 'byed pa dang mu stegs can dang rku thabs su gnas pa dang tha dad du gnas pa dang gnas par mi bya ba rnams ni ngo tsha khrel med chen pos ngo tsha khrel yod chung ngur byas pa dge ba'i chos nyams pa dang*/ rgyal pos bkrabs pa dang rgyal po la gnod pa byas pa dang rgyal po dang mi mthun pa'i las byed pa dang bu lon can dang bran dang phrogs pa dang pha mas ma gnang ba la sogs pa gzhan gyi dbang du gyur pa dang*/ mi'i 'gro ba ma yin pa klu la sogs pa'i sprul par gyur pa rab tu byung na gzhan ma dad par 'gyur bas gzhan rjes su srung ba ste drug po de dag dang*/ mkhan slob dang dge 'dun ma tshang ba ste bdun ni bsnyen par rdzogs par mi bya'o zhes bshad do/ / kha cig gzhan gyi dbang du gyur pa la sogs pa gsum yang nyams pa yin pas nyams pa bdun nges pa lngas mi 'thob ces bya bar 'gyur ro zhes 'chad do/

If the vow does not abandon [actions to be abandoned] relative to all sentient beings, all individual sections, all places, all times, and all occasions or contexts, then it is merely a positive action. Since it does not become a vow, it definitely lacks the five certainties. {[These are:] (1) certainty of person, such as Devadatta, (2) certainty of branch, such as taking life, (3) certainty of place, such as Tibet, (4) certainty of time, such as up to one month, [and] (5) certainty of period, such as when not in dispute.} The Compendium of Ascertainment declares: It is through six causes that beings do not desire to take full-ordination vows or, though desiring to take vows, do not obtain them, because (1) their desire for ordination declines, since they only think of their livelihood, such as kings, thieves, debtors, those who fear having no livelihood, and so on. (2) Their body is defective: they are incapable of paying respect to gurus or receiving the offerings of donors since their body is diseased with lesions or ulcers and so on. (3) The person is defective through being a eunuch, neuter, or hermaphrodite. (4) Their virtuous Dharma is defective through their strong practice of shamelessness and nonembarrassment or their practice of shame and embarrassment is weak due to committing heinous acts, criticizing fully ordained nuns, abiding with non-Buddhists and thieves, and abiding separately from and not among Buddhists. (5) They are controlled by others, such as those appointed by the king, those who harm the king, those acting against the king, debtors, slaves, brigands, and those who do not have the permission of one’s parents and so on. (6) They are not human reincarnating beings but, like nāgas and so forth, take ordination through emanating [as humans]. These six are stated in order to protect others from losing faith. If any of these six [333] plus the seventh, [namely,] that the abbot, master, and Saṅgha are incomplete, then do not give full ordination.[1089] Some say: Since the three causes from 5 to 7, [namely,] being controlled by others and so on, are also defective states, seven defective states exist. However, it is said that vows are not obtained through possessing five.[1090]

{Question: How do those incapable of harm obtain vows? Reply: Vows are taken with the thought not to harm the life of any sentient being. Vaibhāṣikas say that if only those capable [of harm] could obtain vows, then vows would increase or decrease, since humans and gods and so on who are capable [of harm] can become incapable [of harm] and vice versa, and that would occur even without any cause for the obtainment or relinquishment of vows. Vasubandhu says: Vows do not increase or decrease like grass and so on that grows or dies; neither do they transfer. Objection: The analogy is not apt, since sentient beings exist before and after death, but grass and so on do not. Reply: But since they do not possess nirvāṇa, they are similar. Therefore the former proof is sound.}

Negative commitments are obtained by action or accepting. Nonindicative states other than those are obtained relative to the field, to accepting, and to acting respectfully. (4:37)

Negative commitments (asaṃvara) are obtained by beings born into the caste of a butcher, by beings who merely engage in the action of taking life and so on, and by beings of other castes by accepting that “I will live by this livelihood” in front of a king and so on.

THE MEANS OF OBTAINING INTERIM PRECEPTS

sdom pa sdom min gyi lhag ma bar ma'i rnam par rig byed min pa'i dge ba ni rdzas las byung ba dang rdzas las byung ba ma yin pa'i rig byed ma yin pa lta bu zhing dang*/ zas ma zos kyi gong du dkon mchog gsum la phyag 'tshal bar dam bcas nas de ltar byed pa lta bu yi dam nar mar khas len zhing dam bcas pa dang*/ rab tu dang ba dang nyon mongs pa drag pos phyag dang skor ba byed pa lta bu/ dge ba dang brdeg pa sogs/ mi dge ba byed pa lta bu bsam sbyor gus par byed pa las 'thob bo/{ bar ma mi dge ba ni srog gcod pa'i khang ba byas nas ster ba lta bu zhing*/ nyin re la srog chags 'tshe ba lta bu len pa dang*/ nyon mongs drag pos rdeg pa la sogs pa ma gus par byed pa las 'thob pa'o/ /}

Virtuous nonindicative interim precepts — that are other than vows and negative commitments — are obtained relative to the field, such as nonindicative form that is derived or not derived from substance; relative to accepting and pledging to always hold to oaths such as the pledge to prostrate to the Three Jewels prior to taking food; and relative to acting respectfully in thought and preparation, such as acting virtuously due to strong, clear faith by prostrating or circumambulating, or acting nonvirtuously by striking and so on due to intense emotional affliction. {Nonvirtuous interim precepts are obtained from instances such as constructing and donating slaughterhouses, accepting to act with cruelty to living beings during the day [but not at night], or showing disdain by striking others, for instance, out of intense emotional affliction.}

CAUSE OF RELINQUISHING VOWS

Pratimokṣa discipline is relinquished by offering back the training, by death, by both organs developing, by the root being severed, and by the night ending. (4:38)

'dis dbang po 'dul bar byed pas na so so thar pa'i 'dul ba ste ris brgyad las bsnyen gnas ma gtogs pa'i sdom pa rnams ni{ dang po ji srid 'tsho bar du} yang dag par blangs pa dang{ phyis} 'gal ba'i rig byed bskyed pa'i phyir mi brda phrad pa'i drung du bsam pa thag pa nas bslab pa phul ba dang*/{ gang gis sdom pa blangs pa'i} rten bor ba dang 'phen pa'i dus zad pa'i phyir shi 'phos pa dang*/ {pho mo gang rung gi } rten nyams pa'i phyir pho mo'i mtshan gnyis po dag ni dus cig car byung ba dang*/ {sa chad na de la brten pa'i shing chad pa ltar } gzhi skyes thob chad na sbyor byung yang ldog pas dge ba'i rtsa ba chad pa dang bzhis gtong la/ bsnyen gnas ni de dag dang mtshan mo 'das pa las kyang gtong ste/ mda'i shugs zad pa ltar 'phan pa'i dus zad pa'i phyir ro/ / rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las ni/ dge bsnyen dang bsnyen gnas ni mi mthun pa'i sems skyes pa tsam gyis kyang gtong bar bshad do/ /

Except for the one-day vows from among the eight types, the vows of pratimokṣa discipline that tame the faculties are correctly taken {first for as long as one lives} and then {later} they may be relinquished by any of four methods: (1) by offering back the training (śikṣānikṣepaṇa) according to one’s wish, in front of a human capable of understanding language, through generating contradictory indicative form; (2) by death (cyuta), because the basis {of training in the vows} is discarded when projecting karma is exhausted; (3) by both organs of male and female developing simultaneously, because the basis {of either male or female} degenerates; and (4) by the root of virtue being severed, since if that which arises and is obtained from the basis is severed, then that derived from preparation is also stopped, {just as, if the land is destroyed, the trees reliant on the land are destroyed}. [334] Also, one-day vow-holders relinquish vows by the night ending, since the time of projecting those vows is exhausted, like the force of an arrow being spent. The Compendium of Ascertainment notes: Laypeople and one-day vow-holders relinquish vows by merely generating a counter thought.[1091]
kha cig ltung bar 'gyur las smra/ / gzhan dag dam chos nub pa las/ / kha che rnams ni byung ba la/ / bu lon nor bzhin gnyis su 'dod/ / 39

Some assert that they are relinquished through a downfall. Others assert that it is through the pure Dharma subsiding. Kāśmīris assert that one who commits a root downfall has both, like having debt and wealth. (4:39)
