Some Sautrāntikas, Aparāntika Vaibhāṣikas, and so on assert that all vows are relinquished through committing any one of the four root downfalls (patanīya): (1) killing a human or a human embryo, (2) stealing wealth of others of sufficient value, (3) engaging in sexual misconduct, and (4) lying about attaining superhuman states. Other schools, such as the Tāmraśāṭīya, assert that if the pure Dharma subsides, then vows are relinquished through the pure Dharma subsiding (antardhi), since all demarcation of training and karmic limits would have disappeared. Master Vasubandhu asserts that since taking vows would not exist after the pure Dharma has subsided, there would be no new arising of vows. He does not assert that previously existent vows would be relinquished. The Compendium of Ascertainment mentions: If the pure Dharma subsides, there would be no new taking of full-ordination vows not taken before. It should be recognized that those previously taken would not be relinquished.[1092] The Autocommentary also notes: {Because} if the pure Dharma subsides there would be no rites of discipline, no obtainment of discipline {not previously existent}, and no relinquishment of vows already obtained.[1093] Some say: Thus because those possessing full-ordination vows do exist and the pure Dharma therefore has not subsided, the first two[1094] are viable.

gzhi thams cad yod par smra ba'i bye brag kha che bye brag tu smra ba rnams ni rtsa ba'i ltung ba gang rung zhig byung ba la sdom pa yod pa'i cha nas tshul khrims dang ldan pa dang gang btang ba'i cha nas tshul khrims 'chal pa gnyis su 'dod de dper na bu lon dang nor gnyis ka yod pa'i skyes bu bzhin no/ / ltung ba de bshags na ni tshul khrims dang ldan pa kho na yin te des bu lon bcal na nor ldan kho nar 'gyur ba bzhin no/ / 'di la'ang srog gcod pa'i rtsa ltung gcig byung na srog gcod spong ba'i sdom pa'i cha thams cad gtong ba dang*/ de'i yang thams cad mi gtong bar gang bsad pa'i sems can de kho na'i cha'i sdom pa gtong bar 'dod pa'i lugs gnyis yod do/ / de dag gang las shes she na/ lung dang rigs pa las te/ lung ni 'dul ba rnam 'byed las/ dge slong tshul khrims 'chal pa zhig dge slong ma la 'doms par byed na ltung byed do zhes bshad de/ tshul khrims med na ltung ba'i rnam gzhag mi 'thad pa'i phyir ro/ /

The Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣika subsect of the Mūlasarvāstivāda assert that one who commits any one of the root downfalls possesses both ethical conduct from the perspective of having vows and unethical conduct from the perspective of breaking vows. For example, it is like a being who has both debt and wealth. If one confesses that root downfall, one possesses ethics alone, just as one who pays back debt possesses wealth alone. Also, regarding this, two systems are asserted: (1) If one commits the root downfall of taking life, one relinquishes every part of the vow abandoning taking life. And (2) all parts are not relinquished but only the parts of the vow relating to that sentient being who was killed. Question: What is the source of these assertions? Reply: It is from [both] scripture and logic because the Vinaya Divisions explains: If a fully ordained monk with unethical conduct gives instruction to a fully ordained nun, it is a downfall.[1095]

And the Six Times Six Sūtra states: Cunda, the son of Kāra, said: “You surpass others, you have abandoned doubt, you are the Sage who is fully awake, the Supreme Guide, the Supreme Leader, the Great Being who came to this world to train others in virtue.” The Master [335] said: “Cunda, there are four who train in virtue, not five, and I have clearly understood them. There is one who conquers through the path, one who teaches the path, one who lives for the path, one who condemns the path.”[1096] Again: Cunda said: “Why is he called one who conquers through the path? In what way does he teach the unrivaled path? Answer my question why he lives for the path. I want to know clearly who condemns the path.” The Bhagavan said: “One who abandons the ache of doubt, who attains nirvāṇa without being led by others, and who teaches mundane beings and the gods is a buddha who is called ‘one who conquers through the path.’ ” One with supreme cognition of that to be practiced and discarded, who teaches and describes phenomena just as they are, the Sage who severs doubt without being guided by others, is one who possesses the second virtuous training and teaches the path. One who abides in the Dharma and perfectly instructs, who possesses mindfulness and lives for the Dharma, and who trains in states free of transgression is one possessesing the third virtuous training who lives for the path. One who ridicules rivals and householders while attired in the robes of an ārya, who is confused, untamed, and possesses guile, discredits proper conduct as a facade.[1097]

TIka byed dag gis lam gyis rgyal ba slob mi slob dang*/ lam ston sangs rgyas dang*/ lam phyir 'tsho ba dge slong gi tshul khrims dang ldan pa lam la slob pa'i ched du 'tsho ba dang*/ lam sun 'byin pa tshul khrims 'chal bar bshad pas de yang dge sbyong gi dbye bar bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / yang rtsa ltung byung bas sdom pa gtang na lung phran tshegs las dga' ba can rtsa ltung byung nas 'chab sems ma skyes pa de chad pa'i las kyi bslab pa byin pas dge slong du mi 'gyur ba las de ltar 'gyur bar bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / yang lung rab tu byung ba'i gzhi las/ bya rog skrod dang sun phyung dang*/ / rku thabs gnas dang ma ning dang zhes dge slong ma sun phyung ba la sogs pa tshul khrims 'chal ba rab tu dbyung du mi rung bar bshad pa'i phyir te/ de ni tshul khrims ngan pa des go bkag nas sdom pa gsar pa mi skye ba yin gyi gal te de la sdom pa med na phyis blangs pas skye bar 'gyur ro/ / de la mi skye na bslab pa phul ba la'ang phyis blang du med par 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'o/ /

[The Subcommentary] explains these classifications of śramaṇas: One who conquers through the path is a learner or nonlearner. One who teaches the path is a buddha. One who lives for the path is one possessing the ethics of full ordination who lives training in the path. One who discredits the path possesses unethical conduct.[1098] Again, regarding the assertion that if one commits a root downfall, the vows are relinquished, the Kṣudraka Collection explains: Nanda committed a root downfall and did not generate the intention to conceal it. Since a training penalty was imposed on him, he again attained the state of full ordination following a state of not being fully ordained.[1099] Again, the Chapter on Going Forth declares: Chasing away crows, disparaging [nuns], living by stealing, and [disparaging] neuters . . .[1100] This explains that the unethical conduct of disparaging nuns and so on is inappropriate for the ordained, since ethical misconduct prevents understanding and the vows are not newly generated. If [unethical beings] had no vows, they would have to arise when taken later. But if [vows] did not arise in them, then even offering back the training could not occur later.
CONTRADICTING LOGIC

rigs pa'ang sdom pa ni spong bdun yin pas na srog gcod spong ba btang bas gzhan btang bar ni mi 'gyur te/{ lung gzhi'i 'grel pa las/ slob dpon dge legs bshes gnyen gyis/ phyogs gcig 'khrugs kyang dge slong gi dngos po lhag ma dang ma bral ba'i phyir te/ phyogs gcig 'khrugs pas ni sdom pa mtha' dag yongs su gtong bar mi rigs so/ / de ltar yang*/ ji ltar phyogs gcig blangs gyur pas/ / mtha' dag blangs par mi bzhed ltar/ / de bzhin phyogs gcig 'khrugs gyur pas/ / mtha' dag 'khrugs par ji ltar 'gyur/ / zhes gsungs pa dang zhes 'byung ba ltar ro/} de dag gi mi mthun phyogs ma byas pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar na srog gcod pa spong ba blangs pas kyang gzhan blangs par thal ba'i phyir ro/ / phyogs gcig btang bas phyogs thams cad gtang ba ni rigs pa ma yin te/ lag pa bcad na rkang pa la sogs pa ril bcad par thal ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir 'di ni dgongs pa yin na zhes zer ro/ /

'di ni 'thad pa ma yin te/ tshul khrims 'chal pa dge slong ma la 'doms na ltung byed du bshad pa ni ngan song du ltung ba tsam la dgongs pa'i phyir dang*/ de dge sbyong du bshad pa ni ston pa nyid kyis {'phags pa'i rtags kyis g.yogs byas nas/ / 'gran cing khyim sun 'byin pa dang*/ / 'chal zhing ma dul sgyu dang bcas } gzugs brnyan bzhin spyod lam sun 'byin zhes gsungs pas ming tsam gyi dge sbyong ste sa bon rul ba dang sems can shi ba dang mtshe'u skam po la sogs pa bzhin no/ / gzhan yang lung las/ gal te sems ni gcig gis kyang*/ / bcabs pa med par 'chags byed na/ / tha ma byung bar gyur na yang*/ / de ni phas pham mi 'gyur ro zhes pa dang*/ 'dul ba tshig le'ur byas pa las kyang*/ mi 'chab pa yi sems kyis ni/ / gal te byung na gcig la'ang mthol/ / chung ngu la yang 'jigs pa'i phyir/ / de la phas pham mi 'byung ngo zhes 'byung bas kho bo cag kyang mi tshangs spyod byas pa thams cad la pham pa 'byung bar mi 'dod kyi 'on kyang 'chab sems skyes na pham par 'gyur gyi 'chab sems skad cig kyang ma skyes pa ni rtsa ba'i lhung ba ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ {pham pa byung na dge slong ma yin no/ / des byas kyang sems 'gas kyang mi 'chab na pham par mi 'gyur ba'i phyir/ de bshags nas dge slong thams cad las gzhon rabs su 'dug pa sogs chad pa'i las kyi bslab pa rnams byin pas sor chud pa ste dge slong dga' ba can bzhin no/ / de skad du/ gal te sems ni gcig gis kyang*/ / bcabs pa med par 'chags byed na/ / tha ma byung bar gyur na yang*/ / de ni phas pham mi 'gyur ro zhes so }

Reply: No, it does not apply. The teaching that it is a downfall for one with unethical conduct to instruct a fully ordained nun is explained in the context of falling to lower rebirths. And if that is said to be training in virtue, then the Master himself stated: {One who ridicules rivals and householders while attired in the robes of an ārya, who is confused, untamed, and possesses guile,} discredits proper conduct as a facade.[1102] Therefore, [instruction by the unethical] is training in name alone, like a rotten seed, a dead being, or a dry pond. Again, a scripture declares: If single-mindedly, without concealment, one confesses the downfall, one does not commit a fundamental defeat, though one adopts an inferior status.[1103] Also, the Vinaya Verses notes: If with the intention not to conceal, one confesses a downfall when it occurs because one fears even a small downfall, a fundamental defeat will not occur.[1104] Therefore we do not assert that a defeat occurs for all impure conduct. A defeat occurs if a mind of concealment is generated, but if a mind of concealment does not arise even for an instant, it is not a defeat. {If one commits a defeat, one is no longer fully ordained. However, if one does not conceal what was done with any mind whatsoever, one does not commit a defeat. One confesses that act and restores the vow through the imposition of a penalty, such as being ranked as the newest fully ordained monk and so on, like the bhikṣu Nanda. If with just a single mind one confesses an act committed without concealment, a fundamental defeat does not occur, though one accepts inferior rank.[1105]}

tshul khrims 'chal pa rab tu mi 'byin pa ni rgyud ngo tsha khrel med shas chen pos nyams par byas pa'i phyir yin no/ / gtong ba la rtsa ba'i ltung ba gcig byung bas gtong yang len pa na gcig blangs pas kun blangs par ni mi 'gyur te/ sdom pa ni thams cad bsdams pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du phyogs gcig btang bas gzhan dag gtong bar mi rigs zhes pa la ni ston pa nyid kyis dper na shing ta la'i mgo bcad na sngon por 'gyur du mi rung la zhes pa la sogs pas lan btab pa yin te shing ta la'i mgo bcad na thams cad skam pa bzhin no/ / de dag srid pa tsam gyis gzhan la'ang thal bar mi 'gyur te/ khyab pa khas mi len pa'i phyir ro/ /

One with unethical conduct who is not expelled is repeatedly demoted through shamelessness and nonembarrassment. [Some say:] It is illogical to state “When relinquishing vows they are relinquished by committing one root downfall, and when taking vows all vows are taken when one vow is taken, because the vows are all bound together” and, similarly, “Relinquishing one type relinquishes other types” because the Master himself responded, “If the top of a palm tree is cut off, it cannot survive,” for in severing the top of a palm, the entire tree dies. [Reply:] This assertion does not follow even if such outcomes were possible in some circumstances, because there is no logical pervasion.
CONTRADICTING SCRIPTURE

lung dang 'gal ba'ang yod de/ lung rab tu byung ba'i gzhi las/ dge slong gis de byas na byas ma thag tu dge slong du mi rung bar 'gyur/ dge sbyong du mi rung shAkya'i sras kyir mi rung*/ dge slong gi dngos po las nyams par 'gyur te/ de'i dge sbyong gi tshul zhig par 'gyur zhing nyams pa bcom pa ltung ba pham par 'gyur ba ste/ de'i dge sbyong gi tshul phyir blang du med par 'gyur ro/ / 'di lta ste dper na shing ta la'i mgo bcad na sngon por 'gyur du mi rung la 'phel zhing rgyas pa dang yangs par 'gyur du mi rung ba bzhin no zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te don dam pa'i dge slong la dgongs te gsungs pa yin no zhe na ma yin te/ 'di ni nges pa'i don gzhan du drangs pas bka' la thugs thub cher byas shing*/ nyon mongs pa mang po can rnams la 'chal ba'i tshul khrims kyis rkyen byed pa'i phyir ro/ / ji ltar nges don yin zhe na/ lung rnam 'byed las/ dge slong ni rnam pa bzhi ste/ ming gi dge slong dang*/ khas 'che ba'i dge slong dang*/ slong bas na dge slong dang*/ nyon mongs pa bcom pas na dge slong ngo*/ / don 'di la ni gsol ba dang bzhi'i las kyis bsnyen par rdzogs pa'i dge slong yin no zhes pa dang*/ lung rab tu byung ba'i gzhi las kyang*/ bzhi po 'di dag ni bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas mkhyen cing gzigs pa des de ltar rab tu byung ba dang bsnyen par rdzogs pa'i dge slong gi ltung bar 'gyur ba'i chos su gsungs te zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

This also contradicts scripture because the Chapter on Going Forth states: If a fully ordained monk commits such an act, immediately he can no longer be a monk, train in virtue, or be a son of the Śākyas. He falls from the state of full ordination because the system of training in virtue has disintegrated, degenerated, and been destroyed. He commits the downfall of defeat, and there is no means of taking the vows of training in virtue in the future. It is as though, for example, [337] the head of a palm tree is severed: it can no longer remain green, and neither can it grow, develop, or flourish.[1106] Objection: What if this is stated intending a pure fully ordained being? Reply: That is not so. You disregard the word of the Buddha by diverging from the intended meaning and thus encourage unethical conduct in those with many afflictions. Question: How is that [interpretation] the intended meaning? Reply: Vinaya Divisions notes: There are four types of fully ordained monk: (1) fully ordained in name, (2) fully ordained through accepting vows, (3) fully ordained through requesting vows, (4) fully ordained through destroying afflictions. This refers to one who is fully ordained who received highest ordination through the rite of the four requests.[1107] The Chapter on Going Forth states: These four are comprehended and seen by the perfect, complete Buddha, Bhagavan, Tathāgata, Arhat. He stated those rules that are downfalls of the ordained and of the fully ordained, those who have received highest ordination.[1108]

gzhan yang lung las tshul khrims 'chal pa ni dge 'dun gyi zhal zas dang gtsug lag khang dag la kham gcig dang gom pa gcig 'dor ba tsam yang ma gnang par longs spyod thams cad las bkar te/ de'i dbang du mdzad nas mdo las/ dge slong min la dge slong du/ / smra ba sre da bsal bar gyis/ / shing rul dag ni spang bar gyis/ / snying po med pa dor bar gyis zhes bya ba la sogs pa gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / rigs pa dang 'gal ba'ang yod de/ gal te srog gcod byas pas sdom pa ma lus pa mi gtong na sdom pa yan lag thams cad bsdams pa ma yin par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / gal te yan lag thams cad bsdams pa yin na'ang srog bcad pa la sogs pas ji ltar mi gtong bar 'gyur/ / gal te phyogs gcig bsrungs pas sdom par 'gyur na ni len pa na'ang de ltar thal bar 'gyur ro/ / gal te sdom pa dang 'gal bar spyad pas sdom pa mi gtong na bslab pa phul ba la sogs pas kyang mi gtong bar thal ba'i phyir ro/ / 'ga' zhig gis srog bcad kyang 'ga' zhig la ltos pa'i srog gcod pa spong ba yod do zhes bya ba ni shin tu'ang blun pa yin te/ gang gi tshe sngar sdom pa blangs nas bslab pa phul ba la sogs pa med par sdom min la zhugs pa de'i tshe na'ang sdom pa yod par 'gyur te/ sems can thams cad gsod pa dang nor thams cad ma byin par len pa dang gzhan gyi bud med thams cad la spyod pa dang sems can thams cad la rdzun smra ba ni sus kyang mi nus pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yang srog gcod pa la sogs pa byed bzhin du sdom par 'gyur na gang sdom pa'i phyir sdom pa yin pa de soms shig /ma byin len la sogs pa sdom pa yin no zhe na/ des ni bar ma'i dge bar 'gyur gyi sdom pa ni nges pa lnga dang bral ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de ni len pa na yin no zhe na/ srung ba na'ang shin tu yin te/ khyad par med pa'i phyir ro/ /

Again, it is proclaimed in the sūtras that those with unethical conduct are not permitted to use even one morsel of Saṅgha food or take one step toward the main temple. From that perspective, a sūtra remarks: Those who are not fully ordained who claim to be fully ordained should be removed like a blight, eliminated like rotten wood, and expelled as unworthy.[1109] [Objection:] But that is illogical. If by taking life, no vow were relinquished in the least, then no branch of the vows would [need to] be protected. But if every branch were protected, how would [vows against] taking life and so on be relinquished? If something became a vow due to guarding one aspect of it, then in consequence taking a vow would also be just that [i.e., guarding one aspect of it]. And if a vow were not relinquished by breaking the vow, then in consequence even offering back the training would not relinquish the vow. Some say: Even though they kill some living beings, with respect to others they still abandon killing. Reply: But to say this is extremely foolish, for those who have taken vows in the past and who have not given up training [in those vows] and so on yet engage in perverted ethics would still have vows. That is because there are none who can kill all sentient beings, steal all the wealth, engage in sexual misconduct with the every wife, or lie to all sentient beings. Objection: But consider that if something prevents one from engaging in the act of taking life and so on, it should be considered to be a vow (saṃvara) because it restrains one from committing that act. That which [protects against] taking what is not given and so on is a vow. Reply: But vows that become interim virtue [338] lack the five certainties.[1110] Objection: Then they should not be taken. Reply: But if they guard against [nonvirtue], then definitely they should be [taken] because they are not different [in affording protection].
de'i phyir rtsa ltung byung bas sdom pa mi gtong bar 'dod pa 'di ni dge sbyong gi tshul khrims bslu ba'i phyir bdud kyis byas pa yin par shes so/ /
Therefore to assert that a vow is not relinquished when a root downfall arises should be known as the activity of māras to deceive those who possess the ethics of training in virtue.
bsam gtan dang zag med kyi sdom pa gtong ba'i rgyu ni
THE CAUSES OF RELINQUISHING ABSORPTION AND UNCONTAMINATED VOWS
bsam gtan gtogs pa'i dge ba ni/ / sa 'phos nyams pa dag gis gtong / / de bzhin gzugs med gtogs 'phags pa/ / 'bras bu thob sbyangs nyams pa las/ / 40

Virtue belonging to the absorptions is relinquished by changing level or degeneration. That belonging to the formless is relinquished in the same way. The ārya by obtaining the result, upgrading, or degeneration. (4:40)

All {physical} virtue belonging to the absorptions is relinquished by two causes: (1) it is relinquished by changing level, where, respectively, birth on higher levels from lower levels or birth on lower levels from higher levels is relinquishment subsumed by lower level or higher level, or (2) it is relinquished by degeneration after having previously obtained meditative attainment. Also, mere access concentration — which does not obtain the actual basis {and the path of preparation dependent on that and so on} — is relinquished through death because the Autocommentary explains: Relinquishment of the same type is small relinquishment.[1111] And: A non-ārya also, through death from lower levels.[1112] {The path of preparation generated in dependence on the actual basis of absorption is not relinquished due to death because [those who possess it] see the four truths in that life. Also there is relinquishment through separation from attachment to that level, which is the factor conducive to the pure actual basis because it is abandoned like affliction.}

ji ltar gzugs su gtogs pa'i dge ba sa 'phos pa dang yongs su nyams pas gtong ba de bzhin du gzugs med du gtogs pa'i dge ba'ang sa 'phos pa dang nyams pa dag gis gtong ngo*/ / 'phags pa'i{ dge ba sogs} dge ba zag med ni rgyu gsum gyis gtong ste/ 'bras bu phyi ma thob pas{ zhugs pa dang} snga ma dang dbang po rtul po sbyangs pas rnon po thob pa na rtul po'i sems kyis bsdus pa dang de dag las 'bras bu phyi ma gsum las nyams pa las kyang gtong ngo*/ /

Just as virtue belonging to the form realm is relinquished by changing level or through complete degeneration, so virtue belonging to the formless realm is relinquished in the same way, by changing level or through degeneration. The {virtue and so forth and} uncontaminated virtue of the ārya is relinquished by three causes: (1) By obtaining the later result one relinquishes the earlier {enterer} stage.[1113] (2) When one obtains sharp faculty by upgrading from dull faculty, one relinquishes that obtained by a dull mind. (3) One relinquishes those three latter results[1114] through degeneration.
sdom min gyi gtong tshul ni
THE METHOD OF RELINQUISHING NEGATIVE COMMITMENTS
sdom min sdom pa thob pa dang / / shi dang mtshan gnyis byung ba las/ / bar ma shugs blangs bya ba dang / / don tshe rtsa ba chad pa las/ / 41

Negative commitments are relinquished through obtaining vows, death, and the occurrence of two organs. Interim precepts are relinquished through terminating the force, acceptance, action, object, life, root. (4:41)

sdom min rnams ni rgyu gsum gyis gtong ste/ sdom pa {dang po gnyis las } gang yang rung ba thob pa dang shi 'phos pa dang*/ mtshan gnyis byung ba las gtong bar 'gyur te/ gnyen po stobs ldan thob pa'i phyir dang*/ rten bor ba dang shugs chad pa'i phyir dang*/ rten nyams pa'i phyir go rim du sbyar ro/ / {de yang dge slong gi sdom pa thob na las lam bdun po dang*/ lhag ma dge tshul sogs thob na pham par 'gyur ba bzhi po gtong la phra ma sogs gsum bar mar 'gyur zhes zer ro/ / zag med thob na gtong zhes mi brjod pa ni/ de'i sngon du bsam gtan skye dgos la/ des sdom min de'i gong du gtong bas so/ / mtshon dang rgya la sogs pa mi bya ba'i bsam pa thag pas bor kyang sdom pa ma blangs par sdom min mi chad de/ sman med par nad rnying mi bzlog pa bzhin no }

Negative commitments (asaṃvara) are relinquished by three causes: they are relinquished through (1) obtaining either {of the first two} vows (saṃvara), (2) death (mṛtyu), and (3) the occurrence of two organs (dvivañja) because, respectively, (1) a strong antidote to them is obtained, (2) their basis is discarded and their force terminates, and (3) their basis degenerates. {Further, it is said that if one obtains full-ordination vows, seven karmic paths are relinquished, and if one obtains others, such as novice vows and so on, the four defeats are relinquished, and that slander, harsh words, and gossip are relinquished by interim precepts. It is not stated that they are relinquished when one obtains uncontaminated vows for the absorptions must be generated before that, and absorption vows relinquish negative commitments before [uncontaminated vows arise]. Though negative commitments are discarded mentally without making a sign or gesture, they are not [fully] eliminated without taking vows, just as a severe illness is not stopped without taking medicine.}

gal te sdom min dang ldan pa bsnyen gnas blangs te bsrungs pa'i tshe sdom min gtong ba de lta na'ang bsnyen gnas ni mtshan mo 'das pa na gtong ba'i phyir de btang ba na sdom min dang ldan nam/ 'on te ma yin nam zhe na/ kha cig na re lcags kyi tho lum 'bar ba me dang bral ba na sngon por 'gyur ba ltar gtan du gtong ba'i bsam pa dang mi ldan pa'i phyir sdom min dang ldan par 'gyur ro zhes zer ro/ / kha cig na re gsod pa la sogs pa'i sbyor ba mi byed pa de srid du sdom pa dang yang mi ldan la sdom min dang yang mi ldan gyi phyis mi dge ba'i sbyar ba byed pa nas sdom min dang ldan par 'gyur te/ sdom min thob pa ni rig byed la rag las pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes zer ro/ /

Question: When one possessing negative commitments takes and guards one-day vows negative commitments are relinquished, but because one-day vows are relinquished at the end of the night, does one again come to possess those negative commitments after relinquishing them? Some say: One again comes to possess those negative commitments because one does not possess the [339] continuous thought to relinquish them, just as an iron mallet turns blue when extracted from a blazing fire.[1115] Some say: For as long as one does not engage in killing and so on, one does not possess vows and neither does one possess negative commitments. Later, having engaged in nonvirtue, one comes to possess negative commitments because obtaining negative commitments relies on indicative form.
bar ma'i gtong tshul ni
THE METHOD OF RELINQUISHING INTERIM PRECEPTS

bar ma dge mi dge'i rig byed ma yin pa ni rdza mkhan gyi 'khor lo'am mda'i 'phen pa'i shugs ltar rab tu dwang ba dang nyon mongs pa'i shugs {drag po }gang gis rig byed ma yin pa de 'phangs pa na 'phangs pa'i shugs de chad pas gtong ba'ang yod de/ rdzas las byung ba ma yin pa'i gzhi bdun lta bu rab tu dwang ba log pa na gtong ba dang*/ zhe sdang gi shugs chad nas mthun par gyur pa na bar ma mi dge ba gtong ba lta bu bzhin no/ / blangs pa chad pas kyang gtong ste lo gsum du srog gcod pa spong ngo zhes khas blangs pa dang*/ de'i bar du lo re la srog gcod mchod sbyin bya'o/ / zhes khas blangs pa na lo gsum 'das pa na de dag gtong ba lta bu'am yang na yang dag par blangs pa 'dis chog gis da phyin chad bsgrub par mi nus so/ / zhes sngar blangs pa btang bas kyang gtong ngo*/ / bya ba chad pas kyang gtong ste/ lo re la dge 'dun la bsnyen bkur bya bar khas blangs nas byed pa na nam zhig na de ma grub na gtong ba lta bu'o/ / don chad pas gtong ba'ang yod de/ gtsug lag khang la sogs pa zhig pa dang*/ rgya dang rdos la sogs pa zhig pa na bar ma dge mi dge'i rig byed ma yin pa gtong ba lta bu'o/ / tshe chad pa dang dge ba'i rtsa ba chad pa las{ kyang} gtong ba ni shi 'phos pa na bar ma dge mi dge'i rig byed ma yin pa gnyis ka gtong la/ log lta skyes te dge rtsa gcod par rtsom pa na bar ma dge ba'i rig byed ma yin pa gtong ba lta bu'i phyir ro/ /

Nonindicative virtuous or nonvirtuous interim precepts (madhyamā) are propelled, respectively, by the {strong} force of extremely clear faith or the afflictions, just as a potter’s wheel or an arrow is propelled by a strong force. They are relinquished through terminating the force that projects them, such as, for example, relinquishing [interim virtue] through reversing extremely clear faith in the seven bases [of merit] not derived from material generosity, or relinquishing interim nonvirtue through stopping the force of aversion. Also, they are relinquished through terminating the acceptance [of a pledge], such as initially pledging to abandon killing for three years, or to offer blood sacrifice each year at a specific time, and then relinquishing those pledges after three years. Or, that which was initially accepted is relinquished by stating, “It is worthy to do what is noble, but now I cannot accomplish it.” Also, they are relinquished by terminating the action, such as [the case of] having pledged to give support and respect to the Saṅgha each year, and when that action is not performed, that action is relinquished. Also, they are relinquished by destruction of the object, for the destruction of a temple and so on or reducing it in breadth and extent relinquishes nonindicative virtuous or nonvirtuous interim precepts [that arose in relation to that object]. {Also} they are relinquished by the termination of life or severing the root of virtue, because if one dies, both virtuous and nonvirtuous nonindicative interim precepts are relinquished, and by generating wrong view one severs the root of virtue and one relinquishes virtuous and nonvirtuous nonindicative interim precepts.
gzugs can ma yin pa'i gtong tshul ni
THE METHOD OF RELINQUISHING NONPHYSICAL STATES
'dod gtogs dge ba gzugs min ni/ / rtsa chad gong du skyes pa las/ / nyon mongs pa can gzugs min ni/ / gnyen po skyes pas rnam nyams 'gyur/ / 42

Virtuous nonphysical states belonging to the desire realm are relinquished through severing the root or taking higher birth. Afflicted nonphysical states decline through the generation of antidotes. (4:42)

'dod pa'i khams su gtogs pa'i dge ba gzugs can min pa sems dang sems byung dge ba thob pa dang mtshan nyid dang bcas pa dag ni dge rtsa chad pa dang*/ 'dod pa'i gong ma gzugs dang gzugs med du skyes pa las gtong bar 'gyur ro/ / {de dag dang gzhan yang 'dod chags dang bral bas kyang cung zad gtong ba yod de dper na yid mi bde'i dbang po dge ba lta bu'o zhes TIka las 'chad do/ / gang btang ba de spangs pa yin nam zhe na/ dge ba zag bcas ni 'dun pa'i 'dod chags dang bral bas kyang cung zad gtong ba yod de dper na yid mi bde'i dbang po dge ba lta bu'o zhes TIka las 'chad do/ / gang btang ba de spangs pa yin nam zhe na/ dge ba zag bcas ni 'dun pa'i 'dod chags dang bral bas spong bas mu bzhi yod do }

khams gong ma gnyis kyi dge ba'i gtong rgyu ni khyad par med par bshad zin to/ /khams gsum char gyi nyon mongs pa can gzugs can min pa sems sems byung mi dge ba dang bsgribs pa mtshan nyid dang thob pa dang bcas pa dag ni rang rang gi 'jig rten dang 'jig rten las 'das pa'i gnyen po skyes pas rnam par nyams par 'gyur gyi gzhan gyis ni ma yin no/ / de'i phyir so so'i skye bos srid rtse'i nyon mongs spangs pa mi srid de/ 'jig rten pa'i lam gyi gnyen po ni de'i gong na gzhan med la 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam ni ma skyes pa'i phyir ro/ / sa gzhan gyi nyon mongs pa spangs pa ni yod de/ de dag la 'jig rten pa'i lam gyi gnyen po yod pa'i phyir ro zhes bya ba 'di yin no/ /

It has already been explained that the causes of relinquishment of the virtue of both higher realms are not different. The three realms’ afflicted nonphysical minds and mental factors — which obtain nonvirtue and possess the characteristics of obscuration — decline through the generation of their specific mundane and [340] transcendent antidotes (pratipakṣa) but not by other methods. Therefore it is impossible for ordinary beings to abandon afflictions of the root of existence, because the antidote to the mundane path is a path higher than it and no other and the transcendent path has not yet arisen. They abandon afflictions of other levels because they have the antidote to other mundane paths.
rten gyi khyad par/
Difference of karmic agent
za ma ma ning sgra mi snyan/ / mtshan gnyis ma gtogs mi rnams la/ / sdom min sdom pa'ang de bzhin no/ / lha la'ang mi rnams la gsum mo/ / 43

Humans have negative commitments except for eunuchs, neuters, hermaphrodites, and those of Kuru. Wherever negative commitments arise, so too, vows arise. Vows also arise in gods. Humans have three. (4:43)

rten gyi khyad par bshad pa la za ma ni dbang po gang yang med pa'o/ / ma ning ni dbang po yod kyang nyams pa'o/ / mtshan gnyis pa ni pho mo'i dbang po gnyis ka cig car byung ba'o/ / de dag dang byang gi sgra mi snyan pa ma gtogs pa'i mi rnams la sdom min yod de/ 'di ltar za ma la sogs pa la ni sdom min med de/ sdig pa bya ba'i bsam pa mi brtan pa'i phyir dang gnyen po yin pa'i phyir gang la sdom pa yod pa de la sdom min yang yod pa yin na de la gnyen po sdom pa mi skye ba'i yang phyir ro/ / rgyu mtshan de dag dang*/ gzhan yang gang med pas sdom min du 'gyur ba'i ngo tsha khrel yod shas chen po med pa nyid kyi phyir ngan song pa rnams la'ang sdom min med {de gnyen po'i rten du mi rung bas sdom pa'ang med } do/ / byang gi sgra mi snyan pa la ni sdig pa bya ba'i bsam pa med pa'i phyir dang*/ {ting nge 'dzin med pa'i phyir dang } de dag la sdom pa'ang med pa'i phyir dang*/ lha rnams la ni las rgyu 'bras mngon sum du gyur pas sdig pa bya ba'i bsam pa brtan po med pa'i phyir ro/ /

Humans have negative commitments except for eunuchs (ṣaṇḍha), who have no sexual organ at all; neuters (paṇḍa), who have an organ that has degenerated; hermaphrodites (dvidhākṛtin), who have both a male and female organ at the same time; and those of the northern continent of Kuru. Eunuchs and so on do not have negative commitments because their thought to commit immoral actions is not stable. And if they sought to take vows against negative commitments, because vows were their antidote, then for them such vows could also not arise as their antidote. As such, beings of lower rebirths have neither negative commitments {nor vows that would act as their antidote} because they do not have strong shame and embarrassment about negative commitments. Also, those of the northern continent of Kuru do not have vows because they do not have the thought to commit immoral actions {and they do not possess concentration}. Gods do not have a stable thought to commit immoral actions since they perceive karmic causation.

'dul ba las ni/ skyes nas dang*/ zla ba phyed pa dang*/ 'khyud nas ldang ba dang*/ phrag dog can dang*/ nyams pa'o zhes pho ma ning lnga dang*/ mtshan gnyis pa'o/ / gle 'dams pa'o/ / rtag tu zla mtshan zag pa'o/ / zla mtshan mi zag pa'o/ / mtshan ma tsam yod pa'o zhes mo ma ning lnga ste bcu bshad cing*/ {dang po lnga'i mtshan nyid ni } kun las btus las kyang*/ skyes nas ma ning du gyur pa dang*/ ma ning phrag dog can dang*/ ma ning zla ba phyed pa dang*/ rlugs pa'i ma ning dang*/ nyams pa'i ma ning ngo zhes ma ning lnga bshad de/ de dag gi dang po za ma yin zhing*/ mtshan gnyis pa ni de nyid yin la/ gzhan dag ni ma ning gi dbye bar snang ngo*/ / rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las yongs ma ning dang*/ phyogs gcig pa'i ma ning dang*/ nyams pa'i ma ning gsum bshad pa'i dang po ni pho mo'i dbang po dang mi ldan par btsas pa ste za ma dang ma ning gnyis ka yin la/ gnyis pa ni zla ba phyed phyed cing skyes pa'i spobs pa skye ba dang bdag nyid la pha rol gyis sun 'byin pa'am/ gzhan 'dod pa bsten pa mthong na skyes pa'i spobs pa skye bar 'gyur pa ste/ de ni ma ning kho na yin gyi za ma ni ma yin no/ / gsum pa ni mtshon cha la sogs pas bcad pa'am/ nad dang dug dang me dang sngags la sogs pas chad nas skyes pa'i spobs pa mi 'byung ba ste/ de ni gal te pha rol pos bdag la sun 'byin par mi byed na ni za ma kho na yin la sun 'byin par byed na ni gnyis ka yin no zhes bshad do/ /

The Vinaya mentions five male neuters: A neuter by birth, a half-month neuter, a neuter aroused by embrace, an envious neuter, and a neuter [whose organ] degenerates.[1117] and five female neuters: Neuter with two organs, a deformed neuter,[1118] a neuter with continuous menstruation, a neuter without menstruation, and a neuter with just one organ.[1119] Thus it explains ten neuters. {Regarding the characteristics of the first five,} the Compendium of Abhidharma states: A neuter by birth, an envious neuter, a half-month neuter, a moistened neuter, a neuter [whose organ] degenerates.[1120] This text explains five neuters, and from those, the first is a eunuch and a hermaphrodite. The others are classifications of neuters. The Compendium of Ascertainment mentions three neuters: Complete neuter, part neuter, and a neuter [whose organ] degenerates.[1121] The first, who is born without a male or female organ, [341] is both a eunuch and a neuter. The second is a half-month neuter who develops male libido when criticized by others, or one who develops male libido when he sees he can serve the desires of others, and such beings are just neuters and not eunuchs. The third is one whose organ is severed by a knife and so on or whose organ is neutralized by illness, poison, fire, mantra, and so on, and male libido does not arise. It is explained that if that being is not criticized by others, that being is a eunuch alone, but if criticized, that being is both.

'dul ba tshig le'ur byas pa las/ 'khyud chags phrad dog nad dang skyes/ / zla phyed ces bya ma ning lnga/ / 'di dag re re'i mtshan nyid ni/ / rtogs pa'i don du brjod par bya/ / gang la gzhan gyis mnan pa na/ / 'khrig phyir sems la 'dod chags ni/ / rnam rgyas de ni blo ldan gyis/ / 'khyud ldang ma ning shes par bya/ / gzhan gyi mtshan ni mthong ba las/ / rang la 'dod skye phrag dog grags/ / mtshon nad kyis ni rtags nyams pa/ / de ni nad kyi ma ning brjod/ / gang skyes nyid na mtshan ma ni/ / gnyis ka med pa skyes nas yin/ / zla phyed bud med zla phyed ni/ / skyes 'gyur zla phyed ma ning brjod/ / 'dir ni sogs kyi sgra med kyang*/ / zla sogs ma ning grub pa yin/ / gang zhig grong gi chos dag gi / nus med de ni za ma ste/ / gnyis ka'i mtshan ni dod pa ni/ / mtshan gnyis par ni 'dod pa yin zhes dang po nas mtshan gnyis ka med pa ni skyes nas ma ning dang*/ 'khrig pa spyod mi nus pa za ma yin la/ zla ba phyed pa dngos su bshad pas shugs la zla ba gcig pa la sogs pa'i ma ning yang yod par bshad do/ /

The Vinaya Verses explains: (1) Neuter desiring embrace, (2) envious neuter, (3) incapacitated neuter, (4) neuter by birth, and (5) half-month neuter are the five neuters. The characteristics of each are expressed for the purpose of comprehending them. (1) Those who possess a mind of increased desire for sex, when subdued by others are called “neuters aroused by embrace.” (2) Those whose desire arises through seeing another’s sexual organ are known as “envious neuters.” (3) Those whose genitals are removed by the knife or [who are affected by] disease are called “incapacitated neuters.” (4) Those who are born without either sexual organ are “neuters by birth.” (5) Those who are female for half a month and male for half a month are “half-month neuters.” Though here the term “and so on” is not stated, there are neuters for a month and so on. Further, in local custom those regarded as lacking sexual potency are called eunuchs. Those with prominent organs of both sexes are asserted to be hermaphrodites.[1122] Therefore those who lack either organ from the beginning are neuters from birth, and those incapable of performing sexual union are eunuchs. Since this text explicitly teaches half-month neuters, it implies the existence of one-month neuters and so on.
sdom min gang la skye ba de dag la gnyen po yin pa'i phyir sdom pa'ang de bzhin du skye la 'on kyang {bsam gtan zag med kyi } sdom pa ni lha la'ang skye'o zhes bya ba ni khyad par yin no/ /
Wherever negative commitments arise, so too vows arise because they are its antidote. However, there is a difference, in that {absorption and uncontaminated} vows also arise in gods (deva).

'o na ci'i phyir za ma la sogs pa la sdom pa med ce na/ lung dang rigs pa las te/ lung ni ming chen gyi mdo las/ ming chen 'di ltar khyim pa gos dkar po gyon pa skyes pa pho'i dbang po dang ldan pa zhig ces pa la sogs pa dang*/ 'dul ba rab tu byung ba'i gzhi las kyang*/ rku thabs gnas dang ma ning dang zhes pa dang*/ khyod za ma ma yin nam { ma ning ma yin nam} zhes dri zhing gal te yin zhes zer na khyod mi skye ba'i chos can yin gyi song zhig ces brjod par bya'o zhes za ma la sogs pa gsal bar gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ bshes spring las kyang gso sbyong 'dod spyod lha lus yid 'ong ba/ / skyes pa bud med dag la gsol bar bgyi zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / rig pa ni rten pho mo gnyis ka'i nyon mongs pa shas che ba'i phyir dang*/ gnyen po so sor rtog pa'i shes rab mi bzod pa'i phyir dang*/ rgyud la ngo tsha khrel yod shas chen po med pa'i phyir ro/ /

Question: Why do eunuchs and so on not have vows? Reply: That is established from scripture and logic. Regarding scripture, the Mahānāma Sūtra states: Mahānāma, it is like this, a householder wearing white clothes with a male organ . . . and so on.[1123] The Chapter on Going Forth also notes: One who lives through stealing, as a neuter . . .[1124] And: You are questioned, “Are you a eunuch?” {or “Are you a neuter?”} and if you answer “Yes,” you are established as one in whom the vows will not arise and you are told, “Please depart.”[1125] These passages clearly state “eunuch” and so on. Also, Commentary on the Letter to a Friend explains: In the confession ceremony, one makes request for an appealing divine male or female body capable of sexual function.[1126] Regarding logic, [they do not possess vows,] because such physical bases have an excess of both male and female affliction, they have no patience with analytical wisdom that is the antidote [to saṃsāra], and they lack strong shame and embarrassment in their [342] mindstream.

des na 'dul ba tshig le'ur byas pa las/ ma ning la sogs gnas mi bya/ / tshwa sgo'i zhing ltar de dag la/ / tshul khrims sa bon skye ba med/ /
ces 'byung bas za ma dang ma ning dang mtshan gnyis pa dang ngan song la sogs pa de dag ni zhing tshwa sgo can la 'bras bu dang rtswa gnyis ka tshar gcig mi skye ba ltar rten zhan pas sdom min gnyis ka mi skye bar shes par bya'o/ / de ltar na sdom pa ni lha dang mi kho na la yod la/ sdom min ni mi kho na la yod do/ / rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las ni za ma dang ma ning dag nyon mongs pa mang ba dang nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pas bsgribs pas tshul khrims dag pa dang yon tan khyad par can mi thob pa'i phyir dang*/ dge slong gi phyogs su bzhag na'ang reg pa la sogs pa bud med kyi nyes pa bsten par 'gyur la/ dge slong ma'i phyogs su bzhag na'ang nom pa dang kun tu nom pa la sogs pa skyes pa'i nyes pa bsten par 'gyur ba'i phyir rab tu 'byin pa dang bsnyen par rdzogs par ni mi byed do/ / 'on kyang de dag gsum la skyabs su song zhing dge bsnyen gyi bslab pa'i gzhi dag blangs nas bsrung na bsod nams ni dge bsnyen dang mtshungs par thob la/ dge bsnyen zhes bya ba'i ming ni mi 'thob ste/ dge slong pha ma la bsnyen bkur byed pa'i ngang tshul can ni dge bsnyen zhes bya ba yin la/ de dag ni pho mo gnyis ka'i nyes pa bsten pas phyogs gnyis la bsnyen bkur byed pa'i 'os ma yin pas de dag gis kyang dge slong pha ma la kun tu 'dre bas bsnyen bkur mi bya zhing*/ dge slong pha mas kyang de dag gi bsnyen bkur bdag gir mi bya reg pa dang yid brtan par mi bya ba'i phyir ro zhes bshad do/ /

Therefore the Vinaya Verses declares: Neuters and so on are not a proper basis. They are like a salt-encrusted field where the seeds of ethics cannot be planted.[1127]
One should understand that since neuters, eunuchs, hermaphrodites, those of lower rebirth, and so on are inferior bases, neither vows nor negative commitments are generated in them, just as fruit and grass will not grow in salt-encrusted fields. Thus only humans and gods have vows, and only humans have negative commitments. The Compendium of Ascertainment notes: Since neuters and eunuchs have many afflictions and are obscured by affliction, they cannot possess pure ethics or special qualities. If they were to become fully ordained monks, they would indulge in the faults of females, such as the fault of making contact. If they were to become fully ordained nuns, they would indulge in the faults of males, such as touching and intense touching. Therefore vows are not conferred on them, nor do they receive highest ordination. However, if they take refuge in the Three Jewels and accept and guard the basis of training of laypeople, they obtain merit similar to laypeople. But they do not obtain the title “layperson” since those who serve and respect fully ordained monks and nuns are called “laypeople,” but they are unworthy to serve and respect both types since they indulge in faults pertaining to both males and females. Therefore, since they continuously immerse themselves [in actions that would be] defeats for the fully ordained, they cannot serve and respect fully ordained monks and nuns, and fully ordained monks and nuns do not accept their service and respect because they engage in sensual contact with unstable minds.[1128]

'o na mdo las/ dge slong dag sgo nga las skyes pa'i klu ni zla ba phyed phyed kyi tshes brgyad la gnas nas byung nas yan lag brgyad dang ldan pa'i bsnyen gnas la nye bar gnas so/ / zhes dud 'gro la sdom pa skye bar bshad pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/ de ni legs spyad tsam la sdom pa'i ming gis btags pa yin gyi sdom pa ni ma yin no zhes 'chad do/ / mi dang lha la sdom pa thams cad yod dam zhe na

Question: Now, a sūtra states: Monks, there are nāgas who are born from eggs who take [lay vows] on the eighth day of each half-month and abide as one-day vow-holders possessing the eight sections.[1129] Doesn’t this contradict [the assertion that] vows are not generated in animals? Reply: Here the name “vow” is merely applied to a positive action, but it does not constitute a vow. Question: Don’t all vows exist [only] for humans and gods?
mi rnams la ni so so thar pa dang bsam gtan dang zag med kyi sdom pa gsum ga yod do/ /
Reply: Humans (nṛna) have three types of vows: pratimokṣa, absorption, and uncontaminated vows.
'dod dang gzugs skyes lha rnams la/ / bsam gtan skyes yod zag med ni/ / bsam gtan khyad par 'du shes med/ / sems can ma gtogs gzugs med na'ang / / 44

Desire-realm gods and gods born in the form realm have vows arisen from the absorptions. Also gods in the formless realm have uncontaminated vows, except for beings with special absorption and nondiscernment. (4:44)

'dod pa'i lha rnams dang gzugs su skyes pa'i lha rnams la ni bsam gtan las skyes pa'i sdom pa yod kyi gzugs med na ni ma yin te/ rang sa na gzugs med pa'i phyir dang*/ 'og mar thob pa dag kyang sa 'phos pas gtong ba'i phyir ro/ / zag med kyi sdom pa ni bsam gtan khyad par can gyi sems can tshangs pa chen po dang 'du shes med par skyes pa'i sems can ma gtogs pa 'dod pa dang gzugs su skyes pa'i lha rnams {la gnas gtsang na nges par yod pa dang gzhan la yod rung ba } dang gzugs med pa na'ang{ 'phags pa la 'das ma 'ongs ldan pa'i sgo nas} yod de/ gzugs med rang sa na gzugs med kyang gzugs khams su zag med kyi sdom pa thob pa gtong rgyu ma byung bar gzugs med du skyes pa dag la thob pa ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / tshangs pa chen po dang 'du shes med pa'i sems can la mi ldan pa ni dang po ni phyin ci log gi lta ba dang ldan pa'i phyir dang*/ gnyis pa ni mi khom pa'i gnas yin pa'i phyir ro/ / slob dpon gang spel gyis kyang*/ so so thar pa ni mi kho na la yod kyi lha la ni med de/ / mdo las/ lha rnams ni mi dag gis gnas gsum gyis zil gyis gnon te/ dpa' ba dang*/ dran pa dang ldan pa dang*/ 'dir tshangs par spyod pa la gnas pa'o zhes gsungs te/ 'dir tshangs par spyod pa ni rab tu byung ba dang bsnyen par rdzogs pa dge slong gi dngos por 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'i tha tshig go /skyo ba med pas 'dod pa'i lha shes rab can rnams la'ang med na gong du skyes pa rnams la lta smros kyang ci dgos 'on kyang gong ma rnams la bsam gtan dang zag med kyi sdom pa ni ci rigs par rgyu dang las dang chos nyid kyi stobs kyis skye'o/ / bsam gtan khyad par can dang 'du shes med pa'i sems can la ni zag med de/ 'phags pa rnams de gnyis su mi skye ba'i phyir ro/ / gzugs med na zag med ni zag med kyi sdom pa ldan pas yod kyi mngon gyur ni med de/ de ni gzugs med pa'i phyir ro zhes bshad do/ / theg pa gong ma pa dag las kyi dbang gis skyes pa'i tshangs pa chen po la zag med med kyang byang chub sems dpa' ni smon lam gyi dbang gis tshangs pa chen por yang skye bas de la ni zag med yod do zhes bzhed mod kyi bye brag tu smra ba ni der skyes pa'i byang chub sems dpa' 'phags par mi 'dod pas de la zag med yod par mi 'dod do// //

Desire-realm gods and gods born in the form realm have vows arisen from the absorptions, but that is not so in the formless realm because there is no form on that level, and those obtained on lower levels are relinquished through changing level. Gods born in the desire and form realms, {such as gods of the pristine abodes who definitely have vows, while those in other abodes do not definitely have vows,} and also gods in the formless realm, {such as āryas possessing past and future vows,} have uncontaminated vows, except for beings of Mahābrahma [heaven], who have special absorption (dhyānāntara), and beings born in the state of nondiscernment (asaṃjñisattva).[1130] [343] That is because even though there is no form on the formless-realm level, those born in the formless realm possess them, since uncontaminated vows obtained in the form realm are not relinquished. Beings of Mahābrahma and the state of nondiscernment do not possess them, because the first possess incorrect view and the second is an abode lacking freedom. Also, Master Pūrṇavardhana observes that pratimokṣa vows only exist for humans and not gods because a sūtra states: Humans outshine gods in three areas: courage, mindfulness, and abiding with pure conduct.[1131] Here “pure conduct” refers to the pledge to become fully ordained through receiving highest ordination. Even desire gods who possess wisdom do not have it, let alone those born on higher levels, since they possess no disgust with existence. However, absorption and uncontaminated vows arise in those of higher realms by the power of various causes, karma, and reality. Beings of special absorption and the state of nondiscernment do not have uncontaminated vows because āryas do not take birth in those two abodes. Formless-realm beings possess uncontaminated states since they possess uncontaminated vows, but they do not manifest there because there is no form there.[1132] Indeed, in the higher vehicles it is asserted that those born in the heaven of Mahābrahma by the power of karma may have uncontaminated vows, but since Vaibhāṣikas do not assert that ārya bodhisattvas are born there, they do not assert that uncontaminated states exist there.
mdo las gsungs pa'i las rgyas par bshad pa/
20. Elaboration of Karma Found in the Sūtras: Part 1

da ni mdo las gsungs pa'i las kyi dbye ba ni gsum tshan gsum pa'i mdo las/ yon skyon snyigs ma snyigs ma can/ / nyes par spyad pa rnam gsum dang*/ / gtsang thub lus bsod bsod min dang*/ / 'das sogs bde gshegs gsal bar mdzad/ / gnas gsum gyis ni bsdus pa dang*/ / ched du bsam brjod gsum dag dang*/ / las rnams gsum dang 'das dang dge / slob dang mthong dang 'dod dang gzugs/ / mthong ba'i chos la bde ba dang*/ / yid bde ba dang sdug bsngal dang*/ / log lta spang bya chung ngu dang*/ / ser sna dang ni ser sna med/ / brnab sems brnab sems med pa dag / tshoms su yang dag bsdebs pa yin/ / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyi don ston pa yin pas

NOW, THE CLASSIFICATION OF karma found in the sūtras. The Three Times Three Sūtra teaches the meaning of these: The Sugata clarifies qualities, errors, degeneration and that which possesses degeneration, the three types of negative action, purity, silence, killing and not killing the body, transcendence and so on, that subsumed by the three abodes, the three: purpose, contemplation, and expression, the three types of karma, transcendence, and virtue, training, seeing, desire, and form; in this life, pleasure, and mental satisfaction, pain and wrong view, the smaller objects to be abandoned, avarice and that which is free of avarice, and covetous and noncovetous minds. All are assembled in this collection.[1133]

de la las sum chen du dbye ba dang*/ myong 'gyur gyi dbye ba dang*/ dkar nag la sogs pa bzhir dbye ba dang*/ thub pa dang gtsang byed kyi dbye ba dang*/ legs spyad nyes spyad kyi dbye ba dang*/ dge bcu mi dge bcur dbye ba dang*/ las 'bras bu dang bcas par dbye ba dang*/ rigs pa dang rigs pa ma yin pas bskyed pa'i dbye ba dang 'phen byed dang rdzogs byed kyi dbye ba dang*/ sgrib pa gsum bshad pa dang*/ mtshams med lnga bshad pa dang*/ de dang nye ba lnga bshad pa dang*/ bsod nams bya ba'i gzhi gsum bshad pa dang*/ cha mthun gsum bshad pa dang*/ rigs pas rab tu bcug pa'i las gsum bshad pa bco lnga yod pa las/

This has fifteen headings: (1) classification in three divisions, (2) karma to be experienced, (3) classification in four, such as white and black, (4) silence and purification, [344] (5) positive action and negative action, (6) ten virtuous and ten nonvirtuous actions, (7) karmic causation, (8) appropriate and inappropriate karma, (9) projecting and completing karma, (10) the three obscurations, (11) the five heinous actions, (12) the five near-heinous actions, (13) merit, action, and basis, (14) the three conducive factors, and (15) the three karmas engaged by cognition.
dang po ni [las gsum tshan du dbye ba]
Classification in three divisions
gsum tshan gsum pa'i mdo las las dge mi dge lung ma bstan gsum gsungs pa las
The Three Times Three Sūtra states: There are three: virtuous, nonvirtuous, and neutral karma.
las bde mi bde dang gzhan ni/ / dge dang mi dge dang gzhan yin/ / bsod nams bsod nams min mi g.yo/ / bde ba myong 'gyur la sogs gsum/ / 45

Karmic pleasurable experience is from virtue, painful experience is from nonvirtue, other experience is different. Meritorious, nonmeritorious, and invariable karma, and the three: karma to be experienced as pleasure and so on. (4:45)

dus re zhig las kyi rnam smin yid du 'ong ba bde ba myong ba dang gtan du sdug bsngal las skyob pa myang 'das thob byed ni dge ba dang*/ rnam smin yid du mi 'ong ba mi bde ba myong ba ni mi dge ba dang*/ yid du 'ong mi 'ong skyed pa de gnyis las gzhan pa'i las ni dge mi dge las gzhan pa lung ma bstan yin no/ / 'o na bsam gtan bzhi pa dang gzugs med pa'i dge ba'ang lung ma bstan du 'gyur te/ bde mi bde gnyis ka mi myong ba'i las yin pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ ma yin te/ sa de dag gi dge ba ni nye bar zhi ba'i bde ba myong ba'i las yin pa'i phyir ram/ yang na bde ba myong 'gyur dge ba yin no zhes bya ba ni phal che ba'i dbang du byas so zhes shes par bya'o/ / yang de bzhin du

That which gives rise to karmic maturation that is temporary, pleasant, pleasurable experience, and the obtainment of nirvāṇa, which eternally protects from suffering, is virtue. Karma that gives rise to maturation that is unpleasant, painful experience is nonvirtue. Karma that gives rise to experience that is other than pleasant or unpleasant is neutral and different from virtuous and nonvirtuous karma. Objection: But the virtue of the fourth absorption and the formless states is neutral because it is karma to be experienced as neither pleasure nor pain. Reply: That is not so; however, stating “The virtue of these levels is karma to be experienced as the bliss of peace” or “virtue to be experienced as bliss” is from the predominant perspective.[1134] So too,

mdo las bsod nams dang bsod nams min pa dang mi g.yo ba'i las gsum dang*/ bde ba myong bar 'gyur ba dang sogs pa'i sgras gzung ba sdug bsngal myong bar 'gyur ba dang gnyis ka ma yin pa myong bar 'gyur ba gsum yang gsungs so/ /

the sūtras also state three types of karma: (1) meritorious (puṇya), (2) nonmeritorious (apuṇya), and (3) invariable (āniñjya) karma, and the three: (1) karma to be experienced as pleasure (sukhavedya) and so on, which includes (2) karma to be experienced as pain and (3) karma to be experienced as neither pleasure nor pain.[1135]
bsod nams 'dod khams dge ba'i las/ / mi g.yo gong ma las skyes pa'i/ / gang phyir sa ni de dag tu/ / las rnams smin phyir mi g.yo'i phyir/ / 46
Merit is virtuous karma of the desire realm. Invariable karma is virtue arising in higher realms. Because it is karma that matures on its level and it invariably matures there. (4:46)

de la re zhig bsod nams ni 'dod pa'i khams su gtog pa'i dge ba'i las yin la/ mi g.yo ba'i las ni 'dod pa'i gong ma gzugs dang gzugs med las skyes pa'i dge ba yin no/ / 'o na mdo las/ 'di la rnam par brtags pa dang rnam par dpyad pa gang yin pa 'di ni 'dir 'phags pa rnams kyis g.yo ba'o zhes gsungs so zhes bsam gtan dang po gsum g.yo bar gsungs pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/ der ni bsam gtan gyi skyon gyis g.yo bar bshad de/ dang po la ni rtog dpyod dag gis g.yo ba yin zhing*/ gnyis pa la ni yid dga' ba dang ma bral bas g.yo ba yin la/ gsum pa ni bde ba la bde'o snyam pa 'phags pa rnams kyis g.yo bar bshad pa'i phyir dang*/ bzhi pa ni de dag gis g.yo ba med par bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dir ni rnam par smin pa mi g.yo ba'i phyir bsam gtan dang po la sogs pa'ang mi g.yo bar bshad do/ / ji ltar mi g.yo zhe na/

Here merit (puṇya) is virtuous (śubha) karma belonging to the desire realm, and invariable (āniñjya) karma is virtue arising in the form and formless realms, which are higher than the desire realm. Objection: But a sūtra states: In this regard āryas say that investigation and analysis move [the mind],[1136] and this would contradict the statement that karma is invariable in the first three absorptions. Reply: Here it is called “variable” due to the defects of absorption. In the first absorption the mind fluctuates due to investigation and analysis, in the second absorption the mind fluctuates due to not being separated from mental joy, and in the third absorption the mind fluctuates due to āryas thinking “pleasure is blissful,” but in the fourth absorption it does not fluctuate due to these. In this context [karma] is explained to be invariable from the first absorption on up because its maturation is invariable. [345] Question: How is its karmic maturation invariable?

gang gi phyir bsam gtan dang gzugs med pa'i las dge ba ni rnam par smin pa rang rang gi sa de dag tu las kyi 'bras bu rnam par smin pa'i phyir dang sa gzhan du rnam par smin pa mi g.yo ba'i phyir te/ {gzhan yang lus dang longs spyod du 'gyur ba'i las lha'i nang du smin par 'gyur ba ni res 'ga' las dang nyon mongs dang smon lam la sogs pa'i mthus mi dang dud 'gro dang yi dwags rnams su smin par 'gyur ba yod de } 'di ltar 'dod pa na spyod pa'i las dge ba ni 'gro ba gzhan gyi las dge ba'ang 'gro ba gzhan du rnam par smin pa'i phyir te/ mdo las 'di ste/ 'di na la la sbyin pa po yin zhing sbyin bdag yin la de shin tu srog gcod pa yin zhes bya ba nas de glang po cher gyur na glang po che'i rgyan rnam pa sna tshogs pa dag 'thob par 'gyur ro zhes bya ba'i bar du gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ de bzhin du yang 'di lta ste/ 'di na la la sbyin pa las byung ba'i bsod nams bya ba'i dngos po dang tshul khrims las byung ba dang bsgoms pa las byung ba chung ngu kun tu bsten cing bsgoms pa dang lan mang du byas pa yin la/ de 'di snyam du bdag lha bzang po rnams sam mi bzang po rnams dang skal ba mnyam par skye bar gyur na ci ma rung snyam du sems na zhes pa nas de ni der skye'o zhes bya ba'i bar du gsungs pa'i phyir rkyen gyi stobs kyis lha yang lha'i ris gzhan dang*/ lha'i nang du myong bar 'gyur ba de mi dang dud 'gro dang yi dwags kyi nang du rnam par smin par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / bsam gtan dang po la sogs pa ni sa de pa'i dge ba sa de dag kho nar smin pa'i phyir rnam par smin pa mi g.yo ba yin no/ / bsod nams ma yin pa'i las ni mi dge ba yin par grags pa'i phyir ma bshad do/ /

Reply: Because when virtuous karma of the absorptions and the formless realm matures, it is the result of karma that matures on its own specific level, and it invariably matures there and not in other levels. {Again, the karma that would mature among the [desire] gods, as a divine body and resources, sometimes matures among humans, animals, and ghosts by the might of karma, affliction, prayer, and so on.} Thus virtuous karmic action in the desire realm, which is the virtuous karma of one reincarnating being, may mature in another destiny. As it says in a sūtra: It is just like that, since some who are patrons and sponsors who frequently take life become elephants possessing the various ornaments of an elephant.[1137] Also, similarly: It is just like that, since some who properly serve, meditate, and frequently practice that which produces merit derived from giving, derived from ethics, and derived from meditation may think, “Would there be any harm in my being born with fortune equal to a pure god or pure human?” up to thinking, “I am born there.”[1138] Therefore, due to the power of conditions, karma to be experienced as a god, or by a different type of god, or among gods may mature among humans, animals, or ghosts. However, because the virtue of a specific level such as the first absorption and so on matures on that level alone, it is invariable karmic maturation. Nonmeritorious karma is not explained here because it is well known as nonvirtuous karma.
bsam gtan gsum pa'i bar dge ba/ / bde ba myong 'gyur de yan chad/ / sdug min bde min myong 'gyur ba/ / sdug bsngal myong 'gyur 'di'i mi dge / 47
Virtue up to the third absorption is experienced as pleasure. That above is experienced as neither pleasure nor pain. That experienced as pain is nonvirtue of this realm. (4:47)

'dod pa nas bsam gtan gsum pa'i bar gyi dge ba ni bde ba myong bar 'gyur ba'i las zhes bya ste/ sa de dag na tshor ba bde ba yod pa'i phyir dang*/ de yang dge ba kho na las skyes pa'i phyir ro/ / bsam gtan gsum pa de yan chad bsam gtan bzhi pa dang gzugs med pa dag gi dge ba ni sdug bsngal yang min bde ba'ang min pa btang snyoms myong bar 'gyur ba'i las te/ sa de dag na tshor ba de dag med pa'i phyir dang*/ btang snyoms yod pa'i phyir ro/ / sdug bsngal myong bar 'gyur ba'i las ni 'dod pa'i khams 'di'i mi dge ba yin no/ / 'di dag kyang tshor ba 'ba' zhig pa ni ma yin te/ dbang po dang yul dang rnam par shes pa'i tshogs dang bcas pa'o/ / 'di'i zhes smros pa ni 'dod khams kho na na mi dge ba yod par bstan pa'i phyir ro/ / mi dge ba smros pa ni dge ba dang lung ma bstan bsal ba'i phyir ro/ /

Virtue (śubha) from the desire realm up to the third absorption is called “karma to be experienced as pleasure” (sukhavedya) because blissful feeling exists on those levels and it is generated from virtue alone. Virtue of the fourth absorption and the formless realm — which are above the third absorption — is karma to be experienced as neither pleasure nor pain (aduḥkhāsukhavedya) but as equanimity because on those levels those feelings do not exist but equanimity does. Karma to be experienced as pain (duḥkhavedya) is the nonvirtue of this desire realm. Also [such karmic outcomes] are not [instances of] feeling alone because they are associated with faculties, objects, and consciousness. The term “of this” (4:47d) indicates that nonvirtue exists in the desire realm alone, while “nonvirtue” (4:47d) excludes virtuous and neutral states.
'og na'ang bar ma yod do zhes/ / kha cig zer te gang gi phyir/ / bsam gtan khyad par rnam smin las/ / snga phyi med gsum smin 'dod phyir/ / 48
Some say intermediate equanimity even exists below. That is because special absorption has karmic maturation; three karmic maturations are said to occur simultaneously. (4:48)

bsam gtan bzhi pa'i 'og ma gsum pa la sogs pa rnams na'ang bar ma btang snyoms myong bar 'gyur ba'i las yod do zhes sngon gyi slob dpon kha cig zer te/ ci'i phyir zhe na/ gang gi phyir te 'di ltar bsam gtan dang po'i dngos gzhi khyad par can ni tshor ba btang snyoms kyi sa pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ de yang dge ba'i las kyi rnam smin yin pa'i gtan tshigs las shes pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di la'ang rgyu ni snyoms 'jug khyad par can gyi ting nge 'dzin dang*/ 'bras bu ni skye ba'i bsam gtan khyad par can yin no zhes bya bar mngon no/ / de lta ma yin na {de na bde sdug kyang med pas de'i rgyu } snyoms 'jug zag bcas kyi bsam gtan khyad par can la rnam par smin pa med pa'am {dang po'i dngos gzhi ni dman zhing sa tha dad pa'i phyir } skye ba'i bsam gtan khyad par can du las gang gis kyang rnam par smin par mi 'gyur bar thal ba'i phyir ro/ / sngon gyi slob dpon kha cig ni bsam gtan khyad par can gyi rnam smin ni bsam gtan dang po'i mig gi rnam shes la sogs pa gsum gyi 'khor du byung ba'i bde ba'i dbang po yin no/ / zhes zer ro/ /

Some past masters say: Karma to be experienced as intermediate (madhyam) equanimity even exists in the three levels below the fourth absorption and so on. Question: Why? Reply: That is because the special actual basis of the first absorption is the level of the feeling of equanimity, and it should be understood [346] from logical proofs that such equanimity is the karmic maturation (vipāka) of virtuous karma. Further, its cause is the concentration of special meditative attainment (samāpatti), and its result is the special absorption arising from birth. If that were not so, it would follow that {causal} contaminated meditative attainment that is special absorption would have no karmic maturation, {since pleasure and pain do not exist there,} or that karma would possess no karmic maturation at all in the special absorption arising from birth {because the actual basis of the first absorption is of inferior or different level}. One past master says: The karmic maturation of special absorption is the faculty of pleasure that occurs in the retinue of any three such as eye consciousness of the first absorption.[1139]

kha cig ni sa de na rnam smin gyi tshor ba ni med kyi 'on kyang tshor ba btang snyoms pa gang ji snyed pa de ni rgyu mthun las byung ba yin no zhes zer ro/ / de gnyis ka'ang bstan bcos dang 'gal te/ rab tu byed pa las/ las kyi rnam par smin pa sems kyi tshor ba kho na rnam par smin par 'gyur ba yod dam zhe na yod de/ rtog pa med pa'i las dge ba yin no zhes 'byung ste/ rtog pa med pa'i las dge ba ni bsam gtan khyad par can yan chad na yod de dang po'i dngos gzhi man chad rtog pa dang bcas pa'i phyir dang*/ dang po'i dngos gzhi khyad par can yan chad na rtog pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir lung 'di las ni bsam gtan khyad par can gyi las la rnam smin yod cing de yang sems kyi tshor ba yin par bstan pa'i phyir sa de na btang snyoms myong bar 'gyur ba'i las yod par shes so/ /

Some say: Indeed, on that level there is no feeling that is karmic maturation, but any feeling of equanimity that arises is derived from natural outflow.[1140] Reply: Both of these contradict the treatise because Topic Divisions[1141] articulates: Is there karmic maturation that matures as mental feeling alone? Yes, it is virtuous karma not associated with investigation.[1142] Virtuous karma not associated with investigation exists on the special [first] absorption and above because the actual basis of the first absorption and below possesses investigation, and states [on and] above the special actual basis of the first absorption do not. Therefore one understands from this citation that the karma of special absorption has maturation and that it is mental feeling. Thus, due to this, karma to be experienced as equanimity exists on that level.

yang bstan bcos las snga phyi med par las gsum gyi rnam par smin pa smin par 'dod pa'i phyir yang 'og 'dod pa na'ang btang snyoms myong bar 'gyur ba'i las yod par shes te/ bstan bcos ye shes la 'jug pa las/ 'di ltar las gsum po rnams kyi rnam par smin pa snga phyi med par rnam par smin par 'gyur ba yod dam zhe na/ yod de/ bde ba myong bar 'gyur ba ni gzugs so/ / sdug bsngal myong bar 'gyur ba ni sems dang sems las byung ba'i chos rnams so/ / bde ba yang ma yin sdug bsngal yang ma yin pa myong bar 'gyur ba ni sems dang ldan pa ma yin pa'i 'du byed rnams so zhes 'byung ba'i phyir te/ sa gzhan na sdug bsngal myong bar 'gyur ba'i las med pa'i phyir ro/ / lung gi don yang bde ba myong bar 'gyur ba ni gzugs so zhes bya ba ni mtho ris kyi mig la sogs pa'o/ / sdug bsngal myong bar 'gyur ba ni sems dang sems las byung ba'i chos rnams so zhes bya ba ni rnam shes tshogs lnga'i sdug bsngal gyi dbang po ste/ yid mi bde ba ni rnam par smin pa ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / bde ba yang ma yin sdug bsngal ba yang ma yin pa myong bar 'gyur ba ni sems dang ldan pa ma yin pa'i 'du byed rnams so zhes bya ba ni srog gi dbang po la sogs pa'o/ / 'di yang dge ba stobs chung ba'i dbang du byas pa yin te/ stobs chen sems dang sems las byung ba'ang bde ba myong bar 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ mi dge bas bde ba myong bar 'gyur ba mi srid pa'i phyir dang*/ lung ma bstan la rnam smin med pa'i phyir ro/ / des na 'og na btang snyoms myong 'gyur gyi las yod de/ 'dod pa las gzhan na las gsum gyi rnam smin snga phyi med par dus cig car smin pa med pa'i phyir ro/ /

Again, it should be understood that because it is said in the treatise that the three karmic maturations occur simultaneously, karma to be experienced as equanimity exists even in the lower realm of desire. The treatise Attainment of Knowledge states: Is the maturation of the three karmas simultaneous karmic maturation? Yes it is, because the experience of pleasure is form, the experience of pain is the mind and mental factors, and the experience of neither pleasure nor pain is a nonassociated formative factor.[1143] That is because there is no karma to be experienced as pain on other levels. Also, regarding the meaning of that quotation, “the experience of pleasure is form” refers to the eye and so on of higher rebirth; “the experience of pain is the mind and mental factors” refers to the faculty of pain of the fivefold collection of sense consciousness, although mental dissatisfaction is not karmic maturation; and “the experience of neither pleasure nor pain is a nonassociated formative factor” [347] refers to the power of life force and so on. Further, this is from the perspective of virtue that is weak because: strong minds and mental factors experience pleasure, it is impossible to experience pleasure through nonvirtue, and neutral states have no karmic maturation. Therefore the karma to be experienced as equanimity exists on lower levels because there is no simultaneous karmic maturation that is karmic maturation of the three karmas in realms other than in the desire realm.

'o na bsam gtan gsum pa'i bar dge ba/ bde ba myong 'gyur zhes bya ba dang*/ rnam par smin pa yid du 'ong ba ni dge ba yin no zhes bshad pa dang 'gal bar 'gyur te/ btang snyoms myong 'gyur gyi dge ba'ang yod pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ bstan pa de dag ni phal che ba'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi cung zad yod do zhes bya ba ni grub pa'i mtha'o/ /
gal te las de dag tshor ba'i ngo bo ma yin na bde ba myong bar 'gyur ba la sogs par ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/ bde ba'i tshor ba myong bar byed pa'i las yin pa'i phyir 'bras bu'i ming gis btags nas bde ba myong 'gyur gyi las zhes bya ste 'khru bar byed pa'i 'dag chal la 'khru ba'i 'dag chal zhes brjod pa bzhin no/ / de bzhin du sdug bsngal myong 'gyur la sogs pa la'ang brjod par bya'o/ /

Objection: That contradicts the explanations “Virtue up to the third absorption is experienced as pleasure” and “Pleasant karmic maturation is from virtue” because virtue to be experienced as equanimity exists. Reply: The final position would be “Such explanations are from the general perspective, but some [counter-instances] exist.”
Question: If those karmas are not by nature feeling, how would the experience of pleasure and so on occur? Reply: This is because karma that creates the experience of blissful feeling is called “karma to be experienced as pleasure” through imputing the name of the result [to its cause]. It is like detergent that creates a clean state being called “cleaning detergent.” So too, there is “karma to be experienced as pain.”
gnyis pa myong 'gyur gyi dbye ba ni
Karma to be experienced
ngo bo nyid dang mtshungs ldan dang / / dmigs pa dang ni rnam smin dang / / mngon sum du ni gyur pa las/ / myong 'gyur rnam pa lnga yin no/ / 49
Karma to be experienced has five types: its own nature, concomitance, focal object, maturation, and as a manifest state. (4:49)

gzhan yang myong bar 'gyur ba ni rnam pa lnga yin no zhes sbyar te/ gang zhe na ngo bo nyid kyis myong bar 'gyur ba tshor ba dang*/ mtshungs ldan gyis myong bar 'gyur ba ni reg pa ste/ bde ba myong bar 'gyur ba'i reg pa zhes gsungs pa lta bu dang*/ dmigs pa myong bar 'gyur ba ni yul rnams te/ mdo las mig gis gzugs rnams mthong nas gzugs so sor yang dag par myong bar 'gyur gyi gzugs la 'dod chags so sor yang dag par myong ba ni ma yin no zhes gsungs pa lta bu dang*/ rnam par smin pa myong bar 'gyur ba ni mthong ba'i chos la myong bar 'gyur ba'i las zhes bya ba la sogs pa lta bu dang*/ mngon sum du gyur pa myong bar 'gyur ba las ni gleng gzhi chen po'i chos kyi rnam grangs las/ gang gi tshe bde ba'i tshor ba myong bar byed pa de'i tshe de'i tshor ba gnyis 'gag par 'gyur ro zhes gsungs pa lta bu'o/ /

Again, karma to be experienced has five types. Question: Why? Reply: (1) Karma to be experienced by its own nature (svabhāva) is feeling. (2) Karma to be experienced by concomitance (saṃprayoga) is contact, such as stating “contact experienced as pleasure.” (3) Karma to be experienced as a focal object (ālambana) is an object because, for example, a sūtra declares: Through the eyes seeing form, form comes to be separately and correctly experienced, but through attachment to form, form does not come to be separately and correctly experienced.[1144] (4) Karma to be experienced as maturation (vipāka) is called “karma to be experienced in the current life.” (5) Karma that is to be experienced as a manifest state (saṃmukhī) is described in the Enumeration of Great Precendents: Whenever the feeling of pleasure is experienced, at that time two feelings are stopped.[1145]
des na dang po ni tshor ba spyi dang lnga pa ni bye brag myong ba'o/ / de ltar na myong 'gyur rnam pa lnga las 'dir ni rnam smin myong 'gyur yin no/ /
The first is general feeling and the fifth is specific feeling. But from the five types of experience, in this context karma to be experienced refers to karmic maturation.
de yang nges dang ma nges dang / / mthong ba'i chos la sogs pa la/ / myong 'gyur phyir na nges rnam gsum/ / kha cig las rnam lnga zhes zer/ / 50

Further, there is karma certain or uncertain to be experienced. Karma certain to be experienced has three aspects because there is karma to be experienced in the current life and so on. Some say that karma has five types. (4:50)

gong du bshad pa'i bde ba myong 'gyur la sogs pa'i las rnam pa gsum po gang yin pa de yang myong bar nges pa dang myong bar ma nges pa gnyis/ nges pa la'ang mthong ba'i chos skye ba de nyid la myong bar 'gyur ba dang*/ sogs pa'i sgras bzung ba skye ba phyi ma kho na la myong ba skyes nas myong bar 'gyur ba dang*/ skye ba yang phyi phan chad la myong ba lan grangs gzhan la myong bar 'gyur ba gsum yod pa'i phyir na myong bar nges pa'ang rnam pa gsum ste de ltar na nges pa gsum ma nges pa dang bzhi yin no/ /

Further, any of the three aspects of karma previously explained, such as karma to be experienced as pleasure and so on, has two types: (1) karma certain (niyata) to be experienced and (2) karma uncertain (aniyata) to be experienced. Karma certain to be experienced also has three aspects because there is (1.1) karma to be experienced in the current life (dṛṣṭadharma) itself where “and so on” refers to (1.2) karma to be experienced [348] after rebirth that is experienced only in the next life and (1.3) karma to be experienced in a third life that is experienced in a later birth again. Thus there are four: three that are certain to be experienced plus one that is uncertain to be experienced.

sngon gyi slob dpon kha cig ni myong bar 'gyur ba ma nges pa la'ang rnam par smin pa nges pa dang ma nges pa gnyis su phye nas las rnam pa lnga yin no zhes zer te/ 'di'i myong bar nges pa ni mthong ba'i chos la sogs pa gnas skabs nges pa'o/ /

Some past masters say that karma has five types due to classifying karma uncertain to be experienced in two: (2.1) karma whose maturation is certain and (2.2) karma whose maturation is uncertain.[1146] Karma whose maturation is certain is determined in accordance with the time, such as the current life and so on.

{mdo sde pa la sogs pa de lta na mthong chos la myong 'gyur gyi las ni las stobs ldan yin kyang 'bras bu chung bar 'gyur te/ dus thung ba'i phyir ro/ / des na de'i rnam smin ni tshe rabs gzhan na'ang yod mod kyi myong ba'i 'go 'di nas rtsom pas mthong chos la myong 'gyur du gzhag go zhes zer ro/ / bye brag smra ba de mi 'thad de/ de lta na las gsum gyi dus nges pa mi 'thad par thal bas so/ / 'bras bu nye ba ni las kyi rigs las yin gyis stobs che bas min te/ phyi'i sa bon bzhin no/ / zhes zer ro }

{Sautrāntikas and so on say: Thus karma to be experienced in the current life is strong karma, but its result is weak because its duration is short. Though indeed its karmic maturation also may continue in another life, it is posited as the experience of the current life since the primary experience commences in this life. Vaibhāṣikas say that this is untenable because it would follow that the certainty of the time of the three karmas would not be tenable. Further, the proximity of the result is determined by the type of karma and not its strength, like an external seed.}
gzhan dag mu ni bzhi zhes zer/ / gsum gyis rigs ni 'phen par byed/ / thams cad na ni 'phen pa bzhi/ / dmyal ba na ni dge ba'i gsum/ / 51
Others say there are four possibilities. Three project the same type. The four projecting karmas exist in all. In the hells, three virtuous karmas exist. (4:51)

dpes ston pa ni sde pa gzhan dag ni gnas skabs myong bar nges pa dang*/ ma nges pa dang*/ rnam smin myong bar nges pa dang*/ ma nges pa gnyis yod pa'i phyir de dag mu ni rnam pa bzhi yin no zhes zer ro/ / de la gnas skabs nges la rnam smin myong bar ma nges pa ni gal te myong na mthong ba'i chos la myong 'gyur la sogs pa yin la rnam par smin pa ni ma nges pa yin no/ / rnam par smin par ni nges la gnas skabs ma nges pa ni rnam smin ni gdon mi za bar myong la/ mthong ba'i chos la sogs pa ni ma nges pa yin no/ / gnyis ka nges pa ni mthong chos la rnam smin myong bar nges pa la sogs pa lta bu'o/ / gnyis ka ma nges pa ni gnas skabs kyang ma nges la rnam smin yang myong bar ma nges pa'o/ / de'i ltar na nges pa la mthong chos la sogs pa la nges ma nges gnyis gnyis te drug dang ma nges pa la rnam smin ma nges pa dang gnas skabs ma nges pa dang gnyis te las rnam pa brgyad du 'gyur ro/ / kha cig ni mthong chos la myong 'gyur gyi las ni las stobs ldan yin pa'i phyir rnam smin skyes nas myong ba la sogs pa'ang yod de/ gzhan du na las che ba'i 'bras bu chung bar thal ba'i phyir ro/ / 'o na mthong chos la myong 'gyur du 'gal lo snyam na/ de ni thog mar 'go rtsom pa'i dbang gis ming der rnam par bzhag pa'i phyir ro zhes 'dod do/ /

Others, such as the Dārṣṭāntika sect, say there are four possibilities because there is both karma certain to be experienced and karma uncertain to be experienced at a specific time, and karma certain to be experienced and karma uncertain to be experienced as maturation. (1) Karma certain to be experienced at a specific time but uncertain to be experienced as maturation is karma that, if experienced, is experienced in the current life and so on but whose maturation is uncertain. (2) Karma certain to be experienced as maturation but uncertain to be experienced at a specific time is maturation that without doubt will be experienced but may or may not be experienced in the current life and so on. (3) Karma that is both certain to be experienced at a specific time and certain to be experienced as maturation is, for example, karma certain to be experienced as maturation in the current life. (4) Karma that lacks either certainty is karma that is neither certain to be experienced at a specific time nor certain to be experienced as maturation. Thus, for karma certain to be experienced, there are six — both karma certain and karma uncertain to be experienced in the current life and so on; and for karma uncertain to be experienced there are two — karma uncertain to be experienced as maturation and karma uncertain to be experienced at a specific time; [and all of these together] make [a total of] eight. Some say: Because karma to be experienced in the current life is strong karma, karmic maturation would even be experienced after rebirth and so on. Otherwise it would follow that karma of great strength would have a weak result.
