But if you think this contradicts it being karma to be experienced in the current life, then we assert that it is, because it was posited with that name in the beginning, freely.

bye brag tu smra ba ni las kyi rang bzhin tha dad pa'i phyir mthong chos la myong ba ni skyes nas myong ba la sogs pa ma yin te/ dper na lcam pa la sogs pa zla ba phyed dang gnyis na 'bras bu smin la nas dang gro la sogs pa zla ba drug na smin pa bzhin no zhes bya bar 'dod do/ /

Vaibhāṣikas assert that because [different] karmas are distinct in nature, karma to be experienced in the current life is not experienced after rebirth and so on. For example, the fruit of the campa[1147] and so forth ripens in one and a half months, and barley, wheat, and so on ripen in six months.

skyes nas myong 'gyur la sogs pa gsum gyis ni {skye ba gzhan gyi } ris mthun pa'i srog gi dbang po 'phen{ cing rdzogs} par byed pa srid kyi mthong chos la myong 'gyur gyis ni ma yin te/ skye ba de'i srog gi dbang po ni sngar thob zin pa'i phyir dang*/ {skye ba gzhan nas 'phangs pa'i} skye ba gzhan gyis 'phen na mthong chos la myong 'gyur ma yin par thal ba'i phyir ro/ / {des na gzhan gyis 'phangs pa'i ris mthun de nyid du 'bras bu 'byin par byed do } bsod nams bsags pas tshe sring ba la sogs pa'ang bar chad sel ba tsam du zad pa'i phyir ro/ / rnam smin ni bzhi gas kyang 'phen par byed do/ / gal te las bzhis rnam smin 'phen pa {skye ba gzhan nas 'phangs pa'i }khams dang sa thams cad na yod dam zhe na/

It is possible that the three to be experienced after rebirth and so on project (kṣepaṇa) {and complete} the faculty of life force of the same type (nikāya) {in other births,} but karma to be experienced in the current life does not do that because the faculty of life force of that birth has already been obtained. And if it is projected in another life, {itself projected from another life,} [349] it would follow that it would not be something to be experienced in the current life. {Therefore something of the same type that was projected in another life produces a result in that life.} Through the accumulation of merit, lifespan is extended and so on, and also obstacles are eliminated. Thus karmic maturation is projected by these four karmas. Question: Do the four karmas that project karmic maturation exist on all levels or not?

khams gsum dang sa dgu dang 'gro ba lnga po thams cad na ni dge mi dge'i las kyi 'phen pa bzhi car yod do zhes bya ba ni spyir btang ba'o/ / dmigs kyis bsal ba ni dmyal ba na ni las dge ba'i skyes nas myong 'gyur la sogs pa gsum yod kyi mthong chos la myong ba ni med de/ de na rnam smin yid du 'ong ba med pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir mi dge ba'i ni bzhi ga'ang yod do/ /

Reply: In general the four virtuous and nonvirtuous projecting karmas exist in all three realms, nine levels, and five reincarnating beings. The exception is that in the hells, three virtuous karmas to be experienced after rebirth and so on exist but karma to be experienced in the current life does not exist, because pleasant karmic maturation does not exist there. Therefore also four nonvirtuous karmas exist.
gang las 'dod chags bral brtan pa'i/ / byis pa der skyes myong mi byed/ / 'phags pa gzhan du'ang myong mi byed/ / 'dod rtse'i mi brtan pa yang min/ / 52

Childlike beings with stable nonattachment to any level do not produce karma to be experienced. Āryas do not produce karma to be experienced in other lives. Also āryas with unstable nonattachment for the desire realm and summit do not. (4:52)

'dod pa la sogs pa'i sa gang las 'dod chags dang bral ba brtan pa ste yongs su mi nyams pa'i chos can gyi byis pa so so'i skye bo rnams ni 'dod pa la sogs pa'i sa der skyes nas myong bar 'gyur ba'i las mi byed de/ de ni skye ba phyi ma la sogs pa la sa gong ma kho nar skye bar nges pa'i phyir ro/ / mthong chos la myong ba la sogs pa gsum ni byed do/ /

Ordinary beings who are childlike beings with stable (sthira), nondegenerating nonattachment (virakta) to any level, such as the desire-realm level and so on, do not produce karma to be experienced after rebirth on the desire-realm level and so forth because it is certain they will be born only on the higher levels in their next life and so on. They produce the three karmas to be experienced in the current life and so forth.

Ārya beings with {stable} nondegenerating nonattachment to the desire realm and any {of the seven intermediate} levels,[1148] not only do not produce karma to be experienced after rebirth, they do not produce karma to be experienced in other lives, such as in lives after the next, because they do not return again to those levels. They produce karma certain or uncertain to be experienced in the current life. Childlike beings, or āryas whose nonattachment has degenerated, produce karma to be experienced after rebirth and karma to be experienced in other lives. {Further, it is also explained that when āryas who obtain the mind of the summit of existence degenerate, they are born in the form realm.}

'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba dang srid rtse las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i 'phags pa ni mi brtan pa yongs su nyams pa'i chos can yin yang skyes nas myong 'gyur dang lan grangs gzhan la myong 'gyur gyi las byed pa min te/ 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba phyir mi 'ong ba dang srid rtse las 'dod chags dang bral ba dgra bcom pa'i 'bras bu la gnas pa yin pa na 'bras bu las nyams pa ni 'bras las nyams pa 'chi ba med ces 'byung bas nges par sor chud par byed pas khyab pa'i phyir ro/ / {ma nges pa dang mthong chos la myong 'gyur byed pa ni srid do/ / thams cad na 'phen pa bzhi yod na } ci srid pa bar ma na'ang las kyi 'phen pa yod dam zhe na/

Āryas who become unstable and lose nonattachment [i.e., become attached] to the desire realm and nonattachment to the summit of existence also do not produce karma to be experienced after rebirth, or karma to be experienced in other lives, because abiding in the result of nonreturn free from attachment to the desire realm — or the result of an arhat free from attachment to the summit of existence — definitely restores any degeneration from such results, since it is said: “Those who degenerate from their result do not die” (6:60a). {It is possible they produce karma uncertain to be experienced and karma to be experienced in the current life. Question: If the four projecting causes exist for all beings,} do intermediate beings also have projecting causes of karma?
srid pa bar ma 'dod khams su/ / 'phen pa rnam pa nyi shu gnyis/ / de ni mthong chos 'bras bu yin/ / de ni rigs gcig kho na yin/ / 53
Intermediate beings have twenty-two types projected in the desire realm. They are results to be experienced in the current life. They are of the same type alone. (4:53)
yod de
[Reply:] Yes,

'dod pa'i srid pa bar ma ni 'dod pa'i khams su 'phen pa rnam pa nyi shu rtsa gnyis 'phen par byed de/ 'di ltar nur nur po dang*/ mer mer po dang*/ nar nar po dang*/ gor gor po dang*/ rkang lag 'gyus pa'i gnas skabs te mngal gyi gnas skabs lnga dang*/ byis pa dang gzhon nu dang*/ dar la bab pa dang*/ dar yol ba dang*/ rgan po'i gnas skabs te skyes pa'i gnas skabs lnga ste bcu'o/ / de ltar bcu po dang myong bar nges pa dang ma nges pa gnyis gnyis su phye ba'i phyir dang*/ srid pa bar ma rang nyid du myong bar nges pa dang ma nges pa gnyis spyod pa'i phyir ro/ / de dag las myong bar nges pa'i las bcu gcig po de dag ni mthong ba'i chos la myong bar 'gyur ba'i 'bras bu can zhes bya ba yin no/ / ci'i phyir zhe na/ srid pa bar ma dang de'i nges pa'i 'bras bu gnas skabs bcu gcig po {de ni 'phen pa gcig pa'i phyir zhes pas/ byis pa nas rgan po'i bar ltar skyes nas myong 'gyur kho nas 'phangs pas} de dag ni ris mthun pa gcig kho na yin{ pa'i phyir} te/ de dag ni skyes nas myong 'gyur gyi las gcig kho nas 'phangs pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir srid pa bar ma des na bar srid myong bar 'gyur ba'i las gzhan ma bshad do/ / {'di blo mi gsal bas las gzhan gnyis ni mi byed do zhes gsungs te mi zlog par 'dod pas so } myong bar ma nges pa ni bshad zin to/ / 'dod khams su zhes bya ba ni gzugs khams na nur nur po la sogs pa'i gnas skabs bcu po nyid med pa'i phyir dang*/ gzugs med na bar srid kyang med pa'i phyir ro/ / myong bar nges pa'i las gang zhe na/

intermediate beings of the desire realm have projecting causes of the twenty-two types projected in the desire realm. They include the five stages of the womb: (1) kalala, (2) arbuda, (3) peśin, (4) ghana, and (5) praśakhā, and five [350] stages post-birth: (6) child, (7) youth, (8) adult, (9) middle-aged, and (10) elder. These ten are divided into two each: (1–10) karmas certain to be experienced, and (11–20) karmas uncertain to be experienced. And intermediate beings have two types: (21) karma certain to be experienced, and (22) karma uncertain to be experienced. From among them, the eleven karmas certain to be experienced are called “karmas possessing results to be experienced in the current life (dṛṣṭadharma).” Question: Why? Reply: These eleven stages from (1) the intermediate being and (2–11) its karmic results are certain to be experienced {because} they are of the same type (nikāya) alone. {They are projected by karma to be experienced after rebirth from the stage of child to elder, in accordance with the statement “it shares the same projecting karma” (3:13b),} because they are projected by one karma that is to be experienced after rebirth alone. Thus it is said that the intermediate being has no other karma to be experienced as an intermediate being, {and this assertion is irrefutable since it is said, “The other two karmas are not produced since their mind is unclear.”} Thus karma that is uncertain to be experienced has been explained. “In the desire realm” (4:53b) was stated because the ten stages of kalala and so on do not exist in the form realm, and there is also no intermediate being in the formless realm. Question: What is karma that is certain to be experienced?
nyon mongs rab dang drag po dang / / yon tan zhing dang rgyun chags su/ / byas pa gang zhig yin pa dang / / pha ma gsod gang de nges so/ / 54
Karmic maturation is certain for strong affliction, clear faith, fields possessing qualities, any actions continuously engaging virtue or nonvirtue, or killing one’s mother or father. (4:54)

kun slong nyon mongs pa drag pos byas pa'i mi dge ba dang rab tu dwang ba drag pos byas pa'i dge ba {gang yin pa de ni bsam pa'i stobs kyis rnam smin nges pa } dang*/ kun slong nyon mongs dang rab tu dwang ba drag po'ang med la rgyun du byed pa'ang med kyang dkon mchog gsum dang 'bras bu khyad par can rgyun zhugs dang dgra bcom pa'i 'bras bu la gnas pa dang*/ snyoms 'jug khyad par can 'gog pa dang byams pa dang nyon mongs pa med pa'i ting nge 'dzin la gnas pa'i yon tan gyi zhing {'og nas 'byung ba'i dkon mchog gsum dang 'gog pa sogs pa la gnas pa } la phan gnod byas pa dang*/ dge ba dang mi dge ba rgyun chags su byas pa gang zhig yin pa dang*/ de bzhin kun slong drag po dang rgyun du byed pa med kyang pha ma gsod pa'i las gang yin pa de par sig pa rnams kyi ltar bsod nams kyi blas byas kyang mtshams med du 'gyur bas na {kun slong gang gis byas kyang mtshams med du 'gyur bas } rnam par smin pa myong bar nges so/ / {de ltar na de dag ni zhing dang bsam pa dang sbyor ba gsum stobs dang ldan pas myong bar nges pa yin la } de dag las gzhan ni ma nges pa yin no/ / yang mthong chos la myong bar 'gyur ba'i las ci 'dra ba yin zhe na/

Reply: Karmic maturation is certain (1) for nonvirtue produced by strong afflicted motivation; (2) for {any} virtue produced by strong clear faith (prasāda), {where karmic maturation is definite due to the strength of the intention}; (3) for actions benefiting or harming fields (kṣetra) possessing excellent qualities (guṇa), such as the Three Jewels, those abiding in the special result of a stream enterer or the result of an arhat, and those abiding in the special meditative attainment of cessation, love, or unafflicted concentrations even though their motivation is not afflicted, not from clear faith, nor strong, nor even continuous; (4) for any actions continuously engaging virtue or nonvirtue; and, similarly, (5) for any karma of killing one’s mother or father even though there is no strong or continuous motivation. Though for some, such as cannibals, such actions can be committed with a meritorious mind, but it is karma certain to produce maturational experience since it is a heinous act, {for no matter what motivation arises, it is still a heinous act}. {Thus these are karmas certain to be experienced, since they possess three aspects: (1) potent field, (2) thought, and (3) application.} Question: Again, what is karma to be experienced in the current life?
mthong chos 'bras bu can gyi las/ / zhing dang bsam pa'i khyad par las/ / sa de'i 'dod chags gtan bral phyir/ / rnam smin nges pa gang yin pa'o/ / 55

Karma possessing a result in the current life arises from a superior field or superior thought. Because one is definitely free from attachment to this level. It is karma certain to be experienced as karmic maturation. (4:55)
mthong ba'i chos la myong bar 'gyur ba'i 'bras bu can gyi las ni zhing gi khyad par las 'gyur ba dang bsam pa'i khyad par las 'gyur ba gnyis so/ /
Reply: Karma possessing a result to be experienced in the current life has two types: (1) karma that arises from a superior field (kṣetra) and (2) karma that arises from a superior thought (āśaya).
de la zhing gi khyad par las 'gyur ba ni
KARMA THAT ARISES FROM A SUPERIOR FIELD

sngon 'das pa'i dus na sangs rgyas ma pham pa zhes bya ba'i bstan pa la ston pa 'di nyid phyug po'i bur gyur pa na bla na med pa'i byang chub tu sems bskyed cing rab tu byung nas sde snod gsum par gyur to/ / de'i tshe dge 'dun la rtsod pa byung ba la sde snod gsum pa des rtsod pa de slar 'phel bar byas pa dang*/ dge slong mdo sde 'dzin pa zhig gis sde snod gsum pa bton nas rtsod pa zhi bar byas pa dang*/ sde snod gsum pa khros te bud med rnams kyi rtsod pa zhi bar byas sam zhes tshig rtsub po smras pas de ma thag tu bud med du gyur cing slar yang skye ba lnga brgyar bud med du skyes so/ / phyis sangs rgyas rin chen gtsug tor can zhes bya ba la dad par byas pas skyes pa'i lus thob par gyur to/ / 'di nyid phran tshegs las/ sangs rgyas mang po'i rtogs pa brjod par/ / de nas sangs rgyas ma pham pa'i/ / sngon byung sde snod gsum par 'gyur/ / dge slong dge 'dun rtsod pa na/ / dge 'dun bud med ces brjod pa'i/ / ngag gi nyes par sbyang byas pas/ / bud med nyid du nye bar song*/ / slar yang sems rab dwang ba yis/ / skyes pa'i dngos po nyid du gyur/ / ces gsungs pa lta bu'o/ /

In a past era, in the dispensation of Buddha Ajita, the Master was the son of a wealthy family. He developed the mind awakening to highest enlightenment, took ordination, and [351] was called Tripiṭaka. At that time, a dispute erupted within the Saṅgha, and Tripiṭaka inflamed the dispute. A monk who was a holder of Sūtra expelled Tripiṭaka, and the dispute was pacified. Tripiṭaka then became annoyed and spoke harshly, stating, “You have pacified a dispute among women!” and immediately he became a woman and was reborn five hundred times a woman. Later, by developing faith in Buddha Ratnaśikhin, he obtained the body of a male. This is stated in the Kṣudraka, which expresses the knowledge of many buddhas: Then in a former time, when Buddha Ajita appeared, he was Tripiṭaka. Then when dispute arose among the monks, he called the Saṅgha women! To purify this fault of speech, he was born a woman. Then, through developing a mind of clear faith, he attained the state of a male.[1149]
bsam pa'i khyad par las 'gyur ba ni
KARMA THAT ARISES FROM A SPECIAL THOUGHT

sngon rgyal po ka nis ka'i nyug rum long ba zhes bya ba zhig gis mi zhig gis glang lnga brgya ded nas 'gro ba mthong nas ci byed dris pas 'bras bu 'byin to zhes zer ba na de bdag gis kyang sngon 'di lta bu byas pas da ltar sdug bsngal 'di lta bu myong la/ mi 'dis yang las 'di byas pas skye ba mang por bdag lta bur sdug bsngal myong bar 'gyur ro snyam nas glang de rnams nor gyis nyos te bsam pa drag pos 'bras bu 'byin pa las btang ba dang de la mthong ba'i chos de kho na la skyes pa'i dbang po byung ngo zhes grag pa lta bu'o/ /

Formerly, one called “King Kaniṣka’s blind eunuch” saw[1150] a man herding five hundred oxen and asked him, “What are you doing?” “I’m taking them to be castrated,” said the man. The eunuch thought, “I acted like you in the past, and now I experience suffering like this. If this man commits this action, like me he too will experience such suffering for many lives.” Therefore with intense conviction he bought the oxen with his own money, thus releasing them from the act of castration, and in that life itself regained his manhood.

yang na 'dod pa la sogs pa'i sa de'i dge mi dge las 'dod chags dang gtan du bral ba'i phyir phyin chad der mi skye bas yul 'pho ba na bu lon pa ldang ba ltar sa der myong bar nges pa'i las gzhan gang yin pa de'i 'bras bu ni mthong chos de kho na la myong bar 'gyur ro/{ de yang sngon byas pa'i las kyi 'bras bu 'dir myong na mthong chos la myong ba btags pa ba dang 'dir byas pa myong na mtshan nyid pa'o/ / myong 'gyur gyi/} las de yang ji lta bu zhe na/ de ni gnas skabs ma nges kyang rnam smin myong bar nges pa gang yin pa ste/ {de'i rnam smin ma myong na gtan du 'dod chags dang bral ba la gegs byed do } sa de las gtan du 'dod chags dang bral bas skyes nas myong gyur la sogs pa'ang ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / sa de'i las ma nges pa gang yin pa de ni gtan du 'dod chags dang bral ba'i phyir nam yang mi smin pa nyid do/ / 'o na gang la brten nas mthong chos la myong bar 'gyur ba'i zhing de ji lta bu zhe na/

Furthermore, one is not reborn [in the desire realm and so on] in the future because one is definitely free from attachment to the virtue and nonvirtue of this desire-realm level and so on. Therefore, when one relocates from there [at death], it is like being freed from debt, since the result of any other karma certain to be experienced on this level is experienced in the current life alone. {Further, if the result of karma previously committed is experienced here, it is provisional experience in the current life, but if that committed here is experienced [here], it is actual experience.} Question: Further, what is karma {to be experienced}? Reply: It is that karma uncertain to be experienced at a specific time but certain to be experienced as karmic maturation. {If its karmic maturation is not experienced, it is stopped through continuous freedom from attachment.} It is not karma to be experienced after rebirth and so on, since that being is continuously free from attachment to that level. Any karma of that level that is uncertain to be experienced will not mature, because that person has continuous nonattachment [to that level]. Question: However, in relation to what field is karma experienced in the current life?
gang dag 'gog byams nyon mongs med/ / mthong dang dgra bcom 'bras langs pa/ / de la phan gnod byas pa yi/ / 'bras bu 'phral du myong bar 'gyur/ / 56
The result of benefiting or harming those who have arisen from cessation, love, unafflicted states, seeing, or the resultant attainment of an arhat is immediately experienced. (4:56)

sangs rgyas la sogs pa dge slong gi dge 'dun dang gang zag yin yang 'phags pa gang dag 'gog pa dang byams pa dang nyon mongs pa med pa dang mthong ba'i lam dang dgra bcom pa'i 'bras bu la snyoms par zhugs pa las langs pa ste lnga po de dag la phan pa dang gnod pa byas pa'i rnam par smin pa'i 'bras bu ni 'phral du mthong chos kho na la myong bar 'gyur te/ 'gog pa las langs pa ni sems mchog tu zhi ba thob pas mya ngan las 'das pa las slar log pa dang 'dra ba'i phyir dang*/ nyon mongs pa med pa dang byams pa las langs pa ni sems can tshad med pa la nyon mongs pa med pa dang phan pa'i lhag pa'i bsam pa dang rjes su 'brel ba dang*/ shin tu gsal ba'i bsod nams tshad med pas yongs su bsgos pa dang rjes su 'brel ba'i phyir dang*/ mthong lam dang dgra bcom las langs pa'i rgyud ni mthong spang ma lus par spangs pa dang sgom spang ma lus par spangs pas gnas gyur gsar pa thob pas dri ma med pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / lhag ma sgom lam{ gnas pa'i 'bras bu bar ma gnyis} ni rang bzhin dang 'bras bu yongs su ma rdzogs pas de las langs pa'i rgyud ni snga ma gnyis ltar gnas gyur gsar pa dang dag pa ma yin pas mthong lam dang dgra bcom las langs pa ltar bsod nams kyi zhing mchog tu gyur pa ma yin no/ / gal te las kyi rnam smin gyi gtso bo ni tshor ba yin pas de sems kyi tshor ba kho na yin pa dang lus kyi kho na yin pa yod dam zhe na/

Reply: The maturational result of benefiting or harming the fully ordained Saṅgha, such as the Buddha, or any persons who are āryas — such as those five who have arisen from (1) cessation (nirodha), (2) love (maitrī), and (3) unafflicted states, (4) the path of seeing (darśana), or (5) the resultant meditative attainment of an arhat — is immediately [352] experienced in the current life alone. That is because (1) the mindstreams of those arising from cessation, where the mind obtains supreme peace, is similar to a mindstream that returns from nirvāṇa, and the mindstreams of those arising from (2) love and (3) unafflicted states are related, respectively, to the superior intention to benefit immeasurable sentient beings and to minds establishing unafflicted states for immeasurable sentient beings. Thus they are related to minds fully imbued with immeasurable extremely clear merit. The mindstreams of those rising from (4) the path of seeing and (5) the state of an arhat are, respectively, minds abandoning all objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing without exception, and minds abandoning all objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation without exception; and since they obtain a new state, they are stainless. In addition, those on the path of meditation {who abide in the two intermediate results} have not yet attained [either] their inner nature or the final result. When they rise from meditation, their mindstreams are not a supreme field of merit like the former two — those rising from the path of seeing or the state of an arhat — since their mindstreams have neither been transformed nor are they pure yet. Question: Since the main karmic maturation is feeling, is it mental feeling alone or is it physical feeling alone?
rnam par rtog pa med pa yi/ / dge ba'i las kyi rnam smin ni/ / sems kyi tshor ba kho nar 'dod/ / mi dge ba'i ni lus kyi yin/ / 57
The karmic maturation of virtuous karma free from investigation is asserted to be mental feeling alone. That for nonvirtuous karma is physical feeling. (4:57)
yod de/
Reply: It is both,

rnam par rtog pa med pa'i sa bsam gtan khyad par can nas bzung ste srid rtse'i bar gyi dge ba'i las kyi rnam smin ni sems kyi tshor ba yid bde dang btang snyoms kho na yin par 'dod de gnyis pa yan chad na lus kyi tshor ba med pa'i phyir dang*/ sa 'og ma na yod kyang de ni nges par rtog dpyod dang bcas pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / mi dge ba'i las kyi rnam smin{ gyi gtso bo de yang ni tshor ba sdug bsngal yin pa'i phyir ro} ni lus kyi tshor ba sdug bsngal kho na yin no/ / ci'i phyir sems kyi ma yin zhe na/ mi dge ba'i rnam smin ni sdug bsngal yin la sems kyi sdug bsngal ni yid mi bde ba yin na yid mi bde ba ni rnam smin ma yin no zhes bshad zin to/ / de'i phyir bsam gtan dang po'i dngos gzhi man chad kyi dge ba'i las kyi rnam smin ni lus sems gnyis ka'i tshor ba yin par don gyi shugs la rtogs par nus so/ / 'o na sems can rnams kyi sems rnam par g.yengs pa smyo ba'i sems{ de yid mi bde ma yin nam }sems gang la 'byung zhing rgyu ci zhig gis 'gyur zhe na/

because the karmic maturation of virtuous karma, from the special absorption of the level free from investigation (vitarka) up to the summit of existence, is asserted to be the mental feeling (vedanā) of mental satisfaction and equanimity alone, for physical feeling does not exist on the second absorption and above. And though physical feeling exists on lower levels, it definitely possesses investigation and analysis. {Further, the main} karmic maturation of nonvirtuous karma {is the feeling of pain} that is the physical feeling of pain alone. Question: Why is it not mental feeling? Reply: The karmic maturation of nonvirtue is [physical] pain, but with regard to mental suffering that is mental dissatisfaction, it was explained earlier that mental dissatisfaction is not karmic maturation. Therefore it should be implicitly understood that the karmic maturation of virtuous karma on or below the actual basis of the first absorption is both physical and mental feeling. Question: However, {isn’t} the disturbed crazed mind of sentient beings {mental dissatisfaction?} In what mind does it occur, and by what cause does it arise?
g.yengs pa'i sems ni yid sems la/ / de ni las kyi rnam smin skyes/ / skrag gnod ma mnyam mya ngan gyis/ / sgra mi snyan min 'dod ldan rnams/ / 58

The disturbed mind is the mind of mental consciousness. It arises from the maturation of karma and through fear, harm, unbalanced elements, and grief. Those of Kuru are not, but those possessing attachment are. (4:58)

sems rnam par g.yengs pa smyo ba'i sems ni {yang dag min par rtogs pas/} yid kyi rnam shes kyi sems la yin te/ rnam shes tshogs lnga ni {nges par rtog dang rjes dran gyi} rtog pa med pa'i phyir dang*/ g.yengs pa'i sems kyang nges par rtog pa'i bdag nyid yin pa'i phyir ro/ / sems g.yengs pa de ni rgyu bzhi po{ gzhan smyo bar byas pa dang dug dang chang ldud pa dang g.yang la skyur ba la sogs pa} las kyi rnam smin las skyes pa dang*/ mi ma yin {pas gzugs mi sdug pa bstan pa }la sogs pas skrag par byas pa dang*/ mi ma yin khros te gnad du bsnun pas gnod pa byas pa dang*/{rlung mkhris bad kan 'khrugs pas }'byung ba cha ma mnyam pa dang*/ { sngon gnas byed kyi bu dang rus mthun pa'i bram ze mo khyo shug gnyis la bu bdun yod pa las bu drug shi bas mya ngan gyis smyo bar gyur te gcer bu kho nar bcom ldan 'das mi thi la'i a mra'i tshal na bzhugs pa'i drung du phyin pa na sangs rgyas kyi mthus dran pa rnyed nas ngo tsha bar gyur pa la ston pa'i bkas kun dga' bos gos byin te/ de la ston pas chos bstan pas rgyun zhugs kyi 'bras bu thob nas slar rang gi khyim du phyin pa na bu bdun pa'ang shi ba dang de la de mya ngan mi byed pa la/ rang gi khyo na re khyod sngar bu shi ba la mya ngan byed la/ da bu bdun pa shi ba la mya ngan mi byed pa las na bu de dag khyod rang gis zos so zhes zer ba la/ bram ze mos/ bram ze ngas ni yun rings nas/ / bu dang tsha bo stong phrag dang*/ / gnyen mang brgya phrag dag zos te/ / khyod kyis kyang ni de dang 'dra/ / skye ba de dang de dag tu/ / bu dang tsha bo stong phrag dag gcig la gcig ni za rnams kyi/ / tshad ni yod pa ma yin no/ / 'jig rten na ni skye ba dang*/ / 'chi las nges 'byung shes nas ni/ / su zhig mya ngan yongs gdung ba'am/ / smre sngags 'don par byed par 'gyur/ / bdag gis sangs rgyas bstan byas te/ / skye ba dang ni 'chi ba las/ / nges par 'byung ba shes pas na/ / mya ngan mi byed gdung ba med/ / ces smras pa lta bu/ } mya ngan gyi rkyen gyis 'byung bar 'gyur ro/ /

Reply: The disturbed and crazed mind (cittakṣepa) {that is marked as distorted} is the mind of mental consciousness because the fivefold collection of [sensory] consciousness is definitely devoid of decisive conception and recalling conception, yet the disturbed mind is decisive conception itself. That disturbed mind arises from the maturation of karma through the four causes — {(1) causing others to become insane, (2) taking poison, (3) taking alcohol, and (4) hurling oneself into an abyss and so on}; by nonhuman spirits and so on {who reveal repulsive forms} and cause fear (bhaya); by nonhuman spirits who wrathfully afflict the vital essence, causing harm (upaghāta); by imbalance (vaiṣamya) in the primary elements {through the disturbance of wind, bile, and phlegm}; and through grief (śoka). [353] {Once, the son of a sage and a brahman girl of the same clan were married and had seven sons. Since six of her sons died, she became insane through grief and lived alone and naked. One day, she went near to where the Bhagavan was residing in the mango grove of Mithilā, and by the might of the Buddha she regained her memory and became ashamed of her nakedness. The Master ordered Ānanda to offer her clothes, and through the Master teaching her Dharma she obtained the result of stream entry and then returned to her house. She found that also their seventh son had died, but she didn’t grieve. Her husband said, “Before, when our sons died, you grieved; now that the seventh son has died, you do not grieve but you honor them.” The brahman woman said: Brahman, over a long period I have had thousands of sons and nephews, and many hundreds of kinsmen I have nourished. You also have done the same in this and past lives. There is no limit to the thousands of sons and nephews you have individually nourished. Having understood renunciation from mundane birth and death, who would indulge in sorrow, torment, or lamentation? I have received the teachings of the Buddha, and through understanding renunciation from birth and death, I have no sorrow or torment.[1151]}

las kyi rnam smin las skyes pa ni/ rdzas dang gsang sngags kyi sbyor bas gzhan gyi sems g.yengs par byed pa dang*/ mi 'dod bzhin du dug dang chang la sogs pa myos par byed pa ldud pa dang*/ ri dwags la sogs pa sems can gzhan skrag par byed pa dang*/ nags mes gtong ba dang*/ srog chags g.yang du 'ded pa la sogs pa'i las las skyes pa ste de la ni sman dang man ngag dang nus pa can gyis bcos su med do/ / skrag pa ni mi dang mi ma yin pas gzugs mi sdug pa bstan pa la sogs pas sems dngangs par byas pa ste de la ni skyes bu dam pa'i man ngag gis bcos su yod do/ / mi ma yin pas gnod pa ni gdon gyis byas pa ste de la ni rig sngags 'chang la sogs pa'i byin rlabs kyis zhi bar byed do/ / 'byung ba cha ma mnyam pa ni nad kyis byas pa ste/ de ni gso ba rig pa rnams kyis bcos su yod do/ / mya ngan gyis byas pa gnas byed kyi bu ni dang rus mthun pa'i bram ze mo lta bu ste de la ni mya ngan bsal ba dang spyod lam gyis bcos su yod do/ / {de dag ni rim pa ltar bsag sbyang dang*/ skyes bu dam pa'i man ngag dang*/ rigs sngags 'chang la sogs pa'i byin rlabs dang*/ gso ba rig pa dang*/ mya ngan bsal ba'i thabs dang spyod lam gyis bcos su yod do } gal te yid kyi rnam shes la sems g.yengs pa yod pa de yang las kyi rnam smin las skyes pa yin na de lta na sems kyi tshor ba mi dge ba'i las kyi rnam smin du 'gyur ro zhe na/

mi 'gyur te/ mi dge ba'i las kyis ni las las skyes pa'i 'byung ba rnams 'khrug la 'byung ba 'khrugs pas sems 'khrugs shing g.yengs par gyur pa'i phyir ro/ / des na 'byung ba rnams ni las mi dge ba las skyes pa rnam smin yin la sems g.yengs pa ni 'byung ba rnam smin de dag las skyes pas las kyi bdag 'bras yin gyi mi dge ba'i las las dngos su skyes pa ma yin pas rnam smin ma yin no/ / de la 'phros nas 'grel pa las/ sems g.yengs pa dang rnam par g.yengs pa la mu bzhi bshad de/ de la g.yengs pa ni sngar bstan pa'i 'byung ba 'khrugs pa la sogs pa las byung ba'i sems 'khrugs pa yin la rnam par g.yengs pa ni sems nyon mongs can no/ / des na de dag gnyis ka'ang rnam smin ma yin no/ / rnam par g.yengs pa'i sems de yang rten gang la yod ce na/

Reply: That is not so, because nonvirtuous karma agitates the primary elements that arise from karma, and by agitating the primary elements, the mind is agitated and disturbed. Therefore, such primary elements are karmic maturation since they arise from nonvirtuous karma, but since the disturbed mind arises from karmic maturation related to the primary elements, it is a dominant result of karma [354] and not karmic maturation, since it does not directly arise from karma. In elaborating that point, the Autocommentary explains that disturbed mind and distraction have four possibilities. Disturbed mind is the agitation of the mind derived from the agitation of the primary elements and so on, as taught previously, and distraction is an afflicted mind. Therefore neither of those is karmic maturation. Question: Also, what types of sentient beings are a basis for a disturbed mind?

{dge ba'i rnam smin 'ba' zhig la spyod cing g.yengs pa'i rgyu gzhan yang med pas } sgra mi snyan pa min te de ma gtogs pa'i 'dod pa dang ldan pa'i sems can rnams la ci rigs par yod de/ 'dod pa'i lha rnams la'ang smyon pa dag yod na dud 'gro dang yi dwags rnams la lta ci smros pa'i phyir ro/ / dmyal ba rnams ni tshor ba mi bzad pas nyen pas re zhig bdag nyid kyang mi dran na bya ba dang bya ba ma yin pa lta ci smros pas rtag tu rnam par g.yengs pa dag yin no/ / sangs rgyas ma gtogs pa 'phags pa rnams la'ang 'byung ba ma snyoms pa'i sems rnam par g.yengs pa ni yod la/ las kyi rnam par g.yengs pa dang*/ 'jigs pas g.yengs pa dang*/ gnon pas g.yengs pa dang*/ mya ngan gyis g.yengs pa rnams ni med de/ rim pa ltar las nges pa rnams ni smin zin lam nges pa ni de phyin chad mi smin pa'i phyir dang*/ / 'tsho ba med pa dang*/ tshigs su bcad pa med pa dang*/ 'khor gyi nang du skrag pa dang*/ 'chi ba dang*/ ngan 'gro'i 'jigs pa lnga las 'das pa'i phyir dang*/ mi ma yin pa 'khrugs pa'i rgyu mi mdzes pa mi byed pa'i phyir dang*/ mya ngan med pa'i chos nyid mngon par shes pa'i phyir ro/ / sangs rgyas la ni thugs g.yengs pa dang rims kyis 'grongs pa dang gsung 'dzer ba dang dbu skya ba mi 'byung ste/ las shin tu dwang ba'i rnam par smin pa'i snying po yin pa'i phyir ro zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/ /

Reply: Those of Kuru are not, since they enjoy virtuous karmic maturation alone and have no other causes of disturbance. But apart from them, those sentient beings possessing attachment have various types of disturbed mind because desire gods have such experience, and if they have, what need is there to mention animals and ghosts?[1152] If hell beings at times cannot remember their own selves since they cannot bear their own feelings, then what need is there to mention their actions and inaction, since they are always disturbed. Except for buddhas, even āryas experience disturbance of the mind through the imbalance of the primary elements, disturbance by karma, disturbance by fear, and disturbance by harm. But they [i.e., āryas] do not possess disturbance through grief, [both] because they have transcended the five types of disturbing state — (1) [the state in which] karmas that are certain to mature have matured but those uncertain to mature do not subsequently mature, (2) being without a livelihood, (3) being without scripture, (4) having fear within the retinue, and (5) having fear of death and lower rebirths — and because [āryas] are not agitated by repulsive [forms] displayed by nonhuman spirits and perceive reality free of sorrow. Buddhas do not have disturbance of mind, serial death, hoarseness, and white hair because they possess the essence of extremely clear karmic maturation.[1153] This is explained by Master Pūrṇavardhana.
yang gsum tshan gsum pa'i mdo las/ lus ngag yid gsum gyi yon po gsum dang*/ skyon nam nyes pa gsum dang*/ snyigs ma gsum gsungs pa de dag gang zhe na/
Question: The Three Times Three Sūtra mentions three corruptions, three errors or faults, and the three degenerations of body, speech, and mind.[1154] What are they?
yon skyon snyigs mar gsungs pa ni/ / g.yo dang zhe sdang 'dod chags skyes/ /
Those called deceptions, corruptions, and degenerations arise from guile, aversion, and attachment. (4:59ab)

lus dang ngag dang yid kyi las yon po gsum dang {skyon nam nyes pa gsum dang*/ snyigs ma gsum zhes bya bar gsungs pa rnams ni rim pa ltar sgo gsum gyi las sems las byung ba gya gyu ba'i g.yo dang*/ zhe sdang dang*/ 'dod chags las skyes pa rnams so } gsungs pa ni sgo gsum gyi las sems las byung ba gya gyu ba'i g.yo las skyes pa dang*/ skyon nam nyes pa gsum gsungs pa ni sgo gsum gyi las zhe sdang las skyes pa dang*/ snyigs ma{ gsum zhes bya bar} gsungs pa gsum ni sgo gsum gyi las 'dod chags las skyes pa'o/

Reply: Those called the three deceptions (vaṅka) of body, speech, and mind are karmas of the three doors that arise from the crooked mental factor of guile. Those called the three corruptions (doṣa), or faults, are karmas of the three doors that arise from aversion. Those called the {three} degenerations (kaṣāya) are karmas of the three doors that arise from attachment. [355]
gsum pa dkar nag la sogs pa bzhir dbye ba ni
Classification in four, such as white and black
dkar nag la sogs bye brag gis/ / las ni rnam pa bzhi yin no/ / 59
Karma when classified has four types: white, black, and so on. (4:59cd)

mdo las/ las gnag la rnam par smin pa gnag pa'i las dang*/ las dkar la rnam par smin pa dkar ba'i las dang*/ sogs pa'i sgras bzung ba las dkar nag 'dren ma la rnam par smin pa yang dkar gnag 'dren ma dang*/ las mi dkar mi gnag cing rnam par smin pa med la las zad par byed pa'i bye brag gi las ni rnam pa bzhi yin par gsungs pa yin no/ / de dag kyang gang zhe na/

A sūtra declares that karma has four types when exhaustively classified: (1) black karma is karma with black karmic maturation, (2) white karma is karma with white karmic maturation, and the “and so on” refers to (3) mixed black and white karma that is the mixture of white and black karmic maturation, and (4) karma neither black nor white, which has no karmic maturation.[1155] Question: What are those?
mi dge gzugs dang 'dod gtogs pa'i/ / dge ba nyid ni rim bzhin du/ / gnag dang dkar dang gnyis ka'i las/ / de zad byed pa zag med yin/ / 60
Nonvirtuous karma, and virtuous karma belonging to the form and desire realms, are respectively black, white, and karma that is both. Uncontaminated karma eradicates those three. (4:60)

las mi dge ba nyid ni rim pa bzhin du khyad par med pa nyon mongs can yin pas las gnag la 'bras bu rnam smin yid du mi 'ong ba 'byin pas rnam smin kyang gnag pa dang*/ gzugs su gtogs pa'i dge ba ni rim pa bzhin du mi dge ba dang ma 'dres pas las dkar 'bras bu yid du 'ong bas rnam smin kyang dkar ba dang*/ 'dod par gtogs pa'i dge ba nyid ni rim pa bzhin du mi dge ba dang 'dres pas las kyang dkar gnag 'dren ma la rnam smin yang yid du 'ong mi 'ong 'dren mar 'byung bas dkar gnag gnyis ka'i las zhes bya ste/ de yang rgyud kyi sgo nas 'dres pa yin gyi las kyi ngo bo gcig la dkar gnag 'dres pa ni med de 'gal ba'i phyir ro/ / gal te de lta na mi dge ba'ang 'dres par 'gyur te mi dge ba dang ldan pa'i rgyud la dge ba'ang 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / zhe na/ de ltar yin mod kyi 'on kyang 'dod pa rang sa na gnyen po ting nge 'dzin med pas dge bas mi dge ba gtan med par bya bar mi nus la mi dge ba ni stobs dang ldan pa'i phyir log ltas dge rtsa gcod nus pas dge ba dang gdon mi za bar 'dre ba ma yin no/ / de nyid kyi phyir 'dod pa'i dge ba ni stobs chung ba'i phyir 'dre bar 'gyur ro zhes 'grel pa las bshad do/ / kun las btus las ni/ dkar la rnam par smin pa dkar ba'i las gang zhe na/ khams gsum pa'i dge ba'o/ / dkar nag tu gyur la rnam par smin pa dkar nag tu 'gyur ba gang zhe na/ gang 'dod pa dang rab tu ldan pa'i 'dren ma ste/ bsam pas gnag la sbyor bas dkar ba'am/ sbyor bas gnag la bsam pas dkar ba'o zhes 'dod pa'i bsam sbyor dkar nag 'dren ma ni dkar nag gnyis ka'i las su bshad la/ bsam sbyor dkar nag 'dren ma las gzhan pa'i 'dod pa'i dge ba dang gzugs med kyi dge ba'ang dkar la rnam smin dkar ba'i las su bshad do/ / 'o na ci'i phyir gzugs med pa'i dge ba dkar bar ma bshad ce na/ bye brag tu smra ba gang na rnam smin skye srid dang bar srid gnyis yod pa dang lus la sogs pa'i las gsum ga yod pa der de dag gi dbye ba 'chad na gzugs med na de dag med pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes 'chad mod kyi/

Reply: Nonvirtuous karma itself is black (kṛṣṇa) karma since it is uniformly afflicted, and its karmic maturation is also black since it produces an unpleasant maturational result. Virtuous karma belonging to the form realm is white (śukla) karma since it is not mixed with nonvirtue, and its karmic maturation is also white since its result is pleasant. Virtuous karma belonging to the desire realm is mixed white and black karma since it is mixed with nonvirtue, and it is karma that is both white and black since it gives rise to a mixture of pleasant and unpleasant karmic maturation. Further, it is mixed within a continuum because there is no mixture of white and black karma that possesses a single nature, because they exclude each other. Objection: Thus since nonvirtue would also be mixed, virtue would occur in the mindstream of one possessing nonvirtue. Reply: Indeed, though that is so, since concentration does not exist as the antidote [of nonvirtue] in the desire-realm level, virtue cannot completely overcome nonvirtue there because nonvirtue is strong. But since wrong view can sever the root of virtue, nonvirtue is not necessarily mixed with virtue. Therefore the Autocommentary explains that it is mixed because desire [realm] virtue is weak.[1156] The Compendium of Abhidharma discloses: What is white karma with white karmic maturation? It is virtue of the three realms. What is black and white karma with black and white karmic maturation? It is mixed karma of the desire realm that consists of either black intention and white preparation, or black preparation and white intention.[1157] Karma with a mixture of white and black intention and preparation in the desire realm is explained as karma with both black and white karmic maturation. Question: Why is virtue in the formless realm not explained as white? Vaibhāṣikas assert that such classifications are explained wherever both birth existence and intermediate existence exist as karmic maturation, or the three karmas such as physical karma exist, but these don’t exist in the formless realm. [356]
'on kyang mdo gzhan las ni dkar la rnam par smin par dkar ba'i las gang zhe na/ gzugs med pa bzhi'o zhes gzugs med pa'i dge ba'ang der bshad pa'i phyir de yang yin no/ /

However, in another sūtra it says: What is white karma with white karmic maturation? It is the four formless states.[1158] Because formless virtue is also explained here, it may also be taken as white karma.

las dang rnam smin gsum po de dag zad cing skong bar byed pa ni zag pa med pa'i las yin te/ de la ni mi gnag cing mi dkar ba zhes bya ste/ zag bcas kyi las dge mi dge gnyis ka ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ 'khor bar 'jug pa dang 'gal bas khams su ma gtogs pa'i phyir rnam par smin pa'i 'bras bu yid du 'ong mi 'ong gnyis ka med pa'i phyir ro/ / lung bar ma'i stong pa chen po'i don gyi mdo las ni mi slob pa'i chos las brtsams te/ kun dga' bo chos 'di dag ni gcig tu dkar ba/ gcig tu dge ba/ gcig tu kha na ma tho ba med pa yin no zhes gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ bstan bcos rab tu byed pa'i rkang pa las kyang*/ chos dkar po rnams gang zhe na/ dge ba'i chos rnams dang ma bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa rnams yin no zhes gsungs pa'i phyir gcig tu dkar ba ni zag pa med pa yin no zhes bya ba ni don dam pa yin no/ / de la ma bsgribs lung ma bstan ni nyon mongs can ma yin pas dkar ba'o/ / slob dpon gang spel gyis kyang dkar ba ni rnam pa gnyis te/ rang bzhin gyis dkar ba dang*/ rnam par smin pas dkar ba'o/ / de la gzugs su gtogs pa'i dge ba ni gnyis ka yin la/ zag pa med pa ni dang po yin no zhes bshad do/ / gal te zag med kyi las dang lam thams cad dkar ba la sogs pa'i las gsum po thams cad zad par byed pa yin nam zhe na/

Uncontaminated karma eradicates (kṣaya) and abandons those three karmas and karmic maturations. It is called “neither black nor white” because it is neither contaminated virtuous nor nonvirtuous karma. Since it prevents entry to saṃsāra, it does not belong to a realm, and it has neither a pleasant nor an unpleasant result. The Sūtra on the Meaning of Great Emptiness of the Medium-Length Collection states: Beginning with nonlearner Dharmas, Ānanda, these Dharmas are solely white, solely virtuous, solely nonoffensive acts.[1159] Topic Divisions also adds: What are white Dharmas? They are virtuous Dharmas and unobscured-neutral phenomena.[1160] The statement “Dharma that is white alone is uncontaminated” refers to ultimate virtue. Unobscured-neutral phenomena are white since they are not afflicted. Master Pūrṇavardhana writes: White karma has two aspects: white by nature and white by karmic maturation. Virtue belonging to the form realm is both. Uncontaminated phenomena are the first.[1161] Objection: Do uncontaminated karma, and any of the paths, eradicate all three karmas, such as white karma and so on?
chos bzod 'dod chags bral ba yi/ / bar chad med lam brgyad kyi gang / / sems pa rnam pa bcu gnyis de/ / nag po zad par byed pa'i las/ / 61
Any of the twelve intentions such as perseverance for knowledge and the eight uninterrupted paths free from attachment are karmas that eradicate black karma. (4:61)
thams cad ni ma yin no/ /
Reply: They do not eradicate all.

'on kyang mthong lam gyi sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa la sogs pa bzhi dang 'dod pa la 'dod chags dang bral bar byed pa'i 'jig rten las 'das pa'i sgom lam gyi bar chad med pa'i lam brgyad kyi sems pa ste de ltar sems pa rnam pa bcu gnyis po gang dag yin pa de dag ni nag po'i las zad par byed pa'i zag pa med pa'i las yin te/ 'dod pa'i sdig pa mi dge ba'i chos spong bar byed pa'i phyir ro/ / chos shes pa bzhi dang 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i rnam grol gyi lam brgyad de bcu gnyis ni ma yin te/ {bar chad med pa'i lam gyis zad par byas zin pa'i phyir ro } de dag rnam grol gyi lam yin pa'i phyir ro/ / rjes su shes pa'i bzod pa dang shes pa brgyad kyang nag po'i gnyen po ma yin te/ de dag ni khams gong ma'i gnyen po yin gyi 'dod pa'i gnyen po ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

However, any of the twelve intentions (cetanā) including (1–4) the four intentions on the path of seeing, such as perseverance for [Dharma] knowledge of suffering, and (5–12) the eight intentions of the transcendent uninterrupted paths of meditation that are free from attachment, are uncontaminated karmas that eradicate black karma because they abandon nonvirtuous phenomena that are desire-realm immoral acts. The twelve, including the four desire knowledges and the eight liberated paths free from attachment, do not eradicate them because they are liberated paths {and the uninterrupted paths have already eradicated them}. Also, the eight stages of subsequent perseverance and knowledge are not antidotes of black karma because they are antidotes of attachment to higher realms but not antidotes of attachment to the desire realm.
dgu pa'i sems pa gang yin pa/ / de ni dkar nag zad byed yin/ / dkar po bsam gtan chags bral ba'i/ / bar chad med lam skyes tha mas/ / 62
Any intention of the ninth path eradicates white and black karma. White karma is eradicated by the final four arising as uninterrupted paths free from attachment to the absorptions. (4:62)

{'jig rten pa'i bar chad med lam gyis de dag spong yang ma bshad pa ni zag med kyi skabs yin pas so/ / 'dod pa'i nyon mongs dgu pa ma spangs pa de srid du 'dod pa'i dge ba dang ma bsgribs lung ma bstan thams cad 'dun pa'i 'dod chags yod do/ / des na } 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral bar byed pa'i sgom lam bar chad med pa'i lam dgu pa'i sems pa gang yin pa de ni dkar gnag 'dres pa'i las zad par byed pa yin te/{ des yul can 'dod pa'i nyon mongs pa chung ngu'i chung ngu spangs pa na dmigs yul dge ba'ang spong ba'i phyir ro/} de ni 'dod pa'i dge ba'i gnyen po yin pa'i phyir ro/ / bar chad med pa'i lam snga ma dag ni 'dod pa'i dge ba'i gnyen po ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

{Though mundane uninterrupted paths abandon [mixed white and black karma] such [mundane paths] are not explained here in the context of uncontaminated paths. All desire-realm virtue and unobscured-neutral states, and attachment that longs [for the desire realm], exist [357] until the ninth desire-realm affliction is abandoned. Therefore} any intention of the ninth uninterrupted path of meditation free of attachment to the desire realm eradicates mixed white and black karma, {because when it abandons the smallest of the small afflicted minds, it also abandons its virtuous focal objects.} Therefore it is an antidote of desire-realm virtue. However, that former uninterrupted path is not an antidote of desire-realm virtue.

'dir 'dod pa'i dkar nag 'dres pa'i las dgu pa'i bar chad med pa'i lam gyis spong ngo zhes bya ba'ang las de'i rang gi ngo bo thob pa chad pa'i tshul gyis spong ba ni ma yin te/ lan cig spangs kyang yang 'dod pa'i dge ba mngon du byed pa'i phyir ro/ / 'on kyang de la dmigs pa'i yul can gyi nyon mongs spangs pa la de skad brjod de/ mdo las/ dge slong dag mig la 'dun pa'i 'dod chags de spongs shig dang de lta na mig de spangs par 'gyur ro zhes gsungs pa lta bu'o/ / de'i phyir dgu pa'i bar chad med pa'i lam ma gtogs pa snga ma dag ni de'i gnyen por ma bshad de/ dang po'i rnam pa spangs kyang de'i/ / yul can dri ma lhag rnams kyis/ / zhes 'byung bas 'dod pa'i dge ba la dmigs pa'i yul can nyon mongs pa chung ngu'i chung ngu la sogs pa yod pa'i phyir ro/ / nag po ni thob pa chad pa'i tshul gyis spong ba'i phyir snga ma dag gis spong ngo*/ / de bzhin du dkar po zad par byed pa'ang de'i yul can spangs pas yin gyi ngo bo spong ba ni ma yin no zhes shes par bya'o/ / 'o na dkar po'i las zad par byed pa ji lta bu zhe na/

Though it is said that “the uninterrupted path of the ninth stage abandons mixed black and white karma of the desire realm,” it does not abandon it by means of stopping the obtainment of the very nature of such karma because, though abandoned once, desire-realm virtue again manifests. However, this is said with respect to abandoning afflicted minds focusing on it. A sūtra states: Monks, abandon attachment that longs for the eye, and in that way abandon the eye.[1162] Therefore the former paths, except for the ninth uninterrupted path, are not explained to be its antidote because it is said: Though the aspect of the first is abandoned by abandoning the remaining stained minds engaging it . . . Therefore the mind focusing on desire-realm virtue has the smallest of the small affliction and so on. Because black karma is abandoned by means of stopping obtainment, the former abandon them. So too, it should be understood that though virtue is eradicated by abandoning the mind engaging it, its nature is not abandoned. Question: How is white karma eradicated?

dkar po gzugs khams kyi dge ba'i las zad par byed pa ni bsam gtan dang po dang gnyis pa dang gsum pa dang bzhi pa las 'dod chags dang bral bar byed pa'i bar chad med pa'i lam dgu dgu skyes pa'i tha ma bzhi po dag gis yin te/ de dag gis gzugs kyi dge ba'i ngo bo mi spong yang de la dmigs pa'i nyon mongs pa'i spong ba'i phyir ro/ / gang dag gzugs med pa'i dge ba'ang dkar po'i las su 'chad pa de dag gi ltar na {dkar po gzugs med chags bral pa'i/ / bar chad med lam skyes tha mas zhes par 'gyur bas/} gzugs med pa'i nyon mongs pa spong ba'i bar chad med pa'i lam tha ma bzhi yang dkar po zad byed yin no/ / 'jig rten pa'i lam yang de dag gi gnyen po yin mod kyi zag med kyi dbang du byas pa'i phyir 'dir ni mi 'dod do/ /

Reply: The white virtuous karma of the form realm is eradicated by the final four that arise as the ninth stage of the uninterrupted path free from attachment to the first, second, third, and fourth absorptions, because even though they don’t abandon the nature of form-realm virtue, they abandon afflicted states that focus on it. In accordance with the explanation that virtuous or white karma of the formless realm exists, also the four final uninterrupted paths abandoning affliction of the formless realm eradicate white karma, {since it can be said, “White karma of the formless realm is eradicated by the final four that arise as the ninth stage of the uninterrupted path free from attachment to the formless realm”}. Indeed, the mundane path is also an antidote to them, but that is not considered here because this is from the perspective of uncontaminated paths.
gzhan ni dmyal ba myong 'gyur dang / / 'dod gzhan myong 'gyur gnyis su rig / gzhan ni mthong bas spang bya gnag/ / 'dod pa las skyes gzhan dkar gnag/ / 63

Some assert that karma to be experienced in hell is black and karma to be experienced in other desire abodes is both. Others assert that karma to be abandoned by seeing is black and other karma arisen in the desire realm is black and white. (4:63)

sngon gyi slob dpon gzhan dag ni dmyal ba myong bar 'gyur ba'i las ni gcig tu mi dge ba dang rnam smin yid du mi 'ong bar nges pa'i phyir las gnag la rnam smin gnag pa dang*/ dmyal ba ma gtogs pa'i 'dod pa'i khams gzhan myong bar 'gyur ba'i las ni dkar gnag 'dren ma gnyis su rig par bya ste/ gzhan de dag na dge mi dge gnyis ka'i rnam smin yod pa'i phyir ro/ / dkar po dang de dag zad byed kyi las ni snga ma bzhin du shes pas bya'o zhes 'dod do/ / sngon gyi slob dpon gzhan dag ni mthong bas spang bar bya ba'i 'dod pa'i las ni gnag po'i las te dge ba dang ma 'dres pas mi dge ba kho nar nges pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dod pa las skyes pa'i las mthong spang las gzhan sgom spangs ni dkar gnag 'dren ma ste dge mi dge gnyis ka yin pa'i phyir zhes 'dod do/ / dkar po dang mi gnag mi dkar ba ni khyad par med pa snga ma kho na yin no/ /

Some past masters assert that because karma to be experienced in hell is solely nonvirtuous and certain to have unpleasant karmic maturation, it is black karma with black karmic maturation. Karma to be experienced in other desire-realm abodes except for the hells should be understood as a mixture of both black and white karma because the karmic maturation of both black and white karma exists in other abodes. Karma that is white and karma [358] eradicating those should be understood as before.[1163] Other past masters assert that desire-realm karma to be abandoned by the path of seeing is black karma because, being unmixed with virtuous karma, it is certain to be nonvirtuous alone. They assert that karma arisen in the desire realm that is an object to be abandoned by the path of meditation, that is other than an object abandoned by the path of seeing, is mixed black and white karma because it is both virtuous and nonvirtuous.[1164] Karma that is white or neither black nor white is the same as the former.
thub pa dang gtsang byed kyi dbye ba/
Silence and purification
bzhi pa thub pa gsum la sogs par dbye ba ni
mdo las/ thub pa'i gsum ste/ thub pa'i lus dang thub pa'i ngag dang thub pa'i yid do zhes gsungs pa la
A sūtra declares: There are three silences: the silence of body, the silence of speech, and the silence of mind.[1165]
mi slob lus ngag las yid nyid/ / thub pa'i gsum ste go rims bzhin/ / legs spyad gsum po thams cad ni/ / gtsang byed rnam pa gsum yin no/ / 64
Nonlearner verbal, physical, and mental karma are respectively the three silences. All three types of positive action are the three types of purification. (4:64)

rig byed ni zag bcas yin pas mi slob pa'i lus ngag gi las spong ba'i rang bzhin zag med kyi rig byed ma yin pa gnyis dang*/ mi slob pa'i yid nyid thub pa yin gyi yid kyi las ni thub pa ma yin no/ / de nas thub pa'i lus la sogs pa gsum zhes bya ste go rim bzhin du sbyar ro/ / slob pa dang so so'i skye bo dag ni thub pa ma yin te/ nyon mongs pa thams cad spangs pa ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / dgra bcom pa rnams kyis ni spangs pa'i phyir thub pa yin no/ / 'di la'ang bye brag tu smra ba lus ngag gi rig byed ma yin pa'i las las yid thub pa rjes su dpag par bya ba yin no zhes zer ba ni ma yin te/ khyed ltar na spong ba la thub par 'dod cing spong ba'ang rig byed ma yin pa'i gzugs su 'dod na sems la rig byed ma yin pa'i gzugs nyid med pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir sgo gsum gyi mi dge ba dang nyon mongs pa thams cad spong ba'i sems pa nyid thub pa gsum yin la de ni lus ngag gi rig byed kyis dpag par bya ba yin no/ / de'i phyir sgo gsum mi dge ba dang nyon mongs pa las yang dag par bsdams pa ni thub pa yin no/ /

Both nonlearner (1) verbal and (2) physical karma — which are uncontaminated nonindicative form that abandons contaminated indicative form by its very nature — as well as nonlearner (3) mental karma, are silence. But [ordinary] mental karma is not silence. These three are respectively called silences (mauna), such as physical silence and so on. As such, learner ordinary beings do not possess silence because they have not abandoned all affliction, but arhats who have abandoned affliction do possess silence. Regarding this Vaibhāṣikas say: Mental silence is to be inferred from nonindicative physical and verbal karma. Reply: That is not so, because even if you assert that abandonment is silence and you assert that abandoned is nonindicative form, the mind itself does not have nonindicative form. Therefore the intention to abandon all nonvirtue and affliction of the three doors is the three silences, and they are inferred by physical and verbal indicative form. Thus silence is the correct restraint of nonvirtue and afflicted karma of the three doors.

yang mdo las/ lus dang ngag dang yid gtsang byed rnam pa gsum gsungs pa la lus dang ngag dang yid kyi legs par spyad pa{ dge ba} gsum po thams cad ni lus dang ngag dang yid gtsang byed rnam pa gsum yin te/ gtsang byed ni dus re zhig dang gtan du nyes par spyod pa'i dri ma spong ba'i phyir ro/ / legs par spyad pa ni dge ba yin no/ / de dag gi dgos pa ni log pa'i thub pa mi smra bar 'dug pa tsam gyis 'dag par lta ba la mos pa'am/ yang na ser skya dang rkang mig la sogs pa log pa'i thub pa dang*/ lus kyi dri ma dag pa tsam gyis 'dag par lta ba 'jug ngogs bzhir khrus byed pa la sogs pa gtsang byed ma yin pa la yin par mos pa dgag pa'i phyir te/ ji skad du mdo las/ lus kyi dka' thub mi bzang zhes/ / mkhas pa rnams ni de skad gsung*/ / sems kyi dka' thub nyid kyis ni/ / nyon mongs ri kun sreg par byed/ / ces pa dang*/ khyad par du 'phags pa'i bstod pa las kyang*/ lus kyi dka' thub bgyis pa yis/ / mdud pa 'jig par gcer bu 'tshal/ / khyod ni thugs kyi dka' thub kyis/ / mdud pa 'jig par bzhed pa lags/ / zhes pa dang*/ rnam 'grel gyi rgyan las/ skyes bu'i nang na gnas pa'i skyon/ / phyi rol khrus kyis mi 'dag ste/ / de ni lan brgyar khrus byas kyang*/ / chang bum bzhin du gtsang mi 'gyur/ / zhes 'byung ba bzhin no/ /

Again, a sūtra declares: There are three types of purification of the body, speech, and mind (manas).[1166] All three types of {virtuous} positive action (sucarita) of body, speech, and mind are the three types of purification (śauca) of body, speech, and mind, because purifying is abandoning the stain of intermittent and continuous negative action. Positive action is virtuous, and it is necessary to refute the view that “false silence such as merely remaining without speaking is purity,” or to refute the false silence of Viṣṇu and Akṣapāda and so on, or to refute the view that purification arises from merely removing physical stains, such as that one is purified by washing one’s body on the four river banks and so on. In this respect a sūtra asserts: Physical austerity is called impure, and the wise [359] describe it in this way. Mental austerity itself incinerates the entire mountain of affliction.[1167] And Praise of Excellence also states: Those who practice physical austerity seek solitude to destroy the knots. But indeed you have destroyed the knots through your mental austerity.[1168] The Ornament of Valid Cognition says: The faults that dwell within beings {and the faults that dwell within the mind are not purified by bathing at the river bank.} Externally washing a vessel does not remove the faults dwelling in beings. Though it is washed one hundred times, like a beer pot it is not cleaned.[1169]
legs spyad nyes spyad du dbye ba/
Positive and negative action
lnga pa legs spyad nyes spyad du dbye ba ni nyes par spyad pa gsum mdo las gsungs pa'i don gang zhe na/
Question: What are the three negative actions as stated in the sūtras?
lus kyi la sogs mi dge ba/ / nyes par spyad pa gsum du 'dod/ / brnab sems la sogs las min yang / / yid kyi nyes spyad rnam gsum mo/ / 65
Nonvirtuous physical karma and so on is asserted to be the three negative actions. Though covetousness and so on are not karma, they are called the three types of negative mental action. (4:65)

de la{ mdo las nyes par spyad pa dang legs par spyad pa gsum gsungs pa las} lus kyi las mi dge ba dang sogs pa'i sgras gzung ba ngag dang yid kyi las mi dge ba ni 'bras bu yid du mi 'ong ba'i phyir rim pa bzhin du lus ngag yid gsum gyi nyes par spyad pa gsum du 'dod do/ / 'o na yid kyi las mi dge ba kho na yid kyi nyes par spyad pa yin nam zhe na ma yin te/ brnab sems dang sogs pas gzung ba gnod sems dang log lta gsum ni 'dod chags dang rnam par 'tshe ba dang lta ba'i rang bzhin gyi nyon mongs pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ yid kyi las ni sems pa'i rang bzhin las yin pa'i phyir dang*/ las dang nyon mongs pa tha dad yin pa'i phyir yid kyi las kyi rang bzhin min yang yid kyi nyes par spyad pa rnam gsum du gsungs pa yin no/{ mdo sde pa'i bye brag /}dpe ston pa rnams na re ched du bsam par bya ba'i mdo las/ dge slong dag ched bsam par bya ba'i las byas shing bsags pas dmyal ba dag gi nang du skye bar 'gyur ro/ / ji ltar ched du bsam par bya ba'i las byas shing bsags pa yin zhe na/ dge slong dag 'di na la la ched du bsams nas lus kyi las rnam pa gsum byed cing sogs pa yin la ngag gi las rnam pa bzhi dang yid kyi las rnam pa gsum zhes bya ba la sogs pa rgyas par gsungs nas bka' stsal pa/ dge slong dag ji ltar yid kyi ched du bsam par bya ba'i las rnam pa gsum byas shing bsags pa yin zhe na/ 'di na dge slong la la brnab sems dang ldan pa yin/ gnod sems can gyi sems su gyur pa yin/ log par lta ba yin zhes bya ba nas/ dge slong dag yang 'di na la la phyin ci log tu lta ba yin zhes bya ba'i bar du gsungs te/ mdo der brnab sems la sogs pa ma gtogs pa yid kyi las gzhan ma gsungs kyi brnab sems la sogs gsum po nyid yid kyi las su gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ yid kyi las 'ga' zhig ni nyon mongs pa'ang yin pa'i phyir yid kyi las kyang yin la nyon mongs pa'ang yin pa mi 'gal lo zhes zer ro/ / bye brag tu smra ba rnams na re de lta na las dang nyon mongs pa dag gcig tu 'gyur la de 'dod na mdo dang 'gal te/ mdo las ni/ brnab sems dang ldan pa yin zhes bya ba la sogs pas sems pa de nyid ston par byed pa yin pas nyon mongs pa'i sgo nas yid kyi sems pa'i las 'jug par bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes zer ro/ /

Reply: From among the three negative actions and the three positive actions stated in the sūtras, nonvirtuous physical karma and so on, which includes nonvirtuous verbal and mental karma, is asserted respectively to be the three negative actions (duścarita) of body, speech, and mind because they produce unpleasant results. Question: Is nonvirtuous mental karma alone negative mental action or not? Reply: Though the three — (1) covetousness (abhidhyā) and so on, referring to (2) malice and (3) wrong view — are not in essence mental karma, they are called the three types of negative mental action (manoduścarita). That is because they are in essence the afflictions of attachment, violence, and view; mental karma is karma that is in essence intention; and karma and affliction are distinct.[1170] The Dārṣṭāntika {subsect of the Sautrāntikas} say: The Sūtra to Be Reflected Upon declares: Monks, through engaging and accumulating karma that is intention, one is born in the hells. What karma that is intention is produced and accumulated? Monks, some intentionally produce and collect the three physical karmas, or the four types of verbal karma, or the three types of mental karma . . . and so on. Monks, how are the three types of mental karma that is intention produced and accumulated? Some monks possess covetousness, or have a mind of malice, or have wrong view. Monks, for some this is distorted view. . . .[1171] This sūtra does not mention mental karmas other than covetousness and so on. But it is not contradictory to call them mental karmas or afflictions, because this sūtra indicates that the three — covetousness, malice, and wrong view — are also mental karma,[1172] and some mental karmas are also affliction. [360] Vaibhāṣikas say: If that is so, then karma and affliction would become one entity, and if that is asserted it would contradict scripture, because that sūtra explains that since “possess covetousness” teaches just that thought, it engages the karma of mental intention through afflicted means.[1173]
bzlog pa legs par spyad pa yin/ /
That opposing nonvirtue is positive action. (4:66a)

lus dang ngag dang yid kyi las mi dge ba las bzlog pa'i dge ba dag ni legs par spyad pa yin no/ / gal te yang dag pa'i lta ba dang log lta ni dge ba dang mi dge ba ma yin par 'gyur te/ pha rol la phan gnod byed pa'i bsam pa med pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ phan gnod byed pa'i bsam pa'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Virtuous action opposing physical, verbal, and mental nonvirtuous karma is positive action (sucarita). Objection: Right view and wrong view are neither virtuous nor nonvirtuous because they have no intention to benefit or harm others. Reply: They are the cause of the intention to benefit or harm.
drug pa dge bcu mi dge bcur dbye ba
Ten virtuous and ten nonvirtuous actions
['di] la
This has two types: overview and elaboration.
mdor bstan pa ni
OVERVIEW
de las che long bsdus nas ni/ / dge dang mi dge ci rigs par/ / las kyi lam ni bcur gsungs so/ / 66
By broadly summarizing those actions, the path of virtuous or nonvirtuous karma is said to be the ten actions of various types. (4:66bcd)

nyes spyad dang legs spyad de dag las che long tsam zhig mdor bsdus nas ni dge ba'i las kyi lam ni bcu dang mi dge ba'i las kyi lam yang bcur gsungs so/ / dge mi dge'i rags rim tsam zhig bsdus kyi thams cad ma yin pa'i phyir ci rigs par zhes smros so/ / gang dag ma bsdus she na/ re zhig mi dge ba'i lus kyi las gsum gyi sbyor mjug dang*/ nyon mongs pa can gyi lus kyi las mi tshangs spyod dang rdeg pa dang 'ching ba la sogs pa dang*/ srog gcod kyi sbyor ba yin pas mtshams med lnga'i de bzhin gshegs pa la ngan sems kyis khrag 'byin pa dang*/ nye ba lnga'i mchod rten 'jig pa'ang ma bsdus shing ngag gi las chung ba dag kyang ma bsdus la/ yid kyi las khro ba la sogs pa dgu dang ngo tsha khrel med dang sems pa mi dge ba dag kyang ma bsdus so/ / de bzhin du dge ba'i phyogs la'ang lus kyi dge ba bdun gyi sbyor 'jug dang lus kyi dge ba chang mi 'thung ba dang phyi dro'i kha zas spong ba la sogs pa dang sbyin pa dang mchod pa la sogs pa dang ngag gis snyan par smra ba dang bstod pa la sogs pa dang yid kyi sems pa dge ba dang ngo tsha khrel yod dang dad pa la sogs pa bcu yang ma bsdus so/ /

By broadly summarizing those negative and positive actions, the path of virtuous karma, or the path of nonvirtuous karma, is said to be the ten actions of various types, because they constitute just a general summation that does not include all instances of virtue and nonvirtue. Question: What actions are not included? Reply: The karmic path does not include the preparation and conclusion of the three intermittent nonvirtuous physical karmas; afflicted physical karma such as impure conduct — striking and binding and so on; and from the five heinous acts, injuring a tathāgata and causing him to bleed through evil intention, since it is preparation for taking life. And from the five near-heinous acts, destroying stūpas as well as minor verbal karmas also are not included. Mental karmas such as the nine of wrath and so on, nonembarrassment, and nonvirtuous intention also are not included. Similarly, some virtuous states are not included, such as the preparation and conclusion of the seven physical virtues, the physical virtues of not drinking alcohol, abandoning eating food after midday, and so on, as well as giving, enhancing, and so on. Also the verbal karma of speaking pleasantly, praising, and so on are not included. Again the mental intention of virtue, shame, embarrassment, and the ten mental factors of faith and so on are not included.
rgyas par bshad pa
ELABORATION
['di] la rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa dang*/ kun slong dang*/ gzhi dang*/ ngo bo dang*/ las kyi lam du dang sems pa lhan cig tu 'byung ba dang*/ ldan pa'i tshul dang*/ 'bras bu bshad pa bdun las/

This has seven types: (1) indicative and nonindicative form, (2) motivation, (3) basis, (4) nature [of action], (5) the number of karmic paths that arise simultaneously with intention, (6) how they are possessed, and (7) results.
dang po ni
INDICATIVE AND NONINDICATIVE FORM
mi dge drug ni rnam rig min/ / gcig rnam gnyis so de dag kyang / / byed na dge ba bdun rnam gyis/ / ting 'dzin las skyes rnam rig min/ / 67

Six nonvirtuous karmas are nonindicative form. One has two types. Also those committed by oneself and the seven virtuous karmas have two types. Those arising from concentration are nonindicative. (4:67)

las kyi lam de rnams las mi dge ba srog gcod dang ma byin len dang ngag gi las bzhi ste drug ni gzhan byed du 'jug pa na rnam par rig byed min pa'i rang bzhin yin te/ de dag gzhan byed du bcug pas kyang rang nyid la'ang las kyi lam du 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ rang la dngos kyi rig byed med pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dod log gcig pu ni rang nyid kyi rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa rnam pa gnyis ka yin te/ las de ni bdag nyid kyis byas na dngos gzhir 'gyur gyi gzhan byed du bcug pas rdzogs pa ma yin pa'i phyir te/ gzhan gyis byas pa las bdag gis ba mi myong bas so/ / srog gcod pa la sogs pa las kyi lam drug po de dag kyang bdag nyid kyis byed cing dus de nyid kyi tshe shi ba la sogs par gyur na rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa rnam pa gnyis kar 'gyur ro/ / {de yang srog gcod pa la rig byed kyi dus de'i tshe shi na gnyis ka yin gyi phyis shi na ni rig byed min pa kho na yin no } bdag nyid kyis byas kyang sems can de dus phyis shi na ni rig byed ma yin pa kho nar 'gyur te/ sbyor ba'i tshe dngos gzhi ma byung ba'i phyir dang*/ dngos gzhi'i tshe rig byed med pa'i phyir ro/ / yid kyi las gsum ni rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa gnyis ka ma yin no/ /

From those karmic paths, if six — the nonvirtuous (aśubha) karmas of (1) taking life and (2) taking what is not given, and (3–6) the four verbal actions — are committed by making another do them, they are in essence nonindicative form, because by making others do them [361] they become karmic paths for oneself as well and one does not have actual indicative form. One action, sexual misconduct, has two types — one’s own (1) indicative form and (2) nonindicative form — because if that karma is committed by oneself it becomes an actual basis, but if one makes another commit it it is an incomplete action because one does not experience pleasure when others commit it. Also, if those six karmic paths such as taking life and so on are committed by oneself but one dies at just the time they are committed and so forth, then those actions would have two types: (1) indicative and (2) nonindicative form. {Further, if one were to die when manifesting the indicative form of taking life, it would have both types. If one were to die later, it would be nonindicative form alone.} Though one commits that act oneself, if that sentient being were to die after oneself, it would be nonindicative form alone because at the time of preparation, the actual basis does not yet occur, and at the time of the actual basis, there is no indicative form. The three mental karmas are not both indicative and nonindicative.

dge ba srog gcod pa spong ba la sogs pa lus ngag gi las kyi lam gzugs can bdun ni yang dag par blangs pa'i tshul khrims kyi dbang du byas nas de ni gzhan las nod pas rnam par rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa rnam pa gnyis ka'o/ / bsam gtan dang zag med kyi ting nge 'dzin las skyes pa'i srog gcod pa spong ba la sogs pa sdom pas bsdus pa bdun ni mnyam gzhag gi sems tsam la rag las pas rnam par rig byed min pa kho na'o/ /

The seven virtuous physical karmic paths of body and speech, such as abandoning taking life, have two aspects — indicative form and nonindicative form — since from the perspective of correctly taking up ethics they are received from others. The seven including the vows of abandoning taking life and so on that arise from absorption and uncontaminated concentration are nonindicative alone since they rely on just the mind of equipoise.
nyer bsdogs rnams ni rnam rig byed/ / rnam rig byed min 'gyur ba'am/ / ma yin bzlog pa mjug yin no/ / sbyor ba rtsa ba gsum las skyes/ / 68
Preliminary stages are indicative form. It is either nonindicative or not. The opposite is the conclusion. Preparation arises from the three roots. (4:68)

dge ba dang mi dge ba'i las kyi lam bdun po de dag gi nyer bsdogs te sbyor ba rnams ni nges par rnam par rig byed kyi rang bzhin yin te/ lus ngag gi rang bzhin yin pa'i phyir ro/ / sbyor ba de yang gal te kun slong nyon mongs pa drag po'am rab tu dwang ba drag pos rtsom na ni rnam par rig byed min par yang 'gyur ba yin la/ 'on te kun slong drag po ma yin pas sbyor ba rtsom na ni rig byed kho nar 'gyur gyi rig byed ma yin par 'gyur ba ma yin no/ / des na gcig tu ma nges pa'i phyir rnam par brtags pa'i sgra'am zhes smros so/ / sbyor ba nyer bsdogs las bzlog pa rig byed ma yin pa'i rang bzhin ni nges par yin la/ rig byed du ni 'gyur ba'am yang na ma yin pa ni las kyi lam gyi mjug yin no/ / ji ltar zhe na/ gal te las kyi lam byas nas de dang rjes su mthun pa'i chos spyod na ni rig byed du'ang 'gyur la/ 'on te mi spyod na ni rig byed ma yin pa kho nar 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / sbyor ba dang dngos dang mjug gi khyad par gang zhe na/

Preparatory preliminary stages (sāmanataka) to the seven paths of virtuous and nonvirtuous karma are definitely in essence indicative form because they are in essence body and speech. Also, if that preparation is initiated with strong afflicted motivation or strong clear faith, it is nonindicative form. Or if preparation is initiated with weak motivation, it is indicative alone and not nonindicative form. Because they are definitely not the same, the clarifying term “or” is stated. The essence of nonindicative form that is the opposite (viparyaya) of the preparatory preliminary stages is definitely the indicative or nonindicative form that is the conclusion (pṛṣṭha) of the karmic path. Question: Why is that? Reply: If, having committed a karmic path, one later engages in such acts, they also become indicative form; however, if one does not engage in such acts, they are nonindicative alone. Question: What is the difference between the preparation, actual action, and conclusion?

'di ltar 'ga' zhig srog chags gsod par 'dod nas khri la sogs pa las langs te srog chags de'i drung du 'gro ba la sogs pa nas mtshon blangs te lan cig gam gnyis bsnun par byed cing dngos su srog gcod par mi byed pa'i bar ni sbyor bar yin no/ / bsnun pa gang gis dngos su srog gcod par byed pa de'i tshe rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa'i skad cig ma ni las kyi lam dngos yin no/ / de phyin chad kyi rig byed ma yin pa dang*/ lpags pa bshu ba dang*/ 'khrud pa dang*/ sha 'tshong ba dang*/ 'tshed pa dang*/ za ba dang sgrogs pa la sogs pa'i rig byed dag ni mjug yin no/ /
de bzhin du gzhan gyi nor bdag gir bya bar 'dod pas 'gro ba nas bzung ste len pa dang sbed pa la sogs pa ni ma byin par len pa'i sbyor ba yin no/ / gang gi tshe thob pa'i blo skyes te gnas nas spags pa'am bdag gir byas pa de'i tshe'i rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa'i skad cig ni dngos yin no/ / de phyin chad ni mjug yin no zhes bya ba la sogs pa'ang shes par bya'o/ / brnab sems la sogs pa gsum ni mngon du gyur pa tsam gyis dngos gzhir 'gyur ba'i phyir sbyor ba dang mjug med do/ /

Reply: Preparation is when some, desiring to kill a living being, take up a knife and proceed to the vicinity of that being and so on, and raising the weapon, strike once or twice, until life is directly taken. The actual action of the karmic path is the instant of indicative and nonindicative form when that life is directly taken by the action of striking and so on. [362] The conclusion is the nonindicative form following that, or the indicative form such as skinning the carcass, washing it, selling the meat, or boiling it, eating it, proclaiming it, and so on.
Similarly, the preparation for taking that which is not given is desiring to make another’s property mine, proceeding there, taking it, hiding it, and so on. The actual basis is the instant of indicative and nonindicative form when the thought “I have obtained it” arises, having removed it from its normal place and apprehending it as “mine.” The conclusion is what follows that. Because an actual basis occurs by the mere manifestation of the three — covetousness, malice, and wrong view — there is no preparation or conclusion.

gal te gsad bya de 'chi ba'i srid pa la gnas pa de'i tshe gsod pa po'i rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa de las kyi lam dngos yin nam/ 'on te shi zin pa de'i tshe'i rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa de yin/ dang po ltar na gsod pa po dang gsad bya'i srog chags lhan cig shi ba'ang dngos su 'gyur na/ snga dang mnyam du shi ba la/ / dngos med lus gzhan skyes phyir ro/ / zhes 'chad pa dang 'gal la/ gnyis pa ltar na bsnun pa gang gis dngos su srog gcod par byed pa de'i tshe'i rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa de dngos ma yin par 'gyur te/ de'i tshe shi ba med pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ nyes pa med de/ srog gcod par byed pa zhes bya ba ni sbyor ba'i 'bras bu las kyi lam dngos su rdzogs pa la 'dod pa'i phyir na srog chags shi ba'i gnas skabs kyi rig byed dang rig byed ma yin pa'i skad cig ma de nyid las kyi lam dngos yin no/ / 'o na bstan bcos las/ srog chags bsad la srog gcod pa ma 'gags pa yod dam zhe na/ yod de/ 'di lta ste dper na srog chags kyi srog bcad la sbyor ba med par ma gyur pa lta bu'o zhes gsungs pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/ bye brag tu smra ba na re der ni mjug la sbyor ba'i sgrar gsungs te srog chags kyi srog chad kyang 'thub pa dang snying 'byin pa dang mgo gcod pa la sogs pa'i mjug ma 'gag par yod pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ / slob dpon gyis de lta na khyed rang gi 'dod pa dang 'gal te/ khyed srog chags shi nas las kyi lam dngos su 'dod pas de'i tshe srog gcod pa'i dngos gzhi ma 'gags pa'i phyir ro zhes brjod pa na/ bye brag tu smra bas 'o na ni bstan bcos der dngos kho na la sbyor ba'i sgrar gsungs pas nyes pa med do zhes smras pa dang*/ slob dpon gyis 'o na de'i tshe'i rig byed las kyi lam dngos su mi 'gyur te/ shi zin pa la rig byed des yang gsod par mi nus pa'i phyir ro zhes brjod pa na/

Objection: Is the indicative and nonindicative form of the killer, when the being who is killed abides in the death state, the actual karmic path? Or, otherwise, is the indicative and nonindicative form of the killer after that being has died the actual karmic path? (1) In the first case, if the killer and the living being to be killed actually die simultaneously, or the killer dies earlier, that would contradict the explanation, “It is not the actual karmic path because the killer is born in another body.” (2) In the second case, when the killer engages in directly taking that life by striking, his indicative and nonindicative form are not the actual karmic path because death does not occur [precisely] at that time. Reply: There is no fault because “taking life” is asserted to be the actual complete karmic path that is the result of preparation. The actual karmic path is just that instant of indicative and nonindicative form when that living being dies. Objection: But that contradicts the treatise (Attainment of Knowledge),[1174] which states: In the killing of living beings, can killing exist when [the act] has not yet ceased? It can because, for example, taking the life of a living being does not occur without preparation.[1175] Vaibhāṣikas say: Here the term “preparation” is applied to the conclusion because, though the life force of the living being has been severed, before the conclusion of the act has ceased it can be dismembered, its heart removed, its head severed, and so on. Vasubandhu says: If that is so, that contradicts your assertion, because at that time the actual basis of the act of taking life has not yet ceased, since you explicitly assert that the karmic path exists after the death of the living being.[1176] Vaibhāṣikas say: There is no fault since in that treatise the term “preparation” is applied to the actual basis. Vasubandhu says: However, at that time, the karmic path that is indicative form does not become the actual basis because such indicative form is unable to kill after death.[1177]
