bye brag tu smra ba na re de lta na de'i tshe'i rig byed ma yin pa'ang dngos su mi 'gyur te/ shi zin pa la des gsad par mi nus pa'i phyir ro/ / des na de'i tshe mi nus kyang rig byed ma yin pa las kyi lam dngos yin pa ltar rig byed kyang de dang 'dra bar dngos yin no/ / des na shi zin pa la dngos su byas na dngos la sbyor ba'i sgrar gsungs pa yin la/ 'chi ba la dngos su byas na mjug la sbyor ba'i sgrar gsungs pa yin no zhes zer ro/ / gzhan yang las kyi lam gzhan gyi sbyor ba dang mjug gzhan gyi dngos su 'gyur ba'ang yod de/ 'ga' zhig bsad pa'i phyir gzhan gyi nor 'phrog pa dang de'i chung ma la nyal po byed pa dang rdzun smra ba la sogs pa lta bu'o/ / {slob dpon gyis yid kyi gsum bya ba ma brtsams pa'i phyir sbyor bar mi 'gyur bar bzhed do }
gnyis pa kun slong bshad pa la
MOTIVATION

mi dge ba'i las kyi lam de dag kyang mthar phyin par ni 'og nas 'byung ba ltar chags sogs so sos byed la/ dang po'i kun slong gi dbang du byas nas sbyor ba ni mi dge ba'i rtsa ba gsum las skyes pa yin te/ las kyi lam dngos ni sbyor bas skyed pa yin la sbyor ba'ang 'dod chags la sogs pa gsum las skyes pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di ltar srog gcod pa 'dod chags las skyes pa ni sha la sogs pa la sred nas gsod pa'o/ / zhe sdang las skyes pa ni 'khon gyis gsod pa'o/ / gti mug las skyes pa ni mchod sbyin byed pa rnams dang*/ rgyal po rnams kyi bstan bcos las mi ma rungs pa rnams bsad na bsod nams su 'gyur ro zhes bshad do snyam nas gsod pa dang*/ par sig pa rnams pha ma rgas sam nad tshabs chen pos btab pa na bsad na bsod nams su 'gyur ro zhes bya ba dang*/ sbrul dang sdig pa dang sbrang bu t+r+yai ma bu ka la sogs pa ni mi rnams la gnod par byed pa'i phyir bsad na bsod nams su 'gyur ro zhes bya ba dang*/ ri dwags dang phyugs dang bya la sogs pa ni longs spyod par bya ba yin pa'i phyir bsad do zhes zer ba tshad mar byas nas gsod pa dang*/ {'jig rten pha rol med do snyam nas gsad pa } log par lta bas rab tu bcug pa'i srog gcod pa rnams kyang yin no/ / ma byin par len pa 'dod chags las skyes pa ni nor la sogs pa la sred pas len pa'o/ / zhe sdang las skyes pa ni/ 'khon las 'phrog pa'o/ / gti mug las skyes pa ni rgyal po rnams kyi bstan bcos tshad mar byas nas mi srun pa la chad pas gcod pa'i phyir 'phrog pa dang*/ bram ze rnams na re/ 'di thams cad tshangs pa dbang ba yin la bram ze rnams ni tshangs pa'i bu yin pa'i phyir 'di thams cad ni tshangs pas bram ze rnams la byin pa yin na bram ze rnams dmas pas dmangs rigs la sogs pas longs spyod par zad do/ / de lta bas na bram ze rnams gzhan gyi nor len pa ni rang gi nor len pa yin pa'i phyir nyes pa med do { chos su bshad/ / ngo 'thon du ni nor 'phrog nus gyur kyang*/ / rang gi grags pa nyams par 'gyur bas na/ / de phyir ma mthong bar ni blang bar gyis} zhes zer nas rku ba lta bu dang*/ log par blta bas len pa lta bu'o/ /

Also, those nonvirtuous karmic paths are brought to completion by attachment and so on as committed by each, as they occur below. First from the perspective of motivation, preparation (prayoga) arises from the three roots (trimūla) of nonvirtue and so on because the actual karmic path is generated by preparation, and preparation also arises from the three roots such as attachment. Thus taking life that arises from attachment is killing through craving for meat and so on. That arising from aversion is killing through spite. That arising from delusion is taking life while reflecting on treatises of priests and kings that explain it is meritorious to kill evil human beings; or cannibals who say that it is meritorious to club and kill one’s aged parents or those with serious illness, or taking life under the belief that it is meritorious to kill snakes, scorpions, bees, tryambuka flies,[1178] and so on because they harm human beings, or that it is valid to kill deer, cows, birds, and so on because their meat can be consumed; or to take life strongly influenced by wrong view {such as killing with the thought “there is no future world or life beyond this”}. Taking what is not given that arises from attachment is taking property through craving. That arising from aversion is depriving others of their property through spite. That arising from delusion is depriving meek human beings as a punishment through taking the Treatise on Kingship[1179] to be valid. Brahmans say: Because the entire universe is controlled by Brahma, and brahmans are the sons of Brahma, the entire universe is given to the brahmans by Brahma. Brahmans may therefore utilize the property of the śūdras and so on since they are low, and when brahmans take the wealth of others, it is taking what is their wealth, and thus there is no fault. {Further, it relates: When there is great decline, it is said to be virtuous for brahmans to steal. Though they may plunder others’ wealth openly, since the reputation of the brahmans would decline, they should take it without being seen.} Thus such theft is taking through wrong view. [364]

'dod log 'dod chags las skyes pa ni gzhan gyi chung ma la chags pas longs spyod pa'o/ / zhe sdang las skyes pa ni 'khon gyis longs spyod pa'o/ / gti mug las skyes pa ni par sig pa rnams de yang*/ bram ze rgud che rku ba ma la sogs pa la longs spyod pa dang*/ ba lang 'brang gi mchod sbyin las cho ga can gyis chu btung ngo rtswa bcad do/ / ma'i gan du nyal po la 'gro'o/ / sring mo'i gan du 'gro'o/ / rus gcig pa'i gan du 'gro'o/ / zhes bshad pa'i rjes su 'brangs nas de dag la longs spyod pa lta bu'o/ / kha cig nub phyogs kyi bram ze chu skyes zhes bya ba dag na re bud med ni gtun dang*/ me tog dang*/ 'bras bu dang*/ zas smin pa dang*/ ngogs dang*/ lam dang 'dra ba'i phyir spyad kyang nyes pa med pas thams cad kyis spyad par bya'o zhes zer ba dang mthun par byed pa dang*/ log bltas bcug pa'o/ / rdzun la sogs pa chags pa las skyes pa ni bdag dang mdza' bo skyob pa'i phyir dang*/ rnyed pa dang bkur sti'i phyir smra'o/ / zhe sdang las skyes pa ni 'khon las nges par 'byung bar bya ba'i phyir ro/ gti mug las skyes pa ni/ rgyal po gzhad gad ldan dang bud med dang*/ / bag ma len pa'i tshe dang gsod pa dang*/ nor rkun 'phrogs tshe rdzun byas gnod med de/ rdzun lnga ltung bar byed pa min zhes bshad ces drang srong dag gis rgyal po la smras pa'i rjes su 'brangs nas de dag gi tshe dang log bltas smra ba lta bu'o/ / phra ma la sogs pa gti mug las skyes pa ni log bltas kun nas bslang ba dang*/ phyi rol pa'i rig byed la sogs pa'i bstan bcos ngan pa la zhen pa'i blos 'don pa'o/ / gal te brnab sems la sogs pa 'dod chags la sogs pas ji ltar slong ste de dag nyid kun slong gi bsam pa yin pa'i phyir ro zhe na/

Sexual misconduct arising from attachment is copulating with the wife of another through attachment. That arising from aversion is copulating with another through spite. That arisen from delusion is, for example, a cannibal copulating with his mother and so on. It is said that if a priest of the ox sacrifice drinks cinamon water, cuts grass, and then says, “I will copulate with my mother, I will copulate with my sister, I will copulate with a female of the same clan,” he may then copulate with them.[1180] The brahman Maga of the West said: Because females are like a pestle, a flower, ripe fruit, food, the shore, and a path, there is no fault in using them, so use them all. Act in accordance with this and make others do it.[1181] He conforms with the previous and engages wrong view. Lies and so on that arise from attachment are speaking lies to protect oneself and one’s friends, and for the purpose of property and respect. Those arising from aversion are, for example, renouncing home through spite. Those arising from delusion are, for example, when a rishi explains to a king, “If a king kills a jester, a female, or a bride he has taken, or if he lies when he has appropriated others’ wealth, there is no harm because the five lies are not downfalls”[1182] and the king follows such advice; this is lying arising from wrong view. Slander and so on arising from delusion is reciting evil treatises of non-Buddhist science and so on with a mind of craving and motivated by wrong view. Objection: Since covetousness and so on arise from attachment and so forth, they are the motivating thought behind them.
de yi mjug thogs las byung phyir/ / brnab sems sogs rtsa gsum las skyes/ / dge ba sbyor dang mjug bcas rnams/ / chags sdang gti mug med las skyes/ / 69

Because they occur at their conclusion, covetousness and so on arise from the three roots. Virtuous karma possessing preparation and conclusion arises from nonattachment, nonaversion, and nondelusion. (4:69)

'dod chags dang zhe sdang dang gti mug gsum po de'i mjug thog las byung ba'i phyir brnab sems la sogs pa'ang mi dge ba'i rtsa ba gsum las skyes pa yin te/ rin po che'i phreng ba las/ 'dod chags zhe sdang gti mug gsum/ / des bskyed las ni mi dge ba/ / zhes 'byung ba ltar de dag ni mi dge ba'i rtsa ba gsum pos ci rigs par kun nas slong ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: Because they occur at the conclusion of attachment, aversion, and delusion, covetousness (abhidhyā) and so on arise from the three roots of nonvirtue. As the Precious Garland asserts: Nonvirtue arises from the generation of the three: attachment, aversion, and delusion.[1183] Thus they are fully motivated in various ways by the three roots of nonvirtue.

dge ba'i las kyi lam dngos sbyor ba dang mjug dang bcas pa rnams ni khyad par med par chags pa med pa dang sdang ba med pa dang gti mug med pa las skyes pa yin te/ de dag gis kun nas bslang ba'i phyir dang*/ mtshungs par ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dod chags la sogs pa las skyes pa ni dge bar mi rung ba'i phyir dang*/ dge ba dag ni dge ba'i sems las skye ba'i phyir ro/ / dge ba'i las kyi lam gyi sbyor dngos 'jug gsum ni rim pa ltar mi dge ba'i las kyi lam gyi sbyor dngos 'jug gsum spong ba nyid yin te/ 'di ltar dge tshul bsnyen par rdzogs par byed pa na sdom pa'i sbyor ba ni gnas su 'jug pa dang mkhan slob dang dge 'dun la phyag 'tshal ba dang mkhan po la gsol ba 'debs pa la sogs pa nas las lan gnyis brjod pa yan chad do/ / las lan gsum pa brjod pa'i tha ma'i dus kyi rig byed dang de'i skad cig gi rig byed ma yin pa ni las kyi lam dngos yin no/ / de phyin chad gnas bsgo ba dang*/ de'i rten rnam par rig par byed pa dang*/ ji srid du rig byed ma yin pa rjes su 'brang ba sdom pa ma btang ba de srid ni 'jug yin no/ / gal te mi dge ba'i las kyi lam de dag kun nas slong ba na 'dod chags la sogs pa gsum char gyis ci rigs par slong la de dag rdzogs shing mthar phyin par byed pa ni 'dod chags la sogs pa so sos byed do zhes bshad na de dag gang zhig gang gis mthar phyin par byed ce na

Virtuous karmic paths possessing the actual basis, preparation, and conclusion unequivocally arise from nonattachment (alobha), nonaversion (adveṣa), and nondelusion (amoha) because these motivate them and are concomitant with them. Those arising from attachment and so on cannot be virtuous, and those that are virtuous arise from a virtuous mind. The three states of preparation, actual basis, and conclusion of the virtuous karmic path respectively abandon the three states of preparation, actual basis, and conclusion of the nonvirtuous karmic path. That is because if a novice takes full ordination, then (1) the preparation for taking the vows is entering the place, prostrating to the abbot, masters, and Saṅgha, making requests to the abbot and so on, and reciting the rite two [365] or more times. (2) The actual basis of the karmic path is the indicative form occurring at the time of expressing the third and final recitation and the nonindicative form in that instant. (3) The conclusion is the indicative form of appointing an abode and its basis and from that time on adhering to nonindicative form and not relinquishing the vows. Question: It is said that if those nonvirtuous karmic paths are motivated, they are motivated in various ways by the three states of attachment and so on, and attachment and so on accomplish them and bring them each to a conclusion. How do they bring them to a conclusion?
gsod dang gnod sems tshig rtsub po/ / zhe sdang gis ni mthar phyin byed/ / log g.yem brnab sems ma byin len/ / chags pa yis ni rdzogs par byed/ / 70
Killing, malice, and harsh words are accomplished by aversion. Sexual misbehavior, covetousness, and taking that not given are accomplished due to attachment. (4:70)

gsod pa srog gcod dang gnod sems dang tshig rtsub po gsum {dang pos } ni sems can yongs su 'dor ba {gzhan gnyis } dang rtsub pa'i sems mngon du gyur pa'i phyir zhe sdang gis mthar phyin par byed do/ / 'dod pas log par g.yem pa dang brnab sems dang ma byin par len pa rnams ni chags pa yis rdzogs par byed la/

[Reply:] The three actions of killing (vadha), which is taking life, malice (vyāpāda), and harsh words (pāruṣya), are accomplished (niṣṭhā) due to aversion (dveṣa) because {the first} completely destroys sentient beings and {the other two} manifest minds that are coarse. Sexual misbehavior, covetousness, and taking that not given, which are motivated by desire, are accomplished due to attachment.
log par lta ba gti mug gis/ / lhag ma gsum gyis rdzogs par 'dod/ /
Wrong view is accomplished due to delusion. The remainder are completed by the three. (4:71ab)

log par lta ba ni cher rmongs na log par lta bas gti mug gis rdzogs par byed do/ / lhag ma rdzun phra ma ngag kyal rnams ni 'dod chags la sogs pa gsum gyis ci rigs par rdzogs shing mthar phyin par byed par 'dod do/ /

If wrong view greatly confuses the mind, wrong view (mithyādṛṣṭi) is accomplished due to delusion (moha). Also it is asserted that the remainder — lies, slander, and idle speech — are completed and accomplished by various combinations of the three: attachment and so on.
gsum pa gzhi bshad pa ni
BASIS
gzhi ni sems can longs spyod dang / / ming dang gzugs ni ming yin no/ / 71
The basis is sentient beings, objects of enjoyment, name and form, and names. (4:71cd)

zhe sdang gis mthar phyin par byed pa la sogs pa bzhi'i gzhi ni go rim bzhin du gsod bya la sogs pa'i sems can dang*/ reg bya la sogs pa'i longs spyod dang*/ phung po lnga char la skur pa 'debs pas ming dang gzugs dang*/ rdzun la sogs pa ngag yin zhing ngag ming la 'jug pas ming yin no/ / yang na tshig rtsub kyi gzhi sems can yin pa ltar rdzun la sogs pa gsum gyi'ang yin la/ gsum gyi gzhi ming yin pa ltar tshig rtsub kyi'ang yin no zhes phan tshun mtshon pa'o zhes gsung ngo*/ / 'dir gzhi'i sgra ni rten nam yul la brjod pa yin te gsod pa la sogs pa ni sems can la 'jug pa'i phyir dang*/ 'dod log la sogs pa ni longs spyod la 'jug pa'i phyir dang*/ log lta ni phung po lnga ga la skur pa 'debs pa'i phyir dang*/ rdzun la sogs pa ni ngag yin la de ming la 'jug pa'i phyir ro/ /

The basis (adhiṣṭhāna) of the four actions accomplished by aversion and so on consists, respectively, of (1) sentient beings (sattva) who are the objects of killing and so on, (2) objects of enjoyment (bhoga) such as tactile objects, (3) name and form (nāmarūpa), since the five aggregates are deprecated, and (4) names (nāma), since lies and so on are speech, and speech employs names. Again, just as sentient beings are the basis of harsh words, so they are also the basis of the three actions of lying and so on. Just as the basis of three actions is names, so they are also the basis of harsh words, for it is said that they mutually signify each other. Here the term basis represents the support, or object, because (1) killing and so on involves sentient beings, (2) sexual misconduct and so on involves enjoyment, (3) wrong view deprecates the five aggregates, and (4) the speech of lying and so on employs names.
srog gcod pa la khyad par brjod pa ni
ASPECTS OF TAKING LIFE
snga dang mnyam du shi ba la/ / dngos med lus gzhan skyes phyer ro/ / dmag la sogs par don gcig phyir/ / thams cad byed pa po bzhin ldan/ / 72

If he dies before or at the same time, there is no actual basis because the body of another arises. Because in war and so on all possess the same purpose, they possess the actual karma just like the agent. (4:72)

gang zhig gis pha rol po 'chi nges par byas te rang nyid pha rol po 'chi ba'i snga rol dang pha rol dang gsod pa po mnyam du shi ba de la ni srog gcod pa'i sbyor bas reg par 'gyur gyi las kyi lam dngos dang 'jug 'byung ba med de/ gang zhig bsad par bya ba de ma shi bar ni srog gcod pa'i kha na ma tho ba byung bar mi rigs la de shi ba na ni gsod pa po'ang shi ste lus gang gis sbyor ba byas pa'i lus de la brten nas 'bras bu rdzogs pa yin pa na srog chad pa'i tshe sbyor ba byed pa po'i lus {de dang skal ba ma mnyam pa'i } las gzhan pa'i lus skyes pa'i phyir ro/{ der 'gyur ba la gang gis sbyor ba byas pa de la dngos gzhi 'grub dgos pas so/ /} de nyid kyi phyir mdo las/ sbyor ba yang byas la 'bras bu yang yongs su rdzogs par gyur kyang srog gcod pa'i kha na ma tho bas reg par mi 'gyur ba lta mchis sam/ bka' stsal pa yod de/ 'di lta ste gsod pa po sngar ram mnyam du shi ba lta bu'o zhes gsungs so/ /

If someone who definitely arranges the death of another dies before the other, or the killer dies at the same time as the other, he commits the fault of preparing to take life but he has no actual basis (maula) or conclusion of the karmic path, because it is inappropriate that it is the transgression of killing until the death of the being to be killed [actually occurs], and if the killer also dies when that person dies, then the body of another {of different status to the agent} arises distinct from the body of the agent of preparation, yet the result must be completed in dependence on that body that committed the preparation. {Therefore, to become an actual basis, whoever commits [366] the preparation must also accomplish the actual basis.} Thus a sūtra declares: Though the preparation is accomplished and the result fully completed, it is said or proclaimed that the transgression of taking life does not arise because, for example, the killer may die before or at the same time as the being who is killed.[1184]

'o na mang po tshogs te gros byas nas dmag dang ri dwags kyi lings dang rgyar 'chu ba la sogs pa byed pa na dngos su gcig gis sems can srog dang bral bar byas pa na gzhan de dag srog gcod pa la sogs pa dang ldan par 'gyur ram mi 'gyur zhe na/ dmag dang ri dwags kyi lings la sogs pa ni sems can de gsod pa la sogs pa byed par don gcig la zhugs pa'i sbyor ba can yin pa'i phyir dngos su gsod pa po ma yin pa thams cad la'ang dngos su gsod par byed pa po bzhin du srog gcod pa'i dngos kyi las kyi lam dang ldan no/ / 'o na gang zhig nan gyis khrid pa de las kyi lam dang ldan nam zhe na/ de ni dmag la sogs pa'i tshogs pa na yod kyang gal te rang gi srog la thug kyang gzhan gyi srog mi gcod do snyam du nges par byas te 'gro na ni de la srog gcod pa'i nyes pas reg par mi 'gyur la/ 'on te bsam pa nges pa de lta bu med na ni ldan par 'gyur ro/ /

Question: If an assembly of many beings decided to go to war, or to hunt wild game, or seize another’s extensive lands, and if one person directly took the life of a sentient being, would the others come to possess the karma of taking life? Reply: Because in war and hunting wild game and so on all possess the preparation that engages the same purpose of killing sentient beings and so on, they possess the actual karmic path of taking life, just like the agent who actually kills, though all do not actually kill. Question: Would all come to possess the karmic path of the dominant leaders or not? Reply: Though they may have participated in the assembly that decided on war and so on, if they go to war and so forth with the determination not to take the life of another even though one’s life is threatened, they would not commit the fault of taking life. However, if they have no such definite thought, they would come to possess that karma.
bzhi pa ngo bo bshad pa ni
NATURE OF ACTION
srog gcod pa ni bsams bzhin du/ / ma nor bar ni gzhan gsad pa'o/ / ma byin len pa gzhan gyi nor/ / mthu dang 'jab bus bdag gir byed/ / 73
Taking life is killing another, intentionally, and unmistakenly. Taking what is not given is taking as mine the property of others by force or stealth. (4:73)

srog gcod pa ni 'di bsad do snyam du bsams bzhin du gsod pa dang*/ ma nor bar gsod pa dang*/ gzhan bsad pa'i yan lag gsum dang ldan pas gsod pa'o/ / bsam bzhin du zhes bya bas ni gcer bu pa dag /bsregs par ma bsams kyang me la reg na 'tshig pa ltar ma bsams par rkang pa'i 'og tu srog chags shi ba dang*/ sems can gyi bsam pa med pa shing gcod pa la sogs pa'ang srog gcod pa'i nyes pa dang ldan no zhes zer ba spangs te/ gal te gsod pa'i bsam pa med par 'chi ba'i rkyen byas pa tsam gyis srog gcod par 'gyur na pha ma rnams bu dang bu mo shi ba na srog gcod dang ldan par 'gyur te/ de dag bskyed pa nyid kyis 'chi ba'i rgyu byas pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du sman pa rnams kyis sman spyad nyes pa dang*/ yon bdag rnams kyis bsod snyoms phul ba na gsol drags te gsud de shi na sman pa dang yon bdag rnams kyang srog gcod pa dang ldan par 'gyur ro/ / gal te de dag la gsod pa'i bsam pa med pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ de nyid kyis na bsam bzhin du zhes smros so/ / de nyid kyi phyir dran pa nyer gzhag las/ rgyu lngas srog gcod pa byas kyang kha na ma tho bas gos par mi 'gyur te/ 'di lta ste lam du zhugs pa na mi shes pas srog chags phra mo dang grog sbur la sogs pa srog dang bral bar byed pa dang*/ gzhan la mtshon cha gzas pa las bsam pa dang mi ldan pa gzhan la phog ste de srog dang bral ba dang*/ nad pa la sman pa phan par 'dod pas nyes par ma mthong ste sman byin pa las de shi ba dang*/ mas bu 'dul ba'i phyir brdegs pa las de srog dang bral ba dang*/ me 'bar ba'i nang du srog chags mi 'dod bzhin du lhung ba ste rgyu de lngas so zhes gsungs so/ /

Taking life (prāṇātipāta) is killing through possessing three requisites: (1) killing intentionally (saṃcintya), thinking, “I will kill this being,” (2) killing unmistakenly (abhrānta), and (3) killing another. (1) “Intentionally” is stated to refute the assertion of the Jains, who say that one possesses the fault of taking life when, without the thought to burn living beings, they die through contact with fire; or without the thought to kill them, living beings die under one’s feet; or without thinking of sentient beings, they die when one cuts down a tree. If the act of taking life arose due to merely a condition for death occurring without any intention to kill, then parents would possess the karma of taking life if their son or daughter died because giving birth to their children would act as the cause of their death! Similarly, if one were to die through doctors prescribing medicine that turned out to be inappropriate, or through patrons offering alms through fervant request that gave rise to indigestion and death, then even doctors and patrons would possess the karma of taking life. But how could that be, because they have no intention to kill? Due to that, “intentionally” is stated. The Foundations of Mindfulness Sūtra states: Though one takes life due to the five causes, the mind is not imprinted with any transgression. The five causes are: (1) unconsciously killing minute living beings and ants and so on who stray onto a path, (2) killing others through brandishing weapons and unintentionally striking them, (3) with the desire to benefit the sick, giving them medicine without seeing its inappropriateness and they die, [367] (4) a child being killed through being beaten by his mother to discipline him, and (5) causing living beings to fall into a fire without any desire to do so.[1185]

nor bar bsad pa dang bdag bsad pas ni srog gcod pa'i sbyor ba tsam du 'gyur gyi dngos su ni mi 'gyur te/ dang po la bsams pa'i don ma rdzogs pa'i phyir dang*/ gnyis pa la rdzogs pa na lus gzhan skyes pa'i phyir ro/ / srog ces bya ba ci yin zhe na/ lus sems la brten nas 'jug pa'i rlung dang rnam shes la mi 'khrul ba'i drod dang rnam shes ris mthun par gnas pa dang srog gi dbang po rnams la ci rigs par srog ces bya la de dag gcod pa'i phyir srog gcod pa'o/ / de ltar yang mdo las/ gang tshe tshe dang drod rnam shes/ / 'di dag gis ni lus 'dor zhing*/ / bor bas de tshe 'dug pa ni/ / ji ltar shing la sems med bzhin/ / zhes gsungs so/ / {the tshom za nas gang yin bsad snyam nas bsad na'ang dngos yod do }

(2) Mistaken killing and (3) killing oneself merely constitute the preparation for taking life but not the actual basis because in the first, the purpose of the intention is not completed, and in the second, when completed, one is already born in another body. Question: What is life force? Reply: That which maintains heat and consciousness without undermining the winds and consciousness that enter the body and mind is called life force. The faculty of life force is the various types of life force, and taking life is severing them. Thus also a sūtra states: Whenever life, heat, and consciousness are discarded and depart the body, at that time what remains is without mind, like a tree.[1186] {Further, though one kills while in doubt, thinking, “What did I kill?” it is still an actual basis.}

ma byin par len pa ni gzhan gyis bdag gir bzung pa'i nor dbang gis 'phrog pa'i mthu dang ma tshor bar 'jab bus bdag gir byed pa'o/{ rdzas mngon du gyur pa la thob blo skyes pa na dngos gzhir 'gyur ro/ /} 'dir yang bsam bzhin du ma nor bar zhes shes par bya ste/ ma bsams par bdag gi nor gyi gseb tu gzhan gyi nor blangs pa la ni nyes pa med pa'i phyir dang*/ nor bar gzhan gyi nor blangs pa ni sbyor ba'i nyes par 'gyur gyi dngos med pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na mchod rten gyi dkor phrogs pa dang gter brus pa {dang shi ba'i nor blangs na gang las ma byin len du 'gyur zhe na }las ma byin par len par mi 'gyur te/ gzhan gyis bdag tu ma gzung ba'i phyir ro zhe na/ ma yin te/ mchod rten gyi dkor ni sangs rgyas dang mchod rten gyi srung ma dag gis bzung ba'i phyir dang*/ gter ni yul gyi bdag pos yongs su bzung ba'i phyir ro/ / shi ba'i nor blangs pa ni khyim pa yin na nye du rnams kyis bzung ba'i phyir dang*/ rab tu byung ba yin na dge 'dun gyis bzung ba'i phyir de dag las ma byin par len par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / de la'ang dang po tha ma'i cho ga'am gsol ba'i las byas na mtshams nang de'i dge 'dun las ma byin len du 'gyur la/ ma byas na ni sangs rgyas kyi slob ma thams cad las ma byin len du 'gyur te/ lung gos kyi gzhi las/ gsol ba'am thog ma dang tha ma ma byas pa'i shi ba'i yo byad kyi rnyed pa ni sangs rgyas kyi slob ma thams cad dbang bar 'gyur ro zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Taking what is not given (adattādāna) is taking as mine the property that others hold as theirs, by strength of force or silently by stealth. {If the mind of obtainment arises in relation to that actual physical substance, it is an actual basis.} Here, one should know whether property is taken “intentionally and unmistakenly,” because there is no fault in unintentionally taking another’s property by mixing it with one’s own property, or in taking another’s property mistakenly there is the fault of preparation but there is no actual basis. Objection: However, forcefully taking donations made to stūpas and digging up treasures do not constitute taking what is not given because others do not hold [those things] as theirs. {And how does taking the property of the dead become taking what is not given?} Reply: That is not so, because the donations made to stūpas are held by the buddhas and the guardians of stūpas, and treasures are held by local deities. Because the property of the dead is claimed by relatives if that being was a householder, or claimed by the Saṅgha if that being was ordained, taking it constitutes taking what is not given. Also, if the initial and final rites or the rite of prayer have been performed, taking such property is taking what is not given from the Saṅgha of that area. If they are not performed, it is taking what is not given from all the students of the Buddha. The Chapter on Robes notes: The property of the dead for whom the rite of prayer or the initial and final rites have not been performed is owned by all the students of the Buddha.[1187]
bgrod min 'gro ba 'dod pa yis/ / log par g.yem pa rnam pa bzhi/ / rdzun tshig 'du shes gzhan sgyur ba'i/ / tshig don mngon par go ba'o/ / 74
Desiring to proceed in inappropriate ways is the four aspects of sexual misbehavior. Lying is to change another’s discernment and the meaning of those words is actually understood. (4:74)

bgrod par bya ba min pa rnam pa bzhir 'gro ba 'dod pa yis log par spyod pa'i phyir 'dod pas log par g.yem pa rnam pa bzhi ste/ bgrod par bya ba ma yin pa dang*/ yan lag ma yin pa dang*/ yul ma yin pa dang*/ dus ma yin par bgrod pa'o/ / de la dang po ni gzhan gyis bzung ba'i bud med rnams dang ma dang bu mo dang pha ma dang bdun rgyud du 'brel pa rnams so/ / de la dge sbyong ma rnams ni yul gyi bdag pos yongs su bzung ba'i phyir dang*/ gzhon nu ma rnams ni gang la byin pa de las dang*/ byin pa med na de'i pha ma dang ming po la sogs pa dang*/ srung ba gzhan med na tha na rgyal po la ltos nas kyang des yongs su bzung pa'i phyir gzhan gyis bzung ba'i nang du gtogs so/ / rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba dang*/ dran pa nyer gzhag las ni/ skyes pa dang ma ning dang dud 'gro la sogs pa yang bgrod par bya ba ma yin par bshad do/ / gnyis pa ni kha dang bshang ba'i lam la sogs pa rma'i sgo gzhan du stsol ba ste/ de dag kyang rang gi chung ma yin yang 'dod log tu 'gyur na gzhan la lta ci smros pa'i phyir ro/ / rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las/ de la tshod ni lan lnga'i bar du byed pa yin la/ de las lhag pa ni tshad ma yin pa'o zhes 'byung bas lan lnga las lhag pa byed pa'i tshad ma yin pa dang lngar 'gyur ba'am/ yang na de nyid las/ de'i tshod las lhag pa ni dus ma yin pa zhes bya'o zhes dus ma yin par 'dus par yang bshad do/ /

Desiring to proceed in four inappropriate ways through desire for perverse acts is the four aspects of sexual misbehavior (kāmamithyācāra): (1) not a proper object, (2) not a proper passage, (3) not a proper place, and (4) not the proper time. (1) The first is [368] females who are held in a relationship by others, one’s mother or daughter, and those related to one’s mother or father for seven generations. They are defended by others because females training in virtue are defended by the village chief, and because younger females are defended by whomever they are given to in marriage, and if not so given, they are defended by their mother, father, or brothers and so on, and if they have no other guardian they are ultimately defended by the king. The Compendium of Ascertainment[1188] and the Foundations of Mindfulness Sūtra[1189] explain that males, neuters, animals, and so on also are not appropriate objects. (2) Not a proper passage is making sexual exertion in another orifice such as the mouth or anus, and if this is sexual misconduct even with one’s wife, then what need is there to speak of others? The Compendium of Ascertainment mentions: If the correct amount is stated, it may be done up to five times, but more than that is not the correct amount. Therefore, more than five times is not the correct measure, and if committed five times, that text also states: More than the correct measure is not at the proper time.[1190] Also the Compendium of Ascertainment notes that not the proper time [is not the correct measure].

gsum pa ni snang ba dang bcas pa dang*/ skye bo mang po'i mngon sum dang*/ gang du de la gnod pa'i sa phyogs 'bar 'bur can dang srab mo la sogs pa dang*/ mchod rten dang gtsug lag khang dang*/ rang gi pha ma dang*/ slob dpon dang*/ bla ma dang*/ dge sbyong la sogs pa'i drung du spyod pa ste/ de dag ni rang gi chung ma la spyod pa'ang log g.yem du 'gyur ro/ / bzhi pa ni sbrum ma dang nu zho 'thung pa dang 'khrig pa spyad du mi rung ba'i nad kyis thebs pa dang mya ngan gyis yid mi bde ba dang nyin par dang bsnyen gnas la gnas pa'i dus te de dag tu rang gi chung ma yin yang 'dod log tu 'gyur ro/ / 'dir yang ma nor bar zhes shes par bya ste/ nor ba la ni de'i nyes pa med pa'i phyir ro/{ rab byung yin na pham par 'gyur/ /} de'i phyir gzhan gyi chung ma la rang gir 'du shes nas spyad pa la ni 'dod log tu mi 'gyur ro/ / 'o na gzhan gyi chung ma la gzhan zhig gi chung mar 'du shes te spyad na'ang 'dod log tu mi 'gyur te/ ma nor ba med pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ sngon gyi slob dpon kha cig na re khyad par la 'du shes 'khrul bar gyur kyang spyir gzhan gyi chung mar 'du shes pa ma 'khrul bar sbyor ba byas pa'i phyir dang*/ dngos po'ang rdzogs par spyad pa'i phyir 'gyur ro zhes zer ro/ / kha cig ni sbyor ba'i tshe gzhan du 'du shes pas dngos kyi tshe gzhan la spyad pa'i phyir mi 'gyur te dper na srog gcod pa bzhin no zhes zer te lugs snga ma yin no/ / de dag ni lus kyi las gsum mo/ /

(3) Not a proper place is engaging in sexual union in a place well illumined and open to the sight of many beings, and places of potential harm, such as uneven and narrow places, or in front of stūpas, temples, one’s parents, guru, and śramaṇas. Even if one engages in sexual union there with one’s wife, it is sexual misbehavior. (4) Not the proper time is engaging in sexual union when pregnant, and it is unsuitable when breastfeeding, or when ill, or when there is mental dissatisfaction through grief, or during the day, or when abiding in one-day vows. Even engaging in sex at those times with one’s wife is sexual misconduct. Here, one should know whether it is done “unmistakenly” because there is no fault if done mistakenly. Therefore, if one engages in sexual union through discriminating the wife of another as to be one’s own wife, it is not sexual misconduct. {If one is ordained, there is a defeat [of the monastic vows].} Objection: If one engages in sexual union through discriminating the wife of another as the wife of someone else again, it is not sexual misconduct because it is not unmistaken. A past master says: Since in general discriminating her as the wife of another is not mistaken, though the specific discernment of her is mistaken, the preparation is committed and an actual basis occurs, because engaging in sexual union is complete.[1191] Some say: When one prepares for sexual union while discriminating her as another, but at the time of the actual basis engages in sexual union with someone else, it is not an actual basis, as it [also] isn’t [an actual basis in similar mistaken circumstances] when taking life. This is like the former system. These, then, are the three karmas of the body.

rdzun gyi tshig ni smra ba po rang gis don smra ba gang yin pa de la pha rol po 'du shes gzhan du bsgyur ba'i bsam pas mi bden pa smras pas tshig de'i don mngon par go ba'o/ / 'dir yang bsam bzhin du zhes bya ba dang ma nor bar zhes shes par bya ste/ ma bsams pa dang nor ba la dngos med pa'i phyir ro/ / tshig don mngon par go ba'o zhes bya ba ni phra ma la sogs pa la'ang shes par bya'o/{ mthong dang ma mthong thos ma thos/ / rtogs dang ma rtogs shes ma shes/ / ji bzhin smra ba 'phags pa yi/ / tha snyad 'dogs pa byis pa yin/ / zhes so/ /} 'o na brgyad tshan brgyad pa'i mdo las/ 'phags pa ma yin pa'i tha snyad brgyad dang dang 'phags pa'i tha snyad brgyad de bcu drug bshad pa la mthong ba dang thos pa dang rtogs pa dang rnam par shes pa la ma mthong bar smra ba la sogs bzhi dang*/ ma mthong ba la sogs pa bzhi la mthong ba la sogs par smra ba bzhi ste brgyad ni byis pa'i tha snyad de rdzun du 'gyur ro/ / mthong ba la mthong ba la sogs par smra ba bzhi dang*/ ma mthong ba la ma mthong ba la sogs par smra ba bzhi ste brgyad ni 'phags pa'i tha snyad de bden pa'i don can yin no zhes 'byung ba'i mthong ba la sogs pa bzhi nyid gang zhe na/

Lying (mṛṣāvaca) is speaking untruly, with oneself as the speaker, and that spoken is intentionally spoken to change another’s discernment, and the meaning of those words is actually understood. Here, one should know [369] that “intentionally” and “unmistakenly” are stated because unintentional and mistaken speech is not an actual basis. “The meaning of those words is actually understood” is also to be understood for slander and so on. {It is said: I see, I do not see. I hear, I do not hear. I comprehend, I do not comprehend. I know, I do not know. Āryas proclaim things as they are; childlike beings desire [false] conventions.} The Eight Times Eight Sūtra explains sixteen: the eight conventions of the nonārya and the eight conventions of the ārya. The eight conventions of childlike beings are the four lies — “I see, I hear, I comprehend, I know” — when I don’t see and so on, and the four — “I don’t see, I don’t hear, I don’t comprehend, I don’t know” — when I [do] see . . . and so on. The eight conventions of āryas are the truthful statements such as the four “I see . . .” when I see [and so on], and the four “I don’t see . . .” when I don’t see and so on. Question: What are the four such as seeing and so on?
mig rna yid kyi rnam shes dang / / gsum gyis nyams su myong gang de/ / mthong thos rnam par shes pa dang / / rtogs pa yin te rim bzhin bshad/ / 75
Whatever is experienced by the eye, ear, mental consciousness, and the three are explained in that order as seen, heard, known, and comprehended. (4:75)

mig gi rnam shes kyis nyams su myong ba gang yin pa de ni mthong ba yin no/ / rna ba'i rnam shes kyis nyams su myong ba gang yin pa de ni thos pa yin no/ / yid kyi rnam shes kyis nyams su myong ba gang yin pa de ni rnam par shes pa yin no/ / sna dang lce dang lus kyi rnam shes gsum gyis nyams su myong ba gang yin pa de ni rtogs pa yin te de ltar na rim pa bzhin du bshad do/ / de la dri ro reg bya gsum ni ma bsgribs lung ma bstan yin pas rnam smin 'byin mi nus pa'i phyir shi ba dang 'dra bar nus pa chung bas rtogs pa zhes bya ste/ rtogs pa'i sgra ni shi bar yang 'dren pa'i phyir ro/ / yang kha cig na re shi ba'i ro la dge mi dge gnyis rjes su mi 'jug la lung ma bstan rjes su 'jug pa ltar gsum po de dag kyang lung ma bstan yin pas shi ba dang 'dra'o zhes zer ro/ / gal te de ltar yin par gang gis shes she na/ lung dang rigs pa las te/ de la lung ni tshe dang ldan pa mchod byed kyi ma can gyis zhus pa'i mdo las/ mchod byed ma can ji snyam du sems/ gzugs gang dag khyod kyi mig gis ma mthong ste sngon ma mthong zhing mi blta la khyod ni 'di snyam du blta bar bya'o snyam du'ang mi sems na gzhi de las khyod 'dun pa'am/ 'dod chags sam/ 'dod pa'am/ dga' ba'am/ chags pa'am/ 'chums pa'am/ lhag par chags pa skye'am/ btsun pa ma lags so zhes pa dang*/ de bzhin du sgra dang dri dang ro dang reg bya dang chos kyi bar la rna ba dang sna dang lce dang lus dang yid kyi rnam shes la'ang sbyar te rgyas par gsungs nas mdor bsdu ba'i phyir mchod byed kyi ma can khyod 'di la mthong na'ang mthong ba tsam du 'gyur la/ thos pa dang*/ rtogs pa dang*/ rnam par shes na'ang rnam par shes pa tsam du 'gyur ro zhes gsungs pa'i phyir/ mig dang*/ rna ba dang yid shes gsum gyi yul gsum ni rang gi ming gis bstan pas rtogs pa'i sgras dri la sogs pa gsum gzung bar don gyis go ba'i phyir ro/ / de lta ma yin na dri la sogs pa gsum la tha snyad 'dogs pa rgyun chad par 'gyur te/ de dag mthong ba la sogs pa'i nang du ni ma gtogs la rtogs pa'ang ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes bye brag tu smra ba rnams 'dod do/ /

Reply: Whatever is experienced (anubhūta) by eye consciousness is seen. Whatever is experienced by ear consciousness is heard. Whatever is experienced by mental consciousness is known. Whatever is experienced by the three — nose, tongue, and body consciousness — is comprehended, and they are explained in just that order.[1192] The three objects of smell, taste, and tactility are unable to produce karmic maturation since they are unobscured-neutral states. Therefore they are called “comprehended” since they are weak in potency like something dead, because the term “comprehended” is also applied to dead things. Some say: Just as a dead corpse has no subsequent engagement in virtue and nonvirtue but has subsequent engagement in neutral states, so too those three are neutral like death. Question: Given that that is so, how does understanding of it arise? Reply: That is understood from scripture and logic. In terms of scripture, the Sūtra Requested by Mālakīmātar reads: The Buddha inquired: “Mālakīmātar, how do you conceive this, regarding any form that your eyes do not see, have not seen before, nor viewed, and about which you do not think, ‘I will view this,’ then would you generate aspiration for that object, or attachment, or desire, or joy, or greed, or longing, or intense attachment?” Mālakīmātar replied: “No Lord.” “In that way sound, smell, taste, tactility, up to phenomena are to be applied to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mental consciousness because they summarize the extensive presentation. Mālakīmātar, if something is seen it is merely seen, if something is heard it is merely heard, if something is comprehended it is merely comprehended, and if something is known it is merely known.”[1193] The three objects of the three consciousnesses of the eye, ear, and mental consciousness are taught by their individual names, but the objects of the three such as smell are understood by the inclusive term “comprehended.” If that were not so, then [370] imputing that designation to the three such as smell would cease, because they do not belong within “seen” and so on, and also they would not be “comprehended.” This is asserted by the Vaibhāṣikas.

slob dpon 'dun bzang na re gang zhig rang gi dbang po dang phrad pa de ni rtogs pa yin la dbang po gsum po 'di dag kyang rang gi yul dang phrad pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes zer ro/ / sngon gyi slob dpon dag ni mdo'i don ni de ltar ma yin te/ yul lnga po de dag dbang po lnga la brten pa'i rnam par shes pas mngon du byas pa ni mthong ba'o/ / pha rol las 'ongs pa'i sgra la brten nas yul drug car shes pa ni thos pa'o/ / bdag nyid kyis mi 'khrul ba'i rigs pas rjes su dpag nas yul drug rtogs pa ni rtogs pa'o/ / yid kyi mngon sum du gyur pa bsgoms nas rtogs pa so so rang gis rig par bya ba gang yin pa de ni rnam par shes pa yin te/ mthong ba tsam la sogs par shes par bya'i sdug mi sdug tu bden pa dang mtshan mar bzung bar mi bya ba 'di ston pa yin no zhes 'chad do/ / sngon gyi rnal 'byor spyod pa po'i slob dpon gzhan dag ni mig kho nas mngon sum du byas pa gang yin pa de ni mthong ba'o/ / rna bas thos pa dang pha rol las 'ongs pa gang yin pa de gnyis ka ni thos pa'o/ / bdag nyid kyis bsams pa gang yin pa rtogs pa'o/ / bdag nyid kyis mnyam par ma bzhag pas so sor yang dag par rig pa dang 'jig rten pa'i mnyam gzhag gis rtogs pa gang yin pa de ni rnam par shes pa'o zhes zer ro/ / de ltar na lugs snga ma ltar na yul lnga po re re la'ang mthong ba dang thos pa dang rtogs pa dang rnam par shes pa'i tha snyad 'dogs shing chos la ni mthong ba ma gtogs pa'i tha snyad 'dogs la/ lugs phyi ma ltar na yul drug car la yang so sor ci rigs par mthong ba la sogs pa'i tha snyad bzhi 'dogs pa'i phyir dri la sogs pa gsum la tha snyad 'dogs pa med par thal bar 'gyur ba'i nyes pa'ang med do/ / gal te srog gcod lus kyi las kho na yin nam zhe na/ ma yin te/ yid dang ngag gis kyang byed pa'i phyir te/ dang po ni nyi shu pa las drang srong khros pas dan ta ka'i/ dgon pa ji ltar stongs par 'gyur zhes khyim bdag nye bar 'khor gyi mdo las/ drang srong rnams kyi yid rab tu khros pas dan da ka dang ka ling ka dang ma tang ka'i dgon pa'i skye bo rnams shi bar gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ gnyis pa ni gzhan la bsgo nas gsod par byed pa'i phyir ro/ /

Master Saṅghabhadra says: Objects that contact their respective sense faculty are “comprehended,” and those three sense faculties contact their objects.[1194] Past masters explain: The meaning of the sūtra is not this, because (1) the five objects made manifest by consciousness dependent on the five sense faculties are seen, (2) the six objects that are known in dependence on sound traveling over a distance are heard, (3) the six objects comprehended through inference by one’s own unmistaken logic are comprehended, and (4) any object that is individually cognized and comprehended through cultivating mental perception is known. This sūtra teaches that objects understood as merely “seen” and so on do not encompass the truth or characteristics of the beauty or repulsiveness of such objects. Other past Yogācāra masters say: Whatever is made manifest through the eye alone is “seen,” whatever is heard by the ear that comes from others is “heard,” whatever is contemplated by oneself is “comprehended,” and whatever one correctly individually cognizes through nonequipoise and comprehends through mundane equipoise is “known.” Thus, in accordance with the former system, even the five objects are imputed with the designation of seen, heard, comprehended, and known, and phenomena alone are imputed with the designation of seen. In accordance with the latter system, because the six objects together, individually and of various type, are imputed with the four designations such as seeing, there is no fault in consequence that the three of smell and so on are not imputed with a designation. Question: Is taking life physical karma alone? Reply: No, because that is also committed by (1) mental and (2) verbal action. (1) Regarding the first, Twenty Verses notes: Through the wrath of the rishis the monastery of Dantaka became empty.[1195] The Sūtra Requested by the Householder Upāli states: Through the extreme wrath of the rishis, the beings of the monasteries of Dantaka, Kaliṅga, and Mataṅga died.[1196] (2) The second is killing through ordering others to do it.

de bzhin du rdzun ngag gi las kho na yin nam zhe na/ ma yin te/ lus dang yid kyis kyang byed pa'i phyir te/ dang po ni yod pa la lus kyis med pa'i brda byed pa la sogs pa'i phyir dang*/ gnyis pa ni so so thar pa las gso sbyong byed pa na ltung ba yod la dran bzhin du mi mthol na de shes bzhin du rdzun smra ba yin no zhes 'dul ba 'dzin pas ci 'di la khyed yongs su dag gam zhes lan gnyis lan gsum gyi bar du dris pa na/ gal te dge slong 'ga' zhig ltung ba yod bzhin du 'chags par mi byed par cang mi smra bar 'dug par byed na rdzun du smra bar 'gyur bar gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir lus ngag gi rig byed med kyang srog gcod dang rdzun du smra ba yod do zhes bye brag tu smra ba rnams zer ro/ / slob dpon gyis 'o na drang srong gi yid khros pa dang gso sbyong gi rdzun la de'i tshe rig byed med na rig byed ma yin pa'ang med par 'gyur te/ 'dod pa'i rig byed ma yin pa ni nges par rig byed la ltos pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir yid kyis srog gcod dang rdzun gnyis las kyi lam du mi 'grub par thal bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba 'di la bye brag tu smra bas lan gdab dgos so zhes brjod do/ /

Question: Similarly, is lying the karma of speech alone? Vaibhāṣikas say: Lying is committed by (1) physical and (2) mental karma also, because (1) one may indicate through the body that something that exists does not exist and so on, and (2) if one doesn’t confess a downfall as one remembers it during a confession ceremony, that is intentional lying. When a holder of Vinaya asks two or three times, [371] “Are you pure in this?” and if some monks do not confess yet remain silent though they possess that downfall, it is lying. Therefore, though there may be no physical or mental indicative form, taking life and speaking lies may still exist.[1197] However, regarding the mental wrath of rishis and lying during the confession ceremony, Vasubandhu asserts that if indicative form does not exist at that time, also nonindicative form would not exist, because desire-realm nonindicative form definitely relies on indicative form. Therefore these actions would not become the karmic path of taking life and lying by mental karma, and the Vaibhāṣikas must respond to this consequence.[1198]

'di la slob dpon 'dun bzang drang srong khros pa dang gso sbyong gi tshe'ang lus ngag gi rig byed med par ma grub ste/ drang srong la dad pa'i mi ma yin pa dag gis gang gis drang srong de dag la las kyi lam skye bar 'gyur ba skye bo rnams la gnod pa byed pa'i lus kyi rig byed dang*/ drang srong rang nyid la'ang gzhan la khros pa na lus ngag gi g.yo ba dmod pa 'dor ba la sogs pa'i lus ngag gi rig byed cung zad nges par yod pa'i phyir dang*/ gso sbyong gi tshe'ang ma dag bzhin du cang mi smra bas bdag nyid dag par go bar byed pa'i phyir dang*/ yongs su ma dag pa zhig dge 'dun gyi nang du 'jug par byed cing 'dug par byed rang gi spyod lam ston par byed la de dang 'brel ba cung zad smra bar byed na de nyid 'di'i rig byed yin pa'i phyir rtags ma grub pa yin no zhes lan 'debs par byed la/ gzhan dag ni de dag la rig byed med par gyur kyang 'dod pa'i rig byed ma yin pa thams cad rig byed la rag las par nges pa'ang med de dper na lnga sde la sogs pa 'bras bu thob pa'i mod la rig byed med kyang so so thar pa'i sdom pa skyes pa de bzhin du mi dge ba'i rig byed ma yin pa'ang 'ga' zhig rig byed med par yang 'byung ba srid pa'i phyir khyed kyi gtan tshigs de ma nges pa yin no zhes lan 'debs par byed do/ / de yang ngag gis bsgos te srog bcad pa dang lus kyis brda byas te rdzun byas kyang dngos kyis bsdus pa'i rig byed ma yin pa ni rim pa ltar lus dang ngag kho na'i yin te/ de dag rim pa ltar lus ngag gi las yin pa'i phyir ro zhes slob dpon rgyal po'i sras 'chad do/ /

In this respect Master Saṅghabhadra says that at the time of the wrath of the rishis and the confession ceremony, physical and verbal indicative form are not established to be nonexistent, because nonhumans with faith in the rishis have the physical indicative form of harming those beings who generate the karmic path in relation to those rishis; because when the rishis themselves generate wrath toward others, they possess some physical and verbal indicative form such as the physical and verbal movement made in performing a ritual curse;[1199] because at the time of the confession ceremony one is understood to be pure when impure by not speaking at all; and because if one who is not thoroughly pure, who enters and resides within the Saṅgha, makes known his conduct and speaks about it, then this would constitute indicative form. Therefore he responds that the reason is not established. Others respond that though such beings do not come to have indicative form, it is not certain that all desire-realm nonindicative form relies on indicative form. For example, the group of five [first disciples] and so on obtained their specific results and generated pratimokṣa vows without indicative form. Similarly, because it is possible that nonvirtuous nonindicative form arises without indicative form, your proof is indeterminate. Further, though one may take life by giving a verbal order or lie through physical gesture, nonindicative form directly subsuming those is, respectively, physical and verbal alone because those are respectively physical and verbal karma.[1200] This is explained by Master Jinaputra.
phra ma pha rol dbye ba'i phyir/ / nyon mongs can gyi sems kyi tshig/ / tshig rtsub po ni mi snyan pa/ / nyon mongs can kun kyal pa nyid/ / 76
Slander is speaking words with an afflicted mind to divide others. Harsh words is unpleasant speech. All words motivated by afflicted minds are idle speech. (4:76)

phra ma ni pha rol po dag dbye zhing mi mdza' bar bya ba'i phyir nyon mongs pa can gyi sems kyis kun nas bslang ba'i tshig smra ba ste tshig don mngon par go ba dang ma nor ba zhes 'dir yang sbyar ro/ / de la bden pa brjod na phra ma tsam dang mi bden pa smras na rdzun dang gnyis kar 'gyur ro/ /

Slander (paiśunya) is speaking words motivated by an afflicted mind to divide others (parabheda), or so that they don’t treat each other amicably. Also stating that “the words are actually understood and are unmistaken” is applied here. If one expresses the truth it is merely slander, and if one expresses that which is not true it is both slander and a lie.

nyon mongs pas kun nas bslang ba'i tshig rtsub po ni mi snyan pa brjod pa'i ngag ste de yang pha rol la smras shing des kyang don mngon par go la gang la smra bar 'dod pa de nyid la ma nor bar smras pa gang yin pa de ni tshig rtsub po yin no zhes sbyar ro/ / sems nyon mongs pa can gyis kun nas bslang ba'i rdzun la sogs pa'i tshig kun ni ngag kyal ba nyid yin te/ de'i phyir rdzun la sogs pa gsum ga'ang kyal ba yin mod kyi nyes pa che bas logs su phye ba yin no zhes bya ba ni slob dpon kha cig gi yin no/ /

Harsh words (pāruṣya) is unpleasant speech. Again, harsh words refers to any speech that is stated to another who actually understands unmistakenly the meaning desired by the speaker. [372] All words such as lies and so on that are motivated by afflicted minds are idle speech (bhinnalāpitā). Therefore one master said that indeed the three actions such as lies are idle speech, but since their [specific] fault exceeds that [of idle speech] they are classified separately.
gzhan ni de las gzhan nyon mongs/ / kha gsag glu dang zlos gar bzhin/ / bstan bcos ngan bzhin brnab sems ni/ / log pas gzhan gyi nor la chags/ / 77
Others say it is any other afflicted speech like boasting, singing, the lines of actors, or false treatises. Covetousness is desiring the property of others, through wrong means. (4:77)

sngon gyi slob dpon gzhan dag ni ngag gi las rdzun la sogs pa gsum po de dag las gzhan pa'i nyon mongs pa can gyi tshig gang yin pa de ni ngag kyal yin no zhes zer te/ dper na dge slong log 'tsho can kha gsag smra ba dang*/ chags pas glu len pa dang zlos gar mkhan dag gzhan mgu bar bya ba'i phyir ngag kyal gyi tshig 'don pa bzhin dang*/ phyi rol pa'i lta ba la zhen nas de'i bstan bcos ngan pa la kha ton byed pa dang de bzhin du rdzun la sogs pa gsum las gzhan pa'i smre sngags 'don pa dang*/ 'du 'dzi'i gtam la sogs pa nyon mongs can gyi sems gyis kun nas bslang ba'i smra ba thams cad kyang yin no/ / 'o na ni 'khor los bsgyur ba 'jig rten du byung ba na'ang ngag kyal yod par 'gyur te/ glu len pa'i phyir ro/ / de lta na de'i tshe mi dge ba bcu spangs pa ma yin par 'gyur ro zhe na/ de'i tshe 'khor ba las yid nges par 'byung ba dang ldan pa'i glu len gyi smre sngags dang ldan pa ni ma yin no/ / kha cig na re de'i tshe na'ang glu dang bag ma gtong len la sogs pa'i tshig mngon par brjod pa yod pas ngag kyal yod kyang de dag{ la rig byed ma yin pa med pas} las kyi lam ni ma yin no zhes zer ro/ / de dag ni ngag gi las bzhi'o/ /

Other masters say: Any afflicted speech, other than those three verbal karmas such as lying, is idle speech. For example, it would be like the boasting or singing of a fully ordained monk engaged in wrong livelihood through attachment, or the idle speech proclaimed by actors to please others, or reciting the false treatises of non-Buddhists through attachment to their views, or lamentation that is other than the three verbal actions such as lying, or any speech such as noisy discourse and so on that is motivated by afflicted minds. Objection: When a cakravartin king is born in the world, idle speech arises because there is singing. Therefore the ten nonvirtues have not been abandoned. Reply: At that time, such singing is influenced by mental renunciation of saṃsāra and therefore it is not lamentation. Some say that idle speech exists since at that time there is singing, as well as words expressing the giving and taking of a bride and so on, but they are not a karmic path {since nonindicative form does not exist}. These are the four karmas of speech.

brnab sems ni pha rol po'i de bdag gi yin par gyur kyang ci ma rung snyam nas mthu'am 'jab bu'am gzhan gyis kyang rung ste log pa mi rigs pas bdag gir byed 'dod pas gzhan gyi nor la chags pa'o/ / slob dpon gzhan ni 'dod pa na spyod pa'i sred pa thams cad brnab sems yin te/ tshul khrims kyi phung po'i mdo las sgrib pa lnga bstan pa'i skabs su 'dod pa la 'dun pa'i sgrib pa'i dbang du mdzad nas de 'jig rten na brnab sems spangs te brnab sems dang bral ba'i sems kyis lan mang du gnas shing*/ 'jig rten na gnod sems dang*/ rmugs pa dang gnyid dang*/ rgod pa dang 'gyod pa dang*/ the tshom spangs te zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro zhes zer te/ kha cig na re de lta na 'khor los bsgyur ba dang byang gi sgra mi snyan pa la'ang brnab sems kyi las kyi lam yod par thal bar 'gyur du 'ong bas 'dod sred thams cad brnab sems yin yang de'i bye brag log pas gzhan gyi nor la chags pa kho na las kyi lam yin gyi brnab sems thams cad las kyi lam ni ma yin te/ nyes spyad che long bsdus pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes zer ro/ / de'i phyir bshad pa snga ma yin no/ /

Covetousness (abhidhyā) is desiring the property of others and thinking, “What would be wrong if another’s property were mine?” and desiring to make it mine through improper and wrong means such as by force, stealth, or something other. Other masters assert that covetousness is any craving that is active in the desire realm, since in the context of teaching the five obscurations, the Aggregate of Ethics Sūtra states: From the perspective of the obscuration of longing for sensory objects, one who has abandoned covetousness for mundane objects frequently abides with a mind free of covetousness and abandons malice, lethargy and sleep, excitation and regret, and doubt in the world. Some say: According to this assertion, it would follow that cakravartin kings and those of Uttarakuru would have the karmic path of covetousness. Therefore, though all craving of the desire realm is covetousness, only its subset — that is, wrong attachment to others’ wealth — is a karmic path, and not all covetousness is a karmic path because karmic paths subsume only gravely negative actions. Therefore the former explanation is best.
gnod sems sems can la sdang ba/ / dge dang mi dge med lta ba/ / log par lta ba yin 'di la/ / gsum lam bdun ni las kyang yin/ / 78
Malice is aversion for sentient beings. The view that virtue and nonvirtue do not exist is wrong view. From those, three are paths, seven are also karma. (4:78)

gnod sems ni sems can la sdang ba ste gnod par zhugs pa'o/ / las dge ba dang mi dge ba med par lta ba ni rgyu las la skur ba 'debs pa'i log par lta ba yin te/ de yang mdo las/ sbyin pa med do/ / mchod sbyin med do/ / sbyin sreg med do/ / legs par spyad pa med do/ / nyes par spyad pa med do/ / legs par spyad pa dang nyes par spyad pa'i las rnams kyi 'bras bu rnam par smin pa med do/ / 'jig rten 'di med do/ / 'jig rten pha rol med do/ / ma med do/ / pha med do/ / sems can rdzus te skye ba med do/ / 'jig rten na dgra bcom pa med do zhes bya bas rgyu las dang 'bras bu dang 'phags pa la skur pa 'debs pa gsum gsungs te/ de la sbyin pa med do zhes pa nas nyes par spyad pa med do zhes pa'i bar dang*/ ma med do/ / pha med do zhes pa rnams ni rgyu las la skur pa 'debs pa yin zhing*/ legs par spyad pa dang nyes par spyad pa'i las rnams kyi 'bras bu rnam par smin pa med do zhes pa nas sems can rdzus te skye ba med do zhes pa'i bar ni 'bras bu la skur pa 'debs pa yin la/ 'jig rten na dgra bcom pa med do zhes pa ni 'phags pa la skur pa 'debs pa yin pas gsum char log par lta ba yin mod kyi tshigs su bcad par ni mtshon pa'i don du dang po tsam zhig bstan par zad do/ / de ltar mi dge ba bcur gsungs pa 'di la brnab sems la sogs pa gsum ni las kyi lam yin gyi las ni ma yin te/ de dag nyon mongs pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ de dag gi dbang gis de dag dang mthun par mtshungs par ldan pa'i sems pa 'jug pa'i phyir ro/ / lus ngag gi las bdun ni las kyang yin la las kyi lam yang yin te/ bya ba yin pa'i phyir dang*/ de dag kun nas slong ba'i sems pa'ang bdun po de dag la brten nas 'jug pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du brnab sems med pa la sogs pa dge ba bcu po la'ang shes par bya'o/ /

Malice (vyāpāda) is aversion that fosters harm for sentient beings. The view that virtue and nonvirtue [373] do not exist is wrong view (mithyadṛṣṭi) that denies karmic causation. A sūtra elaborates: There is no generosity, no sacrifice, no burnt offerings. There are no positive actions, no negative actions, and no karmic maturation that is the result of positive and negative actions. This world does not exist, worlds beyond this do not exist. There is no mother, no father, no sentient beings who are supernaturally born. There are no arhats in the world.[1201] This sūtra declares the three views that deny (1) karmic cause, (2) karmic result, and (3) āryas. The words from “there is no generosity” up to “no negative actions” and “there is no mother, no father” deny karmic cause. The words from “there is no karmic maturation of the results of positive and negative actions” up to “no sentient beings who are supernaturally born” deny karmic result. The words “there are no arhats in the world” deny the existence of āryas. Indeed, these three are wrong views, but the verse teaches just the first as its representative meaning. From among those ten nonvirtues, the three actions of covetousness and so on are karmic paths but not karma itself because they are afflictions. Intention concomitant with them engages its object due to their influence. The seven karmas of body and speech are karmic paths and also karma [itself] because they are action, and the intention motivating them engages its object in dependence on those seven. The ten virtues such as noncovetousness should be understood in the same way.

ci'i phyir sbyor ba dang 'jug las kyi lam du mi 'gyur zhe na/ sbyor ba ni dngos de'i don du 'jug pa'i phyir dang*/ 'jug ni dngos de'i rtsa ba can du 'jug pa'i phyir dang*/ de las che long bsdus nas ni/ / dge dang mi dge ci rigs par/ / las kyi lam ni bcur gsungs so/ / zhes pas 'dir che long bsdus pa'i phyir las kyi lam du mi 'gyur ro/ / mdo sde pa la sogs pa gang dag brnab sems la sogs pa las su 'dod pa de dag gi ltar na ni de dag bde 'gro dang ngan 'gro'i las dang lam yin pa'am/ yang na phan tshun gcig gis gcig 'dren pas na thams cad las kyang yin la lam yang yin no/ /

Question: Why are preparation and conclusion not the karmic path? Reply: They are not the karmic path because one enters preparation for the purpose of establishing the actual karmic path, one enters the conclusion in order to maintain the essential nature of that actual karmic path, and they are broadly subsumed in karmic paths since it is said: Through broadly subsuming various types of virtue and nonvirtue, the karmic paths are stated to be ten. Sautrāntikas and so on assert that covetousness and so forth are karma, and according to them they are the karma and paths of beings reincarnating in higher and lower realms, or since one leads to the other, all [three such as covetousness] are karma and all are paths.
da ni log lta'i byed pa bstan pa ni
ACTION OF WRONG VIEW
med par lta bas rtsa ba gcod/ / 'dod gtogs skyes nas thob pa rnams/ / rgyu dang 'bras la skur 'debs pas/ / kun gyis rim gyis mi'i nang du/ / 79
The view of nihilism severs roots obtained from birth, belonging to the desire realm. That underestimating cause and effect [severs the root] entirely, serially, among humans. (4:79)

las la sogs pa la skur ba 'debs pa ni sems med par lta ba chen po'i chen po yongs su rdzogs pas ni dge ba'i rtsa ba thams cad gcod par byed do/ / 'o na bstan bcos las/ mi dge ba'i rtsa ba chen po rnams gang dag yin zhe na/ mi dge ba'i rtsa ba gang dag gis dge ba'i rtsa ba gcod par byed pa dang*/ 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba na dang po nyid du spong ba gang dag yin pa'o/ / zhes bshad pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/ de ni log ltas mi dge ba'i rtsa ba kun nas bslang la des dge rtsa gcod pa'i phyir de skad du bshad de dngos su mes bsreg kyang chom rkun pas grong bsregs so zhes brjod pa bzhin no/ / dge ba'i rtsa ba gang gcod ce na/ 'dod par gtogs pa'i skyes nas thob pa rnams te/ dge ba gcod pa'i log lta can la gzugs dang gzugs med khams gong ma gnyis kyi dge ba mi ldan pa'i phyir dang*/ 'dod pa'i sbyor byung gi dge ba ni log lta chung ngu skyes pa'i dus su nyams zin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na gdags pa las/ gang gis bsam bzhin du pha dang ma srog dang phral nas dge ba dang mi dge ba'i las kyi rnam par smin pa med do zhes log par lta zhing 'gyod pa cung zad kyang mi skyed na 'di tsam gyis na gang zag 'dis khams gsum pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba rnams kun du bcad pa yin no zhes bshad pa ji ltar drang zhe na/ de ni rgyud de de'i snod ma yin pas khams gsum pa'i dge ba'i thob pa thag sring ba la dgongs pa yin no/ / log lta ji lta bus she na/

The great of the great degree[1202] of the view of nihilism (chedadṛṣṭi) is a mind that underestimates karma and so on and completely severs all roots (mūlaccheda) of virtue. Objection: Doesn’t this contradict the treatise (Attainment of Knowledge),[1203] which states: What are the great roots of nonvirtue? They are any root of nonvirtue that severs the root of virtue, and if one is free of attachment to the desire realm, it is those that eliminate virtue in the first two absorptions. [374] This is stated because wrong view motivates the roots of nonvirtue that sever the roots of virtue. It is like stating that brigands burned the city though it is fire that actually burns it.[1204] Question: What roots of virtue are severed? Reply: They are those roots of virtue obtained from birth belonging to the desire realm because those possessing the wrong view that severs virtue have no virtue of the two higher realms — the form and formless realms — and virtue derived from preparation declines when even a minor degree of wrong view arises. Question. Why does Presentation on Karma state: Whoever intentionally takes the life of his father or mother, maintains the wrong view that it has no virtuous or nonvirtuous karmic maturation, and generates not the least regret, completely severs his root of virtue in the three realms.[1205] Reply: This text intends that such persons are far from attaining virtue of the three realms since their mindstreams are not a proper vessel for it. Question: What is wrong view?

legs par spyad pa dang nyes par spyad pa med do zhes rgyu la skur pa 'debs pa dang legs par spyad pa dang nyes par spyad pa'i las rnams kyi 'bras bu rnam par smin pa med do zhes 'bras bu la skur pa 'debs pa'i log ltas gcod do/ / sngon gyi slob dpon kha cig na re rgyu dang 'bras bu la skur pa 'debs pa ni rim pa ltar bar chad med pa dang rnam grol gyi lam lta bu yin no zhes zer ro/ / kha cig na re de yang zag bcas sdug kun la dmigs pa dang skal ba mnyam pa'i khams la dmigs pa kho nas gcod kyi zag med 'gog lam la dmigs pa dang skal pa mi mnyam pa'i khams la dmigs pas ni ma yin te/ zag med gong ma'i yul can min/ / bdag gir ma byas gnyen po'i phyir/ / zhes 'byung bas zag med dang skal ba mi mnyam pa'i khams la dmigs pa'i log lta ni mtshungs ldan gyi sgo nas rgyas kyi dmigs pa'i sgo nas rgyas pa med pas stobs chung ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir 'phags pa la skur pa 'debs pa la sogs pas ni dge rtsa gcod pa ma yin no zhes zer ro/ / dge rtsa ji ltar chad ce na/

Reply: It is view underestimating (upavādin) the cause, which holds “there is no positive or negative action,” and view underestimating the effect, which holds “there is no maturational result of the karma of positive or negative action.” A past master says: View underestimating cause and effect are, respectively, like the uninterrupted path and the liberated path. Some say: The root of virtue is severed by focusing on contaminated suffering or focusing on objects of the same realm alone, and it is not severed by focusing on the uncontaminated truths of cessation and path or focusing on objects of different realms, because it is said: It is not for higher-realm mind engaging the uncontaminated because that is the antidote and it does not take it as mine. Therefore wrong view that focuses on uncontaminated states and objects of different realms increases through concomitance but not through focal object, because such a view is weak. Thus the root of virtue is not severed through denying [the existence of] āryas and so on. Question: How is the root of virtue severed?

bye brag tu smra ba rnams ni rgyu 'bras la skur pa 'debs pa dang skal ba mnyam mi mnyam gyi khams la dmigs pa dang zag bcas zag med la dmigs pa'i log lta kun gyis gcod do zhes brjod do/ / kha cig na re dge rtsa dgu po thams cad kyang cig car du chad par 'gyur te bden pa mthong ba na mthong spang chen po'i chen po la sogs pa dgu car yang cig car spong ba bzhin no zhes zer ro/ / kha cig na re log lta chung ngu'i chung ngu la sogs pa dgus dge rtsa chen po'i chen po la sogs pa dgu rim gyis gcod de sgom lam gyis sgom spang spong ba bzhin no zhes zer te/ de ltar na bstan bcos las/ phra mo dang lhan cig tu gyur pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba rnams gang zhe na/ dge ba'i rtsa ba rnams kun tu gcod par byed pa na thams cad kyi tha mar 'dor ba gang yin pa ste/ gang dag med pas dge ba'i rtsa ba kun tu chad pa zhes bya ba'i grangs su 'gro ba yin no zhes 'byung ba 'di legs par drangs par 'gyur ro zhes zer ro/{ kha cig mthong lam ltar stan las ma langs par spyod par 'dod kyang langs nas kyang mi 'gal la/ sngar sdom pa spong la phyis dge rtsa gcod zer yang sdom pa sems gang gi 'bras bu yin pa de btang bas de yang gtong bar 'dod pa yin no/} gang du gcod ce na/ 'dod pa'i khams su gling gsum gyi mi'i nang du gcod kyi ngan song ba dang lha rnams su ni ma yin te/ ngan song ba ni dge sdig gi bsam pa mi brtan pa'i phyir dang*/ lha rnams ni las kyi 'bras bu mngon sum du gyur pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang byang gi sgra mi snyan du ni ma yin te/ sdig pa'i bsam pa de lta bu med pa'i phyir ro/ / sngon gyi slob dpon kha cig 'dzam bu'i gling kho nar gcod do zhes zer ba ni ma yin te/ bstan bcos las/ 'dzam bu'i gling pa thams cad pas nyung na dbang po brgyad dang ldan pa yin te/ shar gyi lus 'phags pa dang nub kyi ba lang spyod pa'ang de dang 'dra'o zhes bshad pa dang 'gal ba'i phyir ro/ /dbang po brgyad ni tshor ba'i dbang po lnga dang lus dang srog dang yid do/ / dad pa la sogs pa ni log lta skyes pa la chad pa'i phyir dang*/ so so'i skye bo la zag med kyi dbang po mi ldan pa dang*/ rim gyis 'chi ba dang zhar ba la sogs pa la mig la sogs pa'ang mi ldan pa'i phyir ro zhes bya ba 'di yin no/ / gang zag gang gis gcod ce na/

Vaibhāṣikas say: Wrong view — which denies cause and effect and focuses on the same or different realms, or focuses on contaminated or uncontaminated states — entirely severs the root of virtue. Some say: All nine roots of virtue are severed at the same time, just as, if one sees the four truths, one abandons at the same time the nine objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing — the great of the great and so on. Some say: The nine wrong views, such as the small of the small, serially sever the nine roots of virtue, such as the great of the great, just as the path of meditation abandons objects to be abandoned by meditation. It is pertinent to quote the treatise[1206] that says: What are the subtle and innate roots of virtue? [375] They are those roots that are destroyed last of all, when the roots of virtue are completely severed and at the point when virtue no longer exists. That is counted as the complete severence of the root of virtue.[1207] {Some say: First the vows are abandoned, then later the root of virtue is severed, like the path of seeing where, though one may desire to enjoy it without rising from one’s seat, still the path of seeing does not stop though one rises. Reply: It is asserted that vows are relinquished through relinquishing the mind that produces the resultant vows.} Question: Where are roots of virtue severed? Reply: They are severed among humans of the three continents of the desire realm. They are not severed in the lower rebirths or among the gods, because those of lower rebirth do not have stable virtuous or negative thoughts, and gods perceive the results of karma. Further, they are not severed in Uttarakuru because such negative thoughts do not exist there. A past master said: They are severed in Jambudvīpa alone. Reply: That is not so, because it would contradict the treatise (Attainment of Knowledge),[1208] which states: All those of Jambudvīpa possess a minimum of eight faculties because they are similar to those of eastern Videha and western Godānīya.[1209] The eight faculties are (1–5) the five faculties of feeling plus the faculties of (6) body, (7) life force, and (8) the mental faculty. This is so because faith and so on are severed when wrong view arises, ordinary beings do not possess uncontaminated faculties, and those who die gradually or who are blind and so on do not possess the eye faculty and so forth. Question: What person severs them?
skyes pa bud med kyis gcod do/ / lta spyad de ni mi ldan pa'o/ / mtshams ni the tshom yod lta bas/ mtshams med byed pa'i 'di la min/ / 80

Males and females sever it through the application of view. It is nonpossession. Connection arises through doubt or the view that it exists. Those who engage in heinous acts do not reconnect in this life. (4:80)

skyes pa dang bud med kyis gcod kyi bla ma la sogs pas ni ma yin te/ bsam pa mi brtan pa'i phyir ro/ / kha cig 'dun pa dang brtson 'grus zhan pas bud med kyis mi gcod do zhes zer ba ni ma yin te/ bstan bcos las/ gang mo'i dbang po dang ldan pa de nges par dbang po brgyad dang ldan no zhes gsungs pa dang 'gal ba'i phyir ro/ / skyes pa dang bud med de yang bsam pa g.yo ba'i phyir sred pa spyad pas ma yin gyi sdig pa'i bsam pa brtan pa dang*/ sdig pa 'chab pa can yin pa'i phyir lta ba spyad pas yin no/ / dge rtsa chad pa de ni dge ba'i thob pa dang mi ldan zhing ma thob pa skyes pa'o/ /

Reply: Males and females sever their roots of virtue, but not eunuchs and so on because their thought lacks stability. Some say: Females do not sever the root since they have inferior aspiration and effort. Reply: This is not so, because it would contradict the treatise (Attainment of Knowledge),[1210] which declares: Those possessing higher faculties definitely possess eight faculties.[1211] Further, it is not severed through craving because craving [merely] agitates the thoughts of males and females, but it is severed through the application of view (dṛṣṭicarita) with stable negative intention and then concealing the misdeed [committed]. The severence of the root of virtue is nonpossession (asamanvaya) of the obtainment of virtue with respect to which its nonobtainment arises.

dge rtsa chad pa de nying mtshams sbyor ba ni las rgyu 'bras la the tshom skyes pa'am las 'bras yod par lta ba'i yang dag pa'i lta bas so/ / gang dag mtshams med pa byed pa'i dge rtsa chad pa de dag ni tshe 'di la dge rtsa nying mtshams sbyor ba yin te/ mdo las/ gang zag 'di ni mthong ba'i chos kho na la dge ba'i rtsa ba rnams nying mtshams sbyor ba'i skal ba dang ldan pa ma yin gyi 'di ni nges par dmyal ba dag tu skye ba'am 'chi 'pho ba na dge ba'i rtsa ba rnams nying mtshams sbyor bar 'gyur ro zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / de la dmyal bar skye ba ni dmyal ba'i bar do'o/ / 'chi ba ni dmyal ba nas 'chi ba'o/ / des na mtshams med ma byas pa'i ni tshe 'di nyid la mtshams sbyor ba'ang yod do zhes shes par bya'o/ / de la gang zhig skal mnyam gyi rgyu'i stobs kyis gcod pa de na 'chi ba na nying mtshams sbyor la/ gzhan gyi sgra'i stobs kyis gcod pa ni skye ba na sbyor ro/ / de bzhin du rang gi rtog ge'i stobs kyis gcod pa dang gzhan las thos pa'i stobs kyis gcod pa'ang de bzhin no/ / yang gang zhig bsam pa nyams pas dge rtsa gcod pa de ni tshe 'di la nying mtshams sbyor bar 'gyur la/ bsam pa dang sbyor ba gnyis ka nyams pas dge rtsa gcod pa de ni lus zhig nas nying mtshams sbyor bar 'gyur ro/ / de la bsam pa nyams pa ni log lta mngon du gyur pa yin la/ bsam pa dang sbyor ba nyams pa ni log lta mngon du gyur pa dang mtshams med gnyis ka byas pa'o/ / de bzhin du log lta skyes Connection (saṃdhi) with severed virtue arises through doubt arising about karmic causation, or through the correct view that karma and its result do exist. Those who have severed their root of virtue and engage in heinous acts (ānantarya) do not connect with their root of virtue in this life, because a sūtra states: This person does not possess the fortune to connect with his roots of virtue in his current life but definitely takes birth in the hells and after death there connects with his roots of virtue.[1212] In this quotation, [376] “birth in the hells” refers to hell intermediate beings and “death” refers to death from the hells. Therefore a person who has not committed a heinous act may reconnect with his root of virtue in this life. If he severs it through the power of the homogeneous cause, he connects with it at death. He connects at birth if he severs it by the power of others’ words, by the power of his own dogmatic arguments, or by the power of listening to others. Again, those who sever the root of virtue through the degeneration of thought can reconnect with it in this life. Those who sever the root of virtue through the degeneration of both thought and application reconnect with it through the destruction of the body. Degeneration of thought arises through manifesting wrong view, while degeneration of thought and application arises through either manifesting wrong view or engaging in heinous acts. Similarly, you should understand the degeneration of view that has arisen from wrong view, and the degeneration of {both} ethics and view that arises through committing heinous acts after wrong view has arisen. Those and degeneration by its own power and degeneration by the power of another are counted among the former [i.e., degeneration of thought and application] alone. Here, therefore, those who sever the root of virtue and those set on a wrong path have four possibilities: (1) The first possibility[1213] is the six tīrthikas: Pūraṇa Kāśyapa, Maskarin Gośālīputra, Sañjayin Vairaṭṭhīputra, Ajita Keśakambala, Kakuda Kātyāyana, Nirgrantha Jñātiputra. (2) The second possibility[1214] is Ajātaśatru. (3) The third possibility [both] is Devadatta. (4) The fourth possibility [neither] is all except for those.

THE NUMBER OF KARMIC PATHS THAT ARISE SIMULTANEOUSLY WITH INTENTION

Up to eight nonvirtues arise simultaneously with intention. Up to ten virtues arise simultaneously, but one, eight, or five do not. (4:81)

From one up to eight of the ten nonvirtues arise simultaneously with intention (cetenā). The ninth and tenth karmic paths do not occur simultaneously with intention because the three mental karmas of covetousness and so on do not occur at the same time. (1) One karmic path arising simultaneously with intention would be covetousness and so forth alone manifesting in the absence of any karmic act such as taking life. Or with virtuous or unobscured-neutral intention, excluding lust, it would be engaging in any physical act such as killing. (2) Two arising simultaneously with intention would be killing living beings with malice and so on. (3) Three arising simultaneously with intention would be, for example, at the same time killing and robbing another living being through malice, or making others take life and steal when covetousness manifests. (4) Four arising simultaneously with intention would be speaking lies and harsh words with the [377] intention to divide through malice and covetousness, or making others commit three actions such as taking life and so on through covetousness and so forth. (5–7) Five, six, or seven that arise simultaneously with intention should be understood in the same way. (8) Eight arising simultaneously with intention would be oneself manifesting any mental action such as covetousness and committing sexual misconduct while making others commit the other six actions of body and speech, and all are completed together.

{If one makes another commit any of the six material karmas other than sexual misconduct[1215] while one manifests any of the three negative mental karmas without any other karmic path, or if one’s intention is not afflicted and that action is completed, then intention and one karmic path arise simultaneously with intention. If through malice one takes life, or through covetousness takes that which is not given, or engages in sexual misbehavior, or idle speech, two arise with intention. If through manifesting any one of the three mental karmas one commits sexual misbehavior and makes others commit the other six actions, eight arise simultaneously. This is how from one to eight karmic paths that arise simultaneously with intention are calculated.}
