In general, it is stated that up to ten virtues arise simultaneously with intention. The exception is that the Master said that one, eight, or five karmic paths do not arise simultaneously with intention. (1) One does not arise simultaneously with intention because virtuous intention is not separate from either noncovetousness or nonmalice. (2) Two arise simultaneously with intention: those who abide with virtuous consciousness of the five sense doors and those who, in dependence on formless meditative attainment, abide with knowledge of elimination and nonarising. Neither has correct view since, respectively, consciousness of the five sense doors is nonconceptual, and the mind of elimination and nonarising is not view. But they definitely have both noncovetousness and nonmalice. I think that “formless” is stated here because if they depended on the absorptions they would have uncontaminated vows, and thus would have vows abandoning seven actions. (3) Three arising simultaneously with intention would be those abiding with mental consciousness concomitant with correct view, since it would be impossible for those possessing correct view to be separated from the three mental virtuous karmas because they definitely have noncovetousness and nonmalice. (4) Four arising simultaneously with intention would be those abiding with a nonvirtuous or neutral mind who take novice or lay vows, who have the three virtues of body and who abandon lying. (5) Five do not arise simultaneously with intention because one who abides with a virtuous mind who takes novice or lay vows definitely has six or seven simultaneously. Full-ordination vows definitely [378] arise simultaneously with seven.

(6) Six arising simultaneously with intention refers to those abiding with the five virtuous consciousnesses such as eye consciousness who take novice or lay vows, who definitely have noncovetousness and nonmalice but do not have correct view. (7) Seven arising simultaneously with intention refers to those with virtuous mental consciousness who have the three roots and the four vows abandoning nonvirtue when they take novice or lay vows, or those with nonvirtuous or neutral minds who take full-ordination vows and have the seven vows abandoning nonvirtue. (8) Eight arising simultaneously with intention do not exist, because if the seven vows abandoning nonvirtue of full ordination are taken with an afflicted or neutral mind, they have seven simultaneously, and if taken with a virtuous mind, they would have nine or ten respectively, if it is consciousness of the five sense doors or mental consciousness. (9) Nine arising simultaneously with intention would be taking full-ordination vows by abiding in virtuous consciousness of the five sense doors, or taking full-ordination vows with mental consciousness concomitant with knowledge of elimination and nonarising, or manifesting knowledge of elimination and nonarising in dependence on the absorptions. (10) Ten arising simultaneously with intention would be taking full-ordination vows with virtuous mental consciousness other than the knowledge of elimination and nonarising. Or they may be all intentions simultaneously engaging absorption and uncontaminated vows {since they are pervaded by taking vows abandoning the seven actions} except for knowledge of elimination and nonarising {since the three roots and seven vows abandoning nonvirtue arise.} These are from the perspective of the vows, but they also exist in minds that are not virtuous. Therefore, {for interim virtue,} if one takes any one branch such as abandoning taking life, or two or five branches with virtuous mental consciousness simultaneously, then interim virtue would have one, five, or eight also arising simultaneously since the three mental actions would arise simultaneously with them.

HOW THEY ARE POSSESSED

Idle speech, harsh words, and malice exist in the hells through both. Covetousness and wrong view exist through being possessed. Three exist in Kuru. (4:82)

From among the ten nonvirtues, the three actions of idle speech (bhinnalāpitā), harsh words (pāruṣya), and malice (vyāpāda) exist in the hells, both through being possessed and through manifesting because hell beings have lamentation, they express unpleasant words, and they have coarse minds. {Since their antidote is not generated,} covetousness and wrong view exist through being possessed but not through manifesting, because appealing things do not exist there, karma and its result manifest there, and there is no antidote to possession. This is from the general perspective. But the statement “Those who engage in heinous acts do not reconnect in this life” (4:80d) explains that those who sever their root of virtue through thought and application reconnect with it after dying from the hells. [379] Taking life does not exist there because while karma is not exhausted one does not die even though one is killed, and one dies when one’s karma is exhausted. Also, taking that which is not given does not exist because there is no appropriation of [material] substance. Sexual misconduct does not exist there because females cannot be embraced and there is no opportunity for [sexual] pleasure. There is no lying and slander because there is no need for them, for hell beings are always divided since they are not mutually attracted to each other and so on. Because that previously obtained such as taking life is relinquished, and because that to be obtained in future does not exist, there is nothing they possess. {Therefore there are five that do not manifest nor exist [in hell], and embodied beings there who desire them do not obtain them.}

byang gi sgra mi snyan na ni brnab sems dang gnod sems dang log lta gsum ldan pa'i sgo nas yod de/ de dag gi gnyen po med pa'i phyir ro/ / mngon du gyur pa'i sgo nas ni med de/ go rim bzhin du nga yir 'dzin pa med pas rdzas bzung ba med pa'i phyir dang*/ rgyud 'jam pa dang kun nas mnar sems kyi dngos po dgu med pa'i phyir dang*/ sdig pa can gyi bsam pa ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

The three actions of covetousness, malice, and wrong view exist, and therefore are possessed, in Uttarakuru because their antidotes do not exist there. But they do not manifest because, respectively, beings there do not grasp at property since they do not grasp objects as mine, their mindstreams are tranquil and they do not possess the nine states of the tormented mind, and they do not have negative thoughts.
de na bdun pa dngos su yang / / 'dod pa gzhan na mi dge bcu/ / dge ba gsum ni thams cad na/ / rnyed dang mngon du gyur sgo nas/ / 83
The seventh also actually exists there. Ten nonvirtuous actions exist in other desire realms. Three virtuous actions exist in all realms by means of attainment and manifestation. (4:83)

sgra mi snyan de na de dag res 'ga' nyon mongs can gyi sems kyis glu len pa'i phyir mi dge ba bdun pa ngag kyal ni dngos sa yang yod do/ / yang gi sgra ni ldan pa'i sgo nas yang yod pa sdud pa'o/ / srog gcod pa ni med de/ sdig pa can gyi bsam pa ma yin pa dang tshe nges pa'i phyir ro/ / rdzas dang bud med yongs su bzung ba med pa'i phyir dang*/ ma la sogs pa bgrod par bya ba ma yin pa yin na ni/ rang gi dpag bsam gyi shing gis mi skyob pas de dag mi spyod pa'i phyir ma byin par len pa dang 'dod log med de/ dgos pa med pa'i phyir dang*/ rgyud 'jam pa'i phyir rdzun dang phra ma dang tshig rtsub kyang med do/ /

The seventh nonvirtuous action of idle speech also actually exists in Kuru because they occassionally sing with afflicted mind. The term “also” indicates that it exists there by means of possession. Taking life does not exist there because they have no negative thoughts and their lifespan is certain. Taking that which is not given and sexual misconduct do not exist there because possessing property and possessing females do not exist there, and if it is one with whom one cannot lie with, such as one’s mother, one’s wish-granting tree will not conceal one, and one cannot engage in sexual union with her. Slander and harsh words do not exist there because their mindstreams are tranquil and there is no need.

dmyal ba dang sgra mi snyan ma gtogs pa'i 'dod pa'i khams gzhan na ni mi dge ba bcu ka ldan pa dang mngon gyur gyi sgo nas kyang ci rigs par yod de/ de la yi dwags dang dud 'gro dang 'dod lha'i nang na ni sdom min gyis bsdus pa med kyi gzhan par ma mi dge bas bsdus pa dag yod la mi'i nang na ni sdom min gyis bsdus pa'ang yod do/ / gal te lha la srog gcod pa ji ltar yod ce na/ kha cig na re lhas lha gsod pa med kyang lhas 'gro ba gzhan dag gsod pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ /

Apart from the hells and Kuru, the ten nonvirtuous actions exist in various ways in other desire realms by means of possession and manifestation. The ten nonvirtuous actions included in negative commitments do not exist among ghosts, animals, and desire gods, but those subsumed by interim nonvirtue exist, and those subsumed by negative commitments exist also among humans. Question: How does taking life exist among the gods? Some say: Though gods killing gods does not exist, gods kill other reincarnating beings.

kha cig na re lha'ang phan tshun mgo dang rked pa bcad na 'chi ba'i phyir yod do zhes zer ro/ / brnab sems med pa dang gnod sems med pa dang yang dag pa'i lta ba zhes bya ba'i{ yid kyi} dge ba gsum ni khams dang sa dang 'gro ba thams cad na rnyed pa dang mngon du gyur pa gnyis ka'i sgo nas yod do/ /

Some say: Because death occurs if both the head and the waist of a god are severed. The three virtuous {mental} actions of noncovetousness, nonmalice, and correct view exist in all realms, levels, and reincarnating beings by means of both attainment (lābhata) and manifestation (saṃmukhībhuta).

Those in the formless realm and beings devoid of discernment possess seven by means of attainment. The rest also by means of those manifesting, except for beings of hell and Uttarakuru. (4:84)

gzugs med par skyes pa'i 'phags pa rnams dang 'du shes med pa'i sems can rnams la ni rnyed pa'i sgo nas sgrog gcod pa spong ba la sogs pa lus ngag gi dge ba bdun yod de/ {gzugs med kyi 'phags pa la ni lus ngag gi bdun rnyed pas yod de/ 'das pa ni sngon sa gang la brten pa'i zag med kyi sdom pa skyed de/ 'gags pa de dang ldan te/ 'di ni skyes pa de kho nas bsnyad do/ / ma 'ongs pa ni sa lnga car la brten pa dang ldan te/ 'di ni ma 'ongs pa mi skye ba'i chos can yin no/ / de yang dgra bcom yin na ni zhugs lam btang bas ma 'ongs pa kho na dang ldan no zhes 'chad do } gzugs khams su zag med kyi sdom pa thob pa gtong ba'i rgyu ma byung na gzugs med du skyes pa'i 'phags pa dag la ni zag med kyi spong ba bdun gyi 'das ma 'ongs kyi thob pa dang ldan pa'i phyir dang*/ 'du shes med pa'i sems can la'ang bsam gtan gyi sdom pa'i thob pa ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / mngon gyur ni med de/ gzugs med na gzugs can thams cad med pa'i phyir dang*/ bsam gtan gyi sdom pa ni sems kyi rjes su 'brang ba'i phyir dang*/ 'du shes med pa'i sems can la sems med pa'i phyir ro/ /

Āryas born in the formless realm and beings devoid of discernment possess seven virtuous actions of body and speech, such as abandoning taking life and so on, by means of [prior] [380] attainment (lābhata). {Formless-realm āryas have seven actions of body and speech through [prior] attainment, since they generated past uncontaminated vows in dependence on former levels. They possess the cessation of those since they were solely attained from having arisen before. Future actions are possessed in dependence on the five levels, and these are states yet to arise in the future. Also arhats possess future action alone through relinquishing the path of entry.} If the cause of relinquishing uncontaminated vows obtained in the form realm does not arise, then those āryas born in the formless realm possess the obtainment of past and future instances of the seven uncontaminated vows abandoning negative actions, and also beings devoid of discernment possess the obtainment of absorption vows. There are no manifest [material actions there] because there is no material entity in the formless realm, and beings devoid of discernment have no mind.

gzugs med pa dang 'du shes med pa'i sems can las lhag mar byas pa'i khams dang 'gro ba gzhan dag na ni srog gcod spong ba la sogs pa bdun po thob par ma zad mngon du gyur pa'i sgo nas kyang yod do zhes spyir bstan nas dmyal ba dang bcas pa'i sgra mi snyan pa ma gtogs zhes dmigs kyis bsal ba yin no/ / de la dud 'gro dang yi dwags na ni sdom pas bsdus pa med kyang bar mas bsdus pa yod do/ / gzugs khams na ni bsam gtan zag med kyi sdom pas bsdus pa yod do/ / mi rnams la ni sdom pa{ gsum ga} dang bar mas bsdus pa gnyis ka yod do/{ 'dod lha la sdom pa gnyis dang bar ma yod do/ /} dmyal ba dang sgra mi snyan pa ma gtogs pa zhes bya ba ni de na yang dag par blangs pa'i tshul khrims med pa'i phyir ro zhes TI ka byed pa 'chad mod kyi de lta na yi dwags dang dud 'gro'ang ma gtogs pa'i nang du bgrang bar thal ba'i phyir ro/ / des na dmyal ba na ni sdug bsngal gyis rnam par g.yeng pas srog gcod spong ba la sogs pa'i sems pa'i skabs med pa'i phyir dang*/ sgra mi snyan pa ni shin tu blun pa'i phyir{ dang len sems dang ting nge 'dzin med pa'i phyir} de dag spong ba'i sems pa med do/ / sems pa med pa'am srog gcod pa med pa tsam gyis ni dge bar mi 'gyur te/ rdo'i dum bu la sogs pa'ang dge bar thal ba'i phyir ro/ / 'o na dud 'gro'ang shin tu blun pa'i phyir srog gcod spong ba la sogs pa med par 'gyur ro zhe na/ dud 'gro kha cig ni blo gsal ba'i phyir ro/ /

It is generally stated that the rest — those in other realms and rebirths who are not formless-realm āryas and beings devoid of discernment — not only obtain seven actions such as abandoning taking life, but they also possess them by means of those actions manifesting, except for beings of hell and Uttarakuru, who are special cases. Animals and ghosts have actions not included as vows but subsumed by interim precepts. Those in the form realm have actions subsumed by absorption and uncontaminated vows. Humans have actions subsumed by {the three} vows and interim precepts. {Desire-realm gods have two vows and interim precepts.} Indeed, the Subcommentary explains that the statement “Except for beings of hell and Uttarakuru” (4:84d) means that those beings do not have proper ethics, and that it follows that they are counted among those [without proper ethics] apart from ghosts and animals.[1216] They do not have the intention to abandon [unethical] actions because they have no opportunity to generate the intention to abandon taking life in the hells, due to the mental disturbance caused by pain and so on, and those of Uttarakuru are extremely dull-witted {and they do not take revenge or possess concentration}. Merely lacking the intention to take life or merely not taking life is not virtuous, because if it were, it would follow that a stone would be virtuous. Objection: Animals also do not abandon taking life and so on because they are extremely dull. Reply: Some animals have clarity of mind.
bdun pa 'bras bu bshad pa ni
RESULTS
thams cad bdag po rgyu mthun dang / / rnam smin 'bras bu 'byin par 'dod/ / sdug bsngal phyir dang bsad phyir dang / / gzi byin med phyir 'bras rnam gsum/ / 85

All are asserted to produce a dominant result, natural outflow, and karmic maturation. There are three results because one makes another suffer, because one kills, and because one destroys vigor. (4:85)

mi dge ba bcu po thams cad kyis kyang bdag po dang rgyu mthun pa dang rnam par smin pa'i 'bras bu gsum gsum 'byin par 'dod de/ de la mi dge ba bcu po de dag chen pos dmyal ba dang 'bring gis dud 'gro dang chung ngus yi dwags su rnam par smin par 'gyur te 'di ni rnam smin gyi 'bras bu'o/ / de ltar yang mdo las/ mi dge ba kun tu bsten pa dang*/ goms par byas pa dang*/ lan mang du byas pa thams cad kyis dmyal ba dag tu skye bar 'gyur te 'di ni de dag gi rnam par smin pa'i 'bras bu yin no zhes pa dang*/ rin po che'i phreng ba las kyang*/ mi nyid la ni 'bras bu 'di/ / kun gyis dang por ngan 'gro'o zhes gsungs te/ de la kun tu bsten pa ni sbyor ba'o/ / goms par byas pa ni dngos so/ / lan mang du byas pa ni mjug ste de dag gsum ga tshang ba ni chen po yin la gnyis tshang ba ni 'bring dang gcig ni chung ngu yin no zhes shes par bya'o/ / las gdags pa las kyang*/ mi dge ba bcu po de dag chen po dang 'bring dang chung ngu gsum las chen po kun tu bsten zhing bsgoms te mang du byas pas ni sems can dmyal ba rnams su skye la/ 'bring gis ni dud 'gro dang*/ chung ngus ni yi dwags su skye bar 'gyur ro/ / de dag gi che chung nyid ji ltar shes par bya zhe na/ kun nas dkris pa chung ngu dang 'bring dang chen pos kun nas dkris te byed na go rim bzhin du rnam par smin pa chung ngu dang 'bring dang chen por 'gyur ro zhes bshad do/ /

All ten nonvirtuous actions are asserted to produce three results each: a dominant result, a result of natural outflow, and a result of karmic maturation. Extensive participation in the ten nonvirtuous actions produces karmic maturation as a hell being, medium participation that of a ghost, small participation that of an animal. Also a sūtra states: All those who continuously rely on nonvirtue, cultivate it, [381] and frequently engage in it are born in the hells, for that is its maturational result.[1217] Also in Precious Garland it is written: These are results for humans, but first of all comes lower rebirth.[1218] “Continuously rely” should be understood as the preparation, “cultivate” should be understood as the actual basis, and “frequently engage” should be understood as the conclusion. If three are complete it is intense participation, if two are complete it is medium participation, and if one is complete it is small participation. Presentation on Karma states: From among intense, medium, and small participation in the ten nonvirtues, intense participation produces birth among hell beings through continuous reliance, cultivation, and frequent engagement. Medium participation produces birth among ghosts, and small participation produces birth among animals. How should one understand their differences? Through the small, medium, and great entanglements one is completely entangled and, respectively, experiences small, medium, or great karmic maturation.[1219]

sa'i dngos gzhi las ni/ chung ngur spyad pas dud 'gror skye bar bshad do/ / rgyu mthun la byed pa rgyu mthun ni mi dge ba byed pa la goms longs can du 'gyur la/ myong ba rgyu mthun ni rin po che'i phreng ba las/ gsod pa yis ni tshe thung 'gyur/ / rku ba yis ni longs spyod phongs/ / byi ba byed pas dgra dang bcas/ / rdzun du smra bas skur mang ste/ / phra ma yis ni bshes dang 'byed/ / rtsub po yis ni mi snyan thos/ / ma 'brel ba yis tshig mi btsun/ / brnab sems yid la re ba 'joms/ / gnod sems 'jigs pa sbyin par bshad/ / log par lta bas lta ngan nyid/ / ces gal te dmyal ba la sogs pa nas thar nas dge bas mir skyes na de lta bu 'byung bar bshad la/ 'di'i 'grel par ni{ rim pa ltar dug gsum shas che bar 'gyur bar} brnab sems kyis ni 'dod chags shas che bar 'gyur ro/ / gnod sems kyis ni zhe sdang shas che bar 'gyur ro/ / log par lta bas ni gti mug shas che bar 'gyur te de la ni gti mug mang ba'i phyir ro zhes bshad la/ gzhan dag ni 'dra bar bshad do/ /

Yogācāra Levels explains: Due to small engagement one is born an animal.[1220] Natural outflow has two types: Habitual natural outflow, which is being accustomed to committing nonvirtue, and experiential natural outflow. Precious Garland notes: Those who kill have short lives. Those who harm experience much suffering. Those who steal are poor in resources. Those who commit adultery have enemies. Those who lie are disparaged. Those who slander are separated from dear ones. Those who employ harsh speech hear unpleasant words. Those who gossip have their words rejected. Those with covetousness have their hopes destroyed. Those with malice experience fear. Those with wrong view come to possess evil views.[1221] This explains what happens once one is liberated from the hells and so on and takes birth as a human through prior virtue. A commentary on this [topic], {which serially takes the three poisons as dominant}, explains: Through covetousness attachment dominates. Through malice aversion dominates. Through wrong view delusion dominates and delusion multiplies.[1222] The others are explained in the same way.

bdag po'i 'bras bu ni yul ngan pa rnams su skye bar 'gyur te/ 'di ltar gsod pas gzi nus pa chung bas chung ba rkus pa yis/ {lo thog la } ser ba btsa' char 'dod log gis/{/spus pa na bas//}rdul 'khrigs can 'gyur rdzun gyis ni/ / dri nga phra mas mthon dman can/ / rtsub pos tshwa sgo can dang ni/{ 'bru mi skye ba/} dgon gdung{ ni chu med pa} tha chad{ ni kla klo'i yul sogs} sdig pa can/{ sems can la gnod pa mangs/ nus pa chung bas/} kyal pas dus log{ char dus su mi 'bab pa sogs} brnab sems kyis/ / 'bras bu phra dang gnod sems kyis/ / 'bras bu kha dang log ltas ni/ / 'bras bu chung ba'am med par 'gyur/ / zhes shes par bya'o/ / 'di la kha cig na re las gcig po de la 'bras bu gsum yod do zhes zer ro/ / kha cig na re sbyor bas ngan song du skye la/ dngos gzhis tshe thung ba la sogs par 'gyur ro zhes zer ro/ / {de dag kyang rang rgyud la smin pa rnam smin dang*/ phyi rol la smin pa bdag 'bras dang*/ ris mthun bkod pa rgyu mthun 'bras yin no/ / dge ba la bral 'bras kyang yod la/ gnyis ka la skyes bu byed 'bras yod kyang*/ 'dir 'bras bu gsum du bsdus nas bstan no } 'o na de dag las 'bras bu gsum 'byung ba ji ltar zhe na/

The dominant result is taking birth in an inferior place. Thus (1) through killing, the land has poor fertility; (2) through stealing, it hails {on the harvest}; (3) through sexual misconduct, the land is {poor in quality and} covered with dust; (4) through lying it has a bad smell; (5) through slander it is high and precipitous or low and inferior; (6) through harsh words the land is encrusted with salt, {seeds will not germinate}, it is isolated and scorched {without water}, wild {a land of barbarians}, evil {with numerous dangers for sentient beings, and there is lack of potency}; (7) through idle speech the seasons are reversed {for it doesn’t rain when it should and so on}; (8) through covetousness the fruit is small; (9) through malice the fruit is sour; and (10) through wrong view the fruit is scarce or nonexistent. Some say: For each karma there are three results. Some say: [382] Through preparation one is born in lower rebirths and through the actual basis one has short lifespan and so on. {That maturing within one’s mindstream is karmic maturation, that maturing externally is the dominant result, and that generated with similar type is the result of natural outflow. Also virtue has a result of separation, and both virtue and nonvirtue have results of conscious effort. Here they are taught by subsuming them in three results.} Question: How are three results derived from such [karmas]?

srog gcod pas pha rol po sdug bsngal bar byas pa'i phyir dang*/ srog dang phral nas bsad pa'i phyir dang*/ bsad nas gzi byin med par byas pa'i phyir rim pa ltar rnam smin ngan song gi sdug bsngal myong ba dang*/ rgyu mthun tshe thung ba dang*/ bdag 'bras yul dang phyi'i sman rnams gzi mthu chung ba'i phyir 'bras bu rnam pa gsum du nges so zhes bya'o/ / de bzhin du ma byin len la sogs pa la'ang sbyar ro/ / dge ba zag bcas rnams kyi rnam smin gyi 'bras bu ni mtho ris su skyes nas bde ba myong ba yin te/ rin po che'i phreng ba las bzlog pas lha dang mi nyid do zhes bshad do/ / byed pa rgyu mthun ni dge ba byed pa la goms par 'gyur ro/ / myong ba rgyu mthun ni srog gcod pa spangs pas tshe ring ba la sogs pa yin no/ / bdag pa'i 'bras bu ni gzi mthu che ba'i yul du skye ba la sogs par 'gyur ro/ / rin po che'i phreng ba las/ mi dge zhes bya de dag gi /rnam smin bsgrags pa gang yin pa/ / dge ba dag ni thams cad la/ / 'bras bu de ni bzlog ste 'byung zhes bshad do/ /

Reply: Through taking life, one definitely experiences three results: (1) its karmic maturation is to experience the suffering of lower rebirth, (2) its natural outflow is a short life, and (3) its dominant result is that the vigor of the land and external spirits are weak, [and one experiences these three,] respectively, because one makes another suffer by taking life, because one kills through separating another from their life force, and because one destroys vigor (ojas). These are to be applied similarly to taking what is not given and so on. The maturational result of contaminated virtue is birth in a high status and the experience of pleasure, since Precious Garland explains that by opposing [nonvirtue one is born as] a god or a human. Habitual natural outflow is being accustomed to the practice of virtue. Experiential natural outflow is having a long life and so on through abandoning taking life. The dominant result is taking birth in a place of great vitality. Precious Garland states: The karmic maturation of these nonvirtuous actions is widely proclaimed. And the results of all virtuous actions manifest as their opposite.[1223]
zhar la log pa'i ngag la sogs pa bshad pa ni
IN ADDITION, EXPLAINING WRONG SPEECH AND SO ON
lus dang ngag las chags las skyes/ / log 'tsho sbyang dka'i phyir logs shig/ / bstan to gal te yo byad la/ / chags bslang mdo dang 'gal phyir min/ / 86

Physical and verbal karma arisen from attachment are wrong livelihood. It is taught separately because it is difficult to purify. If only that which is motivated by attachment to articles were wrong livelihood, it would contradict the sūtra. (4:86)

yang mdo las log pa'i ngag dang log pa'i las kyi mtha' dang log pa'i 'tsho ba gsum gsungs pa la zhe sdang dang gti mug las skye pa'i ngag ni log pa'i ngag go /de gnyis las skyes pa'i lus kyi las ni log pa'i las kyi mtha'o/ / lus dang ngag gi las chags pa las skyes pa ni log pa'i 'tsho ba yin no/ / ci'i phyir chags pa las skyes pa'i las gnyis phyogs gcig tu log 'tshor bstan zhe na/ chags pa las skyes pa'i lus ngag gi las log 'tsho de ni gnyen pos sbyang bar dka' ba'i phyir zhe sdang dang gti mug las skyes pa las log shig tu log pa'i 'tsho bar bstan to/ / de'i phyir slob dpon gyis/ rtag tu lta ba sna tshogs kyi/ / khyim pas lta ba sbyang bar dka'/ / 'tsho ba gzhan la rag lus pa'i/ / dge slong gis ni 'tsho ba nyid/ / ces gsungs pa yin no/ / 'di la sngon gyi slob dpon kha cig na re zas gos la sogs pa 'tsho ba'i yo byad la chags pas bslang ba'i lus ngag gi las kho na log 'tsho yin gyi rang nyid dga' bar bya ba'i ched du glu gar la sogs pa byed pa ni log 'tsho ma yin no/ / zhes zer ba ni min te/ gal te 'tsho ba'i yo byad la chags pas bslang ba'i lus ngag gi las kho na log 'tsho yin na de ni tshul khrims kyi phung po'i mdo dang 'gal ba'i phyir ro/ / mdo ni 'di yin te/ dbyug gu gsum pa/ de la 'di lta ste/ dge sbyong ngam bram ze kha cig dad pas byin pa yongs su longs spyad nas ltad mo sna tshogs 'di lta ste/ glang po che 'thab pa dang*/ rta 'thab pa dang*/ shing rtas 'thab pa dang*/ rkang thang 'thab pa dang*/ dbyug pas 'thab pa dang zhes bya ba nas dmag byin po ston pa la lta bar rtsom pa'i brtson pa dang ldan par gnas pa'am/ 'dus pa chen po nyams sa myong bar byed de/ dge sbyong ni de lta bu'i ltad mo sna tshogs lta bar rtsom par brtson pa spang ba yin no zhes bya ba'i bar du gsungs la/ de bzhin du glang po che'i sgra la sogs pa nyan pa la'ang sbyar nas gsungs te/ gzugs sgra la sogs pa la chags pas lta ba dang nyan pa la sogs pa'ang yang dag pa ma yin pa log pa'i yul la yongs su longs spyod pa'i phyir log 'tshor gsung pa'i phyir ro/ /

The sūtras state the three actions: (1) wrong speech, (2) wrong action, and (3) wrong livelihood. Speech arisen from aversion and delusion is wrong speech, and action arisen from those is wrong action. Physical and verbal karma arisen from attachment are wrong livelihood (mithyājīva). Question: Why are the two karmas arisen from attachment taught to be wrong livelihood? Reply: Physical and verbal karma arisen from attachment is taught to be wrong livelihood separately from karma arisen from aversion and delusion because it is difficult to purify by antidote. Therefore Vasubandhu said: Householders who continuously generate diverse views have difficulty purifying view. Monks who rely on the livelihood of others have difficulty purifying livelihood.[1224] A past master said: Only physical and verbal karma motivated by attachment to articles of livelihood such as food and clothing are wrong livelihood, but singing and dancing and so on out of enjoyment are not wrong livelihood. Reply: That is not so, for if only physical and verbal karma motivated by attachment to articles of livelihood is wrong livelihood, that would contradict the Aggregate of Ethics Sūtra, which states: Tridaṇḍin, view it this way. Some who train in virtue or brahmans who have faith attend various shows, [383] fully enjoying their splendor, such as fighting with elephants, fighting with horses, fighting with chariots, fighting with feet, fighting with staffs . . . up to . . . striving to see military battles, or to experience mass assemblies. But those who train in virtue abandon striving to see such displays.[1225] Similarly, that should be applied to listening to the call of the elephant and so on because viewing or listening and so on to forms or sounds and so forth with attachment and utilizing improper objects is stated to be wrong livelihood.
bdun pa las 'bras bu du dang bcas par dbye ba ni
Karma and its results
'o na las gang zhig 'bras bu lnga las 'bras bu du zhig gis 'bras bu dang bcas pa yin zhe na/
Question: How many results among the five results does karma possess?
drir bcas spong ba'i lam dag gi/ / las ni lnga yi 'bras bur bcas/ / dri med bzhi yi zag bcas gzhan/ / dge dang mi dge gang yin pa'ang / / 87

The karma of those paths abandoning that which is stained possesses five results, the stainless, four, as do any virtuous or nonvirtuous states other than paths abandoning that which is contaminated. (4:87)

dri bcas te zag pa dang bcas pa'i spong ba'i lam {'jig rten pa'i sgom lam bar chad med pa } dag gi las ni rnam smin dang*/ bdag 'bras dang*/ rgyu mthun pa'i 'bras bu dang*/ skyes bu byed 'bras dang*/ bral 'bras dang*/ lnga yis 'bras bur bcas pa yin no/ / de la dri bcas spong ba'i lam ni 'jig rten pa'i sgom pa'i lam bar chad med pa'o/ / 'di'i rnam smin gyi 'bras bu ni rang gi sar gtogs pa'i rnam smin yid du 'ong ba yin la/ bdag 'bras ni sngar byung ma gtogs pa rang gi ngo bo las gzhan pa'i 'dus byas thams cad do/ / rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu ni ting nge 'dzin las skyes pa'i chos 'dra ba phyi ma rnams so/ / skyes bu byed 'bras ni rnam grol gyi lam dang thob pa dang spangs pa la sogs pa de ma thag dang cig car 'byung ba rnams so/ / bral ras ni sa 'og ma'i nyon mongs pa spangs pa'o/ / dri med kyi spong ba'i lam ni 'bras bu bzhi yis 'bras bu dang bcas pa yin te/ zag med la rnam smin gyi 'bras bu med pa'i phyir ro/ / zag pa dang bcas pa spong ba'i lam las gzhan pa'i dge ba dang mi dge ba gang yin pa de'ang 'bras bu bzhis 'bras bu dang bcas pa yin te/ de dag la bral 'bras mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: The karma of those paths abandoning that which is stained (samala) or contaminated possesses five results: (1) karmic maturation, (2) dominant result, (3) result of natural outflow, (4) result of conscious effort, and (5) result of separation. The path abandoning stains is the mundane uninterrupted path of meditation. Its maturational result is the pleasant karmic maturation belonging to its level. Its dominant result is any conditioned state distinct from its own essential nature that does not occur before it. Its result of natural outflow is any subsequent state arisen from concentration that is similar to it. Its result of conscious effort is the liberated path, obtainment, and abandonment and so on occurring immediately after it. Its result of separation is the abandonment of affliction of lower levels. The stainless path of abandonment possesses four results because the uncontaminated has no maturational result. As do any virtuous or nonvirtuous states other than paths abandoning that which is contaminated, they possess four results, because it is impossible for them to have a result of separation.
zag pa med pa lhag ma dang / / lung bstan min gang gsum gyis so/ / dge ba'i dge la sogs pa ni/ / bzhi dang gnyis dang de bzhin gsum/ / 88
The remaining uncontaminated paths and any undeclared states possess three. Results of virtue that are virtuous and so on have four, two, and similarly three. (4:88)

zag pa med pa spong ba'i lam gyi lhag ma sbyor ba dang rnam grol dang khyad par gyi lam dang*/ dge mi dger lung bstan pa min pa bsgribs pa dang ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gang dag yin pa de dag ni rnam smin dang bral 'bras ma gtogs pa 'bras bu gsum gyi 'bras bu dang bcas so/ /

Those remaining uncontaminated paths of abandonment, such as preparatory, liberated, and special paths, and any that are obscured states not declared to be virtuous or nonvirtuous, as well as unobscured-neutral states, possess three results, excluding karmic maturation and separation.

dge ba'i 'bras bu dge ba yin pa la ni 'bras bu bzhi yin te/ de la rnam smin gyi 'bras bu mi srid pa'i phyir dang*/ spong lam gyi bral 'bras kyang don dam par dge ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ / sogs pa'i sgras gzung ba dge bas mi dge ba skyed pa la ni 'bras bu skyes bu byed pa dang bdag 'bras gnyis yin te/ rnam smin dang bral 'bras dang rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu gsum mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du dge bas lung ma bstan skyed pa la ni 'bras bu gsum yin te/ bral ba dang rgyu mthun pa'i 'bras bu gnyis mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ /

Results of virtue that are virtuous are the four results because it is impossible for virtue to be a maturational result, and [384] the result of separation of the abandoning path is ultimate virtue. The “and so on” refers to nonvirtuous states generated by virtue and comprises two results — the result of conscious effort and the dominant result — because it is impossible for [such] nonvirtuous states to be the results of karmic maturation, results of separation, or results of natural outflow. Similarly, neutral states generated by virtue comprise three results because it is impossible for them to be either the result of separation or the result of natural outflow.
mi dge'i dge sogs gnyis dang ni/ / gsum dang bzhi ste rim pa bzhin/ / lung bstan min gyi dge la sogs/ / de dag gnyis dang gsum dang gsum/ / 89

The results of nonvirtue that are virtuous, nonvirtuous, and neutral are respectively two, three, and four results. The results of neutral states that are virtuous and so on are two, three, and three results. (4:89)

mi dge ba'i 'bras bu dge ba yin pa la ni rim pa bzhin du 'bras bu skyes bu byed pa dang bdag 'bras gnyis yin te/ rnam smin dang rgyu mthun dang bral ba'i 'bras bu mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / sogs pa'i sgras bstan pa mi dge bas mi dge ba bskyed pa la ni skyes bu byed pa dang bdag po dang rgyu mthun pa'i 'bras bu gsum yin te/ rnam smin dang bral 'bras mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / mi dge ba'i las kyis lung ma bstan skyed pa la 'bras bu bzhi yin te/ bral 'bras ma gtogs pa'i phyir ro/ / mi dge bas lung ma bstan bskyed pa la rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu ni nyon mongs can du 'dra bas kun 'gro mi dge ba sdug bsngal mthong spang gis/ bsgribs la lung ma bstan 'jig tshogs la lta ba dang mthar 'dzin par lta ba rnams skyed pa la yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

The results of nonvirtue that are virtuous, nonvirtuous, and neutral are, respectively, two results — result of conscious effort and dominant result — because it is impossible that virtuous results are the result of karmic maturation, result of natural outflow, or result of separation. Three nonvirtuous results are generated by nonvirtue — result of conscious effort, dominant result, and result of natural outflow — because it is impossible for them to be the results of karmic maturation or results of separation. Four neutral results are generated by nonvirtuous karma because the result of separation is excluded. When nonvirtue generates neutral states, its natural outflow is similar to an afflicted state. Therefore omnipresent nonvirtuous states, which are objects abandoned by the path of seeing realizing the truth of suffering, generate obscured-neutral afflicted view of the self, and extreme view.

lung du bstan pa min pa nyid kyi 'bras bu dge ba yin pa la ni skyes bu byed pa dang bdag 'bras gnyis te/ rnam smin dang bral ba dang rgyu mthun pa'i 'bras bu gsum ma gtogs pa'i phyir ro/ / sogs dang de dag ces pa'i sgras bzung ba lung ma bstan gyis mi dge ba skyed pa la ni 'bras bu gsum ste/ bral 'bras dang rnam smin gnyis ma gtogs pa'o/ / 'di'i rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu ni bsgribs la lung ma bstan 'jig tshogs mthar 'dzin gyi sdug bsngal mthong spang la sogs pa'i mi dge ba bskyed pa yin te/ de dag ni nyon mongs can du 'dra ba'i phyir ro/ / lung ma bstan gyis lung ma bstan skyed pa la'ang 'bras bu gsum ste/ rnam smin dang bral 'bras ma gtogs pa'i phyir ro/ /

There are two results of neutral states that are virtuous — result of conscious effort and dominant result — excluding maturational result, result of separation, and the result of natural outflow. The “and so on” means that there are three nonvirtuous results generated by neutral states, excluding the result of separation and the result of karmic maturation. Its result of natural outflow includes the obscured-neutral afflicted view of the self, extreme view, and so on. These are objects abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering that will generate nonvirtuous states because they are similar to afflicted states. The “and so on” also means that there are three neutral states generated by neutral states; the results of karmic maturation and separation are excluded.
'das pa'i thams cad bzhi yin no/ / bar ma yi ni ma 'ongs pa'ang / / bar ma gnyis so ma skyes pa'i/ / 'bras bu ma 'ongs gsum yin no/ / 90
All results of past states comprise four results. Future results of interim precepts are also four. Present interim precepts generate two. Future result is the three. (4:90)

'das pa'i chos zag bcas kyis 'das pa dang ma 'ongs pa dang da ltar byung ba thams cad bskyed pa la ni {bral 'bras dus kyis ma bsdus pas de ma gtogs pa } 'bras bu bzhi bzhi yin no/ / gang zhe na/ bral 'bras ma gtogs pa ste/ de ni khams su ma gtogs shing dus kyis ma bsdus pa'i phyir mi srid do/ /

de bzhin du bar ma da ltar byung ba yi ni 'bras bu ma 'ongs pa yin pa la'ang bzhi yin te snga ma dang 'dra'o/ / bar ma da ltar byung bas da ltar byung ba bskyed na rnam smin dang rgyu mthun dang bral 'bras gsum mi srid pas skyes bu byed pa dang bdag 'bras gnyis so/ /

Similarly, the future results of present interim precepts are also the four results, like the former [four results of past contaminated phenomena]. If a present interim precept generates present states, it has two results — the result of conscious effort and a dominant result — since three are impossible: the results of karmic maturation, natural outflow, and separation.

las ma skyes pa ni ma 'ongs pa ste de'i 'bras bu ma 'ongs pa yin na rgyu mthun dang bral 'bras ma gtogs pa gsum yin no/ / da ltar bas 'das pa bskyed pa dang*/ ma 'ongs pas 'das pa dang da ltar ba bskyed pa ni mi srid pa'i phyir dpyad pa ma mdzad do/ /

The future result of future unarisen karma is the three results: those except for the result of natural outflow and result of separation. It is impossible for the present to generate the past and [385] for the future to generate the past and present, and so they are not considered.

rang gi sa pa bzhi yin no/ / gzhan gyi sa pa gsum dang gnyis/ / slob pa'i slob la sogs pa gsum/ / mi slob las kyi 'bras bu ni/ / 91
slob pa yi ni chos la sogs/ / gcig dang gsum dang gnyis yin no/ / de las gzhan pa'i 'bras bu ni/ / slob sogs gnyis dang gnyis dang lnga/ / 92

Those of its level are the four results. Those of other levels are three and two. Learner states generated by learners and so on are three. The results of the karma of a nonlearner that is (4:91)
a learner dharma and so on are one, three, and two. The result other than those is a learner result and so on that is two, two, and five results. (4:92)

zag bcas rang gis pa'i las kyis rang gi sa pa'i chos bskyed na bral 'bras sas ma bsdu pas de las gzhan pa'i 'bras bu bzhi yin no/ / rang sa zag med yin na rnam smin dang bral 'bras las gzhan gsum mo/ /

There are four results if contaminated karma itself generates results of its level, leaving out that subsumed by the level of the result of separation. If its own level is uncontaminated it generates three results, excluding the results of karmic maturation and separation.

gzhan gyi sa pa'i las kyis gzhan gyi sa pa'i chos bskyed na 'bras bu gsum byed pa ni sa dgu'i lam ni phan tshun du zhes 'byung bas zag med sa gzhan la rten pas zag med sa gzhan la rten pa'i rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu'ang byed pa'i phyir dang*/ bdag 'bras dang skyes bu byed 'bras kyang byed pa'i phyir dang*/ rnam smin dang bral 'bras ni mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / gnyis byed pa ni zag pa dang bcas pa ste/ de la skyes bu byed pa dang bdag 'bras yod kyi rnam smin dang rgyu mthun dang bral 'bras rnams mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ /

If the karma of one level generates results of other levels, it produces three results because, since it depends on other uncontaminated levels, it produces results of natural outflow in dependence on other uncontaminated levels; as it is said, “The path of the nine levels is a common cause” (2:52cd). It also produces dominant results and results of conscious effort, but the results of karmic maturation and separation are impossible. Contaminated states produce two because they have results of conscious effort and dominant results, but the results of karmic maturation, natural outflow, and separation are impossible.

slob pa'i las kyis slob pa'i chos bskyed na gsum yin te/ rnam smin dang bral 'bras slob pa ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / sogs pa'i sgras bstan pa slob pas/ mi slob pa skyed pa'ang de dang 'dra'o/ / slob pas slob pa'ang ma yin mi slob pa'ang ma yin pa'i chos bskyed na'ang gsum yin te/ rnam smin dang rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ /

There are three learner results generated by the karma of learners because the results of karmic maturation and separation are not learner states. The “and so on” indicates that nonlearner results generated by learner karma are similar. Three neither-learner-nor-nonlearner results are also generated by learner karma because the results of karmic maturation and natural outflow are impossible.

mi slob pa'i las kyi 'bras bu ni slob pa'i chos yin na bdag po'i 'bras bu gcig kho na yin te/ mi slob pa las nyams pa'i tshe na'ang nyon mongs pa kun tu 'byung bas bar du chod pa'i phyir mi slob pa'i 'jug thogs su de ma thag gam cig car du slob pa 'byung ba med pas skyes bu byed 'bras kyang mi srid pa'i phyir dang*/ rnam smin gyi 'bras bu la sogs pa gsum yang mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / gang dag skyes bu byed 'bras chod pa las kyang skye bar 'dod pa de dag gi ltar na mi slob pas slob pa skyed na 'bras bu gnyis byed pa yin no/ / sogs pas bsdus pa mi slob pas mi slob pa'i chos bskyed na 'bras bu gsum byed pa yin te/ rnam smin dang bral 'bras ma gtogs pa'i phyir ro/ / mi slob pas slob pa'ang ma yin mi slob pa'ang ma yin pa'i chos bskyed na de la rgyu mthun dang rnam smin dang bral 'bras gsum mi srid pas skyes bu byed pa dang bdag po'i 'bras bu gnyis byed pa yin no/ /

The result of the karma of a nonlearner that is a learner dharma is one alone: the dominant result, because when one degenerates from the state of nonlearner one is obstructed by the occurrence of affliction. The result of conscious effort is impossible since the state of learner does not arise immediately after or simultaneously with the end of the state of nonlearner; and the other three results such as the result of karmic maturation are also impossible. The “and so on” includes the three nonlearner results generated by nonlearners, which leave out the results of karmic maturation and separation. It also includes the two neither-learner-nor-nonlearner results generated by nonlearners — the result of conscious effort and the dominant result — since the results of natural outflow, karmic maturation, and separation are impossible.

slob pa dang mi slob pa de gnyis las gzhan pa slob pa'ang ma yin mi slob pa'ang ma yin pa'i las kyi 'bras bu ni slob pa yin na skyes bu byed pa dang bdag 'bras gnyis yin te rnam smin dang rgyu mthun dang bral 'bras gsum ni mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / sogs pa'i sgras gzung ba slob pa'ang ma yin mi slob pa'ang ma yin pa'i 'bras bu mi slob pa yin na'ang 'bras bu gnyis yin te snga ma dang 'dra'o/ / slob pa'ang ma yin mi slob pa'ang ma yin pas slob pa'ang ma yin mi slob pa'ang ma yin pa'i chos skyed pa la ni 'bras bu lnga po thams cad sred pa yin no/ /

If the result of neither-learner-nor-nonlearner karma other than those two learner or nonlearner results is a learner result, there are two — the result of conscious effort and the dominant result — because three are impossible: the results of karmic maturation, natural outflow, and separation. The “and so on” means that if the result of neither-learner-nor-nonlearner karma is a nonlearner result, there are two results, like the former [case for a learner result]. And if neither-learner-nor-nonlearner karma generates neither-learner-nor-nonlearner results, there are five results, for all are possible.
mthong bas spang bya'i de la sogs/ / gsum dang bzhi dang gcig yin no/ / bsgom pas spang bar bya las kyi/ / de dag gnyis dang bzhi dang gsum/ / 93
That abandoned by seeing and so on are three, four, and one result. Karma to be abandoned by meditation is those two, four, and three. (4:93)

mthong bas spang bar bya ba'i las kyi 'bras bu mthong bas spang bar bya ba de yin na 'bras bu gsum yin te/ rnam smin dang bral 'bras ma gtogs pa'i phyir ro/ / sogs pas gzung ba mthong spang gi 'bras bu sgom spang yin na bzhi yin te/ bral 'bras ma gtogs pa'o/ / mthong spang gi 'bras bu spang bya ma yin na gcig ste bdag 'bras kho na yin no/ /

If the result of karma to be abandoned by the path of seeing is abandoned by the path of seeing, [386] there are three results because the results of karmic maturation and separation are excluded. The “and so on” means that if the result of karma to be abandoned by the path of seeing is abandoned by the path of meditation, there are four results because the result of separation is excluded. If the result of karma to be abandoned by the path of seeing is not abandoned, there is one result, the dominant result alone.

bsgom pas spang bar bya ba'i las kyi 'bras bu mthong spang dang*/ sgom spang dang spang bya ma yin pa de dag yin na rim pa bzhin du 'bras bu gnyis dang bzhi dang gsum yin te/ dang po la ni rnam smin dang rgyu mthun dang bral 'bras gsum mi srid pa'i phyir dang*/ gnyis pa la ni bral 'bras mi srid pa'i phyir dang*/ gsum pa la ni rgyu mthun dang rnam smin gnyis mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ /

If the result of karma to be abandoned by the path of meditation is (1) abandoned by the path of seeing, (2) abandoned by the path of meditation, or (3) not to be abandoned, it is respectively two, four, and three results because the three — the results of karmic maturation, natural outflow, and separation — are impossible for the first, the result of separation is impossible for the second, and both the results of natural outflow and karmic maturation are impossible for the third.
spang bya min pa'i de dag gcig/ / gnyis dang bzhi ste go rims bzhin/ /
Results not to be abandoned are respectively one, two, and four. (4:94ab)

spang bar bya ba min pa'i las kyi 'bras bu mthong spang dang sgom spang dang spang bya ma yin pa de dag yin na 'bras bu gcig dang gnyis dang bzhi ste go rim bzhin du sbyar te/ dang po la bdag 'bras dang*/ gnyis pa la zag med kyi lam las langs pa'i tshe de'i 'jug tu sgom spang khams gsum gyi dge ba zag bcas 'byung ba ni skyes bu byed pa dang bdag 'bras gnyis dang*/ gsum pa la ni rnam smin gyi 'bras bu ma gtogs pa bzhi byed pa'i phyir ro/ /

If the result of karma not to be abandoned is (1) abandoned by the path of seeing, (2) abandoned by the path of meditation, or (3) not to be abandoned, then respectively it has one, two, and four results: the first is the dominant result; the second is the result of conscious effort and dominant result occurring at the end of rising from the uncontaminated path, which are contaminated virtuous states of the three realms that are abandoned by the path of meditation; and the third produces the four results excepting the result of karmic maturation.
brgyad pa rigs pa dang rigs pa ma yin pas bskyed pa'i dbye ba ni
Appropriate and inappropriate karma
rigs min bskyed pa nyon mongs can/ / kha cig cho ga nyams pa'ang zhe'o/ / 94
Inappropriate karma is afflicted. Some say it also undermines the rules. (4:94cd)

bstan bcos las rigs pa ma yin pas bskyed pa dang*/ rigs pas bskyed pa dang*/ gnyis kas bskyed pa ma yin pa'i las gsum gsungs pa la rigs pa min pas bskyed pa ni las nyon mongs pa can yin te/ de yang mi dge ba rang bzhin gyis kha na ma tho ba dang bsgribs la lung ma bstan te/ tshul bzhin ma yin pa yid la byed pas skyed pa'i phyir ro/ /

The treatise (Attainment of Knowledge)[1226] mentions three: inappropriate karma, appropriate karma, and karma that is neither.[1227] Inappropriate (ayogavihita) karma is afflicted karma because nonvirtuous natural offenses and obscured-neutral states are generated by inappropriate attention.

sngon gyi slob dpon kha cig na re de ni las nyon mongs can kho nar ma zad kyi bcas pa'i kha na ma tho ba 'gro ba dang gnas pa dang bza' ba dang go ba la sogs pa 'jig rten na 'di ltar bya'o zhes grags pa'i cho ga las nyams nas de dang mi mthun par byed pa'ang rigs pa ma yin pas bskyed pa yin no zhe'o/ / rigs pas bskyed pa ni las dge ba yin no/ / kha cig ni der ma zad kyi cho ga ma nyams pa'ang yin no zhes zer ro/ / de gnyis las gzhan pa ni gnyis ka ma yin pa'o/ /

Some past masters say: It is not only generated by afflicted karma but it is generated through incompatible or inappropriate actions that also undermine the rules (vidhibhraṣṭa) of proscribed offenses such as “One should go, abide, eat, drink, or understand the world in this way and so on.” Appropriate karma is virtuous karma. Some say: Not only that, it is also that which does not undermine the rules. That which is other than those two is neither.
dgu pa 'phen byed dang rdzogs byed kyi dbye ba ni
Projecting and completing karma
ci las gcig gis skye ba gcig kho na 'phen nam/ 'on te du ma'ang 'phen/ de bzhin du las du mas kyang skye ba du ma kho na 'phen nam/ 'on te gcig kyang 'phen zhe na/
Question: Does one karma project one birth or many? [387] Similarly, do many karmas project many births or one?
gcig gis skye ba gcig 'phen to/ / yongs rdzogs byed pa du ma yin/ sems med snyoms par 'jug pa dag/ / 'phen byed ma yin thob pa'ang min/ / 95
One karma projects one birth. Many karmas complete it. Mindless meditative attainments do not project birth. Obtainment does not. (4:95)

las gcig gis skye ba gcig kho na 'phen par byed kyi las gcig gis skye ba du ma 'phen pa'ang med la/ ris mthun pa dum bur 'phen du 'ong bas na {las kyi 'bras bu gcig zad cing gzhan skyes pa na 'chi 'pho ba dang skye bar 'gyur bar thal bas na } las du mas skye ba gcig 'phen pa'ang med do {gcig gis du ma 'phen na skyes nas myong 'gyur la sogs pa gnas skabs nges pa'ang mi 'thad do/ /}zhes bya ba ni bye brag tu smra ba'i yin no/ /

Vaibhāṣikas say: One karma projects (ākṣipa) one birth alone, and one karma does not project many births. Many karmas do not project one birth since they would project states of the same type bit by bit, {and it would follow that when the result of one karma was exhausted and another arose, one would die and be reborn}. {If one karma projected many lives, then the certainty of the time [of maturation] would be untenable, such as karma to be experienced after rebirth and so on.}

'o na rgyal po dang yang dag par ldan pa'i mdo las/ gnas brtan ma 'gags pas dge slong rnams la smras pa tshe dang ldan pa dag bdag ba ra Na ser skyes bu dbul po rtswa thu ba zhig tu gyur pa na rang sangs rgyas steng gnas zhes bya ba'am spyi gtsug me tog ta ka pa lta bu zhes bya ba la bsod snyoms phul te/ bdag ni bsod snyoms gcig po de'i rnam par smin pas lan bdun gyi bar du sum cu rtsa gsum pa'i lha rnams kyi nang du skyes shing lan bdun gyi bar du 'khor los bsgyur ba'i rgyal por gyur pa nas da ltar shAkya phyug po'i rigs su skyes pa'i bar du yin no zhes{ pa dang*/ lung sman gyi gzhi las/ sum cu rtsa gsum lha rnams su/ / bdag gis lan bdun skye ba blangs/ / slar yang mi yi nang du ni/ / mi yi dbang po lan bdun byas/ / de tshe 'dzam gling dbang phyug gi rgyal rigs spyi bor dbang bskur ro/ / 'dir ni bdun dang der bdun te/ / bdag gis lan ni bcu bzhir 'khor zhes} gsungs pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/

Question: Doesn’t this contradict the Authentic King Sūtra, which states: The elder Aniruddha said to the monks: “Venerables, when I was a poor grass cutter in Vārāṇasī, I offered alms to a pratyekabuddha called Ūrdhvasthiti or Mūrdhapuṣpa. Through the maturation of that one karma, I was born among the gods of Trāyastriṃśa seven times, and then I was born a cakravartin king seven times, and from there I was born in the caste of the rich Śākyas.[1228] {and the Chapter on Medicine declares: I took birth seven times among the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa and again among humans I took birth seven times as a powerful lord. At that time I ruled as chief monarch of the lords of Jambudvīpa. I cycled fourteen times, taking birth here seven times and there seven times.[1229]}

mi 'gal te/ bsod nams des bde 'gro'i 'byor ba rnyed nas skye ba dran te yang bsod nams byas pas de dang de dag tu skyes pa la bsod snyoms gcig po des bskyed do zhes bshad de/ gcig po de la brten nas zhes bya ba'i don te dper na dong tse gcig lan du mar bsgyur bas phyug por gyur pa la bdag ni dong tse gcig gis phyug por gyur to zhes brjod pa lta bu'o/ / yang na bsod snyoms gcig phul ba de la brten nas dga' ba dang yid rang ba la sogs pa sems pa'i las du ma yod pa'i phyir de dag de dag gi 'bras bu yin no/ /

Reply: That is not contradictory because it is explained that “by that merit I recall a birth where I attained the riches of a blissful rebirth, and by that merit I recall being born here and there, and this was generated by giving alms once.” The meaning of the statement “in dependence on one karma” is, for example, like stating, “Since I became rich by turning one copper coin into many, I became rich through one copper coin.” Again, because in dependence on offering alms once, many states such as joy and delight arise through that intentional karma, they are the result of that.

las gcig gis 'phangs pa'i ris mthun pa'i skye ba de'i khyad par gyi chos yongs su rdzogs par byed pa'i las ni du ma yin te/ dper na ri mo mkhan dag skya ris ri lu gcig gis byas nas tshon sna tshogs kyis rdzogs par byed pa ltar mir mtshungs kyang kha cig ni {rdzogs byed dge bas } gzugs bzang ba dang dbang po tshang ba dang longs spyod che ba dang nad med pa dang dbang thang phun sum tshogs pa la sogs pa yin la/ kha cig ni {rdzogs byed mi dge bas } gzugs ngan pa la sogs pa yin no/ / gzugs bzang ba la sogs pa ni dge bas rdzogs par byed la/ ngan pa la sogs pa ni mi dge bas rdzogs par byed do/ / 'di la 'phen byed dge bas byas la rdzogs byed mi dge bas byas pa'ang yod de lha dang mi dbul po dang nad pa la sogs pa lta bu'o/ / rdzogs byed dge bas byas la 'phen byed mi dge bas byas pa'ang yod de yi dwags na chos kyi rgyal po gshin rje dang*/ dud 'gro ni klu'i rgyal po nor rgyas la sogs pa lta bu'o/ / gnyis ka dge bas byas pa ni lha'i dbang po brgya byin la sogs pa lta bu'o/ / gnyis ka mi dge bas byas pa ni dmyal ba mnar med lta bu'o/{ gal te kha dog la sogs pa rdzogs byed kyi 'bras bu rigs mod/ dbang po drug 'phen byed gyi 'bras bu ma yin nam zhe na/ de dag la yang rdzogs byed kyi las kyi nus pa 'jug ste/ de lta min na skye ba 'phangs phan chad 'ga' yang dbang po ma tshang bar mi 'gyur ro/} gal te{ las dang lhan cig pa'i tshor ba la sogs pa yang skye ba 'phen byed yin no/ /} las thams cad skye ba 'phen par byed pa yin nam zhe na/

Many karmas complete (paripūraka) the specific attributes of that birth of compatible type projected by one karma. For example, just as artists draw the outline with one stroke and complete it with various colors, so it is for humans. Some say: One has pleasant form, complete faculties, great resources, freedom from illness, an excellent fate, and so on {through virtuous completing karma}. Some say: One has inferior form {through nonvirtuous completing karma}. Pleasant form and so on are produced through virtuous completing karma, and unpleasant form and so on are produced through nonvirtuous completing karma. Virtuous projecting karma and nonvirtuous completing karma exist [in combination], such as when a god or rich human [388] has an illness and so on. Nonvirtuous projecting karma and virtuous completing karma exist [in combination] such as Yama the king of Dharma among the ghosts, Vāsuki the king of nāgas among the animals, and so on. [Projecting karma and completing karma] together being nonvirtuous exists, for example, in the lives of the hell beings of Avīci. {Question: If indeed color and so on are, by type, the result of completing karma, wouldn’t the six faculties be the result of projecting karma? Reply: The six faculties are also affected by the potency of completing karma because were that not so, then a being’s faculties would never become incomplete after their projection at birth.} Question: {Karma, as well as feeling and so on that occur simultaneously with it, project birth.} Do all karmas project birth?

{ rnam smin dang bcas kyang*/} sems med pa 'gog pa dang 'du shes med pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa dag ni 'phen par byed pa ma yin te/ de dag la sems med pas las sems pa dang lhan cig mi 'byung ba'i las ni stobs chung ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir 'du shes med pa'i snyoms 'jug gi rnam smin lha tshe ring po dang*/ 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug gi rnam smin srid rtse ba yin no zhes bya ba'ang rdzogs byed kyi dbang du byas pa yin gyi 'phen byed ni bsam gtan bzhi pa dang*/ srid pa'i rtse mo'i snyoms 'jug yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Vaibhāṣikas say: {Though they possess karmic maturation,} mindless meditative attainments of cessation and nondiscernment do not project birth. Karma that does not arise simultaneously with karmic intention, being mindless, is weak. Also the statement “The karmic maturation of the meditative attainment of nondiscernment is a long-lived god, and the karmic maturation of the meditative attainment of cessation is the summit of existence” is stated from the perspective of completing karma, where the projecting agents are the fourth absorption and the meditative attainment of the summit of existence.

dge ba dang mi dge ba'i thob pa'ang las dang lhan cig pa yin kyang 'phen byed min te/ las dang thob pa 'bras bu mi gcig pa'i phyir dang*/ thob pa la sems pa med par zhar la 'byung bas stobs chung ba'i phyir dang*/ thob pa ni shing gi shun pa ltar las las tha dad pa'i phyir ro/ / {sbyor lam dang 'phags lam yang 'phen byed min gyi rdzogs byed yin no } 'on kyang dge ba zag bcas kyi thob pa dang mi dge ba'i thob pa de dag ni rdzogs par byed pa'i las yin no/ zhes bya ba ni bye brag tu smra ba yin no/ {de bzhin du 'phags pa'i rgyud la yod pa'i zag bcas kyi las dang sbyor lam nges 'byed cha mthun bzhi'ang rdzogs byed kho na yin no } mdo sde pa dang theg pa gong ma pa dag ni las gcig gis skye ba du ma 'phen pa mdo de dang de las rnam pa du ma bshad pa'i phyir las gcig gis skye ba du ma 'phen pa dang*/ gcig gis gcig 'phen pa'ang yod de zhes bya ba 'di 'dod pa yin no/ /

Though obtainment of virtue and nonvirtue is simultaneous with karma, it does not project birth because karma and obtainment do not have the same result, obtainment is weak since it occurs incidentally when there is no intention, and obtainment is distinct from karma like the bark of a tree [is distinct from the trunk itself]. {The path of preparation and the ārya path do not project birth but complete birth.}[1230] However, the obtainment of contaminated virtue and the obtainment of nonvirtue are completing karma. {Similarly, contaminated karma existing in the mindstream of an ārya, and also the four conducive factors of penetrative insight on the path of preparation, are completing karma alone.} Sautrāntikas and Mahāyānists assert that because one karma projecting many births is explained in that and many other sūtras, both one karma projecting many births and one karma projecting one birth do exist.
21. Elaboration of Karma Found in the Sūtras: Part 2
bcu pa sgrib pa gsum bshad pa ni
The three obscurations
mdo las/ las kyi sgrib pa dang*/ nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dang*/ rnam par smin pa'i sgrib pa gsum bshad pa la
The sūtras explain three obscurations: karmic obscuration, afflictive obscuration, and maturational obscuration.[1231]
mtshams med pa yi las rnams dang / / nyon mongs shas chen ngan 'gro dang / / 'du shes med pa'i sems can dang / / sgra mi snyan sgrib gsum du 'dod/ / 96
The karma of heinous acts, strong affliction, and the births in lower rebirth, as a being devoid of discernment, and in Uttarakuru are said to be the three obscurations. (4:96)

ma dang*/ pha dang*/ dgra bcom pa gsod pa dang*/ dge 'dun gyi dbyen 'byed pa dang*/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku la ngan sems kyis khrag 'byin pa ste skye ba phyi ma kho na la dmyal bar skye ba la las dang 'gro ba gzhan gyis mtshams sam bar bcad par mi nus pas mtshams med pa lnga'i las rnams ni las kyi sgrib pa dang*/ nyon mongs pa shas chen po ni nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa yin no/ / de la nyon mongs pa la shas che ba dang rno ba gnyis las dang po ni rgyun chags su 'byung ba gang yin pa ste/ de nyid chung ngu las 'bring*/ 'bring las chen po rgyun mi chad par 'byung bas gnyen pos spong ba'i skabs mi rnyed pas nyon mongs pa'i sgrib par gzhag go {gnyis pa ni} drag tu 'byung ba gang yin pa ste de ni spang sla ba'i phyir sgrib pa gsum gyi nang du ma gtogs so/ / ngan 'gro rnam pa gsum dang 'du shes med pa'i sems can dang byang gi sgra mi snyan du skyes pa rnams ni rnam par smin pa'i sgrib pa ste/ sngar gyi las kyis brgyud ngan par 'phangs pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar na sgrib pa ni rnam pa gsum du 'dod de/ 'phags pa'i lam dang dro bar gyur pa la sogs pa 'phags pa'i lam la sbyor bar byed pa'i dge ba la sgrib pa dang gegs su gyur pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na ni lam phran pa dang sor mo'i phreng ba can dang dga' bo la sogs pa ni nyon mongs pa chen po dang ldan pa'i phyir de dag la 'phags pa'i lam mi skye bar 'gyur zhe na/

(1) Karmic obscuration is the karma of the five heinous acts (ānantarya) of killing one’s mother, one’s father, or an arhat, dividing the Saṅgha, and spilling the blood of a buddha [motivated] by an evil mind. They cannot be limited or obstructed by other karma or other reincarnating beings in their potency to produce [389] birth in hells in one’s next birth. (2) Afflictive obscuration is strong affliction (tīvrakleśa). There are two types: dominant affliction and acute affliction. The first is any affliction that occurs continuously. It is posited as an afflictive obscuration since moderate affliction arises from small affliction, and great affliction arises from moderate affliction without break, and the opportunity to abandon such affliction is not found. {The second} is any affliction that arises intensely that is not included within the three afflictions because it is easier to abandon. (3) Maturational obscuration is birth in one of the three lower rebirths (durgati), as a being devoid of discernment, and in Uttarakuru because one’s past karma projects [or hurls] one into an evil rebirth. These are said to be the three types of obscuration (avaraṇa) because they obscure and hinder the ārya path and the virtuous actions that prepare for the ārya path during the stage of heat and so on. Objection: Kṣudrapanthaka, Aṅgulimālā, and Nanda did not generate the ārya path because they had great affliction.

de dag gi'ang ji srid sgrib pa de dag ma sbyangs pa de srid du lam mi skye ba yin la skye ba na ni nyon mongs pa chen po med pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yang gal te 'phags pa'i lam dang de'i sbyor lam la sgrib pas mtshams med rnams las kyi sgrib pa yin na ngan song gsum dang*/ tshangs pa chen po dang*/ 'du shes med pa'i snyoms 'jug dang*/ 'du shes med pa'i sems can dang*/ sgo nga las skye ba dang*/ drod gsher las skye ba dang*/ bud med du 'gyur ba dang*/ za ma la sogs pa dang*/ sred pa brgyad pa 'grub par 'gyur ba'i las rnams kyang las kyi sgrib par 'gyur te/ de dag tu skyes pa la 'phags pa'i lam dang sbyor ba'i dge ba mi skye ba'i phyir dang*/ 'phags pa rnams kyang de rtag tu mi skye ba'i phyir ro zhe na/ de dag kyang sgrib par ni 'gyur mod kyi {skyes gnas gnyis su skyes pa kha cig bud med la yang 'phags lam skye'o } 'on kyang 'dir mtshams med kho na las sgrib tu bstan pa ni{ rgyu lnga po} gzhi dang*/ 'bras bu dang*/ 'gro ba dang*/ skye ba dang*/ gang zag gi sgo nas gzhan la bstan par skra zhing rang gis tha snyad gdags sla ba'i phyir ro/ / de la pha ma dang dgra bcom gsod pa gsum gyi gzhi ni srog gcod pa'o/ / dge 'dun gyi dbyen gyi gzhi ni rdzun no/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku la ngan sems kyis khrag 'byin pa'i gzhi ni srog gcod pa'i sbyor ba'o/ / 'bras bu ni thams cad kyi 'bras bu ni yid du mi 'ong ba'o/ / 'gro ba ni dmyal ba'i 'gro ba thob par byed pa'o/ / skye ba ni skyes nas myong 'gyur gyi las yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gang zag ni nyon mongs pa shas chen po kun du spyod pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / kha cig na re 'bras bu ni dmyal ba dang*/ 'gro ba ni mtshams med gling gsum dag na yod ces 'byung bas mi dang*/ gang zag ni skyes pa dang bud med kho na yin la/ gzhan ni snga ma bzhin no zhes zer ro/ /

Reply: For as long as they did not purify such obscurations, for that long they did not generate the ārya path, but when the ārya path arose they did not have great affliction. Objection: If heinous acts are karmic obscurations since they obscure the ārya path and its preparatory paths, then the karmas projecting the three lower rebirths, Mahābrahma [heaven], the meditative attainment of nondiscernment, beings devoid of discernment, birth from eggs, birth from heat and moisture, becoming a female, a eunuch, and so on, and the establishment of the eighth link of craving would be karmic obscurations because those born there do not generate the ārya path or its preparatory paths, and āryas are never born there. Reply: Though regarded as obscurations, {some are born in two such birth states, and females generate the ārya path.} Here only heinous acts are taught to be karmic obscuration due to {five causes} — basis, result, journey, birth, and person — because they are easily taught to others and easily imputed by oneself. (1) The basis of the three actions of killing one’s mother, father, or arhat is taking life. The basis of dividing the Saṅgha is lying. The basis of spilling the blood of a buddha [motivated] with an evil mind is the preparation for taking life. (2) The result of all heinous acts is unpleasant. (3) The journey is obtaining a journey to hell. (4) Birth is the karma experienced after rebirth. (5) The person is one who continuously activates strong afflictions. Some say: The result is the hells; the journey [390] is that of a human, since it is said that heinous acts exist in the three [human] continents; the person is only male or female; and the remainder are as before.

sgrib pa gsum po de dag las nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa ni{ skye ba mang por gsor mi rung bas} thams cad kyi tha shal yin la/ de nas{ skye ba gnyis su sgrib pas} las kyi sgrib pa tha shal yin no{ zhes zer ro/ /} de gnyis kyis ni tshe phyi ma la'ang gsor mi rung par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / bye brag tu smra ba rnams na re snga ma snga mas phyi ma phyi ma 'dren pas snga ma snga ma nyes pa che ste/ nyon sgrib kyis las sgrib 'dren la las sgrib kyis rnam smin gyi sgrib pa ngan song la sogs par 'dren pa'i phyir ro/ / des na rnam smin gyi sgrib pa ni mthong chos kho na la sgrib la/ snga ma gnyis kyis ni skye ba gzhan du'ang sgrib pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ /

From among those three obscurations, afflictive obscuration is the most repugnant {since it cannot be healed for many lives}. The next most repugnant is karmic obscuration {since it obscures for two lives}. Through these two, one cannot be healed of obscurations even in one’s next life. Vaibhāṣikas say: The former state is a greater fault than the latter because the former induces the latter. Afflictive obscuration leads to karmic obscuration, and karmic obscuration leads to maturational obscuration, lower rebirth, and so on. Thus maturational obscuration obscures the current life alone, while the former two obscure other lives as well.
mtshams med gling gsum dag na yod/ / za ma sogs la mi 'dod do/ / phan dang ngo tsha chung ba'i phyir/ / lhag ma 'gro ba lnga dag na/ / 97

Heinous acts exist in the three continents. They are not asserted for eunuchs and so on because of having received little benefit or acting with little shame. Five reincarnating beings have the remaining obscurations. (4:97)

sgrib pa gsum po de dag las mtshams med lnga ni gling gsum dag na yod kyi sgra mi snyan dang 'gro ba gzhan dag na med de/ ngan song ba dag na pha gsod pa la sogs pa yod kyang mtshams med par mi 'gyur te/ sdig pa'i bsam pa mi brtan pa'i phyir dang gnyen po lam med pa'i phyir ro/ / lha la ni pha gsod pa la sogs pa med de/ sdig pa'i bsam pa can ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ las 'bras mngon sum du gyur pa'i phyir ro/ / sgra mi snyan la'ang med de/ de dag ni rang bzhin gyi tshul khrims dang ldan pa'i phyir dang*/ de na bstan pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / {zhes slob dpon rgyal po'i sras 'chad pa ni/ de na lus ngag gi tshul khrims med pas mi 'thad kyi/ slob dpon gang spel rang bzhin bzang ba'i phyir dang*/ cha nges pa'i phyir dang*/ de na bstan pa med pa'i phyir zhes pa ni rigs so }

From among these three obscurations, the five heinous acts exist in the three continents. They do not exist in Uttarakuru and other destinations because even though killing one’s father and so on exist in lower rebirths, they do not become heinous acts, because negative thought is not stable nor is there any path acting as an antidote there. Patricide and so on do not exist among the gods because they do not possess negative thoughts and they perceive karma and its results. Also such actions do not exist in Uttarakuru because beings there possess natural ethics and there are no [Dharma] teachings there.[1232] {Master Jinaputra explains that this is unacceptable since physical and verbal ethics do not exist there. But Master Pūrṇavardhana declares that this is logical because they are naturally good, they have definite lifespan, and there are no teachings there.[1233]}

gling gsum gyi yang za ma dang sogs pa'i sgras gzung ba ma ning dang mtshan gnyis pa la'ang mtshams med 'byung bar mi 'dod do/ / ci'i phyir zhe na/ 'grel pa las sdom pa med pa'i gtan tshigs gang yin pa de nyid kyi phyir ro zhes 'byung ste/ sdig pa dag la'ang bsam pa mi brtan pa'i phyir dang*/ gnyen po yin pa'i phyir gang la sdom pa yod pa de la sdom man yang yod pa yin na de dag la sdom pa med pa'i yang phyir ro/ / gzhan yang de dag gi pha ma de dag dbang po ma tshang bar bskyed pa dang byams pa chung bas phan pa chung ba'i phyir dang*/ rang bzhin gyis rgyud zhing tshwa sgo can ltar de dag kyang pha ma la ngo tsha khrel yod shas chung pa'i phyir yang ste/ ngo tsha shes pa dang khrel yod pa shas chen po nyams pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / phan pa dang ngo tsha chung ba de nyid kyi phyir yi dwags dang dud 'gro la'ang med par shes par bya'o/ / btsun pa na re gling gsum du skyes pa las gzhan ni blo mi gsal na pha ma la sogs pa bsad kyang mtshams med par mi 'gyur la/ gang dag blo gsal ba de dag ni dud 'gro yin yang pha la sogs pa bsad na 'gyur te rta cang shes ma la 'dod log spong ba bzhin no zhes zer ro/ / gal te dbang po ma tshang bar bskyed pas phan chung bas de lta bu'i pha ma bsad pas mtshams med par mi 'gyur na skyes pa dang bud med long ba dang 'on pas pha ma bsad kyang der mi 'gyur bar thal bar 'gyur ro zhe na/ 'dir dbang po ma tshang ba zhes bya ba ni mngon par rtogs pa skye ba'i skal ba can gyi dbang po la 'dod pa na long ba la sogs pa la mngon par rtogs pa skye ba'i skal ba can gyi dbang po yod pa'i phyir ro/ / rang nyid mi yin yang pha ma mi ma yin par gyur na de dag bsad kyang mtshams med par mi 'gyur ro/ /

Heinous acts are not asserted to occur for eunuchs and so on, referring to neuters and hermaphrodites belonging to the three continents. Question: Why? Reply: That is because they lack the stable thought required to commit evil acts. As the Autocommentary states, “That is due to the logical argument that they do not have vows.”[1234] And whoever has vows also has negative commitments because [such vows] are the antidote [to negative commitments], but [neuters and so on] do not have vows. In addition, because their parents were of little benefit to them and had little love for them after producing a child with incomplete faculties, they act with scant shame and embarrassment to their parents. Their mindstreams are naturally like a salt-encrusted field in that, for them, strong shame and embarrassment have degenerated and do not exist. It should also be understood that ghosts and animals cannot commit heinous acts because they also receive scant affection from their parents and they have little shame. A venerable (bhadanta) says: Those with mental unclarity who are not born in the three continents do not commit heinous acts even though they kill their mother or father and so on, but those with clarity of mind who commit patricide or matricide, even if they are animals, do commit a heinous act, like the ājāneya horse who abandoned sexual misconduct.[1235] [391] Objection: If those born with incomplete faculties who kill their mother or father do not commit heinous acts since their parents have been of little benefit to them, then it would follow that blind and deaf males or females, if they kill their father or mother, would not commit heinous acts. Reply: Here, if it is asserted that “incomplete faculties” refers to the faculties of fortunate beings who generate realization, then the blind and so on do possess the faculties of fortunate beings who can generate realization. [Another says:] If one is a human and one’s parents are not human and one kills them, it is not a heinous act.

las kyi sgrib pa'i lhag ma ni nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dang rnam par smin pa'i sgrib pa'o/ / de gnyis ni lha la sogs pa'i 'gro ba lnga dag na yod de/ de la rnam smin gyi sgrib pa ni lha'i nang na ni 'du shes med pa'i sems can dang*/ mi'i ni byang gi sgra mi snyan pa dang*/ ngan song gsum ni thams cad kyang rnam smin gyi sgrib pa can no/ / nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa ni 'gro ba lnga po dag la ci rigs par yod do/ /

The remaining karmic obscurations are afflictive obscurations and maturational obscurations. The five reincarnating beings such as gods have both, because when maturational obscuration exists among gods, it refers to beings devoid of discernment, when it exists among humans it refers to those of Uttarakuru, and when it exists among the three lower rebirths it refers to all, since all possess maturational obscuration. Afflictive obscuration exists in various ways for the five types of reincarnating beings.
mtshams med lnga bshad pa
The five heinous acts

bcu gcig pa mtshams med pa lnga bshad pa ni mtshams med lnga po dag las dang po gsum srog gcod dang*/ lnga pa srog gcod kyi sbyor ba yin pas bzhi ni lus kyi las dang*/ bzhi pa ni rdzun yin pas ngag gi las so/ /
Among the five heinous acts, four are physical karmas since the first three are taking life and the fifth is the preparation for taking life. The fourth is verbal karma, since it is lying.
dge 'dun dbyen ni mi 'phrod pa'i/ / rang bzhin ldan pa ma yin chos/ / nyon mongs can min lung bstan min/ / de dag dge 'dun yang dag ldan/ / 98
A schism of the Saṅgha is by nature a lack of harmony. It is a nonassociated factor neither afflicted nor declared. The Saṅgha actually possesses such a schism. (4:98)
de las gzhan dag ni rtogs par sla bas ma bshad la
Only the fourth is explained here since the others are easy to understand.

dge 'dun gyi dbyen ni dge 'dun sde gnyis{ thugs rtse} mi 'phrod pa'i rang bzhin du gyur pa ldan pa ma yin pa'i chos 'du byed rdzas su grub pa zhig yod do zhes bya ba ni bye brag tu smra ba'i yin no/ / de yang nyon mongs pa can yang min la dge bar lung bstan pa'ang min pa'i phyir ma bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa'o/ / de lta bu'i dbyen de dang ni phyogs gnyis kyi dge 'dun rnams yang dag par ldan la mtshams med pa'i las ni ma yin no/ / las de yang gang zhe na/

Vaibhāṣikas say: A schism of the saṅgha (saṅghabheda) is by nature a lack of {empathetic} harmony (asāmagrī) between two sections of the Saṅgha. It is a substantially established nonassociated formative factor. Further, it is an unobscured-neutral state because it is neither afflicted nor declared to be virtuous. The Saṅgha divided into two factions actually possesses such a schism, but it does not possess the karma of the heinous act. Question: What is that karma?
de yi kha na ma tho rdzun/ / de dang 'byed po yang dag ldan/ / bskal par mnar med par smin 'gyur/ / lhag pas gnod pa lhag par 'gyur/ / 99
The offensive karma causing it is a lie. The agent who divides actually possesses it, and it matures in Avīci for an intermediate eon. Through committing more, they experience more harm. (4:99)

dge 'dun gyi dbyen de'i rgyu kha na ma tho ba'i las ni dge 'dun 'byed par byed pa'i rdzun te/ de lta bu'i rdzun de ni mtshams med yin la/ de dang ni dge 'dun 'byed par byed pa po lhas byin la sogs pa yang dag par ldan no/ / dge 'dun gyi dbyen gyi mtshams med pa'i las de'i rnam smin gyis 'byed pa po de bar gyi bskal par mnar med pa'i dmyal bar sdug bsngal rnam par smin par 'gyur ro/ / 'o na mtshams med lhag ma rnams byas pas ji ltar zhe na/

Reply: The offensive (avadya) karma that is the cause of that Saṅgha schism is the lie dividing the Saṅgha. That lie is a heinous act, and the agent who divides the Saṅgha, such as Devadatta, actually possesses that heinous act. That heinous karma of causing a schism in the Saṅgha matures on the schismatic as suffering in the hell of Avīci for an intermediate eon. Question: What of the remaining heinous acts?

mtshams med pa gzhan dag gis ni spyir dmyal bar skye bar nges kyang mnar med kho nar skye bar ni ma nges so/ {gal te mtshams med gnyis la sogs pa byas pas dmyal bar tshe gcig kho na las mi skye na las che chung la khyad med par 'gyur la/ tshe gnyis la sogs par yang skye na ni mtshams med dang skyes nas myong 'gyur kho na ma yin par 'gyur ro zhe na } bye brag tu smra ba na re mtshams med pa gnyis dang gsum la sogs pa lhag par byas pas las kyi grangs bzhin mnar med pa der lus nyis 'gyur la sogs pas che ba dang gzhon sha can du 'gyur te/ gnod pa'i sdug bsngal yang nyis 'gyur la sogs pas lhag par myang bar 'gyur bas skyon gnyis ka las grol zhing*/ de dag kyang snga ma ni 'phen byed yin la phyi ma dag ni rdzogs byed yin no zhes zer ro/ / mdo sde pa la sogs pa ni mtshams med mang po byas pas mnar med par yang dang yang skye yang las byed pa'i lus de dang dmyal ba'i bar du skye ba gzhan gyi mtshams med pa'i phyir dang*/ de skyes nas myong 'gyur du'ang 'dod pa la bsal ba med pa'i phyir dang*/ kyi hud sems zhes bya ba'i rtogs pa brjod pa las/ mtshams med pa'i las kyi rnam par smin pa sems can dmyal bar yang dang yang du 'chi 'pho zhing skye bas rnam par smin pa myong ngo zhes 'byung ba dang*/ kun las btus kyi 'grel pa las kyang rtsom pa'i dbang du byas nas mthong ba'i chos la myong bar 'gyur ba la sogs pa 'di dag rnam par bzhag gi de tsam la myong bar 'gyur ba'i dbang du byas pa ni ma yin no zhes 'byung ba'i phyir dang*/ mdo las skyes nas myong 'gyur du gsungs pa ni dang po 'go rtsom pa'i dbang du byas nas gsungs pa'i phyir 'di la skyon du mi lta'o zhes 'dod do/ / dge 'dun de dag gang zag gang gis 'byed ce na/
