Reply: One is definitely born in hell through committing the other heinous acts, but it is not certain that birth will be in Avīci. {Objection: If by committing two, three, or more heinous acts one is not born as a hell being for multiple lives, there would be no difference in the weight of the karma projecting one life. But if one is born for two or more lives, then heinous acts would not be karma to be experienced after rebirth alone.} [392] Vaibhāṣikas say: Through committing two, three, or more heinous acts, then the body of that hell being in Avīci would be double in size and so on and highly sensitive to suffering in accordance with the number of karmas committed. That hell being would exhaust double the faults, since that hell being would experience more through suffering double the harm and so on. Also the earlier karma would be projecting karma, and the latter would be completing karma. Sautrāntikas and so on assert: Through committing many heinous acts one is born in Avīci many times over because (1) there is no other intervening birth between the body committing that karma and the hells, (2) karma to be experienced after rebirth there cannot be eliminated in the desire realm, and (3) the Story of Hācitta mentions: The karmic maturation of heinous acts is to die and be reborn in the hells over and over again.[1236] (4) Exposition of the Compendium of Abhidharma also notes: From the perspective of committing heinous acts, they are posited as karma to be experienced in the current life and not merely from the perspective of karma to be experienced.[1237] and (5) a sūtra asserts: It is experienced after rebirth.[1238] This quotation is not seen as erroneous because it is stated from the perspective of when the heinous act is first committed. Question: What person divides the Saṅgha?
dge slong lta spyad tshul ldan pas/ / 'byed do gzhan du'o byis pa rnams/
One fully ordained, erudite, and ethical divides the Saṅgha; elsewhere, childlike ordinary beings. (4:100ab)

dge slong yin pa dang*/ lta ba spyad pa dang tshul khrims dang ldan pas 'byed kyi khyim pa dang*/ sred pa spyad pa dang*/ tshul khrims 'chal pas ni ma yin te/ sangs rgyas la 'gran pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ dbang po rno ba'i phyir dang*/ de dag la dge 'dun rnams yid mi ches pa dang tshig btsan par mi 'dzin pa'i phyir ro/ / gang du zhe na/ sangs rgyas bzhugs pa'i gnas de las gzhan du yin gyi ston pa'i mngon sum du ni ma yin te/ sangs rgyas kyi gzi brjid mi bzod pa'i phyir ro/ / gang 'byed ce na byis pa so so'i skye bo'i dge 'dun rnams {kog li ka dang*/ rgya mtsho byin dang*/ khan+da dra ba bya/ ka ta me ra ka ti sh+ya la sogs pa } 'byed kyi 'phags pa rnams ni ma yin te/ chos mngon sum du gyur pas sangs rgyas la shes nas dad pa thob pa'i phyir ro/ / kha cig na re bzod pa thob pa'i so so'i skye bo rnams kyang dbye bar mi nus so zhes{ bden pa mthong ba dang 'dra bas} 'dod do/ /

Reply: A fully ordained monk who is erudite and ethical divides the Saṅgha, but householders, those steeped in craving, or those with unethical conduct do not, because ethical monks can vie with the Buddha, they have sharper faculties, and the Saṅgha does not have conviction in those with unethical conduct, whose words lack authority. Question: Where is the Saṅgha divided? Reply: Elsewhere, and not where the Buddha resides nor in the actual presence of the Master, because schismatics cannot endure the splendor of the Buddha. Question: Who is divided? Reply: The Saṅgha who are childlike ordinary beings {such as the Śākyas: Kokālika, Samudradatta, Khaṇḍadravya, Kaṭamorakatiṣya}. There are no divided āryas because they obtain faith through knowing the Buddha directly. Some say: Those ordinary beings who obtain the stage of patience cannot be divided {since they are like those who see the four truths}.
bye ba'i tshad ni
THE MEASURE OF DIVIDING THE SAṄGHA
ston dang lam gzhan la bzod pa/ / bye ba'o de ni mi gnas so/ / 100
When the Saṅgha tolerates another teacher or path, it is divided. That division does not remain. (4:100cd)

gang gi tshe sangs rgyas las ston pa gzhan dang*/ sangs rgyas kyis bcas pa'i lam las gzhan lhas byin gyis nges par 'byung bar bya ba'i phyir 'o ma mi spyad pa dang sha spang ba dang*/ lan tshwa longs mi spyod pa dang*/ gos ma dras pa bgo ba dang*/ grong gi nang gi gtsug lag khang du 'dug pa zhes bya ba'i bslab pa'i tshigs lnga bcas pa la sogs pa la bzod cing dang du len pa de'i tshe dge 'dun bye ba'o/ / dus ji srid du gnas she na/ bye ba de ni chos nyid kyis zhag gcig las ring du mi gnas so/ /

Whenever the Saṅgha tolerates and accepts a teacher other than the Buddha and a path other than that proclaimed by the Buddha, at that time the Saṅgha is divided, such as when some accepted Devadatta’s five training rules that he proclaimed for the purpose of renunciation: (1) not using milk, (2) abandoning eating meat, (3) not using salt, (4) not wearing uncut cloth, and (5) not staying in temples within cities. Question: How long does a division remain? Reply: That division naturally does not remain longer than a day. [393]
de ni 'khor lo'i dbyen du 'dod/ / 'dzam bu'i gling na'o dgu sogs kyi/ / las kyi dbyen ni gling gsum na/ / de ni brgyad dag yan chad kyis/ / 101

It is considered a disruption of the wheel, on the continent of Jambudvīpa, by nine, and so on. A disruption of the rite exists in three continents established by eight or more fully ordained. (4:101)

Any schism that is declared to be a schism of the Saṅgha is considered a disruption of the wheel (cakrabheda) of Dharma because as long as the Saṅgha remains divided and alienated, for that long the path is not generated in the mindstream of any being. {Also it divides the wheel of Dharma of the Bhagavan.} It is a heinous act, but other schisms are not heinous acts.

'khor lo'i dbyen de yang sangs rgyas bzhugs pas 'dzam bu'i gling na yod kyi gling gzhan na med do/ / gang zag ni dge slong dgu la sogs pa yan chad kyis dbyen 'grub ste/ dge 'dun ni dge slong bzhi yan{ bcom ldan 'das kyi chos kyi 'khor lo yang phye ba yin no} chad yin la/ / {sangs rgyas dang 'byed pa po'i phyogs su bzhi bzhi dang*/ dgu pa ni 'byed pa po/ } de sde gnyis dang 'byed pa po nges par dgos pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di nyung mtha' bzung ba yin gyi mang ba la nges pa med do/ /

Further, a disruption of the wheel exists on the continent of Jambudvīpa since the Buddha lived here but not on other continents. A division is established by nine or more fully ordained beings and so on because the Saṅgha is four or more fully ordained monks and two of those groups plus the schismatic are required. {Thus there are four each for the side supporting the Buddha and the side supporting the schismatic, and the ninth is the schismatic}. This constitutes the minimum number; no maximum number is specified.

las kyi dbyen ni {'dul ba'i las med pas } sgra mi snyan ma gtogs pa gling gsum na yod de bstan pa yod pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang mtshams kyi nang gcig tu gso sbyong la sogs pa'i las blo mi mthun pas byed pa'o/ / dge slong du zhig gis she na/ las kyi dbyen de ni dge slong brgyad dag yan chad kyis 'grub ste/ 'di la 'byed pa po legs pa mi dgos pa'i phyir ro/ / {gso sbyong gi dus na so so thar ba'i mdo gdon pa na/ sdig pa thams cad mi bya ste/ / dge ba phun sum tshogs par spyad/ / rang gi sems ni yongs su gdul/ / 'di ni sangs rgyas bstan pa yin/ / lus kyi sdom pa legs pa ste/ / ngag gi sdom pa legs pa yin/ / yid kyi sdom pa'ang legs pa ste/ / thams cad du yang sdom pa legs/ / kun tu bsdams pa'i dge slong ni/ / sdug bsngal kun las rab tu grol/ / ngag rnams bsrung zhing yid kyis rab bsdams te/ / lus kyis mi dge ba dag mi byed cing*/ / las lam gsum po 'di dag rab sbyangs nas/ / drang srong gsungs pa'i lam ni thob par 'gyur/ / zhes pa kho na ston pas chog go }

A disruption of the rite (karmabheda) exists in three continents because the [Dharma] teachings exist there and not in Uttarakuru, {which has no Vinaya ceremonies}. Further, it is initiated by those not content with the confession ceremony and so on in a single community. Question: How many fully ordained monks initiate it? Reply: That disruption of the rite is established by eight or more fully ordained monks because a leading schismatic is not needed here. {During the confession ceremony when the Pratimokṣa Sūtra is recited, the Master gave permission just to recite: Do not commit any misdeed, practice virtue properly, fully tame one’s mind: this is the teaching of the Buddha. It is excellent to restrain the body. It is excellent to restrain speech. It is excellent to restrain the mind. It is excellent to be restrained in all activities. A fully ordained monk who is fully restrained is fully liberated from suffering. He guards his speech and fully restrains his mind. He does not engage in physical nonvirtue, fully purifies the three karmic paths, and obtains the path described by the rishis.[1239]}
dang po mtha' skyon zung gcig gi/ / snga rol thub pa nongs pa dang / / mtshams ma bcad pa dag tu yang / / 'khor lo'o dbyen ni mi 'byung ngo/ / 102
Disruption of the wheel did not occur at the beginning, or end, before errors arose, before the pair appeared, when grieving for the Muni, or when the communities had not been delineated. (4:102)

'khor lo'i dbyen de ni/ sangs rgyas nas dang po chos kyi 'khor lo bskor nas ring po ma lon pa'i tshe ni mi 'byung ste/ thams cad dga' ba dang rab tu dga' ba skyes par blo mthun {pa dang ston pa dang mi 'bral bar 'dod } pas na sha gcig pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / sangs rgyas kyi sku tshe'i mtha' ma yongs su mya ngan las 'das pa'i tshe'ang ma yin te/ sangs rgyas la dkon par 'dzin pa dang*/ mi rtag pa yid la byed pas sems skyo ba shas che bar blo mthun pa'i phyir ro/ / {bar du yang } 'dul ba tshig le'ur byas pa las/ ston ka'i chu bzhin dri med par/ / ston pa'i bstan pa bcu gnyis lor/ / ltung ba med par legs gnas te/ / nyon mongs spong bar byed pa yin zhes 'byung bas ji srid du bstan pa la {lta ba'i skyon ni dge slong 'chi ltas kyis/ ston pas bar chad kyi chos su gsungs pa de dag ston yang bar chad du mi 'gyur ro zhes sogs so/ / tshul khrims kyi skyon ni ltung ba 'byin pa'o } lta ba dang tshul khrims kyi skyon ma byung gi bar du'ang mi 'byung ste/ bstan pa skyon med yin pa'i phyir ro/ / mchog zung gcig ma byung gi snga rol du'ang mi 'byung ste/ bye ba yun ring du mi gnas shing*/ de dag gis sdum pa yin pa la sdum byed med pa'i phyir ro/ / thub pa nongs pa na'ang mi 'byung ste/ gang la 'gran pa'i sangs rgyas mi bzhugs pa'i phyir ro/ / mtshams che ba dang chung ba ma bcad pa dag tu yang mi 'byung ste/ mtshams gcig tu dge 'dun bye ba ni dbyen yin na de med pa'i phyir ro/ / des na 'khor lo'i dbyen de ni dus drug po de dag tu mi 'byung ngo*/ / dbyen 'di yang nyan thos pa dag sngon gyi las la rag lus pa'i phyir sangs rgyas thams cad la 'byung ba ni ma yin te/ sangs rgyas shAkya thub pas ni sngon byang chub sems dpar gyur pa na drang srong mngon shes lnga dang ldan pa zhig gi 'khor phye bas de'i rnam par smin pa'i phyi ma yin no zhes 'chad de 'di ni dgongs pa'i don du theg pa gong ma bas bzhed do/ / ci'i phyir pha ma bsad pa la sogs pa kho na mtshams med du 'gyur gyi gzhan bsad pa la sogs pas ma yin zhe na/

Disruption of the wheel did not occur at six times: (1) at the beginning in the period soon after the Buddha turned the wheel of Dharma, because all disciples formed a single harmonious community that was happy and joyous {and desired not to be separated from the Master}. (2) Also it did not occur at the time of parinirvāṇa at the end of the Buddha’s life, because they apprehended the rarity of the presence of the Buddha and they were unanimous in their intense grief that arose through focusing on impermanence. {Also, regarding the intermediate period} the Vinaya Verses records: Like an autumn lake, the teaching of the Master remained stainless for twelve years without downfall since afflictions were abandoned.[1240] It did not occur (3) before the errors of view and ethics arose because there were no errors in the teachings. {The fault of view is demonstrated by the Master when he stated that for monks to divine omens is a great obstacle, that they should not create such obstacles, and so on. The fault of ethics is committing downfalls.} (4) It did not occur before the supreme pair [Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana] appeared because division did not remain long then, and there was no need to reconcile those who were already in harmony. [394] (5) Also it did not occur even when grieving for the Sage because at that time the Buddha did not exist for any rival to contend with.[1241] (6) It did not occur also when the great or small communities had not yet been delineated because if a schism is dividing the Saṅgha that exists as a single community, then that did not exist at that time. Mahāyānists assert that the essential point is that schisms rely on karma accumulated while a śrāvaka, and not all buddhas are subject to them. Buddha Śākyamuni, however, when he was a bodhisattva, divided the retinue of a rishi who possessed the five higher perceptions, and the karmic maturation of that act was the schism in his dispensation. Question: Why do killing one’s mother or father and so on become heinous acts while killing others and so forth do not?
phan 'dogs pa dang yon tan zhing / / spangs dang med par byas phyir ro/ / mtshan ni gzhan du gyur kyang 'gyur/ / gang gi zla mtshan las byung ma/ / 103
It is because one rejects and destroys fields of benefit and qualities. Though their sex has changed, it is that. Any who produces it from her own blood is the mother. (4:103)

pha ma bsad pa ni mtshams med yin te/ de dag gis rang gi lus thar pa dang mthun par bskyed pas phan 'dogs par byed pa'i zhing khyad par can yin la de bsam pas spangs pa dang sbyor bas med par byas pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du dgra bcom pa dang*/ {dge 'dun dang } sangs rgyas yon tan gyi zhing yin la/ de dag bsam pas spangs shing{ sbyor bas srog gnas pa dang mthun pa med par byas pa'i phyir dang*/ de bzhin gshegs pa bkrong par mi nus kyang bsam pas spangs pa'i phyir ro} dgra bcom pa bsad pa dang de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku la ngan sems kyis khrag phyung ba dang 'khor lo'i dbyen yang mtshams med yin no/ / las gzhan dag la de lta bu'i nyes pa che ba med pa'i phyir mtshams med du mi 'gyur ro/ / gal te pha ma mtshan gyur pa bsad na pha ma bsad pa'i mtshams med du 'gyur ram mi 'gyur zhe na/

Reply: Killing one’s mother or father is a heinous act because they are superior fields of benefit (upakārikṣetra), comparable to the state of liberation, since they produce our body, yet in thought one rejects (nirākṛti) them and in actual deed one destroys (vipādana) them. Similarly, arhats, {the Saṅgha,} and the Buddha are fields of qualities (guṇakṣetra), and thinking to reject them, to kill an arhat, to spill the blood of a tathāgata [motivated] by an evil mind, and to divide the wheel of Dharma are heinous acts {because one prepares to destroy the continuity of their life force, and thinks to reject a tathāgata though one cannot kill him}. Other karmas are not heinous acts because they do not possess such great fault. Question: If one kills one’s mother or father whose sex has changed, would it be a heinous act or not?

pha ma gnyis kyi mtshan ni gzhan du gyur te bud med dang skyes par gyur pa bsad kyang pha ma gsod pa'i mtshams med du 'gyur te/ rang gi lus khyad par can skyed pa'i pha ma'i bya ba byas pa de bsad pa'i phyir ro/ / de nyid kyi phyir pha yang ma yin dgra bcom pa yang ma yin pa'i skyes pa zhig bsad na mtshams med pa'i kha na ma tho bas reg par 'gyur ba yod dam zhe na yod de/ ma mtshan gyur pa bsad na mtshams med pa'i kha na ma tho bas reg par 'gyur ro zhes bya ba dang*/ de bzhin du ma yang ma yin dgra bcom ma yang ma yin pa'i bud med cig bsad na mtshams med pa'i kha na ma tho bas reg par 'gyur ba yod dam zhe na/ yod de/ pha mtshan gyur pa bsad na mtshams med pa'i kha na ma tho bas reg par 'gyur ro/ / zhes bstan bcos las bshad do/ / de bzhin du las gdags pa las spun drung gis spun drung btang ste/ song la ma gsod cig /bdag nyid kyis gsod la gzhan gsod du ma gzhug ces byas na/ de ci gnyis ka mtshams med pa'i las dang ldan par 'gyur ram/ 'on te gcig ldan par 'gyur zhe na/ smras pa/ gal te bdag nyid kyis bsad na ni gnyis ka mtshams med pa'i las dang ldan par 'gyur ro/ / de ste gzhan gsod du bcug ste bdag nyid kyis ma bsad na ni phyi ma shos mtshams med pa'i las dang ldan par 'gyur gyi snga ma shas ni ma yin no/ / de ste bdag nyid dang gzhan gnyis kas bsad na yang phyi ma kho na mtshams med kyi las dang ldan gyi snga ma shos ni ma yin no/ / spun drung gis spun drung btang ste song la ma gsod cig gzhan gsod du chug la bdag nyid kyis ma bsad cig ces byas na/ de ci gnyis ka mtshams med pa'i las dang ldan par 'gyur ram/ 'on te gcig ldan par 'gyur zhe na/

Reply: Killing one’s father or mother though their sex has changed to female or male is a heinous act of killing one’s parent, because one kills a parent who has produced this specific body. Objection: Therefore if one kills a male who is not one’s father or an arhat, would one commit a heinous transgression? Reply: Yes, because it is said that if one kills one’s mother who has changed sex, one commits a heinous offense. Question: Similarly, if one kills a female who is not one’s mother or an arhat, would one commit a heinous transgression? Reply: Yes, because it is said that one who kills one’s father who has changed sex commits a heinous offense.[1242] This is explained [in the Great Treatise on Differentiation].[1243] So too, the Presentation on Karma declares: Question: If one brother dispatches another brother saying, “Go and kill our mother, kill her yourself, don’t make another kill her,” would both brothers come to possess the [395] heinous karma or would just one possess it? Reply: If the latter brother killed his mother himself, both brothers would come to possess the heinous karma. But if the latter brother makes another kill his mother and he does not kill her himself, then the latter brother comes to possess the heinous karma and the former brother does not. If both the latter brother and another kill the mother, then the latter brother alone would come to possess a heinous karma, and the former brother would not. Question: If one brother dispatches another brother saying, “Go and kill our mother, but make another kill her and do not kill her yourself,” would both brothers come to possess the heinous karma or, otherwise, would just one possess it?

smras pa/ gal te gzhan gsod du bcug ste/ bdag nyid kyis ma bsad na ni gnyis ka mtshams med pa'i las dang ldan par 'gyur ro/ / de ste bdag nyid kho nas bsad kyi gzhan gsod du ma bcug na ni phyi ma shos kho na mtshams med kyi las dang ldan par 'gyur ro/ / gal te bdag dang gzhan gnyis kas bsad na yang phyi ma shos kho na mtshams med kyi las dang ldan par 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du spun drung gis spun drung btang ste/ song la ma gsod cig /bdag dang gzhan gnyis kas gsod cig ces byas na/ gal te bdag dang gzhan gnyis kas bsad na ni gnyis ka mtshams med pa'i las dang ldan par 'gyur la/ 'on te bdag dang gzhan gang rung re res bsad na ni phyi ma shos kho na mtshams med pa'i las dang ldan par 'gyur gyi snga ma shos ni ma yin no/ / de bzhin du mtshon cha dang me dang dug dang dbyug pas bsnun pa la sogs pa thabs rnam pa sna tshogs kyis bsad pa'ang de dang 'dra bar brjod par bya'o/ / de bzhin du ming pos sring mo la bsgo ba dang*/ sring mos ming po la bsgo ba dang*/ phu mo dang nu mo gnyis kyis phan tshun bsgo ba'ang de dang 'dra'o/ / ma ji lta ba bzhin du pha'ang de dang 'dra'o/ / mar 'du shes pas ma bsad par bya'o snyam ste/ nye du ma yin pa'i bud med bsad na de ci mtshams med pa'i las dang ldan par 'gyur ram/ 'on te mi 'gyur zhe na/ smras pa/ ldan par ni mi 'gyur ro/ / nye du ma yin pa'i bud med du 'du shes pas nye du ma yin pa'i bud med bsad par bya'o snyam pa las ma bsad par gyur na/ de ci mtshams med kyi las dang ldan par 'gyur ram mi 'gyur zhe na/ smras pa/ gal te dgra bcom ma bsad na ni de dang ldan par 'gyur ro/ / dgra bcom ma ma yin na ni mi 'gyur ro/ / pha dang mar 'du shes pas de gnyis bsad na ni mtshams med pa'i las dang ldan par 'gyur ro zhes gsungs so/ / gal te bud med gzhan gyi nur nur po gzhan gyi mngal du blugs nas gzhan de'i mngal du bskyed na bud med gnyis po de dag gang bsad na mtshams med du 'gyur zhe na/

Reply: If the latter brother makes another kill her and he does not kill her himself, both brothers come to possess the heinous karma. If the latter brother himself alone kills his mother and another is not made to kill her, then the latter brother alone would come to possess the heinous karma. If both the latter brother himself and another both kill the mother, then the latter brother alone comes to possess the heinous karma. Similarly, if one brother dispatches another brother saying, “Go and kill our mother, and kill her together with another,” then if both the latter brother and another kill the mother, both brothers would come to possess the heinous karma. But if either the latter brother himself or the other person were to kill the mother individually, then only the latter brother would come to possess the heinous karma, and the former brother would not. So too, if the mother is killed with various weapons such as fire, poison, or beaten by a club and so on, it is similar. So too, if a brother orders a sister, or a sister orders a brother, or if an older sister orders a younger sister, it is similar. And whatever is true for the mother, it is similar for the father. Question: If a person thinks “I will kill my mother” but kills an unrelated female thinking her to be his mother, does he come to possess a heinous act or not? Reply: He does not come to possess a heinous act. Question: If a person thinks “I will kill an unrelated female” but kills his mother thinking she is an unrelated female, does he come to possess a heinous act or not? Reply: If he kills a female arhat he comes to possess a heinous act, but if she is not an arhat he does not. If he mistakes his father for his mother and kills both, he comes to possess a heinous act.[1244] Question: If a kalala embryo of one female is placed in another’s womb and is born from that womb,[1245] killing which of these women would constitute a heinous act for that child?

gnyis po de las bud med dang po gang gi zla mtshan las byung ba de nyid bu de'i ma yin pas bud med dang po de bsad na 'gyur te/ lus skyed pa'i gtso bo yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gnyis pa mngal du 'dzin pa de ni mi ma yin te/ de tsam du gtso bo ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang nu zho glud pa dang gso zhing skyed pa'i phyir ma dang 'dra bas ma la zhu ba'i bya ba rnams zhu bar bya dgos so/ / pha ma la sbyor ba byas nas gzhan bsad pa dang*/ gzhan la sbyor ba byas nas pha ma bsad pa la ni mtshams med du mi 'gyur te/ mtshams med ni sbyor ba gang la byas pa de nyid la dngos po rdzogs pa dgos pa las de med pa'i phyir te/ dper na ma khri'u'i 'og na 'dug pa bsad pa dang*/ khrus pa'i bus sbrang bu bsad par 'dod pas tho bas pha'i klad pa bcom pa bzhin no/ /

Reply: Since any female who produces that fetus from her own blood is the mother of that child, such as the first of those two females, then if that child killed [396] the first woman it would be a heinous act because she is the main generator of that child’s body. The second woman who sustains the fetus in her womb is not the mother because she is not the main producer of the child’s body. However, she is like the child’s mother because she suckles, nurtures, and raises the child. Those who are called the mother since they are like the mother should be called the mother. One who prepares to kill his mother or father but kills another, or prepares to kill another but kills his father or mother, does not commit a heinous act because for a heinous act, the object that one prepares to kill must be the same object when completing the actual basis, and that is not the case here. For example, it is like one who killed his mother thinking he was killing a man lying under his mother’s bed, or the son of the laundryman who shattered the brain of his father with a hammer though desiring to kill a fly.

mtshon thabs gcig gis ma dang sems can gzhan zhig kyang bsad na rig byed ma yin pa ni mtshams med kyi dang srog gcod 'ba' zhig pa'i dang gnyis yin la rig byed ni mtshams med kyis bsdus pa kho na'i yin te/ mtshams med kyi las de nyid stobs che ba'i phyir ro/ / btsun pa dbyangs sgrogs na re rig byed ni rdul phra rab bsags pa yin pas rdul la la mtshams med kyi rig byed yin la/ rdul la la ni srog gcod 'ba' zhig pa'i yin pas rig byed kyang gnyis yin no zhes zer ro/ / dgra bcom pa ma yin pa'i 'du shes kyis dgra bcom pa bsad na ni mtshams med du 'gyur te/ 'di bsad do snyam du rten nges par bzung pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te pha'ang yin la dgra bcom pa'ang yin pa'am/ ma'ang yin la dgra bcom ma'ang yin pa bsad na ni dgra bcom pa gsod pa'i mtshams med pa gcig yin te/ rten gcig las med pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na lung rnam 'byed las/ sngon grong khyer sgra sgrogs kyi rgyal po u tra ya na pha'ang yin dgra bcom pa'ang yin pa rang gi bu rgyal bu skra can gyis bsad pa na/ song la skra can la khyod kyis mtshams med pa gnyis byas te/ pha bsad pa gang yin pa dang*/ gang yang dgra bcom pa bsad pa'o/ / zhes smros shig ces phas bsrings pa de ji lta bu zhe na/ de ni khyod kyis mtshams med pa'i rgyu gnyis kyis mtshams med pa byas te zhes bya ba'am/ yang na sgo gnyis nas spyos pa yin gyi mtshams med ni gcig las med do/ /

If one kills one’s mother and another sentient being with one stroke of a weapon, the nonindicative form of the act is both the heinous act [of killing one’s mother] and the act of taking life alone, but the indicative form of the act is subsumed by the heinous act alone because the heinous act is more potent. Bhadanta Ghoṣaka says: Since the indicative form of the act is the accumulation of subtle particles, the individual particles are heinous indicative form. Since individual particles are also the act of taking life alone, the indicative form of the act is both. If one kills an arhat while thinking he is not an arhat, it is a heinous act because one certainly holds that basis while reflecting, “I have killed him.” If one kills one who is both one’s father and an arhat, or who is one’s mother and a female arhat, it is the single heinous act of killing an arhat because there is only one basis. Question: But what of the message sent by the father in Vinaya Divisions, which states: Formerly, when Prince Keśin dispatched someone to kill King Udayana of the city of Rāvaṇa, who was both an arhat and his father, the king said to him [before dying]: “Go to him and tell Keśin that he has committed two heinous acts, killing his father and killing an arhat.”[1246] Reply: It is either that the father is saying, “You have committed one heinous act through engaging two causes of a heinous act” or again the preparation is through two doors but it is just one heinous act.
sangs rgyas brdeg par sems la min/ / bsnun 'og sgra bcom pa la min/ / mtshams med sbyor ba byas pa la/ / 'dod chags bral 'bras mi srid do/ / 104

Intentionally striking a buddha is not. If one beats another who then becomes an arhat, it is not. If one prepares to commit a heinous act, it is impossible to obtain the result of separation from attachment. (4:104)

de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku la ngan sems kyis khrag 'byin pa'ang sangs rgyas bkrongs par 'dod nas mtshon bsnun na 'gyur gyi sangs rgyas la mtshon brdeg par sems pas bsnun pa la ni mtshams med du 'gyur ba min te/ srog gcod pa'i bsam pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du dgra bcom ma thob pa la mtshon bsnun la mtshon bsnun pa'i 'og tu dgra bcom thob par gyur na bsnun pa des dgra bcom grongs pa la'ang mtshams med par 'gyur ba min te/ des de la sbyor ba ma byas pa'i phyir ro/ / yang ci mtshams med kyi sbyor ba byas nas de ma spangs par 'dod chags dang bral ba'i 'bras bu 'thob par 'gyur ram zhe na/

It is a heinous act if one spills the blood of a tathāgata with evil intent or beats a buddha with a weapon with the desire to kill him, but intentionally beating and striking a buddha with a weapon is not a heinous act because there is no intention to take life. Similarly, if one person beats another who has not obtained the state of an arhat and who then obtains the state of an arhat after being beaten and dies due to that beating, then the first person does not commit a heinous act because he did not commit the preparatory act in relation to an arhat. Question: What if a person prepares to commit a heinous act, and without abandoning that preparation he obtains the result of separation from attachment?

mtshams med pa'i sbyor ba byas pa la ni bsam pa shin tu 'gal bas 'dod chags dang bral ba dang 'bras bu thob pa mi srid do/ / mtshams med ma gtogs pa'i las kyi lam gzhan gyi sbyor ba byas pa la ni 'phags pa'i lam skye zhing 'phags lam skyes pa ni sbyor ba byas pa de'i las kyi lam mi skye ste/ 'phags lam skyes pa'i rten de dang las kyi lam de dag shin tu 'gal ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir mtshams med dngos byas na lta ci smros pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dir 'dod chags dang bral ba'i 'bras bu ni dge sbyong gi tshul gyi 'bras bu phyi ma gnyis so/ / mtshams med pa las gzhan pa'i las dag ni 'dod chags dang bral ba dang 'bras bu la gegs su 'gyur ba ma yin par ni rtsen ma'i rtogs pa brjod pa las/ shAkya rtsen ma zhes bya ba bu dang bcas pa rngon pas/ 'tsho ba yang bcom ldan 'das kyis rgyun zhugs kyi 'bras bu la bkod par gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di yang theg pa thun mong ba'i dbang du byas kyi theg chen pa ltar na ni mtshams med byas pas kyang 'bras bu 'thob ste/ ma skyes dgra'i 'gyod pa bsal ba'i mdo las ma bsad pa'i mtshams med byas pas kyang dgra bcom thob par gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na mtshams med de dag las gang lci zhe na/

Reply: If he prepares to commit a heinous act, it is impossible that he obtains the result of separation from attachment since his motivation contradicts [this outcome]. If he prepares to commit other karmic paths that are not heinous acts, the ārya path may be generated. But having generated the ārya path, he will not generate the karmic path that he prepared to commit, because the basis for generating the ārya path, and that karmic path, are completely contradictory. Therefore it goes without saying that this is also the case if he commits the actual basis of a heinous act. Here the result of separation from attachment constitutes the latter two results of the system of training in virtue. Karmas other than heinous acts are not impediments to attaining the result of separation from attachment, as when it says in the Story of Keli: A Śākya prostitute with her son who survived by hunting were told by the Bhagavan to train to achieve the result of stream enterer. This is from the shared perspective of [both] vehicles, but in accordance with the Mahāyāna, the result of separation is obtained even if one has commited a heinous act, for as it says in the Removing the Regret of Ajātaśatru Sūtra: Though one has committed the heinous act of killing one’s mother, the state of arhat is obtained.[1247] Question: Now, from those heinous acts, what is heaviest?
dge 'dun dbye phyir rdzun smra ba/ / kha na ma tho rab cher 'dod/ / 'jig rten pa yi dge ba la/ / srid rtse'i sems pa 'bras rab che// 105
Lying is considered the greatest offense because it divides the Saṅgha. From among mundane virtues, the intention to attain the summit of existence has the greatest result. (4:105)

dge 'dun gnyis su dbye bar bya ba'i phyir rdzun smra ba de ni mtshams med pa rnams kyi nang na kha na ma tho ba rab tu che bar 'dod de/ de bzhin gshegs pa rnams kyi chos kyi sku la bsnun pa'i phyir dang dge 'dun bye ba slar ma dum gyi bar du 'jig rten{ rnams kyi mtho ris dang} nges pa la 'jug pa dang*/ 'bras bu 'thob pa dang*/ 'dod chags dang 'bral ba dang*/ zag pa zad par bya ba rnams la gegs su 'gyur zhing*/ bsam gtan dang klog pa dang kha ton dang sems pa'i las rnams kyang mi 'jug pas mtho ris dang byang grol gyi bar du gcod pa'i phyir dang*/ lha dang bcas pa'i 'jig rten 'khrugs shing yid mi bde ba dang rang dbang med pa dang dran pa nyams par byas pa'i phyir dang*/ rnam smin par bskal gcig tu mnar med du skye ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i rjes la {lnga pa dang de'i rjes la gsum pa dang*/ de'i rjes la dang po dang*/ de nas gnyis pa lci bas } de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku la ngan sems kyis khrag 'byin pa lci'o/ / de'i rjes la dgra bcom pa gsod pa lci'o/ / de'i rjes la ma gsod pa lci'o/ / lnga po de'i nang nas pha gsod pa yang bar bshad do/ / 'o na mdo las/ nyes pa gsum gyi nang na yid kyi las gsum lci ba dang*/ de'i nang nas log lta lci bar bshad pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/ de ni 'di ltar yin te/ mnar med du bar bskal du smin pas 'bras bu rnam smin rgya che ba'i dbang du mdzad nas mtshams med pa'i nang nas dge 'dun dbyen lci ba dang*/ drang srong gi yid khros pas dan ta ka'i dgon pa la sogs pa'i skye bo mang po 'chi ba'i rgyu yin pas skye bo phal po che 'chi ba'i dbang du mdzad nas sgo gsum gyi las gsum las yid kyi las lci ba dang*/ {skyes bu byed 'bras } dge rtsa kun du gcod pa'i dbang du mdzad nas gzhan gyis mi gcod pas yid kyi las kyi nang nas log lta ci ba'am/ {yang na mtshams med lnga dang sgo gsum gyi las dang } lta ba lnga gzhir byas nas{ rim pa ltar dge 'dun gyi dbyen dang yid kyi las dang} log lta ci bar gsungs pa'i phyir 'gal ba med do/ / las dge ba rnams kyi 'bras bu gang che zhe na/

Reply: Lying is considered the greatest offense among heinous acts because it divides the Saṅgha; it harms the Dharma body of the Tathāgata; until the divided Saṅgha is again united, beings are hindered from entering {higher rebirth}, definite liberation, obtainment of the result, separation from attachment, and exhausting the contaminants; they are obstructed from higher rebirth and liberation since they don’t enter absorption, reading, reciting, and karma of intention; and they are born in Avīci for an eon as karmic maturation. After that, spilling the blood of a tathāgata motivated by an evil mind is the next heaviest. After that, killing an arhat is heaviest. After that, killing one’s mother. After that, killing one’s father is explained from the five. Question: Now, this would contradict a sūtra that asserts: From among the three faults, mental karma is heaviest. From among those, wrong view is heaviest.[1248] Reply: That is so, but there is no contradiction because from the perspective of the greater karmic maturation, causing a schism in the Saṅgha is heaviest from among the five [398] heinous acts, since it matures as an intermediate eon in Avīci. From the perspective of the greater number of deaths, mental karma is heaviest from among the three karmas of the three doors, since the wrath of the rishis was the cause of the death of many beings in Dantaka Monastery and so on.[1249] From the perspective of severing all roots of virtue {that are results of conscious effort}, wrong view is heaviest from among the mental karmas, since other karmas cannot sever the root of virtue. Thus, in taking {the five heinous acts, the karmas of the three doors, and} the five views as the basis, {respectively, Saṅgha schism, mental karma, and} wrong view are stated to be the heaviest actions. Question: What result of virtue is greatest?

'jig rten pa'i dge ba la ni srid pa'i rtse mo'i sems pa dge ba 'bras bu rab tu che bar 'dod de/ de'i rnam smin bskal pa chen po brgyad khrir sdug bsngal thams cad nye bar zhi ba 'thob pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang zag bcas dge ba'i rnam smin gyi 'bras bu'i dbang du byas nas de skad bshad kyi bral 'bras kyi dbang du byas na ni 'jig rten las 'das pa la ni rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin bral ba'i 'bras bu che ste/ khams gsum gyi nyon mongs pa spangs pa 'thob pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: From among mundane virtues, the virtuous intention to attain the summit of existence is asserted to have the greatest result because its karmic maturation is to obtain thorough pacification of all suffering for 80,000 great eons. Again, that is said from the perspective of the result of the karmic maturation of contaminated virtue. From the perspective of the result of separation, the transcendent vajra-like concentration that is the result of separation is the greatest, because it is the obtainment of abandonment of all affliction of the three realms.
de de dang nye ba lnga bshad pa/
The five near-heinous acts

bcu gnyis pa mtshams med dang nye ba lnga ni ci mtshams med pa rnams kho nas dmyal ba dag tu gdon mi za bar skye bar 'gyur ram/ 'on te gzhan dag gis kyang skye bar 'gyur zhe na/ mtshams med pa dang cha 'dra ba rnams kyis kyang gdon mi za bar skye bar 'gyur ro/ / de dag kyang gang zhe na/

Question: Is one definitely only born in hell through committing a heinous act, or is one also born there through other karmas? Reply: One is without doubt born in hell also through karma similar to heinous acts. Question: What are they?
ma dgra bcom ma sun byas dang / / byang chub sems dpa' nges gnas dang / / slob pa gsod dang dge 'dun gyi/ / 'du ba'i sgo ni 'phrog pa dag/ / 106
They are defiling one’s mother or a female arhat, killing one definitely abiding as a bodhisattva, or a learner ārya, taking away the Saṅgha’s means of assembling. (4:106)

ma yang yin la dgra bcom ma yang yin pa zhig 'dod log gis sun phyung bar byas pa dang*/ byang chub sems dpa' nges pa la gnas pa bsad pa dang*/ 'phags pa slob pa'i gang zag bdun po gang yang rung ba gsod pa dang*/ dge 'dun gyi zhal gyi 'du ba'i sgo 'phrog pa ste bzhi po

Reply: They are the four actions: (1) defiling (dūṣaṇa) one’s mother or a female arhat through sexual misconduct, (2) killing one definitely abiding as a bodhisattva, (3) killing any of the seven learner ārya beings, and (4) taking away the Saṅgha’s means of assembling.
mtshams med pa dang cha 'dra ste/ / lnga pa mchod rten 'jig pa yin/ / bzod dang phyir mi 'ong dgra bcom/ / 'thob la las gegs shin tu byed/ / 107
They are similar to heinous acts. The fifth is destroying a stūpa. Obtaining patience, nonreturn, and arhat, absolutely obstruct karma. (4:107)

['di] dag ni rim pa ltar ma dang pha dang dgra bcom pa gsod pa dang dge 'dun gyi dbyen byed pa'i mtshams med pa rnams dang nyes pa cha 'dra zhing mtshungs pas de rnams dang nye bar zhes bya ste/ 'di rnams kyis kyang dmyal ba kho nar skye ba'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du de bzhin gshegs pa la ngan sems kyis khrag 'byin pa dang nye ba ni lnga pa zhe sdang la sogs pas kun nas bslangs nas mchod rten sku gsung thugs kyi rten 'jig par byed pa yin no/ / de la dge 'dun gyi 'du ba'i sgo 'phrog pa ni slob dpon dbyig bshes nar mar 'du ba 'phrog pa la 'dod la/ rgyal po'i sras dang gang spel ni gang gi dge 'dun 'tsho bar byed pa zhal du gsol ba gang yin pa de 'phrog pa la 'dod do/ / dran pa nyer gzhag las ni/ dkon mchog gsum la ni chung ngu zhig blangs na'ang chen por 'gyur te/ de dag la ris mthun pa slar phul na sangs rgyas dang chos kyi ni dag par 'gyur la/ dge 'dun gyi ni tshor ba ma myong bar dag par mi 'gyur te zhing lci ba'i phyir ro/ / gal te dge 'dun gyi zhal du 'du ba'i sgo zhig na ni dmyal ba chen por ltung la/ zhal du 'du ba ma yin na ni mnar med pa'i 'khor mun nag chen po la sogs par skye'o zhes gsungs so/ / des na cha 'dra ba dang nye ba ni rnam grangs yin no/ / kha cig 'di dag byas na yang dmyal ba kho nar rnam par smin par 'gyur mod kyi 'on kyang mtshams med dang khyad par med par 'gyur ba'i phyir bar med par kho nar ni ma yin no zhes 'chad la/ kha cig ni bar med par skye yang dus dang rnam smin che chung mi 'dra bas mtshams med dang khyad par yod pas na mtshams med pa dang cha 'dra bar 'dod do/ / gzhan yang gegs byed pa'i rnam smin dang bcas pa'i las gsum bshad de/

These are respectively similar to the heinous acts of killing one’s (1) mother, (2) father, and (3) an arhat and causing a schism of the Saṅgha. Since they are similar to heinous acts, generating birth in hell alone, they are called “near-heinous acts.” Similarly, the fifth is motivated by aversion, destroying a stūpa that is the basis of the buddha’s body, speech, and mind and so on, since it is analogous to spilling the blood of a tathāgata motivated by an evil mind. Master Vasumitra asserts that taking away the Saṅgha’s means of assembling is relentlessly appropriating the wealth of the Saṅgha. Jinaputra and Pūrṇavardhana assert that “taking away” means consuming the Saṅgha’s livelihood [or resources]. The Foundations of Mindfulness Sūtra declares: Taking even a small object belonging to the Three Jewels becomes a great infraction, [399] but it is purified in relation to the Buddha and Dharma if one again offers something of similar type to them. It is not purified in relation to the Saṅgha without experiencing the feeling [that is the outcome of that act] because it is a heavier field. If one destroys that which sustains the Saṅgha, one falls into the great hells. If it is not something that sustains the Saṅgha, one is born in the great darkness surrounding Avīci.[1250] Therefore “similar” or “near” are equivalent terms. Some say: If such near-heinous acts are committed, then indeed they mature in hell alone, but they do not necessarily generate birth in hell immediately without delay, because otherwise there would be no difference between them and heinous acts. Some say: Though one is born without delay in hell, they are different from heinous acts since the size of karmic maturation is different. Still, they are similar to heinous acts. Again, three states that obstruct karmic maturation are explained.

dper na yul 'dor bar byed pa na bu lon pa ldang ba ltar sbyor lam bzod pa 'thob pa dang 'phags pa phyir mi 'ong 'thob pa dang*/ dgra bcom 'thob pa rnam pa gsum la ni rim pa ltar ngan song {du nges par skye 'gyur gyi las } dang*/ mthong chos la myong ba ma gtogs pa 'dod pa dang khams gong du nges par skye ba'i las rnam pa gsum gegs shin tu byed de/ rim pa ltar bzod thob ngan song mi 'gro'i zhes 'byung bas bzod pa thob nas ngan 'gror mi skye ba'i phyir dang*/ phyir mi 'ong thob nas 'dod par mi skye ba'i phyir dang*/ dgra bcom thob nas khams gsum du mi skye ba'i phyir ro/ /

Just like a debtor who is freed from debt when he obtains the means to discard it, so too there are three types of obtainment — (1) obtaining the stage of patience (kṣānti) on the path of preparation, (2) obtaining ārya nonreturn, and (3) obtaining that state of an arhat — that respectively absolutely obstruct (vighna) three types of karma: (1) karma {giving rise to definite birth} in lower realms, (2) karma giving rise to definite birth in the desire realm, except for experience in the current life, and (3) karma giving rise to definite birth in higher realms such as the form realm. That is because, respectively, (1) in obtaining the stage of patience, one is no longer born in the lower rebirths, since it is said, “Those who obtain patience do not proceed to lower rebirths” (6:23b); (2) in obtaining nonreturn, one is no longer born in the desire realm; and (3) in obtaining the state of an arhat, one is no longer born in the three realms.
gang nas byang chub sems dpa' yin/ / gang nas mtshan gyi las byed pa/ / bde 'gro rigs mthor skye dbang tshang / / phor 'gyur tshe rabs dran mi ldog/ / 108
When is one a bodhisattva? When one accumulates karma for the marks, born in blissful rebirths, in high caste, with complete faculties, a male, remembering past lives, irreversibly. (4:108)
byang sems nges gnas bshad pa/

gal te byang chub sems dpa' nges pa la gnas pa bsad na pha gsod pa dang nye ba zhes gang bshad pas sa mtshams gang nas byang chub sems dpa' nges pa la gnas pa yin zhe na/ gang nas bzung ste mtshan sum cu rtsa gnyis rnam par smin pa can gyi las gsog par byed pa de nas nges par gnas pa'i byang chub sems dpa' ste bskal pa brgya na sangs rgyas 'thob par nges pa zhes bya ba'i don te/ de yang ji lta bu zhe na/

Question: Since it is said that killing one who definitely attains the state of a bodhisattva is near to killing one’s father, when does one definitely attain the state of a bodhisattva? Reply: When one begins to accumulate karma that will mature as the thirty-two marks of a buddha, then from that stage one definitely attains the state of a bodhisattva, and it is said one will certainly obtain buddhahood in one hundred eons. Question: How?

byang chub sems dpa' de ni de phan chad bde 'gror skye ba dang de'i nang nas kyang rgyal rigs shing sA la chen po lta bu la sogs pa rigs mtho bar skye ba dang mig la sogs pa'i dbang po tshang ba dang phor 'gyur ba dang skye ba thams cad du tshe rabs dran pa dang*/ bskal pa brgya las phyir mi ldog par sangs rgyas 'thob par 'gyur ba zhes bya ba'i khyad par drug dang ldan pa'o/ /

Reply: Through that bodhisattva possessing six attributes: (1) henceforth being born in blissful rebirths, (2) being born in high caste such as the kṣatriya caste and in great illustrious families (mahāśālakula) and so on, (3) possessing complete faculties such as the eyes, (4) becoming a male, (5) remembering all one’s lives, and (6) irreversibly (anivṛt) obtaining buddhahood after one hundred eons.
de ni 'dzam gling pho gyur nyid/ / mngon sum sangs rgyas la sems pa/ / bsams pa las byung bskal pa brgya/ / lus pa dag tu 'phen par byed/ / 109
That is accumulated in Jambudvīpa, as a male, in his presence, as intention focusing on the Buddha, derived from contemplation, and projects the marks in the remaining one hundred eons. (4:109)

des yon tan de lta bu 'thob pa'i rgyu ni bdag nyid chen po rnams thugs rje chen po'i gzhan dbang du gyur par sems can gyi don du sdug bsngal dang log sgrub thams cad kyis mi skyo bar sems can thams cad la nga rgyal med par gzhan don lhur byed pa'i phyir ro/ /

The cause of obtaining such qualities is due to great beings who come under the control of great compassion, who are not saddened by any suffering or any misdeeds of students, and who are devoted to the purposes of others without generating pride in relation to any being.

mtshan rnam par smin pa can gyi las su bshad pa gang yin pa de ni blo rno ba'i phyir 'dzam bu'i gling gi skyes pa pho'i dbang po ldan par gyur pa nyid kyis gsog par byed kyi 'gro ba gzhan dang gling gzhan dang gang zag gzhan gyis ni ma yin no zhes bya ba ni las gsog pa'i khyad par yin no/ / de yang ston pa mngon sum du bzhugs pa la gsog par byed do zhes bya ba ni yul gyi khyad par yin no/ / sangs rgyas la dmigs pa'i sems pa dge ba yin gyi mtho ris dang thar pa gzhan la dmigs pa ni ma yin no zhes bya ba dang*/ de yang bsam pa las byung ba'i dge ba yin gyi thos pa las byung ba ni ma yin te dman pa'i phyir ro/ / bsgoms pa las byung ba'ang ma yin te/ zag med ma thob cing*/ zag bcas ni khams gong mar skye ba'i rgyu yin na byang chub sems dpa' ni 'dod par rigs mtho ba'i mtho ris su skye ba'i phyir ram/ nang na sgom byung zag bcas la gnyis las srid pa la rten pa phyi rol pa'i sgom byung ni srid rtse thob kyang mtshan gyi rgyur mi rung zhing*/ thar pa la rten pa ni 'di sangs rgyas kyi mtshan gyi rgyu yin la/ de ni ston dang bse ru byang chub bar/ / bsam gtan mtha' rten gcig la kun zhes sbyor lam mam/ mi sdug pa nas bzung nas stan gcig kho na la skyed pas de'i gong du mi 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / zhes bya ba ni ngo bo'i khyad par yin no/ /

That karma, maturing as a mark of a buddha, is said to be accumulated by a person of Jambudvīpa with sharp [intellectual] faculties who possess a male organ. It is a special karmic accumulation since it is not accumulated by other reincarnating beings, [400] in other continents, by other persons. Further, it is said that this karma is accumulated through residing in the presence of the Master since it has a special object. It is virtuous intention focusing on the Buddha that does not focus on other objectives, such as high rebirth or [individual] liberation. Moreover, it is virtuous karma derived from contemplation and not derived from hearing, because hearing is inferior. It is not derived from meditation because they have not obtained uncontaminated states, and if contaminated states are the cause of their birth in higher realms, the bodhisattva is born in the highest of the high castes in the desire realm. Again, there are two contaminated states derived from meditation: (1) non-Buddhist states, derived from meditation dependent on existence, that obtain the summit of existence but that are unsuitable to be the cause of the marks of a buddha, and (2) those dependent on liberation that are the cause of the marks of a buddha. The statement “Masters and the rhinoceros-like generate all [paths] in one session in dependence on the limit of absorption” (6:24ab) teaches the path of preparation, or the statement “Since it is generated in one session alone from [meditation on] repulsiveness, it does not occur in higher realms” indicates that such karma has a special nature.

'tshang rgya ba la bskal pa chen po brgya lus pa dag tu ste lus pa na las de 'phen cing gsog par byed ces bya ba ni dus kyi khyad par te/ 'di bskal pa brgya bas mang du lus pa na ni 'phen pa mi srid la nyung du lus pa na 'phen pa srid de/ sangs rgyas shAkya thub pas bskal pa dgu bcu rtsa gcig lus pa na las de 'phangs par bshad de/ mdo las/ grong dpon ngas 'di nas bzung ste bskal pa dgu bcu rtsa gcig gi bar du yang dag par rjes su dran te/ zas smin pa ster bar bya ba'i phyir khyim 'ga' la'ang mi bde ba'am gnod par 'gyur ba gang yin pa de ni mngon par mi mkhyen to zhes dge sbyong gcer bu pa'i grong dpon ral gri thogs pa la gsungs te/ lung 'dis ni bskal pa dgu bcu rtsa gcig tshun chod skye ba thams cad du tshe rabs dran par ston la/ mtshan rnam par smin pa'i las gsog pa ni skye ba thams cad du tshe rabs dran pa nas yin pa'i phyir ro/ / sngon gyi slob dpon rnams na re bskal pa dang po tshar phyin pa'i byang chub sems dpa' kho nas ngan 'gro dang*/ rigs dma' ba dang*/ dbang po ma tshang ba dang*/ bud med kyi dngos por 'gyur ba'i skyon bzhi ni zlog la tshe rabs dran pa dang*/ phyir mi ldog pa'i yon tan gnyis ni 'thob pa'i phyir na de tshun chad byang chub sems dpa' nges gnas yin no zhes zer ro/ /

That this karma projects and accumulates marks in the remaining one hundred great eons until enlightenment indicates the special time. It is impossible to project those marks if many eons yet remain of the hundred eons, but it is possible to project them if only a few remain, because it is said that Buddha Śākyamuni projected those marks after ninety-one eons. A sūtra states: Village chief, I fully remember ninety-one eons from now, and I do not recall any family who has been made unhappy or harmed through the giving of cooked foods.[1251] This scriptural quotation teaches that he remembered his lives in all births for ninety-one eons, and he remembered his lives in all births where he accumulated karma that matured as the marks of a buddha. Past masters say: A bodhisattva who has just completed the first eon, who stops the four errors of taking birth (1) in lower rebirths, (2) in an inferior caste, (3) with incomplete faculties, and (4) as a female, is a bodhisattva who has attained certainty prior to obtaining the two qualities of remembering past lives and irreversibility.
re re'ang bsod nams brgya las skye/ / rnam gzigs mar me rin chen gtsug/ / grangs med gsum gyi tha mar byung / / dang po shAkya thub pa yin/ / 110
Each arises from one hundred merits. Vipaśyin, Dīpaṃkara, and Ratnaśikhin appeared at the end of three countless eons. The first was Śākyamuni. (4:110)

mtshan sum cu rtsa gnyis po de dag re re'ang bsod nams brgya brgya las skyes so zhes bya ba ni tshad de/ re re'i tshad kyang kha cig ni byang chub sems dpa' nges pa la gnas pa ma gtogs pa'i sems can thams cad kyi longs spyod kyi 'bras bu can gyi bsod nams gcig tu bsdus pa dang mnyam mo zhes 'dod do/ / kha cig ni sems can spyi'i las kyis stong gsum 'chags pa de snyed pa de tsam dang mnyam la/ de dag brgyas skyes bu chen po'i mtshan gcig 'grub pa nas sum cu rtsa gnyis kyi bar du'ang de dang 'dra'o/ / zhes zer ro/ / gzhan dag ni bsod nams de'i tshad sangs rgyas kyis mkhyen par zad kyi gzhan gyis ni dpag par dka'o zhes 'dod do/ /

Stating that each of the thirty-two marks arises from one hundred merits reveals the measure. Also, regarding the measure of each mark: Some say: It is equivalent to the merit required to produce a result enjoyed by all sentient beings except for [401] bodhisattvas who have attained certainty. Some say: It is equivalent to just the merit required for the formation of the trichiliocosm through the general karma of sentient beings. One hundred of those establishes one mark of a great being, and thirty-two of those is similar to that [amount] required for the marks of a buddha. Another says: The measure of that merit is comprehended by buddhas, but others have difficulty in fathoming it.
brgya'i grangs nges pa'ang kha cig ni
THEY ARE FIXED IN NUMBER AS ONE HUNDRED

sangs rgyas kyi skye ba'i sku mtshan sum cu rtsa gnyis dang*/ chos kyi sku ma 'dres pa bco brgyad de lnga bcu la dmigs pa'i sems pa lnga bcu dang*/ bdag kyang lnga bcu po 'di 'dra ba thob par gyur cig snyam pa'i sems pa gzhan lnga bcu ste brgya yin no zhes 'dod do/ / gzhan dag na re 'dod pa'i khams gnas nyi shu dang grang ba'i dmyal ba brgyad de nyi shu rtsa brgyad dang gzugs khams bcu drug dang*/ gzugs med bzhi ste bzhi bcu rtsa brgyad la byang chub sems dpa' snying rje skye la/ snying rje de dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i sems pa bzhi bcu rtsa brgyad dang*/ sangs rgyas kyis khams gsum po 'di las sems can bkrol lo snyam pa gcig dang*/ bdag gis kyang dgrol snyam pa gcig ste lnga bcu yin la/ de lan gnyis yid la byas pas brgya yin no zhes zer ro/ /

Some say: There are one hundred, since there are (1–50) fifty intentions focusing on the fifty objects — the thirty-two marks generated by a buddha and the eighteen unmixed qualities of the Dharma body — and (51–100) fifty intentions reflecting, “Even I can obtain something similar to these fifty.” Others say: Forty-eight types of compassion arise for those in the twenty-eight abodes: (1–20) the twenty abodes of the desire realm and (21–28) the eight cold hells, plus (29–44) sixteen abodes of the form realm, and (45–48) the four formless abodes. There are forty-eight states that arise concomitant with that compassion. There is one karma reflecting “May the Buddha free sentient beings from the three realms” and one karma reflecting “May I free them,” making fifty. By applying that twice, there are one hundred.

kha cig na re sangs rgyas ni srog gcod spong ba la sogs pa dge ba bcu la re re zhing rgyu lnga lnga dang ldan pa yin te srog gcod spong ba la sogs pa'i las kyi lam dngos yongs su dag pa dang*/ nyer bsdogs yongs su dag pa dang*/ rnam par rtog pas ma snas pa dang*/ dran pas yongs su zin pa nyid dang*/ mya ngan las 'das par bsdos pa ste rnam par dag pa lnga lnga dang ldan pas de dag la dmigs pa'i sems pa lnga bcu yin la/ ji ltar sangs rgyas de rgyu las kyi lam lnga bcu po de las byung ba ltar bdag kyang rgyu lnga bcus sangs rgyas su gyur cig snyam pa lnga bcu ste brgya yin no zhes zer mod kyi/ {'di ni mtshan 'grub pa'i bsod nams re re ba brgya la 'dod pa'i phyir 'di dag ni rnam par brtags pa yin par gsal bas/ } blo gros mi zad pas bstan pa'i mdo las ni/ dus gsum gyi so so'i skye bo dang nyan rang thams cad kyi bsod nams bcu 'gyur gyis sangs rgyas kyi ba spu'i khung bu gcig dang*/ ba spu'i khung bu thams cad 'grub pa'i bsod nams brgya 'gyur gyis dpe byad gcig dang*/ dpe byad brgyad cu po thams cad 'grub pa'i bsod nams stong 'gyur gyis mdzod spu dang gtsug tor ma gtogs pa mtshan sum cu'i gang rung gcig dang*/ mtshan sum cu po thams cad 'grub pa'i bsod nams khri 'gyur gyis mdzod spu dang*/ mdzod spu 'grub pa'i bsod nams 'bum 'gyur gyis gtsug tor 'grub la/ de 'grub pa'i bsod nams bye ba phrag 'bum 'gyur gyis gsung chos kyi dung 'grub par gsungs la/

Some say: There are fifty intentions focusing on fifty objects, since each of the ten virtuous actions, such as abandoning taking life and so on, possesses five causes each that are the five purities: (1) completely pure karmic path, (2) completely pure access concentration, (3) unaffected by conceptuality, (4) fully retained by mindfulness, and (5) directed to nirvāṇa. There are fifty reflections “Just as a buddha arises from those fifty causal karmic paths, so I will also become a buddha by relying on these fifty,” thus making one hundred. {Because one hundred are asserted for each merit that establishes a mark, these should be clarified through investigation.} The Sūtra Taught by Akṣayamati observes: Ten times the merit of all ordinary beings, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas of the three times establishes one pore of a buddha. One hundred times the merit establishing all the pores of a buddha establishes one sign (vyañjana). One thousand times the merit establishing all eighty signs establishes any of the thirty marks (lakṣaṇa) except for the spiral hair and the uṣṇīṣa. One thousand times the merit establishing all thirty marks establishes the spiral hair. One hundred thousand times the merit establishing the spiral hair establishes the uṣṇīṣa. One thousand billion times the merit establishing those establishes a Dharma conch.[1252] [402]
[spyod yul]
THE OBJECT OF UTILIZATION OF BODHISATTVAS

byang chub sems dpa'i spyod yul gyi thabs kyi yul la rnam par 'phrul pa bstan pa'i mdo las ni/ stong gsum gyi sems can thams cad mi lus thob nas thams cad 'khor los bsgyur ba'i bsod nams dang ldan par gyur pa'i bsod nams de dag brgya 'gyur gyis sangs rgyas kyi ba spu'i khung bu gcig dang*/ ba spu'i khung bu thams cad 'grub pa'i bsod nams brgya 'gyur gyis dpe byad gcig dang*/ dpe byad brgyad cu po thams cad 'grub pa'i bsod nams brgya 'gyur gyis mdzod spu dang gtsug tor las gzhan pa'i mtshan sum cu'i gcig dang*/ mtshan sum cu po thams cad 'grub pa'i bsod nams brgya 'gyur gyis mdzod spu dang*/ de 'grub pa'i bsod nams brgya 'gyur gyis gtsug tor 'grub bo/ / de'i phyir sangs rgyas ni bsod nams brgya pa'i mtshan dang ldan pa zhes bya'o zhes pa dang*/ {mtshan sum cu po re re'ang dpe byad brgyad cu po 'grub pa'i bsod nams brgya brgya la 'grub par gsungs pa nyid gzhung gi dgongs par 'grig go } bsod nams brgya pa'i mtshan dang ldan pas na/ / lhar bcas 'jig rten nang na bsod nams gter/ / mthong dang thos dang gzhes pa mdzad pas kyang*/ / sems can kun la phan pa mdzad pa lags zhes gsungs so/ gsung chos kyi dung 'grub pa'i tshul ni mdo snga ma dang 'dra'o/ / rin po che'i phreng ba las ni/ dpe byad brgyad cu po thams cad 'grub pa'i bsod nams brgya 'gyur gyis mtshan sum cu'i gcig dang*/ mtshan sum cu po thams cad 'grub pa'i bsod nams stong 'gyur gyis mdzod spu dang*/ gtsug tor 'grub pa'i bsod nams 'bum phrag brgyar bsgyur bas gsung chos kyi dung 'grub par gsungs la/ gzhan ni blo gros mi zad pas bstan pa'i mdo dang mthun par gsungs so/ /

The Range of the Bodhisattva Sūtra asserts: One hundred times the merit obtained by all sentient beings of the trichiliocosm without exception, up to the merit of a cakravartin, establishes one pore of a buddha. One hundred times the merit establishing all the pores of a buddha establishes one sign. One hundred times the merit establishing all eighty signs establishes one of the thirty marks except for the spiral hair and the uṣṇīṣa. One hundred times the merit establishing all thirty marks establishes the spiral hair. One hundred times the merit establishing the spiral hair establishes the uṣṇīṣa. Therefore a buddha possesses the marks of one hundred merits.[1253] {Stating “One hundred times each the merit establishing the eighty signs of each of the thirty marks” conforms with the intention of the text.} Through possessing marks of one hundred merits, he is a treasure of merit within the world with its gods. Through seeing him, hearing him, and by his presence, all sentient beings are benefited by him.[1254] The means for establishing the Dharma conch are similar to those given in the previous sūtra. Precious Garland states: One hundred times the merit establishing all eighty [secondary] signs establishes one of the thirty marks [of a buddha]. One thousand times the merit establishing all thirty marks . . . establishes the spiral hair [between the brows]. Ten million times the merit establishing the uṣṇīṣa establishes the Dharma conch. . . .[1255] Otherwise it is taught in conformity with the Sūtra Taught by Akṣayamati.

byang sa las ni/ sems can thams cad kyi bsod nams dang mnyam pa'i bsod nams kyi phung pos sangs rgyas kyi ba spu'i khung bu re re 'grub la ba spu'i khung bu thams cad 'grub pa'i bsod nams kyi phung pos dpe byad gcig 'grub par bshad cing*/ de las gzhan dpe byad las mtshan sum cu dang*/ de las mdzod spu 'grub pa'i tshul 'di ni rin po che'i phreng ba dang mthun par bshad la/ mdzod spu las gtsug tor dang*/ gtsug tor las gsung chos kyi dung 'grub pa'i tshul ni blo gros mi zad pas bstan pa'i mdo dang mthun par bshad cing*/ gsung chos kyi dung ni mtshan sum cu rtsa gnyis las ldog pa tha dad du bshad kyang rdzas tshangs pa'i sgra dbyangs su 'dus so zhes bshad do/ /
'di la slob dpon rgya mtsho sprin ni byang sa las/ sems can thams cad kyi bsod nams dang mnyam pa'i bsod nams kyi phung pos sangs rgyas kyi ba spu'i khung pu re re 'grub ces 'byung ba'i sems can thams cad ces bya ba ni spyir sems can thams cad brjod pa ma yin gyi 'on kyang 'di ni sems can gyi bye brag 'dzam bu'i gling pa'i sems can kho na brjod pa yin te/ dper na zhun mar gyi phyogs gcig tsam 'thungs pa la zhun mar thams cad 'thungs so zhes brjod pa ltar spyi'i ming gis bye brag la btags pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dzam bu'i gling pa'i sems can kho na gzung ba ni 'dzam bu'i gling pa ni las kyi sa pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / des na 'dzam bu'i gling pa'i sems can rnams kyi longs spyod 'grub pa'i bsod nams kyi phung po'i tshad kyis sangs rgyas kyi ba spu'i khung bu gcig 'grub bo zhes bya ba yin no zhes 'chad do/ / 'o na ston pa shAkya thub pa byang chub sems dpar gyur pa na sangs rgyas ji snyed cig bsnyen bkur nas sangs rgyas she na/ de la spyir sems bskyed pa dang*/ tshogs gnyis bsgrubs pa'i dang po la gnyis las/

Bodhisattva Levels states: An aggregate of merit equal to the merit of all sentient beings establishes each of the pores of a buddha. An aggregate of merit establishing all the pores of the buddha establishes one sign.[1256] Otherwise, when it explains from the thirty marks to the signs, and from that to the spiral hair, its method of establishing the signs is similar to the explanation given in Precious Garland. When it explains from the spiral hair to the uṣṇīṣa, and from the uṣṇīṣa to the Dharma conch, its method of establishing the signs conforms with the explanation of the Sūtra Taught by Akṣayamati. The instruction of the Dharma conch is explained to be distinct from the thirty-two marks, and its substance is included within the melodious voice of Brahma. Master Sāgaramegha says: When Bodhisattva Levels declares, “An aggregate of merit equal to the merit of all sentient beings establishes each pore of a buddha,” then “all sentient beings” does not refer in general to all sentient beings but it refers just to sentient beings of Jambudvīpa, who are a subset [403] of all sentient beings. It is an instance of imputing a general name to a specific case, like, for example, stating, “I have drunk all the melted butter” when one has drunk only a portion of it. In referring only to sentient beings of Jambudvīpa, it refers to the karmic level[1257] of beings of Jambudvīpa. Therefore it explains that the measure of the aggregate of merit establishing the resources of sentient beings on Jambudvīpa establishes one pore of a buddha.[1258] Question: How many buddhas did Master Śākyamuni worship when he was a bodhisattva in order to attain buddhahood? Reply: There are two parts: (1) the general awakening mind and (2) establishing the two collections.
dang po ni
GENERAL AWAKENING MIND

bskal bzang ltar na/ nga ni sngon tshe dman par gyur pa na/ / de bzhin gshegs pa shAkya thub pa la/ / 'jams gang zhig ni dbul ba byas nas kyang*/ / dang por byang chub tu ni sems bskyed do/ / zhes shAkya thub la dang po sems bskyed par gsungs shing*/ snying rje pad ma dkar po las ni bram ze rgya mtsho'i rdul du gyur pa na de bzhin gshegs pa rin chen snying po la sems bskyed par gsungs la/ byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod las ni gzhon nu brtson 'grus spyod ces bya bar gyur pa na de bzhin gshegs pa phung po chen po la sems bskyed par gsungs pa dang*/ ma skyes dgra'i 'gyod pa bsal ba'i mdo las/ tshong dpon gyi bu dri ma med pa'i dpung pa zhes bya bar gyur pas 'phags pa 'jam dpal dge slong chos smra ba ye shes rgyal po zhes par gyur pa la dang po sems bskyed par gsungs pa la sogs pa theg pa chen po'i lung dag las sna tshogs 'byung mod kyi/ nyan thos sde pa ltar na lung sman gyi gzhi las/ kun dga' bos/ 'jig rten gtso bo rnam 'dren pa/ / thub pa khyod kyis byang chub thugs/ / thog mar gang du bskyed pa dag / skal ldan chen po bdag la gsungs zhes zhus pa na/ sangs rgyas 'dod chags bral thos shing*/ / glang po dregs pa'i shas chen dang*/ / 'jig rten sdug bsngal gyur mthong nas/ / ngas ni byang chub sems bskyed do/ / mi dbang 'od ldan gyur pa na/ / ngas ni byang chub 'dod pa'i phyir/ / ngas ni brtan por dam bcas te/ / skyon med pa yi sbyin pa btang*/ / zhes 'byung bas sngon rgyal po 'od ldan zhes bya bar gyur pa na dang po sems bskyed par 'dod do/ /

The Good Fortune Sūtra reads: In a former time when I lacked resources, I offered a fine gift to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and first generated the mind of enlightenment.[1259] This passage reveals that in the presence of Śākyamuni, he first generated the mind of enlightenment. The Lotus Sūtra states: When I was the brahman Samudrareṇu, I generated the awakening mind in the presence of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha.[1260] The Bodhisattva Collection states: When I was the youth Vīryacaryā, I generated the awakening mind in the presence of the Tathāgata Mahāskandha.[1261] The Removing the Regret of Ajātaśatru Sūtra states: When I was the son of the trader called Vimalabala, and Mañjūśrī was the monk preceptor Jñānarāja, I first generated the awakening mind.[1262] In accordance with the śrāvaka division, the Chapter on Medicine states: Ānanda asked: “Lord of the World, Guide, and Sage, when did you first generate the mind of enlightenment?” The Buddha replied: “When I heard that buddhas are free of attachment and I saw the great extent of the tyranny of fate and the suffering in the world, I generated the mind of enlightenment. When, as the human ruler Prabhāvat, I desired enlightenment, I made this firm pledge and practiced faultless generosity.[1263] This sūtra asserts that he first generated the awakening mind when he was King Prabhāvat.
ESTABLISHING THE TWO COLLECTIONS

'dir gnyis pa tshogs gnyis bsgrubs tshul gyi dbang du mdzad nas sngon 'das pa'i dus na sangs rgyas shAkya thub pa zhes bya ba ston pa 'di bzhin du rtsod pa'i dus su byung la/ de'i sku tshe dang 'khor 'dus pa la sogs pa'ang 'di dang 'dra la bstan pa'ang lo stong gi bar du gnas pa zhig byon pa la ston pa 'di rdza mkhan gyi khye'u snang byed du gyur pa na 'bras phor ba gang dang*/ mchil lham dang ras kyi kha tshar dag phul nas/ de bzhin gshegs pa khyed sku ci 'dra dang*/ / 'khor dang tshe yi tshad dang zhing khams dang*/ / de bzhin mtshan mchog bzang po ci 'dra ba/ / de 'dra kho nar bdag kyang 'gyur bar shog ces smon lam btab bo/ / zhes snga ma dag 'chad mod kyi/ lung sman gyi gzhi las ni/ sngon grong khyer yangs pa'i rdza mkhan yangs pa'i 'od ces par gyur pas de bzhin gshegs pa shAkya thub pa bser ma'i snyun gyis zin pa la chu 'jam pos sku khrus gsol te/ mar dang til mar gyis byugs nas/ bu ram chu'i btung ba drangs pas snyun las grol lo/ / de nas de dad nas/ bdag kyang rab tu sbyin pa 'di yis shAkya'i rigs skyes pa/ / yon tan rigs dang rus dag mnyam pa'i sangs rgyas nyid gyur cing*/ / bdag gis tshangs pa'i 'jig rten par gyi nyam thag 'chi ba yi/ / pha rol zhi ba rgya chen 'jigs pa med pas sgrol bar shog ces smon lam btab bo zhes pa dang*/ nga ni rdza mkhan gyur pa na/ / sangs rgyas shAkya thub mthong nas/ / byang chub phyir ni thog mar ngas/ / mar dang til mar gyis mchod do zhes 'byung ngo*/ /

Here, from the perspective of the method of establishing the two collections, long ago one called the master Śākyamuni appeared in the age of conflict. His body was large, as was his retinue and so on, and his teachings likewise lasted a thousand years. At that time our teacher was Prabhāsa, the son of a potter. He offered a bowl of rice, shoes, and a rain cloak [404] and prayed: “Tathāgata, may I come to have a body, retinue, lifespan, buddhafield, and various types of pure supreme marks just like yours.” Indeed, past scholars state this. The Chapter on Medicine declares: Formerly, as the potter Prabhā in the city of Vaiśālī, he offered to wash the body of Tathāgata Śākyamuni with pure water when the latter was afflicted with wind disease in the stomach and anointed him with butter and sesame oil, and through inducing him to drink molasses water the Tathāgata recovered. Then, through faith in the Buddha, Prabhā prayed: “Through these offerings may I be born in the Śākya caste and become a buddha with similar qualities, lineage, and clan, and may I liberate those who experience torment and death up to the heaven of Brahma through establishing great peace and fearlessness.” And: When I was a potter and saw Buddha Śākyamuni, I first made an offering of butter and sesame oil in order to attain enlightenment.[1264]

de nas bzung ste bskal pa grangs med dang po la sangs rgyas bdun khri lnga stong la bsnyen bkur byas pa'i tha mar gzhung gi go rim las bzlog ste sangs rgyas rin chen gtsug tor can zhes pa byung ste/ de'i tshe bskal pa grangs med dang po rdzogs so/ / de nas bzung ste grangs med gnyis pa la sangs rgyas bdun khri drug stong la bsnyen bkur byas pa'i tha mar sangs rgyas mar me mdzad byung ste/ de'i tshe grangs med gnyis pa rdzogs so/ / de nas bzung ste grangs med pa gsum pa la sangs rgyas bdun khri bdun stong la bsnyen bkur byas pa'i tha mar sangs rgyas rnam par gzigs byung ste/ 'di ni bskal pa dgu bcu rtsa gcig 'das pa na byung ste/ de'i tshe grangs med gsum pa rdzogs so/ / de ltar na grangs med pa gsum gyi tha mar sangs rgyas de dag byung la/ de dag thams cad kyi dang po ni sngon gyi sangs rgyas shAkya thub pa nyid yin no zhes shes par bya'o/{ de'i drung du bde bar gshegs pa khyed sku ci 'dra dang*/ zhes sogs kyi smon lam btab bo/}
gal te sangs rgyas rnam par gzigs kyi dus nyid du bskal pa grangs med gsum po rdzogs na gtsug tor can nas 'od srung gi bar du 'tshang mi rgya ba mi rigs te/ bskal pa grangs med gsum gyis tshogs rdzogs shing*/ tshogs rdzogs pa ni bzhes par mi rigs pa'i phyir ro zhe na/

Having made that pledge in the first countless eon, he worshiped 75,000 buddhas. At the end of that period, the buddha called Ratnaśikhin appeared, in the opposite order to that given in the texts. At that time the first countless eon was completed. Then in the second countless eon, he worshiped 76,000 buddhas. At the end of that period the buddha Dīpaṃkara appeared, and at that time the second eon was completed. Then in the third countless eon he worshiped 77,000 buddhas. At the end of that period, after ninety-one eons, the buddha Paśyin appeared, and at that time the three countless eons were completed. Thus those buddhas appeared at the end of each of the three countless eons, but it should be understood that the first of all those buddhas was the former Buddha Śākyamuni.
Objection: If the three eons were completed at the time of the buddha Paśyin, it would be illogical that he was not enlightened from [the time of] Ratnaśikhin up to Kāśyapa. The three countless eons were complete, but it is illogical to assert that the collection was complete.

de'i tshe tshogs rdzogs shing grangs med par rdzogs mod kyi rnam pa thams cad du yongs su rdzogs pa ni ma yin pas 'od srung sangs rgyas pa'i tshe tshangs par spyod pa spyad nas 'di nas shi 'phos nas dga' ldan gyi lha'i rigs su 'khrungs so zhes 'byung ba'i mdo 'di yang tshad mar byas pa yin no zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/ / lung sman gyi gzhi las ni/ kun dga' bos/ 'jig rten gtso bo rnam 'dren pa/ / khyod sngon byang chub spyod pa na/ / sangs rgyas ji snyed dus gang du/ / ji lta bur ni bsnyen bkur mdzad/ / ces pa dang*/ rgyal bu gsal rgyal gyis btsun pa bcom ldan 'das kyis bla na med pa'i byang chub don du gnyer ba'i slad du yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas ji snyed cig la bsnyen bkur bgyis lags zhes zhus pa na/{ rgyal po chen po grangs med pa dang po la/} sangs rgyas shAkya thub pa nas/ / 'dren pa yul 'khor skyong gi bar/ / bdun khri dang ni lnga stong gi /sangs rgyas rnams ni ngas mchod do/ {grangs med gnyis pa la ni } sangs rgyas mar me mdzad nas ni/ / thub pa dbang po'i rgyal mtshan bar/ / bdun khri dang ni drug stong gi /sangs rgyas rnams ni nga yis mchod/ {grangs med pa gsum la yang } sangs rgyas legs mdzad nas bzung ste/ / sangs rgyas 'od srung bar dag tu/ / bdun khri bdun stong nga yis mchod/ / grangs med gsum po de la ni/ / rgyal ba ngas ni mchod byas te/ / byang chub phyir ni spyod pa na/ / de tshe nga la skyo sems med ces grangs med gsum gyi tha mar byung ba'i sangs rgyas kyang 'di dang cung zad mi 'dra bar gsungs so/ / theg chen pa ni rgya cher rol pa la sogs pa las sangs rgyas bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong dpag tu med pa la bsnyen bkur byas pa zhes pa dang*/ sangs rgyas bye ba khrag khrig brgya stong lnga bcu rtsa lnga la sbyin pa phul bar gyur pa zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs pas grangs med pa re re la yang sangs rgyas dpag tu med pa bsnyen bkur bar bzhed do/ / yang byang chub sems dpa' gnas skabs gang du pha rol tu phyin pa drug po gang rdzogs par byed ce na/

Reply: At that time, indeed, the collection was complete and the three countless eons were complete, but since they were not complete in all aspects, he practiced celibacy [up to] the time of Buddha Kāśyapa, and from there he died and was reborn in the lineage of gods of Tuṣita, and this sūtra takes this to be valid. This is explained by Master Pūrṇavardhana. The Chapter on Medicine states: Ānanda asked: “Lord of the World, Guide and Sage, when formerly you practiced the mind of enlightenment, [405] how many buddhas did you worship, for how long, and in what way?[1265] And: King Prasenajit asked the Buddha: “For the purpose of attaining highest enlightenment, how many fully enlightened buddhas did you worship?” “{Great king,} {in the first countless eon} from Buddha Śākyamuni up to the guide Rāṣṭrapāla, I made offerings to 75,000 buddhas. {In the second countless eon} from Buddha Dīpaṃkara up to Sage Indradhvaja, I made offerings to 76,000 buddhas. {In the third countless eon} from Buddha Supracāra up to Sage Kāśyapa, I made offerings to 77,000 buddhas. In those three countless eons I made offerings to conquerors, I practiced for the purpose of enlightenment, and during that time I was never disheartened.[1266] Also the buddha of the last, the third countless eon, differs from the earlier. In the Mahāyāna it is asserted that he worshiped inestimable buddhas for each countless eon, since it is stated in the Extensive Display Sūtra and so on that he worshiped inestimable trillions of buddhas and practiced generosity with regard to fifty-five trillion buddhas and so on.[1267] Question: Also, when did he complete the six perfections while a bodhisattva?
kun la thams cad snying rje yis/ / sbyin par byed pas sbyin pa rdzogs/ / chags bcas yan lag bcad kyang ni/ / mi 'khrugs bzod dang tshul khrims kyi/ / 111

When he practiced giving everything to everyone with compassion, he completed generosity. Though he possessed attachment, he remained undisturbed when his limbs were severed and completed patience and ethics. (4:111)

gang gi tshe sems can kun la dngos po mig nas rkang gi bar du lus dang longs spyod thams cad kun slong mngon mtho'i khyad par la mi re bar snying rje yis sbyin par byed pas dus de'i tshe sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa rdzogs te 'di ni skyes pa'i rabs su blta'o/ / lung gzhi las ni byang chub sems dpa' sbyin pa chen po'i dus na sbyin pa'i phar phyin rdzogs par gsungs so/ / de yang byang sa las ni/ sbyin pa'i skabs su pha ma ni bla ma lta bu'i zhing yin pas gzhan la sbyin par mi bya la/ de bzhin du legs par brda ma sprad pa dang mi dga' bzhin du bu dang chung ma dang bran la sogs pa'ang mi sbyin par bshad cing*/ mchod pa'i skabs su'ang dngos po dman pa bab las byug pa dang*/ mar khus bkru ba dang*/ gu gul gyis bdug pa dang*/ arga'i me tog la sogs pas mchod pa mi bya bar bshad do/ /

Reply: When he practiced giving everything, such as his body from his eyes to his feet, and all objects of enjoyment to every sentient being, motivated with compassion (karuṇā) free from hope for any specific higher rebirth, at that time he completed the perfection of generosity (dāna), and he was looked upon as the best of beings. The Chapters on Vinaya mentions: When the bodhisattva practiced great generosity, he completed the perfection of generosity.[1268] Further, Bodhisattva Levels explains that when giving, one should not merely give to one’s father and mother, who are superior fields of benefit like one’s guru, and not give to others. So too, one should not give to one’s children, wife, servants, and so on with improper words or with dislike.[1269] And when making offerings it explains that one should not offer inferior objects by covering or coating them with melted butter, infusing them with expensive incense, offering them with arga[1270] flowers, and so on.

gang gi tshe 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang ma bral bas chags pa dang bcas bzhin du yan lag bcad kyang sems mi 'khrugs pa de'i tshe sems ma 'khrugs pa'i phyir dang*/ lus ngag gi nyes spyod sdom pa'i phyir go rim bzhin du bzod pa dang tshul khrims kyi pha rol tu phyin pa rdzogs te drang srong bzod par smra ba'i skyes pa'i rabs bzhin no/ /

It is stated in the Jātaka of Rishi Kṣānti that though he possessed attachment since he was not free from attachment to sense objects, his mind remained undisturbed even when his limbs were severed. At that time he completed the perfections of patience (kṣānti) and ethics (śīla) because, respectively, his mind was not disturbed and his physical and mental faults were restrained.[1271] [406]
skar rgyal bstod pas brtson 'grus kyi/ / de ma thag la ting 'dzin blo'i/ /
Effort was completed by praising Puṣya. Immediately before enlightenment, concentration and intelligence. (4:112ab)

ston pa bram ze'i khye'ur gyur pa na sangs rgyas skar rgyal ri'i phug zhig na me'i khams la snyoms par zhugs pa mthong nas rkang pa ya gcig gis 'greng ste zhag bdun gyi bar du/ skyes bu khyu mchog
