'grel pa las lta ba la sogs pa mchog tu 'dzin pa zhes brjod par bya ba'i rigs pa la sogs pa'i sgra mi mngon par byas so zhes 'byung bas lta ba dang po gsum la sogs pa zag bcas nyer len gyi phung po lnga po 'phags pa rnams kyis spangs pas dman pa rnams la dmigs nas bde ba dang gtsang ba la sogs pa mchog dang gtso bo dang khyad par du 'phags pa dang dam par lta ba dang*/ dbang phyug chen po la sogs pa 'jig rten skyed byed kyi rgyu dang*/ me lnga bsten pa dang chur 'jug pa dang g.yang du mchong ba la sogs pa mtho ris kyi rgyu min pa la rgyur lta ba dang*/ 'chal tshul gyi gnyen po tshul khrims dang cha byad dang tshul dang lus ngag gi 'jug pa nges par byed pa'i brtul zhugs tsam dang grangs can dang rnal 'byor gyi shes pa la sogs pa sdig pa'i dri ma dag pa dang nyon mongs pa'i 'ching ba las grol ba ba dang 'khor ba las nges par 'byin pa'i thabs thar pa'i lam min pa la rgyu dang lam der lta ba rnams ni rim pa ltar 'jig tshogs la lta ba dang mthar 'dzin par lta ba dang*/ log lta dang*/ lta ba mchog 'dzin dang*/ phung po lnga pa la sogs pa las tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs dang de'i gnas phung po rnams la dge ba la sogs par 'dzin par bshad cing*/ 'grel pa las kyang sogs pa'i sgra mi mngon par byas so zhes 'byung bas brtul zhugs tsam ni gzugs kyi phung pos bsdus pa yin pas de kho na la mchog tu 'dzin pa ni ma yin gyi nyer len gyi phung po gzhan la mchog tu 'dzin pa'ang yin pas tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs la sogs pa mchog tu 'dzin pa yin pas de ltar na de dag ni lta ba rnam pa lnga yin no/ /

The Autocommentary states: It would be correct to state “clinging to those views and so on as supreme,” but the term “and so on” (adi) does not actually appear.[1404] Therefore (9) [clinging to those views as supreme] focuses on inferior (hīna) states, such as the first three views and the five aggregates appropriated by the contaminants that are abandoned by āryas, and views them as blissful, clean, and so forth or supreme (agra), foremost, superior, and pure. (10) [Clinging to rules and ritual as supreme] views those that are not causes as causes, such as viewing the great Īśvara and so on as the primary cause generating the world; viewing reliance on the five fires, immersion in water, and jumping into an abyss and so forth as causes of higher rebirth; or viewing that which is not the path of liberation to be a cause of the path and the path itself. The last includes viewing such things as rules (śīla) that are the antidote to unethical conduct; mere ritual (vrata) that determines one’s dress, manner, and physical and verbal action; or the philosophy of the Sāṃkhya and Yoga schools and so on to be the means of purifying the stains of immorality and of liberating oneself from the ties of affliction and of definitely releasing oneself from saṃsāra. These are explained, respectively, to be the five views: (6) the afflicted view of the self, (7) view adhering to an extreme, (8) wrong view, (9) clinging to those views as supreme, and (10) clinging to rules and ritual — as well as their abode, the five aggregates — as virtuous and so forth. Since the Autocommentary states that “the term ‘and so on’ does not actually appear,”[1405] only the form aggregate is subsumed by ritual. However, that is not the only thing held as supreme; the other aggregates are also held as supreme. Thus [in this view] rules and ritual and so forth are held as supreme. These are the five types of view (dṛṣṭi).
lta ba lnga po de dag gi las ni
THE FUNCTION OF THOSE FIVE

rim pa ltar lta ba ngan pa thams cad kyi rten byed pa dang*/ dbu ma'i lam rtag chad du 'dzin pa spangs nas rten 'brel du shes pa'i bar du gcod pa dang*/ dge rtsa gcod cing mi dge ba la dam du 'dzin pa'i rten byed pa dang*/ lta ba ngan pa la yon tan du 'dzin pas lta ba ngan pa la mngon par zhen pa'i rten byed pa dang*/ ngal ba 'bras bu med pa'i rten byed pa'i las can yin par gzhung gzhan dag las bshad do/ /

Other texts explain the function of those five views respectively to be: supporting all bad views; obstructing the understanding of dependent origination and the Middle Way path that abandons views that hold to permanence and annihilation; supporting the severence of the root of virtue; holding nonvirtue as pure; and supporting longing for bad views through holding bad views to possess good qualities.
de dag lngar nges pa'i rgyu ni
THE CAUSES FOR DETERMINING THOSE TO BE FIVE

kun las btus ltar na dang po ni shes bya la bdag dang bdag gi med pa la de dag tu sgro 'dogs pas ngo bo nyid du sgro 'dogs pa yin la/ gnyis pa ni de nyid rtag chad du 'dzin pas shes bya'i khyad par du sgro 'dogs pas de gnyis ni shes bya la sgro 'dogs pa'o/ / bzhi pa ni lta ba snga ma gsum dman pa la mchog tu sgro 'dogs la/ lnga pa ni lta ba de dag bdag pa'i thabs ma yin pa la 'dag pa'i thabs su sgro 'dogs pas de gnyis ni lta ba la sgro 'dogs pa'o/ gsum pa ni phal cher la skur pa 'debs pa ste/ de ltar sgro 'dogs kyi lta ba bzhi dang*/ skur 'debs kyi lta ba gcig go /

In accordance with the Compendium of Abhidharma,[1406] the first is natural superimposition, since it overestimates objects of knowledge that are free of being “I” and “mine.” The second [440] is the specific overestimation of objects of knowledge by holding them to be permanent or annihilated. These two views overestimate the status of objects of knowledge. The fourth is overestimation that holds the first three views that are inferior to be supreme. The fifth is overestimating these views that are not the means of purification to be the means of purification. These two latter views overestimate view. The third [wrong view] mostly underestimates its objects. Thus there are four views that overestimate and one view that underestimates.

rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las ni lta ba la sgro skur gnyis su nges shing*/ sgro 'dogs la bdag yod par sgro 'dogs pa dang*/ de nyid la rtag mi rtag tu sgro 'dogs pa dang*/ mngon mtho'i thabs su sgro 'dogs pa dang*/ thar pa'i thabs su sgro 'dogs pa bzhir nges la/ skur 'debs ni log lta yin pa lngar nges par bshad do/ /
de yang phal che ba'i dbang du byas kyi mthar 'dzin la'ang skur 'debs dang log lta la'ang rgyu min la rgyur lta ba'i sgro 'dogs kyang cung zad yod do/ /
gal te dbang phyug la sogs pa rgyu ma yin pa la rgyur lta ba'i tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog tu 'dzin pa ci'i phyir kun 'byung mthong spang ma yin te/ rgyu ni kun 'byung yin la/ de la phyin ci log tu zhugs pa'i phyir ro/ / de lta na'ang sdug bsngal mthong spang kho na ma yin par 'gyur ro zhe na/

The Compendium of Ascertainment explains that views are twofold: those that overestimate and those that underestimate. Those that overestimate are ascertained to have four types: those that overestimate the existence of the “I,” those that overestimate it to be permanent or impermanent, those that overestimate the methods of higher rebirth, those that overestimate the methods of liberation. That which underestimates is wrong view. Thus they are definitely explained to be five.[1407]
Further, in general extreme view also possesses a measure of underestimation, and wrong view possesses a measure of overestimation in that it views noncauses as causes.
Objection: Why isn’t clinging to rules and ritual as supreme, which views a noncause such as Īśvara and so on as the cause [of the universe], not an object to be abandoned by seeing the truth of origin? For isn’t the cause the truth of origin and it wrongly engages that? In that case it would not be an object to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering alone.
dbang phyug sogs rgyur mngon zhen pa/ / rtag bdag phyin ci log pa yis/ / rab tu 'jug pas de phyir de/ / sdug bsngal mthong bas spang bya nyid/ / 8
Conceiving Īśvara and so on to be the cause is only abandoned by seeing suffering because it fully and wrongly engages its object as permanent and a self. (5:8)

gang zhig dbang phyug dang skye dgu'i bdag po la sogs pa rgyu ma yin pa la rgyur mngon par zhen pa de ni sdug bsngal mthong bas spang bar bya ba nyid yin no zhes sbyar ro/ / ci'i phyir zhe na/ lta ba de ni rtag pa dang bdag tu lta ba phyin ci log pa yis rab tu 'jug pa yin pas de'i phyir ro/ / des na de yang sdug bsngal mthong spang {de ni sdug bsngal mi rtag pa dang chos tsam du mthong bas spong ba'i phyir } kho na yin no/ / de'i phyir bstan bcos las/ gang dag skyes bu gang zag gang zhig ba lang gi tshul khrims dang*/ ri dwags kyi tshul khrims dang*/ bya gag gi tshul khrims yang dag par blangs te gnas pa de ni des 'dag par 'gyur/ grol bar 'gyur/ nges par 'byung bar 'gyur/ bde ba dang sdug bsngal las rnam par 'da' bar 'gyur zhing*/ bde ba dang sdug bsngal las rnam par 'das pa'ang rjes su thob par 'gyur ro/ / zhes de ltar lta zhing de skad du smra ba ni rgyu ma yin pa la rgyur yid ches pas tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog tu 'dzin pa ste sdug bsngal mthong bas spang bar bya ba yin no zhes rgyas par 'byung ba yin no/ /
gal te ba lang gi tshul khrims la sogs pa la mtho ris dang thar pa'i rgyur lta ba de rtag bdag gis byas pa ma yin pa'i phyir kun 'byung mthong spang kho nar 'gyur ro zhe na/ ba lang gi tshul khrims la sogs pa ni zag bcas kyi phung po sdug bsngal gyi bden pa yin la des 'deg pa dang rgyur lta bas sdug bsngal la log par zhugs pa'i phyir ro zhes bye brag tu smra bas lan 'debs mod kyi/ de lta na zag bcas la dmigs pa'i mthong spang dang sgom spang thams cad kyang sdug bsngal mthong spang du 'gyur te/ sdug bsngal la log par zhugs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: Conceiving those that are not causes — Īśvara, the Lord of Beings, and so on — to be the cause [of the universe] is only abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering. Question: Why? Reply: It is because that view fully and wrongly engages (viparyāsa) its object by viewing it as permanent (nītya) and a self (ātma). {Because it is abandoned by merely seeing suffering, impermanence, and Dharma,} it is an object abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering alone. The treatise (Attainment of Knowledge)[1408] elaborates: Anyone who views or proclaims that “one who correctly takes up and maintains the ways of oxen, the ways of deer, and the ways of water birds will be purified, liberated, attain renunciation, transcend pleasure and pain, and having transcended pleasure and pain also subsequently maintain that state” possesses the view clinging to rules and ritual as supreme, and holds that which is not a cause to be a cause. That view is abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering.[1409]
Objection: That which views the ways of an ox and so on as the cause of higher rebirth and liberation would be an object to be abandoned by seeing the truth of origin because it does not take permanence or a self to be its object. Indeed, the Vaibhāṣikas would answer that the ways of an ox and so on are contaminated aggregates that are the truth of suffering, and viewing them as purifying and causing [liberation] wrongly engages the truth of suffering. Thus all objects abandoned by the path of seeing and objects abandoned by the path of meditation that focus on contaminated states are [441] objects abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering because they wrongly engage suffering.

gzhan yang tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog 'dzin lam mthong spang yang med par 'gyur te/ de thams cad sdug bsngal la log par zhugs pa yin la/ de yang sdug bsngal mthong spang kho nar khas blangs pa'i phyir dang*/ bstan bcos las kyang ba lang gi tshul khrims la sogs pas dag pa la sogs par lta ba'i tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog 'dzin ni rgyu ma yin pa la rgyur yid ches pas sdug bsngal mthong spang du bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te lam mthong spang la dmigs pa'i tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog 'dzin ni lam mthong spang yin no zhe na/ de yang sdug bsngal la log par zhugs pa'i phyir te/ 'di ltar lam mthong spang log lta la sogs pa phra rgyas brgyad ni tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog 'dzin gyi dmigs pa yin zhing brgyad po de dag kyang zag bcas yin pas sdug bsngal gyi bden pas bsdus la de dag de la log par zhugs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Furthermore, clinging to rules and ritual as supreme would also not be an object to be abandoned by seeing the truth of path, because all [such views] wrongly engage suffering and they are accepted as objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering alone. And the treatise (Attainment of Knowledge)[1410] explains: Clinging to rules and ritual as supreme, which [for instance] views the ways of an oxen and so on as something that purifies and so forth, is an object abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering, since it holds that which is not a cause to be a cause [of purification].[1411] Objection: But clinging to rules and ritual as supreme, which focuses on objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of path, is itself an object to be abandoned by seeing the truth of path. Reply: That also wrongly engages the truth of suffering because eight negative tendencies that are objects abandoned by seeing the truth of path, such as wrong view, are focal objects of the view clinging to rules and ritual as supreme. Also since those eight are contaminated states subsumed within the truth of suffering, it wrongly engages those that are the truth of suffering.

gzhan yang lam gyi bden pa la dmigs pa'i mthong spang ni log lta dang the tshom yin na lam med do zhes skur pa 'debs pa dang the tshom za ba de ji ltar lam med do zhes log par lta ba dang the tshom za ba tsam gyis thar par lta bar 'gyur te/ thar pa dang de'i lam la skur pa dang the tshom za ba tsam kho nas 'dag par yid ches pa ni su yang med pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te sangs rgyas pa'i lam 'di ni thar pa'i rgyu ma yin gyi grangs can pa la sogs pas brtags pa'i lam gzhan gyis dag pa yin no zhes lta ba yin no zhe na/ de yang sdug bsngal la log par zhugs pa yin te/ sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das kyis gsungs pa las gzhan pa'i lam ni thar pa'i lam ma yin pas zag bcas yin pa'i phyir ro/ / yang na grangs can la sogs pas brtags pa'i lam gzhan de kho nas dag par yid ches pa de ni log lta dang the tshom ma yin gyi tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog 'dzin yin la/ de ni grangs can la sogs pa'i lam gzhan de kho nas dag par yid ches pas lam de kho na la dmigs pa yin gyi lam mthong spang la dmigs par ni mi 'grub bo zhes slob dpon rgyal po'i sras 'chad do/ /

Furthermore, if wrong view and doubt are objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing that focuses on the truth of path, then how could that which underestimates and doubts [the path, thinking] “there is no path” become the view of liberation by merely wrong view and doubt [reflecting] “there is no path”? No one believes that one is purified through merely underestimating and doubting liberation and the path of liberation alone. Objection: This is a view that asserts the Buddhist path is not the cause of liberation and one instead is purified by other paths that are delineated by the Sāṃkhya and so on. Reply: This [view] also wrongly engages suffering because paths other than those stated by the Buddha Bhagavan are not paths of liberation, for they are contaminated. Master Jinaputra also explains that the belief that paths delineated by the Sāṃkhya and so on alone purify is not wrong view or doubt but a case of clinging to rules and ritual as supreme. Through the belief that other paths delineated by the Sāṃkhya and so on alone purify, one focuses on those paths alone, but this is not established as focusing on objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of path.[1412]

gzhan yang kun 'byung dang 'gog pa mthong spang la dmigs pa'i log lta dang the tshom gyis kyang dag pa dang grol bar lta bar 'gyur te/ lam la dmigs pa'i de gnyis dang khyad par med pa'i phyir ro/ / de lta na kun 'byung dang 'gog pa mthong spang gi tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog 'dzin yang yod par 'gyur la/ de lta na'ang de dag bdun bdun zhes 'dod pa dang 'gal lo zhes slob dpon gyis brjod de/ rang gi bzhed pa ni ma bkod mod kyi rnal 'byor spyod pa pa'i lugs nyid bzhed pa yin te de ni gong du brjod zin pa nyid do/ / 'o na rtag bdag phyin ci log pa yis zhes bshad na phyin ci log de gnyis kho nar nges sam zhe na/ ma nges te/ mdo las/ mi rtag pa la rtag pa dang*/ sdug bsngal ba la bde ba dang*/ mi gtsang ba la gtsang ba dang*/ bdag med pa la bdag tu lta ba phyin ci log dang*/ sems phyin ci log dang*/ 'du shes phyin ci log ces phyin ci log bcu gnyis kyang gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / de dag gi rang bzhin ci zhe na/

Also, [some who assert] wrong view and doubt focusing on objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of origin and cessation view [such objects] as pure and as liberation, because there is no difference between how both [wrong view and doubt] focus on the path. So too, clinging to rules and ritual as supreme as objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of origin and cessation would also exist. But Vasubandhu observes that this would contradict the assertion: “those are seven, and seven.”[1413] Indeed, we do not make such assertions, but the Yogācāra system asserts this, and this has already been stated. Question: Since it is said that it “wrongly engages its object as permanent and a self” (5:8cd), are only those two wrong engagements ascertained? [442] Reply: It is not [only those two that are] ascertained, because a sūtra declares twelve wrong engagements: Wrong view, wrong mind, and wrong discernment view the impermanent to be permanent, suffering to be blissful, the unclean to be clean, selfless to be a self.[1414] Question: What is their nature?
lta ba gsum las phyin ci log / bzhi tshan phyin ci log phyir dang / / nges rtog phyir dang sgro 'dogs phyir/ / sems dang 'du shes de'i dbang gis/ / 9
Four classes of wrong engagement are posited for three views because they wrongly engage, they are decisive conception, and they overestimate. By their power, mind and discernment are that. (5:9)

mthar 'dzin par lta ba la sogs pa lta ba phyed dang*/ gsum las ni de gsum gyi ngo bo yin pas mi rtag pa la rtag par lta ba la sogs pa phyin ci log bzhi tshan du bzhag ste/ de la mthar 'dzin par lta ba'i rtag lta'i cha las rtag par phyin ci log dang*/ lta ba mchog tu 'dzin pa las bde ba dang gtsang bar phyin ci log dang*/ 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i bdag tu lta ba'i cha las bdag tu lta ba phyin ci log gzhag go /gzhan dag na re 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i bdag tu lta ba dang bdag gir lta ba thams cad bdag tu phyin ci log yin no zhes zer ro/ / ji ltar de dag phyin ci log tu gzhag{ la nyon mongs gzhan dag ma gzhag} ce na/

Four classes of wrong engagement (viparyāsa), such as viewing the impermanent as permanent and so on, are posited for a significant part of three views — extreme view, clinging to those views as supreme, and the afflicted view of the self — since that is the nature of those three. The view of permanence [eternalism], which is one part of extreme view, wrongly engages its object as (1) permanent. The view clinging to those views as supreme wrongly engages its object as (2) blissful and (3) clean. One part of the afflicted view of the self that views a self is posited as view wrongly engaging (4) the self. Another says: All afflicted views of the self, which view “I” and “mine,” wrongly engage the self.[1415] Question: How are these posited as wrongly engaging their objects {yet other afflictions are not posited in this way}?

dmigs pa la gcig tu phyin ci log pa'i phyir dang*/ nges par rtog pa'i phyir dang*/ sgro 'dogs pa gsum dang ldan pa'i phyir phyin ci log tu bshad pa la mthar 'dzin par lta ba'i chad lta dang log lta ni skur 'debs yin pa'i phyir dang*/ tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog 'dzin ni de tsam gyis kyang cung zad dag grol du 'gyur bas mtha' gcig tu phyin ci log ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ nyon mongs pa gzhan dag la ni nges par rtog pa med pa'i phyir ci log tu ma bshad do/ / sems dang 'du shes phyin ci log ni lta ba bzhi po de dag dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i dbang gis phyin ci log tu 'gyur bas der gzhag go /'o na tshor ba phyin ci log la sogs par yang 'gyur ro zhe na/ de skad du 'jig rten na ma grags pa'i phyir ma bshad de snga ma gnyis ni grags pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di la bye brag tu smra ba ni phyin ci log de thag thams cad kyang mthong spang yin te/ dang po bzhi lta ba'i rang bzhin yin pa'i phyir dang*/ 'du shes dang sems lta ba dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i phyir dang*/ mdo las kyang*/ 'di ltar 'phags pa nyan thos thos pa dang ldan pa 'di ni sdug bsngal 'phags pa'i bden pa'o/ / zhes bya bar yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du shes so zhes bya ba nas/ de'i tshe de'i mi rtag pa la rtag go snyam du 'du shes phyin ci log pa dang*/ sems phyin ci log pa dang*/ lta ba phyin ci log pa gang yin pa de spong bar byed do zhes bya ba la sogs pa'i bar du rgyas par gsungs pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ / sde pa gzhan dag ni 'phags pa rgyun du zhugs pa rnams la'ang 'dod pa'i 'dod chags skye bar gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ 'dod chags de yang sdug bsngal ba la bde bar lta ba dang*/ mi gtsang ba la gtsang bar 'du shes dang sems phyin ci log med na mi 'byung ba'i phyir lta ba bzhi ga dang mi rtag pa la rtag par 'du shes dang sems phyin ci log gnyis dang*/ bdag med pa la bdag tu 'du shes dang sems phyin ci log gnyis te brgyad ni mthong spang yin la/ sdug bsngal ba la bde ba dang mi gtsang ba la gtsang bar 'du shes dang sems phyin ci log bzhi ni sgom spang yin no zhes zer ro/ /

Reply: They are explained as those that wrongly engage their objects because they wrongly engage their focal objects, because they are decisive conception (nitīraṇa), and because they overestimate (samāropa) in three ways. Others are not said to wrongly engage their objects because both the extreme view of annihilation and wrong view underestimate their objects, clinging to rules and ritual as supreme to some extent acts to liberate and does not absolutely wrongly engage its object, and the other afflictions do not possess decisive conception. Since they wrongly engage their objects by the power of being concomitant with those four views, distorted mind and discernment (saṃjñā) are posited as that. Objection: Wrong feeling and so on would also become wrong engagers. Reply: They are not explained to be wrong engagers because they are not well known in the world as that, whereas the former two are. Vaibhāṣikas say: All wrong engagers are objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing because the first four are, by nature, view; and discernment and the mind are concomitant with view. Also, it is extensively stated in the sūtras: Thus a learned ārya śrāvaka understands correctly as it is the statement “This is the ārya truth of suffering”. . . up to . . . “At this time he abandons wrong discernment, wrong mind, wrong view that the impermanent is permanent” and so on.”[1416] Other schools say: Because it is said that attachment to desire-realm objects even arises for those entering the ārya stream, and because attachment views suffering as blissful, and that would not occur were there no [distorted] mind and discernment of the unclean as clean, [443] there are eight to be abandoned by the path of seeing: (1–4) the four views, (5–6) both distorted mind and discernment holding the impermanent to be permanent, and (7–8) distorted mind and discernment holding the selfless to be a self. Also there are four wrong engagers that are objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation: both distorted mind and discernment taking suffering to be blissful and the unclean as clean.

bye brag tu smra ba rnams na re lta bas kun nas nas bslang ba'i 'du shes dang sems kho na phyin ci log yin gyi gzhan dag ni ma yin no/ / 'phags pa la 'dod chags skye ba ni 'gal me la 'khor lo dang*/ ri mo'i gzugs la gnod sbyin du 'khrul pa ltar rkyen gyi stobs kyis yud tsam 'khrul pa yin gyi phyin ci log ma yin no/ / gal te de tsam gyis phyin ci log tu 'dod na 'phags pa la bdag tu lta ba phyin ci log kyang yod par 'gyur te/ bud med dang rang nyid la sems can gyi 'du shes med par 'dod pa'i 'dod chags skye ba mi srid pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ / grub mtha' 'dzin pa snga ma gnyis las gzhan dag ni 'phags pa ngag gi dbang phyug ces bya ba rgyun du zhugs pa zhig gis gnas brtan kun dga' bo la/ 'dod pa'i chags pas zin non phyir/ / bdag gi sems ni gdung bar 'gyur/ / gau tam khyod kyis thugs brtse'i phyir/ / zhi ba mchog ni bshad du gsol zhes zhus pa'i lan du 'phags pa kun dga' bos/ 'du shes phyin ci log pa yis/ / khyod kyi sems can yongs su gdung*/ / de phyir 'dod chags ldan pa yi/ / rgyu mtshan sdug pa spong bar gyis zhes gsungs pa'i phyir sems dang 'du shes phyin ci log brgyad ka sgom spang yin la lta ba phyin ci log bzhi ni mthong spang yin no zhes zer ro/ /

Vaibhāṣikas say: Only discernment and the mind motivated by view are distorted; the others are not. Attachment generated in āryas is not distorted but momentarily mistaken due to the force of conditions like mistaking a spinning torch for a circle or mistaking a painted image for a rakṣa. If such things were asserted to be wrong engagement, then āryas would also have wrong view grasping a self. For instance, it is impossible that such desire-realm attachment can arise without [a male] discriminating himself and [an attractive] female as sentient beings. Tenet holders other than the former two say: The stream enterer Vāgīśa said to the elder Ānanda: Because I am oppressed by attachment to desire-realm objects, my mind is tormented. Gautama, have compassion on me and explain the state of supreme peace. In answer Ānanda said: Through wrong discernment your mind is thoroughly tormented. Therefore, since you possess attachment, you should abandon attractive objects.[1417] Thus the eight distorted minds and discernments are objects abandoned by the path of meditation, and the four wrong views are objects abandoned by the path of seeing.
nga rgyal bdun rnam dgu gsum po/ / mthong dang bsgom pas zad bya ba/ / bsgom pas spang bar bya ba ni/ / gsod stsogs kun nas dkris pa'o/ / 10
Pride has seven types, nine types, or three. They vanish due to seeing and meditation. Objects to be abandoned by meditation are killing and so on and the entanglements. (5:10)
lta ba la dbye ba yod par ma zad nga rgyal yang{ yul gyi sgo nas} rnam pa bdun yin no/ / gang zhe na/
It is not only view that has classifications. Pride (māna) also has seven types {by means of its object}. Question: What are they?

sems khengs pa ni nga rgyal spyi'i mtshan nyid yin la rnam pa'am yul gyi bye brag las ni chung ngu bas bdag khyad par du 'phags pa'am mnyam pa dang mnyam mo snyam nas sems khengs pa'i nga rgyal dang*/ mnyam pa bas bdag khyad par du 'phags pa'am mchog dang mnyam mo snyam pa lhag pa'i nga rgyal dang*/ khyad par du 'phags pa bas kyang bdag khyad par du 'phags so snyam pa nga rgyal las kyang nga rgyal dang*/ nyer len gyi phung po lnga la bdag gam bdag gir sems khengs pa nga'o snyam pa'i nga rgyal dang*/ bsam gtan la brten pa'i zag bcas zag med kyi yon tan ma thob pa la thob par rlom pa mngon pa'i nga rgyal dang*/ ches khyad par du 'phags pa bas bdag cung zad cig gis dman no snyam du sems khengs pa cung zad snyam pa'i nga rgyal dang*/ gsod pa la dpa' ba la sogs pa yon tan ma yin pa la yon tan du lta bas sems khengs pa log pa'i nga rgyal dang*/ 'o na mngon pa'i nga rgyal dang*/ log pa'i nga rgyal la khyad par ci yod ce na/ mngon pa'i nga rgyal ni khyad par thob par bya ba dang 'dra ba'i yon tan thob pa'i bsam pa yin pas gzhi dang bcas pa yin la/ log pa'i nga rgyal ni yon tan med pa la bdag ni yon tan dang ldan no snyam pa yin pas gzhi med pa yin no zhes TIka byed dag 'chad do/ /

Reply: In general the definition of pride is “an inflated mind,” and through pride possessing specific aspects or objects there is (1) the inflated pride where one thinks “I am superior or equal” to one who is inferior or equal, (2) excessive pride, where one thinks “I am superior or equal” to one who is equal or superior, and (3) extreme pride, where one thinks “I am superior” to one who is superior, (4) the pride of “I,” where the inflated mind thinks, “The five appropriated aggregates are ‘I’ or ‘mine,’ ” (5) higher pride, where one who has not obtained contaminated or uncontaminated qualities in dependence on the absorptions has the conceit of having obtained them, (6) slight pride, where the inflated mind thinks “I am slightly inferior” to one who is far superior, and (7) wrong pride, where the mind is inflated through viewing oneself, who lacks qualities, as having such qualities as the courage to kill. Question: What is the difference between higher pride and wrong pride? Reply: Higher pride thinks “I have obtained qualities” when one has obtained some attributes that resemble good qualities, and thus it has a basis. Wrong pride thinks “I possess qualities” [444] when one has no such qualities, and thus it has no basis. This is explained in the Subcommentary.[1418]

yang na dang po ni sa gong ma'i yon tan ma thob pa la thob bo snyam du sems khengs pa yin la/ gnyis pa ni rang sa'i yon tan dang mi ldan pa la ldan no snyam du sems khengs pa yin no zhes kha cig 'chad do/ / bye bshad las kyang nga rgyal thams cad kyang 'jig tshogs la lta ba la brten nas sems khengs pa'i mtshan nyid can du khyad par med kyang sems khengs pa'i rgyu'i bye brag gis rnam pa bdun du 'gyur la/ las ni bla ma dang gang zag yon tan can rnams la 'gyong zhing lus dag gi sri zhu med pa'i ma gus pa dang*/ ma gus pas gdams ngag ma thob pas yang srid 'byung bas na sdug bsngal 'byung ba'i rten byed pa'o zhes bshad do/ / 'o na bstan bcos ye shes la 'jug pa las/ {gzhan la ltos nas bdag la sgrub par rlom pa } bdag mchog yin no/ / bdag dang 'dra'o/ / bdag dman no/{ zhes pa gsum dang bdag la ltos nas gzhan la sgrub par rlom pa} bdag pas mchog yod do/ / bdag dang mnyam pa yod do/ / bdag pas dman pa yod do/ {zhes pa gsum dang*/ bdag la ltos na gzhan la dgag par rlom pa } bdag bsam chog med do/ / bdag dang mnyam pa med do/ / bdag pas dman pa med do snyam pa nga rgyal gyi rnam pa zhes{ pa gsum ste} nga rgyal gyi rnam pa dgu bshad pa

Again, some say: The first is the inflated mind thinking “I have obtained the qualities of higher levels” when one hasn’t obtained them. The second is the inflated mind thinking “I possess qualities of my level” when one doesn’t possess them. Also the Great Treatise on Differentiation explains: Though no pride is separate from the mind inflated due to the afflicted view of the self, seven aspects arise through specific causes that inflate the mind. It functions to treat gurus and persons who have qualities with disrespect through rudeness and lack of physical and verbal deference. It leads to suffering in future rebirths since one does not obtain instruction due to disrespect.[1419] Attainment of Knowledge states: {There are three} types of pride thinking “I am superior, I am equal, I am inferior,” {which is the conceit inflating one’s own status when compared to others. There are three thinking} “One who is better than me exists, one who is equal to me exists, one who is inferior to me exists,” {which is the conceit inflating the status of others when compared to oneself. There are three thinking} “One superior to me does not exist, one equal to me does not exist, one inferior to me does not exist,” {which is the conceit negating the status of others when compared to oneself.}[1420] This explains the nine types of pride.

ji ltar drang zhe na/ de las nga rgyal rnam pa dgu gsungs pa ni 'dir bshad pa'i lta ba la rten pa'i nga rgyal dang*/ lhag pa'i nga rgyal dang*/ cung zad snyam pa'i nga rgyal rnam pa gsum po dag gi nang du 'du bar 'gyur te/ thog mar nga'o snyam du bdag lta 'byung la/ de nas nga rgyal 'byung bas na lta ba la rten pa'i nga rgyal zhes bya'o/ / 'di ltar rang dang mnyam pa la dmigs nas bdag mchog yin no snyam pa ni lhag pa'i nga rgyal lo/ / bdag dang 'dra'o snyam pa ni nga rgyal lo/ / rang bas mchog la dmigs nas bdag dman no snyam pa ni cung zad snyam pa'i nga rgyal lo/ / mchog la dmigs nas bdag pas mchog yod do snyam pa ni cung zad snyam pa'i nga rgyal lo/ / mnyam pa la dmigs nas bdag dang mnyam pa yod do snyam pa ni nga rgyal lo/ / mnyam pa la dmigs nas bdag pas dman pa yod do snyam pa ni lhag pa'i nga rgyal lo/ / rang bas dman pa la dmigs nas bdag pas mchog med do zhes bya ba ni nga rgyal lo/ / mnyam pa la dmigs nas bdag dang mnyam pa med do zhes bya ba ni lhag pa'i nga rgyal lo/ / mchog la dmigs nas bdag pas dman pa med do snyam pa ni cung zad snyam pa'i nga rgyal lo/ /

Question: How are those interpreted? Reply: The nine types stated in this text are subsumed in three types explained here — pride dependent on view, excessive pride, and slight pride. Initially the view of self thinking “I” occurs, then pride arises that is called pride dependent on view. If it focuses on those who are equal to oneself and thinks “I am superior,” it is excessive pride. If it thinks “I am equal,” it is pride [dependent on view]. If it focuses on those who are [greatly] superior to oneself and thinks “I am [slightly] inferior,” it is slight pride. If it focuses on those who [appear] equal [but are superior] and thinks “I am equal,” it is pride [dependent on view]. If it focuses on those who are equal and thinks “They are inferior to me,” it is excessive pride. If it focuses on those who are inferior to me and thinks “I am not superior to them,” it is pride [dependent on view]. If it focuses on those who are equal and thinks “They are not equal to me,” it is excessive pride. If it focuses on those who are superior and thinks “I am not inferior to them,” it is slight pride.

gal te ches khyad par du 'phags pa bas bdag cung zad cig gis dman no snyam pa ni khengs pa'i gnas yin pas cung zad snyam pa'i nga rgyal du rigs na bdag pas dman pa med do snyam pa 'di ji ltar nga rgyal yin zhe na/ tshogs pa 'di na bdag pas dman pa med mod kyi 'on kyang bdag kyang bzang ngo zhes khengs pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di ni ye shes la 'jug pa las bshad pa ste/ rab tu byed pa'i rkang pa las ni bdag mchog yin no snyam pa 'di ni dman pa la ltos nas nga rgyal dang*/ mnyam pa la ltos nas lhag pa'i nga rgyal dang khyad par du 'phags pa la ltos nas nga rgyal las kyang nga rgyal yin no zhes bya ba bshad do/ / gsum po de dag gi mtshan nyid tshang ba'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du lhag ma rnams la'ang ci rigs par shes par bya'o/ /

Question: If thinking “I am slightly inferior” with respect to one who is far superior is slight pride, since it is an inflated state, then how could the thought “One inferior to me does not exist” be pride? Reply: In this group indeed there may be none inferior to me, but stating “I am good” is nevertheless an inflated state. This is explained in the Attainment of Knowledge. [445] The verses of the treatise explain that thinking “I am superior” is pride reliant on those who are inferior, that excessive pride relies on those who are equal, and that extreme pride relies on those who are superior.[1421] This completes the definitions of these three. Similarly, also the remaining [types of pride] should be understood as possessing various types.

sngar bshad pa'i nga rgyal bdun po de dag thams cad kyang mthong ba dang sgom pas zad par bya ba yin te/ lhan cig skyes pa ni sgom spang dang*/ kun tu brtags pa ni mthong spang yin pa'i phyir ram/ yang na bye brag tu smra ba'i grub pa'i mthas mthong spang la dmigs pa ni mthong spang yin la/ sgom spang la dmigs pa ni sgom spang yin pa'i phyir ro/ / ci 'phags pa rnams sgom spang ma spangs pa gang yin pa de spyod dam zhe na/ des nges pa med de/{ dad sogs zag bcas dang gnyid dang mig sogs dbang po dang sdug bsngal gyi dbang po rnams ma spangs kyang spyod la}

all the previously explained seven prides vanish (kṣaya) due to the paths of seeing and meditation, because those that are innate are objects abandoned by the path of meditation and those that are mentally fabricated are objects abandoned by the path of seeing. Again, according to the tenets of the Vaibhāṣikas, those [prideful minds] focusing on objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing are objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing, and those focusing on objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation are objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation. Question: Do āryas engage in any actions that are objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation that are not yet abandoned? Reply: There is no certainty, {for they engage in contaminated actions such as faith and so on, or sleep, or utilize faculties such as the eyes, or experience the faculty of pain that is not yet abandoned}.

bsgom pas spang bar bya ba ni gsod pa dang sogs{ pa lus dag gi nyes spyod bdun} pas bsdus pa ma byin par len pa la sogs pa'i mi dge ba lus ngag gi las gang dag yin pa nyon mongs pa kun nas dkris pa rnams kyis bslang ba bdun po de dag kyang yin te/ de dag sgom spang gi chos gzugs can kho na la dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ / {de dag ni ma spangs kyang mi spyod de rgyas byed log lta spangs pa'i phyir rked pa bcag na langs mi shes pa bzhin } 'o na 'jig tshogs la lta ba la sogs pa rnams kyang sgom spang nyer len gyi phung po zag bcas la dmigs pa'i phyir sgom spang du 'gyur ro zhe na/ sgom spang kho na la dmigs pa rnams sgom spang yin na 'jig tshogs la lta ba la sogs pa ni sgom spang la'ang dmigs par byed mod kyi sgom spang kho na la ni dmigs pa ma yin pas sgom spang ma yin no zhes TI ka las 'chad do/ /
de bzhin 'jig sred 'phags pa la/ / rnam sogs nga'o snyam mi 'byung / / lta bas rgyas par 'gyur phyir ro/ / mi dge'i 'gyod pa'ang ma yin no/ / 11
So too, craving destruction, pride thinking “I” and its nine types do not occur in āryas because objects abandoned increase through view. Also regret for nonvirtue does not occur. (5:11)

ji ltar gsod pa la sogs pa sgom spang yin pa de bzhin du 'jig pa la sred pa dang skye ba la sred pa'ang yin no/ / de la 'jig pa la sred pa ni khams gsum pa'i bdag med par gyur kyang ci ma rung snyam du mi rtag pa don du gnyer ba'o/{ de 'phags pa la mi 'byung ste log lta spangs pas so/ /} skye ba la sred pa ni bdag dbang po dang lus ngan po la sogs par skyes na ci ma rung snyam du khams gsum du skye bar smon pa'o/ / {de 'phags pa la mi 'byung ste rtag lta spangs pas so } 'grel pa las ni de bzhin zhes bya ba'i sgras ni skye ba'i srid pa'i phyogs bdag ni glang po che'i rgyal po sa srung gi bur gyur kyang ci ma rung zhes bya ba de lta bu la sogs pa gzung ngo zhes bshad do/ / de dag sgom spang yin kyang 'phags pa rnams la mi 'byung ngo zhes 'brel lo/ / gang mi 'byung zhe na/ nga'o snyam pa'i nga rgyal dang nga rgyal gyi rnam pa dgu po sgom spang gi phyogs la sogs pa'o zhes sbyar ro/ / sogs pas ni gsod pa nas 'jig pa dang skye ba'i sred pa'i bar gzung ngo*/ / ci'i phyir de dag ma spangs kyang 'phags pa la mi 'byung zhe na/

Just as killing and so on are objects abandoned by the path of meditation, so too are craving destruction (vibhava) and craving birth. Craving destruction is seeking to end one’s continued existence by thinking, “Why shouldn’t I, who exist in the three realms, cease to exist?” {That does not occur for āryas, since they abandon wrong view}. Craving birth is wishing for birth in the three realms by thinking, “Why shouldn’t I be born with an excellent body and sense faculties?” {That does not occur for āryas, since they abandon the view of permanence.} The Autocommentary explains: The term “so too” means, for example, wishing for a birth existence by saying, “Why shouldn’t I become Airāvaṇa, the son of the king of the elephants?” and so on.[1423] [446] Though these are objects abandoned by the path of meditation, they do not occur in āryas. Question: What do not occur? Reply: Pride thinking “I,” the nine types of pride, objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, and so on do not occur. The “and so on” refers to those from killing up to craving, destruction, and birth. Question: Why do those that are not abandoned, not arise in āryas?

sgom spang de dag ni lta ba sngon du 'gro ba'i sgo nas rgyas par 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ kun nas slong zhing gsos 'debs byed kyi lta ba rnams kyang bden pa mthong ba tsam gyis spong ba'i phyir rked pa bcag pa'i mis ldang mi nus pa bzhin no/ / 'di ltar gsod pa la sogs pa ni las 'bras med par lta ba'i log ltas rgyas par 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ nga rgyal gyi rnam pa dgu po dang*/ nga'o snyam pa'i nga rgyal sgom spang gi phyogs kyis bsdus pa rnams kyang 'jig tshogs la lta bas gsos 'debs shing rgyas par 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ 'jig pa'i sred pa ni mthar 'dzin par lta ba'i chad ltas rgyas par 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ skye ba'i sred pa ni mthar 'dzin par lta ba'i rtag ltas rgyas par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: That is because objects abandoned by the path of meditation increase through the view that precedes them, and views that motivate and nourish them are abandoned by merely seeing the four truths. It is like a person who has broken a leg being unable to stand up. Thus killing and so on are increased by wrong view that views karma and its result as nonexistent. The nine types of pride and the pride thinking “I” that are included within objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation are nourished and increased by the afflicted view of the self. Craving destruction is increased by the view grasping the extreme of annihilation. Craving birth is increased by the view grasping the extreme of permanence.

de bzhin du mi dge ba'i bdag nyid kyi 'gyod pa'ang ngan par byas pa sgom spang lus ngag gi las la dmigs pas sgom spang yin kyang de ni the tshom las 'gyod ces 'byung bas the tshom gyis kun nas bslang ba'i phyir dang*/ kun nas slong byed the tshom de yang bden pa mthong ba tsam gyis spangs pa'i phyir 'phags pa la 'byung ba ma yin no/ / kha cig spangs kyang 'phags pa rnams kun du spyod pa'ang yod de/ 'jig rten pa'i dad pa dang gnyid dang sdug bsngal gyi dbang po dang mig la sogs pa rnams 'dod par skyes pa'i 'phags pa rnams la 'byung ba'i phyir ro zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/ /

So too, also regret for states of nonvirtue and immorality, since it focuses on physical and verbal karma that are objects abandoned by the path of meditation, is an object to be abandoned by the path of meditation. However, since it is called “regret arising from doubt” and is thus motivated by doubt, it does not occur in āryas because that which motivates doubt is abandoned by the path of seeing alone. Some say: Though it is abandoned, āryas always engage in it because mundane faith, sleep, the faculties of pain and the eyes and so on occur in āryas born in the desire realm.[1424] This is stated by Master Pūrṇavardhana.
rnam pa'i rab dbye bshad pa/
23. The Typology of Negative Tendencies

gnyis pa phra rgyas kyi rnam pa'i rab tu dbye ba bshad pa la kun 'gro dang kun 'gro ma yin pa dang*/ zag bcas zag med la dmigs pa dang*/ rgyas pa dang mi rgyas pa dang*/ mi dge ba dang lung ma bstan gyi dbye ba dang*/ mi dge ba dang lung ma bstan gyi rtsa ba bshad pa dang*/ ldan pa'i tshul dang*/ chos du'i yul can yin pa dang*/ go rim dang*/ skye ba'i rgyu dang*/ zag pa la sogs pa mdo las gsungs pa'i rnam pa'i dbye ba bshad pa bcu las

THIS HAS TEN HEADINGS: (1) pervasive and nonpervasive, (2) those focusing on the contaminated and uncontaminated, (3) how they increase, (4) those that are nonvirtuous or neutral, (5) the roots of nonvirtue and neutral states, (6) how one possesses them, (7) how phenomena become their objects, (8) the sequence of their arising, (9) the causes giving rise to them, and (10) the taxonomy of contaminants and so on in the sūtras.
kun 'gro dang kun 'gro ma yin pa/
Pervasive and nonpervasive negative tendencies
dang po ni phra rgyas dgu bcu rtsa brgyad po de dag las du ni kun du 'gro ba yin du ni ma yin zhe na zhes bya ba'i dri ba ni 'og ma rnams la'ang shes par bya'o/ /
Question: From among those ninety-eight negative tendencies, which are pervasive and which are not? [447] Reply: Understand this as follows.
sdug bsngal rgyu mthong spang bya ba/ / lta dang de bzhin the tshom dang / / gang de lhan cig ma 'dres pa'i/ / ma rig gang yin kun tu 'gro/ / 12
Views abandoned by seeing suffering and cause, and so too doubts, ignorance simultaneously concomitant with any of those, and unmixed ignorance are pervasive. (5:12)

{'dir mthong spang dang po gnyis kyi dngos su log zhugs ni kun 'gro dang gzhan ni min par 'dod pas } de la sdug bsngal mthong bas spang bar bya ba'i lta ba lnga dang*/ de'i rgyu kun 'byung mthong bas spang bar bya ba'i lta ba gnyis dang*/ ji ltar lta ba bdun po kun 'gro yin pa de bzhin du bden pa gnyis po de dag mthong bas spang bar bya ba'i the tshom gnyis dang lta ba dang the tshom gang yin pa de dag dang lhan cig mtshungs par ldan pa'i ma rig pa dang rtsa ba'i nyon mongs pa gzhan dang ma 'dres pa'i ma rig pa gang yin pa sdug bsngal mthong spang dang kun 'byung mthong spang gnyis te de ltar na phra rgyas bcu gcig po de dag ni kun du 'gro ba yin te/ skal ba mnyam pa'i khams kyi spang bya nyon mongs can ris lnga po kun du dmigs shing{ de dag} skyed{ pa'i rgyu yin} pas khyab par 'gro ba'i phyir ro/ / des na bden pa dang po gnyis kyi lta ba dang the tshom dang mtshungs par ldan pa dang ma 'dres pa'i ma rig pa kho na kun 'gro yin gyi 'dod chags la sogs pa dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i ma rig pa ni kun 'gro ma yin no/ / skal ba mnyam pa'i khams kun du 'gro ba zhes bya ba ni 'dod pa'i de dag gis 'dod pa'i khams mtha' dag la dmigs pa yin pas so/ / {bden pa dang po gnyis kyi lta ba la sogs pa kho na kun 'gror bzhag pa ni rang sa'i zag bcas thams cad la dmigs pas bsags pas brtan zhing stobs dang ldan la/ 'gog lam mthong spang ni de lta ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / sgom spang bzhi ni rang gi mtshan nyid pa'i nyon mongs yin pas yul zag bcas thams cad la dmigs mi nus pas kun 'gro min no }

{Here it is asserted that [minds] that directly misconceive the first two truths that are to be abandoned by the path of seeing are pervasive and the others are not. Therefore} eleven are pervasive: (1–5) the five views abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering, and (6–7) two views abandoned by seeing the truth of origin that is the cause of that. And just as those seven are pervasive, so too (8–9) the two doubts abandoned by seeing those two truths, (10) ignorance simultaneously concomitant with any of those views and doubts, and (11) any ignorance unmixed (āvenika) with other root afflictions that are both objects abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering and objects abandoned by seeing the truth of origin are pervasive (sarvatraga) because they always focus on the five types of afflicted objects of abandonment in the same realm. Since these eleven {are causes} generating {them}, they function pervasively. Therefore views and doubt engaging the first two truths, ignorance concomitant with them, and unmixed ignorance alone are pervasive. Ignorance concomitant with attachment and so on is not pervasive. Those of the same realm are called “pervasive” since those of the desire realm focus on the entire desire realm. {Only the views of the first two truths and so on are posited as pervasive because they possess stability and potency through focusing on, and accumulating, all contaminated states of their level. Objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of cessation and path are not like that. The four objects abandoned by the path of meditation are incapable of focusing on all contaminated objects and thus are not pervasive; they are afflictions engaging specific characteristics.}

gal te de lta na rang gi skal ba mnyam pa'i khams mtha' dag la rim gyis sam cig car dmigs/ dang po ltar na 'dod chags la sogs pa'ang kun 'gror 'gyur la/ gnyis pa ltar na 'dod pa'i khams mtha' dag gis 'dag par 'dzin pa la sogs pa mi srid pa'i phyir tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog 'dzin de dag kyang kun 'gro{ lta ba lnga po'ang} ma yin par 'gyur ro zhe na/ rdzas ma lus pa la de ltar mi srid kyang 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal mthong spang la sogs pa'i ris lnga po thams cad la dmigs shing thams cad kyis 'dag par 'dzin pa la sogs pa srid pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te de lta na'ang yul nyer len gyi phung po lnga po gang la bdag tu lta ba yod pa de la bdag tu sred pa yod la de yang 'dod chags yin zhing*/ gang la mchog dang grol ba'i rgyur lta ba de don du gnyer zhing de las nga rgyal du 'gyur bas na 'dod chags dang nga rgyal yang kun 'gror 'gyur te/ lta ba de dag ni skal ba mnyam pa'i khams mtha' dag la dmigs la/ nyon mongs pa gnyis po de dag kyang lta ba'i yul la 'jug pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ bye brag tu smra ba ni/ de lta mod kyi 'dod chags dang nga rgyal ni phyogs gcig la dmigs pas rang gi mtshan nyid pa yin gyi spyi pa ma yin pa'i phyir kun 'gro ma yin te/ kun 'gro ni spang bya'i rigs lnga char la cig car du dmigs pa la 'dod pa'i phyir ro zhes lan 'debs so/ / des na 'dod chags dang nga rgyal mthong spang la dmigs pa ni mthong spang dang*/ sgom spang la dmigs pa ni sgom spang yin no zhes bya ba 'di 'dod do/ / slob dpon ni mthong spang lta ba'i dbang gis zhugs pa'i 'dod chags dang nga rgyal ni mthong spang yin la/ sgom spang gi nyon mongs pa'i dbang gis zhugs pa ni sgom spang yin no/ / yang na mthong spang la dmigs pa'i de gnyis ni mthong spang dang gnyis ka 'dren ma la dmigs pa ni sgom spang yin par bzhed do/ /

Objection: Do they focus on all states of the same realm serially or at the same time? (1) According to the first possibility, even attachment and so on would be pervasive. (2) According to the second possibility, clinging to rules and ritual as supreme {as well as the five views} would not be pervasive because it would be impossible that it could grasp all states of the desire realm as pure [at the same time] and so on. Reply: Although that would be impossible regarding all substance, it is possible to focus on all five types of abandonment, such as objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering in the desire realm and so on, and grasp them as pure. Objection: When the view exists that any of the five appropriated aggregates are the self, then craving that as the self also exists, and that is attachment. And since pride arises from taking that view to be supreme and the cause of liberation, then attachment and pride would be pervasive because those views focus on all states of the same realm, and those two afflictions also engage the objects of those views. Vaibhāṣikas reply: Indeed, that is so. But attachment and pride engage specific characteristics and not general characteristics, since they focus [448] on one part of the object. They are not pervasive because it is accepted that pervasive negative tendencies focus at the same time on the five types of object of abandonment. Therefore they [the Vaibhāṣikas] assert that attachment and pride that focus on objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing are objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing, and those that focus on objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation are objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation. Vasubandhu asserts that attachment and pride that engage objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing by the power of view are objects abandoned by the path of seeing, and those that engage objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation by the power of affliction are objects abandoned by the path of meditation. Again, those two that focus on objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing are objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing, and those two that focus on a mixture of both are objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation.[1425]
de dag las dgu gong du dmigs/ / lta ba gnyis po ma gtogs so/ / de dag dang ni lhan cig gang / / 'byung de'ang kun 'gro thob ma gtogs/ / 13
Nine among those, excluding the two views, focus on higher realms. Any that simultaneously arise with those are also pervasive, except for obtainment. (5:13)

phra rgyas bcu gcig po de dag las dgu ni khams gong ma skal ba mi mnyam pa'i khams dag tu dmigs pas skal ba mi mnyam pa'i khams kun 'gro yin te/ 'jig tshogs la lta ba dang mthar 'dzin par lta ba gnyis po ma gtogs pas so/ / de yang rang gi phung po la bdag tu lta ba dang de rtag chad du lta ba ni 'jig tshogs la lta ba dang mthar 'dzin par lta ba yin pa na 'og ma dang gong ma dag rgyud dang phung po tha dad pa'i phyir ro/ / tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog 'dzin ni rang gi rgyud du gtogs pa las gzhan la'ang 'jug pa'i phyir gong ma la dmigs pa yin te/ bstan bcos las/ res dga' ni skal ba mi snyam pa'i khams gcig la dmigs so/ / res 'ga' ni gnyis la dmigs te 'dod pa dang ldan pa gzugs dang ldan pa la dmigs pa rnams dang*/ 'dod pa dang ldan pa gzugs med pa dang ldan pa la dmigs pa rnams dang*/ 'dod pa dang ldan pa gzugs dang gzugs med pa dang ldan pa la dmigs pa'i phra rgyas gang dag yin pa zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / des na lta ba dang po gnyis ma gtogs pa'i kun 'gro rnams kyis khams gong ma la dmigs kyi kun 'gro ma yin pa rnams kyis ni ma yin la/ khams dang sa gong ma'i ni nyon mongs pa thams cad kyis kyang 'og ma la mi dmigs te/ kun las btus pas kyang ma rig pa dang lta ba dang the tshom ma gtogs par 'dod pa na spyod pa'i nyon mongs pa ni sa gong ma la mi dmigs so/ / sa gong ma'i nyon mongs pa ni sa 'og ma la dmigs pa ma yin no zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/ /

Nine among those eleven negative tendencies, excluding the two views of the afflicted view of the self and extreme view, are pervasive in different realms since they focus on different higher realms. Further, if viewing one’s aggregates as a self and viewing that self as permanent or annihilated are, respectively, the afflicted view of the self and extreme view, then those views of higher or lower realms would have distinct mindstreams and aggregates. Clinging to rules and ritual as supreme focuses on higher realms because it also engages other states separate from one’s mindstream. The treatise (Topic Divisions)[1426] states: At times it focuses on different realms and at times it focuses on both, since it is a negative tendency that focuses on the desire and form realms, or it focuses on the desire and the formless realms, or it focuses on the desire, form, and the formless realms.[1427] Therefore pervasive negative tendencies, except for the first two views, focus on the two higher realms, but those that are not pervasive do not. All afflictions of the higher realms and levels do not focus on those lower because the Compendium of Abhidharma explains: Except for ignorance, view, and doubt, afflictions that engage desire-realm objects do not focus on higher-realm objects. No afflictions of higher levels focus on objects of lower levels.[1428]

{'dod pa na skal ba mnyam pa dang mi mnyam pa'i sa dang khams la dmigs pa thams cad yod la/ bsam gtan bzhi pa na skal ba mnyam pa'i khams la dmigs pa med la/ srid rtse na skal ba mnyam pa'i sa la dmigs pa kho na yod do zhes so/ / 'dir skal ba mi mnyam pa'i khams gcig gam gnyis bsdoms pa la dmigs pa sred kyi gsum bsdoms pa la dmigs nus pa ni med do/ }

{In the desire realm, all focus on the same or different levels and realms, but in the fourth absorption, there are none that focus on the same realm. In the summit of existence, only those that focus on the same level exist. Here it is possible that they focus on one or two different realms together, but they cannot focus on three together.}

gal te lta ba dang po gnyis gong ma la mi dmigs na 'dod pa pa dag tshangs pa la sems can du lta ba dang*/ de rtag par lta ba de ji ltar zhe na/ tshangs pa la sems can du lta ba de ni tshangs pa la bdag dang bdag gir mi 'dzin pas 'jig tshogs la lta ba ma yin la/ tshangs pa la rtag par lta ba'ang mthar 'dzin par lta ba ma yin te/ de ni 'jig tshogs la lta bas kun nas bslang ba yin pa la 'jig tshogs la lta ba med pa'i phyir ro/ / chos mngon pa ba rnams ni tshangs pa la dmigs pa de ni log pa'i shes pa yin gyi lta ba lngar ni mi bgrang ba'i phyir ro zhes 'dod do/ / yang ci phra rgyas kho na kun 'gro yin nam zhe na ma yin te/

Question: If the first two views do not focus on higher realms, how do desire-realm beings view Brahma as a sentient being? And how is he viewed as permanent? Reply: Since the view that Brahma [449] is a sentient being does not hold Brahma as “I” or “mine,” it is not the afflicted view of the self. Also, the view that Brahma is permanent is not extreme view because that is motivated by the afflicted view of the self, and in this case there is no afflicted view of the self. Ābhidharmikas assert that view focusing on Brahma is a distorted consciousness that is not counted among the five views. Question: Are negative tendencies alone pervasive? Reply: No.

phra rgyas bcu gcig po de dag dang ni lhan cig tu 'byung ba'i chos gang dag yin pa sems dang sems byung tshor ba la sogs pa mtshungs ldan rnams dang*/ mtshan nyid la sogs pa de'ang kun 'gro yin no zhes spyir btang nas thob pa ni ma gtogs so zhes dmigs kyis bsal te/ phra rgyas de dag dang thob pa {rnam smin dang rgyu mthun gyi} 'bras bu mi gcig pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir phra rgyas kun 'gro dang rgyu kun 'gro la mu bzhi las/ dang po{ phra rgyas kun 'gro yin la rgyu kun 'gro min pa} ni ma 'ongs pa'i phra rgyas kun 'gro rnams so/ / gnyis pa ni 'das da ltar gyi phra rgyas kun 'gro dang lhan cig 'byung ba rnams so/ / gsum pa ni 'das da ltar gyi phra rgyas kun 'gro rnams so/ / bzhi pa ni de dag ma gtogs pa ma 'ongs pa'i lhan cig 'byung ba dang thob pa la sogs pa'o/ /

In general any phenomena that simultaneously arise with those eleven negative tendencies — such as concomitant minds and mental factors like feeling and so on as well as their characteristics and so forth — are also pervasive (sarvatraga), except for obtainment (prāpti). This exception arises because the obtainment and results {of karmic maturation and natural outflow} of these negative tendencies are not the same. Thus there are four possibilities for pervasive negative tendencies and pervasive causes: (1) The first, {that which is a pervasive negative tendency and that which is not a pervasive cause,} is a future pervasive negative tendency. (2) The second is that arising simultaneously with a past or present pervasive negative tendency. (3) The third is a past or present pervasive negative tendency. (4) The fourth is the obtainment or that arising simultaneously with a future negative tendency that is other than those.

des na phra rgyas dgu bcu rtsa brgyad las kun 'gro kho na nyi shu rtsa bdun dang*/ de ma yin pa drug cu rtsa lnga dang*/ bden pa dang po gnyis kyi spang bya ba ma rig pa drug kar dngos su bstan pas shugs la kun 'gro rnams bden pa dang po gnyis kyi mtshan nyid dang 'gal bar zhugs pas dngos su log zhugs dang*/ kun 'gro ma yin pa rnams dngos po la dmigs kyang mtshan nyid dang mi 'gal bas log zhugs la log zhugs yin no zhes bstan pa yin no/ /

Therefore, from the ninety-eight negative tendencies it is explicitly taught that (1–27) twenty-seven are pervasive alone, (28–92) sixty-five are not pervasive, and (93–98) the six ignorances are objects to be abandoned in relation to the first two truths. It is implicitly taught that pervasive states that directly misconceive [their objects] by the force of excluding those characteristics of the first two truths, and those that are not pervasive misconceive those that wrongly engage [their objects] by not excluding those characteristics, though they focus on functional things.
THOSE THAT DIRECTLY MISCONCEIVE THEIR OBJECT

gong ma ba dag ni lta ba dang po gsum dang ma rig pa dang the tshom lnga ni rim pa ltar bden pa la nga dang nga yir 'dzin pa dang*/ rtag chad du sgro 'dogs pa dang*/ med do zhes skur ba 'debs pa dang*/ gnas lugs mi shes pa dang*/ mtha' gzhan du dogs pas dngos su log zhugs dang*/

Regarding the former, five — (1–3) the first three views, (4) ignorance, and (5) doubt — directly misconceive their objects by, respectively, (1) holding the truths as “I” and “mine,” (2) overestimating them to be permanent or annihilated, (3) underestimating them to be nonexistent, (4) not knowing their mode of being, and (5) doubting other extremes.
MINDS THAT MISCONCEIVE THOSE THAT WRONGLY ENGAGE THEIR OBJECTS
'dod chags dang nga rgyal dang lta ba phyi ma gnyis te bzhi ni rim pa ltar lta ba dang po gsum la sred cing khengs la mchog dang dag grol gyi rgyur 'dzin pas log pa la log zhugs dang*/

Four — (6) attachment, (7) pride, and (8–9) the last two views — misconceive those that wrongly engage [their objects] by, respectively, (6) craving the first three views, (7) inflating them, (8) clinging to them as supreme, and (9) clinging to them as the cause of purity and liberation.
MINDS THAT MISCONCEIVE BY THE POWER OF DISTURBANCE
khong khro ni rang dang lta ba mi mthun pa rnams la 'khrug pas dbang gis log zhugs zhes log zhugs gsum du 'chad do/ /

(10) Anger misconceives [its object] due to the power of the state of disturbance directed to those who have different views from one’s own. These are said to be the three types of misconception [or wrong engagement].
gnyis pa zag bcas zag med la dmigs pa'i dbye ba ni
Those focusing on the contaminated and uncontaminated
'gog dang lam mthong spang bya ba/ / log lta the tshom de dag dang / / ldan dang 'ba' zhig ma rig dang / / drug ni zag med spyod yul can/ / 14
Objects to be abandoned by seeing cessation and path are six: [two] wrong views, [two] doubts, ignorance concomitant with those, and ignorance alone. They possess uncontaminated objects. (5:14)

'gog pa dang lam mthong bas spang bar bya ba log lta gnyis dang the tshom gnyis dang*/ bzhi po de dag dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i ma rig pa dang*/ ma 'dres pa 'ba' zhig pa'i ma rig pa 'gog lam mthong spang gnyis dang bcas pa drug {gam khams kyis phye na bco brgyad} ni zag pa med pa'i spyod yul can yin te/ de dag ni 'gog lam gyi bden pa la log par rtog pa yin la bden pa de gnyis kyang zag med yin pa'i phyir ro/ / {'o na bden pa mthong bar thal lo zhe na ma nges te rnam pa phyin ci log tu zhugs pa'i phyir ro } gzhan {lhag ma brgyad cu po} dag ni zag pa dang bcas pa'i chos kyi yul can yin no/ /

The objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of cessation and path are six: (1–2) two wrong views (mithyādṛg), (3–4) two doubts (vimati), (5) ignorance concomitant with those four, and (6) unmixed ignorance alone. {Or, if classified by realm, [450] they are eighteen.} They possess uncontaminated objects (gocara) because they are misconceptions of the truths of cessation and path, and those two truths are uncontaminated. {Objection: It follows that they would see those truths. Reply: That is not certain because they wrongly engage their aspects}. The remaining {eighty} negative tendencies take contaminated phenomena as objects.
'o na sa gang gi log lta la sogs pas sa gang gi gnyen po 'gog lam la dmigs she na/
Objection: Wrong view and so on that exists on any level focuses on the truths of cessation and path that are its antidotes on any level.
rang gi sa pa'i 'gog pa dang / / lam ni phan tshun rgyu yin pas/ / sa drug sa dgu'i lam ni de'i/ / spyod yul can gyi yul yin no/ / 15
Cessation of its level and path are objects of those that possess that object dependent on six levels and nine levels. They are the causes of each other. (5:15)

'gog pa la dmigs pa'i log lta la sogs pa ni rang rang gi sa pa'i gnyen po 'gog pa kho na la dmigs pa yin te/ 'dod pa'i log lta la sogs pas 'dod pa'i gnyen po 'gog pa la dmigs pa la sogs pa nas srid rtse'i bar du sbyar ro/ / lam ni dang po'i nyer bsdogs la sogs pa zag med kyi sa drug la rten pa'i lam chos shes pa de'i spyod yul can 'dod pa'i log lta {the tshom rmongs pa} la sogs pa gsum gyi yul yin te/ 'dod pa'i gnyen po yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du khams gong ma gnyis kyi gnyen po yin pa'i phyir sa drug po de dang gzugs med dang po gsum ste sa dgu la rten pa'i lam rjes su shes pa ni rjes shes de'i spyod yul can bsam gtan dang po nas srid rtse'i bar gyi log lta la sogs pa gsum gyi yul yin no/ /

Wrong view and so on focusing on the truth of cessation focuses on the truth of cessation that is the antidote of its level alone. In other words, desire-realm wrong view and so on focuses on the truth of cessation that is the antidote of desire-realm affliction, and this is applied up to the summit of existence. The path that is Dharma knowledge of the truth of path (mārge-dharmajñāna) dependent on the six uncontaminated levels, such as access concentration to the first absorption and so on, is the object of three negative tendencies: wrong view, doubt, and confusion [or ignorance] of the desire realm that possesses that object (gocara) because it is the antidote of desire-realm affliction. Similarly, subsequent knowledge of the truth of path (mārge’nvaya jñāna) dependent on the nine levels — the six levels plus the first three formless-realm levels — is an object of three negative tendencies: wrong view and so on that possess that object from the first absorption to the summit of existence because it is the antidote of affliction of the two higher realms.

gal te gong ma rten pa'i lam de dag 'og ma'i log lta la sogs pa'i yul du ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/ sa gong ma dang 'og ma'i lam ni sa dgu'i lam ni phan tshun du/ mnyam dang khyad par can gyi yin/ / zhes 'byung bas phan tshun skal ba mnyam pa'i rgyu yin pas so/ /
'o na ni rjes shes dang chos shes pa'i lam ni phan tshun skal mnyam gyi rgyu yin pa'i phyir rjes su shes pa la chos shes pa'i lam la dmigs pa 'dod pa'i log lta la sogs pa'i yul du 'gyur ro zhe na/ de lta mod kyi rjes shes 'dod pa'i gnyen po ma yin pa'i phyir 'dod pa'i log lta la sogs pa'i yul du mi 'gyur ro/ /
'o na chos shes pa'i lam yang gzugs dang gzugs med na spyod pa'i log lta sogs pa'i yul du 'gyur te/ bsgom pa'i lam la 'gog pa dang*/ / lam la chos shes gang yin de/ / khams gsum gyi ni gnyen po yin/ / zhes 'chad par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro zhe na/

Question: How do those paths dependent on higher levels become objects of wrong view of lower levels and so on? Reply: Paths of higher and lower levels are the homogeneous causes of each other, since the Abhidharmakośa states, “The path of the nine levels is a common cause of those equal or superior” (2:52cd).
Objection: Because the paths of subsequent knowledge (anvayajñāna) and Dharma knowledge (dharmajñāna) are homogeneous causes of each other, subsequent knowledge would become the object of desire-realm wrong view that focuses on the path of Dharma knowledge. Reply: Indeed, that is so, but subsequent knowledge is not the object of desire-realm wrong view and so on because it is not the antidote of desire-realm affliction.
Objection: But the path of Dharma knowledge becomes the object of wrong view and so on manifesting in the form and formless realms, because the Abhidharmakośa explains, “On the path of meditation, Dharma knowledge regarding cessation or path is an antidote to the three realms” (7:9abc).

de ltar 'chad mod kyi {'on kyang 'di ni mtha' dag gi gnyen po byed pa dang mi byed pas phye ba yin te de yang mdzod kyi } 'grel pa las/ dang po med pa'i phyir dang*/ dang po rnams kyi ma yin pa'i phyir dmigs pa ma yin no zhes 'byung ste/ de dag gi don ni chos shes pa ni khams gong ma gnyis kyi log lta la sogs pa'i dmigs pa ma yin te/ de de dag gi gnyen po ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de nyid ji ltar zhe na/ 'di ltar chos shes pa mtha' dag kyang khams gong ma'i gnyen po ma yin te/ bden bzhi la chos shes pa rnams kyi dang po bden pa dang po gnyis kyi chos shes pa gzugs dang gzugs med pa'i gnyen por med pa'i phyir ro/ / gong ma mtha' dag gi yang gnyen po ma yin te/{ chos ni dang po khams gong gi} mthong spang gi gnyen po ma yin pa'i phyir ro zhes pa'o/ / des na de dang mthun par slob dpon gang spel gyis kyang dang po ste sgom lam gyis bsdus pa'i sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung la chos shes pa gnyis ni khams gong ma gnyis kyi gnyen por med pa'i phyir dang*/ sgom spang la ltos nas dang po khams gong ma gnyis kyi mthong spang rnams kyis gnyen po chos shes ma yin pa'i phyir khams gong ma gnyis kyi log lta la sogs pa ni chos shes la dmigs pa ma yin no zhes bshad pas de ltar bye brag tu smra bas lan 'debs mod kyi 'on kyang 'di dag grub pa'i mtha' tshad mar byas pa tsam zad do/ / de ltar na khams gsum gyi phra rgyas bco brgyad zag med la dmigs par bshad pas lhag ma phra rgyas brgyad cu ni zag bcas la dmigs par 'gyur ro/ / yang ci'i phyir log lta la sogs pa de dag kho na zag med la dmigs pa yin gyi 'dod chags la sogs pa ni ma yin zhe na/

Reply: Indeed, that is stated, {but they are differentiated since they act or do not act as antidotes to all.} The Autocommentary {to the Abhidharmakośa} states: It is not the focal object because the first does not exist and because it is not of the first.[1429] The meaning of that quotation is that Dharma knowledge is not the focal object of wrong view and so on of the two higher realms because it is not the antidote to them. Question: Why is that so? Reply: All Dharma knowledge is not an antidote to higher-realm affliction because the first Dharma knowledge of the four truths is Dharma knowledge of the first two truths, and it does not exist as an antidote [451] to form- and formless-realm affliction. It is not an antidote of all those of higher realms because {the first Dharma knowledge} is not an antidote of objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing {of higher realms}. In conformity with that, Master Pūrṇavardhana also explains that the first two Dharma knowledges of the truths of suffering and origin subsumed by the path of meditation do not act as antidotes to afflictions of the two higher realms. And regarding objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, distorted minds of both higher realms and so on do not focus on Dharma knowledge because the antidote to objects abandoned by the path of seeing of both higher realms is not Dharma knowledge.[1430] Indeed, the Vaibhāṣikas respond in this way. But such assertions are taken to be valid merely within their own tenet system. Thus this completes the explanation of the eighteen negative tendencies of the three levels that focus on uncontaminated states. The remaining eighty negative tendencies focus on contaminated states. Question: Again, why do just those wrong views and so on focus on uncontaminated states but attachment and so forth do not?
'dod chags min te spang bya'i phyir/ / gnod mi byed phyir zhe sdang min/ / zhi dang dag dang mchog gyur phyir/ / nga rgyal ma yin mchog 'dzin min/ / 16

Attachment does not, because its object is to be abandoned. Aversion does not, because they do not harm. Pride does not, because they are peace. Because it purifies. Clinging to those as supreme does not, because they are supreme. (5:16)

'gog lam ni 'dod chags kyis dmigs pa min te/ de'i yul ni spang bya yin la 'gog lam ni spang bya ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / {zag med la dmigs pa ni gcig tu spang byar ma nges te 'dun pa bzhin no } 'gog lam thob cing bsgrub par 'dod pa ni dge ba'i chos la 'dun pa yin gyi 'dod chags ma yin no/ / de bzhin du 'gog lam ni zhe sdang gis kyang dmigs pa min te/ zhe sdang ni gnod pa byas pa'am byed pa'am byed par 'gyur ba la dmigs pa yin na 'gog lam ni kun nas mnar sems kyi gzhi dgu'i mtshan nyid las 'das pas su la'ang gnod pa mi byed pa'i phyir ro/ / 'gog lam ni zhi ba'i phyir nga rgyal gyi dmigs pa ma yin te/ de ni sems khengs pa la brjod pa'i phyir ro/ / lam bden ni yang dag par nyon mongs pa'i dri ma spangs pa'i phyir dag pa'i phyir tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog tu 'dzin pas dmigs pa ma yin te/ de ni yang dag pa'i rgyu ma yin pa la der 'dzin pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'gog lam ni yang dag pa'i don du dag pa yin pas chos thams cad kyi mchog tu gyur pa yin pa'i phyir lta ba mchog tu 'dzin pas dmigs pa min te/ de ni dngos po dman la mchog tu 'dzin pa'i lta ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ / des na phra rgyas dgu bcu rtsa brgyad las zag med la dmigs pa kho na yin pa bcu gnyis dang*/ zag bcas kho na la dmigs pa brgyad cu dang zag bcas zag med gnyis ka la dmigs pa 'gog lam mthong spang gi ma rig pa drug yin no zhes dngos su bstan pas shugs la zag med la dmigs pa rnams dngos su log zhugs dang*/ 'gog lam mthong spang gi zag bcas la dmigs pa rnams dngos su log lta la sogs pa de dag la dmigs pas log pa la log zhugs yin no zhes shes par bya'o/ /

Reply: Attachment does not focus on the truths of cessation and path because its object is to be abandoned whereas cessation and path are not to be abandoned. {Those such as aspiration that focus on uncontaminated states are not ascertained to be solely objects of abandonment}. The desire to obtain and establish the truths of cessation and the path is the aspiration for virtuous Dharmas, but attachment is not like that. Similarly, aversion does not focus on the truths of cessation and path because aversion focuses on objects that have harmed oneself, do harm, or will harm, and cessation and path do not harm anyone since they transcend the characteristics of the nine bases of the tormented mind. Pride does not focus on them because the truths of cessation and path are peace, and pride’s objects are said to inflate the mind. Clinging to rules and ritual as supreme does not focus on them because the truth of path correctly abandons the stain of the afflictions and it purifies, but [clinging to rules and ritual as supreme] holds incorrect causes to be the cause of purification. The view clinging to those three [views] as supreme does not focus on the truths of cessation and path since the latter purify through being taken as the correct object because they are the supreme among all phenomena, while [clinging to those three views as supreme] holds inferior states to be supreme. Therefore, it is taught explicitly that among the ninety-eight negative tendencies, twelve focus on uncontaminated states alone, eighty focus on contaminated states alone, and six types of ignorance abandoned by seeing the truths of cessation and path focus on both contaminated and uncontaminated states. It is taught implicitly that those such as wrong view and so on that directly misconceive those [minds] that focus on uncontaminated states, and directly misconceive [minds] that focus on contaminated states abandoned by seeing the truths of cessation and path, should be understood to misconceive those that wrongly engage their objects.

gong ma ba ltar na 'gog lam mthong spang gi log lta la sogs pa drug po de dag gis kyang rtog bcas kyi yid kyis brtags pa'i 'gog lam gyi ming tsam la dmigs pa yin gyi de dag la dngos su ni mi dmigs te/ gal te zag med la dngos su dmigs na de dag 'phags pa'i ye shes su thal bar 'gyur ba'i phyir ro zhes 'dod do/ / rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las mthong spang sgom spang de dag gi dmigs pa ni bsdu na lnga ste/ log par rnam par brtags pa'i dngos po la dmigs pa dang*/ lta ba la dmigs pa dang*/ tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs la dmigs pa dang*/ rang gis rnam par brtags pa'i ming la dmigs pa dang*/ rang gi ngang gis ye yod pa'i dngos po la dmigs pa'o/ / de la dang po ni bden pa dang po gnyis la dmigs pa rnams so/ / gnyis pa ni the tshom ma gtogs pa lta ba mchog 'dzin dang 'dod chags la sogs pa mthong spang rnams so/ / gsum pa ni tshul khrims dang brtul zhugs mchog 'dzin no/ / bzhi pa ni 'gog lam la dmigs pa dang khams mi 'dra ba la dmigs pa rnams te/ nyon mongs pa ni nam yang 'gog lam la dmigs par ma gyur/ dmigs par mi byed/ dmigs par mi 'gyur la/ khams mi 'dra ba la'ang ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / lnga pa ni sgom spang rnams so/ / des na dang po bzhi ni mthong spang gi dmigs pa yin la/ lnga pa ni sgom spang gi dmigs pa yin no zhes pa dang*/ kun las btus las kyang*/ 'gog pa dang lam la dmigs pa'i nyon mongs pa gang yin pa de ni de dag la dmigs pa ma yin par lta ste/ de'i dmigs pa ni de yongs su rtog pa'o zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / 'on kyang bye brag tu smra ba rnams ni zag med la dmigs kyang 'phags par 'gyur ba ni ma nges te/ sgra rtag 'dzin bzhin no zhes lan 'debs par byed do/ /

In accordance with [452] the foregoing, wrong views and so forth that are abandoned by seeing the truths of cessation and path focus on the mere names of “cessation” and “path” imputed by mental conception but do not directly focus on these truths. If they did directly focus on uncontaminated states, they would become ārya transcendent wisdom. The Compendium of Ascertainment notes: If the focal objects of those states to be abandoned by the path of seeing and those to be abandoned by the path of meditation are summarized, there are five: (1) those that focus on things that are wrongly mentally fabricated, (2) those that focus on view, (3) those that focus on rules and ritual, (4) those that focus on names imputed by oneself, (5) those that focus on things that naturally exist from the beginning. The first is those focusing on the first two truths. The second is those abandoned by the path of seeing, such as clinging to those views as supreme, attachment, and so on, excluding doubt. The third is clinging to rules and ritual as supreme. The fourth is those focusing on cessation and path and those focusing on different realms, because afflictions have never focused on cessation and path, nor do they focus on them, nor will they focus on them, and also they do not focus on different realms. The fifth is those abandoned by meditation. Therefore the first four focus on objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing, and the fifth focuses on objects abandoned by the path of meditation.[1431] The Compendium of Abhidharma declares: Any afflicted conception that focuses on the truths of cessation and path should not be viewed as focusing on them, for its focal object is entirely imagined.[1432] However, Vaibhāṣikas respond that though [that conception] focuses on uncontaminated states, it is not certain [that person] becomes an ārya because it is like the conception holding that sound is permanent.
gsum pa rgyas pa dang mi rgyas pa'i dbye ba ni
How they increase
yang phra rgyas dgu bcu rtsa brgyad las dmigs pas rgyas 'gyur du/ / mtshungs ldan gyis rgyas 'gyur du zhe na/
Question: Again, do the ninety-eight negative tendencies increase due to their focal object, or do they increase through concomitance?
phra rgyas kun tu 'gro rnams ni/ / dmigs pa'i sgo nas rang gi sa/ / thams cad du ni rgyas par 'gyur/ / kun 'gro ma yin rang ris su/ / 17
Any pervasive negative tendency increases all of its level by means of its focal object; those not pervasive increase those of their type. (5:17)

{dmigs pas rgyas pa de ni mtshungs ldan gyis kyang rgyas la/ gang dag mtshungs ldan kho nas rgyas pa'ang yod do/ / de yang phra rgyas kun 'gro ni gnyis te rang gi khams dang sa kun tu 'gro ba dang*/ skal ba mi mnyam pa'i khams dang sa kun tu 'gro ba'o }

Reply: {Increase due to their focal object is also increase through concomitance, and increase through concomitance alone also exists. Further, pervasive negative tendencies are twofold: pervasive in its own realm and level, and pervasive in different realms and levels.}

phra rgyas gang dag kun du 'gro bar bshad pa gang dag yin pa de rnams ni dmigs pa'i sgo nas rang gi sa pa'i spang bya ris lnga po thams cad du rgyas par 'gyur ba dang*/ kun 'gro ma yin pa rnams ni rang rang gi ris su gtogs pa la rgyas par 'gyur gyi ris gzhan la ni ma yin no/ / des na sdug bsngal mthong spang ni sdug bsngal mthong spang kho na la rgyas par 'gyur ro zhes bya ba la sogs par sbyar ro/ /

Any negative tendency that is said to be pervasive increases (anuśerate) all five objects of abandonment of its level by means of its focal object (ālambana), and those not pervasive (asarvaga) increase those belonging to their type (svanikāya) but not different types. Therefore those to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering increase those to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering alone. [453]
zag med gong ma'i yul can min/ / bdag gir ma byas gnyen po'i phyir/ / gang zhig gang dang mtshungs ldan pa/ / de ni der mtshungs ldan sgo nas/ / 18

Question: Now, do they increase by focusing on all their objects? Those with objects that are uncontaminated or of higher level do not increase because they do not take them as “mine,” and they are antidotes. Those that are concomitant are increased by means of concomitance. (5:18)
