kun nas dkris pa bcu bshad pa gang dag yin pa de dag las ngo tsha med pa dang khrel med pa dang rmugs pa dang gnyid dang rgod pa ste lnga ni mthong spang dang sgom spang dang mtshungs par ldan pa rnams rim pa ltar mthong spang dang sgom spang yin pas rnam pa gnyis ka yin te/ de la ngo tsha med pa dang khrel med gnyis ni mi dge ba thams cad dang mtshungs par ldan zhing*/ rmugs rgod gnyis ni nyon mongs pa thams cad dang mtshungs par ldan la/ gnyid ni yid kyi sa pa 'dod pa na spyod pa thams cad dang mtshungs par ldan no/ /

From among those called the ten entanglements, five — shamelessness, nonembarrassment, lethargy, sleep, and excitation, which are concomitant with that which is abandoned by the path of seeing and by the path of meditation — have two types, since they are respectively abandoned by the paths of seeing and meditation. Both shamelessness and nonembarrassment are concomitant with all nonvirtuous states, both lethargy and excitation are concomitant with all afflicted states, and sleep is a level of the mental faculty concomitant with all actions in the desire realm.
de las gzhan ni bsgom spang bya/ / rang dbang de bzhin dri ma rnams/ / 'dod na mi dge gsum rnam gnyis/ / de yan chad ni lung ma bstan/ / 52

Those other than these five are abandoned by meditation. So too, the stains are autonomous. In the desire realm they are nonvirtuous, but three have two types. Those above the desire realm are neutral. (5:52)

lnga po de dag las gzhan pa nye nyon kun dkris kyis bsdus pa phrag dog dang ser sna dang 'gyod pa dang khro ba dang 'chab pa ni bden pa la dngos dang brgyud nas log par mi {'jug cing yul la 'jug } pas bsgom pas spang bar bya ba kho na dang*/ rang dbang can yang yin te/ sgom spang gi ma rig pa tsam dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te gang zhig ma rig pa tsam dang mtshungs par ldan pa de rang dbang can yin no zhes bya ba 'di la rigs pa ci yod ce na/ de dag 'jug pa la ni rang nyid gtso bo yin gyi 'dod chags la sogs pa nyon mongs pa gzhan la mi ltos la/ ma rig pa tsam dang mtshungs par ldan yang ma rig pa ni glen pa'i phyir 'jug par byed pa ma yin no zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/{ de dag ni rang nyid dbang che'i/ ma rig pa la sogs pa ltar chags sogs kyi dbang du mi 'gyur bas so/ /} ji ltar nye nyon phrag dog la sogs pa sgom spang dang rang dbang can yin pa de bzhin du dri ma drug po rnams kyang sgom spang dang rang dbang can yin no/ / kun nas dkris pa ngo tsha med pa la sogs pa bdun dang dri ma drug po rnams ni 'dod pa'i khams na mi dge ba yin no/ /

Branch afflictions that are subsumed by the entanglements other than these five of envy, avarice, regret, wrath, and concealment are abandoned by the path of meditation alone, since they do not directly or indirectly wrongly engage [480] the four truths {but engage objects}. Also they are autonomous because they are concomitant with ignorance alone. Question: Why is it logical to say that if it is concomitant with ignorance alone, it is autonomous? Reply: When such an affliction engages objects, it itself is the main engager; it does not rely on other afflictions such as attachment. It is concomitant with ignorance, but ignorance does not act to engage the object because ignorance is dull. This is explained by Master Pūrṇavardhana.[1501] {Thus they are autonomous, and like ignorance and so forth, they are not controlled by attachment and so on.} Just as branch afflictions such as envy are abandoned by the path of meditation and are autonomous, so too the six stains (mala) are abandoned by the path of meditation and are autonomous (svatantra). In the desire realm, the seven entanglements such as shamelessness and the six stains are nonvirtuous states.

rmugs pa dang rgod pa dang gnyid gsum ni gnyid la dge ba yod kyang kun nas dkris pa'i skabs yin pas{ dge ba ma yin gyi} bsgribs la lung ma bstan dang mi dge ba rnam pa gnyis ka yin no/ / 'dod pa'i khams de yan chad khams gong ma gnyis na yod pa'i nye nyon rnams ni bsgribs la lung ma bstan yin no/ / yang nye nyon de dag khams dang sa gang na du zhig yod ce na/

The three branch afflictions of lethargy, excitation, and sleep have two types: obscured-neutral and nonvirtuous, and though sleep may also be virtuous, in the context of the entanglements {it is not virtuous}. Branch afflictions existing above the desire realm, in the two higher realms, are obscured-neutral states. Question: How many branch afflictions exist on which realm and level?
'dod dang bsam gtan dang po na/ / g.yo sgyu tshangs pas 'drid phyir ro/ / rmugs rgod rgyags pa khams gsum na/ / gzhan dag 'dod khams las skyes pa/ / 53

Guile and deceit exist in the desire realm and the first absorption because Brahma tried to deceive Aśvajit. Lethargy, excitation, and arrogance exist in the three realms. The others arise in the desire realm. (5:53)

'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang po na ni g.yo sgyu yod de/ tshul khrims kyi phung po'i mdo las/ 'phags pa rta thul gyis tshangs pa la 'byung ba chen po bzhi po 'di dag ma lus par gang du 'gag par 'gyur zhes dris pa na/ de ma shes par bdag ni tshangs pa'o/ / tshangs pa chen po'o/ / dbang phyug go /byed pa po'o/ / sprul pa po'o/ / 'byin pa po'o/ / 'byin byed do/ / dngos po rnams kyi phar gyur pa yin no zhes tshangs pa chen po'i g.yo sgyus gtam rlung la bskur te 'phags pa rta thul 'drid par bshad pa'i phyir ro/ {nyon mongs kyi sa pa yin pas } rmugs pa dang rgod pa dang rgyags{ gang na yang mi 'gal bas} pa gsum ni khams gsum ga na yod do/ /gsum po de dag dang g.yo sgyu gnyis te lnga las gzhan bcu gcig po de dag ni 'dod pa'i khams las skyes pa dag kho na yin no/ /

Guile (śāṭhya) and deceit (māyā) exist in the desire realm and the first absorption because Brahma tried to deceive Aśvajit through speech conveyed with guile and deceit. The Ethics Sūtra states: Ārya Aśvajit questioned Brahma: “Where are these four great elements without exception blocked?” Not knowing the answer, he said: “I am Brahma, the great Brahma, Īśvara, the creator, the emanator, the producer, one who produces, the dispenser of objects.”[1502] The three — lethargy {since it exists on the level of affliction}, excitation, and arrogance {since it does not exclude any state} — exist in the three realms. Eleven that are other than the five (those three plus both guile and deceit) arise in the desire realm alone.
mthong spang bya gnyid nga rgyal bcas/ / yid kyi rnam shes sa pa yin/ / nye ba'i nyon mongs rang dbang yang / / gzhan ni rnam shes drug rten can/ / 54
Those abandoned by seeing plus sleep and pride exist on the level of mental consciousness. So too, the autonomous branch afflictions. Others possess support of the six consciousnesses. (5:54)
yang rtsa ba dang nye ba'i nyon mongs pa de dag las
From the root and branch afflictions,

mthong bas spang bar bya ba thams cad dang {ni kha nang bltas yin pas } sgom spang yin yang gnyid dang nga rgyal dang bcas pa ni yid kyi rnam shes kyi sa pa yin te/ rtog bcas dang mi gsal bas yid kyi rnam shes las gzhan gyi 'khor du ma 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du nye ba'i nyon mongs pa rang dbang can bcu gcig po yang sgom spang yin yang rtog bcas yin pas yid kyi sa pa yin no/ / mthong spang dang sgom spang gi gnyid dang nga rgyal las gzhan pa'i nyon mongs pa dang nye ba'i nyon mongs pa sgom spang gi ma nges pa'i chags sdang gnyis/ mi dge ba'i sa pa gnyis/ nyon mongs pa chen po'i sa pa drug po ni rnam par shes pa drug car gyi rten can yin no/ / yang nyon mongs pa nye ba'i nyon mongs pa de dag tshor ba lnga po gang dang mtshungs par ldan zhe na/

all those abandoned by the path of seeing, plus the sleep and pride that are abandoned by the path of meditation exist on the level of mental consciousness {since they view internal states}. They don’t occur in the retinue of those other than mental consciousnesses since they are conceptual and unclear. So too, the eleven autonomous branch afflictions that are abandoned by the path of meditation exist on the level of the mental faculty because they are conceptual. Root and branch afflictions other than sleep and pride that are abandoned by the paths of seeing and meditation, both attachment and aversion that are not definitely abandoned by seeing, and both the levels of nonvirtue and the six levels of great affliction [481] possess the support of the six consciousnesses. Question: Which of the afflictions and branch afflictions are concomitant with the five feelings?
bde ba dag dang 'dod chags su/ / mtshungs ldan zhe sdang bzlog pa'o/ / ma rig pa dag thams cad dang / / med lta yid bde sdug bsngal dang / / 55
Attachment is concomitant with pleasure, aversion with the opposite, ignorance with all, and wrong view holding them as nonexistent with mental satisfaction and pain. (5:55)

bde ba dang yid bde ba dag dang dga' ba'i rnam par 'jug pas 'dod chags su mtshungs par ldan te/ rnam shes drug car gyi 'khor du 'byung bas sgo lnga'i rnam shes dang yid shes kyi 'khor du byung ba ni rim pa ltar lus kyi bde ba dang yid bde dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / zhe sdang ni skyo ba'i rnam par 'jug pas 'dod chags bde ba dag dang mtshungs par ldan pa las bzlog pa sdug bsngal dang yid mi bde ba dang mtshungs par ldan pa'o/ / de yang rnam shes lnga dang yid shes kyi 'khor du byung ba ni rim pa ltar sdug bsngal dang yid mi bde ba dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / spang bya ris lnga'am 'dres pa dang ma 'dres pa'i ma rig pa dag ni tshor ba lnga po thams cad dang ci rigs mtshungs par ldan te/ rnam shes thams cad dang nyon mongs pa thams cad dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / bden bzhi med par lta ba'i log lta ni log lta can sdig pa dang bsod nams byas pa rnams rim pa ltar sdig pa dang bsod nams byas pa'i 'bras bu mi 'byung ba dang 'bad pa don med par mthong bas yid bde ba dang sdug bsngal te yid mi bde ba dag dang mtshungs par ldan no/ / yid mi bde ba dang the tshom mtshungs par ldan te/ {nges pa } gang zhig don du gnyer ba de la 'jug pa la the tshom za ba na yang mi bde ba'i phyir ro/ /

Attachment is concomitant with pleasure and mental satisfaction that engages a joyous aspect [or object] since it occurs in the retinue of the six consciousnesses. Attachment, in other words, occurring in the retinue of a consciousness of the five sense doors or in mental consciousness is concomitant, respectively, with physical pleasure or mental satisfaction. Aversion is concomitant with pain and mental dissatisfaction that is the opposite of concomitance with attachment and pleasure, since it engages a disappointing aspect [or object]. It occurs in the retinue of the five sense consciousnesses and mental consciousness that are concomitant, respectively, with pain and mental dissatisfaction. Ignorance that is mixed or not mixed with the five objects of abandonment is concomitant with various instances of all five feelings because feeling is concomitant with all consciousnesses and all afflictions. Wrong view holding the four truths to be nonexistent is wrong view that holds that those who engage in immorality or meritorious acts do not experience, respectively, the result of having engaged in immorality or meritorious acts and holds [virtuous acts] to be meaningless. Therefore it is concomitant with mental satisfaction and pain that is mental dissatisfaction.
yid mi bde dang the tshom mo/ / gzhan yid bde dang 'dod las skyes/ / btang snyoms dad kun sa gong ma/ / sa ji bzhin du rang rang dang / / 56

Doubt is concomitant with mental dissatisfaction; others with mental satisfaction. These arise in the desire realm. All is concomitant with equanimity, and those of higher levels with each level according to the level. (5:56)

de dag las gzhan pa'i nyon mongs pa lta ba bzhi dang nga rgyal ni yid bde ba dang mtshungs par ldan te/ de dag yid kyi sa pa kho na yin la dga' ba'i rnam pas 'jug pa'i phyir ro/ / {chad lta'ang dga' rnam can yin no } de dag kyang 'dod pa las skyes pa'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi khams gong ma na {khong khro dang yid mi bde dang } sdug bsngal med pa'i phyir dang*/ bde ba'ang bsam gtan bzhi pa nas med pa'i phyir ro/ / btang snyoms dang ni nyon mongs pa kun mtshungs par ldan te/ nyon mongs pa rgyun chad pa ni gzhan pas nges par btang snyoms yod pa'i phyir te/ 'grel pa las/ phra rgyas 'di dag thams cad ni btang snyoms kyi dbang po dang mtshungs par ldan te/ nyon mongs pa rnams rgyun chad pa'i dus na gdon mi za bar btang snyoms kun du gnas so zhes pa dang*/ chos mngon pa kun las btus las kyang*/ ci'i phyir nyon mongs pa thams cad ni btang snyoms dang mtshungs par ldan zhe na/ tha mal par 'dug pa la brten nas nub par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro zhes bshad do/ / sa gong ma gzugs dang gzugs med pa dag gis nyon mongs pa rnams ni sa ji bzhin du sa rang rang gi rnam shes dang tshor ba'i dbang po gang yod pa de dang mtshungs par ldan te/ sa gang na rnam shes dang tshor ba du yod pa ni bshad zin to/ /

Doubt is concomitant with mental dissatisfaction because seeking {certainty} about something one has doubt about is painful. Others, such as four afflicted views and pride, are concomitant with mental satisfaction because they are levels of the mental faculty alone that engages a joyous aspect {and also the view of annihilation possesses joy}. Furthermore these arise in the desire realm, since suffering {anger and mental dissatisfaction} do not exist in the higher realms and pleasure does not exist from the fourth absorption. All affliction is concomitant with equanimity because equanimity certainly exists when the continuum of affliction is severed by others. The Autocommentary declares: All these negative tendencies are concomitant with the faculty of equanimity because when the continuum of afflicted states is severed, without doubt equanimity continues to abide.[1503] And the Compendium of Abhidharma states: Why are all afflicted states concomitant with equanimity? Because they subside in dependence on the mind existing in its ordinary [or natural] state.[1504] Those of the higher form and formless-realm levels are concomitant with consciousness of each level according to the level and any existent faculty of feeling. The number of consciousnesses and feelings on any level has been explained.
'gyod dang phrag dog khro ba dang / / rnam 'tshe khon du 'dzin pa dang / / 'tshig pa yid mi bde ba dang / / ser sna dag ni bzlog pa yin/ / 57
Regret, envy, wrath, violence, resentment, and spite are concomitant with mental dissatisfaction. Avarice is the opposite of those. (5:57)

nye ba'i nyon mongs pa rnams las 'gyod pa nas 'tshig pa'i bar drug po dag ni yid mi bde ba dang mtshungs par ldan te/ 'di dag skyo ba'i rnam par 'jug pa'i tshor ba yin pa'i phyir dang*/ dga' ba'i rnam par mi 'jug pas yid bde dang mtshungs par mi ldan la yid kyi sa pa kho na yin pa'i phyir sdug bsngal dang yang mtshungs par mi ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / ser sna ni yid mi bde dang mtshungs par ldan pa drug po de dag las bzlog pa chags pa'i rgyu las byung bas dga' ba'i rnam par 'jug cing yid kyi sa pa kho na yin pas yid bde dang mtshungs par ldan pa yin no/ /

Six branch afflictions from regret (kaukṛtya) to spite (pradāśa) [482] are concomitant with mental dissatisfaction because they engage feelings of disappointment. Since they do not engage a joyous object, they are not concomitant with mental satisfaction, and because they solely exist on the level of the mental faculty, they are not concomitant with [physical] pain. Avarice engages the aspect of joy since it arises from the cause of attachment that is the opposite of those six concomitant with mental dissatisfaction. And since it exists on the level of the mental faculty alone, it is concomitant with mental satisfaction.
g.yo dang sgyu dang 'chab dang gnyis/ / gnyis ka dang ldan bde dag dang / / rgyags pa btang snyoms kun tu 'gro/ / bzhi po gzhan ni lnga dag dang / / 58
Guile, deceit, concealment, and sleep are concomitant with both. Arrogance with pleasure. Equanimity is pervasive. The other four are concomitant with five. (5:58)

g.yo dang sgyu dang 'chab pa dang gnyid rnams ni g.yo sgyu dang bcas pa'i bya ba 'grub pa dang ma grub pa na rim pa ltar yid bde ba dang mi bde bar 'gyur zhing gnyid ni kun la mi 'gal la thams cad yid shes kyi sa pa yin pas yid bde yid mi bde gnyis ka dang mtshungs par ldan no/ / dga' ba'i rnam par 'jug cing yid kyi sa pa kho na yin pas bsam gtan gsum pa'i sems bde dang gnyis pa man chad kyi yid bde dag dang rgyags pa mtshungs par ldan la/ bzhi pa yan chad na bde ba med pa'i phyir btang snyoms kho na dang mtshungs par ldan te/ ji ltar ma rig pa nyon mongs pa dang nye ba'i nyon mongs pa gang la'ang mtshungs par ldan par rung pa ltar btang snyoms kyang sa dang rnam shes dang nyon mongs pa dang nye ba'i nyon mongs pa thams cad la kun tu 'gro ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir TIka byed dag gis kyang ma rig pa dang btang snyoms gnyis ni nyon mongs pa dang nye ba'i nyon mongs pa gang dang yang mtshungs par ldan pa bkag pa med do zhes bshad do/ / kun dkris gzhan ngo tsha khrel med dang rmugs rgod bzhi po ni tshor ba'i dbang po dag dang mtshungs par ldan par srid de/ dang po gnyis mi dge ba'i sa pa dang phyi ma gnyis nyon mongs pa'i sa pa chen po yin la/ de dag kyang rnam shes drug car gyi 'khor du 'byung zhing drug car la mi dge ba dang nyon mongs pa'ang srid pa'i phyir ro/ /

Guile, deceit, concealment, and sleep are concomitant with both mental satisfaction and mental dissatisfaction, for if one’s purpose is accomplished with guile and deceit then mental satisfaction arises, or if with guile and deceit one fails, then mental dissatisfaction arises. But sleep is not incompatible with any, and all four exist on the level of mental consciousness. Arrogance is concomitant with pleasure of the mind of the third absorption, and mental bliss of the second absorption and below, since it engages joy and it exists on the level of the mental faculty alone. On the fourth absorption and above, it is concomitant with equanimity alone because pleasure does not exist there. Just as ignorance is concomitant with any root or branch affliction, also equanimity is pervasive (sarvatraga) regarding all levels and consciousnesses and in terms of root and branch afflictions. Therefore Purṇavardhana’s commentary explains: That both ignorance and equanimity are concomitant with afflictions and branch afflictions cannot be refuted.[1505] It is possible that the other four entanglements of shamelessness, nonembarrassment, lethargy, and excitation are concomitant with the five faculties of feeling because the first two exist on the level of nonvirtue and the latter two exist on the wider level of affliction. These four arise in the retinue of the six consciousnesses, and it is possible they are nonvirtuous or afflicted with respect to those six.
bcu gcig pa sgrib pa lnga bshad pa ni
The five obscurations

mdo las 'dod pa la 'dun pa dang*/ gnod sems dang*/ rmugs pa dang*/ gnyid dang*/ rgod pa dang*/ 'gyod pa dang*/ the tshom dag sgrib pa lngar gsungs na/ 'dod 'dun dang gnod sems dang gnyid dang 'gyod pa rnams 'dod pa ba yin mod kyi rmugs rgod dang the tshom rnams khams gsum ga na yod pas de dag khams gsum char gyi gzung ngam zhe na/

Question: Indeed, a sūtra states: Longing for sensory objects, malice, lethargy-sleep, excitation-regret, and doubt are the five obscurations.[1506] But since longing for sensory objects, malice, sleep, and excitation are associated with the desire realm, and lethargy and excitation exist in all three realms, shouldn’t the five obscurations be held as belonging to the three realms?
'dod na sgrib rnams mi mthun dang / / zas dang bya ba gcig pa'i phyir/ / gnyis gcig phung po gnod byed dang / / the tshom phyir na lnga nyid do/ / 59

The five obscurations exist in the desire realm. Two are explained as one because their opposing factor, their nourishment, and their action are the same. They are just five because they harm the [three] aggregations and because one would doubt them. (5:59)

ma yin te/ bsam gtan dang rnam par thar pa dang ting nge 'dzin dang snyoms par 'jug pa la sgrib pas na sgrib pa lnga po rnams ni 'dod pa'i khams kho na na yod de/ mdo las/ dge slong dag sgrib pa lnga ni mi dge ba'i phung po yin no zhes smra ba de dag ni yang dag par smra ba smra bar 'gyur ro/ / ci'i phyir zhe na/ / dge slong dag 'di ni mi dge ba'i phung po ma 'dres pa yongs su rdzogs pa yin te/ 'di lta ste sgrib pa lnga'o zhes sgrib pa lnga gcig tu mi dge ba kho nar gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / yang ci'i phyir rmugs gnyid gnyis dang rgod 'gyod gnyis sems byung tha dad yin bzhin du sgrib pa re rer bshad ce na/ rmugs gnyid gnyis yod kyang sgrib pa gcig tu bshad de/ de gnyis kyi mi mthun phyogs gnyen po gcig pa'i phyir dang*/ zas te skyed byed kyi rgyu gcig pa'i phyir dang*/ bya ba'ang gcig pa'i phyir ro/ / de la gnyis ka'i mi mthun phyogs snang ba'i 'du shes te gnyen po dang zas ma yin pa zhes kyang brjod do/ / zas ni lnga ste/ smya ba dang mi dga' ba dang*/ bya smyangs dang*/ kha zas kyi drod mi zin pa dang*/ sems zhum pa nyid de/ de dag gis de gnyis rgyas par byed pa'i phyir ro/ / gnyis po de'i bya ba ni sems zhum par byed pa'o/ / de bzhin du rgod 'gyod gnyis kyang sgrib pa gcig tu bzhag ste/ mi mthun phyogs dang zas dang bya ba gcig pa'i phyir ro/ / de la 'di gnyis kyi mi mthun phyogs ni zhi gnas yin la/ zas ni bzhi ste/ nye du'i rnam par rtog pa dang*/ yul gyi rnam par rtog pa dang*/ mi 'chi ba'i rnam par rtog pa dang*/ sngon dgod pa dang rtses pa dang dga' mgur spyad pa rnams rjes su dran pa'o/ / bya ba ni gnyis kas sems rnam par ma zhi bar byed pa'o/ / gal te nyon mongs pa dang nye ba'i nyon mongs pa thams cad kyang sgrib pa yin na ci'i phyir lnga po kho na sgrib par bstan zhe na/

Reply: No, the five obscurations (nīvaraṇa) exist in the desire realm since they obscure [or obstruct] the absorptions, liberation, concentration, and meditative attainments. A sūtra observes: Monks, those who say that the five obscurations are aggregations of nonvirtue speak correctly. Why? Monks, that which completes the aggregation of unmixed nonvirtue is the five obscurations.[1507] This sūtra states that the five obscurations are nonvirtuous alone. Question: Again, why are both lethargy and sleep, or both excitation [483] and regret, which are distinct mental factors, explained as single obscurations? Reply: Though lethargy and sleep are two distinct states, they are explained as one obscuration because the antidote that is their opposing factor (vipakṣa) is the same, the nourishment (hāra) that is their primary efficient cause is the same, and their action (kṛtyata) is the same. The opposing factor of both, also called their antidote and that which does not nourish them, is the discernment of brightness. Their nourishment has five types: bad omens, joylessness, physical exhaustion, inability to digest food, and mental lassitude. They both act to increase the other and generate mental lassitude. Similarly, both excitation and regret also are taken as a single obscuration because their opposing factor, nourishment, and action are the same. Their opposing factor is calm abiding. Their nourishment has four types: speculating about one’s relatives, speculating about one’s possessions, speculating about the deathless state, and recalling former laughter, games, and exuberance. They both act to destroy mental peace. Question: If all afflictions and branch afflictions are obscurations, why are they taught to be five alone?

25. How Negative Tendencies Are Eliminated
['di] la dngos dang*/ zhar la gnyen po'i dbye ba gnyis las
THIS HAS TWO HEADINGS: the actual method of abandoning negative tendencies and, in addition, the classification of antidotes.
dang po ni
The actual method of abandoning negative tendencies
dmigs pa yongs su shes pa dang / / de la dmigs pa yang dag par/ / zad dang dmigs pa spangs pas so/ / gnyen po skyes pas zad par 'gyur/ / 60

They are abandoned by fully understanding their focal object, by correctly eliminating minds that focus on them, and by abandoning their focal object. They are eliminated by the antidote arising. (5:60)
spyir spang bya spong tshul la bzhi las
In general, there are four methods of abandoning objects of abandonment,
re zhig mthong spang rnams ni

but here three are mentioned: (1) abandoning objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing by fully understanding (parijñāna) their focal object (ālambana), (2) abandoning them by correctly eliminating (saṃkṣaya) the minds that focus on them, and (3) abandoning minds by abandoning (prahāṇa) their focal object. The first comprises fifty of the eighty-eight objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing: (1–2) the first two pervasive views [focusing on] the same realm, which focus on objects of its own desire realm to be abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering, (3–5) three nonpervasive states of attachment, anger, and pride, and (6–8) three nonpervasive states of attachment and so on, which are objects abandoned by seeing the truth of origin, (9–26) nine objects abandoned by seeing the truth of suffering (anger is excluded in each of the two higher realms), (27–38) six for each higher realm, objects abandoned by seeing the truth of origin, making twelve in total, and (39–50) twelve more — wrong view and doubt focusing on uncontaminated objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of cessation and path of the three realms (excluding the six ignorances). The path of seeing with full knowledge of the real nature of the four truths abandons these fifty that wrongly engage their focal objects because their [apprehended] objects exclude each other, just as knowledge attained through seeing eliminates grasping [an inanimate object] to be a human being.

gnyis pa ni de dag las dgu gong du dmigs zhes pa'i 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung mthong spang skal ba mi mnyam pa'i khams kun 'gro dgu po rnams te/ de dag ni de dag la dmigs pa'i yul can 'dod pa'i skal ba mnyam pa'i khams kun 'gro rnams spangs pas spong ste/ skal ba mnyam pa'i khams kun 'gro'i dmigs pa ni skal ba mi mnyam pa'i khams kun 'gro yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

The second are nine of the eighty-eight called “the nine focusing on higher realms,” which are (1–9) nine pervasive states [focusing on] different realms. These are objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of suffering and origin of the desire realm. They are minds focusing on those states to be abandoned by abandoning the pervasive states of the same desire realm because the focal objects of pervasive states of the same realm are pervasive states of different realms.

gsum pa ni khams gsum gyi 'gog lam mthong spang zag bcas la dmigs pa log pa la log zhugs 'dod pa na 'gog pa mthong spang bzhi dang*/ lam mthong spang lnga ste dgu dang*/ khams gong ma gnyis na khong khro ma gtogs pa bdun bdun te nyi shu rtsa gsum po rnams ni de dag gi dmigs pa'i yul dngos su log zhugs 'gog lam mthong spang zag med la dmigs pa log lta la sogs pa de dag spangs pas yul can lta ba mchog 'dzin la sogs pa zag bcas la dmigs pa log pa la log zhugs de dag kyang spangs par 'gyur te/ 'gog lam la chos bzod chos shes dang rjes bzod rjes shes kyi yul zag med la dngos su dmigs pa log lta la sogs pa dag dmigs yul shes pas spangs pa na yul med pa'i yul can mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / khams gsum gyi 'gog lam mthong spang gi ma rig pa drug ni dngos su log zhugs zag med la dmigs pa dang log pa la log zhugs zag bcas la dmigs pa ni rim pa ltar dmigs pa yongs su shes pa dang dmigs yul spangs pas spong ngo*/ / de bzhin du khams gong ma gnyis kyi spang bya cig car spong zhing bden pa cig car mthong bas gzugs khams kyi skal ba mi mnyam pa'i khams kun 'gro rnams kyang dmigs pa shes pas spong la/ sngar bshad pa'i 'dod pa'i kun 'gro dgu'i skal ba mnyam pa'i khams kun 'gro'i cha rnams kyang dmigs pa shes pas spong ngo*/ /

The third is the twenty-three that misconceive those that wrongly engage their focal objects: contaminated states abandoned by seeing the truths of cessation and path in the three realms. They consist of nine in the desire realm — four (1–4) abandoned by seeing the truth of cessation and five (5–9) abandoned by seeing the truth of the path — and (10–23) fourteen in the two higher realms, seven for each, since anger is excluded. Since they abandon states to be abandoned by seeing the truths of cessation and path that directly misconceive their focal objects, such as wrong view focusing on uncontaminated states, they also abandon [minds] that misconceive those that wrongly engage their focal objects: contaminated states such as minds clinging to those views as supreme. That is because Dharma perseverance, Dharma knowledge, subsequent perseverance, and subsequent knowledge of the truths of cessation and path abandon wrong view and so on that directly focus on uncontaminated objects. They do this by understanding their focal objects because it is impossible that a mind has no object. The six ignorances that are objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of cessation and path of the three realms either directly misconceive their focal objects (uncontaminated states) or misconceive those that wrongly engage their focal objects (contaminated states). They are abandoned, respectively, by fully understanding their focal objects or by abandoning their focal objects. Similarly, since the abandonments of the two higher realms are simultaneously abandoned and the four truths simultaneously seen, minds that are pervasive [negative tendencies focusing on] realms other than the form realm are abandoned through knowing their focal objects. Also, pervasive states [focusing on] realms that are the same as the nine pervasive states of the desire realm previously explained, are abandoned through knowing their focal objects.

de ltar na thams cad kyang dmigs pa yongs su shes pas spong ba'i rtsa ba can yin te/ 'dod pa'i skal ba mi mnyam pa'i khams kun 'gro rnams kyang lam gyis dmigs yul bden pa shes pas yul can skal ba mnyam pa'i khams kun 'gro rnams spangs pas spong ba'i phyir dang*/ khams gsum gyi 'gog lam mthong spang zag bcas la dmigs pa rnams kyang 'gog lam shes pas dmigs yul zag med la dmigs pa rnams spangs pa'i stobs kyis spong ba'i phyir ro/ / de dag rang rang gi dmigs pa shes pa tsam gyis ni mi spong ste/ skal ba mi mnyam pa'i khams kun 'gro rnams kyi dmigs pa ni khams gong ma gnyis yin la/ gong ma gnyis ni sdug bsngal kun 'byung la rjes bzod rjes shes kyis shes pa yin pa na skal ba mi mnyam pa'i khams kun 'gro rnams ni sngar 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal kun 'byung la chos bzod chos shes kyi yul can spangs pa'i tshul gyis spangs zin pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin 'gog lam mthong spang zag bcas la dmigs pa rnams kyis dmigs pa zag med la dmigs pa log lta la sogs pa de dag ni sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung gis bsdus pa yin pas sdug bsngal kun 'byung la chos dang rjes su shes bzod kyis shes kyang de'i tshe mi spong ste/ de dag 'gog lam mthong spang yin pas phyis 'gog lam la chos dang rjes su shes bzod kyi zag med la dmigs pa de dag spangs pas na yul spangs pas spong ba'i phyir ro/ / spong tshul gsum po de dag kyang rang rgyud kyi mthong spang spong tshul yin gyi gzhan rgyud kyi mthong spang thams cad ni/ gang la de skyes ma spangs pa'i/ / dngos po de dang ldan pa yin/ / zhes 'byung bas yul can rang rgyud kyi kun 'gro rnam pa gnyis spangs pa kho nas spong ngo*/ / spong tshul bzhi pa sgom spang rnams ni

Thus all are abandoned at the root through full knowledge of focal objects, because pervasive [negative tendencies focusing on] realms other than the desire realm are abandoned by the path that knows the four truths — its focal object. This is done by abandoning pervasive [negative tendencies focusing on] minds of different realms. Also those that focus on cessation and path that are contaminated objects abandoned by the path of seeing are abandoned by the power of abandoning, through knowing cessation and path, those that focus on uncontaminated focal objects. They are not abandoned merely by knowing their individual focal object, because the focal objects of pervasive states [focusing on] different realms are the two higher realms, and the higher two realms are known by subsequent perseverance and subsequent knowledge of the truths of suffering and origin, while pervasive [negative tendencies focusing on] different realms have already been abandoned by means of abandoning the minds of Dharma perseverance and Dharma knowledge of the desire-realm truths of suffering and origin. Similarly, those that focus on contaminated objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of cessation and path, such as wrong view focusing on uncontaminated focal objects, are recognized by perseverance for Dharma knowledge and subsequent knowledge of the truths of suffering and origin, since they are subsumed by the truths of suffering and origin. But they are not abandoned at that time because they are abandoned later, by Dharma knowledge and subsequent knowledge of the truths of cessation and path that focus on uncontaminated states. This is because they are objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of cessation and path. [486] Those three methods of abandonment are methods of abandoning objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing in one’s own mindstream. All those abandoned by the path of seeing in the mindstreams of others are abandoned by abandoning the two aspects of pervasive states in others’ mindstreams. For as the Abhidharmakośa states, “One who possesses them is bound by attachment, anger, and pride that arose in the past and abide in the present toward the objects of those arisen and unabandoned [afflictions focusing] on any of the five” (5:23).[1510] Thus those minds are solely abandoned by abandoning the two aspects of pervasive states in one’s own mindstream.

The fourth method of abandonment is abandonment by the path of meditation. This is taken as the nine aspects of affliction for each level. These afflictions are eliminated (kṣaya) and abandoned by the antidote (pratipakṣa) arising, such as the small of the small path [as antidote] to the great of the great afflictions and so on. Though the path of seeing knows its focal object, the four truths, it doesn’t abandon objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation by {having previously known the truths,} nor also by knowing its focal objects. And since it is said “Though one abandons any aspect of the first, one possesses the remaining stains of the mind focusing on it” (5:28cd),[1511] therefore [the path of meditation] abandons minds that are pervasive states and objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation up to the eighth stage. It does not do so, however, by eliminating those actively focusing on them, since it does not abandon the last object to be abandoned by meditation; and it also does not do so by abandoning focal objects. It abandons the earlier eight stages that are focal objects abandoned by the path of meditation, but it does not abandon the last, the ninth mind. {Thus the method of abandoning objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation is twofold: (1) abandoning objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation that are abandoned due to the individual antidote of each arising, and (2) exhaustively abandoning minds with afflicted physical objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation in one’s mindstream along with those that are not afflicted and all objects of abandonment in the mindstreams of others.}
gnyis pa [zhar la gnyen po'i dbye ba bshad pa] ni
Types of antidotes
'o na gnyen po nyid du yod ce na/
Question: Now, how many antidotes are there?
gnyen po rnam bzhi spong ba dang / / gzhi dang srid nyid rnam par ni/ sun 'byin zhes bya dmigs pa las/ / nyon mongs pa ni spang byar 'dod/ / 61
Antidotes have four types: that which abandons, maintains, extends, and counteracts. It is asserted that afflictions are abandoned though counteracting focal objects. (5:61)

gnyen po ni rnam pa bzhi ste/ spong ba'i gnyen po dang*/ gzhi gnyen po dang*/ thag sring ba'i gnyen po nyid dang*/ rnam par sun 'byin pa'i gnyen po zhes bya'o/ / de la dang po ni gang gis nyon mongs pa'i thob pa gcod pa ste bar chad med pa'i lam{ thams cad de} sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa la sogs pa'o/ / gnyis pa ni bar chad med pa'i lam gyis spangs pa'i bral thob 'dzin pa ste bar chad med pa'i lam dang po ma gtogs pa sdug bsngal la chos shes pa la sogs pa rnam par grol ba'i lam{ la sogs pa thams cad do} mo/ / des na bar chad med lam dang po ni spong ba gnyen po kho na yin gyi gzhi gnyen po ni ma yin no/ / gsum pa ni rnam grol gyi lam dang po sdug bsngal la chos shes ma gtogs pa de yan chad kyi khyad par gyi lam ste thob pa thag sring ba'i phyir ro/ / des na rnam grol gyi lam dang po sdug bsngal la chos shes de ni gzhi gnyen po kho na yin no/ / kha cig na re rnam grol gyi lam dang po des kyang thob pa thag sring bas thag sring gi gnyen po'ang yin no zhes zer ro/ / bzhi pa ni bden pa dang po gnyis la dmigs pa'i lam gang gis dmigs pa de mi rtag pa la sogs pa'i rnam par sun 'byin pa'o/ / des na 'di skad du bden pa dang po gnyis la dmigs pa'i spong ba gnyen po la sogs pa ni sun 'byin pa'i gnyen po'ang yin no zhes bstan pa yin no/ / slob dpon gyis ni them skas kyi tshul la brten nas skye ba'i rim pa dang mtshan nyid mi 'chol ba thugs la bzhag nas dang po ni bden pa dang po gnyis la dmigs pa'i sbyor lam drod la sogs pa kho na yin la/ gnyis pa ni bar chad med pa'i lam brgyad cu rtsa dgu pa'i thams cad do/ / gsum pa ni rnam grol gyi lam thams cad de rnam grol gyi lam ni dang po nas gzhi kho na yin gyi thag sring ba'i gnyen po ni ma yin no/ / bzhi pa ni khyad par gyi lam ste snga ma gsum las gzhan pa'i lam thams cad de/ des na go rim 'di ni ches legs pa yin no zhes bshad do/ / gnyen po de dag gis gang las spong zhe na/

Reply: Antidotes have four types: (1) antidotes that abandon (prahāṇa), (2) antidotes that maintain (ādhāra), (3) antidotes that extend (dūratva), and (4) antidotes that counteract (dūṣaṇa). The first is {all} uninterrupted paths that sever the obtainment of affliction, such as persevering for knowledge of the truth of suffering and so on. The second is {all} liberated paths that maintain the separation from affliction obtained by the uninterrupted path, such as Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering. This excludes the first uninterrupted path since the first uninterrupted path is an antidote that abandons alone and not an antidote that maintains. The third is the special path beyond the first liberated path because it extends obtainment. This excludes Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering, since Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering, which is the first liberated path, is solely an antidote that maintains. Some say: That first liberated path extends obtainment, and therefore it is also an antidote that extends. The fourth is any path focusing on the first two truths that counteracts its focal object in terms of its aspects such as impermanence. Therefore it is said that an antidote that abandons that which focuses on the first two truths [487] is also an antidote that counteracts. Vasubandhu explains that these should be kept in mind without confusing the order in which they arise, in an upward series, and their characteristics: (1) The first is solely the heat stage and so on of the path of preparation, focusing on the first two truths. (2) The second is all ninety-eight uninterrupted paths. (3) The third is all liberated paths. These are liberated paths, but those from the first [moment] are solely antidotes that maintain and not antidotes that extend. (4) The fourth is the special path that is all paths other than the former three. This presentation of their sequence is excellent.[1512] Question: Through what means do these paths abandon that which is to be abandoned?

dmigs pa'i yul sun phyung ba las ni nyon mongs pa spang byar 'dod kyi{ gnyen po dang spang bya} mtshungs par ldan pa las ni ma yin te/ {mtshungs ldan yin na de gnyis } phan tshun med na mi 'byung bar skyes pas rang gi tshogs dbye bar mi nus pa'i phyir dang*/ dmigs pa las dbye bar nus pa'i phyir ro/ / ji tsam gyis na nyon mongs pa spangs par brjod ce na/ {lam gyi dus na rang rgyud kyi phra rgyas da ltar ba med pas de spong gsung ste/ 'gag par 'gyur ba'i lam gyis nyon mongs 'das ma 'ongs dmigs yul du byas nas spong la/ de yang yul de'i gnas lugs shes pas spong ste yul kha cig gi gnas lugs ma shes na rgyud la de'i yul can gyi nyon mongs pa'i stobs kyis de'i yul can yin pa'i nyon mongs rnams kyi thob pa yang 'byung ste/ de yul sun dbyung med par ni/ / de blo spong bar nus ma yin zhes pas so } de yang rang gi rgyud la yod pa'i nyon mongs pa ni thob pa chad pa dang bral thob skyes pa'i tshul gyis spong la/ rang gi rgyud la yod pa'i nyon mongs pa can ma yin pa dge ba zag bcas dang ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gzugs can dang gzugs can ma yin pa thams cad ni de dag la dmigs pa'i yul can rang gi rgyud la yod pa'i nyon mongs pa 'dun pa'i 'dod chags spangs pa la de dag spangs pa'i tha snyad du byed de/ shes par byed pa'i lung dang bcas te bshad zin to/ / {de yang mthong spang cig car dang sgom spang rim gyis spong la mthong spang yang byis pas spong na rim gyis spong gsung }
mtshan nyid mi mthun mi mthun phyogs/ / yul rnam chad dang dus kyis te/ / 'byung dang tshul khrims phyogs dang ni/ / dus gnyis ring ba nyid lta bu'o/ / 62

thag sring ba'i ngo bo ring ba nyid kyang rnam pa bzhi yin te/ tshogs pa gcig na gnas kyang mtshan nyid mi mthun pa tha dad pas ring ba ni sa la sogs pa'i 'byung ba bzhi lta bu dang*/ mi mthun phyogs dang gnyen pos ring ba ni tshul khrims dang 'chal ba'i tshul khrims lta bu dang*/ yul rnam par chad pas ring ba ni shar nub kyi rgya mtsho la sogs pa phyogs tha dad pa lta bu dang*/ dus kyis ring ba ni chos mngon pa las/ chos ring ba dag gang zhe na/ 'das pa dang ma 'ongs pa'i chos rnams so/ / chos nye ba dag gang zhe na/ da ltar byung ba'i chos rnams dang*/ 'dus ma byas so zhes 'byung bas 'das pa dang ma 'ongs pa'i dus gnyis ring ba nyid lta bu'o/ / gal te dus gnyis po gang las ring ba yin zhe na/ bye brag tu smra ba rnams na re da ltar las so zhe'o/ /

The nature of extension or distance has four aspects: (1) Distant from another through having distinct incompatible characteristics (vailakṣana) even when abiding together — for example, the four primary elements such as earth. (2) Distant from another through being its antidote and opposing factor (vipakṣa) — for example, ethics and unethical conduct. (3) Distant from another through existing in separate places (deśaviccheda) — for example, distinct sites such as the eastern or western ocean and so on. (4) Distant through time (kāla). An Abhidharma treatise states: What are distant phenomena? Past and future phenomena. What are near phenomena? Phenomena occurring in the present and unconditioned phenomena.[1513] For example, the two times, the past and future, are distant. Question: What are these two times [488] distant from? Vaibhāṣikas say: They are distant from the present.

'o na 'das ma thag pa dang skye ba la mngon du phyogs pa'i ma 'ongs pa'ang nye bar 'gyur te/ da ltar la gzhan gyis bar du ma chod pa'i phyir ro/ /
gal te bar du chod ma chod kyis nye ring du bzhag pa ma yin gyi 'on kyang dus tha dad pas ring bar bzhag go zhe na/ de lta na da lta yang ring bar 'gyur te/ 'das ma 'ongs las dus tha dad pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na ni dus gnyis byed pas ring ba yin te/ byed pa zhig pa dang ma thob pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ de lta na 'dus ma byas kyang ring bar 'gyur te/ byed pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dod par mi nus te/ bstan bcos las nye bar bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te 'gog gnyis kyi zhes pas 'dus ma byas 'gog pa gnyis kyi thob pa yul thams cad du skye ba'i phyir nye ba yin no zhe na/ de lta na dge mi dge gzugs can ma yin pa'i 'das ma 'ongs nye ba dang 'dus ma byas nam mkha' ring bar 'gyur te/ dus gsum pa yi rnam pa gsum/ / zhes pas dus gnyis kyi thob pa'ang yul thams cad du 'byung ba'i phyir dang*/ nam mkha' la thob pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te 'das ma 'ongs ni da ltar gyis bar du chod pas phan tshun ring ba yin zhing*/ da ltar ni dus gnyis kyis bar du ma chod pas dus gnyis la ltos nas nye ba yin la/ 'dus ma byas ni gang gis kyang bar du ma chod pas nye ba yin no zhe na/ de ltar na'ang 'das ma 'ongs ni nye ring gnyis kar 'gyur te 'das pa ma 'ongs pa la ltos nas ring ba dang da ltar la ltos nas nye ba dang ma 'ongs pa'ang da ltar la ltos nas nye ba dang 'das pa la ltos nas ring ba'i phyir ro/ / 'dod par mi nus te/ 'das ma 'ongs ring ba kho nar 'dod pa dang 'gal ba'i phyir ro zhes da ltar slob dpon gyis bye brag tu smra ba'i lugs bkag nas rang nyid ni 'das ma 'ongs ni rang gi ngo bo zhig pa dang ma thob pas chos kyi rang gi mtshan nyid kyi dngos po las ring ba yin no zhes bzhed do/ /

However, the past that has just occurred, and the future that is about to arise would also be near the present because they are not separated from the present by another.
Objection: Being near or distant is not posited through being separated or not separated; being distant is posited through having a different time. Reply: If that is so, even the present would be distant because it is time that is different from the past and future. Objection: It is distant due to action pertaining to two times, because one action is destroyed and the other not obtained. Reply: If that is so, even unconditioned states would be distant because they lack action. But that is unacceptable because it is explained to be “near” in the treatise.[1514] Objection: It is near because obtainment of both unconditioned cessations is generated in relation to all objects. As the Abhidharmakośa states, “The obtainment of both cessations occurs” (2:36d). Reply: If that is so, then past and future nonphysical virtuous and nonvirtuous states would be near, and space would be distant. Why? Because even obtainment in two times would occur in relation to all objects, since the Abhidharmakośa notes, “Obtainment in the three times has three types” (2:37a). Objection: Since the past and future are separated by the present, they would be mutually distant. Since the present would separate the two times, it would be near since it relies on the two times. Since none divides the unconditioned, it would also be near. Reply: Also, if that is so, then the past and future would be both near and distant because the past is distant in reliance on the future and near in reliance on the present, and also the future is near in reliance on the present and distant in reliance on the past. But that is unacceptable because it contradicts the assertion that the past and future are distant alone! Vasubandhu, having refuted the Vaibhāṣika system, asserts that the past and future are distant from things that are real [i.e., present] phenomena since their nature is either destroyed or not yet obtained.[1515]
gsum pa spangs pa'i 'bras bu yongs shes bshad pa ni
Perfect knowledge, the result of abandoning negative tendencies
gal te lam khyad par du 'gro na nyon mongs pa rnams kyi spangs pa'ang khyad par du 'gro ba yod dam zhe na/
Question: If the path is progressive, are the afflicted states that are objects to be abandoned also progressive?
lan cig tu zad de dag gi / bral ba'i thob pa yang dang yang / / gnyen po skyes dang 'bras thob dang / / dbang po rnam par 'phel rnams su/ / 63

Afflicted states are eliminated just once, but obtaining freedom from them arises frequently: when antidotes arise, when resultant states are obtained, and when upgrading one’s intellectual faculty. (5:63)

nyon mongs pa thams cad ni rang rang gi gnyen po spong lam gang yin pa de kho nas spong zhing thob pa chad pas spangs pa lan cig tu zad{ pas khyad par med} kyi/ 'on kyang nyon mongs pa de dag gis bral ba'i thob pa ni yang dang yang du khyad par du 'gro'o/{/dus drug tu ste/} gang du zhe na/ gal te dbang po rtul po yin na rang rang gi gnyen po skyes pa dang*/ rgyun zhugs la sogs pa'i dge sbyong gi tshul gyi 'bras bu bzhi thob pa dang dbang po rtul po las dbang po rnon por rnam par 'phel ba'i dus dang drug po rnams su'o/ / dbang po rnon po yin na dbang po 'pho ba med pas dus lngar khyad par du 'gro'o/ / de la gnyen po skyes pa ni bral thob dang lhan cig skyes pas rnam grol gyi lam yin te/ bar chad med pa'i lam gyi tshe bral ba'i thob pa skye ba la mngon du phyogs pa tsam las da ltar du ma skyes pa'i phyir ro/ / bral ba des ni gnas skabs de dag tu yongs su shes pa'i ming 'thob bo/ / de la spyir yongs su shes pa ni ye shes kyi yongs su shes pa dang*/ spangs pa'i yongs su shes pa gnyis las dang po ni zag med{ rnam grol} kyi ye shes yin la/ gnyis pa ni de'i yul spang bya dang bral ba so sor brtags 'gog yin no/ / de ltar gnyis las 'dir ni phyi ma yin te/ de la yongs shes su gzhag pa ni yul la yul can gyis btags pa'am/ 'bras bu spangs pa la rgyu ye shes kyis btags pa'i phyir dang*/ mdo las kyang*/ yongs su shes pa gang zhe na/ 'di la 'dun pa'i 'dod chags spangs pa dang*/ 'dun pa'i 'dod chags las yang dag par 'das pa ste 'di ni yongs su shes pa zhes bya'o zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: All afflicted states are abandoned by an antidote that is a path abandoning them alone, and since their obtainment is severed, they are eliminated (kṣaya) just once {without distinction}, but obtaining freedom (visaṃyoga) from those afflicted states arises frequently and progressively. Question: When? Reply: If one is of dull faculty, this occurs at six times: (1) when specific antidotes arise, (2–5) when the four resultant bases of training in virtue such as that of a stream enterer are obtained, and (6) when upgrading [489] one’s intellectual faculty from dull to sharp. If one is of sharp faculty, there is progression at five times since there is no upgrade of intellectual faculty. “When antidotes arise” refers to the liberated path, since it arises simultaneously with the obtainment of freedom. During the uninterrupted path one merely approaches the obtainment of freedom; it does not arise at that time. By obtaining that freedom, one is called “one who possesses perfect knowledge at those times.” In general, perfect knowledge has two types: (1) the perfect knowledge of transcendent wisdom and (2) the perfect knowledge of abandonment. The first is uncontaminated transcendent wisdom, and the second is the analytical cessation free from that which is to be abandoned. Here is it is the second of these two, because positing it as perfect knowledge is designating the mind with [the name of] its object, or designating the resultant abandonment with [the name of] the causal transcendent wisdom. A sūtra notes: What is perfect knowledge? That which abandons longing desire, and perfectly transcends longing desire, is called perfect knowledge.[1516]
yongs su shes dgu 'dod pa na/ / dang po rnams gnyis zad la gcig / gnyis zad pa ni de gnyis so/ / de bzhin gong ma'i de gsum nyid/ / 64
Perfect knowledge has nine types. One eliminates two aspects of the first two truths in the desire realm, two eliminate two, so too there are three in higher realms. (5:64)

de lta bu'i yongs su shes pa de yang spang bya spangs pa'i sgo nas dbye na rnam pa dgu ste/ 'di ltar 'dod pa'i khams na bden pa dang po gnyis kyi mthong bas spang bya rnam pa gnyis zad pa la ni 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes gcig dang*/ 'gog lam mthong spang rnam pa gnyis zad pa ni 'gog pa mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes dang*/ lam mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes de gnyis so/ / ji ltar 'dod pa'i mthong spang spangs pa la yongs shes gsum yin pa de bzhin du khams gong ma gnyis po'i mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs su shes pa de yang gsum nyid de/ gong ma gnyis po'i bden pa dang po gnyis kyi mthong spang la sogs pa'o/ / de ltar na khams gsum gyi mthong spang spangs pa ni yongs shes drug tu bzhag go /

Such perfect knowledge (parijñā) has nine types, classified by means of abandoning the object to be abandoned: (1) One perfect knowledge abandons objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of suffering and origin in the desire realm, which eliminates (kṣaya) two aspects to be abandoned by seeing the first two truths in the desire realm. (2–3) Two eliminate the two aspects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of cessation and path. They are perfect knowledge abandoning objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of cessation, and perfect knowledge abandoning objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of path. (4–6) Just as there are three perfect knowledges abandoning objects to be abandoned by seeing in the desire realm, so too there are three perfect knowledges abandoning objects to be abandoned by seeing in the two higher realms, such as objects to be abandoned by seeing the first two truths of the two higher realms and so on. Thus, those that abandon objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing in the three realms are posited as the six perfect knowledges.
yongs su shes pa gzhan gsum ste/ / tha ma'i cha dang mthun gzugs dang / / zag pa kun zad drug bzod 'bras/ / lhag ma rnams ni shes pa'i yin/ / 65

There are three other perfect knowledges eliminating factors associated with inferior states, those of the form realm, and all contaminants. Six are the result of perseverance. The others are knowledges. (5:65)

sgom spang spangs pa la yongs su shes pa sngar gyi drug po las gzhan gsum ste/ khams gsum gyi sgom spang spangs pa las rim pa ltar{ 'dod pa'i dgu pa zad pas spangs pa na} tha ma'i cha dang mthun pa zad cing spangs pa dang*/ gzugs khams kyi{ nyon mongs zad par spangs pa} zag pa'am 'dod chags zad pa dang*/ gzugs med kyi nyon mongs zad par spangs pa zag pa kun zad pa'am kun sbyor thams cad yongs su gtugs pa'i yongs su shes pa'o/ / gal te khams gong ma gnyis kyi mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes gcig tu bsdoms la sgom spang spangs pa'i tha dad du phye zhe na/ sgom spang ni khams gong ma gnyis nas dang sa na sgom spang dgu dgu'i gnyen por bar chad med pa dang rnam grol gyi lam nyer bsdogs mi lcogs med la sogs pa zag med dang zag bcas gnyis pa'i nyer bsdogs la sogs pas bsdus pa dgu dgu yod pas gnyen po tha dad pa'i phyir dang*/ mthong spang rnams kyi ni gzugs na spyod pa'i gnyen po rjes bzod la sogs pa de dag kho na gzugs med kyi mthong spang gi yang gnyen po yin pas gnyen po gcig pa'i phyir yin no/ /

Other than the former six, there are three perfect knowledges that abandon objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation. Those that abandon objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation in the three realms are respectively: (7) perfect knowledge eliminating and abandoning factors associated with inferior states {when the nine desire stages are exhaustively abandoned}, (8) perfect knowledge exhaustively abandoning afflictions of the form realm and eliminating contaminants or attachment, and (9) perfect knowledge eliminating all contaminants or all fetters entirely {and exhaustively abandoning formless-realm affliction}. Objection: Perfect knowledges that abandon objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing in the two higher realms are combined as one, but those abandoning objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation are classified separately. Reply: Objects abandoned by the path of meditation have separate antidotes since there are nine for each realm. They are subsumed by uncontaminated and contaminated access concentrations and so on, such as uninterrupted and liberated unrestricted access concentration. These act as antidotes to the nine stages of objects abandoned by the path of meditation on each level of the two higher realms. Objects abandoned by seeing [490] all share the same antidote, in that antidotes active in the form realm, such as subsequent perseverance, are also antidotes to objects abandoned by seeing in the formless realm.

yongs su shes pa dgu po de las dang po drug ni bzod pa'i 'bras bu yin te/ mthong lam bar chad med pa'i lam gyi 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te yongs shes ni bzod pa'i 'bras bu ma yin te/ de ni zag med kyi shes pa'i 'bras bu yin la dri med bzod rnams shes pa min zhes pas bzod pa ni shes pa ma yin pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ yongs shes bzod pa'i 'khor shes pa'i 'bras bu yin yang shes bzod gnyis 'bras bu gcig pas shes pa'i 'bras bu la bzod pa'i 'bras bur bstan pa yin te/ dper na rgyal po'i 'khor gyis byas pa la rgyal pos byas so zhes brjod pa bzhin no zhes pa'am/ yang na shes pa gtso bo dang bzod pa 'khor yin pas dngos su gtso bo shes pa'i 'bras bu yin yang 'khor la rgyal por btags pa ltar 'khor bzod pa'i 'bras bur btags pa yin no zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/ / yongs shes drug gi lhag ma tha ma gsum po rnams ni shes pa'i 'bras bu yin te/ sgom lam gyi 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir dang*/ sgom lam la bzod pa med pa'i phyir ro/ /

From those nine perfect knowledges, the first six are the result of perseverance (kṣāntiphala) because they are the result of the uninterrupted path of seeing. Objection: Perfect knowledge is not the result of perseverance because it is the result of uncontaminated knowledge, and perseverance is not knowledge since the Abhidharmakośa states, “Stainless perseverance is not knowledge” (7:1a). Reply: Though perfect knowledge is the result of knowledge in the retinue of perseverance, the result of knowledge is taught to be the result of perseverance, since the results of both knowledge and perseverance are the same. For example, it is like saying “If it is done by the king’s retinue, it is done by the king,” or since knowledge is dominant and perseverance is its retinue, [perseverance] is explicitly designated as the result of knowledge, just as the retinue is designated as the king. This is said by Master Pūrṇavardhana.[1517] The three final perfect knowledges that are other than the six perfect knowledges are the results of knowledges (jñāna), because they are the results of the path of meditation and there is no perseverance in the path of meditation.
mi lcogs med 'bras thams cad do/ / bsam gtan rnams kyi lnga'am brgyad/ / nye bar bsdogs pa'i gcig yin te/ / gzugs med dngos gzhi gsum gyi yang / / 66

All are the result of unrestricted access concentration. Five or eight are the result of absorption. The result of access concentration is the eighth alone, also the three actual bases of the formless realm. (5:66)

yang yongs shes de dag bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs mi lcog pa med pa ni spang bya thams cad kyi gnyen por 'gyur ba srid pas de'i 'bras bu ni yongs shes dgu po thams cad do/ / bsam gtan dngos gzhi zag med rnams kyi 'bras bu ni khams gong ma gnyis kyi mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes gsum dang*/ sgom spang spangs pa'i yongs shes phyi ma gnyis te lnga yin la/{ bsam gtan ni dngos gzhi la brten nas de dag nyon mongs spong ba da pa'i phyir te chags bral sngon 'gro la bsams so/} gzhan dag{ 'dod pa'i nyon mongs spangs pa'i yongs shes} ni mi lcogs med kyi 'bras bu yin no zhes bye brag tu smra ba phal che ba 'dod la{ de yang dngos gzhi'i 'dod pa'i gnyen po ma yin pa'am/ 'dod pa la 'dod chags dang ma bral ba dngos gzhi la mi 'jug pa'i phyir zhes 'chad do/ / des na chags bral sngon 'gro la 'dod pa'i mthong spang gi bral thob zag med yod kyang de'i 'bras bu ma yin te/ tha ma'i cha mthun spangs pa'i yongs shes bzhin no zhes so/ /} 'am zhes bya ba ni lugs tha dad ston pa ste btsun pa dbyangs sgrogs na re bsam gtan dngos gzhi'i 'bras bu ni {chags bral sngon 'gros 'dod pa'i mthong spang spangs pa gsum bsnan nas } yongs shes brgyad yin te/ 'dod pa'i mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes gsum yang chags bral sngon 'gro'i phyir mi 'ong dag gis mthong lam thob pa'i bsam gtan gyi stobs kyis bral ba'i thob pa zag med rnyed pa'i phyir dang*/ tha ma'i cha mthun spangs pa'i yongs shes gcig pu ni mi lcogs med kyi 'bras bu kho {dang de'i bral thob ni gong ma'i lam mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes dang gcig tu 'dus so } nar nges pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ / bsam gtan khyad par can yang bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi dang 'dra bar shes par bya'o/ /

Again, regarding perfect knowledge, all nine perfect knowledges are the result of unrestricted access concentration (anāgamya), since it is possible that unrestricted access concentration of the first absorption acts as the antidote to all objects of abandonment. Five are the result of the uncontaminated actual bases of absorption (dhyāna): (4–6) three perfect knowledges abandoning objects to be abandoned by seeing in the two higher realms, and (8–9) the two latter perfect knowledges abandoning objects to be abandoned by meditation. {Here this refers to āryas previously freed from attachment, because it is possible that those dependent on the actual bases of the absorptions abandon those afflictions}. The others, {namely, perfect knowledge abandoning afflictions in the desire realm,} are the result of unrestricted access concentration. This is asserted by most Vaibhāṣikas. {Further, they explain that it is not the antidote of desire of the actual basis, or it is not free from attachment to the desire realm, because it does not engage the actual basis. Therefore, though one who is previously freed from attachment has the uncontaminated obtainment of freedom from objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing in the desire realm, it is not the result of that, since it is like perfect knowledge abandoning factors associated with inferior states}. The term “or” teaches a distinct system, since Ghoṣaka says: Eight perfect knowledges are the result of the actual basis of absorption, {through adding the three objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing in the desire realm by one previously freed from attachment,} because there are also (1–3) three perfect knowledges abandoning objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing in the desire realm. That is because nonreturners previously freed from attachment gain uncontaminated obtainment of separation by the power of absorption obtaining the path of seeing, the single perfect knowledge that abandons factors associated with inferior states is solely ascertained as the result of unrestricted access concentration, {and obtainment of freedom from them is included within perfect knowledge abandoning objects to be abandoned by seeing the path in higher realms}. [491] One should understand that special absorption is similar to the actual basis of absorption.

gzugs med nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched kyi nye bar bsdogs pa'i 'bras bu ni yongs shes brgyad pa gcig pu yin te/ de zag bcas yin yang 'phags pas de la brten nas yongs shes 'di 'thob pa srid pa'i phyir ro/ / nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched la sogs pa gzugs med dngos gzhi zag med dang po gsum gyi 'bras bu yang zag pa kun zad kyi yongs shes gcig na kho yin no/{ de dag kyang zag med kyi yin gyi gzhan gyi gong sa las mi rgyal bsam/} des na 'dod pa dang srid rtse'i sems ni zag med kyi lam gyi rten du mi rung ba'i phyir yongs shes kyi rgyur mi 'gyur ro/ /

The result of access concentration to the basis of infinite space is the eighth perfect knowledge alone, because though that is contaminated, it is possible that āryas obtain this perfect knowledge in dependence on that. Also, the result of the three uncontaminated actual bases of the formless realm, such as the base of infinite space, constitutes one perfect knowledge fully eliminating contaminants alone. {Those are uncontaminated since they remain unconquered in other higher levels.} Therefore, because the minds of the desire realm and the summit of existence are unsuitable to be the basis of the uncontaminated path, they are not the causes of perfect knowledge.
thams cad 'phags pa'i lam gyi yin/ / 'jig rten pa'i gnyis rjes kyi yang / / chos shes pa'i ni gsum yin no/ / de'i phyogs mthun gyi drug dang lnga/ / 67
All are the result of the ārya paths. Two of the mundane path. Also subsequent knowledge. Dharma knowledge is three final knowledges. Six or five are compatible with it. (5:67)

yongs shes dgu po thams cad ni 'phags pa'i lam gyi 'bras bu yin te/ dang po drug dang phyi ma gsum rim pa ltar mthong lam dang sgom lam gyi 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / zag bcas 'jig rten pa'i sgom lam gyi 'bras bu ni yongs shes bdun pa dang brgyad pa gnyis yin te/ 'phags pa dag 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis 'dod gzugs las 'dod chags dang bral ba srid pa'i phyir ro/ / sgom lam gyis bsdus pa'i rjes shes kyi 'bras bu yang yongs shes tha ma gnyis yin la/

All perfect knowledge is the result of ārya paths because the first six and the latter three are, respectively, the results of the path of seeing and the path of meditation. Two are the result of the contaminated mundane path of meditation — the seventh and eighth perfect knowledges — because it is possible that āryas attain freedom from attachment to the desire and form realms through the mundane path. Also, the result of subsequent knowledge subsumed by the path of meditation is the two final perfect knowledges,

sgom lam gyis bsdus pa'i chos shes pa'i 'bras bu ni sgom pa'i lam la 'gog pa'am/ lam la chos shes gang yin de/ / khams gsum gyi ni gnyen po yin/ / zhes 'byung bas yongs shes tha ma gsum yin no/ / {de yang de khams gsum gyi gnyen po yin pas so } chos shes de'i phyogs dang mthun pa chos shes pa'i bzod pa dang shes pa rnams kyi 'bras bu ni yongs shes drug yin te/ dang po { 'dod pa'i} gsum chos bzod kyi 'bras bu dang*/ tha ma gsum{ sgom spang spangs pa'i} chos shes kyi 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang sgom lam gyis bsdus pa'i sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung shes pas bsdus pa'i ni tha ma'i cha mthun spangs pa'i yongs shes gcig pu yin la 'gog lam shes pa'i ni yongs shes gsum char yin no/ / rjes shes de'i phyogs dang mthun pa rjes su shes pa'i bzod pa dang shes pa'i 'bras bu ni yongs shes lnga yin te/ khams gong ma gnyis kyi mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes gsum rjes bzod kyi 'bras bu dang*/ tha ma gnyis rjes shes kyi 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te la lar ni spangs pa mang po bsdoms nas yongs shes re rer 'jog la/ la lar ni spangs pa re re la yongs shes re rer 'jog pa la rgyu mtshan ci yod ce na/

and the result of Dharma knowledge subsumed by the path of meditation is the three final perfect knowledges {as well as antidotes to the three realms} since the Abhidharmakośa notes, “On the path of meditation, Dharma knowledge regarding cessation or path is an antidote to the three realms” (7:9abc).[1518] Dharma knowledge, perseverance for Dharma knowledge that is compatible with it, and resultant knowledge constitute six perfect knowledges because (1–3) the first three {of the desire realm} are results of Dharma perseverance, and (4–6) the latter three are results of Dharma knowledge {that has abandoned objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing}. Further, the knowledge of the truths of suffering and origin subsumed by the path of meditation constitute a single perfect knowledge abandoning factors associated with inferior states. That, plus the knowledge of the truths of cessation and path, constitute three types of perfect knowledge. Five perfect knowledges are results of subsequent perseverance and subsequent knowledge that are compatible with that subsequent knowledge because (1–3) three perfect knowledges abandoning that which is to be abandoned by the path of seeing in the two higher realms are results of subsequent perseverance, and (4–5) the latter two are results of subsequent knowledge. Question: At times one perfect knowledge is posited relative to many objects to be abandoned in combination, and at times one perfect knowledge is posited relative to a single object to be abandoned. What is the reason?
bral ba'i thob pa zag med dang / / srid rtse nyams par byas pa dang / / rgyu gnyis kun tu bcom pa'i phyir/ / yongs shes khams las 'das pa las/ / 68
It is perfect knowledge because it is the uncontaminated obtainment of freedom, it discards the summit of existence, it completely destroys the two causes, and it transcends the three realms. (5:68)

de la shes bzod rnams kyi 'bras bu bral ba ni rgyu gsum gyis yongs shes su bzhag ste zhes sbyar te/ gang zhe na bral ba'i thob pa zag med gsar du rnyed pa dang*/ srid rtse'i nyon mongs pa nyams par byas pa dang*/ rgyu sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung mthong spang gi kun 'gro gnyis kun du bcom pa'i phyir ro/ / de la so so'i skye bo la ni rgyu gnyis bcom pa yod kyang{ snga ma gnyis med pas 'di spangs pa la yongs shes kyi ming mi thob la 'phags pa la'ang ji srid/} sdug bsngal la chos shes pa la ni dang po yod kyang phyi ma gnyis med de{ rgyu gnyis bcom pa dang srid rtse nyams pa med pa'i phyir ro} sdug bsngal la rjes su shes pa la ni dang po gnyis yod kyang phyi ma{ rgyun gyi bcom pa} med de/ kun 'byung mthong spang gi kun 'gro ma spangs pa'i phyir ro/ / kun 'byung la chos shes pa'i gnas skabs na ni gsum ga yod pa'i phyir 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes gcig tu gzhag go /de bzhin du khams gong ma gnyis kyi la'ang shes par bya'o/ / 'dod pa'i 'gog lam la chos shes pa gnyis ni re re la'ang rgyu gsum ga tshang ba'i phyir yongs shes re rer gzhag gi bzod pa rnams ni ma yin te/ bral thob zag med gsar du ma rnyed pa'i phyir ro/ / de dag ni bzod pa'i 'bras bu yongs shes drug tu 'jog pa'i rgyu yin no/ / sgom lam la bzod pa med pas shes pa'i 'bras bu yongs shes tha ma gsum ni rgyu gsum po de dag dang*/ bzhi pa 'dod pa la sogs pa'i khams gsum las 'das pa las kyang rim pa ltar gzhag go /chos mngon pa pa gang dag dmigs par bya ba'i nyon mongs pa dang dmigs par byed pa'i nyon mongs pa gnyis dang bral ba'i rgyu lnga pa 'dod pa ni 'dir ma brjod de/ rgyu gnyis kun tu bcom pa dang*/ khams las 'das pa'i nang du 'dus pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: The resultant freedom arising from knowledge and perseverance is posited as perfect knowledge (parijñā) due to three causes. Question: Why? Reply: Because (1) it is the uncontaminated obtainment of freedom that is newly attained, (2) it discards (vikalīkṛta) afflictions of the summit of existence (bhavāgra), and (3) it completely destroys (samudghāta) the two causes: pervasive states that are abandoned by seeing the truths of suffering and origin. [492] Ordinary beings possess [the third of these — namely,] destruction of the two causes — {but since they do not have the first two, they are not called “those who possesses perfect knowledge that abandons such states.” This is also true for āryas as long as they lack the first two}. Those with Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering have the first but not the latter two {because they do not possess destruction of the two causes and they do not discard afflictions of the summit of existence}. Those with subsequent knowledge of the truth of suffering possess the first two but not the latter — {destruction of the stream} — because they do not abandon pervasive states that are objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of origin. Because all three exist in the context of Dharma knowledge of the truth of origin, they are posited as one perfect knowledge abandoning objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of suffering and origin. This should be applied in a similar way to the two higher realms. Two Dharma knowledges of the truths of cessation and path in the desire realm are posited as one perfect knowledge because the three causes are complete for each. But the Dharma perseverance of either is not so posited because they do not newly attain the uncontaminated obtainment of freedom. Still, they act as causes for establishing the results of perseverance as the six perfect knowledges. Since there is no perseverance on the path of meditation, the final three perfect knowledges that are the results of knowledge are posited, respectively, due to those three causes and through a fourth cause: the [perfect knowledge] that transcends the three realms. Ābhidharmikas assert a fifth cause: freedom both from afflictions that focus on objects and from the afflictions that are focused on. However, it is not mentioned here because it is included in two causes: completely destroying the two causes, and transcending the three realms.
gang zag gang la du zhig ldan tshul/
'o na yongs shes de dag gang zag gang la du zhig ldan zhe na/
Question: What persons possess what perfect knowledges?
gcig min mthong la gnas pa ni/ / lnga yi bar dang yang dag ldan/ / bsgoms la gnas pa drug gam ni/ / gcig gam yang na gnyis dang ngo/ / 69
One does not. Those who abide on the path of seeing correctly possess up to five. One abiding on the path of meditation possesses six, or one, or again two. (5:69)

gcig ste so so'i skye bo ni yongs shes dang ldan pa min te/ ye shes kyis spangs pa med pas bral thob zag med med pa'i phyir ro/ / der ma zad sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa nas bzung ste kun 'byung la chos shes pa'i bzod pa'i bar ye shes skad cig ma lnga la gnas pa'ang rgyu gnyis kun tu ma bcom pa'i phyir yongs shes dang mi ldan no/ / de las gzhan pa'i 'phags pa mthong lam la gnas pa ni gcig nas lnga'i bar dang yang dag par ldan te/ 'di ltar kun 'byung la chos shes pa dang kun 'byung la rjes su shes pa'i bzod pa gnyis la gnas pa ni 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes gcig dang ldan no/ / kun 'byung la rjes su shes pa dang 'gog pa la chos shes pa'i bzod pa gnyis la gnas pa la ni yongs su shes pa snga ma dang khams gong ma gnyis kyi sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes te gnyis dang ldan no/ / 'gog pa la chos shes pa dang 'gog pa la rjes su shes pa'i bzod pa la gnas pa la ni snga ma gnyis dang 'dod pa'i 'gog pa mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes te gsum dang ldan no/ / 'gog pa la rjes su shes pa dang lam la chos shes pa'i bzod pa la gnas pa la ni gsum po de dag dang gong ma gnyis kyi 'gog pa mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes te bzhi dang ldan no/ /

One who is an ordinary being does not possess perfect knowledge. He does not have the uncontaminated obtainment of freedom in that he lacks abandonment by transcendent wisdom. Not only that, he does not possess perfect knowledge because he does not fully destroy the two causes. He may abide, however, in the [first] five [of the sixteen] moments of transcendent wisdom, from perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering up to perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of origin. But āryas who abide on the path of seeing are different, for they correctly possess from one up to five perfect knowledges. Thus one abiding either in Dharma knowledge of the truth of origin or in perseverance for subsequent knowledge of the truth of origin possesses one perfect knowledge that abandons objects to be abandoned by seeing the desire-realm truths of suffering and origin. One abiding either in subsequent knowledge of the truth of origin or in perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of cessation possesses two: (1) the former perfect knowledge plus (2) the perfect knowledge abandoning objects to be abandoned by seeing the truths of suffering and origin of the higher realms. One abiding either in Dharma knowledge of the truth of cessation or in perseverance for subsequent knowledge of the truth of cessation possesses three: (1–2) the former two plus (3) the perfect knowledge abandoning objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of cessation of the desire realm. One abiding either in subsequent knowledge of the truth of cessation or in perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of the path possesses four: (1–3) those three [493] plus (4) the perfect knowledge abandoning objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of cessation of the two higher realms.

lam la chos shes pa dang lam la rjes su shes pa'i bzod pa la gnas pa la ni bzhi po de dag dang 'dod pa'i lam mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes te lnga dang ldan no/ / lam la rjes shes ni sgom lam yin pas 'di'i nang du mi gtogs so/ / sgom lam la gnas pa ni yongs shes drug gam ste lam la rjes shes thob pa nas bzung ste 'dod pa la 'dod chags dang ma bral ba sgom spang dang po nas brgyad pa spangs pa'i bar la gnas pa yang sngar gyi lnga dang gong ma gnyis kyi lam mthong spang spangs pa'i yongs shes te drug dang ldan la/ 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba las nyams na'ang drug po de dag nyid dang ldan no/ / {'di ni mthar gyis par nges so } gal te lam la rjes shes thob pa na yongs shes drug dang ldan par mi 'gyur te/ 'bras bu bzhir rnam gzhag pa ni/ / rgyu lnga dag ni srid phyir ro/ / 'bras la sngon lam btang ba dang*/ / gzhan thob pa dang zad bsdoms dang*/ / shes pa brgyad chen thob pa dang*/ / rnam pa bcu drug thob pa'o zhes {skad cig bcu drug pa'i tshe zhugs lam btang ba la sogs pa'i rgyu tshang bas }spangs pa bsdoms par bshad pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ {de'i tshe } spangs pa bsdoms pa yin gyi yongs shes bsdoms pa ni ma yin pas 'gal med do zhes TIka byed dag 'chad do/ /

One abiding either in Dharma knowledge of the truth of the path or in perseverance for subsequent knowledge of the truth of path possesses five: (1–4) those four plus (5) the perfect knowledge abandoning objects to be abandoned by seeing the the truth of the path of the desire realm. Since Dharma knowledge of the truth of the path is the path of meditation, it is not included here. One abiding on the path of meditation possesses six perfect knowledges. Therefore one who has obtained subsequent knowledge of the truth of the path, and who has abandoned from one to eight objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation but is not free from attachment to the desire realm, possesses six: (1–5) the former five plus (6) perfect knowledge abandoning objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of the path of the two higher realms. Even though freedom from attachment may degenerate, he possesses those six. {This person is certainly a serial abandoner.} Objection: If one obtains subsequent knowledge of the truth of the path, one does not possess six perfect knowledges because it is said: The theory of the four results exists because the five causes are possible. To attain the result, the path is first activated, and one obtains the others. Elimination is combined, one obtains the eight great knowledges, and one obtains the sixteen aspects. This passage explains that abandonment [or elimination] is combined, {since the causes activating entry to the [ārya] path are complete at the time of the sixteenth moment}. Reply: This does not contradict the root text, for though {at that time} abandonment is combined, perfect knowledges are not combined. This is explained by the Subcommentary.[1519]

yang bsgom pa'i lam la gnas pa kha cig ni yongs su shes pa gcig gam ste 'phags pa thog mar 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral bar byas te phyis nges pa la 'jug pa'am/ thog mar mthong lam thob nas phyis 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral bar byed pa'i 'phags pa phyir mi 'ong yin kyang rung ste lam la rjes shes kyi tshe snga ma rnams bsdoms te {tha ma'i cha mthun spangs pa } bdun pa gcig pu dang ldan la/ {'phags pa } gzugs las 'dod chags dang bral ba las nyams na'ang de nyid dang ldan no/ / dgra bcom pa thob pa'i tshe yang yongs shes snga ma thams cad bsdoms pa'i phyir yongs shes tha ma gcig pu dang ldan no/ / sgom lam la gnas pa yang na gnyis dang po ste gzugs kyi 'dod chags dang bral ba'i 'phags pa phyir mi 'ong de nyid gzugs kyi 'dod chags dang bral ba thob pa dang*/ gzugs med pa'i nyon mongs pas dgra bcom pa las nyams na'ang bdun pa dang brgyad pa gnyis dang ldan no/ /
gal te gzugs kyi 'dod chags dang ma bral ba'i phyir mi 'ong{ gi 'bras gnas tsam po} dang dgra bcom pa'i 'bras bu thob pa'i tshe spangs pa mang po yod bzhin du yongs shes gcig tu{ 'am re re kho nar} ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/

Or some abide on the path of meditation with one perfect knowledge and definitely enter the state of an ārya initially freed from attachment to desire-realm objects due to the mundane path. Or some who first obtain the path of seeing and later attain freedom from attachment to the desire realm and become ārya nonreturners possess the seventh alone — {the abandonment of factors associated with higher states} — since the five former are combined at the time of subsequent knowledge of the truth of path. Again, one abiding on the path of meditation possesses two, since an ārya nonreturner free from attachment to the form realm obtains freedom from attachment to the form realm, and an arhat who degenerates through formless-realm affliction possesses the seventh and eighth perfect knowledges.
