bar du yin la/ yongs su dag pa ni zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa dang mi slob pa'i yang dag pa'i lta ba yin no/{ bslab pa ni dri ma lhag ma dang bcas pa'o/} zhes zer ro/ /

Reply: They are advice with six causal aspects: (1) counting (gaṇana) and so on, which refers to (2) monitoring, (3) fixing, (4) investigating, (5) transforming, and (6) fully purifying. (1) Counting means directing the mind to inhalation and exhalation {while maintaining the body and mind in their natural state, without collecting the mind,} and mentally counting from one to ten. One does not count less than that, out of concern for laxity (saṃsīdana), or more than that, out of concern for excitation (auddhatya). Further, taking two breaths as one is undercounting and one as two is overcounting. Counting inhalation as exhalation and exhalation as inhalation is confused counting. Counting free of these three errors is correct counting. (2) Monitoring should be understood as monitoring inhalation of greater or lesser strength, which respectively fills a full span or the full height of the body from the stomach, to the heart, navel, waist, thighs, calves, soles of the feet. Monitoring exhalation is monitoring exhalation from the soles of the feet to the nostrils, which is, respectively, a full span if weak and the full height of the body if strong. Some say: Inhalation refers to the wind maṇḍala, and exhalation refers to the scattering wind. Reply: That is not so, because this is for attention focused on reality (tattva), which is impossible here. (3) Fixing is observing the abidance of wind from the tip of the nose to the soles of the feet, which is like a thread of jewels, and investigating whether the body is benefited or harmed, cooled or warmed. (4) Investigating is investigating inhalation and exhalation that is not just the wind [element] but that which possesses the essential nature of the eight physical substances of the primary elements and derivative form. Also it is investigating the five aggregates associated with the phenomena of minds and mental factors that depend on [the breath]. (5) Transforming is correctly preparing the root of virtue, which is enhanced from the heat stage to the supreme mundane state stage [of the path of preparation] through transforming the mind focusing on wind. (6) Fully purifying is entering the paths of seeing and meditation. Some say: Transforming is from close placement of mindfulness to vajra-like concentration. Fully purifying is the knowledge of elimination and nonarising and the correct view of no more learning. {Training possesses remaining stains.}

de nyid kyi phyir slob dpon gyis 'grel par/ dbugs rngub dbugs 'byung dran pa ni/ / bgrang dang rjes 'gro 'jog pa dang*/ / rtog pa dang ni bsgyur ba dang*/ / yongs dag rnam pa drug tu 'dod/ / ces bsdu ba'i tshigs bcad mdzad pa yin no/ /

Thus Vasubandhu has summarized this in verse in his Autocommentary: Mindfulness of inhalation and exhalation is asserted to be the six aspects: counting, monitoring, fixing, investigating, transforming, and fully purifying.[1558]
dbugs rngub dbugs 'byung gang las lus/ / sems can zhes bya ma zin pa'o/ / rgyu mthun las byung 'og ma yi/ / yid kyis de gnyis ma rtogs so/ / 13

On what level do inhalation and exhalation exist? That on which the body depends. It pertains to sentient beings. It is unconscious and arises from natural outflow. Lower minds do not comprehend those two. (6:13)

dbug rngub pa dang dbugs 'byung ba sa gang las yin zhe na/ lus kyi phyogs gcig yin pa'i phyir sems gang la rten pa'i lus sa gang yin pa de'i sa par rig par bya ste/ 'dod pa'i sems la rten na 'dod pa'i sa pa yin la bsam gtan dang po la rten la bsam gtan dang po'i sa pa nas gsum pa la rten na gsum pa'i sa pa'i rlung yin pa'i bar du'o/ / bsam gtan bzhi pa na rlung rgyu ba med pa'i phyir de'i sa pa ma yin no/ / yang lus sems khyad par can sbubs dang bcas pa dang sems dang bcas pa la rten pas nur nur po la sogs pa dang sems med pa dang gzugs med pa rnams la ni ma yin no/ / skye ba dang bsam gtan bzhi pa las ldang ba na rlung 'jug pa kho na dang*/ 'chi ba dang bsam gtan bzhi pa la snyoms par 'jug pa na rlung 'byung ba kho na yin no/

Question: On what level do inhalation and exhalation exist? Reply: One should recognize that level [509] to be the level of the body reliant on [specific types of] mind, because inhalation and exhalation exist at the same place as the body (kāya). If the wind depends on the desire-realm mind, then it is the breath of the desire-realm level. If it depends on the first to third absorption, it is the level of breath of the first to third absorptions. But because there is no movement of wind in the fourth absorption, inhalation and exhalation do not exist on that level. Breathing does not exist for the embryonic states of kalala and so on, nor for beings of mindless and formless states, since they depend, respectively, on the special capsule of the body and mind or on the mind [alone]. A being who is born when arising from the fourth absorption has only inhalation of breath. A being who dies when entering meditative attainment on the fourth absorption has only exhalation of breath.

{/mi sdug pa dang*/}dbugs rngub pa dang 'byung ba ni sems can zhes bya ba'i grangs su gtogs kyi rgyud kyis ma bsdus pa ni ma yin {te thob mthong dang ldan pa'i phyir ro } 'on kyang dbang po dang tha dad par 'jug pas na sems kyis ma zin pa zhes bya'o/ / rlung de dag skal mnyam gyi rgyus bskyed pas rgyu mthun pa las byung ba yin gyi rnam smin dang rgyas pas byung ba ni ma yin no/ / chad nas mtshams sbyor ba'i phyir dang*/ rnam smin gyi gzugs la ni chad nas mtshams sbyor ba med pa'i phyir dang*/ lus rgyas pa na rlung 'grib pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir 'grel pa las/ lus rgyas pas rlung 'grib par 'gyur ba'i phyir rgyas pa las byung ba ma yin no/ / dbugs rngub pa dang 'byung ba rnams chad nas yang nying mtshams sbyor ba'i phyir rnam par smin pa las skyes pa ma yin no/ / rnam par smin pa'i gzugs la ni de lta bu med do zhes 'byung ba la TIka byed dag gis kyang rnam par smin pa'i bdag nyid kyi gzugs mig la sogs pa la ni yang nying mtshams sbyor ba 'di med kyi/ sems dang sems las byung ba la ni yang nying mtshams sbyor ba mi bzlog go zhes sems dang sems byung ni rnam smin skyes yin kyang chad nas yang mtshams sbyor ba la 'gal ba med par bshad do/ / de bzhin du mi ldan pa'i 'du byed rnam smin skyes kyang gzugs dang 'dra bar mngon no/ / rlung de gnyis kyang rang gi sa pa dang sa gong ma'i sems kyis rtogs kyi 'og ma'i yid kyis ni rlung de gnyis mi rtogs so/ /

{Repulsiveness,} inhalation, and exhalation pertain to sentient beings (sattva), but they are not subsumed within their mindstreams {because they can be obtained and seen}. Moreover, breathing is said to be an unconscious activity of the mind since it can be engaged separately from the faculties. Since breathing is generated by a homogeneous cause, it arises from natural outflow (naiṣyandika). It does not arise from karmic maturation and enhancement, because the breath recovers when its continuum is severed, maturational form does not recover when its continuum is severed, and the breath may subside when the body is enhanced. Therefore the Autocommentary observes: It does not arise from enhancement, because the breath may subside when the body is enhanced. It does not arise from karmic maturation, because the breath recovers even though the continuum of inhalation and exhalation has been severed. Maturational form is not like that.[1559] Also the Subcommentary explains: Maturational form such as the eyes does not again recover. The recovery of minds and mental factors is not stopped.[1560] Though minds and mental factors arise from karmic maturation, there is no contradiction in them recovering after having been severed. Though nonassociated formative factors arise from karmic maturation, they are actually like form. These two breaths are comprehended by minds of higher level and one’s own level. Minds (manas) of lower level do not comprehend those two breaths.

gong ma'i lus la 'og ma'i sems ji ltar 'byung zhe na/ 'dod pa nas bsam gtan bzhi pa'i bar du sa gong ma thob pa'i lus la 'og ma 'dod pa la sogs pa'i sprul sems dang spyod lam pa'i sems gnyis 'byung bar 'dod de/ de gnyis kyis mi rtogs so zhes bya ba'i don to/ / {de gnyis kyis kyang mi rtogs na nyon mongs can gyis lta ci smros zhes pa'o/ /de la mi sdug pa dang dbugs dran pa ni lam la 'jug pa'i sgo yin no }

Question: How does a lower mind arise in a higher body? Reply: It is asserted that from the desire realm to the fourth absorption, both the minds of emanation and mind governing demeanor arise in a body obtained in higher levels. But those two minds do not comprehend their objects. {If these two do not comprehend their objects, then obviously afflicted minds also do not. Mindfulness of repulsiveness and breath are the door for entering the path.}
gnyis pa lhag mthong bskyed pa ni
GENERATING INSIGHT
zhi gnas grub par gyur pa yis/ / dran pa nyer gzhag bsgom par bya/ / lus tshor sems dang chos rnams la/ / mtshan nyid gnyis su yongs brtags pas/ / 14
Having established calm abiding, one should meditate on the four foundations of mindfulness by thoroughly investigating the two characteristics of body, feeling, mind, and phenomena. (6:14)

de ltar 'jug pa'i sgo gnyis kyis zhi gnas kyi ting nge 'dzin grub kyang lhag mthong gi shes rab med na nyon mongs pa rnams rtsa ba nas mi spong ste/ mdo las/ nyon mongs pa rnams ni ye shes kyis gzhom par bya ba yin no zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

Though these two doors establish the concentration of calm abiding, if the wisdom of insight does not exist, afflicted states are not abandoned from the root. A sūtra notes: Afflicted states are annihilated by transcendent wisdom.[1561] [510]

{The nine mental placements that are the means for attaining calm abiding are: (1) the three means of making abide on its object the mind that does not abide, (2) the three means of stabilizing the mind’s abidance, and (3) the three means of attaining mastery over the stabilized result. The first three are (1) mental placement, (2) continuous placement, (3) definite placement. Ornament of the Mahāyāna Sūtras explains, respectively: One directs one’s mind to the focal object. And: One is not distracted from continuous engagement. And: One quickly comprehends distraction and resets the mind on its focal object.[1562] These passages teach that first one directs the mind single-pointedly to its focal object, one holds that object without dissipation, and one returns to the focal object if it is lost. The second group of three are (4) close placement, (5) subduing, (6) pacifying. Ornament of the Mahāyāna Sūtras explains, respectively: The intelligent progressively collect the mind within. And: Then, because one sees its qualities, one subdues the mind through concentration. And: Because one sees the faults of distraction, one pacifies them through dislike.[1563] These passages teach that one stabilizes the placement of mind, one strengthens stabilization through seeing the advantages of subduing the mind, and through seeing the faults of distraction one does not lose the object due to distraction. The third group of three are (7) close pacification, (8) single-pointed continuum, and (9) balanced placement. Ornament of the Mahāyāna Sūtras declares, respectively: One pacifies the arising of covetousness, mental dissatisfaction, and so on as soon as they arise. And: Then, through exertion in restraint with application of the mind, one obtains natural abidance. And: Through familiarity one achieves nonapplication.[1564] These passages teach that one pacifies the branch afflictions caused by distraction, one obtains control over one’s mind with exertion, and one obtains control of one’s mind without exertion. Engaging in the Deeds of a Bodhisattva states: Through insight fully based in calm abiding, one comes to know the annihilation of afflictions. First seek calm abiding, and then establish joy free of attachment to the world.[1565]}

de'i phyir zhi gnas grub par gyur pa yis nyon mongs rtsa ba nas spang zhing lhag mthong gi shes rab skyed pa'i phyir dran pa nye bar bzhag pa bzhi bsgom par bya'o/ / de la dran pa nyer gzhag bsgom pas lhag mthong 'grub par yang mdo las/ dge slong dag bgrod pa gcig pa'i lam ni 'di yin no/ / 'di lta ste dran pa nye bar bzhag pa rnams so/ / dge ba'i phung po ma 'dres pa ni 'di yin te/ 'di lta ste dran pa nye bar bzhag pa bzhi'o zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / ji ltar bsgom zhe na/

Therefore, having established calm abiding (śamatha), one should meditate on the four foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna) in order to generate the wisdom of insight and to abandon afflictions from the root. With respect to insight being established by meditating on the four foundations of mindfulness, a sūtra states: Monks, the one path that one should develop is just this, the close placement of mindfulness. The unmixed aggregate of virtue is just this, the four foundations of mindfulness.[1566] Question: How should one meditate on them?

lus gzugs kyi phung po dang*/ tshor ba'i phung po dang*/ sems rnam shes tshogs drug dang*/ chos 'du shes dang 'du byed dang 'dus ma byas rnams la rim pa ltar 'byung ba dang 'byung gyur ram gzugs su rung ba dang*/ rang stobs kyis don gyi khyad par myong ba dang*/ rang stobs kyis don gyi ngo bo tsam myong ba dang*/ mtshan mar 'dzin pa la sogs pa rang gi mtshan nyid dang*/ 'dus byas thams cad mi rtag pa dang*/ zag bcas thams cad sdug bsngal ba dang*/ chos thams cad stong pa dang*/ bdag med pa ste spyi'i mtshan nyid gnyis su yongs su rtags pas bsgom par bya'o/ / de la dran pa nyer gzhag ni dbye na

Reply: One should meditate by thoroughly investigating the two characteristics (lakṣaṇa) of (1) the aggregate of form that is the body, (2) the aggregate of feeling, (3) the six consciousnesses that are mind, and (4) phenomena that are discernment, formative factors, and unconditioned states. These [two characteristics] constitute their specific characteristics, such as (1) that which is the primary elements, derivative form, or capable of materiality, (2) that which experiences the attributes of objects by its own power, (3) that which experiences the mere nature of its objects by its own power, and (4) that which apprehends signs and so on; and their generic characteristics, such as: all conditioned states are impermanent, all contaminated states are associated with suffering, and all phenomena are empty and selfless. If the close placement of [511] mindfulness is classified,
rang bzhin dang*/ 'brel ba dang*/ dmigs pa'i dran pa nyer gzhag gsum las
there are three: (1) the essential nature of mindfulness, (2) related mindfulness, and (3) the focal object of mindfulness.
shes rab thos sogs las byung ba'o/ / gzhan ni 'brel dang dmigs pa las/ / rim ni ji ltar skye ba bzhin/ / phyin ci log gi gnyen por bzhi/ / 15
It is wisdom derived from hearing and so on. Others are associated mindfulness and focal objects. Their order accords with how they arise. The four are antidotes to misconception. (6:15)

dang po'i ngo bo ni shes rab yin no/ / de yang thos pa las byung ba la sogs pa sbyor ba las byung ba yin gyi skye bas thob pa tsam ni ma yin no/ / shes rab dran pa nye bar bzhag par ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/ bye brag tu smra ba na re dran pa'i stobs bskyed pas shes rab de dag skyed cing 'jug pa'i phyir dran pa nye bar bzhag pa ste rgyus 'bras bu la btags pa'i phyir ro zhes 'chad do/ / slob dpon ni shes rab 'dis dran pa nye bar 'jog pa'i phyir dran pa nye bar bzhag pa ste 'bras bus rgyu la btags pa'i phyir ro zhes 'chad do/ / de dag kyang dbye na mdo las/ nang gi lus dang phyi'i lus dang phyi nang gi lus la lus kyi rjes su lta zhing gnas so zhes bya ba la sogs pa gsungs pas gsum gsum du 'gyur te/ de la nang gi lus la sogs pa ni rim pa ltar rang dang*/ phyi snod dang*/ gzhan rgyud kyi gzugs so/ / phyi'i tshor ba la sogs pa ni phyi la sogs pa la dmigs pa'i tshor ba la sogs pa'o/ / rjes su lta ba ni lhag mthong dang gnas pa ni zhi gnas yin par shes par bya'o/ / yang na nang gi lus la sogs pa ni rim pa ltar rang gi nang gi skye mched gzugs can dang rang gi phyi'i skye mched gzugs can dang*/ phyi snod dang*/ gzhan rgyud kyi nang gi skye mched gzugs can dang rang gi nang gi skye mched gzugs can gyi tshogs pa na yod pa'i phyi'i skye mched rnams yin la/ tshor ba la sogs pa gsum ni lus gsum po de dag la brten nas 'byung ba rnams so zhes slob dpon thogs med kyis bshad do/ /

(1) The essential nature of mindfulness is wisdom. Further, it is derived from hearing, preparation, and so on, and it is not merely derived from birth. Question: How is wisdom the close placement of mindfulness? Vaibhāṣikas say: The name of the result wisdom is imputed to its cause, the close placement of mindfulness, because these wisdoms are generated and entered due to the strong generation of mindfulness. Vasubandhu explains that the result [wisdom] is imputed to its cause [the close placement of mindfulness] because the close placement of mindfulness arises due to wisdom.[1567] If classified, there are three types. As a sūtra states: One subsequently views and abides in the body as the internal body, as the external body, and as the external and internal body.[1568] The internal body and so on refer, respectively, to (1) one’s body, (2) the external environment, and (3) form conjoined to the mindstreams of others. External feelings and so on are feeling focusing on external objects and so forth. The term “subsequently views” should be understood to mean wisdom and “abides” to mean calm abiding. Again, the internal body and so on are, respectively, (1) one’s internal physical bases and one’s external physical bases, (2) the external environment, and (3) the internal physical bases of others and the external bases that exist as the collection of one’s internal physical bases. Master Asaṅga explains that the three feelings and so on are those derived in dependence on those three bodies.[1569]

rang bzhin dran pa nyer gzhag las gzhan ni shes rab de dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i sems sems byung rnams 'brel ba dran pa nyer gzhag dang*/ snga ma gnyis po de dag gi dmigs pa'i yul du gyur pa las lus la sogs pa bzhi la'ang yul can gyis btags nas dmigs pa'i dran pa nyer gzhag ces bya'o/ / de la shes rab dang dran pa ni dran pa nyer gzhag gi ngo bo nyid dang*/ 'brel pa mtshungs ldan gyi sems sems byung rnams ni grogs dang*/ lus la sogs pa ni dmigs pa yin no zhes kun las btus las bshad do/ /

Others that are distinct from the essential nature of the close placement of mindfulness are minds and mental factors concomitant with that wisdom. They constitute associated (saṃsarga) close placement of mindfulness. The focal objects (ālambana) of those former two mindulnesses are called “close placement of mindfulness of the focal object.” This imputes the name of the subject to the four objects — the body and so on. Wisdom and mindfulness are the very nature of the close placements of mindfulness, minds and mental factors that are concomitantly related are its companions, and the body and so on are its focal objects. This is explained in the Compendium of Abhidharma.[1570]

dran pa nyer gzhag de dag gi rim pa ni ji ltar skye ba'i rim pa bzhin yin te/ rags pa'i rim pas sngar rtogs pa'i phyir ro zhes bye brag tu smra ba rnams 'dod do/ / slob dpon ni 'dod pa'i 'dod chags kyi rten ni lus yin la/ de yang tshor ba bde ba 'dod pa'i phyir dang*/ de yang sems ma zhi ba'i phyir dang*/ de yang nyon mongs pa'i chos ma spangs pa'i phyir ro zhes 'jug pa'i rim pa ltar bstan par bzhed do/ /

Vaibhāṣikas assert: The order (krama) of these close placements of mindfulness accords with the order of how they arise, and their order of coarseness was previously comprehended. Vasubandhu asserts the order of their engagement when he mentions that the basis of desire-realm attachment is the body, then one desires the feeling of pleasure, then the mind is not at peace, and then afflicted phenomena are not abandoned.[1571]

lus la gtsang ba dang*/ tshor ba la bde ba dang*/ sems la rtag pa dang*/ chos la bdag tu 'dzin pa'i phyin ci log gi rtog pa bzhi'i gnyen por lus la sogs pa dran pa nyer gzhag bzhi bstan to/ / dbus mtha' las ni/ gnas ngan len phyir sred rgyu'i phyir/ / gzhi yi phyir dang ma rmongs phyir/ / bden pa bzhi la 'jug bya bas/ / dran pa nye bar bzhag pa bsgom zhes bden bzhi la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir de dag bsgom par gsungs te/ de la lus ni gnas ngan len 'du byed kyi sdug bsngal dang ldan pa yin pas de la brtags pas sdug bsngal gyi bden pa la 'jug la/ tshor ba la sred pa'i rgyur brtags pas kun 'byung gi bden pa la 'jug go /bdag tu zhen pa'i gzhi sems yin pas de la brtags pas 'gog bden la 'jug ste/ bdag chad par dogs pa'i 'jigs pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / 'du shes la sogs pa'i chos rnams la so sor brtags pas lam bden la 'jug ste/ kun nas nyon mongs dang rnam byang gi chos rnams la rmongs pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar na de dag gis ni dgos pa'ang bstan to/ /

The four foundations of mindfulness of the body and so on are taught as antidotes to the four misconceptions that hold the body as clean, feelings as blissful, the mind as permanent, and phenomena as the self. [512] Differentiating the Middle and Extremes states: One should cultivate the four close mindfulnesses since they engage the four truths: because it is dysfunctional, because it is the cause of craving, because it is the basis, because it is not confused.[1572] This passage says that since they engage the four noble truths, the four foundations of mindfulness need to be cultivated. As such mindfulness of body engages the truth of suffering since it investigates the body that possesses the dysfunctional nature of the suffering of contaminated formations. Mindfulness of feeling engages the truth of origin since it investigates feelings that are the cause of craving. Mindfulness of mind engages the truth of cessation since it investigates the mind that is the basis for conceiving a self and it has no fear of severing the self. Mindfulness of phenomena engages the truth of path since it investigates phenomena such as discernment and so on and is not confused as to what phenomena are afflicted and what phenomena are pure. Thus these statements also teach their need.

de la dang po gsum ni rang rang gi dmigs pa lus la sogs pa so so la dmigs pas ma 'dres pa la dmigs pa yin la/ bzhi pa ni chos thams cad la dmigs na 'dres pa dang*/ 'du shes dang 'du byed dang 'dus ma byas kho na la dmigs na ma 'dres pa la dmigs pa yin no/ /

The first three [mindfulnesses] focus on unmixed states since they focus separately on their individual focal object such as the body. The fourth focuses on mixed states when it focuses on all phenomena, but it focuses on unmixed states when it focuses solely on discernment, conditioned states, and unconditioned phenomena.
de ni chos dran nyer gzhag pa/ / spyi la dmigs pa la gnas te/ / de dag la ni mi rtag dang / / sdug bsngal stong bdag med par lta/ / 16
Close placement of mindfulness of phenomena places the mind on its focal objects and views them as impermanent, suffering, empty, and selfless. (6:16)

DEFINITION

kha cig thar pa la brtson pa'i dge ba zhes zer ba ni mi slob pa'i lam la ma khyab ste/ sangs rgyas rnams ni thar pa la 'bad pa dang rtsol ba med pa'i phyir te/ dge mthar phyin pa khyod la ni/ / sbyor byung dge ba 'ga' ma mchis/ / khyod ni gang zhig bzhed na yang*/ / bzhed pa tsam la rag las so zhes bshad pa'i phyir dang*/ nyan rang mi slob pa dag kyang thar pa thob zin pas de la brtson pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / kha cig gis thar par phyin byed ces zer ba ni gang zag la khyab ches par 'gyur ro/ / de'i phyir rnam par grol ba'i 'jug ngogs su gyur pa yin te/ mi slob pa'i lam yang lhag med myang 'das kyi 'jug ngogs yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Some say: The definition of the path is “virtue that strives for liberation.” Reply: This is not necessary in relation to the path of no more learning because buddhas have exertion but do not strive for liberation. It is said: You have gone to the limit of virtue, but you have no virtue derived from preparation. No matter what statements you make, one may rely on your statements alone. Even śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas on the path of no more learning who have obtained liberation do not strive for liberation. Some say: It is that which proceeds to liberation. Reply: This definition indicates an overpervasion, for it includes the person. Therefore it is the point of crossing to liberation, because also the path of no more learning is the point of crossing to nirvāṇa without remainder.

kha cig lam dang po gnyis ni lam gyi rgyu la 'bras bu'i ming gi btags pa dang*/ phyi ma ni 'bras bu la rgyu'i ming gis btags pa yin gyi mtshan nyid pa ni mthong sgom gnyis kho na yin no zhes zer ba ni ma yin te/ mi slob pa'i lam mtshan nyid pa ma yin na lam gyi bden par mi 'du bar 'gyur la/ de lta na bden bzhir ma 'dus pa'i 'dus byas yod par thal ba la lan med do/ / lam bden yin yang lam ma yin na 'phags pa rnams 'khrul par 'gyur te/ lam ma yin pa la lam bden du gzigs pa'i phyir ro/ / kha cig gis tshogs sbyor gyi lam yang mtshan nyid par 'dod pa ni rigs pa ma yin te/ de dag lam bden mtshan nyid pa yin na ni zag med du 'gyur na de lta na'ang lam de dag thob pa na 'phags par 'gyur te/ zag med kyi lam rgyud la skyes pa'i phyir ro/ / zag med skad cig ma dang po sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa kho nar yang dang yang du bshad pa dang yang 'gal ba'i phyir ro/ /

Some say: Regarding the first two paths, the name of the result is imputed to the cause of the path in the case of the former, and the name of the cause is imputed to the result in the case of the latter. The actual paths are the paths of seeing and meditation alone. Reply: That is not so, because if the path of no more learning were not an actual path, it would not be subsumed within the truth of path. In that case you would have no rejoinder to the consequence that there would be conditioned states not subsumed in the four truths. If something were the truth of path but not a path, then you could not unmistakenly identify āryas, because nonpaths would be seen to be the truth of path. Some say: It is illogical to assert that the paths of accumulation and preparation are actual paths, because if those are true paths they would be uncontaminated, and in obtaining those one would become an ārya, and the uncontaminated path would arise in their mindstreams. This would contradict the explanation that the first moment of the uncontaminated path is perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering alone.

{kun las btus las bden pa rnams la rnam pa bcu drug ni 'jig rten pa yang yod/ 'jig rten las 'das pa yang yod de/ 'jig rten pa rnams dang*/ 'jig rten las 'das pa dag la bye brag ci yod ce na/ shes bya la legs par ma zhugs pa dang*/ legs par zhugs pa dang*/ sgrib pa dang bcas pa dang*/ sgrib pa med pa dang*/ rnam par rtog pa dang bcas pa dang*/ rnam par rtog pa med pa'i phyir te/ 'di ni bye brag go zhes pa'i 'grel par de la 'jig rten pa rnams ni shes bya la legs par ma zhugs pa dang*/ sgrib pa dang bcas pa dang*/ rnam par rtog pa dang bcas pa ste bden bzhi'i de bzhin nyid ma rtogs pa dang*/ nyon mongs pa'i bag la nyal yod pa dang*/ mngon par brjod pa ming don bsre ba'i ldog pa'i sgo nas spros pa'i phyir te go rim bzhin no/ / bzlog pa ni 'jig rten las 'das pa ste shes bya la legs par zhugs pa dang*/ sgrib pa med pa dang*/ rnam par mi rtog pas 'jig rten pa rnams las khyad par du 'gyur ro/ / gal te de dag rnam par mi rtog pa yin na ji ltar shes bya la legs par zhugs pa yin zhe na/ zhes pa dang*/ 'di ltar 'jig rten las 'das pa'i mi rtag pa la sogs pa'i rnam par 'jug pa na mi rtag pa la sogs pa'i don rang mtshan mngon sum du mthong gi mi rtag pa nyid ces bya bar rtog bcas su mthong ba ni ma yin no/ / zhes pa'i 'grel par 'di ltar de dag ni/ 'di la gnas pa na mi rtag pa'i don mthong zhing mngon du myong gi mi rtag go zhes mngon par brjod pa dang spros pa'i sgo nas mthong ba ni ma yin te/ de bzhin du sdug bsngal la sogs pa'i rnam pa lhag ma rnams la'ang sbyar bar bya'o zhes bshad do }

{The Compendium of Abhidharma states: The sixteen aspects of the four truths are either mundane or transcendent states. What are the subdivisions of these mundane and transcendent states? They either do not properly engage or they properly engage objects of knowledge, they either possess or do not possess obscurations, and they either possess or do not possess discursive investigation. These are their subdivions.[1573] Its commentaries reveal: Mundane states do not properly engage objects of knowledge, they possess obscurations, and they possess discursive investigation because, respectively, they do not comprehend the suchness (tathatā) of the four truths, they possess dormant states of affliction, and they proliferate through conceptual isolates, combining descriptive names and meaning. The opposites of those are the transcendent states that properly engage objects of knowledge, do not possess obscurations, and do not possess discursive investigation. They are distinguished from mundane states. But if they do not possess discursive investigation, how do they properly engage objects of knowledge?[1574] And: When aspects such as impermanence are engaged when abiding in a transcendent state, the reality of the object is directly perceived, but “impermanence” is not seen conceptually.[1575] Thus according to this commentary, when abiding in that [transcendent state], the meaning of impermanence is seen and manifestly experienced, but it is not seen by declaring “it is impermanent” or by means of conceptual elaboration. Similarly, that is also applied to the remaining aspects, such as suffering.}[1576]

de'i phyir kha cig bden pa dang po gnyis kyis bsdus pa'i phyir dang*/ rtog bcas phyin ci log yin pa'i phyir dang*/ zag bcas spang bya yin pa'i phyir dang po gnyis mtshan nyid pa ma yin no zhes zer ba dang*/ kha cig rgyud bla ma las/ dag gsal gnyen po'i phyogs nyid kyis zhes gsungs pa'i lam gyi bden pa'i chos gsum dang*/ lam dang rigs pa dang sgrub pa dang nges par 'byin pa'i chos bzhi med pa'i phyir dang po gnyis lam bden mtshan nyid pa ma yin no zhes zer ba'ang rigs par blta'o/ / des na lam dang po gnyis ni rim pa ltar lam dngos la 'jug pa'i sgo dang dngos su sbyor ba yin pas lam du btags pa yin la/ phyi ma gsum ni rim pa ltar bden pa mngon sum du mthong ba dang*/ de'i rgyun goms par byed pa dang*/ goms pa mthar phyin pa'i phyir lam mtshan nyid pa yin no/ /

Therefore some say: The first two are not actual paths because they are subsumed by the first two truths, mental conception is distorted, and contaminated states are objects to be abandoned. Some say: The first two truths are not the actual truth of path because they do not have the three attributes of the truth of path mentioned in the Sublime Continuum: Purity, clarity, the state of the antidote,[1577] nor the four attributes of the path: path, appropriateness, establishment, definite release. [514] Therefore the first two are not the actual truth of path. Reply: One should investigate whether this assertion is appropriate. Therefore, since the first two paths are, respectively, the door for actually entering the path and the actual preparation for the path, they are designated as the path. The latter three are, respectively, directly seeing the truth, cultivating the continuum of seeing, and the culmination of that seeing. Therefore they are the actual path.

The first is the special path of accumulation that is conducive to liberation, and this will be explained below.
gnyis pa ni

las dang po pas thar par bsngos pa'i sgo gsum gyi las dge ba thams cad yin te/ de yang 'di nyid las/ tshul gnas thos dang bsam ldan pas zhes pa nas zhi gnas kyi lam gnyis kyi bar du bshad pa dang*/ kun las btus las/ tshogs kyi lam gang zhe na/ so so skye bo'i tshul khrims dang*/ dbang po'i sgo bsdams pa dang*/ zas kyi tshod shes pa dang*/ nam gyi cha stod dang nam gyi cha smad la mi nyal ba rnal 'byor la brtson pa dang*/ shes bzhin du mngon par dga' ba'o/ / yang gang rgyur gyur pa'i dge ba gzhan dang*/ thos pa las byung ba dang*/ bsams pa las byung ba dang*/ bsgoms pa las byung ba'i shes rab kyang rung ste zhes pa dang*/ nyan thos kyi sa las/ bdag dang gzhan gyi 'byor pa dang*/ / 'dun dang tshul khrims dbang po dang*/ de bzhin zas dang mi nyal dang*/ / shes bzhin du ni spyod pa dang*/ / de bzhin dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang*/ / dam chos nyan cing sems pa dang*/ / bar chad med dang gtong ba dang*/ / dge sbyong rgyan ni tha ma yin zhes 'jig rten dang 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam gnyis kyi 'dod chags dang bral bar 'gyur ba'i rgyu tshogs bcu gsum bshad pa la sogs pa rnams so/ /

The second is all the virtue accumulated through the three doors and dedicated to liberation by a beginner, for this is explained in the Abhidharmakośa from “They maintain ethics, strive to hear, and having contemplated its meaning . . .” (6:5ab)[1578] up to the two paths [for attaining] calm abiding.[1579] The Compendium of Abhidharma states: What is the path of accumulation? It is the ethics of an ordinary being, restraining the doors of the sense faculties, knowing the [proper] measure of food, making exertion in yoga without sleeping in the first or last part of the night, and taking joy in introspection. It is also knowing other virtues that act as its cause, and it is wisdom derived from hearing, wisdom derived from contemplation, and wisdom derived from meditation.[1580] Also Śrāvaka Levels says: The wealth of self and others, aspiration, ethics, the faculties. So too, restraint with food, not sleeping, practicing with introspection. So too, hearing and contemplating [the words of] one’s virtuous spiritual friend and the holy Dharma. Free from and relinquishing obstacles. The last is the ornament of the śramaṇa.[1581] These explain the thirteen causes for separating from attachment by both the mundane and transcendent paths and so on.
khyad par gyi chos
SPECIFIC ATTRIBUTES
['di] la lnga las
This has five headings.

rtogs pa'i khyad par ni thos bsam gyi shes rab kyis chos thams cad bdag med par spyi'i tshul du rtogs pa'o/ / kha cig na re sgom byung gis rtogs pa'ang yod de/ kun las btus las/ bsgoms pa las byung ba'i shes rab kyang rung ste zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro zhes 'chad do/ / spangs pa'i khyad par ni nyon mongs pa la dgrar lta ba'i sgo nas sun 'byin par byed do/ / yon tan ni spangs rtogs kyi chos de dag dang*/ gzhan yang zag bcas kyi mngon par shes pa dag kyang ci rigs par yod do/ / sgra don ni thar par 'jug pa'i tshogs sgrub pa'i phyir tshogs kyi lam mo/{ sam+b+ha ra mArga zhes pa la san tan rgyun du/ b+ha wa sgom pa/ ra ti ni yang nas yang du/ mArga lam ste rgyun mi chad par yang nas yang du sgom pa dang*/ bgrod bya'i 'jug ngogs yin pas tshogs lam mo/ / yang na tshogs gnyis goms pas thar pa cha mthun gyi lam la 'jug pas tshogs lam mo/ /}

(1) Special realization is the wisdom of hearing and contemplation realizing all phenomena are selfless through the general method. Some say: Realization derived from meditation also exists because it says in the Compendium of Abhidharma: Also wisdom derived from meditation is suitable.[1582] (2) Special abandonment is counteracting afflictions through viewing them as enemies. (3) Qualities are the attributes of realization and abandonment, and it is appropriate to include all types of contaminated higher perception. (4) Etymology. It is the “path of accumulation” because it establishes the collection of merit and wisdom for entering liberation. {The term in Sanskrit is sambhāramārga. Santana refers to the mindstream, bhava refers to meditation, rati refers to “frequent,” [515] and mārga refers to the path. Thus it is the path of accumulation since it meditates continuously without break, and it is the entry point of the journey. Again, it is the “path of accumulation” since it enters the path conducive to liberation through cultivating the two collections.}

lus kyi rten ni kha cig gling gsum gyi skyes pa dang bud med kyi rten la skye'o zhes zer ro/ / 'on kyang klu la sogs pa la'ang skyabs su 'gro ba yod par bshad la/ 'dod gzugs na spyod pa'i lha'i bu rnams la'ang tshogs lam skye ba la 'gal ba med pa'i phyir de dag kyang rten du rung ngo*/ / gzugs med pa dang byang gi sgra mi snyan pa la ni ma yin te/ skyes bu dam pa la yang dag par gdams pa nod pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / dmyal ba ni sdug bsngal gyis rnam par g.yengs pas skabs mi rnyed pa'i phyir thar pa'i lam mi skye ba kho na yin no/ /

(5) Physical basis. Some say: It is generated on the basis of males and females of the three continents. Reply: But it is explained that nāgas and so on have refuge, and it is not incorrect to say that the children of gods active in the desire realm and form realm are suitable bases for generating the path of accumulation. But that is not so for beings of the formless realm and the northern continent of Kuru; they are not vessels for the perfect instruction of holy beings. Hell beings never generate the path of liberation because they are distracted by suffering and lack the opportunity [for practice].
gnyis pa sbyor ba'i lam ni
The path of preparation
{ pra yo ga mAr+tha zhes pa sbyor lam ste/ pra ni pa ra ma an+pa ni don dam pa yo ga sbyor ba ste/ mthong lam don dam mngon sum du mthong ba la sbyor bar byed pas sbyor lam mo/ /}

{Prayogamārga means path of preparation, since pra refers to paramārtha, meaning “ultimate,” and yoga is “union.” It is the path of preparation since it is the preparation for directly perceiving ultimate truth on the path of seeing.}
de las dro bar gyur pa 'byung/ / de ni bden bzhi'i spyod yul can/ / rnam pa bcu drug dro ba las/ / rtse mo de yang de dang 'dra/ / 17
From that arises heat. It possesses the four truths as its object fields. The aspects are sixteen. From heat, peak arises. Also peak is similar to heat. (6:17)

chos dran pa nyer gzhag spyi la dmigs pa de las ni dro bar gyur pa'i ye shes 'byung ste/ mthong spang gi nyon mongs pa'i bud shing sreg byed mthong lam gyi me'i snga ltas su gyur pa'i phyir dro ba zhes bya'o/ / ye shes de ni skad cig gcig gis bzhi ga la dmigs par mi nus kyi rgyun chags pa yin pas sdug bsngal la sogs pa 'phags pa'i bden bzhi'i spyod yul can yin no/ / des na tshogs lam ni bden bzhi la mi dmigs la sbyor lam drod nas bden bzhi la dmigs par shes par bya'o/ /

From focusing on the general object of the close placement of mindfulness of phenomena arises the pristine wisdom that is heat (ūṣma). It is called “heat” because it observes the five fires of the path of seeing that incinerate the fuel of the afflicted objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing. Though pristine wisdom at this stage is unable to focus on the four truths in a single moment, still it possesses the four ārya truths (satya), such as suffering and so on, as its object fields (gocara) since they appear serially. Thus it should be understood that the path of accumulation does not focus on the four truths but the path of preparation focuses on the four truths starting at the stage of heat.

gal te tshogs lam na phung po la dmigs pas bden pa la'ang dmigs par 'gyur ro zhes na/ mi 'gyur te/ de ni bden par ma phye ba'i phung po la dmigs la/ sbyor lam nas bden bzhir phye nas dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ / rnam pa ni 'og nas 'chad pa'i mi rtag pa la sogs pa bcu drug tu lta ba ste de yang zag pa dang bcas pa'o/ / dro ba'i ye shes de nyid chung 'bring chen por 'phel ba las ni rtse mo'i ye shes 'byung la/ rtse mo de yang dmigs rnam dro ba de dang 'dra bar bden bzhi dang zag bcas bcu drug dang ldan pa yin no/ / gal te dmigs rnam 'dra na logs shig tu ston par mi rigs so zhe na/ ches mchog tu gyur pas na ming gzhan du btags so/ / 'di ni dro ba'i ye shes mngon par 'phel ba'i rtse mo'am/ de dag las nyams pa'am bzod pa mngon du 'gyur bas dge ba'i rtsa ba g.yo ba'i rtse mo yin pa'i phyir de skad brjod do/ / de la drod rtse gnyis ni nyams pa srid pas g.yo ba yin la/ de la yang g.yo ba chung ngu ni dro ba dang chen po ni rtse mo'o/{ che chung ni drod rtse gnyis rim pa ltar yin la} bzod pa dang chos mchog ni nyams pa mi srid pas mi g.yo ba yin la/ de yang mi g.yo ba chung ngu ni bzod pa dang chen po ni chos mchog go /

Objection: The path of accumulation focuses on the four truths since it focuses on the aggregates. Reply: That is not so. The path of accumulation focuses on the aggregates without differentiating them as truths, but the path of preparation focuses on the aggregates while differentiating them as the four truths. The aspects (ākāra) are viewed as sixteen states — impermanence and so on — that are contaminated, and these are explained below. From the development of the small, medium, and great stages of that pristine wisdom of heat, the pristine wisdom of peak (mūrdhāna) arises. Similar to the focal objects and aspects of the heat stage, the peak stage of the path of preparation also possesses the four truths and sixteen contaminated aspects. Objection: If they have similar focal objects, it makes no sense to teach them separately. Reply: Since [patience] becomes the supreme mundane state, it is designated with another name. Something is called peak because it fully develops the pristine wisdom of the stage of heat. Alternatively, it is the peak stage where one may degenerate from those states, or it is the peak stage where the root of virtue can still become unstable prior to the manifestation of the stage of patience. Both heat and peak can become unstable since both can degenerate. Further, heat is less stable and peak is more stable.[1583] {The measure of instability corresponds to the order of both heat and peak.} Patience and the supreme mundane state are not unstable since they cannot degenerate. Moreover, patience has less stability and the supreme mundane state has more [516] stability.
gnyis ka chos kyis rnam pa gtod/ / gzhan dag gis kyang 'phel bar byed/ / de las bzod pa gnyis de bzhin/ / thams cad chos kyis 'phel bar byed/ / 18
Both target those aspects through phenomena. Also the other three enhance. Patience arises from peak. Both in accordance with that. All are enhanced by phenomena. (6:18)

drod rtse gnyis ka'ang chos dran pa nyer gzhag nyid kyis dmigs pa la 'jug cing rnam pa gtod par byed pa yin te/{ lam gyi dmigs rnam thams cad nyer gzhag bzhir 'du bas so/ /} dang por mi rtag pa la sogs pa'i rnam pa 'god cing 'jog ces bya ba'i tha tshig go /{snga ma dman pa ni 'phel nas sngon du mi byed do } phyis 'phel ba ni chos dran pa nyer gzhag tu ma zad lus la sogs pa dran pa nyer gzhag gzhan gsum po dag gis kyang 'phel bar te goms shing byang bar byed do/ /

Also, both heat and peak engage those focal objects and target those aspects through the close placement of mindfulness of phenomena, {since all aspects and focal objects of the path are included as objects of the four foundations of mindfulness}. First the aspect of impermanence is definitively formulated and established. {One only advances after one’s earlier inferior [meditation] has been enhanced and not before.} Later, enhanced [meditation] is achieved not only by the close placement of mindfulness of phenomena but also by the other three close placements of mindfulness — of the body and so on — which enhance (vardhana) meditation through cultivating and purifying that meditation.

des na rnam pa gtod pa ni thog mar sgom pa yin la/ 'phel ba ni bsgom pa de goms shing byang bar byed pa yin te dper na bzod pa 'bring dmigs rnam phri nas yang yang bsgom pa lta bu'o/ / rtse mo de chung 'bring chen por rim gyis 'phel ba las bzod pa'i ye shes skye ste/ drod rtse'i gnas skabs na rim pa ltar bden pa la chung ngu dang 'bring du bzod la/ bzod pa ni mi nyams pa'i sgo nas rtse mo'i mngon par rtogs pa goms pa'i rim gyis bden pa la cher bzod pa'i phyir ro/ / bzod pa la'ang gsum yod pa las chung 'bring rnam pa gnyis ni ji ltar drod rtse thog mar bden pa rnams la rnam pa gtod cing 'god pa chos dran pa nyer gzhag gis rnam pa gtod cing 'god pa bzhin du chos dran pa nyer gzhag kho nas bden pa rnams la thog mar rnam pa gtod cing 'god par byed {pas chos dran pa nyer gzhag gi ngo bor skye bar byed } de/ /

'phel ba la ni drod rtse las khyad par yod de/ bzod pa ni chung 'bring chen po thams cad chos dran pa nyer gzhag nyid kyis 'phel bar byed kyi lus dran pa nyer gzhag la sogs pa gzhan gyis ma yin te/ de ni chos mchog dang nye zhing chos mchog mthong lam dang nye la mthong lam chos dran pa nyer gzhag gi ngo bo yin pas 'dra bar bstan pa'i phyir ro/ / de la bzod pa chung ngu ni 'dod pa'i bden pa bzhi la rnam pa bcu drug dang khams gong ma gnyis dril ba'i bden bzhi la rnam pa bcu drug ste rnam pa'i skad cig ma sum cu rtsa gnyis tshang bar sgom pa yin la/ bzod pa 'bring ni 'grel pa las/ gang gi tshe gzugs dang gzugs med pa'i gnyen po la sogs pa'i bden pa'i rnam pa dmigs pa re re nas phri nas 'dod pa na spyod pa'i sdug bsngal kho na la skad cig ma gnyis su yid la byed pa'i bar de thams cad ni bzod pa 'bring yin la/ gang gi tshe skad cig ma gcig kho na yin pa de'i tshe ni chen po yin no zhes 'byung ba'i TI kar thog mar rnam pa re re nas phri nas mthar dmigs pa'ang dor nas sgom pa dang*/ dmigs yul bden pa dang rnam pa dus mnyam du phri nas lhag ma sgom pa'i lugs gnyis bshad pa'i

How patience is enhanced and how heat and peak are enhanced is different. All small, medium, and great stages of patience are enhanced by the close placement of mindfulness of phenomena but not by the close placement of mindfulness of the body and the rest. [Patience, the supreme mundane state, and seeing] are similar in this respect, since patience is close to the supreme mundane state, the supreme mundane state is close to the path of seeing, and the path of seeing is in essence the close placement of mindfulness of phenomena. Small patience cultivates all thirty-two moments of the aspects, including the sixteen aspects of the four noble truths of the desire realm and the sixteen aspects of the four noble truths of the two combined higher realms. Regarding medium patience, the Autocommentary states: All [meditation] from the time when there is a reduction — one at a time — in the number of aspects and focal objects of the four noble truths that are antidotes to form- and formless-realm affliction, up until when [the meditator] can pay attention to desire-realm suffering alone for two moments, is medium patience. Great patience arises whenever such attention focuses on one moment alone.[1584] The Subcommentary explains two systems: (1) meditating by first reducing the number of aspects one by one and then later discarding the focal object, and (2) meditating on the remainder by reducing the number of focal objects and aspects of the noble truths simultaneously.

dang po ni kha cig bden pa'i rnam pa re re nas phri ba dang dmigs pa re re nas phri nas zhes bya ba slob dpon gyi dgongs pa yin pas bzod pa chung ngu'i rnam pa sum cu rtsa gnyis tshang bar bsgoms pa'i rjes su thog mar khams gong ma gnyis kyi gnyen po lam bden gyi rnam pa bzhi'i dang po lam bor te lhag ma sum cu rtsa gcig sgom pa dang*/ de bzhin du de nas rigs pa bor te sum cu dang*/ de nas sgrub pa bor te lhag ma nyi shu rtsa dgu dang*/ de nas nges par 'byin pa bor te lhag ma nyi shu rtsa brgyad dang*/ de nas lam bden la dmigs pa bor te khams gong ma'i 'gog pa dang kun 'byung dang sdug bsngal gyi bden pa rnams kyi rnam pa dang dmigs pa rnams snga ma ltar rim gyis re re nas dor nas lhag ma sgom pa dang*/ de nas 'dod pa'i gnyen po lam bden nas sdug bsngal gyi bden pa'i bar gyi rnam pa rnams kyang snga ma ltar re re nas dor nas mthar 'og nas 'byung ba ltar gang zag bzhi'i gnyen po'i dbang gis sdug bsngal gyi bden pa'i rnam pa bzhi las gang rung gcig lan gnyis su bzlas te sgom pa rnams te/ de ltar na khams gong ma'i gnyen po lam bden ma rnam pa gcig phri nas sgom pa nas bzung ste mthar 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal gyi bden pa'i rnam pa gcig lan gnyis su sgom pa'i bar rnams bzod pa 'bring yin pas de ni skad cig ma bzhi brgya dang dgu bcu rtsa bdun yin no zhes 'dod do/ /

One scholar says that (1) the first [method] reduces the number of aspects of the noble truths one by one and then reduces the number of focal objects one by one.[1585] This is the thought of Vasubandhu. Therefore, after meditating on the complete thirty-two aspects of the small stage of patience, a practitioner first relinquishes the aspect of path that is the first [517] of the four aspects of the truth of path that are antidotes to the two higher realms. Next he meditates on the remaining thirty-one aspects. So too, he then meditates on thirty aspects, through relinquishing the aspect of appropriateness. Then he meditates on the remaining twenty-nine, through relinquishing the aspect of establishment. Then he meditates on the remaining twenty-eight, through relinquishing definite release. Then, having relinquished the focal object of the truth of path, he meditates as before on the remainder, through serially discarding each aspect and focal object of the truths of cessation, origin, and suffering of the higher realms. Then, as before, he discards each of those aspects, from the truth of path up to the truth of suffering, that are antidotes to the desire realm, and finally, due to the power of the antidotes to the four persons, he meditates twice on any one aspect of the four aspects of the truth of suffering, as explained below. Therefore meditating in that way — by reducing the aspects of the truth of path as an antidote to the higher realms one by one until, finally, he meditates twice on one aspect of the truth of suffering — is medium patience, and this process is asserted to have 497 moments.[1586]

de'i phyir 'di'i grangs kyi dbang du mdzad nas dang po gsum la dgu bcu ste/ de nas dgu nyid phri ba dgu/ / tha ma'i rnam pa gnyis bsnan pa/ / 'di yis grangs su nges par bzung zhes gsung ngo*/ / gnyis pa ni kha cig na re dmigs yul bden pa yod bzhin du rnam pa 'dor ba mi 'thad cing dmigs yul bden pa dor na dmigs pa med pa'i rnam pa mi 'thad pas thog mar dmigs pa 'dor ba nyid 'thad pas slob dpon gyi dgongs pa'ang bden pa'i rnam pa re re dang dmigs pa re re nas zhes bya ba ni ma yin gyi 'on kyang bden pa re re'i rnam pa gang dag yin pa de dag gi dmigs pa phri nas zhes bya ba yin la/ bstan bcos las kyang bzod pa 'bring skad cig ma brgya rtsa bcu dgu yin no zhes bshad pas na bzod pa 'bring ni skad cig ma brgya dang bcu dgu yin te/ 'di ltar bzod pa chung ngu snga ma ltar rnam pa sum cu rtsa gnyis tshang bar bsgoms pa'i rjes la khams gong ma gnyis bsdoms pa'i gnyen po lam bden rnam pa bzhi dang bcas pa bor te lhag ma nyi shu rtsa brgyad sgom pa dang*/ de nas 'dod pa'i gnyen po lam bden rnam pa bzhi dang bcas pa bor te lhag ma nyi shu rtsa bzhi sgom pa dang*/ de nas khams gong ma gnyis kyi 'gog bden rnam pa bzhi dang bcas pa bor te lhag ma nyi shu sgom pa dang*/ de nas 'dod pa'i 'gog bden rnam pa bzhi dang bcas pa bor nas lhag ma bcu drug sgom pa dang*/ de nas khams gong ma gnyis kyi kun 'byung gi bden pa rnam pa bzhi dang bcas pa bor te lhag ma bcu gnyis sgom pa dang*/ de nas 'dod pa'i kun 'byung gi bden pa rnam pa bzhi dang bcas pa bor nas lhag ma brgyad sgom pa dang*/ de nas khams gong ma gnyis kyi sdug bsngal gyi bden pa rnam pa bzhi dang bcas pa bor te lhag ma 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal gyi bden pa'i rnam pa bzhi sgom pa dang*/

Therefore it is said, “The first three definitely have ninety, then nine are reduced by nine, and two final aspects are added. They are definitely enumerated in this way.” (2) Meditating on the remainder by reducing the number of focal objects and aspects of the noble truths simultaneously. Some say: Since it is unacceptable to discard the aspects while the noble truths exist as focal objects, and it is unacceptable to have aspects without focal objects when the noble truths as focal objects are discarded, it is acceptable to first discard the focal objects. However, it is not the thought of Vasubandhu that “each aspect of the noble truths is discarded by discarding each focal object,” but it is his thought that “each aspect of the noble truths is discarded by reducing the number of focal objects of the noble truths.” Also, a treatise mentions: Medium patience has 119 moments.[1587] Therefore medium patience has 119 moments. Just like the former small patience, it first meditates on the complete thirty-two aspects, then it meditates on the remaining twenty-eight aspects, having relinquished four aspects of the truth of path that are combined antidotes to the two higher realms. Then it meditates on the twenty-four remaining aspects, having relinquished the four aspects of the truth of path as antidotes to the desire realm. Then it meditates on the twenty remaining aspects, having relinquished the four aspects of the truth of cessation that are antidotes to the two higher realms. Then it meditates on the sixteen remaining aspects, having relinquished the four aspects of the truth of cessation that are antidotes to the desire realm. Then it meditates on the twelve remaining aspects, having relinquished the four aspects of the truth of origin as antidotes to the two higher realms. Then it meditates on the eight remaining aspects, having relinquished the four aspects of the truth of origin as antidotes to the desire realm. [518] Then it meditates on the four remaining aspects of the truth of suffering of the desire realm, having relinquished the four aspects of the truth of suffering of the two higher realms.

de nas sgom pa po de yang dbang po rnon po lta ba spyad pa dang rtul po sred pa spyad pa gnyis yod pa las dang po yin na 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal gyi bden pa'i rnam pa dang po gnyis gang rung gcig dor nas lhag ma gsum sgom pa dang*/ de nas rnam pa snga ma gnyis dor nas phyi ma gnyis sgom pa dang*/ de nas lta ba spyad pa de la'ang bdag tu lta ba spyad pa dang bdag gir lta ba spyad pa gnyis yod pa las dang po yin na bdag tu lta ba'i gnyen po bdag med pa'i rnam pa lan gnyis su sgom la/ gnyis pa yin na bdag gir lta ba'i gnyen po stong pa'i rnam pa lan gnyis su sgom mo/ / sred pa spyad pa yin na 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal gyi bden pa'i rnam pa bzhi las rnam pa phyi ma gnyis gang rung gcig dor nas lhag ma dang po gsum sgom pa dang*/ de nas rnam pa phyi ma gnyis dor nas dang po gnyis sgom pa dang*/ de nas sred pa spyad pa de la'ang nga'o snyam pa'i nga rgyal shas che ba dang le lo shas che ba gnyis las dang po yin na nga rgyal gyi gnyen po mi rtag pa'i rnam pa lan gnyis su sgom la/ gnyis pa yin na le lo'i gnyen po sdug bsngal gyi rnam pa lan gnyis su sgom pa rnams te/

Then there are two types of meditator: (1) a meditator with sharp intellectual faculty who engages view, and (2) a meditator with dull intellectual faculty who engages craving. (1) The first discards either of the first two aspects of the truth of suffering of the desire realm and meditates on the remaining three aspects. He then meditates on the two latter aspects through discarding the two earlier aspects. Meditators engaging view have two types: those engaging the view of self [or the view of “I”] and those engaging the view of “mine.” The first meditates for two moments on the aspect of selflessness as the antidote to the view of self. The second meditates for two moments on the aspect of being empty as the antidote to the view of “mine.” (2) The second, who engages craving, discards either of the latter two aspects of the four aspects of the truth of suffering of the desire realm and meditates on the remaining three. Then he meditates on the first two aspects, having discarded the latter two aspects. Meditators engaging craving have two types: those in whom pride thinking “I” predominates, and those in whom laziness predominates. The first meditates for two moments on the aspect of impermanence as an antidote to pride. The second meditates for two moments on the aspect of suffering as an antidote to laziness.

de ltar na khams gong ma gnyis kyi gnyen po lam bden rnam pa dang bcas pa bor nas lhag ma nyi shu rtsa brgyad sgom pa nas bzung ste 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal gyi bden pa'i rnam pa bzhi'i gang rung gcig lan gnyis su sgom pa'i bar rnams bzod pa 'bring yin pas skad cig ma brgya dang bcu dgur 'gyur ro zhes zer ro/ / 'dir yang*/ nyer brgyad rtsa bzhi nyi shu dang*/ / bcu drug bcu gnyis brgyad dang bzhi/ / gsum gnyis rnam pa tha ma gcig /lan gnyis bsnan pa 'di yi grangs zhes bya'o/ / de ltar bzod pa 'bring la skad cig gi grangs mang nyung gi lugs gnyis bshad kyang 'grel pa'i dgongs pa ni phyi ma nyid yin par mngon no zhes mkhas pa dag gsung ngo*/ / 'o na bzod pa chung ngu la dmigs rnam tshang bar sgom la 'bring la rim gyis phri nas mthar 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal gyi bden pa kho na la dmigs shing de'i rnam pa kho na sgom pa nyid ji ltar zhe na/ khams gsum sun 'byin par byed pa na des dang por ni gnyen po mtha' dag la dmigs la phyis ni 'dod khams kho na dang por shes shing spang bar bya ba yin pas de kho na la dmigs pa yin no zhes TIka byed dag 'chad do/ /

Thus one meditates on the remaining twenty-eight aspects, having relinquished the aspects of the truth of path as antidotes to the two higher realms, up to meditating on the two moments on any of the four aspects of the truth of suffering of the desire realm. Since it is medium patience, it has 119 moments. In this context it is said: Twenty-eight, twenty-four, twenty, sixteen, twelve, eight, four, three, two, finally one aspect in two moments are enumerated. Scholars say that though the commentary explains two systems that enumerate more or fewer moments of medium patience, the thought of the Autocommentary is that the latter is the actual system. Question: Why do meditators on the small stage of patience meditate on all aspects and focal objects, those [who meditate] on medium patience serially reduce [their number], and in the end those [who meditate] on great patience just meditate on the focal object and aspect of the truth of suffering of the desire realm alone? Reply: The Subcommentary explains: When a meditator counteracts affliction of the three realms, first he focuses on all the antidotes, then later he focuses on the desire realm alone, since he first knows and abandons just desire-realm [affliction].[1588]

chen po 'dod gtogs sdug bsngal yul/ / de ni skad cig gcig de bzhin/ / chos mchog thams cad phung po lnga/ / thob pa ma gtogs de ltar na/ / 19 nges 'byed cha mthun rnam pa bzhi/ / bsgoms byung mi lcogs med pa dang / / khyad par bsam gtan sa pa'o/ / gnyis ni 'og na'ang yod pa'am/ / 20

Great patience takes suffering belonging to desire as its object. It lasts one moment. So too, the supreme mundane state. All four possess five aggregates. Obtainment does not pertain. In accordance with that, (6:19)
the four aspects are conducive to penetrative insight. They are derived from meditation. They belong to the levels of unrestricted access concentration, special absorption, and the four absorptions. Two also exist in the lower desire realm. (6:20)

ji ltar bzod pa 'bring gi mthar snga ma ltar na skad cig ma drug dang phyi ma ltar na skad cig ma bcu gcig 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal gyi bden pa kho na la dmigs pa ltar bzod pa chen po yang 'dod par gtogs pa'i sdug bsngal gyi bden pa kho na dmigs yul du byed pa yin la/ khyad par du bzod pa chen po de ni skad cig ma gcig yin gyi snga ma rnams ltar rgyun chags pa ni ma yin no/ / ji ltar bzod pa chen po 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal gyi bden pa kho na la dmigs pa dang skad cig ma gcig yin pa de bzhin du 'jig rten pa'i chos kyi mchog kyang 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal gyi bden pa kho na la dmigs shing skad cig ma gcig yin no/ / de ni zag bcas yin zhing sngar zag med med pas skal mnyam gyi rgyu med par rang gi rtsal gyis mthong lam dngos su 'dren pas na 'jig rten pa'i chos kyi mchog ces bya'o/ /

Just as the last stage of medium patience focuses on the truth of suffering in the desire realm alone, whether it lasts six moments according to the earlier system, or eleven according to the latter, so too great patience takes as its focal object the truth of suffering belonging to the desire realm alone. Moreover, great patience lasts one moment, and it does not exist as a continuum like the former states. Just as great patience focuses [519] on the truth of suffering of the desire realm and lasts one moment, so too the supreme mundane state focuses on the truth of suffering of the desire realm and lasts one moment. It is contaminated and not a homogeneous cause since uncontaminated states do not exist before it. It is called the supreme mundane state since it directly produces the path of seeing through its own exertion.

Thus, since it is taught here that the three — great patience, the supreme mundane state, {and perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering} — each focus on the truth of suffering of the desire realm alone and each lasts a moment, one should recognize that, from heat probably up to medium patience, one focuses on any of the four noble truths of the three realms and that this is done continuously. {Again, from the stage of heat up to the stage of medium patience, there is a difference in the targeted aspects and enhancement, but in great patience and the supreme mundane state, there is no difference in the targeted aspects and enhancement. The Autocommentary declares: Targeting aspects is first arranging the aspects in terms of the truths.[1589] The Subcommentary notes: Enhancement is purifying through cultivating.[1590] If they are said to be the initial meditation on those aspects and the continued cultivation of those aspects, they would be untenable as momentary states.}

rnam pa ni ji ltar dang por shes shing spang bya yin pas bzod pa 'bring gi skad cig ma tha ma gnyis dang bzod pa chen po dang chos mchog dang sdug bsngal la chos bzod chos shes rnams kyi dmigs pa 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal gyi bden pa kho na yin pa ltar bzod pa 'bring gi skad cig ma tha ma gnyis dang bzod pa chen po dang chos mchog dang sdug bsngal la chos bzod chos shes rnams kyi rnam pa rnams kyang mthun te/ de yang sngar bshad pa ltar gang zag gi bye brag gis bdag tu lta ba dang bdag gir lta ba spyad pa dang nga'o snyam pa'i nga rgyal dang le lo shas che ba yin na rim pa ltar thams cad bdag med pa dang stong pa dang mi rtag pa dang sdug bsngal gyi rnam pa can yin te/ TIka byed dag gis bzod pa chen po ni gang zag gis ji ltar dpyad pa bzhin du mi rtag pa'i rnam pa dang*/ sdug bsngal gyi rnam pa dang*/ stong pa'i rnam pa dang*/ bdag med pa'i rnam pa dang mtshungs par ldan par yin no zhes pa dang*/ de la dmigs pa nyid skad cig ma gsum pa la ni bzod pa chen po yin no/ / de la dmigs pa nyid skad cig ma bzhi pa la ni chos kyi mchog yin no zhes pa dang*/ bdag tu lta ba spyad pa'i rnam pa tha ma gnyis kyi skabs su de'i 'og tu sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa dang sdug bsngal la chos shes pa dang 'dra bas bdag med pa'i rnam pa gcig la lan gnyis su mngon du byed de zhes gang zag gang yang rung bas bzod pa 'bring gi skad cig ma gnyis la rnam pa gang yid la byas pa de nyid bzod pa chen po la'ang yid la byed par bshad cing*/ bzod pa 'bring gi skad cig ma gnyis kyi rjes kyi skad cig ma gsum pa dang bzhi pa nyid bzod pa chen po dang chos mchog tu bshad la/ bzod pa 'bring gi skad cig ma tha ma gnyis dang sdug bsngal la chos bzod chos shes kyang rnam pa 'dra bar bshad pa'i phyir dang*/

The focal object of the last two moments of medium patience, great patience, the supreme mundane state, perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering, and Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering is the truth of suffering in the desire realm alone, since it is the first to be known and abandoned. Therefore the last two moments of medium patience, great patience, the supreme mundane state, persevering for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering, and Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering are similar. Furthermore, as stated before, specific beings with strong view of the self, view of “mine,” pride thinking “I,” or laziness should take everything as possessing the aspect of being, respectively, selfless, empty, impermanent, and suffering. The Subcommentary states: Great patience possesses the aspect of impermanence, the aspect of suffering, the aspect of being empty, and the aspect of selflessness, in just the way a person engages in analysis.[1591] And: That which focuses on that in the third moment is great patience. That which focuses on that in the fourth moment is the supreme mundane state. And: After the final two aspects that engage the view of self, the single aspect of selflessness manifests twice, since perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering and Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering are similar. Whatever aspect a person pays attention to in the final two moments of medium patience, the person [who meditates] on great patience also pays attention to just that aspect. The third moment and fourth moments [520] after the two moments of medium patience are explained as great patience and the supreme mundane state. Also the two final moments of medium patience, perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering, and Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering have similar aspects.

'grel pa las kyang*/ bzod pa chen po 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal la dmigs pa'i rgyu mtshan du de ni chos kyi mchog dang nye ba'i phyir 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal la dmigs pa kho na'o zhes pa dang*/ TIka byed dag gis kyang bzod pa chen po chos mchog dang nye la chos mchog mthong lam dang nye ba'i phyir de dag dran pa nyer gzhag dang dmigs rnam mthun par bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang bzod pa chung 'bring gnyis dang yang dmigs rnam la sogs pa 'dra bar thal bar 'gyur bas chos mchog dang nye ba tsam gyis ni der mi 'grub kyi 'on kyang chos mchog mthong lam dang nye la mthong lam gyi shes bzod dang po gnyis kyi dmigs rnam de dag yin pa nyid rgyu mtshan du 'gyur ro/ /

The Autocommentary notes: It stands to reason that great patience focuses on the truth of suffering of the desire [realm], and because it is close to the supreme mundane state, it focuses solely on the truth of suffering of the desire [realm].[1592] Also the Subcommenary explains: Because great patience is close to the supreme mundane state and the supreme mundane state is close to the path of seeing, they have the same focal object and aspect as the close placement of mindfulness.[1593] Further, these states are not established as possessing the same focal object and aspect merely because they are close to the supreme mundane state; otherwise it would follow that both small and medium patience would have similar focal objects and aspects and so on. However, the reason here is that the supreme mundane state is close to the path of seeing, and these are the focal objects and aspects of the first two states of perseverance and knowledge of the path of seeing.

de ltar bye brag tu smra bas drod rtse mo bzod pa rnams la chung 'bring chen po gsum gsum yod kyi chos mchog ni skad cig ma gcig kho na yin no zhes 'dod pa ni mi rigs te/ de la'ang chung 'bring chen po'i dbye ba yod pa la gnod pa med pa'i phyir dang*/ thams cad kyang bden pa bzhi char la dmigs pa dang de dag gi rnam pa'ang yid la byed pa 'gal ba med pa'i phyir ro/ /
des na 'di ni bye brag tu smra bas kun brtags pa'o zhes theg pa gong ma pa dag 'chad do/ / slob dpon seng ge bzang pos ni brgyad stong 'grel pa las/ ji ltar bzod chen skad cig ma/ / gcig yin de bzhin chos kyi mchog /ces gang bshad pa de ni rang don gyi dbang du byas pa yin la 'dir bzod pa chen po skad cig ma du ma yin par bstan pa dang*/ chos kyi mchog la chung 'bring chen po'i dbye ba bshad pa ni gzhan gyi don la brten pa'i chung 'bring chen po'i dbye ba bshad pa yin te/ gzhan gyi don la brtson pa la ni rab dang mchog rab la sogs pa'i gnas skabs srid pa'i phyir ro zhes pa la sogs pa pa ni nyan thos rang don byed pa dang byang chub sems dpa' gzhan don byed pa'i dbang du byas nas 'dir bzod pa chen po dang chos mchog skad cig ma re re dang*/ gzhung gzhan du bzod pa chen po la skad cig mang po dang chos mchog la'ang chung 'bring chen po'i dbye ba byas par bshad do/ / dro ba la sogs pa'i ye shes bzhi po thams cad kyang dran pa nyer gzhag gi ngo bo nyid yin pa'i phyir gtso bo shes rab yin la grogs ni dad pa la sogs pa dang mtshungs par ldan no/ /

Vaibhāṣikas assert that heat, peak, and patience have small, medium, and great stages, but the supreme mundane state has just one moment. Reply: This is illogical, because logic cannot harm the assertion that the supreme mundane state has small, medium, and great stages, and there is no contradiction that all focus on the four truths and pay attention to their aspects.
Therefore the higher vehicle explains that this assertion is fabricated by the Vaibhāṣikas. Master Haribhadra observes in his commentary on the Eight-Thousand-Verse Perfection of Wisdom: Just as great patience is one moment, so too is the supreme mundane state.[1594] This explanation is for achieving one’s own purpose. But here also, teaching that great patience has many moments and explaining that the supreme mundane state has small, medium, and great stages is an explanation of the classification of small, medium, and great stages that achieves the purpose of others, because those striving for the purpose of others may on occasion be classified as supreme, and greatly supreme, and so on. From the perspective of śrāvakas who act for their own purpose and bodhisattvas who secure the purpose of others, in this text great patience and the supreme mundane state are each classified as one moment. But in other texts great patience is explained to have many moments, and the supreme mundane state also has the classification of small, medium, and great stages. All four pristine wisdoms, those of heat and so on, are predominantly wisdom because they are by nature the close placement of mindfulness, while their companions are the concomitant states of faith and so on.

'khor dang bcas na ni bzhi po thams cad kyang phung po lnga pa yin te/ 'di dag mnyam gzhag gi sa pa yin pas 'di dag la gzugs ni bsam gtan gyi sdom pa yin la gzhan dag ni shes par sla'o/ / dro ba la sogs pa'i thob pa ni dro ba la sogs par ma gtogs te gtogs na 'phags pa mthong lam pas dro ba la sogs pa mngon du byas par 'gyur ro/ / {de la yang } de dag gi thob pa{ ra sam bor gyi bar du} mngon du gyur pa'i phyir ro zhes bye brag tu smra ba 'dod mod kyi 'di la thob pa rdzas su med pa'i phyir dpyad pa ni don med pa kho na yin no/ / sngar bshad pa de ltar na nges par 'byed pa'i cha dang mthun pa ni dro ba la sogs pa rnam pa bzhi yin no/ / ci'i phyir de dag la nges par 'byed pa'i cha dang mthun pa zhes bya zhe na/ mthong spang thams cad spong yang spang bya'i gtso bos mtshon nas the tshom spong ba'i phyir bden pa nges pa dang*/ bden pa rnams la 'di ni sdug bsngal lo zhes bya ba nas 'di ni lam mo zhes bya ba'i bar du rnam par 'byed pa'i phyir nges par 'byed pa ni mthong lam yin la/ de'i cha ni mthong lam gyi phyogs gcig sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa ste/ de nyid dro ba la sogs pas dngos dang brgyud nas 'dren par byed pa nyid kyis de la phan 'dogs pa'i phyir cha dang mthun pa zhes bya'o/ /

If they possess a retinue, all four [pristine wisdoms] possess five aggregates. For them the aggregate of form is the absorption vows since these exist on the level of equipoise, while the other aggregates are easy to understand. The obtainment of heat and so on [521] does not pertain to the stage of heat and so forth, because if [the obtainment of] heat belonged to [the stage of] heat, then [the stage of] heat and so forth would be manifested by a being on the path of seeing. {Further} the Vaibhāṣikas indeed say: They manifest their obtainment {until they relinquish that level}. Reply: Such analysis is meaningless because after their obtainment, they don’t exist. In accordance with that previously explained, the four aspects of heat and so on are factors conducive to (sabhāga) penetrative insight (nirvedhabhāgīya). Question: Why are they called “factors conducive to penetrative insight”? Reply: The path of seeing is penetrative insight because it penetrates (nirvedha) the four truths — that is, it abandons all objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing as well as doubt, which represent the main objects to be abandoned. It differentiates (bhāgīkṛ) because it differentiates “this is the truth of suffering” up to “this is the truth of path.” Its factors (Tib. cha) are heat and so on, which directly or indirectly produce the path of seeing that perseveres for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering. They are factors conducive to (Tib. cha mthun) the path of seeing because they benefit that state.
nges 'byed cha mthun bzhi char yang{ mnyam gzhag yin pas} bsgoms pa las byung ba yin gyi thos bsam las byung ba ni ma yin no/ /
Moreover, the factors conducive to penetrative insight are derived from meditation {since they are equipoise}, but they are not derived from hearing and contemplation.

sa ni bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs mi lcogs pa med pa dang bsam gtan khyad par can dang bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi bzhi ste drug gi sa pa ste/ mthong lam gyi 'khor yin pa'i phyir dang*/ mthong lam gzugs med la mi rten{ 'dod pa ni thos bsam gyi sa pa yin pas de ni nges 'byed du mi rung ngo zhes kha cig ste 'dod pa la mi dmigs} pa'i phyir ro/ / ci'i phyir gzugs med la mi rten zhe na/ dang por shes shing spang bya yin pas mthong lam 'dod pa la dmigs pa la gzugs med pas 'dod pa la mi dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ / drod rtse gnyis ni 'og ma 'dod pa'i khams na'ang yod pa'am zhes bya ba ni btsun pa dbyangs sgrogs kyi lugs te sa bdun pa yin no/ / de dag lus gang la brten zhe na/

They belong to six levels: the level of (1) unrestricted access concentration of the first absorption and (2) special absorption, and (3–6) the four actual bases of absorption, because they are the retinue of the path of seeing, and the path of seeing does not depend on the formless realm. {Some say: Since the desire realm is the level of hearing and contemplation, it is not compatible with penetrative insight, and as such it is not observed there.} Question: Why does it not depend on the formless realm? Reply: Since the path of seeing first knows and abandons desire-realm afflictions, it focuses on the desire realm, but formless states do not focus on the desire realm. In the system of Bhadanta Ghoṣaka, it is said that two — heat and peak — also exist in the lower realm of desire. Question: On what body do they depend?
'dod rten chos mchog bud med kyis/ / gnyis ka'i rten can 'thob par 'gyur/ / 'phags pas de dag sa bor nas/ / gtong ngo 'phags min 'chi bas so/ / 21

They depend on a desire-realm body, the supreme mundane state [among gods]. They are obtained by the basis of both, since females obtain a male basis. Āryas relinquish them by discarding those levels. Non-āryas relinquish them through death. (6:21)

nges 'byed cha mthun bzhi po thams cad kyang 'dod khams pa'i lus la brten pa yin gyi khams gong ma la rten pa ni med do zhes bye brag tu smra ba rnams 'dod do/ / de yang dang po gsum ni thog mar gling gsum gyi mi'i nang du bskyed cing sngon bskyed zin pa rnams ni lha'i nang du yang mngon du byed do/ {/bzod chen dang*/}chos mchog ni lha dag gi nang du yang dang po skyed par byed do/ / dang po gsum ni skyes pas kyang bud med kyi rten can dang bud med kyis kyang skyes pa'i rten can yang thob pas gnyis ka'i rten can thob par 'gyur{ 'di dag gi dus su phan tshun mtshan gyur pa dang 'chol bar skye ba la dgongs la/} chos mchog ni bud med kyis skyes pa dang bud med gnyis ka'i rten can thob par 'gyur gyi skyes pas ni gnyis ka'i rten can thob pa ma yin te/ chos mchog thob pa'i skyes pa ni bud med so sor brtags min gyi 'gog pa thob pas bud med du mi skye ba'i phyir ro/ / {chos mchog gi de ma thag mthong lam skye la de skyes pa dang bud med du skye ba med do zhes pa grub pa'i mtha' } nges 'byed cha mthun rnams na gzugs na spyod pa'i dge ba zag bcas yin pa la de dag gi rnam smin ni gzugs khams kyi phung po lnga yin no/ / de dag gis mi rtag pa la sogs pa'i rnam pas sun 'byin pas srid pa'i gnyen po yin pas rdzogs byed yin gyi ris mthun 'phen byed ni ma yin no/ / nyams pa cha mthun gyi bsam gtan ni 'phen byed yin no zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/ / nges par 'byed pa rnams ji ltar gtong zhe na/

'phags pa rnams kyis ni nges 'byed cha mthun de dag sa gang la brten nas thob pa'i sa de bor nas{ gong du skyes pa'i sa 'phos pas sa de'i thob pa} gtong ste/ bsam gtan dang po'i sa pas bsdus pa ni bsam gtan gnyis par 'phos pas{ te skyes pas de'i thob pa} gtong ba lta bu'o/ / de yang shi ste gong du 'phos pas gtong gi 'dod chags dang bral{ ba'i sa 'phos} bas ni ma yin no/{ gzhan yang skye bo ltar 'chi ba'am/ yongs su nyams pas kyang ma yin te/ de'i dge ba'i rtsa ba'i rgyud ni mthong lam gyis nye bar brtan par byas pas so/ / 'di 'og tu sa 'phos pas gtong ba ni med de/ gong ma'i rten la sbyor lam med pas so zhes gsung ngo*/ /} 'phags min so so'i skye bo ni sa bor ram ma bor yang rung ste 'chi ba{ ste ris mthun 'dor ba} kho nas gtong bar 'gyur gyis 'phos pas ni ma yin/{/ma 'dris pas ma brtan pa'i phyir ro/ / slob dpon 'dun bzang gis kyang*/ so so'i skye bo ni gong du 'phos pa'i tshe nges 'byed cha mthun dag 'dor ba ma yin nam zhe na de ni med de ris mthun gtong ba kho nas bor ba'i phyir ro/ / 'chi ba'i srid pa la gnas pas de dag 'dor bar srid pa bar ma la gnas pas dor zin te/ de'i gang du skye ba na 'dor bar 'gyur ba gang yin pa de ni med pas 'chi ba kho nas bshad do zhes gsung ngo*/ / gal te de lta ma yin na 'di la thob pa dang mngon gyur lhan cig tu yod pas khams gong na sbyor lam yod par thal bar ma spangs so/ / 'phags pa la mi mtshungs te/ thob pa ni sbyor lam ma yin par bshad zin pas so/}/

Reply: Āryas relinquish (tyajati) {the obtainment of those levels by relocating to levels of higher birth} by discarding (tyāga) those levels in dependence on which the factors conducive to penetrative insight were obtained. For example, states subsumed by the level of the first absorption are relinquished through transferring to the second absorption {and obtaining that state through birth}. Further, they are relinquished at death by relocating to higher levels, but that is not {changing level} due to attaining freedom from attachment. Non-ārya ordinary beings relinquish them through death (mṛtyu) alone {by discarding states of the same type}, whether or not they discard their level. They do not relinquish them through relocation {because they do not rely on other levels, since they are not familiar with them. Master Saṅghabhadra explains: When ordinary beings relocate to higher levels, do they discard the factors conducive to penetrative insight or not? They do not, because they discard states of the same type alone through relinquishing them. They discard them when abiding in the death state and completely discard them when abiding in the intermediate state. It is said that birth in higher states is due to death alone, since they have nothing to discard.[1596] If that is not so, then one could not refute the fallacy that the path of preparation would exist in higher realms, since obtainment and manifestation would exist simultaneously. Āryas are not similar, because it has already been explained that obtainment is not the path of preparation.}
dang po gnyis yongs nyams pas kyang / dngos gzhis de nyid la bden mthong / / rnam par nyams tshe sngon med 'thob/ / nyams pa gnyis ni mi ldan pa/ / 22

The first two, due to complete degeneration. Those with the actual basis see the truth in that life. If they degenerate, those not previously existent are obtained. Both degenerations do not possess specific phenomena. (6:22)

nges 'byed cha mthun dang po gnyis ni{ bsam gtan gtogs pa'i dge ba ni/ / sa 'phos nyams pa dag gis gtong zhes pas} so so'i skye bo dag yongs su nyams pas kyang gtong gi 'phags pa la ni de dag las {mi mthun phyogs kyis }nyams pa med pa'i phyir dang*/{ 'thob pa nas 'phos pas gtong ba'i phyir ro/} phyi ma gnyis so so'i skye bo la'ang nyams pa med pa'i{ 'phags lam gyi sbyor ba ma bskyed pas} phyir ro/ /
