The first two factors conducive to penetrative insight are also relinquished by ordinary beings due to complete degeneration (parihāṇi) {since the Abhidharmakośa mentions, “Virtue belonging to the absorptions is relinquished by changing level or degeneration” (4:40ab)}. But for āryas they do not degenerate {due to their opposing factors}, {though they relinquish them through changing level, having previously obtained them}. Also the latter two conducive factors do not degenerate for ordinary beings {since the preparation of ārya paths has not been generated.}

gang zhig gis nges 'byed cha mthun de dag bsam gtan dngos gzhi la brten nas skyed pa yin na ni des tshe de nyid la bden pa mthong bar 'gyur te/ yid 'byung ba shas che ba'i phyir ro/ / {mi lcogs med dang bsam gtan khyad par can la rten pa'i sbyor lam gyis ni tshe de nyid la bden pa mthong bar ma nges te nyams pa srid pas so/ / des na dngos gzhi'i sbyor lam thams cad 'phags pas gtong bar nges so gsung ngo } gal te sngar{ bzod 'bring man chad} thob pa{ las} rnam par nyams pa dag gis yang{ phyis} thob pa yin na ni so so thar pa'i sdom pa ltar sngon med pa{ kho na} gsar du thob pa yin gyi 'das pa thob pa ni ma yin te/ sngon{ 'phags lam gyi sbyor ba ma skyed pas} yang nas yang du ma goms pa dang{ 'dod chags dang bral bas mi thob pa'i phyir ro/ /} 'bad pas bsgrub par bya ba yin{ pas sngon rang sa mi 'thob} pa'i phyir ro/{/smon nas shes pa gcig gis sos 'debs mkhan yon na 'phro nas skye la med na gzhi nas skyed do/}/ 'o na rnam par nyams pa dang yongs su nyams pa dag la khyad ci yod ce na/

nyams pa gnyis ni{ chos} mi ldan pa'i rang bzhin yin par ni khyad par ci yang med do/ / 'on kyang yongs su nyams pa ni log lta skyes pa na dge rtsa nyams pa lta bu nyon mongs pa'i nyes pa byas pa kho nas nyams pa yin la rnam par nyams pa ni snga ma{ log lta skyes pa} lta bu nyes pas nyams pa dang*/ mthong lam skyes pa na so so'i skye bo nyams pa lta bu dang lam la rjes shes skyes pa na mthong lam gtong ba lta bu yon tan gyis nyams pa'ang yin pas nyams pa spyir smros pa yin te/ des na yongs nyams la rnam nyams kyis khyab kyang rnam nyams la yongs nyams kyis ma khyab pa{ yod de bcu drug pa thob pa na mthong lam lta bu'o des na} bye brag dang spyi'i khyad par yod do zhes shes par bya'o/ /

Reply: Both degenerations (hānī) have the essential nature of not possessing (asamanvita) {specific phenomena}, and therefore they are not different at all. (1) Complete degeneration is degeneration through negative afflicted actions alone, just as the root of virtue degenerates if wrong view is generated. (2) Broad degeneration is [a] degeneration through negative afflicted actions, such as the prior example {of wrong view arising}, and [b] degeneration through manifesting qualities, such as the degeneration of the state of an ordinary being through [i] the ārya path arising or [ii] relinquishing the path of seeing when the knowledge of the higher-realm path arises. Such degeneration is described as general degeneration. Therefore complete degeneration is necessarily broad degeneration, but broad degeneration is not necessarily complete degeneration, {as when the path of seeing degenerates once the sixteenth moment is obtained}. Therefore they are distinguished as a general set and subset.
rtse mo thob pa rtsa mi 'chad/ / bzod thob ngan song mi 'gro'o/ / gnyis slob rigs las bzlog nas ni/ / sangs rgyas su 'gyur gzhan gsum yang / / 23

Those who obtain peak never sever their root. Those who obtain patience do not proceed to lower rebirths. Those of trainee lineage who obtain both enter the Buddha lineage through rejecting. Others, even after three. (6:23)

de la drod {kyi yon tan }thob pa ni yongs su nyams kyang nges par mya ngan las 'da' ba'i chos can yin la/ thar pa cha mthun dang gnyis kyi khyad par ni bar chad byed pa med na bden pa mthong ba la chos nye ba yin te/{tshe 'di la bden pa mthong ba srid pa'i phyir ro/}/

Though obtainment {of the quality of} of heat may completely degenerate, that being will definitely attain nirvāṇa. This is because the second path is distinguished from the factors conducive to liberation, for it is close to seeing the four truths when obstacles are removed. {In other words, it is possible that he sees the four truths in that life.}

rtse mo thob pa dag ni yongs su nyams kyang dge ba'i rtsa ba kun tu mi chad pa yin/{te dkon mchog la mi phyed pa'i dad pa brtan po thob pas rten lhag pa'i phyir ro/}/de ni ngan song du yang 'gro ba srid la mtshams med pa byed pa dag kyang srid do/ / bzod pa thob pa ni rnam par nyams kyang ngan song gsum du mi 'gro ste/ der 'gro ba'i rgyu las dang nyon mongs pa spangs pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar na 'gro ba gsum dang*/ des mtshon nas sgo nga dang drod gsher las skye ba'i skye gnas gnyis dang*/ 'du shes med pa'i sems can dang byang gi sgra mi snyan dang tshangs pa chen po ste skye ba gsum dang*/ za ma dang ma ning dang mtshan gnyis pa ste lus gsum dang*/ brgyad pa phan chad la sogs pa'i srid pa dang*/ mthong spang gi nyon mongs pa ste/ 'gro ba dang skye gnas dang skye ba dang lus dang srid pa dang nyon mongs pa{ 'di dag la so sor brtags min thob pas de dag} mi skye ba'i chos nyid drug 'thob pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang bzod pa chung ngu dang 'bring pos ni ngan song gi 'gro bar mi skye ba 'thob la/ chen pos ni thams cad mi skye ba'i chos nyid 'thob mod kyi rtsa bar ni ngan song du mi 'gro ba gcig pu smros so/ / de la spyir rigs gsum yod pa las

Though those who obtain the peak (mūrdhalābhi) can degenerate completely, they never sever their root (mūla) of virtue. {They are extremely stable, since they obtain stable faith that is never separated from the Three Jewels}. It is possible, however, that such beings proceed to lower rebirths, and it is possible that they commit heinous actions. Those who obtain patience (kṣānti) can degenerate, but because they have abandoned karma and affliction, they do not proceed to the three lower rebirths (anapāyaga); they no longer have the causes for proceeding there. Thus they obtain the six qualities of not taking birth in rebirth states, birth processes, birth states, bodies, existences, and afflicted states {since they obtain the nonanalytical cessation of those states}. They are also not born in (1) the three evil rebirth states, (2) the two birth processes of birth from egg and birth from heat and moisture that illustrate birth, (3) the three birth states of beings devoid of discernment, in Uttarakuru, and in the heaven of Mahābrahma, (4) the three bodies as eunuchs, neuters, and hermaphrodites, (5) existences beyond the eighth and so on, and (6) afflicted states that are objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing. Further, those of small and medium patience obtain freedom from birth in lower rebirths. Those of the great stage of patience indeed obtain freedom from birth in any of the six states, but just the root quality of not proceeding to lower rebirths is mentioned. In general, three lineages exist.

dang po srid pa tha ma pa'i bar du slob dpon la slob pa la ltos pas slob ma nyan thos kyi rigs ni drod rtse gnyis thob pa dag kyang nyan thos las bzlog nas ni sangs rgyas su 'gyur ba srid kyi bzod pa thob yin ni sangs rgyas kyi rigs su 'gyur ba mi srid de/ bzod pa thob pa nas ngan song du mi 'gro la byang chub sems dpa' ni gzhan don du ngan song du 'gro ba'i phyir ro/ / nyan thos kyi rigs de nyid sangs rgyas las gzhan pa rang sangs rgyas su ni chos mchog ma gtogs pa gsum yang nyan thos kyi rigs las bzlog nas kyang 'gyur te/ de ni{ rang don gtso las} gzhan don du yang ngan song du mi 'gro ba'i phyir ro/ / chos mchog las ni rang sangs rgyas su yang mi 'gyur te/ de ni skad cig ma gcig yin pa'i phyir dang*/ de'i de ma thag par mthong lam skye bas de nas rigs nges pa'i phyir ro/ /

(1) The first is those of the śrāvaka trainee lineage (śiṣyagotra) who train with a master until their final existence. Those who obtain both heat and peak may become buddhas through rejecting the śrāvaka lineage. But it is impossible for them to enter the buddha lineage [524] after obtaining patience because, having obtained patience, they do not proceed to lower rebirths whereas bodhisattvas proceed to lower rebirths for the sake of others. (2) Others of śrāvaka lineage who aspire to the pratyekabuddha lineage but not the buddha lineage can reject the śrāvaka lineage after obtaining even three stages. The supreme mundane state is excepted because they do not proceed to lower rebirths for the sake of others; {for them their own purpose is paramount}. They do not enter the pratyekabuddha lineage even when they attain the supreme mundane state because that lasts one moment, and from that point their lineage is fixed, since the path of seeing arises immediately.
ston dang bse ru byang chub bar/ / bsam gtan mtha' rten gcig la kun/ / de yi sngon du thar cha mthun/ / myur ba srid pa gsum gyis thar/ / 24

Masters and the rhinoceros-like generate all in one session in dependence on the limit of absorption up to enlightenment. Prior to that, factors conducive to liberation arise. The swift attain liberation in three existences. (6:24)

rang rgyal dang sangs rgyas kyi rigs gnyis ni gzhan du bzlog par mi nus te/ ston pa sangs rgyas dang bse ru lta bu'i rang sangs rgyas{ kyi lam} ni skyon brgyad las grol bas ting nge 'dzin mi g.yo ba dang dbang po rno bas gsal zhing sbyangs pas nges 'byed cha mthun nam mi sdug pa nas gzung ste byang chub zad mi skye shes pa'i bar gyi lam kun bsam gtan gyi ya mtha' bzhi pa la brten nas stan gcig kho na la bskyed pa'i phyir te/ de la ni bar skabs {der shes pa mi mthun pa mi 'byung ba dang rang gi 'bras bu de ma thag tu thob pas sgyid lug pa }med pas rigs gzhan du{ theg pa 'og mar} 'gyur ba mi rigs phyir ro zhes bye brag tu smra ba zer ro/ / de'i phyir nyan thos ni chos mchog nas phyir mi ldog pa dang*/ rang sangs rgyas bse ru lta bu dang sangs rgyas ni sbyor lam mam tshogs lam nas phyir mi ldog pa yin la/ chos mngon pa ba gang dag gi ltar na bse ru lta bu las gzhan pa tshogs shing spyod pa'i rang sangs rgyas kyang yod par 'dod pa de dag gi ltar na ni nyan thos ltar drod rtse gnyis thob nas kyang rang sangs rgyas kyi rigs las bzlog nas sangs rgyas su 'gyur ba srid de/ de'i lam bgrod tshul ni nyan thos dang mtshungs pa'i phyir ro/ / bse ru lta bu'i rigs kho na bsgyur bar mi nus par dmigs kyis bkar ba'i phyir ro/ / des na 'di ni nyan thos sngon du 'gro ba'i rang sangs rgyas te sngar nges 'byed cha mthun bskyed pa zhig yin no zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad de de dag gi sde pa dag gi lugs so/ / theg pa gong ma pa dag ni de las gzhan du 'chad de 'dir ni skabs ma yin pas kho bos ma bshad do/ / sbyor ba'i lam de yang rgyu gang las shes na/

Those of both (3) buddha and pratyekabuddha lineage do not reject other lineages because buddha masters (śāstṛ) and rhinoceros-like (khaḍga) pratyekabuddhas generate all paths from the factors conducive to penetrative insight or the meditation on repulsiveness up to the enlightenment (bodhi) of elimination and nonarising of the afflictions in one session in dependence on the limit of the fourth absorption (dhyāne’ntye). Their concentration does not waver since they are liberated from the eight errors, and they are clear and fully trained since their faculties are sharp. It is illogical that they would enter another lineage {of a lower vehicle} since they have no opportunity {to become discouraged with their lineage. At that point contrary thoughts do not arise, and they immediately obtain their result}. This is said by the Vaibhāṣikas. Thus śrāvakas attain irreversibility from the supreme mundane state, and rhinoceros-like pratyekabuddhas and buddhas attain irreversibility from the path of preparation or the path of accumulation. Ābhidharmikas assert that there are communal pratyekabuddhas and active pratyekabuddhas who are different from rhinoceros-like pratyekabuddhas, who, like śrāvakas, obtain both heat and peak and enter the buddha lineage while rejecting the pratyekabuddha lineage; their means of progressing on the path are similar to that of śrāvakas. In particular, only those of the rhinoceros-like lineage cannot transform. Therefore this refers to a pratyekabuddha who was previously a śrāvaka and who previously generated the factors conducive to penetrative insight. This is explained by Master Pūrṇavardhana, and this is their system. Higher vehicles explain these issues differently, but since this is not the context to present them, Vasubandhu did not do so here. Question: Also, from what cause does the path of preparation arise?

sbyor ba'i lam de'i sngon du ni nges par thar pa'i cha dang mthun pa'i dge ba 'gro ba yin no/ / de nas ji srid na thar zhe na/ thams cad pas shin tu myur ba ni srid pa gsum gyis thar te sa bon 'debs pa dang*/ myu gu skye ba dang 'bras bu 'chags pa ltar skye ba dang po la thar pa'i cha mthun dang gnyis pa la nges 'byed cha mthun dang gsum pa la dge sbyong gi tshul gyi 'bras bu rnams skyed par byed de/ 'grel pa las kyang*/ chos nyid 'di la ni rgyud rim gyis 'jug pa dang yongs su smin pa dang rnam par grol bar 'gyur ro zhes 'byung ste/ de la 'jug pa{ dang smon pa dang grol ba} la sogs pa ni rim pa ltar thar pa'i cha mthun dang nges 'byed cha mthun dang 'phags pa'i lam yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang dbang po rnon po brtson pa dang ldan pa rnams kyi dbang du byas kyi gzhan dag gis ni ma nges pa'i phyir ro/ / de bas kyang shin tu myur ba gang zhig gi cha snga ma la thar pa'i cha mthun gyi tshogs bsags pa de ni{ de'i phyi ma la} tshe gcig kho na las nges 'byed cha mthun dang 'phags pa'i lam skyed par byed do zhes bya bar khong du chud par bya'o zhes tshe gnyis la'ang thar par TIka rgyal sras ma las bshad de/ lung las kyang 'di nyid mang du gsungs shing*/ dngos gzhis de nyid la bden mthong zhes pa dang mthun pas de nyid rigs so zhes gsung ngo*/ / nyan thos kyi sa las ni snga ma dang mthun par bshad do/ /

Reply: Prior to that path of preparation, the virtue of the factors conducive to liberation (mokṣabhāgīya) definitely arises. Question: Then how long does it take to attain freedom? Reply: All those who are extremely swift (kṣipra) attain liberation (mokṣa) in three existences (bhava), like (1) planting a seed, (2) the sprout growing, and (3) forming fruit. In the first life the factors conducive to liberation are generated, in the second the factors conducive to penetrative insight, and in the third the results of virtuous practice. Also the Autocommentary declares: In this dispensation beings serially enter a lineage, [525] thoroughly mature it, and are liberated.[1597] Entry, {prayer, liberation,} and so on serially represent the factors conducive to liberation, the factors conducive to penetrative insight, and the ārya path. This presentation is from the perspective of beings of sharp faculty who possess exertion; for others it is uncertain. Also, however swift the extremely swift are, you should understand that they accumulate the collection of merit of the factors conducive to liberation in a prior life, and in one life alone {after that life}, they generate the factors conducive to penetrative insight and the ārya path. Thus the Subcommentary {of Jinaputra} explains that liberation is obtained in two lives.[1598] This explanation is logical since it is stated many times in scripture and conforms with [the Abhidharmakośa, which states], “Those with the actual basis see the truth in that life” (6:22b). The explanation of Śrāvaka Levels is also compatible with this.
thos bsams las byung las gsum mo/ / mi yi nang nas 'phen par byed/ /
They are derived from hearing and contemplation. Three karmas. It is invoked among humans. (6:25ab)

thar pa'i cha mthun de yang thos pa dang bsams pa las byung ba yin gyi bsgoms pa las byung ba ni ma yin te/ de ni rnam g.yeng gi sa pa yin pa'i phyir ram/ yang na phyi rol pa'i sgom byung{ bsod nams kyi cha'i sgom byung ni} thar char mi rung zhing*/ nang pa'i da dung ma skyes pa'i phyir ro/ / dge ba de yang yid gtsor gyur pa'i sgo gsum gyi las gsum yin no/ / de'i tshad ni ma nges te/ / {de yang thar pa thob par bya snyam pa'i dge ba ni yid gtso bas/ des kun nas bslang ba'i lus ngag gis las kyang thar char 'gyur ro } 'grel pa las/ la la zhig gis zas 'ga' tsam byin nas sam bslab pa 'ga' tsam yang mnos nas thar pa 'dod pa'i stobs bskyed pas thar pa'i cha dang mthun pa 'phen par 'gyur ro zhes pa dang*/ slob dpon gang spel gyis kyang gang zhig la bsam pa thag pa nas 'khor ba 'dor ba'i blo dang mya ngan las 'das pa la mos pa 'jug pa yod pa des ni sbyin pa dang tshul khrims dang thos pa dang bsam pa las byung ba nyung zad kyis kyang thar pa'i cha dang mthun pa 'phen gyi de las bzlog pas ni mang pos kyang mi 'phen no zhes pa dang*/ slob dpon rgyal po'i sras kyis kyang 'di ni chung ngu zin kyang thar pa 'dod pa'i stobs bskyed pas thar pa'i cha dang mthun pa 'phen par 'gyur ro zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/ /

The factors conducive to liberation are derived from hearing and contemplation (śruticintāmaya). They are not derived from meditation because they are levels where distraction exists. For non-Buddhists, factors derived from the meditation {that are factors conducive to merit derived from meditation} cannot be conducive to liberation as long as [the factors conducive to liberation] of a Buddhist have not yet been generated. Also, that virtue is the three karmas of the three doors of which the mental faculty is dominant. Their measure is uncertain because, as the Autocommentary states: Some say that merely giving some food or reflecting on some aspects of training produces factors conducive to liberation since it generates strong desire for liberation.[1599] Also, Master Pūrṇavardhana writes: For those who consciously resolve to discard saṃsāra, {the virtuous mind reflecting “I will obtain liberation” is the mental faculty that is dominant, and due to it the physical and verbal karma motivated by it become factors conducive to liberation}. Those who are resolved to enter nirvāṇa invoke the factors conducive to liberation through even the minor practice of generosity and ethics and through that which is derived from hearing and contemplation. Their counter states are many and they do not invoke such factors.[1600] Master Jinaputra also explains: With even minor [effort in] practice, the desire for liberation is strongly generated and the factors conducive to liberation are invoked.[1601]
nges tshig ni
ETYMOLOGY
thar pa mya ngan las 'das pa yin zhing de'i cha ni de 'thob byed kyi rgyu nges 'byed cha mthun yin la de la phan pas na de skad ces bya'o/ /

It is called the “factors conducive to liberation” since liberation is nirvāṇa, the factors (Tib. cha) are the causes producing it, and they are conducive to (Tib. mthun) liberation since they promote [the attainment of nirvāṇa].

dge ba de ni gling gsum gyi mi'i nang kho na nas dang po 'phen par byed kyi lha rnams la shes rab yod kyang skyo ba shas chung zhing ngan song ba la skye ba yod kyang shes rab mi gsal la sgra mi snyan pa la gnyis ka med pa'i phyir mi 'phen no/ / 'o na sbyor lam gyi mnyam gzhag gi blo de chos kyi dbyings la blo'i rigs ci yin zhe na/ kha cig gis rnal 'byor mngon sum dang*/ kha cig gis yid kyi mngon sum du 'dod pa ni mi rigs te/ de dag gi mtshan nyid med pa'i phyir dang*/ bden pa mthong ba dang*/ zag pa med pa'i ye shes su thal ba'i phyir dang*/ rgyud bla ma las/ so so'i skye bo phyin ci log /bden pa mthong pa bzlog pa ste/ / zhes pa dang*/ dbus mtha' las/ rjes su mthun pa phyin ci log ces pa dang*/ mngon par rtogs pa'i rgyan las kyang*/ rnam rtog bzhi po ldan bstan pa zhes gsungs pa dang 'gal ba'i phyir ro/ / gang yang brgyad stong pa'i 'grel pa las gsal snang yod par bshad pa de yang nges par rtog pa'i dbang du byas nas gsungs pa yin no/ / {kha cig shes rab gsum gyis goms dar byas pa'i rang rig mngon sum yin te/ dper na 'dod chags la sogs pa goms pa'i rang rig bzhin no zhes 'dod do } de'i phyir 'di ni chos kyi dbyings la sngar thos bsam las byung ba'i shes rab kyis rtogs pa'i don ji lta bar dran pa nyid yin la/ spyi la phyi rol tu rlom pa'i cha nas ni log shes nyid yin no/ /

That virtue is first invoked among the humans (laukika) of the three continents alone. Such virtue is not invoked in gods, whose disgust with saṃsāra is weak though they have wisdom; nor in beings in lower rebirths, who generate disgust but whose wisdom is not clear; nor in those of Uttarakuru, who have neither. Question: What type of awareness is equipoise on the path of preparation that engages the expanse of reality (dharmadhātu)? Some say: It is yogic perception. Others say: It is mental perception. Reply: Such responses are illogical because [526] this awareness does not have such characteristics. In consequence, as well, it would see the four truths, be uncontaminated transcendent wisdom, and contradict the Sublime Continuum, which declares: The distorted minds of ordinary beings stop them seeing the [four noble] truths.[1602] And Differentiating the Middle and Extremes, which notes: Concordant states are distorted.[1603] Also it is said in the Ornament of Realization: Rely on possessing the four conceptions.[1604] Also, [Haribhadra’s] commentary on the Eight-Thousand-Verse Perfection of Wisdom explains that it has clear appearance, but this is from the perspective of it being decisive conception. {Some say: It is self-perception produced through familiarity with the three wisdoms since it is like self-cognition that is familiar with attachment and so on.} Therefore it is the recollection of the object just as it is, comprehended by wisdom derived from previously studying and contemplating the expanse of reality. But in general, if external objects are presumed to exist, it is distorted consciousness.

kha cig gis bcad shes dang*/ kha cig gis yid dpyod du 'dod pa la'ang 'gal ba med de/ dran pa yang dag bcad shes kyi nang du bsdus pa'i phyir dang*/ dmigs rnam sngar ma gtogs pa la mos pa yid la byed pa'i phyir ro/ / spangs rtogs kyi khyad par la sogs pa na bshad zin la/ theg pa chen po'i rnam bzhag ni 'dir mi 'dod pa nyid do/ /

Some assert: It is subsequent consciousness. Others assert: It is assumption. Reply: There is no contradiction, because right mindfulness is subsumed within subsequent consciousness. It is also resolute attention pertaining to earlier focal objects and aspects. The difference in abandonment and comprehension has already been explained, and the Mahāyāna presentation is not accepted here.
mthong ba'i lam bshad pa ni
The path of seeing
'jig rten pa yi chos mchog las/ / chos kyi bzod pa zag pa med/ / 25
Uncontaminated Dharma perseverance arises from the supreme mundane state. (6:25cd)
'dod sdug bsngal la...

'jig rten pa'i chos kyi mchog gi ye shes las ni chos shes kyi bzod pa zag pa med pa'i ye shes skye'o/ / chos bzod de gang la dmigs she na/ chos mchog dang 'dra bar 'dod pa na spyod pa'i sdug bsngal la dmigs{ nas sred pa spyod pa la sogs pa'i gang zag gi bye brag gis rnam pa bzhi po gang rung} pa yin no/ / de'i phyir sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa zhes bya ste/ sdug bsngal gyi chos nyid shes shing de la mi skrag pa'i phyir ro/ / yang na 'bras bu chos shes pa'i rgyu yin pas na 'bras bus mtshon nas chos shes pa'i bzod pa zhes bya ste me tog dang 'bras bu shing bzhin no/ de skyes na 'phags pa'i gang zag dang*/ yang dag pa myang 'das nyid du nges par 'gro bas na nges par 'jug pa zhes kyang bya'o/ {'di ma 'ongs pa skye bzhin pas ni so skye zlog par byed pa'i phyir/ / de'i phyir de ni so so'i skye bo bzlog par byed pa zhes kyang bya'o/ /} kha cig na re so so'i skye bo ni 'jig rten chos mchog gis bzlog par byed de zhes zer te/ de'i ltar na chos mchog so so'i skye bo ma yin par thal ba'i phyir ro/ / kha cig na re chos mchog dang sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa ni so so'i skye bo zlog pa la bar chad med pa dang rnam grol gyi lam dang rjes su mthun pa yin no zhes zer te/ rnam pa 'gal ba tsam yin pa'i phyir rjes su mthun pa'i sgra sbyar te don du na so so'i skye bo ni sgom spang yin pas mthong lam gyis ni spong ba ma yin no zhes bye brag tu smra ba rnams 'dod do zhes 'chad mod kyi bye brag tu smra ba'i 'dod pa ni chos mchog gis spong yang so so'i skye bo ma yin par thal ba'i nyes pa med de/ 'gag par 'gyur ba'i lam gyis ni/ de yi sgrib pa rab tu spong*/ / zhes 'byung bas chos mchog gis spong bzhin pa yin gyi spangs zin pa ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

The uncontaminated transcendent wisdom of Dharma perseverance (dharmakṣānti) arises from the pristine wisdom of the supreme mundane state (agradharma). Question: What does Dharma perseverance focus on? Reply: It is like the supreme mundane state since it focuses on the truth of suffering extant in the desire realm, {which is any of the four aspects engaged by specific persons who manifest craving and so on}. It is called “perseverance for knowledge of the truth of suffering” because it knows the reality (dharmatā) of suffering and does not fear it. Moreover, it is called “perseverance for Dharma knowledge” since it is the cause of resultant Dharma knowledge and it is represented by that result, like a flower and a fruit tree. When it arises one becomes an ārya being. It is called “definite entry” since through it one definitely proceeds to perfect nirvāṇa. It is also called the “agent opposing the state of an ordinary being” {because it acts to oppose the state of an ordinary being when it arises in the future.} Some say: The state of an ordinary being is stopped by the supreme mundane state. Reply: If that were so, it would follow that one on the stage of the supreme mundane state would not be an ordinary being. Some say: The supreme mundane state and perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering stop the state of an ordinary being, and this accords with the uninterrupted and liberated paths. Reply: The term “accords” is applied, but this is simply contradictory, for the point is that the state of an ordinary being is an object to be abandoned by the path of meditation and not an object to be abandoned by the path of seeing. The above assertion is made by Vaibhāṣikas, and indeed Vaibhāṣikas claim that the supreme mundane state abandons the state of an ordinary being. But it does not follow that they are [527] not ordinary beings, because the Abhidharmakośa mentions, “The path that will cease fully abandons its obscurations” (6:77cd).[1605] Therefore the supreme mundane state initially engages the process of abandonment, but it does not complete the process of abandonment.

gzhan yang de sgom spang yin kyang ngan song skyed byed kyi las rkyen ma tshang bas mthong lam thob pa na 'gag pa ltar chos bzod skye bzhin pa na rkyen ma tshang bas so so'i skye bo'i thob pa chad pas sdong ste/ de lta ma yin na mthong lam pa 'phags pa ma yin par thal ba'i phyir ro/ /

Again, though the state of an ordinary being is an object to be abandoned by the path of meditation, when one obtains the path of seeing, it is as if that state has ceased, since the conditions for karma to generate lower rebirths are incomplete. And when the path of seeing is obtained, and while Dharma perseverance arises as the state of an ordinary being ceases, obtainment of that state is abandoned and ends due to conditions being incomplete. If that were not so, it would follow that one on the path of seeing would not be an ārya.

des na 'di'i don ni 'grel pa las ma 'ongs pas ni so so'i skye bo nyid zlog par byed do/ / ma 'ongs pa de'i bya ba ni de kho na yin par khas len gyi gzhan ni ma yin te/ mar me dang skye ba bzhin no zhes pa dang*/ slob dpon gang spel gyis kyang ma 'ongs pa byed pa dang ldan pa ni gsum ste/ skye ba dang mar me dang sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa'o/ / ji ltar skye bzhin pa'i mar mes mun pa sel zhing 'gag bzhin pas sdong bu dang mer sreg pa bzhin du sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa skye bzhin pas so so'i skye bo nyid spong la 'gag bzhin pas phra rgyas bcu spong ngo zhes pa dang*/ slob dpon rgyal po'i sras kyis kyang 'phags pa'i chos ma thob pa ni so so'i skye bo yin la/ de ni 'phags pa'i chos thob pa na rnam par nyams pa'i sgo nas thob pa chad pas ldog gi /nyon mongs pa can ma yin pas gnyen pos dngos su spangs pa ni ma yin te/ nyon mongs pa can gzugs min ni/ / gnyen po skyes pas rnam nyams 'gyur zhes 'byung bas nyon mongs can gzugs can ma yin na gnyen po skyes pas spang ba yin pa la 'di ni ma bsgribs lung ma bstan yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na rnam par nyams pa dang spangs pa dag la khyad par ci yod ce na/ dang po ni rkyen ma tshang ba tsam gyis thob pa chad pa yin la/ gnyis pa ni gnyen po skyes pas spangs pa yin no/ / des na thob pa chad pa so so'i skye bo dang mi ldan pa'i phyir chos bzod kyi gnas skabs na 'phags pa kho na yin gyi so so'i skye bo ni ma yin no zhes bshad pas sdug bsngal la chos bzod skye bzhin pa na so so'i skye bo'i brtags min thob pas spangs pa yin no zhes bya ba 'di yin no/ /

Therefore, regarding this point, it is stated in the Autocommentary: Future events stop the state of an ordinary being. We accept that future actions do just that but not others, like the flame of a butter lamp and its arising.[1606] Also, Master Pūrṇavardhana writes: Future states that possess functionality constitute three states, for they refer to arising, the flame of a butter lamp, and perseverance for Dharma knowledge of suffering. Just as the flame of a butter lamp that is arising eliminates darkness and that which is ceasing burns the wick, so too the arising of perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering abandons the state of an ordinary being, and that which is ceasing abandons the negative tendencies.[1607] Further, it is said by Master Jinaputra: An ordinary being is one who does not obtain ārya Dharmas. When he obtains ārya Dharmas, he stops the state of an ordinary being; he ends its obtainment through causing its degeneration. Since [the state of an ordinary being] is not [by nature] afflicted, it is not directly abandoned by an antidote. As the Abhidharmakośa states, “Afflicted nonphysical states decline through the generation of antidotes” (4:42cd).[1608] Therefore if something is not afflicted, it may be abandoned by an antidote arising [but not directly] because it is an unobscured-neutral state. Question: What is the difference between broad degeneration and abandonment? Reply: The first ends obtainment due to conditions being incomplete. The second is abandonment due to its antidote arising. Therefore it is said that those manifesting Dharma perseverance are solely āryas and not ordinary beings because ordinary beings do not possess the end of the obtainment [of the state of an ordinary being]. Therefore, when perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering arises, the state of an ordinary being is abandoned through obtaining the nonanalytical cessation of that state.
...de nas ni/ / de nyid la chos shes de bzhin/ / sdug bsngal lhag la rjes bzod shes/ / bden pa gsum la'ang de bzhin no/ / 26

From that arising, knowledge focusing on just that desire-realm suffering arises. So too subsequent perseverance and knowledge focusing on that beyond. So too those focusing on the three truths also. (6:26)

sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa skyes pa de nas ni 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal de nyid la dmigs pa'i chos shes pa'i ye shes skye'o/ / 'di ni dang por 'dod pa'i chos kyi de nyid shes pa na chos shes pa yin gyi bzod pa ni ma yin te/ sngar gyi ye shes kyis skrag pa bcom zin pa'i phyir ro/ / ji ltar 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal la dmigs pa'i bzod shes zag med skye ba de bzhin du sdug bsngal chos shes kyi mjug thogs su 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal gyi lhag ma khams gong ma gnyis kyi sdug bsngal gyi bden pa la dmigs pa'i rjes su shes pa'i bzod pa dang shes pa skye'o/ / ye shes de dag ni chos shes pa'i rjes su skyes pa'i phyir rjes su shes pa dang*/ gong ma'i sdug bsngal gyi chos nyid la mi skrag pa'i phyir bzod pa dang*/ skrag pa bcom zin la 'jug pa'i phyir shes pa yin no/ / sdug bsngal gyi bden pa la dmigs pa'i ye shes bzhi skye ba ji lta ba bzhin du kun 'byung la sogs pa'i bden pa gsum la'ang de bzhin du shes par bya'o/ /

From perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering arising, the transcendent wisdom of Dharma knowledge focusing on just that desire-realm truth of suffering arises. If it is the first knowledge of just that desire-realm Dharma, it is Dharma knowledge but not Dharma perseverance, because the earlier transcendent wisdom [of Dharma perserverance] has already annihilated fear. Just as uncontaminated perseverance and knowledge focusing on the truth of suffering arise with respect to the desire realm, so too subsequent perseverance and knowledge focusing on the truth of suffering in the two higher realms — beyond desire-realm suffering — arise at the conclusion of Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering. These transcendent wisdoms are subsequent knowledge because they arise subsequent to Dharma knowledge, they are perseverance because they do not fear the reality of the truth of suffering of higher realms, and they are knowledge because [528] they have destroyed fear. And just as the four transcendent wisdoms focusing on the truth of suffering arise, so too those focusing on the three truths of origin and so on also arise.
de ltar bden pa mngon rtogs 'di/ / sems bcu drug go rnam gsum ste/ / mthong dmigs bya ba zhes bya'o/ / de ni chos mchog dang sa gcig / 27
Thus realization of the truths is the sixteen minds. It has three types: seeing, focal object, and action. They belong to the same level as the supreme mundane state. (6:27)

de ltar na bden pa mngon par rtogs pa'i lam 'di ni sems kyi skad cig ma{ zag med} bcu drug go /mngon par rtogs pa zhes bya ba ni mngon sum du mthong ba'o/ / 'dir dpyad pa 'di yod de bden pa rnams cig car rtogs sam/ 'on te rim gyis yin/ dang po ltar na bden pa mngon par rtogs pa bcu drug ma yin par 'gyur la/ gnyis pa ltar na spang bya rim gyis spong bar 'gyur na stong chen mo rab tu 'joms pa las/ lta ba 'di la sbyar ma thag tu ni/ / 'jigs tshogs lta dang tshul khrims brtul zhugs dang*/ / the tshom dang ni nyon mongs gsum po dag /cig car spangs te 'phags pa'i bden mthong ba zhes gsungs pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/ 'phags pa gnas brtan pa dang chos srung ba'i sde pa la sogs pa rnams na re bden pa ni cig car mngon par rtogs te/ ye shes kyi rnam pa bcu drug bshad pa ni bden pa bzhi la chos kyi rnam pa bcu drug bshad pa'i dbang du mdzad pa yin te/ gzhan du na sngar smros pa'i mdo dang 'gal ba'i phyir ro zhes 'dod do/ /

Thus the path of realization (abhisamaya) of the four truths (satya) is the sixteen {uncontaminated} moments of mind (ṣoḍaśacitta). “Realization” means directly seeing, and here one should analyze whether the truths are realized simultaneously or in stages. According to the first possibility, the realization of truth would be the sixteen moments. According to the second possibility, objects of abandonment would be serially abandoned. Objection: This contradicts the Great Empty State that Fully Destroys, which states: Immediately this is applied to [afflicted] view, three afflictions are simultaneously abandoned — the afflicted view of the self, the view clinging to rules and ritual as supreme, and doubt — and one sees the ārya truths.[1609] Schools such as the Āryasthavira and the Dharmagupta assert that the four truths are simultaneously realized, since the explanation of sixteen aspects of transcendent wisdom is from the perspective of sixteen attributes pertaining to the four truths. Otherwise it would contradict the previously quoted sūtra.[1610]

'di la thams cad yod par smra ba la sogs pa rnams ni bden pa mngon par rtogs pa ni bcu drug rim gyis rtogs pa yin gyi cig car ni ma yin no/ / gal te bden bzhi cig car mngon par rtogs na zhugs pa dang gnas pa'i rnam bzhag mi rung bar thal ba'i phyir dang*/ bcom ldan 'das kyis dpe dang bcas pa'i mdo gsum gsungs pa dang 'gal ba'i phyir ro/ / de la mdo dang po ni yang dag par ldan pa'i mdo las/ khyim bdag mgon med zas sbyin gyis btsun pa ci lags/ 'phags pa'i bden pa bzhi po mthar gyis mngon par rtogs sam/ 'on te mngon par rtogs pa gcig lags zhes zhus pa dang*/ khyim bdag 'phags pa'i bden pa bzhi ni mthar gyis mngon par rtogs kyi mngon par rtogs pa gcig pa ni med do/ / khyim bdag gang zhig 'di skad du bdag gis sdug bsngal 'phags pa'i bden pa mngon par ma rtogs par kun 'byung ba 'phags pa'i bden pa mngon par rtogs par bya'o zhes bya ba nas rgyas par sdug bsngal 'gog pa 'phags pa'i bden pa mngon par ma rtogs par sdug bsngal 'gog par 'gro ba'i lam 'phags pa'i bden pa mngon par rtogs par bya'o zhes bya ba'i bar du smra na de skad du ni ma smra zhig ces brjod par bya'o/ /

The Sarvāstivādins and so on say: Realization of the four truths comprehends the sixteen aspects serially and not simultaneously. Simultaneous realization of the four truths is unacceptable because the principles of entry and abidance would become untenable and it would contradict three sūtras and their examples laid out by the Bhagavan. The first sūtra is from the Connected Discourses: The housholder Anāthapiṇḍada said to the Venerable One: “What is correct? Are the four ārya truths realized serially or are they realized simultaneously?” The Venerable One replied: “Householder, the four ārya truths are realized serially. They are not comprehended by the same realization. Householder, it is not said that ‘I realize the ārya truth of origin without realizing the ārya truth of suffering’ or ‘I realize the ārya truth of path proceeding to the cessation of suffering without realizing the ārya truth of the cessation of suffering.’[1611]

de ci'i phyir zhe na/ sdug bsngal 'phags pa'i bden pa mngon par ma rtogs par kun 'byung ba 'phags pa'i bden pa mngon par rtogs par 'gyur ba gang yin pa de ni gnas med cing go skabs med do/ / sdug bsngal 'phags pa'i bden pa mngon par rtogs nas kun 'byung ba 'phags pa'i bden pa mngon par rtogs pa 'di ni gnas yod cing go skabs yod do zhes bya ba nas/ de bzhin du bden pa gzhan la'ang sbyar nas dpe ni khang pa brtsegs ma'am khang pa brtsegs pa chen po'i rmang dang rtsig pa dang phyam so dang g.yogs ma rnams snga ma snga ma la rkang pa ma bzhag par phyi ma phyi ma la rkang pa gzhag par bya ba'i gnas med cing go skabs med pa dang*/ snga ma snga ma la bzhag nas phyi ma phyi ma la gzhag pa'i gnas dang go skabs yod pa'i sgo nas gsungs so/ /

Why? There is no place or opportunity to assert ‘I realize the ārya truth of origin without realizing the ārya truth of suffering,’ nor to apply that to the other truths. Take, for example, the earlier stages of erecting or constructing a building. If the broad foundation, the walls, beams, and roof, and so on, do not act as the foundation for the later stages, then there is no place nor possibility for the building to be erected.[1612]

mdo gnyis pa ni dge slong zhig la don snga ma bzhin la dpe ni bang rim bzhi pa'i them skas la 'dzig pa'i sgo nas gsungs so/ / mdo gsum pa ni 'phags pa kun dga' bo la don snga ma bzhin la dpe ni gdang bu bzhi pa'i skas la 'dzegs te khang bzang gi steng du 'dzeg pa'i dpe'i sgo nas gsungs pa yin no/ / bden pa cig car mngon par rtogs par gsungs pa ni bya ba'i mngon par rtogs pa gcig pa'i dbang du mdzad nas gsungs pa yin te/ sdug bsngal mthong ba na de'i kun 'byung spong zhing 'gog pa mngon du byed la de dag kyang lam goms pas yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dir rim gyis mngon par rtogs pa ni mthong ba'i mngon par rtogs pa yin no/ / 'o na mngon par rtogs pa du ma yod dam zhe na/

The second sūtra states an example that conforms with the earlier point — namely, that of a monk climbing steps of four levels.[1613] The third sūtra notes an example that also conforms with the earlier point — namely, of Ārya Ānanda ascending within a mansion by climbing stairs with four steps.[1614] The statement that “one realizes the four truths simultaneously” is stated from the perspective of one single act of realization: if one sees suffering, one abandons its origin and manifests its cessation through cultivating the path. In this context serial realization is the realization of seeing. Question: Are there many realizations?

mngon par rtogs pa de ni rnam pa gsum ste/ mthong ba'i mngon par rtogs pa dang*/ dmigs pa'i mngon par rtogs pa dang*/ bya ba'i mngon par rtogs pa zhes bya ba'o/ / de la dang po ni zag med kyis shes rab kyis bden bzhi'i rnam pa bcu drug mngon sum du mthong ba ste/ mdo las/ dge slong dag zag pa med pa'i shes rab kyis mthong ba gang yin pa de ni mthong ba'o zhes 'byung bas shes rab nyid mthong ba yin no/ / gnyis pa ni shes rab mtshungs ldan{ gyi sems sems byung} dang bcas pa'o/ / gsum pa ni shes rab mtshungs ldan dang bcas pa dang*/ ldan pa ma yin pa tshul khrims dang mtshan nyid dang thob pa la sogs pa dag kyang yin te/ de dag gis sdug bsngal shes par bya ba dang*/ kun 'byung spang bar bya ba dang*/ 'gog pa mngon du bya ba dang*/ lam rgyud la bsten pa'i bya ba bzhi po byed pa'i phyir ro zhes bya bar 'dod do/ / des na shes rab gsum char dang*/ shes rab las gzhan pa'i mtshungs ldan rnams ni phyi ma gnyis dang*/ shes rab dang lhan cig pa'i mtshungs ldan ma yin pa rnams ni tha ma kho na'o/ /

Reply: That realization has three types: the realization of seeing, the realization of the focal object, and the realization of action.[1615] (1) The first is uncontaminated wisdom directly seeing the sixteen aspects of the four truths. A sūtra declares: Monks, whatever is seen by uncontaminated wisdom, that is seen.[1616] Therefore wisdom itself is seeing. (2) The second is {minds and mental factors} concomitant with wisdom. (3) The third is ethics, characteristics, obtainment, and so on that are either concomitant or not concomitant with wisdom because they engage in the four actions: knowing suffering, abandoning origin, manifesting cessation, and relying on the path in their mindstreams. Therefore wisdom is all three, those concomitant with states other than wisdom are the latter two, and those not simultaneously concomitant with wisdom are the third alone.

mngon par rtogs pa bcu drug po de dag ni chos mchog dang sa gcig cing chos mchog ni/ mi lcogs med pa dang*/ khyad par bsam gtan sa pa'o zhes 'byung ba'i phyir 'di dag kyang sa drug la rten pa yin no/ / {bzod 'bring man chad ni bsam gtan la rten yang bye brag gi sa mi mtshungs pa srid do/ /

These sixteen realizations belong to the same level as the supreme mundane state. The supreme mundane state and those sixteen depend on the six levels because the Abhidharmakośa says, “They belong to the levels of unrestricted access concentration, special absorption, and the four absorptions” (6:20bc). [530] {It is possible that states on and below medium patience depend on the absorptions but have different specific levels.}
bzod dang shes pa go rims bzhin/ / bar chad med dang rnam grol lam/ / de la skad cig bco lnga ni/ / ma mthong mthong phyir mthong ba'i lam/ / 28
Perseverance and knowledge are respectively uninterrupted paths and liberated paths. Fifteen moments are the path of seeing because that not previously seen is seen. (6:28)
bcu drug tu grangs nges pa ni }
{THEY ARE FIXED IN NUMBER AS SIXTEEN}

bcu drug po de'i bzod pa brgyad dang shes pa brgyad po de dag gi go rim bzhin du{ nyon mongs kyi thob pa gcod pas} rkun po 'byin pa ltar spang bya la gnod pa byed pa la gzhan gyis bar chad bya bar mi nus pa'i phyir dang*/ sgo 'phar gcod pa ltar spang bya las rgyal ba'i bral thob dang lhan cig skye ba'i phyir bar chad med pa'i lam dang rnam par grol ba'i lam yin no/ / skad cig ma yang shes bya la shes pa skye ba'i bya ba rdzogs pa'i skad cig yin gyi dus mtha'i skad cig ma ni ma yin te/ kun las btus las/ sems kyi skad cig ni shes bya la shes pa 'byung ba yongs su rdzogs par rig par bya'o zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / kha cig chos mchog nyid mthong spang la gnod byed yin par 'dod pa la ni chos mchog bar chad med pa'i lam dang mthong lam rnam grol gyi lam 'ba' zhig par thal ba'i skyon yod do/ / gang dag shes pa thams cad sgom lam du 'dod pa de dag la'ang mthong lam skad cig bco lnga ma yin par 'gyur ro/ {gal te bzod pas nyon mongs spong na bstan bcos las kun sbyor ni dgu ste/ chos shes pas spang bar bya ba bzhi dang*/ rjes su shes pas spang bar bya ba bzhi dang*/ sgom pas spang bar bya ba'o zhes pa dang 'gal zhe na/ bzod pa rnams ni shes pa'i 'khor yin pas bzod pas spang bya la shes pa'i spang byar bshad de 'khor gyis bcom pa la rgyal pos bcom zhes pa bzhin no/ / sgom spang ni shes pa kho nas te/ de la bar chad med lam yang shes pa'i ngo bo yin pa'i phyir ro } gang dag 'dir theg pa gong ma'i mthong lam gyi rnam bzhag du ma 'chad pa de dag ni skabs lam 'das pa yin no/ /

Those eight types of perseverance (kṣānti) and eight types of knowledge (jñāna) of the sixteen aspects are respectively uninterrupted (anantaryamārga) and liberated paths (muktimārga). They are uninterrupted paths {since the [first] eight end the obtainment of affliction}, for they destroy the object to be abandoned like expelling a thief, and other states cannot obstruct them. They are liberated paths because they arise simultaneously with the obtainment of freedom that conquers the object of abandonment, like shutting the door [on that thief]. Also, here a “moment” refers to the moment required to complete the action of generating knowledge of an object of knowledge. It is not the smallest moment, for as the Compendium of Abhidharma explains: A moment of mind should be recognized as the time taken to fully produce knowledge of an object of knowledge.[1617] Some assert: The supreme mundane state harms objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing. Reply: It would then erroneously follow that the supreme mundane state would either be the uninterrupted path or the liberated path of seeing. [Some assert:] All knowledge is the path of meditation. Reply: If so, the path of seeing would lack fifteen moments. {Objection: If affliction is abandoned by perseverance, it would contradict the treatise[1618] that observes: There are nine fetters: the four to be abandoned by Dharma knowledge, the four to be abandoned by subsequent knowledge, and the one to be abandoned by meditation.[1619] Reply: Since the eight types of perseverance are the retinue of knowledge, objects to be abandoned by perseverance are explained as objects to be abandoned by knowledge, just as those oppressed by the king’s retinue are said to be oppressed by the king. Objects to be abandoned by meditation are abandoned by knowledge alone because the uninterrupted path is, by nature, knowledge.} Here the principles of the path of seeing of the higher vehicle are not explained. They surpass this presentation in both context and path.

ye shes skad cig ma bcu drug po de dag las skad cig ma dang po bco lnga ni mthong ba'i lam yin te/ bden pa rnams sngar ma mthong ba mngon sum du mthong ba'i phyir ro/{ zhe na rtags de chos can gyi phyogs gcig la ma grub ste/ shes pa ni bzod pa'i dmigs pa 'dzin pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ de dag kyang mthong lam gyi bar na yod pa'i shes pa yin pa'i phyir rgyud la bsams pa'am/ yang na ma mthong ba'am mthong ba'i phyir te/ gang zag 'di'i ma mthong ba mthong ba 'jug pa ste de srid du mthong ba'i lam mo/ / lam la rjes shes ni sgom lam yin te dge sbyong tshul gyi 'bras bu 'dus byas yin pa'i phyir dang*/ shes pa brgyad dang rnam pa bcu drug thob pa'i phyir dang*/ lam snga ma nyams pa'i phyir dang*/ rgyun chags pa phyin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di sgom lam yin na nyams pa srid par 'gyur ro zhe na/ ma yin te mthong spang gi spangs pa 'dzin pa'i gzhi'i gnyen po yin pas so zhes zer te de lta na sgom lam thams cad kyang mthong lam du ha cang thal bas mi 'thad do/ / ci'i phyir shes pa bdun mthong lam yin zhe na/ bden pa mthong ba thams cad ma rdzogs pas bzod pa gnyis kyi bar mar gyur pa'i phyir ro/ / kha cig mthong lam gyi skal mnyam gyi rgyu yin pa'i phyir zhes zer ro/ /}

The first fifteen moments (kṣaṇa) of the sixteen moments of transcendent wisdom are the path of seeing (dṛṅmārga), because the truths not previously seen (adṛṣṭa) are directly seen (dṛṣṭa). {Objection: If that is said, then the reason would not apply to some aspects of the subject[1620] here, because knowledge apprehends the focal object of perseverance. Reply: They are the path of seeing for as long as that person contemplates them in his mindstream because they are knowledge existing within the path of seeing, or for as long as that person strives to see what is unseen in order to see what is unseen. Subsequent knowledge of the truth of path is the path of meditation because it is the conditioned result of training in virtue, it obtains the eight knowledges and sixteen aspects, the former paths degenerate, and their continuum is severed. Objection: If subsequent knowledge is the path of meditation, then it is possible that it degenerates. [Some say:] That is not so, since it is the basic antidote apprehending that to be abandoned by the path of seeing. Reply: That is unacceptable, because the extreme fallacy would arise that all paths of meditation would be paths of seeing. Question: Why are seven knowledges the path of seeing? Reply: They are the path of seeing because they exist between states of perseverance, and the process of seeing the four truths is not yet complete. Some say: They are homogeneous causes of the path of seeing.}

bcu bzhi pa man chad kyis ni khams gong ma'i lam ma mthong ba'i phyir mthong lam du ma bshad do/ / bcu drug pa ni snga ma rnams kyis mthong zin pa'i bden pa la dmigs nas lam goms par byed pa'i phyir sgom lam yin no/ / shes pa snga ma bdun ni mthong ba'i bya ba ma rdzogs pa'i phyir mthong lam du bshad kyi sgom lam ni ma yin no/ / 'o na bcu drug pa'ang lam la nges par 'byin pa'am/ lam la rjes bzod sngar ma mthong ba mthong ba'i phyir mthong lam du 'gyur ro zhe na/ mthong ma mthong ni bden pa mthong ba dang ma mthong ba'i dbang du byas kyi rnam pa'i dbang du ma byas pas{ shes pa'i} rnam pa gcig ma mthong bas ni ma mthong bar mi 'gyur te nyag ma gcig ma brngas kyang zhing ma brngas par mi 'gyur ba bzhin no/ /

[Some assert:] The moments prior to and including the fourteenth moment are not the path of seeing because they do not see the higher realms. [Some say:] The sixteenth moment is the path of meditation because it cultivates the path through focusing on the truths previously seen by the former moments. [531] [Some say:] The seven former moments of knowledge are explained to be the path of seeing and not the path of meditation because they have not completed the act of seeing. Objection: The sixteenth moment is the path of seeing because it sees definite release as an aspect of the truth of path that was not previously seen, or because perseverance for subsequent knowledge of the truth of path sees that which was not previously seen. Reply: Seeing that which was not previously seen is from the perspective of seeing or not seeing the four truths and not from the perspective of the aspects. Therefore it is not [the case] that the sixteenth moment does not see if it does not see one aspect {of knowledge}, just as one does not say that when a single plant is not harvested, the field is not harvested.
dbang po rno rtul de dag tu/ / dad dang chos kyi rjes 'brang ba/ /
Those of sharp faculty are followers of reality; those of dull faculty are followers of faith. (6:29ab)

mthong lam skad cig ma bco lngar bshad pa gang dag yin pa de dag tu dbang po rnon po ni sngon rang nyid kyi mdo la sogs pa'i chos kyi don gyi rjes su 'brang bas na chos kyi rjes su 'brang ba dang*/ rtul po ni sngon gzhan gyi lung la brten nas dad pas tshig gi rjes sa 'brang bas na dad pas rjes su 'brang ba zhes bya ba'i ming 'thob bo/ / don de ltar gnas pa na spyi'i don ni gsum yin te/ mthong lam gyi rten dang*/ lam dang*/ 'bras bu'o/ /

Among those abiding in any of the fifteen moments of the path of seeing, those of sharp faculty (tīkṣṇendriya) are called followers of reality (dharmānusārin) since they follow the meaning of Dharma in earlier sūtras and so on. Those of dull faculty (mṛdu indriya) obtain the name of followers of faith (śraddhānusārin) since they follow words through faith dependent on other earlier scriptures. Given that this is so, the general meaning of the path of seeing has three types: basis, path, and result.
de la dang po
BASIS
['di] la'ang
[This has two types: physical basis and mental basis.]
[lus rten]
PHYSICAL BASIS

lus kyi rten ni gling gsum gyi skyes pa dang bud med dang 'dod khams pa'i lha ris drug la skye'i gzhan la ni ma yin te/ ngan song gsum dang byang gi sgra mi snyan pa ni rnam smin gyi sgrib pas bsgribs pa'i phyir dang*/ za ma dang ma ning dang mtshan gnyis pa rnams rten dman pa'i phyir dang*/ khams gong ma'i skye bo dag ni 'khor ba la skyo ba med pa'i phyir ro/ /

The first is that these moments arise on the physical basis of a male or female human of the three continents or the six types of desire-realm gods. They do not arise in other beings because those of the three lower rebirths and Uttarakuru are obscured by maturational obscuration; eunuchs, neuters, and hermaphrodites are inferior bases; and beings of the higher realms do not seek refuge from saṃsāra.
MENTAL BASIS
sems kyi rten ni bsam gtan sa drug pa yin te/ zag med yin zhing gzugs med 'dod pa la mi dmigs la/ de ni chos mchog dang sa gcig ces bshad pa'i phyir ro/ /

The mental basis is the six levels of absorption, since uncontaminated and formless-realm states do not focus on the desire realm and, as the Abhidharmakośa states, “They belong to the same level as the supreme mundane state” (6:27d).
gnyis pa
PATH
['di] la'ang bzhi las
This has four headings: definition, classification, attributes, and synonyms.
DEFINITION
mthong lam gyi mtshan nyid ni bden bzhi'i de kho na nyid sngar ma mthong ba mngon sum du mthong ba yin no/ /
The definition of the path of seeing is “that which directly sees the reality (tattva) of the four truths not previously seen.”

gang dag bdag med mngon sum du mthong ba mthong spang gi gnyen po byed pa zhes zer ba de dag gi ltar na gnyen po mtshan nyid pa la 'dod na shes pa rnams mthong lam ma yin par 'gyur te/ gnyen po mtshan nyid pa ni bar chad med pa'i lam yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'on te gnyen po tsam la 'dod na ni sgom lam yang der 'gyur te/ mthong spang thag sring ba'i gnyen po yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Some say: Whatever directly sees selflessness acts as the antidote to objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing. Reply: If they assert that [vision of selflessness] to be the actual antidote, then the eight knowledges would not be the path of seeing. The actual antidote is the uninterrupted path. If those knowledges are asserted to be mere antidotes — distant antidotes of objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing — then they would become the path of meditation.

kha cig chos mchog chen po'i rjes su bdag med mngon sum du mthong ba sgom lam chung ngu'i rgyur gyur pa zhes zer ba de la'ang gal te sgom lam chung ngu'i dngos kyi rgyu yin na ni lam la rjes bzod ma gtogs pa rnams mthong lam ma yin par 'gyur la/ brgyud pa'i rgyu yin na ni bzod pa phyi ma de nyid mthong lam ma yin par 'gyur ro/ / dngos dang brgyud pa'i rgyu ci rigs pa zhes bya bar 'dod na ni mtshan nyid ma nges pa yin par 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du chos mchog gi rjes su 'byung ba la'ang de ma thag gam brgyud nas zhes brjod par bya'o/ / de'i phyir bshad pa snga ma nyid skyon med pa yin no/ /

Some say: The [definition of the path of seeing is] the mind directly seeing selflessness that exists after the great stage of the supreme mundane state and that acts as the cause of the small path of meditation. Reply: If [the path of seeing] were the direct cause of the small stage of the path of meditation, then minds other than subsequent perseverance for knowledge of the truth of path would not be the path of seeing. If it were the indirect cause, then that subsequent perseverance would not be the path of seeing. If it were asserted that it is either the direct or indirect cause, then the persons [asserting this would] not have ascertained their definitions. Moreover, that which occurs after the stage of the supreme mundane state is called “that which immediately arises” or “that which gradually arises,” and the first explanation is free of error.
CLASSIFICATION

rab tu dbye ba ni gang zag gis ni nyan thos la sogs pa gsum dang*/ yul gyis ni sdug bsngal mthong ba la sogs pa bzhi dang*/ ngo bos ni bzod pa dang shes pa gnyis dang*/ rnam pa las ni sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa la sogs pa bco lnga dang*/ khams kyi gnyen po las ni chos shes dang rjes shes gnyis yin no/ / sngon gyi slob dpon dag gis ye shes mthong ba dang*/ bden pa mthong ba gnyis su bshad pa ni 'dir mi 'dod do/ / ye shes kyang lam bden gyi nang du 'dus pa'i phyir ro/ / mang pos bkur pa pa dag mthong lam skad cig ma bcu gnyis su smra ba'ang gal te bden pa ma mthong ba mthong ba mthong lam yin na bco lnga pa man chad mthong lam du 'gyur te/ bden bzhi sngar ma mthong ba ni ye shes de dag yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'on te rnam pa ma mthong ba mthong ba tsam gyis yin na ni skad cig ma dang po kho na mthong lam du 'gyur ro/ / bden pa dang rnam pa tshogs pa sngar ma mthong ba yin na ni lam la chos shes pa la sogs pa gsum yang mthong lam du thal bar 'gyur ro/ /

Classification by person is the three types of person: [532] śrāvakas, [pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas]. Classification by object is the four objects: seeing the truths of suffering, [origin, cessation, and path]. Classification by essential nature is perseverance and knowledge. Classification by aspect is the fifteen aspects, such as perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering. Classification by antidote according to realm is the two: Dharma knowledge and subsequent knowledge. Past masters explain two types: the seeing of transcendent wisdom and the seeing of truth. Reply: Here that is unacceptable because transcendent wisdom is included in the truth of path. Bahuśrutīyas advocate that the path of seeing has twelve moments. Reply: If seeing the truths that have not been previously seen is the path of seeing, then up to and including the fifteenth moment would constitute the path of seeing, because these transcendent wisdoms have not previously seen the four truths. However, if merely not seeing aspects that were not previously seen constitutes the path of seeing, then the first moment alone would be the path of seeing. But if it were seeing the collection of truths and aspects that were not previously seen, then it would follow that the three moments of Dharma knowledge of the truth of path and so on would be the path of seeing.
[khyad par gyi chos]
ATTRIBUTES
khyad par gyi chos ni mthong spang ma lus pa spangs pa dang*/ bden pa'i chos nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa dang*/ mi skye ba'i chos nyid drug gam brgyad thob pa la sogs pa'i yon tan dang ldan no/ /

This refers to possessing qualities such as abandoning objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing without exception, directly comprehending the reality (dharmatā) of truth, obtaining the six or eight realities of nonarising, and so on.
ming gi rnam grangs ni
SYNONYMS

chos rnams la chos kyi mig rdul med cing dri ma dang bral ba thob pa dang*/ mi skye ba'i chos la bzod pa thob pa dang*/ byang chub sems dpa'i mthong lam gyi dbang du byas nas byang chub sems dpa'i skyon med pa la zhugs pa la sogs pa mdo las rnam pa mang du bshad do/ /

There are many synonyms explained in the sūtras, such as “the eye of Dharma free of dust,” “that which obtains freedom from stains,” and “that which obtains perseverance in the attribute of nonarising.” And from the perspective of the bodhisattva path of seeing, there is “that which enters the faultless state of a bodhisattva” and so on.
RESULT
'bras bu ni sgom lam 'dren par byed pa'o// //
The result is activating the path of meditation.
28. Classifications of Ārya Beings
PRESENTATION OF THE PERSON AS PRACTITIONER

da ni gang zag bshad par bya ste/ de la gang zag ces bya ba ni phung po bzhi'am lnga'i rgyun la btags pa yin te/ lung sil bu las/ rgyun la gang zag ces bya ste/ / mtshan nyid 'dzin la chos zhes brjod/ / 'di la gang yang 'khor ba med/ / su yang mya ngan 'das pa med/ / ces pa dang*/ mdo las kyang*/ / phung po rnams la gang zag ces bya'o zhes gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ dgra bcom ma brag gis kyang*/ ji ltar yan lag tshogs rnams la/ / shing rta'i ming du bshad pa ltar/ / de bzhin phung po rnams brten nas/ / kun rdzob sems can zhes bya'o/ / zhes pa dang*/ btsun pa gzhon nu len gyis kyang*/ phung po'i rgyun ni gang la dge / mi dge'i 'bras bu yod pa nyid/ / de la srog ces bya ste de/ / srog med bstan pas med par 'gyur zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/ /

Now the person is explained. That called “person” is that which is imputed on the continuum of four or five aggregates. As it is said in the Miscellaneous Discourses: The continuum is called “the person,” and that which retains its characteristics is called “dharma.” As such there is no saṃsāra, and there is no one who attains nirvāṇa.[1621] Also, a sūtra declares: The aggregates are called the person.[1622] And Arahantī writes: Just as a collection of parts is given the name of a chariot, so too one is called a conventional sentient being in dependence on the aggregates.[1623] It is also said by Bhadanta Kumāralāta: The continuum of the aggregates is where the result of virtue and nonvirtue exists. It is called life force but ceases to exist when life force ceases.[1624]

kha cig na re phung po lnga tshogs pa la gang zag tu brjod na gzugs med na gang zag med par 'gyur la/ kha yar ba la brjod na bum pa'ang gang zag tu 'gyur bas sa bon thams cad pa'i rnam par shes pa'i rgyun ni gang zag yin te/ rgyud gsum gyi rnam par nges pa las/ kha yar ba dang tshogs pa zhes/ / brtags na phung po lnga'i rgyun/ / gang zag ma yin de yi phyir/ / sa bon kun gyi rnam shes kyi/ / rgyun ni gang zag yin par 'dod/ / ces bshad pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ba ni rnal 'byor spyod pa pa'i lugs yin no/ / des na 'phags pa'i gang zag ni zag med kyi ye shes dang ldan pa'i phung po bzhi'am lnga'i rgyun la brjod pa yin no/ /

Some say: If the collection of [five] aggregates is called the person, then there would be no person in the formless realm. If each aggregate is called the person, then even a vase would become a person. Therefore the continuum of consciousness [533] containing all karmic seeds is the person. As Ascertaining the Three Streams declares: The stream of the five aggregates, designated separately or collectively to be the person, is not the person. But the continuum of consciousness containing all karmic seeds is asserted to be the person.[1625] This is the system of the Yogācāras. Therefore ārya beings are called the continuum of four or five aggregates possessing uncontaminated transcendent wisdom.
de 'chad pa na brgyad du dbye ba dang*/ bdun du dbye ba dang*/ gnyis su dbye ba gsum las
This explanation has three headings: classification in eight, classification in seven, and classification in two.
dang po [gang zag brgyad du dbye ba]

['di] la'ang 'dod chags dang bral ba sngon du 'gro ba dang*/ mthar gyis pa dang*/ khyad par bshad pa gsum gyi
This has three headings: āryas previously freed from attachment, serial abandoners, and specific attributes.
dang po ni
ĀRYAS PREVIOUSLY FREED FROM ATTACHMENT

'jig rten pa'i sgom lam gyis srid rtse ma gtogs pa'i sa brgyad po las ci rigs par 'dod chags bral ba sngon du song nas mthong lam thob par byed pa ste/ de yang 'grel pa las phal cher las 'dod chags dang bral ba dang 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba gnyis bshad pa las dang po ni 'dod pa'i rnam pa drug pa nas brgyad pa'i bar spangs pa dang*/ gnyis pa ni 'dod pa'i rnam pa dgu pa spangs pa nas ci yang med pa'i skye mched kyi dgu pa spangs pa'i bar la TIk+kas bshad kyi rnam pa lnga pa spangs nas mthong lam thob pa ni chags bral sngon 'gror ma bshad la/ 'jig rten pa yis thob 'bras ni zhes pa'i 'grel par yang 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis thob pa'i 'bras bu gnyis zhes 'byung ba'i phyir 'bras bu bar pa gnyis la yod kyi snga phyi gnyis la ni chags bral sngon 'gro med do/ / {nyan sa las kyang*/ dang po nas 'dod pa la 'dod chags dang bral ba zhig yin na ni de mthong lam thob ma thag tu phyir mi 'ong bar 'gyur ro/ / gal te shas cher la 'dod chags dang bral ba zhig yin na ni/ de mthong lam thob ma thag tu lan cig phyir 'ong bar 'gyur ro/ / de 'dod pa la 'dod chags dang ma bral ba zhig yin na ni rgyun ni zhugs par 'gyur ro/ / zhes 'byung zhing*/ 'di'i bzhugs gnas ni rdzas tha dad do }

This refers to āryas previously freed from attachment to any of the eight levels — leaving off the summit of existence through the mundane path of meditation — who obtain the path of seeing. Further the Autocommentary explains two types: (1) those largely free of attachment to the desire realm and (2) those fully free of attachment to the desire realm.[1626] The Subcommentary explains[1627] that (1) the first refers to those who abandon attachment to the sixth through eighth stages of the desire realm, and (2) the second is those who abandon attachment to the ninth stage of the desire realm up to those who abandon nine stages of the base of nothingness. Those who obtain the path of seeing having abandoned five degrees of attachment are not called “āryas previously freed from attachment.” Those who are previously freed from attachment belong to the two intermediate results, but not the first and last result. As the Abhidharmakośa notes, “An ārya freed from attachment by the mundane path” (6:46a), and the Autocommentary states, “The two results obtained by the mundane path.”[1628] {Śrāvaka Levels states: If those freed from attachment to the desire realm from the beginning obtain the path of seeing, they immediately become nonreturners. If āryas previously freed from most degrees of attachment obtain the path of seeing, they immediately become once returners. If they are not free from attachment, they become stream enterers.[1629] Enterers and abiders in those states are substantially different.}

kun las btus las kyang*/ phal cher las 'dod chags dang bral ba ni yang dag pa nyid du nges par gyur pa la zhugs nas lan cig phyir 'ong bar 'gyur ro/ / 'dod pa rnam pas 'dod chags dang bral na ni yang dag pa nyid du nges par gyur pa la zhugs nas phyir mi 'ong bar 'gyur ro zhes gnyis po kho na bshad cing*/ yang dag pa nyid du nges par gyur pa la zhugs pa ni mthong lam nyid la bshad do/ /

The Compendium of Abhidharma states: Those free from most degrees of attachment who enter perfect ascertainment become once returners. Desire-realm beings free from attachment who enter perfect ascertainment become nonreturners.[1630] This passage explains just two types of āryas, and it explains that that which enters perfect ascertainment is the path of seeing.
