gnyis pa ni
SERIAL ABANDONERS
bsgoms pas spang bya ma spangs na/ / 'bras bu dang po la zhugs pa// 29
If they have not abandoned one object to be abandoned by meditation, they enter the first result. (6:29cd)

sngar mthong sgom gyi spang bya ma spangs pas 'ching ba mtha' dag dang ldan pa zhig dang por mthong lam gyis mthong spang rnams spangs nas de nas 'jig rten las 'das pa'am 'jig rten pa'i sgom lam yang rung ste sgom spang rnams rim gyis spong ba'o/ /

Since those who possesses all the ties (bandhana) have not previously abandoned objects to be abandoned by the paths of seeing or meditation, they first abandon objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing.

de la mthong lam skad cig bco lnga man chad la zhugs pa'i dad pa dang chos kyi rjes su 'brang ba de dag gal te sngon 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis sgom pas spang bar bya ba gcig kyang ma sdangs pa'i 'ching ba mtha' dag dang ldan pa yin na 'bras bu dang po rgyun zhugs kyi 'bras bu la zhugs pa yin no/ /

Then they serially abandon objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, through either the mundane path or the transcendent path. If followers of faith or followers of reality who have not abandoned even one object to be abandoned by the path of meditation, and who thus possess all the ties (bandhana), enter the first fifteen moments of the path of seeing, then they enter the first result (phalādi), the result of stream entry.
rnam lnga'i bar bcom gnyis pa la/ / dgu pa tshun chad zad pa yin/ / 'dod pa'am yang na gong ma las/ / chags bral gsum pa la zhugs pa/ 30
Those entering the first destroy up to the fifth degree. Those in the second eliminate up to the ninth. Those freed from desire-realm attachment or higher attachment enter the third. (6:30)

yang skad cig bco lnga man chad la gnas pa'i gnyis po de nyid sngar 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis 'dod pa'i sgom spang gcig nas rnam pa lnga pa 'bring gi 'bring po'i bar du bcom pa gang yin pa de yang 'bras bu dang po la zhugs pa yin no/{ 'bras bu dang po thob pa'i ched du brtson bzhin pa'i 'phags pa yin pa'i phyir 'ching ba kun ldan bzhin no/ /}

Both followers of faith and followers of reality who abide from the first to fifteenth moment of the path of seeing — who have previously destroyed (ghna) from the first up to the fifth degree (prakāra), which constitutes the medium of the medium stage of objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation — enter the first result. {They possess all the ties (bandhana) because they are āryas who strive to obtain the first result.}

yang de gnyis 'bras bu gnyis pa lan cig phyir 'ong la zhugs pa ni {zhes pa 'di la ni smra sgo las/ la ni gnyis pa bzhi pa dang*/ / bdun pa sdug dang sbyor ba dang*/ / smon dang tshad 'dzin gzhi dang ni/ / tshe skabs dag tu 'dod pa yin/ / zhes 'byung bas shing la gcod ces pa lta bu gnyis pa dang*/ shing la chu 'dren zhes pa lta bu bzhi pa dang*/ / shing la bya gnas zhes pa lta bu bdun pa dang*/ / lag pa bsnyal la zan bza' zhes pa lta bu sdud pa dang*/ gang na du ba yod pa 'di na ni/ me yod la 'di na ni me med do/ / zhes pa lta bu sbyar ba dang*/ bdag nam zhig na 'di lta bu zhig tu gyur la gyur nas kyang zhes pa lta bu smon pa dang*/ gzhi de tsam du bya ba la ji tsam la de tsam la zhes pa lta bu tshad 'dzin pa'i gzhi dang*/ dus de la'am der zhes pa lta bu tshe skabs la 'jug pa dang*/ brgyad las 'bras bu gnyis pa'i phyir zhes bzhi pa dgos ched kyi la yin par 'grel TIka gis bshad do } sngar 'dod pa'i sgom spang drug pa nas dgu pa tshun chad ni dgu pa ma gtogs pa ste/ brgyad pa chen po'i 'bring gi bar 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis zad cing spangs pa skad cig ma bco lnga pa la gnas pa yin no/ /

Now when those two enter the second result, once return, it is as follows. {In this context[1631] Entry to Speech declares: The postposition la is asserted to be the second case, the fourth case, the seventh case, collecting, applying, entreating, the basis for apprehending the measure, and occasion.[1632] Its commentary, Commentary on the Entry to Speech, remarks that the fourth case is the purposive preposition: The second case is, for instance, “cutting the tree.” The fourth case is, for instance, “bring water for the tree.” The seventh case is, for instance, “a bird lives in the tree.” Collecting is, for instance, “I eat food in my washed hand.” Applying is, for instance, “wherever smoke exists fire exists, and fire does not exist in this place.” Entreating is, for instance, “give it to me at this time.” The basis for apprehending the measure is, for instance, “act in this way for that basis.” And the occasion is, for instance, “also at that time.”}[1633] They abide in the fifteen moments, having previously eliminated (kṣaya) and abandoned desire-realm objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation due to the mundane path from the sixth level up to and including the eighth level, which is the medium of the great stage, but excluding the ninth.

yang de gnyis sngar 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis 'dod pa'i nyon mongs pa ma lus pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba'am yang na de nas bzung ste gong ma ci yang med pa'i skye mched kyi bar gang yang rung ba las 'dod chags bral ba zhig gis mthong lam skad cig ma bco lnga pa thob pa ni 'bras bu gsum pa phyir mi 'ong la zhugs pa yin no/ /

Again, if those two are previously freed from all desire-realm attachment (kāma) and affliction without exception due to the mundane path — or if they are free from attachment up to the higher realm of the base of nothingness and then they obtain the fifteen moments of the path of seeing — then they enter (pratipanna) nonreturn, the third result.
Those who abide in the entry to any result
gang zhig gang la zhugs pa ni/ / bcu drug pa la de 'bras gnas/ / de tshe dbang po rno rtul dag / dad pas mos dang mthong bas thob/ / 31

enter abidance in that result in the sixteenth moment. At that time those of sharp and those of dull faculties are called [respectively] those who obtain their result through seeing and those resolute in faith. (6:31)

dad pa dang chos kyi rjes su 'brang ba gang zhig 'bras bu dang po rgyun zhugs la sogs pa gang la zhugs pa'i skad cig ma bco lnga pa la gnas pa de ni skad cig ma bcu drug pa la ni rgyun zhugs la sogs pa de'i 'bras bu la gnas par 'gyur gyi zhugs pa dang dad pas rjes 'brang dang chos kyi rjes 'brang du ni mi 'gyur ro/ / de'i phyir chags bral sngon 'gro'i zhugs gnas la rtogs pa la khyad par yod kyi spangs pa la khyad par med de/ ye shes skad cig ma bco lnga pa dang bcu drug pas phye ba'i phyir dang*/ spangs pa ni 'dra ba'i phyir ro/ / dgra bcom pa la ni chags bral sngon 'gros thob pa med de/ srid rtse'i sgom spang ma spangs par dgra bcom mi thob cing mthong lam gyis sgom spang mi spong ba'i phyir

Those followers of faith or followers of reality who abide in the fifteen moments of entry to any result, such as the first — stream entry — and so on, enter abidance in that result (phalasthāna) such as stream entry in the sixteenth moment. But followers of faith do not [535] become followers of reality. Therefore the entry and the abidance of āryas previously freed from attachment are differentiated by their realization and not by their abandonment because the fifteen moments are differentiated from the sixteenth moment of transcendent wisdom, and the objects they abandon are similar. Arhats do not obtain prior freedom from attachment because they do not obtain the state of an arhat without abandoning objects to be abandoned on the summit of existence, and the path of seeing does not abandon objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation.

{te bzod pas gzhom min sgom kho nas/ / zhes 'jig rten pa'i sgom lam gyis spong ngo zhe na } dang*/ zag{ pa dang} bcas{ pa'i} 'og sa dang rang sas mi spong la de bas mtho ba'i 'jig rten pa'i sa med pas srid rtse'i sgom spang spong ba'i 'jig rten pa'i lam yang med pa'i phyir ro/ /

{But if it is said that they are abandoned by the mundane path of meditation, since the Abhidharmakośa declares, “Those not eliminated by perseverance, by meditation alone” (5:6d),} then they are not abandoned by contaminated states of lower or equal level. Since there is no mundane path that abandons objects to be abandoned at the summit of existence by the [mundane] path of meditation, there is no mundane level higher than that.

{rgyun zhugs la'ang chags bral sngon 'gro med de/ bden pa thams cad ma mthong bar srid rtse'i mthong spang mi spong bas sngar 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis rang gi spang bya thams cad spangs pa mi srid pa'i phyir ro } gang zhig mthong lam skad cig bco lnga pa man chad la 'dod pa'i sgom spang lnga pa man chad spangs nas bcu drug pa la drug pa spong ba ni mi srid de/ de ni bco lnga pa man chad zhi gnas gang la brten pa de la bcu drug pa yang rten gyis gzhan la brten pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du bco lnga pa la brgyad pa man chad spangs nas bcu drug pa la dgu pa spong ba'ang mi srid par shes par bya'o/ / de'i phyir 'dod chags dang bral ba sngon du 'gro ba'i 'phags pa ni bar ma gnyis kho nar zad do/ /

{Also, there are no stream enterers who obtain prior freedom from attachment because it is not possible to first abandon all objects to be abandoned on the level [of stream entry] by the mundane path without seeing all four truths and without abandoning objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing at the summit of existence.} It is not possible for those abiding on the fifteenth moment of the path of seeing, who have abandoned five or fewer desire-realm objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, to abandon the sixth stage in the sixteenth moment. For whatever stage of calm abiding they depend on in the fifteenth moment or earlier, they also depend on in the sixteenth moment; they are not dependent on any other stage. So too, you should understand that it is impossible for those who have abandoned eight stages or fewer in the fifteenth moment to abandon the ninth stage in the sixteenth moment. Therefore āryas previously freed from attachment must be either of the two intermediate āryas alone.

gang gi tshe mthong lam gyi 'bras bu skad cig ma bcu drug pa thob pa de'i tshe sngar gyi dbang po rnon po chos kyi rjes 'brang dang rtul po dad pas rjes 'brang dag ni rim pa ltar mthong bas thob pa dang dad pas mos pa zhes bya ba'i ming 'thob ste/ de nas gzung nas dgra bcom pa'i 'bras bu la zhugs pa'i bar du yang de bzhin du shes par bya'o/

Whenever an ārya obtains the sixteenth moment of the result of the path of seeing, at that time former followers of reality with sharp faculty (tīkṣṇendriya) and former followers of faith with dull faculty (mṛdu indriya), respectively, obtain the titles “those obtaining results by insight” (dṛṣtyāpta) and “those resolute in faith” (śraddhādhimukta), and they are called that until they enter the result of an arhat.

{ rgyun zhugs kyi dbye ba la zhugs gnas gnyis las/ zhugs pa ni lam gyis phye na mthong lam skad cig bco lnga la gnas pas bco lnga'o/ / de re re'ang 'dod chags dang bral bas drug ste/ sgom spang ma spangs pa nas lnga pa spangs pa'i bar ro/ / de re re yang gnyis gnyis te dad pa'i rjes 'brang ni rigs kyis lnga ste/ nyams pa'i chos can nas rtogs pa'i skal ba can gyi bar ro/ / de re re'ang dbang pos gsum mo/ / de re re yang rten gyis dgu dgu ste gling gsum dang lha drug go /de ltar bsdoms pas khri nyis stong bdun brgya lnga bcu'o/ / de bzhin du chos kyi rjes 'brang la rigs la dbye ba med pas nyis stong bzhi brgya sum cu'o/ / 'bras gnas la dad mos ni gzhan pa'i rjes 'brang dang 'dra la lam gyi dbye ba med de thams cad bcu drug bar zad pas na brgyad brgya dang bcu yod do/ / mthong thob ni gzhan chos kyi rjes 'brang dang 'dra la/ lam gyi dbye ba med pas brgya dang drug cu rtsa gnyis te rgyun zhugs kyi dbye ba ni de lta bu yin no/ /

{If stream enterers are classified, there are two types: enterers and abiders. (1) If enterers [to stream entry] are classified by path, there are fifteen, since there are fifteen abiders who abide in the fifteen moments of the path of seeing. Also, for each there are six by freedom from attachment — from those who have not abandoned any objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation up to those who have abandoned five stages. Also, for each of these are two [(1.1) followers of faith and (1.2) followers of reality]. (1.1) There are five by lineage of followers of faith, from those who degenerate up to those who enter realization.[1634] For each of those there are three by intellectual faculty. There are nine classified by basis, since there are three humans and six gods. Thus in total there are 12,150.[1635] (1.2) Similarly, for followers of reality there are 2,430,[1636] since there is no classification by lineage. (2) Abiders in the result [of stream entry] have two types: (2.1) those resolute in faith are related to other followers of faith and not classified by path. There are 810,[1637] since all are included in the sixteenth [path]. (2.2) Those obtaining results by insight are similar to followers of reality. Since they are not classified by path there are 162,[1638] for their classification is like that of [enterers to] stream entry.

chags bral sngon 'gro'i phyir 'ong la zhugs gnas gnyis las/ zhugs pa la'ang gnyis las dad pas rjes 'brang ni gzhan rgyun zhugs dang 'dra la/ 'dod chags dang bral bas gsum ste/ bzhi stong brgyad brgya drug cu'o/ / chos kyi rjes 'brang ni rigs la dbye ba med la gzhan chos rjes 'brang ba snga ma dang 'dra bas stong nyis brgya bco lnga'o/ / de'i gnas pa la dad mos ni rigs la dbye ba med cing gzhan dad pa'i rjes 'brang bzhin te bzhi brgya dang lnga bcu'o/ / gnas pa gnyis pa mthong thob ni lam la dbye ba med la gzhan ni chos kyi rjes 'brang bzhin te brgyad cu rtsa gcig go /chags bral sngon 'gro'i phyir mi 'ong la zhugs gnas gnyis las/ zhugs pa gnyis ni rigs lnga dang gcig yin pa dang dbang po gsum gsum du 'gyur bar dang rten gyis dgu yin pa ni snga ma kho na bzhin yin la/ bye brag tu dad pas rjes 'brang ni 'dod chags dang bral bas drug cu re bzhi ste bsam gtan bzhi dang gzugs med dang po gsum gyis phye ba drug cu re gsum dang*/ 'dod pa'i chung ngu spangs pa'am/ bsam gtan dang po'i 'ching ba mtha' dag dang ldan pa gang rung ngo*/ / de lta na 'bum nyis khri dgu stong drug brgya yod do/ / chos kyi rjes 'brang ni rigs kyis dbye ba med la gzhan de dang 'dra ste nyis khri lnga stong dgu brgya nyi shu'o/ / 'di'i gnas pa ni bye brag mang bas brjod pa mang por 'gyur te phal cher 'og gi mthar gyis pa dang 'dra bar sbyor gsung ngo*/ /}

Once returners previously freed from attachment have two types: enterers and abiders. (1) Enterers [to once return] have two types: (1.1) Followers of faith are similar to other enterers. Since they are free from attachment there are three, making 4,860.[1639] (1.2) Followers of reality are not classified by lineage, but there are 1,215[1640] since they are like the previous followers of reality. [536] (2) Abiders in once return have two types: (2.1) Those resolute in faith who are not classified by lineage, making 450.[1641] (2.2) The second type is those who obtain results by insight. They have no classification by path, and like other followers of reality, there are 81.[1642] Nonreturners previously free of attachment have two types: enterers and abiders. (1) Enterers [to nonreturn] have two types: five lineages and one lineage; three types according to intellectual faculty; and nine types by basis, as before. Specifically, (1.1) followers of faith have sixty-four types through freedom from attachment: they abandon sixty-three types when differentiated by the four absorptions and the first three formless [realms] and the small level of desire, or else they possess all ties (bandhana) of the first absorption. Thus there are 129,600.[1643] (1.2) Followers of reality are similar to other followers of reality who are not classified by lineage and thus have 25,920.[1644] (2) Abiders [in nonreturn] are many since there are many subsets, and the terms applied to them are similar to [those for] the serial abandoners.}
'o na ci'i phyir 'dod pa'i sgom spang lnga pa'i bar du spangs kyang sems bcu drug pa la rgyun du zhugs pa kho na zhes bya'i lan cig phyir 'ong la zhugs pa zhes mi bya zhe na/

Question: But why are those who have abandoned up to five desire-realm objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation just called “stream enterers,” and not “enterers to once return,” when they enter the sixteenth moment of mind?
'bras thob 'bras bu khyad par gyi/ / lam thob med pas de yi phyir/ / 'bras gnas khyad par bya ba'i phyir/ / mi brtson pa ni zhugs ma yin/ / 32
They do not enter that path. They obtain the ordinary result and do not obtain the special result of the path because they do not strive to obtain special abidance in the result. (6:32)

gang gi phyir rgyun du zhugs pa'i 'bras bu{ tsam po} thob pa'i sems bcu drug pa la gnas pa des de dus na 'bras bu khyad par can gyi lam phyir 'ong la zhugs pa thob pa med pas so de'i phyir de ni de la zhugs pa ma yin no zhes sbyar ro/ / ci'i phyir zhe na/ rgyun ni zhugs kyi 'bras bu la gnas pa khyad par can thob par bya ba'i phyir{ nyon mongs pa spong ba'i sbyor ba la} mi brtson pa{ de srid du zhugs pa ma} yin pa'i phyir ro/{ zhugs pa yin na gnyen po la sbyor ba dang bral thob zag med skyes nas zhugs pa yin na/ /} 'di ltar 'bras bu snga ma la gnas pa rnams ni phyi ma thob par bya ba'i phyir mi brtson pa na sems kyi skad cig bcu drug pa de'i tshe 'bras bu la gnas pa tsam yin gyi 'bras bu la gnas pa khyad par can ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gnas pa khyad par can ni phyi ma thob par bya ba'i phyir brtson pa'o/ / 'dis ni 'dod pa'i sgom spang brgyad pa spangs pa sems bcu drug pa la gnas pa dang*/ 'dod pa'am ci yang med pa'i skye mched las 'dod chags dang bral ba sems bcu drug pa la gnas pa de dag kyang rim pa bzhin phyir mi 'ong dang dgra bcom pa'i 'bras bu la zhugs par mi 'gyur ba'i rgyu mtshan yang bshad pa yin no/ / de dag kyang 'bras bu la gnas pa khyad par can nas ni phyi ma la zhugs pa yin no zhes bshad par bya'o/ / des ni sems bco lnga la gnas pa de dag 'dod pa'i sgom spang lnga pa spangs kyang phyir 'ong la zhugs par mi 'gyur ba'ang shes par bya ste/ 'bras bu thob pa'i tshe phyir 'ong mi thob pa'i phyir ro/ / de nyid ji ltar zhe na/ sems bcu drug pa thob pa na 'bras bu la gnas pa thob pa yin na de ni phyir 'ong ma yin te/ phyir 'ong ni 'dod pa'i sgom spang drug pa spangs pa'i phyir dang*/ de ni lnga pa spangs pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du brgyad pa spangs pa sems bco lnga pa la gnas pa phyir mi 'ong la zhugs par mi 'gyur ba dang*/ / ci yang med pa'i skye mched man chad las 'dod chags dang bral ba sems bco lnga pa la gnas pa dgra bcom la zhugs par mi 'gyur ba la sogs pa'ang shes par bya'o/ / des na chags bral sngon 'gro ni 'phags pa snga ma gsum gyi zhugs 'bras rdzas tha dad cing phyir mi 'ong khyad par can nyid dgra bcom la zhugs pa'ang yin pas rdzas bdun du 'gyur ro/ /

Reply: The reason is because those abiding in the sixteenth mind obtain the {ordinary} result of stream entry, and at that time they do not obtain entry to the special result of the path (phalaviśiṣṭa) of once return. Therefore it is applied to the fact that they do not enter that path. Question: Why? Reply: Because they do not strive (prayukta) {to abandon affliction} in order to obtain special abidance in the result (viśeṣāya phalastha) of stream entry, {and until they do, they do not enter it}. If those abiding in the former result {who have spontaneously entered that result after the uncontaminated state free from engaging the antidote has arisen} do not strive to obtain the later result, then they are abiders in the ordinary result in the sixteenth moment of mind, not abiders in the special result. Special abiders are those who strive to obtain the later result. This also explains why those abiding in the sixteenth mind who abandon eight desire-realm objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, and those abiding in the sixteenth mind who are free of attachment to the desire realm or the base of nothingness, do not enter the results of nonreturn and arhat, respectively. Also it explains that they enter the later result from the special abidance in the result. Therefore you should understand that though those abiding in the fifteenth moment of mind may abandon five desire-realm objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, they do not enter once return; they do not obtain once return when they obtain their result. Question: Why? Reply: If they obtain abidance in the result when they obtain the sixteenth mind, then that result would not be once return. Once returners abandon the sixth object to be abandoned by the path of meditation in the desire realm, and they have abandoned only the fifth stage. So too, you should understand that those who abandon eight stages and abide on the fifteenth moment of mind do not enter nonreturn, and those abiding [537] in the fifteenth moment of mind who are free of attachment to the base of nothingness and below do not enter the state of an arhat and so on. Therefore they constitute seven different substances, for āryas previously freed from attachment are different in substance from the first three ārya enterers and abiders, and special nonreturners are arhats.

kha cig 'di bye brag tu smra bas kun brtags par 'chad pa ni ma yin te/ kun las btus las kyang bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te kun las btus las bshad pa ni 'di dang mthun pa ma yin te/ 'dod pa'i sgom spang drug pa spangs pa sems bco lnga pa la gnas pa phyir 'ong la zhugs pa dang*/ de nyid sems bcu drug pa la gnas pa phyir 'ong gi 'bras bu la gnas pa dang*/ 'dod pa'i sgom spangs thams cad spangs pa sems bco lnga pa la gnas pa phyir mi 'ong la zhugs pa dang*/ sems bcu drug pa la gnas pa phyir mi 'ong gi 'bras bu la gnas par bshad pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ der ni spang bya'i nyung ba'i mtha' dngos su bshad nas 'dir smros pa mang ba'i mtha' shugs la go bar bya ba'i phyir yin la/ 'dir ni mang ba'i mtha' dngos su bshad nas de las bshad pa'i nyung ba'i mtha' spangs pa shugs la go bar bya ba'i phyir sgo gnyis su bstan pa yin pa'i phyir gnyis kas kyang gnyis ka 'dod do/ / gal te 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis sgom spang spong na khams las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i so so'i skye bo slar mi ldog pa dang*/ phyis de las 'og ma'i nyon mongs pa kun tu mi 'byung bar 'gyur te/ sngar spangs zin pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te spangs kyang 'byung na 'phags pa de dag la'ang 'byung bas phyir mi 'ong la sogs par mi 'gyur ro zhe na/ 'di la bye brag tu smra ba ni 'phags pa rnams la'ang nyams pa yod na so so'i skye bo rnams la lta ci smros/ 'on kyang 'dod chags dang bral ba sngon du 'gro ba'i 'phags pa de dag la ni nyams pa mi srid de/ 'jig rten dang 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam gnyis kyis brtan par byas pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ /

Some say: This explanation is not contrived by the Vaibhāṣikas because it is also stated in the Compendium of Abhidharma.[1645] Objection: The explanation in the Compendium of Abhidharma is not compatible with this explanation because [the Compendium] delineates (1) an enterer to once return who abides in the fifteenth moment of mind, having abandoned six desire-realm objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, and (2) an abider in the result of once return who abides in the sixteenth moment of mind, and (3) an enterer to nonreturn who abides in the fifteenth moment of mind, having abandoned all desire-realm objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, and (4) an abider in the result of nonreturn who abides in the sixteenth moment of mind. Reply: It teaches both methods because one can indirectly infer the maximum limit of objects to be abandoned from the explicit explanation of the minimum limit, and one can implicitly infer the minimum limit of objects to be abandoned from the explicit explanation of the maximum limit. Therefore both teach both. Objection: If the mundane path abandons objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, then an ordinary being free of attachment to the realms would attain irreversibility, and lower-realm affliction would not occur later because he would have previously abandoned it. Yet if it recurred though it was previously abandoned, then āryas for whom it recurred would not become nonreturners and so on. Vaibhāṣikas say: If degeneration also exists for āryas, then what need is there to speak of ordinary beings? However, it is impossible for āryas previously freed from attachment to degenerate, because their state is stabilized by both the mundane and the transcendent paths.

mdo sde pa la sogs pa ni 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis spang bya'i mngon gyur spong ba dang sa bon nyams smad par byed pa tsam yin gyi rtsa ba nas mi spong bas 'dod chags dang bral ba'ang slar ldog la/ 'on kyang 'dod chags dang bral ba sngon du 'gro ba'i 'phags pa de dag ni 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis sgom spang gi nyon mongs pa'i mngon gyur spangs pa'i phyir dang*/ sa bon yang de ma thag par skye ba'i 'jig rten las 'das pa'i sgom lam gyis spong ba'i phyir de phyin chad 'dod par lan cig las 'ong mi srid pa dang phyir mi 'ong ba'i phyir de dang der brjod do zhes 'chad do/ / kun las btus las/ rgyun du bzhugs pa cig car nges par 'byin pa zhes gsungs pa ni bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs mi lcogs med la brten nas mthong lam thob pas mthong spang spangs te rgyun zhugs kyi 'bras bu thob par byas te/ de'i rjes la 'jig rten las 'das pa'i sgom lam gyis khams gsum gyi bden pa la cig car dmigs nas sgom pas 'dod pa'i sgom spang chung ngu'i chung ngu la sogs pa spangs pa ni srid rtse'i yang chung ngu'i chung ngu la sogs pa spong bas phyir 'ong dang phyir mi 'ong thob pa med par dgra bcom pa mngon du byed pa'o/ /

Sautrāntikas and so on say: The mundane path abandons manifest afflictions and merely suppresses seeds. Since it does not abandon afflictions from the root, it must again stop and free the mind from attachment. However, āryas previously freed from attachment are given that name because they have abandoned manifest afflictions that are objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation through the mundane path, they immediately abandon the seeds of affliction through the transcendent path of meditation, and they become nonreturners, since it is impossible for them to subsequently return once more to the desire realm. The Compendium of Abhidharma observes: Stream enterers attain definite release simultaneously. This means that those who abandon objects to be abandoned [538] by the path of seeing in dependence on unrestricted access concentration to the first absorption obtain the result of stream entry. After that, they manifest the state of arhat without obtaining the state of a once returner or nonreturner, for when they abandon the small of the small desire-realm objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, they abandon the small of the small objects to be abandoned at the summit of existence, since their transcendent path of meditation simultaneously focuses on the four truths of the three levels.
mthar gyis pa brjod pa/

da ni mthar gyis pa brjod par bya ste/ de ni sngar mthong sgom gyi spang bya gcig kyang ma spangs pa 'ching pa mtha' dag dang ldan pa zhig dang por mthong lam gyis khams gsum gyi mthong spang spangs te/ de nas sgom lam zag bcas zag med gang rung gis sgom spang spangs te 'bras bu bzhi rim gyis tshang bar thob pa dang gsum mam gnyis 'thob pa'ang yod do/ / de la rgyun zhugs dang*/ lan cig phyir 'ong dang*/ phyir mi 'ong dang*/ dgra bcom pa la zhugs pa dang gnas pa bshad pa bzhi las

Those called “serial abandoners” are those who possess all the ties (bandhana) and have not previously abandoned even one object to be abandoned by the paths of seeing or meditation. First they abandon objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing in the three realms through the path of seeing, then they abandon objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation through either the contaminated or uncontaminated path of meditation. These are explained in four headings: enterers and abiders in stream entry, enterers and abiders in once return, enterers and abiders in nonreturn, and enterers and abiders in the state of arhat.
rgyun zhugs bshad pa/
Enterers and abiders in stream entry
sa dang sa na nyes rnam dgu/ / de bzhin du ni yon tan rnams/ / chung dang 'bring dang che rnams kyi/ / chung ngu la sogs tha dad phyir/ / 33

The desire-realm level and higher levels have nine stages of fault. So too, qualities. Because the path of meditation is differentiated as small, medium, and great and each has small of the small and so on. (6:33)

dang po ni ji ltar 'dod khams na sgom spang gi nyon mongs pa rnams pa dgu yod pa de bzhin du bsam gtan dang po nas srid rtse'i bar gyi sa dang sa brgyad po re re na yang spang bar bya ba'i nyes pa chen po 'bring chung ngu gsum gsum dang de dag re re la'ang chen po'i chen po nas chung ngu'i chung ngu'i bar rnam pa dgu dgu yod pas spyir brgyad bcu rtsa gcig yod do/ / ji ltar sa de dag re re na spang bya dgu dgu yod pa de bzhin du gnyen po yon tan sgom pa'i lam bar chad med pa dang rnam grol gyi lam rnams kyang dgu dgu brgyad cu rtsa gcig yod {mi lcogs med nas bzung ste } do/ / ji ltar zhe na/

Just as there are nine degrees of affliction that are objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation in the desire realm, so too they exist from the first absorption to the summit of existence. The desire-realm level (bhūmi) and the eight higher levels have three degrees of fault (doṣa) that are objects to be abandoned — the great, medium, and small; and each of those has three degrees — great, medium, and small. Therefore each level has nine stages (navaprakāra), from the great of the great to the small of the small, making eighty-one overall. And just as there are nine objects to be abandoned on each level, so too there are nine each with respect to the uninterrupted and liberated paths meditating on the qualities (guṇa) of the antidotes, making eighty-one. Question: How are those eighty-one calculated {from unrestricted access concentration}?

de dag re re na sgom lam chung ngu dang 'bring dang chen po rnam pa gsum gsum yod la de rnams kyi re re zhing yang chung ngu'i chung ngu la sogs pa'i dbye bas tha dad pa'i phyir ro/ / de la spang bya chen po'i chen po ni spang sla ba'i phyir gnyen po sgom lam chung ngu'i chung ngus spong ba yin te gos kyi dri ma rags pa 'bad pa chung ngus spong ba bzhin no/ / de bzhin du spang bya chung ngu ni chung ngu'i sgom lam chen po'i chen pos spong ba la sogs pa'ang shes par bya ste/ dang po ni lam chen po mi srid pa'i phyir dang*/ lam chen po skyes pa na nyon mongs pa chen po mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / de la mthong lam skad cig ma bco lnga ni 'bras bu dang po la zhugs pa dang bcu drug pa ni gnas pa tsam po yin par sngar bshad {spyir dad mos tsam la dbye na dbang pos gsum mo rigs kyis lnga'o/ / spangs pas 'ching ba kun ldan nas lnga pa spangs pa'i bar drug go /rten gyis dgu'o/ / lam gyis dbyer med de thams cad kyang bcu drug par zad pa'o/ / mthong thob kyang rigs kyis dbyer med gzhan ni snga ma dang 'dra ste spyir brgya dang drug cu rtsa gnyis so } la/

Reply: Because for each of those levels the path of meditaton is differentiated in three stages — the small, medium, and great — and each of those is classified as “small of the small” and so on. The great-of-the-great object to be abandoned is abandoned by its antidote, the small-of-the-small path of meditation, because it is easy to abandon, just as a small amount of exertion eliminates the gross stains in clothes. Similarly, the small-of-the-small object to be abandoned is abandoned by the great-of-the-great path of meditation and so on, because it is impossible to first generate the great path and great affliction is impossible once the great path is generated. The fifteen moments of the path of seeing are entry to the first result, and the sixteenth moment is ordinary abidance, as previously explained. {In general, if just those resolute in faith are classified, there are three by intellectual faculty; five by lineage; six by abandonment, from possessing all ties (bandhana) up to abandoning five stages; and nine by basis. There is no classification by path because all are completed in the sixteenth moment. In general, therefore, there are 810.[1646] Also, for those obtaining results by insight there are 162,[1647] since as before they are not classified by lineage.}
'bras gnas bsgom spang bya ma zad/ / re ltar thogs na lan bdun pa/ / rnam gsum rnam bzhi las grol ba/ / tshe gnyis gsum du rigs nas rigs/ / 34

Abiders in the result who do not eliminate that which is to be abandoned by meditation are “stream enterers who take seven existences” when obstructed in that way. Those liberated from three or four stages are born as the same type for two or three lives. (6:34)

rgyun zhugs kyi 'bras gnas gang zhig sngar sgom pas spang bar bya ba'i nyon mongs pa gcig kyang ma zad de ma spangs na da ni re ltar te rab tu thogs na lan bdun skye ba srid pa'i phyir srid pa lan bdun pa zhes bya ste/ mdo 'ga' zhig las po zos na lan bdun pa dang*/ mchog tu thogs na lan bdun pa zhes bshad do/ / spyir brgyad brgya dang bcu'o/ / bye brag tu smra ba rnams na re lha'i srid pa bdun dang mi'i srid pa bdun dang bar do'i srid pa bdun tshan gnyis te nyi shu rtsa brgyad len kyang bdun tshan du chos mthun pa'i phyir srid pa bdun pa zhes bya ste shing lo ma bdun pa bzhin no zhes zer ro/ /

Abiders in the result (phalastha) of stream entry who do not eliminate (akṣīṇa) or abandon even one affliction that is to be abandoned by prior meditation (bhāvanāheya) are called “stream enterers who take seven existences” (saptakṛtpara) because they are born seven times when obstructed in that way. In some sūtras they are called “stream enters delayed for seven existences” [539] or “stream enterers obstructed seven times at most.” Vaibhāṣikas say: They take twenty-eight existences: (1–7) seven god existences, (8–14) seven human existences, and (15–28) twice seven [or fourteen] intermediate existences. However, they are called “stream enterers who take seven existences” because they exhibit a sevenfold pattern, like a plant with leaves possessing seven facets.

mdo sde pa la sogs pa na re de lta na khams mang po'i mdo las/ gang zag lta ba phun sum tshogs pa srid pa brgyad pa mngon par 'grub pa gang yin pa de ni gnas ma yin zhing go skabs med de 'di ni gnas med do zhes bshad pa dang 'gal lo zhes zer ro/ / bye brag tu smra ba na re de ni 'gro ba ris mthun cig tu mi skye ba'i dbang du byas pa yin te/ de lta ma yin par sgra ji bzhin du brtag na ni mdo las/ lha dang mi rnams kyi nang du lan bdun 'khor zhing song nas sdug bsngal gyi mthar byed do zhes 'byung bas bar srid kyang med par 'gyur ro zhes zer ro/ / 'o na de lta na gnas thams cad du 'chi ba mi rung bar 'gyur ro zhe na/ mdo las srid pa lan bdun par gsungs pa ni 'dod pa'i srid pa'i dbang du byas pa'i phyir {de la dgongs nas gsungs pas } nyes pa med do zhes zer ro/ /

Sautrāntikas and so on say: This contradicts the explanation of the Multiple Elements Sūtra, which declares: Beings with excellent view are not the basis for establishing an eighth existence. They are not the basis since they do not provide the opportunity for that.[1648] Vaibhāṣikas say: This is from the perspective of not being born as one type of reincarnating being. If that were not so, then even the fourteen intermediate existences would not exist when one investigates the literal meaning of the sūtra, which states: They cycle seven times among gods and humans, and having completed that, reach the end of suffering.[1649] Objection: If intermediate existences were counted, then it would be untenable to die in all abodes. Reply: Because the sūtra mentions “seven existences” from the perspective of desire-realm existences, there is no fault; {it is stated with that intention}.[1650]

'di ni las kyi stobs kyis 'phangs pa'i phyir dang*/ dus de srid kyis rgyud smin pas srid pa bdun las lhag par yang mi skye la de'i gong du{ bar skabs su lam gong ma dang} yang dgra bcom pa mngon du mi byed {de srid du myong bar nges pa'i las yod pa'i phyir/ 'di ni re ltar thogs na zhes pa dang 'gal lo } de sbrul gom pa bdun pas zin pa dang rims nyin bzhi pa bzhin no/{ rgyun zhugs 'bras gnas tsam po ni srid pa lan bdun pa yin te/ gong ma'i lhar bskyed pa na mir skye ba med de/ 'bras bu la nyams bzhin du 'chi ba la sogs par thal ba'i skyon yod pas so/ / gang zhig mi'i rten la rgyun zhugs su gyur pa de ni mthar de kho nar 'ongs na mya ngan las 'da' la/ lha'i nang du de thob pa'ang mthar lha'i rten la mya ngan las 'da'o/ / srid pa brgyad pa mi 'byung ba ni lam de'i rang bzhin de yin pa'i phyir te de srid kyis nges par rgyud smin pa'i phyir sbrul gom pa bdun pas zin pa bzhin no/ / de srid du skye ba 'grub ste/ tha ma'i cha mthun gnyis dang gong ma'i cha mthun lnga ste kun sbyor bdun lus pa'i phyir ro/ / so skye rgyud smin pa kha cig yang lan bdun pa yod do/ /} de ni sangs rgyas{ kyi bstan pa dang sangs rgyas} 'jig rten du mi 'byung ba na ni khyim pa'i rten nyid la chos nyid kyis thob pa'i dgra bcom thob pas dge slong yin no/ /

This is established because desire-realm existences are projected by the power of karma, and they are not born more than seven times since their mindstreams are matured by entering existence that many times. Before it is over they do not manifest {occasional higher paths or} the state of an arhat, {because until then they have karma that will definitely be experienced. This contradicts the statement “when obstructed in that way” (6:34c)}. It is like one bitten by a snake who dies after seven steps or fever arising on the fourth day. {Ordinary abiders in the result of stream entry are stream enterers who take seven existences, for when they take birth as higher gods, they do not take birth as a human. Otherwise it would erroneously follow that they would die when they degenerated from that result and so on. Those who become a stream enterer on a human basis ultimately progress on that basis alone. Those who obtain stream entry among the gods also ultimately attain nirvāṇa on a divine basis. They do not have eight existences because that is the essential nature of the path, and those seven existences definitely mature the mindstream, just as one who is bitten by a snake dies after seven steps. Birth is established for that period because seven fetters (saṃyojana) — (1–2) two factors associated with inferior states and (3–7) five associated with higher states — endure. Some ordinary beings who possess mature mindstreams also take seven existences.} At a time when {the teachings of} a buddha do not exist in the world, one who obtains the state of an arhat on a lay basis becomes a fully ordained monk spontaneously.
kha cig na re phyi rol pa la sogs pa'i dge sbyong gi tshul gyis dgra bcom thob bo zhes zer ro/ /
Some say: Outsiders and so on also obtain the state of an arhat by means of training in virtue.

rgyun zhugs kyi 'bras gnas gang zhig sgom lam zag bcas zag med gang rung gis 'dod pa'i sgom spang gi nyon mongs pa'i rnam pa gsum mam rnam pa bzhi'i bar las rnam par grol ba{ ste 'di ni bden pa mthong ba'i sngon nam phyis spang kyang rung ngo*/ / gang zag} de ni{ bzhi spangs na} tshe gnyis sam{ gsum spangs na} gsum du rigs nas rigs su skye ba ste/ de la'ang lha'i rigs nas rigs su skye ba dang*/ mi'i rigs nas rigs su skye ba gnyis so/ / nyon mongs pa gcig dang gnyis spangs pa de ni tshe drug gam sngar rigs nas rigs su skye ba yin no zhes ma smros kyang shugs la go'i zhes smon gyi slob dpon kha cig 'chad do/ / kha cig na re de yang lan gnyis sam gsum du rigs nas rigs su skye ba yin pa'i phyir logs su ma bshad do zhes zer ro/ / ci'i phyir lnga pa spangs pa'ang rigs nas rigs su skye bar ma smros she na/ 'dod pa'i nyon mongs pa lnga pa spangs pa ni drug pa'ang{ tshe de nyid la} nges par spong ba'i phyir rigs nas rigs su skye ba ma yin te/ rnam pa drug pa gcig pus ni phyir 'ong gi 'bras bu la gegs bya bar mi nus pa'i phyir ro/ / de lta na bar chad gcig pa'i rnam pa dgu pa gcig pus kyang phyir mi 'ong ba'i 'bras bu la gegs byed par mi 'gyur{ khams las mi 'da' ba'i phyir ro} ro/ zhe na/ de ni mi mtshungs te/ bar chad gcig pa ni 'dod khams las 'da' dgos pas dka' ba'i phyir rnam pa gcig gis kyang gegs bya bar nus la/ {'grel par ni lha dag gi nang du song nas mi'i 'jig rten du lan cig 'ong ba'i phyir/ phyir 'ong ba ste/ phan chad skye ba med pa'i phyir ro zhes 'dod lhar song nas mir lan cig phyir 'ong du bshad la mdo las 'dod chags dang zhe sdang dang gti mug rnams bsrabs pa'i phyir lan cig phyir 'ong ba zhes 'byung ba ni sgom spang chung gsum pus pa yin la } phyir 'ong ni khams las 'da' mi dgos pas rnam pa drug pa gcig pus gegs bya bar mi nus pa'i phyir ro/

Reply: Those abiding in the result of stream entry who are liberated from three or four stages of affliction to be abandoned by meditation in the desire realm through either the contaminated or uncontaminated path of meditation, {either before or after seeing the four truths, are persons} born the same type (kulaṅkula) for two lives {when four stages are abandoned} or three lives (janmā) {if three stages are abandoned}. They have two types: stream enterers born the same type as gods and stream enterers born the same type as humans. [540] A past master explains that though it is not stated, it is implicitly understood that those abandoning one or two afflictions are born the same type for five or six lives. Some say: They are not explained separately because they are born the same type two or three times. Question: Why are those who have abandoned five stages not called “stream enterers who are born the same type”? Reply: Because those abandoning five desire-realm afflictions definitely also abandon six stages {in that life}. They do not take birth as the same type because the sixth stage alone cannot impede the result of once return. Objection: Thus for once returners with one obstruction, the ninth stage alone would not impede attainment of the result of nonreturn. {They do not transcend the desire realm.} Reply: That is not similar, because it is difficult for once returners with one obstruction to transcend the desire realm, and one stage can impede that. {The Autocommentary declares: Because they proceed to the community of the gods and return once to the world of humans, they are once returners. After that they have no rebirths [in the desire realm].[1651] This explains that, having proceeded to the gods, they return once as humans. A sūtra notes: Because attachment, aversion, and delusion are diminished, they are once returners.[1652] Thus the three small objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation remain.} Since once returners necessarily do not transcend the desire realm, the sixth stage alone cannot impede once return.
gnyis pa phyir 'ong bshad pa ni
Enterers and abiders in once return
rnams pa lnga yi bar bcom pa/ / gnyis pa la ni zhugs pa'ang yin/ / rnam pa drug pa zad gyur pa/ / de ni lan cig phyir 'ong ba/ / 35
Anyone who has destroyed up to five stages also enters the second result. Anyone who exhausts six stages is a once returner. (6:35)

rgyun zhugs kyi 'bras gnas 'dod pa'i sgom spang{ gcig nas} rnam pa lnga'i bar du bcom pa{ drug pa spong ba'i bar chad med lam la gnas pa} gang yin pa de ni 'bras bu dang po la gnas par ma zad 'bras bu gnyis pa phyir 'ong la zhugs pa'ang yin no/ / lan cig phyir 'ong 'bras gnas tsam po ni bden pa mthong nas 'dod pa'i sgom spang rnam pa drug pa zad par gyur pa{ 'i rnam grol la gnas pa} gang yin pa de ni lan cig phyir 'ong ba ste/ nyon mongs pa chung ngu gsum gyis ni 'dod par lan cig las skye ba mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / {'di la dbye na zhugs pa la dad mos mthong thob gnyis ka yang dbang pos gsum gsum dang*/ rten gyis dgu dgu dang*/ spangs pa dang lam gyis lnga lnga'o/ / dad mos ni ris kyis lnga ste spyir drug brgya dang bdun cu rtsa lnga'o/ / mthong thob ni rigs kyis dbyer med pas brgya dang sum cu rtsa lnga'o/ / gnas pa gnyis ni gzhan dang snga ma 'dra la spangs pa dang lam gyis gsum gsum ste/ dad mos ni brgyad cu rtsa lnga dang*/ mthong thob ni nyi shu rtsa bdun yod do }

Anyone abiding in the result of stream entry who has destroyed (ghna) up to five stages of desire-realm objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation {or who abides on the uninterrupted path abandoning the sixth stage} not only abides in the first result but also enters once return, the second result. Any ordinary abider in the result of once return who has seen the four truths, and who {abides on the liberated path that} exhausts (kṣīṇa) six stages of desire-realm objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, is a once returner (sakṛdāgāmi), because it is impossible for them to be born more than once in the desire realm due to the three small afflictions. {If once returners are classified, there are both enterers and abiders. (1) Enterers [to once return] have two types: (1.1) those resolute in faith and (1.2) those obtaining results by insight. Those two are each divided, in three each by faculty, nine each by basis, and five each by abandonment and path. In general, since those resolute in faith are five by lineage, they number 675.[1653] Since those obtaining results by insight are not classified by lineage, they number 135.[1654] (2) Abiders have two types, like the previous. They have three types each by abandonment and path, because those resolute in faith number 85[1655] and those obtaining results by insight number 27.[1656]}
nyes cha bdun dang brgyad zad pa/ / tshe gcig bar chad gcig pa dang / / gsum pa la ni zhugs pa'ang yin/ / de dgu zad pas phyir mi 'ong / / 36
Those who exhaust seven or eight stages of fault have one life or one obstruction. They also enter the third result. Since they exhaust nine, they are nonreturners. (6:36)

phyir 'ong gi 'bras gnas 'dod pa'i sgom spang gi nyes pa'i cha bdun dang brgyad zad pa gang yin pa de ni {dgra bcom thob pa la }tshe gcig pa dang{ phyir mi 'ong thob pa la nyon mongs kyi} bar chad gcig pa zhes bya ste gnas pa khyad par can no/ / tshe gcig gis phyir mi 'ong la bar chad byed pa ni sngar bshad pa ltar 'di ni 'dod khams las 'da' dgos shing khams las 'da' ba ni/ bzod dang phyir mi 'ong dgra bcom/ / 'thob la las gegs shin tu byed ces 'byung la/ nyon mongs pa'ang las dang 'dra bas spang dka' ba'i phyir nyon mongs pa gcig gis kyang bar chad byed pa'i phyir ro/ / {mthong lam ma thob kyi sngon du gsum dang bzhi spangs pa dang bdun dang brgyad spangs pa 'bras bu tsam thob pa ni rigs skye'am bar chad gcig pa ma yin te/ de dag gi gnyen po zag med kyi dbang po ma thob pa'i phyir ro/ / de dag gam de dag gi gong ma'i gnyen po 'bras bu khyad par can mngon sum du byas na yin no }
gsum pa phyir mi 'ong bshad pa ni
Enterers and abiders in nonreturn

phyir 'ong gi 'bras gnas khyad par can de nyid 'bras bu gsum pa phyir mi 'ong ba'i 'bras bu la zhugs pa'ang yin no/ / phyir 'ong gi 'bras gnas de nyid 'dod pa'i sgom spang dgu pa zad pas phyir mi 'ong ba yin te/ 'dod par phyir skye ba len pa mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / phyir mi 'ong gi 'bras bu la gnas pa de nyid ni gsum du dbye ste/ gzugs su nye bar 'gro ba dang*/ gzugs med par nye bar 'gro ba dang*/ tshe 'di la mya ngan las 'da' ba'o/ /

Special abiders in the result of once return also enter the result of nonreturn, the third result. Since those abiders in the result of once return exhaust nine desire-realm objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, they are nonreturners. It is impossible for them to take rebirth in the desire realm. Abiders in the result of nonreturn are classified in three types: nonreturners proceeding to the form realm, nonreturners proceeding to the formless realm, and nonreturners attaining nirvāṇa in this life.

NONRETURNERS PROCEEDING TO THE FORM REALM

rnam pa lnga ste/ bar ma dor mya ngan las 'da' ba dang*/ skyes nas mya ngan las 'da' ba dang*/ mngon par 'du byed pa dang bcas pa dang*/ mngon par 'du byed pa med par yongs su mya ngan las 'da' ba dang*/ gong du 'pho ba rnams so/ /

There are five types: (1) nonreturners attaining nirvāṇa in the intermediate state, (2) nonreturners attaining nirvāṇa after birth, (3) nonreturners attaining nirvāṇa with application, (4) nonreturners attaining nirvāṇa without application, and (5) nonreturners relocating to a higher level.

de ni bar skyes 'du byed dang / / 'du byed med yongs mya ngan 'da'/ / gong du 'pho ba rnams de ni/ / bsam gtan spel na 'og min 'gro/ / 37
de 'phar phyed 'phar thams cad du/ / 'chi 'pho gzhan srid rtse mor 'gro/ / gzhan ni gzugs med 'gro rnam bzhi/ / gzhan ni 'di la mya ngan 'da'/ / 38

They attain nirvāṇa in the intermediate state, after birth, with application, without application, by relocating to a higher level. Those who augment absorption and proceed to Akaniṣṭha (6:37)
are those who advance, half advance, or die in all abodes. Others proceed to the summit of existence. Others proceed to the formless realm. There are four types. Others attain nirvāṇa in just that life. (6:38)

NONRETURNERS ATTAINING NIRVĀṆA IN THE INTERMEDIATE STATE
'di nas shi 'phos te gzugs kyi{ gnas bcu drug gang rung gi} bar der{ lhag med} dgra bcom thob par byed pa{ 'di chos nyid kyis bar dor yun ring gnas la skye ba'i nyon mongs pa med pas so 'o/}

They die from here and obtain the state of an arhat {without remainder} in the intermediate state (antara) {of any of the sixteen abodes of} the form realm. {They abide naturally for a long time in the intermediate state and have no birth affliction.}

NONRETURNERS ATTAINING NIRVĀṆA AFTER BIRTH

{ bar dor 'da' ma dus ba de} lam sgom pa la mngon par brtson pa dang lam ngang gis 'byung ba gnyis ka yod pas tshangs ris la sogs par skyes ma thag tu dgra bcom thob par byed pa'o/ / {kha cig phung po lhag med du 'da' zer ba ni mi rigs te/ tshe 'dor ba'i dbang med pa'i phyir ro/ / de la dbang thob pa la rab mtha'i bsam gtan bzhi pa thob pa'i mi dgra bcom dbang rnon dgos pa'i phyir ro/ / de lta na bar dor 'da' ba de tshe la dbang bar 'gyur ro zhe na mi dbang yang bar dor gnas par byed pa'i las ni skyes nas myong 'gyur lta bu'i mthu can med pas myur du lhag med du 'da' la/ 'di ni tshad de rdzogs nas so/ / des na mi mtshungs so/}

They obtain the state of arhat immediately after birth (utpanna) in Brahmakāyika and so on, since they have both the path cultivated with exertion and the path naturally arisen, {and they cannot transcend saṃsāra in the intermediate state}. {Some say: They are called “nonreturners who transcend without remainder of the aggregates.” Reply: That is illogical, because they lack the power to relinquish life. Those who obtain that power must be human arhats of sharp faculty who obtain the limit of the fourth absorption. Objection: If that is so, then those who transcend saṃsāra in the intermediate state gain control over life. Reply: Though they don’t gain such control, they quickly transcend saṃsāra in the state of remainderless nirvāṇa, since the karma to abide in the intermediate state lacks the power of karma to be experienced after birth, for instance, and such karma is quickly exhausted. Therefore it is not similar.}
gsum pa ni
NONRETURNERS ATTAINING NIRVĀṆA WITH APPLICATION
brtson pa yod kyang lam ngang gis 'byung ba med pas de lam sgom pa la rtsol ba dang bcas pas dgra bcom thob par byed pa'o/ /
Since they strive to cultivate the path, they obtain the state of an arhat through exertion and not through the path that naturally arises.
bzhi pa ni
NONRETURNERS ATTAINING NIRVĀṆA WITHOUT APPLICATION

brtson pa dang lam ngang gis 'byung ba gnyis ka med pas tshangs ris la sogs par skyes nas yun ring po lon nas lam sgom pa la rtsol ba med par dgra bcom thob par byed pa'o zhes bye brag tu smra ba 'dod la/ slob dpon ni mdo las/ mngon par 'du byed pa med par yongs su mya ngan las 'da' ba dang*/ mngon par 'du byed pa dang bcas pas yongs su mya ngan las 'da' ba zhes mngon par 'du byed med par myang 'das sngar 'byung bas de dang mthun yang 'bad rtsol med pa dang yod pas 'thob pa'i sgo nas mngon par 'du byed pa med pa dang 'du byed pas bsgrub par bya ba yin pas lam ngang gis 'byung ba dang ngang gis 'byung ba ma yin pas 'du byed med pa gsum par bzhed do/ /
lam ngang gis 'byung bar 'dra yang skyes nas dang khyad par med par mi 'gyur te/ skyes nas myang 'das ni lam ches ngang gis 'byung ba dang*/ rgyu bsags pa'i sgo nas lam ches che ba dang*/ las ches che ba nyid kyis zad par byas pas phra rgyas ches chung ba yin la/ 'du byed med pa ni de lta ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Without striving to cultivate the path, they obtain the state of an arhat neither through exertion nor through the path that naturally arises, long after they have taken birth in Brahmakāyika and so on. This is asserted by Vaibhāṣikas. A sūtra mentions: Attaining nirvāṇa without application and attaining nirvāṇa with application.[1657] Therefore attaining nirvāṇa without application occurs first. In conformity with that, Vasubandhu asserts three types: nonreturners who establish nirvāṇa without application (asaṃskāra parinirvṛti) [542] or with application (saṃskāra parinirvṛti), since they obtain it with exertion or without exertion, and the path without application may naturally arise or not naturally arise.
Though such paths are similar to others that naturally arise, they are not the same. That which attains nirvāṇa from birth is a greater natural path, it is an even greater path in terms of accumulating causes, and due to being an even greater path it has fewer negative tendencies. But the path without application is not like this.
lnga pa ni
NONRETURNERS RELOCATING TO A HIGHER LEVEL

tshangs ris la sogs pa bsam gtan dang po'i gnas gzhan dag tu dgra bcom ma thob par 'od chung la sogs pa gong du 'phos nas dgra bcom thob par byed pa ste/ gong du 'pho ba{ ni 'dir phyir mi 'ong thob kyang lan grangs gzhan la myong 'gyur gyi las kyi mthus bar do dang skyes gnas 'da' mi nus pa ste} de ni rgyu'i sgo nas shes rab la dga' bas lhag mthong spyad pa bsam gtan spel ba dang*/ ting nge 'dzin la dga' bas zhi gnas spyad pa bsam gtan ma spel ba gnyis las

They do not obtain the state of an arhat in abodes such as the first absorption of Brahmakāyika and so on, but they obtain the state of an arhat by relocating to a higher level (ūrdhvaṃsrotā) such as Parīttābha. Nonreturners who relocate to higher levels {obtain nonreturn on such levels, but they cannot transcend intermediate states or birth states due to the force of karma to be experienced in a third life.} There are two types: (1) nonreturners who like wisdom and augment absorption through insight and (2) nonreturners who like concentration and do not augment absorption through calm abiding.
dang po
NONRETURNERS WHO LIKE WISDOM AND AUGMENT ABSORPTION THROUGH INSIGHT

rgyu'i sgo nas bsam gtan spel ma bsgoms na 'bras bu'i sgo nas 'og min gyi mthar thug par 'gro ba de yang dbye na 'phar ba dang phyed du 'phar ba dang gnas thams cad du 'chi 'pho ba gsum las dang po ni 'dod par skye ba'i 'phags pas bsam gtan bzhi pa goms par byas pa zhig bsam gtan dang po'i bde ba'i ro myangs pas gong ma gsum las nyams te shi 'phos pa na tshangs ris la sogs par skyes nas sngon goms pa'i shugs kyi bsam gtan bzhi pa{ bco lnga} spel {bsgoms } te 'og min du skyes nas dgra bcom thob par byed pa'o/ / gnyis pa ni{ tshangs ris kyi rten la gsum spel lam drug spel goms nas} rgyun snga ma la gtsang ma ris kyi lha lnga'i 'og ma gang rung gcig tu skyes nas de nas bco lnga pa bsgoms nas 'og min du skyes te dgra bcom thob par byed pa'o/ / gsum pa ni tshangs chen ma gtogs pa gnas ris bcu drug po thams cad du song ste 'og min gyi lus la dgra bcom thob par byed pa'o/ / tshangs chen du mi skye ba ni lta ba'i gnas yin pa dang*/ gtso bo gcig pa'i gnas yin pas 'phags pa rnams kyis spangs pa'i phyir ro/ / gang dag 'od gsal man chad du rim gyis skyes nas de'i rten la dgra bcom thob pa la sogs pa'ang yod par rigs pa'i phyir 'di gsum du nges pa ni ma yin par gsal lo/ / phyir mi 'ong ba zhes bya ba'ang 'dod pa kho nar phyir mi 'ong ba ni ma yin gyi 'on kyang sa gang du skyes pa'i 'phags pa de sa de dang 'og mar phyir mi 'ong{ bas phyir mi 'ong rdzogs} pa'i phyir te/ bsam gtan dang por skyes pa'i phyir mi 'ong ba 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang por phyir mi 'ong ba la sogs pa lta bu ste/ 'phags pa de dag yang na ni rten de la dgra bcom thob par byed la/ der ma thob na ni gong du 'pho ba yin te/ khyad par du 'gro ba yin pa'i phyir ro/{ spel ma nyams nas sprin med la sogs par skye ba ni med de/ spel ma'i ting nge 'dzin bzhi pa'i sa pa yin la de rang sa'i nyon mongs kyis nyams par mi 'gyur la ma nyams na gnas gtsang du skye ba'i phyir ro/}

Nonreturners who augment (vyavakīrṇa) causal absorption and proceed to the resultant final abode of Akaniṣṭha have three types: (1) nonreturners who advance (pluta), (2) nonreturners who half advance (ardhapluta), and (3) nonreturners who die in all abodes (sarvachyuta). Nonreturners who advance are āryas born in the desire realm who cultivate the fourth absorption but experience the taste of pleasure in the first absorption, when the three higher absorptions degenerate. When they die and change abode, they are reborn in Brahmakāyika and so on, and through augmenting the fourth absorption due to the strength of their prior familiarity, they are reborn in Akaniṣṭha and there obtain the state of an arhat. Nonreturners who half advance are those who took birth as any of the gods below the gods of the five pristine abodes in their former lives {through a threefold or sixfold augmention on the basis of Brahmakāyika}. Then, through meditating on the fifteenth form-realm state, they are born in Akaniṣṭha, where they obtain the state of an arhat. Nonreturners who die in all abodes proceed to all sixteen abodes except Mahābrahma and obtain the state of an arhat in the body of a god of Akaniṣṭha. They do not take birth in Mahābrahma because āryas abandon it, since it is an abode of pernicious views and the view of a single creator deity. They take birth in progressive stages up to Ābhāsvara, but because it is possible for them to obtain the state of an arhat as a being of this stage, there is no certainty that they will take birth in the higher three stages. They are called nonreturners not merely due to not returning to the desire realm but because āryas born on any level do not return to that level {where they actualized the state of nonreturn} or to lower levels, just as a nonreturner who is born in the first absorption does not return to the desire realm or to the first absorption and so on. Again, such āryas obtain the state of arhat on that basis, but if not obtained there, then they relocate to higher levels because they can proceed in extraordinary ways. {They do not take rebirth in Anabhraka and so on if augmentation degenerates because augmented concentration exists on the level of pacification, and affliction of their level does not degenerate it. And if it does not degenerate, then they are born in the pristine abodes.} [543]
gnyis pa
NONRETURNERS WHO LIKE CONCENTRATION AND DO NOT AUGMENT ABSORPTION THROUGH CALM ABIDING

rgyu'i sgo nas bsam gtan spel ma bsgoms pa las gzhan rgyu'i sgo nas bsam gtan ma spel ba ni srid pa'i rtse mo'i mthar thug par 'gro ba yin te/ bsam gtan dang po nas bzhi pa'i gnas gtsang ma lnga ma gtogs pa rnams su rim gyis song ste/ de nas gzugs med pa rnams su song nas srid rtser dgra bcom thob par byed pa'o/ / gong du 'pho ba de dag la bar skabs sa 'og ma dag tu dgra bcom thob pa'ang yod mod kyi 'og min dang srid rtse'i mthar thug pa zhes bya ba ni de dag las gong du 'gro ba med pa'i phyir te/ dper na rgyun zhugs la srid pa gnyis sam gsum mngon par grub nas mya ngan las 'da' ba srid kyang phyin chad srid pa brgyad pa mi 'grub pas na mchog tu thogs na lan bdun pa zhes bshad pa bzhin no/ / gal te srid rtse'i mthar thug par 'gro ba gzugs su 'gro bar ji ltar 'gyur te/ de ni gzugs med du 'gro ba yin pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ bden mod kyi gnas gtsang ma ma gtogs pa rnams su rim gyis 'ongs nas gzugs med par 'gro ba'i phyir de skad du brjod do/ / 'di dag gnas gtsang mar mi 'gro ba ni gnas gtsang ma dag ni 'phags pa'i gnas yin pas de nas shi 'phos nas gzugs med byis pa'i gnas su mi skye ba'i phyir dang*/ skye ba de dag kyang 'phags pa'i gnas su mi 'gro ba ni chos nyid yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Others who do not cultivate the augmentation of causal absorption, and thus do not augment causal absorption, proceed to the limit of the summit of existence (bhavāgra). They serially proceed to all abodes from the first to fourth absorptions except for the five pristine abodes. Then they proceed to the formless states, where they obtain the state of an arhat at the summit of existence. Indeed, nonreturners who relocate to higher levels may obtain the state of an arhat while on lower levels, yet “Akaniṣṭha” and “the final summit of existence” are stated because there is no level above them. For example, it is possible for a stream enterer to attain nirvāṇa after two or three existences, but they are still called “stream enterers obstructed for seven existences at most,” even though their eighth existence is not established. Question: How can nonreturners who proceed to the final summit of existence, which is in the formless realm, be nonreturners who proceed to the form realm? Reply: Good question! They are so called because they proceed to the formless realm after serially proceeding to all form-realm levels except for the pristine abodes. They do not proceed to the pristine abodes, because when those of the pristine abodes that are abodes of āryas die, they do not take birth in the formless realm, which is [in general] an abode of childlike beings. And those who are born [in the formless realm] do not proceed to the ārya abodes, because that is the nature of reality.
NONRETURNERS PROCEEDING TO THE FORMLESS REALM

gzugs su nye bar 'gro ba las gzhan ni gzugs med par nye bar 'gro ba'i phyir mi 'ong ba ste/ 'dod par phyir mi 'ong thob pa gzugs las 'dod chags dang bral ba dag ni gzugs med du skyes nas dgra bcom 'thob pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang dbye na skyes nas dang*/ mngon par 'du byed bcas dang*/ byed pa med par mya ngan las 'da' ba dang*/ gong du 'pho ba dang rnam pa bzhi'o/ / de na bar srid med pas bar ma dor mya ngan 'da' ba ni med do/ / rnam pa bzhi zhes bya ba'ang ci yang med pa'i skye mched man chad kyi dbang du byas kyi srid rtse la ni gong du 'pho ba'ang med pa'i phyir ro/ /

Others who do not proceed to the form realm are nonreturners who proceed to the formless realm (arūpyaga). Those who obtain nonreturn to the desire realm and who are free of attachment to the form realm obtain the state of an arhat having taken birth as formless-realm beings. If classified, there are four types: (1) nonreturners attaining nirvāṇa after birth, (2) nonreturners attaining nirvāṇa with application, (3) nonreturners attaining nirvāṇa without application, (4) nonreturners relocating to higher levels. Here there is no category of nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa as an intermediate being since there are no intermediate beings in the formless realm. Also “four types” (6:38c) is stated from the perspective of the base of nothingness, because there are none who transfer to a higher level from the summit of existence.
NONRETURNERS ATTAINING NIRVĀṆA IN THIS LIFE

Others from those earlier nonreturners attain nirvāṇa having obtained the state of an arhat in just that current life. {If nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa in this life are classified, there are nine by basis; and seventy-one by abandonment: twice thirty-six — four times the nine objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation in the absorptions and four formless states — minus the ninth abandonment of the peak of existence. Other classifications are similar, and in general there are 1,662.}

Thus there are seven nonreturners: (1–5) five nonreturners who proceed to the form realm, (6) one nonreturner who proceeds to the formless realm, and (7) one nonreturner who attains nirvāṇa in this life. If those who proceed to the form realm are enumerated as one, there are really just three. For Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas, if the five nonreturners such as nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa in the intermediate state are individually classified by their abode, then in the four absorption levels there are sixteen abodes. [The heaven of] Mahābrahma is not regarded as distinct from that of Brahmapurohita, and it is excluded [544] since it is an abode of pernicious views. If those beings are classified by lineage, there are six, such as those who degenerate. If they are classified by freedom from attachment, then there are nine, from possessing all ties (bandhana) to being free from attachment to the eighth stage on one’s own level. If they are classified by intellectual faculty, there are three — those of sharp faculty and so on. Thus the classification of nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa in the intermediate state is 2,592.[1658] So too, if that is applied to the other four, such as nonreturners attaining nirvāṇa from birth and so on, then in general there would be 12,960[1659] nonreturners. For nonreturners who proceed to the formless realm, there are four by basis, three by intellectual faculty, six by lineage, nine by freedom from attachment, and four by essential nature, excluding attainment of nirvāṇa in the intermediate state. Therefore for each there are 648,[1660] and together they are classified as 2,592.[1661] All nonreturners who are free from attachment to the nine stages of all lower levels possess all ties (bandhana) of higher levels, so those who have abandoned nine stages of desire affliction possess all ties (bandhana) of the first absorption and so on. Nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa in this life are classified as six by lineage and three by intellectual faculty. They are not classified by basis or freedom from attachment, because desire is exhausted on the same basis and those who don’t abandon desire-realm affliction are not nonreturners. Thus there are 16,164,[1662] since there are nine by basis, including humans of the three continents and the six types of god, and seventy-two classified by freedom from attachment, including nine stages for each of the eight levels from the first absorption to the summit of existence.

{Some say: In total there are ten on each level, if the nine to be abandoned on each level and all the ties (bandhana) are added. Reply: That is not so, since immediately before they abandon the nine of the lower level they possess all ties (bandhana) of higher level and they are calculated as one. Abandonment of the nine of one’s level is classified as that, since it is untenable to establish existence on that level. Thus, if classified by specific abode, type, freedom from attachment, and intellectual faculty, there are 12,960. As such, there are six types in one abode, and as there are nine to be abandoned for each type, there are six times nine, making fifty-four. Fifty-four times sixteen is 864. That is multiplied by the three types of intellectual faculty, [making 2,592]. And by applying the five yet to be explained, in total there are 12,960.} Question: What is the meaning of the sūtra that explains that nonreturners who proceed to the form realm are nine in number?

Nonreturners who proceed to the form realm are explained as nine types, since each of those three is classified in three. The difference in those is due to categorization by karma, faculty, affliction, and further divisions. (6:39)

bar ma dor mya ngan las 'da' ba la zhogs ma'i me stag chung ngu mngon par grub bzhin du 'chi ba dang*/ lcags kyi tshwa tshwa steng du yar bzhin du 'chi ba dang*/ lcags kyi tshwa tshwa steng du yar nas sa la ma lhung bar 'chi ba'i dpe gsum gyis myur ba dang*/ myur ba ma yin pa dang*/ yun ring mo zhig nas mya ngan las 'da' ba gsum dang*/ skyes nas mya ngan las 'da' ba la skyes ma thag dang*/ 'du byed bcas dang*/ byed pa med pa gsum dang*/ gong du 'pho ba la 'phar ba la sogs pa gsum ste/ de ltar gsum po re re la'ang rnam pa gsum gsum du phye nas gzugs su nye bar 'gro ba'i phyir mi 'ong ba ni dgur bshad do/ /

Reply: Nonreturners who proceed to the form realm (rūpopaga) are explained as nine types, since each of those three is again classified in three. Therefore nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa in the intermediate state have three types: (1) nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa swiftly, (2) nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa slowly, and (3) nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa after a long time. These are illustrated by three examples: (1) those who die like a small spark from a burning woodchip, (2) those who die like an ascending iron spark, and (3) those who die like an iron spark that ascends [545] and then falls to the ground. Nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa after birth have three types: (1) nonreturners who attain it immediately after birth, (2) nonreturners who attain it with application, and (3) nonreturners who attain it without application. Nonreturners relocating to higher levels are classified in three — those who advance and so on.[1663]

The difference in those three or nine types of nonreturners is due to categorization (viśeṣata) by three types of karma: (1) karma that establishes the intermediate state, (2) karma to be experienced by birth, and (3) karma to be experienced in a third life; by three types of intellectual faculty: (1) sharp, (2) medium, and (3) dull; and by the three types of affliction: (1) small, (2) medium, and (3) great. Also, intellectual faculty and afflictions have further divisions, such as sharp of the sharp or small of the small — that are easier to abandon. Nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa swiftly in the intermediate state and so on are similar to this. Further, the first two of the three divisions are differentiated by intellectual faculty and affliction, but they are not differentiated by karma, because the first three are similar in having karma that is actually established, the second set of three are similar in having karma to be experienced after rebirth, and the final three are differentiated by karma, faculty, and affliction. Objection: Now, why is it said in the Medium-Length Discourses that there are seven holy beings who proceed to higher levels?[1664]
gong du 'pho ba ma phye bar/ / dam pa'i 'gro ba bdun du 'dod/ / dam pa dam min 'jug mi 'jug / son pa phyir mi 'ong phyir de/ / 40

Those who proceed in purity are asserted to be seven when those who relocate to higher levels are not divided. They are pure because they engage in pure action, they don’t engage in impure action, and they do not return to life. (6:40)

de ni gzugs su nyer 'gro'i phyir mi 'ong ba dgu po de las gong du 'pho ba gsum du ma phye bar bgrangs pa las ni skyes bu dam pa'i 'gro ba bdun du 'dod pa yin no/ { gong 'pho mi 'byed pa ci zhe na/} de ni bsam gtan spel ma spel dang*/ khams gcig dang gnyis su 'gro ba dang*/ 'phar ba la sogs pa shin tu mang bas gdul bya'i blo 'khrug bsam phye zhes so/ ci'i phyir{ slob pa'i nang na} 'di dag kho na dam par brjod ce na/

Reply: From those nine nonreturners who proceed to the form realm, nonreturners who proceed in purity (sadgata) are asserted to be seven when nonreturners who relocate to higher levels (ūrdhvaṃsrotu) are not divided (abheda) in three. {Question: Why are nonreturners who transfer to higher levels not differentiated? Reply: I think such differentiation confuses the minds of disciples since there are so many divisions — those who augment or do not augment absorption, nonreturners who proceed to one realm or two realms, nonreturners who advance, and so on.} Question: Why, {among learners,} are only these beings called “pure”?

las dam pa dge ba la 'jug pa'i phyir dang*/{/'dod pa la 'dod chags dang bral bas mi dge ba spangs pa'i phyir/}dam min mi dge ba la mi 'jug pa'i phyir dang*/ 'gro ba 'di dag tu son pa phyir mi 'ong ba'i phyir de dag kho na skyes bu dam pa'i 'gro ba yin gyi so so'i skye bo dang slob pa chags bcas la ni de dag med pa'i phyir dang*/ mi slob pa'i 'phags pa dag dam pa yin kyang khams gong mar 'gro ba ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na mdo las/ skyes bu dam pa gang zhe na/ slob pa'i yang dag pa'i lta ba nas ting nge 'dzin gyi bar dang ldan pa'o zhes gsungs pa ji ltar zhe na/ de ni srog gcod pa nas chang 'thung ba'i bar sdig pa lnga po gtan mi byed pa'i sdom pa thob pa'i phyir dang*/ sdig pa gzhan yang mthong spang dang 'dod pa'i sgom spang ci rigs pa spangs pas phal cher spangs pa'i phyir de tsam gyis rnam grangs pa'i dam par bshad pa yin la/ 'dir ni rnam grangs ma yin pa'i dam par bstan pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te 'dod par{ tshe dang po la} 'phags pa'i bden pa mthong ba tshe rjes nas phyir mi 'ong thob pa la'ang bar ma dor mya ngan las 'da' ba la sogs pa'i dbye ba yod dam zhe na/

Reply: That is because they engage (vṛtti) in virtuous pure (sat) action: {they abandon nonvirtue since they are free of desire-realm attachment}, they do not engage (avṛtti) in nonvirtuous impure (asad) action, and they do not return to life (apratyāgata) in those rebirths. Ordinary beings and learners with attachment do not have these qualities. Though nonlearner āryas are pure, they do not proceed to higher realms. Question: Now why does a sūtra state, “What is a pure being? It is one who possesses the qualities from learner correct view to concentration”?[1665] Reply: A person is said to be nominally pure merely because he obtains the vows for never committing the five misdeeds — from taking life to drinking alcohol — or because he abandons other misdeeds, objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing, or objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation in the desire realm. But this passage teaches genuine purity. Question: Are those who see [546] the four ārya truths {in their first life} in the desire realm, and who obtain nonreturn in their next life, classified as nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa in the intermediate state and so on?

Those who become āryas in the desire realm do not proceed to other realms. Those born in higher realms do not degenerate, and they do not rely on upgrading intellectual faculty. (6:41)
med de/
Reply: No,

gang zhig 'dod par tshe yongs su gyur pa'i 'phags pa de ni gzugs la sogs pa'i khams gzhan du 'gro ba med {de phyir mi 'ong thob pa'i tshod la mya ngan las 'da' }pa'i phyir ro/{ de yang 'dod pa sdug bsngal mang bas skyo bas so/ /} de la 'dod par tshe yongs su gyur pa'i 'phags pa zhes bya ba ni 'dod par tshe dang po la rgyun zhugs sam lan cig phyir 'ong thob ste shi 'phos nas slar yang tshe gnyis par 'dod par skyes pa'o/ / de ni khams gzhan du 'gro ba ma yin te/ 'dod pa sdug bsngal mang bas sdug bsngal gyis shin tu skyo zhing yid 'byung bas tshe de nyid dam/ yang na tshe gnyis pa la 'dod par skyes te phyir mi 'ong thob par byas nas dgra bcom thob par byed pa'i phyir ro/ / gzugs kyi tshe yongs su gyur pa'i phyir mi 'ong ba ni res 'ga' khams gzhan gzugs med du yang 'gro ste gong du 'pho ba srid rtse'i mthar thug par 'gro ba bzhin no/ / {'di ni mthar gyis pa'i 'bras bu la dka' bar bshad pas chags bral sngon 'gro'i phyir mi 'ong gong du 'gro bar srid par gsal lo zhes sher 'od gsung ngo } 'o na brgya byin gyis zhus pa'i mdo las/ brgya byin gyis/ bdag ni tha mar nyams na lha gang 'og min zhes/ / rnam par grags pa der ni skye bar 'gyur bar shog /bcom ldan bdag ni rgyun zhugs bde gshegs rgyun zhugs te/ / zhes rang nyid rgyun zhugs yin par yang bshad cing*/ de nas mir skyes nas mya ngan las 'da' bar gyur cig der myang 'das ma thob na gzugs khams su skye bar gyur cig ces/ de nas gzugs khams su skye bar smon lam btab la/ ston pas kyang*/ legs so brgya byin bag yod par ni gnas par gyis zhes gsungs nas dgag pa ma mdzad pa'i phyir de dang 'gal te/ brgya byin ni mir skyes na 'dod par tshe yongs su gyur pa'i 'phags pa yin pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ de ni brgya byin gyis chos mngon pa ma shes pa'i phyir yin la/ ston pas ma bkag pa ni brgya byin{ 'chi ltas kyi skyo ba las} dga' bar bya ba'i phyir {yin gyi smad pa'i phyir} ni ma yin no zhes bye brag tu smra ba 'chad do/ /

because those who become āryas in the desire realm[1666] do not proceed to other realms such as the form realm, {because they attain nirvāṇa in the life in which they obtain nonreturn, being completely disgusted with the many sufferings in the desire realm.}[1667] They are called “those who become āryas in the desire realm” because they obtain stream entry or once return in their first life in the desire realm, and after death they take birth for a second time in the desire realm. They do not proceed to other realms because they are entirely disgusted with the many sufferings of the desire realm, and through their intense revulsion they obtain nonreturn or the state of an arhat in that very life or in a second life in the desire realm. Those who become nonreturners in the form realm at times proceed to the formless realm, like those who proceed to the final summit of existence after having relocated to higher levels. {Sherap Ö[1668] explains that it is said that such a result for a serial abandoner is difficult, but it is clear that it is possible for a nonreturner previously freed from attachment to proceed to higher levels.[1669]} Objection: The Sūtra Addressing the Question of Śakra states: Devadatta said: “My final thought is, ‘May I be born in the divine realm of Akaniṣṭha.’ Bhagavan, I am a stream enterer and have entered the stream proceeding to bliss.”[1670] This passage explains that he thought he was a stream enterer. “I pray to attain nirvāṇa, having taken birth as a human. But if I do not obtain nirvāṇa here, I will take birth in the form realm.” Then he prayed to take birth in the form realm. The Master said, “Excellent Devadatta, abide with diligence.”[1671] The Bhagavan did not refute Devadatta’s statement. But his statement is contradictory, because if Devadatta were born human, he would be one who becomes an ārya in the desire realm. Reply: Devadatta’s statement is contradictory because he did not understand Abhidharma. The Master did not refute his statement but sought to protect Devadatta from the signs of death through inspiring him and not censuring him. This is explained by the Vaibhāṣikas.
