Those who become āryas in the desire realm and āryas born in higher realms (ūrdhvaja) do not fully degenerate because they obtain a special {physical} basis {for the path} compatible with manifesting the path. They also possess the special results of the natural outflow of faculties such as wisdom {without upgrading their intellectual faculty}, since they are acquainted with the path for many births. They do not rely on upgrading their intellectual faculty through maturing their mental faculty, and they do not proceed to other realms. Question: Why do learners with attachment not attain nirvāṇa in the intermediate state? Vasubandhu asserts that this pertains to those [547] free from attachment alone, because those unfamiliar with the antidotes to higher realms do not manifest nirvāṇa [in the intermediate state], and their afflicted negative tendencies are not sufficiently small. Vaibhāṣikas say: Intermediate beings cannot do this, because it is difficult for them to transcend the desire realm, and it is difficult for them to engage in many actions to attain nirvāṇa. That is because a stream enterer must obtain three: (1) abandon all afflicted nonvirtuous states of the desire realm and all afflicted obscured-neutral states of the two higher realms, (2) transcend the three realms, and (3) attain the result of training in virtue. A once returner must obtain two. Question: How is absorption augmented, as explained in the Abhidharmakośa, “Those who augment absorption and proceed to Akaniṣṭha” (6:37cd)?
dang po bzhi pa spel bar byed/ / skad cig ma ni bsres pas grub/ / skye dang gnas par bya phyir dang / / nyon mongs pas ni 'jigs phyir yang / / 42
First they augment the fourth. They accomplish it by combining three moments. To attain birth and abide in pleasure, also due to fear of affliction. (6:42)

spel ba ni bsam gtan zag bcas dang zag med spel ba ste/ de yang dang por ni bsam gtan bzhi pa{ 'i dngos gzhi} spel bar byed de/ de ni skyon brgyad las grol bas mchog yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang dang por dgra bcom mam phyir mi 'ong yang rung bsam gtan bzhi pa zag med rgyun ldan dang*/ de yang zag bcas rgyun ldan dang*/ yang zag med rgyun ldan te rgyun dang ldan par spel la/ de nas snga ma ltar skad cig ma gnyis gnyis pa spel nas sgom ste de dag ni sbyor ba yin no/ / gang gi tshe zag med kyi skad cig ma gcig dang zag bcas kyi skad cig ma gcig dang yang zag med kyi skad cig ma gcig ste/ de ltar skad cig ma gsum ni bsres nas snyoms par 'jug nus pas de'i tshe spel ma'i dngos gzhi grub pa yin te/ {skad cig ma } de la dang po gnyis ni bar chad med lam dang gsum pa ni rnam grol gyi lam lta bu yin no zhes bye brag tu smra ba 'dod do/ /

Vaibhāṣikas assert that augmentation is augmenting contaminated and uncontaminated absorption. First they augment (ākīryate) the fourth {actual basis of} absorption because it is supreme, being liberated from the eight errors. Preparation for it consists of either an arhat or a once returner practicing augmention of the continuum of the uncontaminated fourth absorption through first sustaining it, then sustaining the contaminated continuum, then sustaining the uncontaminated continuum. Then they cultivate augmentation for two moments each, as before. They accomplish (sidhyate) the actual basis when they are able to enter meditative attainment by combining (miśraṇat) three moments (kṣaṇa) in the series — one uncontaminated moment, one contaminated moment, one uncontaminated moment — where the first two {moments} are uninterrupted paths and the third is the liberated path.

slob dpon ni skad cig ma spel ba ni sangs rgyas ma gtogs pas mi nus pa'i phyir ro/ / rgyun spel ba la rung ngo zhes 'dod do/ / de ltar dang po bsam gtan bzhi pa spel nas phyis goms nas dang po la sogs pa'i{ dngos gzhi'ang} spel bar byed do/ / {rten ni } de yang dang por 'dod khams kyi gling gsum du spel bar byed la phyis nyams pa dag gis ni gzugs su yang spel bar byed do/ / spel ba'i dgos pa ni gsum ste/

Vasubandhu asserts that momentary augmentation can only be achieved by buddhas, but augmention of the continuum is tenable for others.[1672] Thus the fourth absorption is augmented initially, and then the {actual basis of the} first absorption and so on are augmented, having gained familiarity with the fourth. {The basis of the practice} is a human {basis} of the three continents in the desire realm, where augmentation first occurs. Then, later, those who degenerate also practice augmentation in the form realm. The need for augmentation is threefold:

phyir mi 'ong ba dbang po rnon po rnams ni gnas gtsang mar skye bar bya ba'i phyir dang*/ mthong ba'i chos la bde bar gnas par bya ba'i phyir{ gnyis po de'i don du} spel bar byed kyi de dag las nyams pa mi srid pas nyon mongs pas 'jigs pa'i phyir ni ma yin no/ / rtul po rnams ni de dag gi steng du nyon mongs pas 'jigs pa'i phyir yang ste/ ro myang ba dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i bsam gtan thag bsring ba'i sgo nas 'bras bu las mi nyams par bya ba'i phyir ro/ / dgra bcom pa dbang po rnon po ni{ gzhan gnyis mi 'byung bas} mthong ba'i chos la bde bar gnas pa{ kho na'i ched du} dang*/ rtul po ni{ mthong chos la bder gnas dang 'bras bu las mi nyams pa'i ched du spel te de} 'bras bu las nyams pa'i rkyen nyon mongs pas 'jigs pa'i phyir yin no/ / rgyun zhugs dang phyir 'ong gis ni spel ba mi srid de/ de dag gis bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi ma thob pa'i phyir ro/ / yang ci'i phyir gnas gtsang ma lngar nges she na/

nonreturners with sharp faculty practice augmentation {for two purposes} — (1) to attain birth in the pristine abodes and (2) to abide in comfort in this life — but not out of fear of affliction since they cannot degenerate. Those of dull faculty practice agumentation also (3) due to fear of affliction (kleśabhīruta), because they won’t degenerate from their result if they distance themselves from the absorption that experiences the taste of its pleasure [or bliss]. Arhats with sharp faculty practice augmentation {for the purpose of} abiding {alone} in comfort in this life, {since the other two purposes don’t arise for them}. [548] Those of dull faculty {who practice augmentation for the purpose of not degenerating from the result of abiding in the bliss of this life} fear conditions that produce degeneration of the result through affliction. It is impossible for stream enterers and once returners to practice augmentation because they do not obtain the actual basis of absorption. Question: Why are the pristine abodes definitely five in number?
de ni rnam pa lnga yi phyir/ / gnas gtsang skye ba lnga kho na/ / 'gog pa thob pa'i phyir mi 'ong / / lus kyis mngon sum byed par 'dod/ / 43
There are just five pristine birth abodes because there are five types. It is asserted that nonreturners who obtain cessation physically manifest that state. (6:43)

There are just five pristine abodes (śuddhāvāsa) of resultant birth, such as Avṛha,[1673] because there are five types of augmentation. They are, respectively: (1) a threefold small agumentation that cultivates an uncontaminated state, a contaminated state, and then an uncontaminated state; (2) a sixfold medium augmentation; (3) a ninefold great augmentation; (4) a twelvefold extremely great augmentation; and (5) a fifteenfold supremely great augmentation. Birth in these five states is due to the power of contaminated {completing karma and not projecting karma}. It is not projecting karma since uncontaminated states are the antidote of existence. {Uncontaminated states of the sixfold augmentation and below are meditated on repeatedly). Pūrṇavardhana asserts that one is born in those states through the five great and medium stages of faith and so on.} Bhadanta Śrīlāta says: The pristine abodes are definitely five in number, from the special faculty of faith up to the special faculty of wisdom.[1674] Master Pūrṇavardhana says: That is illogical. The pristine abodes are definitely five in number because they are differentiated in five types — “small” and so on — through separating the five such as faith just as one would grass bundles. It is not because one state excels another.

'gog pa thob pa'i phyir mi 'ong ba ni mya ngan las 'das pa dang 'dra ba'i sems zhi ba mngon du byed nus pa'i phyir lus kyis mngon sum du byed pa zhes bya bar 'dod de/ 'gog pa la snyoms par zhugs pa na sems med pas lus la brten nas skye ba'i phyir lus kyis mngon sum du byed pa'o/ / slob dpon ni 'gog pa la snyoms par zhugs pa'i dus na de dang mthun pa'i lus kyis 'gog pa thob pa mngon sum du byed pa'i phyir dang*/ de las langs pa na rnam shes dang bcas pa'i lus zhi ba thob pas kye ma 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug ni myang 'das dang 'dra bar zhi ba yin no snyam du langs pa'i sems kyis de so sor yang dag par myong ba'i shes pas mngon sum du byed pas na lus kyis mngon sum du byed pa zhes bya'o zhes bzhed do/ /

It is asserted that nonreturners (anāgāmī) who obtain cessation (nirodhalābha) physically manifest (kāyasākṣī) that state because they manifest a mental pacification that is similar to nirvāṇa.[1675] When they enter meditative attainment they manifest that state physically. It is generated in dependence on their bodies, since they have no minds. Vasubandhu asserts that it is said to “physically manifest” because when entering meditative attainment they manifest obtainment of cessation through the body that is compatible with it. When arising from meditative attainment, it manifests through the mind’s correct unique experience. The mind that arises reflects, “The meditative attainment of cessation is peace that is similar to nirvāṇa,” due to obtaining pacification of the body and consciousness.[1676]

Objection: Why is the term “physically manifests” not applied to the eighteen learners mentioned in the sūtras?[1677] Reply: The causes for designating them to be learners are possessing the three uncontaminated trainings and possessing their results that are the essential nature of freedom. However, the meditative attainment of cessation is not a learner path since it does not possess the essential nature of the path of abandonment, and it is not the result of training since it is not analytical cessation that is the essence of freedom. The eighteen are identified in a sūtra: The householder Anāthapiṇḍada asked the Bhagavan: “Venerable, in the world how many are worthy of offerings?” The Buddha replied: “Householder, those worthy of offerings [549] are of two types, the learner and the nonlearner. Householder, the learner has eighteen types, the nonlearner has nine.” Anāthapiṇḍada inquired: “What are these eighteen?”
{ zhugs gnas zung gsum ya gcig dang*/ / rno rtul zung gnyis rigs su skye/ / tshe gcig phyir mi 'ong lnga ste/ / yon gnas slob pa bco brgyad do zhes mkhan chen pas sdom tshig mdzad de/}

{A great scholar composed the following words: “Both enterers and abiders, three less one. Sharp and dull, both pairs, same type. One life, five nonreturners. [These] are the eighteen learners worthy of offerings.”}

rgyun du zhugs pa'i 'bras bu mngon du bya ba'i phyir zhugs pa nas dgra bcom pa'i 'bras bu mngon du bya ba'i phyir zhugs pa'i bar bdun dang*/ dad pas rjes su 'brang ba dang*/ chos kyi rjes su 'brang ba dang*/ dad pas mos pa dang*/ mthong bas thob pa dang*/ rigs nas rigs su skye ba dang bar chad gcig pa dang*/ bar ma dor yongs su mya ngan las 'da' ba nas gong du 'pho ba'i bar lnga ste de dag ni slob pa bco brgyad yin no/ / mi slob pa dgu gang zhe na/ yongs su nyams pa'i chos can dang*/ 'chi bar sems pa'i chos can dang*/ rjes su bsrung ba'i chos can dang*/ gnas pa las mi bskyod pa dang*/ /rtogs pa'i skal ba can dang*/ mi g.yo ba'i chos can dang*/ yongs su mi nyams pa'i chos can dang*/ shes rab kyis rnam par grol ba dang*/ gnyis ka'i cha las rnam par grol ba ste/ de dag ni mi slob pa dgu yin no zhes 'byung ba rnams so/ /

The Buddha replied: “They are (1–7) the seven from those who enter the stream to manifest the result of stream enterer up to those who enter the path to manifest the result of arhat, (8) followers of faith, (9) followers of reality, (10) those resolute in faith, (11) those obtaining results by insight, (12) stream enterers born the same type, (13) once returners with one obstruction, and (14–18) the five from nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa in the intermediate state up to nonreturners who relocate to higher realms, making eighteen.” Anāthapiṇḍada inquired: “What are the nine nonlearners?” The Buddha replied: “(1) Arhats who fully degenerate, (2) arhats intent on death, (3) arhats guarding the path, (4) arhats who are steadfast, (5) arhats who enter realization, (6) arhats who are immutable, (7) arhats who do not fully degenerate, (8) arhats liberated by wisdom, (9) arhats liberated from both aspects. These are the nine nonlearners.”[1678]

Those who exhaust up to eight parts of the summit of existence enter the state of an arhat. The ninth uninterrupted path is also vajra-like concentration. (6:44)

THE ENTERER

phyir mi 'ong ba de nyid bsam gtan dang po'i rnam pa gcig las 'dod chags dang bral ba nas bzung ste srid pa'i rtse mo'i nyon mongs pa'i cha brgyad kyi bar du zad pa ni dgra bcom pa nyid la zhugs pa yin no/ / der ma zad srid rtse'i nyon mongs pa dgu pa spong ba'i bar chad med pa'i lam la gnas pa de yang dgra bcom la zhugs pa yin no/ / dgu pa'i bar chad med pa'i lam de ni rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin yin te/ / {sngar gyi lam thams cad kyi skal mnyam gyi rgyu rgyas pas bar chad med lam thams cad las nus pa che ba'i bar chad med lam yin pa'i phyir ro } khams gsum gyi phra rgyas 'joms par nus pa'i phyir dang*/ de ni mi mthun phyogs kyis gzhom par mi nus pa'i phyir ro/ /

When nonreturners are free from attachment except for one stage of the first absorption and exhaust up to eight parts of affliction of the summit of existence (bhavāgra), they enter the state of an arhat. Moreover, abiders in the uninterrupted path that abandons the ninth affliction of the summit of existence are enterers to the state of an arhat. The ninth uninterrupted path (anantaryapatha) is also vajra-like concentration. {It is an uninterrupted path possessing greater potency than all other uninterrupted paths, since all earlier paths together act as its homogeneous cause.} It is capable of annihilating the negative tendencies of the three realms, and its opposing factors cannot destroy it.

rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin de yang sa'i sgo nas dbye na dgu ste/ bsam gtan gyi sa drug dang*/ gzugs med dang po gsum la brten pa'i phyir ro/ / dmigs pa'i sgo nas dbye na bzhi ste/ bden bzhi la dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ / rnam pa'i sgo nas dbye na bcu drug ste/ bden bzhi'i mi rtag pa la sogs pa rnam par byed pa'i phyir ro/ / sa dang dmigs pa dang rnam pa gsum char gyis dbye na ni rnam pa shin tu mang ste/ mi lcogs med la brten pa'i rdo rje lta bu de nyid 'og sa'i zag bcas la mi dmigs kyi srid rtse kho na'i sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung la dmigs pa'i rjes shes phyogs kyi rnam pa brgyad yin te srid rtse'i sdug bsngal la mi rtag pa la sogs pa rjes su shes pa'i rnam pa bzhi dang*/ kun 'byung la rgyu la sogs pa rjes su shes pa'i rnam pa bzhi yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'gog pa'i bden pa la dmigs pa ni sum cu rtsa drug yin te/ sa thams cad kyi 'gog pa la dmigs pa srid pas 'dod pa'i 'gog pa la dmigs pa'i chos shes bzhi dang sa gong ma brgyad kyi 'gog pa la dmigs pa'i rjes shes bzhi tshan brgyad yin pa'i phyir ro/ / lam la dmigs pa ni rnam pa brgyad yin te/ 'dod pa'i lam la dmigs pa'i chos shes bzhi dang*/ gong ma'i lam spyi la dmigs pa'i rjes shes bzhi yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar na bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs kyis bsdus pa'i rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin ni lnga bcu rtsa gnyis yin no/ / de bzhin dus lhag ma lnga la brten pa'ang shes par bya'o/ / gzugs med dang po gsum gyis bsdus pa ni rim pa bzhin du nyi shu rtsa brgyad dang rtsa bzhi dang nyi shu yin te/ de dag ni 'dod pa'i lam dngos 'og ma'i 'gog pa la'ang mi dmigs pa'i phyir dang lam ni phan tshun rgyu yin pas/ sa drug sa dgu'i lam ni de'i/ / spyod yul can gyi yul yin no zhes 'byung bas 'og ma gzugs khams pa'i gnyen po lam spyi la dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar na bsam gtan sa drug gis bsdus pa la sum brgya bcu gnyis dang*/ gzugs med dang po gsum la bdun cu rtsa gnyis te bsdoms pas sum brgya brgyad cu rtsa bzhi 'gyur la/ de dag rigs drug dang dbang po gsum gyis bsgyur na drug stong dgu brgya bcu gnyis su 'gyur ro/ /

If vajra-like concentration is classified by level, there are nine, since it depends on (1–6) the six levels of absorption and (7–9) the first three formless-realm levels. If classified by focal object, there are four: focusing on the four truths. If classified by aspect, there are sixteen: the aspects of the four truths such as impermanence. If classified by the components of the levels, focal object, and aspect, there are very many types. Vajra-like concentration dependent on unrestricted access concentration does not focus on contaminated lower levels. But there are eight types of subsequent knowledge focusing on the truths of suffering and origin of the summit of existence alone: (1–4) four types of subsequent knowledge of impermanence and so on in relation to the truth of suffering and (5–8) four types of subsequent knowledge of cause and so forth in relation to the truth of origin of the summit of existence. There are thirty-six focusing on the truth of cessation, [550] since they can focus on cessation on all levels: (1–4) four types of Dharma knowledge focusing on the truth of cessation of the desire realm and (5–36) eight times four types of subsequent knowledge focusing on the truth of cessation of the eight higher levels. There are eight types focusing on the truth of path: (1–4) four types of Dharma knowledge focusing on the truth of path of the desire realm and (5–8) four types of subsequent knowledge focusing in general on the higher paths. Thus there are fifty-two vajra-like concentrations subsumed by access concentration to the first absorption. Those dependent on the five remaining levels should also be understood in this way. Vajra-like concentrations subsumed by the first three formless-realm states are, respectively, twenty-eight, twenty-four, and twenty in number. They don’t focus on the actual path of the desire realm and lower cessation but focus on the general path that is the antidote of the lower form realm. As the Abhidharmakośa observes, “[They are] objects of those that possess that object dependent on six levels and nine levels” (5:15bc). Thus, in total, there are 384, with 312 subsumed by the six levels of absorption and 72 by the first three formless realms. When those are multiplied by the six lineages and three faculties, there are 6,912.[1679]

chos mngon pa ba gang dag lam gyi bden pa'ang 'gog pa'i bden pa dang 'dra bar sa re re la dmigs par 'dod pa ltar na gong ma'i lam spyi la dmigs pa'i rjes shes bzhi mi 'byung bas sa dgu'i lam bden la dmigs pa'i chos shes bzhi dang rjes shes sum cu rtsa gnyis te bsam gtan sa drug po re re la brgyad cu brgyad cu ste/ bsdoms pas bzhi brgya brgyad cu dang*/ gzugs med dang po gsum la rang sa dang gong sa'i lam bden la dmigs pa bcu gnyis dang brgyad dang bzhi bsnan pas go rim bzhin du bzhi bcu dang sum cu rtsa gnyis dang nyi shu rtsa bzhi yin pas dgu bcu rtsa drug tu 'gyur bas thams cad bsdoms na lnga brgya bdun cu rtsa drug tu 'gyur la/ de dag snga ma ltar rigs dang dbang po'i bye brag gis drug 'gyur dang sum 'gyur du bsgyur na rdo rje lta bu khri sum brgya dang drug cu rtsa brgyad du 'gyur ro zhes shes par bya'o/ / rdo rje lta bu'i dmigs pa sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung ni srid pa'i rtse mo pa kho na yin la 'gog lam ni spang bya'i dbang gis sa dgu char gyi yin no/ / zhes bya ba ni grub pa'i mtha' las yin te/ bsgom pa'i lam la 'gog pa'am/ / lam la chos shes gang yin de/ / khams gsum gyi ni gnyen po yin zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

Ābhidharmikas assert that vajra-like concentration focuses on each level, as it is similar to the truth of path and the truth of cessation. Therefore there are four Dharma knowledges and thirty-two subsequent knowledges focusing on the truth of path of the nine levels, since four types of subsequent knowledge focusing on the general path of higher realms do not arise. Thus there are eighty each focusing on the six levels of absorption, and in total there are 480. By adding the twelve, eight, and four focusing on the truth of path of the first three formless realms, its own level, and higher level, they are, respectively, forty, thirty-two, and twenty-four, making ninety-six. Thus, in total, there are 576. If multiplied six times and three times, due to specific lineage and faculty, as before, then vajra-like concentrations should be understood to number 10,368.[1680] The statement “The truths of suffering and origin that are focal objects of vajra-like concentration, belong to the summit of existence alone. The truths of cessation and path are components of the nine levels due to the power of being objects to be abandoned” should be recognized as a philosophical assertion. As the Abhidharmakośa states, “On the path of meditation, Dharma knowledge regarding cessation or path is an antidote to the three realms” (7:9abc).
gnyis pa gnas pa ni
THE ABIDER
de zad thob dang zad pa shes/ / de tshe de mi slob dgra bcom/ /
When elimination is obtained and knowledge of elimination arises, they are called nonlearners and arhats. (6:45ab)

srid rtse'i sgom spang rnam pa dgu po de{ rdor ting gis} zad pa'i thob pa dang de zad pa shes pa'i rnam grol gyi lam lhan cig tu skye ste/{ 'di ni rnam grol tha ma yin no/ / zad pa shes pa skyes pa} de'i tshe 'phags pa de mi slob pa zhes kyang bya/ dgra bcom pa'i 'bras bu la gnas pa zhes kyang bya ste/ 'bras bu thob par bya ba'i phyir bslab pa gsum la slob mi dgos pa'i phyir dang*/ rang don rdzogs nas gzhan gyi don byed pa dang*/ so so'i skye bo dang slob pa thams cad kyis mchod par 'os pa'i phyir dang*/ khams gsum gyi nyon mongs pa thams cad pham par byas pa'i phyir ro/ / {dgra bcom la dbye na dus kyi rnam grol ni rigs kyis lnga'o/ / dbang pos gsum mo/ / rten gyis nyer dgu ste spyir bzhi brgya dang sum cu rtsa bdun no/ / dus mi sbyor ni rigs kyis dbyer med la/ dbang po dang rten gyis bsgyur bas brgyad cu gya bdun no/ / shes rab kyis rnam grol la'ang dbang pos gsum/ rigs kyis drug /rten gyis nyer dgu ste/ spyir lnga brgya dang nyi shu rtsa gnyis so/ / gnyis ka'i cha las rnam grol yang de bzhin no }

When elimination is obtained (kṣayāptyā) of the nine stages to be abandoned by the path of meditation of the summit of existence {through vajra-like concentration}, and the liberated path that is knowledge of elimination (kṣayajñāna) arises simultaneously, {it is final liberation}. When {knowledge of elimination arises}, such āryas are called nonlearners (aśaikṣa). They are also called “those who abide in the result of an arhat” because they no longer need to train in the three higher trainings [551] to obtain that result. Having fulfilled their own purpose, they can act for the purpose of others, they are worthy of receiving offerings from ordinary beings and all learners, and they have defeated all afflictions of the three realms. {If arhats are classified, then in general arhats liberated according to circumstances number 437,[1681] since there are five by lineage, three by intellectual faculty, and twenty-nine by basis. Arhats liberated regardless of circumstances number 87, since they have no classification by lineage but are classified by intellectual faculty and basis. Arhats liberated by wisdom number 522,[1682] since there are three by faculty, six by lineage, and twenty-nine by basis. Arhats liberated from both aspects are similar to that.}

sngar bshad pa'i 'phags pa gzhan bdun ni slob pa yin te/ zag pa zad par bya ba'i phyir bslab pa gsum la rtag tu slob pa'i phyir ro/ / so so'i skye bo rnams ni slob pa ma yin te/ bden pa yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin mi shes pas{ shes rab kyi bslab pa med pa'i} phyir dang*/ bslab pa{ gzhan gnyis kyang} gtong ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir kun du rgyu zhi byed kyis zhus pa'i mdo las/ go'u ta ma slob pa zhes brjod pa ci'i phyir slob pa slob pa zhes bya zhe na/ zhi byed bslab pa la slob cing bslab pa la slob pas na de'i phyir slob pa zhes bya'o zhes lan gnyis su bzlas te gsungs so/ / {'phags pa ni slob pa cung zad gtong yang thams cad gtong ba mi srid de 'phags pa mnyam par ma bzhag kyang slob pa'i bsam pa mi 'dor ba'i sgo nas der brjod de mgron po lam na 'dug pa bzhin no yang slob pa gsum gyi thob pa dang yang ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / slob pa'i chos ni mthong sgom mo/ / mi slob pa'i chos ni mi slob lam mo }

The other seven āryas that were previously explained are learners because they continuously train in the three higher trainings to exhaust the contaminants. Ordinary beings are not learners; {they do not possess the higher training in wisdom} since they do not know the four truths correctly as they are, and they relinquish {the other two} higher trainings. Therefore the Sūtra Requested by the Wandering Ascetic Śāntikara states: “Gautama, why are learners called ‘learners who are learners’?” Gautama replied: “Śāntikara, they learn the higher trainings, and by learning the higher trainings, therefore they are called learners.”[1683] Gautama repeats his answer twice. {Āryas may relinquish some aspects of higher training, but it is impossible for them to relinquish all higher training. This is said because āryas who are not in equipoise do not discard the higher trainings, just as a traveler who rests by the road is still a traveler. Moreover, they obtain and possess the three higher trainings. The Dharmas in which one trains are the paths of seeing and meditation. The object in which one does not train is the path of no more learning.}

mya ngan las 'das pa ni slob mi slob gnyis ka ma yin te/ de ni so sor brtags 'gog yin na so so'i skye bo dang slob mi slob thams cad la ci rigs par ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar na nyan thos 'phags{ pa mthar gyis} pa'i gang zag ni zung bzhi ya brgyad kho na yin la/ de dag kyang ming gis brgyad yin gyi rdzas su ni mthar gyis pa la zhugs pa dang po dang 'bras bu la gnas pa bzhi dang lnga yin te/ bzhugs pa phyi ma gsum ni 'bras bu la gnas pa dang po gsum la btags pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / chags bral sngon 'gro la phyir mi 'ong khyad par can nyid dgra bcom la bzhugs pa'ang yin la zhugs pa snga ma gsum dang 'bras gnas bzhi ste bdun du 'gyur ro/ / ming gis brgyad du rnam par bzhag pa'ang mthar gyis thob pa'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi 'dod chags dang bral ba sngon du 'gro ba la ni ma yin te/ phal cher dang 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba bden pa mngon rtogs skad cig bco lnga dang bcu drug pa thob pa ni rim pa ltar phyir 'ong dang phyir mi 'ong la zhugs gnas kho na yin gyi rgyun zhugs dang phyir 'ong zhugs gnas ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Nirvāṇa is neither a learner nor a nonlearner, because nirvāṇa is analytical cessation and it is possessed by all ordinary beings, learners, and nonlearners in some sense. Thus a person who is a śrāvaka ārya {and a serial abandoner} is one part of the eight that constitute the four pairs alone. They are eight by name but five by substance — an enterer who is a serial abandoner and four abiders in the result — because the last three enterers are designated as the first three abiders in the result. Since the special nonreturner previously freed from attachment is also an enterer to the state of an arhat, there are seven: the first three enterers and the four abiders in the result. Though in principle there are eight in name, this is from the perspective of obtaining serial abandonment and not being previously freed from attachment. Those who obtain, respectively, fifteen moments and the sixteenth moment of realization of the four truths free of attachment to the desire realm are enterers and abiders to once return and nonreturn alone, and not enterers and abiders to stream entry and once return. [552]
29. Specific Attributes of Ārya Beings
gsum pa khyad par gyi chos 'chad pa
EXPLAINING SPECIAL ATTRIBUTES

['di] na sa dang lam gyi khyad par dang*/ zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa'i khyad par dang*/ 'bras bu'i rnam par bzhag pa'i khyad par dang*/ chos kyi 'khor lo'i khyad par dang*/ khams dang dbye ba'i khyad par dang*/ rigs dang nyams pa'i khyad par dang*/ dbang po 'pho ba'i khyad par bdun las

This has seven headings: (1) specific level and path, (2) specific elimination and nonarising, (3) specific principle of result, (4) the wheel of Dharma, (5) specific realm and classification, (6) specific type and degeneration, and (7) specific upgrade of intellectual faculty.
dang po [sa dang lam gyi khyad par] ni
Specific level and path
gal te 'phags pa dag sa dang sa las 'dod chags dang bral na gnyen po gang gis sa gang las 'dod chags dang 'bral zhe na/
Question: If āryas are free from attachment to various levels, what antidote frees them from attachment to what level?
'jig rten 'das kyis srid rtse las/ / chags 'bral gzhan las rnam pa gnyis/ / 45
One is freed from attachment to the summit of existence by the transcendent path and from other levels by both. (6:45cd)

'di ltar sgom pa'i lam ni 'jig rten dang de las 'das pa gnyis las 'jig rten las 'das pa'i{ kho na} lam gyis srid pa'i rtse mo las 'dod chags dang bral bar 'gyur gyi 'og sa dman zhing gong ma med la rang nyid gnyen por mi 'gyur bas{ te de yi nyon mongs rgyas par 'gyur bas} 'jig rten pas ni ma yin te/ gal te yin na dang po nas grol bar thal ba'i phyir ro/ / srid rtse las gzhan pa'i sa{ brgyad po} thams cad las ni 'jig rten dang de las 'das pa'i lam rnam pa gnyis kyis ci rigs par 'dod chags dang bral bar 'gyur te/ 'jig rten pa ni gong ma'i nyer bsdogs dang*/ 'jig rten las 'das pa ni bden pa'i rnam pa can rang sa dang 'og sa'i lam mthong zin sgom pa'o/

Reply: The path of meditation has two types — mundane and transcendent — but one is freed from attachment (vairāgya) to the summit of existence (bhavāgra) by the transcendent (lokottara) path {alone}. Since lower levels are inferior to the summit of existence, there are no levels higher than it. It does not act as an antidote to itself {since it increases the afflictions of the summit of existence.} One is not freed from it by the mundane path because if one were, then it would follow that one would be free from the beginning. One is freed from any type of attachment to {the eight} levels other than the summit of existence by both mundane and transcendent paths because the mundane path cultivates access concentration to higher levels and the transcendent path cultivates minds that possess the aspect of truth, having seen the paths of one’s level or lower level.
'jig rten pa yis chags bral ba'i/ / 'phags la bral ba'i thob rnam gnyis/ / kha cig 'jig rten 'das kyis kyang / / btang la nyon mongs mi ldan phyir/ / 46
An ārya freed from attachment by the mundane path obtains freedom by both types. One says: The transcendent path also produces both because they relinquish yet do not possess affliction. (6:46)

{bral thob kyi bye brag na/} zhi gnas spyad pa 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis 'dod chags dang bral ba'i 'phags pa la{ rnam pa re re zhing} bral ba'i thob pa ni 'jig rten pa dang 'jig rten pa las 'das pa rnam pa gnyis gnyis skye bas byis pa ltar spangs pa slar ldog{ de yang nyon mongs spong ba'i bya ba gcig yin pa'i phyir ro} par mi 'gyur ro/

One who mainly engages calm abiding {as a subset of those who obtain freedom from attachment}, who is an ārya freed from attachment (āryavairāgya) by the mundane (laukika) path, obtains freedom {from each aspect} by generating both types of path: mundane and transcendent. He does not need to eliminate these abandonments again, as childlike beings do. {Moreover, he is one with one affliction to be abandoned.}

sde pa kha cig na re 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam gyis kyang bral ba'i thob pa zag bcas dang zag med gnyis ka 'dren{ par snga ma dang 'dra} te/ gal te des 'jig rten pa'i bral thob mi 'dren sngon 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam gyis ci yang med pa'i skye mched las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i phyir mi 'ong dbang po rtul po zhig bsam gtan gyi sems la brten nas dbang po rnon por 'pho ba na lam snga ma{ zad par} btang ba'i phyir dang*/ 'jig rten pa'i bral thob kyang med pa'i phyir nam mkha' mtha' yas la sogs pa gong ma'i{ sa brgyad kyi} nyon mongs pa dang ldan par 'gyur te/{ de dag gis bral thob zag med btang la zag bcas med pa'i phyir/ des na/} de 'dra ba'i 'phags pa des 'jig rten las 'das pa'i bral thob btang ba la gong ma'i nyon mongs pa mi ldan pa'i phyir 'jig rten pa'i bral ba'i thob pa yod do zhes zer ro/ /

One school says: The transcendent (lokottara) path {as before} also produces both the contaminated and uncontaminated obtainment of freedom from attachment. If it did not produce the obtainment of freedom from mundane states, then nonreturners who are of dull faculty and free of attachment to the base of nothingness through the transcendent path would {completely} relinquish the former path when they upgraded their intellectual faculty in dependence on the mind of the absorptions. And even though they obtained freedom from mundane states, they would come to possess affliction of higher {level}, such as infinite space, {because in relinquishing the obtainment of uncontaminated freedom, they would not have contaminated freedom either. Therefore} because they relinquish obtainment of transcendent freedom, such āryas obtain mundane freedom yet do not possess higher affliction.
srid rtse'i phyed las rnam grol dang / / gong du skyes pa bzhin mi ldan/ / zag med mi lcogs med pa yis/ / thams cad las ni 'dod chags 'bral/ / 47

Those liberated from half the summit of existence and those born in higher absorptions do not possess them. Unrestricted access concentration to uncontaminated states is free from attachment to all nine levels. (6:47)
thal ba de ni mi 'gyur te/
Reply: That consequence does not occur,

de la zag med bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs mi lcogs pa med pa yis ni stobs che zhing{ sa gong dang} 'og sa las kyang 'dod chags dang 'bral nus pas sa dgu po thams cad las 'dod chags 'bral bar 'gyur ro/ / {'og sa ste 'dod pa la 'di zag bcas dang zag med gnyis las gzhan pa'i gnyen po med la/ sa gzhan gyi la 'di las gzhan yang yod do } gal te nyer bsdogs la brten nas 'og sa las 'dod chags dang 'bral na rnam grol gyi lam tha ma de thams cad du nyer bsdogs kyi ngo bor skye'am 'on te dngos gzhi'i ngo bor skye zhe na/

Reply: Unrestricted access concentration to the uncontaminated first absorption is free from attachment to all nine levels, since it has great strength and is capable of freeing one from attachment to {one’s own, higher, and} lower levels. {Since there is no antidote to lower desire-realm affliction other than either contaminated or uncontaminated antidotes, so too there are no other antidotes to afflictions of other levels.} Question: If they are freed from attachment to lower levels in dependence on access concentration, do all final liberated paths arise with the essential nature of access concentration, or do they arise with the essential nature of the actual bases?
sa gsum rgyal la bsam gtan nam/ / nyer bsdogs las mtha'i rnam grol lam/ / gong ma'i nyer bsdogs las min 'phags/ / brgyad kyis rang gong sa las rgyal/ / 48

For those who conquer three levels, the final liberated paths arise due to absorption or access concentration. Higher levels do not give rise to it due to access concentration. Āryas conquer that or higher due to eight. (6:48)

gang zhig{ skye ba'i sa dgu la} 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang po dang gnyis pa ste sa gsum gyi nyon mongs pa las nyer bsdogs kyis rgyal ba la ni gang zag de gal te dbang po rnon po yin na bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi las rnam grol gyi lam tha ma skye ste/ nyer bsdogs kyi tshor ba btang snyoms de dngos gzhi'i yid bde dang bde bar spo nus pa'i{ phyir dang nyer bsdogs la dga' ba chung ba'i} phyir ro/ / 'on te dbang po rtul po yin na ni nyer bsdogs las mtha'i rnam grol gyi lam dgu pa skye'i dngos gzhi las ni ma yin te/ bsam gtan gsum na ni nyer bsdogs dang dngos gzhi tshor ba tha dad pas tshor ba spo bar mi nus pa'i{ phyir dang btang snyoms kyi rjes su bde ba dang yid bde skye dka' ba'i} phyir ro/ / sa gsum gyi gong ma bsam gtan gsum pa la sogs pa las 'dod chags dang 'bral ba bzhi pa yan chad kyis ni nyer bsdogs las rnam grol tha ma skye ba min gyi 'on kyang sa de dag gi dngos gzhi las skye ste/ nyer bsdogs dang dngos gzhi tshor ba btang snyoms su tha dad med pa'i phyir rtsol ba la ma ltos par dngos gzhi skye ba'i phyir ro/{/de yang sngar 'dod chags dang bral ba'i sa la gus pa'i phyir ro/ / 'on kyang 'og sa'i dngos gzhi la ma yin te/ de'i nyer bsdogs kyis 'dod chags dang bral zin pas so/}

There are those who conquer the afflictions of three levels — the desire realm, first absorption, and second absorption {from the nine levels where they arise} — through access concentration. If that being is of sharp faculty, then the final liberated path arises from the actual basis of absorption, because they are capable of changing the feeling of equanimity of access concentration to mental satisfaction and pleasure of the actual basis, {and there is little joy in the state of access concentration}. Or, if that being possesses dull intellectual faculty, the nine final liberated paths arise due to access concentration (sāmanataka) and not due to the actual basis; they cannot change feelings, since the feeling of access concentration and the feeling of the actual basis are different in the three absorptions {and it is difficult for pleasure or mental satisfaction to arise after equanimity}. [554] The fourth level and above, which are higher than the third level and free from attachment to the third absorption, do not give rise to the final liberated path due to access concentration but due to the actual bases of those absorptions. The feeling of equanimity of access concentration and the actual basis are not different, [because] the actual basis is not generated from exertion {and because they respect the former level that is free from attachment. However, they do not depend on the actual basis of lower level, because they maintain freedom from attachment through the access concentration to that absorption.}
zag med kyi sa dang pos 'dod chags dang bral ba'i tshul bshad zin nas lhag ma bshad pa ni
HAVING EXPLAINED HOW ONE IS FREED FROM ATTACHMENT BY THE FIRST UNCONTAMINATED LEVEL, NOW THE REST ARE EXPLAINED

'phags pa ste zag med kyis lhag ma brgyad kyis ni rang sa dang gong sa'i nyon mongs pa las rgyal bar 'gyur gyi 'og sa las ni ma yin te/ nyer bsdogs kho nas rgyal zin pa'i phyir ro/ / de la 'phags pa brgyad ni bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs ma gtogs pa rnams te/ sa de dag gi bar chad med pa dang rnam grol gyi lam rnams ni mi rtag pa la sogs pa bden pa'i rnam pa can du skyes pa dag yin no/ / 'o na 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam bden pa'i dmigs rnam can yin na 'jig rten pa'i lam gang zhe na/

Āryas conquer affliction of that or higher level due to the eight remaining uncontaminated levels but not by lower level because they conquer due to access concentration alone. The eight āryas exclude those reliant on access concentration to the first absorption. The uninterrupted and liberated paths of those levels arise with the aspects of the four truths, such as impermanence. Question: If the transcendent path possesses, as its aspect and focal object, the four truths, what does the mundane path possess?
'jig rten pa yi rnam grol dang / / bar chad med lam go rims bzhin/ / zhi sogs rags sogs rnam pa can/ / gong dang 'og ma'i spyod yul can/ / 49
The mundane uninterrupted and liberated paths respectively engage coarse and refined aspects and so on and higher and lower object fields. (6:49)

'jig rten pa'i bar chad med pa'i lam ni go rim bzhin du gong sa las ltos nas mngon par 'du byed pa shin tu ches chen pos bsgrub par bya ba yin pas rags pa dang*/ sogs pa'i sgras gzung ba gnas ngan len shin tu ches mang bas mi mthun par gyur pas tha ba ngan pa dang*/ rtsig pas rtsig pa de nyid las nges par mi 'byung ba ltar sa de nyid kyis sa de nyid las nges par mi 'byung bas rtsig pa stug po lta bur lta ba'i rnam pa can dang 'og ma'i spyod yul can te sa 'og ma la dmigs pa yin no/ / rnam par grol ba'i lam ni go rim bzhin du snga ma las bzlog pa zhi ba dang*/ sogs pa gya nom pa dang*/ nges par 'byung ba'i rnam pa can dang*/ gong ma'i spyod yul can te sa gong ma la dmigs pa yin no/ /

Reply: Respectively, the mundane (laukika) uninterrupted path (anyaryapatha) engages coarse (udāra) aspects, since it is established by intense application (saṃskāra) reliant on higher level. This term “and so on” refers to rigid negativity established by intense dysfunction, and [distorted] view like a dense wall, since one definitely cannot get beyond a wall when obstructed by that wall nor get beyond an embankment when obstructed by that embankment. And it possesses lower object fields (gocara) since it focuses on lower levels. The liberated path engages refined (śānta) aspects since it counters the former. The term “and so on” refers to sublime qualities and definite emergence. It possesses higher object fields since it focuses on higher levels and so on.
gnyis pa ni
Specific elimination and nonarising
'o na zad pa shes pa'i 'jug thogs su shes pa gang skye zhe na/
Question: What knowledge arises at the conclusion of contaminated knowledge?
gal te mi g.yo'i zad shes las/ / mi skye'i blo gros gal te min/ / zad pa shes sam mi slob lta/ / de ni dgra bcom thams cad la/ / 50
If they are immutable arhats, awareness of nonarising arises from knowledge of elimination. If not, merely knowledge of elimination or the view of a nonlearner. That arises in all arhats. (6:50)

gal te dgra bcom pa dbang po rnon po mi g.yo ba'i chos can zhig yin na ni mi nyams pas zad pa shes pa las mi skye ba'i blo gros te shes pa skye la/ gal te mi g.yo ba'i chos can yin na ni zad pa shes pa las zad pa shes pa 'i rgyun tsam kho na'am/ yang na mi slob pa'i yang dag pa'i lta ba skye'i mi skye ba shes pa ni ma yin te/ nyon mongs pa skye ba'i skabs yod pas nyams pa srid pa'i phyir dang*/ mi skye ba shes pa las nyams pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / mi slob pa'i yang dag pa'i lta ba de ni dgra bcom pa thams cad la skye ste/ mi g.yo ba'i chos can la'ang res 'ga' mi skye ba shes pa las mi skye ba shes pa kho na dang*/ / res 'ga' mi slob pa'i yang dag pa'i lta ba skye ba'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: If they are immutable (akopya) arhats of sharp faculty, awareness of nonarising (anutpādamati) arises from the knowledge of elimination (kṣayajñāna), since it does not degenerate. If they are not immutable arhats, merely the continuum of knowledge of elimination arises from the knowledge of elimination. Or else correct view of a nonlearner (aśaikṣa) arises but not knowledge of nonarising, because it is possible that they degenerate since the opportunity for affliction to arise exists. Nonlearner correct view arises in all arhats because at times knowledge of nonarising arises from knowledge of nonarising alone in immutable arhats, and at times nonlearner correct view arises. [555]
gsum pa ni ['bras bu'i rnam par bzhag pa'i khyad par]
Specific principle of result
dge sbyong tshul ni dri med lam/ / 'bras bu 'dus byas 'dus ma byas/ / de dag brgyad cu rtsa dgu'o/ / grol lam zad pa rnams dang bcas/ / 51

The system of training in virtue is the stainless path. The result is either conditioned or unconditioned, and when classified, there are eighty-nine. There are liberated paths as well as complete cessations. (6:51)
gal te dge sbyong gi tshul gyi 'bras bu bzhi zhes brjod na dge sbyong ni gang*/ tshul ni gang*/ 'bras bu ni gang zhe na/
Question: If there are “four results” of the system of training in virtue, what trains in virtue? What is the system? What is the result?

dge sbyong ni nyon mongs pa ci rigs par gtan du zhi ba'i rgyud de/ 'phags pa'i gang zag yin la/ nyon mongs pa gtan du zhi bar byed pa'i thabs dge sbyong gi tshul ni dri ma med pa'i bar chad med lam ste rnam grol gyi lam ni dge sbyong gi tshul gyi 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir lung bar ma las/ ji ltar na dge sbyong du 'gyur zhe na/ 'dis sdig pa mi dge ba'i chos yang srid par kun nas nyon mongs pa can nad dang bcas shing rnam par smin pa sdug bsngal ba ma 'ongs pa'i skye ba nas 'chi ba'i bar rnams zhi bar byas pa ste/ 'di ltar na dge sbyong du 'gyur ro zhes gsungs pas zag med kyi lam yin gyi zag bcas kyis ni{ lci yang las grol yang nyes pa'i 'phro dang bcas pas} gtan du zhi bar byed pa ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / dge sbyong gi tshul de'i 'bras bu ni 'dus byas dang 'dus ma byas gnyis yin te de dag kyang dbye na re re la'ang brgyad cu rtsa dgu dgu'o/ /

Reply: That which trains in virtue is the mindstream in which all afflictions are continuously pacified; that is the ārya being. The system of training in virtue (śrāmaṇya) is the stainless (amala) uninterrupted path that is the way to continuously pacify affliction. The result of the system of training in virtue is the liberated path. Therefore it is said in the Medium-Length Discourses: How does one become someone who trains in virtue? One becomes someone who trains in virtue through pacifying the afflicted, negative, nonvirtuous phenomena of rebirth and illness and the maturational suffering that will arise from future birth up to future death.[1684] Therefore it is the uncontaminated path because the contaminated path does not continuously pacify; {it possesses a residue of fault even though it liberates from heavy and light karma}. The result (phala) of that system of training in virtue is either conditioned or unconditioned, and when classified there are eighty-nine each.
gang zhe na/
Question: What are they?

khams gsum gyi mthong spang las rnam par grol ba'i lam brgyad dang sgom spang dgu dgu brgyad cu rtsa gcig las rnam par grol ba'i lam brgyad cu rtsa gcig ste/ de ltar rnam grol gyi lam brgyad cu rtsa dgu dang*/ de dag gi bar chad med pa'i lam yang brgyad cu rtsa dgu dang*/ spang bya zad pa'i 'gog pa brgyad cu rtsa dgu rnams dang bcas pa ste/ de ltar na bar chad med pa'i lam brgyad cu rtsa dgu ni dge sbyong gi tshul yin la/ rnam par grol ba'i lam brgyad cu rtsa dgu ni dge sbyong gi tshul gyi 'bras bu 'dus byas dag yin te/ rgyu mthun rgyu dang 'dra ba'o zhes pa dang*/ gang gi stobs kyis gang skye ba/ / 'bras de skyes bu byed las skyes zhes 'byung bas bar chad med pa'i lam dang 'dra ba dang*/ de'i stobs kyis skye ba'i phyir bar chad med pa'i lam gyi rgyu mthun dang skyes bu byed pa'i 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / spang bya zad pa'i 'gog pa brgyad cu rtsa dgu ni dge sbyong tshul gyi 'bras bu 'dus ma byas dag yin te/ gang gi stobs kyis gang 'thob pa/ / de ni skyes bu byed pa'i 'bras zhes 'bras bu 'dus ma byas kyang bar chad med pa'i lam gyi skyes bu byed pa'i 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir ro/ /de dag bsdus nas mdo las dge sbyong tshul gyi 'bras bu bzhir bshad do/ / de'i phyir slob dpon 'phags pas kyang*/ dge sbyong gang zhe na/ nyon mongs pa zhi ba'i rgyud do/ / tshul gang zhe na/ lam snga ma'o/ / tshul gyi 'bras bu gang zhe na/ lam phyi ma dang 'dus ma byas so zhes bshad do/ / gal te de ltar 'bras bu rnam pa mang po yod na 'o na 'bras bu bzhir ji ltar gzhag ce na/

Reply: There are eighty-nine liberated paths (muktimārga), since there are (1–8) eight paths liberated from objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing of the three realms, and (9–89) eighty-one paths liberated from the nine times nine objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, their eighty-nine uninterrupted paths, as well as the eighty-nine complete cessations of objects to be abandoned. Thus the eighty-nine uninterrupted paths are the system of training in virtue, and the eighty-nine liberated paths are the conditioned results of the system of training in virtue. They are similar to the uninterrupted path, for as the Abhidharmakośa explains, “Natural outflow is similar to its cause” (2:57c), and, “Any result arising due to the power of its cause is a result arisen from conscious effort” (2:58ab). Therefore, because they arise due to its power, they are results of natural outflow and results of conscious effort. The eighty-nine complete cessations of objects to be abandoned are the unconditioned results of the system of training in virtue because even unconditioned results are results of conscious effort of the uninterrupted path. As it is said, “Anything obtained by the power of any action is the result of conscious effort.” In summary, the sūtras explain four results of the system of training in virtue.[1685] Therefore Master Ārya explains: What trains in virtue? The mindstream in which affliction is pacified. What is the system? The five paths. What is the result of that system? The latter path and the unconditioned.[1686] Question: Why are just four results posited if in fact there are many results?
'bras bu bzhir rnams gzhag pa ni/ / rgyu lnga dag ni srid phyir ro/ / 'bras la sngon lam btang ba dang / / gzhan thob pa dang zad bsdoms dang / / 52
Results are posited as four because five reasons exist: relinquishing former paths for each result, obtaining a different path, attaining combined elimination, (6:52)

'bras bu mang mod kyi de dag mdo las 'bras bu bzhir rnam par bzhag pa ni rgyu mtshan rnam pa lnga dag srid pa'i phyir ro/ / lnga gang zhe na/ rgyun zhugs la sogs pa'i 'bras bu re rer 'jog pa la ni sngon gyi zhugs pa'i lam snga ma btang ba dang*/ de las gzhan pa'i 'bras bu la gnas pa'i lam thob pa dang*/ spang bya zad pa bsdoms pa'i thob pa gcig rnyed pa dang*/

Reply: Indeed, there are many results. But results are posited as four in the sūtras because five reasons exist (saṃbhava). Question: What are those five? Reply: (1) Relinquishing the former path of entry for each result established such as stream entry, [556] (2) obtaining the path of an abider as a result that is different from it, (3) attaining a single obtainment of the combined elimination (kṣayasaṃkala) of objects to be abandoned,
shes pa brgyad tshan thob pa dang / / rnam pa bcu drug thob pa'o/ / 'jig rten pa yis thob 'bras ni/ / bsres dang zad med thob 'dzin phyir/ / 53

obtaining the eight divisions of knowledge, and obtaining all sixteen aspects. Two results are obtained by the mundane path because it is through mixing and they bear a single uncontaminated obtainment. (6:53)

sdug bsngal la chos shes pa la sogs pa chos shes pa bzhi dang sdug bsngal la rjes su shes pa la sogs pa rjes su shes pa bzhi ste/ shes pa brgyad tshan thob pa{ ste cig car du ldan pa} dang*/ mi rtag pa la sogs pa ye shes kyi rnam pa bcu drug tshang bar thob pa'o/ /

(4) {simultaneously} obtaining the eight divisions of knowledge — the four Dharma knowledges such as Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering and the four subsequent knowledges such as the subsequent knowledge of the truth of suffering — and (5) obtaining all sixteen aspects of transcendent wisdom such as impermanence.

{de yang zad pa sdom pa ni spangs pa so so ba rnams btang nas thams cad sdom pa'i bral thob zag med gcig rnyed pa ste/ 'bras bu dang po la mthong spang gi zad pa sdom pa gcig rnyed pa dang*/ gnyis pa la mthong spang dang 'dod pa'i sgom spang drug zad pa sdom pa la sogs pa'o }

{Further, “combined elimination” is obtaining uncontaminated freedom that is combined elimination through relinquishing individual objects of abandonment. The first result is attaining combined elimination of objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing; the second is elimination of objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing along with six objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation and so on.}

de la mthong lam skad cig ma bco lnga pa man chad{ zhugs pa dang po} la ni rgyu mtshan lnga ga med pa'i phyir dang zhugs pa phyi ma gsum la ni rgyu mtshan phyi ma gnyis yod kyang snga ma gsum med pa'i phyir 'bras bur ma bshad do zhes bye brag tu smra ba 'dod do/

The {first enterer} on or before the fifteenth moment of the path of seeing is not said to be a result, because the five reasons do not apply to him. The latter three enterers are not results, because the last three reasons do not apply to them even though the first two do apply. This is asserted by Vaibhāṣikas.

{ nyan thos kyi sa las ni/ nyon mongs pa rnam pa bzhi spangs pa'i phyir/ gnyen po 'bras bu bzhi bzhag ste/ nyon mongs pa ngan song du 'gro bar 'gyur ba'i rgyu spangs pa'i phyir rgyun zhugs kyi 'bras bu bzhag go /lha dang mi'i srid pas bsdus pa'i skye ba'i rgyun gyi nyon mongs spangs pa'i phyir lan cig phyir 'ong gi 'bras bu bzhag go /'dod par skye zhing phyir 'ong ba'i nyon mongs pa spangs shing lha'i srid pa kho na mngon par bsgrub pa'i phyir phyir mi 'ong gi 'bras bu bzhag go /khams gsum gyi srid par skye ba'i nyon mongs pa thams cad zad par spangs pa'i phyir dgra bcom pa'i 'bras bu bzhag go /zhes 'byung ngo*/ /}

{Śrāvaka Levels declares: Because they abandon the four types of affliction, they are posited as the four results of the antidote. Because it abandons afflictions that are the cause of proceeding to lower rebirths, it is posited as the result of stream entry. Because it abandons afflictions within the stream of birth subsumed by god and human existence, it is posited as the result of once return. Because it abandons birth in the desire realm and the affliction of once return and actually establishes divine intermediate beings alone, it is posited as the result of nonreturn. Because it completely abandons all affliction pertaining to birth existence in the three realms, it is posited as the result of an arhat.}[1687]

kha cig 'bras bu dang po gnyis la gnas pa la'ang spangs pa bsdoms pa med de/ bral ba'i thob pa zag med dang*/ / srid rtse nyams par byas pa dang*/ / rgyu gnyis kun tu bcom pa'i phyir/ / yongs shes khams las 'das pa las zhes khams las 'das pa las spangs pa sdom par bshad pa la khams las 'das pa med pa'i phyir ro zhes 'chad pa ni ma yin te/ lung de ni yongs shes su 'jog pa'i rgyu mtshan yin pa'i phyir dang*/ 'grel pa las/ spangs pa bsdoms pa ni thams cad kyi thob pa gcig rnyed pa'i phyir ro zhes bya ba dang*/ rgyu lnga po de dag ni 'bras bu re re la yod do zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te zag med kyi lam kho na dge sbyong gi tshul yin na chags bral sngon 'gros 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis 'bras bu bar pa gnyis thob pa srid pas de dag ji ltar dge sbyong gi tshul gyi 'bras bu yin zhe na/

Some say: Those abiding in the first two results do not have combined abandonment because they do not transcend the realms. For transcending the realms is explained as combined abandonment in the Abhidharmakośa when it states, “It is perfect knowledge because it is the uncontaminated obtainment of freedom, it discards the summit of existence, it completely destroys the two causes, and it transcends the three realms” (5:68). Reply: This is not so. This passage teaches the reason for positing that as perfect knowledge, and the Autocommentary notes: Combined abandonment is acquiring the single obtainment of everything.[1688] And: These five causes exist for each result.[1689] Question: If the uncontaminated path alone is the system of training in virtue, then how would the two intermediate results be results of the system of training in virtue? Isn’t it possible for āryas previously freed from attachment to obtain the two intermediate results by the mundane path?

Reply: The two intermediate ārya results obtained by the mundane (laukikāptaphala) path are the result of training in virtue {because the result of both paths is attained as a single result of each obtainment of abandonment,} because they obtain them through mixing (miśrā) abandonments of the contaminated path of meditation and the uncontaminated path of seeing, and because they bear (dhāraṇa) a single uncontaminated obtainment (anāsravaprāpti) subsumed by the two intermediate results. {By the power of the uncontaminated obtainment of freedom, one does not die even though one degenerates. Since the Abhidharmakośa states, “An ārya freed from attachment by the mundane path obtains freedom by both types” (6:46ab), [557] it is not contradictory to say that present obtainment of uncontaminated states arisen due to the mundane path, and future obtainment due to the power of the eightfold noble path, are conditioned states that are results of the system of training in virtue.}

de nyid kyi phyir mdo las/ lan cig phyir 'ong ba'i 'bras bu gang zhe na/ kun du sbyor ba gsum spangs pa dang 'dod chags dang zhe sdang dang gti mug rnams bsrabs pa gang yin pa de yin no/ / phyir mi 'ong ba'i 'bras bu gang zhe na/ kun du sbyor ba tha ma'i cha dang mthun pa lnga spangs pa gang yin pa de yin no zhes gsungs te/ gal te spangs pa 'dren mar 'jug pa ma yin na 'bras bu de dag tu gzhag par mi nus te/ kun sbyor gsum dang kun sbyor tha ma'i cha mthun lnga'i phyogs gcig kun sbyor gsum po mthong lam gyis spangs pa'i phyir ro/ / des na spangs pa 'dren mar 'jug pa de skad du gsungs so/ / de'i phyir 'jig rten pa yis chags bral ba'i/ / 'phags la bral ba'i thob rnam gnyis/ / zhes pas bral thob zag med de'i stobs kyis 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis thob pa'i spangs pa de 'dzin par byed pas yongs su nyams kyang mi 'chi ste/ 'bras las nyams pa 'chi ba med/ / ces 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

Therefore a sūtra states: What is the result of once return? It is the abandonment of the three fetters, reducing attachment, aversion, and delusion. What is the result of nonreturn? It is the abandonment of five fetters and the factors associated with inferior states.[1690] If those abandonments do not merge, one cannot posit those results because the path of seeing abandons the three fetters through combining the three fetters and five factors associated with inferior states. Therefore abandonments are said to merge. Because the Abhidharmakośa observes, “An ārya freed from attachment by the mundane path obtains freedom by both types” (6:46ab),[1691] then by the power of uncontaminated obtainment of freedom, one does not die even though one degenerates; one obtains that by the mundane path and maintains it. Thus the Abhidharmakośa states, “Those who degenerate from their result do not die” (6:60a).
chos kyi 'khor lo'i khyad par/
The wheel of Dharma
bzhi pa dge sbyong gi tshul du bshad pa
EXPLAINING THE SYSTEM OF TRAINING IN VIRTUE
de nyid tshangs tshul tshangs pa yi/ / 'khor lo tshangs pas bskor phyir ro/ / chos kyi 'khor lo mthong ba'i lam/ / myur bar 'gro sogs rtsibs sogs kyis/ / 54

Just that is purity and the system. It is the wheel of purity turned by the pure. The wheel of Dharma is the path of seeing because it proceeds quickly and so on. It is like the spokes and so forth. (6:54)

bar chad med pa'i lam zag med rnam grol 'dus byas dang bcas pa gang yin pa de nyid ni sdig pa mi dge ba'i chos rnam pa du ma spangs pas tshangs pa dang*/ nyon mongs pa spong ba'i zag med kyi lam yin pas tshangs pa'i tshul yang yin te/ brgya byin gyi mdo las/ bcom ldan 'das de ni tshangs pa zhes kyang bya/ zhi ba dang*/ bsil bar gyur pa zhes kyang bya'o zhes kyang gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / des na tshangs pa dang*/ zhi ba dang*/ bsil bar gyur pa zhes bya ba ni bcom ldan 'das yin te/ tshangs pa'i tshul zag med kyi lam bla na med pa dang ldan pa'i phyir dang*/ nyon mongs pa tshangs pa dang zhi ba dang bsil ba'i phyir ro/ / tshul ni nyon mongs pa spong ba de'i thabs zag med kyi lam yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de ni tshangs pa'i 'khor lo'ang yin te/ 'khor lo dang 'dra ba'i phyir dang tshangs pa bcom ldan 'das kyis bskor ba'i phyir ro/ /

Just that uninterrupted path, along with uncontaminated liberation and its conditioned states, is purity (brāmaṇya), due to abandoning many negative nonvirtuous phenomena. It is also the system of purifying, since it is the uncontaminated path that abandons afflictions. The Indra Sūtra declares: The Bhagavan is called pure, peaceful, and also one who has become cool.[1692] The one who is called “pure,” “peaceful,” and “one who has become cool” is the Bhagavan, because he possesses the unsurpassed, uncontaminated path that is the system of purifying, and he has purified, pacified, and cooled affliction. The method that is the system of abandoning affliction is the uncontaminated path. That is also the wheel of purity (brahmacakra), because it is similar to a wheel and it is turned by the pure (brahmavartana) Bhagavan.

de la chos kyi 'khor lo ni mthong ba'i lam de nyid yin te/ myur bar 'gro ba dang*/ sogs pas bsdus pa 'dor ba dang 'jug pa dang*/ ma rgyal ba las rgyal bar byed pa dang rgyal ba rnal du 'god pa dang*/ 'phar ba dang 'bab pa zhes bya ba 'khor lo rin po che dang chos mthun pa'i phyir ro/ / de la mthong lam gyi ye shes skad cig ma bco lngas bden pa mngon par rtogs pa'i phyir ram skad cig ma snga ma snga ma'i rjes thogs su phyi ma phyi ma myur du skye ba'i phyir dang*/ bden pa'i dmigs pa dang ye shes kyi rnam pa dang bar chad med pa'i lam snga ma rnams 'dor ba'i phyir dang*/ bden pa'i dmigs pa dang ye shes kyi rnam pa dang rnam grol gyi lam phyi ma rnams la 'jug pa'i phyir dang*/ ma rgyal ba las rgyal bar byed pa ni bar chad med pa'i lam gyis mthong spang rnams kyi thob pa gcod pa'i sgo nas spong ba'i phyir ro/ / rgyal ba rnal du 'god pa ni rnam grol gyi lam gyis bral thob 'dzin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'phar ba ni rnam grol gyi lam mam khams gong ma'i bden pa la 'jug pa'i phyir ro/ / 'bab pa ni bar chad med pa'i lam mam 'dod pa'i bden pa la 'jug pa'i phyir ro/ / btsun pa dbyangs sgrogs na re mthong lam 'phags lam yan lag brgyad ni 'khor lo'i rtsibs dang sogs kyis bzung ba lte ba dang mu khyud dang 'dra ba'i phyir chos kyi 'khor lo yin no/ / de la shes rab kyi bslab pa yang dag pa'i lta ba dang rtog pa dang rtsol ba dang dran pa rnams ni rtsibs lta bu yin te/ phan tshun 'jug pa'i phyir dang*/ mthong spang gcod pa'i phyir ro/ / yang dag pa'i ngag dang las kyi mtha' dang 'tsho ba rnams ni lte ba dang 'dra ste/ de dag ni tshul khrims kyi bslab pa yin pas de la brten nas sems kyi bslab pa ting nge 'dzin 'thob la de thob pas shes rab kyi bslab pa skye ba'i phyir ro/ / ting nge 'dzin ni mu khyud dang 'dra ste/ des gzhan dag nye bar 'dzin pa'i phyir ram/ dmigs pa la sems sdud pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ /

The wheel of Dharma (dharmacakra) is the path of seeing (dṛṅmārga). It is similar to a precious wheel, since it proceeds quickly (āśugata), eradicates, engages, conquers the unconquered, sustains victory, ascends and descends, and so on. It proceeds quickly because the fifteen moments of transcendent wisdom of the path of seeing actually comprehend the four truths, or they are quickly generated at the conclusion of the former moment. It eradicates because it eradicates earlier focal objects of truth, aspects of transcendent wisdom, and uninterrupted paths. It engages because it engages later focal objects of truth, aspects of transcendent wisdom, and liberated paths. It conquers [558] the unconquered because the uninterrupted path abandons by means of severing obtainment of objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing. It sustains victory because it maintains the obtainment of freedom by the liberated path. It ascends because it enters the liberated path or higher truth. And it descends because it enters the uninterrupted path or desire-realm truth. Bhadanta Ghoṣaka says: It is a wheel of Dharma because the eightfold noble path of seeing is like the spokes (ara) of the wheel, the hub, the rim, and so on. The higher trainings of wisdom of right view, right investigation, right exertion, and right mindfulness are like spokes because they mutually engage, and they sever objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing. Right speech, right action, and right livelihood are like a hub because they are the higher training of ethics; based on them one obtains right concentration that is the higher training of mind, and by obtaining that the higher training in wisdom arises. Concentration is like the rim because it closely binds the others or because it contracts the mind to its focal object.[1693]

chos kyi 'khor lo mthong lam la zer ba yang mdo las/ bcom ldan 'das kyis lnga sde rnams la bka' stsal pa/ dge slong dag sngon ma thos pa'i chos rnams la 'di ni sdug bsngal 'phags pa'i bden pa'o zhes tshul bzhin du yid la byed pa na mig skyes so/ / shes pa dang rig pa dang blo skyes so/ / nga sngon ma thos pa'i chos rnams la 'di ni sdug bsngal kun 'byung ba'o/ / 'di ni sdug bsngal 'gog pa'o/ / 'di ni sdug bsngal 'gog par 'gyur ba'i lam 'phags pa'i bden pa'o zhes tshul bzhin du yid la byed pa na mig skyes so/ / shes pa dang rig pa dang blo skyes so zhes bya ba dang*/ dge slong dag nga sngon ma thos pa'i chos rnams la sdug bsngal 'phags pa'i bden pa de bdag gis mngon par shes pas yongs su shes par bya'o/ / kun 'byung spang bar bya'o/ / 'gog pa mngon du bya'o/ / sdug bsngal 'gog par 'gro ba'i lam 'phags pa'i bden pa de bsgom par bya'o zhes tshul bzhin du yid la byed pa na mig la sogs pa skyes so zhes bya ba dang*/ de bzhin du dge slong dag nga sngon ma thos pa'i chos rnams la sdug bsngal 'phags pa'i bden pa de bdag gis mngon par shes pas yongs su shes so/ / kun 'byung spangs so/ / 'gog pa mngon du byas so/ / lam bsgoms so/ / zhes tshul bzhin du yid la byed pa na mig la sogs pa skyes so zhes bya ba la sogs pa rgya cher gsungs nas/ chos kyi rnam grangs 'di bshad pa na tshe dang ldan pa kun shes ko'u Di n+ya dang lha brgyad khri la chos rnams la chos kyi mig rdul med cing dri ma dang bral ba skyes so/ / de nas bcom ldan 'das kyis tshe dang ldan pa kun shes ko'u Di n+ya la bka' stsal pa/ kun shes ko'u Di n+ya khyod kyis chos kun shes sam/ bcom ldan 'das bdag gis chos kun 'tshal to/ / bde bar gshegs pa bdag gis chos kun 'tshal to zhes gsol pa dang*/ sa bla ba'i gnod sbyin rnams kyis tshe dang ldan pa kun shes ko'u Di n+ya chos kun shes so zhes sgra bsgrags te/ grogs po dag bcom ldan 'das kyis yul wA rA Na ser drang srong lhung ba ri dwags kyi gnas 'dir chos kyi 'khor lo chos dang mthun pa dge sbyong ngam bram ze'am lha'am bdud dam tshangs pa'am sus kyang 'jig rten na skye bo mang po la phan par bya ba'i phyir chos dang mthun par ma bskor ba lan gsum du bzlas te rnam pa bcu gnyis pa bskor to zhes kun shes ko'u Di n+ya la mthong lam skyes pa na chos kyi 'khor lo bskor bar gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

With respect to calling the path of seeing “the wheel of Dharma,” a sūtra states in great detail: The Bhagavan addressed the group of five, saying: “Monks, these Dharmas have not been heard before: ‘This is the ārya truth of suffering,’ and when I applied proper attention, the eye [of Dharma] arose [in me], and knowledge, recognition, and insight arose. Regarding these Dharmas that have not been heard by me before: ‘This is the origin of suffering, this is the cessation of suffering, this is the ārya path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ And when I applied proper attention, the eye [of Dharma] arose, and knowledge, recognition, and insight arose. “Monks, these Dharmas have not been heard before. I should thoroughly know with actual knowledge the ārya truth of suffering, abandon origin, manifest cessation, and meditate on the ārya truth of path proceeding to the cessation of suffering. By applying proper attention, the eye [of Dharma] arose and so on. “Similarly, monks, these Dharmas have not been heard by me before. I have thoroughly known with actual knowledge the ārya truth of suffering, abandoned origin, manifested cessation, and meditated on the path. By applying proper attention, the eye [of Dharma] and so on . . .” In explaining the synonyms of Dharma, the sūtra states: The venerable, all-knowing Kauṇḍinya and 80,000 gods generated the stainless Dharma eye free of dust. [559] Then the Bhagavan said to the all-knowing Kauṇḍinya: “All-knowing Kauṇḍinya, do you know all Dharmas?” Kauṇḍinya replied: “Bhagavan, I have sought all Dharmas. Sugata, I have sought all Dharmas.” Yakṣas abiding above the earth proclaimed: “The venerable, all-knowing Kauṇḍinya knows all Dharmas. Friends, in Varaṇasī, in this abode of mendicant rishis and wild deer, the Bhagavan has turned the wheel of Dharma that is in harmony with Dharma, for śramaṇas, brahmans, gods, māras, or Brahma, for the benefit of the many beings in the world. He turned the wheel of Dharma that is in harmony with Dharma twelve times, repeating it three times each.” When the path of seeing was generated in the all-knowing Kauṇḍinya, the wheel of Dharma had been turned.[1694]

de la lan gsum du bzlas pa ni bye brag tu smra ba na re 'di ni sdug bsngal 'phags pa'i bden pa'o zhes sdug bsngal gyi ngo bo la bzlas pa gcig dang*/ sdug bsngal yongs su shes par bya'o zhes bya ba la bzlas pa gcig dang*/ sdug bsngal yongs su shes so zhes mthar thug pa la bzlas pa gcig ste gsum mo/ / rnam pa bcu gnyis ni bzlas pa de dag re re la'ang sdug bsngal gyi ngo bo mngon sum du gyur pas mig dang*/ the tshom med pas shes pa dang*/ yang dag pa'i don shes pas rig pa dang*/ rnam par dag pa'i phyir blo zhes pa bzhi bzhi dang*/ de bzhin du bden pa gzhan gsum po re re la'ang bzlas pa gsum gsum dang*/ bzlas pa re re la'ang mig skyes pa la sogs pa rnam pa bzhi bzhi yod pas rnam pa bcu gnyis bcu gnyis yin no/ / 'o na ni bden pa bzhi po re re la'ang bzlas pa gsum gsum bcu gnyis dang*/ bzlas pa re re la'ang rnam pa bzhi bzhi dang ldan pas rnam pa bzhi bcu rtsa brgyad yod pa'i phyir bzlas pa gsum dang rnam pa bcu gnyis su ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/ bden mod kyi bden pa re re la'ang bzlas pa gsum dang rnam pa bcu gnyis par 'dra ba'i phyir lan gsum du bzlas te rnam pa bcu gnyis zhes brjod de dper na gnyis bstan pa dang gnas bdun la mkhas pa bstan pa bzhin no/ / de la gnyis bstan pa ni mdo las/ dge slong dag khyed la gnyis bstan par bya'i/ de legs par rab tu ston pa nyon la yid la zung zhig dang bshad do/ / gnyis gang zhe na/ mig dang gzugs rnams zhes bya ba nas yid dang chos rnams so zhes bya ba'i bar du sbyar te gnyis tshan drug yod kyang gnyis gnyis su chos mthun pa'i phyir gnyis su gsungs pa dang*/ gnas bdun ni mdo las/ dge slong gnas bdun la mkhas pa ni chos 'dul ba 'di la myur du zag pa zad pa 'thob par 'gyur ro/ / bdun gang zhe na/ gzugs yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du rab tu shes so/ / gzugs kun 'byung ba dang*/ gzugs 'gog pa dang*/ gzugs 'gog par 'gyur ba'i lam dang*/ gzugs kyi ro myang ba dang*/ nyes dmigs dang*/ nges par 'byung ba'ang yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin rab tu shes so zhes pa dang*/ de bzhin du tshor ba la sogs pa'i phung po la'ang sbyar nas bdun lnga gsum bcu rtsa lnga yod kyang bdun tshan du 'dra bas bdun du gsungs pa bzhin no/ / de la bden pa bzhi char gyi bzlas pa gsum gyis rim pa ltar mthong sgom mi slob pa'i lam gsum bstan to zhes zer ro/ /

Vaibhāṣikas say: It was repeated three times, since the statement “This is the ārya truth of suffering” is the first repetition of the essential nature of suffering, the statement “I should thoroughly know suffering” is repeated once, and the statement “I have thoroughly known suffering” is repeated once, making three repetitions. Twelve aspects arise, since each of those repetitions has four aspects: the eye directly sees the nature of suffering, knowledge arises without doubt, recognition arises through knowing the perfect meaning, and insight arises because of its purity. So too, each of the three other truths has three repetitions and four aspects. And for each repetition, the eye [of Dharma] arises and so on, making twelve aspects in all. Question: Since each of the four truths has three repetitions, there are twelve repetitions, and since each repetition has four aspects, there would be forty-eight aspects. Therefore how can there be three repetitions and twelve aspects? Reply: Indeed, that is true. Because each truth has three repetitions and four aspects, there are twelve aspects, and it is said that there are three repetitions and twelve aspects. For example, it is like the instruction on pairs, or the instruction on those learned in seven abodes. Regarding the instruction on pairs, a sūtra states: Monks, I will teach you two things; listen well and pay attention, and I will explain. What are the pairs? There are six pairs, from the eye and form up to the mental faculty and phenomena. Because they exist in pairs, they are expressed in pairs.[1695] Regarding the seven abodes, a sūtra explains: Monks, those learned in the seven abodes in this discipline quickly come to obtain elimination of the contaminants. What are these seven? Properly know form correctly [560] as it is. Properly know the origin of form, the cessation of form, the path leading to the cessation of form, the experience of the taste of form, its disadvantages, and its renunciation, correctly as they are.[1696] So too, by applying this to the aggregate of feeling and so on, there are thirty-five. But since they exhibit a sevenfold pattern, they are also said to be seven. Further, since there are three repetitions of the four truths, they respectively teach three paths: the paths of seeing, meditation, and no more learning.

slob dpon ni de lta na mthong lam kho na chos kyi 'khor lo ma yin par 'gyur te/ bzlas pa gcig dang rnam pa bzhi las med pas lan gsum du bzlas pa dang rnam pa bcu gnyis ma tshang ba'i phyir ro/ / des na chos kyi rnam grangs de nyid chos kyi 'khor lo rab tu ston pa'i phyir chos kyi 'khor lo dang*/ bzlas pa gsum dang rnam pa bcu gnyis kyi don rab tu ston pas lan gsum du bzlas pa dang rnam pa bcu gnyis dang*/ gdul bya'i rgyud la de'i don shes par byed pa'i sgo nas gtod cing go bar byed pa'i phyir bskor ba'ang yin no/ / yang na mthong sgom mi slob pa'i lam gsum ga'ang gdul bya'i rgyud la 'jug pas chos kyi 'khor lo yin no/ / kun shes ko'u Di n+yas mthong lam thob pa na chos kyi 'khor lo bskor bar gsungs pa ni kun shes ko'u Di n+ya la sogs pa'i rgyud la mthong lam bskyed pa'i phyir dang por bskor bar brtsams pa'i phyir bskor ba zhes bya'o/ / bzlas pa gsum ni sdug bsngal 'phags pa'i bden pa'o zhes pa nas lam 'phags pa'i bden pa'o zhes pa'i bar ni bden bzhi'i rang gi ngo bo la bzlas pa dang*/ sdug bsngal yongs su shes par bya'o zhes pa nas lam bsgom par bya'o zhes pa'i bar ni bya ba la bzlas pa dang*/ sdug bsngal yongs su shes so zhes pa nas lam bsgoms so zhes pa'i bar ni mthar thug pa la bzlas pa'o/ / rnam pa bcu gnyis ni bden bzhi'i dbang du byas nas 'di ni sdug bsngal lo zhes pa nas/ 'di ni lam mo zhes pa'i bar du bden bzhi'i rang gi ngo bo la dmigs pa'i rnam pa bzhi dang*/ yongs su shes par bya ba nas bsgom par bya ba'i bar ni bya ba la dmigs pa'i rnam pa bzhi dang*/ yongs su shes so nas bsgoms so'i bar ni mthar thug pa la dmigs pa'i rnam pa bzhi yin no zhes bzhed do/ / de ltar na bye brag tu smra ba ltar na bden pa bzhi po re re la'ang bzlas pa gsum gsum dang rnam pa bcu {gnyis bcu gnyis su 'dod la/} slob dpon ni bden pa bzhi ga bsdoms pa la bzlas pa gsum dang rnam pa bcu gnyis su bzhed do/ /

Vasubandhu notes that according to that [latter assertion], the path of seeing alone would not be the wheel of Dharma; it lacks three repetitions and twelve aspects, since it would have no more than one repetition and four aspects. Therefore, because just this synonym of Dharma fully reveals the wheel of Dharma, it fully reveals the meaning of the wheel of Dharma, its three repetitions and twelve aspects. And because it is repeated three times with twelve aspects, and it is delivered to generate knowledge of its meaning in the mindstreams of disciples and it causes that understanding, it is also said to be turned. Moreover, the three paths of seeing, meditation, and no more learning are the wheel of Dharma, since they enter the mindstreams of disciples. It is said that the wheel of Dharma had been turned when all-knowing Kauṇḍinya obtained the path of seeing, for “turning” of the wheel was first initiated to generate the path of seeing in the continuum of all-knowing Kauṇḍinya and so on. Regarding the three repetitions, the repetition of the essential nature of each of the four truths is stated from “the ārya truth of suffering” up to “the ārya truth of path.” The second repetition is stated from “I should thoroughly know suffering” up to “I should thoroughly know the path.” The third repetition is stated from “I have thoroughly known suffering” up to “I have meditated on the path.” The twelve aspects consist of: the four aspects focusing on the nature of each of the four truths, which are stated from “This is suffering” up to “This is the path”; the four aspects focusing on action, which are stated from “I should thoroughly know” up to “I should meditate”; and the four aspects focusing on the final state, which are stated from “I have thoroughly known” up to “I have thoroughly meditated.”[1697] Thus Vaibhāṣikas assert three repetitions and twelve aspects each for each of the four truths. Vasubandhu asserts that, in sum, the four truths have three repetitions and twelve aspects.[1698]
lnga pa [khams dang dbye ba'i khyad par] ni
Specific realm and classification
'o na khams gang du dge sbyong gi tshul gyi 'bras bu gang 'thob ce na/
Question: Now what result of the system of training in virtue is obtained in what realm?
'dod par gsum 'thob tha ma ni/ / gsum du'o gong na mthong lam med/ / mi skyo lung las 'dir rtsom zhing / / der mthar phyin ces 'byung phyir ro/ / 55

Three are obtained in the desire realm. The last, in three. The path of seeing does not exist in higher realms because they are not disgusted and the scriptures declare that they commence here but finish there. (6:55)

'dod par ni 'bras bu dang po gsum sngar ma thob pa 'thob par 'gyur la 'bras bu tha ma dgra bcom pa ni khams gsum char du thob par 'gyur ro/ / gal te 'bras bu dang po gnyis ni 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang ma bral bas thob par bya ba yin pa'i phyir de ltar rigs na khams gong mar skyes pa zhig nges pa la 'jug pa na skad cig ma bcu drug pa la phyir mi 'ong du 'gyur bas na de khams gong mar ji ltar 'thob par mi 'gyur zhe na/

Reply: The first three results that were not previously obtained are obtained in the desire realm. The last, the result of an arhat, is obtained in all three realms. Question: If it is logical that the first two results are obtained without freedom from attachment to the desire realm, [561] then if those certain to enter the higher realms become nonreturners in the sixteenth moment, how would they not obtain the higher realms?

Reply: I think that is because the path of seeing (dṛkpatha) does not exist in higher realms, and because those beings do not obtain the result of nonreturn even though freed from attachment to the desire realm, since the path of seeing did not arise previously. The path of seeing that does not exist [in higher realms] refers to the path of seeing that focuses on the three realms, for [uncontaminated] formless-realm states do not focus on lower realms. As the Abhidharmakośa observes, “The object fields of those virtuous, formless, actual bases are not contaminated lower levels” (8:21ab).[1699] {Objection: It exists [in higher realms] since it arises even when the Dharma is not heard. Reply:} It is impossible for the two self-arisen beings to exist in the formless realm, and there is no obtainment of śrāvaka realization from listening to others because they cannot listen to Dharma from a holy being {and because they cannot focus on the desire realm. The path of seeing needs to first focus on the suffering of the desire realm, but formless minds cannot focus on that.}

gzhan yang mdo las/ skyo na 'dod chags dang bral bar 'gyur ro zhes gsungs na/ gzugs khams su skyes pa'i so so'i skye bo ni snyoms 'jug gi bde ba la chags pa'i phyir dang*/ sdug bsngal gyi tshor ba med pa'i phyir 'khor ba la yid mi skyo la/ skyo ba med par yang 'phags lam 'thob par mi nus pa'i phyir ro zhes pa'i rigs pa dang*/

Moreover, a sūtra declares: When one is disgusted one is freed from attachment.[1700] Ordinary beings born in the form realm are not disgusted (asaṃvega) with saṃsāra because they are attached to the pleasure of meditative attainment, and they have no sensibility that that is suffering. And because they lack disgust, it is logical that they cannot obtain the ārya path.
