bcu tshan bcu pa'i lung las kyang gang zag ni bcu ste/ bcu gang zhe na/ rigs nas rigs su skye ba dang*/ mchog tu thogs na lan bdun pa dang*/ bar chad gcig pa dang*/ lan cig phyir 'ong ba dang*/ bar ma dor mya ngan las 'da' ba nas gong du 'pho ba'i bar lnga dang*/ dgra bcom pa'o/ / gang zag bcu po de dag las dang po bzhi dang dgra bcom pa ni 'dir rtsom zhing 'dir mthar phyin par 'gyur ro/ / bar ma dor mya ngan las 'da' ba nas gong du 'pho ba'i bar gang zag lnga ni 'dir rtsom zhing der mthar phyin par 'gyur ro zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / {'phags pa ma yin pa ni der rtsom par ma gsungs so } de la 'dir zhes bya ba ni 'dod pa'i khams yin la/ rtsom pa ni myang 'das kyi thabs kyis 'go 'dzugs pa'o/ / der zhes bya ba ni khams gong ma yin no/ / re zhig khams kyis ni de lta bu yin no/ / gal te mi g.yo'i zad shes las/ / mi skye'i blo gros gal te min/ / zhes bshad pa de ci dgra bcom pa la'ang dbye ba yod dam zhe na/

The scriptures — namely, the Ten Times Ten Sūtra — declare: What are the ten? (1) Stream enterers born the same type, (2) stream enterers obstructed for seven existences at most, (3) those with one obstruction, (4) once returners, (5–9) the five from nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa in the intermediate state to nonreturners relocating to higher levels, and (10) arhats. From among those ten persons, the first four and the arhat commence here and finish here. The five persons from nonreturners who attain nirvāṇa in the intermediate state to nonreturners relocating to higher levels commence here but finish there.[1701] {It is not stated that nonāryas commence there.} “Here” means the desire realm, “commence” means to initiate the means of attaining nirvāṇa, “there” means the higher realms. At times the realms are referred to in this way. Question: Since the Abhidharmakośa declares, “If they are immutable arhats, awareness of nonarising arises from knowledge of elimination” (6:50ab),[1702] aren’t arhats also classified?
dgra bcom drug 'dod de dag las/ / lnga ni dad pas mos las skyes/ / de dag rnam grol dus dang sbyor/ / mi g.yo'i chos can mi g.yo ba/ / 56
Arhats are asserted to be six. From among them five are born from resolute faith. They are liberated according to circumstances. Those who possess immutability are immutable. (6:56)
yod de/
Reply: They are [so classified]

dgra bcom pa'i dbye ba ni mdo las/ dge slong dag drug po 'di dag ni dgra bcom pa ste/ drug gang zhe na/ yongs su nyams pa'i chos can dang*/ 'chi bar sems pa'i chos can dang*/ rjes su bsrung ba'i chos can dang*/ gnas pa las mi bskyod pa dang*/ rtogs pa'i skal ba can dang*/ mi g.yo ba'i chos can no/ / zhes gsungs pas drug tu 'dod de/ de dag ni rim pa ltar dang po lnga char la nyams pa srid kyang rkyen chung ngus rang gi rtogs pa las nyams pa dang*/ nyams par dogs pas mya ngan las 'da' bar sems pa dang*/ nyams par dogs pas lam bsrung ba la brtson pa dang*/ rkyen chung ngus rtogs pa las mi bskyod pa dang*/ dbang po 'phos te mi g.yo ba rtogs pa'i skal ba dang ldan pa dang*/ dbang po rno bas rtogs pa las nyams mi srid pa rnams so/ / de ltar dbang po rnon po la'ang rang bzhin gyis rno ba dang dbang po 'phos pas rno ba gnyis su 'gyur ro/ /

because when arhats are classified, they are asserted to be six. A sūtra states: Monks, there are six who are arhats. What are these six? (1) Arhats who fully degenerate (parihāṇadharman), (2) arhats intent on death (cetanādharman), (3) arhats guarding the path (anurakṣaṇādharman), (4) arhats who are steadfast (sthirākampya), (5) arhats who enter realization (prativedhanādharman), and (6) arhats who are immutable (akopyadharman).[1703] From among them, respectively, it is possible that the first five degenerate: [562] (1) those whose realization degenerates due to a minor condition, (2) those intent on attaining nirvāṇa through fear of degeneration, (3) those striving to protect the path through fear of degeneration, (4) those whose realization remains steadfast despite minor counter-conditions, (5) those who enter the realization of immutability through upgrading their intellectual faculty, and (6) those of sharp faculty whose realization cannot degenerate. Those of sharp intellectual faculty also have two subtypes: those who are of sharp faculty naturally and those who upgrade their intellectual faculty.

de ltar dgra bcom pa drug po de dag las dang po lnga ni sgom lam gyi tshe dbang po brtul po dad pas mos pa las skyes pa yin la/ lnga po de dag gis sems kyi rnam par grol ba ni dus dang sbyor ba yin te/ zas gos dang gnas la sogs pa'i mthun rkyen tshang ba dang nad dang dgra'i tsher ma la sogs pa'i 'gal rkyen med pa la ltos pa'i phyir dus kyi rnam par grol ba zhes bya'o/ / drug pa mi g.yo ba'i chos can ni rtogs pa las mi nyams pas mi g.yo ba

Thus, from among these six arhats, the first five are born from the resolute faith (śraddhādhimuktaja) of those of dull faculty on the path of meditation. The minds of these five are liberated according to circumstance (sāmayika) because their liberation relies on the presence of conducive conditions such as food, clothing, abode, and so on, and the absence of counter-conditions such as the harm of enemies, and thus they are called “arhats liberated according to circumstances.” The sixth are those who possess immutability (akopydharman). They are immutable (akopya) since their realization does not degenerate.
de phyir de dus mi sbyor grol/ / de ni mthong thob rgyu las byung / / kha cig dang po nas de'i rigs/ / kha cig sbyangs pa las gyur to/ / 57

Thus they are liberated regardless of circumstances. They arise from the cause of obtaining results by insight. Some say they are that type from the beginning. Some say they change through upgrading. (6:57)

de nyid kyi phyir de ni mthun rkyen dang 'gal rkyen yod med la mi ltos{ te 'dod dgur ting nge 'dzin mngon du 'gyur} pas dus dang mi sbyor bar rnam par grol ba yin la/ de ni sgom lam gyi dus kyi dbang po rnon po mthong bas thob pa'i rgyu las byung ba yin te/ 'bras bu'i khyad par ni rgyu'i khyad par la ltos pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang slob pa'i tshe dad mos mthong thob tu dbang po 'phos pa'am rang bzhin gyis dbang po rnon po las byung ba'i mi g.yo ba'i chos can ni mthong thob kyi rgyu las byung ba yin gyi mi slob pa'i tshe dbang po brtul po rnon po mi g.yo ba'i chos can du dbang po 'phos pa'i mi g.yo ba'i chos can de ni mthong thob kyi rgyu las byung ba ma yin no zhes TIka las 'chad do/ /

Thus they do not rely on the existence of conducive conditions or the absence of counter-conditions, {since all sense objects manifest through concentration}, and they are liberated regardless of circumstances (asamayamukta). Those with sharp faculty on the path of meditation arise from the cause of obtaining [results] by insight (dṛṣṭiprāpta) because a special result relies on a special cause. Immutable arhats either upgrade their intellectual faculty from one resolute in faith to one obtaining results by insight when a learner, or through possessing naturally sharp intellectual faculty, and [the latter] arises from the cause of obtaining results by insight. Immutable arhats who upgrade from dull to sharp faculty when a learner, arise from the cause of obtaining results by insight. Immutable arhats who upgrade their intellectual faculty from dull to sharp when not a learner do not arise from the cause of obtaining results by insight. This is explained in the Subcommentary.[1704]

rnam par grol ba dus dang sbyor ba dang mi sbyor ba ni 'dod dgur ting nge 'dzin mngon du 'gyur ba dang mi 'gyur ba'am/ yang na rtogs pa nyams pa srid pa dang mi srid pa'i phyir dus gzhan gyi bar du rnam par grol ba dang gtan du rnam par grol ba nyid yin par shes par bya'o/ /

You should understand that arhats liberated according to circumstances or regardless of circumstances refers, respectively, to those who are not liberated at a fixed time and those who are liberated at a fixed time. They manifest or do not manifest concentration according to their desire, and their realization may or may not degenerate.
drug pa [rigs dang nyams pa'i khyad par] ni
Specific type and degeneration
dgra bcom pa de dag dang po nas de dag gi rigs can du nges pa'am 'on te phyis de dag tu gyur pa yin zhe na/
Question: Are arhats determined by type from the first, or do they later become a specific type?

{dbang po ma 'phos pa } kha cig ni dang po nas yongs su nyams pa'i chos can la sogs pa de'i rigs su nges pa'ang yod la kha cig ni phyis rigs{ sam dbang po} sbyangs pa las gyur pa'ang yod de yongs su nyams pa'i chos can gyi rigs dbang po sbyangs pas 'chi bar sems pa'i chos can du 'gyur ba la sogs pa bzhin no/ / de dag ris drug tu 'gyur ba'i rgyu ni rim pa ltar slob pa'i tshe lam sgom pa la rgyun sbyor gus sbyor gnyis ka med pa dang*/ gnyis ka med la khyad par du gus sbyor med pa dang*/ rgyun sbyor tsam dang ldan pa dang*/ gus sbyor dang ldan pa dang*/ sbyor ba gnyis ka dang ldan pa'i dbang po brtul po dang*/ sbyor ba gnyis ka dang ldan pa'i dbang po rnon po las gyur pa'i phyir ro/ / yongs su nyams pa'i chos can la sogs pa'ang de ltar srid pa'i phyir yin gyi nges pa ni ma yin no/ / de ltar na khams gsum char na dgra bcom pa drug gi dbye ba yod par rung ngo*/ / gang dag nges par yongs su nyams par 'gyur ba la sogs pa 'dod pa de dag gi ltar na 'dod pa na drug gi dbye ba yod kyi gong ma gnyis na ni bzhi pa dang drug pa las gzhan ni ma yin te/ de dang gong mar skyes pa ni/ / yongs nyams dbang po 'pho mi bsten/ / zhes pas de gnyis{ kyi 'phags pa ni dbang po smin pa dang*/ skyo ba dang*/ rang gzhan la gnod pa med pa des} na yongs su nyams pa med pas dang po gsum med la/ dbang po 'pho ba med pas lnga pa'ang med phyir ro/ / gal te 'di dag thams cad rang gi 'bras bu dang rigs las nyams par 'gyur ram zhe na/

Some say: {Regarding those who do not upgrade their intellectual faculty,} arhats who fully degenerate and so on are definitely that type (gotrā) from the beginning (ādita). Some say: They change their type through upgrading (uttāpanāgata) their type {or faculty}, because one who fully degenerates may become one intent on death and so on through upgrading their intellectual faculty. The causes of becoming these six types of arhat are, respectively: (1) learners meditating on the path who lack both continuous application and respectful application, (2) those lacking both, but respectful application more so, (3) those possessing continuous application alone, (4) those possessing respectful application, (5) those with dull faculty who possesses both applications, and (6) those with sharp faculty who possess both applications. It is possible that arhats who fully degenerate [563] and so on exist in the way described here, but it is not certain. But it is suitable to classify six arhats relative to the three realms. According to those who assert that arhats who fully degenerate and so on definitely exist in the desire realm, the sixfold classification of arhats exists in the desire realm. But only the fourth and sixth exist in the two higher realms, since the Abhidharmakośa mentions, “Those born in higher realms do not degenerate, and they do not rely on upgrading intellectual faculty” (6:41cd). Therefore the first three do not exist, since {āryas of} the two higher realms {possess mature faculties, disgust, and do not harm self or others} and they do not fully degenerate. The fifth also does not exist in higher realms since they do not upgrade their intellectual faculty there. Question: Do all degenerate in terms of their result and type?
bzhi ni rigs las lnga 'bras la/ / nyams 'gyur dang po las ma yin/ / slob dang 'phags min rigs drug ldan/ /
The four in terms of type. Five degenerate in terms of result, but those from the beginning do not. Learners and nonāryas possess six types. (6:58abc)

bar pa bzhi ni rang rang gi rigs las nyams par 'gyur gyi dang po ni rang gi rigs las nyams pa ma yin te/ rigs de bcos ma ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ de bas dman pa'i rigs med pa'i{ phyir dang de la sbyangs pa las gyur pa mi srid pa'i} phyir ro/ / dang po lnga po thams cad kyang 'bras bu las nyams par 'gyur te/ sgom spang gzhi dang bcas shing 'bras bu glo bur ba yin pas yongs su nyams pa'i chos can yang 'bras bu las nyams pa srid do/ / 'on kyang dang po nas rigs nges pa las ni thams cad kyang nyams pa ma yin te/ dgra bcom pa 'chi bar sems pa la sogs par nges pa ni slob pa dang mi slob pa'i lam gnyis kyis brtan por byas pa'i phyir dang*/{slong pa'i dus na dbang po sbyangs pa'i mi slob pa yang ma nyams par slob dpon 'dun bzang gis gsungs so/ / slob pa'i rigs dang po'ang 'das ma 'das kyi lam gnyis kyis brtan par byas pas mi nyams kyi sbyangs pas thob pa las ni nyams par 'gyur ro/ / de ltar na 'bras bu dang po nyams par 'gyur te 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis brtan par ma byas pas so zhe na/ gtan tshigs de ni rigs kyi phyir bshad kyi 'bras bu'i phyir ma bshad pa skyon med do/ / 'bras bu 'das ma 'das kyi lam gyi cig car thob pa ni mi srid la/ rigs lam gnyis kyis brtan pa ni tshe 'di pa'i drod la sogs pa dang phyi ma'i spong lam mam/ 'di nyid las gnyis ka sgom pa'ang yod de/ / zhes so/}/

Reply: The four intermediate arhats degenerate in terms of their type (gotrā). But the first does not degenerate in terms of type — that type is not enhanced, there is no type inferior to it, {and it is impossible to upgrade to that stage}. All of the first five degenerate (hāni) in terms of their result (phala). It is even possible that arhats who completely degenerate do so in terms of their result, since they possess a basis of objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation and the result is spontaneous. However, all with fixed type from the beginning do not degenerate, because arhats such as arhats intent on death definitely achieve stability through both the mundane and transcendent paths. {Master Saṅghabhadra stated that one who upgrades intellectual faculty as a learner will not degenerate as a nonlearner. Also, the first type of learner does not degenerate due to achieving stability through the mundane and transcendent paths, but he degenerates from obtainment through upgrading his intellectual faculty. Objection: Thus the first result degenerates, since it is not stabilized by the mundane path. Reply: There is no error, since this proof is stated for type and not for result. Simultaneous obtainment of the resultant mundane and transcendent paths is impossible, but stabilization through both type and path exists for those who attain the stage of heat and so on in this life, the abandoning paths of later stages, or meditation on both that is distinct from the first two.}

slob pa na{ rigs} nges pa{ 'i rigs de} 'ang 'jig rten dang 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam gnyis kyis brtan por byas pa'i phyir ro/ / 'on kyang nyams pa'i chos can phyis 'chi bar sems par dbang po sbyangs pa la sogs pa las ni nyams pa yod do/ / 'bras bu dang po rgyun du zhugs pa las kyang nyams pa ma yin te/ de ni mthong spang spangs pas rab tu phye ba yin zhing de yang 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i rtsa ba can yin la de yang gzhi med pa can yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhi ni 'dir yul yin te/ bden pa la dmigs nas bdag med pa la bdag tu rtogs pa'i phyir dang*/ bdag med par mngon sum du shes na bdag tu rtogs pa'ang mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dod chags la sogs pa sgom spang rnams ni gzugs la sogs pa bden pa la dmigs pa'i phyir gzhi dang bcas pa yin pas spangs kyang slar skye ba srid pa'i phyir 'bras bu phyi ma rnams las ni nyams pa srid do/ / gzhan yang 'phags pa nges par mi rtog pa dag la dran pa nyams pas nyon mongs pa skye bar 'gyur na nges par rtog pa la ni ma yin te/ thag pa la thag par rtogs pa la sbrul du 'dzin pa mi skye ba bzhin no/ / nges par mi rtog pa'i 'phags pa la'ang mthong spang rnams mi skye ste/ de dag ni nges par rtogs pa'i bdag nyid yin pa'i phyir zhes bye brag tu smra ba rnams 'dod do/

Also, those who are definitely learners {by type} achieve stability through both the mundane and transcendent paths. However, arhats who fully degenerate and later upgrade their intellectual faculty and attain the stage of one intent on death may degenerate. But there is no degeneration from the first result of stream entry because such beings are differentiated from others; they abandon objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing and they do not possess a basis for the root afflicted view of the self. Basis here refers to an object, because those who possess that basis conceive that which is selfless to be a self through focusing on the four truths, and if they directly know selflessness, then it is impossible that they conceive a self. It is possible that beings degenerate from the later results because objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation, such as attachment, focus on the four truths such as material form. And though abandoned, it is possible that attachment and so on rearise due to [564] possessing a basis. For āryas with indecisive conception, affliction may arise through mindfulness degenerating, but not for those with decisive conception, just as a mind comprehending a rope to be a rope does not apprehend it to be a snake. Also, objects abandoned by the path of seeing do not rearise for āryas with indecisive conception, because they are beings with decisive realization. This is asserted by Vaibhāṣikas.

{Vaibhāṣikas assert that “type” refers to someone of specific type, but it is uncertain that they always become that type, for that person can degenerate from that type and become another type. But if they are definitely that type from the beginning, they do not become another type. It is possible that the first five types of arhat [can] degenerate to the three intermediate results. Sautrāntikas assert that it is possible that the two intermediate results [can] degenerate due to obtainment by the mundane path but that that is impossible through the transcendent path.}

mdo sde pa la sogs pa rnams ni 'bras bu dang po las nyams pa med par ma zad dgra bcom pa las kyang nyams pa med de/ des nyon mongs pa'i sa bon rtsa ba nas spong ba'i gnyen po thob pas gtan du mi skye ba'i phyir ro/ / de lta ma yin na zag pa zad pa ma yin par 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / re zhig nyon mongs pa thams cad log pas dgra bcom par 'dod na ni sems med pa'i gnas skabs thams cad der 'gyur pa'i phyir ro/ / bcom ldan 'das kyis kyang*/ dge slong dag 'phags pa'i shes rab kyis spangs pa gang yin pa de ni spangs pa yin no zhes gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ slob pa la bag yod pa la bag yod par bya'o zhes pa smra'o zhes gsungs kyi dgra bcom pa la ni ma gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ chos mngon pa las kyang*/ gnas gsum gyis 'dod pa'i 'dod chags kyi phra rgyas skye bar 'gyur te/ 'dod pa'i 'dod chags kyis phra rgyas ma spangs shing yongs su ma shes pa yin 'dod pa'i 'dod chags kyi kun nas dkris par gyur pa'i chos rnams snang bar gyur pa yin/ de la'ang tshul bzhin ma yin pa yid la byed pa yin zhes gsungs la dgra bcom pa la de dag med pa'i phyir ro/ /

Sautrāntikas and so on assert that not only is there no degeneration from the first result but there is also no degeneration from the state of an arhat, because for them afflictions never arise, since they obtain the antidote that completely abandons the seeds of affliction. If that were not so, then they would not exhaust the contaminants. If one were to assert that an arhat is one who intermittently stops all afflictions, then all instances of mindless states would become the state of an arhat. Also, the Bhagavan has said: Monks, ārya wisdom abandons every object of abandonment whatsoever.[1705] And it is said that learners should be diligent in their diligence, but this is not said for arhats. The Abhidharma also mentions: Due to the three abodes, negative tendencies of desire-realm attachment arise. Due to desire-realm attachment, negative tendencies are not abandoned and they are not fully understood. Entangled states of desire-realm attachment appear, and inappropriate attention arises for them.[1706] That does not exist for arhats.

gang yang mdo las/ kun dga' bo dgra bcom pa la'ang rnyed pa dang bkur sti bar chad byed pa yin no zhes nga smra'o zhes gsungs pa de ni bsam gtan dngos gzhi la snyoms par 'jug pa mthong ba'i chos la bde bar gnas pa la bar du gcod pa gsungs pa yin la/ bcu las 'phros pa'i mdo las/ bskyed par bya ba'i chos ni gcig ste/ sems rnam par grol ba dus dang sbyor ba pa yid du 'ong ba yin no zhes gsungs pa ni slob pa'i dbang du mdzad pa yin la/ dgra bcom pa drug tu gsungs pa ni mthar gyis gnas pa'i snyoms 'jug gi yon tan la sogs pa las nyams pa la nyams pa'i chos can la sogs par gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ mdo gzhan las/ tshe dang ldan pa gnag tshogs can dus kyis sems rnam par grol ba yid du 'ong ba lus kyis mngon sum du byas pa las lan drug gi bar du yang dang yang du yongs su nyams pa dang yi chad nas lus dang srog la mi lta ba'i phyir mtshon gyis 'debs par byed la 'chi ba'i dus kho nar dgra bcom pa nyid thob cing yongs su mya ngan las 'das par gyur to zhes gsungs pa yang slob pa'i dus kho na na nyams pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ sol ba'i phung po lta bu'i mdo las/ 'phags pa nyan thos thos pa dang ldan pa de ltar spyod cing de ltar gnas pa de la rgyal res 'ga' zhig dran pa nyams pa las sdig pa mi dge ba'i rnam par rtog pa dag skye bar 'gyur ro zhes gsungs pa'ang slob pa'i dbang du mdzad nas gsungs pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ / gang dag theg pa gong ma'i rjes su smra ba rnams ni 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam gyis nyon mongs pa dang rnam par rtogs pa'i sa bon spangs pa rnams ni slob pa'i 'phags pa la'ang nyams pa med de rgyu med pa'i phyir ro/ / gang yang de dang de las nyams par bshad pa ni sgom spang gi sa bon ma spangs pa rnams yin la/ slob pa dang mi slob pa thams cad la'ang dus dang sbyor ba dang mi sbyor ba dang nyams pa dang ma nyams pa la sogs pa ni dbang po rtul po dang rnon po gzungs dang ting nge 'dzin dang rnam par thar pa la sogs pa la 'jug pa'i dbang du byas nas gsungs pa yin no zhes 'dod de/ rigs pa mkhyen pa dag gis/ bdag lta'i sa bon spangs pa'i phyir/ / slar mi ldog pa nyid yin no zhes gsungs pa bzhin no/ / ci dgra bcom pa de dag kho na rigs drug dang ldan nam/ 'on te gzhan dag kyang rigs drug dang ldan zhe na/

A sūtra notes: Ānanda, I declare that also property and respect are obstacles to arhats.[1707] This passage explains that if one enters meditative attainment on the actual basis of absorption to abide in comfort in this life, then this is an obstacle. The Sūtra Elaborating Ten states: There is one Dharma to be generated, and that is the appealing liberation of the mind that accords with circumstances.[1708] This is stated from the perspective of learners. When arhats are stated to be six, then the one who degenerates is the serial abider for whom the qualities of absorption and so on degenerate. In another sūtra it is said: The venerable Godhika fully degenerated six times from physically manifestating the pleasant state of liberation according to circumstance. Out of contempt for his body and life, he stabbed [565] himself, and only at the time of death did he obtain the state of an arhat and attain nirvāṇa.[1709] Though this is said, degeneration exists only when one is a learner, and the Simile of Charcoal Sūtra explains: For ārya śrāvakas who are learned and who act in that way and abide in that way, at times nonvirtuous conceptions arise due to the degeneration of mindfulness.[1710] This is stated from the perspective of learners. Those who advocate higher-vehicle tenets assert that those who abandon afflictions and the seeds of conception by transcendent paths do not degenerate as ārya learners because there is no cause for that. Furthermore, the explanation that they degenerate from this or that state applies to those who have not abandoned seeds to be abandoned by the path of meditation. Also degeneration or nondegeneration for all learners and nonlearners, according to circumstances or regardless of circumstances and so on, is stated from the perspective of whether they are of dull or sharp faculty, or whether they engage mantra, concentration, liberation, and so forth. Thus it is said, “Because those who comprehend logic abandon the seed of the view of self, they do not need to eliminate it again.” Question: Do arhats alone possess six types or do others also possess six types?

ji ltar dgra bcom pa la rigs drug yod pa de bzhin du 'phags pa slob pa dang 'phags min so so'i skye bo rnams kyang yongs su nyams pa'i chos can la sogs pa rigs drug dang ldan te/ dgra bcom pa'i rigs de dag kyang dngos dang brgyud nas de dag sngon du 'gro ba'i phyir dang*/ 'bras bu rgyu la mi 'khrul ba'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: Just as arhats possess six types, similarly ārya learners (śaikṣa) and nonārya (anārya) ordinary beings who fully degenerate and so on also possess six types, because these six types directly or indirectly precede the six types of arhat, and the result is unmistaken with respect to its cause.
bdun pa [dbang po 'pho ba'i khyad par]
Specific upgrade of intellectual faculty
gal te dbang po rtul po rnon por 'pho ba na gnas skabs gang du 'pho zhe na/
Question: If one of dull faculty upgrades to sharp faculty, when do they upgrade?
mthong ba la ni 'pho ba med/ / 58
They do not upgrade on the path of seeing. (6:58d)

Reply: They do not upgrade (saṃcara) their faculty on the path of seeing (dṛnmārga) because {apart from that action} they do not {enter other actions nor} prepare to upgrade their intellectual faculty, since there is just one single continuum of equipoise. {Those resolute in faith upgrade through uncontaminated paths alone. It is not contradictory for childlike beings to upgrade in dependence on any path comparing coarse and refined aspects, but they upgrade due to the stages of the uninterrupted and liberated paths with the thought, “May my intellectual faculty grow sharper by any appropriate means.”}

des na so so'i skye bo dang*/ slob pa dad mos dang*/ mi slob pa dus sbyor gyi gnas skabs na dbang po 'pho ba yod do/ / gang yang mdo las/ 'dis mthong ba'i chos la bde bar gnas pa lhag pa'i sems las byung ba bzhi thob pa gang dag yin pa de las gang yang rung ba zhig las 'di yongs su nyams par 'gyur bar ni nga smra'i/ 'di gcig pus sems kyi rnam par grol ba mi g.yo ba'i bar du lus kyis mngon sum du byas pa gang yin pa de las ni 'di rnam grangs gang gis kyang yongs su nyams par 'gyur bar nga mi smra'o/ / zhes dgra bcom pa mi g.yo ba'i chos can la'ang mthong ba'i chos la bde bar gnas pa las nyams par bshad pa de ji ltar mi g.yo bar 'gyur zhe na/

Therefore upgrading [one’s intellectual] faculty exists in the context of ordinary beings, learners resolute in faith, and nonlearners liberated according to circumstance. A sūtra states: I do say that there is complete degeneration from any obtainment of the four special mental factors that abide in comfort in this life. I do not say that there is any corresponding complete degeneration of the physical manifestion of the immutable liberation of mind alone.[1711] Question: If it is said that immutable arhats can degenerate [566] from abiding in comfort in this life, then how are they immutable?
thob dang ma thob nyer spyad las/ / yongs nyams rnam pa gsum shes bya/ / ston la tha ma mi g.yo la/ / bar ma'ang gzhan la rnam gsum mo/ / 59

Complete degeneration should be known as three types: degeneration of obtainment, nonobtainment, and enjoyment. The Master has the last. Immutable arhats have the second and last. Others have three types. (6:59)
yongs su nyams pa ni rnam pa gsum du shes par bya'o zhes sbyar ro/ / gang yin zhe na/
Reply: Complete degeneration (parihāni) should be known as three types. Question: Why is that?

yon tan thob pa las nyams pa dang ma thob pa las nyams pa dang thob pa nye bar spyad pa las nyams pa'o/ / de la dang po ni rnyed pa las nyams pa yin la phyi ma gnyis ni ldan pa las nyams pa yin te rang bzhin gyis blun pa la blo gros nyams pa zhes brjod pa bzhin no/ / nyams pa gsum po de dag las ston pa sangs rgyas la ni nyams pa tha ma yod de/ gdul bya'i don la zhugs pas mthong chos la bde bar gnas pa'i yon tan 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug la sogs pa thob kyang mngon du mi byed pa'i phyir ro/ / dgra bcom pa mi g.yo ba'i chos can la ni nyams pa bar ma dang tha ma'ang yod de/ sangs rgyas kyi chos ma 'dres pa la sogs pa ma thob pa'i phyir ro/ / 'ang gi sgras ni nye bar spyad pa las nyams pa sdud pa'o/ / dgra bcom pa gzhan lnga dang slob pa sgom lam pa dang so so'i skye bo dbang po rtul po la ni nyams pa rnam pa gsum ga yod do/ / de'i phyir dgra bcom pa mi g.yo ba'i chos can mthong ba'i chos la bde bar gnas pa las nyams par bshad pa ni nye bar spyad pa las nyams pa yin la mi g.yo ba las gzhan ni rnam par grol ba las yin no/ / dgra bcom pa gzhan ni mdo las/ rkyen lnga dang rgyu lngas dus kyis rnam par grol ba'i dgra bcom pa yongs su nyams par 'gyur ro/ / lnga gang zhe na/ las kyi mtha' la zhugs pa yin/ smra ba la zhugs pa yin/ rtsod pa la zhugs pa yin/ ring du rgyu ba'i sbyor ba dang ldan pa yin/ nad kyi rnam pa yun ring pos thebs pa yin zhes 'byung bas mthong ba'i chos la bde bar gnas pa dang*/ rnam par grol ba gnyis ka las nyams pa yin no zhes bye brag tu smra ba rnams zer ro/ /

Reply: There is (1) degeneration of the obtainment (prāpta) of qualities, (2) degeneration of the nonobtainment (aprāpta) of qualities, and (3) degeneration of the enjoyment (upabhoga) of qualities obtained. From those, (1) the first is degeneration of attainment (lābha), and the latter two (2–3) are degeneration of possession, as it is stated that insight degenerates for one who is naturally a fool. From those three degenerations, Buddha, the Master, has the last degeneration. He obtains qualities, such as the meditative attainment of cessation for abiding in comfort in this life, for the purpose of disciples, but he does not manifest them. Immutable arhats possess the second and also the last degeneration because they do not obtain the eighteen unmixed qualities of a buddha and so on. The term “also” includes the degeneration of enjoyment. Other beings of dull faculty, such as the five arhats, learners on the path of meditation, and ordinary beings, have three types of degeneration. Therefore the explanation that immutable arhats can degenerate from abiding in comfort in this life refers to the degeneration of enjoyment. Arhats who are not immutable possess degeneration of liberation. Regarding those other arhats, a sūtra states: Arhats liberated according to circumstances fully degenerate due to five conditions and five causes. What are those five? They are: engaging in action, engaging in speech, engaging in dispute, roaming for long periods, and succumbing to long-term illness.[1712] Vaibhāṣikas say that such outcomes constitute both the degeneration of abiding in comfort in this life and the degeneration of liberation.

mdo sde pa la sogs pa ni mdo las/ mthong ba'i chos la bde bar gnas pa lhag pa'i sems las byung ba bzhi zhes bya ba ni bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi bzhi'o/ / bzhi po de dag las gang yang rung ba zhig las las 'di yongs su nyams par 'gyur ba ni nga smra'i zhes gsungs pa ni yongs su nyams pa'i chos can la sogs pa lnga'i dbang du byas pa yin no/ / 'di gcig pus sems kyi rnam par grol ba mi g.yo ba'i bar du lus kyis mngon sum du byas pa gang yin pa de las ni 'di rnam grangs gang gis kyang yongs su nyams par 'gyur bar nga mi smra'o zhes gsungs pa ni rnam par grol ba las ni dgra bcom pa thams cad la nyams pa med par ston pa yin la/ ma thob pa las nyams pa dang nye bar spyad pa las nyams pa ni ma thob pa dang ma spyad pa la nyams pa'i ming gis btags pa tsam yin la nyams pa don dam pa ni thob pa las nyams pa yin no zhes 'dod do/ / de lta mod kyis bye brag tu smra ba dgra bcom pa la'ang rnam par grol ba la nyams pa 'dod pas dgra bcom pa nyams pa'i phyir shi nas 'khor bar skye bar 'gyur ro zhe na

Sautrāntikas and so on assert that this is stated from the perspective of the five arhats such as arhats who fully degenerate. For the statement in a sūtra that “the four special mental factors that abide in comfort in this life”[1713] refers to the four actual bases of absorption, and “I do say that there is complete degeneration from any obtainment of these four” is stated from the perspective of the five arhats, such as arhats who fully degenerate. The statement in a sūtra that “I do not say there is any corresponding complete degeneration of the physical manifestion of the immutable liberation of mind alone” teaches that there is no degeneration of any arhat from the state of liberation. The degeneration of nonobtainment and the degeneration of enjoyment are merely designated as “degeneration of nonobtainment” and “degeneration of enjoyment,” but ultimate degeneration is the degeneration of obtainment. Question: Indeed, since Vaibhāṣikas assert that arhats can degenerate from liberation, wouldn’t arhats whose liberation has degenerated be reborn in saṃsāra after death?
'bras las nyams pa 'chi ba med/ / bya ba ma yin de mi byed/ / mi g.yo rnam grol bar chad med/ / lam dgu'o shin tu bsten phyir ro/ / 60
Those who degenerate from their result do not die. They do not commit improper actions. Immutable arhats upgrade during the nine liberated and uninterrupted paths. Dull faculty relies on both. (6:60)
mi 'gyur te/
Reply: They would not [be reborn in saṃsāra], [567]

'bras bu las yongs su nyams pa ni 'ga' yang nyams bzhin du 'chi 'pho ba med de/ dran pa dang shes bzhin gyis myur ba kho nar sor chud par byed pa'i phyir te/ mdo las/ dge slong dag 'phags pa nyan thos thos pa dang ldan pa la dran pa nyams pa chung ngu 'byung mod kyi 'on kyang yang kho nar nub pa dang yongs su zad pa dang yongs su gtugs par 'gyur ro zhes 'byung 'i phyir ro/ / de lta ma yin na tshangs par spyod pa yid brtan du mi rung bar 'gyur ro/ / gal te 'bras bu la gnas pa dang 'gal ba'i bya ba byed pa srid pa'i phyir yongs su nyams pa sor chud par mi 'gyur ba dag kyang srid par 'gyur ro zhe na/ 'bras bu la gnas pa de ni bya ba ma yin pa srog gcod pa la sogs pa gang yin pa de mi byed de/ zag pa med pa'i lam mngon du gyur pas dran pa dang shes bzhin myur ba kho nar skye ba'i phyir rtsal bo che 'gred kyang rdeg mi 'cha' ba bzhin no/ / yang gal te dbang po 'pho ba dag bar chad med pa dang rnam grol gyi lam dus 'pho zhe na/

because arhats who fully degenerate from their result do not die and change abodes while existing in a degenerated state; they necessarily restore their former state quickly through mindfulness and introspection. A sūtra observes: Monks, indeed ārya śrāvakas who are learned may experience a minor degeneration of mindfulness, but that [degeneration] subsides, fully ends, and fully vanishes.[1714] If that were not so, it would be unsuitable to rely on celibacy.[1715] Question: Because it is possible to abide in the result but engage in actions that counter it, is it also possible to completely degenerate and not restore that state? Reply: Those abiding in the result do not commit improper actions (akārya) such as taking life because mindfulness and introspection quickly arise for they have manifested the uncontaminated path. They are just like an agile person who slips but does not strike the ground. Question: Do those who upgrade their intellectual faculty do so when on the interrupted or the liberated path?

rtogs pa'i skal ba dang ldan pa zhig mi g.yo bar 'pho na rnam par grol ba'i lam dgu dang bar chad med pa'i lam dgu ste bco brgyad kyis 'pho ste/ mi slob pa dbang po rtul po'i rigs de slob pa dang mi slob pa'i lam gnyis kyis shin tu bsten cing goms par byas pas spang dka' ba'i phyir ro/ / rgyu mtshan de mtshungs pa'i phyir nyams pa'i chos can la sogs pa 'chi bar sems pa la sogs par 'pho ba la'ang rnam grol gyi lam dgu dang bar chad med pa'i lam dgu yin par gsal lo/ /

Reply: If one who penetrates to realization upgrades to one who is immutable (akopya), he upgrades during the eighteen stages of the nine liberated paths (vimuktimārga) and the nine uninterrupted paths (ānantaryamārga). One who is by type a learner of dull faculty fully relies on and cultivates both learner and nonlearner paths because that state is difficult to abandon. When one who fully degenerates and so on upgrades to one intent on death, it is clear that it is through the nine liberated paths and the nine uninterrupted paths, because the earlier reason equally applies.

mthong bas thob la re re'o/ / zag med mi yi nang du 'phel/ / mi slob sa dgu la bsten te/ / slob pa drug la gang gi phyir/ / 61 'phel ba 'bras bu khyad par can/ / btang ste 'bras bu thob par 'gyur/ / sangs rgyas gnyis dang nyan thos bdun/ / de dgu dbang po rnam dgu can/ / 62

One who obtains results through insight, in each, uncontaminated, enhanced among humans. A nonlearner, in dependence on nine. A learner depends on six levels. (6:61)
Why do they upgrade? They relinquish the special result to obtain the result. Both buddhas and seven śrāvakas are nine because they possess nine types of faculty. (6:62)

{slob pa }dad pas mos pa zhig mthong bas thob pa rtogs par byed pa la ni bar chad med pa dang rnam grol gyi lam re re{ kho na la skye ba} yin te/ goms pa chung bas spang sla ba'i phyir ro/ / {slob mi slob gang yin yang } sbyor ba'i lam ni mi g.yo bar 'pho ba dang mthong thob tu 'pho ba thams cad kyi yang gcig kho na yin no/ /

{A learner} resolute in faith who upgrades his realization to one who obtains results through insight (dṛṣṭlabha) {only generates that realization} in each uninterrupted and liberated path. Abandonment is easier [for one who upgrades] since it requires less cultivation. {Whether one is a learner or nonlearner,} the path of preparation is the single means of all who upgrade to immutability or upgrade to obtainment by insight.

dbang po sbyor ba'i bar chad med pa dang rnam grol gyi lam de yang 'phags pa yin na zag med kho na yin te/ dor bar bya ba'i dbang po'am lam yang zag med yin na zag bcas kyis 'dor ba mi srid pa'i phyir{ te dman pas mchog las nges par mi 'byung bas so/ /} {mthong ba las 'pho ba med ces } so so'i skye bo ni zag bcas kyis 'pho ba yin no/ /

Further, if those working to upgrade their intellectual faculty on the uninterrupted and liberated paths are āryas, they utilize the uncontaminated (anāsrava) path alone. If the faculty or path to be replaced is uncontaminated, it is impossible for it to be replaced by a contaminated path {since inferior states certainly do not arise from superior states.} Ordinary beings upgrade through contaminated paths, {for it is said “They do not upgrade on the path of seeing. (6:58d)”}

dbang po 'pho pa de yang{ rten} mi kho na'i nang du{ nyams pa srid pas} 'phel zhing 'pho'i gzhan du ni ma yin te/ ngan song ba la lam mi rten pa'i phyir dang*/ khams gong ma na nyams pa med pa'i phyir dang*/ nyams pas 'jigs nas dbang po 'pho ba yin pa la/ 'dod pa'i lha bden pa mthong ba rnams ni dbang po rnon po kho na yin te/ yul bzang po dag gis yid byung nas lam goms pas de la dmigs nas nyon mongs pa mi 'byung bas nyams pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang khams gsum char na dgra bcom pa drug gi dbye ba yod par 'dod pa ltar na khams gong ma na'ang dbang po sbyong ba yod de/ nyams pa'i chos can la sogs pa srid pa'i phyir dang*/ nyams bzhin du dgra bcom pa mya ngan las 'da' ba'ang mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te nyams par dogs pa dang bcas pa yin gyi nyams pa ni ma yin no zhes bya bar 'dod na de ni 'chi bar sems pa dang rjes su bsrung ba'i chos can yin no/ / nyams pa'i chos can med na rjes su bsrung ba'i chos can dang 'chi bar sems pa'ang mi srid de/ de dag ni nyams pas 'jigs pa yin na de yang khams gong ma na mi srid pa'i phyir zhes bya ba'ang dpyad par bya'o/ /

Intellectual faculty is upgraded or enhanced (vardhana) among human (nṛṣu) {beings, since degeneration is possible for them,} but not among others, because those of lower rebirths are not a basis of the path and there is no degeneration in higher realms. Arhats who do degenerate upgrade their intellectual faculty out of fear. Desire-realm gods who see the four noble truths possess sharp faculty alone. And those of the fine abodes do not degenerate, since they cultivate the path out of disgust and afflictions do not arise from focusing on that. Moreover, in accordance with the assertion of the sixfold classification of arhats in the three realms, [568] upgrading faculty also exists in the higher realms because arhats who degenerate and so on are possible, and it is impossible for an arhat to attain nirvāṇa once he has degenerated. It is said that one who has fear of degeneration but has not degenerated is one intent on death or one guarding the path. If there are none who degenerate, then also one intent on death and one who guards the path would be impossible, because they fear degeneneration. Also, that would be impossible in higher realms. These statements should be analyzed.

Regarding those who upgrade intellectual faculty, a nonlearner (aśaikṣa) who upgrades his intellectual faculty upgrades it in dependence on nine uncontaminated levels — (1–6) the six levels of absorption and (7–9) the first three formless-realm states — {because it is possible that such a result is subsumed by the nine levels. It is similar to the method of obtaining the result}. A learner (śaikṣa) {who is a once returner depends on unrestricted access concentration, and a nonreturner} depends on the six levels of absorption {and does not depend on formless-realm levels}. Why do they upgrade (vardhaya) their intellectual faculty from dull to sharp? They relinquish (tyaktva) the ordinary and special result (saviśeṣaphala) of once return and nonreturn of those of dull faculty, because they seek to obtain (āpnoti) the ordinary result (phala) of once return and nonreturn of those of sharp faculty. And since nonreturners abandon factors associated with inferior states, they are differentiated [from once returners]; and since they do not focus on desire-realm objects, the path of seeing does not exist at this point; and also those {ordinary abiders in the result of nonreturn and so on} of the formless realm do not [upgrade].
yang dgra bcom pa de dag ni rnam pa dgur dbye ste/
Again, these arhats are classified in nine

sangs rgyas dang rang sangs rgyas gnyis dang*/ nyan thos yongs su nyams pa'i chos can la sogs pa lnga dang*/ mi g.yo ba la sbyangs pa las gyur pa dang*/ dang po nas mi g.yo ba'i chos can te mi g.yo ba gnyis te bdun no/ / de la sangs rgyas gnyis ni mi g.yo ba'i bye brag kho na yin la gnyis ka'i cha las rnam grol yang yin no/ / 'phags pa'i gang zag de dag dgur bzhag pa ni dbang po rtul po dang 'bring po dang rnon po gsum po re re la'ang gsum gsum du phye bas rnam pa dgu can yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de la nyams pa'i chos can dang 'chi bar sems pa dang rjes su bsrung ba'i chos can gsum ni dbang po rtul po'i chung ngu 'bring chen po gsum dang*/ gnas pa las mi bskyod pa dang rab tu rtogs pa'i skal ba can dang sbyangs pa las gyur pa'i mi g.yo ba gsum ni 'bring po'i chung ngu 'bring po gsum dang*/ dang po nas mi g.yo ba'i chos can dang rang sangs rgyas dang sangs rgyas gsum ni rnon po'i chung ngu 'bring chen po gsum yin no/ /

because there are both (1) buddhas and (2) pratyekabuddhas, and seven śrāvakas, including the five (3–7) who fully degenerate and so on, and the two immutable arhats: (8) immutable arhats arising from training and (9) immutable arhats from the beginning. The first two buddhas [i.e., buddhas and pratyekabuddhas] are subsets of immutable arhats alone. They are also arhats liberated from both aspects.[1716] These ārya beings are posited as nine because they possess nine types due to classifying intellectual faculty as dull, medium, and sharp, and differentiating each of those in three. Three arhats — (1) arhats who fully degenerate, (2) arhats intent on death, and (3) arhats who guard the path — represent the small, medium, and great stages of dull faculty. Three more arhats — (4) arhats who are steadfast, (5) arhats who enter realization, and (6) immutable arhats who arise from training — are the small, medium, and great stages of medium faculty. Three remaining arhats — (7) immutable arhats from the beginning, (8) pratyekabuddhas, and (9) buddhas — are the small, medium, and great stages of sharp faculty. [569]
gnyis pa gang zag bdun du bsdu ba ni
Sevenfold classification of ārya beings
gang zag bdun po sbyor ba dang / / dbang po snyoms 'jug rnam grol dang / / gnyis kas byas pa'o de dag drug / 'di ltar lam gsum la gnyis gnyis/ / 63
Those seven beings arise due to preparation, faculty, meditative attainment, liberation, and both. There are six, two each for the three paths. (6:63)

'phags pa'i gang zag ni bdun te/ dad pas rjes 'brang dang*/ chos kyi rjes 'brang dang*/ dad pas mos pa dang*/ mthong bas thob pa dang*/ lus kyis mngon sum du byed pa dang*/ shes rab kyis rnam par grol ba dang*/ {sangs rgyas gnyis kyang 'dir 'dus so } gnyis ka'i cha las rnam par grol ba'o/ /

Ārya beings have seven types because there are (1) followers of faith, (2) followers of reality, (3) those resolute in faith, (4) those obtaining results by insight, (5) those who physically manifest cessation, (6) arhats liberated by wisdom, {and the two types of buddha are subsumed here}, and (7) arhats liberated from both aspects.

gang zag bdun po de dag kyang sbyor bas byas pa las ni dang po gnyis te/ dang po sbyor lam la sogs pa'i dus nas gzhan gyi dring la 'jog pa dang mi 'jog pa'i { ra don la sbyar bas thob pa} phyir ro/ / dbang pos byas pa las ni gsum pa dang bzhi pa ste/ gnyis ka la gnyis ka yod kyang dad pas mos pa lhag pa dang shes rab lhag par yod pa'i sgo nas rim pa ltar dbang po rtul ba dang rno {bas der 'jog } ba'i phyir ro/ / snyoms 'jug gis byas pa las ni lnga pa ste/ 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug lus kyis mngon sum du byed nus{ pas 'jog} pa'i phyir ro/ / {nyon mongs las } rnam par grol bas byas pa las ni drug pa ste/ bdag med rtogs pa'i shes rab kyis khams gsum gyi nyon mongs pa las grol ba'i phyir ro/ / snyoms par 'jug pa dang rnam par grol ba gnyis kas byas pa las ni bdun pa ste/ ting nge 'dzin dang shes rab kyi stobs kyis rim pa ltar snyoms 'jug dang nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa'i cha gnyis ka las grol ba'i phyir ro/ /

Among those seven beings (pudgala), (1–2) the first two arise due to preparation (prayoga) because from the time of the path of preparation and so on, {those states are obtained by the preparation producing that,} where the first is established in reliance on other states but the second is not so established. (3–4) The third and fourth arise due to their faculty (akṣa) because {they are established here by} dull faculty and sharp faculty due to excelling in either resolute faith or wisdom, though each exists for both. (5) The fifth type arises due to meditative attainment (samāpatti); {they are established due to} being able to physically manifest the meditative attainment of cessation. (6) The sixth arises due to liberation (vimukta) {from affliction} because they are liberated from affliction of the three levels by wisdom comprehending selflessness. (7) The seventh arises due to both meditative attainment and liberation because they are liberated from both aspects — the obscurations to meditative attainment and afflictive obscurations — by the power of concentration and wisdom, respectively.

de ltar na ming gi sgo nas bdun yin la bdun po de dag kyang rdzas su ni drug yin te/ 'di ltar mthong sgom mi slob pa'i lam gsum po la dbang po rno rtul gyis rim pa ltar dad pas rjes 'brang dang chos kyi rjes 'brang dang*/ dad mos mthong thob dang*/ dus dang sbyor ba dang mi sbyor ba'i gang zag gnyis gnyis yin pa'i phyir ro/{ gzhan dag ni rdzas logs su med do/ /} de la dad pa'i rjes 'brang la dbang pos dbye na rno rtul 'bring po gsum dang*/ rigs kyis nyams pa'i chos can la sogs pa lnga dang*/ lam gyis shes bzod bco lnga dang*/ 'dod chags dang bral bas ni bdun cu rtsa gsum ste/ 'dod pa'i sgom spang gcig kyang ma spangs pa 'ching ba mtha' dag dang ldan pa dang 'dod pa nas ci yang med pa'i bar sa brgyad la nyon mongs pa dgu dgu las 'dod chags dang bral ba'o/ / rten gyis dgu ste/ sgra mi snyan na lam med pas rten du mi rung ba'i phyir gling gsum gyi mi dang 'dod pa'i lha drug go /de ltar na dbang po dang rigs dang lam dang 'dod chags dang bral ba dang rten gyi sgo nas dbye na 'bum bzhi khri bdun stong brgyad brgya nyi shu rtsa lngar gyur te gang zag gzhan dag kyang ci rigs par de bzhin du dbye bar bya'o/ / de yang chos kyi rjes 'brang dang mthong thob dang dus dang mi sbyor bar grol ba rnams la ni rigs kyis dbye ba med la/ dad mos dang dus kyis rnam grol gnyis la ni rigs lnga'i dbye ba yod do/ /

yang dad mos mthong thob la lam gyi sgo nas ni slob dpon rgyal po'i sras ltar na 'bras bu la gnas pa'i sems kyi skad cig bcu drug pa lam la rjes shes kyi dbang du byas nas dbye ba med la/ skal ldan khyad par can ni sa dgu la rten pa'i lam dgur 'dod do/ / lus kyis mngon sum du byed pa ni dad mos mthong thob tu 'dus pas logs su brtsir med de/ gal te brtsi na dbang po'i sgo nas gsum dang*/ rigs kyi sgo nas dad mos yin na lnga dang*/ mthong thob yin na dbye ba med do/ / lam dang 'dod chags dang bral ba la'ang dbye ba med do/ / rten ni skal ldan khyad par can ni 'dod pa nas srid rtse'i bar du 'dod la rgyal po'i sras ni gling gsum gyi mi dang lha ris drug ste dgu dang*/ gzugs na gnas bcu drug dang*/ srid rtse dang nyi shu rtsa drug tu 'dod do/ / shes rab kyis rnam grol kyang dus kyis rnam grol yin na rigs lnga dang*/ dus dang mi sbyor ba yin na ni rigs la dbye ba med do/ / de las gzhan ni dad pas rjes 'brang bzhin no/

Again, according to Jinaputra those resolute in faith and those obtaining results by insight are not classified from the perspective of subsequent knowledge of the truth of path of the sixteenth moment of mind that abides as a result, but those with special status have nine paths supported on nine levels. Those who physically manifest cessation are included in those resolute in faith and those obtaining results by insight, and therefore they have no separate enumeration. If enumerated there are three by faculty, and if those resolute in faith are classified by type there are five. Those obtaining results by insight have no classification: they have no classification by path or classification by freedom from attachment. Their basis is those with special status who exist from the desire realm to the summit of existence. Jinaputra asserts twenty-six: (1–3) humans of the three continents, (4–9) the six types of desire-realm god, (10–25) the sixteen abodes of the form realm, and (26) the summit of existence. Arhats liberated by wisdom or liberated according to circumstances have five by lineage. But arhats liberated regardless of circumstances are not classified by lineage. Those different from that are like followers of faith.

{Followers of reality are 29,565.[1717] They are not classified by lineage but are classified in three, fifteen, seventy-three, and nine types by faculty, path, freedom from attachment, and basis. Followers of faith are classified as five by type. Those resolute in faith are 9,855,[1718] since they are classified in three, five, seventy-three, and nine by faculty, lineage, freedom from attachment, and basis; they are not classified by path since they exist on the sixteenth moment of the path alone. Those obtaining results by insight are 1,971.[1719] They are not classified by type or path but are classified in three, seventy-three, and nine by faculty, freedom from attachment, and basis. They constitute one-fifth the number of those resolute in faith.}
'di dag gi dbye ba ni grangs zhib tu TIk+ka las 'byung mod kyi 'dir ma bkod do/ / 'o na gnyis ka'i cha las rnam par grol ba dang shes rab kyis rnam par grol ba gang zhe na/
The classification of these indeed occurs in great detail in the Subcommentary, but it is not set out here. Question: Who are arhats liberated from both aspects and arhats liberated by wisdom?
'gog thob gnyis ka las rnam grol/ / shes rab kyis ni cig shos so/ /
Those who obtain cessation are liberated from both aspects. A liberation by wisdom is distinct from that. (6:64ab)

gang zhig bsam gtan dngos gzhi la brten nas 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug thob pa{ 'i dgra bcom pa} de ni gnyis ka'i cha las rnam par grol ba yin te/ shes rab kyis nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dang ting nge 'dzin gyis rnam par thar pa'i sgrib pa las kyang grol ba'i phyir ro/ / de la rnam par thar ba'i sgrib pa ni{ le lo dang} dmigs pa brjed pa dang bying pa dang rgod pa dang rtsol ba dang mi rtsol ba'i nyes pa lnga la sogs pa ste/ TIka byed dag gis rnam par thar pa'i sgrib pa ni gang gis rnam par thar pa dang bsam gtan dag skyed par mi nus pa ste lus dang sems las su mi rung ba nyid do zhes pa dang*/ snyoms par 'jug pa'i sgrib pa ni gang zhig yod na sems las su mi rung bas khams gsum gyi 'dod chags dang bral ba dag gis kyang bsam gtan dang po'i dngos gzhi yang bskyed par mi nus pa ste zhes bshad pas bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs kho na la brten pa yin la/ de yang gang zag ni nyan thos la srid kyi sangs rgyas gnyis ni gnyis ka'i cha las rnam grol kho na yin pas rnam thar dang snyoms 'jug gi sgrib pa ma spangs pa mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang rgyud bla ma las/ nyon mongs shes bya snyoms 'jug gi /sgrib gsum las ni nges grol te/ / zhes sgrib pa gsum par bshad pa'am/ yang na dbus mtha' las/ nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dang*/ shes bya'i sgrib pa nyid du bstan/ / der ni sgrib pa thams cad de/ / de zad nas ni grol bar 'dod ces gsungs pa ltar na shes bya'i sgrib par 'dus so/ /

Reply: Those {arhats} who obtain the meditative attainment of cessation (nirodha) in dependence on the four actual bases of absorption are liberated from both aspects (ubhayato vimukta): (1) liberated from afflictive obscurations by wisdom and (2) liberated from obscurations to liberation[1720] by concentration. Obscurations to liberation are the five faults: (1) {laziness}, (2) forgetting the focal object, (3) laxity and excitation, (4) exertion, and (5) nonexertion and so on. The Subcommentary states: The obscurations to liberation are the inflexibility of body and mind that is the incapacity to generate liberation and the absorptions.[1721] And: If obscurations to meditative attainment exist, then even those who are free of attachment to the three realms cannot generate the actual basis of the first absorption since their minds are not flexible. Therefore they depend on access concentration to the first absorption [571] alone. In terms of the person, it is possible for a śrāvaka. But it is impossible that the two buddhas do not abandon obscurations to liberation and meditative attainment since they are necessarily liberated from both aspects. Further, the Sublime Continuum explains: They are definitely liberated from the three obscurations of affliction, knowledge, and meditative attainment.[1722] This passage states three obscurations. Again, Differentiating the Middle and Extremes declares: Afflictive obscurations and knowledge obscurations are taught. They constitute all obscurations here. Their elimination is asserted to be liberation.[1723] According to this passage, they [that is, meditative attainment obscurations] are included in knowledge obscurations.

de lta na nyan rang gis shes sgrib spangs par 'gyur ro zhe na/ shes sgrib mtha' dag spang ba la ni khyab pa med la shes sgrib kyi bye brag 'ga' zhig spangs pa ni 'dod pa nyid de/ dper na nyer bsdogs la 'jug mi shes pa shes sgrib yin kyang des spangs pa bzhin no/ / de nyid kyi phyir rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las kyang rnam thar rnams ni shes bya'i sgrib pa las rnam par thar bas rab tu phye ba yin te/ shes bya'i sgrib pa ji tsam las nyan thos dang rang sangs rgyas rnams kyi sems rnam par grol bar 'gyur ba yin no/ / zhes bshad do/ / gang zhig bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs tsam la brten nas bdag med rtogs pa'i shes rab kyi stobs kyis nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa 'ba' zhig las rnam par grol ba de ni gnyis ka'i cha las rnam grol las cig shos shes rab kyis rnam par grol ba ste/ de dag las dgra bcom pa rgyan can dang*/ rgyan med ces bya bar grags so/

Objection: In that case śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas would abandon knowledge obscurations? Reply: There is no logical pervasion that they abandon all knowledge obscurations, but it is asserted that they abandon some specific knowledge obscurations. For example, not knowing entry to access concentration is a knowledge obscuration, but they abandon it. Therefore the Compendium of Ascertainment explains: Liberation is differentiated as liberation from knowledge obscurations, for it is the liberation of the minds of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas from any measure of knowledge obscuration.[1724] Liberation from just afflictive obscurations by the power of wisdom (prajñā) realizing selflessness, in dependence on access concentration to the first absorption alone, is a liberation by wisdom that is distinct from liberation from both aspects. Beings possessing them are known as ornamented or unornamented arhats.
gsum pa gnyis su dbye ba ni
Twofold classification of ārya beings
gal te slob pa dang mi slob pa rdzogs pa gnyis bshad na de dag ji ltar yin zhe na/
Question: If both learners and nonlearners are said to be “completed by something,” how are they completed?
snyoms 'jug dbang po 'bras rnams kyis/ / slob pa yongs rdzogs zhes bya'o/ / 64
They are called learners who achieve fruition by meditative attainment, faculty, or the result. (6:64cd)

snyoms par 'jug pas slob pa rdzogs pa ni 'gog pa lus kyis mngon sum du byed pa'i phyir mi 'ong ba'o/ / dbang pos rdzogs pa ni mthong bas thob pa'o/ / 'bras bus rdzogs pa ni phyir mi 'ong ba'i 'bras bu la gnas pa'o/ / de ltar na chos gsum po rnams kyis slob pa yongs su rdzogs pa zhes bya ste/ mdo las/ 'di la gang zhig nyon mongs lnga spangs te/ / mi 'phrogs chos ldan slob pa yongs su rdzogs/ / zhes gsungs te/ de la nyon mongs ni tha ma'i cha mthun lnga ste/ de spangs pas ni 'bras bus rdzogs pa bstan to/ / gzhan gyis bslab pa mi 'phrog pas ni mthong thob yin pas dbang pos rdzogs pa'o/ / mthong ba'i chos la bde bar gnas pa 'gog pa lus kyis mngon sum du byed pa dang ldan pas ni snyoms 'jug gis rdzogs pa'o/ /

Reply: Learners who achieve fruition by meditative attainment (samāpatti) are nonreturners who physically manifest cessation. Those who achieve fruition by [intellectual] faculty (indriya) are those who obtain results by insight. Those who achieve fruition by the result (phala) are those abiding in the result of nonreturn. Thus they are called learners who achieve fruition (paripūrṇatā) by three factors. A sūtra declares: Here those who abandon five afflictions, those not deprived, and those who possess [comfort] in this life are learners who achieve fruition.[1725] “Afflictions” refer to the “five” factors associated with inferior states, and those who abandon them are those who achieve fruition by the result. “Those not deprived” of training by others are those who obtain results by their insight who achieve fruition by [intellectual] faculty. “Those abiding in comfort in this life” are those who achieve fruition by meditative attainment through possessing the physical manifestation of cessation.

'di la'ang phyir mi 'ong gi 'bras bu ma thob par 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug mi 'thob pas na 'bras bus rdzogs pa ni khyab che la dbang po dang snyoms 'jug gis rdzogs pa ni khyab chung ba yin no/ / de'i phyir 'bras bus rdzogs pa ni phyir mi 'ong ba'i 'bras bu thob pa thams cad yin la/ dbang po dang gnyis kyis rdzogs pa ni phyir mi 'ong ba'i 'bras bu la gnas pa mthong thob lus kyis mngon sum du mi byed pa'o/ / snyoms 'jug dang gsum gyis rdzogs pa ni phyir mi 'ong ba'i 'bras bu la gnas pa mthong thob lus kyis mngon sum du byed pa'o/ / 'bras bu dang snyoms 'jug gnyis kyis rdzogs pa ni phyir mi 'ong dad mos lus kyis mngon sum du byed pa'o/ / dbang po kho nas rdzogs pa ni mthong thob 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang ma bral ba'i 'phags pa'o/ / 'bras bu kho nas rdzogs pa ni phyir mi 'ong dad mos lus kyis mngon sum du mi byed pa'o/ / dbang po dang snyoms 'jug gnyis kho nas rdzogs pa dang*/ snyoms 'jug kho nas rdzogs pa ni mi srid de/ mthong thob yin kyang phyir mi 'ong ba/ 'bras bu ma thob par slob pa rdzogs pa mi srid pa'i phyir dang*/ 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang ma bral bar phyir mi 'ong gi 'bras gnas mi 'thob la de ma thob par 'gog pa la snyoms par 'jug pa mi srid pa'i phyir dang*/ 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i slob pa'ang phyir mi 'ong ba'i 'bras bu la gnas par nges pa'i phyir ro/ /

Those who do not obtain the result of nonreturn are more likely to achieve fruition by the result and less likely to achieve fruition by meditative attainment, since they do not obtain the meditative attainment of cessation. [572] Therefore those who achieve fruition by the result are all those who obtain the result of nonreturn. Those who achieve fruition by two factors, including [intellectual] faculty, are those obtaining results by insight who abide in the result of nonreturn but who do not physically manifest cessation. Those who achieve fruition by three factors, including meditative attainment, are those obtaining results by insight who abide in the result of nonreturn and physically manifest cessation. Those who achieve fruition by both the result and meditative attainment are nonreturners resolute in faith who physically manifest cessation. Those who achieve fruition by [intellectual] faculty alone are āryas free of attachment to desire-realm objects who obtain results by insight. Those who achieve fruition by the result alone are nonreturners resolute in faith who do not physically manifest cessation. Those who achieve fruition by both [intellectual] faculty and meditative attainment alone and those who achieve fruition by meditative attainment alone are not possible, because it is impossible for nonreturners who obtain results by insight to complete the path of a learner without obtaining the result. That is because without freedom from attachment to sense objects, they do not obtain abidance in the result of nonreturn, the meditative attainment of cessation is impossible without obtaining that, and learners free of attachment to desire-realm objects definitely abide in the result of nonreturn.
gnyis kyis mi slob yongs su rdzogs/ /
Nonlearners achieve fruition by both. (6:65a)

dbang po dang snyoms 'jug gnyis kyis ni mi slob pa yongs su rdzogs pa yin te/ 'bras bus yongs su ma rdzogs pa'i mi slob pa mi srid pas 'bras bu rdzogs pa ni ma bshad do/ / dbang pos rdzogs pa ni shes rab kyis rnam par grol ba dus dang mi sbyor ba'o/ / snyoms 'jug gis rdzogs pa ni gnyis ka'i cha las grol ba dus kyi rnam par grol ba'o/ / dbang po dang snyoms 'jug gnyis kas rdzogs pa ni gnyis ka'i cha las rnam par grol ba dus dang mi sbyor ba'o// //

Nonlearners achieve fruition by both faculty and meditative attainment. Those who achieve fruition by the result are not mentioned since it is impossible that nonlearners achieve fruition by the result. Those who achieve fruition by [intellectual] faculty are arhats liberated by wisdom regardless of circumstances. Those who achieve fruition by meditative attainment are arhats liberated from both aspects according to circumstances. Those who achieve fruition by both [intellectual] faculty and meditative attainment are arhats liberated from both aspects regardless of circumstances.
lnga pa mngon par rtogs pa'i lam ston pa ni
30. The Path of Realization
lam gyi dbye ba dang*/ byang chub kyi phyogs dang mthun pa'i lam bshad pa gnyis las
There are two types: classification of the path, and the path conducive to enlightenment.
dang po ni
Classification of the path

'o na 'jig rten pa dang*/ 'jig rten las 'das pa dang*/ mthong ba dang*/ sgom pa dang*/ mi slob pa'i lam dang*/ sbyor ba dang*/ bar chad med pa dang*/ rnam grol dang*/ khyad par gyi lam zhes bya ba mang po zhig bshad pa de dag bsdu na du zhig yin zhe na/

Question: Many paths are explained, such as mundane and transcendent paths; the paths of seeing, meditation, and no more learning; and the path of preparation and the uninterrupted, liberated, and special paths. If these are summarized, how many are there?
mdor na lam ni rnam bzhi ste/ / khyad par can dang rnam grol dang / / bar chad med dang sbyor zhes bya/ / 65
In brief, paths have four types: special, liberated, uninterrupted, and preparation. (6:65bcd)

mdor bsdu na lam thams cad ni 'chad pa na 'don pa bsgyur te/ sbyor dang bar chad med pa dang*/ / rnam grol khyad par can zhes bya ba rnam pa bzhir rig par bya ste/ de la dang po ni bar chad med pa'i lam gyi rgyu yin no/ / gnyis pa ni sgrib pa la dngos su gnod pa byed pa'o/ / gsum pa ni sgrib pa las grol ba dang por skyes pa'o/ / bzhi pa ni de phyin chad kyi rnam par grol ba'i lam ste/ de yang mthong ba'i lam lta bu la dper brjod na go rim bzhin du nges 'byed cha mthun rnams dang*/ bzod pa brgyad dang*/ shes pa rnams dang*/ sgom pa'i lam rnams sbyor ba la sogs pa bzhi yin pa bzhin no/ / de la dang po gnyis ni rnam par grol ba'i khang bzang du 'gro ba'i phyir lam yin la/ phyi ma gnyis ni de dang 'dra ba'i phyir rgyu bsags pa'i sgo nas snga ma bas ches khyad par du 'gro ba'i phyir dang*/ gong nas gong du phyin par byed pa'i phyir ram/ de dag skyes na lhag med du 'jug pa'i phyir lam mo/ /

Reply: You should recognize that, in brief, all paths have four types, explained in the verse, “Preparation (prayoga), uninterrupted (anantara), liberated (vimukti), and special (viśeṣa).” The first is the cause of the uninterrupted path. The second directly harms the obscurations. The third is when liberation from obscuration first arises. The fourth [573] is the liberated path beyond that. To illustrate this with the path of seeing, then (1) the factors conducive to penetrative insight, (2) the eight types of perseverance, (3) the eight types of knowledge, and (4) the path of meditation are, respectively, the four paths of preparation and so on. The first two are paths because they lead to the pristine mansion of liberation. The latter two are paths because they are paths similar to the former two, they more strongly accumulate the causes for proceeding there than the former, they progressively increase the strength of those causes, or they enter remainderless nirvāṇa when they arise.
bsam gtan dag gi lam rnams sla/ / sa gzhan dag gi dka' ba yin/ / blo rtul mngon shes bul ba ste/ / cig shos kyi ni mngon shes myur/ / 66
Those paths of absorption are easy. Paths dependent on other levels are difficult. Higher perception for those with dull intellect is slower. Higher perception for others is faster. (6:66)

yang mdo las/ dge slong dag lam ni rnam pa bzhi ste/ mngon par shes pa bul la dka' ba'i lam dang*/ mngon par shes pa myur la dka' ba'i lam dang*/ mngon par shes pa bul la sla ba'i lam dang*/ mngon par shes pa myur la sla ba'i lam mo zhes gsungs pa de la

Again, a sūtra states: Monks, there are four types of path: higher perception that is a path difficult to slow, higher perception that is a path difficult to speed up, higher perception that is a path easy to slow, and higher perception that is a path easy to speed up.[1726]

bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi bzhi la brten pa dag gi lam rnams ni goms par sla ba yin te/ yan lag gis yongs su zin pa dang*/ zhi gnas dang lhag mthong cha mnyam par 'jug pas 'bad mi dgos par ngang gis 'jug pa'i phyir ro/ / sa gzhan mi lcogs med dang bsam gtan khyad par can dang gzugs med pa rnams la brten pa dag gi lam rnams ni goms par dka' ba yin te/ gzugs med thams cad kyang yan lag gis ma zin pa'i phyir dang*/ dang po gnyis lhag mthong shas che la gzugs med zhi gnas shas che bas 'bad pas bsgrub dgos pa'i phyir ro/ / {lam de'ang gnyis te } gang zag blo gros rtul po ni lam dka' 'am sla yang rung ste shes bya mngon par shes pa bul ba yin la/ blo gros rtul po las cig shos rnon po rnams kyi ni lam dka' 'am sla yang rung ste shes bya mngon par shes pa myur ba yin no/ / des na dbang po rnon po sa gzhan la brten pa ni lam dka' la mngon shes myur ba dang*/ dbang po rtul po bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi la brten pa ni lam sla la mngon shes bul ba dang*/ dbang po rnon po bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi la brten pa ni lam yang sla la mngon shes kyang myur ba dang*/ dbang po rtul po sa gzhan la brten pa ni lam yang dka' la mngon shes kyang bul ba yin no/ /

Those paths dependent on the four actual bases of absorption (dhyāna) are easy (sukhā) to cultivate; one enters them without need for exertion, since they are conjoined with the branches, and they evenly engage calm abiding and insight. Paths dependent on other levels (anyabhūmi), such as unrestricted access concentration, special absorption, and the formless-realm states, are difficult (duḥkha) to cultivate; no formless-realm state is conjoined with the branches, and one must establish them through exertion, since the first two are predominantly insight and the formless realm is predominantly concentration. {Each of those paths has two types, since} higher perception (abhijñā) of objects of knowledge for persons with dull intellect (mandabuddhi) is slower (dhandha), whether the path is difficult or easy. Higher perception of objects of knowledge for others with sharp intellect, who are distinguished from those with dull intellect, is faster (kṣiprā), whether the path is difficult or easy. Therefore those of sharp faculty who depend on other levels have difficult paths but faster higher perception. Those with dull faculties who depend on the actual basis of absorption have easy paths but slower higher perception. Those with sharp faculties who depend on the actual basis of absorption have easy paths and faster higher perception. Those of dull faculty who depend on other paths have difficult paths and slower higher perception.
gnyis pa [byang chub kyi phyogs dang mthun pa'i lam bshad pa]
The path conducive to enlightenment

['di] la rdzas yod dang brtags yod kyi khyad par dang*/ go rim gyi khyad par dang*/ ngo bo dang sa'i khyad par dang*/ shes nas dad pa'i khyad par dang*/ mi slob pa'i chos bcu'i khyad par bshad pa lnga las

There are five topics: (1) substantial existence and nominal existence, (2) the attribute of sequence, (3) the attribute of nature, (4) faith through knowledge, and (5) the ten attributes of a nonlearner.
dang po [rdzas yod dang btags yod kyi khyad par] ni
SUBSTANTIAL EXISTENCE AND NOMINAL EXISTENCE

lam 'di dag gis ni byang chub kyi phyogs mthun zhes bya ba'i ming 'thob bo/ / de dag kyang dran pa nyer gzhag nas 'phags lam yan lag brgyad pa'i bar sum cu rtsa bdun no/ / ci'i phyir de dag la byang chub kyi phyogs dang mthun pa zhes bya zhe na/

These paths are called “factors conducive to enlightenment,” and they number thirty-seven, from the foundations of mindfulness to the eightfold noble path. Question: Why [574] are they called “factors conducive to enlightenment”?
zad dang mi skye shes pa ni/ / byang chub de dang mthun nyid phyir/ / sum cu rtsa bdun de'i phyogs mthun/ / ming gi sgo nas rdzas su bcu/ / 67
Knowledge of elimination and nonarising is enlightenment. Because they are compatible, there are thirty-seven factors conducive to enlightenment in name but ten in substance. (6:67)

sgrib pa zad pa dang phyin chad kyang mi skye ba shes pa ni{ gang zag gi dbye bas} byang chub{ gsum} ces bya ste/ sgrib pa zad cing byang ba'i phyir dang*/ zad cing mi skye bar chub cing rtogs pa'i phyir ro/ / de la zad shes kyis ni bdag gis sdug bsngal shes so zhes pa nas bdag gis lam bsgoms so zhes pa'i bar du yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin rab tu shes so zhes bya bar rang gi don byas pa yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin rtogs pa'i phyir byang chub yin la/ mi skye ba shes pas ni bdag gis sdug bsngal yongs su shes te yang yongs su shes par byar med do zhes pa nas bdag gis lam bsgoms te yang sgom du med do zhes pa'i bar du yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin rab tu shes so zhes bya bar yang byar med pa nyid yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin rtogs pa'i phyir byang chub yin no/ / de lta bu'i byang chub ni nyan thos la sogs pa'i bye brag gis gsum yin no/ /

Reply: Knowledge of the elimination (kṣayajñāna) and subsequent nonarising (anutpāda) of obscurations is called {the three types of} enlightenment (bodhi, Tib. byang chub) {classified by person} because it eliminates and purifies (byang) obscurations, and because it comprehends (chub) and realizes that obscurations are eliminated and do not arise. Knowledge of elimination that correctly knows phenomena as they are is expressed in the words “I know suffering” up to “I have meditated on the path.” It is enlightenment because it comprehends phenomena correctly as they are for achieving one’s own purpose. Knowledge of nonarising that correctly knows phenomena as they are is expressed by the words “I fully know suffering; there is no further training in knowledge” up to “I have meditated on the path; there is no further meditation.”[1727] It is enlightenment because it comprehends phenomena as they are, and there is no further training. Such enlightenment has three categories — śrāvaka enlightenment and so on.

byang chub de dang dngos dang brgyud pa'i sgo nas rjes su mthun pa'i rgyu nyid yin pa'i phyir mdo las dran pa nyer gzhag bzhi la sogs pa sum cu rtsa bdun po la byang chub de'i phyogs dang mthun pa zhes 'byung ngo*/ / sum cu rtsa bdun zhes bya ba'ang ming gi sgo nas yin gyi kha cig gi gzhung lugs ltar na{ mtshan nyid kyi sgo nas} rdzas su ni bcu yin te/

Because they are causes directly or indirectly compatible (anuloma) with enlightenment, in the sūtras they are called “thirty-seven factors (pakṣa) conducive to enlightenment” such as the four foundations of mindfulness. There are said to be thirty-seven in name (nāmata) but are, according to some textual systems, ten in substance (dravyata), {due to their characteristics}.
gang zhe na/
Question: What are they?
dad dang brtson 'grus dran pa dang / / shes rab ting 'dzin btang snyoms dga'/ / rtog dang tshul khrims shin tu sbyangs/ / dran pa nyer gzhag shes rab ste/ / 68
Faith, effort, mindfulness, wisdom, concentration, equanimity, joy, investigation, ethics, pliancy. The foundations of mindfulness are wisdom. (6:68)

rnam par dpyad na dad pa dang brtson 'grus dang dran pa dang shes rab dang ting nge 'dzin dang btang snyoms dang dga' ba dang rtog pa dang tshul khrims dang shin tu sbyangs pa zhes bya ba'i rang bzhin yin pa'i phyir ro/ / {shes rab brgyad dang*/ yang dag spong bzhi/ brtson 'grus kyi dbang stobs gnyis/ brtson 'grus yang dag byang chub kyi yan lag yang dag pa'i rtsol ba dang brgyad brtson 'grus so/ / dbang stobs kyi dran pa gnyis/ dran pa yang dag byang chub yan lag /yang dag pa'i dran pa dang bzhi dran pa/ dbang stobs kyi ting nge 'dzin gnyis/ rdzu 'phrul rkang bzhi/ ting nge 'dzin yang dag byang chub kyi yan lag /yang dag pa'i ting nge 'dzin dang brgyad ting nge 'dzin/ dbang stobs kyi dad pa gnyis dad pa ste rdzas lnga dang*/ yang dag pa'i ngag las mtha' 'tsho ba gsum tshul khrims te rdzas gcig dang*/ btang snyoms dga' ba/ rtog pa shin tu sbyangs pa rnams rdzas re re spyir rdzas bcur 'dod la } ji ltar zhe na/

Reply: If analyzed, there are faith (śraddhā), effort (vīrya), mindfulness (smṛti), wisdom (prajñā), concentration (samādhi), equanimity (upekṣa), joy (prīti), investigation (saṃkalpa), ethics (śīla), and pliancy (praśrabdhi). {In general, ten substances are asserted: (1) the eight that are wisdom;[1728] (2) the eight that are effort: the four correct abandonments, both the faculty and power of effort, the requisite of enlightenment of correct effort, and correct exertion; (3) the four that are mindfulness: both the faculty and power of mindfulness, the requisite of enlightenment of correct mindfulness, and right mindfulness; (4) the eight that are concentration: both the faculty and power of concentration, the four supernatural limbs, the requisite of enlightenment of correct concentration, and right concentration; and (5) two that are faith: the faculty and power of faith. These constitute five substances. (6) Three are ethics and constitute one substance: right speech, right action, and right livelihood. (7) Equanimity, (8) joy, (9) [right] investigation, and (10) pliancy constitute separate substances. Therefore they are, generally speaking, asserted to be ten substances.} Question: How?
{ yang dag pa'i lta ba chos rab tu rnam 'byed dbang stobs kyi shes rab ste bzhi dang*/} dran pa nyer gzhag bzhi{ ste brgyad} ni shes rab kyi rang bzhin yin pa'i phyir dang*/

Reply: (1–4) The four foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthiti) {and the four including (5) right view, (6) correct analysis of phenomena, (7) the faculty of wisdom, and (8) the power of wisdom} constitute {the eight states} that are in essence wisdom (jñāna).
brtson 'grus yang dag 'jog ces bya/ / rdzu 'phrul rkang pa ting 'dzin to/ / gtso bo smos pa de dag ni/ / sbyor byung yon tan kun kyang yin/ / 69
Effort is called correctly setting [the mind]. The supernatural limbs are concentration. This is the central presentation. All are qualities derived from preparation. (6:69)

brtson 'grus la yang dag par 'jog cing spong ba bzhi zhes bya bar brjod pa'i phyir dang*/ rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa bzhi ni ting nge 'dzin gyi rang bzhin yin pa'i phyir dang*/ byang chub kyi yan lag bdun gyi nang nas chos rab tu rnam par 'byed pa yang dag byang chub kyi yan lag dang*/ 'phags lam brgyad kyi nang nas yang dag pa'i lta ba gnyis shes rab yin zhing*/ yang dag pa'i rtsol ba dang brtson 'grus yang dag byang chub kyi yan lag gnyis brtson 'grus yin la/ yang dag pa'i ngag dang las kyi mtha' dang 'tsho ba gsum tshul khrims kyi rang bzhin yin pa'i phyir dang*/ rdzas gcig dbang po lnga dang stobs lnga dang byang chub kyi yan lag gi nang nas dga' ba dang shin tu sbyangs pa dang btang snyoms yang dag byang chub kyi yan lag gsum dang 'phags lam brgyad kyi nang nas yang dag pa'i rtog pa ste dgu po de dag ni rang rang gi ming gis bstan pa'i phyir ro/ / bye brag tu smra ba ltar na tshul khrims kyi yan lag lus ngag gi las rdzas tha dad cing rigs mi mthun pa'i phyir rdzas bcu gcig yin no/ / gzhan dag ni tshul khrims spong ba'i sems pa la 'dod la de gcig yin pa'i phyir rdzas gcig tu 'dod do/ /

Effort (vīrya) is called “correctly setting [the mind]” or the four correct abandonments (samyakprahāṇa). The four supernatural limbs (ṛddhipāda) are the essence of concentration (samādhi). Both the requisite of enlightenment of correct analysis of phenomena from the seven requisites of enlightenment and right view from the eightfold noble path are wisdom. Both right exertion and [575] the requisite of enlightenment of correct effort are effort. The three — right speech, right action, and right livelihood — are in essence ethics. The individual substances of the five faculties; the five powers; the three requisites of enlightenment of correct joy, correct pliancy, correct equanimity; and right investigation from the eightfold noble path are taught by their individual names. In accordance with the Vaibhāṣikas, there are eleven substances, because for them the actions of body and speech, as branches of ethics, are distinct substances of dissimilar type. Others assert that there is one substance of ethics: they assert ethics to be the mind of abandonment and that it is a single mind.

kha cig na re rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las/ dad sogs lnga dang byang chub kyi phyogs dang mthun pa'i chos sum cu rtsa bdun po dag phan tshun bsdus sam zhe na/ sum cu rtsa bdun gyis lnga bsdus kyi lngas ni sum cu rtsa bdun ma bsdus so/ / gang dag ma bsdus she na/ yang dag pa'i ngag dang*/ las kyi mtha' dang*/ 'tsho ba dang*/ dga' ba dang*/ shin tu sbyangs pa dang*/ btang snyoms te drug po rnams so zhes 'byung bas slob dpon 'phags pa ni yang dag pa'i rtog pa shes rab kyi nang du 'dus pa'i phyir dang*/ tshul khrims lus ngag gi las gnyis tha dad par byas nas rdzas bcu yin par bzhed do zhes zer ro/ /

Some say: Master Ārya Asaṅga asserts ten substances because he subsumes right investigation in wisdom and he distinguishes ethics as physical and verbal karma. As the Compendium of Ascertainment states: Do the five of faith and so on and the thirty-seven factors conducive to enlightenment mutually subsume each other? The thirty-seven subsume the five, but the five do not subsume the thirty-seven. What do they not subsume? There are six: right speech, right action, right livelihood, correct joy, correct pliancy, and correct equanimity.[1729]
