de ltar dran pa nyer gzhag shes rab dang*/ yang dag par 'jog pa brtson 'grus dang rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa ting nge 'dzin yin no zhes bya ba'ang gtso bo smros pa yin gyi de dag kyang 'khor dang bcas na ni skyes thob kyi yon tan dad pa la sogs pa ma gtogs pa sbyor ba las byung ba'i yon tan thos pa dang bsam pa dang sgom byung zag bcas zag med dang dga' ba dang shin tu sbyangs pa dang btang snyoms dang yang dag pa'i rtog pa dang dad pa dang dran pa dang tshul khrims la sogs pa kun kyang dran pa nyer gzhag la sogs pa yin no/ / {de dag gi mtshan nyid dang thob pa dang mnyam gzhag gi rig byed ma yin pa yod na'ang de'i skal mnyam yin pas der 'dus la/ sbyor byung smros pa na skyes thob kyi dad sogs der mi 'dod pa'o}

But the assertion that the foundations of mindfulness are wisdom, correct setting [of the mind] is effort, and the supernatural limbs are concentration is the central presentation. Moreover, if these [thirty-seven] possess attributes, then except for qualities obtained from birth such as faith and so on, all are qualities (guṇa) derived from preparation (prāyogika), such as contaminated and uncontaminated [wisdom] derived from hearing, contemplation, and meditation, plus joy, pliancy, equanimity, right investigation, faith, mindfulness, ethics, and so on — and these constitute the foundations of mindfulness and so on. {Their defining characteristics, obtainment, and nonindicative form associated with equipoise also exist. And these are included here, since they share homogeneity with [the thirty-seven]. Faith obtained from birth and so on cannot be asserted in this context since the Abhidharmakośa states “derived from preparation” (6:69d).}

de la dran pa nyer gzhag bzhi ni bshad zin la/ yang dag par spong ba la sogs pa ma bshad pas 'dir bshad par bya ste/ de la sdig pa mi dge ba'i chos skyes pa rnams spang ba'i phyir 'dun pa skyed do/ / 'bad do/ / brtson 'grus rtsom mo/ / sems rab tu 'dzin to/ / yang dag par rab tu 'jog go zhes bya ba dang*/ de bzhin du {ma skyes pa rnams mi skyes pa'i phyir zhes bya ba dang*/}dge ba'i chos ma skyes pa rnams bskyed pa'i phyir zhes bya ba dang*/ skyes pa rnams gnas pa dang*/ mi brjed pa dang*/ bsgom pa yongs su rdzogs par bya ba dang*/ phyir zhing goms pa dang*/ 'phel zhing rgyas pa dang*/ ye shes kyi mngon sum du bya ba'i phyir 'dun pa bskyed do/ / 'bad do/ / brtson 'grus rtsom mo/ / sems rab tu 'dzin to/ / yang dag par rab tu 'jog go zhes mdo las gsungs te/ de la 'dun pa ni bsam pa'o/ / 'bad pa ni sbyor ba'o/ / brtson 'grus ni dngos gzhi'o/ / sems rab tu 'dzin pa dang*/ yang dag par rab tu 'jog pa ni rjes so/ / sdig pa skyes pa spong ba ni mi 'chab pa dang 'gyod pa dang bdag la rnam par smod pa dang bshags pa'i rang bzhin dag yin no/ / de'i phyir 'dun pa la sogs pa ni brtson 'grus so/ / ma skyes pa mi bskyed pa ni dran pa dang shes bzhin dang ldan pas spong bar sems pa'o/ / dge ba ma skyes pa skyed pa ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsten pa la sogs pa'o/ / skyes pa gnas shing 'phel ba ni de'i yon tan shes nas dga' ba'o/ /

The four foundations of mindfulness have been explained already. I will now explain those that have not been previously explained — the correct abandonments and so on. A sūtra instructs: Generate aspiration, apply exertion, initiate effort, properly sieze the mind, and correctly set the mind in order to (1) abandon nonvirtuous immoral states already arisen, so that (2) those not yet arisen do not arise, and to (3) generate virtuous Dharmas not yet arisen. Generate aspiration, apply exertion, initiate effort, properly seize the mind, and correctly set the mind in order to (4) maintain virtue already arisen, not forget it, perfect meditation on it, and later cultivate it, enhance it, increase it, [576] and manifest it with transcendent wisdom.[1730] “Aspiration” is contemplation, “exertion” is preparation, and “effort” is the actual basis, while “sieze the mind” and “correctly set the mind” are subsequent states. “Abandon immoral states already arisen” is in essence nonconcealment, regret, self-criticism, and confession. Therefore “aspiration” and so on are effort. “Not generating those not yet arisen” is intentional abandonment through possessing mindfulness and introspection. “Generating virtue not yet arisen” is relying on a virtuous spiritual friend and so on. “Maintaining and enhancing that already arisen” is knowing and liking its qualities.

theg pa gong ma pa dag ni yang dag par spong ba bzhi ni gnyen po stobs bzhi'i rang bzhin yin te/ sdig pa skyes pa spong ba ni rten gyi stobs dang rnam par sun 'byin pa'i stobs so/ / ma skyes pa mi bskyed pa ni nyes pa las ldog pa'i stobs so/ / phyi ma gnyis ni gnyen po kun tu spyod pa'i stobs yin no zhes bzhed do/ / rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa'i dbang du byas nas mdo las 'dun pa'i ting nge 'dzin spong ba'i 'du byed dang ldan pa'i rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa dben pa la gnas pa/ 'dod chags dang bral ba la gnas pa/ 'gog pa la gnas pa/ rnam par spong ba/ yongs su bsgyur ba/ phyogs gcig tu mos par byas te khyab par byed do zhes pa dang*/ de bzhin du brtson 'grus dang*/ sems dang dpyod pa la'ang sbyar nas gsungs te/ de la 'dun pa ni zhi gnas don du gnyer bas gus par sbyor ba'o/ / brtson 'grus ni de la spro bas rgyun du sbyor ba'o/ / sems ni sngar goms par byas pa'i sems kyi nus pa dang ldan pa'o/ / dpyod pa ni dmigs pa dang rnam pa la rnam par dpyod pa'i shes rab bo/ / bzhi po de dag las byung ba'i ting nge 'dzin la ni 'dun pa'i ting nge 'dzin spong ba'i 'du byed dang ldan pa zhes bya ba la sogs par bshad de rnga'i sgra dang nas kyi myu gu la sogs pa bzhin no/ / rnam pa gcig tu na 'dun pa la sogs pa dang mtshungs par ldan pa la de dang der brjod de ba lang dang ldan pa'i shing rta la ba lang gi shing rta zhes brjod pa bzhin no/ /

The higher vehicle asserts that the four correct abandonments are in essence the four opponent powers. Abandoning immorality already arisen constitutes (1) the power of the basis and (2) the power of repudiation. Not generating nonvirtue that has not yet arisen is (3) the power of not committing that fault again. The latter two are (4) the power of always applying the antidote. From the perspective of the supernatural limbs, a sūtra states: The supernatural limb of concentration of (1) aspiration associated with the abandoning applications refers to abiding in isolation, abiding free from attachment, abiding in cessation, abandonment, thorough transformation, resolute in a specific state, and pervasive engagement. So too, that should also be applied to (2) effort, (3) mind, and (4) analysis.[1731] “Aspiration” is respectful preparation to attain calm abiding, “effort” is continuous preparation through delight, “mind” is possessing mental power through prior familiarity, and “analysis” is wisdom analyzing its focal object and aspect. Concentration derived from these four may be called “concentration of aspiration associated with the abandoning applications” and so on, like the terms “sound of a drum” and “a sprout of barley” and so forth. In one sense these states that are concomitant with aspiration and so on are designated thus just as a cart pulled by an ox is called an “ox cart.”

de yang spong ba'i 'du byed ni dbus mtha' las/ der gnas las su rung ba nyid/ / don rnams thams cad 'byor par 'gyur/ / nyes pa lnga spong 'du byed brgyad/ / bsten pa'i rgyu las byung ba'o/ / zhes bshad pa'i nyes pa lnga ni de nyid las/ le lo dang ni gdams ngag rnams/ / brjed dang bying dang rgod pa dang*/ / 'du mi byed dang 'du byed de/ / 'di dag nyes pa lngar 'dod do zhes bshad do/ / de la bying rgod ni gcig tu byas la/ 'du mi byed pa ni ting nge 'dzin la snyoms par zhugs pa na bying grod du gyur pa na de dag spong ba la g.yel bar gyur pa'o/ / 'du byed pa ni zhi gnas dang lhag mthong 'brel bar 'jug pa na dmigs rnam la rtsol ba na rnam g.yeng du 'gyur ba'i phyir skyon yin no/ / le lo dang gdams ngag brjed pa ni sla'o/ /
spong ba'i 'du byed brgyad ni de nyid las/ / gnas dang de la gnas pa dang*/ / rgyu dang 'bras bu nyid du'o/ / dmigs pa brjed par ma gyur dang*/ / bying dang rgod pa rtags pa dang*/ / de spong mngon par 'du byed dang*/ / zhi che rnal du 'jug pa'o zhes bshad de/ /

Further, regarding the term “abandoning application,” Differentiating the Middle and Extremes states: In abiding in that, there is flexibility, and one comes to attain every goal. The eight applications that abandon the five faults arise from the cause they depend on.[1732] This passage mentions the five faults. This same text observes: Laziness, forgetting the instruction, laxity and excitation, nonapplication, and application — these are asserted to be the five faults.[1733] Regarding those, (3) laxity and excitation are taken as one. (4) Nonapplication is when, upon entering balanced concentration, laxity and excitation occur, and one is distracted and neglects to abandon them. (5) Application is when, having already entered the union of calm abiding and insight, one exerts effort to engage the focal object and aspect; [577] this is a fault because it is a distraction. (1) Laziness and (2) forgetting the instruction are easy to understand.
Regarding the eight abandoning applications, this same text declares: The basis and what is based on that, the cause, and result, not forgetting the focal object, noticing laxity and excitation, and the application abandoning that enter a natural state of great peace.[1734]

de la le lo'i gnyen po rtsol ba'i gnas ni gang la 'dun pa de la brtson 'grus 'byung bas 'dun pa'o/ / de la gnas pa ni rtsol ba'o/ / yid ches par gyur na mngon par 'dod pa'i 'dun pa 'byung bas rtsol ba'i gnas 'dun pa de'i rgyu ni dad pa'o/ / gnas pa rtsol ba de'i 'bras bu ni shin tu sbyangs pa ste bzhi po des ni le lo sel bar byed do/ / dmigs pa brjed par ma gyur pa ni dran pa ste des brjed ngas spong bar byed do/ / bying dang rgod pa rtogs pa ni shes bzhin te dran pa ma brjed par gyur nas bying rgod rtogs par byed do/ / de spong mngon par 'du byed ni sems pa ste bying rgod rtogs nas des spang ba'i phyir 'du byed pas 'du mi byed pa sel bar byed do/ / zhi tshe rnal du 'jug pa ni btang snyoms te bying rgod zhi ba na sems btang snyoms su byed pas 'du byed drags pa sel bar byed do/ / rdzu 'phrul ni med pa 'phrul ba dang yod pa bsgyur ba la sogs pa yin la/ rkang pa ni ting nge 'dzin yin te/ yon tan thams cad 'byor ba'i rdzu 'phrul gyi rten yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar byas na mdo las/ dge slong dag ngas khyed la rdzu 'phrul yang bshad/ rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa rnams kyang bshad par bya'o zhes bya ba nas rdzu 'phrul gang zhe na/ 'di na dge slong rdzu 'phrul gyi yul rnam pa du ma nyams su myong bar byed cing gcig tu gyur nas mang por 'gyur zhes bya ba la sogs pa dang*/ de bzhin du tshangs pa'i 'jig rten gyi bar du lus kyis dbang bsgyur bar byed de 'di ni rdzu 'phrul zhes bya'o/ / rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa dag gang zhe na/ 'dun pa'i ting nge 'dzin dang*/ brtson 'grus kyi ting nge 'dzin dang*/ sems kyi ting nge 'dzin dang*/ dpyod pa'i ting nge 'dzin te 'di dag ni rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa zhes bya ba'i bar du gsungs pa'ang legs par drangs par 'gyur ro/ /

The first four abandon the fault of laziness. (1) Aspiration is “the basis of” exertion, since one makes effort to attain what one aspires for. (2) Exertion “is based on that.” (3) Faith is “the cause” of the aspiration to exertion, since one aspires for a desired object when conviction [that is faith] arises. (4) Pliancy is “the result” of that exertion which is based on that aspiration. [The next four abandon their respective faults.] (5) Mindfulness does “not forget its focal object” since it abandons forgetfulness. (6) Introspection “notices laxity and excitation,” and it does so through mindfulness not forgetting the instruction. (7) Intention is “the application that abandons that” since nonapplication is eliminated due to application, because it abandons them through noticing the existence of laxity and excitation. (8) Equanimity “enters a natural state of great peace,” for when laxity and excitation are pacified, excessive application is eliminated and one applies equanimity to the mind. “Supernatural” (ṛddhi) refers to emanating what is nonexistent and transforming what is existent and so on. “Limb” (pāda) refers to concentration because it is the basis of the supernatural powers that attain all qualities. As such a sūtra explains: Monks, I have explained what is supernatural to you, and I will explain the supernatural limbs. What is supernatural? Monks, one may experience many types of supernatural object, and even from just one object many may arise. So too: Up to the mundane abode of Brahma, that which engages in transformation through the body is called “supernatural.” What are the supernatural limbs? The concentration of aspiration, concentation of effort, concentration of mind, and concentration of analysis are called the “supernatural limbs.”[1735]

des na bye brag tu smra ba gang dag rdzu 'phrul ni ting nge 'dzin kho na yin la/ rkang pa ni 'dun pa dang sems dang brtson 'grus dang byed pa bzhi yin no zhes zer ba de dag gi ltar na de lta bu'i mdo dang yang 'gal zhing*/ byang chub kyi phyogs dang mthun pa'ang rdzas bcu gsum du 'gyur te/ 'dun pa dang sems kyang byang chub kyi phyogs dang mthun par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / dben pa la gnas pa ni 'dod pas dben pa'o/ / 'dod chags dang bral ba ni khams las 'das pa'o/ / 'gog pa ni sdug bsngal 'gog pa'o/ / rnam par spong ba ni kun 'byung spong ba'o/ / yongs su bsgyur ba ni thar par byed pa'o/ / phyogs gcig tu mos par byas te zhes bya ba ni yul lo/ / khyab par byed pa ni dmigs pa'o/ / 'di dag ni tshad med pa dang byang chub kyi yan lag bdun la sogs pa la'ang shes par bya'o/ /

Vaibhāṣikas say that supernatural (ṛddhi) refers to concentration alone, and limb (pāda) refers to the four: aspiration, mind, effort, and analysis. Reply: But such assertions contradict this sūtra, and factors conducive to enlightenment would have thirteen substances, because aspiration and mind would become states conducive to enlightenment. “Abiding in isolation” refers to desiring isolation. “Free from attachment” refers to overcoming attachment to the realms. “Cessation” refers to the cessation of suffering. “Abandonment” refers to abandoning the truth of origin. “Thorough transformation” refers to attaining liberation. “Resolute in a specific state” refers to the object. “Pervasive engagement” [578] refers to the focal object. You should understand these as immeasurable states and the seven requisites of enlightenment and so on.

dbang po lnga ni dbus mtha' las/ / thar pa'i cha dang mthun bskyed nas/ / 'dun dang sbyor ba dbang byed de/ / dmigs pa brjed par ma gyur dang*/ / mi 'phro rnam par 'byed kyang ngo zhes bshad pas dad pa dang*/ brtson 'grus dang*/ dran pa dang*/ ting nge 'dzin dang*/ shes rab ste rnam par byang ba la dbang byed pa'i phyir ro/ / stobs lnga yang de dag nyid yin te/ khyad par ni mi mthun phyogs kyis mi brdzi ba'i phyir te/ de nyid las/ mi mthun phyogs ni bsrabs pa'i phyir/ / stobs ldan 'bras bu phye ma yin zhes bshad do/ / des na dbang po rnams ni mi mthun phyogs ma dad pa dang le lo dang brjed ngas dang rnam g.yeng dang shes bzhin ma yin pa rnams bar skabs su 'byung bas mi mthun phyogs kyis brdzi ba'i phyir chung ngu yin la/ stobs rnams ni mi mthun phyogs kyis mi brdzi ba'i phyir chen po yin no/ / de dag gi go rim ni dad par 'gyur na 'bras bu'i don du brtson 'grus rtsom la/ brtson 'grus brtsams na dran pa nye bar gnas par 'gyur ba dang*/ dran pa gnas na rnam par mi g.yeng bas sems mnyam par 'jog cing*/ mnyam par bzhag pas yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin rab tu shes par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / byang chub kyi yan lag bdun la byang chub ni chos nyid rtogs pa yin la/ yan lag ni 'dir cha shas la brjod pa yin no/ / yan lag rnam pa bdun yang de nyid las/ rang bzhin yan lag gnas yan lag gsum pa nges 'byung yan lag ste/ / bzhi pa phan yon yan lag yin/ / rnam gsum nyon mongs med yan lag ces bshad de/

Regarding the five faculties (indriya), Differentiating the Middle and Extremes states: Having generated the factors conducive to freedom, aspiration empowers preparation, one does not forget the focal object, stops proliferation, and engages in analysis.[1736] Therefore faith, effort, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom empower enlightened states. The five powers (bala) are also just these five, but the difference is that they are not oppressed by their opposing factors. The same text says: Because the opposing factors are diminished, they are powers. The latter are effects.[1737] The faculties are weaker since their opposing factors of faithlessness, laziness, forgetfulness, distraction, and nonintrospection intermittently arise, and they are oppressed by these opposing factors. The powers are stronger because they are not oppressed by their opposing factors. In terms of their order, first (1) faith arises, and then one initiates (2) effort in search of that result. Once effort has been initiated, one abides with (3) close mindfulness. While abiding with mindfulness, the mind is placed in undistracted (4) equipoise [or concentration], and one comes to (5) fully know the perfect meaning as it is, through such equipoise. Regarding the seven requisites of enlightenment (bodhyaṅga), enlightenment is the comprehension of reality, and requisite here refers to a causal factor. Regarding the seven requisites, that text states: The requisite of essence, the requisite of abode, the third is the requisite of renunciation, the fourth is the requisite of benefit, three types are the requisite devoid of affliction.[1738]

de la rang bzhin gyi yan lag ni ches rab tu rnam par 'byed pa ste/ de kho na nyid rtogs pa'i phyir ro/ / gnas kyi yan lag ni dran pa ste/ shes rab ni dran pa la gnas pa'i phyir ro/ / nges par 'byung ba'i yan lag ni brtson 'grus te/ so so'i skye bo'i sa la sogs pa 'og ma las nges par 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / phan yon gyi yan lag ni dga' ba te/ zag pa med pa'i bde bas lus sems la phan 'dogs pa'i phyir ro/ / nyon mongs pa med pa'i yan lag ni de nyid las/ 'di la gzhi dang gnas dang ni/ / ngo bo nyid du bstan pa yin zhes 'byung bas shin tu sbyangs pa dang ting nge 'dzin dang btang snyoms te/ nyon mongs pa'i gnas ngan len gyi gnyen po yin pas gsum po rim pa ltar nyon mongs pa med pa'i gzhi dang gnas dang ngo bo yin pa'i phyir ro/ / des na chos rab tu rnam par 'byed pa ni byang chub dang yan lag gnyis ka yin la/ gzhan dag ni byang chub kyi yan lag ste 'khor yin pa'i phyir lhas byin gyi ril ba zhes brjod pa bzhin no/ / 'phags lam yan lag brgyad ni de nyid las/ yongs su gcod dang go byed dang*/ / rnam gsum gzhan yid ches par byed/ / mi mthun phyogs kyi gnyen por ni/ / lam gyi yan lag de brgyad do zhes gsungs te/ de la yongs su gcod pa ni yang dag pa'i lta ba ste/ rjes thob na yang dag pa'i lta bas mnyam gzhag gi dus kyi rtogs pa nges par 'byed pa'i phyir ro/ / go bar byed pa ni yang dag pa'i rtog pa dang ngag ste/ rtog pa kun slong dang bcas pa'i ngag gis rtogs pa'i don de gzhan la go bar byed pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yid ches par byed pa'i yan lag ni de nyid las/ lta dang tshul khrims yo byad bsnyungs/ / gzhan la rnam par rig byed 'dod ces 'byung bas yang dag pa'i ngag dang las kyi mtha' dang 'tsho ba gsum yin te/ yang dag pa'i ngag gis 'bel gtam nges par byed pa dang*/ bya ba ma yin pa mi byed pa dang*/ chos gos la sogs pa tshod zin par 'tshol bas rim pa bzhin lta ba dang tshul khrims dang yo byad bsnyungs pa 'dod pa chung bar yid ches par byed pa'i phyir ro/ /

“The requisite of essence” refers to the correct analysis of phenomena because it comprehends reality (tattva). “The requisite of abode” refers to mindfulness because wisdom abides in mindfulness. “The requisite of renunciation” refers to effort because due to it one definitely emerges from lower levels, such as the level of ordinary beings and so on. “The requisite of benefit” refers to joy because the mind and body are benefited through uncontaminated pleasure [or bliss]. Regarding “the requisite devoid of affliction,” this text states: It is taught to be the basis, abidance, and nature.[1739] Therefore, since pliancy, concentration, and equanimity are antidotes to afflicted dysfunction, these three are respectively the basis, abode, and nature that are devoid of affliction. The correct analysis of phenomena is both enlightenment and a requisite, while the others are requisites of enlightenment alone because they are its retinue, as in the statement, “the vase of Devadatta.” Regarding the eightfold noble path (āryāṣṭāṅgamarga), that text says: Complete differentiation, making others understand, three types that create conviction in others, [579] and the antidotes of opposing factors are eight that are branches of the path.[1740] “Complete differentiation” refers to right view because right view in post-equipoise definitely separates itself from comprehension at the time of equipoise. “Making others understand” refers to right investigation and right speech because speech motivated by investigation makes understood that which is to be comprehended by others. Regarding the branch of “creating conviction in others,” that text remarks: View, ethics, few articles are asserted to reveal [one’s motivation] to others.[1741] This refers to three: right speech, right action, and right livelihood. Engaging in discourse through right speech, not engaging in improper action, and seeking just the proper amount of robes refer, respectively, to philosophic view, ethics, and having conviction in few desires with regard to articles.

mi mthun phyogs spong ba'i gnyen po'i yan lag ni de nyid las/ nyon mongs nye ba'i nyon mongs dbang*/ / mi mthun phyogs kyi gnyen po'o zhes 'byung bas yang dag pa'i rtsol ba dang dran pa dang ting nge 'dzin te gsum gyi rim pa bzhin brtson 'grus brtsams shing dran pa nye bar gnas la bsam gtan la brten nas mngon shes la sogs pa'i yon tan sgrub pas le lo'i nyon mongs pa dang*/ nye ba'i nyon mongs pa bying rgod dang*/ dbang snyoms 'jug gi sgrib pa rnams spong ba'i phyir ro/ /
'di la'ang yang dag pa'i lta ba ni shes rab yin pas 'phags pa'i lam yang yin la yan lag kyang yin la/ gzhan dag ni de'i 'khor yin pas 'phags pa'i lam yan lag brgyad pa yin no zhes bye brag tu smra ba 'dod do/ /

Regarding remedial branches that abandon counter-conditions, that text says: They are antidotes to afflictions, branch afflictions, and the counter conditions to mastery.[1742] Right exertion initiates effort that abandons the affliction of laziness. Right mindfulness closely abides in mindfulness that abandons the branch afflictions of laxity and excitation. Right concentration establishes qualities such as higher perception in dependence on the absorptions, which abandon obscurations to the mastery of meditative attainment.
Moreover, right view is not only an ārya path but also a branch, since it is wisdom, and the others are its retinue. Therefore they are the eightfold noble path. This is the presentation of the Vaibhāṣikas.
go rim gyi khyad par/
SEQUENCE OF THE SEVEN DIVISIONS
sde tshan bdun ni go rims bzhin/ / las ni dang po pa dag dang / / nges 'byed cha mthun rnams dang ni/ / bsgom dang mthong la rab tu phye/ / 70
The seven divisions are respectively differentiated as the stage of a beginner, the factors conducive to penetrative insight, meditation, and seeing. (6:70)

gnyis pa ni dran pa nyer gzhag la sogs pa'i sde tshan bdun ni gnas skabs de dang der gtso bo yin pas go rim bzhin du las dang po pa tshogs lam pa dag dang nges 'byed cha mthun bzhi po rnams dang ni sgom lam dang mthong lam la gnas pa'i gnas skabs kyis rab tu phye zhing bzhag ste/ de la las dang po pa tshogs lam du dran pa nyer gzhag bzhi bshad de/ dbus mtha' las/ gnas ngan len phyir sred rgyu'i phyir/ gzhi yi phyir dang ma rmongs phyir/ / bden pa bzhi la 'jug bya bas/ / dran pa nye bar bzhag pa sgom zhes pa dang*/ 'di nyid las/ phyin ci log gi gnyen por bzhi zhes 'byung bas lus la sogs pa la phyin ci log bzhi spangs nas bden pa la 'jug par bya ba'i ched du nye bar brtag pa'i phyir ro/ /

The seven divisions [of the thirty-seven factors] such as the foundations of mindfulness are central practices at different times, since respectively they are differentiated and established as the stage of a beginner (ādikarmika) on the path of accumulation, the four factors conducive to penetrative insight (nirvedhabhāgīya), the path of meditation (bhāvana), and the path of seeing (darśana). The beginner is explained in terms of (1) the four foundations of mindfulness. Differentiating the Middle and Extremes states: Because it is dysfunctional, because it is the cause of craving, because it is the basis, and because it is not confused, meditate on the foundations of mindfulness to engage the four noble truths.[1743] Also the Abhidharmakośa mentions: The four are antidotes to misconception. (6:15d) Therefore they closely investigate the four truths, in order to engage the four truths through abandoning the four misconceptions regarding the body and so on.

nges 'byed cha mthun dro bar gyur pa'i gnas skabs su ni yang dag par spong ba bzhi ste/ dmigs pa dang rnam pa'i khyad par thob pa'i rgyus brtson 'grus spel ba'i phyir ro/ / rtse mo la ni rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa rnams te/ rtse mo thob pa rtsa mi chad ces pas thob pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba mi nyams pa'i bzod pa la 'jug par bya ba'i phyir ro/ / bzod pa la ni dbang po rnams te/ snga ma gnyis la ni nyams pa srid cing 'di la nyams pa mi srid pas mi nyams pa la dbang thob par bya ba'i phyir ro/ / chos mchog la ni stobs rnams te/ mi mthun phyogs nyon mongs pa dang*/ 'jig rten pa'i chos gzhan dag gis mi brdzi bar bya ba'i phyir ro/ / sgom lam la ni byang chub kyi yan lag rnams te/ mthong lam ni sgom lam gyis bar du chod pas ring la sgom lam ni lam gzhan gyis bar du ma chod pas byang chub zad mi skye shes pa dang nye ba'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / mthong lam du ni 'phags lam yan lag brgyad de/ sgom lam ni sa'i dbye ba yod pas myur du 'gro ba ma yin gyi mthong lam la ni sa'i dbye ba med pas myur du 'gro ba'i phyir ro/ / mdo las/ byang chub kyi yan lag sngon la bstan pa ni bdun dang brgyad grangs kyi rim pa dang mthun par bstan pa yin no zhes bye brag tu smra ba rnams 'dod do/ /

(2) The four correct abandonments are engaged during the heat stage of the factors conducive to penetrative insight because they enhance effort; they are the cause for obtaining a special focal object and aspect. (3) The supernatural limbs are engaged at the peak stage of the path of preparation, and then they enter the stage of patience, where the root of virtue does not degenerate. As it is said, “Those who have obtained the peak will not sever their root.” (4) The faculties are engaged at the patience stage of preparation. There one obtains control over nondegeneration, since degeneration [580] is still possible in the prior two stages but degeneration is not possible at this stage. (5) The powers are engaged at the stage of the supreme mundane state. One is not oppressed by the counter-conditions of the afflictions and other mundane phenomena. (6) The requisites of enlightenment are engaged on the path of meditation. They are proximate causes of the knowledge of enlightenment, elimination, and nonarising, since while the path of meditation is not obstructed by other paths, the path of seeing is obstructed by the path of meditation. (7) The eightfold noble path is engaged on the path of seeing because they [i.e., the eight branches of the noble path] proceed quickly. The path of meditation does not proceed quickly, since it has many classifications of levels, but the path of seeing does not have such classifications. A sūtra states: The requisites of enlightenment are taught first, since they are taught in accordance with the order of seven, then eight.[1744] This is the presentation of the Vaibhāṣikas.

slob dpon la sogs pa gzhan dag ni mdo las gsungs pa'i go rim dang mthun par re zhig dang por yul gzugs sgra la sogs pa dang de dag gi bye brag kha dog dang dbyibs la sogs pa mang po la g.yeng ba'i blo tshar bcad par bya ba'i phyir de'i gnyen por dran pa nyer gzhag bzhi sgom ste/ dbus mtha' las/ mi mthun pa dang gnyen po rnams/ / rnam pa thams cad yongs shes nas/ / de dag spang phyir brtson 'grus ni/ / rnam pa bzhi dag rab tu 'byung zhes 'byung ba ltar dran pa nyer gzhag gi stobs kyis brtson 'grus 'phel bas dgos pa brtson 'grus bzhi bskyed pa'i phyir sems yang dag par rab tu 'jog pas yang dag par spong ba rnams so/ / de nas ting nge 'dzin rnam par sbyong ba'i phyir rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa rnams so/ / ting nge 'dzin la brten nas 'jig rten las 'das pa'i chos rnams 'dren pa'i bdag por gyur pa'i dad sogs lnga ni dbang po rnams so/ / de dag nyid mi mthun phyogs las rgyal ba ni stobs rnams so/ / dang po nyid du chos rnams kyi de kho na nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa'i phyir mthong lam la byang chub kyi yan lag rnams so/ / mthong sgom gyi lam gnyis ka la bsgom pa'i phyir 'phags lam yan lag brgyad pa ste/ skye mched drug gi tshogs chen po'i mdo las/ 'phags pa'i lam yan lag brgyad pa bsgom pa yongs su rdzogs pa gyur na dran pa nye bar bzhag pa bzhi bsgom pa yongs su rdzogs par 'gyur ba nas byang chub kyi yan lag bdun gyi bar du yongs su rdzogs par 'gyur ro zhes sgom lam la'ang yan lag brgyad yod par gsungs la/ yang mdo las/ dge slong yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin gyi tshig brjod pa zhes bya ba 'di ni 'phags pa'i bden pa bzhi'i tshig bla dgas so/ / dge slong ji ltar rtogs pa'i lam gyi 'jug ces bya ba 'di ni 'phags pa'i lam yan lag brgyad kyi tshig bla dgas yin no zhes gsungs te/

Vasubandhu and other scholars conform with their order as stated in the sūtras. Therefore one first meditates on the four foundations of mindfulness in order to completely eradicate from the mind various distractions by objects such as forms, sounds, and so on and their subsets such as colors, shapes, and so forth. Differentiating the Middle and Extremes states: Having thoroughly understood all types of adverse state and their antidotes, the four types of effort fully arise to eliminate them.[1745] (1) The foundations of mindfulness, due to their power, enhance effort. For the need is to generate the four types of effort that are (2) the four correct abandonments, since they correctly set the mind. Then, because one trains in concentration (3) the supernatural limbs arise. In dependence on concentration, (4) the five faculties of faith and so on also arise, and these act as dominant [conditions] leading to transcendence. When their opposing factors are conquered (5) the five powers arise. (6) The requisites of enlightenment arise on the path of seeing for they are the first to directly realize the reality (tattva) of phenomena. (7) The eightfold noble path is cultivated on both the path of seeing and the path of meditation. The Great Assembly of Six Bases Sūtra states: When one completes meditation on the eightfold noble path, one completes meditation from the four foundations of mindfulness up to the seven requisites of enlightenment.[1746] This passage indicates that the path of meditation also engages the eightfold noble path. Again, a sūtra states: Monks, words that express perfect reality are descriptions of the four ārya truths. Monks, words that reveal entry to the path comprehending reality as it is are descriptions of the eightfold noble path.[1747]

tshig de gnyis kyis ni rim pa ltar mthong sgom gyi lam bstan pa yin te/ ji ltar rtogs pa'i lam gyis byang chub kyi bar du 'jug cing 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / de ltar na mthong lam la'ang lam gyi yan lag yod par gsungs pa'i phyir mdo las bstan pa'i go rim rnam par dkrug par mi bya'o zhes 'dod la/ theg pa gong ma ba rnams ni dbus mtha' las/ dbang po rnams dang stobs rnams la/ / nges 'byed cha mthun gnyis gnyis so zhes 'byung bas sde tshan bdun po mdo las gsungs pa'i go rim ltar tshogs lam chung ngu dang*/ 'bring dang*/ chen po dang*/ drod rtse dang*/ bzod mchog dang*/ mthong lam dang*/ sgom lam rnams su rim pa ltar sgom ste/ 'di ni 'jug pa bde ba'i lam yin no zhes bzhed do/ /

Those two lines teach the path of seeing and the path of meditation, respectively, because the path that comprehends reality as it is [581] is engaged and arises until enlightenment. Therefore, because it is said that the path of seeing also has branches of the path, the order taught in the sūtras should not be confused. Those of the higher vehicle assert that, since Differentiating the Middle and Extremes observes: The faculties and powers have two factors conducive to penetrative insight each,[1748] and in accordance with the order stated in the Seventh Division Sūtra, it follows that serially meditating on the small, medium, and great path of accumulation, heat, peak, patience, the supreme mundane state, the path of seeing, and the path of meditation, and entering these paths, is the path of bliss.
gsum pa [ngo bo dang sa'i khyad par] ni
NATURE OF THE FACTORS
'o na byang chub phyogs mthun du zhig zag bcas dang du zhig zag med yin la de dag sa gang pa yin zhe na/
Question: Some factors conducive to enlightenment are contaminated, and some are uncontaminated. On what level do they exist?
byang chub yan lag lam yan lag / zag pa med gzhan rnam gnyis so/ / bsam gtan dang po na thams cad/ / mi lcogs med na dga' ma gtogs/ / 71
The requisites of enlightenment and the path are uncontaminated. The others have two types. All exist in the first absorption. All except joy in unrestricted access concentration. (6:71)

byang chub kyi yan lag bdun dang 'phags pa'i lam yan lag brgyad ni zag pa med pa yin te/ gnas skabs khyad par can{ mthong sgom} dang khyad par can ma yin{ pas mi slob} pa'i sgo nas mthong sgom mi slob pa'i lam gsum gyis bsdus pa'i phyir ro/ / de dag las gzhan dran pa nyer gzhag nas stobs kyi bar dag ni gnas skabs khyad par can dang khyad par can ma yin pa'i sgo nas zag bcas dang zag med rnam pa gnyis yin te/ so so'i skye bo'i rgyud la yod pa sbyor lam gyis bsdus pa dag ni zag bcas dang*/ 'phags pa'i rgyud la yod pa lam gsum gyis bsdus pa dag ni zag med yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: The seven requisites of enlightenment (bodhyaṅga) and the eightfold noble path (mārga) are uncontaminated (anāsrava) because they are included in the three paths of seeing, meditation, and no more learning as temporary states {of seeing and meditation} and as nontemporary states {of no more learning}. The others, from the foundations of mindfulness to the powers, have two types, either contaminated or uncontaminated, because those included in the path of preparation existing in the mindstream of an ordinary being are contaminated, and those included in the three paths in the mindstream of an ārya are uncontaminated.

sa ni bsam gtan dang po na sum cu rtsa bdun po thams cad yod la/ bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs mi lcogs pa med pa na ni dga' ba yang dag byang chub kyi yan lag ma gtogs pa sum cu rtsa drug yod de/ bde blag tu 'thob pa dang*/ dogs pa med na dga' bar 'gyur ba yin pa la nyer bsdogs ni rtsol ba'i stobs kyis bskyed dgos pa'i phyir dang*/ sa 'og mar nyams kyis dogs pa dang bcas pa'i phyir dang*/ tshor ba btang snyoms pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

In terms of level, all thirty-seven exist in the first absorption (dhyāna). Thirty-six, except for the requisite of enlightenment of correct joy (prāti), exist in unrestricted access concentration to the first absorption. This is because ease of obtainment and the absence of doubt are joyful, but access concentration must be generated by the power of exertion, lower levels possess doubt due to degeneration, and access concentration possesses the feeling of equanimity.
gnyis pa na ni rtog ma gtogs/ / gnyis na de gnyis ma gtogs pa/ / bsam gtan bar na'ang gzugs med pa/ / gsum na'ang de dang tshul yan lag / 72
All except investigation exist on the second. All except for two on both. Also between absorptions. Those and the branch of ethics do not exist in the three formless states. (6:72)

bsam gtan gnyis pa na ni yang dag pa'i rtogs pa ma gtogs pa sum cu rtsa drug yod de/ yang dag pa'i rtog pa ni rtog pa yin la de na gnyis pa bas spangs zin {phyir dang de las 'das pa'i sa yin pa'i } pa'i phyir ro/ / bsam gtan gsum pa dang bzhi pa gnyis na ni dga' ba dang rtog pa de gnyis ma gtogs pa sum cu rtsa lnga yod de/ rtog pa sngar nas nub la dga' ba las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i phyir ro/ / bsam gtan dang po'i dngos gzhi tsam po dang gnyis pa'i bar ma bsam gtan dang po'i dngos gzhi khyad par can na'ang rtog pa dang dga' ba ma gtogs pa sum cu rtsa lnga yod de/ rtog pa spangs la tshor ba btang snyoms kyi sa pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / nam mkha' mtha' yas la sogs pa gzugs med pa dang po gsum na'ang rtog pa dang dga' ba de gnyis dang tshul khrims kyi yan lag gsum med de/ rtogs pa spangs shing tshor ba btang snyoms pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ de dag ni lus ngag gi las med pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan sum cu rtsa gnyis ni yod do/ /

Thirty-six except for right investigation (saṃkalpa) exist on the second absorption. This is because right investigation is investigation, and one on the second level has abandoned investigation {for this is a level transcending investigation}. Thirty-five except for two — joy and investigation — exist on both the third and fourth absorptions. This is because investigation has previously subsided and one is free from attachment to joy. Thirty-five — except for investigation and joy — also exist on the special actual basis of the first absorption: that is, between the ordinary actual basis of the first absorption and the second absorption (dhyānāntara). This is because it abandons investigation and it is a level possessing the feeling of equanimity. Both investigation and joy and a third — the branch of ethics[1749] (śīlāṅga) — do not exist in the first three formless (arūpa) states such as infinite space. This is because these states have abandoned investigation, [582] they possess the feeling of equanimity, and they do not possess physical and verbal action. But the other thirty-two exist.
byang chub dang ni lam yan lag / ma gtogs 'dod khams srid rtse na/ /
Those except for the requisites of enlightenment and the path exist in the desire realm and summit of existence. (6:73ab)

byang chub kyi yan lag bdun dang 'phags pa'i lam yan lag brgyad ma gtogs pa nyi shu rtsa gnyis ni 'dod pa'i khams dang srid pa'i rtse mo na yod de/{ bsod nams cha mthun gyi dad sogs kyis 'di'i ming mi thob bo/ / bco lnga po} de/ de dag med pa ni 'dod pa mnyam par ma bzhag pa dang srid rtse sems kyi rgyu ba mi gsal bas sa de gnyis la zag med kyi lam mi brten pa'i phyir ro/ /

Twenty-two, except for the seven requisites of enlightenment (bodhyaṅga) and the eightfold noble path (mārgāṅga), exist in the desire realm and the summit of existence, {where faith and so on are factors conducive to merit (puṇyabhāgīya). The remaining fifteen that are not called factors conducive to merit} do not exist there. The uncontaminated path is not supported in either [the desire realm or the summit of existence], since the desire realm is not a level of equipoise and the movement of mind in the summit of existence is unclear.

'o na gzugs med na lus dran pa nyer gzhag ji ltar yod par 'gyur te/ lus dran pa nyer gzhag ni lus la dmigs pa'i shes rab yin na de dag rang sa na med pa'i phyir dang*/ gzugs med dngos gzhi dge rnams kyi/ /spyod yul zag bcas 'og ma min zhes 'byung bas 'og sa la mi dmigs pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ gzugs med rang sa na gzugs med kyang nam mkha' mtha' yas kyi nyer bsdogs la brten pa'i dran pa nyer gzhag dge ba zag bcas kyis bsam gtan bzhi pa'i gzugs zag bcas la dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ 'og ma la mi dmigs par bshad pa ni dngos gzhi'i dge bas zag bcas la mi dmigs pa yin la/ gzugs med dang po gsum gyi dngos gzhi dge ba zag bcas zag med kyis bsam gtan sa drug la brten pa'i zag med kyi sdom pa la dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ srid rtse'i shes rab dge ba zag bcas kyis bsam gtan la brten pa'i zag med kyi sdom pa la dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ de yang 'byung gyur gyi gzugs su 'dod pa'i phyir ro zhes rgyal po'i sras{ grags pa'i bshes gnyen} 'chad do/ / yang gal te khams gong ma gnyis na mi dge ba med pa'i phyir de dag skyes pa spong ba dang ma skyes pa mi bskyed pa'i phyir brtson pa'i yang dag par spong ba gnyis ji ltar yod par 'gyur zhe na/ de lta mod kyi nyon mongs pa dang snyoms 'jug gi sgrib pa dang zag bcas kyi chos la sdig pa'i sgrar brjod de don dam pa'i mi dge ba yin pa'i phyir ro zhes bya bar bsams so/ /

Objection: How could the foundations of mindfulness of the body exist in the formless realm? For close placement of mindfulness of the body is wisdom focusing on the body, and bodies do not exist on that level. Also it does not focus on lower levels, since the Abhidharmakośa observes that “The object fields of those virtuous, formless, actual bases are not contaminated lower levels” (8:21ab)? Jinaputra {Yaśomitra} explains that though form does not exist in the formless [realm, mindfulness of body exists in the formless realm, and he gives three reasons.] (1) Contaminated virtuous close placement of mindfulness, from access concentration to infinite space, focuses on the contaminated form of the fourth absorption. (2) The Abhidharmakośa’s explanation that it does not focus on lower levels means that the virtuous actual basis does not focus on contaminated states but that virtuous contaminated and uncontaminated actual bases of the first three formless realms focus on uncontaminated vows dependent on the six levels of absorption.[1750] (3) The virtuous contaminated wisdom of the summit of existence focuses on the uncontaminated vows dependent on the absorptions that are asserted to be derived form. Question: Now, if nonvirtue does not exist in the two upper realms, then how could the two correct abandonments striving to abandon the nonvirtue already arisen and not generating the nonvirtue not yet arisen exist there? Reply: Indeed, that is a good question. But I think that they do exist there, since afflictive obscurations, obscurations to meditative attainment, as well as contaminated phenomena exist there, and they are termed “immoral” because they are ultimate nonvirtue.
bzhi pa [shes na dad pa'i khyad par] ni
FAITH THROUGH KNOWLEDGE

mdo las/ sangs rgyas dang chos dang dge 'dun la shes nas dad pa thob cing 'phags pa dgyes pa'i tshul khrims thob pa zhes shes nas dad pa thob pa bzhi bshad na byang chub kyi phyogs mthun la gnas pa de dag gnas skabs gang du shes nas dad pa ji ltar thob cing de dag gi ngo bo yang gang zhe na/

Question: A sūtra states: Through knowing the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, one obtains faith and one obtains ethics pleasing to āryas.[1751] In explaining the four types of obtainment of faith through knowledge, then when and how do those abiding in the factors conducive to enlightenment obtain faith through knowledge, and what is their nature?
bden gsum mthong na tshul khrims dang / / chos la shes nas dad pa 'thob/ / 73
When one sees three truths, one obtains faith through knowledge of ethics and Dharma. (6:73cd)

mthong lam du sdug bsngal la sogs pa'i bden pa dang po gsum mngon sum du mthong na de dag chos yin pa'i phyir dang*/ sangs rgyas dang dge 'dun gyi ngo bo ma yin pas 'phags pa dgyes pa'i tshul khrims dang chos la shes nas dad pa 'thob/{ ste zag med kyi spong bdun thob cing shes rab kyi bden pa bdag med par mngon sum du mthong bas chos tsam du yid ches pa'i phyir ro/ /}

Reply: When one directly sees (darśana) the first three noble truths (trisatya) on the path of seeing, one obtains faith through knowledge (avetyaprasāda) of ethics (śīla) and Dharma that is pleasing to āryas. This is because they [i.e., knowledge of ethics and Dharma] are the nature of Dharma and not the nature of the Buddha and Saṅgha. {One develops conviction in Dharma alone, since one obtains the seven uncontaminated abandonments and one directly sees the truth of wisdom as selfless.}
lam mngon rtogs na sangs rgyas dang / / de yi dge 'dun dag la yang / / chos bden gsum dang rang sangs rgyas/ / byang chub sems dpa'i lam yin no/ / 74
When one realizes the truth of path, one also obtains faith in the Buddha and his Saṅgha. Dharma refers to three truths and to the paths of pratyekabuddhas and bodhisattvas. (6:74)

sangs rgyas dang dge 'dun la shes nas dad pa mi 'thob la/ lam gyi bden pa mngon sum du rtogs na{ mi slob pa dang slob pa dang mi slob pa'i} lam bden ni{ sangs rgyas dang dge 'dun} de gnyis su byed pa'i chos yin pas sangs rgyas dang sangs rgyas de'i nyan thos kyi dge 'dun dag la yang shes nas dad pa 'thob ste slob mi slob kyi lam bden la yid ches 'thob bo/ / yang gi sgra ni tshul khrims dang chos la shes nas dad pa 'thob pa'ang sdud pa'o/ / 'dir 'di la 'phags pa rnams dgyes shing mnyes par gyur pas na 'phags pa dgyes pa'i tshul khrims ni zag med kyi sdom pa yin la shes nas dad pa ni bden pa rnams yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin mngon sum du rtogs nas yid ches pa'o/ / bden pa dang po gsum mthong ba na ji ltar chos la shes nas dad pa 'thob par 'gyur te/ chos ni slob pa dang mi slob pa yin la de yang lam gyi bden pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te bden pa de kho na la chos su 'dod na sdug bsngal mthong ba tsam na chos la shes nas dad pa 'thob par 'gyur ro/ / de lta na'ang bden gsum mthong na zhes ji ltar brjod ce na/

One does not obtain faith through knowledge of the Buddha and Saṅgha. [583] But when one directly realizes (abhisamaya) the truth of path, one also obtains (lābha) faith through knowledge of the Buddha and his śrāvaka Saṅgha, since the truth of path {of a nonlearner, or learner and nonlearner,} is a Dharma activated in both {the Buddha and Saṅgha.} And one obtains conviction in the truth of path of learners and nonlearners. The term “also” {applied to obtaining conviction in the learner and nonlearner truths of path} includes obtainment of faith through knowledge of ethics and Dharma. In this context, the ethics that pleases āryas is the uncontaminated vows, since due to them āryas are elated and delighted. Faith through knowledge is conviction that arises through directly realizing the four truths perfectly as they are. If one sees the first three truths, one obtains faith through knowledge of Dharma as it is, because “Dharma” refers to learner and nonlearner Dharma, and that is the truth of path. But if truth alone is asserted to be Dharma, then one would obtain faith through knowledge merely by seeing the truth of suffering. Question: Even so, why is it said, “When one sees three truths” (6:73c)?

'dir chos kyi sgra ni bden pa dang po gsum la brjod de/ de dag gi de kho na nyid ni chos yin pa'i phyir dang*/ 'gog pa ni chos rnams kyi mchog kyang yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir bden pa gsum mthong na chos la shes nas dad pa 'thob ces bya ba'ang bden pa gsum ci rigs par mthong ba la 'dod kyi tshogs pa ni ma yin no/ / de bzhin du rang sangs rgyas kyi slob mi slob kyi lam dang*/ byang chub sems dpa'i slob pa'i gnas skabs kyi lam zag pa med pa'ang chos yin te/ de dag gi mngon par rtogs pa'i chos yin zhing tshogs pa ma yin pas dge 'dun ma yin la sangs rgyas kyang ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: In this context, Dharma refers to the first three truths because their reality (tattva) is Dharma, and cessation is supreme among all Dharmas. Therefore, even though when one sees these three truths it is called “obtaining faith through knowledge of Dharma,” it is asserted that one sees any one of these three truths and not their collection. Similarly, the paths of learner and nonlearner pratyekabuddhas, and also the paths of learner bodhisattvas, are uncontaminated states as well as Dharma because they are their realizational Dharmas. And they are neither Saṅgha nor the Buddha since they are not a collection.

{Some say: They are not Saṅgha, because rhinoceros-like pratyekabuddhas do not gather together, their path does not depend on the words of others, and the path of a bodhisattva is not posited relative to the kindness of others. Others say: If one realizes the truth of path, one obtains appropriate convictional faith in the Buddha and his śrāvaka Saṅgha because these are Dharma. But Jinaputra explains: The Abhidharmakośa says that [taking refuge] “is taking refuge in the Buddha in both learners and nonlearners,” (4:32bc) and the Dharma that represents the Buddha is termed “nonlearner” and the Dharma that represents the Saṅgha is termed “learner and nonlearner paths” because these are the truth of path of the Buddha and his śrāvaka Saṅgha. However, both paths are not called “Dharma,” for one obtains faith when one directly comprehends those [four truths that are the actual Dharma] and through comprehending the Buddha and Saṅgha.}[1752]

des na rang sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa'i lam chos yin pas bden pas bzhi char yang chos yin pa'i phyir bden pa bzhi char mngon par rtogs na chos la shes nas dad pa 'thob par 'gyur ba yin no/ /

Therefore, one obtains faith when one comprehends the four noble truths and by comprehending Dharma, since the paths of pratyekabuddhas and bodhisattvas are Dharma, they are true, and also the four noble truths are Dharma.
rdzas su gnyis te dad pa dang / / tshul khrims dri ma med pa yin/ /
There are two in terms of substance: faith and ethics that are not stained. (6:75ab)

shes nas dad pa bzhir gsungs pa de dag kyang dad pa'i yul lam gzhi dkon mchog gsum gyi bye brag gis ming gi sgo nas bzhi yin gyi rdzas su ni gnyis yin te/ dkon mchog gsum la dad pa{ 'i dad pa gsum} ni dad pa'i rang bzhin dang 'phags pa dgyes pa'i tshul khrims ni tshul khrims kyi rang bzhin no/ / 'di yang sems dang ba'i stobs kyis tshul khrims kyang dag pa yin pa'i phyir rgyu'i ming gis 'bras bu la btags nas shes nas dad pa'i ming gis btags so/ / dad pa dang tshul khrims de gnyis ka'ang dri ma ste zag pa med pa yin te/ zag pa'i gnyen po yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te gzhi la ltos nas shes pas dad pa rnam par 'jog na chos la shes nas dad pa sngar gdon dgos par 'gyur te/ bden pa dang po gsum mthong ba na chos la shes nas dad pa 'thob pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ 'di dag gi rim pa ni ting nge 'dzin las langs nas ji ltar mngon du byed pa ltar bkod pa yin te/ ji ltar mngon du byed ce na/ kye ma bcom ldan 'das ni yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas yin no/ / de'i chos 'dul ba ni legs par gsungs pa yin no/ / de'i nyan thos kyi dge 'dun ni legs par zhugs pa yin no zhes mngon du byed de/ rim pa ltar chos kyi sman ston pa dang*/ nyon mongs pa'i nad gso zhing mya ngan las 'das pa nad med pa thob par byed pa dang mya ngan las 'das pa nad med pa 'thob pa'i grogs byed pa'i phyir sman pa dang sman dang nad g.yog lta bur gyur pa'i phyir dang*/ dang ba'i stobs kyis tshul khrims kyang dang bar gyur pa'i sgrub pa yin pa'i phyir mtha' bzhi par bshad do/ / yang na dkon mchog gsum ni sngar bstan pa ltar sman pa la sogs pa lta bu yin la tshul khrims ni nad med pa lta bur gyur pa yin pas sam/ yang na bzhi po de dag rim pa ltar lam ston par byed pa dang lam dang lam gyi grogs dang bzhon pa lta bu yin pas sems rab tu dad pa'i phyir ro/ /

Faith through knowledge is said to have four types, and these are the four nominal subsets of the Three Jewels as the object, path, and basis of faith. There are two in terms of substance (dravya): (1) {the three faiths that are} faith in the Three Jewels that is the essence of faith (śraddhā), and (2) ethics pleasing to the āryas [584] that is the essence of ethics (śīla). Further, it is designated as faith through knowledge where the name of the cause is imputed to the result, because even ethics becomes pure by the power of purity of mind. Both faith and ethics are not stained (nirmala) or contaminated, because they are antidotes to the contaminants. Objection: If faith through knowledge is posited in reliance on the basis, then faith through knowledge of Dharma must arise first, because when one sees the first three truths, one obtains faith through knowledge of Dharma. Reply: Their order is formulated according to how they manifest after one rises from concentration. How do they manifest? They manifest in the statements “Listen, the Bhagavan is the perfectly complete Buddha. Listen, his Dharma that subdues is excellently explained. Listen, his śrāvaka Saṅgha is excellently established,” indicating they are like a doctor, medicine, and the nurse. Respectively, the Buddha is the doctor; the medicine of Dharma heals the illness of afflictions and obtains freedom from illness that is nirvāṇa; and the Saṅgha, like nurses, assist in obtaining the freedom from illness that is nirvāṇa. Finally pure ethical conduct is established by the power of purity. Therefore they are explained as the four possibilities. Again, the mind develops faith since the Three Jewels as previously taught are like a doctor and so on and ethics is like the absence of illness. Alternately, these four are like one who teaches the path, the path itself, those who assist on the path, and the vehicle.
lnga pa [mi slob pa'i chos bcu'i khyad par] ni
THE TEN ATTRIBUTES OF A NONLEARNER

'o na ci'i phyir mdo las/ slob pa ni slob pa'i yang dag pa'i lta ba nas yang dag pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi bar yan lag brgyad dang ldan no/ / mi slob pa ni mi slob pa'i yang dag pa'i lta ba nas ting nge 'dzin gyi bar brgyad dang*/ mi slob pa'i yang dag pa'i rnam par grol ba dang*/ mi slob pa'i yang dag pa'i shes pa ste yan lag bcu dang ldan no zhes gsungs pa'i slob pa la yang dag pa'i rnam par grol ba dang yang dag pa'i shes pa ma bshad ce na/

Question: A sūtra declares: A learner is one who possesses eight branches,[1753] from learner right view to learner right concentration. A nonlearner is one who possesses ten branches: eight from nonlearner right view to nonlearner right concentration, plus nonlearner correct liberation and nonlearner correct knowledge.[1754] Why does this passage not explain correct liberation and correct knowledge for a learner?
bcings phyir slob pa'i yan lag tu/ / rnam grol ma bshad de rnam gnyis/ / 75
Liberation is not explained as a learner branch because learners are bound. That liberation has two types. (6:75cd)

nyon mongs pa'i 'ching ba las gtan du nges par grol ba dang grol ba de so so rang gis shes pas de gnyis su 'jog pa la/ slob pa rnams ni da dung nyon mongs pas bcings pa'i phyir slob pa'i yan lag tu yang dag pa'i rnam grol dang yang dag pa'i shes pa ma bshad do/ / 'ching ba'i phyogs gcig las rnam par grol bas ni yang dag pa'i rnam grol gyi yan lag tu mi 'gyur ro/ / rnam par grol ba de yang 'dus byas dang 'dus ma byas rnam pa gnyis yod pa las

Reply: Those two are established through full liberation from the ties (bandhana) of afflictions and individual complete knowledge of that liberation. Correct liberation (samyagvimukti) and correct knowledge (samyagjñāna) are not explained as branches (śaikṣāṅga) because learners are still bound (baddhatva) by afflictions. Liberation from one type of tie does not become the branch of correct liberation. Further, that liberation has two types: unconditioned and conditioned.
nyon mongs bcom pa 'dus ma byas/ / mos pa 'dus byas yan lag ni/ / de yin de nyid rnam grol gnyis/ / byang chub ji skad bshad ces pa/ / 76

Unconditioned liberation is the destruction of the afflictions; conditioned liberation is resolution. That branch is that resolution. Just that is both liberations. That explained to be enlightenment is knowledge. (6:76)

nyon mongs pa bcom pa so sor brtags 'gog ni rnam grol 'dus ma byas yin la/ rnam par grol ba la der nges pa mi slob pa'i mos pa ni rnam grol 'dus byas yin la/ gang zhig mi slob pa'i yan lag tu gsungs pa'i yang dag pa'i rnam grol ni rnam grol 'dus byas mos pa de yin te/ yan lag bcu char 'dus byas yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dus ma byas ni skal ba mi mnyam pa'i phyir dang*/ slob pa dang mi slob pa gnyis ka ma yin pa'i phyir yan lag ma yin no/ / rnam par grol ba'i yan lag 'dus byas de nyid ni mdo las sems 'dod chags las rnam par grol ba dang*/ shes rab ma rig pa las rnam par grol ba gnyis su gsungs te/ rnam grol 'dus byas de nyid tshul khrims kyi phung po la sogs lnga'i nang nas rnam par grol ba'i phung po'ang yin no zhes bye brag tu smra ba rnams 'dod do/ / slob dpon ni mos pa 'ba' zhig rnam par grol ba ma yin gyi sems rnam par grol ba dang shes rab rnam par grol ba dang 'dod chags la sogs pa las rnam par grol ba'i zag med kyi sems dang sems byung 'dun pa dang brtson 'grus la sogs pa gzhan dag kyang yin te/ mdo las/ stag gi byang chub kyi bu dag rnam par grol bar yongs su dag pa'i gtso bo gang yin zhe na/ 'di dag dge slong 'dod chags las sems 'dod chags dang bral zhing rnam par grol ba yin/ zhe sdang dang gti mug las sems 'dod chags dang bral zhing rnam par grol ba yin te/ 'di ltar rnam par grol ba'i phung po yongs su ma rdzogs pa yongs su rdzogs par byed pa'am/ yongs su rdzogs pa rjes su 'dzin par byed pa 'dun pa dang brtson 'grus gang yin pa zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro zhes 'chad do/ / gal te yang dag pa'i shes pa ni yan lag bcu pa ma yin te/ yang dag pa'i lta ba'i nang du 'dus pa'i phyir ro zhe na/

Unconditioned liberation (asaṃskṛtavimukti) is the analytical cessation that is the destruction of the afflictions (kleśahāna). Conditioned liberation (saṃskṛtavimukti) is the nonlearner resolution (adhimukti) discerning it to be liberation. Correct liberation, which is described as a nonlearner branch, [585] is that resolution which is conditioned liberation, because it is a conditioned state that is one of the ten branches. Unconditioned liberation is not a branch, because it is not a homogeneous state and it is neither a learner nor a nonlearner. Just that conditioned branch of liberation is stated in the sūtras to be both liberations — the mind liberated from attachment and wisdom liberated from ignorance — since just that conditioned liberation is the aggregate of liberation from among the five aggregates of ethics and so on. This is asserted by Vaibhāṣikas. Vasubandhu[1755] explains that resolution alone is not liberation; liberation also consists of the mind of liberation, the wisdom of liberation, and the uncontaminated minds and mental factors liberated from attachment, such as aspiration, effort, and so on, because a sūtra states: Vyāghrabodhānaya, what is the main fully purified liberation? Monks, it is the mind freed and liberated from attachment and it is the mind freed and liberated from aversion and delusion, for it is that which completes any incomplete aggregate of liberation. Alternately, it is any aspiration and effort that subsequently maintain the completed aggregate of liberation.[1756] Objection: Correct knowledge is not the tenth branch because it is included within correct view.
ma yin te/
Reply: That is not so,

byang chub sngar ji skad bshad pa'i zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa gang yin pa de nyid yang dag pa'i shes pa yin la de yang dag pa'i lta ba ni ma yin te/ zad dang mi skye'i blo lta min zhes 'chad par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / yang dag pa'i shes pa de ni rnam par grol ba'i ye shes gzigs pa'i phung po'ang yin te/ rang gi byang chub shes pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te sems rnam par grol na sems 'das pa'am/ ma 'ongs pa'am/ da ltar byung ba gang zhig rnam par grol bar 'gyur zhe na

because just that knowledge of elimination and nonarising that was previously explained to be enlightenment is correct knowledge. But that is not correct view because awareness of elimination and nonarising is not view. Correct knowledge is also the aggregate of seeing that is the transcendent wisdom of liberation because it is knowledge of one’s enlightenment. Question: If the mind is liberated, then is the mind that occurs in the past, future, or present liberated?
mi slob sems ni skye 'gyur ba/ / sgrib pa las ni rnam grol 'gyur/ / 'gag par 'gyur ba'i lam gyis ni/ / de yi sgrib pa rab tu spong / / 77
The nonlearner mind that will arise will be liberated from obscurations. The path that will cease fully abandons its obscurations. (6:77)

mi slob pa'i sems ni skye bar 'gyur ba ma 'ongs pa sgrib pa las rnam par grol bar 'gyur ba yin te/ 'das pa'i sgrib pa yod pa yin la da ltar ba ni sgrib pa la dngos su gnod pa rdo rje lta bu yin te/ de sgrib pa'i thob pa dang dus mnyam pa'i phyir dang*/ de'i rjes thogs su sgrib pa las rnam par grol ba'i sems skye ba'i phyir ro/{ nyon mongs pa ni de'i thob pa la bzhag ste de skye ba la gegs byed pas so/ /} 'o na mi skye ba'i chos can dag ji ltar sgrib pa las grol ba yin zhe na/ de dang 'dra ba'i phyir yin no/ / de nyid kyi phyir bstan bcos las mi slob pa'i sems ma 'ongs pa sgrib pa rnams las rnam par grol bar 'gyur ro zhes bshad do/ / 'o na lam 'das pa la sogs pa gang gis sgrib pa de spong zhe na/

Reply: The nonlearner mind that will arise will be liberated from future obscurations. It is the vajra-like mind directly harming past obscurations and present obscurations, because it occurs at the same time as the obtainment of obscurations and it generates the mind liberated from obscurations immediately after it. {It is established at the time of the obtainment of afflictions, but it impedes the generation of afflictions.} Question: How is one liberated from obscurations that are unarisen states? Reply: This is similar to future states. Thus the treatise [Attainment of Knowledge][1757] mentions: The mind of a nonlearner is liberated from future obscurations.[1758] Question: What past path and so on abandons that obscuration?

'gag par 'gyur ba de 'gag pa la mngon du phyogs pa da ltar ba'i lam gyis ni da ltar ba de'i sgrib pa rab tu spong ba yin te/ 'di ltar spong ba ni bya ba 'gal ba'i sgo nas gnod pa byed pa yin na 'das pa dang ma 'ongs pa ni bya ba 'gags pa dang ma skyes pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te da ltar ba'i lam gyis da ltar ba'i sgrib pa spong ba ni ma yin te/ rgyud gcig la nyon mongs pa dang ye shes kyi shes pa rgyud gnyis su thal ba'i phyir dang*/ 'gal ba lhan cig tu 'byung bar thal ba'i phyir dang*/ ye shes nyon mongs pa'i 'jig rgyur thal ba'i phyir ro zhe na/ de lta ma yin te/ nyon mongs pa'i thob pa'am sa bon spang byar 'dod pas yun ring du mi gnas shing gnod pa byed bzhin pa'i lhan cig pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ spang bya phyi ma bskyed pa'i nus pa dang mi ldan par bskyed pa la gnod par brjod pa'i phyir skyon med do/ / 'o na nyon mongs bcom pa 'dus ma byas zhes rnam grol 'dus ma byas su bshad pa gang yin pa de dang mdo'am bstan bcos las spangs pa'i khams dang*/ 'dod chags dang bral ba'i khams dang*/ 'gog pa'i khams zhes khams gsum bshad pa de dag la khyad par ci yod ce na/

Reply: The present path [586] will cease and, manifesting cessation, fully abandon its present obscurations. For when it harms that which is to be abandoned through countering its action, past and future actions are stopped and do not arise. Objection: The present path does not abandon present obscurations. If it did, there would be both streams of affliction and transcendent wisdom in one mindstream, mutually excluding states would occur simultaneously, and transcendent wisdom would be the cause of destroying affliction. Reply: There is no error. The obtainment of affliction and the desire to abandon the seeds of affliction do not abide long together, for they simultaneously harm each other, and generating the nonobtainment of the capacity for generating future objects to be abandoned is called “harming.” Question: What is the difference between the Abhidharmakośa stating “Unconditioned liberation is the destruction of the afflictions” (6:76a) and a sūtra or a treatise[1759] stating “realms of abandonment, realms free from attachment, and realms of cessation,” which explains three realms?
'dus ma byas nyid khams zhes bya/ / 'dod chags kun zad 'dod chags bral/ / spangs pa'i khams ni gzhan dag go/ / 'gog pa'i khams zhes bya ba gzhi/ / 78

Unconditioned liberation is known as the three realms. It is free from attachment since it fully eliminates all attachment. It is the realm of abandonment since it eliminates other. It is the realm of cessation since it eliminates the basis. (6:78)

rnam grol 'dus ma byas su bshad pa gang yin pa de nyid spangs pa la sogs pa'i khams gsum du shes par bya ste/ 'di ltar spang bya khams gsum gyi 'dod chags kun zad cing spangs pa ni 'dod chags dang bral ba'i khams yin la/ spangs pa'i khams zhes bya ba ni 'dod chags las gzhan pa'i nyon mongs pa zhe sdang la sogs pa dag yang dag par zad cing spangs pa'o/ / 'gog pa'i khams zhes bya ba ni nyon mongs pa'i gzhi yang dag par zad pa ste/ gzhi'i sgra yang 'dir yul dang rgyu la brjod par 'dod pa ste nyon mongs pa las gzhan pa'i gzugs la sogs pa zag pa dang bcas pa dag go { 'di ni 'dun pa'i 'dod chags dang bral ba la 'dod do}/ / 'o na dngos po gang gis yid 'byung bar 'gyur ba'i dngos po des 'dod chags dang 'bral bar 'gyur ram zhe na/

Reply: That which is called unconditioned liberation should be known as the three realms such as the realm of abandonment and so on. It is the realm free from attachment (virāgadhātu) since it fully eliminates and abandons all attachment to the three realms to be abandoned. It is the realm of abandonment (prahāṇadhātu) since it correctly eliminates and abandons afflictions other than attachment, such as aversion and so on. It is the realm of cessation (nirodhadhātu) since it correctly eliminates the basis of the afflictions. In this context, the term “basis” refers to objects and causes that are contaminated states, such as form, that are other than affliction. {It is asserted to be freedom from longing desire.} Question: Do those things that induce disgust also induce freedom from attachment?
sdug bsngal rgyu bzod shes rnams kyis/ / yid 'byung gang gis spong 'gyur ba/ / kun gyi 'dod chags 'bral bar 'gyur/ / de ltar na ni mu bzhi srid/ / 79
Disgust arises through perseverance and knowledge of suffering and its cause. Freedom from attachment to all arises due to those abandoning afflictions. Thus four possibilities exist. (6:79)

sdug bsngal dang rgyu kun 'byung la dmigs pa'i bzod pa dang shes pa rnams kyis ni bden pa de gnyis zag bcas yin pas yid 'byung bar 'gyur la {yul dman pa la skyon du brtag pas } bzod pa{ bzhi} dang{ sgom lam} shes pa gang gis dngos su nyon mongs pa spong bar 'gyur ba de ni bden pa bzhi po gang la dmigs kyang rung kun gyi 'dod chags dang 'bral bar 'gyur ro/ / de lta na ni yid 'byung ba dang 'dod chags dang bral ba la mu bzhi srid de/ yid 'byung bar 'gyur la 'dod chags dang 'bral bar mi 'gyur ba ni sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung la dmigs pa'i sgom lam yin yang rung sbyor ba dang rnam grol dang khyad par can gyi lam dang*/ chags bral sngon 'gro'i bden pa dang po gnyis la dmigs pa'i chos shes pa'i bzod pa dang shes pa rnams te/ thams cad kyang yid 'byung ba'i dngos po la dmigs pas yid skyo bar byed pa'i phyir dang*/ sbyor ba'i lam la sogs pa gsum ni spong lam ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ chags bral sngon 'gro'i bden pa dang po gnyis la dmigs pa'i chos shes pa'i bzod pa spong lam yin yang 'jig rten pa'i sgom lam gyis sngar du spangs zin pa'i phyir dang*/ shes pa ni spong lam ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / rjes su shes pa'i bzod pa dag gis ni nges par nyon mongs pa rnams spong ste/ 'jig rten pa'i lam gyi srid rtse las 'dod chags dang mi 'bral ba'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: Disgust arises through perseverance and knowledge focusing on the truth of suffering and its cause, the truth of origin, {and investigating the faults of inferior objects}. Freedom from attachment to all arises due to those {four types of} perseverance and knowledge {of the path of meditation} focusing on any of the four truths and directly abandoning afflictions. Thus four possibilities exist for disgust and freedom from attachment. (1) Disgust arising but freedom from attachment not arising. This is, for instance, the path of meditation focusing on the truths of suffering and origin; the path of preparation, the liberated path, and the special path; and perseverance for Dharma knowledge and Dharma knowledge itself that focus on the first two truths of those who were previously freed from attachment. These are disappointed with all objects since they focus on repulsive things. [587] But these three such as the path of preparation are not abandoning paths. And though perseverance for Dharma knowledge focusing on the first two truths in those previously freed from attachment is an abandoning path, those afflictions have already been abandoned by the mundane path of meditation; and knowledge also is not an abandoning path. Though perseverance for subsequent knowledge definitely abandons afflictions, the mundane path does not free one from attachment to the summit of existence.

'dod chags dang 'bral bar 'gyur la yid 'byung bar mi 'gyur ba ni 'gog lam la dmigs pa'i spang bya dngos su spong ba'i bar chad med pa'i lam chags bral sngon 'gro'i 'gog lam la chos shes pa'i bzod pa ma gtogs pa rnams te/ de dag ni 'jig rten pa'i sgom lam gyis sngar du spangs zin pa'i phyir dang*/ gzhan ni spang bya la dngos su gnod byed yin pa'i phyir dang*/ de dag gi dmigs pa 'gog lam zag med la yon tan du lta bas mchog tu dga' ba'i dngos po la dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ /

(2) Freedom from attachment arising but disgust not arising. This is, for instance, the uninterrupted path directly abandoning objects to be abandoned that focuses on the truths of cessation and path. It excludes perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truths of cessation and path of those previously freed from attachment, which were previously abandoned by the mundane path of meditation. The other three directly harm the objects of abandonment, but [disgust does not arise] here, because this one focuses on objects of supreme joy through viewing the qualities of uncontaminated cessation and path, its focal objects.

gnyis ka yin pa ni bden pa po dang gnyis la dmigs pa'i bar chad med pa'i lam chags bral sngon 'gro'i bden pa dang po gnyis la dmigs pa'i chos shes pa'i bzod pa las gzhan pa rnams te/ yid 'byung ba'i dngos po la dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ nyon mongs pa dngos su spong bar byed pa'i phyir ro/ /

(3) That which is both. This is, for instance, the uninterrupted path focusing on the first two truths. It is distinct from perseverance for Dharma knowledge focusing on the first two truths of those previously freed from attachment because it focuses on disgusting things and because it acts to directly abandon afflictions.

gnyis ka ma yin pa ni 'gog lam la dmigs pa'i sbyor ba dang rnam grol dang khyad par can gyi lam dang*/ chags bral sngon 'gro'i 'gog lam la chos shes pa'i bzod pa dang shes pa rnams dang*/ bar chad med pa'i lam yin yang nyon mongs pa mi spong ba dbang po 'pho ba la sogs pa'i gnas skabs kyi bar chad med pa'i lam kha cig kyang yin {de la 'dod pa'am ci yang med pa'i bar la chags pa dang bral ba zhig bden pa rnams la lta na chos shes chos bzod rnams kyis nyon mongs mi spong ste/ 'jig rten pa'i sgom lam gyis sngar spangs zin pa'i phyir bral thob zag med skye ba 'ba' zhig tu zad do/ / rjes shes rjes bzod dag gis ni nges par nyon mongs spong ste/ 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis srid rtse la chags pa dang mi 'bral ba'i phyir ro/ / lan cig phyir 'ong chags bral sngon 'gro bden pa la lta ba ni mthong spang spong dgos pas de dang mi 'dra'o/ / shes pa rnams kyi sgom lam la sbyor ba dang*/ rnam grol dang*/ khyad par gyi lam dang*/ kha cig gis kyang mi spong ngo } no/ /

(4) That which is neither. This is, for instance, the path of preparation, the path of liberation, and the special path focusing on cessation and path; perseverance and knowledge of the truths of cessation and path of those previously freed from attachment; and the uninterrupted path in the context of not abandoning afflictions but upgrading faculty and so on. {Those free from attachment to the desire realm up to nothingness do not abandon afflictions through Dharma knowledge or Dharma perseverance viewing the four truths; they have already previously abandoned them by the mundane path, since those who obtain freedom eliminate afflictions by generating the uncontaminated path alone. Dharma knowledge and Dharma perseverance definitely abandon afflictions because they are not freed from attachment to the summit of existence by the mundane path. Since once returners previously freed from attachment who view the truths must abandon objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing, that is not similar. Also, among those with knowledge who prepare for the path of meditation, the liberated path, or the special path, some do not abandon afflictions.}
dmigs pa shes dang bsgom pa'i rim/ / sgom pa po dang de yi lam/ / ji bzhin shes nas der 'jug 'dod/ / dge slong gnas 'di mnyan par rigs/ /

Monks it is proper to listen to this chapter, and having understood focal objects, knowledge, the stages of meditation, meditators, and their paths, you should generate the desire to enter those states.
chos mngon pa'i mdzod kyi tshig le'ur byas pa las/ /lam dang gang zag bstan pa zhes bya ba ste gnas drug pa'o// //
chos mngon pa'i mdzod kyi 'grel pa mngon pa'i rgyan las lam dang gang zag bstan pa zhes bya ba ste gnas drug pa'i bshad pa'o// ! //
This has been part VI, called the “Exposition of Paths and Beings,” from Ornament of Abhidharma: A Commentary on the Verses of the Abhidharmakośa. [588]
31. Perseverance, Knowledge, and View
gnas bdun pa ye shes bstan pa/
THE EXPOSITION OF EPISTEMOLOGY
da ni gnas bdun pa 'chad pa na bzod pa dang shes pa dang lta ba'i khyad par bshad pa dang*/ shes pa bye brag tu bshad pa dang*/ de dag gi yon tan bshad pa gsum las/
In explaining part VII, there are three headings: (1) distinguishing perseverance, knowledge, and view; (2) detailed explanation of knowledge; and (3) the qualities of knowledge.
bzod pa dang shes pa dang lta ba'i khyad par/
Distinguishing perseverance, knowledge, and view
dang po ni gal te bzod pa dang shes pa dang yang dag pa'i lta ba dang yang dag pa'i shes pa rnams la khyad par ci zhig yod ce na/
Question: How does one distinguish perseverance, knowledge, correct view, and correct knowledge?
dri med bzod rnams shes pa min/ / zad dang mi skye'i blo lta min/ / de las gzhan 'phags blo gnyis ka/ / gzhan shes drug ni lta ba'ang yin/ / 1
Stainless perseverance is not knowledge. Awareness of elimination and nonarising is not view. Ārya awareness other than those is both. Other wisdom is knowledge. Six are also view. (7:1)

Reply: The eight types of stainless perseverance are not knowledge. Knowledge possesses intrinsic certainty, whereas perseverance has doubt about its object. Perseverance is an uninterrupted path, and at that time it has not yet abandoned the negative tendencies {and doubt} that are its objects of abandonment. {“Its” is stated to refute the fallacious consequence that the first seven knowledges are not knowledge}. These states of perseverance are view since they correctly comprehend {the four truths as impermanent and so on.} {“Stainless” is stated since contaminated perseverance is knowledge; knowledge of elimination necessarily abandons doubt; but that which abandons doubt should not be ascertained as knowledge, like the perseverance of one previously freed from attachment. Knowledge of elimination and knowledge of nonarising are not view (dṛṣṭi) because they merely comprehend lack of activity and do not investigate the four truths and because the result has already been completed.}

zad pa shes pa dang mi skye ba shes pa'i bla ni lta ba min te/ yang dag par rtog pa med pa'i phyir dang*/ dmigs pa dang rnam pa 'tshol ba'i bsam pa can ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de ni yang dag pa'i shes pa zhes bya'i shes pa tsam yang ma yin no/ /

Awareness (dhī) that is knowledge of elimination and knowledge of nonarising is not view. It has no right investigation, and it does not possess contemplation seeking the focal object and aspect. It is called “correct knowledge” but not “mere knowledge.”

bzod pa brgyad dang zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa de dag las gzhan pa'i 'phags pa zag pa med pa'i blo ste sdug bsngal la chos shes pa nas lam la rjes su shes pa'i bar gyi shes rab rnams ni shes pa dang yang dag pa'i lta ba gnyis ka yin te/ rnam grol gyi lam yin pas rang gi yul la the tshom spangs pas nges pa'i bdag nyid can yin pa'i phyir dang*/ yang dag par rtog pa'i bdag nyid can yang yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Uncontaminated ārya awareness, which is other than those eight types of perseverance and the knowledge of elimination and nonarising, comprise the wisdoms from Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering up to subsequent knowledge of the truth of path. They are both knowledge and right view because they possess intrinsic certainty (being liberated paths that abandon doubt) and they possess intrinsic right investigation.

'phags pa'i blo las gzhan zag bcas 'jig rten pa'i shes rab thams cad ni kun rdzob shes pa yin te/ zag bcas la shes pa ma yin pa'i shes rab mi srid pa'i {phyir dang shes rab gang yin yang shes pa yin pa'i } phyir ro/ / de yang sgo lnga'i rnam shes kyi 'khor du byung ba'i shes rab dge mi dge lung ma bstan thams cad dang ye shes kyi 'khor du byung ba'i shes rab lta ba drug po ma gtogs pa nyon mongs pa can dang ma bsgribs lung ma bstan rnams ni shes pa kho na yin no/ / yid shes kyi 'khor du byung ba'i shes rab 'jig tshogs la lta ba la sogs pa nyon mongs pa can lnga dang 'jig rten pa'i yang dag pa'i lta ba ste drug ni kun rdzob shes pa yin par ma zad lta ba'ang yin te/ nges par rtog pa'i bdag nyid yin pa'i phyir ro/ / {des na lta ba kho na yin pa ni med do }

All contaminated mundane wisdom other than ārya awareness is conventional knowledge, because it is impossible that it is wisdom not aware of contaminated states {and because any wisdom is knowledge}. Moreover, all virtuous, nonvirtuous, and neutral wisdom occurring in the retinue of consciousness of the five sense doors, as well as afflicted wisdom and the unobscured-neutral wisdom occurring in the retinue of transcendent wisdom except for the six views, are knowledge alone. The six — including (1–5) five afflicted wisdoms such as the afflicted view of the self [589] occurring in the retinue of mental consciousness and (6) correct mundane view — are not only conventional knowledge but also view because they are states of decisive conception. {Therefore those that are view alone do not exist.}
gnyis pa shes pa bye brag tu bshad pa
DETAILED EXPLANATION OF KNOWLEDGE

['di] la shes pa'i ngo bo'i dbye ba dang*/ grangs nges pa dang*/ rnam pa dang*/ sa dang brten pa dang*/ dran pa nyer gzhag tu bzhag pa dang*/ dmigs pa dang*/ ldan pa'i tshul dang*/ thob pa'i tshul brgyad yod pa las

This has eight headings: (1) classification of the nature of knowledge, (2) set number, (3) aspects of knowledge, (4) levels and the basis of knowledge, (5) knowledge as foundations of mindfulness, (6) focal objects of knowledge, (7) how knowledge is possessed, and (8) how knowledge is obtained.
dang po [shes pa'i ngo bo'i dbye ba] ni
The nature and types of knowledge

{chos dang rdzas dang kun rdzob dang*/ / gzhan gyi sems dang sdug bsngal dang*/ / kun 'byung ba dang 'gog pa dang*/ / lam dang zad dang mi skye zhes/ / zhes pa bsdu tshig go } mdo las shes pa ni bcu ste/
{The Compendium declares: Desire realm, higher, conventional, others’ minds, suffering, origin, and cessation, path, elimination, and nonarising.} Also a sūtra records: There are ten.

'di lta ste/ chos shes pa dang*/ rjes su shes pa dang*/ kun rdzob shes pa dang*/ pha rol gyi sems shes pa dang*/ sdug bsngal shes pa dang*/ kun 'byung shes pa dang*/ 'gog pa shes pa dang*/ lam shes pa dang*/ zad pa shes pa dang*/ mi skye ba shes pa'o zhes gsungs pa'i

It is like this: there is Dharma knowledge, subsequent knowledge, conventional knowledge, knowledge of others’ minds, knowledge of suffering, knowledge of origin, knowledge of cessation, knowledge of path, knowledge of elimination, and knowledge of nonarising.
shes pa zag bcas zag pa med/ / dang po kun rdzob ces bya'o/ / zag med rnam gnyis chos dang ni/ / rjes su shes pa kho na yin/ / 2
Knowledge is contaminated or uncontaminated. This first is called conventional. Uncontaminated knowledge has just two types, desire knowledge and higher knowledge. (7:2)
