Knowledge of the minds of others exists in the four absorptions. It is based in the desire realm and form realms. That called Dharma knowledge is based in the desire realm alone. Those based in the three realms are the eight others. (7:15)
gzhan gyi yid shes pa ni bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi bzhi kho na na yod kyi gzhan na med do/{/'di mngon shes kyis bsdus la/ rnam gnas ni gzugs la rtsom pas de nyer bsdogs dang gzugs med na med do/} /

Knowledge of the minds of others (anyamanojñāna) exists only in the four actual bases of absorption and does not exist on other levels. {It is subsumed by higher perception but does not exist in the formless realm since its aspects and abidance are initiated in the form realm}.

gzhan gyi sems shes de ni 'dod pa dang gzugs kyi rten can yin gyi gzugs med pa la rten pa ni ma yin te/ gang zag phan tshun yul ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / chos shes pa zhes bya ba ni 'dod pa'i rten can kho na yin te/ 'dod pa'i gnyen po yin pa'i phyir khams gong ma gnyis su ni chos shes mngon du mi byed de/ chos shes 'dod pa la dmigs pa la gzugs med 'dod pa la mi dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ chos shes ni gtsor 'dod pa sun 'byin pa yin na gzugs khams su skyes pa na 'dod pa la 'dod chags dang bral ba dang*/ sa 'phos pas btang bas de sun mi 'byin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dod par skyes pa ni 'dod chags dang bral yang 'dod khams kyi phung po'i lhag ma lus pa'i phyir chos shes mngon du byed de zhes kha cig zer ro/ / slob dpon 'dun bzang na re cho shes ni 'dod pa kho nar mngon du byed kyi khams gong ma gnyis su ni ma yin te/ chos shes de la snyoms par 'jug ldang gi sems rnams 'dod pa kho na na yod pa'i phyir ro/ / yang na chos shes kyi rjes su 'brang ba'i tshul khrims kyi rten 'dod pa'i 'byung bzhi yin pas de dag khams gong ma gnyis na med pa'i phyir chos shes 'dod pa'i rten can kho na yin no zhes zer ro/ / khams gsum pa'i rten can ni pha rol sems shes dang chos shes las gzhan pa'i shes pa brgyad po dag yin no/ /

Knowledge of the minds of others is based in the desire and form realms, but it is not based in the formless realm, because beings there cannot take each other as objects. That called Dharma knowledge is based in the desire realm alone because it is the antidote of desire-realm affliction. Dharma knowledge does not manifest in the two higher realms. This is because Dharma knowledge focuses on desire-realm objects and formless-realm states do not focus on desire-realm objects. Dharma knowledge mainly counters desire. When one is born in the form realm, one is free of attachment to the desire realm, but this is not by countering desire; it is relinquished merely by changing level. Thus, though one is free of attachment to the desire realm, one may still be reborn in the desire realm. Dharma knowledge would manifest because residual desire-realm aggregates remain. This is stated by one scholar. Master Saṅghabhadra says: Dharma knowledge is manifested in the desire realm alone and not in the two higher realms because minds entering and rising from meditative attainment that is Dharma knowledge [604] exist only in the desire realm. Again, since the [physical] basis of ethics as a complement of Dharma knowledge is the four primary elements of the desire realm, it does not exist in the two higher realms. Therefore, Dharma knowledge is based in the desire realm alone.[1789] Knowledge that is based in the three realms consists of the eight remaining knowledges — those other than knowledge of the minds of others and Dharma knowledge.
lnga pa [dran pa nyer bzhag tu bzhag pa] ni
Knowledge as foundations of mindfulness
'o na shes pa 'di dag dran pa nyer gzhag gang gi ngo bo yin zhe na/
Question: These knowledges are naturally included within which close placement of mindfulness?
'gog blo dran pa nyer gzhag pa/ / gcig ste pha rol sems blo ni/ / gsum mo lhag ma bzhi yin no/ /
Awareness knowing cessation is close placement of mindfulness alone. Awareness knowing the minds of others is three. Those remaining are four. (7:16abc)

'gog pa shes pa'i blo ni dran pa nye bar bzhag pa gcig kho na ste/ dran pa nyer gzhag bstan pa las/ chos ni lus dang tshor ba dang sems dag las gzhan pa yin no zhes 'byung bas chos dran pa nyer gzhag kho na yin pa'i phyir ro/ / pha rol gyi sems shes pa'i blo ni lus la mi dmigs pas dran pa nyer gzhag phyi ma gsum mo/ / 'gog pa dang pha rol sems shes las gzhan pa shes pa lhag ma brgyad ni ci rigs par sdug bsngal shes pa la sogs pa de dag res 'ga' lus nas res 'ga' chos kyi bar la dmigs shing*/ lam shes pa'ang gal te zag med kyi sdom pa la dmigs na de lus dran pa nyer gzhag tu'ang 'gyur bas dran par nyer gzhag bzhi ga yin {kun rdzob shes pa ni thams cad kyi yul can yin pa'i phyir } no/ /
drug pa [shes pa de dag phan tshun gang gis dmigs par bshad pa] ni
Focal objects of knowledge
'o na shes pa de dag phan tshun gang gis dmigs par gang gyur zhe na/
Question: What types of knowledge focus on what knowledge?
chos blo'i spyod yul dgu yin no/ / 16
Nine are the object field of awareness that is Dharma. (7:16d)

chos shes pa'i blo'i spyod yul te dmigs pa ni shes pa dgu yin te/ lam la chos shes pas rjes shes ma gtogs pa'i zag med kyi shes pa bdun la dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung shes pas bsdus pa'i chos shes pas kun rdzob shes pa dang gzhan gyi sems shes zag bcas la dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: Nine knowledges are the focal objects or object fields (gocara) of awareness (dhī) that is Dharma knowledge because Dharma knowledge of the truth of path focuses on the (1–7) seven uncontaminated knowledges except for subsequent knowledge, and Dharma knowledge that subsumes knowledge of the truths of suffering and origin focuses on (8) contaminated conventional knowledge and (9) the knowledge of others’ minds.
lam rjes blo yi dgu yin no/ / sdug bsngal rgyu blo'i gnyis yin no/ / bzhi yi bcu yin gcig gi min/ / chos bcu dag ni sbyar bar bya/ / 17

Nine are objects of awareness that is path and subsequent knowledge. Two are the objects of awareness of suffering and cause. Ten are the objects of four. None are the object of one. Ten phenomena are known through applying them. (7:17)

lam shes pa'i blo'i dmigs pa'ang shes pa dgu yin te/ de ni zag med kho na la dmigs par nges pas kun rdzob shes pa ma gtogs pa'i phyir ro/ / rjes su shes pa'i blo'i dmigs pa'ang chos rjes blo phyogs phan tshun min zhes 'byung bas chos shes ma gtogs pa'i shes pa dgu yin no/ / sdug bsngal dang de'i rgyu kun 'byung shes pa'i blo'i spyod yul ni bden pa dang po gnyis kyis bsdus pa'i kun rdzob shes pa dang pha rol sems shes zag bcas gnyis yin no/ / kun rdzob shes pa dang gzhan gyi sems shes dang zad pa shes pa dang mi skye ba shes pa bzhi'i spyod yul ni shes pa bcu char yin te/ ci rigs par thams cad la dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang gzhan ni go sla la pha rol sems shes zag med kyi dmigs pa ni shes pa dgu yin la/ zag bcas kyi ni kun rdzob shes pa dang pha rol sems shes zag bcas yin no/ / gcig gi ste 'gog pa shes pa gcig pu'i dmigs pa ni shes pa thams cad min te/ de ni so sor brtags 'gog kho na la dmigs la de ni shes pa'i rang bzhin ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Also nine knowledges are the focal objects of awareness that is path knowledge because it definitely focuses on (1–9) uncontaminated knowledge alone that excludes conventional knowledge. Also, nine knowledges excluding Dharma knowledge are the focal object of awareness that is subsequent knowledge, since it is said, “Awarenesses compatible with Dharma and subsequent knowledge do not mutually cognize each other” (7:6ab). Two are the object field of awareness knowing the truths of suffering and origin that is the cause of that: (1) contaminated conventional knowledge subsumed by both the first two truths and (2) knowledge of others’ minds. Ten knowledges are the object field of four knowledges — (1) conventional knowledge, (2) knowledge of others’ minds, (3) knowledge of elimination, and (4) knowledge [605] of nonarising — because they focus on all types. The others are easy to understand. Nine knowledges are the focal object of uncontaminated knowledge of others’ minds. Conventional knowledge and contaminated knowledge of others’ minds are the focal object of contaminated knowledge of others’ minds. None at all are the focal object of one, the knowledge of cessation alone, because that focuses on analytical cessation alone and that is not of the nature of knowledge.
shes bya'i chos thams cad rnam pa bcur phye la chos bcu po dag ni shes pa du zhig gi yul du 'gyur ba sbyar te shes par bya'o/ /
Ten phenomena that are classified as the ten aspects of all phenomena to be known are known through applying those knowledges to multiple objects.
chos bcu po gang dag ce na/
Question: What are the ten phenomena?
khams gsum pa dang dri med chos/ / 'dus ma byas rnams gnyis gnyis so/ / kun rdzob gcig pus rang tshogs las/ / gzhan ni bdag med nyid rig 'gyur/ / 18
Phenomena of the three realms, the stainless, and the unconditioned are classified as two each. Conventional knowledge alone cognizes all, except for its own retinue, to be selfless. (7:18)

chos 'dus byas la 'dod pa dang gzugs dang gzugs med pa ste khams gsum pa'i chos dang dri ma med pa'i chos te rnam pa bzhi dang*/ 'dus ma byas kyi chos rnams te lnga la re re la'ang rnam pa gnyis gnyis su phye bas so/ / ji ltar zhe na dang po bzhi la mtshungs ldan dang mtshungs ldan ma yin pa gnyis gnyis te brgyad dang*/ 'dus ma byas la so sor brtags 'gog dge ba dang nam mkha' dang brtags min lung ma bstan yin pas gnyis su 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / ji ltar sbyar zhe na/ kun rdzob shes pa'i yul du bcu po thams cad dang*/ chos shes kyi yul du 'dod pa{'i chos gnyis }dang zag med 'dus byas kyi gnyis gnyis te{ chos shes zag med kyi cha gnyis te} bzhi dang 'dus ma byas dge ba ste lnga dang*/ rjes shes kyi yul du khams gong ma gnyis dang zag med 'dus byas kyi{ mtshungs ldan yin min} gnyis gnyis te drug dang 'dus ma byas dge ba ste bdun dang*/ sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung shes pa'i yul du khams gsum gyi chos drug drug dang*/ 'gog pa shes pa'i yul du 'dus ma byas dge ba gcig pu dang*/ lam shes pa'i yul du zag med 'dus byas kyi gnyis dang*/ pha rol sems shes kyi yul du 'dod gzugs dang zag med kyi mtshungs ldan gsum dang*/ zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa'i yul du 'dus ma byas lung ma bstan ma gtogs pa dgu 'gyur te/ shes pa de dag gi dmigs yul shes bya de dag yin pa'i phyir ro/ / des na bye brag tu smra ba ltar na nam mkha' dang brtags min gyi 'gog pa ni bden bzhir ma 'dus par 'dod de/ TIka byed dag gis kyang zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa dag ni bden pa bzhi la dmigs pa'i phyir la/ 'dus ma byas lung du ma bstan pa ni bden pa bzhi la ma gtogs pa'i phyir ro zhes bshad do/ /

Reply: They are the four — (1) the conditioned phenomena of the desire realm, (2) form realm, and (3) formless realms, which are phenomena of the three realms, and (4) stainless phenomena — and (5) unconditioned phenomena. Each of these five also is classified as two each. Question: How? Reply: (1–8) The first four have two types each: concomitant and the nonconcomitant, making eight. Unconditioned states have two types: (9) the virtuous state of analytical cessation and (10) the neutral states of space and nonanalytical cessation. Question: How are those knowledges applied to them? Reply: All ten are objects of conventional knowledge. Five are objects of Dharma knowledge: four including (1–2) {two phenomena} of the desire realm and (3–4) two uncontaminated conditioned states, {both uncontaminated objects of Dharma knowledge,} and (5) virtuous unconditioned phenomena, making five. Seven are objects of subsequent knowledge: both {concomitant and nonconcomitant} for (1–4) each of the two higher realms, and (5–6) conditioned uncontaminated states, making six, and (7) virtuous unconditioned states, making seven. There are six phenomena in the three realms as objects of the knowledge of the truth of suffering and the knowledge of the truth of origin. One virtuous unconditioned phenomenon alone is the object of the knowledge of the truth of cessation. The two uncontaminated conditioned phenomena are objects of knowledge of the truth of path. Three that are concomitant in the desire realm, form realm, and formless realms are objects of the knowledge of others’ minds. Nine except for unconditioned neutral phenomena are objects of the knowledge of elimination and nonarising. These are the focal objects of these knowledges. The Vaibhāṣikas assert that space and nonanalytical cessation are not included in the four truths because Pūrṇavardhana’s commentary explains: Because the knowledges of elimination and nonarising focus on the four truths, and because unconditioned-neutral states are not included in the four truths.[1791]

gal te shes pa gcig gis chos thams cad cig car shes par 'gyur ba yod dam zhe na/ de ni med de/ mdo las/ dge sbyong ngam brang ze yang rung gang cig car thams cad shes pa'am mthong ba de ni 'ga' yang med do zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

Question: Does one knowledge simultaneously know all phenomena? Reply: That does not exist. A sūtra maintains: Śramaṇas and brahmans, there is no simultaneous knowledge or vision of all objects whatsoever.[1792]

'on kyang kun rdzob shes pa gcig pus rang gi ngo bo dang rang gi tshogs te rang dang lhan cig 'byung ba'i chos mtshungs ldan dang de ma yin pa las gzhan pa'i chos thams cad ni bdag med pa nyid du skad cig ma gcig la rig par 'gyur te/ mos pas spyod pa'i sa dag thos bsam las byung ba'i kun rdzob shes pas chos thams cad bdag med do zhes yid la byed pa'i phyir ro/ / skad cig ma gnyis pa'i yul du dang po'ang 'gyur bas skad cig ma gnyis kyi yul du ni chos thams cad 'gyur ro/ / de yang 'dod pa na thos bsam gnyis ka dang gzugs na thos byung kho na'o/ / rang nyid ni yul du mi byed de/ yul dang yul can la tha dad kyis khyab pa la yul dang yul can tha dad med pa'i phyir dang*/ rang nyid la byed pa 'gal ba'i phyir te/ ral gris rang nyid mi gcod pa bzhin no/ / rang dang lhan cig 'byung ba'i mtshungs ldan rnams kyang mi 'dzin te/ de dag dang dmigs pa gcig pas rang nyid la'ang dmigs par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / rang dang lhan cig 'byung ba ldan pa ma yin pa rnams kyang mi 'dzin te ha cang nye ba'i phyir mig sman dang mig sman gyi thur ma bzhin no/ / kun rdzob shes pa bsgoms pa las byung bas ni chos thams cad cig car shes pa ma yin te/ gong dang 'og ma'i spyod yul can zhes pa rnam par chad pa la dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ gal te cig car dmigs nas thams cad las cig car 'dod chags dang bral bar 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ des na kun rdzob shes pa sgom byung gis ni sa tha dad pa'i bden pa la so sor nges pa nyid du dmigs so zhes bye brag tu smra ba 'dod do/ /

However, conventional knowledge alone, in one moment, cognizes all phenomena, except for its own nature and [606] its collective retinue (svakalāpa) that are coemergent and concomitant with it, to be selfless (anātma), because conventional knowledge derived from hearing and contemplation of the level of resolute practice mentally engages [the idea that] “all phenomena are selfless.” Since objects of the first moment of knowledge also become objects of the second moment, all phenomena become objects of the two moments. Further, that derived from both hearing and contemplation exists in the desire realm, and that derived from hearing alone exists in the form realm. Conventional knowledge does not take itself as its own object because it is necessary that subject and object remain distinct. If it did, there would be no distinction between the subject and object, and it is contradictory that it takes itself as its own object, just as a sword does not cut itself. Also conventional knowledge does not apprehend states simultaneously concomitant with it, because it would then focus on itself, since they would have the same focal object. Also it does not apprehend coemergent, nonconcomitant states because they are too close, like eye ointment and the ointment spoon. Conventional knowledge derived from meditation does not simultaneously know all phenomena because it focuses on separate aspects, as the Abhidharmakośa states, “higher and lower object fields” (6:49d). If it focused on all objects simultaneously, it would be simultaneously free from attachment to all. Thus conventional knowledge derived from meditation focuses on truths of distinct levels and ascertains them separately. This is asserted by Vaibhāṣikas.

mdo sde pa la sogs pa ni rang rig 'dod pas rang gi tshogs pa'ang bdag med par shes par 'dod la/ theg pa gong ma pa ni sgom byung gis kyang chos thams cad bdag med pa nyid du shes pa yin la cig car 'dod chags dang bral ba'ang kho bo cag 'dod pa yin te/ 'di la bsam pa'ang bcal bar bya dgos so zhes 'dod do/ /

Sautrāntikas and others, since they assert self-cognition, assert that conventional knowledge knows its collective retinue to be selfless. In the higher vehicles we assert that conventional knowledge derived from meditation knows the selflessness of all phenomena and also simultaneously frees oneself from all attachment. But this assertion needs to be contemplated and assessed.
bdun pa [ldan pa'i tshul] ni
How knowledge is possessed

'o na gang zag gang zhig shes pa du dang ldan zhe na/ re zhig so so'i skye bo chags bcas dang gzugs med kyi byis pa rnams ni kun rdzob shes pa gcig pu dang ldan la{ 'dod gzugs kyi} chags bral zhig yin na ni pha rol sems shes dang yang ldan no/ /

Question: What beings possess what knowledge? Reply: Some ordinary beings with attachment and childlike beings of the formless realm possess just one, conventional knowledge. If they are free of attachment to the desire and form realms, they also possess knowledge of others’ minds.
zag med skad cig dang po la/ / chags can shes pa gcig dang ldan/ / gnyis pa la gsum yan chad ni/ / bzhi la re re 'phel dang ldan/ / 19

Āryas possessing attachment in the first moment of uncontaminated transcendent wisdom possess one knowledge alone. In the second moment they possess three. In the four after that they possess those through separately adding each. (7:19)

'phags pa ni chags can te 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang ma bral ba zhig yin na zag med kyi ye shes kyi skad cig ma dang po sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa dang ldan pa la ni dri med bzod rnams shes pa min zhes 'byung bas bzod pa ni shes pa ma yin la shes pa gzhan yang mi ldan pas kun rdzob shes pa gcig pu dang ldan no/ / ye shes skad cig ma gnyis pa sdug bsngal la chos shes pa la ni kun rdzob shes pa dang chos shes pa dang sdug bsngal shes pa ste gsum dang ldan te/ 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal shes pa de nyid chos shes kyang yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de yan chad kyi skad cig ma sdug bsngal la rjes shes dang po kun 'byung dang 'gog pa dang lam la chos shes bzhi la ni sngar gyi steng du rim pa ltar gong ma'i sdug bsngal dang 'dod pa'i kun 'byung dang gnyen po 'gog lam gsar du shes pas rjes shes dang kun 'byung dang 'gog pa dang lam shes pa re re 'phel bas rim pa ltar bzhi dang lnga dang drug dang bdun dang ldan no/ / gal te 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba zhig yin na ni sdug bsngal la chos bzod nas lam la chos shes kyi bar thams cad du pha rol sems shes bsnan te ldan par shes par bya'o/ / bzod pa phyi ma bdun dang rjes shes phyi ma gsum la ni shes pa sngar med gsar du 'phel ba med de/ bzod pa shes pa ma yin zhing rjes shes ni sngar du bgrangs zin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Āryas possessing attachment who are not free of attachment to the desire realm and who possess perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering existing in the first moment of uncontaminated transcendent wisdom possess (1) conventional knowledge alone since, as the Abhidharmakośa says, “Stainless perseverance is not knowledge” (7:1a) and they do not possess other types of knowledge. Those with Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering existing in the second moment of transcendent wisdom possess three — (1) conventional knowledge, (2) Dharma knowledge, and (3) knowledge of suffering — because that Dharma knowledge of desire-realm suffering is also Dharma knowledge. The four moments beyond that — first subsequent knowledge of the truth of suffering, then Dharma knowledge of the truths of origin, cessation, and path — possess, respectively, four, five, six, or seven knowledges by separately adding subsequent knowledge, knowledge of origin, cessation, and path, for in addition to the previous three, they also newly know higher-realm suffering, desire-realm origin, and cessation and path that are their antidotes. If they are free of attachment to desire-realm objects, they possess in addition knowledge of others’ minds in all the moments from Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering to Dharma knowledge of the truth of path. The latter seven types of perseverance and the latter three types of subsequent knowledge are not knowledges that are newly added, because perseverance is not knowledge and subsequent knowledge has been counted previously.

kha cig lam la rjes shes kyi tshe na chags bcas la lam shes pa de nyid dang chags bral la pha rol sems shes dang gnyis ldan gyi gzhan ni ma yin te/ 'bras bu thob pas shes pa snga ma rnams btang ba'i phyir te/ 'phags pa/ 'bras bu thob sbyangs nyams pa las zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes 'chad mod kyi/ TIk+ka las ni/ lam la rjes su shes pa la ni 'dod chags dang ma bral ba zhig yin na bdun po de dag dang ldan no/ / 'dod chags dang bral ba zhig yin na brgyad de/ de dag dang gzhan gyi sems shes pa dang ldan no zhes bshad do/ / de bzhin du sgom lam la gnas pa'ang chags bcas yin na pha rol sems shes dang zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa ma gtogs bdun dang*/ chags bral yin na pha rol sems shes bsnan te brgyad dang ldan no/ / mi slob pa'i lam la gnas pa ni shes rab kyis rnam grol la pha rol sems shes ma gtogs dgu dang*/ gnyis ka'i cha las rnam grol la bcu dang ldan no zhes shes par bya'o/ / brgyad pa ni 'o na gnas skabs gang du shes pa du 'thob ce na/

Some say: When subsequent knowledge of the truth of path arises, those possessing attachment have knowledge of the path and those free of attachment possess both that and knowledge of others’ minds. Others do not, because they relinquish the former knowledges when they obtain their result. For indeed, the Abhidharmakośa notes, “[The virtue of absorption of] the ārya [is relinquished] by obtaining the result, upgrading, or degeneration” (4:40d). The Subcommentary explains: If one with subsequent knowledge of the truth of path is not free of attachment, he possesses those seven. If free of attachment, he possesses eight, since he also possesses knowledge of others’ minds.[1793] Similarly, those abiding on the path of meditation who possess attachment possess seven knowledges excluding knowledge of others’ minds, knowledge of elimination, and knowledge of nonarising. Those free of attachment possess eight, for in addition they possess knowledge of others’ minds. Those abiding on the nonlearner path who are liberated by wisdom possess nine except for knowledge of others’ minds. Arhats liberated from both aspects possess ten. How knowledge is obtained Question: How many knowledges does one obtain, and in what circumstances?
mthong ba'i lam la bzod pa dang / / shes pa ji ltar skyes pa rnams/ / ma 'ongs pa 'thob de nyid la/ / rjes gsum la ni kun rdzob kyang / / 20
In just the way that perseverance and knowledge arise on the path of seeing, future states will be obtained. On that, three subsequent, as well as conventional. (7:20)

mthong ba'i lam la ni bzod pa brgyad dang shes pa bdun po ji ltar skyes pa rnams rang rang gi rigs 'dra ba ma 'ongs pa 'thob par 'gyur te/ 'di ltar sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa skyes pa nas gang la brten nas skyes pa de ni da ltar ba dang ma 'ongs pa 'thob pa la sa gzhan la rten pa ni ma 'ongs pa kho na 'thob ste/ de yang mi skye ba'i chos can dag yin gyi skye ba'i chos can ni ma yin te/ mthong lam lan du ma skyes par thal ba'i phyir ro/ / 'grel pa las/ mthong ba'i lam la bzod pa'am shes pa gang dang gang skyes pa de dang 'dra ba ma 'ongs pa de'i rnam pa bzhi kho na 'thob par 'gyur ro zhes 'byung ba'i rnam pa bzhi ni dran pa nyer gzhag bzhi yin te/ rnam pa rnams ni dran pa nyer gzhag tu bshad pa'i phyir ro zhes gsungs mod kyi TIk+ka las ni ji ltar skyes pa rnams 'thob ces bya ba ni gang dang gang skyes pa de dag 'thob bo zhes bya ba'i tha tshig ste/ dper na sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa skyes na de dang 'dra ba'i bzod pa ma 'ongs pa kho na 'thob bo/ / des rnam pa bzhi zhes bya ba ni skal ba 'dra ba'i phyir bzod pa'i rnam pa ste mi rtag pa la sogs pa'i rnam pa bzhi yin gyi gzhan ni ma yin no/ / de bzhin du sdug bsngal la chos shes pa skyes na de nyid ma 'ongs pa 'thob cing de'i{ mi rtag pa la sogs pa'i} rnam pa bzhi kho na 'thob bo/ /

Reply: In just the way the eight types of perseverance and seven types of knowledge arise on the path of seeing, future states of similar type will be obtained. Thus it is in dependence on whatever level perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering arises that present and future perseverance will be obtained. But if they arise in dependence on another level, future perseverance alone will be obtained. Further, this applies to unarisen instances and not arisen instances; otherwise it would follow that the path of seeing would arise many times. The Autocommentary declares: In whatever way perseverance or knowledge arises on the path of seeing, only the four aspects of future perseverance or knowledge similar to them are obtained.[1794] The “four aspects” refer to the four foundations of mindfulness. [608] Indeed, the Subcommentary notes: Because these aspects are explained to be the foundations of mindfulness.[1795] “In just the way perseverance and knowledge arise on the path of seeing, future states will be obtained” (7:20abc) signifies that whatever arises will be obtained. For example, if perseverance for Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering arises, perseverance similar to that alone will be obtained in the future. “The four aspects” refers to aspects of perseverance that are the four aspects such as impermanence, because they have similar status, but not others.

de bzhin du sdug bsngal la rjes su shes pa'i bzod pa la sogs pa la'ang sbyar bar bya'o zhes bden pa gang dang gang gis shes bzod yin pa'i bden pa de dang de'i rnam pa mi rtag pa la sogs pa kho na 'thob cing*/ de yang bzod shes rnams ni skal mnyam gyi rgyu ma thob pas de dang 'dra ba kho na 'thob la rnam pa ni bzhi ga'ang dmigs yul bden pa mtshungs shing 'dra bas bzhi char gyi rigs 'thob par bshad do/ / sgom lam la ni shes pa rigs 'dra ba dang mi 'dra ba dang de dag gi rnam pa'ang thams cad mngon sum du 'gyur ba'i phyir thams cad kyi rgyu 'thob pas mthong lam las khyad par 'phags pa'i rnam pa ma 'ongs pa 'thob par 'gyur ro/ / 'o na mthong ba'i lam la rigs mi 'dra ba mi 'thob bam zhe na/

Similarly, if Dharma knowledge of the truth of suffering arises, just that and its four aspects {of impermanence and so on} will be obtained in future. So too, that is to be applied to perseverance for subsequent knowledge of the truth of suffering and so on. This explains that whatever perseverance and knowledge arises, that truth and its aspects alone, such as impermanence, will be obtained. Further, it is said that due to not obtaining the homogeneous cause of perseverance and knowledge, states merely similar to them are obtained, but since they are similar and alike in their four aspects or the truths that are their focal objects, one obtains that by type possessing four parts. On the path of meditation, aspects that excel those of the path of seeing are obtained through obtaining the cause of all, because all knowledge of similar and dissimilar type — and their aspects — manifest. Question: Is knowledge of dissimilar type obtained or not on the path of seeing?

mthong ba'i lam de nyid la sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung dang 'gog pa la rjes su shes pa gsum la ni sngon ma thob pa las kun rdzob shes pa'ang 'thob pa'i phyir mi 'dra ba'ang 'thob bo/ / gsum po de'i chos shes la ni 'thob pa ma yin te/ khams gong ma gnyis kyi sdug bsngal ma shes shing kun 'byung ma spangs la 'gog pa mngon du ma byas pas bden pa zad par ma rtogs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: On that path of seeing, knowledge of dissimilar type is obtained because the three subsequent knowledges of the truths of suffering, origin, and cessation that were not obtained before are obtained as well as conventional knowledge. The Dharma knowledge of those three does not obtain them because they do not exhaustively comprehend the four truths: they do not know suffering, nor abandon origin, nor manifest cessation of both higher realms.
de phyir mngon rtogs mtha' zhes bya/ / de ni mi skye'i chos can yin/ / rang dang 'og sa 'gog pa'i mtha'/ / rang bden rnam can 'bad las byung / / 21

It is called “the end of realization” because of that. That is an unarisen state. On its level and lower level. At the end of cessation, it possesses the aspect of its truth, derived from exertion. (7:21)

bden pa gsum po re re zad par rtogs pa'i rjes la thob pa de nyid kyi phyir kun rdzob shes pa de ni mngon par rtogs pa'i mtha' las byung ba zhes bya'o/ / 'di la'ang sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung dang*/ / 'gog pa la rjes su shes pa rnams la rim pa ltar bden pa gsum po de dag la dmigs pa'i rjes su shes pa thob bo zhes shes par bya'o/ / lam la rjes shes la ni kun rdzob shes pa mi 'thob ste/ sngon 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis bden pa dang po gsum rtogs kyi kun rdzob shes pas lam bden ni nam yang rtogs mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di ni bden pa zad par mngon par rtogs pa'i mtha' las byung ba yin na lam ni zad par sgom par mi nus te/ nyan rang sangs rgyas gsum gyi lam gyi rigs mang zhing de dag re re la'ang chung 'bring la sogs pa'i dbye ba mang bas mtha' med pa'i phyir dang*/ {gang rung gcig bsgoms na gang rung brtags min 'thob pas } de dag gang zag gcig gis{ dus gcig tu} sgom pa'ang mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / mngon par rtogs pa zhes bya ba'ang sdug bsngal shes pa nas lam sgom pa'i bar rang gi bya ba byas pa yin no/ / 'o na ni kun 'byung la rjes su shes pa la'ang mi 'thob par 'gyur te/ kun 'byung mtha' dag ma spangs pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ kun 'byung mthong spang ni mtha' dag spangs pa'i phyir 'thob bo/ / lam ni rigs mang ba'i phyir mthong spang gi gnyen po mtha' dag sgom par mi nus pa'i phyir mi 'thob bo/ / kha cig na re mngon par rtogs pa'i mtha' las byung ba'i kun rdzob shes pa 'di ni mthong lam gyi 'khor yin pa'i phyir mthong lam la bden pa gsum gyi rjes kho na la 'thob kyi lam gyi rjes la ni ma yin te/ lam la rjes shes ni sgom lam yin pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ba ni mi rigs te/ de ni sgom lam gyi 'khor yang yin pas mthong lam kho na'i 'khor yin pa'i sgrub byed med pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na kun rdzob shes pa mngon par rtogs pa'i mtha' las byung ba de res 'ga' mngon du byed dam zhe na/

Conventional knowledge is called “that occurring at the end of realization” (abhisamayāntya) because it is post-equipoise knowledge exhaustively comprehending each of the three truths. You should also understand that subsequent knowledge of the truths of suffering, origin, and cessation respectively obtains subsequent knowledge focusing on those three truths. Subsequent knowledge of the truth of path does not obtain conventional knowledge because, though the prior mundane path comprehends the first three truths, it is impossible for conventional knowledge ever to comprehend the truth of path. If it occurs after fully realizing the truths, it cannot exhaustively meditate on the path because paths are limitless, there being many types of path, such as the three: śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, and buddha paths. And there are many classifications of each of those — small, medium, and great and so on — and it is impossible for one person to {simultaneously} meditate on those, {since one obtains the nonanalytical [cessation of other paths] if one meditates on any one path}. The term “realization” refers to engaging in specific action from knowing suffering [609] up to meditating on the path. Objection: Then it would not obtain subsequent knowledge of the truth of origin because it has not abandoned all origin. Reply: It obtains that because all objects to be abandoned by seeing the truth of origin have been abandoned. But it does not obtain the path because the path has many types and it cannot meditate on all the antidotes of objects to be abandoned by seeing. Some say: Because conventional knowledge in the retinue of the path of seeing occurs at the end of realization, it is obtained only after the three truths on the path of seeing. It is not obtained at the end of the path, because subsequent knowledge of the truth of path is the path of meditation. Reply: This is illogical. There is no way to establish that it is in the retinue of the path of seeing alone, since it is in the retinue of the path of meditation. Question: Does that conventional knowledge occurring at the end of realization ever manifest?

kun rdzob shes pa de ni gcig tu mi skye ba'i chos can yin pas nam yang mngon du byed pa ni ma yin no/ / des na mi skye ba'i chos can dag de dang der 'thob bo zhes 'dod de/ mi skye ba'i chos can dag yin na ji ltar 'thob par 'gyur/ 'thob na'ang ji ltar skye bar mi 'gyur te/ chos med pa 'thob pa 'gal ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir mthong lam la mnyam par bzhag pas bden bzhi la dmigs pa'i kun rdzob shes pa rjes las thob pa skye bar nus pa'i phyir kun rdzob shes pa rnyed pa zhes brjod do zhes sngon gyi slob dpon dag{ sems tsam gyis 'dod par} 'chad do/ / de'i phyir kun las btus las kyang*/ mthong ba'i lam la bden pa rnam par 'jog pa mngon par rtogs pa'i mtha' las byung ba'i kun rdzob shes pa rnams 'thob ste/ mngon du byed pa ni ma yin no/ / de dag ni sgom pa'i lam la mngon du byed do zhes bshad do/ / bye brag tu smra ba rnams na re de ni mthong lam gyis 'thob pa yin pas sgom lam la mngon du byed par mi rigs la/ kho bo cag ltar na mthong lam du de dag skye ba'i go skabs med pas mi skye ba'i chos can yin no zhes brjod do zhes zer ro/ /

Reply: That conventional knowledge never manifests since it is solely an unarisen state. But if you assert that unarisen states are obtained intermittently, how could unarisen states be obtained? And if obtained, how could they not be arisen? That is not so; it is contradictory to obtain a nonexistent state. Past {Cittamātra} scholars explain that because those in equipoise on the path of seeing are capable of generating post-equipoise conventional knowledge focusing on the four truths, they are called “those who attain conventional knowledge.” Therefore the Compendium of Abhidharma states: Conventional knowledge that occurs at the end of realization and establishes the four truths is obtained on the path of seeing, but it does not manifest. It manifests on the path of meditation.[1796] Vaibhāṣikas say: It is illogical that it manifests on the path of meditation since it is obtained by the path of seeing. For us it is an unarisen state since there is no opportunity for it to arise on the path of seeing.

sa yang mthong lam sa gang dag yin pa de rang gi sa pa'i kun rdzob shes pa dang 'og sa'i kun rdzob shes pas 'thob ste/ gal te mthong lam mi lcogs med la brten na 'dod pa dang mi lcogs med kyis bsdus pa gnyis kyis kun rdzob shes pa 'thob pa nas bsam gtan bzhi pa la brten na 'dod pa dang bsam gtan sa drug ste sa bdun gyis bsdus pa'i kun rdzob shes pa thob pa'i bar du sbyar ro/ /

Also, one obtains the conventional knowledge of its level and the conventional knowledge of lower level on whatever level the path of seeing is generated. If the path of seeing depends on unrestricted access concentration, then one obtains conventional knowledge subsumed by two levels: (1) desire-realm level and (2) unrestricted access concentration. If it depends on the fourth absorption, one obtains conventional knowledge subsumed by seven levels: (1) desire-realm level, and (2–7) the six levels of absorption.

'o na de dran pa nyer gzhag du dag cig yin zhe na/ 'gog pa mngon par rtogs pa'i mtha' las byung ba'i kun rdzob shes pa ni dran pa nyer gzhag bzhi'i tha ma chos dran pa nyer gzhag yin te/ de ni 'gog bden la dmigs la de yang chos kho nar nges pa'i phyir ro/ / sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung mngon par rtogs pa'i mtha' las byung ba ni de dag la lus la sogs pa yod pas dran pa nyer gzhag bzhi ga yin no/ / mngon par rtogs pa'i mtha' las byung ba'i kun rdzob shes pa de ni sdug bsngal nas 'gog pa'i bar gyi bden pa gang zhig mngon par rtogs pas thob pa'i rang rang gi bden pa de'i rnam pa can dang dmigs pa'ang rang rang gi bden pa de nyid yin te/ sdug bsngal mngon par rtogs pa'i mtha' las byung ba'i rnam pa mi rtag pa la sogs pa dang dmigs pa'ang sdug bsngal nyid yin pa la sogs pa'o/ / de yang skyes thob ma yin gyi sbyor ba 'bad rtsol las byung pa yin te/ mthong lam sgom pa'i stobs kyis 'thob pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang 'khor dang bcas na ni 'dod pa dang gzugs na spyod pa'i kun rdzob shes pa gnyis rim pa ltar bsam gtan gyi sdom pa'i gzugs rjes su 'brang ba med pa dang yod pa'i phyir phung po bzhi pa dang lnga pa yin no/ /

Question: What is it from among the foundations of mindfulness? Reply: Conventional knowledge occurring at the end of the realization of cessation is the close placement of mindfulness of phenomena that is the last of the four foundations of mindfulness, because it focuses on the truth of cessation and ascertains phenomena alone. Conventional knowledge occurring at the end of the realization of suffering and origin is the four foundations of mindfulness, since it focuses on the body [610] and so on. Conventional knowledge occurring at the end of realization realizes any truth from suffering to cessation. Therefore it possesses the aspect of its truth (svasatyākāra) that is obtained and the focal object that is its truth. And they are just the aspect of impermanence and so on occurring at the end of realizing suffering and so forth and the focal object of suffering and so on as well. Further, it is not obtained by birth but derived from exertion because it is obtained due to the power of meditating on the path of seeing. Again, if it possesses a retinue, it has four or five aggregates, since both conventional knowledge engaging desire-realm objects and conventional knowledge engaging form-realm objects respectively possess and do not possess complements of the form of the absorption vows.
bsgom pa'i lam la shes pa du 'thob bshad pa ni
EXPLAINING HOW MANY KNOWLEDGES ARE OBTAINED ON THE PATH OF MEDITATION
chags bcas bcu drug pa la drug / 'dod las chags dang bral bas bdun/ / de yi gong ma chags bcas kyi/ / bsgom pa'i lam la bdun 'thob bo/ / 22
Those with attachment in the sixteenth moment obtain six. Those free from attachment obtain seven. Those who possess attachment on the path of meditation beyond that obtain seven. (7:22)

'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bcas pa skad cig ma bcu drug pa lam la rjes shes la gnas pa la ni bden pa bzhi shes dang chos shes rjes shes dang drug 'thob ste/ de yang mthong spang las rnam par grol ba'i shes pa yin gyi sgom spang las grol ba ni ma yin te/ 'bras bu la gnas pa tsam po yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang lam la rjes shes ni lam shes pa dang rjes shes gnyis ka'i ngo bo yin pa'i phyir lam shes pa dang rjes shes gnyis ni da ltar byung ba yin la shes pa gzhan bzhi ni ma 'ongs pa kho na 'thob bo/ / sa ni chags bcas yin pas mi lcogs med kyis bsdus pa yin la/ mthong ba rdzogs pas bskyed pa'i phyir skal mnyam gyi rgyu rgyas pa las 'thob bo/ pha rol sems shes dang kun rdzob shes pa dang zad pa dang mi skye ba bzhi mi 'thob pa ni rim pa ltar 'dod pa las chags bcas yin pa'i phyir dang*/ sngon rnyed mi 'thob bo zhes pas sngon rnyed zin pa'i phyir ram/ yang na mngon par rtogs pa'i mtha' med pa'i phyir dang*/ slob pa yin pa'i phyir ro*/ /

Those with attachment who abide with subsequent knowledge of the truth of path in the sixteenth moment obtain six: (1–4) knowledge of the four truths, (5) Dharma knowledge, and (6) subsequent knowledge. Further, they have knowledge of liberation from objects to be abandoned by the path of seeing and not liberation from objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation because they are ordinary abiders in the result. Again, because subsequent knowledge of the truth of path has the nature of being both path knowledge and subsequent knowledge, both path knowledge and subsequent knowledge occur in the present, but the four other knowledges are obtained in the future alone. Such knowledge is subsumed by unrestricted access concentration since it is the level possessing attachment. It is obtained from an enhanced homogeneous cause because it arises from having completed the path of seeing. Four knowledges — (1) knowledge of others’ minds, (2) conventional knowledge, (3) knowledge of elimination, and (4) nonarising — are not obtained because, respectively, (1) they are attached to desire-realm objects, (2) they have previously attained it, for as the Abhidharmakośa observes, “Those previously acquired will not be obtained” (7:26d), (3) realization has not ended, and (4) they are learners.

'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba nas ci yang med pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i bar ci rigs pa'i gang zag skad cig ma bcu drug pa lam la rjes shes la gnas pas ni sngar gyi drug dang pha rol sems shes dang bdun 'thob ste/ de la'ang sa ni gang la rten pa de'i rang sa dang 'og sas bsdus pa 'thob par shes par bya'o/ / snga ma ltar na da ltar ba ni gnyis dang lnga ni ma 'ongs pa 'thob bo/ / sngon rnyed zin pa dang slob pa yin pas gzhan gsum ni mi 'thob bo/ /

Those beings abiding on the sixteenth moment of subsequent knowledge of the truth of path, who are free from attachment from the desire realm up to nothingness, obtain seven: (1–6) the former six plus (7) knowledge of others’ minds. Also, you should know that beings based on any level obtain that which is subsumed by that level and lower levels. According to the previous, two are obtained in the present and five in the future. The remaining three are not obtained, since these are previously attained and learner states.

skad cig ma bcu drug pa lam la rjes su shes pa de'i gong ma 'dod pa la chags bcas kyi bsgom pa'i lam la ni sbyor ba dang bar chad med pa dang rnam grol dang khyad par can gyi lam thams cad la chos shes rjes shes dang bden pa bzhi shes dang kun rdzob shes pa dang bdun 'thob bo/ / de yang gal te sgom lam 'jig rten pa zhi rags kyi rnam pa can zhig yin na ni kun rdzob shes pa da ltar byung ba dang*/ 'on te 'jig rten las 'das pa zhig yin na ni rjes shes 'dod pa'i gnyen po ma yin la chos shes 'dod pa'i gnyen po yin pas chos shes dang bden pa bzhi shes gang rung gcig da ltar byung ba yin la gzhan dag ni ma 'ongs pa 'thob ste/ rang rang gi rigs kyi skal mnyam gyi rgyu rgyas pa'i phyir ro/ / chags bcas dang slob pa yin pas gzhan gsum ni mi 'thob bo/ /

Those who possess attachment to desire-realm objects and abide on the path of meditation beyond the sixteenth moment of subsequent knowledge of the truth of path obtain seven: the (1) path of preparation, (2) uninterrupted path, (3) liberated path, (4–5) Dharma knowledge and subsequent knowledge of all special paths, (6) knowledge of the four truths, and (7) conventional knowledge. Further, if the path of meditation is the mundane path of meditation comparing coarse and refined aspects, then conventional knowledge occurs in the present. [611] If it is a transcendent path, then Dharma knowledge and any knowledge of the four truths occurs in the present, since subsequent knowledge is not the antidote of desire-realm affliction and Dharma knowledge is the antidote of desire-realm affliction. The others are obtained in the future because of the enhanced homogeneous cause of each type. They do not obtain the other three, since they possess attachment and are learners.
sa bdun las rgyal mngon shes dang / / mi g.yo 'thob dang spel bsgom pa'i/ bar chad med pa'i lam dag dang / / gong ma'i grol ba'i lam brgyad la'ang / / 23

Those who conquer seven levels and those with higher perception obtain seven. The immutable obtain nine. Those on uninterrupted paths meditating on enhancing absorption obtain seven. As do those on the eight paths liberated from higher realms. (7:23)

slob pa bsam gtan bzhi dang gzugs med pa gsum ste sa bdun gyi nyon mongs pa las rgyal ba ste 'dod chags dang 'bral bar byed pa'i bar chad med pa'i lam la ni shes pa sngar bshad pa bdun po kho na 'thob ste/ de yang gal te 'jig rten pa'i sgom lam yin na ni kun rdzob shes pa da ltar byung ba gzhan drug ma 'ongs pa 'thob la/ pha rol sems shes dang zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa mi 'thob ste/ bar chad med pa'i lam la bkag pa'i phyir dang slob pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'on te 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam yin na ni 'di gnyis ci rigs khams gsum gyi gnyen por rung bas 'gog pa dang lam la chos shes pa gang yang rung ba'am/ khams gong ma'i gnyen po yin pas rjes shes dang bden pa bzhi shes las gang rung zhig da ltar ba dang gzhan dag ni ma 'ongs pa 'thob bo/ / bar chad med pa'i lam dang slob pa yin pas gzhan gsum ni mi 'thob bo/ /

Learners who conquer (jayā) afflictions of the seven levels — (1–4) the four absorptions and (5–7) the three formless states — obtain the seven previously explained knowledges alone on the uninterrupted path that frees from attachment. Further, if that uninterrupted path is a mundane path of meditation, then conventional knowledge occurs in the present, and the other six are obtained in the future. They do not obtain knowledge of others’ minds and knowledge of elimination and nonarising, because [the first] stops during the uninterrupted path and because they are learners. However, if it is a transcendent path, they obtain subsequent knowledge of the truth of cessation and path since those two are antidotes to any affliction of the three realms, or they obtain any subsequent knowledge or knowledge of the four truths in the future since they are antidotes of affliction of the three realms. They do not obtain the remaining three knowledges, since they are learners and that is an uninterrupted path.

slob pa zhig mngon par shes pa dang po lnga thob par byed pa'i bar chad med pa'i lam la'ang shes pa bdun 'thob ste/ de yang 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba zhig gis 'thob na sngar bshad pa ltar yin la sbyor ba'i stobs kyis 'thob na ni kun rdzob shes pa da ltar ba yin no/ / mi slob pas mngon par shes pa 'thob par byed pa la ni mi g.yo ba la dgu dang gzhan la ni brgyad 'thob par 'gyur ro/ /

Learners on the uninterrupted path who obtain the first five higher perceptions (abhijñā) obtain seven knowledges. Further, one who is free from desire-realm attachment obtains knowledge in the way previously explained. One who obtains knowledge due to the power of preparation obtains conventional knowledge in the present. Among nonlearners who obtain higher perception, immutable arhats obtain nine, and the others, eight.

rab tu rtogs pa'i skal ba can zhig mi g.yo ba 'thob par byed pa'i bar chad med pa'i lam la'ang chos shes rjes shes dang bden pa bzhi shes dang zad shes dang bdun 'thob pa las chos shes rjes shes gang rung zhig dang bden pa bzhi shes gang rung zhig dang zad pa shes pa dang gsum da ltar ba dang gzhan ni ma 'ongs pa 'thob bo/ / snying po zag med kyi dbang po 'pho ba'i phyir dang*/ bar chad med lam yin pas gzhan gsum ni mi 'thob ste/ kun rdzob shes pa zag bcas yin pas dbang po rtul po dang srid rtse'i gnyen po ma yin pa dang*/ shes pa gzhan gnyis rnam grol gyi lam yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Those who possess full realization who abide on the uninterrupted path seeking to obtain the immutable state obtain seven: (1) Dharma knowledge, (2) subsequent knowledge, (3–6) knowledge of the four truths, and (7) knowledge of elimination. They obtain three [in the present]: (1) one from either Dharma knowledge or subsequent knowledge, (2) one from any of the knowledges of the four truths, and (3) knowledge of elimination in the present. The others are obtained in the future. Because they upgrade their intellectual faculty of their uncontaminated heart, and since they abide on the uninterrupted path, they do not obtain the other three knowledges. That is because conventional knowledge, since it is contaminated, is neither the antidote of dull intellectual faculty nor the summit of existence and because the other two knowledges are liberated paths.

slob pa zhig bsam gtan zag bcas dang zag med spel mar bsgom pa'i bar chad med pa'i lam dag la'ang bdun 'thob ste/ 'di la'ang zag med la ni 'gog lam la chos shes pa gnyis gang rung ngam rjes shes dang bden pa bzhi shes las gang rung zhig da ltar byung ba dang gzhan ni ma 'ongs pa 'thob bo/ / zag bcas la ni kun rdzob shes pa da ltar byung ba yin no/ /

Learners abiding on the uninterrupted path meditating on enhancing contaminated or uncontaminated absorption obtain seven. Those who are enhancing uncontaminated absorption obtain either of the two Dharma knowledges of the truths of cessation and path, and either subsequent knowledge or any knowledge of the four truths in the present. The others are obtained in the future. Those who are enhancing contaminated absorption have conventional knowledge in the present.

sa bdun las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i gong ma srid rtse las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i rnam par grol ba'i lam brgyad la'ang chos shes rjes shes dang bden pa bzhi shes dang pha rol sems shes dang bdun 'thob ste/ bdun po de la'ang 'gog lam la chos shes gnyis gang rung ngam rjes shes dang bden pa bzhi shes las gang rung zhig da ltar byung ba yin la gzhan dag ni ma 'ongs pa 'thob bo/ / srid rtse'i gnyen po ma yin pa dang*/ slob pa yin pas gzhan gsum ni mi 'thob bo/ /

Those abiding on the eight liberated paths that are [612] free from attachment to the seven levels and free from attachment to the higher summit of existence obtain seven: (1) Dharma knowledge, (2) subsequent knowledge, (3–6) knowledge of the four truths, and (7) knowledge of others’ minds. Among those seven, either of the two Dharma knowledges of the truths of cessation and path, and either subsequent knowledge or any knowledge of the four truths, occur in the present. The others are obtained in the future. The other three are not obtained, since they are not antidotes to the summit of existence and they are learners.
slob pa sbyong ba'i grol ba la/ / shes pa drug dang bdun 'thob bam/ / bar chad med pa'i lam la drug / de bzhin srid rtse rnam rgyal la'ang / / 24
Learners on the liberated path who upgrade possess six or seven knowledges. Those on the uninterrupted path, six. So too those conquering the summit of existence. (7:24)

slob pa zhig dbang po rtul po rnon por sbyong ba'i rnam par grol ba'i lam la ni gal te chags bcas yin na chos shes rjes shes dang bden pa bzhi shes te shes pa drug dang 'on te chags bral zhig yin na pha rol sems shes bsnan nas bdun 'thob cing*/ da ltar byung ba ni chos shes dang bden pa bzhi shes las gang yang rung ba zhig dang gnyis yin la gzhan dag ni ma 'ongs pa 'thob bo/ / 'am zhes bya ba ni lugs gzhan ston pa ste/ kha cig 'di ni mthong lam dang 'dra ba'i phyir ji ltar mthong lam gyis 'bras bu gsum dang kun rdzob shes pa 'thob pa ltar 'di la'ang mngon par rtogs pa'i mtha' las byung ba'i kun rdzob shes pa'ang 'thob pa'i phyir{ de gnyis kyis} bdun{ dang brgyad} 'thob bo zhes 'dod pa bstan pa'i phyir ro/ / kha cig ni sngar rtogs zin pas mngon par rtogs pa'i mtha' med pa'i phyir dang*/ mthong lam ni 'thob par byed pa yin la 'di ni thob zin pa'i phyir mthong lam dang 'dra ba'ang ma yin no/ / 'on kyang sbyor ba'i lam la ni chags bcas dang chags bral gnyis kas kyang kun rdzob shes pa'ang 'thob bo zhes 'dod do/ / slob pa dbang po sbyong ba'i bar chad med pa'i lam la ni chags bcas chags bral gnyis kas chos shes rjes shes dang bden pa bzhi shes dang drug 'thob kyi/ 'dir yang bar chad med lam dang slob pa yin pas shes pa gsum mi 'thob la/ kun rdzob shes pa'ang mi 'thob ste/ mthong lam dang 'dra ba'i phyir ro/ /

Learners abiding on the liberated path who upgrade to sharp faculty and who possess attachment possess six knowledges: (1) Dharma knowledge, (2) subsequent knowledge, and (3–6) knowledge of the four truths. Or, if free from attachment, they possess seven, since (7) knowledge of others’ minds is added. They have two in the present: Dharma knowledge and any knowledge of the four truths. They obtain the others in the future. “Or” indicates other systems. Some say: They obtain seven {or eight} {for two reasons:} because it is similar to the path of seeing where those on the path of seeing obtain three results and conventional knowledge, and also they obtain conventional knowledge that occurs at the end of realization. Some say: It is not like the path of seeing. In the path of seeing there is obtainment, whereas here there is no obtainment at the end of realization since it was obtained previously. However, those on the path of preparation, both those who possess attachment and those free from attachment obtain conventional knowledge. Both learners possessing attachment and those free from attachment who abide on the uninterrupted path and train to upgrade their intellectual faculty obtain six: (1) Dharma knowledge, (2) subsequent knowledge, and (3–6) knowledge of the four truths. In this context they do not obtain three knowledges, since they abide on the uninterrupted path and are learners. They do not obtain conventional knowledge, because it is similar to the path of seeing.

ji ltar 'dra zhe na/ ji ltar mthong lam gyis 'bras bu dang po gsum gang rung zhig 'thob pa ltar 'dis kyang bar chad med pa'i lam gyis slob pa dbang po sbyong ba na 'bras bu dang po gsum po dbang po rnon pos bsdus pa 'dus byas gang rung zhig 'thob la/ yang mthong lam bar chad med pa'i lam bzod pa rnams la kun rdzob shes pa mi 'thob pa ltar 'dir yang de dang 'dra'o/ /

Question: How is that similar? Reply: Just as they obtain any of the three results through the path of seeing, so too these learners who have upgraded their faculty through the uninterrupted path obtain any of the first three conditioned results that are possessed by those of sharp faculty. Again, those abiding on perseverance that is the uninterrupted path of seeing do not obtain the conventional path. That, too, is similar.

ji ltar slob pa dbang po sbyong ba'i bar chad med pa'i lam la shes pa drug 'thob pa de bzhin du srid rtse'i nyon mongs pa las rnam par rgyal ba ste 'dod chags dang bral bar byed pa'i bar chad med pa'i lam rnams la'ang shes pa drug po de dag nyid 'thob kyi srid rtse'i gnyen po ma yin zhing slob pa'i bar chad med lam yin pas gzhan mi 'thob pa ni sngar bzhin no/ /

Just as learners on the uninterrupted path who upgrade their intellectual faculty obtain six knowledges, so too those conquering the afflictions of the summit of existence while abiding on the uninterrupted path free from attachment also obtain just those six knowledges. [Those with knowledges that] are not antidotes of the summit of existence but are learner uninterrupted paths do not obtain other knowledges, as before.
zad pa shes pa la dgu'o/ / mi g.yo bas ni bcu 'thob bo/ / der 'pho grol ba'i tha ma la'ang / / bshad pa'i lhag ma la brgyad 'thob/ / 25
Those possessing knowledge of elimination, nine. Immutable arhats obtain ten. As do those on the last path of liberation who upgrade. The rest previously explained obtain eight. (7:25)

srid rtse'i rnam grol gyi lam dgu pa zad pa shes pa la ni dbang po rtul po la nyams pa srid pas mi skye ba shes pa ma gtogs pa shes pa dgu 'thob cing*/ mi g.yo ba'i chos can gyis ni mi skye ba shes pa'ang 'thob pas bcu 'thob la/ mi g.yo ba der dbang po 'pho ba'i rnam par grol ba'i lam tha ma la'ang bcu po thams cad 'thob bo/ / 'di dag la sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung shes pa gang rung zhig dang rjes shes dang zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa gang rung zhig ste gsum ni da ltar byung ba yin la gzhan dag ni ma 'ongs pa 'thob bo/ /

Those possessing the knowledge of elimination, which is the ninth liberated path of the summit of existence, obtain nine knowledges, excluding knowledge of nonarising, since those of dull faculty may degenerate. Immutable arhats obtain ten since [613] they also obtain knowledge of nonarising. Also, those abiding on the final path of liberation who upgrade to immutability obtain all ten. They have three in the present: (1) either knowledge of suffering or knowledge of origin, (2) subsequent knowledge, and (3) either knowledge of elimination or knowledge of nonarising. They obtain the others in the future.

sngar bshad pa'i lhag ma 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i rnam grol gyi lam dgu pa dang*/ sa bdun las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i rnam par grol ba dang*/ mngon par shes pa dang*/ spel ma sgom pa dang*/ mi g.yo ba rtogs par byed pa gsum gyi rnam par grol ba'i lam dang po brgyad po rnams dang*/ de bzhin du sngar ma smros pa 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i phyir mi 'ong ba'i sbyor ba dang khyad par can gyi lam rnams la tshogs pa'o/ /ni zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa ma gtogs pa shes pa brgyad brgyad ma 'ongs pa 'thob ste slob pa'i dbang du byas pa'o/ / mi slob pa ni mngon par shes pa dang spel ma sgom pa dang mi g.yo ba rtogs par byed pa'i bar chad med pa'i lam la dus kyi rnam grol yin na pha rol sems shes dang mi skye ba shes pa ma gtogs pa brgyad 'thob la/ mi g.yo ba'i chos can zhig yin na ni bar chad med lam la bkag pas pha rol sems shes ma gtogs pa dgu 'thob bo/ / mngon par shes pa dang spel mar sgom pa dang mi g.yo ba rtogs par byed pa'i sbyor ba dang rnam par grol ba dang khyad par can gyi lam rnams la dus kyi rnam grol gyis mi skye ba shes pa ma gtogs pa dgu dang*/ mi g.yo ba sa bcu po thams cad 'thob bo/ / de yang*/ mig dang rna ba'i mngon shes ni/ / lung du ma bstan zhes 'byung bas lha'i mig dang rna ba'i mngon shes gnyis kyis ni rnam grol gyi lam yang lung ma bstan yin la lung ma bstan la ni ma 'ongs pa 'thob pa med do/ / de dag ni mi slob pa'i dbang du byas pa'o/ / so so'i skye bo 'dod pa dang bsam gtan snga ma gsum las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i rnam grol gyi lam tha ma rnams la ni rim pa ltar bsam gtan dang po dang gnyis pa dang gsum pa dang bzhi pa'i sas bsdus pa'i kun rdzob shes pa dang pha rol sems shes ma 'ongs pa 'thob bo/ / bsam gtan bzhi pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i rnam grol gyi lam dgu pa la ni nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched kyi dngos gzhis bsdus pa'i kun rdzob shes pa 'thob kyi pha rol sems shes ni mi 'thob ste/ de ni gzugs la brten nas bsgrub par bya ba yin pas gzhan gyi sems shes gzugs med kyi sas bsdus pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du gzugs med lhag ma rnams la'ang shes par bya'o/ /

The rest of those previously explained — those on the nine liberated paths free of attachment to desire-realm objects, those possessing liberation free from attachment to the seven levels, those possessing higher perception, those with enhancing meditation, those with the first eight liberated paths of the three realizations of immutability, and so too those who were not previously mentioned, [namely,] those on the preparatory and special paths of nonreturn who are free of attachment to desire-realm objects — each obtains eight in the future, excluding knowledge of elimination and knowledge of nonarising from the perspective of the learner. Nonlearners abiding on the uninterrupted path in order to comprehend higher perception, enhancing meditation, and immutability, and who are liberated according to circumstances, obtain eight, excluding knowledge of others’ minds and knowledge of nonarising. Immutable arhats obtain nine, excluding knowledge of others’ minds, since the uninterrupted path stops it. Those abiding on the special path who possess higher perception, enhancing meditation, and preparation for realizing immutability, and who are liberated according to circumstances, obtain nine, excluding knowledge of nonarising. Immutable arhats obtain all ten. Further, since it is said: The higher perception of eye and ear are neutral,[1797] both higher perceptions of divine eye and ear and also the liberated path are neutral, and there is no future obtainment of neutral states. These are from the perspective of learners. Ordinary beings [abiding] on the final liberated paths freed from attachment to the desire realm and the first three absorptions obtain, respectively, conventional knowledge subsumed by the first, second, third, and fourth absorption, and they obtain knowledge of others’ minds in the future. Those abiding on the ninth liberated path free from attachment to the four absorptions obtain conventional knowledge subsumed by the actual basis of infinite space. They do not obtain knowledge of others’ minds; there is no knowledge of others’ minds subsumed by the formless-realm level, since such knowledge is established in dependence on form. The remaining formless states should also be understood in this way.

bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi'i sa pa'i sbyor ba'i lam rnams dang*/ lha'i mig dang rna ba'i mngon shes ma gtogs pa'i mngon shes gsum gyi rnam grol gyi lam dang chad med dang rnam thar zil gnon dang zad par gyi skye mched la sogs pa yon tan mngon par sgrub pa'i rnam grol gyi lam la ni kun rdzob shes pa dang pha rol sems shes gnyis ka 'thob ste/ de dag ni bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi la rten pa'i phyir ro/ / mngon shes sprul pa ma gtogs so zhes bya ba ni bsam gtan dge ba'i stobs kyis de dag ma 'ongs pa 'thob par bshad pa yin la/ 'dir de dag gi ma 'ongs pa mi 'thob par 'dod do/ / nges 'byed cha mthun dag la ni bsam gtan gyi sa pa dag gis kyang pha rol sems shes 'thob pa med de/ mthong lam gyi 'khor yin pa'i phyir te/ ji ltar mthong lam la pha rol sems shes mi 'thob pa ltar de'i 'khor la'ang mi 'thob bo snyam du bsams pa'o/ / de yang so so'i skye bo 'dod pa dang bsam gtan snga ma gsum las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i rnam grol gyi lam tha ma ma gtogs pa dang sbyor ba dang bar chad med pa dang khyad par can gyi lam dang mngon shes gsum dang chad med pa la sogs pa yon tan mngon par sgrub pa dag gi bar chad med pa'i lam rnams la ni kun rdzob shes pa kho na ma 'ongs pa 'thob kyi gnyen po ma yin pas pha rol sems shes ni mi 'thob bo zhes TI ka las 'chad do/ /

Those abiding on the path of preparation of the level of the actual basis of absorption, those abiding on the liberated path of three higher perceptions excluding the higher perceptions of divine eye and divine ear, [614] and those abiding on the liberated path establishing qualities such as the immeasurables, the base of totality (kṛtsnāyatana), or subjugating liberation obtain both conventional knowledge and knowledge of others’ minds because these depend on the actual bases of absorption. The words of the Abhidharmakośa “except for emanation and higher perception” (2:38d) explain that these are obtained in the future by the power of virtuous absorption. But in this context it is asserted that these are not obtained in the future. Those abiding in the factors conducive to penetrative insight who exist on the level of absorption do not obtain knowledge of the minds of others because that is the retinue of the path of seeing. I think that just as they do not obtain knowledge of others’ minds, they also do not obtain its retinue. Further, ordinary beings who abide on the uninterrupted path and establish the path of preparation, uninterrupted path, and special path, and qualities such as the immeasurables and so on — excluding the final liberated path free from attachment to the desire realm and the first three absorptions — obtain the conventional path alone in the future. They do not obtain the knowledge of others’ minds, since they are not antidotes. This is explained in the Subcommentary.[1798]

'o na zag bcas zag med kyi lam gang las du pa'i shes pa 'thob ce na/ de la lam gnyis las dang po 'jig rten pa'i lam la ni mi lcogs med la brten nas 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral nas bsam gtan dang po'i dngos gzhi 'thob pa na rnam grol gyi lam dgu pa la bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs dang dngos gzhis bsdus pa'i kun rdzob shes pa 'thob pa nas srid rtse'i nyer bsdogs la brten nas ci yang med pa las 'dod chags dang bral nas srid rtse'i dngos gzhis 'thob pa na rnam grol gyi lam dgu pa la srid rtse'i nyer bsdogs dang dngos gzhis bsdus pa'i kun rdzob shes pa 'thob pa'i bar du sbyar ro/ /

Question: How many knowledges are obtained through the contaminated and uncontaminated paths? Reply: There are two paths. (1) Regarding the mundane path, if one obtains the actual basis of the first absorption free of attachment to the desire realm in dependence on mundane access concentration, one obtains conventional knowledge subsumed by access to the first absorption and the four actual bases on the ninth liberated path. If one obtains the actual basis of the summit of existence free from attachment to nothingness in dependence on access to the summit of existence, one obtains conventional knowledge subsumed by access concentration and the actual basis to the summit of existence on the ninth liberated path.
gang las chags bral bya phyir gang / / thob pa der yang 'og ma'ang 'thob/ / zad pa shes la zag bcas kyang / / sa kun sngon rnyed mi 'thob bo/ / 26

In order to be free from attachment to any level, one obtains that and also one obtains lower level. Knowledge of elimination, also contaminated qualities on all levels. Those previously acquired will not be obtained. (7:26)

gnyis pa 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam la ni sa bsam gtan gnyis pa lta bu gang las 'dod chags dang bral bar bya ba'i phyir gnyis pa'i sas bsdus pa'i zag med kyi bsam gtan gnyis pa gang zhig thob pa der yang 'og ma bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs dang dngos gzhi dang dngos gzhi khyad par can dang rnam grol dgu pa'i tshe bsam gtan gsum pa'i sas bsdus pa'i zag pa med pa'ang 'thob ste/ gnyen po'i rigs rgyas pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin dus gzhan gyi zag med la'ang sbyar bar bya'o/

(2) Regarding the transcendent path, if in order to be free from attachment to any level such as the second absorption, one obtains that uncontaminated absorption subsumed by the second level. One also obtains uncontaminated states of access concentration, actual basis, and special actual basis of the lower first absorption and that subsumed by the level of the third absorption at the time of the ninth liberated path because the class of antidotes is enhanced. So too, this should be applied also to the uncontaminated states of other times.

gang gis zad pa shes pa 'thob pa de la ni zag pa dang bcas pa'i yon tan mi sdug pa dang dbugs 'byung rngub dran pa dang dran pa nyer gzhag dang tshad med dang rnam thar zil gnon dang zad par la sogs pa rnams kyang 'thob bo/ / de yang sa kun gyis bsdus pa'i yon tan 'thob ste/ de yang 'dod chags dang bral bas 'thob pa rnams 'thob kyi sbyor bas thob pa rnams ni ma yin te/ de dag ni bsam gtan gyi stobs kyis bskyed par bya ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dod chags dang bral bas thob pa rnams ni dar gyi spreg ma thag pa bcad pa'am rgyal srid chen po thob na 'bul ba dang bcas pas yul mi rnams kyis bsu ba byed pa bzhin du rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin gyis nyon mongs pa'i thob pa bcad pa dang sems kyi rgyal srid chen po thob pa la yon tan gyi tshogs rnams kyi thob pas bsu ba'i phyir ro/ / yon tan de dag kyang 'dod pa dang gzugs dang gzugs med pa'i rten can gyi dgra bcom yin na rim pa ltar khams gsum char gyis bsdus pa dang khams gong ma gnyis dang gzugs med kyis bsdus pa kho na 'thob la de bzhin du sa'i sgo nas kyang rtogs par bya'o/ /

Whoever obtains knowledge of elimination also obtains contaminated qualities, such as knowledge of repulsiveness, mindfulness of inhalation and exhalation, close placement of mindfulness, the immeasurables, subjugating liberation, [base of] totality, and so on. They also obtain qualities subsumed by all levels. Those [qualities] obtained [615] by freedom from attachment are not obtained through preparation for obtainment; those are generated by the power of absorption. Those who obtain freedom from attachment are like those who cut the thread [binding] a silk basket or like those who attain sovereign dominion and are welcomed by their subjects with gifts. Similarly, when vajra-like concentration severs the obtainment of affliction, one attains supreme dominion over one’s mind and is welcomed with the bestowal of qualities. Also, if those qualities belong to an arhat based in the desire, form, or formless realms, they are obtainments subsumed, respectively, by the three realms, the two higher realms, and the formless realm alone. They are also comprehended in that way in terms of level.

de yang sngon rnyed zin pa ni mi 'thob ste/ de ni thob zin pa'i phyir dang{ dman pa'i phyir dang} thob pa btang ba yin na 'das pa mi 'thob pa'i phyir ro/ / slob dpon 'dun bzang ni thob pa btang ba de dag sngon 'dris par byas pas sngon du 'gyur kyang ma 'ongs pa ni mi 'thob ste stobs nyams pa'i phyir ro zhes 'dod do/ / slob dpon dbyig bshes ni sngon rnyed pa dag da lta mi ldan pa las rnyed na btang yang ma 'ongs pa 'thob par 'dod la/ kha cig ni btang ba rnams ni ma 'ongs pa mi 'thob kyi/ ma btang na ma 'ongs pa 'thob bo zhes 'dod de/ 'di dag ni gzhi med par khyad par gyi chos la dpyod pa yin no/ / ci thob pa rnyed pa kho na yin nam zhe na/

Further, qualities previously acquired (labdha) will not be obtained (bhāvyate). They were already obtained {because they are inferior}, and past qualities will not be obtained if their obtainment is relinquished. Master Saṅghabhadra asserts that those qualities whose obtainment has been relinquished manifest first due to prior habit. However, future qualities are not obtained because their strength is weak.[1799] Master Vasumitra asserts that if those qualities were previously acquired in the present without being previously possessed, they will be obtained in the future even though they are relinquished.[1800] Some say: Those qualities that are relinquished will not be obtained in the future, but if not relinquished they will be obtained in the future. These assertions are without basis, and special attributes should be analyzed. Question: Is whatever is obtained solely acquired?
rnyed dang bsten ces bya ba ni/ / dge ba 'dus byas thob pa'o/ / gnyen po dang ni thag bsring pa'i/ / thob pa zag dang bcas pa'i yin/ / 27
That which is called acquisition acquires conditioned virtue. Adherence is obtaining that. The obtainment of the antidote and removal refer to the contaminated. (7:27)
thob pa ni rnam pa bzhi ste/ rnyed pa dang*/ bsten pa dang*/ gnyen po dang*/ thag sring ba 'thob pa'o/ /
Reply: Obtainment has four types: acquisition, adherence, antidote, and removal.

de la rnyed pa 'thob pa zhes bya ba ni dge ba 'dus byas rnams{ goms pas de dag ma 'ongs pa rnams} kyis gsar du rnyed pa lta bu 'o/ / sten pa 'thob pa zhes bya ba ni dge ba 'dus byas{ thob zin} rnams kyis yang dang yang du mngon du byas pa'i thob pa'o/ / de yang da ltar ba'i chos la ni rnyed pa dang bsten pa gnyis yod la ma 'ongs pa la rnyed pa 'ba' zhig dang 'das pa la gnyis ka med do/ / gnyen po 'thob pa dang thag sring ba 'thob pa ni zag pa dang bcas pa'i chos rnams kyis gnyen po 'thob pa dang de dag spangs pa thag sring ba yin te/ rim pa ltar lus sems la 'dod chags dang bral bar byed pa dang*/ nyon mongs pa'i thob pa gcod pa'o/ / de ltar na dge ba zag bcas rnams kyis ni thob pa bzhi char yin no/ / de yang dang po gnyis ni dge ba zag bcas rang gis 'thob pa yin la phyi ma gnyis ni de dag gi gnyen po dang rnam grol thob pa la de dag gi thob pa zhes btags nas brjod pa yin no/ / zag med kyi ni 'thob pa dang po gnyis yin gyi phyi ma gnyis ni ma yin te/ zag med la gnyen po med pa'i phyir dang*/ de nyid kyis thag sring ba'ang med pa'i phyir ro/ / nyon mongs can bsgribs la lung ma bstan rnams kyis ni gnyen po 'thob pa dang spangs pa thag sring ba'i thob pa gnyis yin te/ shes pa kha cig ni de dag gi gnyen po yin pa'i phyir dang*/ kha cig ni de dag thag sring ba yin pa'i phyir dang*/ 'dir gang cung zad bshad pa'i thob pa'i dbye ba ni shes pa'i thob pa la brtsams nas bshad pa'i phyir dang*/ spyir thob pa'i dbye ba yang sngar bshad zin pa'i phyir ro/ /

(1) That which is called the obtainment of acquisition (pratilambha) is, {for example,} newly acquiring {future} conditioned virtue (śubhasaṃskṛta) {through cultivating it}. (2) That which is called obtainment of adherence (niṣeva) is obtaining (bhāvana) conditioned virtue {already obtained} through frequently manifesting it. Further, acquisition and adherence exist for present phenomena, but only acquisition exists for future phenomena, and neither exists for past phenomena. (3) Obtainment of the antidote (pratipakṣa) and (4) obtainment of removal (vinirdhāva) are the obtainment of the antidote to all contaminated (sāsrava) phenomena and removing them through abandoning them because, respectively, the antidote acts to free the body and mind from attachment, and removal severs the obtainment of affliction. Therefore the obtainment of contaminated virtue has four aspects. Moreover, the first two, which are the obtainment of contaminated virtuous states by oneself, and the latter two, which are the obtainment of their antidote and liberation, are imputed to be obtainment. Uncontaminated states are obtained by the first two but not the latter two, because, respectively, the antidote is not an antidote to uncontaminated states and removal does not remove such states. Both the obtainment of antidotes [616] and the obtainment of the removal of objects to be abandoned exist in relation to obscured-neutral states, because some types of knowledge are their antidote, some remove them, the classification of obtainment just explained is explained as the obtainment of knowledge, and in general the classification of obtainment has been explained before.

'o na ni kun rdzob shes pa mi dge ba dang lung ma bstan yod pas de dag rnyed pa dang bsten pa'i thob pa'ang yod pa'i phyir de dag gi thob pa bzhir 'gyur ro zhe na/ de lta mod kyi phal che ba'i dbang du byas nas de dag gi thob pa gnyis yin par bstan to/ / nyi 'og pa rnams ni sdom pa 'thob pa dang*/ rnam par 'jig pa 'thob pa gnyis bsnan nas drug 'dod de/ dang po ni mdo las/ dbang po drug po 'di dag shin tu dul ba dang shin tu bsgoms pa zhes gsungs pa mig sogs dbang po drug gi sgo sdom pa dran shes bzhin gyi bdag nyid yin la/ gnyis pa ni lus la dmigs pa'i nyon mongs pa thag sring ba ste phyi nang gi lus dran pa nyer gzhag 'thob pa yin no/ / kha che ba rnams ni de dag kyang rim pa ltar phyi ma gnyis kyi nang du 'dus so zhes zer ro/ / yang na gnyis ka'ang gnyis ka'i khongs su 'dus so zhes byas kyang 'gal ba med do zhes rgyal po'i sras 'chad do/ /

Objection: Since nonvirtuous and neutral conventional knowledge exist, their obtainment would be fourfold because obtainment of acquisition and adherence would also exist. Reply: Indeed, that is so, but in general their obtainment is taught to be two. Aparāntaka Vaibhāṣikas assert six obtainments by adding obtainment of restraint and obtainment of destruction.[1801] Regarding the first, a sūtra declares: One fully tames and fully meditates on those six faculties.[1802] This passage states that restraint of the six doors of the sense faculties, such as the eyes, refers to the states of mindfulness and introspection. The second refers to obtaining close placement of mindfulness of the external and internal body that removes afflicted states focusing on the body. Kāśmīri Vabhāṣikas say that these are included, respectively, in the latter two of the original four.[1803] Yaśomitra explains that their assertion does not contradict the statement, “Also two are included in two.”
32. The Unique Qualities of a Buddha
da ni gsum pa [de dag gi yon tan]
THE QUALITIES OF KNOWLEDGE
de dag gi yon tan ston te/ de yang sngar ni zad pa shes la zag bcas kyang zhes nyan rang sangs rgyas rnams kyi zad shes kyi skad cig la thob pa'i yon tan spyir bshad la/

This section teaches the qualities of knowledge. Futher, the statement in the Abhidharmakośa “Knowledge of elimination, also contaminated qualities on all levels” (7:26c) explains in general the qualities obtained in one moment of the knowledge of elimination of a śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, and buddha.
'dir ni sangs rgyas kyi yon tan thun mong ma yin pa dang thun mong gnyis las/
This has two headings: the unique qualities of a buddha and the shared qualities of a buddha.
dang po [sangs rgyas kyi yon tan thun mong ma yin pa]
THE UNIQUE QUALITIES OF A BUDDHA
['di] la'ang gsum las
This has three headings: (1) overview, (2) elaboration, and (3) in conclusion, equality and inequality.
mdor bstan pa ni
Overview
rnam bshad rigs pa las/ gti mug gnyid gnyis sangs phyir dang*/ /blo rgyas phyir na sangs rgyas pa zhes 'byung bas
Master Vasubandhu’s Rational System of Exposition states: He is a buddha because he clears away both delusion and sleep and because he develops insight.[1804]
sangs rgyas chos ni ma 'dres pa/ / stobs la sogs pa bco brgyad do/ /
The Buddha acquires the eighteen unmixed qualities such as the powers and so on. (7:28ab)

ma rig pa'i gnyid sangs pa dang ye shes kyi snang ba rgyas pa'i sangs rgyas kyis zad pa mkhyen pa'i tshe brnyes pa'i yon tan gyi chos nyan thos la sogs pa gzhan dang thun mong ma yin pas ma 'dres pa'i stobs bcu dang sogs pa'i sgras gzung ba mi 'jigs pa bzhi dang dran pa nyer gzhag gsum dang thugs rje chen po ste bco brgyad do/ / mdo gzhan las de bzhin gshegs pa la 'khrul pa mi mnga' ba la sogs pa bco brgyad gsungs pa ni mdo sde'i rgyan du/ spyod pa dang ni rtogs pa dang*/ / ye shes dang ni phrin las kyis/ / nyan thos rang sangs rgyas kun gyi/ / bla ma khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/ / zhes bzhir bsdus pa ni theg pa gong ma pa'i lugs yin no/ /

When the Buddha cleared away the sleep of ignorance and fully developed the illumination of transcendent wisdom, he realized the elimination of affliction and acquired the eighteen unmixed qualities (aṣṭādaśāveṇika) and so on, including (1–10) the ten powers (balā), (11–14) the four fearlessnesses, (15–17) three foundations of mindfulness, and (18) great compassion. [They are “unmixed”] since they are not shared with others such as śrāvakas. Other sūtras state the eighteen to be the Tathāgata not possessing distortion and so on. The Ornament of the Mahāyāna Sūtras explains: I pay homage to you, the guru of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, who possesses practice, realization, transcendent wisdom, and enlightened action.[1805] Condensing these into four is the system of the higher vehicle [the Mahāyāna]. [617]
rgyas par bshad pa
ELABORATION
['di] la bzhi las
This has four headings: the ten powers, the four types of fearlessness, three foundations of mindfulness, and great compassion.
dang po stobs bcu bshad pa ni
The ten powers
gnas dang gnas min shes pa bcu/ / las 'bras la brgyad bsam gtan sogs/ / 28
Viability and nonviability are the ten knowledges. Karma and its results are eight. Absorption and so on. (7:28cd)

gnas dang gnas min pa ni srid pa dang mi srid pa ste/{ 'dus byas dang 'dus ma byas kyi chos thams cad do/ /} de la gnas dge ba las mtho ris 'byung ba dang mi dge ba las ngan song 'byung ba dang skyes pa rang sangs rgyas su 'gyur ba la sogs pa dang*/ gnas ma yin pa dge bas ngan song du 'gro ba gnas ma yin pa la sogs pa rgyu dang rgyu ma yin pa thams cad mngon sum du mkhyen pa'i stobs ni shes pa rnam pa bcu ste/ de la gnas dang gnas ma yin pa ni bsdu na 'dus byas dang 'dus ma byas gnyis yin la/ {gnas mkhyen pas ni rgyu med par smra ba 'gog la/ gnas ma yin pa mkhyen pas ni mi mthun pa rgyur smra ba 'gog go } 'dus byas la khams gsum dang zag med la mtshungs ldan dang de ma yin pa gnyis gnyis su phye bas brgyad dang*/ 'dus ma byas la dge ba dang lung ma bstan gnyis su phye bas bcur 'gyur/ de la kun rdzob shes pa'i yul ni bcu char yin la/ chos shes pa'i ni 'dod pa dang zag med 'dus byas gnyis gnyis dang 'dus ma byas dge ba ste lnga dang*/ rjes su shes pa'i ni khams gong ma gnyis dang 'dus byas zag med gnyis gnyis dang 'dus ma byas dge ba ste bdun dang*/ sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung shes pa'i ni khams gsum gyi drug go /'gog pa shes pa'i ni 'dus ma byas dge ba kho na'o/ / lam shes pa'i ni 'dus byas zag med gnyis so/ / pha rol sems shes kyis ni 'dod gzugs dang 'dus byas zag med kyi mtshungs ldan gsum mo/ / zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa'i ni 'dus ma byas lung ma bstan ma gtogs pa dgu'o/ /
