(1) Viability (sthāna) and nonviability (asthāna) refer to that which is possible and not possible {regarding all conditioned and unconditioned phenomena}. What is viable is higher rebirth arising from virtue and unpleasant rebirth arising from nonvirtue, a person becoming a pratyekabuddha, and so on. What is not viable is proceeding to evil abodes through virtue. The power directly realizing all causes and noncauses and so on constitutes the ten types of knowledge. If viability and nonviability are summarized, there are two: conditioned and unconditioned states. {Through comprehending viability, those advocating causelessness are refuted. Through comprehending nonviability, those advocating impossible modes of causation are refuted.} There are ten in total, for there are eight conditioned states, through dividing the three realms and the uncontaminated into concomitant or nonconcomitant states, and there are two unconditioned states, through dividing them into virtuous or neutral states. These are the ten objects of conventional knowledge. Dharma knowledge has five: two each for the desire realm and conditioned uncontaminated states, and one for unconditioned virtue. Subsequent knowledge has seven: two each for the two upper realms and conditioned uncontaminated states, and one for unconditioned virtue. Knowledge of suffering and origin have six: the six of the three realms. Knowledge of cessation has one: unconditioned virtue alone. Knowledge of the path has two: conditioned and uncontaminated states. Knowledge of others’ minds has three: that concomitant with desire-realm states, form-realm states, and conditioned uncontaminated states. Knowledge of elimination and nonarising have nine: those except for unconditioned-neutral states.

zag bcas kyi las dang{ de'i} 'bras bu rnam par smin pa sna tshogs{ ni bden pa dang po gnyis yin la de} mkhyen pa'i stobs la ni 'gog lam shes pa ma gtogs pa shes pa brgyad yin te/ 'gog lam shes pa ni zag med kho na la dmigs la las de'i rnam smin ni zag bcas bden pa dang po gnyis kyis sems shes kyi khams 'og ma gnyis kyi {sems sems byung dge mi dge shes la/ chos shes cha dang bcas pas 'dod pa dang rjes shes cha dang bcas pas gong ma gnyis shes so } bsdus pa'i phyir{ kun rdzob shes pa ni khams gsum ga'i las 'bras la dmigs so} ro/ /

(2) The power comprehending contaminated karma and {its} results as diverse karmic maturation constitutes eight [knowledges], excluding knowledge of cessation and the path; knowledge of cessation and the path focus on uncontaminated states alone, and the karmic maturation of action is subsumed by the first two truths. {Knowledge of others’ minds knows virtuous and nonvirtuous minds and mental factors of the two lower realms. Since it has a component of Dharma knowledge, it knows the desire realm, and since it has a component of subsequent knowledge, it knows both higher realms.} {Conventional knowledge focuses on karma and its result in the three realms.}

bsam gtan bzhi dang*/ sogs pas gzung ba rnam thar brgyad dang*/ stong pa nyid la sogs pa'i ting nge 'dzin gsum dang*/ 'du shes med pa dang 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug gnyis dang*/ mthar gyis gnas pa'i snyoms 'jug dgu dang*/ gzugs med snyoms 'jug bzhi'i rang bzhin dang thob pa dang phan 'dogs pa dang ro myang ldan la sogs pa dang nyams pa cha mthun la sogs pa'i{ nyon mongs dang rnam byang gi} don rnams thogs pa med par mkhyen pa'i stobs ni shes pa dgu yin te/ de dag 'dus byas zag bcas zag med kho na la dmigs pa'i phyir dang 'gog pa shes pa ma gtogs pa'i phyir ro/ /

(3) The power of unobstructed realization of {afflicted and pure} objects of the four absorptions; the eight liberations; the three concentrations such as emptiness; both meditative attainments of nondiscernment and cessation; the nine meditative attainments of serial abandoners and so forth; the essence, obtainment, benefit, taste, and so on of the four formless meditative attainments and so forth; states compatible with degeneration and so on — [all these] constitute nine knowledges because they focus on conditioned contaminated and uncontaminated states alone, excluding the knowledge of cessation.
dbang po mos dang khams la ni/ / dgu'o lam dag la bcu 'am/ / gnyis ni kun rdzob shes pa yin/ / zad pa drug gam bcu yin no/ / 29
Faculties, resolutions, and dispositions are nine. The paths are ten, two are conventional knowledge. Elimination is six or ten. (7:29)

de bzhin du dad pa la sogs pa'i dbang po mchog dang mchog ma yin pa dang*/ nyan thos la sogs pa la mos pa sna tshogs dang*/ nyan thos la sogs pa'i khams sna tshogs mkhyen pa'i stobs rnams la ni 'gog pa shes pa ma gtogs pa shes pa dgu dgu yin te/ de la dbang po dang mos pa ni sems byung yin zhing khams ni slob dpon 'dun bzang sems can rnams kyi sngon goms pa'i bag chags kyis yang dag par grub pa'i bsam pa la 'dod pas de yang sems dang sems byung khyad par can yin la/ / {de yang bden pa dang po gnyis dang lam mo } de dag kyang zag bcas zag med 'dus byas kho na la dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Similarly, (4) the power comprehending diverse supreme and nonsupreme faculties such as faith, (5) the power comprehending diverse resolutions (adhimokṣa) of śrāvakas and so on, [618] and (6) the power comprehending diverse dispositions (dhātu) of śrāvakas and so on constitute nine knowledges each, excepting the knowledge of cessation. Faculties and resolutions are mental factors. Master Saṅghabhadra asserts dispositions to be thoughts fully established by the imprints of the prior habits of sentient beings, and thus they are special minds and mental factors. {Further, they constitute the first two truths and the path}. They also focus on contaminated and uncontaminated conditioned states alone.

dmyal ba nas 'gog pa'i bar thams cad du 'gro ba'i lam mkhyen pa'i stobs dag la ni shes pa bcu yin te/ lam ni rgyu yin la de nyid 'bras bu dang bcas pa mkhyen par 'dod na ni 'gog pa shes pa'ang yod pa'i phyir te/ 'gog pa ni lam gyi skyes bu byed pa dang bral ba'i 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / lam 'ba' zhig mkhyen pa stobs su 'dod na ni lam 'dus byas yin pas 'gog shes ma gtogs pa shes pa dgu yin no/ / de ltar lugs tha dad pa'am zhes smros pa yin no/ /

(7) The power comprehending the paths proceeding to all rebirths, from hell to cessation, constitutes ten knowledges because if the path that is a cause is asserted to realize the path and its result, it would also be knowledge of cessation, because cessation is a result of conscious effort on the path and a result of separation. If it is asserted to be the strength realizing the path alone, it would be knowledge of nine except for knowledge of cessation, since the path is a conditioned state. Thus distinct systems are expressed.

sngon gyi gnas rjes su dran pa dang 'chi 'pho dang skye ba mkhyen pa'i stobs gnyis ni kun rdzob shes pa yin gyi gzhan ni ma yin te/ 'di dag bden pa la mi dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di ltar sngon gyi gnas rjes su dran pa ni rang gzhan gyi skye ba snga ma dran pa yin la/ 'chi ba dang 'pho ba bar do dang skye ba mkhyen pa ni rang gzhan gyi ma 'ongs pa'i srid pa mkhyen pa ste/ 'di dag rang gi mtshan nyid la dmigs kyi spyi'i mtshan nyid bdag med pa'i rnam par ma zhugs pa'i phyir bden pa la mi dmigs so/ /

Two powers — (8) the power recalling former lives and (9) the power comprehending death and rebirth — are conventional knowledge (saṃvṛtijñāna) and not the others because they do not focus on these truths. Thus, recalling former lives recalls former births of self and others. Realization of death and rebirth realizes the future existence of self and others. Because it focuses on real objects and does not engage abstract objects such as selflessness, it does not focus on the four truths.

zag pa zad pa mkhyen pa'i stobs kyis gal te zag pa zad pa 'gog bden 'ba' zhig mkhyen par 'dod na ni chos shes rjes shes dang 'gog pa shes pa dang zad mi skye shes pa dang kun rdzob shes pa dang drug yin te/ 'gog pa shes pa'i rigs kho na chos shes la sogs pa'i bye brag gis tha dad du byas pa'i phyir dang*/ 'dus ma byas yin pas bden pa gzhan gsum shes pa dang pha rol sems shes mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / 'on te zad pa shes pa zag pa zad pa'i rgyud la yod pa'i shes pa la 'dod na ni de'i rgyud la ni shes pa thams cad 'byung bas shes pa bcu yin no/ / da ni de dag gang la brten pa'i sa bshad par bya ste/

If it is asserted that (10) the power comprehending the elimination (kṣaya) of contaminants realizes the truth of cessation to be the elimination of the contaminants alone, then it would consist of six — Dharma knowledge, subsequent knowledge, knowledge of cessation, knowledge of elimination, knowledge of nonarising, and conventional knowledge — because only those of the class of knowledge of cessation, such as Dharma knowledge and so on, would be individually differentiated, and knowledge of the other three truths and knowledge of others’ minds would be impossible, since cessation is unconditioned. But if it is asserted that knowledge of elimination is knowledge existing in the mindstream of one who has exhausted the contaminants, it would consist of ten knowledges, since all knowledges exist in that mindstream. Now the levels on which they depend will be explained.
sngon gnas 'chi 'pho skye ba'i stobs/ / bsam gtan dag na lhag ma ni/ / sa rnams kun na ci yi phyir/ / 'di'i stobs gang phyir thogs mi mnga'/ / 30
The power of former lives, and death and rebirth, exist in the absorptions. The remaining eight exist on all levels. Why? They are powers because they engage all without obstruction. (7:30)

de la sngon gyi gnas rjes su dran pa dang 'chi 'pho dang skye ba mkhyen pa'i stobs gnyis ni bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi bzhi po dag na yod de/ 'di dag zhi gnas dang lhag mthong zung du 'brel ba'i ting nge 'dzin la brten nas skyed par bya ba yin pa nas gzhan ni de lta ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / stobs lhag ma brgyad po ni {de dag 'og sa spong ba yin gyi yon tan bskyed pa'i sa min pas } nyer bsdogs phyi ma bdun ma gtogs pa sa rnams kun na yod de/ bskyed sla ba'i phyir zag med rnams ni ci rigs par zag med kyi sa rnams la rten la/ kun rdzob shes pas bsdus pa'i stobs rnams ni sa thams cad la rten par 'dod do/ / 'on kyang 'di dag yongs su dag pa'i ting nge 'dzin la brten nas mkhyen pa'i phyir bsam gtan bzhi ba'i sems la phal cher rten pa yin no/ / lus kyi rten ni gling gzhan dang khams gzhan dang 'gro ba gzhan gyi rten la sangs rgyas mi 'byung ba'i phyir dang*/ bud med rten dang bsam sbyor dman pa'i phyir 'dzam bu'i gling gi skyes pa kho na la rten par 'dod do/ / 'o na shes pa bcu po de dag nyan rang la sogs pa la'ang ci rigs par yod bzhin du ci'i phyir sangs rgyas kho na'i la stobs zhes bya zhe na/

Both the power recalling former lives (prāṇnivāsa) and the power comprehending death and rebirth (cyutpāda) exist on the four actual bases of absorption because they are generated in dependence on concentration that is the union of calm abiding and insight, and the others are not like that. Because they are easy to generate, the eight remaining powers exist on all levels except for the latter seven access concentrations {for though [access states] abandon lower levels, they are not levels where qualities are generated.} [619] Uncontaminated states depend on uncontaminated levels of any type. Powers subsumed by conventional knowledge depend on all levels. However, they mainly depend on the minds of the four absorptions because they realize their objects in dependence on thoroughly pure concentration. Their physical basis is asserted to be males of Jambudvīpa alone. Buddhahood does not occur on the basis of other humans, other realms, or reincarnating beings, and the female basis has inferior thought and application. Question: If any of these ten knowledges also exist for śrāvakas and so on, then why are they powers for a buddha alone?

sangs rgyas la mnga' ba'i shes pa bcu po 'di dag ni stobs yin te/ gang gi phyir 'di'i mkhyen pa shes bya thams cad la thogs pa mi mnga' bar 'jug pa de'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir sangs rgyas las gzhan la'ang gnas dang gnas ma yin pa mkhyen pa la sogs pa nyi tshe ba yod mod kyi/ 'ga' zhig shes kyang 'ga' zhig mi shes pas shes bya la thogs pa dang bcas pa'i phyir stobs zhes bya ba'i ming mi 'thob ste/ gnas brtan shA ri'i bus khang bdag dpal skyes kyi thar ba'i cha mthun gyi dge ba ma shes pas rab tu ma phyung ba dang bya zhig khras gcas pa'i skye 'chi'i mtha' ma shes pa lta bu'o/ / de ltar na mkhyen pa la thogs pa mi mnga' ba'i phyir sangs rgyas kyi thugs kyi stobs ni shes bya bzhin du mtha' yas pa yin no/ / 'o na thugs kyi stobs de ltar thogs pa mi mnga' na sku'i stobs ji ltar zhe na/

Reply: These ten knowledges are powers (balā) possessed by a buddha because these powers engage all objects of knowledge without obstruction (avyāhata). Indeed, beings other than buddhas occasionally realize viability and nonviability and so on. But these are not termed “powers” because they are obstructed to objects of knowledge — they know some and do not know others. It is like the elder Śāriputra, who did not confer ordination on the householder Śrījāta since Śāriputra did not see that Śrījāta possessed virtue conducive to liberation, nor did he know all the births and deaths of a pigeon chased by a hawk. Thus the power of the mind of a buddha is infinite, like objects of knowledge, because the Buddha does not possess [the least] obstruction to realization. Question: If his power of mind is unobstructed, what about the power of his body?
sku la sred med bu yi stobs/ / gzhan dag tshigs na glang chen sogs/ / bdun cus blags pa'i stobs yin no/ / de ni reg bya'i skye mched do/ / 31
His body has the strength of Nārāyaṇa. Others say, each joint. There are seven elephants and so on, for each surpasses the former in power by a factor of ten. It is the tactile base. (7:31)

Reply: The body of a buddha has the power of Nārāyaṇa. The term “Nārāyaṇa” is a term for power, like [the number marked by] the sixtieth decimal place being called “countless.” Other past masters say: The jointed bones of his body and even each joint has the power of Nārāyaṇa.[1806] {Bodhisattva Levels states: Even each joint of all the joints of his body has the power of Nārāyaṇa.}[1807]

dpes ston pa'i gnas brtan btsun pa na re thugs kyi stobs mtha' yas pa ltar sku'i stobs kyang mtha' yas te/ de lta ma yin na thugs kyi stobs ji ltar bzod par 'gyur zhes zer ro/ / de'i phyir rus pa'i tshigs kyi khyad par ni sangs rgyas dang rang sangs rgyas dang 'khor los bsgyur ba rnams kyi rim pa ltar klu'i mdud pa dang lu gu rgyud dang gzer bus btab pa ltar sra ba yin no/ /

A Dārṣṭāntika elder says: Just as his power of mind is infinite, so too the power of his body is infinite. Were that not so, how could his body bear the mind whose power is infinite?[1808] Therefore, in terms of the difference of their skeletal joints, those of the buddha, pratyekabuddha, and cakravartin are, respectively, hard like the serpent demon (nagāgranthi), hard like a lamb tether (śaṅkalā), and hard enough to nail a tack (śaṅku).

'o na sred med kyi bu'i stobs kyi tshad ji tsam zhe na/ glang chen phal pa dang*/ sogs pas bsdus pa spos kyi glang po che dang*/ tshan po che chen po dang*/ rab gnon dang*/ yan lag mchog dang*/ stobs mchog dang*/ sred med kyi bu rnams te bdun po de dag snga ma snga ma bcus glags shing bsgyur ba ni phyi ma phyi ma'i stobs yin no/ /

Question: What is the measure of the power of Nārāyaṇa? Reply: There are seven elephants: (1) ordinary elephant, (2) incense elephant, (3) great of the great, (4) supreme oppressor, (5) possessing supreme limbs, (6) possessing supreme power, and (7) the Nārāyaṇa elephant. Each surpasses the former by a factor of ten — each of the latter has ten times the power of the former and so on.

kha cig na re stobs mchog bcu'i stobs ni sred med kyi bu'i stobs phyed yin la de gnyis su bsgyur ba ni sred med kyi bu'i stobs yin no zhes zer ro/ / slob dpon ni gnas brtan btsun pa'i gzhung gzugs pa'i phyir sku'i stobs ji ltar ches che ba de ltar rung ste/ de lta ma yin na mkhyen pa'i stobs mtha' yas pa bzod par mi 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ gzhan du na lhas byin gyis bsad pa'i glang po che'i ro'i zhabs kyi mthe bos ra ba dang 'obs bdun zlo bar yang mi 'gyur ba'i phyir ro zhes 'dod do/ /

Some say: The power of ten elephants with supreme power is half the power of a Nārāyaṇa elephant, [620] and double that is the power of a Nārāyaṇa elephant.[1809] Vasubandhu asserts that the text of the venerable elder explaining that the power of the [Buddha’s] material body is extremely great is tenable. Were it not so, it could not bear the infinite power of his mind; nor could the toe [of Siddhārtha] hurl the corpse of an elephant killed by Devadatta beyond the seven walls and moats [of the city].[1810]

de lta bu'i sku'i stobs de'i ngo bo ni reg bya'i skye mched de 'byung ba chen po'i khyad par kho na yin gyi 'byung ba las gyur pa ni ma yin no/ / kha cig na re stobs de ni 'byung ba ma yin gyi sngar bshad pa'i 'bras bu'i reg bya 'jam pa nyid la sogs pa bdun las don gzhan du gyur pa rgyur byas pa'i reg bya brgyad pa zhig yin no zhes zer ro/{ 'khregs pa la 'dod par mngon no/}

The nature of the power of such a body is the tactile base specifically composed of the great elements alone and not element derivatives. Some say: That power is not a primary element but an eighth tactile object beyond the seven tactile objects such as smoothness that are results previously explained. {It is asserted to be solidity.}
gnyis pa mi 'jigs pa bshad pa ni
The four types of fearlessness
mi 'jigs pa ni rnam pa bzhi/ / ji ltar stobs ni dang po dang / / bcu pa gnyis pa bdun pa bzhin/ /
Fearlessness has four types. The first is like the first power, the second like the tenth, the third like the second, the fourth like the seventh. (7:32abc)

mi 'jigs pa ni rnam pa bzhi yin par mdo las/ kye ma nga mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas pa la 'di na chos 'di dag mngon par rdzogs par sangs ma rgyas so zhes nga la dge sbyong ngam bram ze'am lha'am bdud dam tshangs pa yang rung ste 'ga' yang chos dang mthun pas rgol zhing gleng bar byed pa'i rgyu mtshan yang dag par rjes su ma mthong ngo*/ / de ltar ngas rgyu mtshan yang dag par rjes su ma mthong bas bdag bde ba dang*/ bag tsha ba med pa dang*/ mi 'jigs pa thob par gnas te khyu mchog rlabs po che'i gnas su zhal gyis 'tsho zhing 'khor gyi nang du seng ge'i sgra sgrogs so/ / tshangs pa'i 'khor lo 'jig rten na dge sbyong la sogs pa gang gis kyang ma bskor ba'i chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba 'di ni mi 'jigs pa dang po zhes pa dang*/ de bzhin du nga nyid kyis zag pa rnams zad do zhes zhal gyis bzhes pa dang*/ nyan thos rnams la 'dod chags la sogs pa bar du gcod pa'i chos su bstan pa dang*/ lam nges par 'byung ba nyid du bstan pa la rgol ba ma mthong ba la sogs pa rgya cher gsungs so/ /

Fearlessness (vaiśāradya) has four types. A sūtra states: Friends, having attained the state of a perfect buddha, I do not see any correct reason why śramaṇas, brahmans, gods, māras, or Brahma should oppose and dispute with me, saying that I have not attained the state of a perfect buddha in relation to this or that dharma,[1811] since I am always in harmony with the Dharma. Since I do not see such a correct reason, I abide in bliss, without apprehension, without panic. Having obtained fearlessness, I live as supreme leader of the herd, proclaiming Dharma to my followers with the roar of a lion. The first fearlessness is turning the wheel of Dharma or turning the wheel of purity that cannot be turned in the world by śramaṇas and so on. And: So too I have eliminated the contaminants. This he mentioned, and he explained more broadly: To śrāvakas I have taught that attachment and so on are obstructive phenomena and I have taught the path to be renunciation and so on. I have seen no one who can oppose this.

de la bdag nyid mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas pa ni shes bya thams cad mngon sum du mkhyen pa ste/ ji ltar stobs dang po gnas dang gnas ma yin pa mkhyen pa'i stobs shes pa bcu dang sa thams cad kyis bsdus pa de bzhin du mi 'jigs pa dang po 'di yang yin no/ / bdag nyid kyi zag pa rnams zad pa nyid du zhal gyis bzhes pa ni sgrib pa ma lus pa spangs pa nyid mkhyen pa ste/ ji ltar stobs bcu pa zag pa zad pa mkhyen pa {'gog shes cha mthun dang bcas pa } shes pa drug gam bcu dang sa bcu gcig gis bsdus pa de bzhin du mi 'jigs gnyis pa 'di yang yin no/ / bar du gcod pa'i chos su bstan pa ni nyon mongs pa'i bdud la sogs pa lam la bar du gcod pa nyid du mkhyen ste/ ji ltar stobs gnyis pa las {las de ni sdug kun du 'dus pas } bdag gir bya ba mkhyen pa 'gog lam shes pa ma gtogs brgyad ngad mas thams cad kyis bsdus pa de bzhin du mi 'jigs pa gsum pa 'di yang yin te/ bden pa dang po gnyis kyis bsdus pa kho nas bar du gcod pa'i phyir ro/ / lam nges par 'byung ba nyid du bstan pa ni nyan thos la sogs pa'i lam mkhyen pa ste/ ji ltar stobs bdun pa thams cad du 'gro ba'i lam mkhyen pa shes pa bcu'am dgu dang sa thams cad kyis bsdus pa de bzhin du mi 'jigs pa bzhi pa 'di yang yin te/ zag bcas zag med kyi lam 'bras bu dang bcas pa bzung na bcu dang 'bras bu med pa bzung na dgu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / bye brag tu smra ba ni shes pa nyid mi 'jigs par 'dod la/ slob dpon ni mi 'jigs pa ni mi skrag pa yin pas shes pa nyid ma yin gyi shes pa'i 'bras bu yin te/ shes pa la brten nas mi skrag pa 'byung ba'i phyir 'bras bu'i ming gis rgyu la btags pa yin te steng ka rkang nad ces bya ba bzhin no zhes bzhed do/ / don 'di nyid mdo sde'i rgyan las kyang*/ rang gzhan don du ye shes dang*/ / spangs dang nges 'byung gegs mdzad pa/ / ston mdzad mu stegs gzhan dag gis/ / mi rdzi khyod la phyag 'tshal lo zhes gsungs so/{ stobs ni gzhan gyi zil gyis mi gnon pa yin la mi 'jigs pa ni gzhan slar zil gyis gnon pa'o/}

(1) His proclamation that “I am a perfect buddha” means that he has directly comprehended all objects of knowledge. The first fearlessness subsumes all ten knowledges and levels, just like the first power comprehending viability and nonviability. (2) His proclamation “I have eliminated the contaminants” means that he has comprehended the abandonment of all obscurations without exception. The second fearlessness subsumes six or ten knowledges {when associated with states compatible with knowledge of cessation} and the ten levels, like the tenth power comprehending elimination of contamination. (3) His proclamation: “I have taught obstructive phenomena” means that he comprehends the māras of the afflictions and so on that obstruct the path. The third fearlessness encompasses eight knowledges; it does not include knowledge of cessation and knowledge of the path and all levels, like the second power comprehending karma. {That karma is included in suffering and origin} [621] because the first two truths alone obstruct. (4) His proclamation “I have taught the path to be renunciation” means that he has comprehended the paths of śrāvakas and so on. The fourth fearlessness subsumes ten or nine knowledges and all levels, like the seventh power comprehending the paths proceeding to all rebirths. For if one apprehends contaminated and uncontaminated paths and their results, one has ten, and if one apprehends those without result, one has nine. Vaibhāṣikas assert that fearlessness is knowledge itself. Vasubandhu asserts that since fearlessness refers to not being terrified, it is not knowledge but the result of knowledge, because not being terrified depends on knowledge. Here the name of the result is imputed to the cause, like calling a disease of the upper leg a disease of the foot.[1812] Regarding this point, Ornament of the Mahāyāna Sūtras states: I pay homage to you who possesses transcendent wisdom, abandonment, and renunciation for the purpose of self and others, and who is not dominated by various tīrthikas who obstruct through their teachings.[1813] {Power refers to not being overpowered by others; fearlessness is easily overpowering others.}
gsum ba dran pa nye bar bzhag pa gsum bstan pa ni
Three foundations of mindfulness
dran dang shes bzhin bdag nyid gsum/ / 32
Three are states of mindfulness and introspection. (7:32d)

mdo las/ dge slong dran pa nye bar bzhag pa gsum po 'di dag ni gang dag 'phags pa bsten par byed pa ste 'phags pas de dag bsten na 'khor la rjes su ston par 'os so/ / gsum gang zhe na/ dge slong dag 'di na ston pa thugs brtse ba/ thugs rje can/ don bzhed pa/ phan par bzhed pa/ thugs rje chen po dang ldan pas nyan thos rnams la 'di ni khyed la phan par byed pa/ 'di ni khyed la bde bar byed pa/ 'di ni khyed la phan pa dang bde bar byed pa'o zhes chos ston par mdzad cing*/ nyan thos de dag de la nyan par byed/ rna ba gtod par byed/ kun shes pa'i sems nye bar 'jog par byed/ chos kyi rjes su mthun pa'i chos sgrub par byed/ ston pa'i bstan pa las mi 'gal bar byed na/ des de bzhin gshegs pa kun du dgyes par yang mi 'gyur/ yid bde ba dang thugs ya ya bor yang mi 'gyur gyi/ de la de bzhin gshegs pa dran pa dang shes bzhin du btang snyoms su bzhugs te/ 'di ni gang dag 'phags pa bsten par byed pa ste 'phags pas de dag bsten na tshogs la rjes su ston par 'os pa'i dran pa nye bar bzhag pa dang po yin no zhes pa dang*/ de bzhin du ston pa chos ston pa na nyan thos de dag de la nyan par mi byed pa nas ston pa'i bstan pa las 'gal bar byed pa'i bar du gyur na/ des de bzhin gshegs pa kun tu mi dgyes pa dang yid mi bde ba dang thugs ya ya po dang kun nas mnar sems su mi 'gyur la/ mi bzod pa dang tshig pa dang thugs ma rangs pa mi mnga' bar de la de bzhin gshegs pa dran pa dang shes bzhin du btang snyoms su bzhugs pa ni dran pa nyer gzhag gnyis pa dang*/ de bzhin du nyan thos kha cig ni de la nyan par byed pa nas ston pa'i bstan pa las mi 'gal ba'i bar du byed la/ kha cig ni nyan par mi byed pa nas ston pa'i bstan pa las 'gal ba'i bar du byed kyang des de bzhin gshegs pa dgyes pa dang mi dgyes pa gnyis kar mi 'gyur bar dran pa dang shes bzhin du btang snyoms su bzhugs pa ni dran pa nyer gzhag gsum pa'o zhes 'khor gus par nyan pa dang mi nyan pa dang gnyis ka'i bye brag gis gsum gsungs la gsum po 'di dag ni dran pa dang shes bzhin nam shes rab kyi bdag nyid dag yin la/ shes rab kyi cha ni kun rdzob shes pa yin no/ /

A sūtra declares: Monks, there are three foundations of mindfulness that āryas should cultivate, and having cultivated them, āryas should teach them to their followers. What are those three? Monks, since the Master has mental altruism and compassion, desires others’ purpose, desires to benefit others, and possesses great compassion, he teaches Dharma to śrāvakas, stating that this will benefit you, this will bring you bliss, this will cause you benefit and bliss. Śrāvakas should listen to it, direct their ears to it, place their minds in full knowledge upon it, and act to establish Dharmas that conform with it. And if they act in harmony with the teachings of the Master, the Tathāgata is not gladdened, nor does he experience mental satisfaction, but remains indifferent; for the Tathāgata enters equanimity through mindfulness and introspection. Āryas should cultivate it, and having cultivated it, then they should teach it to the assembly. This is the first foundation of mindfulness. So too, if the Master teaches Dharma, and if śrāvakas do not listen to that Dharma and do not act in harmony with the teachings of the Master, then the Tathāgata is not saddened, nor does he experience mental dissatisfaction, but he remains indifferent, without being tormented; nor does he possess impatience, spite, or discontent, for the Tathāgata enters equanimity through mindfulness and introspection. This is the second foundation of mindfulness. So too, [622] if one śrāvaka listens to it and acts in harmony with the teachings of the Master, and another does not listen to it and does not act in harmony with the teachings of the Master, the Tathāgata is neither gladdened nor upset but enters equanimity through mindfulness and introspection. This is the third foundation of mindfulness.[1814] This passage lists three types of followers: (1) those who listen with respect, (2) those who do not listen with respect, and (3) those who engage in both. These three are states of mindfulness (smṛti) and introspection (prajñā) or wisdom. The central factor of wisdom here is conventional knowledge.

'o na nyan thos nyon mongs pa spangs pa rnams la'ang 'khor gus par nyan mi nyan dang gnyis ka la chags sdang mi 'byung ba yod pa'i phyir sangs rgyas kyis ma 'dres par ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/ nyan thos kyi ni chags sdang gi bag chags ma spangs la sangs rgyas kyis spangs pa'i phyir ro/ / de la bag chags ni rgyal po'i sras dang gang spel ni nyan thos la sngon nyon mongs pa spyad pa'i mthus lus ngag gi g.yo ba 'gyur ba'i rgyu nus pa'i khyad par sems la yod pa la 'dod cing*/ btsun pa go cha mtha' yas ni/ lung du ma bstan pa'i sems kyi khyad par yin no zhes zer bas nyan thos la chags sdang dngos med kyang lung du ma bstan pa'i sems kyi khyad par yod la/ ston pa ni dran pa dang shes bzhin gyi bdag nyid dge ba yin pa'i phyir ro mnyam du bsam pa'o/ / slob dpon ni nyan thos dag ni gus par nyan pa dang mi nyan pa dang gnyis ka la yid bde ba dang mi bde ba dang gnyis kar 'gyur ba kho na yin pa'i phyir 'di ni sangs rgyas kho na'i chos su bstan pa'am/ yang na chags sdang gnyis ni nyan thos la'ang med mod kyi 'on kyang nyan thos rnams ni sangs rgyas kyi phyir rab tu byung bas de'i slob ma yin pas nyan thos kyi yon tan ni sangs rgyas la brten nas thob pa'i phyir ma 'dres par mi bzhag la sangs rgyas kyi ni de lta ma yin pa'i phyir ma 'dres par bzhag go zhes 'chad do/ /

Question: Because śrāvakas who have abandoned affliction do not have attachment or aversion for their retinue who listen with respect, do not listen with respect, or who engage in both, why is that an unmixed quality of a buddha [alone]? Reply: Śrāvakas do not abandon imprints of attachment and aversion, but a buddha does abandon them. Regarding imprints, Jinaputra [Yaśomitra] and Pūrṇavardhana assert that śrāvakas possess a special mind with the causal potency to move the body and speech due to the force of their previous engagement in afflictions. Bhadanta Anantavarma says: It is a special neutral mind.[1815] Reply: Therefore I think that though attachment and aversion do not manifest in śrāvakas, still they exist within a special neutral mind, while the Master has a virtuous state of mindfulness and introspection. Vasubandhu explains that listening with respect, without respect, and with both attitudes induces mental satisfaction, mental dissatisfaction, and both in śrāvakas. Thus it is taught to be a quality of the Buddha alone. Or again, indeed, śrāvakas have neither attachment nor aversion, but they do not have unmixed qualities, because śrāvakas take ordination due to the Buddha, they are students of the Buddha, and the qualities of śrāvakas are obtained in dependence on the Buddha. But a buddha has unique qualities because he is not like that.[1816]
bzhi pa thugs rje chen po bshad pa la
Great compassion
thugs rje chen po kun rdzob blo/ / tshogs dang rnam pa spyod yul dang/ / mnyam pa'i phyir dang ches che'i phyir/ / tha dad bya ba rnam pa brgyad/ / 33
Great compassion is conventional knowledge. It has the collection, aspect, object field, and equality and is greater than the great. The two are differentiated in eight ways. (7:33)

The great compassion (mahākṛpa) of the Buddha Bhagavan is the intrinsic state of conventional knowledge (saṃvṛtidhī), since it observes all sentient beings who possess the three types of suffering and examines three times during the day and three times during the night who in the world is progressing, who is declining, whose time has come to be tamed, and so on. {If that were not so, it could not be established as possessing the aspect of suffering through focusing on the three realms.} Moreover, its essential nature is nondelusion. Question: Why is great compassion called “great”?

bsod nams dang ye shes kyi tshogs chen pos yang dag par 'grub pa'i phyir dang*/ rnam pa sdug bsngal gsum la rtog pa'i rnam pa can yin pa'i phyir dang*/ spyod yul khams gsum gyi sems can thams cad la dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ khams gsum gyi sems can thams cad la 'du byed kyi sdug bsngal can du dran par mnyam pa nyid du 'jug pa'i phyir dang*/ shes rab kyi ngo bo yin pas shin tu rno ba'i phyir de bas ches che ba gzhan med pas ches che ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na snying rje dang thugs rje chen po gnyis la khyad par ci yod ce na/

Reply: Because it is established by a great collection (saṃbhāra) of merit and transcendent wisdom; it possesses the aspect (ākāra) of investigation into the three types of suffering; it focuses on its object field (gocara) [623] — all sentient beings of the three realms; it engages all sentient beings of the three realms with equality (samatva), since it is mindful that they possess the suffering of contaminated formations; and it is extremely sharp, since it has the nature of wisdom. Therefore, since there is nothing greater than it, it is greater than the great. Question: What is the difference between compassion and great compassion?

ngo bo nyid la sogs pa tha dad du bya ba ste{ ngo bo dmigs rnam sa dang rgyud/ / thob dang skyob pa 'dra mi 'dra zhes pa'i} khyad par rnam pa brgyad yod de/ de la snying rje ni zhe sdang med pa'i ngo bo nyid dang*/ sdug bsngal gyi sdug bsngal gyi rnam pa can dang*/ 'dod pa'i khams kyi sems can kho na la dmigs pa dang*/ mi lcogs med dang bsam gtan khyad par can yang yin mod kyi/ de gnyis ni bsam gtan dang por bsdus te bsam gtan dang po la sogs pas bzhi dang*/ nyan rang dang so so'i skye bo'i rgyud la yod pa dang*/ 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral bas thob pa dang*/ nyan thos la sogs pas ni snying rje ba 'ba' zhig tu zad kyi 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal las yongs su mi skyob pa dang*/ sdug bsngal gyi sdug bsngal can kho na la snying rje skye bas sems can thams cad la mi 'dra bar snying rje ba yin no/ / thugs rje chen po ni gti mug med pa'i ngo bo nyid dang*/ sdug bsngal gsum gyi rnam pa can dang*/ khams gsum gyi sems can thams cad la dmigs pa dang*/ ting nge 'dzin las su rung ba nyid kyis de kho nas de bskyed par nus pa'i phyir bsam gtan bzhi pa'i sa pa kho na dang*/ sangs rgyas kyi rgyud la yod pa dang*/ srid rtse las 'dod chags dang bral bas thob pa dang*/ sems can thams cad la thugs rje mdzad pa na 'khor ba'i 'jigs pa chen po las yongs su skyob pa dang*/ sdug bsngal can dang de ma yin pa'i sems can thams cad la 'dra bar thugs brtse ba yin no/ /
gsum pa mnyam mi mnyam gyis 'jug bsdu ba ni
Similarities and differences between buddhas
sangs rgyas thams cad rnam pa thams cad kyis mnyam pa yin nam zhe na/
Question: Are all buddhas equal in all aspects?
sangs rgyas thams cad tshogs dang ni/ / chos sku 'gro ba'i don spyod pas/ / mnyam pa nyid de sku tshe dang / / rigs dang sku bong tshod kyis min/ / 34
All buddhas are equal in their collections, Dharma body, and actions for the purpose of reincarnating beings. They are not equal in lifespan, caste, or size. (7:34)

sangs rgyas thams cad ni rgyu sngon gyi bsod nams dang ye shes kyi tshogs rdzogs pas yang dag par 'grub pa dang*/ 'bras bu zag med kyi chos kyi rgyun gyi tshogs sam sems gnas gyur pa chos kyi sku 'grub pa dang*/ 'phrin las 'gro ba'i mtho ris dang byang grol gyi don sgrub par spyod pa'i rgyu thugs rje chen po thob pa gsum gyis ni mnyam pa nyid de/ sku tshe dang rigs dang gdung dang sku'i bongs tshod kyis ni mnyam pa min te/ / skye dgu rnams kyi tshe ring ba dang thung ba dang*/ 'jig rten na rgyal rigs dang bram ze gang bkur ba dang*/ gdung 'od srung dang go'u ta ma la sogs pa gang bkur ba dang*/ 'jig rten pa lus bongs tshod che ba dang chung ba'i tshe dus ji lta ba bzhin du sangs rgyas rnams kyang sku tshe dang rigs dang gdung dang sku'i bongs tshod rnams de dag dang mthun par sngon pas khyad par yod pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: All buddhas are equal (samatā) in three factors that obtain great compassion: (1) the cause properly establishing great compassion through having previously completed the collection of merit and pristine wisdom, (2) the resultant Dharma body (dharmakāya) that is the transformed collection or mind within the stream of uncontaminated phenomena, and (3) the enlightened activity that is the cause of actions securing the purpose of reincarnating beings, such as higher rebirth and enlightenment. They are not equal in (1) lifespan (āyur), (2) caste (jāti), (3) relics, and (4) body size (pramāṇa). (1) Lifespan varies according to the specific period in which beings exist, (2) reverence varies in the world for kṣatriyas or brahmans, (3) reverence varies for the relics of Kāśyapa or Gautama and so on, and (4) the size of worldly beings varies from small to large, and buddhas possess the lifespan, caste, relics, and body size specific to their current situation. [624]

'dir smras pa/ rgyu dang 'bras bu phan 'dogs pa/ / gsum po re re'ang bzhi bzhi ste/ / tshogs kun yun ring bar chad med/ / gus byas goms pa bzhi ni rgyu/ / ye shes dang ni spangs pa dang*/ / mthu dang gzugs sku phun tshogs pa/ / rnam bzhi 'bras bu de dag kyang*/ / rnam pa zhi bzhir shes bya ste/ / ma bstan mkhyen dang thams cad mkhyen/ / rnam kun ma 'bad mkhyen pa bzhi/ / ye shes phun tshogs nyon mongs kun/ / gtan du spangs dang bag chags bcas/ / ting 'dzin snyoms 'jug sgrib kun spangs/ / rnam bzhi spangs pa phun tshogs so/ / phyi'i yul sprul bsgyur byin rlabs pa/ / yul la mnga' brnyes stong byin rlob/ / tshe la'o thogs bcas thogs med dang*/ / ring la myur gshegs chung ngur ni/ / mang 'jug spyod lam mnga' brnyed pa'o/ / ya mtshan nar ma sna tshogs pa/ / ston la mnga' brnyes rnam pa bzhi/ / rgyal ba'i mthu ni phun tshogs pa'o/ / mtshan dang dpe byad stobs dang ni/ / sku gdung ring bsrel rdo rje ltar/ / sra ba gang yin sangs rgyas kyi/ / gzugs sku phun tshogs rnam bzhi'o/ / dmyal ba yi dwags dud 'gro dang*/ / 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal dag las ni/ / gtan du thar mdzad rnam pa bzhi/ / phan 'dogs pa de rnam gcig tu/ / bde 'gro dang ni theg gsum 'god/ / bzhi yin 'gro ba'i bla ma de'i/ / yon tan rgya mtsho dpag med phyir/ / rab tu dbye na mtha' yas mod/ / che ba'i bdag nyid mdor bsdus pa'o/ / gang dag skyob pa kun mkhyen gyi/ / yon tan dam pa gang shes nas/ / rgyal dang de yi dam chos dang*/ / de yi rjes 'jug dge 'dun la/ / rab dad de dag mkhas pa yin zhes bya'o/ /

Here it is said: The three equal factors are (1) cause, (2) result, and (3) benefit, and each has four types. Cause has four: (1.1) collecting all, (1.2) collecting for a long time, (1.3) collecting without obstruction, and (1.4) cultivating respect. Result has four: (2.1) excellent transcendent wisdom, (2.2) excellent abandonment, (2.3) excellent might, and (2.4) excellent form body. Those four have four types each. Excellent transcendent wisdom has four types: (2.1.1) comprehending without instruction, (2.1.2) comprehending all, (2.1.3) comprehending every aspect, and (2.1.4) comprehending without exertion. Excellent abandonment has four types: (2.2.1) abandoning all afflictions (2.2.2) complete abandonment, (2.2.3) abandoning imprints, and (2.2.4) abandoning all obscurations to concentration and meditative attainment. Excellent might of the conqueror has four types: (2.3.1) empowering the transformation of external objects and empowering the attainment of objects, (2.3.2) obstructing and not obstructing life, (2.3.3) traveling quickly to distant states and entering many minute states, and (2.3.4) attaining various wonderful and ordinary states. The excellent form body of the Buddha has four types (2.4.1) the marks, (2.4.2) the signs, (2.4.3) the powers, and (2.4.4) physical relics hard like a vajra. There are four types [of benefit]: absolutely freeing (3.1) hell beings, (3.2) ghosts, (3.3) animals, and (3.4) others from the suffering of saṃsāra. Alternately the fourfold benefits are: establishing others (3.1) in higher realms and (3.2–4) in the three vehicles. Indeed, their qualities have infinite classifications because the qualities of the gurus of reincarnating beings are like an infinite ocean. In brief, they are great beings. Whoever knows the pure qualities of these omniscient protectors, and generates faith in the Conqueror, his Dharma, and the Saṅgha who follow him, is learned.

de lta bu'i yon tan dang ldan pa'i sangs rgyas dang de'i chos la dad pa tsam gyis kyang rnam smin ma nges pa'i sdig pa thams cad zil gyis mnan nas lam gyi rten mtho ris lha mi'i legs pa du ma brgyud de bgrod par bya ba'i mchog mya ngan las 'da' bar 'gyur te/ lung sman gyi gzhi las/ gang dag rgyal ba rnam 'dren la/ / bya ba chung ngu byed 'gyur ba'ang*/ / de dag mtho ris sna tshogs dag /bgod nas bdud rtsi'i go 'phang thob ces pa dang*/ 'grel pa las kyang*/ de nyid kyi phyir de bzhin gshegs pa rnams ni bsod nams kyi zhing bla na med pa zhes bya ste/ nges par 'byin pas 'bras bu med pa ma yin pa dang*/ de yang gnas skabs mtho ris su 'byin pas yid du 'ong ba dang*/ lan mang du 'byin pas mchog tu gyur pa dang*/ mthong chos la sogs pa la myong bas myur ba dang*/ mthar myang 'das 'thob pas mtha' bzang ba'i phyir ro zhes bshad do/ /

Those who merely generate faith in the Buddha, who possesses such qualities, and his Dharma [at the very least] overcome all immorality that may produce karmic maturation. [They may even] progress to excellent lineages of higher rebirth such as humans and gods and attain supreme nirvāṇa. The Chapter on Medicine states: Whoever engages in a minor deed relative to the conquerors who guide will establish various higher rebirths and then obtain the abode of nectar.[1817] Also, the Autocommentary explains: Therefore tathāgatas are called “peerless fields of merit.”[1818] It is not the case that definite release produces no result, since at times it produces higher rebirth. Having produced pleasant existence many times, one attains superior states, and having attained experience in this life, one reaches the pure limit through seeing nirvāṇa.[1819]

33. Shared Qualities of a Buddha
['di] la'ang gnyis las
THIS HAS TWO HEADINGS: overview and elaboration.

Overview
chos gzhan slob dang thun mong yin/ / kha cig so so'i skye bo dang / / nyon mongs med dang smon nas shes/ / so so yang dag rig mngon sogs/ / 35
Other qualities are common to learners. Some say they are common to ordinary beings. Absence of conflict, knowledge through prayer, analytical knowledges, higher perceptions, and so on. (7:35)

ma 'dres pa bco brgyad ma gtogs pa sangs rgyas kyi yon tan gyi chos gzhan ni slob ma nyan thos dang des mtshon nas rang rgyal dang yang thun mong ba yin la/ yon tan gyi chos kha cig ni so so'i skye bo dang yang thun mong ba yin no/ / chos de dag kyang gang zhe na/ nyon mongs pa med pa dang*/ smon nas shes pa dang*/ so so yang dag par rig pa bzhi dang*/ mngon shes drug dang*/ sogs pas gzung ba bsam gtan bzhi dang*/ gzugs med bzhi dang*/ tshad med bzhi dang*/ rnam thar brgyad dang*/ zil gyis gnon pa'i skye mched brgyad dang*/ zad par gyi skye mched bcu dang*/ ting nge 'dzin gsum la sogs pa'o/ / de la nyon mongs pa med pa nas so so yang dag par rigs bzhi'i bar dang*/ zag zad kyi mngon shes dang*/ 'gog pa'i rnam thar dang*/ rnam par thar pa'i sgo gsum ni 'phags pa kho na dang thun mong ba dang*/ lhag ma rnams ni so so skye bo dang yang thun mong ba yin no/ /

Beyond the eighteen unmixed qualities there are other qualities (dharma) of a buddha that are common to learner (śiṣya) śrāvakas, those represented by them, [625] as well as pratyekabuddhas. Some say: There are qualities that are also common to ordinary beings (pṛthagjana). Question: What qualities are being discussed? Reply: Absence of conflict (araṇā), knowledge through prayer (praṇidhijñāna), the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), the six higher perceptions, and so on, including the four absorptions, the four formless states, the four immeasurables, the eight liberations, the eight bases of subjugation, the ten bases of totality (kṛtsnāyatana), the three concentrations, and so on. From the absence of conflict up to the four analytical knowledges, as well as the higher perception of the elimination of contaminants, liberation of cessation, and the three doors of liberation are common to āryas alone. The remainder are common to ordinary beings.

ELABORATION
['di] la gnyis las 'phags pa kho na dang thun mong ba nyon mongs pa med pa la sogs pa bshad pa
This has two headings: qualities of āryas alone, such as the absence of conflict, and the higher perceptions mostly shared with ordinary beings.
['phags pa kho na]
Qualities of āryas alone
['di] la bzhi las
This has four headings: absence of conflict, knowledge through prayer, the four analytical knowledges, and the analytical knowledge of prowess.
dang po nyon mongs pa med pa ni
ABSENCE OF CONFLICT
nyon mongs med pa kun rdzob shes/ / bsam gtan mtha' na mi g.yo'i chos/ / mis skyes nyon mongs 'dod gtogs pa/ / ma skyes gzhir bcas spyod yul can/ / 36

Absence of conflict is conventional knowledge. Its level is the limit of absorption, an immutable arhat, generated by humans, possessing an object field that belongs to the desire realm, unarisen, possessing a basis. (7:36)

dgra bcom pa dag sems can rnams kyi sdug bsngal ni nyon mongs las byung ba dang rang nyid kyang yon gnas kyi khyad par du rig nas pha rol po'i nyon mongs pa spang bar 'dod nas bdag mthong ba dang bdag la dmigs nas gzhan dag la nyon mongs pa chags sdang dang nga rgyal dang bag med pa skye bar ma gyur cig snyam du mnyam par bzhag nas/{ lam 'dis su yang nyon mongs par mi byed pas na nyon mongs pa med pa'i/ 'di ni gzhan gyi sems bsrung ba'i thabs mkhas kyi khyad par ro/} de las langs na'ang de dang rjes su mthun par de lta bu'i shes pa skyed par byed pa ste de ni kun rdzob shes pa'i bdag nyid yin no/{ gzhan rgyud kyi sgom spang gi nyon mongs ma 'ongs pa kho na'i yul can yin pa'i phyir te zag med ni de lta bu med do/} sa ni lam sla ba rnams kyi mchog yin pas bsam gtan rnams kyi ya mtha' bzhi pa kho na na yod la/ gang zag ni dgra bcom pa mi g.yo ba'i chos can yin gyi nyams pa'i chos can la sogs pa dgra bcom gzhan gyi ni ma yin te/ de dag la nyams pa srid pas rang gi rgyud kyi'ang res 'ga' nyon mongs spang bar mi nus{ na gzhan gyis lta ci smros} pa'i phyir ro/ / lus kyi rten ni gling gsum gyi mi kho nas skyed par byed pa yin te/{ grogs nyon mongs mang ba dang de na/} blo gsal ba'i phyir ro/ / 'di'i dmigs pa ni pha rol chags sdang can dag la nyon mongs skye bar ma gyur cig ces sgom pa'i phyir nyon mongs pa 'dod par gtogs pa dang ma skyes pa ma 'ongs pa gzhir bcas 'dod chags la sogs pa sgom spang rnams kyi spyod yul can yin te/ khams gong ma pa dag 'phags pa la dmigs nas nyon mongs pa skye ba shas chung ba'i phyir dang*/ sngar skyes pa rnams spang bar mi nus pa'i phyir dang*/ mthong spang gzhi med pa brtags pa la dmigs pa kun 'gro rnams ni rang gis thams cad la dmigs pas gzhan rgyud la dmigs pa'ang yod pas spang bar mi nus pa'i phyir dang*/ sgom spang ni bden pa dang po gnyis la dmigs pas gzhi dang bcas pa spang bar nus pa'i phyir ro/ /
gnyis pa smon nas shes pa ni
KNOWLEDGE THROUGH PRAYER
smon nas shes pa'ang de bzhin no/ de yi dmigs pa thams cad do/ /
Also knowledge through prayer is similar; however, its focal object is all phenomena. (7:37ab)

ji ltar nyon mongs pa med pa'i ngo bo kun rdzob shes pa dang sa bsam gtan bzhi pa dang gang zag mi g.yo ba'i chos can dang rten gling gsum gyi mi'i rten can yin pa de bzhin du smon nas shes pa'i ngo bo la sogs pa'ang yin no/ / 'on kyang smon nas shes pa de'i dmigs pa ni nyon mongs pa gzhi dang bcas pa kho na ma yin gyi gzugs la sogs pa chos thams cad do/ / de la smon nas shes pa ni 'di dang 'di shes par bya'o snyam du smon pa sngar btang nas rab mtha' bzhi pa la mnyam par bzhag nas de'i yul du ji tsam gyur pa shes pa'i/ de yang bye brag tu smra ba na re gzugs med pa ni mngon sum du mi shes te/ 'di ni bsam gtan bzhi pa'i sa pa yin pas gong ma gzugs med pa yul ma yin pa'i phyir te/ 'di ni mngon shes dang 'dra ba yin la de ni rang dang 'og sa'i yul can yin zhes 'chad par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / 'on kyang lus dang sems dman zhing zhi ba'i rgyu mthun pa las ni gzugs med nas skyes so zhes bya ba dang*/ snyoms 'jug gi spyod pa dang ldan pa las gzugs med skyes so zhes bya ba dang*/ gzugs med kyi ting nge 'dzin thob lam nyams pa dang ldan pas gzugs med du skye bar 'gyur ro zhes bya bar shes te zhing pa rnams kyis 'bru las zhing dang zhing las 'bru dpog pa bzhin no zhes zer ro/ /

Just as absence of conflict is by nature conventional knowledge, its level is the fourth absorption, the person establishing it is the immutable arhat, and its basis is a human of the three continents, so also knowledge through prayer (praṇidhijñāna) is similar in having that nature and so on. However, the focal object (ālambana) of knowledge through prayer is not beings possessing a basis of affliction alone, but all phenomena such as form and so on. Knowledge through prayer arises through first making the prayer “May I come to know this specific object,” and knowledge of that object fully arises based on equipoise at the limit of the fourth absorption. Vaibhāṣikas explain: It does not directly know formless states; it does not take formless states as its object, since its level is the fourth absorption and it is similar to higher perception. As the Abhidharmakośa notes, “They possess objects of its level and lower level” (7:44a). But like farmers who infer the grain from the crop and the crop from the grain, [it knows formless states through inference]: it knows “He is reborn from the formless realm since his body and mind are inferior and he has peace that is compatible with its cause,” “He is reborn in the formless realm since he possesses the practice of meditative attainment,” and “He is reborn in the formless realm since he obtained formless concentration and the path degenerated.”

gzhan dag gi gzhung lugs ltar na ni sangs rgyas rnams kyi mngon sum gyi yul du ma gyur pa ni 'ga' yang med pas gzugs med pa'ang mngon sum du mkhyen par 'dod do/ / mngon par rtogs pa'i rgyan las ni/ nyan thos nyon mongs med pa'i lta/ / mi yi nyon mongs yongs spong nyid/ / grong sogs su de'i nyon mongs rnams/ / rgyun gcad rgyal ba'i nyon mongs med ces nyan rang gi nyon mongs pa med pa'i ting nge 'dzin ni bdag la dmigs nas mi 'ga' zhig gi rgyud la nyon mongs pa skyes par gyur na mi rung ngo zhes mi nyon mongs skye ba yongs su spong ba'i thabs la 'bad pa yin pas nyi 'tshe ba dang re zhig pa dang*/ sangs rgyas kyi nyon mongs pa med pa'i ting nge 'dzin ni grong la sogs par sems can nyon mongs pa can thams cad kyi nyon mongs pa'i sa bon rtsa ba nas 'byin par bzhed pas khyab pa dang gtan du ba yin par bshad la/ smon nas shes pa'ang nyan thos la sogs pa rnams 'bad pa dang bcas pa dang*/ mtshan mar 'dzin pa dang*/ shes sgrib dang bag chags ma spangs pas thogs pa dang bcas pa dang*/ lhag med du 'jug pas res 'ga' ba dang*/ shes sgrib ma spangs pas 'dri ba thams cad kyi lan mi ldon pa yin la/ sangs rgyas kyi ni mtshan ma med par rang gi ngang gis 'jug pas 'bad pa med pa dang*/ dngos po la mngon par ma zhen pas gzugs sogs la chags pa dang bral ba dang*/ sgrib gnyis bag chags dang bcas pa spangs pas shes bya thams cad la thogs pa med pa dang*/ 'khor ba ji srid par gnas pas rtag tu gnas pa dang*/ yang dag pa'i so so rigs bzhi brnyes pas 'dri ba kun gyi lan ldon pa yin te/ de nyid las/ sangs rgyas smon nas mkhyen pa ni/ / lhun gyis grub dang chags spangs dang*/ / thogs pa med dang rtag gnas dang*/ 'dri ba kun lan 'debs par bzhed ces bshad do/ /

Other textual systems assert that since there is nothing whatseover that is not an object of the direct perception of buddhas, also the formless realm is directly perceived. The Ornament of Realization states: A śrāvaka’s view of the absence of conflict fully eliminates the conflict in a human. A conqueror’s absence of conflict severs the continuance of conflict in villages and so on.[1820] Thus the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha concentration viewing the absence of conflict focuses on the self and strives to fully abandon the arising of human conflict, reflecting, “Conflict should not arise in the mindstreams of these humans.” Therefore it is brief and nonpervasive. A buddha’s concentration viewing the absence of conflict definitely releases all sentient beings such as villagers from the root seeds of all affliction. Therefore it is said to be pervasive and stable. Also the knowledge through prayer of śrāvakas and so on is associated with exertion, apprehending signs, and possessing obstruction since it does not abandon knowledge obscurations and imprints; it exists intermittently since it is engaged by those without remainder; and it cannot respond to all questions since it does not abandon knowledge obscurations. That of a buddha is not associated with exertion since it arises naturally without apprehending signs; it is free from attachment to form and so on since it does not crave things; it is unobstructed to all objects of knowledge since it abandons both obscurations [627] along with their imprints; it exists eternally since it abides for as long as saṃsāra exists; and it responds to all questions since it attains the four analytical knowledges. The Ornament of Realization states: A buddha’s knowledge through prayer is spontaneous, abandons attachment, lacks obstruction, abides eternally, and responds to all questions.[1821]
gsum pa so so yang dag rigs bzhi ni
THE FOUR ANALYTICAL KNOWLEDGES
de bzhin chos don nges tshig dang / / spobs pa so so yang dag rig / 37
So too, the analytical knowledge of phenomena, meaning, language, and prowess. (7:37cd)

ji ltar nyon mongs pa med pa'i ting nge 'dzin gang zag mi g.yo ba'i chos can ga yin pa dang gling gsum gyi mis skyed pa de bzhin du chos dang don dang nges pa'i tshig dang spobs pa so so yang dag par rig pa dag kyang de dang 'dra'o/ /

Just as concentration viewing the absence of conflict belongs to an immutable arhat and is generated by humans of the three continents, so too the four types of analytical knowledge (saṃvida) of phenomena, meaning (artha), language (nirukta), and prowess (pratibhāna) also are like this.
gsum ni go rims bzhin ming dang / / don dang ngag la thogs med shes/ bzhi pa rigs pa thags thogs med/ / mngon brjod lam la dbang nyid la/ / 38
Three are, respectively, the unobstructed knowledge of names, objects, and speech. The fourth is appropriate, unimpeded expression, and mastery of the path. (7:38)

de dag gi dmigs pa dang sa dang ngo bo la ni khyad par yod de/ de dag las dang po gsum ni go rim bzhin du ming dang don dang ngag rnams la gzhan gyis bzlog par mi nus pas thogs pa med par shes pa yin te/ de la chos so so yang dag par rig pa ni sgrub pa'i chos 'phags lam brgyad dang*/ 'bras bu'i chos myang 'das rig pa ma yin gyi chos rnams kyi ming tshig yi ge'i tshogs rig pa ste don rnams kyi rjod byed yin pa'i phyir na bstan pa'i chos so/ / don so so yang dag par rig pa ni chos rnams kyi rang gi mtshan nyid dam mya ngan las 'das pa rig pa ste/ brjod par bya ba'i don ni don gyi mchog yin pa'i phyir ro/ / nges pa'i tshig so so yang dag par rig pa ni chos rnams kyis bshad pa'i rgyu mtshan can gyi ngag rig pa ste/ don gyi rgyu mtshan can gyi tshig yin pas nges pa'i tshig go /

But they are different in their focal object, level, and nature. The first three are, respectively, unobstructed (avivartya) knowledge of names (nāma), objects (artha), and speech (vag), since they cannot be refuted by others. (1) The analytical knowledge of phenomena does not recognize the eightfold noble path as a phenomenon to be established nor nirvāṇa as a phenomenon to be manifested, but it recognizes collections of nouns, predicated phrases, and letters as revelatory phenomena because they are factors expressing meaning. (2) The analytical knowledge of meaning recognizes the specific characteristics of phenomena or nirvāṇa because they constitute [mundane] meaning that is expressed or the supreme meaning. (3) The analytical knowledge of language recognizes purposive speech that informs through the phenomena [of nouns and so on], and language comprised of meaningful words.
bzhi pa spobs pa so so yang dag par rig pa ni
THE ANALYTICAL KNOWLEDGE OF PROWESS

(4) The fourth, the analytical knowledge of prowess, is that which is appropriate (yukta) in its relationship to the meaning whether in contradistinction or in its connection with the meaning; that is unobstructed knowledge in terms of the unimpeded expression (muktābhilāpa) of the meaning and the unobstructed knowledge of the mastery of the path (mārgavaśitva) since it is attentive, forgetting neither calm abiding nor insight. The first is skill in language, and the second is skill in attentiveness. It is the analytical knowledge of prowess because it is prowess as well as analytical knowledge. Again, prowess is said to be knowledge and liberation, and because it is the knowledge of that, it is the analytical knowledge of prowess. {Jinaputra states that all four focus on name and meaning in equipoise and post-equipoise, but speech exists in post-equipoise alone.}
de yi dmigs pa ngag dang lam/ / shes pa dgu'o sa thams cad/ / yang dag don rig bcu 'am drug / de ni kun na gzhan kun rdzob/ / 39
The focal object is speech and the path. It is nine knowledges on all levels. The analytical knowledge of meaning is ten or six. It exists on all levels, but others are conventional. (7:39)

spobs pa so so yang dag par rig pa de'i dmigs pa ni ngag dang lam yin te/ ngag dang mngon par brjod pa la dbang ba ni ngag la dmigs pa yin la lam la dbang ba ni lam la dmigs pa'o/ / {lam yang zag bcas zag med gang rung yin no de lta min na/ sa thams cad par mi 'gyur ro zhes 'dod do } de'i ngo bo ni shes pa dgu yin te/{ ngag ni bden pa dang po gnyis yin pas/} ngag la dmigs pa ni kun rdzob dang sdug bsngal kun 'byung chos shes rjes shes zad mi skye shes pa'i{ shes pa bdun gyi} rang bzhin yin zhing*/ lam la dmigs pa ni lam dang chos shes rjes shes zad mi skye shes pa dang pha rol sems shes kyi { shes pa drug gi} rang bzhin yin la/ 'dus ma byas la mi dmigs pas 'gog shes ma gtogs pa'i phyir ro/ /

The focal object of the analytical knowledge of prowess is speech (vāc) and the path (mārga) because mastery over speech and expression focuses on speech, and mastery over the path focuses on the path. {Also the path is either contaminated or uncontaminated; if that were not so, it would not pervade all levels.} By nature it is nine knowledges (jñāna) because that focusing on speech {constituting the first two truths} has the nature {of seven knowledges}: (1) conventional knowledge, (2) knowledge of suffering, (3) knowledge of origin, (4) Dharma knowledge, (5) subsequent knowledge, (6) knowledge of elimination, and (7) knowledge of nonarising. That focusing on the path has the nature of {six knowledges} [628] — (1) knowledge of the path, (2) Dharma knowledge, (3) subsequent knowledge, (4) knowledge of elimination, (5) knowledge of nonarising, and (6) knowledge of others’ minds; but knowledge of cessation is excluded since it does not focus on unconditioned states.

gal te ngag dang lam la dmigs pa'i phyir sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung shes par ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/ ngag de nyid zag bcas yin pa'i phyir sdug bsngal yin la/ phyi ma bskyed pa'i phyir kun 'byung yang yin pas de shes pa na de dag shes par gzhag go /sa ni 'dod pa nas srid rtse'i bar thams cad na ci rigs par yod de/ ngag dang lam gang yang rung ba la dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Question: Because [the analytical knowledge of prowess] focuses on speech and the path, how is it knowledge of suffering and origin? Reply: Speech is [the truth of] suffering because it is contaminated. It is also [the truth of] origin when it generates the [the truth of suffering]. Since [the analytical knowledge of prowess] knows [such speech], it is posited as knowledge of [suffering and origin]. It exists on all levels, from the desire realm to the summit of existence, because it focuses on any speech and path.
don so so yang dag par rig pa ni

gal te don chos thams cad rig pa la 'dod na ni shes pa bcu'i dmigs par mi 'gyur ba'i chos gang yang med pas shes pa bcu yin pa'am/ 'on te myang 'das rig pa la 'dod na 'gog pa shes pa ni sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung dang lam dang sems shes pa bzhi las gzhan pa drug gi rang bzhin yin pa'i phyir ro/ / don so so yang dag par rig pa de ni sa kun na yod la/ de dag las gzhan chos dang nges pa'i tshig so so yang dag par rig pa gnyis ni kun rdzob shes pa'i rang bzhin yin te/ rim pa ltar ming gi tshogs la sogs pa bstan pa'i chos dang ngag la dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ /

If it is asserted that the analytical knowledge of meaning (arthasaṃvit) recognizes all meaning, then it would consist of ten knowledges, since there are no phenomena that are not focal objects of the ten knowledges. Or, if it recognizes nirvāṇa, then it would have the nature of six, since the knowledge of cessation excludes four: knowledge of suffering, origin, path, and others’ minds. The analytical knowledge of meaning exists on all levels, but others — both the analytical knowledge of phenomena and the analytical knowledge of language — have the nature of conventional knowledge because they focus on what is instructive, such as the collections of nouns and speech, respectively.
chos rig 'dod dang bsam gtan na/ / ngag ni 'dod dang dang po na/ / ma tshang bar ni de thob med/ / drug po de dag rab mtha' bas/ / 40

The knowledge of phenomena, desire, and the absorptions. Speech, in the desire realm and the first absorption. None are obtained if any one is incomplete. These six are obtained by the supreme limit. (7:40)

de yang chos so so yang dag par rig pa ni sa 'dod pa dang bsam gtan bzhi po dag { ste sa lnga na yod de/} de yan chad na ni rjod byed ming tshig yi ge'i tshogs med pa'i phyir ro/ / dag ste nges pa'i tshig so so yang dag par rig pa ni 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang po kho na na yod de/ mdo las/ brtags shing dpyad nas tshig tu smra'o zhes 'byung bas ngag ni rtog pas kun nas bslang ba'i bdag nyid yin na bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad na rtog pa med pa'i phyir ro/ /

The analytical knowledge of phenomena exists {on five levels:} (1) the desire realm and (2–5) the four absorptions. But on levels above that, the collection of nouns, predicated phrases, and letters does not exist. Speech that is associated with the analytical knowledge of language exists in the desire realm and first absorption alone. As a sūtra states: One expresses words through investigation and analysis.[1822] If speech is a state motivated by investigation, then it cannot exist on the second absorption and above, for those levels lack investigation.

so so yang dag par rig pa de dag gcig thob na thams cad 'thob pas gang rung gcig ma tshang bar ni de dag 'thob pa med {lam gcig gi 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir ro } de/ 'di dag gi rgyu sngon gyi sbyor ba ni kha cig go rim bzhin du rtsis dang*/ sangs rgyas kyi bka' dang*/ sgra rig pa dang*/ gtan tshig rig pa la mkhas par byas pas 'thob par 'dod la/ bye brag tu smra ba rnams ni thams cad kyi sbyor ba sangs rgyas kyi bka' kho na'i rnam grangs ngo bo nges tshig dbye ba la mkhas par byas pas 'di dag 'thob par 'dod do/ / {rnam bshad rig pa'i 'brel ba las kyang*/ rnam grangs kyis ni chos so so yang dag par rig pa'i nye rgyu byas pa yin no/ / de bzhin du sbyar te mtshan nyid kyis ni don so so yang dag par rig pa yin/ nges pa'i tshig gis ni nges pa'i tshig so so yang dag par rig pa yin/ rab tu dbye bas ni spobs pa so so yang dag par rig pa yin no zhes 'byung ba dang mthun no } go rim yang tshig yi ge'i rjes su 'brangs nas/ don rtogs pas chos so sor rig nas don dang*/ don las ming gi rnam grangs shes pa 'byung bas nges pa'i tshig dang*/ de dag las ni rig grol gyi spobs pa thogs pa med par 'gyur ba'i phyir de ltar bstan to/ { 'di dag gi go rim ni tshig dang yi ge'i rjes su 'brangs nas don rtogs la/ don gyi gcig gnyis la sogs pa'i tshig bla dgas dang*/ de dag la thogs pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes gdags pa las so/ /}

These six — (1) absence of conflict, (2) knowledge from resolve, and (3–6) the four analytical knowledges — are obtained by the power of the fourth absorption that is the supreme limit (prāntakoṭika).
de ni rnam drug bsam gtan mtha'/ / de ni sa kun gyis mthun byas/ / 'phel pa'i rab tu phyin pa yin/ / sangs rgyas las gzhan sbyor las skyes/ / 41
It has six aspects. The limit of absorption conforms with the forward system on all levels. One completes supreme enhancement. Those other than buddhas arise from exertion. (7:41)

nyon mongs pa med pa dang smon nas shes pa dang so so yang dag rigs bzhi ste drug po de dag ni rab kyi mtha' pa bsam gtan bzhi pa'i stobs kyis 'thob la/ rab kyi mtha' pa zhes bya ba'i bsam gtan bzhi pa de ni nyon mongs pa med pa dang*/ smon nas shes pa dang*/ chos dang*/ don dang*/ spobs pa so so yang dag par rig pa gsum dang*/ rab kyi mtha' pa'i bsam gtan bzhi pa de nyid dang rnam pa drug gi bdag nyid yin la/ bsam gtan bzhi pa la la ni nyon mongs pa med pa dang*/ la la ni smon nas shes pa dang*/ la la ni so so yang dag par rig pa gsum dang*/ la la ni de dag ma gtogs pa rab kyi mtha' pa 'ba' zhig yin pa'i phyir ro/ / nges pa'i tshig so so yang dag par rig pa ni rtog dpyod kyis kun nas slong ba'i phyir 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang po'i sa pa yin no/ / 'o na drug po de dag rab mtha' pas zhes khyad par med par bshad ce na/ de ni rab kyi mtha' pa'i bsam gtan gyi stobs kyis 'thob pa'i phyir de skad bshad kyi bsam gtan bzhi pa'i sa pa ni ma yin no/ / de la rab kyi mtha' pa zhes bya ba ni bsam gtan gyi ya mtha' bsam gtan bzhi pa yin no/ / ji ltar zhe na/

The fourth absorption, called “the supreme limit,” consists of six aspects: (1) the absence of conflict, (2) knowledge through prayer, (3–5) the three analytical knowledges of phenomena, meaning, and prowess, and (6) the fourth absorption of the supreme limit. Some assert that the fourth absorption is the absence of conflict. Some assert that it is knowledge through prayer. Some assert that it is the three analytical knowledges. Some assert that it is the supreme limit alone excluding the rest. The analytical knowledge of language exists in the desire realm and the first absorption because it is motivated by investigation and analysis. Objection: It is not differentiated in this way, since the Abhidharmakośa explains, “These six are obtained by the supreme limit” (7:40d). Reply: This is explained because these are obtained by the power of the absorption of the supreme limit, but they do not belong to the level of the fourth absorption. It is called supreme limit since it is absorption existing at the upper limit of the fourth absorption. Question: In what way?

rab mtha' bsam gtan bzhi pa de ni 'dod pa'i sems las bsam gtan dang po la snyoms par 'jug pa nas ci yang med pa las srid rtse la snyoms par 'jug pa'i bar dang*/ yang srid rtse las langs nas ci yang med pa'i skye mched la snyoms par 'jug pa nas bsam gtan dang po las langs nas 'dod pa'i sems la gnas pa'i bar dang*/ de nas yang 'dod pa'i sems las bsam gtan dang po la snyoms par 'jug pa nas bsam gtan gsum pa las langs nas bsam gtan bzhi pa la snyoms par 'jug pa'i bar sa kun gyis lugs dang mthun pa dang mi mthun pa'i snyoms par 'jug pas mthun par byas pa'i phyir dang*/ bsgom pa chung ngu bsam gtan dang po las 'bring gnyis pa las chen po gsum pa la snyoms par 'jug pas gsum pa ni 'phel ba'i mchog tu gyur pas 'phel ba'i rab yin la/ rab de'i ya mtha' yin pas na bzhi pa ni 'phel ba'i rab tu phyin pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: The supreme limit of the fourth absorption conforms with the forward system, having entered meditative attainment in the forward and reverse systems on all levels. After first abiding in the desire realm, one enters meditative attainment from the first absorption to the peak of existence; then, having arisen from the peak of existence, one enters meditative attainment from nothingness to the first absorption and arises from that to abide in the desire realm; then, again, from abiding in the desire realm, one enters meditative attainment in the first absorption; and after arising from the third absorption, one enters the fourth absorption. “Supreme enhancement” covers the three stages of first entering meditative attainment on the lesser meditation of the first absorption, then the intermediate meditation of the second absorption, then the great meditation of the third absorption since it is superior enhancement. In the fourth stage one completes supreme enhancement (vṛddhikāṣṭhāgata) since one attains the upper limit of what is supreme.

nyon mongs pa med pa la sogs pa yon tan drug po de dag kyang sangs rgyas las gzhan pa'i gang zag gi rgyud la yod pa rnams ni sbyor ba 'bad rtsol las skyes pa yin gyi 'dod chags dang bral ba tsam gyis 'thob pa ni ma yin no/ /
sangs rgyas kyi ni chos thams cad kyi dbang phyug yin pa'i phyir yon tan thams cad mngon du 'gyur ba ni bzhed pa tsam las rag las pa yin gyi sbyor ba las byung ba ni cung zad kyang med do/ /

Those six qualities, such as the absence of conflict and so on, existing in the mindstreams of beings other than buddhas arise from exertion (prayogajā), and they are not obtained by mere freedom from attachment. Because the Buddha is the Lord of Dharma, all qualities are reliant on his mere wish to manifest them and do not occur from exertion [or preparation] in the least. [630]
gnyis pa phal cher byis pa dang thun mong ba la mngon par shes pa ni
The higher perceptions mostly shared with ordinary beings
rdzu 'phrul rna ba yid dang ni/ / sngon tshe 'chi 'pho skye ba dang / / zad shes mngon du bya ba yi/ / mngon shes rnam drug rnam grol blo/ / 42

There are six: knowledge of the supernatural, ear, mind, past lives, death and rebirth, and elimination. Since they act to perceive, they are higher perception, like awareness of the liberated path. (7:42)
rnam pa drug tu shes par bya'o/ /
You should understand there are six.
gang zhe na/
Question: What are they?

rdzu 'phrul gyi yul sprul pa dang 'gro ba shes pa dang*/ lha'i rna ba dang*/ gzhan gyi yid dug gsum bcas bral la sogs pa'i khyad par dang*/ res 'ga' chags res 'ga' sdang ngo zhes pa la sogs pa'i go rim shes pa dang*/ rang gzhan gyi sngon gyi tshe rabs rjes su dran pa dang*/ 'chi 'pho dang skye ba shes pa dang*/ zag pa zad pa shes pa mngon sum du bya ba ste byed pa'i mngon par shes pa'o zhes thams cad la sbyar ro/ / drug po de dag las dang po lnga ni/ so so'i skye bo dang thun mong ba yin la drug pa ni 'phags pa kho na'i rgyud la yod do/ / ngo bo ni mngon shes drug po de dag thams cad ni dper na dge sbyong gi tshul gyi 'bras bu 'dus byas rnam grol gyi lam gyi rang bzhin yin pa ltar rnam par grol ba'i lam gyi blo shes rab kyi rang bzhin yin no/ {gal te bar chad med lam gyis bsdus na dgra bcom gnyis ka'i cha las rnam grol la mngon shes med par 'gyur te bar chad med lam btang nas med pa'i phyir ro/ / lha'i mig dang rna ba'i mngon shes ni dbang shes yin pas rnam grol lam ji ltar yin zhe na/ lam gzhan gyi rnam grol du de dag 'gal yang mngon shes kyi rnam grol yin pas skyon med do/ / de lta min na sgom byung gi mngon shes su 'gal te rnam grol gyi lam min pas so }

Reply: (1) The knowledge of emanating supernatural (ṛddhi) objects, and movement; (2) the divine ear (śrota); (3) the knowledge of whether another’s mind possesses the three poisons and so on or not,[1824] or when attachment or aversion arises and so forth; (4) the recollection of the past lives (pūrvajanma) of self and others; (5) the knowledge of death and rebirth (cyutyudaya); and (6) the knowledge of the elimination (kṣaya) of the contaminants. Since they act to perceive [or make evident] (sākṣātkriya), they are called higher perception (abhijñā), and this is applied to all six. From among these six, the first five are common to ordinary beings, but the sixth only exists in the mindstream of a buddha. In terms of their nature, all six higher perceptions are, for example, like the awareness of the liberated path (muktimārgadhī) that is in essence wisdom, just as the result of virtuous training is the essence of the conditioned liberated path. {If the higher perceptions are subsumed by the uninterrupted path, arhats liberated from both aspects would not have higher perception, because for them the uninterrupted path has been relinquished and does not exist. Question: Since the higher perceptions of divine eye and ear are sense consciousness, how could they be liberated paths? Reply: Though it would be contradictory if they were the liberation found on other paths, there is no error since they are the liberation borne of higher perception. If it were otherwise, they would not be liberated paths, which would contradict their being higher perception derived from meditation.}
bzhi ni kun rdzob shes pa ste/ / sems la shes pa lnga yin no/ / zad pa'i mngon shes stobs bzhin no/ / lnga ni bsam gtan bzhi dag na/ / 43
Four are conventional knowledge. Knowledge of others’ minds is five. Higher perception of elimination is like the power. Five exist on four absorptions. (7:43)

gsum pa dang drug pa ma gtogs pa bzhi'i ngo bo ni kun rdzob shes pa ste/ zag bcas kho na yin pa'i phyir ro/{/de yang gsum gyis ni zag med dang gcig sngon gyi mtha' la dmigs pas so}/ gzhan gyi sems la dmigs nas de'i khyad par shes pa ni rdzas kyi rang gi mtshan nyid la dmigs pa dang*/ kun du rtog cing 'tshol ba'i bsam pa can dang*/ zag med lam gyi rnam pa can dang*/ zag bcas pha rol gyi sems chags bcas dang chags bral la sogs pa'i rnam pa can yin na zad pa dang mi skye ba shes pa ni de lta bu ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ 'gog pa mtshungs ldan ma yin zhing sdug bsngal dang kun 'byung shes pa'i rnam pa can yang ma yin pas shes pa lnga po de dag ma yin gyi 'on kyang zag med kyi cha chos shes rjes shes dang lam dang pha rol sems shes yin la/ zag bcas kyi cha kun rdzob shes pa dang pha rol sems shes gnyis yin pas shes pa lnga yin no/ / zag pa zad pa'i mngon par shes pa ni ji ltar zad pa mkhyen pa'i stobs shes pa drug gam bcu'i rang bzhin dang sa bcu gcig gis bsdus pa de bzhin du zag pa zad pa 'ba' zhig la dmigs pa yin na shes pa drug dang*/ zag pa zad pa'i rgyud la yod pa'i shes pa yin par 'dod na ni de'i rgyud la shes pa bcu ka yod pa'i phyir shes pa bcu char yin no/ / sa yang ci rigs par bcu gcig po thams cad yin par shes par bya'o/ /

Because they are contaminated alone, the nature of four higher perceptions, excluding the third and sixth, is conventional knowledge. {Further, three focus on uncontaminated states and one focuses on an initial beginning.} Knowledge of the attributes of others’ minds that focuses on others’ minds is not five types of knowledge since it is not (1) knowledge of elimination or (2) knowledge of nonarising; it focuses on real substance, it possesses investigative and probing contemplation, it possesses the uncontaminated path as its aspect, and it possesses attachment or nonattachment to the contaminated minds of others as its aspect. Further, it is not concomitant with the (3) knowledge of cessation, and it does not possess aspects of (4) the knowledge of suffering and (5) the knowledge of origin. But it is five knowledges: since it has uncontaminated objects, it is (1) Dharma knowledge, (2) subsequent knowledge, (3) knowledge of the path, and (4) knowledge of others’ minds. And since it has contaminated objects, it is both (5) conventional knowledge and (4) knowledge of others’ minds. Higher perception of the elimination (kṣayābhijñā) of contaminants is like the power comprehending elimination that consists of six or ten knowledges and is subsumed by eleven levels. It consists of six knowledges if it focuses on the elimination of contaminants alone, and ten knowledges if it is asserted to consist of any knowledge in the stream of the elimination of contaminants because ten knowledges exist in its stream.

mngon shes dang po lnga ni bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi bzhi dag na yod la/{ mngon shes 'di dag bsam gtan khyad par can na med de lhag mthong shas che bas lam sla ba ma yin pa'i phyir ro/} gzugs med na ni med de/ rdzu 'phrul dang lha'i rna ba dang 'chi 'pho dang skye ba shes pa gsum ni gzugs la dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ sems kyi rnam grangs dang sngon gyi gnas rjes su dran pa'ang gzugs kyi dmigs pa la brten nas bsgrub dgos pa'i phyir te/ 'di ltar bsam gtan pa dag bsam gtan la brten nas gzugs 'di 'dra bas na sems 'di 'dra bar 'gyur ro zhes dang*/ lus 'di la sems kyi rnam pa ci 'dra ba zhig ces pha rol la yid gtod de/ gang gi tshe gzugs la ma ltos par pha rol gyi sems shes pa de'i cha sems shes pa grub pa yin no/ /

The first five higher perceptions exist on the four actual bases of absorption. {These higher perceptions [631] do not exist for special absorption; the special path is not the easiest path [for developing higher perception] since, for it, insight is predominant.} They don’t exist in the formless realm because the three — (1) knowledge of supernatural power, (2) divine ear, and (3) death and rebirth — focus on form, and because (4) knowledge of the categories of mind [or knowledge of others’ minds] and (5) knowledge of past lives must be established in dependence on focusing on form. Thus, in dependence on the absorptions, beings possessing absorption direct their minds to another being and reflect, “His mind should be like this since his body is like this” or “What type of mind exists for this body?” When they know the mind of another without relying on form, then at that time knowledge of that mind is established.

yang bsam gtan la brten nas bdag gzhan gyi yid kyi rnam par shes pa 'gags ma thag pa'i mtshan ma bzung nas de'i snga ma snga ma la yid gtad de mthar nying mtshams sbyor ba'i sems dang*/ de nas snga ma'i bar do'i gnas skabs dang*/ de nas snga ma'i 'chi ba'i srid pa dang*/ de nas snga ma'i sngon dus kyi srid pa la yid gtod de/ gang gi tshe bar srid dran pa de'i tshe sngon gnas rjes dran grub pa yin no/ / de yang dang po ni rim gyis dran la mngon par grub nas ni tshe gcig dang gnyis la sogs pa rgal te thod rgal du yang dran la/ de yang sngon nyams su myong ba kho na dran no/ / gal te sngon nyams su myong ba kho na dran na 'o na rten 'dod pa pa'i sngon gnas rjes dran gyis gnas gtsang ma rnams ji ltar dran te phyir mi 'ong yin pas de dag 'dir mi skye zhing so so'i skye bo rnams der mi skye ba'i phyir ro zhe na/ nyams su myong ba ni mthong ba dang thos pas nyams su myong ba gnyis las gnas gtsang ma pa rnams ni 'di lta bu yin no zhes thos pas nyams su myong ba'i phyir ro/ / des na sngon gnas rjes dran ni rang gzhan gyi sngon 'dod pa la sogs pa'i gnas gzhan dag rjes su dran pas bsgrub dgos pa la/ gzugs med dngos gzhi dge rnams kyi/ / spyod yul zag bcas 'og ma min zhes 'dod pa la sogs pa'i gnas gzhan 'og ma la mi dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ mdo las/ bdag ming 'di zhes bya rigs ni 'di lta bur kha zas ni 'di lta bu za za/ bde ba dang sdug bsngal ni 'di lta bu zhig nyams su myong*/ tshe ni 'di tsam zhig thub/ bdag gnas de nas shing 'phos nas che ge mo zhig tu skyes so/ / de nas shi 'phos nas ni 'dir skyes so zhes pa dang*/ sngon gyi gnas rnam pa du ma rnam pa dang bcas/ yul phyogs dang bcas/ gleng gzhi dang bcas pa rjes su dran no zhes gsungs pas sa 'og ma'i sngon gyi gnas dang rus dang rigs dang ming dang kha zas la sogs pa dran dgos pa'i phyir gzugs la ltos pa yin pa la gzugs med 'og sa la mi dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Again, in dependence on the absorptions, first he apprehends the characteristics of the mental consciousness of himself or another that has just ceased. Then he directs his mind to progressively earlier moments of that mind, until finally he directs his mind that links [to this life], then to the mind at the time of the intermediate-state being preceding that, then to the dying being, and then to the mind of the being preceding that. When he recalls the intermediate-state being, he establishes recall of his past life. Moreover, first he establishes serial recall, then he develops alternating recall that passes over one or two lives and so on, but he only recalls past-life experience. Question: Now, if one recalls past-life experience alone, then how could those of the pristine abodes remember being a desire-realm being through recalling past lives? For nonreturners are not born here, and ordinary beings are not born there.
