Reply: Experience is either experience through seeing or experience through hearing, and beings of the pristine abodes experience the desire realm through hearing “It is like this.” Therefore, recalling previous lives must be established through recalling other lives of oneself or others, such as past desire-realm lives and so on. [Formless-realm beings] do not focus on other lower lives, such as desire-realm lives and so on, since the Abhidharmakośa observes, “The object fields of those virtuous, formless, actual bases are not contaminated lower levels” (8:21ab). And a sūtra declares: I had this name, with this caste, ate this food, experienced this happiness and pain, had this lifespan, and from that life I died and I was reborn in such a place, and then I died and was reborn here. And: I recall many prior lives and their many details as well as their specific place and their central theme.[1825] Therefore one relies on form in order to recall prior lives, family, caste, name, food, and so on in lower levels, but formless states do not focus on lower levels.

de yang mngon shes grub nas ni gzugs la ma ltos par shes so/ / rdzu 'phrul dang lha'i rna ba dang mig gi mngon shes gsum gyi sbyor ba ni bsam gtan la brten nas rim pa ltar lus yang ba dang 'phar ba la sogs pa dang*/ chung ngu dang thag ring po'i sgra dang*/ snang ba yid la byed pa yin la/ zag zad kyi mngon shes kyi sbyor ba ni gnas drug par tshul gnas thos dang bsam gtan pa zhes nyon mongs pa spong ba'i thabs rgyas par bstan pa'i phyir yang 'dir mi brjod do zhes slob dpon gang spel 'chad do/ / de dag ni/ rnam gnas kyi rgyu yin la/ rnam par smin pa'i rgyu ni rin po che'i phreng ba las gsungs pa bzhin du shes par bya'o/ /

Further, having established higher perception, it it knowledge without relying on form. Master Pūrṇavardhana explains that preparation for the three higher perceptions of (1) supernatural power, (2) divine ear, and (3) divine eye rely on absorptions attentive to, respectively, (1) a body that is light and radiant and so on, (2) sound that is [632] soft and distant, and (3) appearance. Preparation for the higher perception of the elimination of contaminants exists in the six abodes, because the Abhidharmakośa extensively explains the means of abandoning afflictions when it says, “They maintain ethics, strive to listen, and having contemplated its meaning . . .” (6:5ab), but that is not what is being expressed here.[1826] These are causes of abidance, but the causes of karmic maturation should be understood in accordance with the Precious Garland.[1827]
rang dang 'og sa'i yul can yin/ / thob bya 'dris pa chags bral bas/ / gsum pa dran pa nyer gzhag gsum/ / dang po rdzu 'phrul rna ba mig / 44

They possess objects of its level and lower level. Culivated states are obtained through freedom from attachment. The third is the three foundations of mindfulness. Supernatural power, ear, and eye are the first. (7:44)

mngon shes lnga po 'di dag ni rang sa dang 'og sa'i spyod yul can yin gyi gong ma'i ni ma yin te/ dman pa'i yul mchog ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / {rdzu 'phrul gyis de'ang 'og mar 'gro zhing sprul gyi gong du ma yin pa sogs gzhan la'ang sbyar ro } de'i phyir gzugs med pa'i sems ni sems kyi rnam grangs shes pa dang sngon gnas dran pa'i mngon shes kyis mi 'dzin te/ de ni gong ma'i sems yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de lta na gzugs med nas shi 'phos nas 'dir skyes pa ji ltar sngon gyi gnas dran pa'i mngon shes kyis dran te/ de ni bsam gtan bzhi pa'i sa pa yin pas des gong ma gzugs med kyi sems mi 'dzin pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ de ni pha rol po'i rgyud la brten nas bskyed de/ pha rol po'i yid shes 'gags ma thag pa'i mtshan ma bzung nas bskyed pa'i phyir ro/ / gang dag gzugs med nas shi 'phos pa ma yin pa de dag ni sla ba'i phyir dang rang gi rgyud la brten nas skyed par byed do/ / de yang bar do tshun chad du dran par 'dod kyi gzhan ni mi dran no zhes bya ba ni grub pa'i mtha'o/ /

These five higher perceptions possess objects (viṣaya) of its level and lower level but not of higher level because inferior objects cannot be superior objects. {Emanations generated by supernatural power proceed also to lower levels but not to higher levels. This should also be applied to the other five higher perceptions.} Therefore the higher perceptions perceiving categories of mind or recalling previous lives do not apprehend the formless mind, because those are higher minds. Question: Then how does the higher perception recalling past lives recall birth in the desire realm after dying from the formless realm? It cannot apprehend the higher formless-realm mind, since higher perception belongs to the level of the fourth absorption. Reply: It is generated in dependence on another’s mindstream. That is, it is generated through apprehending the characteristics of another’s mental consciousness that has just ceased. It is easier to comprehend lives that do not involve death from the formless realm, since such comprehension is generated in dependence on one’s own mindstream. One tenet system asserts that past lives are recalled from the intermediate state but not at other times.
de dag 'thob pa'i tshul ni
HOW THEY ARE OBTAINED

mngon par shes pa bye brag can sngon ma bskyed pas ma 'dris pa rnams ni sbyor bas 'thob par bya ba yin la/ {khyad par can ni 'phags lam dang 'bral ba'o } gang dag tshe rabs snga ma la goms shing 'dris pa rnams ni 'dod chags dang bral ba tsam gyis 'thob bo/ / de dag mngon sum du 'gyur ba ni 'dris pa dang ma 'dris pa gnyis ka'ang sbyor ba'i stobs kho nas 'thob par bya ba yin no/ /

Specific higher perceptions — that are unfamiliar since they were not previously generated — are obtained through preparation. {“Specific” refers to those not related to the ārya path.} Higher perceptions that one became familiar with and cultivated (ucita) in previous lives are obtained through mere freedom from attachment (virāgata). Obtainment of their manifest state, whether one is familiar with them on not, is due to the power of preparation alone.
dran pa nye bar bzhag par bshad pa ni
EXPLAINING THE CLOSE PLACEMENT OF MINDFULNESS

mngon par shes pa gsum pa sems kyi rnam grangs shes pa ni mtshungs ldan kho na la dmigs pas tshor ba dang sems dang chos dran pa nyer gzhag gsum yin te gzhan gyis sems dang sems las byung ba la dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ / rdzu 'phrul gyi yul shes pa dang lha'i rna ba dang lha'i mig gi mngon shes gsum ni dran pa nyer gzhag dang po lus dran pa nyer gzhag yin te/ rdzu 'phrul gyi mngon par shes pa ni 'dod par gtogs pa'i sprul pa ni/ phyi'i skye mched bzhi zhes 'chad par 'gyur bas sgra ni rgyun chad pas sprul par mi byed pas gzugs dri ro reg bya bzhi la dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ lha'i rna ba ni bskal pa dang ma bskal ba'i sgra la dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ lha'i mig gis ni 'chi ba dang bar do dang skye ba'i srid pa'i kha dog bzang ngan la sogs pa'i gzugs la dmigs pa'i phyir dang*/ de thams cad kyang gzugs can yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te lha'i mig gi mngon shes kyi dmigs yul gzugs kyi skye mched kho na yin na/ 'o na mdo las 'chi 'pho skye shes kyis sems can 'di dag ni lus kyi nyes par spyod pa dang ldan no zhes pa la sogs pa sgo gsum gyi las dang ldan pa shes par gsungs pa dang 'gal te/ lus kyi rig byed ma yin pa dang ngag dang yid kyi las gzugs kyi skye mched ma yin pa'i phyir ro zhe na/

The third higher perception, knowledge of the categories of mind, is the three foundations of mindfulness (upasthāna) of feeling, mind, and phenomena; it focuses on others’ minds and mental factors, since it focuses on concomitant states alone. Three — knowledge of objects of supernatural power (ṛddhi), higher perception of divine ear (śrotra), and divine eye (cakṣu) — are the first foundation of mindfulness, the foundation of mindfulness of the body. That is because (1) the higher perception of supernatural power focuses on four objects — form, smell, taste, and tactility — since the Abhidharmakośa notes, “Emanations belonging to the desire realm are the four external bases” (7:49ab), and the continuum of sound is severed. (2) The divine ear focuses on pleasing and displeasing sound. (3) The divine eye focuses on such forms as the attractive or unattractive color of the death existence, intermediate existence, birth existence, and so on, and all these possess form. Objection: If the focal object of the higher perception of divine eye is the form base alone, then this would contradict the statement in the sūtras that it is knowledge of those who possess karma of the three doors; that is not indicative physical form, and verbal and mental karma [633] are not the form base: Those sentient beings with knowledge of death and rebirth possess negative action of the body.[1828]

bye brag tu smra ba dag de dag lha'i mig gi mngon shes kyis mi shes kyi 'on kyang lha'i mig gi mngon shes kyi 'khor du gyur pa'i yid kyi rnam shes kyis shes pa yin pas sgo gsum gyi las dang ldan pa shes pa ni yid shes yin no zhes 'dod pa ni mi rigs te/ yid shes de mngon shes drug tu ma 'dus na drug las tha dad pa'i mngon shes yin pas mngon shes bdun par thal bar 'gyur la/ 'dus na 'khor du rnam par bzhag pa mi 'thad par 'gyur ro/ / des na lus ngag gi nyes spyod ni lha'i mig dang rna ba'i mngon shes kyis shes la yid kyis nyes spyod de dag las dpog pa'am sems kyi rnam grangs shes pas shes pa yin no zhes bya bar rigs so/ / sngon gnas rjes dran ni gzugs dang sems dang sems byung gsum ga la dmigs pas dran pa nyer gzhag bzhi ka'i bdag nyid yin la/ zag zad kyi mngon shes kyang gal te zag pa zad pa 'ba' zhig la dmigs pa yin na ni chos dran pa nyer gzhag dang*/ 'on te de'i rgyud la dmigs pa yin na ni shes pa bcu'i ngo bo yin pas dran pa nyer gzhag bzhi ka yin no/ / yang na zag pa zad pa 'ba' zhig la dmigs pas shes pa drug gi ngo bo yin yang dran pa nyer gzhag gzhan gsum yang ma 'ongs pa 'thob pas dran pa nyer gzhag bzhi char gyi rang bzhin zhes TIka byed dag 'chad de 'grel pa'i dgongs pa'ang de nyid du gsal lo/ /

Vaibhāṣikas assert that the higher perception of divine eye does not know these karmas, which is knowledge possessing karma of the three doors, but that mental consciousness in the retinue of the higher perception of divine eye knows them. Reply: This is illogical. If that mental consciousness were not included in the six higher perceptions, it would follow that it would be a seventh higher perception, a higher perception distinct from those six. If it were included as a higher perception, it would be unacceptable to posit it within its own retinue. Therefore it is logical that negative physical and verbal actions are known by the higher perceptions of divine eye and divine ear. Negative mental action is known through inference or the knowledge of the categories of mind. Recalling previous lives is the four foundations of mindfulness since it focuses on three states: form, mind, and mental factors. However, the higher perception of the elimination of contaminants is the foundation of mindfulness of phenomena if it focuses on the elimination of contaminants alone. If, however, it focuses on the stream of elimination, it is the four foundations of mindfulness, since it would be by nature the ten knowledges. Again, though it would by nature be six knowledges if it focused on the elimination of contaminants alone, it would also be by nature all four foundations of mindfulness, since it would obtain the other three foundations of mindfulness in the future. This is explained in Pūrṇavardhana’s commentary.[1829] Clearly this is also the intention of the Autocommentary.
mig dang rna ba'i mngon shes ni/ / lung du ma bstan lhag rnams dge / gsum ni rig pa sngon mtha' sogs/ / ma rig pa ni bzlog phyir ro/ / 45
The higher perceptions of eye and ear are neutral. The remainder are virtuous. Three are cognition because they counter ignorance of an initial beginning and so on. (7:45)

yang mngon shes de dag las lha'i mig dang rna ba'i mngon shes gnyis ni nyon mongs pa can ma yin zhing dge ba bzhir yang ma 'dus pas ma bsgribs la lung du ma bstan pa kho na yin no/{ de dag skyes thob min la/ sbyor byung yang min te de ni thos bsam sgom gsum gyis bsdus la de la skyes thob dang sbyor byung gnyis ka mi srid pas so/ /} de dag kyang mig dang rna ba'i rnam shes dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i shes rab yin no/ /

Again, from among those higher perceptions, both the higher perceptions of divine eye and of divine ear are solely unobscured-neutral states, since they are neither afflicted nor included in the four virtuous states. {They are not obtained from birth, nor do they arise from preparation, since it is impossible for states subsumed by the three wisdoms arising from hearing, contemplation, and meditation to both be obtained from birth and arise from preparation.} They are wisdoms concomitant with eye and ear consciousness.

'o na de dag bsam gtan bzhi pa'i sa par mi 'gyur te/ gnyis pa sogs na lus mig dang*/ rna ba'i rnam shes rnam rig slong*/ / gang yin de ni dang por gtogs zhes 'chad par 'gyur bas mig dang rna ba'i rnam shes de dag bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad na med la/ de dag med par de dag dang mtshungs ldan gyi shes rab mi 'thad pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ de lta mod kyi 'on kyang gzugs kyi khams na bcu bzhi'o zhes 'byung bas rnam shes de dag gi rten mig dang rna ba'i dbang po bsam gtan bzhi pa'ang yin pas rten dag gi dbang gis bsam gtan bzhi par brjod do/ / yang na bar chad med pa'i lam gyi dbang gis de skad brjod de/ thog mar sgrub pa na lam sla ba'i mchog yin pas bar chad med lam bsam gtan bzhi pa la brten nas bsgrub dgos pa'i phyir ro/ / mngon shes lhag ma bzhi po rnams ni dge ba kho na yin no/{ de yang bsam gtan gyis bsdus pa'i rnam grol gyi lam yin pas so/ /} 'o na rab tu byed pa las/ mngon par shes pa gang zhe na/ shes rab dge ba yin no zhes bshad pa ji lta bu zhe na/ de ni mngon shes dge ba gtso bor gyur pa'am/ yang na mngon shes phal cher dge ba yin pa'i dbang du byas nas de skad du bshad pa yin te dper na mon sran gre'u la sogs pa yod bzhin du mon sran gre'u phal che bas de'i phung por brjod pa bzhin no/ /

Objection: They do not occur on the level of the fourth absorption because eye and ear consciousnesses do not exist on the second absorption and above. As it says in the Abhidharmakośa, “On the second absorption and so on, consciousnesses of body, eye, ear, and that which motivates indicative form belong to the first absorption” (8:13abc). Since they don’t exist, wisdom concomitant with them is untenable. Reply: Indeed, that is so; however, it is called the fourth absorption from the perspective of the supportive basis, since the eye and ear sense faculties that are the support of those consciousnesses belong to the fourth absorption. As the Abhidharmakośa explains, “Fourteen exist in the form realm” (1:30b). Again, it is called that from the perspective of the uninterrupted path. [634] One must establish the uninterrupted path in dependence on the fourth absorption, since when it is initially established, the easier path is supreme. The four remaining higher perceptions are solely virtuous (śubhā) {since they are liberated paths subsumed by the absorptions}. Question: Why does Topic Divisions state: What is higher perception? It is virtuous wisdom.[1830] Reply: This is explained from the perspective that higher perception is predominantly virtuous, or higher perception is probably virtuous. For example, a heap of mung beans may be called a heap of “mon” peas since it resembles a heap of “mon” peas.
mngon shes drug po 'di dag las phyi ma gsum ni mi slob pa'i rig pa gsum zhes bya'o/ /
From among the six higher perceptions, the latter three are called “three nonlearner cognitions (vidyā).”

ci'i phyir gsum po de dag kho na rig pa yin gyi dang po gsum ma yin zhe na/ de gsum gyis sngon gyi mtha' dang sogs pas gzung ba phyi ma'i mtha' dang bar la kun du rmongs pa'i ma rig pa rnam par bzlog pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di la skal ldan khyad par can la sogs pa ni zag zad kyi mngon shes kyi skabs su mdo las 'di las srid pa gzhan mi shes so zhes 'byung ba dang*/ 'das pa dang da ltar byung ba dang ma 'ongs pa'i dus zhes bya ba'i rim pa dang mthun par sngon gnas rjes dran dang 'chi 'pho skye shes dang zag pa zad pa shes pa gsum gyis rim pa ltar sngon dang bar dang phyi ma'i mtha' la kun du rmongs pa bzlog par byed do zhes 'chad mod kyi/ slob dpon 'dun bzang dang pos rang gzhan gyi rgud pa mthong la/ bar mas gzhan gyi rgud pa mthong nas skyo ba skye la/ de ltar skyo na gsum pas yang dag pa'i don rtogs pas na de gsum gyis rim pa ltar sngon dang phyi ma'i mtha' dang bar da ltar byung ba la kun du rmongs pa bzlog go zhes 'chad pas nyid rigs te/ 'grel pa las/ sngon gyi gnas dang 'chi 'pho ba dang skye ba dang zag pa zad pa shes pa mngon sum du bya ba rnams ni mi slob pa'i rig pa gsum zhes bya'o zhes bshad nas/ 'di dag gis ni go rim bzhin du sngon gyi mtha' dang phyi ma'i mtha' dang bar la kun du rmongs pa bzlog par byed do zhes bshad pa'i phyir slob dpon gyi dgongs pa'ang de nyid yin par mngon no zhes rgyal po'i sras 'chad do/ /

Question: Why are just these three called “cognition” and the first three are not? Reply: Because these three counter (nirvartana) ignorance (avidyā) that is fully confused to an initial beginning (pūrvānta) and so on (meaning the interim present and a final end). Regarding those possessing special merit and so on, a sūtra mentions in the context of the higher perception of the elimination of the contaminants: After this no other existences are known.[1831] Indeed, it explains: The three states of (1) recalling past lives, (2) knowledge of death and rebirth, and (3) knowledge of the elimination of contaminants that are compatible with the stages of past, present, and future time counter confusion regarding, respectively, an initial beginning, the interim present, and a final end. Master Saṅghabhadra explains that by comprehending the first, one sees the decline of self and others. By comprehending the second, one sees the decline of others, and disappointment arises. By comprehending the third error in that way, one comprehends the perfect meaning. Thus due to those three, one serially stops confusion about an initial beginning, confusion about a final end, and confusion about what occurs in the present. This is logical because the Autocommentary observes: Those perceptions of past lives, death and rebirth, and elimination of the contaminants are called nonlearner knowledge.[1832] Master Jinaputra explains that this is the intention of Vasubandhu because it clarifies that these respectively counter confusion about an initial beginning, [the limit of] the interim present, and a final end.[1833]
mi slob tha ma gnyis ni de'i/ / rgyud la skyes phyir de zhes bya/ / slob la 'dod de ma rig dang / / bcas rgyud phyir na rig ma bshad/ / 46

Nonlearner cognition is the last. Two are called that because they arise in nonlearner mindstreams. Learners are said to have them but they are not called cognition because the learner mindstream is associated with ignorance. (7:46)
mngon shes gsum po de dag kho na rig pa gsum yin par ni
Further, regarding the three higher perceptions alone being the three cognitions,

a sūtra states: Nonlearner cognitions are of three types: the cognition manifesting knowledge recalling past lives of a nonlearner, the cognition manifesting knowledge of death and rebirth of a nonlearner, and the cognition manifesting knowledge of the elimination of the contaminants of a nonlearner. And: They are the three collections and the three cognitions.[1834] Therefore, from among those three, ultimate nonlearner (aśaikṣya) cognition is the last — higher perception of the elimination of contaminants alone — since [635] cognition of it is also uncontaminated. The first two are explicitly called “nonlearner cognitions” because they arise in mindstreams (saṃtāna) of nonlearners. But they are not nonlearner cognitions, since both are contaminated, and they are not both learner and nonlearner cognitions. Question: Since learners have these higher perceptions, why are they not called learner cognitions? Reply: Though it is asserted that even learners have these higher perceptions, they are not called “cognitions” (vidya). Question: Why? Reply: Because the learner mindstream (saṃtata) is oppressed by ignorance, it is not worthy to be cognition. {It is an object to be abandoned by the path of meditation,} since it is associated with ignorance (sāvidya) {when they arise from equipoise, and a tie (bandhana) is not explained to be liberation}.
dang po gsum pa drug pa ni/ / cho 'phrul rnams yin bstan pa mchog / mi 'khrul phyir dang phan pa dang / / yid 'ong 'bras la sbyor byed phyir/ / 47
The first, third, and sixth are miracles. Instruction is supreme because it is not mistaken, it benefits, and it prepares the appealing result. (7:47)

yang drug gi tshogs kyi bzhi pa reg pa bzhi pa'i mdo'i ral pa can stong rab tu byung ba'i dge slong rnams la gdams pa las rdzu 'phrul gyi cho 'phrul dang kun brjod pa'i cho 'phrul dang rjes su bstan pa'i cho 'phrul rnam pa gsum gsungs pa las mngon par shes pa drug gi dang po rdzu 'phrul gyi yul shes pa'i mngon par shes pa dang*/ gsum pa sems kyi rnam grangs shes pa dang*/ drug pa zag zad kyi mngon shes rnams ni rim pa bzhin du rdzu 'phrul dang khyod kyi sems ni 'di 'dra'o zhes kun brjod pa dang lam yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin ston pas rjes su bstan pa'i cho 'phrul rnams yin no/ / ci'i phyir cho 'phrul zhes bya zhe na/ dang por gdul bya gzhan gyi yid 'phrog par byed pa'i phyir te ha ra'i don to/ / de la dang pos ni pha rol gyi yid 'dun pa'i sgo nas 'phrog par byed cing*/ gnyis pas ni pha rol gyi bsam pa shes nas chos bstan pa'i sgo nas yid 'phrog par byed la/ gsum pas ni bstan pa bzhin bsgrubs pas smin cing grol ba'i sgo nas yid 'phrog pa'i phyir ro/ / yang na 'di dag gis rim pa ltar bstan pa la zhe 'gras pa dang bar mar gnas pa dang zhugs pa rnams kyis yid 'phrog pa'i phyir ram/ yang na 'dun pa dang 'jug pa dang zhugs pa rnams kyis yid 'phrog pa'i phyir ro/ /

Again, the Sūtra on the Four Assemblies, the fourth in the Collection of Six Sūtras,[1835] states that a thousand matted-haired ascetics who took full ordination were given instruction through the three: the miracle of supernatural display, the miracle of expression, and the miracle of instruction. From these, the first of the six higher perceptions is the higher perception of supernatural objects, the third is knowledge of the categories of minds, and the sixth is the higher perception of elimination. These are the miracles (prātihārya) of, respectively, supernatural display, conventional knowledge that “your mind is like this,” and instruction, since instruction is given in accordance with the perfect path. Question: Why are they called “miracles”? Reply: First, the meaning of hārya is “to impress,” because it impresses disciples. The first impresses through generating mental aspiration in others, the second impresses by means of teaching Dharma through knowing the thoughts of others, and the third impresses by means of maturing and liberating others through instruction that accords with the teachings. Again, they impress by, respectively, opposing, abiding in the middle, and converting; or they impress by inspiring, engaging, and converting.

cho 'phrul gsum po 'di dag gi nang na rjes su bstan pa'i cho 'phrul kho na mchog yin te/ nyon mongs pa zad pa med na mi 'byung zhing*/ bar chad med pa'i lam zag med kho na las skyes pas rgyu de la ma 'khrul ba'i phyir dang*/ 'dir nyon mongs pa dang bral bas phan pa'i phyir dang*/ phyi mar sdug bsngal gyi khur dang bral bas gtan du yid du 'ong ba'i 'bras bu la sbyor bar byed pa'i phyir ro/ / cho 'phrul dang po gnyis ni g+han+d+ha ri zhes bya ba'i rig sngags kyis nam mkha' la 'gro ba dang*/ rtog byed ces bya ba'i rig sngags kyis pha rol gyi sems shes pa dang*/ sman dang mi ma yin pa'i nus pas kyang de ltar 'gyur ba'i phyir zag med kyi rgyu la mi 'khrul ba'ang ma yin la/ gdul bya 'dun pa dang bsam pa shes pa tsam gyis dngos su phan pa dang yid du 'ong ba'i 'bras bu la mi sbyor bas mchog ma yin no/ / 'o na rdzu 'phrul zhes bya ba 'di ci zhig ce na/

From among these three miracles, the miracle of instruction (śāsana) alone is supreme (agrya) because it does not occur if there is no elimination of affliction; it is not mistaken (avyabhicāra) as to its cause, since it is generated from the uninterrupted path alone; it benefits, since it is free of afflictions; and it always prepares for an appealing result (phala) through freeing from the burden of suffering. The first two miracles are proceeding in the sky through mantras called gāndhārī[1836] and knowing the minds of others through mantras called īkṣaṇikā.[1837] They are not unmistaken as to the cause of the uncontaminated state because they arise due to the potency of medicine and through nonhuman spirits; they directly benefit merely through knowing the aspirations and thoughts of disciples; and they are not supreme since they do not prepare for the attractive result of liberation. [636] Question: What is supernatural power?
rdzu 'phrul ting 'dzin de las ni/ / sprul dang 'gro ba ston pa la/ / yid mgyogs 'gro ba gzhan dag la/ / phyin byed mos pa las byung yang / / 48
Supernatural power is concentration. From that, emanation and movement are accomplished. The Master possesses swift as thought. Others have activated body and resolute movement. (7:48)

bye brag tu smra ba rdzu 'phrul ni ting nge 'dzin yin no zhes 'dod de/ 'dis 'byor zhing 'grub par byed pa'i phyir ro/ / ci zhig 'byor zhing 'grub ce na/ rdzu 'phrul ting nge 'dzin de las ni yul sprul pa dang 'gro ba dbang 'byor ba 'grub pa'i phyir ro/ / de la rdzu 'phrul gyis 'gro ba ni rnam pa gsum te/ bya bzhin du rim gyis lus kyis mgyogs por phyin par byed pa lus phyin byed dang*/ lam thag ring po'ang thung ngur mos pa byas pas myur du sleb pa mos pa las byung ba dang*/ yid kyis bsams pa tsam gyis der slebs pa'i yid mgyogs so/ / de dag las yid bzhin du mgyogs pas na yid mgyogs kyis 'gro ba ni ston pa sangs rgyas kho na la mnga' ste/{ yid la bsams pa tsam gyis der phyin pas yid mgyogs so/ /} yul thag shin tu ring bar yang thugs bskyed pa tsam gyis byon pa'i phyir ro/ / de nyid kyi phyir bzhi las 'phros pa'i mdo las/ sangs rgyas rnams kyi sangs rgyas kyi yul ni bsam gyis mi khyab bo zhes gsungs so/ / 'gro ba gzhan gnyis ston pa la mnga' bar dngos su ma bshad kyang mnga' bar grub bo/ / sangs rgyas las gzhan nyan rang la sogs pa dag la ni lus phyin byed kyi 'gro ba'ang yod la mos pa las byung ba yang yod do/ / sprul pa ci lta bu zhe na/

Vaibhāṣikas assert that supernatural power (ṛddhi) is concentration (samādhi) because through it one attains and accomplishes. Question: What is attained and accomplished? Reply: From that supernatural concentration, the emanation (nirmāṇa) of objects and control over movement (gamana) is accomplished. Movement due to supernatural power has three types: (1) conveying the body, where the body moves swiftly in stages, like a bird, (2) resolute movement, which is quickly arriving at a distant place through the resolution that it is near, and (3) swift as thought, which is to arrive as swiftly as thought. From among those, swift as thought (manojavā) means proceeding by the swiftness of thought, and only the Master Buddha possesses that because he proceeds to extremely distant places by merely having the thought. {It is as swift as thought since it arrives there merely by thinking.} Therefore the Sūtra Elaborating Four proclaims: The enlightened domain (buddhaviṣaya) of buddhas is inconceivable.[1838] Though it is not explicitly stated that the other two types of movement are possessed by the Master, it is established that he possesses them. Those other than buddhas, meaning śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, possess conveying movement (śarīravāhini) and also resolute movement (ādhimokṣiki). Question: What is emanation like?
'dod par gtogs pa'i sprul pa ni/ / phyi yi skye mched bzhi rnam gnyis/ / gzugs gtogs gnyis sprul sems dag gis/ / de dag kyang ni bcu bzhi'o/ / 49

Emanations belonging to the desire realm are the four external bases. There are two types. Emanations belonging to the form realm have two bases. Emanating minds also project, and those are fourteen. (7:49)
sprul pa ni rten 'dod gzugs kyi sprul pa gnyis las
Reply: Emanation is twofold: emanations of desire-realm beings and form-realm beings.
EMANATIONS OF DESIRE-REALM BEINGS

dang po la yang gnyis las re zhig dang po{ 'dod pa'i rten can gyis} 'dod par gtogs pa'i sprul pa ni phyi'i skye mched gzugs dri ro reg bya bzhi sprul gyi nang gi skye mched ni sprul par mi byed de/ de sprul na sngon med pa'i sems can 'byung bar thal ba'i phyir ro/ / sgra ni rgyun med pa'i phyir mi sprul lo/ / de yang bdag nyid seng ge dang glang po che la sogs par bsgyur bas bdag gi lus dang 'brel ba dang*/ bdag nyid las phyi rol tu seng ge dang glang po che la sogs par sprul pas gzhan gyi lus dang 'brel ba rnam pa gnyis so/ /

This first has two types. {When a desire-realm being generates} emanations (nirmāṇa) belonging to the desire realm, these are emanations of the four external bases (bāhyāyatana) of form, smell, taste, and tactility. Internal bases are not emanated, for if they were emanated, it would follow that previously nonexistent sentient beings would arise. Sound is not emanated because it has no continuity. Again, there are two types: that related to one’s own body, such as transforming one’s body into a lion or elephant and so on, and that related to a separate body, such as projecting an external emanation as a lion or elephant and so on.

gnyis pa rten 'dod pa pa des gzugs su gtogs pa ni de na dri ro med pas gzugs dang reg bya'i skye mched gnyis kho na sprul zhing de yang snga ma ltar bdag gzhan gyi lus dang 'brel ba gnyis gnyis bzhi'o/ / de ltar na 'dod pa'i rten can gyi{ 'dod pa dang gzugs kyi gnyis gnyis te} sprul pa rnam pa bzhi yin no/ /

The desire-realm being [who generates emanations] belonging to the form realm emanates only two bases — form and tactility — since smell and taste do not exist there. As before, such emanations can be related to either oneself or another. Therefore there are two for each realm, making four. As such, emanations of a desire-realm being have four aspects, {two each for the desire realm and the form realm}.
EMANATIONS OF FORM-REALM BEINGS

de bzhin du gnyis pa rten gzugs khams pas kyang rang sa dang 'dod pa'i skye mched gnyis dang bzhi sprul zhing de gnyis ka re re zhing bdag gzhan gyi lus dang 'brel bar sprul pas spyir sprul pa ni rnam pa brgyad yin no/ / gal te des 'dod par bdag gi lus dang 'brel ba'i dri ro sprul na de de gnyis dang ldan par 'gyur ro zhe na/ de dag las sred pa med pas sprul kyang ldan par mi 'gyur te dper na gos dang rgyan lus dang 'brel kyang sems can du mi bgrang bas sems dang ldan par mi 'gyur ba bzhin no/ / yang ci mngon shes kho nas sprul pa sprul par byed dam zhe na/ ma yin te/

So too, a form-realm being emanates two and four bases of its own level and the desire-realm level, respectively. And for each of those there are emanations related to one’s own body and separate bodies. Therefore there are in general eight types of emanation. Objection: If that form-realm being emanates smell and taste related to his own body in the desire realm, he would possess those two bases. Reply: He does not possess them, for even though he emanates them, he has no craving for them. For example, though clothes and ornaments are related to the body, they do not come to possess mind since they are not counted as sentient beings. Question: Are emanations projected through higher perception alone? Reply: No.
mngon shes kyi 'bras bu sprul pa'i sems dag gis sprul par byed la/ sprul sems de dag kyang dbye na ni bcu bzhi'o/ / gang zhe na/
The emanating minds (nirmāṇacitta) that are the result [637] of higher perception also project such emanations. If those emanating minds are classified, there are fourteen. Question: What are they?
bsam gtan 'bras gnyis nas lnga'i bar/ / rim bzhin gong ma las skyes min/ / de rnyed bsam gtan bzhin de ni/ / dag dang rang las de las gnyis/ / 50

The results of absorption are, respectively, two to five levels. They do not arise from higher levels. Acquiring these is similar to the absorptions. That arises from pure absorption, and itself. Two arise from that. (7:50)

bsam gtan dang po'i 'bras bu sprul sems ni 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang po'i sa pa'i gnyis yin pa nas bsam gtan gnyis pa'i 'bras bu sa 'og ma pa gnyis dang rang gi sa pa ste gsum dang*/ gsum pa'i sa 'og ma pa gsum dang rang gi sa pa ste bzhi dang*/ bzhi pa'i sa 'og ma pa bzhi dang rang gi sa pa dang lnga yin pa'i bar du rim pa bzhin du shes par bya'o/ / des na bsam gtan gyi 'bras bu sprul sems ni rang sa dang 'og sa pa'i yin gyi bsam gtan 'og ma'i sa pa dag gi 'bras bu sa gong ma las skyes pa'i sprul sems ni min te { yin na 'og sa la brten nas gong sa sprul nus par thal bas so/} gong sa ma thob na bskyed mi nus la thob na de nyid kyi 'bras bu yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: The emanating mind that is the result of the first absorption (dhyānaphala) should be understood respectively as (yathākrama): (1–2) two levels of the desire realm and the first absorption, (3–5) three that are the result of the second absorption — the two lower levels and one’s own level, (6–9) four that are the result of the third absorption — the three lower levels and one’s own level, and (10–14) up to five that are the result of the fourth absorption — the four lower levels and one’s own level. Therefore the minds of emanation that are the results of the absorptions are minds of one’s own level and lower levels. The results of those lower levels of absorption are not minds of emanation that arise from higher (ūrdhvaja) levels, because if one has not obtained higher levels one cannot generate them, and if they are obtained they are the result of those. {If the [results of lower-level absorption] were [minds of emanation that arise from higher levels], it would follow that one could emanate on higher levels in dependence on lower levels.}

de ltar na 'dod pa'i sprul sems bsam gtan bzhi po kho na'i 'bras bu yin pa las bsam gtan 'og ma'i 'bras bu 'dod pa'i sprul sems kyis sprul pa'i 'dod pa'i sprul pa bas bsam gtan gong ma'i 'bras bu 'dod pa'i sprul sems kyis sprul pa'i 'dod pa'i sprul pa 'gro ba'i sgo nas khyad par du 'phags te/ bsam gtan dang po'i 'bras bu 'dod pa'i sprul sems kyis sprul pa'i 'dod pa'i sprul pa des bsam gtan dang po'i sa pa'i bar du 'gro nus kyi gnyis pa la sogs par 'gro mi nus la/ bsam gtan gnyis pa'i 'bras bu 'dod pa'i sprul sems kyis sprul pa'i 'dod pa'i sprul pa des bsam gtan gnyis pa'i bar du 'gro nus pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du bsam gtan gsum pa la sogs pa'i 'bras bu 'dod pa'i sprul sems kyis sprul pa la'ang sbyar te shes par bya'o/ /

Thus the desire-realm emanating mind is the result of the four absorptions alone. That which is projected by the desire-realm emanating mind that is the result of a lower absorption and that which is projected by the desire-realm emanating mind that is the result of a higher absorption are distinguished by means of the movement of such desire-realm emanations. That is because the desire-realm emanation projected by a desire-realm emanating mind, itself the result of the first absorption, is capable of proceeding to the first absorption level but incapable of proceeding to the second absorption and so on. But the desire-realm emanation projected by a desire-realm emanating mind that is the result of the second absorption is capable of proceeding to the second absorption. So too, that should be applied to that which is projected by a desire-realm emanating mind that is the result of the third absorption.

sprul sems de dag rnyed pa'i tshul ni bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi bzhin du 'og sa las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i sgo nas rnyed do/ / 'o na sprul sems de rang nyid kyi rjes kho na las 'byung zhing ldang ngam gzhan las kyang 'byung zhing gzhan yang 'byung zhe na/

The method of acquiring these emanations is similar to the actual basis of absorption that is acquired by means of becoming free of attachment to lower levels. Objection: Does the emanating mind arise from the substance of just that emanating mind alone, or does it arise from rising from emanation, or from others, or from something else again?

sprul sems de ni thog mar mngon du byed cing sprul sems la 'jug pa na bsam gtan dag pa pa dang rgyun gyi tshe sprul sems rang nyid las skye bar 'gyur la/ sprul sems la gnas pa de ldang ba na ting nge 'dzin la ma zhugs par ldang ba med pas sprul sems de las kyang sprul sems las langs pa'i tshe bsam gtan dag pa pa dang*/ rgyun gyi tshe sprul sems rang nyid dang gnyis skye bar 'gyur gyi gzhan dang gzhan las ni 'byung ba med do/ / {des na sprul sems kho na las 'dod pa'i sems lta bus ldang ba ni mi srid de bya 'phur ba dang 'bab pa nges par 'dab ma la brten pa bzhin no }

Reply: When first manifesting and engaging the mind of emanation, that emanating mind arises from pure absorption. When maintaining that state, it arises from the emanating mind itself. When rising from abiding in the emanating mind, two arise from that emanating mind: (1) when rising from the emanating mind, pure absorption arises, and (2) when maintaining that state, that emanating mind itself arises, since it cannot arise without entering concentration and it does not arise from other minds. {Therefore it is impossible for something like a desire-realm mind to arise from the emanating mind alone, just as a bird definitely depends on its wings to fly and land.}
rang gi sa pas sprul par byed/ / smrar 'jug pa ni 'og mas kyang / / ston min sprul pa po dang bcas/ / byin gyis brlabs nas gzhan 'jug phyir/ / 51

All are projected by the mind of one’s level. Those higher engage in speech by lower level also. Those not of the Master speak along with the emanator. Because one empowers it, it engages with others. (7:51)

sprul pa thams cad kyang rang rang gi sa pa'i sprul pa'i sems kyis rang sa'i sprul pa sprul par byed kyi sa gzhan pa'i sprul sems kyis ni sa gzhan gyi sprul pa sprul pa mi byed do zhes spyir btang nas dmigs bsal bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad pa dag gi sprul pa ngag smrar 'jug pa ni rang sa nas rtog dpyod med cing ngag smra ba kun slong rtog dpyod la nges par ltos pas sa 'og ma bsam gtan dang po'i sa pa'i smra sems kho nas smrar 'jug la/ kyang zhes pa ni 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang po na ni rang gi sa pa'i sems kho nas smrar 'jug go zhes pa bsdu ba'i phyir ro/ /

In general, all emanations are projected (nirmāṇa) as emanations of one’s level by the emanating mind of one’s level (svabhūmi), and the emanating mind of another level does not project emanations of one’s level. The exception is the emanations of the second absorption and above that engage in speech (bhāṣaṇa) [638] through the mind of speech of the lower level of the first absorption alone. This is because engaging in speech relies on investigation and analysis to motivate speech, but there is no investigation and analysis on their level. “Also” includes emanations of the desire realm and the first absorption who engage in speech through minds of their level alone.

ngag smra ba de yang lha dang bcas pa'i ston pa sangs rgyas min pa'i sprul pa ni sprul pa po dang bcas nas smra bar byed de/ lung ring po las/ gcig gis smra bar byed pa na/ / sprul pa thams cad smra bar byed/ / gcig mi smra bar gyur pa dang*/ / de dag thams cad smra mi 'gyur zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / sangs rgyas kyi sprul pa ni thams cad bzhed pa tsam gyis 'byung ba'i phyir snga phyi ji ltar bzhed par smra bas nges pa med de/ las gdags pa las/ ci'i phyir sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das kyis sprul pa skyes bu chen po'i mtshan sum cu rtsa gnyis dang ldan pa sprul pa ni gang gi tshe sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das gsung ba de'i tshe sprul ba mi smra la sprul pa smra ba de'i tshe sangs rgyas mi gsung ba dang*/ nyan thos kyi sprul pa nyan thos kyi cha byad can sprul pa ni nyan thos smra ba'i tshe sprul pa'ang smra la nyan thos mi smra ba'i tshe sprul pa'ang mi smra zhe na/ sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das ni sems dang ting nge 'dzin la mnga' brnyes pas myur du snyoms par 'jug cing bzhengs te dmigs pa'ang mi gtong la nyan thos ni de lta ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yang sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das ni thams cad mkhyen pa yin te/ ye shes dang dbang gi pha rol tu phyin pa yin la nyan thos ni de lta ma yin pa'i phyir ro zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / 'di la gal te smra ba'i ngag mang po sprul na ni sgra yang sprul par 'gyur bas phyi'i skye mched bzhi zhes pa dang*/ 'gal bar 'gyur la/ 'on te ngag gcig las med na mang po smra bar byed pa mi 'thad do/ / gal te mang por smra bar snang ba yin gyi ngag gcig las med do zhe na/ de ni phyi'i skye mched bzhi la'ang mtshungs pa'i phyir ro/ / de'i phyir bye brag tu smra bas sems can gsar skye med pas dbang po lnga mi sprul la/ sgra la rgyun med pas mi sprul lo zhes bya ba'ang sprul pa 'di dag sems kyi snang ba ma gtogs pa don la yod pa'i chos yin na ni ji ltar sprul pa yin/ med na'ang gsar du skye ba dang rgyun med pa dag kyang shes pa la snang bar 'gyur ro zhes brtag par bya'o/ / 'o na rgyud gcig la sems gnyis cig car mi 'byung bas smra sems yod pa'i tshe sprul sems med la sprul sems yod pa'i tshe smra sems med pas ji ltar sprul pa smrar 'jug ce na/

Further, when emanations of gods, but not those of the Master Buddha, speak, they speak along with the emanator (nimātr), because it is said in the Longer Discourses: When one speaks, all emanations speak. When one does not speak, none of them speak.[1839] Because emanations of a buddha all speak together, there is no certainty, however, as to whether they speak earlier or later. Presentation on Karma explains: Why does an emanation possessing the thirty-two marks of a great being projected by a buddha bhagavan not speak when a buddha bhagavan speaks, or why, when the emanation speaks, does the buddha not speak? Why does an emanation of a śrāvaka possessing the articles of a śrāvaka speak when the śrāvaka speaks, and why, when the śrāvaka does not speak, does that emanation also not speak? A buddha bhagavan quickly enters and arises from meditative attainment without relinquishing its focal object since he has mastery over the mind and concentration, but a śrāvaka is not like that. Again, a buddha bhagavan comprehends all because he has perfected transcendent wisdom and faculties, but a śrāvaka is not like that.[1840] Objection: If many speakers were emanated, sound would also be emanated, and it would contradict the Abhidharmakośa when it says “the four external bases” (7:49b). If there were just a single speech, it would be unacceptable for many to speak it. But even so, if many speakers appeared, there would be still be just one speech. Reply: That would also be similar to the four external bases. Therefore Vaibhāṣikas say that five faculties are not emanated since sentient beings are not newly born, and sound is not emanated since it has no continuity. If these emanations are not just an appearance to mind but phenomena existing as objects, how are they emanated? If not, then newly arisen states lacking continuity would appear to cognition. This should be investigated. Question: Since two minds do not simultaneously occur in one mindstream, when the mind activating speech exists, the emanating mind does not exist; when the emanating mind exists, the mind activating speech does not exist. Therefore how does the emanation engage in speech?

dang po sbyor ba'i tshe sprul sems kyis sprul pa sprul nas bdag gi sprul pa 'di yun ring du gnas par gyur cig /de nas smra sems kyis smra bar gyur cig ces rim pa ltar 'byung bar byin gyis brlabs nas ji ltar byin gyis brlabs pa ltar phyis sprul sems las gzhan smra sems kyis smrar 'jug pa'i phyir skyon med do/ / ci gson po kho na la byin rlabs yod dam/ 'on te shi ba la'ang yod ce na/

Reply: There is no error. During the initial preparation one projects an emanation with a emanating mind and empowers (adhiṣṭhāya) it by serially thinking, “May my emanation abide for a long time, then may it speak through the mind activating speech,” and in just the way it is empowered, it later engages in speech with others [639] due to the mind activating speech having been first projected through the emanating mind. Question: Does such empowerment exist only for the living, or does it also exist for the dead?
shi ba la yang byin brlabs yod/ / mi brtan la med gzhan dag min/ / dang po du mas gcig yin te/ / byang bar gyur nas bzlog pa'o/ / 52

Even one who has died has influence through empowerment. But it does not exist for unstable objects. For others it does not. At first many minds emanate one. Once trained, he stops the former method. (7:52)

{sprul pa po } shi ba la yang byin gyis brlabs nas yun ring du 'jug pa yod de/ lung phran tshegs las/ ston pa 'das nas 'phags pa kun dga' bo dang nye bar 'khor gyis mdo sde dang 'dul ba bsdus pa'i rjes la 'phags pa 'od srungs chen pos mngon pa'i sde snod bsdus te/ kye ma stobs bcu mnga' ba'i gsung ni tshad med pa/ / 'gro la phan phyir chos kyi bstan bcos 'di bsdus pas/ / gang na 'jig rten blo ngan mun byed chud zos pa/ / blo gros rab rib bsal bas sgron mer yang dag ldan zhes smras nas/ 'di snyam du bdag gis ston pa'i bka' drin mtha' dag bsab par mi nus mod kyi 'on kyang sde snod gsum bsdus na bstan pa yun ring du gnas par 'gyur ro zhes gsung ba'i ston pa'i gsung bsgrubs shing bstan pa yun ring du gnas par byas pas 'jig rten la phan btags shing tshangs spyod yun ring du spyad pas de ni lus rnag can 'dis skyo bas bdag mya ngan 'das ba'i dus la bab bo snyam nas/ bdag gi thub pa'i mdo sde ni/ / yang dag bsdus nas chos lam gzhag gcig nas gcig tu yun ring bar/ / ston pa'i gsung rab 'di gnas 'gyur/ / ngo tsha med rnams chad pas bcad/ / ngo tsha byed ni yongs su gzung*/ / bdag gis phan dang dge byas pas/ / bdag ni mya ngan 'das dus bab ces smras te/ kun dga' bo la bstan pa gtad nas ston pa'i sku gdung gi mchod rten brgyad kyi drung du song ste mchod cing*/ klu'i gnas dang sum cu rtsa gsum du'ang song nas ston pa'i mche ba la mchod pa byas te/ slar rgyal po'i khab tu 'ongs nas rgyal po ma skyes dgra la mya ngan las 'da' bar smra bar 'dod pa na rgyal po gnyid du song bas ma phrad par gyur to/ /

Reply: Even {an emanator} who has died (mṛta) has influence for a long time through such empowerment (adhiṣṭhāna). As it is said in the Kṣudraka Collection: After the passing of the Master, Ānanda and Upāli proclaimed the Sūtra and Vinaya Piṭakas. Then Ārya Mahākāśyapa proclaimed the Abhidharma Piṭaka and said, “Ah, the speech of one possessing the ten powers is immeasurable. But when condensed in Dharma treatises for the sake of reincarnating beings, they will possess a lamp eliminating the distortions of their thinking, which has declined through the darkness of evil mundane minds.” Then, reflecting on this, he said, “Indeed, I cannot repay all the kindness of the Master; however, if his instruction is condensed in the three piṭakas, his teachings will remain long.”[1841] Then he thought, “The time has come for me to attain nirvāṇa, since the Master’s instructions have been accomplished and his teachings will be preserved for a long time, since the world has been benefited and the practice of purity guaranteed for a long time, and I have become disgusted with this pestilent body.” He said “This sūtra division of my Master sets forth the path of Dharma when properly condensed, and the Master’s discourses will endure when passed from one disciple to another over a long period. Those who lack shame will destroy it by destroying this heritage. Those with shame will fully maintain it. I have acted with virtue to benefit others, and now the time has arrived for me to attain nirvāṇa.” Then he made Ānanda patriarch of the teachings and proceeded to the eight stūpas containing the relics of the Master and made offerings. Then he proceeded to the land of the nāgas and to the gods of Trāyastriṃśa, and made offerings to the tooth of the Master. Then he returned to Rājagṛha desiring to speak of attaining nirvāṇa to King Ajātaśatru, but the king was asleep and they did not meet.

de nas 'od srungs chen po ri bya rkang can du song ste ri gsum ga dbus su rtswa bting ba la 'dug nas bdag gi lus 'di sangs rgyas byams pa'i slob ma rnams skyo bar bya ba'i phyir byams pa'i bstan pa rgyas kyi bar du ri kha zum ste ri'i dbus su ma nyams par gnas par gyur cig rgyal po ma skyes dgra lus bltar 'ongs na ri rnams bye nas mthong bar gyur cig /tshe'i 'du byed btang ma thag tu sa g.yo ba la sogs pa'i ltas sna tshogs 'byung bar gyur cig snyam du bsams nas glog 'byin pa la sogs pa'i cho 'phrul sna tshogs bstan te rang gi lus byin gyis brlabs nas ston pas gnang ba'i na bza' phyag dar khrod kyis lus dang gsil byed dang lhung bzed rnams btums te glo g.yas pa phab rkang pa'i steng du rkang pa bzhag nas nyal te mya ngan las 'das so/ / gang gi tshe sangs rgyas byams pa byon pa de'i tshe byams pa 'dus pa dang po'i nyan thos kyi dge 'dun bye ba phrag dgu bcu rtsa drug dang bcas pa ri bya rkang can du gshegs nas ri gsum bsal te byams pas 'od srungs chen po'i rus pa phyag tu bsnams nas chos bstan pas nyan thos bye ba phrag dgu bcu rtsa drug gis dgra bcom 'thob par gsungs la/ snying rje chen po pad+ma dkar po'i mdo las byams pa'i 'dus pa gnyis pa nyan thos bye ba phrag dgu bcu rtsa bzhi dang*/ 'dus pa gsum pa nyan thos bye ba phrag dgu bcu rtsa gnyis te/ 'dus pa gsum char la 'od srungs chen po'i lus byams pas bstan nas gdul bya mang po'i don byed par gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / kha cig 'od srungs chen po mya ngan las 'das par bshad pa ni theg chung pa'i lugs yin gyi theg chen pa ni 'gog pa la snyoms par zhugs par bzhed do/ / zhes gsungs pa ni mi rigs te/ snying rje chen po pad+ma dkar po las kyang mya ngan las 'das pa kho nar gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Then Mahākāśyapa went to Birdsfoot Peak, and near the central peak of the three peaks he arranged straw, sat down, and reflected on the purpose of creating disgust [for existence] in the students of Buddha Maitreya and spreading the teachings of Maitreya. Then the mountain enveloped him, and he remained within the mountain without physical degeneration. When King Ajātaśatru came to look at the body, the mountain opened and he saw Mahākāśyapa.
Immediately after he [mentally] relinquished his composite of lifespan, Mahākāśyapa reflected, “May many omens such as earthquakes and so on occur,” and he revealed various miracles such as lightning and so on. Then he empowered his body, held the robes given to him by the Buddha, and with a layer of dust covering his body, staff, and bowl, he lay down on his right side, placing one leg on the other, and attained nirvāṇa.[1842] When Buddha Maitreya appears on earth, Maitreya along with 960 million śrāvaka saṅgha of the first assembly will go to Birdsfoot Peak, and [640] the three peaks will open. Maitreya will hold the relics of Mahākāśyapa in his hand and teach Dharma to the assembly, and 960 million śrāvakas will obtain the state of arhat. The White Lotus of Great Compassion Sūtra states: In the second assembly of Maitreya there will be 940 million śrāvakas, and in the third assembly there will be 920 million śrāvakas. Maitreya will demonstrate the body of Mahākāśyapa to the third assembly and fulfill the purpose of many disciples.[1843] Some say: The explanation that Mahākāśyapa attained nirvāṇa is the system of the Hīnayāna. The Mahāyāna asserts this to be the meditative attainment of cessation.

shi nas byin gyis brlabs pa de yang kha che ba rus pa lta bu brtan pa la yod kyi mi brtan pa sha khrag dang pags pa la sogs pa la med de/ de'i phyir 'od srungs kyi yang keng rus 'ba' zhig gnas kyi sha la sogs pa byin gyis ma brlabs pa'i phyir ro zhes 'dod la/ gzhan dag na re shi ba las ni byin rlabs yod pa min gyi 'od srungs kyi keng rus gnas pa ni gnas gtsang ma'i lha rnams kyi mthus gnas pa yin no zhes 'dod do/ / 'o na sprul sems gcig gis du ma sprul lam gcig gis gcig kho na sprul zhe na/

Reply: This is illogical, because the White Lotus of Great Compassion Sūtra clearly reveals that he attained nirvāṇa.[1844] Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas assert that such a blessing after death exists for stable objects such as the bones but does not exist for unstable (nāsthira) objects such as flesh, blood, skin, and so on. Therefore the blessing abides on the skeleton of Mahākāśyapa but not on the flesh and so on. Others assert that blessing after death does not exist. Instead, the blessing remained on the skeleton of Mahākāśyapa due to the might of the gods of the pristine abodes. Question: Does one emanating mind project many emanations, or does one mind project one alone?

dang por te ma byang ba'i tshe ni sprul sems du mas sprul pa gcig sprul pa yin te/ yun ring du 'bad dgos pa'i phyir ro/ / phyis mngon shes byang bar gyur nas ni snga ma las bzlog pa sprul sems gcig gis du ma sprul par byed do/ / zhes sprul sems thams cad lung ma bstan yin nam zhe na/

Reply: At first, when he is not trained, many emanating minds project one emanation, because exertion must be applied for a long time. Later, once trained in higher perception, he stops (viparyaya) the earlier method and projects many emanations with one mind. Question: Are all minds of emanation neutral?
bsgoms las skyes pa lung ma bstan/ / skye ba las skyes rnam gsum mo/ / rdzu 'phrul gsang sngags sman dag dang / / las las skyes dang rnam pa lnga/ / 53
Any arisen from meditation is neutral. That arisen from birth has three types. Supernatural powers have five types including arisen from mantras, medicines, and karma. (7:53)

bsgoms pa las skyes pa'i sprul sems gang yin pa de ni nges par lung ma bstan yin la/ {sa gong mar skyes pas kyang 'og ma'i de mngon du byed pa'i phyir ro } lha klu dang sha za la sogs pa'i skye ba las skye shing thob pa'i sprul sems ni phan pa dang gnod pa bya ba'i phyir sprul par byed pa dang btang snyoms pa yin pa'i phyir dge mi dge lung ma bstan rnam pa gsum mo/ / lha klu la sogs pa de dag gis byas pa'i sprul pa rang dang gzhan gyi rgyu dang 'brel ba ni sgra ma gtogs pa'i gzugs can gyi skye mched thams cad yin pa'i phyir skye mched dgu pa yin no/ / dbang po dang tha mi dad pa'i phyir de skad du brjod kyi dbang po ni dngos su na sems can du ston pa kho na yin pas sngon med pa'i sems can 'byung bar thal bar 'gyur ba'i phyir sprul par mi byed do/ / sprul pa sems med yin pa'i phyir yid dang chos kyi skye mched dag kyang sprul par mi byed do/ /

Reply: Any emanating mind that is arisen from meditation is certainly neutral {because those arisen in higher realms manifest those of lower level}. The emanating mind arisen and obtained from birth as gods, nāgas, gandharvas, and so on has three types — virtuous, nonvirtuous, and neutral — because they emanate to benefit or harm or else they stem from equanimity. The emanations projected by those gods and nāgas and so on that are causally related to oneself or another consist of nine bases (āyatana); they constitute all physical bases except for sound. This is stated because sentient beings do not exist separately from the faculties (indriya), and since only sentient beings are explicitly taught to have faculties, they are not taken to be emanations. If they did, it would then follow that sentient beings who did not previously exist would arise. Also, the bases of mind and phenomena are not taken to be emanations because emanations do not have mind.
sprul pa sems med yin par ni

gdags pa las/ sprul pa de 'byung ba chen po bzhi las gyur pa zhes brjod par bya'am/ 'byung ba chen po bzhi las gyur pa ma yin zhes brjod par bya/ smras pa/ 'byung ba chen po bzhi las gyur pa'o zhes brjod par bya'o/ / rgyur byas pa'i gzugs can nam/ rgyur byas pa'i gzugs can ma yin pa zhes brjod par bya/ smras pa/ rgyur byas pa'i gzugs can no zhes brjod par bya ste/ sems med pa zhes kyang brjod par bya'o/ / sprul pa gang gi sems kyi dbang gis 'jug par bya zhes brjod par bya/ smras pa/ sprul pa ni gnyis te/ skyes nas thob pa dang*/ bsgoms pa las byung ba'o/ / de la dang po ni sems can de'i sems kyi dbang gis 'gyur la/ gnyis pa ni sprul pa po'i sems kyi dbang gis 'jug go zhes brjod par bya'o zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / des na 'di ni sgom byung gi dbang du byas kyi skyes thob ni de nyid las/ sprul pa sems yod pa zhes bya'am med pa zhes bya zhe na/ sprul pa ni gnyis te/ skyes nas thob pa dang*/ bsgoms pa las byung ba'o/ / de la skyes thob ni sems yod pa zhes bya la/ sgom byung ni sems med pa zhes bya'o/ / zhes skyes thob la sems yod par bshad do/ / de bzhin du sprul pas kha zas zos pa na skyes thob kyi ni sprul pa nyid kyi ltor 'ju la sgom byung gi ni sprul pa po'i ltor 'ju bar bshad do/ / des na rang gzhan gyi lus dang 'brel ba'i sprul pa ni skye mched dgu pa yin la/ rang gzhan gyi lus dang ma 'brel ba'i sprul pa ni sngar bshad pa ltar skye mched bzhi pa kho na yin no zhes shes par bya'o/ / ci rdzu 'phrul sgom byung dang skye thob kho nar zad dam zhe na ma zad de/

As Presentation on Karma states: Should we say that emanations are derived from the four great elements? Or should we say they do not arise from the four great elements? We should say they are derived from the four great elements. [641] Should we say they possess derivative form? Or should we say they do not possess derivative form? We should say that they possess derivative form. And we should say they have no mind. What emanations are engaged by the power of mind? Emanations have two types: (1) those obtained from birth and (2) those derived from meditation. The first arises by the power of the mind of that sentient being. The second is engaged by the power of the mind of the emanator.[1845] This is stated from the perspective of emanations derived from meditation. Regarding emanations obtained from birth, this text states: Should we say that emanations have mind? Or should we say emanations do not have mind? Emanations are of two types: (1) those obtained from birth and (2) those derived from meditation. Those obtained from birth have mind, whereas those derived from meditation have no mind.[1846] This passage explains that emanations obtained from birth have mind. So too, it explains that if the emanation eats food, it is an emanation obtained from birth that digests food, but if it is an emanation derived from meditation, then it digests the food of the emanator. Therefore, as explained before, an emanation related to the body of oneself or another has nine bases, and an emanation not related to the body of oneself or another has four bases alone. Question: Why are supernatural powers just derived from meditation or obtained at birth alone? Reply: They are not just that.

rdzu 'phrul ni snga ma gnyis po de dag dang*/ g+han+d+ha ri la sogs pa'i gsang sngags las skyes pa dang*/ rus sbal gyi ze ba dang rma bya'i mdongs la sogs pa'i sman dag las skyes pa dang*/ rgyal po nga las nu dang bar srid pa rnams kyi lta bu las las skyes pa dang rnam pa lnga yin no zhes shes par bya'o/ / lha'i rna ba dang mig tu bshad pa gang yin pa de dag ci lha'i dngos yin nam/ 'on te byang chub sems dpa' dang 'khor los bsgyur ba dang khyim bdag rin po che rnams kyi mig ltar lha'i dang 'dra bas btags nas de skad du brjod ce na/

Supernatural powers (ṛddhi) should be understood as five types: (1–2) the former two; (3) those arisen from secret mantra, such as gandharvas and so on; (4) those arisen from medicines (auṣadha), such as the jewel of a tortoise, the eye of a peacock, and so on; and (5) those arisen from karma, such as those of King Māndhātṛ, intermediate beings, and so on. Question: Are any states that are called divine eyes and ears actually divine, or are they designated “divine” since the eyes of bodhisattvas, cakravartins, and special householders are like those of the gods?
lha yi mig dang rna ba yin/ / bsam gtan sa pa'i gzugs dang ba/ / rtag tu rten bcas ma tshang med/ / thag ring phra sogs spyod yul can/ / 54
They are divine eyes and ears, translucent form of the level of the absorptions. They are always homogeneous, unimpaired, and possess object fields such as the distant and subtle. (7:54)

de gnyis ni lha'i mig dang lha'i rna ba dngos kho na yin te/ bsam gtan pa dag bsam gtan la mnyam par bzhag nas sgra dang snang ba la gtod pa'i sbyor ba'i stobs kyis mig dang rna ba'i thon kor du bsam gtan gyi sa pa'i 'byung bzhi rgyur byas pa'i gzugs can dang ba { sha dang pags pa dang rus pa dang khrag dang ma 'brel zhing*/ lha'i mig gis rgyab phyogs su'ang mthong la shas mi mthong ba khyad par ro/ /} thag ring po na gnas pa dang chod pa dang phra ba'i gzugs dang sgra thos pa'i rgyur gyur pa'i dbang po 'grub pas bsam gtan gyi sa pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / lha'i mig dang rna ba de gnyis kyang gzugs nyams su myong ba'i sgo nas bsgrubs pa'i phyir rtag tu rnam shes dang bcas pas brten pa dang bcas pa kho na yin la/ gtan med pa'i zhar ba dang nong pa yo ba dang 'on pa lta bu ma yin pas ma tshang ba med pa'ang yin no/ / de gnyis kyi yul ni gzugs sgra thag ring ba dang phra ba dang sogs pas bsdus pa bsgribs pa'i spyod yul can yang yin pas sha'i mig las khyad par du 'phags te/ gang phyir sha'i mig gis gzugs/ / thag ring gnas dang sgrib pa dang*/ / phra dang thams cad mi mthong ba/ / de phyir lha yis mthong bar 'dod ces 'grel pa las 'byung ba bzhin no/ / 'o na lha'i mig gis ji tsam mthong zhe na/

Reply: These two are actual divine eyes and divine ears because they are the translucent form (rūpaprasāda)[1847] derived from the four primary elements of the level of absorption (dhyānabhūmika), which is the source of such eyes and ears. They are also derived through those abiding in the absorptions who engage in equipoise on the absorptions, strongly directing their minds to sound and appearance. {That form is not related to flesh, skin, bones, or blood; it sees by way of the divine eye and not the flesh.} Existing on the level of the absorptions, they establish faculties that are the cause of seeing form and hearing sound that is distant, concealed, and subtle. Both the divine eye and ear are always associated with consciousness because they are established through the experience of form. Therefore they are solely homogeneous (sabhāga). They are unimpaired (avikala) since they are never blind, mistaken, distorted, or deaf. They possess obscure object fields (gocara) such as distant and subtle form [642] and sound. Therefore they surpass the flesh eye. As the Autocommentary observes: Why does the flesh eye not see any form that is distant, obscured, or subtle? That is because these are seen by the divine eye.[1848] Question: What does the divine eye see?
dgra bcom bse ru ston rnams kyis/ / stong gnyis gsum dang grangs med mthong/ / gzhan yang skye bas thob des ni/ / srid pa bar ma mi mthong ngo/ / 55
Arhats, rhinoceros, and the Master see a dichiliocosm, trichiliocosm, or countless realms. Others are also obtained from birth. It does not see intermediate beings. (7:55)

bsam gtan dang po'i lha'i mig gis 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang po mthong ba la sogs pa sngar bshad zin to/ / nyan rang sangs rgyas gsum gyi lha'i mig mngon par 'du byed pa med pas ni rim pa ltar stong dang stong gnyis dang stong gsum gyi 'jig rten gyi khams mthong la/ mngon par 'du byed pa'i stobs kyis ni rim pa ltar dgra bcom pa rnams kyis stong gnyis dang bse ru lta bu'i rang rgyal rnams kyis stong gsum dang ston pa sangs rgyas rnams kyis ni ji tsam bzhed pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams grangs med pa mthong ngo*/ /

Reply: As previously mentioned, the divine eye of the first absorption sees the desire realm and the first absorption and so on. The divine eyes of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and buddhas, respectively, see the world systems of the first chiliocosm, the dichiliocosm, and the trichiliocosm without applying exertion. But through strong exertion, respectively, arhats see a dichiliocosm, rhinoceros-like pratyekabuddhas see a trichiliocosm, and the Master Buddha sees countless world systems that exist.

ci rdzu 'phrul kho na skyes thob yin nam/ 'on te gzhan yang skyes thob yin zhe na/ rdzu 'phrul las gzhan lha'i mig dang rna ba dang sngon gnas rjes dran dang pha rol sems shes bzhi la yang skye bas thob pa yod mod kyi{ de ni 'gro ba de thams cad kyis skyes pa'i dus nyid na rang bzhin gyis thob pa yin gyi kha cig gam bya nam mkha' la 'gro ba ltar skyes pa'i 'og tu thob pa ni ma yin no/ / rdzu 'phrul ni lnga ste 'di rtog ges byas pa med do/ / mig dang rna ba'i mngon shes gsum ste/ sngags dang sman las byung ba ma gtogs so/ / sems shes ni bzhi ste sman las byung ba med do/ / dge ba 'dis sems can thams cad sangs rgyas thob pa'i rgyur ces kyang gyur cig /'di bzhi skye bas thob pa ni ma yin no/ / 'di bzhi skyes pas thob pa ni 'dod pa'i lha klu dang gzugs kyi lha rnams la yod do/ /}

Question: Why is supernatural power alone obtained from birth, or are others also obtained from birth? Reply: Four — divine eye, ear, recalling past lives, and knowledge of others’ minds — that are other than supernatural power are indeed also obtained from birth. {Some say they are naturally obtained by all reincarnating beings at the time of birth, but like a bird who takes to the sky they are not retained subsequent to birth. Supernatural power has five, and it is not produced by logical reasoning. The higher perceptions of eye and ear have three: those except being derived from mantra or medicine. Knowledge of others’ minds has four: those except being derived from medicine. Those who dedicate this virtue as a cause for all sentient beings obtaining buddhahood do not obtain these four from birth. Desire gods, nāgas, and form gods possess these four from birth.}

'on kyang skyes thob kyis ni cung zad kyang mngon shes kyi ming mi 'thob bo/ / skyes thob kyi lha'i mig gang yin pa des ni srid pa bar ma mi mthong ste/ de ni skyon bcu gcig dang bral ba mngon par shes pa'i lha'i mig rnam par dag pa kho na'i yul yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de la lha'i mig skyes thob ni klu dang 'dod gzugs kyi lha rnams la yod do/ / gzugs med na ni mngon shes lnga dang skyes thob kyang med de/ TI ka las/ gzugs med na mngon shes lnga dang skyes thob thams cad med de/ gzugs med pa'i phyir dang*/ de lta bu'i lus yang dag par mi 'grub pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

However, that obtained from birth does not obtain the name of higher perception in the least. Any divine eye obtained from birth does not see intermediate beings (antarabhāva) because they are the object of the pure divine eye that is higher perception entirely free of the eleven faults. Nāgas, desire gods, and form-realm gods obtain the divine eye from birth. Five higher perceptions and those obtained from birth do not exist in the formless realm: as the Subcommentary declares: Five sublime knowledges and all those derived from birth do not exist in the formless realm because there is no form there, and no appropriate body is established there.[1849]
sems shes de ni rnam gsum gang / / rtog dang rig sngags kyis byas pa'ang / / dmyal ba pas ni dang po shes/ / mi la skye bas thob pa med/ / 56
Knowledge of others’ minds has three types, as does that produced by logical reasoning and mantra. Hell beings know from the first moment. Humans do not obtain them from birth. (7:56)

{skyes thob kyi chos kyi khyad par la } pha rol sems shes skyes thob de ni dge mi dge lung ma bstan rnam pa gsum mo/ gang yang rtog ge ba rnams kyi mtshan ma las sems shes pa dang rig sngags kyis byas pa'i sems shes pa de yang dge mi dge lung ma bstan rnam pa gsum yin la sems shes sgom byung ni dge ba kho na yin no/ / pha rol sems shes dang sngon gnas rjes dran skyes thob ni dmyal ba pas ni dang po skyes nas ji srid du sdug bsngal gyi tshor bas ma nyan pa de srid du pha rol kyi sems dang sngon gyi gnas shes kyi phyis ni sdug bsngal gyi tshor bas nyen pa yid nyams par byas pa'i phyir{ bdag kyang ma dran} mi shes so/ / 'gro ba gzhan lha dang dud 'gro dang yi dwags kyi pha rol sems shes dang sngon gnas rjes dran skyes thob kyis ni sdug bsngal gyi tshor bas ma nyen pas rtag tu shes so/ / de la re zhig lhas ni mdo las/ drang srong tshogs kyis bsten pa dang*/ / chos kyi rgyal po bzhugs gyur cing*/ / bdag la dga' ba bskyed pa yi/ / rgyal byed tshal de 'di yin no zhes pa dang*/ bdag gang nas shi 'phos gang du skyes gang gi sa skyes zhes gnas gsum shes par bshad pa lta bu'o/ / dud 'gros kyang shes te klu la sogs pa bzhin no/ / yi dwags kyis kyang shes te/ ji skad du/ bdag gi mthun dang mi mthun pas/ / longs spyod dag ni gang bas gsar/ / de dag gzhan gyis longs spyad de/ / kho bo cag ni sdug bsngal bsten/ / zhes 'byung ba bzhin no/ /

{Regarding specific attributes obtained from birth,} knowledge of others’ minds that is obtained from birth has three types: virtuous, nonvirtuous, and neutral. As does the knowledge of others’ minds produced through the signs of logical reasoning (tarka) and knowledge of others’ minds produced through mantra. But the knowledge of others’ minds derived from meditation is virtuous alone. Hell beings (nāraka) who obtain knowledge of others’ minds and the recall of past lives from birth know others’ minds and past lives from the first moment of birth for as long as they are not oppressed by feelings of suffering. [643] Later, when oppressed, such minds (manas) degenerate, and they do not know others’ minds or lives {or even their own selves}. Other reincarnating beings such as gods, animals, and ghosts who obtain knowledge of others’ minds and the recall of past lives from birth fully know such things when not oppressed by feelings of suffering. In this regard a sūtra mentions: It was just so in Jeta’s grove where the king of Dharma dwelled served by the assembly of rishis generating joy within us. And: I know from where I died, where I was reborn, and on what level I was reborn.[1850] This explains that gods know the three abodes. Also animals know this, like nāgas. Ghosts know this, for it is said: Due to appropriate and inappropriate actions, at first I accumulated wealth, but when it was enjoyed by others, I came to experience suffering.[1851]

mi rnams la ni rdzu 'phrul la sogs pa sngar ji skad bshad pa de dag bsgoms pa las byung ba dang rtog ge dang rig sngags dang sman dang las las skyes pa rnams yod kyi de dag skye bas thob pa ni med de/ skyes pa tsam gyis mi ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na rang bzhin gyis tshe rabs dran pa de ji lta bu zhe na/ de ni las kyi khyad par las skyes pa yin te/ rin po che'i phreng ba las/ chos kyi ched dang de bzhin du/ / gzhung gi don dag dran pa dang*/ / chos kyi sbyin pa dri med pas/ / tshe rabs dran pa thob par 'gyur zhes 'byung ba bzhin no/ /

Humans (nṛṇā) have those previously explained higher perceptions, such as supernatural power derived from meditation and arisen from logical reasoning, mantra, medicine, and karma. But they do not obtain them from birth because they do not possess them merely through taking birth. As the Precious Garland observes: One obtains the recall of past lives through [serving] the purpose of Dharma, through recalling the meaning of texts, and through stainlessly giving the Dharma.[1852]
de'i phyir sngon gnas rjes dran ni bsgoms pa las byung ba dang*/ skyes thob dang las las skyes pa dang gsum yod par rig par bya'o/ /
Therefore recalling past lives should be understood as three types: derived from meditation, obtained from birth, and generated from karma.
bzed dang bshes pa lta ba'i bye brag dang*/ / shes pa'i rang bzhin ji snyed ldan tshul dang*/ / shes pas bsdus pa'i yon tan rnam pa gnyis/ / shes shing thob 'dod gnas 'di mnyan par gyis/ /

Those who desire knowledge and its obtainment should listen to this part that elucidates perseverance, knowledge, and specific views, the nature of knowledge, how one comes to possess it, and the two types of qualities subsumed by knowledge.
chos mngon pa'i mdzod kyi tshig le'ur byas pa las/ ye shes bstan pa zhes bya ba ste gnas bdun pa'o// //
chos mngon pa'i mdzod kyi 'grel pa mngon pa'i rgyan las ye shes bstan pa zhes bya ba ste gnas bdun pa'i bshad pa'o// ! //
This has been part VII, the “Exposition of Epistemology,” from Ornament of Abhidharma: A Commentary on the Verses of the Abhidharmakośa. [644]
gnas brgyad pa snyoms 'jug bstan pa/
34. Absorption and Formless States
THE EXPOSITION OF MEDITATIVE ATTAINMENT

gnas brgyad pa 'chad pa na de ltar shes pa'i rang bzhin gyi yon tan {stobs nas mngon shes kyi bar } rnams bshad nas/ {de dag kyang mnyam par bzhag las 'byung bas } da ni bsam gtan dang gzugs med la sogs pa shes pa las gzhan ting nge 'dzin la sogs pas bsdus pa'i yon tan rnams bshad par bya ste/

The essential qualities of knowledge {from the powers to the higher perceptions} have already been explained. Now we will explain the qualities of the absorptions and the formless-realm states and so on as well as the qualities subsumed by concentration that are distinct from knowledge and so forth {since they are derived from equipoise}.
de la'ang bsam gtan dang gzugs med bshad pa dang*/ de la brten pa'i yon tan bshad pa gnyis las/
This has two headings: (1) absorptions and formless-realm states, and (2) qualities dependent on them.
dang po
ABSORPTIONS AND FORMLESS-REALM STATES
['di] la'ang ngo bo dang*/ dbye ba dang*/ yan lag rnam par bzhag pa dang*/ 'thob pa'i tshul dang*/ khyad par gyi chos dang*/ nyer bsdogs dang*/ ting nge 'dzin gyi dbye ba bshad pa bdun las/
This has seven headings: (1) definitions, (2) classification, (3) branches, (4) obtainment, (5) specific attributes, (6) access to higher levels, and (7) classifications of concentration.
ngo bo bshad pa/
Definitions of the absorptions and formless-realm states
dang po la'ang gzugs med rnams kyang yon tan gyi rten yin mod kyi yon tan thams cad kyi rten ma yin la/
Indeed, formless-realm states act as the basis of qualities, but they do not act as the basis for all qualities.
bsam gtan rnams ni yon tan thams cad kyi rten yin pa'am dang por bshad pa la
Therefore the absorptions are explained first, since they act as the basis for all qualities {and this accords with the order in which they arise}.
bsam gtan dag ni rnam gnyis bzhi/ / der skye ba dag rab tu bshad/ / snyoms 'jug dge ba rtse gcig pa/ / rjes 'brang bcas na phung po lnga/ / 1

The absorptions have two or four types. Those generated there were properly explained. Meditative attainment is the same as single-pointed virtuous mind. If it possesses a complement, it has five aggregates. (8:1)
bsam gtan dag ni
ABSORPTIONS

mdor bsdus na 'bras bu skye ba dang*/ rgyu soms par 'jug pa rnam pa gnyis yin la/ / {'di gnyis kyi khyad par bod kha cig /rang sa kho nar mngon du 'gyur ba ni 'bras bu'o/ / 'og sar mngon du byed pa ni rgyu'o/ / mnyam gzhag kho na yin pa ni rgyu'o/ / gnyis ka yin pa ni 'bras bu'o/ / dge ba kho na yin pa ni rgyu'o/ / dge ba dang lung ma bstan yang yin pa ni 'bras bu'o/ / sgom byung kho na yin pa ni rgyu'o/ / deng thos byung dang skyes thob kyang yin pa ni 'bras bu'o/ / tshe ji srid par rgyun chags pa ni 'bras bu'o/ / res 'ga' ba ni rgyu'o/ / nyer bsdogs dang bcas pa ni rgyu'o/ / dngos gzhi kho na yin pa ni 'bras bu'o/ / 'og ma'i rten la'ang gong ma'i ting nge 'dzin skyer rung ba ni rgyu'o/ / de'i 'bras bu gong ma'i phung po snod dang bcas pa ni 'bras bu'o zhes so }

If summarized the absorptions (dhyāna) have two types: resultant-birth meditative attainment, and causal meditative attainment. {Regarding the difference between them, one Tibetan says: That which manifests on one’s level alone is resultant; that which manifests on lower level is causal. That which is equipoise alone is causal; that which is both is resultant. That which is virtuous alone is causal; that which is virtuous and also neutral is resultant. That which is derived from meditation alone is causal; that which is now derived from hearing and obtained from birth is resultant. That which continues for as long as one lives is resultant; that which is intermittent is causal. That which is associated with access concentration is causal; that which is an actual basis alone is resultant. That which is suitable to arise as higher concentration on a lower basis is causal; the higher aggregates that are the result of what is associated with the environment are resultant.}

de dag re re zhing yang sa'i sgo nas rgyas par dbye na bsam gtan dang po nas bzhi pa'i bar rnam pa bzhi bzhi yin no/ / de la 'bras bu bsam gtan dang po la sogs{ skyes rim ltar} pa der skye ba'i bsam gtan dag ni/ gnas gsum par so so yi/ / bsam gtan sa ni gsum pa yin/ / bzhi pa sa ni brgyad pa yin zhes rab tu ste dang por bshad zin la/ rgyu snyoms 'jug gi bsam gtan thams cad kyang gtso bo ting nge 'dzin gyi rang bzhin yin zhing*/ ting nge 'dzin thams cad kyi rang bzhin mtshan nyid kyang rtse gcig pa yin pas nyon mongs can dang{ g.yo ba'i dge ba dang} ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gyi sems rtse gcig pa'ang yod pas de dag bcas pa'i phyir dge ba'i sems rtse ste dmigs pa gcig par byed pa'i sems byung yin gyi sems dmigs pa gcig pa tsam ni ma yin no/ / de nyid rjes su 'brang ba'i 'khor dang bcas na ni gzugs bsam gtan zag med kyi sdom pa gang rung yang yod pas phung po lnga'i rang bzhin no/ / ting nge 'dzin dang mtshungs ldan thams cad dmigs pa la rtse gcig bzhin du sems kho na la dmigs pa la rtse gcig pa zhes brjod pa ni gtso bo yin pa'i phyir ro zhes TIka byed dag 'chad do/

If each is extensively classified by means of its supportive field or level, then there are four types, from the first absorption to the fourth absorption. Absorptions arisen there, in the first resultant absorption and so on, were first properly explained in part III, where the Abhidharmakośa declares, “Each absorption level has three stages. The fourth level has eight” (3:2bcd).[1853] Every absorption of causal meditative attainment (samāpatti) has concentration as its primary nature, and the essential defining characteristic of all concentration is single-pointed engagement. Therefore [causal meditative attainment] is defined [645] as “the mental factor single-pointedly engaging the same focal object [as its concomitant] virtuous mind, which also exists [in the retinue of] single-pointed afflicted minds, {mutable virtuous minds,} and unobscured-neutral minds.” A mind with merely the same focal object as [that concentration] is not [causal meditative attainment]. If it possesses a complement (sānuga), by nature it has five aggregates, since it has either vows of the form-realm absorptions or those of the formless realm. Pūrṇavardhana’s commentary explains: All states concomitant with concentration are single-pointed toward their focal object, but only the mind itself is called “single-pointed toward its focal object” because it is the primary state.[1854]

{Vasubandhu notes:} Someone may say, “Since all minds are momentary they cannot be single pointed because they do not have time to change their focal object; or, due to that, one should identify {something besides} concentration {that has the specific property} of making [the mind] single-pointed. For [concentration] would lack that capacity.” But that is not so, because though [making the mind single-pointed] is not necessary in the first moment of mind, that capacity exists; for the second moment of mind, {which focuses on the object of the first moment,} is not distracted from its focal object due to concentration that possesses that object. [In response it may be said:] “But that [is not so]. Concentration would then serve no purpose for the mind of the first [moment] concomitant with concentration {because it would not perform that function}. It would also be contradictory for concentration of the first moment to engage in action in the second moment if it had already ceased at the time of the second moment. And if it had not ceased, it would not be synchronous with the mind of the former moment.[1855] Moreover, if the mind can be made single-pointed — merely by reason of mindfulness not degenerating and so on or merely by reason of asserting concentration to be single-pointed — there would be no point in identifying something besides concentration as its cause.
