And if these cannot make [the mind single-pointed], then that would also apply to concentration itself.[1856] Furthermore, since concentration is a universal mental state, it would follow that {all} minds would become single-pointed.”[1857] Vaibhāṣikas assert: This is not so. The mind concomitant with strong concentration is single-pointed, and the mind concomitant with weak concentration is not single-pointed. Concentration that is the mere universal mental state, because it is weak, is not ascertained to be solely virtuous.[1858]

mdo sde pa na re sems rtse gcig pa kho na ting nge 'dzin yin gyi sems las don gzhan du gyur pa'i ting nge 'dzin ni med de/ lam gyi tshogs kyi bslab pa'i sgo'i mdo las/ lhag pa'i sems kyi bslab pa gang zhe na/ bsam gtan bzhi'o zhes pa dang*/ stag gi byang chub kyi bu'i mdo dang*/ nyan thos kyi rnam par bshad pa las/ sems yongs su dag pa'i gtso bo ni bsam gtan bzhi yin no zhes ji ltar tshul khrims dang shes rab kyi bslab pa tshul khrims dang shes rab kho na yin pa ltar sems kyi bslab pa'ang sems kho nar gsungs so zer ro/ / sgra'i don ci'i phyir bsam gtan zhes bya zhe na/ 'dis mchog tu sems par byed pas bsam gtan te mnyam par bzhag na yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin rab tu shes pa'i phyir rab tu shes pa'i byed ces bya ba'i tha tshig go /gal te sems par byed pa bsam gtan yin na ting nge 'dzin {nyon mongs can sogs } thams cad bsam gtan du thal bar 'gyur ro zhe na/ ma yin te/ phul du phyin pa dang ldan pa'i sems par byed pa'i ting nge 'dzin la bsam gtan du brjod de nya mi la snang ldan zhes brjod pa bzhin no/ / phul du phyin pa'i sems par byed pa'ang 'dir yan lag dang ldan pas rta gnyag sbrel bas 'dren pa'i shing rta ltar zhi gnas dang lhag mthong zung du 'brel bar ngang gis 'byung ba la 'dod de/ de'i phyir mdo las/ mthong ba'i chos la bde bar gnas pa dang*/ lam sla ba zhes gsungs so/ / 'o na mchog tu sems pa med pas nyon mongs can bsam gtan du mi 'gyur ro zhe na/ de la'ang log par nges par sems pa yod pas de dang 'dra ba tsam la de skad du brjod de sa bon rul ba bzhin no/ / {mi dge ba'i bsam gtan yod pa } bcom ldan 'das kyis kyang tshangs pa'i tshogs kyi mdo las/ mi dge ba'i bsam gtan sgrib pa lnga las skyes shing nges par 'byung ba mi shes la de dag gis bar du gcod cing bsgom ste bsngags par mi 'os pa'i bsam gtan gyi bsngags pa mi gsung ngo zhes gsungs so/ /

Sautrāntikas say: It is the mind’s single-pointed nature alone that is concentration; there is no concentration separate from the mind. As Entering Training on Multiple Paths Sūtra states: What is the higher training of the mind? It is the four absorptions.[1859] The Offspring of the Tiger’s Enlightenment Sūtra and the Śrāvaka Exposition say: The main factor that thoroughly purifies the mind is the four absorptions.[1860] Just as the higher training in ethics and wisdom is ethics and wisdom alone, so too the higher training of mind also is stated to be the mind alone. [646] Question: Why is absorption said to be the meaning of the term mind? Reply: This signifies that absorption is the supreme mental application, and it is full knowledge because [the mind] in equipoise fully knows reality as it is. Objection: If mental application is absorption, then it would follow that all concentration would be absorption, {whether afflicted and so on}. Reply: That is not so. Concentration that is mental application possessing superior attainment is called absorption, just as the sun is called Radiant One. Also, the mental application of superior attainment here refers to that which possesses attributes, and it arises by means of the union of calm abiding and insight, just as a cart is drawn by yoking it to the neck of the horse. Therefore a sūtra states: In this life it is that which abides in comfort and easily attains the path.[1861] Objection: Afflicted states would not become absorption since they lack supreme mental application. Reply: Some states that bear a mere resemblance to it are called mental application since wrong mental application exists, just as a decayed seed is called a seed. {That nonvirtuous absorption exists} is declared by the Bhagavan in the Assembly of Brahma Sūtra: Nonvirtuous absorptions arise from the five obscurations. Since they do not know renunciation they obstruct, and meditation on them is not praiseworthy. Therefore such absorptions should not be praised.[1862]
dpyod dang dga' dang bde dang ldan/ / yan lag snga snga spangs pa yi/ / de bzhin gzugs med phung po bzhi/ /
It possesses analysis, joy, and pleasure. They progressively abandon the former branches. So too, formless states have four aggregates. (8:2abc)
'o na bsam gtan dang po la sogs pa de dag ji lta bu zhe na/
Question: What are the first absorption and so on like?

bsam gtan dang po ni sa de na du ba la mes khyab pa ltar lhan cig spyod pa yin pas rtog pa med par dga' bde dang ldan pa'i dpyod pa mi srid pas dpyod pa dang des mtshon pa'i rtog pa dang dga' ba dang bde ba dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i dge ba rtse gcig pa'o/ / de lta na lhan cig dpyod pas rtog pas dpyod pa'ang go bas rtog dang dga' dang bde dang ldan zhes ci'i phyir mi smros zhe na/ yan lag snga snga spangs pa yi zhes brjod pa na bsam gtan khyad par can yang gnyis par thal bar 'gyur ba spangs ba'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: The first absorption is single-pointed virtuous mind that possesses concomitance with analysis (vicāra), investigation characterized by that [analysis], joy (prīti), and pleasure (śubha). It is impossible for analysis possessing joy and pleasure to exist without investigation, for they are simultaneously activated, just as fire necessarily exists in a place where smoke exists. Question: Why does the Abhidharmakośa not say “concomitant with investigation, joy, and pleasure,” since analysis and investigation are simultaneously activated and analysis is understood from investigation? Reply: Stating “they progressively abandon the former branches (aṅga)” rebuts the consequence that the ordinary first absorption is special absorption or even the second absorption.

bsam gtan lhag ma gsum ni rim pa ltar yan lag snga ma snga ma rtog dpyod spangs shing dga' bde dang ldan pa dang*/ rtog dpyod dang dga' ba spangs shing bde ba dang ldan pa dang*/ rtog dpyod dang dga' bde spangs pa'i gzugs kyi dge ba rtse gcig pa'o/ /

Regarding the three remaining absorptions, the second progressively abandons the former branches of investigation and analysis and possesses joy and pleasure; the third abandons investigation, analysis, and joy and possesses pleasure; and the fourth is a single-pointed virtuous physical state that abandons investigation, analysis, joy, and pleasure.

ji ltar bsam gtan rnams 'bras bu skye ba dang rgyu snyoms 'jug gnyis dang re re la'ang bzhi bzhi yin pa de bzhin du gzugs med kyang rnam pa gnyis dang bzhi bzhi pa yin no/ / de la 'bras bu skye ba'i gzugs med ni gzugs med pa na gnas med do/ / skye ba las ni rnam pa bzhi zhes bshad zin la/ rgyu snyoms 'jug gi gzugs med kyang gzugs las 'dod chags dang bral ba'i snyoms 'jug dge ba rtse gcig pa'o/ / rjes su 'brang ba'i gzugs med pas 'khor dang bcas na ni phung po bzhi'o/ /

Just as the absorptions are divided into both resultant-birth meditative attainment and causal meditative attainment, and each division has four parts, so too formless-realm states have two divisions and four parts each. Formless-realm resultant-birth meditative attainment does not remain without form. The four from birth have been explained already. Formless-realm causal meditative attainment is single-pointed virtuous meditative attainment free of attachment to the form realm, for it has already been explained in the Abhidharmakośa that “It has four types through specific generation” (3:3b). If they have a retinue, they have four aggregates, since they have no physical complements.
bzhi po'i khyad par ni
DIFFERENCES AMONG THE FOUR FORMLESS STATES [647]
'og ma'i sa las dben las skyes/ / 2
By separation from lower levels and arising from access concentration. (8:2d)

lam gang gis bsam gtan bzhi pa la sogs pa 'og ma'i sa las dben pa ste rnam par 'byed cing 'dod chags dang 'bral ba'i nyer bsdogs bar chad med lam las skyes pa ni rim pa ltar nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched la sogs pa'o/ / {'di dag gi bar chad med lam gyi 'og sa las rgyal bar byed pa tsam du ma zad dmigs pa las kyang 'da' bar byed de gzugs med dmigs pa las nges par 'byung bas so }

The base of infinite space and so on [that is, the formless-realm states] are differentiated by their separation (viveka) from lower levels such as the fourth absorption and so forth, and arising (ja) from their respective uninterrupted paths that are access concentrations that free oneself from the attachment [to lower levels]. {They are not merely victorious over lower levels due to their uninterrupted paths; they also transcend their lower focal objects. Therefore formless-realm states definitely emerge [or separate] from lower-level focal objects.}
nyer bsdogs gsum dang bcas par ni/ / gzugs kyi 'du shes bshig ces bya/ / gzugs med pa na gzugs med do/ / gzugs ni sems las skye bar 'gyur/ / 3
They are called destroyers of the discernment of form, along with three access concentrations. There is no form in the formless realm. Form is generated from mind. (8:3)

gzugs med pa de dag kyang dngos gzhi bzhi nyer bsdogs phyi ma gsum dang bcas par ni{ dngos gzhi ni} rang sa na gzugs med cing 'og sa'i zag bcas kyi gzugs la mi dmigs {la nyer bsdogs ni rang gi 'og sa la dmigs kyang sa rgal nas mi dmigs } pas gzugs kyi 'du shes bshig pa zhes bya ste/ nam mkha' mtha' yas kyi nyer bsdogs na ni bsam gtan bzhi pa'i gzugs la dmigs nas rags sogs su {lta bas gang la dmigs pa de'i 'du shes 'byung } ba'i phyir gzugs kyi 'du shes yod pa'i phyir ro/{ 'di dag na'ang rjes shes pa drug gi rigs min pa la dmigs pa ni yod do/ /}

Such formless states are called destroyers (vibhūta) of the discernment of form (rūpasaṃjñā), since the four actual bases along with the latter three access concentrations focus on formless states of their level but do not focus on the form of lower material levels. {And though access concentrations focus on lower levels, they do not focus on them when they skip levels}. But the access concentration to infinite space possesses discernment of form because it views coarse states and so on through focusing on form of the fourth absorption, {and in focusing on form, it becomes discernment of form}.

'dir dge 'dun phal chen po'i bye brag 'jig rten las 'das par smra ba'i sde pa dang*/ thams cad yod smra'i bye brag gos dmar ba'i sde pa dang*/ mang pos bkur ba pa rnams gzugs med na'ang gzugs cung zad yod de/ lung bar ma'i bsus po che'i mdo las/ tshe dang ldan pa bsus po che tshe gang yin pa dang drod gang yin pa'i chos 'di dag ni 'dres pa ste ma 'dres pa ma yin no zhes tshe dang drod gnyis 'dres par gsungs shing*/ gzugs med na'ang tshe yod la tshe yod na drod kyang yod la drod ni gzugs yin pa'i phyir dang*/ de bzhin du tshe dang ldan pa shA ri'i bu dper na 'dam bu'i shog gnyis gnam du bsgreng ste phan tshun brten cing 'dug pa de la 'ga' zhig gis gcig bor na cig shos 'gyel bar 'gyur la/ cig shos bor na'ang cig shos 'gyel bar 'gyur ro/ / tshe dang ldan pa shA ri'i bu de bzhin du ming dang gzugs dag kyang phan tshun rten cing gnas so zhes pa dang*/ yang rten cing 'brel bar 'byung ba'i mdo las kyang nying mtshams sbyor ba'i mtshan nyid kyi skabs su rnam par shes pa'i rkyen gyis ming dang gzugs zhes ming gzugs phan tshun brten pa dang*/ rnam shes kyis ming gzugs bskyed par gsungs shing*/ gzugs med na'ang ming dang rnam shes yod pa'i phyir dang*/ rnam shes gnas pa bzhi ston pa'i mdo las/ dge slong dag rnam par shes pa gzugs su nye bar 'gro ba/ gzugs la dmigs pa/ gzugs la brten pa gnas so/ / dge slong dag gang la la zhig 'di skad du bdag ni gzugs dang tshor ba nas 'du byed kyi bar dag las gzhan du rnam par shes pa 'gro ba'am 'ong bar smra'o zhes zer na de'i ngag de ni de'i tshig tsam du zad do zhes gsungs te/ phung po bzhi las gzhan du rnam shes 'gro 'ong bkag pa'i phyir ro/ / gzugs med par bshad pa ni bu ngan pa rked pa phra ba la bu med pa dang rked med ces dman pa'am phra ba la dgag pa'i sgra brjod pa bzhin no zhes zer ro/ /

In this context the Lokottaravāda school (who are a subsect of the Mahāsāṃghika), the Tāmraśāṭīya school (who are a subsect of the Sarvāstivāda), and the Sammatīyā school state that even in the formless realm a degree of form exists, because (1) the Mahākoṣṭha Sūtra from the Medium-Length Discourses observes: Honorable Mahākoṣṭha, those phenomena consisting of life or heat are mixed; it is not that they are not mixed.[1863] This passage states that life and heat are mixed, and that even in the formless realm life exists, and that if life exists heat also exists, and heat is form. And (2) similarly: Venerable Śāriputra, take, for example, two cane stalks that are propped upright by leaning each against the other. If the first is removed, the second topples, and if the second is removed, the first topples. Venerable Śāriputra, similarly, name and form abide in mutual dependence.[1864] Again, (3) also Dependent Origination Sūtra proclaims, in the context of the characteristics of the links, that: Due to the condition of consciousness, name and form — in the link of name and form — depend on each other, and name and form are generated by consciousness.[1865] Thus, even when there is no form, both name and consciousness exist. And the Sūtra Teaching the Four Abodes of Consciousness states: Monks, consciousness approaches form, focuses on form, abides dependent on form. Monks, whoever declares that I have said that consciousness comes or goes by some means other than through form and feeling up to formation, such speech is mere heresay.[1866] That is stated to refute the assertion that consciousness goes and comes by some means other than through the four aggregates. [648] Some say: The term formless expresses a term negating inferior form or subtle form, like calling a weak boy “a girl”[1867] or one with a small waist “waistless.”

kha che ba la sogs pa dag 'di ni rigs pa ma yin te/ lung dang po gnyis ni mdo las/ tshe dang drod dang rnam shes kyis/ / gang tshe lus 'di 'dor byed cing zhes gsungs pas gzugs med na lus nyid kyang med na de 'dor ba ga la yod/ phan tshun brten pa'ang gnyis ka yod na phan tshun brten pa nyid srid pas 'dod gzugs na spyod pa'i dbang du byas nas gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ gsum pa ni 'dod gzugs kyi ming gzugs rnam shes kyi rkyen can yin gyi gzugs med kyi rnam shes ni ming kho na'i rkyen yin pa'i phyir ming gzugs thams cad rnam shes kyi rkyen can du gsungs kyi rnam shes thams cad ming gzugs kyi rkyen du ston pa ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ phung po bzhi las gzhan du rnam shes 'gro 'ong bkag pa ni phung po bzhi po las gang yang rung ba zhig med na rnam shes 'gro 'ong bkag pa yin gyi gzugs la sogs pa thams cad dus gcig tu tshogs pa med par bkag pa ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de la tshe snga ma nas bar srid kyi rgyun gyis 'dir skye ba ni 'ong ba yin la/ bar srid kyi rgyun gyis 'di nas phyi mar skye ba ni 'gro ba'o/ / gal te gzugs med na gzugs cung zad yod par 'dod na de ji lta bu zhig yod par 'dod/ gal te lus ngag gi sdom pa tsam zhig yod par 'dod na ni mi rigs te/ rten lus ngag med par de dag gi sdom pa mi rigs pa'i phyir ro/ / sdom pa ni 'byung 'gyur yin na gzugs med na rten 'byung ba med pas 'bras bu 'byung 'gyur mi rung ba'i phyir ro/ / gal te dper na zag med kyi 'byung ba med kyang zag med kyi sdom pa 'byung 'gyur gyi gzugs yod pa ltar gzugs med rang sa na 'byung ba med kyang gzugs kyi 'byung ba rgyur byas pa bsam gtan gyi sdom pa yod do zhe na/ de ni mi mtshungs te/ zag med la 'byung ba med kyang zag med kyi sdom pa ni gang du skyes pa de na yod pa'i zag bcas kyi 'byung ba rgyur byas nas skye la bsam gtan gyi sdom pa ni zag bcas yin pas de lta ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas and so on assert that this is illogical, because with regard to the first two passages, a sūtra notes: Due to life, heat, and consciousness, any life and body is destroyed.[1868] Thus if no body exists in the formless realm, how could it be destroyed? Therefore it is said that mutual dependence exists since mutual dependence itself is possible when both exist, for both are active in the desire and form realms. The third passage reveals that consciousness conditions name and form of the desire and form realms, but because formless-realm consciousness conditions name alone, consciousness conditions all name and form, yet it does not indicate that all consciousness conditions name and form. And the refutation that “consciousness comes and goes by some means other than” the four aggregates refutes that consciousness comes or goes by any means other than the four aggregates, but it does not refute that the collection of all aggregates such as form does not exist at the same time. “Coming” refers to birth in this life through the mindstream of the intermediate existence from the past life. “Going” refers to birth in a later life after this life through the mindstream of the intermediate existence. Objection: If one asserts that there is a small amount of form in the formless realm, how could it exist? Reply: Such form is just the vows of body and speech. Objection: That it is illogical. Without a basis of body and speech, it is illogical that such vows exist. Reply: The vows are derivative form. Objection: But since the basis of the elements does not exist in the formless realm, their result, namely, derivative form, would be untenable. Reply: Though the primary elements do not exist in the formless realm, absorption vows causally activated by primary elements of the form realm do exist there. It is like uncontaminated vows consisting of derivative form existing in the form realm even though uncontaminated elements do not exist there. Objection: That is not similar. Though uncontaminated states don’t have primary elements, uncontaminated vows exist wherever they arise, and they arise through contaminated primary elements acting as their cause. But absorption vows, since they are contaminated, are not like that.

gzhan yang lus dang dbang po dang gnas dang yul rnams yod na ni ji ltar gzugs cung zad yod par 'gyur/ gal te rdul phra rab tsam gyi gzugs shig yod pas bongs tshod chung ba'i phyir gzugs med na cung zad yod do zhes bya bar 'dod na ni chu'i skye bo phra mo'i gzugs ltar mi snang ba dag kyang gzugs med du thal bar 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ srid rtse ba'ang sems med par ji ltar mi 'gyur/ srid rtse ba de kho na gzugs med du ji ltar mi 'gyur te/ shin tu cha phra ba'i phyir ro/ / gal te gzugs dang ba'i phyir gzugs med par 'dod na ni dang ba'i phyir rdo rje'i ri la'ang thogs pa med par 'gro bas gzugs na spyod pa dang srid pa bar ma'ang gzugs med par 'gyur ro/ / gal te gang las ches mchog tu dang ba gzhan med pa zhig gzugs med yin no zhe na/ de ltar na snyoms 'jug gis khyad par du 'phags pa ltar skye bas kyang ches mchog tu dang bas srid rtse ba kho na gzugs med du 'gyur ro/ / gal te gzugs med na gzugs yod kyang de ni dang bas sa 'og ma'i dbang pos gzung bar mi nus pas gzugs med du brjod do zhe na/ de lta na bsam gtan bzhi par skyes pa'i gzugs kyang gzugs med du 'gyur te/ gong ma gong ma'i gzugs rnams dang bas 'og ma 'og ma'i dbang pos mi zin pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te 'dod pa'i yon tan gyis rab tu phye ba ni 'dod khams yin la/ gzugs kyis rab tu phye ba ni gzugs khams pa yin pas de gnyis kyi ming ni don dang mthun pa yin gyi gzugs med ces pa'i ming ni 'dod rgyal ba yin no zhe na/ snga ma gnyis don mthun yin la phyi ma 'dod rgyal yin pa la rigs pa ci yod/ bcom ldan 'das kyis kyang gzugs med pa rnams ni gzugs rnams las nges par byung ba yin no zhes bya ba dang*/ lung bar ma las gzugs med pa'i rnam par thar pa zhi ba gang dag gzugs rnams las 'das nas zhes bya ba dang*/ rnam par shes pa'i gnas bdun dang*/ sems can gyi gnas dgu bstan pa'i mdo las/ gzugs can ma yin pa'i sems can dag yod ces bya ba dang*/ rnam pa thams cad du gzugs kyi 'du shes rnams las yang dag par 'das te zhes bya ba la sogs pas rgyu snyoms 'jug la gzugs bkag nas 'bras bu skye ba la'ang gzugs dgag pa gsungs pa'i phyir/

Again, if bodies, sense faculties, abodes, and objects existed in the formless realm, how would form exist merely in a small amount? Reply: If the form of subtle particles alone were to exist in the formless realm, then form would exist in the formless realm in a small amount, because such particles possess dimension, though small. Objection: Then it would follow that invisible objects like the form of subtle marine creatures would be formless. And wouldn’t beings of the summit of existence also be mindless? And why wouldn’t such beings of the summit of existence be solely formless, since they are extremely subtle? Reply: They are formless because their form is translucent. Objection: Then form-realm beings and intermediate-state beings would be formless, since they proceed unimpededly even through the Vajra Mountain [649] due to their translucent form. Reply: Those without equal in their supreme transparency are formless. Objection: Thus only those beings of the summit of existence would be formless, since supreme transparency would be generated by the highest meditative attainment. Reply: Though form exists in the formless realm, it is called “formless” because it is translucent and cannot be apprehended by sense faculties of a lower level. Objection: Thus even the form of one born in the fourth absorption would be formless, because it is form of higher realms that is not apprehended by sense faculties of lower levels. Reply: Since the desire realm is differentiated by qualities of the desire realm and the form realm is differentiated by form, their names conform with their meaning. But the name for the formless realm is arbitrary. Objection: How is it logical that the former two names conform with their meaning but the latter is arbitrary? The Bhagavan has stated that the formless definitely emerges from form,[1869] and it is said in the Medium-Length Discourses: The peace of liberation of the formless realm is due to transcending form.[1870] The Sūtra Teaching the Seven Abodes of Consciousness and the Sūtra Teaching the Nine Abodes of Sentient Beings declare: Nonembodied sentient beings exist.[1871] And: In all respects they fully exist beyond the discernment of form.[1872] These passages state that form is stopped in causal meditative attainment, and it is also stopped in resultant-birth meditative attainment.

gzugs med pa na gzugs cung zad kyang med do/ gal te yod na ji ltar gzugs kyi 'du shes su mi 'gyur zhes rang gi phyogs gzhung 'dzugs par byed de/ {de'i gzugs de ni mdo sde pa sems la gzugs kyi sa bon yod pas de las skye bar 'dod/ bye brag smra ba gzugs med du skyes pa dag gzugs kyi sems mngon du gyur na de'i 'chi ltas kyang gzugs kyi rkyen yin la/ rnam smin dang skal mnyam gyi rgyu ni 'das pa'i gzugs rdzas grub tu 'dod do } 'o na gzugs med nas shi 'phos te khams 'og mar skyes pa dag la ji ltar gzugs 'byung bar 'gyur te/ de ni gzugs med cing gzugs kyi nye bar len pa ni gzugs kho na yin pa'i phyir ro zhe na/

Therefore there is no form in the formless realm in the least. And the question “Wouldn’t discernment of form occur if form existed in the formless realm?” authentically establishes our position. {Sautrāntikas assert that such form is generated from mind, since the seed of form exists in the mind. Vaibhāṣikas assert that if the mind apprehending form manifests in those born in the formless realm, it is an omen of death and also a condition of form. Past form that is a cause of karmic maturation and homogeneity is substantially established.} Objection: How do those taking birth in lower realms, having died from the formless realm, take on form? For aren’t they formless, and doesn’t only form approach form?

de'i tshe gzugs ni lhan cig byed pa'i rkyen las kyis 'phangs pa'i sems las skye bar 'gyur la/ nye bar len pa'i rgyu ni 'dod gzugs na yod pa'i 'byung bzhi nyid yin no/ / de'i phyir kha cig mdo sde pa lus sems phan tshun sa bon can yin no zhes bya ba dang*/ bye brag tu smra ba gnas skabs de'i gzugs 'das pa'i gzugs las skye'o zhes bya ba dang*/ sems tsam pa kun gzhi las skye bar 'dod do zhes 'chad pa ni legs pa ma yin te/ dang po ni tshu rol mdzes pa pa'i lugs yin pa'i phyir dang*/ gnyis pa ni da ltar ba'i gzugs yod bzhin du 'das pa la ltos mi dgos pa'i phyir dang*/ gsum pa ni gzugs rdzas su med par 'dod pas de'i rgyu la 'bad pa don med pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: At that time, form arises from the mind that is projected by karma that constitutes its cooperative condition. The four primary elements existing in the desire and form realms constitute the substantial cause (upādānahetu). Some say: The explanations of the Sautrāntikas, who assert that the body and mind possess the seeds of each other, the Vaibhāṣikas, who assert that the form of a specific time arises from past form, and the Cittamātrins, who assert that form arises from foundation consciousness, are incorrect. The first is the system of hedonists. The second is incorrect because form currently existing in the present does not rely on the past. And [650] the third is incorrect because it would be meaningless [for Cittamātrins] to strive to establish the cause of form, since they assert that it does not exist as the substance of form.
gzugs med pa'i snyoms 'jug bzhi'i sgra'i don ni
'o na nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched la sogs pa de dag nam mkha' la sogs pa kho na la dmigs pas ming de skad ces bya'am/ 'on te sbyor ba'i ming gis btags she na/

Question: Regarding the meaning of the names of the four formless-realm meditative attainments — the base of infinite space and so on — are they given those names since they focus on space alone and so forth, or they are designated according to their preparation?
rnam shes mtha' yas mkha' mtha' yas/ / ci yang med ces bya de ltar/ / sbyor phyir dman phyir 'du shes med/ / 'du shes med pa'ang ma yin no/ / 4
Because they prepare by reflecting: “Space is infinite,” “Consciousness is infinite,” “It is nothingness.” It is not discernment because it is inferior, but it is also not nondiscernment. (8:4)

sbyor ba'i ming gis te/ 'di ltar sbyor ba'i tshe nam mkha' mtha' yas so zhes bya ba dang*/ rnam shes mtha' yas so zhes bya ba dang*/ ci yang med do zhes bya ba de ltar sbyor ba'i phyir nam mkha' mtha' yas la sogs pa de skad brjod kyi gzhan na ni ci rigs par chos gzhan dag la'ang dmigs so/ / bzhi pa ni 'du shes chung zhing mi gsal bas dman pa'i phyir 'du shes med pa zhes kyang bya la/ 'du shes cung zad yod pa'i phyir 'du shes med pa'ang ma yin no zhes brjod do/ / srid pa gsum na de bas mtho ba'i sa med pas srid rtse zhes kyang bya'o/ / yang na sbyor ba'i tshe 'du shes ni nad do/ / 'bras so/ / zug rngu'o zhes 'du shes rags pa la'ang skyon du lta la/ 'du shes med pa ba ni kun tu rmongs pa'o zhes 'du shes med pa'ang kun du rmongs pa'i rgyu yin no zhes pa dang*/ 'du shes med 'du shes med min skye mched 'di ni zhi ba dang gya nom pa'o zhes sbyor ba'i phyir yang de skad du brjod do/ /

Reply: They are designated according to their preparation because when preparing they prepare (prayoga) by reflecting, “Space is infinite” (ākāśānantya), “Consciousness is infinite” (vijñānānantya), and “It is nothingness” (akiñcanya). Though they are called infinite space and so on; they also focus on various other phenomena. The fourth formless state is called “not discernment” because its discernment is inferior since it is weak and unclear. But it is also called “not nondiscernment” because it has some discernment. It is also called “the summit of existence” since there is no level higher than it in the three realms of existence. Again, it is called this because while preparing to generate the base of neither discernment nor nondiscernment that is viewed as peace and sublime, one views coarse discernment as flawed, reflecting, “Discernment is a sickness, a boil, and painful,” and one also views the state of nondiscernment as fully confused and nondiscernment as the cause of being fully confused.
gnyis pa dbye ba ni
Classification of the absorptions and formless-realm states
de ltar snyoms 'jug dngos gzhi'i rdzas/ / rnam pa brgyad bdun rnam pa gsum/ / ro myang ldan dang dag pa dang / / zag med brgyad pa rnam pa gnyis/ / 5
There are eight types of substance of the actual bases of meditative attainment. Seven have three: they possess enjoyment, pure states, and uncontaminated states. The eighth has two types. (8:5)

gong du smros pa'i tshul de ltar na yan lag ma gtogs pa bsam gtan bzhi dang gzugs med bzhi ste snyoms par 'jug pa'i dngos gzhi'i rdzas ni rnam pa brgyad yin la/ / {'dis yan lag dang nyer bsdogs dang khyad par can ma bstan par 'dod do } brgyad po de dag las srid rtse ma gtogs pa bdun ni rnam pa gsum gsum yin te/ ro myang ba dang mtshungs par ldan pa dang*/ dag pa pa dang*/ zad pa med pa rnams so/ / brgyad pa srid rtse ni ro myang ldan dang dag pa pa rnam pa gnyis yin gyi 'du shes dman zhing rgyu ba mi gsal bas de la 'phags pa'i lam mi rten pas zag med ni ma yin no/ /

There are eight types of substance of the actual bases (maula) of meditative attainment (samāpatti): (1–4) the four absorptions, not including their branches, in accordance with the previous explanation, and (5–8) the four formless states. {But this passage does not teach the branches, access concentration, or special states.} From among those eight, seven, excluding the summit of existence, have three each, for they possess (1) concomitance with enjoyment (āsvāda), (2) pure states, and (3) uncontaminated states (anāsrava). The eighth, the summit of existence, has two types: enjoyment and purity. It lacks uncontaminated states since its discernment is inferior. It lacks clarity because it moves, and the ārya path does not depend on it.
ro myang mtshungs ldan sred bcas so/ / 'jig rten pa yi dge ba ni/ / dag pa de ni des myang bya/ / zag med 'jig rten 'das pa'o/ / 6
Enjoyment has craving as a concomitant. Mundane virtuous states are called pure. That enjoys its taste through that. The uncontaminated transcends the mundane. (8:6)

de la ro myang ldan ni mtshungs ldan gyi grogs sred pa dang bcas pa'o/ / zag bcas 'jig rten pa'i snyoms 'jug dge ba ni ma chags pa la sogs pa dang mtshungs par ldan pas dag pa zhes bya'o/ / ro myang ldan des ci zhig ro myang bar byed ce na/ dag pa pa de ni ro myang ldan des ro myang bar bya ba yin te/ dag pa pa 'di ni bzang po zhes de la zhen cing sred pa'i phyir ro/ / des na ro myang ldan ni bsam gtan nyon mongs can yin pas dag pa pa las langs pa dang ro myang ldan la snyoms par zhugs pa yin no/ / lta ba dang nga rgyal la sogs pa dang ldan pa'i bsam gtan yang yod mod kyi sred bcas kho na ro myang ldan du bshad pa ni de kho na dmigs pa la zhen pas de las nges par ma byung na gong mar 'gyur mi srid pa'i phyir de skad ces bshad do/ / zag med ni 'jig rten las 'das pa'i snyoms 'jug bden pa'i rnam pa can no/

That possessing enjoyment (āsvāda) of it has craving (satṛṣṇa) as a concomitant (saṃprayukta). Contaminated mundane virtuous (laukikaśubha) meditative attainments are called pure (śuddhaka) because they are concomitant with nonattachment. Question: Why does that which possesses enjoyment enjoy its taste? Reply: That being with pure meditative attainment comes to enjoy its taste through possessing enjoyment because he longs for and craves for that object, reflecting, “The pure is good.” That which possesses enjoyment is afflicted meditative attainment, and meditative attainment that enjoys its taste is entered after rising from pure meditative attainment. Though absorptions that possess view, pride, and so on also exist, only that which possesses craving is said to “possess enjoyment.” This is because it craves its focal object specifically [651] and because it is impossible for it to attain higher states if it does not withdraw from that very craving. Uncontaminated (anāsrava) meditative attainment is meditative attainment transcending the mundane (lokattara). Its aspect is the four truths.
gsum pa yan lag rnam par bzhag pa

SYNOPSIS
['di] la gsum gyi
This has three headings: why branches are not taught for the formless realm, their definite number, and recognizing the meaning of branches and those possessing branches.

WHY BRANCHES ARE NOT TAUGHT FOR THE FORMLESS REALM

ci bsam gtan ltar gzugs med pa dag la'ang yan lag yod dam zhe na med de/ 'grel pa las/ snyoms par 'jug pa'i rdzas de dag las bsam gtan rnams kho na yan lag dang ldan pa yin gyi gzugs med pa rnams ni ma yin no zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / de'i rgyu mtshan ni kun las btus las/ gzugs med pa rnams na ni zhi gnas su ro gcig pa nyid kyi phyir yan lag rnam par bzhag pa med do zhes bshad cing*/ slob dpon rgyal po'i sras kyis kyang de kho na ltar bshad la/ de'i don yang slob dpon gang spel gyi TI ka las kha cig na re zhi gnas su ro gcig pa'i phyir te/ gang dag gang na rgyu ba rags pa de dag ni der yan lag tu bzhag na gzugs med na ni nye bar zhi ba lhag pas sems dang sems byung de dag rgyu ba zhan pas de dag la yan lag rnam par bzhag pa mi srid pas ting nge 'dzin shas che ba de dag na ni sems las byung ba gzhan 'ga' yang gtso bo ma yin pas gzugs med du yan lag rnam par mi gzhag go zhes zer ro/ / gzhan dag na re sa gang du sems byung tshar phyin par 'gag pa der yan lag bzhag ste/ de ltar bsam gtan dang po ni sdug bsngal dang yid mi bde 'gag cing*/ de bzhin du gnyis par rtog dpyod dang*/ gsum par dga' ba dang*/ bzhi par ni bde ba 'gag la/ de man chad na ni sems byung gang yang tshar phyin par 'gag pa med do zhes bshad do/ / de ltar na chos mngon pa las ni bsam gtan dngos gzhi bzhi po ma gtogs pa la yan lag med par bshad cing*/ 'phags pa rnam par grol ba'i sdes ni gzugs med pa dag btang snyoms dang rtse gcig pa'i yan lag gnyis dang ldan zhing snal ma phra sbom las byas pa'i ras ltar sems zhi ma zhi'i khyad par gong nas gong du yod par bshad la/ brang ti ni gzugs med bzhi po dran pa dang shes bzhin dang btang snyoms dang ting nge 'dzin te yan lag bzhi bzhi dang ldan no zhes zer ro/ /

Question: Do branches exist in the formless realm as they do for the absorptions? Reply: They do not. As the Autocommentary states: From among those substances of meditative attainment, only the absorptions possess branches, not the formless realm.[1873] The reason is given in the Compendium of Abhidharma, which explains: There is no system of branches in the formless realm because calm abiding has just one taste.[1874] Master Jinaputra also explains just that,[1875] and in terms of its meaning, Master Pūrṇavardhana’s commentary also states: Some say: Because calm abiding has just one taste, no system of branches can be posited in the formless realm. If branches are posited as those states that move the mind in any gross way, then a system of branches would be impossible in the formless realm since intense pacification is dominant there, movement of minds and mental factors is minimal, and no other mental factor is dominant. Others say: That which completely stops any mental factor in any way is posited as a branch. Thus suffering and mental dissatisfaction are stopped in the first absorption, investigation and analysis are stopped in the second, joy is stopped in the third, and pleasure is stopped in the forth. No mental factor is completely stopped above that.[1876] The Abhidharma explains that except for the four actual bases of absorption, there are no branches.[1877] Ārya Vimuktisena clarifies that the formless realm possesses the branches of equanimity and single-pointedness, and different stages of pacified or nonpacified mind exist as one progresses higher, just as cloth is made from fine or coarse thread.[1878] Drangti says that the four formless states possess the four branches of mindfulness, introspection, equanimity, and concentration.[1879]

slob dpon ka ma la shrI las ni bsgom pa'i rim pa dang po las bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs mi lcogs med kyang tshor ba btang snyoms dang rtog dpyod dang rtse gcig pa'i yan lag bzhi dang ldan par bshad do/ /

Ācārya Kamalaśīla explains in the first of his Stages of Meditation that unrestricted access concentration to the first absorption possesses the four branches of the feeling of equanimity, investigation, analysis, and single-pointedness.[1880]

Question: Why are only investigation and analysis posited as branches [652] if other mental factors such as discernment, contact, and so on also exist? Reply: The answer to this has two headings: the system of others and our own system.
dang po ni
OTHERS’ SYSTEM

kha cig na re gang dag bsam gtan snga ma la yod pa phyi mas spangs shing bor ba de dag yan lag tu bshad kyi 'du shes la sogs pa ni snga ma la yod kyang phyi mas bor ba med pa'i phyir yan lag tu ma bshad de/ 'di ltar bsam gtan dang po la yan lag lnga yod pa'i rtog dpyod gnyis bor nas gnyis par bzhag la/ dang po'i rtog dpyod gnyis dang gnyis pa'i dga' ba dang gsum bor nas gsum pa dang*/ de gsum dang gsum pa'i bde ba dang bzhi bor nas bsam gtan bzhi par bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar ting nge 'dzin kyang yan lag ma yin par 'gyur ro zhe na/ ting nge 'dzin snyoms 'jug gi gtso bo yin pa'i phyir mi mtshungs so/ / yang na bsam gtan dang po la sogs pa'i yan lag lnga la sogs pa kho nar bzhag ste/ yan lag de dag bsam gtan dang po la sogs pa la ches phan pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ / de lta na bsam gtan dang po la rtog dpyod yan lag tu mi 'jog par dran pa dang shes rab dag yan lag tu 'jog par 'gyur te/ dran pa nye bar gnas pa dang yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du shes pa la zhum rgod la sogs pa mi 'byung bas rtog dpyod gnyis pas dran pa dang shes rab ches phan pa'i phyir ro/ /

Some say: Branches are explained as those states that exist in lower absorptions but are abandoned and discarded by higher absorptions. Discernment and so on are not explained to be branches because they exist in lower absorptions and are not discarded by higher absorptions. Thus the first absorption has five branches; the second discards investigation and analysis; the third discards three mental factors, including (1–2) both investigation and analysis of the first and (3) joy of the second; and the fourth absorption discards four — those three, plus pleasure of the third absorption. Objection: Thus concentration would also not be a branch. Reply: It’s not the same. Concentration is the dominant factor in meditative attainment. Objection: Because they greatly benefit the first absorption and so forth, only those five branches of the first absorption and so on are posited as branches. Reply: If that were so, investigation and analysis would not be posited as branches, but mindfulness and wisdom would. Both investigation and analysis greatly benefit mindfulness and wisdom, since defeatism, excitation, and so on do not arise in the presence of the foundations of mindfulness and the knowledge of reality as it is.
gnyis pa ni
OUR SYSTEM

'grel pa las/ kha cig de skad du rgol ba yod mod kyi/ sngon gyi slob dpon rnams ni ji snyed mngon pa de ltar mi ston te/ de lta bas na 'di ni dpyad par bya ba yin no zhes 'byung ba la TIka byed dag 'di ni rnal 'byor spyod pa'i sa mthong bas dpyad par bya ba yin no zhes slob dpon gyis der blta bar khungs 'byin pa yin pas de dang mthun par bshad par bya'o zhes 'chad do/ / 'o na de las ji ltar 'byung zhe na/ 'di ltar bsam gtan rnams la 'du shes la sogs pa'i chos gzhan dag yod kyang rtog dpyod la sogs pa kho na yan lag tu bzhag pa ni so sor gnyen po dang phan yon dang de gnyis ka'i rten nam gnas kyi yan lag gi phyir ro zhes 'byung bas de dag gi dbang du byas te grangs nges bsam par bya'o/

The Autocommentary states: Indeed, such statements should be opposed. Past masters did not teach Abhidharma in that way, and so it must be analyzed.[1881] This is why the Subcommentary explains that this issue should be analyzed after reviewing Yogācāra Levels.[1882] Vasubandhu explains that this should be analyzed according to the source texts. Question: How are they presented in those sources? Reply: Only investigation and analysis are posited as branches, even though other phenomena such as discernment exist in the absorptions. It is said, “the branches of specific antidotes and benefit, and the abidance that is the support of both of them.” I think this passage teaches the definite number of branches.
gsum pa yan lag dang yan lag can gyi don ngos gzung ba ni
RECOGNIZING THE MEANING OF BRANCHES AND THOSE POSSESSING BRANCHES

bye brag tu smra ba ting nge 'dzin bsam gtan dang bsam gtan gyi yan lag gnyis ka yin la gzhan dag ni yan lag kho na yin no/ / zhes zer ro/ / slob dpon ni yan lag las don gzhan du gyur pa ma yin yang yan lag bzhi pa'i dmag ces brjod pa ltar tshogs pa'i spyi dang bye brag yin no zhes 'dod do/ /

Vaibhāṣikas say that concentration is both absorption and a branch of absorption. The others are branches alone. Vasubandhu asserts that though the term branch (aṅga) retains its meaning, it refers to general and specific collections, just like an army with four divisions.[1883]
gnyis pa gzhung don la
THE MEANING OF THE TEXT: BRANCHES OF THE FOUR ABSORPTIONS
dang po la lnga rtog dpyod dang / / dga' dang bde dang ting 'dzin rnams/ / gnyis pa la ni yan lag bzhi/ / rab dang dang ni dga' la sogs/ / 7
The first has five: investigation, analysis, joy, pleasure, and concentration. The second has four branches: pure clarity, joy, and so on. (8:7)

bsam gtan dang po la ni yan lag lnga ste/ mi mthun phyogs 'dod pa'i 'dod chags dang gnod sems dang rnam 'tshol sogs pa spong bas gnyen po'i yan lag rtog pa dang dpyod pa dang*/ rtog dpyod kyi mi mthun phyogs spangs nas dben pa las skyes pa'i dga' bde 'thob pas phan yon gyi yan lag dga' ba dang bde ba dang*/ sems rtse gcig pa'i stobs kyis snga ma de dag 'grub pas de gnyis ka'i rten gyi yan lag ting nge 'dzin rnams so/ /

The first absorption has five branches: [653] (1) investigation (vitarka) and (2) analysis (vicāra), which are remedial branches, since they abandon desire-realm attachment, malice, violence, and so on. (3) Joy (prīti) and (4) pleasure (sukha) are the beneficial branches, since by abandoning states opposing investigation and analysis one obtains joy and pleasure that arise in their absence. And (5) concentration (samādhi) is a supportive branch and acts as the basis of the former two, since it establishes those by the power of single-pointed mind.

bsam gtan gnyis pa la ni yan lag bzhi ste/ mi mthun phyogs dang po'i rtog dpyod spong bas gnyen po'i yan lag nang rab tu dang ba dang*/ phan yon dang gnas sam rten gyi yan lag ni snga ma ltar dga' ba dang sogs pas gzung ba bde ba gnyis dang ting nge 'dzin to/ /

The second absorption has four branches (aṅga): (1) pure internal clarity (prasāda) is a remedial branch, since it abandons its opposing factors: investigation and analysis. “And so on” refers to the beneficial branch and the abiding or supportive branch that were previously explained as (2) joy, (3) pleasure, and (4) concentration.
gsum pa la lnga btang snyoms dang / / dran dang shes bzhin bde dang gnas/ / mtha' na bzhi dran btang snyoms dang/ / bde min sdug min ting 'dzin rnams/ / 8
The third has five: equanimity, mindfulness, introspection, pleasure, and abidance. The last has four: mindfulness, equanimity, neither pleasure nor pain, and concentration. (8:8)

bsam gtan gsum pa la ni yan lag lnga ste/ mi mthun phyogs 'og sa'i dga' ba spong bas gnyen po'i yan lag dga' ba la rtsol ba med pas dmigs pa la lhun gyis grub pa'i mtshan nyid can 'du byed kyi btang snyoms dang btang snyoms kyi rgyu mtshan mi brjed pa'i dran pa dang mi brjed pa'i shes bzhin gsum dang phan yon dang rten gyi yan lag ni rim pa ltar bde ba dang sems gnas pa ting nge 'dzin rnams so/ / sems gnas pa ting nge 'dzin yin par lam gyi tshogs kyi mdo las/ yang dag pa'i ting nge 'dzin gang zhe na/ gang sems gnas pa dang*/ yang dag par gnas pa'o zhes 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /

The third absorption has five branches: the three of (1) applied equanimity (upekṣā), which spontaneously and effortlessly focuses on joy and which is a remedial branch that abandons its opposing factor, the joy of lower levels; (2) mindfulness (smṛti), which doesn’t forget applied equanimity and the reason for equanimity; and (3) introspection (saṃprajñāna), which doesn’t forget mindfulness. The beneficial branch and the supportive branch are, respectively, (4) pleasure (sukha), and (5) the abidance (sthiti) of the mind, which is concentration. In terms of the abidance of the mind being concentration, the Multiple Paths Sūtra declares: What is right concentration? That which is the abidance and the correct abidance of the mind.[1884]

bsam gtan kyi mtha' bzhi pa na ni yan lag bzhi ste/ mi mthun phyogs 'og sa'i bde ba spong bas gnyen po'i yan lag gnyis ka'ang sa 'og ma'i skyon brgyad dang bral bas dran pa yongs su dag pa dang 'du byed btang snyoms yongs su dag pa gnyis dang*/ phan yon dang rten gyi yan lag ni rim pa ltar bde ba yang min sdug bsngal yang min pa'i tshor ba btang snyoms dang*/ ting nge 'dzin yongs su dag pa rnams so/ / de ltar na de dag ni bsam gtan gyi yan lag bco brgyad do/ { 'di dag gi gnyen po ni thag sring gi gnyen por 'dod pa nyid legs so/ /}

The last absorption, the fourth, has four branches. There are two remedial branches that abandon their opposing factors of lower-level pleasure — (1) thoroughly pure mindfulness (smṛti) and (2) thoroughly pure equanimity — which are free of the eight errors of lower levels. The beneficial and supportive branches are, respectively, (3) the feeling of equanimity that is neither pleasure nor pain and (4) thoroughly pure concentration (samādhi). Thus there are eighteen branches of the absorptions. {It is correct to assert that these antidotes are antidotes that distance oneself from the object to be countered.}

gnyen po'ang dran pa dang shes bzhin dang btang snyoms gsum yin yang sems dga' ba'i nye ba'i nyon mongs pas kun nas dkris pa'i phyir de dag rang ming gis ma bstan par rtog dpyod kyi 'khrug pa zhi bas pa dang bzhi par bzhag la/ bsam gtan bzhi'i khyad par ni dang po dang gnyis pa la ni ting nge 'dzin yongs su rdzogs pa'i khyad par yod do/ gnyis pa dang gsum pa la ni phan 'dogs pa yongs su rdzogs pa'i khyad par yod do/ gsum pa dang bzhi pa la ni yongs su dag pa yongs su rdzogs pa'i khyad par yod do zhes bshad do/ /

The Compendium of Ascertainment explains: The opposing factors to the first absorption are fivefold: (1) the conceptions of desire-realm attachment, malice, and violence taken as one, (2) suffering, (3) mental dissatisfaction, (4) unethical conduct, and (5) distraction. The opposing factors of the second absorption are fivefold: (1) attachment to the first absorption, (2) investigation and analysis taken as one, (3) suffering, (4) excitation, and (5) incomplete concentration. The opposing factors of the third absorption are fourfold: (1) attachment to the second absorption, (2) mental satisfaction, (3) joy, and (4) incomplete concentration. The opposing factors to the fourth absorption are fivefold: (1) inhalation and exhalation, (2) attachment to the third absorption, (3) pleasure, (4) striving for [654] pleasure, and (5) incomplete concentration.[1885]
In the context of the remedial branches, then, mindfulness, introspection, and equanimity are the antidotes that abandon the five opposing factors of the first absorption. However, these three are not taught by name; since these three establish entry to investigation and analysis, investigation and analysis are taught to be remedial branches. So too, the states of mindfulness, introspection, and equanimity are also antidotes that abandon opposing factors of the second absorption. But because the mind is ensnared by the branch affliction of joy, they are not taught by their own names but by the term “complete internal clarity,” since they pacify the disturbance of investigation and analysis. Therefore complete internal clarity possesses the nature of mindfulness, introspection, and equanimity. In the third absorption, the characteristics of equanimity, mindfulness, and introspection alone are taught because the mind is free of the branch affliction of joy. Thus, from the perspective of the three branches: remedial, beneficial, and supportive, the branches of each absorption are posited as five or four. The fourth absorption is different, since the first and second absorptions have specific complete concentration, the second and third absorptions have specific complete benefit, and the third and fourth absorptions have specific complete purity.
rdzas su bcu gcig dang po na/ / shin tu sbyangs pa bde ba yin/ / rab tu dang ba dad pa yin/ / lung rnam gnyis phyir dga' yid bde/ / 9
There are eleven by substance. Pliancy in the first is pleasure. Pure clarity is faith. Therefore these two scriptures state that mental satisfaction is joy. (8:9)

bco brgyad po de dag kyang ming gi sgo nas yin gyi rdzas su ni bcu gcig yin te/ 'di ltar bsam gtan dang po'i yan lag lnga dang*/ gnyis pa'i nang rab tu dang ba dang gsum pa'i ting nge 'dzin ma gtogs pa bzhi dang*/ bzhi pa'i tshor ba btang snyoms rnams so/ / gal te rtog dpyod dang dran pa dang 'du byed btang snyoms dang sems bde dang tshor ba btang snyoms rnams ni rdzas re re zhing yan lag tu rung mod kyi bsam gtan snga ma gnyis kyi bde ba bsam gtan gyi yan lag tu ji ltar 'gyur te/ sa de gnyis na dga' ba las 'dod chags dang ma bral bas sems kyi bde ba med pa'i phyir dang*/ lus kyi bde ba'ang mnyam par bzhag pa na bsam gtan gyi yan lag tu mi 'gyur te/ de ni sgo lnga'i rnam shes kyi 'khor du byung ba yin na de yang ngo bo nyid kyis rnam par g.yeng ba yin pas mnyam gzhag tu mi 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yang bsam gtan gsum pa'i bde ba rdzas gzhan du mi 'grub par 'gyur te/ bsam gtan dang por bgrangs zin pa'i phyir dang*/ der bgrangs kyang rdzas gzhan du bgrang na gnyis pa'i bde ba'ang rdzas gzhan du bgrang bar thal bar 'gyur ba'i phyir ro zhe na/

There are eighteen branches by name and eleven by substance because there are (1–5) five branches of the first absorption, (6) complete internal clarity of the second, (7–10) the four except concentration of the third, and (11) the feeling of equanimity of the fourth. Indeed, investigation, analysis, mindfulness, applied equanimity, mental bliss, and the feeling of equanimity are separate substances and suitable to be branches. But how could the pleasure of the former two absorptions be a branch of absorption, given that (1) there is no mental bliss on those two levels since they are not free from attachment to joy, and (2) physical pleasure could not be a branch of the absorptions engaged in equipoise because when pleasure arises in the retinue of consciousness of the five sense doors, equipoise cannot arise; [physical pleasure] is by nature distracted. Objection: Pleasure of the third absorption would not be established as another substance because it has already been counted in the first absorption, and though already counted, if it were counted as another substance, it would follow that pleasure of the second absorption would be counted as another substance.

skyon med do/ / bsam gtan gsum pa'i bde ba ni sems bde{ yin pas tshor ba} yin la/ bsam gtan dang po dang gnyis pa dag na ni dge ba'i sa mang po pa'i sems shin tu sbyangs pa la bde ba zhes brjod pa yin no/ / bsam gtan snga ma gnyis na ni tshor ba bde ba mi srid de/ tshor ba bde ba la lus sems kyi tshor ba gnyis las med cing*/ de la lus tshor ni ma yin te/ snyoms par zhugs pa la rnam par shes pa'i tshogs lnga med pa'i phyir ro/ / sems tshor yang ma yin te/ yan lag dga' ba zhes bgrangs zin pa'i phyir dang*/ dga' ba ni yid bde yin na bde ba dang yid bde gnyis cig car mi 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / de gnyis rnam grangs kyi yan lag yin par yang ma rigs te/ yan lag lnga zhes tshogs pa gcig la 'byung bar bshad pa'i phyir ro zhes bye brag tu smra ba rnams 'dod do/ / dpes ston pa na re bstan bcos bye brag tu bshad pa las/ mdo sde pa btsun pas chos mngon pa ba rnams kyi ltar na zo chun 'khyud mo ltar mig gi rnam par shes pa la sogs pa 'og nas gong du 'dren to zhes bshad de/ de'i 'dod pa ni mig shes la sogs pa ni bsam gtan gnyis pa la sogs pa'i sa pa'ang yod do zhes bya ba yin no zhes TI kar bshad cing*/ bsam gtan ston pa'i mdo las kyang bsam gtan gsum pa ston pa na de dga' ba las 'dod chags dang bral nas btang snyoms dang dran pa dang shes bzhin du gnas shing bde ba lus kyi myong la zhes gsungs pas lus bde ni 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang po'i sa pa kho nar ma zad kyi/ gnyis pa dang gsum pa'i sa pa'ang yod pas des na bsam gtan gsum char na'ang lus bde kho na yan lag yin no zhes zer ro/ /

Reply: There is no error. Pleasure of the third absorption is {feeling, since it is} mental bliss. Pliancy (praśrabdhi) that is a virtuous mental state in the first and second absorptions is called pleasure (sukha). But the feeling of pleasure [655] is impossible in both earlier absorptions because there is no feeling of pleasure other than physical and mental feeling. It is not physical feeling because the fivefold collection of consciousness does not exist in meditative attainment, and it is not mental feeling because that is already counted as the branch of joy, and if joy were mental satisfaction, then both pleasure and mental satisfaction would not occur together. Vaibhāṣikas assert that it would be illogical for those two to be counted as branches because they explain that the five branches arise in a single collection. Dārṣṭāntikas cite the Great Treatise on Differentiation as follows: A venerable Sautrāntika says: According to the Ābhidharmikas, eye consciousness and so on is drawn from lower to higher levels like the rim of a water wheel.[1886] The Subcommentary explains: By accepting that, eye consciousness and so on exists even on the level of the second absorption and so on.[1887] Also, the Sūtra Teaching the Absorptions states: In the third absorption, one abides in equanimity, mindfulness, and introspection free of attachment to joy, and pleasure is an experience of the body.[1888] Therefore physical pleasure is a branch in three absorptions, since not only does physical pleasure exist on the levels of the desire realm and the first absorption, it also exists on the second and third levels.

'o na lam gyi tshogs kyi mdo las/ bde ba'i dbang po gang zhe na/ bde ba myong bar 'gyur ba'i reg pas reg pa la lus kyi dang sems las byung ba'i tshor ba tshor ba'i rnam pa bde ba sim pa skye ba gang yin pa de ni bde ba'i dbang po zhes bya'o zhes gsungs pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/ mi 'gal te/ sde pa gzhan thams cad kyi gzhung las lus kyi tshor ba zhes pa kho na 'byung bas sems las byung ba'i zhes pa ni 'ga' zhig gis sgro btags pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ mdo las kyang bde ba lus kyis myong la zhes rang gi sgras gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te de ni yid kyi lus kyis zhes bya ba yin no zhe na/ ma yin te/ de lta na bde ba yid kyis myong la zhes gsungs pas chog gi lus kyis zhes gsungs pa la dgos pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yang bsam gtan snga ma gnyis su shin tu sbyangs pa la bde bar brjod na snga ma gnyis kyi bas shin tu sbyangs pa khyad par du 'phags pa yod pas bsam gtan bzhi pa la'ang yan lag bde ba smros par 'gyur na der ma smros pas na dang po gsum na tshor ba bde ba yod pas de yan lag tu bshad kyi bzhi pa na tshor ba bde ba med pas de yan lag tu ma bshad do/ / gal te bsam gtan snga ma gnyis kyi shin tu sbyangs pa ni bde ba'i tshor ba dang mthun pas bde bar bshad kyi bzhi pa'i shin tu sbyangs pa ni bde ba'i tshor ba dang mi mthun pas bde bar ma bshad do zhe na/ 'o na bde ba'i tshor ba dang mthun pas gsum pa'i shin tu sbyangs pa'ang ci'i phyir bde bar ma bshad/ gal te bde ba'i tshor ba dang mthun mod kyi las su rung ba'i mtshan nyid can gyi btang snyoms kyis bcom pas der bde bar ma bshad do zhe na ma yin te/ bsam gtan snga ma gnyis kyis shin tu sbyangs pa bas gsum pa'i shin tu sbyangs pa khyad par du 'phags pas btang snyoms kho nas de 'phel ba'i phyir ro/ /

Objection: This contradicts the Multiple Paths Sūtra, which says: What is the faculty of pleasure? Any type of feeling arising as pleasure and well-being — that is, any feeling derived from physical or mental contact where contact leads to the experience of pleasure — is called the faculty of pleasure.[1889] Reply: It does not contradict this passage. The texts of all other schools state “physical feeling” alone, but some expand on this by stating “derived from mind.” A sūtra also declares in its own words: Pleasure is experienced by the body.[1890] Question: What if this passage said “. . . by the body of the mental faculty”? Reply: That would be incorrect. If it were so, it would be sufficient to state that “pleasure is experienced by the mental faculty”; there would be no need to say “. . . by the body.”[1891] Objection: Again, if pliancy in the first and second absorptions is called “pleasure,” then pliancy in the fourth absorption should also be called “the branch of pleasure,” since its pliancy is superior to that of the preceding two. Reply: But it is not called that here. The feeling of pleasure that exists in the first three [absorptions] is called a branch, but since the fourth absorption lacks the feeling of pleasure, pliancy in the fourth absorption is not called a branch. Objection: Pliancy of the two initial absorptions is explained to be pleasure since it is compatible with the feeling of pleasure. Pliancy of the fourth absorption is not explained to be pleasure since it is not compatible with the feeling of pleasure. [656] Reply: But since it is compatible with the feeling of pleasure, why isn’t pliancy of the third absorption said to be pleasure? Objection: Indeed, it is compatible with the feeling of pleasure, but since [such pliancy] is destroyed by equanimity characterized by flexibility, it is not explained as pleasure in this context. Reply: That is not so, because equanimity is only enhanced by the pliancy of the first two absorptions and by the superior pliancy of the third absorption.

gzhan yang bsam gtan snga ma gnyis na shin tu sbyangs pa kho na bde ba ma yin te/ mgon med zas sbyin gyis zhus pa'i mdo las/ gang gi tshe 'phags pa nyan thos rab tu dben pa las skyes pa'i bde ba lus kyis mngon sum du byas nas rdzogs par byas te gnas pa de'i tshe 'di'i 'dod pa nye bar sdud pa'i yid bde gnyis dang*/ mi dge ba nye bar sdud pa'i yid bde mi bde btang snyoms gsum ste chos lnga ni spong bar 'gyur la/ chos lnga po nang rab tu dang ba dang dga' ba dang shin tu sbyangs pa dang bde ba dang ting nge 'dzin ni bsgom pa yongs su rdzogs par 'gyur ro zhes shin tu sbyangs pa dang bde ba tha dad du gsungs pa'i phyir dang*/ gsungs kyang tha dad ma yin na lngar mi rung zhing tha dad yin na bsam gtan gsum char gyi bde ba lus bder grub pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na sgo lnga'i shes pa rang bzhin gyis g.yeng ba'i phyir kha phyir lta yin pas mnyam gzhag tu lus kyi rnam shes ji ltar 'byung la/ gal te 'byung na'ang phyi rol tu g.yengs pa dang lus shes skyes pas ting nge 'dzin las nyams pa dang*/ gnas pa las langs par yang 'gyur ba dang*/ lus bde mnyam gzhag tu mi 'byung bas bsam gtan gyi yan lag tu mi 'thad cing*/ gzhan yang 'dod pa'i rten can zag bcas zag med kyi bsam gtan la mnyam par bzhag pa nas bsam gtan gyi sa pa yin pas rim pa ltar 'dod pa'i lus shes kyis gzugs kyi reg bya 'dzin mi nus pas reg bya dang lus shes gzugs kyi sa pa yin pas 'dod pa'i lus dbang gi gzugs na spyod pa'i reg bya 'dzin pa'i lus shes skyed mi nus pa'i phyir dang*/ tshogs pa gcig la yan lag zag bcas zag med gnyis mi rung bas shin tu sbyangs pa'i reg bya dang lus shes kyang zag med du 'gyur ro zhe na/

Again, in the first and second absorptions it is not that pliancy alone is pleasure. The Sūtra Requested by Anāthapiṇḍada reveals that pliancy and pleasure are different: Whenever an ārya śrāvaka accomplishes the physical manifestation of pleasure arising from separation, at that time he abandons five phenomena: (1–2) two types of mental satisfaction subsumed by the desire realm, and (3–5) three subsumed by nonvirtue: mental satisfaction, mental dissatisfaction, and equanimity. He also completes the cultivation of five phenomena: pure internal clarity, joy, pliancy, pleasure, and concentration.[1892] If [pliancy and pleasure] are not different, then the preceding passage would be untenable, and if they are different, then pleasure of the third absorption would be established as physical pleasure. Objection: The consciousness of the five sense doors is naturally distracted, since it views external objects; therefore how could body consciousness occur in equipoise? If it did occur, one would be distracted to external objects and body consciousness would arise, and then concentration would degenerate and one would rise from abiding in equipoise. Since physical pleasure does not occur in equipoise, it is untenable that it is a branch of absorption. And not only that. Desire-realm beings attain the level of absorption through generating equipoise in contaminated and uncontaminated absorption, and their desire-realm-body consciousness cannot apprehend form-realm tactile objects. They cannot generate body consciousness apprehending tactility in the form realm with their desire-realm-body sense faculty, since that tactility and body consciousness exist at the level of the form realm. And since both contaminated and uncontaminated branches cannot exist in a single collection, even tactility and body consciousness qualified by pliancy would be uncontaminated.

nyes pa de dag med de/ mnyam par bzhag pa na ting nge 'dzin gyi khyad par las skyes pa shin tu sbyangs pa'i reg bya zhes pa lus yang zhing zo mdog bde bar byed cing bde ba'i tshor ba dang mthun pa'i rlung gis lus la rgyas shing khyab pas de'i mthus shin tu sbyangs pa'i reg bya la dmigs pa'i ting nge 'dzin dang mthun pa'i lus shes mtshungs ldan dang bcas pa 'byung ba'i phyir dang*/ ting nge 'dzin las skyes pa'i lus shes mtshungs ldan dang bcas pa de nyid lus kyi nang du 'byung bas phyi rol tu g.yengs par yang mi 'gyur la/ ting nge 'dzin dang mthun pa'i phyir de skyes pa na ting nge 'dzin las nyams pa dang*/ langs par yang mi 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ spyir 'dod pa'i lus dbang gis gzugs kyi reg bya la dmigs pa'i lus shes skyed pa'i khyab pa med kyang*/ 'dir ting nge 'dzin gyis stobs bskyed pa'i mthus mnyam gzhag gi 'dod pa'i lus dbang gis gzugs kyi shin tu sbyangs pa'i reg bya la dmigs pa shin tu sbyangs pa'i lus shes mtshungs ldan dang bcas pa bskyed nus shing*/ de nyid kyis na lus bde bsam gtan gyi yan lag tu'ang grub la/ shin tu sbyangs pa'i reg bya dang lus shes zag med du thal ba ni 'dod pa nyid de/ lam gyi tshogs kyi mdo las/ lus shin tu sbyangs pa yang dag byang chub kyi yan lag mngon par shes pa dang*/ rdzogs par byang chub pa dang*/ mya ngan las 'da' bar 'gyur ba gang yin pa dang*/ sems shin tu sbyangs pa yang dag byang chub kyi yan lag mngon par shes pa dang*/ rdzogs par byang chub pa dang*/ mya ngan las 'da' bar 'gyur ba gang yin pa zhes lus shin tu sbyangs pa byang chub kyi yan lag tu gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: Those faults would not arise. In equipoise the lightness and buoyancy of the body that are tactile objects of pliancy arising from specific concentration produce pleasure, the wind compatible with the feeling of pleasure expands and pervades the body, and by its might body consciousness compatible with concentration that focuses on the tactile objects of pliancy and its concomitant states arises. Body consciousness arising from concentration and its concomitant states is not distracted to external objects since it arises inside the body; it is compatible with concentration. And when that has arisen, concentration [657] does not degenerate, nor does one rise from it. In general, there is no logical pervasion that the body sense faculty of the desire realm generates the body sense faculty focusing on the tactile objects of the form realm. However, in this context, the body sense faculty of a desire-realm being in equipoise, due to the power of his concentration, is capable of generating pliancy concomitant with body consciousness that focuses on tactile objects of pliancy of the form realm. And due to that, physical pleasure is also established as a branch of absorption. But for those who assert that it follows that tactile objects of pliancy and body consciousness would be uncontaminated, the Multiple Paths Sūtra states: Any requisite of enlightenment of physical pliancy that becomes higher perception, complete enlightenment, and nirvāṇa, and any requisite of enlightenment of mental pliancy that becomes higher perception, complete enlightenment, and nirvāṇa . . .[1893] This passage suggests that physical pliancy is a requisite of enlightenment.

'o na skye mched drug gi tshogs kyi mdo las/ zag pa dang bcas pa'i chos rnams gang zhe na/ mig ji snyed pa dang gzugs rnams ji snyed pa dang mig gi rnam par shes pa ji snyed pa dang zhes pa nas lus ji snyed pa dang reg bya rnams ji snyed pa dang lus kyi rnam par shes pa ji snyed pa'o zhes bya ba'i bar du khams bco lnga po thams cad zag bcas kho nar gsungs pa dang 'gal lo zhe na/ dpes ston pa na re de ni shin tu sbyangs pa'i reg bya dang lus shes ma gtogs pa'i reg bya dang lus shes gzhan la dgongs nas gsungs pa'i phyir nyes pa med do zhes zer ro/ /

Objection: Now, this contradicts the Assembly of Six Bases Sūtra, which declares: What are contaminated phenomena? Any eye, any form, any eye consciousness . . . up to . . . any body, any tactile object, any body consciousness . . . all fifteen elements are contaminated states alone.[1894] Dārṣṭāntikas say: There is no fault, because that is stated with the intention of [ordinary] body consciousness and tactile objects that are other than the body consciousness and tactile objects of pliancy.

bsam gtan gnyis pa'i yan lag nang rab tu dang ba ni rgyu bsam gtan dang po'i rtog dpyod kyi 'khrug pa dang bral zhing dang pos 'dod pa las nges par 'byung bar ma zad 'dis mnyam gzhag gi sa dang po las kyang nges par 'byung bas de la yid ches pa'i dad pa yin no/ / 'dir skal ldan khyad par can na re sems kyi gnas skabs rtog dpyod zhi ba tsam nang rab tu dwang ba yin la/ de bzhin du rtog dpyod dang ting nge 'dzin la sogs pa'ang sems las rdzas gzhan ma yin gyi sems kyi gnas skabs la btags pa yin no zhes zer ba ni mi rigs te/ de dag rgyu 'bras yin pas rdzas tha dad pa'i phyir ro/ / yang gal te bsam gtan snga ma gnyis kyis dga' ba yid bder 'dod pa ni mi rigs te/ sde pa gzhan dag dga' ba sems byung gi chos gzhan {yid kyi sa pa kho na } yin la yid bde bsam gtan gsum char gyi'ang bde bar 'dod pa ltar bsam gtan gsum char gyi bde ba ni dga' ba las gzhan pa'i yid bde yin no zhe na/

Pure internal clarity (prasāda) that is a branch of the second absorption is free of the disturbance of investigation and analysis of the first absorption that is its cause, and it is convictional faith (śraddhā). For not only does the first absorption definitely emerge from the desire realm, but the second definitely emerges from equipoise of the first [absorption]. In this context, Bhagavadviśeṣa declares: Pure internal clarity is the mind when investigation and analysis are pacified. So too investigation, analysis, concentration, and so on are not different in substance from the mind and imputed [or defined] within the sphere of the mind. Reply: This is illogical because pure internal clarity and the mind, since they are cause and effect, are distinct in substance. Question: If it is illogical to assert that joy of the first two absorption levels is mental satisfaction, then pleasure of the third absorption would be mental satisfaction that is other than joy, since other schools assert that joy is another mental factor {of the level of mind alone} and mental satisfaction is pleasure of the third absorption.

bsam gtan snga ma gnyis na ni dga' ba las 'dod chags dang ma bral bas nye bar ma zhi bas dga' ba kho na yid bde ba yin la/ gsum pa ni dga' ba las 'dod chags dang bral bas nye bar zhi bas sems bde kho na yin gyi yid bde ni ma yin te/ bsam gtan yan lag las nges 'byung yin pas rnam par bsgyur pa'i mdo las bsam gtan gsum pa bka' bstsal nas/ 'dir 'di'i yid bde ba'i dbang po skyes pa ma lus par 'gag par 'gyur ro zhes pa dang*/ bsam gtan bzhi pa la ni bde ba'i dbang po 'gag par 'gyur ro zhes pa dang*/ bsam gtan gyi yan lag ston pa'i mdo las/ de 'dod pas dben sdig to mi dge ba'i chos kyis dben pa rtog pa dang bcas shing dpyod pa dang bcas pa dben pa las skyes pa'i dga' ba dang bde ba can bsam gtan dang po nye bar bsgrubs te gnas so/ / de rnam par rtog pa dang rnam par dpyod pa nye bar zhi nas nang yongs su dang ste sems kyi rgyud gcig tu gyur pas rtog pa med pa dpyod pa med pa ting nge 'dzin las skyes pa'i dga' ba dang bde ba can bsam gtan gnyis pa nye bar bsgrubs te gnas so/ / de dga' ba las 'dod chags dang bral bas dran pa dang ldan zhing shes bzhin du btang snyoms la gnas te/ bde ba lus kyis smyong la 'phags pa rnams kyis de la dran pa dang ldan pa bde ba la rnam par spyod pa btang snyoms pa'o zhes brjod pa ste dga' ba med pa'i bsam gtan gsum pa nye bar bsgrubs te gnas so/ / de bde ba yang spangs sdug bsngal ba yang spangs shing yid bde ba dang yid mi bde ba snga nas kyang nub pas bde ba yang med sdug bsngal ba yang med pa btang snyoms dang dran pas yongs su dag pa'i bsam gtan bzhi pa nye bar bsgrubs te gnas so zhes lung rnam pa gnyis las gsum par yid bde 'gag cing bzhi par bde ba de ma thag pa sems bde dang yid bde ni snga ma{ bsam gtan} gsum pa nas grangs par gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / {dga' bde gnyis tshor ba bde bar 'dra yang dga' bas sems ma zhi bar byed la/ zhi bar gyur pa'i tshe sa gzhan thob na de'i rigs can gyi tshor ba la bde ba zhes brjod do }

Reply: In the first two absorptions, joy alone is mental satisfaction since one neither is free from nor has pacified attachment to joy. In the third absorption, it is [658] mental bliss alone, since one is free from, and has pacified, attachment to joy. It is not mental satisfaction since one has definitely transcended that branch of absorption. The Range of the Bodhisattva Sūtra notes: According to the description of the third absorption, the arising of the faculty of mental satisfaction fully ceases on this level without exception.[1895] And: On the fourth absorption, the faculty of pleasure ceases.[1896] And the Branches of Absorption Sūtra states: One establishes and abides in the first absorption that possesses investigation and analysis free from the desire realm and free from evil nonvirtuous states, and one possesses joy and pleasure arising from that separation. One establishes and abides in the second absorption that possesses joy and pleasure arising from concentration free from investigation and free from analysis, since the single continuum of the mind attains complete internal clarity through pacifying investigation and analysis. One establishes and abides in the third absorption free of joy that possesses mindfulness and abides in equanimity through introspection, since one is free of attachment to joy but possesses pleasure experienced by the body that is called by āryas “equanimity possessing mindfulness that experiences pleasure.” One establishes and abides in the completely pure fourth absorption since it is mindful of equanimity free of pleasure and free of pain, having abandoned pleasure and abandoned pain, and mental satisfaction and mental dissatisfaction have previously subsided.[1897] Therefore these two scriptures (āgama) state that in the third absorption mental satisfaction ceases, and in the fourth absorption mental bliss ceases immediately after pleasure ceases while mental satisfaction was abandoned earlier in the third {absorption}. {Though both joy and pleasure are similar in being the feeling of pleasure, the mind is not pacified by joy. The type of feeling that arises when the mind is pacified and one obtains another level is called “pleasure.”}

des na bsam gtan snga ma gnyis kyis bde ba ni shin tu sbyangs pa dang yid bde ni dga' ba yin la/ gsum pa la ni sems kyi sim pa nyid bde bar bzhag go zhes bye brag tu smra ba 'dod cing*/ kha cig yid bde ni yid dga' ba yin la/ bsam gtan la bde ba yan lag tu bshad pa ni lus bde yin te/ de yang lus shin tu sbyangs pa las skyes pa'i bde ba yin par 'dod la/ bzhi pa la ni de yang spangs par 'dod do/ / ci nyon mongs can gyi bsam gtan la'ang sngar bshad pa'i yan lag de dag yod dam zhe na/

Therefore the pleasure of the first two absorptions is pliancy, and mental satisfaction (saumanasya) is joy (prīti). On the third absorption the joy of the mind itself is posited as pleasure. This is asserted by Vaibhāṣikas. Some say: Mental satisfaction is mental joy, and that which is explained as the branch of pleasure in the absorptions is physical pleasure, since that is asserted to be pleasure arising from physical pliancy. Mental satisfaction is abandoned on the fourth absorption. Question: Do those branches previously explained also exist for afflicted absorption?
nyon mongs can la dga' bde dang / / rab dang shes bzhin dran pa dang / / btang snyoms dran pa dag pa med/ / kha cig shin tu sbyangs btang snyoms/ / 10

Some say: Afflicted absorption has no joy nor pleasure, nor internal clarity, nor introspection and mindfulness, nor equanimity, mindfulness, and purity. Some say: They have no pliancy nor equanimity. (8:10)
kha cig yod la kha cig med de/
Some say: Yes.

'di ltar nyon mongs pa can gyi bsam gtan dang po la ni de'i sa pa'i nyon mongs las dben pa ma yin{ zhing de dang mtshungs par ldan} pas dben pa las skyes pa'i dga' ba dang bde ba med cing*/ gnyis pa la ni de'i sa pa'i nyon mongs pas brnyogs pas rab tu ma dang bas nad rab tu dang ba med la/ gsum pa la ni nyon mongs can gyi bde bas kun tu rmongs shing bslad pas shes bzhin dang dran pa med cing*/{ dge ba'i sa mang po pa yin pas btang snyoms kyang med do/ /} bzhi pa la ni de'i sa pa'i nyon mongs pas dri ma can du byas pas btang snyoms dang dran pa yongs su dag pa med do/ grub mtha' 'dzin pa kha cig na re nyon mongs can gyi bsam gtan dang po dang gnyis pa na ni shin tu sbyangs pa med la/ gsum pa dang bzhi pa na ni 'du byed btang snyoms med de/ de dag ni nyon mongs can yin la shin tu sbyangs pa dang btang snyoms ni dge ba'i sa mang po ba yin pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ / des na dga' ba ni 'dod pas dben pa las skyes pa'i dga' ba dang*/ nang rab tu dwang ba ni rtog dpyod zhi ba dang*/ dran pa dang shes bzhin ni dmigs pa ma brjed pa dang shes rab tsam la 'dod pa'i phyir nyon mongs can la'ang yod do zhes bya bar 'dod do/ / 'o na lugs snga ma ltar na{ gnyis pa'i} shin tu sbyangs pa dang{ gsum pa'i} btang snyoms yod dam med ce na/ kha cig na re de dag dge ba yin pas dngos su med par ma bshad kyang med par grub bo zhes zer ro/ / kha cig na re de dag med par ma bshad pas yod do zhes {gnyis pa'i shin tu sbyangs pa dang*/ gsum pa'i btang snyoms kha cig de gnyis dge ba yin pas med par 'dod la kha cig med par ma bshad pas yod par 'dod do } zer ro/ /

Some say: No. That is because the first afflicted (kliṣṭa) absorption has no joy (prīti) nor pleasure (sukha) arising from separation, since it is not free from the affliction of its level {but is instead concomitant with affliction}. The second absorption does not have internal clarity (prasāda) since it is disturbed by affliction of its level through internal nonclarity. [659] The third has no introspection (saṃpradhī) and mindfulness (smṛti) through being fully affected by afflicted pleasure. {Also it has no equanimity since it is a virtuous mental state.} The fourth has no equanimity (upekṣā), mindfulness, or thorough purity (śuddha) since it is stained by affliction of its level. Some holders of tenets say: The first and second afflicted absorptions do not have pliancy (prasrabdhi), and the third and fourth have no applied equanimity because they are afflicted, and pliancy and equanimity are virtuous mental states. Therefore, because joy is the joy that arises from separating from the desire realm, pure internal clarity pacifies investigation and analysis, mindfulness does not forget the focal object, and introspection is mere wisdom, they also exist for afflicted states. Question: In accordance with the above system, do pliancy {of the second absorption} and equanimity {of the third absorption} exist or not? Some say: Since they are virtuous states, they are not explicitly described as not existing there. However they are established as not existing there. Others say: They exist there, since they are not described as not existing there. {One asserts: Those two — pliancy of the second and equanimity of the third — do not exist there since they are virtuous. Another asserts: They exist there since they are not described as not existing there.}[1898]
skyon brgyad las ni grol ba'i phyir/ / bzhi pa g.yo ba med pa yin/ / rtog dang dpyod dang dbugs dag dang / / bde ba la sogs bzhi yin no/ / 11
The fourth is immovable because it is liberated from the eight flaws: investigation, analysis, breath, and the four such as pleasure. (8:11)

gzhan yang bcom ldan 'das kyis lung bar ma las/ bsam gtan dang po gsum ni skyon dang bcas pa'i phyir g.yo ba dang bcas pa dag yin no zhes gsungs pas bsam gtan bzhi pa ni g.yo ba med pa yin te/ 'og sa'i skyon brgyad las grol ba'i phyir ro/ / de la skyon brgyad ni rtog pa dang dpyod pa gnyis dang dbugs rngub pa dang 'byung ba dag ste gnyis dang bde ba dang*/ sogs pas gzung ba sdug bsngal dang*/ yid bde dang yid mi bde dang bzhi ste brgyad yin no/ / gzhan dag na re bsam gtan dang po ni rtog dpyod dang gnyis pa ni dga' ba dang*/ gsum pa ni bde bas g.yo bas skyon dang bcas la bzhi pa ni de dag dang bral bas mi g.yo ba yin te/ lu hi ta'i mdo las/ bsam gtan bzhi pa ni dper na rlung med pa'i mar me rlung gis mi g.yo ba de dang 'dra'o zhes rlung med pa'i mar me dper mdzad nas gsungs pa'i phyir ro zhes zer ro/ / 'o na snga ma gnyis na yid bde dang gsum pa na bde ba dang*/ bzhi pa na btang snyoms kho na yod par bshad na ci rgyu snyoms 'jug bsam gtan dang po na bde ba dang gnyis pa na yod pa'i tshor ba yid bde dang gsum pa na bde ba dang bzhi pa na yod pa'i btang snyoms de dag 'bras bu skye ba na'ang yod dam zhe na/

The Bhagavan stated in the Medium-Length Discourses: The first three absorptions are movable because they possess flaws.[1899] Therefore the fourth absorption is immovable (āniñjya) because it is liberated (mukta) from the eight flaws (aṣṭāpakṣāla). The eight flaws are (1–2) both investigation (vitarka) and analysis (vicāra), (3–4) both inhalation and exhalation of the breath (śvāsa), and the four (5–8) such as pleasure (sukha) and so on, which includes pain, mental satisfaction, and mental dissatisfaction. Another says: Since the first absorption is moved by investigation and analysis, the second is moved by joy, and the third is moved by pleasure, they possess flaws. The fourth is immovable since it is free of such flaws. As the Lohita Sūtra says: The fourth absorption is like the flame of a lamp free of wind, not moved by the wind.[1900] Question: If it is said that mental satisfaction exists in the first two absorptions, pleasure exists in the third, and equanimity alone on the fourth — and in terms of causal meditative attainment, pleasure exists in the first absorption, the feeling of mental satisfaction exists in the second, pleasure exists in the third, and equanimity exists in the fourth — then do they also exist for resultant-birth meditative attainment or not?
skye ba'i bsam gtan dag na ni/ / yid bde bde dang btang snyoms dang / / btang snyoms yid bde bde ba dang / / btang snyoms btang snyoms tshor ba yod/ / 12
From birth in those absorptions, mental satisfaction, pleasure, and equanimity exist; equanimity and mental satisfaction; pleasure and equanimity; and the feeling of equanimity. (8:12)
bzhi pa na de lta yin mod kyi gzhan na ni de lta ma yin te/
Reply: Indeed, that is so on the fourth absorption but not so for the other absorptions,
