skye ba'i bsam gtan bzhi po dag las bsam gtan dang po na ni yid kyi sa pa'i yid bde dang mig rna lus kyi rnam shes gsum dang mtshungs ldan gyi bde ba dang rnam shes bzhi char gyi btang snyoms dang*/ gnyis pa na ni rnam shes gzhan med pas yid kyi sa pa kho na'i btang snyoms dang yid bde dang*/ gsum pa na ni yid kyi sa pa'i sems kyi bde ba dang btang snyoms dang*/ bzhi pa na ni yid kyi sa pa'i btang snyoms kyi tshor ba kho na yod do/ gal te bsam gtan gnyis pa la sogs pa na min shes la sogs pa gsum dang rtog dpyod med na gzugs dang sgra dang reg bya 'dzin pa dang lus ngag gi rnam par rig byed slong bar ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/

since from birth in those four absorptions (dhyānopapatti), mental satisfaction (saumanasya) of the level of the mental faculty, pleasure (sukha) concomitant with the three consciousnessess of eye, ear, and body, and equanimity (upekṣa) of the four parts [660] of consciousness exist on the first absorption. Equanimity and mental satisfaction (sumanaska) of the level of the mental faculty alone exist on the second absorption. Mental bliss and equanimity of the level of the mental faculty exist on the third absorption. The feeling of equanimity of the level of the mental faculty exists on the fourth absorption alone. Question: How could form, sound, and tactile objects be apprehended, and the indicative form of body and speech arise, on the second absorption if the three consciousnesses of eye, ear, and body, as well as investigation and analysis, do not exist there?
gnyis pa sogs na lus mig dang / / rna ba'i rnam shes rnam rig slong / / gang yin de ni dang por gtogs/ / de lung ma bstan nyon mongs min/ / 13
On the second absorption and so on, consciousnesses of body, eye, ear, and that which motivates indicative form belong to the first absorption. They are neutral and not afflicted. (8:13)
gnyis pa la sogs par skyes pa rnams la mig shes la sogs pa de dag med pa'ang ma yin la rang gi sa pa'ang ma yin no/ / 'o na ji lta bu zhe na/

Reply: It is not that those born on the second absorption and so on do not have eye consciousness and so forth, it is just that it does not belong to that level. Question: Now, how is that established?

bsam gtan gnyis pa la sogs pa sa gong ma gsum po dag na lus dang mig dang rna ba'i rnam shes gsum dang lus dang ngag gis rnam par rig byed kun slong rtog dpyod la nges par ltos shing rang sa na de med pas kun nas slong bar byed pa'i rtog dpyod gang yin pa de ni bsam gtan dang po'i sar gtogs pa yin te dper na sa gong ma pa dag 'og sa'i sprul pa sprul par 'dod pa na 'og sa'i sprul sems gong ma'i rten la mngon du byed pa bzhin no zhes bye brag tu smra ba 'dod la/ / {des nas des bsdus pa med kyi rten de la yod la/ des bslang ba'i chos de dag kyang dang po'i sa pa dang ma bsgribs lung ma bstan yin no gsung ngo } de yang gong sar mngon da byed pa'i mig la sogs pa'i rnam shes dang rtog dpyod gang yin pa de ni ma bsgribs lung ma bstan yin gyi de dag mi dgos pa'i dman pa yin pa'i phyir dge ba ma yin pa'am/ yang na dang po'i dge ba ni rnam smin dang bcas pa yin na dang po'i rnam smin ni gnyis pa la sogs pa don du mi gnyer bas de'i rgyu dge ba'i sems mngon du bya ba la 'bad pa mi byed do zhes rgyal po'i sras 'chad do/ / 'og sa las 'dod chags dang bral { zhing dang po'i de dag spangs} ba'i phyir nyon mongs can yang min te sprul pa'i sems bzhin no/ / bsam gtan dang po'i lung ma bstan de dag ni dman pa yin yang{ mthong thos sogs la} dgos pa'i phyir mngon du byed kyi de yang gus pas ni ma yin no/ / dpes ston pa la sogs pa ni bsam gtan phyi ma gsum na'ang rnam shes tshogs gsum ga yod par 'dod do/ /

Reply: On the three higher levels — the second absorption and so on — beings definitely rely on the three consciousnesses of body (kāya), eye (akṣi), and ear (śrotra), as well as investigation and analysis that motivates (utthāpaka) the indicative form (vijñapti) of body and speech. But since [investigation and analysis] don’t exist on those [three] levels, that investigation and analysis which motivates body and speech belong to the level of the first absorption. For example, it is like one of higher level who desires to project an emanation of lower level and manifests the mind of a lower-level emanation in a higher-realm being. This is asserted by Vaibhāṣikas. {Therefore such states are not subsumed by higher levels, but that being has them. Phenomena motivated by such states belong to the first level and are unobscured-neutral states}. Moreover, any eye consciousness and so on, or investigation and analysis, that manifest in higher levels are unobscured-neutral (avyākṛta) states. They are not virtuous because they are inferior states that are not required in higher realms. Or, again, if virtuous states of the first absorption possess karmic maturation, then beings of higher realms do not strive to manifest the virtuous mind that is their cause, since karmic maturation of first-absorption states is not sought after the second absorption. This is explained by Jinaputra. Also they are not afflicted (akliṣṭa) because they are free of attachment to lower levels {and abandon first-absorption states} like the emanating mind. Though those neutral states of the first absorption are inferior, they are manifested because they possess required functions {such as seeing and hearing}. They are not manifested out of admiration for them. Dārṣṭāntikas and so on also assert that the threefold collection of consciousness exists on the three latter absorptions.
bzhi pa 'thob tshul
How the absorptions and formless states are obtained
['di] la gsum las
This has three headings: pure meditative attainment, uncontaminated meditative attainment, and afflicted meditative attainment.
de dang mi ldan 'dod chags bral/ / skye ba las ni dag pa 'thob/ /
Those who did not possess the pure state obtain it through freedom from attachment or from birth. (8:14ab)
dang po dag pa ba ni
PURE MEDITATIVE ATTAINMENT

'og sa las 'dod chags dang bral ba dang*/ gong nas 'og tu skye ba dang*/ sbyor ba dang*/ chags bral las nyams pa bzhis 'thob pa las dag pa pa de dang sngar gtan mi ldan pa ni 'og sa las 'dod chags dang bral ba'am/ srid rtse ma gtogs pa gong sa nas 'og sar skye ba las ni nges 'byed cha mthun gyi dag pa ba ma gtogs pa gsum 'thob kyi/ srid rtse ni de bas mtho ba'i sa med cing 'og sa nas der skye ba na {rgyu snyoms 'jug} de sngar nas ldan pa skye bas gsar 'thob med pas 'og sa las 'dod chags dang bral ba kho nas 'thob kyi skye bas 'thob pa med do/{ 'dod chags dang bral bas 'thob pa de yang nges 'byed cha mthun ma gtogs so/ /}

The pure state is obtained by four causes: (1) freedom from attachment to lower levels, (2) being born in lower levels from higher levels, (3) preparation, and (4) degeneration from nonattachment. Those who did not previously possess it, obtain pure (śuddha) meditative attainment through freedom from attachment (vairāgya) to lower levels or from birth (upapatti) in lower levels from higher levels except for the summit of existence. Three are obtained except for the pure factor conducive to penetrative insight. The summit of existence [661] has no level above it, and when one is born there from lower level, it is obtained through freedom from attachment to lower levels alone; one is born there through possessing prior {causal meditative attainment}. It is not newly obtained since one was previously born in possession of it, and it is not obtained from birth. {Obtainment through freedom from attachment excludes the factor conducive to penetrative insight.}

de yang sngar mi ldan pa'i dbang du byas kyi dag pa pa dang sngar nas ldan pa ni nges 'byed cha mthun gyi bsam gtan dag pa pa chags bral dang skye bas mi 'thob kyi sbyor bas 'thob la/ gnas pa cha mthun las nyams na nyams pa'i cha mthun dang*/ bsam gtan dang po las 'dod chags dang bral ba las nyams pa las dang po'i nyams pa'i cha mthun 'thob pa lta bu nyams pa las kyang 'thob bo/ / de nyid kyi phyir bstan bcos las/ bsam gtan dag pa pa 'dod chags dang bral bas 'thob par 'gyur la/ 'dod chags dang bral bas 'dor bar 'gyur ba dang*/ de bzhin du yongs su nyams pa dang skye ba las 'thob pa dang 'dor bar 'gyur ba yod dam zhe na/ yod de/ bsam gtan dang po nyams pa'i cha dang mthun pa'o/ / de ni 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral bas 'thob la/ tshangs pa'i 'jig rten las 'dod chags dang bral bas 'dor ro/ / tshangs pa'i 'jig rten las 'dod chags dang bral ba las yongs su nyams pa las 'thob la/ 'dod pa las 'dod chags dang bral ba las yongs su nyams pa las 'dor ro/ / gong nas tshangs pa'i 'jig rten du skye ba na 'thob la/ de nas 'dod pa'i khams su skye ba na 'dor ro zhes 'byung ngo*/ / tshangs pa'i 'jig rten ni bsam gtan dang po'o/ / des na bsam gtan dang po las 'dod chags dang bral bas ni dang po'i nyams pa'i cha mthun 'dor te/ dang po'i nyon mongs dang mthun pa'i phyir dang po'i nyon mongs bzhin no/ /

Further, the pure state not possessed previously and that which was previously possessed are not obtained through freedom from attachment and from birth; they are obtained by preparation. If it degenerates and is no longer conducive to abidance, it is conducive to decline. For example, through detachment to the first absorption degenerating, one obtains the state conducive to the first absorption degenerating. Therefore the Great Treatise on Differentiation[1901] remarks: Is pure absorption obtained by freedom from attachment? Is it lost due to freedom from attachment? So too, is it obtained and lost from degeneration and from birth? Yes, factors conducive to degeneration of the first absorption exist. It itself is obtained from freedom from attachment to the desire realm. It is lost through freedom from attachment to the heaven of Brahma. It is obtained from the complete degeneration of freedom from attachment to the heaven of Brahma. It is lost through the complete degeneration of freedom from attachment to the desire realm. It is obtained when one is born in the heaven of Brahma from a higher level, and then lost when one is born in the desire realm.[1902] “The heaven of Brahma” refers to the first absorption. Therefore through freedom from attachment to the first absorption, the factor conducive to degeneration of the first absorption subsides. Because something is compatible with affliction of the first absorption, it is like affliction of the first absorption.
gnyis pa
UNCONTAMINATED MEDITATIVE ATTAINMENT
zag med 'dod chags bral ba yis/ /
The uncontaminated is obtained by freedom from attachment. (8:14c)

{bsam gtan gzugs med kyi } snyoms 'jug zag med ni rgyu bzhi po de dag las sngar mi ldan pa las ni 'dod chags dang bral ba yis 'thob cing {de yang lam ni zag bcas zag med gang gis bral yang rung ngo*/ / de ni phyir mi 'ong kho na ste/ 'bras bu dang po gnyis ni dngos gzhis ma bsdus bas so/ /} de dag sngar nas zag med dang ldan pa ni sbyor ba'i stobs kyis zad shes las kyang mi slob pa dngos gzhis bsdus pa 'thob la/ dbang po rtul po rnon por 'phos na rnon pos bsdus pa'i slob pa dang mi slob pa 'thob bo/ / phyir mi 'ong chags bral sngon 'gros bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi la brten nas nges pa la 'jug pa las kyang zag med kyi bsam gtan dngos gzhi 'thob kyang mthar gyis pa mi lcogs med kho na la brten nas nges pa la 'jug na dngos gzhi mi 'thob pas thams cad kyis 'thob par ma nges pas nges pa la 'jug pas 'thob pa ma bshad cing*/ mi slob pa nyams na slob pas bsdus pa'i snyoms 'jug dngos gzhi 'thob kyang snyoms 'jug zag med kyi rigs tsam sngar nas ldan pas gsar thob med pas nyams pas 'thob pa'ang ma bshad la/ / {sa de dag tu skyes pa'i byis pa'ang zag med dang ldan par thal bas } zag med la skye bas 'thob pa ni med do/

Uncontaminated (anāsrava) meditative attainment {of the absorptions and formless states} is obtained by freedom from attachment (vairāgya) through not possessing those four previous causes. {Further, the path may also [be designated as] the freedom attained by any contaminated or uncontaminated state. This refers to nonreturn alone, since the first two results [stream entry and once return] are not subsumed by the actual basis.} Possessing prior uncontaminated states is due to the power of preparation. If one upgrades from dull faculty to sharp faculty, one obtains learner or nonlearner states subsumed by sharp faculty. Nonreturners previously freed from attachment definitely enter uncontaminated meditative attainment in dependence on the actual basis. Though serial abandoners obtain the actual basis of uncontaminated absorption, they definitely enter uncontaminated meditative attainment in dependence on unrestricted access concentration, but it is not said that they definitely enter obtainment. They do not obtain the actual basis, since it is not definite that they obtain it by all paths. If nonlearners degenerate, they obtain the actual basis of meditative attainment subsumed by the learner path. But it is not said that they obtain it, since they previously possessed the mere lineage of uncontaminated meditative attainment and it is not newly obtained. There is no obtainment through uncontaminated states arising, [662] {since it would then follow that even childlike beings born in those levels would possess uncontaminated states}.
gsum pa snyoms 'jug nyon mongs can ni
AFFLICTED MEDITATIVE ATTAINMENT
nyon mongs can nyams skye ba yis/ / 14
The afflicted is obtained by degeneration and birth. (8:14d)

sngar de dang mi ldan pa las bsam gtan dang po las 'dod chags dang bral ba las yongs su nyams na bsam gtan dang po nyon mongs can 'thob pa lta bu yongs su nyams pas 'thob pa dang srid rtse ma gtogs pa bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad nas dang por skyes na dang po'i nyon mongs can 'thob pa lta bu gong sa nas 'og sar skye ba yis 'thob pa gnyis yod kyi 'di 'og nas gong du skye ba'am chags bral gyis mi 'thob ste 'di sngar nas ldan pas sbyor ba dang 'dod chags dang bral bas 'thob pa ni med do/ /

Afflicted (kliṣṭa) meditative attainment has two types: (1) if freedom from attachment to the first absorption fully degenerates for one who did not previously possess such attachment, one obtains the afflicted first absorption, and this is obtained by complete degeneration (hānya). And (2) if one is born in the first absorption from the second absorption or higher, excluding the summit of existence, one obtains the afflicted first absorption, and this is obtained by birth (upapatti) in a lower level from a higher level. It is not obtained due to birth in a higher level from a lower level, nor due to freedom from attachment, since it is possessed from before and not obtained by preparation or freedom from attachment.
lnga pa khyad par gyi chos bshad pa ni
Specific attributes
zag pa med pa'i mjug thogs su/ / ltag 'og gsum pa'i bar dge ba/ / skye'o dag pa las de bzhin/ / rang gi sa pa'i nyon mongs kyang / / 15
After uncontaminated states, the virtue of three, including higher and lower levels, arises. After pure states is similar. But afflicted states of its level also occur. (8:15)
'o na snyoms 'jug gi rdzas de dag gang gi 'jug tu du zhig skye zhe na/
Question: At the end of what states is the substance of meditative attainment generated?

zag pa med pa'i bsam gtan dang gzugs med pa'i 'jug thogs su rang sa dang { bcas na }ltag gi sa gnyis te sa gsum gyi bar gyi dge ba{ zag bcas} zag med dang*/ {rang dang } 'og ma{ gnyis te sa} gsum pa'i bar gyi dge ba zag bcas zag med dag skye'o/ / 'di yang spyir bstan pa tsam zhig yin gyi thams cad du ni ma yin te/ bsam gtan dang po zag pa med pa'i 'jug thogs su 'og ma'i snyoms 'jug dag pa pa dang zag med skye ba med pa'i phyir dang*/ ci yang med pa'i skye mched zag med kyi 'jug thogs su yang gong ma'i zag med skye ba med pa'i phyir ro/ /

Reply: After (anantara) uncontaminated (anāsrava) absorption and formless-realm states, the {contaminated and} uncontaminated virtue of three levels — its level {and associated states} and two higher levels — and the contaminated and uncontaminated virtue of three {levels — its own and two} lower {levels} — arises. In general, this is merely a general presentation and it does not apply in all cases because after the uncontaminated first absorption, pure or uncontaminated lower meditative attainments do not arise; and after the uncontaminated base of nothingness, higher uncontaminated states do not arise.

des na zag med kyi bsam gtan dang po'i 'jug thogs su drug skye ste/ rgyun gyi tshe rang gi sa pa'i zag med dang*/ snyoms mjug las langs pa'i rang gi sa pa'i dag pa pa dang*/ zag bcas dang spel nas lugs bzhin snyoms par 'jug pa'i tshe bsam gtan gnyis pa'i dag pa pa dang*/ zag bcas dang ma spel bar lugs bzhin snyoms par 'jug pa dang thod rgal gyi sbyor ba'i tshe ma spel bar lugs dang mthun par snyoms par 'jug pa na bsam gtan gnyis pa'i zag med dang*/ spel nas ris mi mthun pa gsum par 'gro ba'i tshe thod rgal dngos bsam gtan gsum pa'i dag pa pa dang*/ ma spel bar gsum par 'gro ba na nye ba'i sbyor ba gsum pa'i zag med skye ba'i phyir ro/ / gong 'og gi bzhi pa phan chad ni skye ba mi srid de/ shin tu ring ba'i phyir dang*/ 'dod pa na zag med mi srid pa'i phyir dang*/ 'dod pa'i dge ba tsam skye yang snyoms 'jug ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / bsam gtan gnyis pa'i zag med kyi 'jug thogs su ni brgyad skye ste/ rgyun gyi tshe dang*/ de las langs pa'i tshe rim pa ltar rang gi sa pa'i zag med dag pa pa dang*/ ma spel bar lugs dang mthun par snyoms par 'jug pa'i tshe bsam gtan gsum pa'i zag med dang*/ spel nas lugs dang mthun par snyoms par 'jug pa'i tshe bsam gtan gsum pa'i dag pa pa dang*/ ma spel bar gsum par 'gro ba na nye sbyor bzhi pa'i zag med dang spel na thod rgal dngos bzhi pa'i dag pa pa dang*/ lugs dang mi mthun par snyoms par 'jug pa'i tshe ma spel na dang po'i zag med dang*/ spel na dag pa pa'ang skye ba'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du bsam gtan gsum pa'i zag med kyi 'jug thogs su bcu 'byung ste/ rang sa'i gnyis dang*/ bzhi pa'i gnyis dang*/ nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched kyi gnyis dang*/ bsam gtan gnyis pa'i gnyis dang*/ lugs dang mi mthun par gsum par 'gro ba na bsam gtan dang po'i gnyis kyang 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du bsam gtan bzhi pa dang*/ nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched kyi 'jug tu bcu bcu 'byung ba'ang ci rigs par shes par bya'o/ /

Therefore six arise after the uncontaminated first absorption: (1) the uncontaminated meditative attainment of one’s level arises when maintaining that state; (2) pure meditative attainment of one’s level arises when rising from meditative attainment; (3) the pure second absorption arises when entering meditative attainment of the forward order through enhancing contaminated states; (4) the uncontaminated second absorption arises through entering meditative attainment of the forward order without enhancing contaminated states, or through entering meditative attainment of the forward order without enhancement when preparing to skip levels; (5) the pure third absorption arises by omitting [or passing over] levels when advancing three stages through enhancement; and (6) the uncontaminated third absorption arises through preparing to proceed there without enhancement. It is impossible for a fourth stage higher or lower and beyond to arise because such stages are remote, because uncontaminated states are impossible in the desire realm, and because though desire-realm virtuous states arise, it is not meditative attainment. After the uncontaminated second absorption, eight arise: the uncontaminated pure meditative attainment of one’s level arises (1) when maintaining that state and (2) when rising from meditative attainment; (3) the uncontaminated third absorption arises when entering [663] meditative attainment of the forward order without enhancement; (4) the pure third absorption arises when entering meditative attainment of the forward order through enhancement, (5) the uncontaminated fourth absorption arises through preparing to proceed to the third absorption without enhancement, (6) the pure fourth absorption arises by omitting [or passing over] levels through enhancement, (7) the uncontaminated first absorption arises without enhancement when entering meditative attainment of the reverse order, and (8) pure absorption also arises through enhancement. So too, ten arise after the uncontaminated third absorption: (1–2) two of the third absorption, (3–4) two of the fourth absorption, (5–6) two of the base of infinite space, (7–8) two of the second absorption, and (9–10) two of the first absorption arise when advancing three stages in the reverse order. So too, you should understand that there are ten occurring after the fourth absorption and the base of infinite space.

rnam shes mtha' yas skye mched zag med kyi 'jug thogs su ni dgu 'byung ste rang sa'i gnyis dang*/ lugs dang mthun par snyoms par 'jug pa na ci yang med pa'i skye mched kyi gnyis dang*/ lugs dang mthun par ris mi mthun pa gsum par 'gro ba na snyoms 'jug las langs pa'i tshe srid rtse'i dag pa pa kho na 'byung ste/ de na rgyu ba zhan pas zag med med pa'i phyir ro/ / lugs dang mi mthun par snyoms par 'jug pa na nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched dang bsam gtan bzhi pa'i sa pa'i dag pa pa dang zag med gnyis gnyis dang*/ ci yang med pa'i skye mched kyi rjes su ni rang sa dang 'og sa rnam shes dang nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched kyi dag pa pa dang*/ zag med gnyis gnyis dang*/ gong sa srid rtse'i dag pa pa kho na dang bdun 'byung ngo*/ / de yang rjes shes kyi 'jug thogs su ni gzugs med la snyoms par 'jug gi chos shes kyi 'jug thogs su gzugs med la snyoms par mi 'jug ste/ gzugs med 'dod pa la mi dmigs shing*/ chos shes 'dod pa'i rten can dang*/ 'dod pa'i sdug bsngal la sogs pa la dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Nine occur after the uncontaminated base of infinite consciousness: (1–2) two of its own level and (3–4) two of the base of nothingness arise when entering meditative attainment of the forward order. (5) Pure meditative attainment of the summit of existence alone arises when rising from meditative attainment and advancing three stages in the forward order (it has no uncontaminated state since the summit possesses inferior movement) and when entering meditative attainment of the reverse order. (6–7) Both the pure and uncontaminated meditative attainments of the base of infinite space arise as well as (8–9) both the pure and uncontaminated meditative attainments of the fourth absorption. After the base of nothingness, seven occur: (1–6) both the pure and uncontaminated meditative attainments of its level and the two lower levels — the base of infinite consciousness and the base of infinite space — and (7) the pure meditative attainment of the higher level — the summit of existence. After subsequent knowledge, there is entry to formless-realm meditative attainment, but after Dharma knowledge there is no entry to formless-realm meditative attainment. For the formless realm does not focus on the desire realm, but Dharma knowledge focuses on beings of the desire realm, desire-realm suffering, and so on.

snyoms 'jug dag pa pa las dag pa pa dang zag med skye ba'ang dag pa pa yi 'jug thogs su/ ltag 'og gsum pa'i bar dge ba/ / skye'o zhes ji ltar zag med las du 'byung bshad pa de bzhin du rig par bya'o/ / 'on kyang khyad par ni 'di yod de/ dag pa pa las ni sngar 'byung ba de dag gi steng du lhag par snyoms 'jug nyon mongs can gyis gzir ba'i {tshe 'am ro myang ba na} rang rang gi sa pa'i nyon mongs can gyi bsam gtan yang 'byung gi zag med kyi 'jug thogs su ni nyon mongs can 'byung ba med do/ /

You should understand that after pure meditative attainment, pure and uncontaminated meditative attainments arise that are similar to those explained to arise after uncontaminated meditative attainment. Therefore, after pure states, “the virtue of three, including higher and lower levels, arises” (8:15ab). However, there is a difference because after pure meditative attainment, as well as those previously mentioned, afflicted absorptions of its level also occur when oppressed by afflicted meditative attainment {or when enjoying meditative attainment}. But no afflicted state occurs after uncontaminated meditative attainment.
nyon mongs can las rang dag dang / / nyon mongs 'og ma'i dag gcig kyang / / 'chi 'pho'i dag las nyon mongs kun/ / nyon mongs can las gong ma min/ / 16

After afflicted states, a pure state of its level as well as one pure state of lower level. At death any afflicted state can arise after the pure. Higher states do not arise from afflicted states. (8:16)

snyoms 'jug nyon mongs can las ni gal te shes bzhin dang dran pas zin na langs pa'i tshe rang sa'i dag pa pa dang*/ rgyun gyi tshe rang sa'i nyon mongs can dang*/ de dag tu ma zad rang sa'i nyon mongs des gzir ba las 'og ma'i dag pa pa la dga' bar 'gyur bas langs pa na sa 'og ma'i dag pa pa{ 'am dge ba kha} gcig kyang 'byung bar 'gyur ro/ gal te bdag gis bsam gtan 'di ni nyon mongs can zhig ste de bas ni 'og ma bzang ngo zhes rang sa'i nyon mongs can la skyon du shes nas 'og mar 'pho na ni dge ba las 'phos pa yin la/ 'on te nyon mongs can du ma shes na ni de las ji ltar 'og ma'i dge bar 'pho zhe na/ dang po snyoms par 'jug pa na gong ma'i nyon mongs can pas ni 'og ma'i dag pa pa bzang bas gong ma'i sems nyon mongs can du gyur na de ma thag tu 'og ma'i dag pa pa la gnas par gyur cig snyam du 'phangs pa'i phyir gong ma'i nyon mongs can gyi 'jug thogs su 'og ma'i dag pa pa 'byung ste dper na dus 'di tsam na ldang bar bya'o snyam du bsams nas gnyid log pa 'dod pa'i dus su sad par 'gyur ba bzhin no/ /

After afflicted (kliṣṭa) meditative attainment, pure (śuddha) meditative attainment of its level occurs when rising; afflicted meditative attainment of its level occurs when maintaining that state; and also one pure {or virtuous} meditative attainment of lower level occurs through taking joy in pure meditative attainment of lower level when oppressed by affliction of its level, [664] due to the influence of introspection and mindfulness. Question: It must be that he relocates to a lower virtuous level through realizing that his level is afflicted and thus flawed, reflecting, “My absorption is afflicted but the lower level is fine.” For if he does not know it is afflicted, how does he shift to a lower virtuous level? Reply: Because when he first enters meditative attainment, he sets his mind by thinking, “May I abide in the pure lower level as soon as higher mind becomes afflicted, since my level would be afflicted and lower level would be fine.” Then the pure mind of lower level arises after afflicted higher mind. For example, with the intention “I will get up at this time,” one awakens at just the time one wants to stop sleeping.
zag med ni nyon mongs can gyi 'jug thogs su rang sa dang 'og sa pa'ang rnam pa thams cad du mi skye'o/ /
After afflicted absorption, uncontaminated absorption does not arise either on its own level or on a lower level.

de yang snyoms par 'jug pa'i dus kyi dbang du byas nas dag pa pa dang nyon mongs can gyi 'jug tu rang sa'i nyon mongs can kho na skye'i gzhan sa'i nyon mongs can mi 'byung ngo zhes bshad kyi 'chi 'pho ba'i tshe ni skye ba'i bsam gtan dag na skyes thob kyi dge ba mnyam gzhag ma yin pas kyang bsam gtan dag pa pa'i ming thob pas snyoms 'jug dag pa pa las ni rang sa dang gong 'og gis gang du skye ba de dag thams cad kyi nying mtshams sbyor sems nyon mongs pa can kun 'byung ba srid de/ 'di ltar bsam gtan dang po pa lta bu'i dge ba skyes thob la gnas te rang sa dang gong 'og thams cad du skye ba srid la/ skye ba'i srid pa nyon mongs can zhes 'byung bas skye ba'i sems thams cad nyon mongs can du nges pa'i phyir ro/ / de yang 'chi 'pho'i tshe snyoms 'jug nyon mongs can las ni rang sa dang 'og sa'i nyon mongs can skye'i sa gong ma'i nyon mongs can mi 'byung bas gong ma skye ba min no/ / 'og sa'i nyon mongs ma spangs par gong mar mi skye bas na des der nying mtshams sbyor ba 'gal ba'i phyir ro/ / ci snyoms 'jug dag pa pa thams cad kyi 'jug thogs su rang sa dang gong 'og gi nyon mongs can dang dag pa pa dang zag med kyi snyoms 'jug 'byung ngam zhe na/

Further, from the perspective of the time of meditative attainment, it is said that after pure or afflicted absorption, only afflicted absorption of its level arises, and afflicted absorption of other levels does not arise. But at the time of death (cyuta) it is possible that any afflicted mind linking with any mind occurring on its level or any higher or lower level can arise after pure meditative equipoise. This is the case even if that being is called “one with pure absorption,” since it is not virtuous equipoise obtained after birth in the absorptions. So too it is possible that one abiding in virtue obtained from birth, such as a being of the first absorption, may be born on the same level, or on all higher or lower levels, because it is definite that all minds of birth are afflicted, since the birth existence is called “afflicted.” Further, at the time of death, afflicted absorption of the same or lower level arises, but higher afflicted absorption does not arise from afflicted meditative attainment. Thus it would be contradictory for it to link to it, since afflicted lower-level absorption is not abandoned and does not arise in higher levels. Question: Do afflicted, pure, or uncontaminated meditative attainment of the same level or higher or lower level occur after all meditative attainments?
dag pa nyams pa'i cha mthun sogs/ / rnam bzhi de ni go rims bzhin/ / nyon mongs skye dang rang sa dang / / gong dang zag med rjes mthun pa/ / 17

Pure states have four types, such as factors conducive to degeneration and so forth. They are antecedents of the arising of, respectively, affliction, same level, higher states, and uncontaminated states. (8:17)
ma yin te/
Reply: That is not so

srid rtse ma gtogs pa'i snyoms 'jug dag pa pa de dag ni nyams pa'i cha dang mthun pa dang*/ sogs pas bsdus pa gnas pa'i cha dang mthun pa dang*/ khyad par gyi cha dang mthun pa dang*/ nges par 'byed pa'i cha dang mthun pa dang*/ rnam pa bzhi bzhi pa yin la/ srid rtse la ni gong na sa gzhan med pas khyad par gyi cha mthun ni med pa'i phyir gsum yin no/ / {mthong lam dang mthun pa'i nges 'byed cha mthun ni gzugs med na med do } nyams pa'i cha mthun la sogs pa de dag ni go rim bzhin du nyon mongs pa skye ba dang rjes su mthun pa dang {'phel 'grib med par } rang gi sa pa dang rjes su mthun pa dang*/ sa gong ma'i sems skye ba dang rjes su mthun pa dang*/ de las zag med skye bas zag med kyi lam skye ba dang rjes su mthun pa'o/ / de la rjes su mthun pa zhes bya ba'ang de dang de skye ba la phyogs pa tsam yin gyi dngos su skye ba ni ma yin te/ thams cad kyang dag pa pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'on kyang gnas pa'i cha dang mthun pa ni skyes pa'i ngo bo nyid yin no/ / des na zag med kyi bsam gtan gzugs med ni nges 'byed cha mthun gyi bsam gtan gzugs med dag pa pa las skye ba yin no/ /

because pure (śuddha) meditative attainments other than the summit of existence have four types each: (1) factors conducive to degeneration (hānabhāgīya) and so forth, which includes (2) factors conducive to abidance (sthitibhāgīya), (3) factors conducive to superior states (viśeṣabhāgīya), and (4) factors conducive to penetrative insight (nirvedhabhāgīya). Since there is no level higher than the summit of existence, it has only three types because it has no factor conducive to superior states. {Factors conducive to penetrative insight are conducive to the path of seeing and do not exist in the formless realm.} Factors conducive to degeneration and so on are, respectively, (1) antecedents (anuguṇa) of the arising of affliction (kleśotpatti), (2) antecedents of the same level (svabhūmi) {that lack augmentation nor diminishment}, (3) antecedents of the arising of higher (ūrdhva) minds, and, from them (4) antecedents of the arising [665] of uncontaminated (anāsrava) paths. Also, the term antecedent refers to something that merely approaches something and its arising but does not directly give rise to another, because all these are pure meditative attainments. Still, the antecedent of abidance by its very nature gives rise to something. Therefore uncontaminated absorption and formless states arise from pure absorption and formless states that are factors conducive to penetrative insight.
'o na nyams pa cha mthun la sogs pa bzhi po de dag gang gi 'jug thogs su du 'byung zhe na/
Question: How many states occur after any of the four, such as the factor conducive to degeneration?
nyams cha mthun sogs mjug thogs su/ / gnyis dang gsum dang gsum dang gcig / sa brgyad rnam gnyis 'brel pa dang / / gcig rgal song zhing 'ongs nas ni/ / 18

After the factor conducive to degeneration and so on there are two, three, three, and one. It has two types in eight levels that are sequential, ascending and descending through omitting one level. (8:18)

nyams pa'i cha mthun gyi 'jug thogs su rgyun gyi dus su nyams pa'i cha mthun rang nyid dang*/ khyad par du 'gro ba'i dus su gnas pa'i cha mthun te gnyis gnyis dang*/ sogs pas gzung ba gnas pa'i cha mthun gyi 'jug thogs su nges 'byed cha mthun ma gtogs pa gsum dang*/ khyad par cha mthun gyi 'jug thogs su nyams pa'i cha mthun ma gtogs pa gsum dang*/ {'di las nyams kyang gnas pa ma btang na nyid skyer rung ba'i phyir ro } nges 'byed cha mthun gyi 'jug thogs su zag med 'byung yang dag pa pa ma yin pas rgyun gyi tshul gyis nges 'byed cha mthun de gcig pu 'byung ste/ de ltar na rang sa'i nyon mongs pa dang dag pa pa dang gong sa'i dag pa pa dang zag med 'byung ba ni go rim bzhin du nyams pa'i cha mthun dang gnas pa'i cha mthun dang khyad par gyi cha mthun dang nges 'byed cha mthun kho na yin par shes par bya'o/ / {zag med las ldang ba'i tshe nyams pa'i cha mthun ma gtogs pa gang rung mngon du byed do gsung ngo }

Reply: After the factor conducive to degeneration (hānabhāga), two occur: the factor conducive to degeneration itself when maintaining that state, and the factor conducive to abidance when proceeding to a superior state. The term “and so on” indicates that after the factor conducive to abidance, three occur, leaving off the factor conducive to penetrative insight. After the factor conducive to superior states, three occur, leaving off the factor conducive to degeneration. {For even though it may degenerate, if abidance is not relinquished, that itself can arise.} After the factor conducive to penetrative insight, one occurs: the factor conducive to penetrative insight when maintaining that state, since it is not pure even though uncontaminated meditative attainment will occur. Thus you should understand that the occurrence of afflicted absorption and pure absorption of the same level, and pure absorption and uncontaminated absorption of higher level, are, respectively, a factor conducive to degeneration, a factor conducive to abidance, a factor conducive to superior states, and a factor conducive to penetrative insight alone. {It is said that when rising from uncontaminated absorption, any may occur except for the factor conducive to degeneration.}
'o na thod rgal gyi snyoms 'jug ji ltar skyed ce na/
Question: How is alternating meditative attainment generated?
de la bzhi las
Reply: There are four parts: [basis, practical basis, physical basis, and person].
dang po gang la snyoms 'jug bya ba'i gzhi ni/
(1) The first is the basis of entering such meditative attainment.
bsam gtan bzhi dang gzugs med bzhi ste zag bcas gyi sa brgyad dang zag med gyi sa bdun te de ltar zag bcas zag med rnam pa gnyis so/
This consists of two types: contaminated and uncontaminated levels comprising the eight contaminated levels — the four absorptions and the four formless states — and the seven uncontaminated levels.
gnyis pa ji ltar snyoms par 'jug pa'i tshul la sbyor ba dngos gzhi gnyis kyi
(2) The way one enters such meditative attainment. This has two headings: preparation and actual basis.
dang po
PREPARATION

['di] la'ang gnyis las ring ba'i sbyor ba ni 'brel ba ste thog mar zag bcas kyi sa brgyad dang zag med kyi sa bdun pa dang ris ma bar bar lugs dang mthun par go rim bzhin du song zhing lugs dang mi mthun par go rim bzhin du 'ongs nas snyoms par 'jug pa dang*/ de nas phyis nye ba'i sbyor ba ni zag bcas su ris mthun pa'i bsam gtan dang po nas gsum pa dang*/ de nas nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched dang*/ de nas ci yang med pa'i skye mched la snyoms par 'jug pa sa re re rgal nas lugs dang mthun par yar song zhing*/ de bzhin du zag bcas su ris mthun pa'i ci yang med pa'i skye mched nas bsam gtan dang po'i bar du yang sa re re rgal nas lugs dang mi mthun par snyoms par 'jug pas mar 'ongs pa dang*/ de bzhin du zag med du ris mthun pa'i bsam gtan dang po nas gsum pa dang*/ de nas nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched dang*/ de nas ci yang med pa'i skye mched la snyoms par 'jug pa sa re re rgal nas lugs dang mthun par yar song zhing*/ de bzhin du zag med du ris mthun pa'i ci yang med pa'i skye mched nas bsam gtan dang po'i bar du'ang re re rgal nas lugs dang mi mthun par snyoms par 'jug pas mar 'ongs pa ste/ de ltar zag bcas dang zag med du ris mthun pa'i sa gcig ste re re rgal nas lugs dang mthun par yar song zhing ris mthun pa'i sa re re rgal nas lugs dang mi mthun par mar 'ongs pa'i sgo nas byang bar byas nas/

This has two headings: (1) Prolonged preparation refers to sequential (antara) preparation, where one first enters meditative attainment and ascends via each stage according to the forward order of the eight contaminated levels and the seven uncontaminated levels and then descends according to the reverse order. (2) Intense preparation refers to entering meditative attainment of the same contaminated type by ascending according to the forward order by omitting every other level from the first absorption to the third, then to the base of infinite space, and then to the base of nothingness. [666] So too, one descends by entering meditative attainment of the same contaminated type according to the reverse order by omitting alternate levels, through entering meditative attainment from the base of nothingness to the first absorption. Similarly, one enters meditative attainment of the same uncontaminated type by ascending according to the forward order by omitting alternate levels from the first absorption to the third, then to the base of infinite space, and then to the base of nothingness. So too, one descends by entering meditative attainment of the same uncontaminated type according to the reverse order by omitting alternate levels, through entering meditative attainment from the base of nothingness to the first absorption. Thus one trains by means of ascending (gatva) according to the forward order by omitting [or passing over] one (aikalaṅghita) or alternate levels of the same contaminated or uncontaminated type, and descending (āgamya) according to the reverse order by omitting alternate levels of the same type.
gnyis pa dngos gzhi ni
ACTUAL BASIS
rigs mi mthun pa gsum par 'gro/ / thod rgal gyi ni snyoms 'jug yin/ / bsam gtan gzugs med rang dang ni/ / 'og sa'i rten can 'og dgos med/ / 19

One proceeding to three meditative attainments of different type accomplishes alternating meditative attainment. Absorption and formless states possess a basis of the same or lower level. There is no need for lower level. (8:19)

gong gi tshe zag bcas kyi bsam gtan dang po nas zag med kyi bsam gtan gsum pa dang*/ de nas zag bcas kyi nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched dang*/ de nas zag med kyi ci yang med pa'i skye mched la lugs dang mthun par sa re re rgal zhing ris mi mthun pa gsum pa la snyoms par 'jug pa dang*/ de bzhin du zag bcas kyi ci yang med pa'i skye mched nas zag med kyi bsam gtan dang po'i bar du lugs dang mi mthun par sa re re rgal zhing ris mi mthun pa gsum par 'gro ba dang*/ de bzhin du zag med kyi bsam gtan dang po nas zag bcas kyi ci yang med pa'i skye mched kyi bar du lugs dang mthun par sa re re brgal zhing ris mi mthun pa gsum par 'gro ba dang*/ de bzhin du zag med kyi ci yang med pa'i skye mched nas zag bcas kyi bsam gtan dang po'i bar du lugs dang mi mthun par sa re re brgal zhing ris mi mthun pa gsum par 'gro ba ste/ de ltar zag bcas sam zag med ris mi mthun pa gsum par 'gro ba ste spel mar snyoms par 'jug nus pa de'i tshe thod rgal gyi snyoms 'jug dngos gzhi grub pa yin no/ /

One enters three meditative attainments of different type: from the contaminated first absorption then one enters the uncontaminated third absorption, then the contaminated base of infinite space, then the uncontaminated base of nothingness, by omitting alternate levels in the forward order. So too, one then proceeds to three meditative attainments of different type: from the contaminated base of nothingness to the uncontaminated first absorption by omitting alternate levels in the reverse order. So too, one then proceeds to three meditative attainments of different type: from the uncontaminated base of the first absorption up to the contaminated base of nothingness by omitting alternate levels in the forward order. So too, one then proceeds to three meditative attainments of different type: from the contaminated base of nothingness to the uncontaminated first absorption by omitting alternate levels in the reverse order. Thus, when one is capable of proceeding to three meditative attainments of different (visabhāga) contaminated or uncontaminated type, and thus capable of enhancing meditative attainment, at that time he accomplishes the actual basis of alternating (vyutkrāntaka) meditative attainment.

de bzhin du zag bcas zag med kyi bsam gtan gnyis pa nas srid rtse'i bar dang*/ srid rtse nas gnyis pa'i bar du lugs dang mthun pa dang mi mthun par sa re re brgal nas ris mi mthun pa gsum par 'gro ba'i thod rgal la sogs pa'ang sbyar te shes par bya'o/ / sngar bshad pa ltar shin tu ring ba'i phyir bzhi pa la ni snyoms par mi 'jug go /gsum pa rten ni de lta bu'i thod rgal de yang blo gsal bas gling gsum gyi skyes pa bud med dang*/ bzhi pa gang zag ni mthong thob dbang po rno bas ting nge 'dzin la dbang yang nyon mongs pa med pa ma yin la/ dus kyis rnam grol nyon mongs pa med pa yin yang dbang po rtul bas ting nge 'dzin la dbang ba ma yin pas dus dang mi sbyor bar rnam par grol bas dgra bcom pa mi g.yo ba { gnyis ka'i cha las rnam grol} kho nas skyed par byed de/ mi slob pa yin pas nyon mongs pa med pa'i phyir dang*/ dbang po rno zhing bsam gtan dngos gzhi thob pas ting nge 'dzin la dbang 'byor ba'i phyir ro/ /

So too, you should understand that proceeding from the contaminated or uncontaminated second absorption up to the summit of existence in the forward order, and proceeding from the summit of existence down to the second aborption in the reverse order, by omitting alternate levels, is alternating meditative attainment proceeding to three meditative attainments of different type and so on. In accordance with that previously explained, one does not enter a fourth meditative attainment [by omitting or skipping the intervening three] meditative attainments because it is extremely remote. (3) The physical basis of such alternating meditative attainment is those with clarity of mind who are males or females of the three continents. (4) The person is one who obtains results by insight, with sharp faculty, who has control over concentration but is not free from affliction. Or else it is an arhat liberated according to circumstances, who is without affliction but who, being of dull faculty, has no control over concentration and solely strives to generate the state of an immutable arhat {liberated from both aspects} who is liberated regardless of circumstances. [Arhats liberated according to circumstances] have no affliction since they are nonlearners, and those of sharp faculty gain control over concentration by obtaining the actual basis of absorption.

{ting nge 'dzin ni zag pa bcas ma bcas gnyis ka'o } sangs rgyas rnams kyi thod rgal yang tshul 'di nyid yin par sde pas 'dod la/ shin tu rgyas pa'i sde snod ltar na ni mngon par rtogs pa'i rgyan las/ 'gog dang bcas pa'i snyoms 'jug dgur/ / rnam pa gnyis su song 'ongs nas/ / 'dod par gtogs pa'i rnam par shes/ / mnyam gzhag min pa'i mtshams gzung ste/ gcig dang gnyis gsum bzhi dang lnga/ / drug dang bdun dang brgyad rgal nas/ / 'gog pa'i bar du mi 'drar 'gro/ / thod rgal gyi ni snyoms 'jug yin zhes tshul gzhan du bshad do/ /

{Such concentration is either contaminated or uncontaminated.} This school [the Dārṣṭāntikas] asserts that the method of alternating meditative attainment practiced by a buddha is just this. In accordance with the Avataṃsaka Sūtra,[1903] the Ornament of Realization explains another method: Through ascending and descending in both types within the nine meditative attainments including cessation, [667] consciousness belonging to the desire realm is held as the limit of nonequipoise {for both contaminated and uncontaminated concentration}. Through omitting one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, one proceeds in different ways to cessation. This is alternating meditative attainment.[1904]

lus kyi rten yang bsam gtan dang gzugs med pa'i snyoms 'jug de dag ni rang gi sa pa'i lus dang 'og sa'i lus kyi rten can yin te/ srid rtse'i snyoms 'jug ni srid rtser yang mngon sum du byed la 'og ma 'dod khams kyi bar du yang mngon sum du byed pa{ pos dgu pa yin pa} nas bsam gtan dang po'i snyoms 'jug dang po rang sa dang 'og ma 'dod pa'i rten la mngon sum du byed pas sa gnyis pa yin pa'i bar du sbyar ro/ / {de yang zag bcas ni 'bras bu rang sa dang rgyu 'og sa la brten par nges so } 'o na ci'i phyir gong du skyes pa'i rten la snyoms 'jug 'og ma mngon sum du mi byed ce na/ 'di ltar gang du skyes pa de la rang sa na mchog yod pas 'og ma'i dman pas dgos pa byed pa med pa'i phyir ro/ /
srid rtser 'phags pa'i ci yang med/ / mngon sum byas nas zag pa zad/ / sred bcas rang gi srid la dmigs/ / bsam gtan dge yul yod dgu yin/ / 20

An ārya at the summit of existence eliminates contaminants through the base of nothingness. That associated with craving focuses on existent states of its level. The object of virtuous absorption is all objects. (8:20)

de ltar spyir bstan nas dmigs kyis bsal ba ni srid pa'i rtse mor skyes pa'i phyir mi 'ong ba ni 'phags pa ste zag pa med pa'i ci yang med pa'i skye mched kyi ting nge 'dzin mngon sum du byas nas srid rtse'i zag pa zad par byas te dgra bcom thob par byed de/ ci'i phyir zhe na/ srid rtse rang sa na zag med kyi lam med pa'i phyir dang*/ ci yang med pa'i skye mched zag med de yang srid rtse la thag nye ba'i phyir ro/ / bsam gtan gnyis pa la sogs par dang po'i mig shes la sogs pa mngon du byed pa ni de dag ma bsgribs lung ma bstan yin pas bsam gtan dang gzugs med pa'i ting nge 'dzin ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ 'dir ni de dag gi rten bsam pa skabs su bab pa'i phyir ro/ / yang na de dag dman yang rang sa na med pa'i phyir lta ba la sogs pa la dgos pa yod pas mngon du byed do zhes shes par bya'o/ / yang snyoms 'jug de dag gi dmigs pa gang zhe na/

Thus, in the general presentation, the exception is an ārya nonreturner born at the summit of existence (bhavāgra) who obtains the state of an arhat who eliminates contaminants (āravakṣaya) of the summit of existence through manifesting uncontaminated concentration of the base of nothingness (akiṅcanya). Question: Why is that? Reply: That is because there is no uncontaminated path on the same level as the summit of existence, and the uncontaminated base of nothingness is near to the summit of existence. Eye consciousness and so on of the first absorption manifest on the second absorption and so forth because they are not concentration of the absorptions and formless-realm levels since they are unobscured-neutral states, and the [physical] basis possessing those [sense consciousnesses] has the opportunity to contemplate [their objects] there. [Eye consciousness and so on] manifest [on higher levels] even though they are inferior because sight and so on are needed on [higher] levels; they don’t exist there [naturally]. Question: Again, what is the focal object of those meditative attainments?

sred pa dang bcas pa ro myang ba dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i snyoms 'jug rnams ni rang rang gi sa pa'i srid pa zag bcas kyi phung po'i dngos po kho na la dmigs pa yin gyi/ rang gi ngo bo nyon mongs can yin zhing 'og sa las 'dod chags dang bral{ ba'i nyon mongs can yin} bas 'og sa la dmigs pa'ang ma yin la/{ de la dmigs nas sred pa skye na de 'dod chags dang ma bral bar thal bas so/ /} sa gang gi sred pa gang yin pa de ni sa de kho na la rgyas par 'gyur bas gong 'og rang rang gi sred pas yongs su bcad pa'i phyir sa gong ma la'ang dmigs pa ma yin no/ / de lta ma yin na de gong ma nyid du mi 'grub ste/ sa tha dad du ma bcad pa'i phyir sa gcig pa'i gnas gzhan bzhin no/ / de nyid kyi phyir gnas gzhan gsum gsum pa rnams dang brgyad po dag ltag 'og tu 'dug kyang sa gcig pa nyid du 'grub bo zhes rgyal po'i sras 'chad do/ /

Reply: Meditative attainment concomitant with enjoyment associated with craving (satṛṣṇa) focuses on (ālambana) the specific existent states of its own (svabhava) level — the things of its contaminated aggregates alone. It does not focus on lower levels since it is free of attachment to lower levels and is by nature afflicted. {If craving arose through focusing on it, in consequence such meditative attainment would not be free from attachment to it.} Any craving of any level increases through focusing on its level alone. Therefore since craving arises for objects of its own level, whether that is higher or lower, it does not focus on higher levels because [such craving] subsides there. If that were not so, and [if its subsidance] on higher levels were not established, then because [such craving] would not subside on other levels, then abidance on its own level would be like other [levels — that is, it would not subside]. [668] Therefore Jinaputra explains that, though the first three absorptions have three abodes each and the fourth has eight abodes that are classified as higher and lower stages, they are established as the same level.

zag med la dmigs pa'ang ma yin te/ zag med don du gnyer na dge ba'i chos la 'dun par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / bsam gtan dge ba dag pa pa dang zag med kyi dmigs yul ni ci rigs par yod dgu cog yin te/ / {dag pa pas gong ma rtogs pa yang mngon shes min gyi bsam gtan gyi sesam kyis sems de gnyis kyi dmigs pa ni }'dus byas dang 'dus ma byas gang yang rung ba la dmigs nas sems nye bar 'jog pa'i phyir ro/ / gzugs med kyi nyer bsdogs kyis 'og sa'i zag bcas la dmigs shing dngos gzhi nyon mongs can yang yod la dngos gzhi dge bas chos shes phyogs mthun gyi lam dang 'og sa'i 'gog pa la ma dmigs kyang zag med 'og sa'i gnyen po rjes shes phyogs mthun phyi lam bden dang rang sa dang gong sa la dmigs pas de rnams las khyad par du bya ba'i phyir dang*/

They do not focus on uncontaminated states because when they seek uncontaminated states, they become aspiration for virtuous Dharmas. The focal object of pure virtuous absorption and uncontaminated absorption is all objects (sadviṣaya) of any type because such minds are set to focus on any conditioned or unconditioned object. Formless-realm access concentration focuses on contaminated lower levels, while the actual basis also takes afflicted states as its object. Though the virtuous actual basis does not focus on the truth of path compatible with Dharma knowledge or the truth of cessation of lower level, {pure minds comprehend higher states, and the mind of absorption that is not higher perception} does not focus {on focal objects of those two minds}. However, since subsequent knowledge that is the uncontaminated antidote of lower levels focuses on the compatible truth of path of its level and higher levels, it is superior to them.
gzugs med dngos gzhi dge rnams kyi/ / spyod yul zag bcas 'og ma min/ / zag pa med pas nyon mongs rnams/ / spong ngo nyer bzlog dag pas kyang / / 21
The object fields of those virtuous, formless actual bases are not contaminated lower levels. Uncontaminated actual bases abandon affliction. Also access concentration and pure states. (8:21)

bsam gtan rnams ni kun tu lta ba pa yin pas dngos gzhi kyang 'og sa'i zag bcas la dmigs kyang gzugs med pa'i dngos gzhi dge ba dag pa pa dang zag med rnams kyi spyod yul ni sa 'og ma'i zag bcas min te/ gzugs med pa'i dngos gzhi rnams ni dmigs pa las nges par byung ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gong ma la dmigs so zhes bya ba'ang srid rtse'i 'phags pa ci yang med pa'i sems mngon du byas pa'i dbang du byas kyi thams cad ni ma yin no shes par bya'o/{ shugs la 'og sa'i lam zag med la gong sa'i rdzas shes phyogs mthun gyi dmigs par bstan no de yang sa dgu'i lam na phan tshun du zhes pa'i tshul du'o/ /}

Since the absorptions observe everything, the actual basis focuses on contaminated lower levels. However, the object fields (gocara) of those virtuous (kuśala) pure and uncontaminated formless actual bases (maula) are not contaminated lower (sāsravādhara) levels, because formless actual bases definitely withdraw from that focal object. Also, it is said to “focus on higher level,” but you should understand that this is stated for an ārya of the summit of existence who manifests the mind of nothingness; it is not meant for all. {Indirectly this teaches that the uncontaminated path of lower level is the focal object of compatible subsequent knowledge of higher level. Further, that is the method common to the nine levels.}

bsam gtan dang gzugs med dag pa pa la sogs pa gsum po 'di dag las zag pa med pa'i dngos gzhi rnams kyis rang sa dang gong sa'i nyon mongs pa rnams spong gi{ dag pa pa ni} nyer bsdogs kyis 'dod chags dang bral zin pa'i phyir dang*/{ nyon mongs can ni/} srid bas srid pa las nges par mi 'byung bas rang sa'i gnyen po ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ 'og sa'i dag pa pa bas gong sa'i nyon mongs can ches khyad par du 'phags pas{ sun mi 'byin pas} dman pas khyad par can spang bar mi nus pa'i phyir go rim bzhin du dag pa pa'i dngos gzhis kyang 'og sa dang rang sa dang gong sa'i nyon mongs pa rnams mi spong na nyon mongs can gyis lta smros kyang ci dgos/ bsam gtan dang gzugs med gong sa gong sa'i nyer bsdogs ni sa 'og ma 'og ma'i gnyen po yin pas zag med kyis spong bar ma zad{ nyer bsdogs} dag pa pas kyang nyon mongs pa rnams spong ngo zhes sbyar ro/ /

From among those three — pure absorption, formless states, and so on — uncontaminated actual bases abandon affliction (kleśa) of the same level and higher levels. Pure actual bases abandon affliction of lower levels, the same level, or higher levels, respectively, because (1) {pure meditative attainment} maintains freedom from attachment established by access concentration. (2) {Afflicted meditative attainment} is not the antidote of affliction of the same level since, being attached to existence, it does not definitely withdraw from existence. (3) Pure meditative attainment of lower level is superior to afflicted absorption of higher levels, and inferior states cannot abandon superior states {since they do not counteract them}. But if pure absorption doesn’t abandon them, then what need is there to speak of afflicted absorption? Since access concentration (sāmanataka) to progressively higher absorptions and formless-realm levels is the antidote to lower levels, not only does uncontaminated meditative attainment abandon afflictions, but also pure meditative attainment {and access concentration} abandon affliction.
nyer bsdogs bshad pa/
Access to higher levels
de dag la ni nyer bzlog brgyad/ / dag pa bde min sdug bsngal min/ / dang po 'phags pa'ang kha cig gsum/ / rtog med bsam gtan khyad par can/ / 22
They have eight access concentrations that are pure, neither pleasure nor pain. The first is also an ārya path. Some say three. Special absorption lacks investigation. (8:22)
drug pa nyer bsdogs bshad pa ni/ 'o na nyer bsdogs du yod ce na/
Question: How many access concentrations are there?

snyoms 'jug dngos gzhi{ brgyad yod pas} brgyad po de dag la ni gang gis 'jug pa'i sbyor ba nyer bsdogs kyang brgyad yod la/ thams cad kyang nyon mongs can la 'bral lam med pas sred pa dang mtshungs ldan gyi lam gyis nyon mongs spang bar mi nus la 'di dag ni 'dod chags dang 'bral bar byed pa'i lam yin pa'i phyir ngo bo re myong ba dang mtshungs ldan ma yin gyi dag pa pa kho na {yin te nyon mongs can ni 'og sa'i gnyen po ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / phyi ma bdun mi gsal bas zag med med do/ / rgyu mnyam gzhag gi bsam gtan gzugs med la nyon mongs can med pas/ 'bras bu'i de dag tu skye ba na nying mtshams sbyor sems ni rang rang gi nyer bsdogs mnyam par ma bzhag pa nyon mongs can gyis sbyor ro zhes pa ni grub mtha'o } mngon par 'du bya ba med par 'byung ba dang*/ 'og sa las yid byung ba dang bral na dga' bde dang mtshungs par ldan pa yin na de dag ni 'bad de drang dgos pas

Reply: {There are eight} actual bases of meditative attainment, [669] and those eight also have eight access concentrations (sāmantaka) that prepare to enter the actual bases. But since all of them abandon affliction or are free from affliction, while paths concomitant with craving cannot abandon affliction, they are by nature not concomitant with enjoying the taste [of meditative pleasure]. They are solely pure (śuddha) because they are paths that give rise to freedom from attachment. If they arise without application, which is without disgust for lower levels, yet are concomitant with joy and pleasure, then that must be produced through exertion, {because afflicted states are not an antidote to lower-level affliction. The latter seven states are not uncontaminated since they are not clear. One school asserts that since causal equipoise of absorption and formless states is not afflicted, when one is born in their resultant states, the linking mind connects through its specific access concentration that is afflicted and not equipoise.}

mngon par 'du bya ba dang bcas pa dang*/ 'og sa las yid byung ba dang ma bral bas tshor ba'ang bde ba yang min sdug bsngal yang min pa btang snyoms kyi dbang po kho na dang mtshungs par ldan pa yin no/ / yang na 'bad de drang bar bya ba yin pas btang snyoms dang mtshungs par ldan la/ 'og sa las yid byung ba dang ma bral ba dang*/ 'dod chags dang 'bral ba'i lam yin pas dag pa pa yin gyi ro myang ba dang mtshungs ldan ma yin no zhes bya'o/ /

Thus they arise with application. And since they do not lack disgust for lower levels, they are concomitant with the faculty of equanimity that is a feeling of neither pleasure nor pain (aduḥkhāsukha). Again, it is pure and not concomitant with enjoyment since it arises through exertion, it is concomitant with equanimity, it does not lack disgust for lower levels, and it is a path free from attachment.

slob dpon 'phags pas ni snyoms 'jug dngos gzhi brgyad po de dag la 'jug pa'i yid la byed pa bdun bdun bshad de/ de las 'og ma rnams tshe thung zhing sdug bsngal mang ba la sogs pa'i sgo nas rags sogs dang gong ma rnams de las zlog pa zhi sogs su lta ba'i sgo nas spang bya dang thob bya shes par byas shing spang ba dang thob pa bya ba'i phyir sems gtod par byed pa thos bsam dang 'dres pa mtshan nyid so sor rig pa'i yid la byed pa dang*/ spang bya dang thob bya'i sbyor ba rtsom par byed pa'i rtse gcig pa zhi rags kyi mtshan ma la mos pa thos bsam las 'das pa mos pa las byung ba'i yid la byed pa dang*/ 'og sa'i nyon mongs pa che gsum spong bar byed pa rab tu dben pa yid la byed pa dang*/ dben pa la dga' ba rgyas shing nyon mongs pa 'bring gsum spong bar byed pa dga' ba sdud pa'i yid la byed pa dang*/ 'og ma'i nyon mongs mngon du rgyu dang bral bas de zad ma zad brtag pa'i phyir de skye ba'i mtshan ma yid la byed pa dang thob pa la mngon pa'i nga rgyal med pa la sems 'jog pa byed pa dpyod pa'i yid la byed pa dang*/ de ltar brtags pas nyon mongs pa chung gsum yod par rtogs nas chung gsum spong zhing dngos gzhi'i dngos rgyur gyur pa sbyor ba mthar thug pa'i yid la byed pa dang*/ gong ma'i dngos gzhi thob pa ni sbyor ba mthar thug pa'i 'bras bu yid la byed pa'o/ /

Master Ārya Asaṅga explains that there are seven attentions that prepare for each of the eight actual bases of meditative attainment: (1) Attention discerning characteristics is attention mixed with hearing and contemplation that directs the mind to abandon that which is to be abandoned and obtain that which is to be obtained through comparing lower levels that are coarse — since beings there have short lives, more suffering, and so on; to higher levels that are refined — since beings there experience the opposite of that. (2) Attention arising from resolution is attention transcending hearing and contemplation that resolutely focuses on such refined and coarse characteristics, single-pointedly preparing to abandon that which is to be abandoned and to obtain that which is to be obtained. (3) Attention that isolates abandons the three great afflictions of lower level. (4) Attention of combined joy increases the joy of isolation and abandons the three intermediate afflictions. (5) Attention of analysis pays attention to the signs of the arising of lower-level affliction in order to examine whether it has been eliminated through fully eradicating its causes, and when [such elimination] is obtained, then placing the mind on that without pride. (6) Attention of final preparation examines whether affliction exists, and when it comprehends that the three small afflictions still exist, it abandons the three small afflictions, acting as the direct cause of the actual basis. (7) Attention that is the result of final preparation obtains the actual basis of higher level.[1905]

de rnams kyi'ang dang po drug sbyor ba dang bdun pa ni dngos gzhi'o/ / de ltar gong ma pas 'jig rten pa'i gong ma'i nyer bsdogs kyis 'og sa'i sgom spang dgu car spangs par bshad pa de ni gong ma pa'i lugs yin gyi bye brag smra ba'i lugs ni ma yin te/ gal te yin na gang zhig bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi ma thob pa mi lcogs med la brten nas mthong lam thob pa des dang po'i nyer bsdogs thob pa'i phyir 'dod pa'i sgom spang mtha' dag spangs par 'gyur na bsgom pas spang bya ma spangs na/ 'bras bu dang po la zhugs pa zhes bya ba'i 'grel par 'dod pa la chags bcas kyi mthong lam pa de khams gsum gyi sgom spang gcig kyang ma spangs pa 'ching ba mtha' dag dang ldan par bshad pa'i phyir ro/ /

Thus, from among them, the first six are preparatory states, and the seventh is the actual basis. In the system of the higher schools, it is said that a being of higher level abandons nine objects to be abandoned on the lower level by the path of meditation [670] through mundane access concentration to higher level. The Vaibhāṣika system does not assert this. If this were so, they say, then a person would obtain the path of seeing in dependence on unrestricted access concentration without obtaining the actual basis of absorption. And if he were to abandon all desire-realm objects to be abandoned by the path of meditation because he obtained access concentration to the first absorption, he would not abandon them by the path of meditation. That is expressed in the Autocommentary when it says, “he would enter the first result.” This explains that one with attachment to the desire realm on the path of seeing has not abandoned even one object to be abandoned by the path of meditation of the three realms; he possesses every tie (bandhana).[1906]

nyer bsdogs brgyad po de dag las dang po bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs mi lcogs med ni dag pa pa yin par ma zad 'phags pa zag pa med pa'ang yin te/{ 'di ni gsal bas rang 'og gong gsum gyi nyon mongs las rgyal lo/ /} bsam gtan gyi dngos gzhi ma thob pa dag 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam de la brten nas bskyed pa'i phyir ro/ /

From those eight access concentrations, the first is unrestricted access concentration to the first absorption that is not only pure but also an uncontaminated ārya path. This is because those who have not obtained the actual basis of absorption generate the transcendent path in dependence on it, {and due to its clarity, it conquers the affliction of three stages — the same, lower, and higher levels.}

nyer bsdogs gzhan dag ni 'og ma'i dngos gzhi la brten pa'i phyir de dag la/ 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam mi brten to/ / nyer bsdogs gzhan rnams la'ang mnyam par bzhag pa dang ma bzhag pa gnyis yod pa las dang po ni dge ba dag pa pa kho na yin la/ gnyis pa ni TI kar bsam gtan gzugs med brgyad car gyi nyer bsdogs nyon mongs pa can mnyam gzhag ma yin pas nying mtshams sbyor ro zhes bya ba 'di ni grub pa'i mtha' yin no zhes 'byung bas nying mtshams sbyor sems kyang yin pas nyon mongs can yang yin te/ 'grel pa las/ nyer bsdogs kyi sems kyis nying mtshams sbyor ba nyon mongs can yin mod kyi mnyam par bzhag pa la ni nyon mongs pa can nyid dgag go zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / sngon gyi slob dpon kha cig ste {'dun bzang ni } bsam gtan dang po'i nyer bsdogs mi lcogs med ni gsal ba'i phyir dag pa pa dang zag med dang ro myang ldan dang gsum ga yod do zhes 'dod la/ slob dpon 'dun bzang na re mi lcogs med ni dngos gzhi la snyogs pa'i phyir ro/ / myang ldan gyi snyoms 'jug kyang yod do zhes zer ro/ / {'di la'ang nying mtshams sbyor sems 'dod na de srid do }

Other access concentrations, because they depend on actual bases of lower levels, do not depend on the transcendent path. Also, other access concentrations are either (1) equipoise or (2) nonequipoise. (1) The first is virtuous pure [access concentration] alone. (2) Regarding the second, the Subcommentary notes that it is a linking mind as well as afflicted: One tenet system asserts that afflicted access concentrations to the eight absorption and formless states link [to afflicted states] since they are not equipoise. The Autocommentary states: Indeed, the mind of access concentration links to afflicted states, but equipoise stops afflicted states.[1907] Some past masters {such as Saṅghabhadra} say: Unrestricted access concentration to the first absorption possesses three types — pure, uncontaminated, and enjoyment — because it is clear. Again, Saṅghabhadra says: Unrestricted access concentration disturbs the actual basis. It also has meditative attainment possessing enjoyment.[1908] {If it is asserted that it has linking mind, then that is possible.}
'o na nyer bsdogs zhes kyang 'byung*/ bsam gtan khyad par can zhes kyang 'byung na gcig gam tha dad ce na/
Question: Is that which is called “access concentration” and that which is called “special absorption” the same or different?

tha dad de/ nyer bsdogs ni 'dod chags dang 'bral ba'i lam yin la/ bsam gtan dang po'i dngos gzhi de nyid rtog pa dang bral bas khyad par du 'phags pas rtog pa med la dpyod pa dang bcas pa ni bsam gtan khyad par can yin la/

Reply: They are different. Access concentration is the path that frees from attachment. Special absorption (dhyānāntara) lacks investigation (atarka) but possesses analysis. It is superior [to ordinary first absorption] since it is free of the investigation that characterizes the actual basis of the first absorption.
rnam gsum bde min sdug bsngal min/ / de ni tshangs chen 'bras bu can/ /
It has three types. It is neither pleasure nor pain. One possesses the result of Mahābrahma. (8:23ab)

de ni{ 'bras lam min gyi bral zin yin pas de la dbye na} dag pa pa dang zag med dang ro myang ldan dang rnam pa gsum ga dang*/ {mi lcogs med de ni } 'bad nas skyed par bya ba yin pas tshor ba'ang bde ba yang min sdug bsngal yang min pa btang snyoms kho na dang mtshungs par ldan pa yin no/ / de nyid kyis na { bde ba dang mi ldan pas} lam bskyed dka' ba zhes bya'o/ /

{Since it [special absorption] is not a resultant path but maintains such freedom, if classified} it has three types: (1) pure, (2) uncontaminated, and (3) enjoyment. {Unrestricted access concentration,} since it is generated through exertion, is concomitant with equanimity that is neither pleasure nor pain (aduḥkhāsukha). {Since it does not possess pleasure,} it is difficult to generate [671] it as the path.

des na bsam gtan dang po la rtog dpyod gnyis ka dang bcas pa'i dngos gzhi tsam dang rtog pa med la dpyod pa tsam dang ldan pa'i khyad par can gyi dbye ba yod kyi gnyis pa la sogs pa la ni de lta bu'i khyad par med pas dngos gzhi la dbye ba med do/ / bsam gtan khyad par can zag bcas gang yin pa de ni bsgoms na tshangs chen du skye bas tshangs pa chen po'i 'bras bu can yin no/ / des na byams pa la sogs pa ni rdzogs byed yin pa'i phyir tshangs pa'i gnas pa zhes kyang bya'o/ /

Though both the ordinary actual basis of the first absorption that possesses investigation and analysis and the special actual basis that possesses analysis alone exist, these two are not classified as distinct actual bases. If one cultivates that contaminated special absorption, one possesses the result of Mahābrahma (mahābrahmāphala), for one is born in Mahābrahmaṇa. Since they are fulfilled there, love and so on are called “abodes of Brahma” (brahmavihāra).
bdun pa ting nge 'dzin gyi dbye ba ni
Classifications of concentration
man chad rtog dpyod bcas pa yi/ / ting 'dzin yan chad gnyis ka med/ / 23
Concentrations below possess investigation and analysis. Those above that lack both. (8:23cd)

yang ting nge 'dzin thams cad mdor bsdus te mdo las/ ting nge 'dzin ni rnam pa gsum ste/ rtog pa dang bcas shing dpyod pa dang bcas pa dang*/ rtog pa med la dpyod pa tsam dang*/ rtog pa yang med la dpyod pa yang med pa'i ting nge 'dzin to zhes ting nge 'dzin gsum gsungs pa la bsam gtan khyad par can de ni rtog pa tsam zhig bkag pas rtog med dpyod tsam gyi ting nge 'dzin yin la/ khyad par can de man chad bsam gtan dang po'i dngos gzhi tsam po dang nyer bsdogs mi lcogs med gnyis ni rtog pa dang bcas shing dpyod pa dang bcas pa'i ting nge 'dzin to/ / khyad par can de yan chad bsam gtan gnyis pa'i nyer bsdogs nas srid rtse'i bar rnams ni sa de bsdus kyi rtog dpyod gnyis ka med pa'i ting nge 'dzin to/ /

Again, if all concentration is summarized, a sūtra lists three varieties: Concentration has three types: (1) concentration possessing investigation and possessing analysis, (2) concentration without investigation but with analysis alone, (3) concentration without investigation or analysis.[1909] Since special absorption merely stops investigation, it is concentration without investigation but with analysis alone. Both concentrations (samādhi) of the ordinary actual basis of the first absorption and unrestricted access concentration, which are below special absorption, possess investigation and analysis (savitarkavicāra). Above special absorption, concentrations from access concentration to the second absorption up to the summit of existence lack both investigation and analysis.
mtshan med zhi ba'i rnam pa dang / / stong nyid bdag med stong nyid du/ / 'jug pa'o smon pa med pa ni/ / de las gzhan bden rnam pa dang / 24
Signlessness has aspects of pacification. Emptiness engages selflessness and emptiness. Wishlessness has the first aspects of truth. Six are excluded. (8:24)

yang mdo las/ ting nge 'dzin rnam pa gsum ste/ stong pa nyid dang smon pa med pa dang mtshan ma med pa'i ting nge 'dzin to zhes ting nge 'dzin gsum gsungs pa las yul myang 'das so sor brtags 'gog ni yul lnga dang pho mo dang 'dus byas kyi mtshan nyid gsum mam bzhi'i mtshan ma{ ste bcu dang} bral bas mtshan med yin la/ / {'dir dbang po rnams mtshan mar ma smros pa ni dbang po ni yul ltar yid 'phrog par byed pa min pas so } de la dmigs pa'i ting nge 'dzin yin pas mtshan ma med pa'i ting nge 'dzin ni mtshan ma thams cad zhi ba 'gog pa'i rnam pa bzhi dang mtshungs par ldan pa dang*/ stong pa nyid kyi ting nge 'dzin ni stong pa'am bdag med la dmigs nas sdug bsngal gyi bden pa'i bdag med pa dang stong pa nyid du 'jug pa'i rnam pa nyid dang mtshungs par ldan pa'o/{ 'di yang 'jig lta'i gnyen po'o/ /}

smon pa med pa'i ting nge 'dzin ni yul smon bya ma yin pa'i 'dus byas la dmigs nas yid 'byung ba'i rnam pa yin la/ stong pa dang bdag med pas kyang sdug bsngal gyi bden pa la stong pa dang bdag med kyi rnam par dmigs mod kyi de gnyis ni chos thams cad kyi mtshan nyid yin pas myang 'das la mtshan nyid kyang yin na de dag gis myang 'das las yid mi 'byung ba ltar sdug bsngal las kyang yid mi 'byung la 'gog bden gyis kyang yid mi 'byung gi /mi rtag pa dang sdug bsngal gyi rnam pa gnyis dang kun 'byung gi bden pa dang lam gyi bden pa'i rnam pa brgyad po'i nang nas lam gyi rnam pa bzhi'ang lung bar ma las re zhig blang bya yin yang 'dus byas yin pas chu rgal ba'i gzings ltar lhag med du 'jug pa na nges par 'dor bas spang byar gsungs pas sdug bsngal gyi bden pa'i rnam pa phyi ma gnyis dang 'gog bden gyi rnam pa bzhi ste drug po de dag las gzhan pa sdug bsngal gyi bden pa'i rnam pa dang po gnyis dang kun 'byung dang lam gyi bden pa'i rnam pa brgyad de rnam pa bcu dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i ting nge 'dzin {ni smon med kyi ting nge 'dzin } no/ / slob dpon thogs med dang seng ge bzang po la sogs pas ni mtshan ma med pa ni zhi ba'i ngo bo yin pa'i phyir 'gog lam gyi rnam pa brgyad dang*/ smon pa med pa ni de dag gis khams gsum la smon pa ldog pa'i phyir mi rtag pa dang sdug bsngal ba dang kun 'byung gi rnam pa bzhi ste drug ldan du bshad do/ /

The concentration of wishlessness (apraṇihita) possesses the aspect of disgust through focusing on undesired conditioned states, and since conditioned states are empty and selfless, indeed it focuses on the empty and selfless aspects of the truth of suffering. These two aspects are also the characteristics of all phenomena, and therefore they are also the characteristics of nirvāṇa. [672] But just as they don’t induce disgust with nirvāṇa, they do not induce disgust with suffering. Also the truth of cessation does not generate disgust. As such it is both the aspects of impermanence and suffering and, from among the eight aspects of the truths of origin and path, it is also the four aspects of the path. It is said in the Medium-Length Discourses: Though some are [Dharma] to be practiced at present, they are to be abandoned. Since they are conditioned states, they are definitely discarded when one enters nirvāṇa without remainder, just as one discards a vessel when one has crossed the ocean. Therefore {the concentration of wishlessness} is concentration possessing ten common aspects: (1–2) the first two aspects of the truth of suffering and (3–10) the eight aspects of the truths of origin and path. Six aspects are excluded: the two latter aspects of the truth of suffering and the four aspects of the truth of cessation. Masters Asaṅga and Haribhadra and so on explain that signlessness possesses the eight aspects of cessation and path because it is by nature pacification, and wishlessness possesses six — (1) impermanence and (2) suffering, and the (3–6) four aspects of origin — because these stop the wish to exist in the three realms.
dag dang dri ma med de dag / dri med rnam thar sgo gsum mo/ / stong nyid stong nyid ces la sogs/ / gzhan yang ting nge 'dzin gsum mo/ / 25
They are pure or stainless. The three stainless are called the three doors of liberation. Three other concentrations are called the emptiness of emptiness and so on. (8:25)

ting nge 'dzin gsum po de dag ni zag bcas 'jig rten pa dag pa pa dang*/ {de yang nges 'byed cha mthun dang 'phags lam gyi sbyor rjes kha cig gis bsdus la } 'jig rten las 'das pa dri ma med pa gnyis yin la/ de dag sa ni dang po 'dod pa dang bsam gtan sa drug dang gzugs med bzhi ste bcu gcig na yod la/ gnyis pa ni zag med kyi lam gang na yod pa'i sa 'dod pa dang srid rtse dang bsam gtan gnyis pa la sogs pa'i nyer bsdogs bdun ma gtogs pa zag med sa dgu na yod do/ / de ltar dag pa pa dang zag med gnyis las ting nge 'dzin gsum po de dag dri ma med pa ni thar pa'i rgyu dang der 'jug pa'i sgo yin pas mdo las rnam par thar pa'i sgo stong pa nyid la sogs pa rnam par thar pa'i sgo gsum zhes kyang gsungs so/ /

yang mdo las/ stong pa nyid stong pa nyid ces bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin dang*/ sogs pas gzung ba smon pa med pa smon pa med pa dang*/ mtshan ma med pa mtshan ma med pa'i ting nge 'dzin to zhes snga ma gsum las gzhan yang ting nge 'dzin gsum gsungs te/ rim pa ltar stong pa nyid la sogs pa snga ma gsum la dmigs pa'i phyir ming de skad ces bya'o/ /

Again, three concentrations (samādhi) other than the former three are stated, for a sūtra mentions a concentration called “the emptiness of emptiness” (śūnyatāśūnyatā) and so on, referring to the concentration of “the wishlessness of wishlessness” and the concentration of “the signlessness of signlessness.”[1911] They are called “the emptiness of emptiness” and so on because they focus on the former three, respectively — emptiness and so on.
gnyis ni stong dang mi rtag par/ / mi slob pa'i la dmigs pa yin/ / mtshan ma med pa mtshan med ni/ / zhi bar ma brtags zad pa la/ / 26
Two focus on nonlearner emptiness and impermanence. The signlessness of signlessness focuses on elimination without analysis and engages peace. (8:26)

de ltar gsum po de dag las dang po gnyis ni rim pa ltar mi slob pa'i stong pa nyid dang smon pa med pa'i ting nge 'dzin la dmigs nas de gnyis la bdag 'dzin dang srid pa'am dga' ba dgag pa'i phyir mi slob pa'i stong pa nyid kyi ting nge 'dzin 'di ni bdag gi ma yin no zhes stong pa'i rnam pa dang mi slob pa'i smon pa med pa'i ting nge 'dzin 'di ni mi rtag pa'o zhes mi rtag pa'i rnam par yid la byed pa yin no/ / 'o na stong nyid stong nyid kyi ting nge 'dzin de stong nyid kyi ting nge 'dzin ltar stong bdag med gnyis kar mi dmigs par stong nyid kyi rnam pa kho nar dmigs she na/ {stong pa nyid kyi ting nge 'dzin ni nyer len gyi phung po stong nyid du yid la byed la } stong nyid stong nyid ni/ stong nyid kyi ting nge 'dzin de nyid yang sun 'byin pas na 'dus byas thams cad las yid 'byung ba'o/ / stong nyid kyi ting nge 'dzin stong bdag med kyi rnam pa gnyis pa can yin yang stong nyid stong nyid kyi ting nge 'dzin 'di stong nyid kyi rnam par zhugs pa'i stong nyid kyi rjes kho na la bskyed pa'i phyir dang*/ lam du zhugs pa grogs dang bral ba na mgron po ngo mi shes pa mthong bas kyang dga' la gcig pu ni grogs kyis stong pas mi dga' ba ltar srid pa la bdag med par mthong yang stong par ma mthong na dga' bar 'gyur gyi/ stong par mthong na mi dga' zhing skyo bar 'gyur bas des na skyo ba dang mthun pas stong pa'i rnam pa kho nar dmigs kyi bdag med pa'i rnam par ni ma yin no/ / de bzhin du ting nge 'dzin gnyis po de dag bden pa dang po'i sdug bsngal gyi rnam pa dang kun 'byung dang 'gog lam gyi rnam pa bcu gnyis su'ang dmigs pa ma yin te/ go rim bzhin du dmigs yul ting nge 'dzin de dag zag med yin pas zag bcas 'phags pa dang mi mthun pa'i sdug bsngal dang*/ sdug bsngal bskyed pa'i rgyu la sogs pa'i mtshan nyid ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ 'gog bden ma yin pa'i phyir dang*/ lam bden yin pas sun dbyung bya yin la sun dbyung bya de nyid sun 'byin byed du mi 'thad pa'i phyir ro/ /

Thus, from among those three, the first two respectively focus on the nonlearner (aśaikṣa) concentrations of emptiness and wishlessness in order to prevent both grasping at a self or liking existence: The nonlearner concentration of emptiness (śūnyatā) engages the aspect of emptiness, reflecting, “It is not mine.” The nonlearner concentration of wishlessness engages the aspect of impermanence (anityata), reflecting, “It is impermanent.” Question: Does the concentration of the emptiness of emptiness only focus on the aspect of emptiness and not focus on both emptiness and selflessness, like the concentration of emptiness? [673] Reply: {The concentration of emptiness engages the emptiness of the appropriated aggregates,} whereas the concentration of the emptiness of emptiness is disgusted with all conditioned states, since it even counteracts the concentration of emptiness. Though the concentration of emptiness possesses both aspects of emptiness and selflessness, the concentration of the emptiness of emptiness [possesses emptiness alone], because it is generated through adhering to emptiness that engages the aspect of emptiness alone. For example, if one lacks a companion when setting out on a road, one takes joy in seeing an unknown traveler, but since one lacks a companion, one lacks joy due to being alone. So too, when one sees existence to be selfless without seeing it to be empty, joy arises, but if it is seen as empty, one is joyless and saddened. Therefore focusing solely on the aspect of emptiness brings sadness, but focusing on the aspect of selflessness does not.
