So too, those two concentrations do not focus on the aspect of suffering of the first truth, nor on the twelve aspects of the truths of origin, cessation, and path, because the focal objects of those concentrations are uncontaminated. However, characteristics such as suffering and the productive cause of suffering — which are contaminated states incompatible with āryas — are not; they are not the truth of cessation. Furthermore, the truth of path will counteract that which should be counteracted, but it is unsuitable that it counteracts itself.

mtshan ma med pa mtshan ma med pa'i ting nge 'dzin ni mi slob pa'i mtshan med las langs pa'i rjes la zag bcas sam zag med kyi shes pa gzhan ma skyes na mtshan med kyi rgyun 'byung bar 'gyur ba las/ mtshan med las langs pa'i rjes la zag bcas sam zag med skye ba na mtshan med 'byung ba'i rkyen ma tshang bas 'gag par 'gyur zhing 'gag pa de ni so sor brtags min gyi 'gog pa yin gyi so sor brtags 'gog ni ma yin te/ zag bcas gnyen pos bral ba ni so sor brtags 'gog yin pa la mi slob pa'i mtshan med ni zag med yin pas 'phags pa dang mi mthun pa med pas gnyen pos bral ba mi srid pa'i phyir ro/ / des na dmigs pa mi slob pa'i mtshan ma med pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi so sor ma brtags pas zad pa ste 'gog pa la dmigs nas zhi ba'i rnam pa kho nar yid la byed pa yin gyi/ 'gog pa dang gya nom pa dang nges par 'byung ba'i rnam par ni yid la byed pa ma yin te/ rim pa ltar 'gog pa ni mi rtag pa'i 'gog pa dang thun mong ma yin pas mi rtag pa'i 'gog par dmigs na brtags min rtag pa sun phyung bar 'gyur la/ de sun phyung na mtshan med sun 'byin byed sun phyung bas sun dbyung bya'i mtshan med sun dbyung bar mi 'gyur ba'i phyir dang*/ gya nom pa ni dge ba yin na brtags min lung ma bstan yin pa'i phyir dang*/ gnyen pos spang bya dang bral nas 'khor ba las nges par byung ba ni nges 'byung yin na brtags min ni gnyen po'i stobs kyis bral ba ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

The concentration of the signlessness of signlessness (ānimittānimitta) continues as the continuum of signlessness after rising from nonlearner signlessness if another contaminated or uncontaminated knowledge does not arise. It ceases after rising from signlessness if contaminated or uncontaminated knowledge arises, since the conditions for the arising of signlessness are then no longer complete. That cessation is nonanalytical cessation and not analytical cessation because freedom obtained by the antidotes of contaminated states is analytical cessation. But nonlearner signlessness is uncontaminated, and not incompatible with ārya states, and thus it is impossible for it to be freedom obtained by antidotes. Therefore the nonlearner concentration of signlessness focuses on elimination (kṣaya) or cessation without analysis (asaṃkhya) and engages the aspect of peace (śānta) alone. It does not engage the aspects of (1) cessation, (2) sublimity, and (3) definite emergence. (1) Since cessation is the specific cessation of impermanent [entities], if one focuses on the cessation of impermanence, then permanent nonanalytical states would [not] be refuted since cessation is the specific cessation of impermanence. And if permanent nonanalytical states were refuted by the agent that repudiates signlessness being refuted, then the signlessness of the object to be repudiated would not be refuted. (2) If sublimity were virtuous, it would be a nonanalytical neutral state. (3) If definite emergence from saṃsāra due to eliminating objects to be abandoned by their antidote were definite emergence, [674] then nonanalytical states would not be freedom due to the power of the antidote.
zag bcas mi nang mi g.yo la/ / nyer bsdogs bdun ni ma gtogs so/ / dge ba'i bsam gtan dang po ni/ / bde 'gyur ting 'dzin sgom pa yin/ / 27
Contaminated, among humans, immutable. Their level excludes the seven access concentrations. It is the first virtuous absorption that cultivates concentration abiding in comfort. (8:27)

ting nge 'dzin phyi ma gsum po 'di dag ni gcig tu zag pa dang bcas pa yin te/ zag med 'phags lam la{ yon tan du lta bas de la} mi sdang gi 'di dag ni ting nge 'dzin snga ma gsum la rgyab kyis phyogs pas 'phags pa'i lam la sdang bas dor bya nyid du lta ba'i phyir ro/ / de nyid kyis na 'di dag la rnam par thar pa sun 'byin pa'i ting nge 'dzin zhes kyang grag go /rten ni blo gsal bas {gling gsum gyi }mi'i nang kho nar skyed par byed la/ {ste mi'i lus ni na rgas 'chi ba la sogs pa'i rten du byung bas nad la sogs pa dang 'dra bar 'du byed zag med 'jug pa la yang mi mthun pa'i 'du shes 'dren la/ lha la ni ma yin te phal cher lus kho na ma thob med pa'i phyir ro } gang zag ni dbang po rno bas de skyed pa'i mthu yod pa'i phyir dgra bcom pa mi g.yo ba'i chos can kho na la skye'i dbang po rtul bas dgra bcom pa gzhan la ni ma yin te/ {slob pa ni bya ba lhag ma dang bcas pas 'phags lam la mi sdang la/ dus kyi rnam grol ni 'phags lam rjes su srung ba la brtson pas de sun mi 'byin no/ / sa ni bsam gtan bzhi gzugs med gsum 'dod pa dang bcas pa na yod } bskyed par mi nus pa'i phyir ro/ /

des na 'phags pa dag mthong chos la bde bar gnas par bya ba dang*/ kun tu chags pa'i gnas su gyur pa mi slob pa'i stong nyid la sogs pa'i ting nge 'dzin de dag la rgyab kyis phyogs par bya ba'i phyir ting nge 'dzin gzhan dang gzhan dag la snyoms par 'jug go zhes sde pas 'dod la/ theg pa gong ma pa rnams ni rnam snang mngon byang las/ sems ni rang dngos med phyir dang*/ / 'bras bu rgyu rnams spangs phyir dang zhes 'byung ba bzhin du chos rnams kyi rang gi ngo bo dang 'bras bu dang rgyus stong pa la mnyam par bzhag pa'i ting nge 'dzin ni stong pa nyid kyi ting nge 'dzin la sogs par 'dod la/ de dag kyang chos rnams kyi rang gi ngo bos stong pa las sogs pa'am/ / stong pa nyid kyang stong pa nyid du shes pa'i ting nge 'dzin la sogs pa la 'dod pa'i phyir zag med du 'dod do/ / rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las ni kun brtags dang gzhan dbang dang yongs grub kyi yul can gsum gyi dbang du byas nas stong nyid smon med mtshan med kyi ting nge 'dzin gsum gsungs so/ / des na thos bsam las byung ba dang*/ 'jig rten pa'i sgom byung dang 'jig rten las 'das pa'i sgom byung gi ting nge 'dzin gsum rim pa ltar stong pa nyid la sogs pa dang*/ stong pa nyid kyi ting nge 'dzin la sogs pa dang*/ rnam par thar pa'i sgo stong pa nyid la sogs pa yin no zhes gsungs so/ / sa ni bsam gtan gnyis pa nas srid rtse'i bar gyi nyer bsdogs bdun ma gtogs {na nyer bsdogs bdun gong 'og la zhi rags su dmigs nas 'og sa sun 'byin gyi 'phags lam sun mi 'byin pas so } pa 'dod pa dang bsam gtan gyi sa drug dang gzugs med pa sa bzhi ste bcu gcig na yod do/ /

Therefore this school asserts that āryas enter meditative attainment on diverse concentrations in order to abide in comfort in this life and to support concentrations such as the emptiness of nonlearners in states of complete attachment. As for the higher vehicle {the Enlightenment of Vairocana} states: Because the mind itself [engages] nonthings, because it has abandoned effects and causes. Therefore they assert that concentration in equipoise on emptiness is concentration on emptiness and so on, since it is the nature, result, and cause of phenomena. Also they assert that [such concentration itself] is uncontaminated because it is empty due to the nature of phenomena and so on, and that it is concentration which understands that emptiness is emptiness and so forth. The Compendium of Ascertainment notes: The three concentrations of emptiness, wishlessness, and signlessness are differentiated from the perspective of three object fields: imputed nature, dependent nature, and perfected nature.[1912] Therefore this passage explains that the three concentrations that are (1) derived from hearing and contemplation, (2) derived from mundane meditation, and (3) derived from transcendent meditation are, respectively, (1) emptiness and so on, (2) the concentration on emptiness, and (3) the door of liberation of emptiness. Their level is from the second absorption to the summit of existence excluding the seven access concentrations (saptasāmanta), {since the seven access concentrations counteract lower levels and do not counteract higher levels, since they focus on the refined nature of higher levels and coarse nature of lower levels}. They exist on eleven levels: (1) the desire realm, (2–7) the six levels of absorption, and (8–11) the four formless states.

yang bcom ldan 'das kyis ting nge 'dzin bsgom pa ni rnam pa bzhi ste/ ting nge 'dzin bsgom pa kun du bsten goms par byas lan mang du byas na mthong ba'i chos la bde bar gnas par 'gyur ba'ang yod ces bya ba nas ting nge 'dzin bsgom pa kun tu bsten goms par byas lan mang du byas na shes pa mthong bar 'gyur ba'ang yod/ shes rab rab tu rnam par 'byed par 'gyur ba'ang yod/ zag pa zad par 'gyur ba'ang yod ces bya ba'i bar du gsungs pa de la zag bcas sam zag med kyang rung ste/

Again, the Bhagavan declares: Meditation on concentration has four aspects: (1) that which possesses and abides in comfort [675] in this life through frequently cultivating and relying upon meditating on concentration, (2) that which possesses knowledge that sees by frequently cultivating and relying upon meditating on concentration, (3) that which possesses wisdom through the proper differentiation of phenomena, (4) that which possesses the elimination of contaminants.[1913]

dag{ bdag pa ba'am zag pa med} pa'i bsam gtan dang po la mnyam par 'jog pa ni mthong ba'i chos la bde bar gnas par 'gyur ba'i ting nge 'dzin bsgom pa yin no/ / 'di ni 'dod pa las 'das pa'i dang po yin pas de skad du bshad kyi bsam gtan gzhan dag kyang mthong chos la bder gnas yin no/ / slob dpon gang spel gyi TI ka las kyang gal te bsam gtan thams cad mthong ba'i chos la bde bar gnas pa yin bzhin du mdo las dang po kho na der bshad ce na/ rnal 'byor pa ni 'dod khams nyes pa mang ba las 'das pas de'i bde bas blo lhag par yongs su tshim pas yin te dper na 'brog tu ngal zhing skom pa chu rnyog pa can gyis tshim pa bzhin no zhes bshad do/ /

They may be contaminated or uncontaminated, since equipoise in the first virtuous (śubha) {pure or uncontaminated} absorption (dhyāna) cultivates concentration (samādhibhāvana) that abides in comfort (sukha) in this life. It is so called since it is the first absorption beyond the desire realm, but other absorptions also abide in comfort. Master Pūrṇavardhana explains in his commentary: If all absorptions abide in comfort in this life, why does a sūtra explain that it exists in the first absorption alone? This yoga transcends many of the faults of the desire realm, and since its pleasure fully satisfies, it is like the satisfaction of drinking muddy water when tired and thirsty in the wilderness.[1914]

phyi ma la bde ba myong bar nges pa ni med de/ nyams pa dang*/{de spangs nas/}phyi ma la bsam gtan gnyis pa la sogs par skyes pa dang*/ mthong chos la mya ngan las 'das pa rnams la tshe phyi ma la bde bar gnas pa med pa'i phyir dang*/ zag med la rnam smin kyang med pa'i phyir ro/ /

There is no certainty that pleasure will be experienced later. Those who degenerate, those {who abandon it} and are subsequently born in the second absorption and so on, and nonreturners attaining nirvāṇa in this life do not abide in pleasure in their next life. Moreover, uncontaminated states have no karmic maturation.
mig gi mngon shes mthong 'gyur 'dod/ / sbyor ba las byung blo dbyer 'gyur/ / rdo rje lta bu'i bsam gtan mtha'i/ / gang yin de zag zad 'gyur bsgom/ / 28

Higher perception of divine eye is said to see. Awareness derived from preparation differentiates. Vajra-like concentration of the limit of absorption cultivates that which eliminates contaminants. (8:28)

'chi 'pho dang skye ba shes pa'i lha'i mig gi mngon shes dang de'i rjes su byung ba'i yid shes dang mtshungs ldan gyi shes rab ni shes pa mthong bar 'gyur ba'i ting nge 'dzin bsgom par 'dod do/ / skye ba shes par 'gyur ba dang mthong bar 'gyur ba gnyis las dang po ni sems can 'di dag ni lus kyi nyes par spyod pa dang ldan pa'o zhes bya ba la sogs pa shes pa mig gi mngon shes kyi rjes su rgyu ba yid kyi rnam shes dang mtshungs ldan gyi shes rab rtog bcas yin la/ gnyis pa ni da ltar gyi gzugs kyi skye mched la dmigs pa mig gi rnam shes dang mtshungs ldan gyi shes rab rtog pa med pa'o/ /

Higher perception of divine eye (akṣyabhijñā) aware of death and rebirth, and the wisdom concomitant with mental consciousness arising after it, are said to cultivate the concentration that sees (darśana) consciousness. There are two types: knowing rebirth and seeing rebirth. The first is wisdom possessing investigation that is concomitant with mental consciousness activated by the higher perception of divine eye, one that knows “this sentient being possesses that negative physical action” and so on. The second is wisdom lacking investigation that is concomitant with eye consciousness focusing on the present form base.

'o na mdo las lha'i mig gi mngon shes shes pa mthong 'gyur gyi ting nge 'dzin du bshad pa dang 'gal te/ mngon shes ni shes rab yin la de ni ting nge 'dzin bsgom pa ma yin pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ ting nge 'dzin gyi 'bras bu la rgyu ting nge 'dzin gyi ming gis btags pa ste lteng ka rkang nad ces brjod pa bzhin no/ / kha cig na re/ mngon shes rnam drug rnam grol blo/ / zhes pas{ mngon shes} 'di ni yid rnam grol gyi lam bsam gtan gyis bsdus pa mnyam gzhag kho na yin pas ting nge 'dzin sgom pa dngos yin pas mdo dang 'gal ba med do zhes zer ro/ / TIka byed dag ni phyogs snga ma ni chos mngon pa'i mdzod sems pa rnams kyi lugs yin te/ mngon shes mtshan nyid pa dang ting nge 'dzin bsgom pa btags pa bar 'dod la/ lugs phyi ma ltar na mig gi mngon shes ting nge 'dzin yin pas ting nge 'dzin bsgom pa dngos su 'dod par 'chad do/ /

Objection: This would contradict the explanation in the sūtras that the higher perception of divine eye is concentration that sees consciousness.[1915] Since higher perception is wisdom, it does not cultivate concentration.
Reply: Concentration that is the cause [of higher perception] here gives its name to the result of concentration [i.e., higher perception], like the name “pond-foot disease.”[1916] Some say: This does not contradict the sūtras. The Abhidharmakośa observes, “Since they act to perceive, they are higher perception, like awareness of the liberated path” (7:42cd). This {higher perception} is equipoise alone subsumed by absorption that is the path of liberation {of the mental faculty}, since it actually cultivates concentration.[1917] Pūrṇavardhana writes in his commentary: The former position is the system of adherents of the Abhidharmakośa because they assert that higher perception is the actual state and cultivating concentration is the nominal state. [676] In the latter system, they explicitly assert that cultivating concentration [is the actual state], that the higher perception of divine eye is concentration.

sbyor ba las byung ba'i yon tan khams gsum gyis bsdus pa mi sdug pa dang*/ dbugs 'byung rngub dran pa dang*/ nyon mongs pa med pa dang*/ smon nas shes pa dang*/ so so yang dag par rig pa dang*/ mngon shes dang po lnga dang*/ zag bcas kyi rnam thar dang*/ zil gnon la sogs pa zag bcas dang zag med rnam thar sgo gsum dang*/ thod rgal gyi snyoms 'jug dang*/ zag zad kyi mngon shes la sogs pa rnams la'ang ting nge 'dzin dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i phyir ting nge 'dzin gyi ming gis btags nas blo ste shes rab rab tu rnam par dbye bar 'gyur ba'i ting nge 'dzin ces bya ste/ ting nge 'dzin gyi stobs kyis gong nas gong du phul du phyin par chos rab tu rnam par 'byed pa'i shes rab khyad par du 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ /

Qualities derived from preparation (prayogajā) and subsumed by the three realms — such as mindfulness of repulsiveness, inhalation and exhalation, freedom from affliction, knowledge through prayer, analytical knowledge, the first five higher perceptions, contaminated liberation, contaminated states such as subjugation and so on, the uncontaminated three doors of liberation, alternating meditative attainment, higher perception of the elimination of contaminants and so on — are called “concentration” because they are concomitant with concentration. Such awareness (dhī) or wisdom is called concentration that differentiates (bheda) because it is superior wisdom differentiating phenomena that is perfected by the power of concentration.

bsam gtan gyi ya mtha' bzhi pas bsdus pa'i rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin gang yin pa de ni des zag pa ma lus par zad par 'gyur bas zag pa thams cad zad par 'gyur ba'i ting nge 'dzin sgom pa zhes bya'o/ / {sa gzhan la brten pa'i rdor ting yang de yin mod kyang } ting nge 'dzin bzhi po 'di dag bye brag tu smra ba ni bcom ldan 'das nyid kyi thugs rgyud la ji ltar bskyed pa'i dbang du mdzad nas gsungs pa yin te/ 'di ltar las kyi mtha' la gzigs pa'i ched du zhing pa'i grong du byon pa na shing 'dzam bu'i drung du bsam gtan dang po bskyed pa dang*/ de nas byang chub kyi shing drung du thun dang po la lha'i bu'i bdud btul ba'i rjes la lha'i spyan gyis sems can gyi 'chi 'pho dang skye ba nyam nga bar gzigs pa dang*/ de nas de dag bskyab pa'i phyir gung thun la bsam gtan dang rnam par thar pa dang snyoms par 'jug pa rnams bskyed pa dang*/ de'i rjes la thun gsum pa la bsam gtan bzhi pa la brten te rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin bskyed nas des kun sbyor thams cad spangs pa rnams ni rim pa ltar mthong chos la bde bar gnas par 'gyur ba'i ting nge 'dzin bsgom pa la sogs pa yin pa'i phyir ro/ / des na ting nge 'dzin bzhi kho nar gsungs so zhes 'dod do/

That vajra-like (vajropama) concentration subsumed by the upper limit (antya) of the fourth absorption cultivates (bhāvana) samādhi that eliminates contaminants (sāsravakṣya) by eliminating all contaminants without exception. {Indeed, vajra-like concentration dependent on other levels also does that.} Vaibhāṣikas explain such fourth-level concentrations from the perspective of how the Bhagavan generated them in his mindstream. Thus, in order to comprehend the limit of action, Siddhārtha went to a farmer’s village and there generated the first absorption under a rose-apple tree. Then, under the bodhi tree in the first period of the night, he tamed the devaputra māra. Then, with his divine eye, he saw the pitiable state of sentient beings trapped in cycles of death and rebirth. Then, from midnight on, he generated absorption, liberation, and meditative attainment in order to protect such beings. Finally, in the third period, he generated vajra-like concentration in dependence on the fourth absorption and abandoned all the fetters. These are, respectively, cultivating concentration that abides in comfort in this life and so on. Therefore only four concentrations are explained.[1918]
35. Qualities and Attributes of Concentration
gnyis pa de la brten pa'i yon tan bshad pa
EXPLAINING QUALITIES DEPENDENT ON THEM
['di] la dngos dang*/ khyad par kyi chos bshad pa gnyis kyi
This has two headings: authentic qualities and their attributes.
dang po
Authentic qualities
['di] la bzhi las
This has four types:
tshad med pa ni bzhi yin no/ / gnod sems la sogs gnyen po'i phyir/ / zhe sdang med byams snying rje yang / / yid bde ba ni dga' ba yin/ / 29
The immeasurables are four because they are the antidotes to malice and so on. Nonaversion is love as well as compassion. Mental satisfaction is joy. (8:29)
tshad med bzhi bshad pa/

yul sems tshad med pa la dmigs shing 'bras bu bsod nams tshad med 'byung ba'i tshad med pa ni byams pa dang snying rje dang dga' ba dang*/ btang snyoms te rnam pa bzhi yin no/ / de dag bzhir nges pa ni rim pa ltar gnod sems dang*/ sogs pas bsdus pa rnam par 'tshe ba dang*/ gzhan gyi phun sum tshogs pa la ma dga' ba dang*/ 'dod pa'i 'dod chags dang gnod sems mang ba rnams kyi gnyen po yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gal te btang snyoms kyis 'dod pa'i 'dod chags kyi gnyen po byed pa ltar mi sdug pas kyang byed na de gnyis la khyad par ci yod ce na/ kha dog gi 'dod chags dang 'khrig pa'i 'dod chags kyi gnyen por go rim bzhin du mi sdug pa dang btang snyoms so zhes bye brag tu smra ba rnams 'dod la/ slob dpon ni 'khrig pa'i 'dod chags kyi gnyen por mi sdug pa dang*/ snyoms nye du la'ang 'bral med ltar sgom pas pha ma la sogs pa nye du'i 'dod chags kyis gnyen por btang so zhes bzhed do/ /

The immeasurables (apramāṇa) focus on immeasurable sentient beings as objects and derive the result of immeasurable merit in four ways: through (1) love, (2) compassion, (3) joy, and (4) equanimity. They are definitely four in number because they are antidotes to, respectively, (1) malice (vyāpāda) and so on, which refers to (2) violence, (3) disliking [677] the excellent qualities of others, and (4) excessive desire-realm attachment and malice. Question: If equanimity acts as the antidote to desire-realm attachment and repulsiveness also acts as its antidote, what is the difference between these two? Vaibhāṣikas assert that repulsiveness and equanimity act as antidotes to attachment to color and attachment to sex, respectively. Vasubandhu asserts that repulsiveness is the antidote to attachment to sex and equanimity is the antidote to attachment to family such as parents. One meditates on family members as if they were unrelated to oneself.[1919]
tshad med pa'i ngo bo ni
THE NATURE OF THE FOUR IMMEASURABLES

sems can la zhe sdang med pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba ni byams pa yin la/ snying rje yang de dang 'dra bar zhe sdang med pa'i dge ba'o/ / gzhan bde ba dang ldan par shes na yid bde ba ni dga' ba tshad med pa yin la/

The root of virtue of nonaversion (adveṣa) to all is love (maitri) as well as compassion (karuṇā), which are similar in being the virtue of nonaversion. Mental satisfaction (sumanaska) knowing that others possess happiness is immeasurable joy (muditā).
btang snyoms ma chags rnam pa ni/ / kye ma bder gyur sdug bsngal dang / / dgar gyur sems can rnams snyam pa/ / spyod yul 'dod pa'i sems can rnams/ / 30

Equanimity is nonattachment. One engages their aspects, reflecting, “May sentient beings possess happiness, without suffering, but possess joy.” Their object field is desire-realm sentient beings. (8:30)

btang snyoms ni ma chags pa'i rang bzhin gyi dge ba'o/ / 'o na de gnod sems kyi gnyen por ji ltar 'gyur zhe na/ de'i spang bya'i gnod sems ni chags pas drangs pa'i gnod sems yin pa'i phyir 'gyur ro/ / slob dpon ni 'dod chags dang gnod sems gnyis ka'i gnyen por 'gyur ba ni ma chags pa dang zhe sdang med pa gnyis ka'i rang bzhin yin na rung bas gnyis ka'i rang bzhin du bzhed do/ / de yang chos gcig la gnyis ka'i rang bzhin yin par ni mi gzung {bar mar gnas pa'i } gi ma chags pa dang zhe sdang med pa so so la btang snyoms su brjod pa'o/ /

Equanimity (upekṣa) is virtue that is in essence nonattachment (alobha). Question: How does that become the antidote to malice? Reply: The malice it abandons is malice induced by attachment. Vasubandhu asserts that if it were tenable that the antidote to both attachment and malice is in essence both nonattachment and nonaversion, then [that antidote] would be the essence of both.[1920] But a single phenomenon possessing the essence of both is nowhere apprehended. Instead, a specific state, associated with nonattachment and nonaversion {and abiding between them}, is called equanimity.

de dag gi rnam pa ni go rim bzhin du kye ma sems can rnams bde ba dang ldan par gyur cig /sdug bsngal las grol bar gyur cig snyam pa dang*/ yid dga' ba dang ldan par gyur cig /nye ring dang chags sdang med par mnyam par bya'o snyam du yid la byed cing de dag la snyoms par 'jug pa'o/ / gal te sems can rnams bde ba la sogs pa dang mi ldan pa la bde ba la sogs par yid la byed ba'i phyir phyin ci log yin la/ phyin ci log kyang mi dge ba yin pa'i phyir ji ltar dge bar 'gyur zhe na/ sdug bsngal la sogs pa la bde ba'o snyam du shes pa la sogs pa ni ma yin gyi/ 'on kyang sdug bsngal ba'i sems can 'di dag bde bar gyur cig ces mos pa yid la byed pa'i phyir dge ba yin no/ / de lta na'ang sems can thams cad bde ba dang ldan pa mi srid pa'i phyir phyin ci log par mos pa yin no zhe na/ de lta mod kyi bsam pa bzang ba'i phyir dang*/ gnod sems la sogs pa mi dge ba'i gnyen po byed pa'i phyir dang*/ gcig tu sems can la phan par zhugs pa'i phyir dge ba yin te/ rin po che'i phreng ba las/ gzhan la gcig tu phan pa bde/ / mi phan phyir na cig shos min zhes gsungs pa bzhin no/ / gal te sems can thams cad bde bar gyur cig snyam pa la sogs pa ni mos pa'am 'dun pa'i rang bzhin yin pa'i phyir dang*/ byams pa la sogs pa'ang zhe sdang med pa la sogs pa sems las byung ba gzhan la 'dod pa'i phyir ji ltar de dag gi rnam par 'gyur zhe na/ bden mod kyi sems can thams cad bde ba dang ldan par gyur cig ces 'dun pa dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i zhe spang med pa la 'dod pa'i phyir skyon med do/ /

One engages and enters meditative attainment on their aspects, (ākāra) reflecting, “May all sentient beings (sattva) possess happiness (sukhitā), may they be liberated from suffering (duḥkhitā), may they possess mental joy, may they become equal, without being either close or distant through attachment and aversion.” Question: The mind engaging sentient beings who do not possess happiness and so on to be happy and so forth is distorted. Since distorted minds are nonvirtuous, how then could it be virtuous? Reply: It is not cognition that reflects “May suffering and so on be happiness.” However, because it engages the resolution “May those suffering sentient beings be happy,” it is virtuous. Objection: That resolution is distorted. It is impossible for all sentient beings to possess happiness. Reply: Indeed, that is so, but it is virtuous because it possesses a good intention, it acts as the antidote of nonvirtuous minds such as malice, it engages solely in benefiting sentient beings, and the Precious Garland states: Through solely benefiting others, happiness arises. Through not benefiting others, its opposite, unhappiness.[1921] Question: How do the reflections “May all sentient beings be happy” and so on become aspects of the immeasurables? Aren’t they by nature resolution or aspiration and [678] thus different mental factors from love and so forth, or even nonaversion and so on? Reply: Indeed, that is true, but there is no error. The reflection “May all sentient beings be happy” is asserted to be nonaversion concomitant with that aspiration.

tshad med pa 'di dag gi spyod yul te dmigs pa ni/ 'dod pa'i khams kyi sems can rnams yin te/ 'dod pa'i sems can la dmigs pa'i gnod sems la sogs pa'i gnyen po yin pa'i phyir ro/ / mdo las/ de byams pa dang ldan pa'i sems kho na med pa/ 'gran zla med pa/ gnod pa med pa/ yangs pa/ rgya chen por gyur pa/ tshad med pa/ shin tu bsgoms pa/ phyogs gcig tu mos te khyab par byas nas rdzogs par byas te gnas so zhes bya ba la sogs pa gsungs pa'i don ni byams pa dang mtshungs ldan gyi sems ni byams pa dang ldan pa'i sems yin la/ de nyid rim pa ltar nye ba'i nyon mongs pa khon 'dzin dang*/ phrag dog dang*/ zhe sdang gi gnyen po yin pas kho na med pa la sogs pa gsum dang*/ de nyid kyi 'bras bu che bas yangs pa dang*/ sa gzugs na spyod pa yin pas rgya chen por gyur pa dang*/ sems can tshad med pa la dmigs pas tshad med pa dang*/ mi mthun phyogs spangs pas shin tu bsgoms pa'o/ / de ltar na kho na med pa la sogs pa tshigs gsum dang*/ gcig dang*/ gcig dang*/ gcig dang*/ gcig gis rim pa ltar mi mthun phyogs kyi gnyen po byed pa dang*/ 'bras bu dang*/ sa dang*/ dmigs pa dang*/ rnam par dag pa'i phan yon gyi sgo nas byams pa de bstan pa yin no/ / phyogs gcig tu zhes pa ni gnas phyogs kyis mtshon nas gnas pa po phyogs can gyi sems can ston pa'o/ / mos pa yid la byed pa yin pas mos te'o/ / sems can thams cad la cig car mos par byed pas khyab par byas nas so/ / dngos gzhi'i snyoms 'jug thob pas na rdzogs par byas te'o/ / dus yun ring por rjes su 'jug pas na gnas so zhes gsungs so zhes rnam bshad rigs pa las bshad do/ /

The focal object or object field (gocara) of those immeasurables is sentient beings of the desire realm (kāmasattva). They [i.e., love and so forth] are the antidotes to malice and so on that focus on desire-realm sentient beings. A sūtra states: A mind possessing love is without spite, without rivals, without harm. It is spacious, greatly expansive, immeasurable, and fully developed. It is in harmony, resolute, pervasive, accomplished, and sustained.[1922] The “mind possessing love” is the mind concomitant with love. It is “without spite” since it is the antidote to the branch affliction of spite; it is “without rivals” since it is the antidote to envy; and it is “without harm” since it is the antidote to aversion. It is “spacious” since it has an extensive result. It is “greatly expansive” since it acts on the level of form. It is “immeasurable” since it focuses on immeasurable sentient beings. It is “fully developed” since it abandons opposing factors. Thus it is taught that love has three components such as “without spite,” and that it also acts as the antidote to opposing factors to four individual factors that benefit by means of result, level, focal object, and purity, respectively. “In harmony” is illustrated by a single abode and the sentient beings who abide there. “Resolute” refers to being resolute in applying the mind. It is “pervasive” since it takes interest in all sentient beings at the same time. It is “accomplished” since it obtains meditative attainment of the actual basis. It is “sustained” since it functions for a long time. This is stated in Rational System of Exposition.[1923]
dga' ba bsam gtan gnyis na yod/ / gzhan ni drug na kha cig lnga/ / de yis mi spong mi dag gi / nang du skyed de nges gsum ldan/ / 31
Joy exists in two absorptions. The others exist on six levels. Some assert five. They do not abandon afflictions. First generated among humans. He definitely possesses three. (8:31)

de dag gis ni dga' ba tshad med pa ni yid bde yin pas bsam gtan snga ma gnyis na yod la/ tshad med pa gzhan gsum ni mnyam gzhag kho na yin pas mi lcogs med kyang gsal bas dngos gzhi dang 'dra bas bsam gtan gyi sa drug na yod par kha cig 'dod cing*/ kha cig dngos gzhi kho na yin pas bsam gtan khyad par can dang dngos gzhi bzhi ste lnga na yod par 'dod la/ kha cig mnyam par ma bzhag pa dang sbyor ba'ang smros te/ 'dod pa dang bsam gtan gyi nyer bsdogs bzhi dang dngos gzhi lnga ste bcu na yod par 'dod do/ / 'o na gnod sems la sogs gnyen po'i phyir zhes gang bshad pa ci byams pa la sogs pas nyon mongs pa dngos su spong ngam zhe na/

Since immeasurable joy (muditā) is mental satisfaction, it exists in the former two absorptions. Some assert: The three other immeasurables exist in the six levels of absorption, for since they are equipoise alone they are access concentrations, and since they are clear they are like actual bases. Some assert: They exist on five levels since they exist on the actual bases alone: (1) special absorption and (2–5) the four actual bases. Some assert: They exist on ten levels since they are said to exist in nonequipoise and preparatory states: (1) the desire realm, (2–5) the four access concentrations of the absorptions, and (6–10) the five actual bases. Question: Since the Abhidharmakośa states, “Because they are the antidotes to malice and so on” (8:29b), do love and so on directly abandon affliction?

tshad med bzhi po de yis gnod sems la sogs pa dngos su mi spong ste/ bsam gtan dag pa pa dngos gzhi'i sa pa yin la/ dag pa pa'i dngos gzhis ni nyon mongs pa mi spong ngo zhes bshad zin pa'i phyir dang*/ {spong lam yin pa'i phyir dang } de kho na nyid yid la byed pas nyon mongs spang ba yin pa la 'di dag mos pa yid la byed pa yin pa'i phyir dang*/ chos thams cad kyi spyi'i mtshan nyid la byed pas nyon mongs spang ba yin pa la 'di dag sems can la dmigs pas nyi tshe ba yin pa'i phyir te/ rnam 'grel las kyang*/ byams sogs rmongs dang 'gal med phyir/ / nyes pa shin tu tshar gcod min zhes bshad do/ / 'on kyang de dag gi sbyor bas gnod sems la sogs pa rnam par gnon pa'i phyir dang*/ dngos gzhis spangs pa thag sring bar byed pa'i phyir gnod sems la sogs pa'i gnyen por bshad do/ /

Reply: These four immeasurables do not directly abandon (prahāna) malice and so on [679] because they exist on the level of the actual basis of pure absorption. It has already been explained that those pure actual bases do not abandon affliction, {they are not abandoning paths,} and they are resolute attentions even though attention engaging reality (tattva) abandons affliction. Those minds that engage the general characteristics of all phenomena can abandon afflictions, but these states focusing on sentient beings are of limited duration. Exposition of Valid Cognition states: Love and so on do not fully sever faults because they do not exclude confusion.[1924] However, they are called antidotes to malice and so on because their preparatory states subjugate malice and so on, and their actual states make remote that which is to be abandoned.
nyon mongs pa spong ba ni
ABANDONING THE AFFLICTIONS

gal te 'jig rten pa'i lam gyis spong na ni nyer bsdogs kyang spong ba yin la/ 'on te{ mgo mnan pa de dag} 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam gyis spong na ni bden brtogs pa'i spong lam gyis{ dngos su rtsa ba nas} spong ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ / {'dod chags dang bral te dngos gzhi thob nas dngos gzhis bsdus pa'i tshad med rnyed pa'i phyir gnod sems la sogs pa'i rkyen stobs ldan gyis kyang mi rdzi'o } 'on kyang byams sogs gsum 'dod pa dang nyer bsdogs na yod par 'dod pa ltar na ni sbyor ba dang dmigs rnam dang ngo bo dngos gzhi'i tshad med dang 'dra zhing*/ de dag gi sbyor bas nyon mongs pa rnams rnam par mnan nas spong lam bar chad med pa'i lam rnams kyis dngos su spong ngo*/ /

If afflictions are abandoned by the mundane path, then access concentrations would abandon them. However, if {suppressed states} are abandoned by the transcendent path, they are {directly} abandoned {from the root} by the abandoning path that comprehends the four truths. {One is not oppressed by the presence of potent conditions such as malice because one obtains the actual basis free from attachment and one attains the immeasurables subsumed by the actual basis.} How then to address the assertion that the three immeasurables such as love exist in the desire realm and the access concentrations — and the preparatory states, focal objects, aspects, and natures of the immeasurables are similar to the actual basis? Their preparatory states suppress the afflictions, and their abandoning paths are uninterrupted paths that directly abandon them.
'di sgom pa'i tshul ni
THE MEANS OF CULTIVATING THEM

sgom pa po nyon mongs pa chung na ji ltar rang nyid kyi rgyud la bde ba yod pa'am/ gzhan sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' dang 'phags pa dgra bcom pa la sogs pa'i rgyud la bde ba mnga' bar thos pa de bzhin du sems can thams cad kyang de lta bu'i bde ba dang ldan par gyur cig ces cig car mos par byed do/ / gal te nyon mongs pa'i 'jug pa shas che bas sems can thams cad la de ltar mos par mi nus na ni sems can la mdza' bo dang*/ tha mal pa dang*/ dgra bo'i phyogs gsum du dbye zhing*/ mdza' bo'ang che 'bring chung ngu gsum du phye la/ dang por bskyed sla bas mdza' bo che 'bring chung ngu gsum la rim gyis mos par byed la/ gal te gsum ga la byams pa mnyam por thob na de nas tha mal pa dang*/ de nas dgra bo'i phyogs la'ang chung 'bring chen po gsum du phye nas chung 'bring chen po gsum la rim gyis khyab par byed cing gal te dgra bo chen po la mdza' bo chen po ltar bde bar mos pa mi ldog par gyur na/ de nas rim gyis khyim dang grong dang yul phyogs gcig gi sems can dang*/ de nas rim gyis phyogs gcig nas 'jig rten thams cad kyi bar du byams pas rgyas shing khyab par byed do/ / de yang dge rtsa chad pa dang rang rgyal la'ang sngon gyi bsod nams dang de ma yin pa'i dbang gis rim pa ltar{ rang sangs rgyas} gzugs bzang ngan la sogs pa dmigs pas sems can rnams la skyon yon gnyis ka yod kyang yon tan gyi cha nas bsams na byams pa myur du skye bas skyon ni bsam par mi bya ste/ 'grel pa las/ gang zhig thams cad du yon tan 'dzin pa de ni byams pa myur du skyed par byed do/ / sngon gyi bsod nams dang bsod nams ma yin pa'i 'bras bu snang ba'i sgo nas dge ba'i rtsa ba kun du chad pa la'ang yon tan gzung bar nus la/ rang sangs rgyas la'ang skyon gzung bar nus so zhes bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du sems can sdug bsngal rnam pa mang po'i chu bor bying zhing mngon par dga' ba dang mi ldan pa 'di rnams sdug bsngal las myur du thar ba dang*/ mngon par dga' ba dang ldan par gyur na ci ma rung snyam du mos pas snying rje dang dga' ba la'ang sgom par byed la/ btang snyoms ni dang po tha mal pa'i phyogs la brtsams nas mthar dgra dang gnyen la mtshungs par lta ba yin no/ /

One generates the resolution that reflects, “May all sentient beings right now come to possess happiness, just as happiness exists in the mindstream of a meditator with little affliction, or just as one has heard that happiness is possessed in the mindstreams of others such as buddhas, bodhisattvas, āryas, and arhats.” Those overwhelmed by afflicted states cannot generate such resolution for all sentient beings. Therefore sentient beings get divided into three types: loved ones, strangers, and enemies. Loved ones are also threefold: greater, medium, and lesser. Since it is easier to generate immeasurable love for the first, you generate that resolution serially toward those loved to a greater, medium, and lesser extent. When you obtain equal love for those three, then you divide strangers and enemies into three degrees of lesser, medium, and greater, and serially apply that resolution to the three stages of lesser, medium, and greater for each. When you cannot stop generating the resolve that your greatest enemy be happy in just the way that you wish happiness for those you greatly love, then you serially expand and extend that love to sentient beings of your own family, village, and region until it extends to the entire world. Further, sentient beings have both qualities and faults. You can focus on those [with faults] who sever their root of virtue, or on pratyekabuddhas with prior merit [who possess qualities], or otherwise on {pratyekabuddhas} [680] with good or bad physical features. But I think love is more quickly generated if you contemplate their qualities and not their faults. The Autocommentary states: Those who apprehend the positive qualities of all sentient beings generate love more quickly. Through seeing the result of former merit and demerit, one can recognize qualities in those who sever their root of merit and one can apprehend faults even in pratyekabuddhas.[1925] Similarly, through the resolution that reflects “May those sentient beings who are sunk in the river of many sufferings and do not possess genuine joy be quickly emancipated from suffering. Where is the harm in their possessing genuine joy?” you cultivate compassion as well as joy. Equanimity commences at first with strangers and then views enemies and friends as similar.

tshad med pa bzhi po 'di dag ni dang po blo gsal bas mi dag gi nang du bskyed kyi gzhan du ni ma yin te/ de dag blo mi gsal bas bskyed par mi nus pa'i phyir{ dang gzhan gyis 'doms pa la ltos pa'i phyir} ro/ / ci tshad med de dag gcig dang ldan pa de nges par thams cad dang ldan nam zhe na/ thams cad ni ma yin gyi 'on kyang dga' ba ma gtogs pa gsum ni gcig ldan na gzhan gnyis ldan pas gcig yod na nges par gsum gsum dang ldan la/ dga' ba ni yid bde yin pas de ni bsam gtan gsum pa dang bzhi pa'i sa la mi ldan pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di yang thob pa la bsams kyi mngon gyur ni rnam pa 'gal bas re re dang ldan pa yin no/ /

These four immeasurables are newly generated (janyante) among humans (nṛsu), since they have clarity of mind. They are not generated among others, because they lack mental clarity {and they rely on others’ instruction}. Question: If a person possesses one immeasurable, does he possess all immeasurables? Reply: He does not possess all. However, if he possesses one of the three other than joy, he possesses the other two. For joy is not possessed on the third and fourth absorption since this is mental satisfaction. Therefore, if he possesses one, he definitely possesses three. Furthermore, I think this refers to obtainment, and that they are possessed separately, since each manifest state excludes the others.
rnam thar brgyad bshad pa/
THE EIGHT LIBERATIONS
rnam par thar brgyad dang po gnyis/ / mi sdug bsam gtan gnyis na yod/ / gsum pa mtha' na de ma chags/ / gzugs med mnyam gzhag dge rnams so/ / 32
There are eight liberations. The first two are repulsiveness and exist on two absorptions. The third, in the limit, is nonattachment. Formless-realm virtuous equipoise is liberation. (8:32)

yang mdo las/ nad gzugs su 'du shes pas phyi rol gyi gzugs rnams la lta ba 'di ni rnam par thar pa dang po'o/ / nad gzugs med par 'du shes pas phyi rol gyi gzugs rnams la lta ba 'di ni rnam par thar pa gnyis pa'o/ / sdug pa'i rnam par thar pa lus kyi mngon sum du byas te rdzogs par byas nas gnas pa 'di ni rnam par thar pa gsum pa'o zhes pa dang*/ de bzhin du gzugs med pa bzhi dang*/ rnam pa thams cad du 'du shes med 'du shes med min skye mched las yang dag par 'das te/ 'du shes dang tshor ba 'gog pa lus kyis mngon sum du byas te rdzogs par byas nas gnas pa 'di ni rnam par thar pa brgyad pa'o zhes rnam par thar pa brgyad gsungs pa las rnam thar dang po gnyis ni rnam par sngos pa la sogs pa'i rnam par lta ba'i phyir mi sdug pa'i rang bzhin yin te/ 'di'i ngo bo ma chags pa dang*/ dmigs pa 'dod par gtogs pa'i gzugs kyi skye mched yin par ni{ mi sdug ma chags pa sogs su} sngar mi sdug par bshad pa bzhin no/ / khyad par ni 'di yin te/ mi sdug pa ni sa bcu pa yin la/ rnam thar dang po gnyis ni bsam gtan gnyis pa yan chad na mig shes med pas kha dog gi 'dod chags med de/ gang yul la 'dod chags dang bral ba de ni yul can shes pa las kyang 'dod chags dang bral te sna lce'i rnam shes bzhin no/ /

Further, a sūtra discloses: That which discerns internal form while viewing external form is the first liberation. That which discerns the absence of internal form while viewing external form is the second liberation. That which abides in the complete physical manifestation of the liberation of beauty is the third liberation.[1926] And: So too, having fully transcended the four formless states, including the base of neither discernment nor nondiscernment in all its aspects, one abides in the physical manifestation of the complete cessation of discernment and feeling. These are the eight liberations. These passages list the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa).[1927] (1–2) The first two are the nature of repulsiveness (aśubha) because they view a bluish corpse[1928] and so on. They are by nature nonattachment, and their focal object is the form base belonging to the desire realm. They are similar to the repulsiveness previously explained, {where repulsiveness is nonattachment and so on}. But they are different in that repulsiveness has ten levels while the first two liberations have no attachment to color, since there is no eye consciousness on the second absorption and above. [681] They are free from attachment to any object since they are free from attachment to minds such as nose consciousness and tongue consciousness.

{bsam gtan phyi ma gsum na nang gi dbang po gzugs can la chags pa yod do/ / rnam thar 'di gsum bsam gtan gsum par ci'i phyir ma bzhag ce na/ rang gi spang bya gnyis pa'i kha dog gi 'dod chags med pas mi sdug pa'i rnam thar med la } bsam gtan gnyis pa la sogs pa na'ang mig shes med pas kha dog gi 'dod chags dang bral ba yin no zhes TI kar bshad pas go rim bzhin du 'dod pa dang bsam gtan dang po'i sa pa'i kha dog gi 'dod chags kyi gnyen po yin pas bsam gtan snga ma gnyis kho na na yod do/ /

{Question: In the three latter absorptions, attachment to the internal physical faculties exists; therefore why are these three liberations not posited for the three absorptions? Reply: There is no liberation of repulsiveness there, since in the second absorption there is no attachment to color as an object of abandonment.} The Subcommentary explains: Since eye consciousness also does not exist on the second absorption, it is free from attachment to color.[1929] Therefore they exist on the two initial absorptions (dhyāna) alone; they are the antidote to attachment to color in, respectively, the desire realm and the first absorption.

de yang dngos gzhis bsdus pa'i dag pa pa dang*/ mos pa yid la byed pa yin pas rnam par gnon pa tsam mam thag sring ba'i gnyen po yin gyi dngos su spong ba ni ma yin no/ / de la nad gzugs dang gzugs med par 'du shes pa ni{ gzugs kyis sems thob pa gang zhig} gzugs las 'dod chags dang ma bral ba dang bral ba'am/ TI kar rang nyid kyi 'du shes ma bshig pa dang bshig nas phyi rol gyi gzugs la lta ba yin par bshad pa'am/ yang na kun las btus kyi 'grel par gzugs med pa'i snyoms 'jug la brten nas lta ba po bdag nyid la gzugs su 'du shes mngon du byed pa dang gzugs kyi 'du shes spangs nas ming bzhi'i 'du shes mngon du byed pa la rim pa bzhin bshad do/

Furthermore, since they are pure states subsumed by the actual base of absorption, they are antidotes that subjugate the afflictions, or make them remote, but they do not directly abandon afflictions. The discernment of internal form and the discernment of the absence of form is {due to obtaining minds that apprehend form that} are either free or not free from attachment to form. Or the Subcommentary explains: They view external form through the discernment of its own form either enduring or subsiding.[1930] Or the Exposition of the Compendium of Abhidharma explains: In dependence on formless meditative attainment, one manifests discernment of form regarding the viewer himself, or one manifests discernment of the aggregates of name[1931] through abandoning the discernment of form.[1932]

(4–7) Formless-realm virtuous equipoise (samāhita) that is pure and uncontaminated alone is liberation, but afflicted minds and the nonequipoise mind of death existence are not. {These can only be virtuous}. One asserts: When I think of those formless-realm minds and mental factors that arise from karmic maturation, I accept that there are other nonequipoise minds besides the mind of death. In accordance with the first part [of his argument], he accepts that formless nonequipoise states are minds and mental factors of the [being experiencing] death existence. In the formless realm, not only is the liberated path of the actual basis called “liberation,” but also [the liberated path of] access concentration [is called liberation]. However, the uninterrupted path is not called liberation, because if liberation were to reject lower levels, it would focus on lower levels. {Further, the first two [liberations] reject attachment to color, the third rejects repulsiveness, and formless states reject focal objects of lower levels.}
'gog pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa'o/ phra ba phra ba'i mjug thogs su/ / rang gi dag dang 'og ma yi/ / 'phags pa'i sems kyis de las ldang / / 33
It is meditative attainment of cessation. After the subtle of the subtle, it arises from that with an ārya pure mind of its level or below. (8:33)

rnam thar brgyad pa 'gog pa'i rnam thar ni gnas gnyis par bshad pa'i 'gog pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa'o/ / 'di dag la ci'i phyir rnam par thar pa zhes bya zhe na/ dang po gnyis dang gsum pa dang gzugs med rnams dang 'gog pa rnams ni go rim bzhin du kha dog gi 'dod chags dang*/ zhum zhing chags pa dang*/ gzugs kyi 'du shes dang*/ 'du shes dang tshor ba'am/ 'du byed thams cad la rgyab kyis phyogs pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan dag na re 'gog pa ni snyoms 'jug gi sgrib pa las rnam par thar pa'i phyir rnam par thar pa zhes bya'o zhes zer ro/ / de la snyoms 'jug gi sgrib pa ni sgrib pa gang zhig yod na sems las su mi rung bas khams gsum pa'i 'dod chags dang bral ba dag gis kyang bsam gtan dang po'i dngos gzhi'ang skyed par mi byed pa de yin no zhes TIka byed dag 'chad do/ / 'gog pa de la 'jug pa'i sems ni khams gsum na shin tu phra ba srid rtse yin la de nyid kyang{ 'gog pa la dmigs nas} ches phra bar byas pa'i 'jug thogs su snyoms par 'jug ste{ sems rgyun gcod dgos pa'i phyir ro} ldang ba na ni 'phen pa ji lta ba bzhin du srid rtse rang gi sa pa'i dag pa pa dang 'og ma ci yang med pa'i skye mched kyi sa pa'i 'phags pa zag pa med pa'i sems kyis 'gog pa de las ldang bar 'gyur te/ de ltar na 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug dang de la snyoms par 'jug sems ni srid rtse ba yin pas zag bcas kho na yin la/ ldang sems ni zag bcas zag med gnyis ka yin no/ /

(8) The eighth liberation is the liberation of cessation that is the meditative attainment of cessation (nirodhasamāpatti) explained in part II. Question: Why are these called liberations? Reply: (1–2) The first two, (3) the third, (4–7) formless states, and (8) cessation reject, respectively, (1–2) attachment to color, (3) discouragement and attachment, (4–7) discernment of form, and (8) discernment and feeling, or all discernment. Others say: Cessation is called liberation because it is freed from the obscurations of meditative attainment.[1933] Regarding the obscurations to meditative attainment, the Subcommentary explains: If obscurations exist, those free of attachment to the three realms, since their minds are unworkable, do not generate even the actual basis of the first absorption.[1934] The mind entering that cessation, {because it must sever the continuum of the mind,} enters meditative attainment after becoming extremely subtle (sūkṣma) {through focusing on cessation} in the summit of existence, the most subtle (sūkṣma) state in the three realms. When the mind arises, it arises (vyutthāna) from that cessation with an ārya uncontaminated pure mind of its level (svaśuddha) — the summit of existence — or the level below (adhara), the base of nothingness, in accordance with the initial projection [or intention of the ārya]. Thus the meditative attainment of cessation and the mind entering that meditative attainment are always contaminated since they exist on the summit of existence. The mind arising from those [683] is either contaminated or uncontaminated.
dang po 'dod gtogs snang yul can/ / gang dag gzugs can min de dag / spyod yul gong dang rang gi sa'i/ / sdug bsngal sogs dang rjes shes phyogs/ / 34

The first two possess objects of visible form of the desire realm. The formless have object fields of the suffering of the same and higher level and so on, including states of subsequent knowledge. (8:34)

rnam thar 'di dag las dang po gsum las snga ma gnyis ni 'dod par gtogs pa'i snang ba gzugs kyi skye mched yid du mi 'ong ba dang gsum pa ni yid du 'ong ba'i yul can yin no/ / gal te 'di dag ting nge 'dzin la brten nas sprul pa ma yin nam zhe na/ yin mod kyi 'dod par gtogs pa sprul pa yin no/ / gang dag gzugs can min pa'i rnam thar bzhi po de dag gi spyod yul te dmigs pa ni sa gong ma pa dang rang gi sa pa'i sdug bsngal {'di ni nyer bsdogs gong ma bdun ma gtogs pa sa bcu par bshad } dang*/ sogs pas bsdus pa kun 'byung dang 'gog pa dang*/ rjes su shes pa'i phyogs dang mthun pa'i lam gyi bden pa sa gong ma dang 'og ma dang rang gi sa pa'i thams cad dang*/ rtsa bar ma sgos kyang gzugs med kyi rnam thar de dag mtshan ma med pa mtshan ma med pa'i ting nge 'dzin yin pa srid pas de dag mi slob pa'i mtshan ma med pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi so sor ma brtags pas 'gog pa la dmigs pa'i phyir so sor ma brtags pas 'gog pa'ang yin la/ nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched kyi dmigs pa ni 'dus ma byas nam mkha' yang yin no/ / bsam gtan gsum par rnam thar ma bzhag pa ni bsam gtan gnyis pa'i sa pa'i kha dog gi 'dod chags med pa'i phyir dang*/ bde ba mchog tu gyur pa'i snying pos bskyod pas g.yo ba'i phyir ro/ / de ltar na bsam gtan gsum pa na'ang kha dog gi 'dod chags med pas bsam gtan bzhi par sdug pa'i rnam thar ci'i phyir skyed ce na/

From among the first three liberations, the first two possess as objects (viṣaya) unattractive visible (dṛśya) forms of the desire realm (kāmāpta), and the third possesses attractive forms as objects. Question: Aren’t these emanations dependent on concentration? Reply: Indeed, they are, for they are emanations belonging to the desire realm. The four formless (arūpiṇa) liberations have object fields (gocara) or focal objects of suffering of higher levels and the same level. {This is explained as ten levels, excluding the seven higher access concentrations.} “And so on” refers to all states in higher, lower, and the same level constituting the truths of origin and cessation, and the truth of path compatible with states of subsequent knowledge (anvayajñāna). Though it is not mentioned in the root text, it is possible that signless formless liberation is signless concentration as well as nonanalytical cessation, because it focuses on cessation through not analyzing nonlearner signless concentration. And the focal object of the base of infinite space is also unconditioned space. The third absorption is not posited as liberation because it has no attachment to color, as does the second absorption, and it is moved by the protean essence of supreme bliss. Question: Since attachment to color does not exist in the third absorption, why is the liberation of beauty generated in the fourth?

de ni mi sdug pas rgyud zhum pa rab tu dga' bar bya ba dang brtag pa'i phyir ro zhes bshad zin to/ / gzugs med dang po gsum ni zag bcas zag med gnyis ka yin te/ de dag mnyam gzhag dge ba yin pas de la gnyis ka yod pa'i phyir dang*/ bden pa la dmigs par bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na rnam thar dang zil gnod la sogs pa 'di dag la dgos pa ci'i phyir snyoms par 'jug ce na/ thag sring gi gnyen po yin pas nyon mongs pa thag sring ba dang*/ snyoms 'jug la dbang thob par bya ba gnyis kyi phyir te/ nyon mongs pa thag ma bsrings shing snyoms 'jug la dbang ma thob na nyon mongs pa med pa la sogs pa'i yon tan dang*/ gang gi sa la sogs pa gser la sogs par yod pa'i dngos po bsgyur ba dang*/ de nyid dus ring por gnas par byin gyis rlob pa dang*/ sku tshe gtong 'jog dang*/ ri rab rdul phran du 'jug par byed pa la sogs pa 'phags pa'i rdzu 'phrul mi 'grub pas de dag mngon par sgrub par bya ba'i ched du'o/ / yang ci'i phyir rnam thar gsum pa dang brgyad pa kho na la lus kyi mngon sum du byas te rdzogs par byas nas gnas zhes bshad la/ gzhan dag la ni ma yin zhe na/ go rim bzhin du rnam thar dang po gnyis dang gzugs med dang po gsum pos gzugs can dang gzugs med kyi rnam thar gyi sgrib pa mtha' dag spangs pas gtso bo yin pa'i phyir dang*/ gzugs dang gzugs med pa'i khams dang sa'i mtha' na gnas pa'i phyir ro zhes 'grel par 'byung mod kyi/ 'on kyang de gnyis rim pa ltar gzugs dang gzugs med kyi sa pa'i rnam thar rdzogs par mngon du byas pa yin pas de skad bstan to zhes gzung ngo*/ / yang na 'phags pa rnams de gnyis la lan mang du gnas pas na de skad ces gsungs so zhes kun las btus kyi 'grel par bshad do/ /

Reply: It has already been explained that it is to create joy in those discouraged by repulsiveness. The first three liberations of the formless realm have both contaminated and uncontaminated objects because both exist there, since they are virtuous equipoise, and it has been explained that they focus on the four truths. Question: For what purpose does one enter such meditative attainment, subjugation, and so on? Reply: It is so that one may actually establish them, so that one may either distance oneself from affliction, since they are distancing antidotes, or permit one control over meditative attainment. For if one does not distance oneself from afflictions or obtain control over meditative attainment, then one does not establish the qualities of freedom from affliction and so on, or transform substance such as earth into gold and so on, or bless one’s faculties to abide for a long time, or relinquish or extend lifespan, or accomplish ārya supernatural powers such as entering the atoms of Meru. Question: Again, why are only the third and eighth liberations said to fully abide [684] through physical manifestation, and not the others? Reply: That is because they are the main liberations. The first two liberations and the first three of the formless states abandon all obscurations to liberation of form and nonform, respectively, and they abide at the limit of the form and formless realms and levels. This is stated in the Autocommentary.[1935] They are described in this way since these two completely manifest liberation in the form- and formless-realm levels, respectively. Moreover, Elucidation of the Compendium of Abhidharma explains that they are described in that way because āryas frequently abide in these liberations.[1936]
zil gnon brgyad bshad pa/
THE EIGHT BASES OF SUBJUGATION
zil gyis gnon pa'i skye mched brgyad/ / gnyis ni rnam thar dang po bzhin/ / gnyis ni gnyis pa bzhin de gzhan/ / sdug pa'i rnam par thar pa bzhin/ / 35
There are eight bases of subjugation. Two are like the first liberation, two are like the second. The others are like the liberation of beauty. (8:35)

'du shes par gyur pa 'di ni zil gyis gnon pa'i skye mched lnga pa'o zhes pa dang*/ de bzhin du ser po dang dmar po dang dkar po rnams la de ltar lta ba bzhi ste zil gyis gnon pa'i skye mched brgyad gsungs pa'i nang gzugs su 'du shes pa dang de med par 'du shes pa ni rnam thar gyi dang mtshungs la/ chung ngu dang chen po ni sems can dang snod kyi gzugs sam/ phra rags so/ / kha dog bzang ngan ni yid du 'ong mi 'ong ngam/ yang na lha dang mi'i gzugs so/ / zil gyis mnan nas zhes bya ba ni dbang bsgyur nas so/ / shes pa ni zhi gnas dang mthong ba ni lhag mthong yin no zhes 'phags pa thogs med kyis bshad la/ kha dog bzhi'i dpe don gnyis ka'i skabs su re re zhing sngon po la sogs pa tshig bzhi bzhi smros pa ni go rim bzhin du mdor bstan pa dang lhan skyes dang*/ bcos ma dang*/ lhan skyes dang bcos ma gnyis ka'i thun mong gi kha dog yin la zar ma dang dong ga dang ban du ji ba ka'i me tog dang skar ma pa ba sangs dang ras ni rim pa ltar lhan skyes dang bcos ma'i dpe'o/ / de lta bur 'du shes par gyur pa ni zil gyis gnon nam ma non kyang rung ste de la mngon pa'i nga rgyal gyi 'du shes med pa'o/ /

The Sūtra Elaborating Eight declares four: That which views the color of lesser external form as good or bad by discerning internal form, and sees by subjugating consciousness through subjugating form, is the first base of subjugation. Then: So too, that which views the color of greater external form as good and bad by discerning internal form, [and sees by subjugating consciousness through subjugating form], is the second base of subjugation.[1937] So too, it describes the next two bases of subjugation: that which views lesser or greater external form by discerning the absence of internal form. Thus there are four. It also describes a further four views: That which views blue external form, color revealing blueness, the arising of blue light such as the blue of the sesame flower, or the excellent blue of Varānaṣī silk, blue color, color revealing blueness, and the arising of blueness through discerning inner states as formless, and sees these forms through subjugating consciousness, is discernment that is the fifth base of subjugation.[1938] So too, there are those (6) that view yellow, (7) red, and (8) white. These constitute the eight bases of subjugation (abhibhvāyatana). The discernment of internal form and the discernment of the absence of internal form are similar to the states of liberation. “Lesser” and “greater” refer to sentient beings and the environment, or to subtle and coarse form. “Good and bad color” refers to appealing and unappealing color, or divine and human form. “Subjugating” refers to controlling. “Consciousness” is calm abiding, and “seeing” is insight. This is stated by Ārya Asaṅga.[1939] In the context of both the example and meaning of the four colors, then, four terms are applied for each color such as blue: respectively, (1) abbreviated, (2) innate, (3) fabricated, and (4) both innate and artificial. The flowers of the sesame, the karṇikāra,[1940] the bandhujīvaka,[1941] and star-venus[1942] on the one hand and cloth on the other are examples, respectively, of innate and artificial colors. [685] Though such discernment may either suppress or not suppress [certain states], the discernment of higher pride does not arise.

slob dpon gang spel ni shes pa ni dang po shes pa tsam ste bar chad med pa'i lam mo/ / mthong ba ni de'i rgyu mtshan can gyi rnal 'byor rdzogs pa ste rnam grol gyi lam mo zhes 'chad do/ / de dag kyang dang po bzhi ni kha dog dang dbyibs gnyis ka la chags sdang skye ba'i gnyen po dang*/ lhag ma bzhi ni gzhan gyi kha dog la chags pa dang yid rnam par zhum pa'i gnyen po yin no/ /

Master Pūrṇavardhana explains that “consciousness” refers just to the first knowledge that is uninterrupted knowledge. “Sees” refers to the liberated path that brings to fruition the yoga generated for that purpose.[1943] Also, the first four are the antidotes to generating attachment and aversion to both color and shape, and the remaining four are different for they are antidotes to attachment and disgust directed to colors [alone].
