Thus, from among those eight, you should recognize the nature, level, antidote, and focal object of the first two subjugations to be like the first liberation (vimokṣa), where that possessing form views form. So too, you should recognize the nature, level, antidote, and focal object of two — the third and fourth subjugations — to be like the second liberation where that lacking form views form. You should recognize the level, nature, and so on of (5–8) the four subjugations of other color to be like the third liberation, the liberation of beauty (śubhavimokṣa). The difference between liberation and subjugation is that liberation eliminates affliction through merely rejecting the focal object, but it does not subjugate it. Subjugation suppresses focal objects because it resolutely engages unappealing form such as blue, or blueness, and so on freely and instantly, and it does not generate afflictions even though it focuses on blue afflicted entities. Subjugation is not explained to exist in the formless realm because if form is subjugated, [the formless] is also subjugated. Āryas subjugate through engaging the suchness (tathatā) and sign of form. Childlike beings subjugate through resolution that discerns the single taste of beauty, where beauty and repulsiveness rely on each other, are mutually related to each other, and mutually include all form due to that. This is explained by Ārya Asaṅga. Master Pūrṇavardhana observes that some say: Focal objects are subjugated through not having attachment or aversion to color as good or bad.[1944] Some say: Because those bases of subjugation are explained to be the essence of nonattachment as well as the essence of nonaversion, they are seen to possess the single taste of repulsiveness through subjugating both good and bad [color].[1945] This teaches the system of past scholars.
zad par bcu bshad pa/
THE TEN BASES OF TOTALITY
zad par bcu'o brgyad ma chags/ / bsam gtan mtha' na spyod yul ni/ / 'dod pa gnyis ni gzugs med dag / spyod yul rang gi phung po bzhi/ / 36

There are ten totalities. Eight are nonattachment. Earth exists in the limit of absorption. The object field is desire-realm form. Two are pure formless states. Their object field is the same four aggregates. (8:36)

yang bcu las 'phros pa'i mdo las/ zad par sa dang chu dang me dang rlung dang sngon po dang ser po dang dmar po dang dkar po dang nam mkha' dang rnam par shes pa ste bar chad med par zad par sa la sogs par rgyas par khyab par byed pa'i zad par gyi skye mched bcu'o zhes bshad pa'i dang po brgyad ni chags pa'i gnyen po ma chags pa'i rang bzhin yin la/ / {de yang sngo sogs bzhi ni zil gnon phyi ma bzhi'i 'bras bu yin pas so } sa ni bsam gtan gyi ya mtha' bzhi kho na ni yod de/{ zil gnon phyi ma bzhi'i sbyor ba las byung bas so/ /} dang po brgyad kyi spyod yul te dmigs pa ni {'byung bzhi yang kha dog dang dbyibs la 'dod pa'ang yod de } 'jig rten gyi ni tha snyad du/ / kha dog dbyibs la sa zhes brjod/ / chu me yang ngo rlung tshogs khams/ / nyid yin de dang 'dra ba'ang yin zhes 'byung bas 'dod pa na spyod pa'i gzugs kyi skye mched yin la/ gang dag rlung gzugs kyi skye mched yin par mi 'dod pa de dag na re zad par rlung gi dmigs pa ni reg bya'i skye mched yin no zhes zer ro/ /

Again, the Sūtra Elaborating Ten states: The totality of earth, water, fire, wind, blue, yellow, [686] red, white, space, and consciousness are the ten bases of totality (kṛtsna), through extensively pervading the earth and so on without obstruction.[1946] The first eight are antidotes to attachment and by nature nonattachment (alobha), {since four — blue and so on — are the result of the four latter subjugators}. Earth exists only in the upper limit (antya) of the fourth absorption (dhyāna), {since it arises from preparation in the four latter subjugators}. The object field (gocara) or focal object of the first eight, {even when the four primary elements are asserted to be color and shape,} is the base of form utilized in the desire realm. As the Abhidharmakośa states, “In common usage, what is called ‘earth’ is color and shape. Also water and fire. The element of wind is movement itself, or else it is similar” (1:13). Those who do not assert that wind is the base of form say: The focal object of the totality of wind is the base of tactility.[1947]

zad par nam mkha' dang rnam shes gnyis ni gzugs med dang po gnyis dag pa pa'i rang bzhin yin la/ de gnyis kyi spyod yul ni rang gis pa'i phung po bzhi yin{ zag med ni yul thams cad du rgyas par byed mi nus pas 'di dag gi dmigs pa yin no no/ /} skye mched gzhan la zad par du mi 'jog pa ni mig sogs bdun gyis snod kyi 'jig rten la{ de'i rigs med pas} ma khyab cing dri ros gzugs khams su ma khyab la sgra la rgyun med pas zad par du mi bzhag go zhes pa las 'byung la/ ci yang med pa srid dang rtse gnyis zad par du mi bzhag pa ni{ dmigs par mi gsal ba dang spro bsdu dang mi mthun mi mthun pa'i phyir ro} bsdu ba las nam mkha' dang rnam shes mtha' yas kyis zad par mtha' yas shing tshad med pa grub pas de dag las bogs dbyung du med pa'i phyir ro zhes bshad pa'am/ kha cig na re de gnyis zad par gyi 'bras bu yin pas zad par du mi bzhag go zhes zer ro/ / rnam thar la sogs pa gsum gyi khyad par ni yon tan rnams rim gyis 'jog pas dang por dmigs pa la rgyab kyis phyogs/ de nas zil gyis gnon de nas khyab par byed pas snga ma snga ma rdzogs shing dag pa las phyi ma phyi ma 'byung bas gong nas gong du khyad par du 'phags pa'i phyir chung ngu dang 'bring dang chen po dang*/ rgyu dang rgyu 'bras gnyis ka dang 'bras bu kho na'o zhes 'grel pa dang TI kar bshad do/ / de dag las 'gog pa'i rnam thar las gzhan rnams ni so so skye bo dang yang thun mong ba yin la/ 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug ni 'phags pa kho na la yod pa yin no zhes kyang gnas gnyis par bshad zin la/ thams cad kyang thag sring gi gnyen po yin no/ /

Two — the totality of space and consciousness — have the nature of the first two pure formless states (śuddhakārūpya). The object field (gocara) of those two is the four aggregates of the same level. {Their focal object is uncontaminated states since they cannot extend to all objects.} The other bases are not posited as totalities, since the seven such as the eyes do not pervade the physical cosmos {since they lack that capacity}, smell and taste do not pervade the form realm, and sound lacks continuity. Nothingness and the summit of existence are not posited as totalities {because their focal object is unclear and they are incompatible with expansion and contraction}. In addition, the Compendium of Ascertainment explains: Infinite space and infinite consciousness cannot be expanded further since they are established as limitless and immeasurable totalities. Some say: Since they are the result of totalities, they are not posited as totalities. The Autocommentary and the Subcommentary explain that the three of liberation and so on are distinguished by their respective qualities. At first the focal object is rejected, then it is suppressed, then it pervades. Therefore they are said to be small, medium, or large because they excel the former and exist progressively as the cause, the cause and effect, and the effect alone.[1948] From among those, states other than the liberation of cessation are common to ordinary beings, but the meditative attainment of cessation exists only in āryas. This was explained in part II.[1949] All are distant antidotes.
gnyis pa khyad par gyi chos bshad pa ni
The attributes of concentration
rnam thar la sogs pa 'di dag ji ltar 'thob ce na/
Question: How does one obtain those states such as liberation? [687]
'gog pa bshad zin lhag ma ni/ / 'dod chags bral dang sbyor bas 'thob/ / gzugs med ces bya khams gsum gyi/ / rten can lhag ma mi las skye/ / 37

Cessation has been explained. The remainder are obtained through freedom from attachment and through preparation. Those called formless are possessed by beings of the three realms. The remainder arise in humans. (8:37)

nyi shu rtsa drug las 'gog pa'i rnam thar gyis thob pa dang rten la sogs pa ni gnas gnyis par bshad zin la lhag ma nyi shu rtsa lnga po rnams ni sngar 'dris pa yin na 'dod chags dang bral ba tsam dang {'dris pa ni dang po nas srid rtse'i bar sngar thob pa btang ba dag go } ma 'dris pa rnams ni sbyor ba 'bad rtsol gyis 'thob ste/ goms pa dang ma goms pa'i mthu las byung ba'i phyir ro/ / yang gzugs med ces bya ba'i rnam thar bzhi dang zad par gnyis ni khams gsum gyi rten can yin la/ de dag gi lhag ma {rnam thar dang po gsum zil gnon brgyad zad par brgyad de } bcu dgu po rnams ni mi las skye bas mi'i rten can kho na yin te/ lha la sogs pa'i 'gro ba gzhan na lung med pa'i phyir dang*/ 'di dag ni lung gi stobs kyis bskyed par bya ba yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na lung med pas bsam gtan gzugs med dag khams gong ma gnyis su {rang rang gi gong ma gong ma } ji ltar skye zhe na/

Reply: From among those twenty-six,[1950] that obtained by the freedom of cessation (nirodha) and the basis have been explained in part II. Regarding the remaining twenty-five, those having prior familiarity with them obtain them merely through freedom from attachment (vairāgya), {where “familiarity” means previously obtained and relinquished from the first absorption to the summit of existence.} And those without prior familiarity obtain them through preparatory (prayoga) exertion; they arise due to the force of habitual engagement or lack of it. (1–4) Four liberations and (5–6) two totalities called formless states are possessed by beings of the three realms (tridhātvāśraya). The remaining nineteen {namely, (7–9) the first three liberations, (10–17) the eight subjugators, and (18–25) the eight totalities} are possessed by human beings alone, since they arise in humans (manuṣyaja) and there is no scripture stating that they exist in other reincarnating beings such as gods. And if such states arise in gods, this should be established by scripture. Question: How do they arise in {progressively higher states of} the two higher realms of the absorptions and formless states, since there is no scripture establishing this?
khams gnyis dag tu gzugs med pa/ / rgyu dang las kyi stobs kyis skye/ / gzugs kyi khams su bsam gtan rnams/ / de dag dang chos nyid kyis kyang / / 38
In two realms, formless states arise by the powers of cause and karma. In the form realm, the absorptions arise through those as well as reality. (8:38)

bsam gtan gzugs med kyi snyoms 'jug ni spyir lung dang rgyu dang*/ las dang*/ chos nyid kyi stobs dang bzhi las skye ba las khams gong ma gnyis po dag tu ni lung med kyang gzugs med pa'i snyoms 'jug rgyu dang las kyi stobs gnyis kyis skye'o/ / de la gzugs su rgyu'i stobs kyis skye ba ni sngon mi'i rten la gzugs med kyi snyoms 'jug goms par byas pa las nyams pa dag gzugs khams su skyes te/ der sngon goms pa'i skal mnyam kyi rgyu stobs dang ldan pa nye pas gzugs med kyi ting nge 'dzin skye la/ las kyi stobs kyis skye ba ni sngon mi'i rten la gzugs med kyi snyoms 'jug thob nas nyams pa de nyid lan grangs gzhan la myong 'gyur gyi las su gyur pa'i stobs kyis gzugs khams su skyes pa na'ang gzugs med kyi ting 'dzin thob nas yang gzugs med par skye ste/ 'og ma 'i sa las 'dod chags dang ma bral bar gong mar mi skye ba'i phyir ro/ / ji ltar gzugs med gzugs su skye ba ltar gzugs med gzugs med nyid du skye ba'ang rgyu dang las kyi stobs gnyis las skye ste/ de la rgyu'i stobs kyis skye ba ni gong ma'i nyer bsdogs sgom par byed pa la yin la/ las kyis stobs kyis skye ba ni skye bas thob pa'i gzugs med do/ /

Reply: In general, the meditative attainments of the absorptions and formless states arise from four powers: scripture, cause, karma, and reality. As there is no scripture in the two higher realms, formless meditative attainment arises due to the powers of both cause (hetu) and karma. That which arises due to the power of the cause in the form realm is formless meditative attainment existing upon a human basis. It arises in the form realm through the degeneration of meditation. Formless concentration arises due to the increasing power of a homogeneous cause previously cultivated. That which arises due to the power of karma is just that formless meditative attainment previously obtained on a human basis; once it has degenerated, it regenerates in the form realm due to the power of karma to be experienced in a third life. Also, having obtained formless concentration, one is born in the formless realm, but one is not born in higher realms if one is not free of attachment to lower {levels}. Just as formless states arise in the form realm, so too formless states arise in the formless realm through both the powers of both cause and karma. That which arises by the power of the cause is through the cultivation of higher access concentration. That which arises by the power of karma is formless states obtained through birth.

gzugs kyi khams su bsam gtan rnams ni rgyu dang las kyi stobs de dag dang chos nyid kyi stobs kyis kyang skye'o/ / de la chos nyid kyis skye ba ni 'jig rten 'jig pa'i tshe bsam gtan 'og ma'i sems can la dge ba'i chos rnams kyis 'jug pa shas che bas bsam gtan gong ma'i sems ngang gis skye ba bzhin te/ bsam gtan gyi gdams ngag ston pa'i lung la ma ltos par sngon bsam gtan goms pa'i bag chags kyis skye ba la chos nyid kyis skye ba zhes brjod do/ / bye brag tu smra ba bag chags kyi rnam gzhag mi 'dod pas sngon bsam gtan goms pa'i skal mnyam gyi rgyu las 'byung ba la 'dod do/ / 'dod pa'i khams su ni lha la rgyu gsum po de dag dang*/ mi la de dag gi steng du yid la byed pa bdun dang sems gnas pa'i thabs dgu la sogs pa lung gi stobs las kyang skye'o/ / 'di yang legs par dpyad na las kyi stobs kyis skye ba de gal te las kyi rnam smin gyi 'bras bur 'dod na ni 'dod khams su bsam gtan gzugs med dang*/ gzugs su gzugs med kyi sems las kyi stobs kyis mi skye bar 'gyur te/ de dag ni gzugs dang gzugs med kho nar rnam par smin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'on te las kyi rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bur 'dod na ni de'i rgyu dang chos nyid kyis skye ba'ang yin pas rnam pa gsum gyi dbye ba mi 'thad par 'gyur mod kyi 'on kyang gtso che chung gi bye brag la dgongs nas 'di'i rnam dbye mdzad do/ / 'jig rten 'jig pa na de'i rkyen gyis bsam gtan bzhi pa la gzugs med kyi ting nge 'dzin mi skye bas gzugs med la chos nyid kyi stobs kyis skye ba ma bshad la/ rang sa'i ting nge 'dzin skye ba ni chos nyid ma yin pas 'jig rten 'jig pa na lung med par 'og sa'i rten la gong sa'i ting nge 'dzin skye ba kho na la 'dir chos nyid ces bya'o/ / las dang chos nyid la'ang rgyu yod mod kyi de dag gtso che bas de skad bstan to/ /

In the form realm, the absorptions arise by the power of cause and karma, as well as by the power of reality (dharmatā). That which arises spontaneously is the minds of the higher absorptions that naturally arise in sentient beings through having previously engaged in virtuous Dharmas, when the cosmos is destroyed. Thus absorption arising due to the imprints of previously having cultivated absorption, without reliance on scripture that reveals the instruction on how the absorptions arise, is called “arising through reality.” Vaibhāṣikas assert that it arises from the prior homogeneous cause of cultivating absorption, since they do not assert a theory of imprints (vāsanā). As well as arising in gods in the desire realm due to those three causes, [688] in addition they also arise in humans by the power of scripture revealing the seven attentions,[1951] the nine mental placements,[1952] and so on. This should be well analyzed, for if that which arises by the power of karma is asserted to be the maturational result of karma, then absorptions and formless states would not arise in the desire realm. Likewise, formless states would not arise in the form realm by the power of karma because they mature separately in the form and formless realms. However, if they are asserted to be the result of natural outflow, then indeed the threefold classification would be untenable, since they arise by their causes as well as by reality. But this classification was made considering their specific dominant modes of arising. When the cosmos is destroyed, formless concentration does not arise in the fourth absorption due to that condition, nor is it said to arise spontaneously in the formless realm. Also, concentration of the same level does not arise spontaneously. Therefore, when the cosmos is destroyed, only concentrations of higher realms are said to arise on lower physical bases due to reality. But this is stated without scriptural authority. Indeed, the causes of karma and reality exist, and they are dominant causes.
spyi'i don gsum pa bshad pa
EXPLAINING THE THREE GENERAL MEANINGS
yongs su rdzogs pa'i bya ba la bstan pa dang de 'dzin pa bshad pa dang*/ bdag nyid kyis bstan pa bzung ba la skyon dor ba dang*/ gzhan bstan pa 'dzin pa rnams la bag yod par gdams pa gsum las
There are three: teaching that which is complete and explaining those who hold it, discarding faults so that one may hold the teachings, and instructing others to hold the teachings with diligence.
dang po [yongs su rdzogs pa'i bya ba la bstan pa dang de 'dzin pa bshad pa] ni
TEACHING THAT WHICH IS COMPLETE AND EXPLAINING THOSE WHO HOLD IT
ston pa'i dam chos rnam gnyis te/ / lung dang rtogs pa'i bdag nyid do/ / de 'dzin byed pa smra byed dang / / sgrub par byed pa kho na yin/ / 39
The holy Dharma of the Master is of two types: scriptural Dharma and the Dharma of realization. Those who hold scripture can teach others. Only those who hold realization establish it. (8:39)

ston pa sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das kyi bstan pa dam pa'i chos ni rnam pa gnyis te/ lung gi chos dang*/ mngon par rtogs pa'i chos kyi bdag nyid do/ / de la lung gi chos ni mdo sde dang 'dul ba dang mngon pa'i sde snod gsum yin te/ rim pa ltar dang pos ni bslab pa gsum dang gnyis pas ni tshul khrims dang ldan na 'gyod pa med pa la sogs pa'i rim gyis ting nge 'dzin 'thob pa'i phyir sems kyi bslab pa dang tshul khrims kyi bslab pa dang*/ gsum pas ni don phyin ci ma log par rab tu 'byed pas shes rab kyi bslab pa sgrub pa'i phyir dang*/ blang dor gyi gnas la the tshom za ba dang*/ spyod pa mtha' gnyis la sbyor ba dang*/ lta ba mchog tu 'dzin pa'i gnyen po byed pa'i phyir dang*/ blang dor gyi gnas ston pa dang*/ de blang dor gyis sgrub pa dang*/ 'bel gtam la mkhas par byed pa'i phyir ro/ / de skad du yang mdo sde'i rgyan las/ sde snod dag ni gsum mam gnyis kyang rung*/ bsdus pa'i phyir de'i rgyu ni dgus 'dod do zhes bshad do/ / sde snod gsum po de dag la thos pa dang bsam pa dang zhi gnas dang lhag mthong gi sgom pa byas pas rim pa ltar sems la bag chags 'jog pa dang*/ rtog par byed pa dang*/ sems zhi bar byed pa dang*/ rab tu rtogs pa'i sgo nas spang bya las rnam par grol bar byed de de nyid las/ de ni bag chags rtogs dang zhi ba dang*/ / rab tu rtogs pas rnam par grol bar byed ces 'byung ngo*/ / lung gi chos kyi ngo bo dang tshad la sogs pa ni gnas gnyis par bshad zin to/ / mngon par rtogs pa'i chos ni byang chub kyi phyogs dang mthun pa'i chos sum cu rtsa bdun dang 'bras bu rnam grol gyi lam zad pa dang bcas pa ste de dag kyang gnas drug par bshad zin to/ / de ltar na bstan pa dam pa'i chos ni lung dang*/ sgrub pa dang*/ 'bras bu'i chos gsum du'ang 'gyur ro/ / 'o na chos de dag 'dzin pa gang zhe na/

The holy Dharma of the teachings of the Master Buddha Bhagavan is of two types: scriptural (āgama) Dharma and the Dharma of realization (adhigama). Scriptural Dharma is the three piṭakas: the categories of Sūtra, Vinaya, and Abhidharma. Due to the first, one engages in the three higher trainings, and due to the second, one possesses the higher training of ethics. They are, respectively, training the mind in order to serially obtain concentration free of regret and so on, and training in ethics. Due to the third, one establishes the higher training of wisdom, since it correctly distinguishes the meaning of Dharma. Again, they act, respectively, as the antidote to doubt about what should be practiced and what should be rejected, as the antidote to engaging in the two extremes of action, and as the antidote to grasping afflicted views as supreme. Or they indicate what should be practiced and rejected, what is accomplished by such practice and rejection, and what discourses should be mastered. The Ornament of the Mahāyāna Sūtras notes: The piṭakas can be condensed into three or two, but their causes are asserted to be nine.[1953] Since one cultivates the three piṭakas through hearing, contemplation, calm abiding, and insight, one is liberated from objects to be abandoned through placing imprints on the mind, causing realization, [689] pacifying the mind, and gaining full realization. That text continues: One is liberated through imprints, realizing, pacification, and fully realizing.[1954] The nature and measure of scriptural Dharma and so on has been explained in part II. The Dharma of realization is the thirty-seven factors conducive to enlightenment, the resultant liberated path, and the elimination [of contaminants]. These have been explained in part VI. Therefore the holy Dharma of the teachings consist of three: scriptural Dharma, established Dharma, and resultant Dharma. Question: Who holds these Dharmas?

de la lung gi chos de 'dzin par byed pa ni lung bzhin du shes nas nyon mongs pa can ma yin pa'i bsam pas gzhan la smra bar byed pa yin pa'i phyir sde snod 'dzin pa dang*/ lung gi chos 'dzin pa dang*/ bstan pa 'dzin pa zhes kyang bya'o/ / rtogs pa'i chos de 'dzin par byed pa ni byang chub kyi phyogs dag mthun pa'i chos rang gi rgyud la sgrub cing nyams su len par byed pa yin pa'i phyir bslab pa gsum la slob pa de dag ni ston pa'i bstan pa dam pa'i chos 'dzin pa yin no/ / de gnyis las gzhan pa ni dam pa'i chos 'dzin pa ma yin pas na kho na'i sgra smros so/ / de'i phyir skyes bu dam pa kha cig ni lung gi chos gtsor 'dzin par byed la/ skyes bu dam pa kha cig ni mngon par rtogs pa'i chos 'dzin par byed do/ / skyes bu dam pa kha cig ni gnyis ka'ang 'bad pas 'dzin par byed de/ des na de dag ji srid du gnas pa de srid du bstan pa dam pa'i chos gnas par rig par bya'o/ / 'o na shAkya'i rgyal po'i bstan pa dus ji srid du gnas she na/ 'grel pa las/ de dag kyang lo stong du gnas so zhes bshad do/ / gzhan dag na re rtogs pa ni de lta bu yin gyi lung ni yun ring du gnas so zhes zer ro zhes 'byung ba la/ TIka byed dag yun ring du gnas pa ni lo stong gi 'og tu'ang gnas so zhes bya ba ste phyogs 'di nyid rigs par blta'o/ / zhes 'chad do/ / de yang bskal pa bzang po'i mdo las ni lugs snga ma dang mthun par de bzhin gshegs pa shAkya thub pa'i dam pa'i chos ni lo lnga brgya'i bar du gnas so/ / lo lnga brgya'i bar du ni dam pa'i chos ltar snang ngo*/ / zhes lo stong gnas par gsungs la/ lung phran tshegs las kyang lo stong kho na gnas par gsungs so/ /

Reply: Those who hold scriptural Dharma hold the piṭakas, because they are able to teach them to others with a mind that is not afflicted and with knowledge that accords with scripture. They are called “those who hold scriptural Dharma” and “those who hold the teachings.” Those who hold the Dharma of realization hold the holy Dharma of the teachings of the Master, for they are trained in the three higher trainings because they establish the factors conducive to enlightenment in their mindstreams and practice them. Since no one other than those two hold the holy Dharma, the term “only” is stated. Therefore one holy being says: You should hold scriptural Dharma as chief. Another holy being says: You should hold the Dharma of realization. Again, another holy being says: You should hold both through exertion. Therefore you should understand that for as long as both exist, for that long the holy Dharma teachings will exist. Question: How long will the teachings of the king of the Śākyas remain? Reply: The Autocommentary explains: They will remain one thousand years.[1955] Other scholars say: That is so for the Dharma of realization, but scriptural Dharma will remain longer.[1956] The Subcommentary states: It is said that abiding long is abiding for more than a thousand years. This position is logical.[1957] Also, the Fortunate Eon Sūtra says: In accordance with the former system, the holy Dharma of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni will abide for five hundred years. Then an ersatz Dharma will abide for five hundred years.[1958]
This passage states that it will last for one thousand years. Also, the Kṣudraka Collection remarks: It will abide for just one thousand years.[1959]

gang dag lung phran tshegs las bstan pa lo bdun stong du gnas pa las skye dgu'i bdag mo la sogs pa bud med rab tu phyung bas nyis stong 'gribs nas lo lnga stong gnas par gsungs so zhes 'chad pa de dag gis ni lung phran tshegs ma mthong bar zad de/ phran tshegs kyi skye dgu'i bdag mo go'u ta ma la sogs pa la bla ma'i chos brgyad gsungs pa'i skabs dang*/ 'phags pa kun dga' bo mya ngan las 'da' bar bzhed nas sha na'i gos can la bstan pa gtod pa'i skabs dang*/ 'phags pa nyi ma'i gung pas ri spos kyi ngad ldang gi klu btul ba'i skabs la sogs pa rnams las bstan pa lo stong kho na gnas par gsungs kyi lo nyis stong 'grib pa dang lnga stong gnas par gsungs pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / 'bum TIka las ni lugs phyi ma dang mthun par lnga stong la phyed phyed du byas nas lnga brgya pa phrag bcu las dang po la dgra bcom pa dang*/ gnyis pa la phyir mi 'ong ba dang*/ gsum pa la rgyun zhugs mang du 'byung bas 'bras bu'i dus kyi le'u gsum dang*/ bzhi pa la shes rab kyi bslab pa dang*/ lnga pa la sems kyi bslab pa dang*/ drug pa la tshul khrims kyi bslab pa la gnas pa mang du 'byung bas sgrub pa'i dus kyi le'u gsum dang*/ bdun pa la mngon pa dang*/ brgyad pa la mdo sde dang*/ dgu pa la 'dul ba 'dzin pa mang du 'byung bas lung gi dus kyi le'u gsum dang*/ bcu pa ni rtag tsam 'dzin pa'i dus kyi le'u zhes bya ste/{ de dag tu gtso che bas de skad bshad kyi thams cad la thams cad med pa ma yin gsungs so } de nyid la lnga brgya pa tha ma zhes bya'o zhes bshad do/ / de nas dam pa'i chos nub par 'gyur te/ de'i dus na 'dzam bu'i gling pa'i mi'i tshe tshad lnga bcu pa yin la/ da ltar ni tshe tshad drug cu pa dang mngon pa'i dus yin par mkhas pa dag gsung ngo*/ / zla ba'i snying pos zhus pa'i mdo las ni lo nyis stong gnas par gsungs so/ /

Some assert that the teachings will abide for five thousand years because [they claim] the Kṣudraka Collection states they will last seven thousand years but that period is then reduced by two thousand years due to the ordination of women — Mahāprajāpatī and so on.[1960] Reply: But that assertion should be discarded, since no such statement has been observed in the Kṣudraka Collection. In the Kṣudraka Collection, it says instead that the teachings will last one thousand years when describing how the eight rules were given to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī and so on, when describing how Ārya Ānanda entrusted the teachings to Śāṇakavāsa when he attained nirvāṇa, [690] and when describing how the ārya Madhyāhna tamed the nāga of Mount Gandhamādana and so on. There is no statement declaring that the teachings would remain for five thousand years due to being reduced by two thousand years. The Commentary on the Hundred-Thousand-Verse Perfection of Wisdom explains: In accordance with the latter system, the teachings will last five thousand years, divided into ten periods of five hundred years. There are three periods of the time of the result: in the first many arhats arise, in the second many nonreturners arise, and in the third many stream enterers arise. There are three periods of the time of establishment: in the fourth there are many who abide in the higher training of wisdom, in the fifth there are many who abide in the higher training of mind, and in the sixth there are many who abide in the higher training of ethics. There are three periods of the time of scripture: in the seventh there are many who hold the teachings of Abhidharma, in the eighth there are many who hold the teachings of Sūtra, and in the ninth there are many who hold the teachings of Vinaya. The tenth is called the period of the time of adhering to the outer signs, and that is the final five-hundred-year period. {They are given these names since they indicate the dominant activity, but there is no absolute certainty.}[1961] Then the holy Dharma will disappear, and at that time the lifespan of human beings of Jambudvīpa will be fifty years. Thus scholars have stated that when the lifespan is sixty years, that will be the time of Abhidharma. The Sūtra Requested by Candragarbha states that Dharma abides for two thousand years.[1962]
gnyis pa ni bdag gis mngon pa'i chos 'di phal cher ni
DISCARDING FAULTS SO THAT ONE MAY HOLD THE TEACHINGS
bdag gis mngon pa'i chos 'di phal cher ni/ / kha che bye brag smra ba'i tshul grub bshad/ / nyes par zin gang de 'dir bdag gis nyes/ / dam chos tshul la tshad ma thub rnams yin/ / 40

I have mainly explained Abhidharma in conformity with the established system of the Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas. Any faults detected in this text are my faults. Only the Sage is authoritative in expounding holy Dharma. (8:40)

kha che bye brag tu smra ba'i tshul grub pa dang mthun par bshad la/ cung zad ni mdo sde pa dang nyi 'og bye brag tu smra ba'i 'dod pa'i tshul yang bshad pa'i phyir phal cher zhes smros so/ / de ltar bshad pa la gzhung 'dir tshig dang don gyi cha la nyes par mkhas pa rnams kyis zin te mkhyen pa gang yin pa de ni rtsom pa po bdag gis nyes pa yin pas mkhas pa rnams kyis bzod par mdzod cig ces pa'o/ / gal te kha che bye brag tu smra ba'i slob dpon mkhas pa rnams gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa'i lung bzhin bshad pas na nyes pa med do snyam na/ lung dang rtogs pa'i dam pa'i chos kyi tshul te mtshan nyid brjod pa la ni thub pa sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das dang*/ de'i sras sha ri'i bu la sogs pa rnams kho na tshad ma yin gyi gzhan la ni 'khrul ba srid pa'i phyir ro/ /

I have mainly explained Abhidharma in conformity with the established system of the Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣikas. “Mainly” is stated because [Vasubandhu] has also explained the systems of the Sautrāntikas and the Aparāntaka Vaibhāṣikas, but to a lesser extent. Any faults detected (durgṛhīta) and comprehended by scholars about the words and meaning in this text thus explained are mine as the author, and I request the patience of scholars. Some may think: There is no fault, for Kāśmīri Vaibhāṣika scholars have explained this in conformity with scripture within their lineage of interpretation. Reply: Only the Sage, the Buddha Bhagavan, and his sons such as Śāriputra are authoritative (pramāṇa) in expounding the means or characteristics of the holy scriptural and realizational Dharma (saddharma). Others can be mistaken.

After the Master, the eye of the world, taught the liberated paths and the classifications of the path to learners, the Buddha Bhagavan smiled and attained nirvāṇa. Most ārya beings, such as Ārya Kāśyapa who was a lord of Dharma like the Buddha, also attained nirvāṇa and departed. Then quarreling arose about the words and meaning of the teachings of the Sage. Question: Who quarreled? Reply: Those who quarrel are those [691] who do not see the four truths, who do not see reality since they are obscured by the darkness of ignorance, who do not depend on the scriptures of the Master, and who possess evil conceptions that are appealing to themselves and cannot be corrected by others. Question: How did they quarrel? Reply: One hundred and ten years after the parinirvāṇa of the Buddha, monks of the city of Vaiśālī who did not comprehend reality engaged in ten unsuitable bases of action, such as the rite of hulu hulu,[1963] and quarreled about the teachings. Then seven hundred arhats, including the elder Ānanda and all the elders abiding with him, from Kāma and Kīrti up to Candra and Śānta, assembled in Vaiśālī and settled the dispute after forming two conclaves.[1964] Then, one hundred sixty years after the passing of the Master, in a city called Puṣpita,[1965] during the reign of King Kālāśoka, arhats recited the discourses of the Master in Sanskrit, Prākṛt, Apabhraṃśa, and Paiśācī, and their students individually split and formed eighteen sects, with various mutually incompatible tenet systems. Later, when they quarreled, arhats and learned ordinary beings assembled at Jalandhara Monastery and pacified the dispute. At that time three hundred years had passed since the passing of the Master. Some say: One hundred thirty-seven years after the parinirvāṇa of the Buddha, during the reign of kings Nanda and Mahāpadma, the elders Mahākāśyapa and Guru and so on lived in the city of Pāṭaliputra. Then a demon called Bhadra, who wore the robes of a monk, demonstrated many miracles, divided the Saṅgha, and caused disturbance to the teachings. At that time the elders Nāgasena and Manojña split the Saṅgha into sects, and for sixty-three years the elder Vātsīputra maintained the teachings.[1966]
rang byung rang byung bstan pa gces 'dzin rnams/ / mchog tu zhir gshegs 'gro mgon med pa na/ / 'doms med yon tan 'joms par byed pa yi/ / dri mas dga' mgur deng sang 'di na spyod/ / 2

gzhan yang rang byung rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas dang rang byung de'i bstan pa gces par 'dzin pa rnams kyang 'khor ba las mchog tu gyur pa sdug bsngal rgyu dang bcas pa zhi ba'i mya ngan las 'das par gshegs te/ 'gro ba rnams la skyob par byed pa'i mgon med par gyur pa na yang dag pa'i gdams ngag 'doms par byed pa med pas sngar bshad pa'i yon tan rnams 'joms par byed cing bstan pa nub par byed pa'i rgyu lta ba la sogs pa'i dri ma rnams kyis dga' mgur te rang dgar dus deng sang 'jig rten 'di na spyod par byed do/ /

Again, those who cherished the self-arisen perfect Buddha and the self-arisen teachings proceeded to nirvāṇa and attained the supreme state beyond saṃsāra that pacifies suffering and its cause. Reincarnating beings were then without a protector, and the previously explained qualities declined, since there were none who gave correct instruction. Those with corrupt views and so on that cause the degeneration of the teachings took joy, and these days such careless beings are active in the world.
de ltar thub pa dag gi bstan pa ni/ / lkog mar srog phyin 'dra dang dri ma rnams/ / stobs dang ldan pa'i dus su rig nas ni/ / thar pa 'dod pa dag gis bag yod gyis/ / 3

gong du bstan pa'i tshul de ltar na thub pa sangs rgyas dag gi bstan pa ni dper na 'chi ba'i dus na lkog mar srog phyin pa na 'chi ba la nye ba dang 'dra bar ring du mi gnas pa'i phyir dang*/ lta ba ngan pa la sogs pa'i dri ma rnams kyang stobs dang ldan pa'i dus su rig par byas nas ni thar pa 'dod pa dag gis bag yod par gyis la bstan pa 'dzin pa la rnam par brtson par gyis shig ces 'doms pa ste/ ji skad du so so thar pa las/ tshe dang ldan pa dag rga ba dang 'chi ba mngon par 'ong zhing ston pa'i bstan pa yang 'jig par 'gyur bas tshe dang ldan pa dag gis bag yod pas rnal 'byor du bya'o/ / de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas rnams kyi byang chub dang*/ gzhan yang gang dag de lta bu dang mthun pa dge ba'i chos byang chub kyi phyogs rnams kyang bag yod pas thob bo zhes gsungs pa lta bu'o/ / gang phyir yon tan rten gyur yan lag nyer bsdogs dang bcas pa'i/ / bsam gtan dang ni gzugs med snyoms 'jug rab dbye 'thob tshul dang*/ / de dag la brten yon tan ting 'dzin tshad med rnam thar sogs/ / ji bzhin rtogs pa gnas 'di las yin de phyir 'di mnyan rigs/ /

Compared to the former method of teaching, the teachings of the Sage are now like a person nearing death when the life force proceeds to the throat, death approaches, and that person will not abide long. Corrupt beings who possess [692] false view now vent their arguments when they are in a position of strength. But those who desire freedom are instructed to hold the teachings with diligence, through exertion. The Pratimokṣa Sūtra declares: Venerables, aging and death will actually come, and even the teachings of the Buddha will be destroyed; therefore practice yoga with diligence. Obtain the enlightenment of a tathāgata, arhat, perfectly complete buddha, and apply yourselves with diligence to the virtuous Dharmas compatible with it, such as the factors conducive to enlightenment.[1967] Because they are the basis of qualities, listen to this part. You will comprehend their classifications just as they are, as well as the methods for obtaining the absorptions and formless meditative attainments. Then, in dependence on them, you will obtain qualities, concentrations, the immeasurables, liberation, and so on.

36. Conclusion: The Purpose of Engaging in Virtue

brtan dang g.yo ba'i rang bzhin gang yin de sgrub byed/ / skye ba dang ni skyed byed de dag rnam pa ma lus las/ / rnam grol de yang de bzhin nyid yin dpag yas yon tan la/ / thogs med spobs pa'i 'byung gnas chos mngon 'di ni sangs rgyas gsungs/ / gnas brtan ka t+ya'i bu sogs sde bdun gzhung gi rjes 'brang zhing*/ / sdom brtson dam pa chu dbus pa dang nyer sbas la sogs pa/ / 'phags tshogs rnams kyi grub chen bye brag bshad mtsho chen po yi/ / don gyi rin chen ma lus mdzod gyur 'di ni mdzad pa gang*/ / dbyig gnyen zhes bya sangs rgyas bstan pa ma lus mkhyen pa yi/ / nyi ma nyid gyur de yis thub dang de sras zhir gshegs shing*/ / bsdu ba'i gzhi yang nyams gyur gsung rab rnam par bslad mthong nas/ / snyigs dus bstan pa'i dbang gyur gzhung mang mdzad par gyur pa yin/ / de ltar phan bde'i 'byung gnas bstan pa'i mig gyur gzhung bzang 'di ni slob dpon gyis mdzad pa'i/ / rab gsal 'grel chen nyi 'od la brten rnam par phye ba'i bshad sbyar dag kyang mthong gyur cing*/ / mkhas dang mkhas pa rim nas rim par brgyud pa'i man ngag nyer thob legs bshad goms pa'i mthus/ / 'jam dbyangs zhes byas sangs rgyas bstan la mos pa lhur byas rnams bshad 'di ni byas pa yin/ /

THE BUDDHA PROCLAIMED ABHIDHARMA to be the state liberated from all arising and generation without exception, which is reality itself and the very source of unobstructed courage to attain such limitless qualities, and the existence of which is proven by the very nature of stable and immovable states. The elder Kātyāyanīputra and so on adhered to the textual tradition in the seven treatises, and pure ethical beings such as Dhītika and Upagupta and great siddhas of the ārya assembly collected this treasure of the entire precious meaning of the great ocean of Vaibhāṣika explanation. Vasubandhu was like the sun itself and comprehended all the Buddha’s teachings without exception. He saw that, after the Sage and his sons had proceeded to peace, the basis of the collected teachings was declining and scripture was becoming corrupted. Thus, in this degenerate time, he composed many texts conforming with the teachings. And this pure text, which is the very eye of the teachings and a source of benefit and bliss, was composed by the master. Even those who composed discerning commentaries came to see the meaning of Abhidharma in dependence on the sun’s rays of this great clarifying commentary. And by the might of cultivating excellent explanation, infused with the advice passed down within the lineage of scholars, he is called Mañjuśrī, and this explanation is faithful to the intention of the Buddha’s teachings.

dge ba dri med rgya chen bsags pa gang des mun par 'khyams pa yi/ / 'gro ba 'di dag ma lus thar pa'i snang ldan 'phags lam bzang por ni/ / kun nas 'khrid byed thub mchog nyid du gyur nas skyabs med sems can rnams/ / srid dang zhi ba'i 'jigs pa kun las ma lus rab tu sgrol bar shog / sa chen mnga' ba rkang gnyis rnams kyi rje/ / skyabs gsum rin chen dbu yi cod pan gyis/ / nyer mdzes sras dang bcas pa snyun med cing*/ / yun ring zhabs brtan chab srid bde bar gyur/ / skye dgu rnams kyang phan tshun byams ldan zhing*/ / yams dang nye bar 'tshe ba kun zhi ste/ / tshe dang 'byor pas brgyan pa'i dal 'byor dag /'bras bu yod par kun du spyod par shog /bdag kyang skye ba kun du mi yi lus/ / tshul khrims gtsang ma'i gos kyis rab brgyan pa/ / thob nas sangs rgyas gsung rab ma lus pa/ / ji bzhin rtogs nas gzhan la ston gyur cig /don mang phra dang tshig kyang brling ba dang*/ / shin tu mkhas pa rnams kyis rnam dpyad pa'i/ / tshul yang tha dad sna tshogs 'gro ba'i slad/ / sangs rgyas gsung yang rnam pa mang mthong bas/ gzhung 'dir ji bzhin min par bdag gis ni/ / bshad gyur nyes pa gang de rgyal rnams dang*/ rgyal ba'i sras sogs mkhas rnams spyan sngar ni/ / ci zhig gyur zhes yid ni gnong bar gyur/ / gang dag rang gzhan gzhung la ma sbyangs shing*/ / phyogs re'i don la mos pa lhur byed pa/ / de dag blo dang 'tsham par ma gyur pa/ / de dag gang yin shes pas brtag dgos so/ /

Through the extensive accumulation of stainless virtue, may all reincarnating beings who wander in darkness without exception be led to the pure ārya path possessing the light of liberation and [693] become supreme sages, fully liberating all sentient beings from the fears of existence and peace. You are lord of two-legged beings, sovereign over this great earth possessing the crown of the Three Jewels of refuges. May your splendid sons be free from disease; may they live long and happiness prevail in your dominion. May all beings possess mutual love for each other, and may epidemics and violence be pacified. May beings have leisure and opportunity endowed with life and wealth; may beings always act with mindfulness of the results of their actions. May I have a human body in all my lives, adorned with the garment of pure ethics. And with this may I comprehend as it is the complete words of the Buddha and teach it to others. Scholars with the means to analyze numerous subtle meanings and profound terms study the many different facets of the Buddha’s words in order to raise dubious distinctions. May I not act like that regarding this text. For if I raise a supposed fault in front of scholars who are buddhas and bodhisattvas, stating “What is this?” I may be embarrassed. Those not trained in ours or others’ texts, who are subservient to their own position, do not attain satisfaction of mind. We must examine why this is so.
COLOPHON

chos mngon pa'i mdzod kyi 'grel pa mngon pa'i rgyan zhes bya ba rgyal ba'i bstan pa lnga brgya phrag bdun pa'i mthar nye ba na/ shes bya rnam par 'byed pa'i blo gros mtshungs pa med pas thub pa'i bstan pa'i rgyal mtshan 'dzin cing*/ thugs rje dang 'phrin las kyi dpal 'byor bzang pos skye dgu rnams smin cing grol bar mdzad pa bla ma dam pa chos gyi rgyal po rin po che dang*/ shes bya'i nam mkha' la mkhyen pa'i dkyil 'khor rab tu rgyas shing snyan grags kyi 'od zer gyis phyogs ma lus pa khyab par gyur pas sdom brtson mkhas pa rnams kyi gtsug gi nor gyur cing*/ gangs can gyi rgyud kyi gnas brtan chen po mchims thams cad mkhyen pa la sogs pa'i zhabs kyi rdul rnyog pa med pa spyi bos len pa mang du thos pa shAkya'i dge slong 'jam pa'i dbyangs kyis/ dpal sa skya'i chos grwa chen por dbu brtsams nas/ sa'i dbang phyug rgyal po chen po'i pho brang cong tu'i mkhar du legs par grub par byas pa'o// ! //

The Ornament of Abhidharma: A Commentary on the Verses of the Abhidharmakośa was composed near the end of the seventh[1968] five-hundred-year period of the Conqueror’s teachings by the Śākya [Buddhist] monk Jampaiyang, who commenced it at the great and glorious Sakya College and completed it at the Zhongdu palace of the great king, ruler of the earth. I place my crown at the stainless feet of Chim Thamché Khyenpa, the great elder of the lineages of the Land of Snow, from whom I have received and heard many teachings, who holds the banner of the Muni’s teachings with unequaled intelligence that fully differentiates objects of knowledge, who matures and liberates beings through the pure resources of compassion and enlightened action, who is a precious lama and king of the Dharma, who is the crown jewel of scholars practicing restraint and effort, whose maṇḍala of realization fully extends throughout space, containing all objects of knowledge, and the light of whose fame pervades every direction.
